english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from high heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Providing steady moisture and compost prevents flower drop so fruit can form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fũuɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi ni eha aduawai aba.

english: Why should I buy seeds produced here in Ghana instead of expensive seeds imported from abroad?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni afee yɛ Ghana biɛ lɛ moŋ fe dumɔwui ni jara wa ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ?

english: Locally produced hybrid seeds are bred specifically to thrive in Ghana's soil, heat, and weather conditions, making them more reliable and often higher-yielding than imported seeds that were made for different climates.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni afee yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛshwere yɛ Ghana shikpɔŋ, dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ, ni bei pii lɛ, amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ ni afee kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi lɛ.

english: What does it actually mean when someone says a seed is a high-yielding hybrid?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɛ́ mɔ ko kɛɛ dumɔwu ko ji tso ni akɛfee nɔ ko ni woɔ yibii babaoo?

english: A hybrid seed is created by cross-breeding two strong parent plants to combine their best qualities, resulting in crops that grow faster, resist diseases better, and produce a much bigger harvest.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ feɔ kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi tsei enyɔ ni he wa ni akɛfoɔ mli koni akɛ amɛsui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ afee ekome lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni daa oya. Helai ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai ni ekɛ yibiiwoo babaoo baa

english: How can another farmer get double the harvest I get even though we have the exact same size of land?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni okwaafoi krokomɛi ana ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe mi lɛ shii enyɔ, eyɛ mli akɛ wɔyɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ tamɔ mi pɛpɛɛpɛ moŋ?

english: Higher yields depend heavily on the quality of the seed variety planted, alongside proper plant spacing, correct fertilizer timing, and good weed management, rather than just land size alone.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni yaa hiɛ lɛ damɔ dumɔwui ni adu lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ waa. kɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa Be ni sa ni akɛbaatsu nii kɛ jwɛi akwɛmɔ kpakpa Jeee shikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ pɛ.

english: Can I harvest seeds from my hybrid crop this season and keep them to plant next year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa dumɔwui kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli yɛ be nɛɛ mli ni mikɛto koni madu afi ni baa lɛ?

english: It is not recommended to replant seeds saved from hybrid crops because the second generation loses its special strength, leading to uneven crop growth and significantly lower yields.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli ekoŋŋ. Ejaakɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ laaje hewalɛ krɛdɛɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraaa jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why do my crops dry up so quickly whenever the rains stop for just two weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ lɛ baakpa otsii enyɔ pɛ lɛ?

english: Standard or poorly adapted crop varieties have shallow root systems and low drought tolerance, whereas improved local varieties are developed to withstand short dry spells without wilting.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ loo ni esaaa amɛhe lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hɔmɔ naa jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, afee maŋ lɛ mli tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli ni amɛshwieee shi.

english: Why do insects destroy my crops while my neighbor's farm right next to mine stays healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miifite miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo ŋmɔ ni bɛŋkɛ minɔ lɛ kã he ehi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Your neighbor may be using certified improved seeds that have built-in natural resistance to common local pests and diseases, allowing the plants to defend themselves better.
ga: Ekolɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni teɔ shi ewoɔ kooloi kɛ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ miitsu nii. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ.

english: Do high-yielding crop seeds require more fertilizer than the traditional seeds I usually plant?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni miduɔ daa lɛ?

english: Yes, high-yielding varieties grow faster and produce much more food, which means they feed more aggressively and need adequate soil nutrients to reach their maximum potential.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ niyenii babaoo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyeɔ nii babaoo ni amɛbiɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛshɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ he.

english: How can I be sure that the seeds I am buying at the agro-dealer shop are genuine and good quality?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko ŋɔɔ lɛ ji anɔkwale ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Always buy certified seeds in sealed packages carrying official agricultural inspection tags from recognized local seed companies or government-approved distributors.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, hemɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase yɛ kotoku mli ni akɛ okwaayeli he kwɛmɔ he okadi wo nɔ lɛ kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui nitsumɔhe ko ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ loo maŋ nɔyeli lɛ hegbɛ ni ekɛjaa lɛ dɛŋ.

english: Why do some maize varieties mature in three months while others take over four months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli lɛ? yɛ be mli ni henɔi komɛi heɔ be fe nyɔji ejwɛ.

english: Plant breeders create early-maturing seed varieties specifically for areas with short rainy seasons, allowing farmers to harvest early before dry conditions set in.
ga: Mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra titri lɛ kɛha hei ni nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa okwaafoi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛkpaa nii oya dani hɔmɔ shihilɛi baa.

english: If I want to expand my farm to a commercial scale, what is the most important change I need to make to my crops?
ga: Kɛji miisumɔ ni magbɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya jarayeli nitsumɔ mli. Mɛni ji tsakemɔi ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Transitioning to commercial farming requires switching from saved traditional seeds to high-performing certified hybrids, combined with consistent soil feeding and precise planting methods.
ga: Tsakemɔ kɛmiiya jarayeli okwaayeli mli lɛ biɔ tsakemɔ kɛjɛ blema dumɔwui ni aŋmala ashwie shi lɛ anɔ kɛya dumɔwui ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ, ni akɛwo mli lɛ anɔ. Kɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ niyenii ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ dumɔ gbɛi pɔtɛɛ fata he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green leaves, or it could mean the roots are sitting in too much water after heavy rain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli Aloo ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need plantain trees planted next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni adu dumɔwu yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong sunlight; plantain trees grow very quickly and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and cool soil they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋtayaai. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: How do I pick the best cassava stems to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should select mature, healthy cassava stems from plants that are 8 to 12 months old, cutting stems from the middle section of the plant where they are thick and have healthy buds.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala ŋmei tso ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ ŋmei tso ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 mli. Okɛ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot and dry, or when the plant does not get enough water while flowering, preventing the flower from forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ awooo yibii.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks in the soil for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi tsei kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni mi sweet potato tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting the yam vines off the ground using sticks allows the leaves to get full sunlight to feed the growing tuber under the ground, while keeping the leaves dry to protect them from fungal diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei niji tsu nii kɛwo sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la ni fa babaoo koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni miida lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ agbi koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote mli.

english: What naturally causes small holes in the leaves of my young corn crops?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Small holes in corn leaves are usually caused by caterpillars like fall armyworms that hide inside the central leaf funnel of the plant to feed on fresh growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ cutworms ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmeii heei ni eda lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites living on the underside of the leaves and sucking out the plant's juice.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ pepper tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa.

english: How many suckers or shoots should I allow to grow on one plantain tree root?
ga: Esa akɛ maŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii enyiɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu kome shishifãi anɔ?

english: It is best to leave only two or three strong suckers around the main plant so they do not fight each other for nutrients, light, and water in the soil.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi ŋmeii fioo komɛi pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ tso titri lɛ he koni amɛkɛ amɛhe akatswa akaŋ yɛ niyenii, la, kɛ nu he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: What can I put in my soil to feed my crops if I cannot afford chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni mikɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii kɛji minyɛɛɛ mahe tsofa ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You can use dried animal manure, plant leaves, and decomposed food scraps to make compost, which enriches the soil naturally and helps it hold water during dry spells.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbi, tsei ahe baai, kɛ niyenii ni egbo ni eshwɛ lɛ afee ŋmei. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli sɛɛnamɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why does weed grass grow so much faster than my crops right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshinii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have deeper, stronger root systems that absorb rain and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops, allowing them to shoot up quickly if not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa. Amɛheɔ nugbɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa oya kɛji ajieee amɛ oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong, direct sunlight because their young leaves burn easily. They need shade from taller plants like plantains or cassava to protect them during their first two to three years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ tamɔ plantains loo yucca amli. Koni abu tsei ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ mli

english: Which kind of plantain suckers should I select from my old farm to start a new field?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain tsei esa akɛ mahala kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: You should choose 'sword suckers'—the ones with narrow, spear-like leaves and a heavy base. They grow much stronger and produce larger fruit bunches than suckers that have broad, flat leaves early on.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala ‘sword shoot’, ni yɔɔ baai ni mli tseee ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ ni shishitoo lɛ tsii. Amɛdaraa waa ni amɛwoɔ kui wuji fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ shishijee.

english: Officer, why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape?
ga: Officer Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a major food the plant needs to grow leaves and stalks. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure around the plants will restore their green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ Tsei ahe lɛ baaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting maize in the same spot continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas puts nitrogen back into your soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsake lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Do my cowpea plants need a lot of chemical fertilizer to give a good yield like maize does?
ga: Ani mi-cowpea tso lɛ he miihia tsofa babaoo koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai tamɔ ŋmãa?

english: No, cowpea plants make their own nitrogen nutrient from the air through tiny bumps on their roots. They usually only need a small amount of phosphorus fertilizer at planting to produce healthy pods.
ga: Dabi, Cowpea tsei lɛ feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, fɔsfɔs ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara bɔni afee ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What is eating small holes into the middle funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ nɔ

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the central growing point. Applying recommended pesticides or neem extract directly into the central leaf funnel early in the morning will stop them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ wo baai lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akpa amɛ.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or a virus carried by whiteflies. Spraying your plants with insecticidal soap or recommended crop protection products helps control these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ kɛbaa Kɛ́ akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo nibii ni akɛbuɔ tsei ahe ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛbuɔ tsei ahe lɛ afɔ tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when plants don't get enough water, or when there is a lack of pollination. Regular watering and keeping the soil moist helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo be mli ni pollination bɛ lɛ Nu ni awoɔ daa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable farm in the early morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the plants absorb moisture before the sun gets strong. Afternoon watering causes most of the water to evaporate quickly, wasting your efforts.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi koni tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu la lɛ mli awa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli shwane mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ oya. Ehaa ofiteɔ hewalɛ

english: How can I tell under the ground when my cassava roots are ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is ready when the lower leaves yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ.

english: Why should I plant soybeans alongside my maize in my farm here in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu soybeans yɛ ŋmãa masɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Soybeans naturally take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, which acts as a free natural fertilizer that helps your maize grow stronger and yield more.
ga: Soybeans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa o-abele lɛ ni enáa hewalɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why does planting the same local corn on the exact same piece of land every season reduce my yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Maize continuously drains specific nutrients like nitrogen from the soil, so growing it repeatedly exhausts the land unless you rotate it with leguminous crops like soya or groundnuts that restore soil fertility.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ agbɔjɔ Ja ootsake ŋmãa tamɔ soybeans loo ŋmãa. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow and stay small during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ bibii yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen in the soil or that weeds are stealing their food and water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Aloo jwɛi miiju niyenii kɛ nu.

english: Why do my corn leaves curl up tight into tubes during the middle of the hot day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ paipii yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural defense trick maize uses to reduce its leaf surface area so it loses less water to evaporation when the afternoon sun is harsh.
ga: Baai ni atsiɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu ŋaa ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛba baa lɛ hiɛ shi. No hewɔ lɛ, nu fioo pɛ laajeɔ kɛyaa lasu mli kɛ́ shwane hulu la lɛ mli wa waa.

english: Why do I need to heat or roast soya beans before feeding them to livestock or using them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo soybean mli la loo mawo lɛ la dani mikɛha kooloi loo mikɛtsu nii lɛ?

english: Raw soya beans contain natural anti-nutrients that stop animals and humans from digesting them properly; heating breaks down these compounds so the body can absorb the rich protein.
ga: Soybeans ni ahoo lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni gbeɔ niyenii ni tsiɔ kooloi kɛ gbɔmɛi anaa koni amɛkaye amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Dɔlɛ lɛ gbálaa nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ amli bɔni afee ni gbɔmɔtso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ protein ni fa babaoo lɛ.

english: Why must I dry my harvested local corn under the sun until it is hard before storing it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahã mimaŋ ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa dani mikɛto?

english: Freshly harvested corn contains moisture that causes mold to grow and attracts grain weevils, whereas drying the kernels thoroughly keeps them safe and edible for months.
ga: Abɛi ni akpa ehee lɛ mli nu ni haa ŋmei daa ni egbalaa ŋmaa ŋmeii. Yɛ be mli ni agbiɔ dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe ni amɛye nii nyɔji babaoo.

english: How can I stop weevils and insects from destroying my stored maize without expensive chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ naa ni mikɛ tsofai ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: Ensuring your maize is completely dry and storing it in airtight containers or specialized hermetic bags suffocates insects and prevents them from multiplying.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ koni o-abele lɛ agbi kwraa ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo kotoku krɛdɛɛ ko ni akɛwo mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha kooloi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafɔ.

english: Which local crops can I grow in Ghana to produce my own vegetable oil?
ga: Mɛɛ maŋ tsei manyɛ madu yɛ Ghana koni mafee mi diɛŋtsɛ mi tsofa ni akɛwoɔ niyenii mli lɛ?

english: You can successfully grow oil palm, soybeans, groundnuts, and sunflower seeds in Ghana, as all of these crops produce seeds or fruits rich in natural vegetable oil.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ oil palm, soybeans, ŋmei kɛ hulutsoo dumɔwui atsu nii yɛ Ghana yɛ omanyeyeli mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei nɛɛ woɔ dumɔwui loo aduawai ni adebɔɔ mli fɔji babaoo yɔɔ mli.

english: Why do oil palm trees take several years to produce fruit while soya and maize produce in just a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mu tsei heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, soybean kɛ ŋmãa woɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ mli.

english: Maize and soya are annual food crops that complete their life cycle quickly, whereas oil palm is a perennial tree that spends its first few years building a strong trunk and deep root system before it starts bearing fruit.
ga: Abɛi kɛ soybeans ji niyenii ni aduɔ daa afi ni gbeɔ amɛwala shihilɛ naa oya. Yɛ be mli ni oil palm ji tso ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ, eheɔ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ dani ekɛ shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ baa dani ebɔi yibiiwoo.

english: Can soybean crops grow well in all regions across Ghana?
ga: Ani soybean tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpokpai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ anɔ?

english: Soya grows best in areas with moderate rainfall and well-drained soil, making the northern and middle savanna belts of Ghana ideal for its growth compared to extremely waterlogged areas.
ga: Soybeans kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa Savannah kpokpai ni yɔɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ kɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ akɛto hei ni nu babaoo yɔɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Larger trees provide essential shade and retain soil moisture, protecting the delicate leaves of young cocoa from burning before they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã dani amɛdara.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dry from the tips inward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi kɛmiijɛ amɛmligbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants use to build green leaves and grow strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when water stays on my field for too long after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni nu hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When water sits on the field for days without draining, it suffocates the roots, allowing fungus and bacteria to enter and cause rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Beni nu hiɔ ŋmɔ ko mli gbii babaoo ni nu bɛ mli. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ boteɔ mli ni ekɛ fitemɔ baa.

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato pollen becomes dry and sterile. Because the flowers cannot be fertilized, the plant sheds them to conserve water and energy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato pollen lɛ mli egbi ni ebɛ fɔmɔ nii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, fɔfɔi nyɛŋ afee fɔmɔ nii. No hewɔ lɛ tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves curling upward and shrinking into tight little shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miibɔle ehe ni eefee bibioo ko ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding under the leaves, or by viral diseases spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why does planting beans or cowpeas make my soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, leaving free natural fertilizer behind for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ ahaa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to grow big tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ koni ekɛwo bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in sunlight to make food. Staking lifts the vine off the ground, maximizing sunlight exposure so the plant can send energy down into building heavy tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato baai lɛ aha hulu la ashɛ amɛhe koni amɛhoo. Staking baawó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ. Koni hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ atsu hewalɛ kɛba shi koni amɛfee tsɔnei ni tsii.

english: Why should I remove extra shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ midumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Extra suckers compete with the main plantain tree for water and soil nutrients, which results in smaller bunches and slower harvest times for the main stalk.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ feɔ bibioo, ni kpamɔ be lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do armyworm caterpillars hide deep inside the central funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The central funnel of the maize plant provides dark, moist protection from the hot sun and birds, while giving caterpillars direct access to the softest, newest leaves.
ga: Abɛi tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛ okpoi ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ehee fe fɛɛ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds sprout and grow so much faster than my planted crop seeds after the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe dumɔwui ni midu yɛ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally adapted to local conditions and produce tough seeds that sleep in the soil, waiting to burst open immediately at the first sign of water, unlike domesticated crops.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui ni wa ni kã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni miimɛ ni amɛtswa kɛji nu klɛŋklɛŋ okadi ko ba. Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ shia tsei ahe.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot survive full sunlight because their leaves are tender and lose water quickly. They require temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees to protect them from heat and conserve soil moisture during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ baai lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni akɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, wet, and humid conditions. Trimming bushy branches allows sunlight and air to dry out the trees, which stops the fungus from destroying your pods.
ga: Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ black pod hela baa. Tsoi ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ afite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Will cutting off lower branches from my cocoa trees reduce my harvest?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mifo mi-kokoo tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha mi-cocoa tso lɛ nɔ yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi?

english: Pruning lower or extra branches actually increases your yield. It removes wasted energy so the tree can focus on growing bigger cocoa pods, while also improving air movement to prevent diseases.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ loo niji krokomɛi ni oookpa lɛ baaha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Enɛ jieɔ hewalɛ ni afiteɔ lɛ kɛyaa bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ koni helai akamɔ mɔ.

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You can tell it is mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a mostly bare stem with a green top, or by carefully digging up one plant to check the tuber size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baa ko egbɔ kɛji baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Trunk lɛ mli babaoo bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni eyɛ ŋwɛigbɛ eŋɔli. aloo kɛtsɔ tso kome ni oootsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ koni okwɛ bɔ ni eyitso lɛ da ha lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is early weeding so important for a newly planted cassava farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ani ehe miihia ni adu ŋmɔji heei?

english: Young cassava plants grow slowly during their first three months and easily get choked by weeds. Removing weeds early ensures the young plants get maximum sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to form strong tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei bibii lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ amli, ni jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ amɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛfee bulbs ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant cassava between my young cocoa trees, or will it hurt them?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ateŋ? Aloo ebaaye amɛ awui?

english: You can plant cassava with young cocoa during the first year to provide shade and quick food. However, cassava drains a lot of water and nutrients, so it must be harvested and removed before it starts competing with the growing cocoa trees.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmei kɛ kookoo bibii adu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli koni eha hulutsoo kɛ niyenii oya, shi kɛlɛ, ŋmei shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akpa amɛ ni ajie amɛ dani amɛje shishi amɛkɛ kookoo tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ akaŋ.

english: Why should I clear my land in stages instead of planting all 40 acres at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli moŋ fe ni madu acre 40 lɛ fɛɛ shikome?

english: Planting a massive area all at once can overwhelm you when it comes time to weed, harvest, and manage pests. Clearing and planting in smaller blocks allows you to care for each section properly without losing crops to poor maintenance.
ga: Shikpɔŋ wulu ko ni ooodu shikome lɛ baanyɛ anu he akɛ eji nɔ ni tsii fe nine kɛji akɛ eba jwɛi ni ajieɔ, nikpamɔ, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ he. Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni aduɔ yɛ blɔkii bibii amli lɛ Haa okwɛɔ fã fɛɛ fã nɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni ŋmɔshi nibii fiteee yɛ nɔ ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ

english: Why do my crops produce plenty of green leaves but very little fruit or tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi aduawai loo ŋmeii fioo pɛ woɔ lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes plants to focus on leaf growth rather than root or fruit development. Crops need balanced nutrients, particularly phosphorus and potassium, to develop thick cassava roots and healthy pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ yeɔ hiɛ fe shishifãi loo aduawai lɛ adalɛ. Niyenii ni sa he miihia tsei. titri lɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium Koni ekɛ ŋmeii shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa aba

english: How can I stop the soil around my crops from drying out during the Harmattan season?
ga: Matsĩ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃. Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ Harmattan be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground around your crops with dry grass, fallen leaves, or plant stalks creates a protective blanket called mulch. This keeps the soil cool and prevents water from evaporating quickly in the heat.
ga: Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ. baai ni egbee shi loo tsei ahe tsei koni akɛfee nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry heat spell that can scorch germinating seeds. It is safer to wait until the rains become regular so the soil stays moist enough for young roots to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ hɔmɔ ni mli wa ni baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ daa bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi bibii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Which direction should I lay out my crop rows when planting on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei akutsei ama shi kɛ́ midu nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Planting crop rows in a North-to-South direction allows your crops to receive balanced sunlight from East to West throughout the day without taller plants completely blocking light from shorter ones.
ga: Tsei ni ooodu yɛ sɛɛkuu mli yɛ kooyigbɛ kɛyaa anaigbɛ lɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa hulu la ni jɛɔ bokagbɛ kɛyaa anaigbɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli. he ni tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ tsiii kane ni jɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ kuku lɛ amli lɛ naa kwraa lɛ.

english: How should I position my seedling nursery shade to protect my young crop shoots from the harsh sun?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ midumɔwui lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ awo midumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he?

english: Positioning your nursery shelter so its roof length runs East to West helps cast continuous shade over tender seedlings during the hottest midday hours when sunlight is direct and intense.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ otsu lɛ to he ko bɔni afee ni ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ ajɛ bokagbɛ kɛya anaigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ aná hulutsoo be fɛɛ be yɛ shwane mli ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli, beni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants stunt the growth of cassava planted right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ miitsi ŋmei ni adu yɛ emasɛi lɛ dalɛ naa lɛ?

english: Maize grows rapidly and tall, casting a shadow that blocks sunlight from reaching the lower leaves of cassava plants, which stops the cassava from making enough food to grow well.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni ekwɛɔ. Susumɔ ko yɛ ni tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ ŋmei lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmei nyɛɛɛ ewo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop and curl up during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Under intense afternoon sunlight and high heat, crop leaves lose moisture faster than roots can draw water from the soil, causing the plant to wilt temporarily to conserve water.
ga: Yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ latsaa ni naa wa shishi lɛ, tsei ahe baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbimɔ tsei yɛ be kukuoo mli koni nu akafite.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field without tall trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle intense direct sunlight because their roots and leaves are tender; they need shade trees to act like umbrellas until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi bibii kɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahewɔ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo koni amɛtsu nii akɛ umbrella kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Can excessive sunlight burn crop leaves the same way it causes heat stress in farm animals?
ga: Ani hulu la ni fa fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ahe baai yɛ gbɛ ni ekɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa ŋmɔ mli kooloi anɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, extreme afternoon sun combined with dry soil can scorch crop leaves, turning the edges dry and brown because the intense heat damages the delicate plant tissues.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, shwane hulu ni naa wa ni akɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi fata he lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ahe baai lɛ ashã. Ehaa baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Do all crops in Ghana need direct sunlight all day long to yield well?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: No, while sun-loving crops like maize and tomatoes need full sun, shade-tolerant crops like cocoyam, ginger, and young cocoa perform better under indirect light or partial shade.
ga: Dabi, eyɛ mli akɛ tsei ni sumɔɔ hulu tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ tomato he miihia hulu ni fa babaoo moŋ. Shi tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli tamɔ kookoo, ŋmei, kɛ kookoo ni mli tse lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ la ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ loo hulutsoo fioo ko shishi.

english: Why does the harsh sun dry out my farm soil so quickly after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Direct sunlight striking bare soil heats up the ground surface and rapidly evaporates stored soil moisture into the air before plant roots can absorb it.
ga: Hulu la ni tswaa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔɔ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni ato lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: How can I prevent the intense afternoon sun from baking the roots of my vegetables?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ naa koni ekashã mi-vegetable shishifãi lɛ?

english: Covering the bare soil around your crop roots with dried grass or leaves, known as mulching, blocks direct sunlight and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni okɛwoɔ ohe lɛ Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo otsei lɛ ashishi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why is it harmful to water my crops in the middle of a hot, sunny afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Watering under direct scorching sun causes high evaporation loss, and sudden cold water on hot leaves can shock the plant while wasting most of the water before it reaches the roots.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni fa babaoo fiteɔ. Ni nu ni mli ejɔ ni baa trukaa yɛ baai ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ he akpokpo ejaakɛ nu lɛ fa ko fiteɔ dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out the soil. Leaving taller trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains creates a cool shelter that protects the young cocoa plants during their early years.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa anáa he ko ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential food for plant growth. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps keep the leaves green and enables the plant to grow big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave standing water in the field, the roots drown from a lack of air and rot-causing organisms begin to destroy them.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ kpɛɔ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ ni nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ baabɔi amɛfitemɔ.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my pepper plants without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni pepper ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or lack of water. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot weather helps the flowers stay on the plant and turn into healthy fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Planting maize continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season and encourages maize pests to stay in the ground. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans restores nitrogen to the soil and disrupts pest life cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni ewo ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ koni amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛtsakeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni efoɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ mli

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes through the central leaves of my young maize crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu kɛmiitsɔ mi-baby corn lɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the tender growing tips of young maize plants. Early detection and spraying recommended organic mixtures or safe pest treatments help protect the plant before it suffers severe damage.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni miida lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ. Akɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ ana nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ mra ni akɛshwie nɔ. Aloo, tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛbaagbe tso lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni ebu tso lɛ he dani efite waa.

english: The first rain often wet only the top layer of dirt while the deep soil stays dry, and a long dry period usually follows. Waiting until the rains become steady ensures the soil has deep moisture to support seeds through germination.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ hiɔ shi ni egbiɔ ni bei pii lɛ, egbiɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ enɛ hewɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ mɛ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ waa koni eye ebua dumɔwui lɛ kɛtsɔ amɛkwɛ̃mɔ nɔ.

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to make food for the plant. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground, maximizing sunlight capture so the plant can send energy down to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ hulu la ni anáa lɛ nɔ babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Enɛ haa tsei tsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal nutrients, water, and sunlight from the main plantain tree. Pruning away all but one or two strong shoots ensures the main tree gets full nourishment to yield a large bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsoi loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ mli, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa niyenii ni yeɔ emuu koni ewo plantains babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and turning small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or aphids transmitting a virus. Controlling these insects early with insecticidal soap or recommended treatments keeps the plant leaves healthy and broad.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ tomato mli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ baai lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni egbɛ ashwã.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo lolo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient that helps plants build healthy stems and green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛ naa tsei ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is damp after a good rain so the roots can easily drink in the nutrients, and avoid putting it on very dry or flooded land.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mlɛo. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ he ni nu egbi loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ni oookɛwo lɛ he.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize in the exact same spot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be fɛɛ be lɛ ehiii kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that feed on that specific crop to build up in your field.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow plenty of flowers but then drop them without making fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii babaoo shi egbeeɔ shi ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the air gets extremely hot and dry, or when the plant doesn't get enough water, causing it stress that prevents fruit creation.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni tsiɔ aduawai anaa lɛ baa.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes when there is a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei kɛji amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Rolling up leaves is a self-defense reaction. It hides the leaf surface from the hot sun so the plant loses less water through evaporation while waiting for rain.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji nɔ ko ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he. Ha hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he baa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu fioo kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ be mli ni amɛmiimɛ nugbɔ lɛ.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and fall off, typically around 9 to 12 months after planting, leaving bare main stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Kɛtsɔ tsɔne lɛ mli tsɔne titri lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers turn soft and rot underground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔɔ lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot underground when water sits in heavy soil for too long without draining, or when tiny worms called nematodes damage the tubers under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Aloo kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ kpata shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: How do weeds cause my crops to grow smaller and weaker?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa?

english: Weeds act like thieves in your field—their roots steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from your crops, leaving the main plants with less food to grow big.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛshishifãi lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ náa niyenii fioo ni ekɛbaadara.

english: Why should I leave clear space between my crop seeds instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaving proper space prevents plants from competing with each other for light and nutrients, and allows fresh air to pass through, which keeps crop diseases away.
ga: Kɛ́ aha he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaatsi tsei anaa koni amɛkaye la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai anaa

english: Why is March considered the best month for me to start planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abuɔ March akɛ eji nyɔŋ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: March marks the beginning of the major rainy season in many parts of Ghana. Planting in March ensures your seeds get enough early moisture to germinate well and build strong roots before the peak rains.
ga: March ji nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ shishijee yɛ Ghana hei babaoo. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ March mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa nu oya bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. ni amɛma shishifãi ni wa dani nugbɔ lɛ ayashɛ eshishijee he.

english: What is the difference between planting my crops in March versus planting in September?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ mi tsei ni miduɔ yɛ March mli kɛ September mli ni miduɔ lɛ teŋ?

english: March is the start of the major rainy season, which brings longer and heavier rainfall suitable for crops that take time to mature. September is the start of the minor rainy season, which is shorter and better suited for fast-growing crops.
ga: March ji nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ shishijee. ni haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ Ehi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa be koni amɛkwɛ̃. September ji nugbɔshiimɔ be fioo lɛ shishijee, ni eyɛ kuku ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ adumɔ.

english: How many times in a single year can I clear and plant crops on my farm?
ga: Shii enyiɛ manyɛ mafo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni madu yɛ afi mli?

english: In areas with two rainy seasons, you can plant up to two or three times a year—typically starting the main cycle around March or April and a second cycle around September.
ga: Yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ shii enyɔ lɛ, obaanyɛ odu shii 2-3 yɛ afi mli, ni bei pii lɛ, ojeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ shishi yɛ March loo April he. kɛ fã ni ji enyɔ lɛ yɛ September aaafee.

english: What should I do if the March rains arrive late on my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji March nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ fo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: If the rains are delayed in March, hold off on planting until the soil receives steady rain. Sowing seeds in dry soil can cause them to scorch or fail to sprout.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ yɛ March mli lɛ Kpa dumɔ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná nugbɔ be fɛɛ be. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ ashã loo amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Why do some farmers plant new crops every three months instead of once a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei daa nyɔji etɛ, shi jeee shikome yɛ afi mli lɛ?

english: Planting every three months allows you to produce a continuous supply of food, maximize the use of your land, and earn income throughout the year instead of waiting for a single annual harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ odu nii daa nyɔji etɛ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii be fɛɛ be. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii ni oná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo ni oná shika yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ daa afi ŋmaakpamɔ kome pɛ.

english: Which crops should I select for the short rainy period that begins in September?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ mahala yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku ni jeɔ shishi yɛ September mli lɛ mli?

english: For the September season, choose quick-maturing crops like beans, cowpeas, or short-duration vegetables, as the rainfall period is shorter than the major season.
ga: Kɛha September be lɛ Halamɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ ŋmeii, tsina ŋmeii, loo aduawai ni yeɔ be kukuoo. Ejaakɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ faaa fe be titri lɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to plant the exact same crop on my land every three months?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa nyɔji etɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously can drain specific nutrients from the soil and cause pest problems to build up. It is best to rotate different types of crops between planting cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aaaya nɔ akwɛ lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni abua naa lɛ ahe naagbai aba. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni atsake ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi. Yɛ be mli ni aduɔ nii lɛ

english: How do I know when my farm is ready for a second planting season in September?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni miŋmɔ lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ be ni ji enyɔ yɛ September mli lɛ?

english: Your land is ready for September planting after you have harvested your main season crops, cleared the field, and the second rains have moistened the soil enough for land preparation.
ga: Oshikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ yɛ September mli beni okpa be titri lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ he lɛ Ni nugbɔ ni nɛ ni ji enyɔ lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ.

english: How does staggering my planting every few months help my farm income?
ga: Te nyɔji fioo komɛi baanyɛ aye abua ni aná shika kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Staggering your planting schedules spreads out your harvests across the year, helping you avoid selling all your produce when market prices are low during peak harvest seasons.
ga: Odumɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ ni ooofee lɛ naakpɛɛ lɛ baaha odumɔ nii lɛ agbɛ ashwã afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni otsiɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ onibii fɛɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ ahɔ̃ɔmɔ he beni jara nɔ jara baa shi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow faster during the March-April season than later in the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya yɛ March-April mli fe afi lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ?

english: Crops often grow faster and stronger in the March-April season because rising temperatures combined with early rains create warm, moist soil conditions ideal for rapid plant development.
ga: Tsei lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa kɛjɛɔ March kɛyashi April. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulutsoo ni yaa hiɛ ni akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ fataa he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei ni yaa hiɛ oya lɛ baa.

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow from the bottom up when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, or when the soil stays too wet for too long, which prevents the roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai.

english: Why do groundnut plants push their stems into the soil after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ tsiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts naturally form their fruits underground. After the flowers are pollinated above ground, the plant produces 'pegs' that grow downward into the soil where the groundnut pods develop safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii woɔ yibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Beni atswa fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ feɔ ‘ŋmeii’ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves up toward direct sunlight. When the leaves get enough sunlight, they make more food for the plant, resulting in much larger tubers under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la lɛ aba amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa Ebaafee niyenii babaoo aha tsei lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji babaoo baa.

english: Why do my fruiting plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy rain or wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not go deep into the ground. When a heavy bunch grows, the plant becomes top-heavy and needs a strong wooden pole or bamboo fork for support.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ kuu lɛ da Tsei lɛ tsii ni amɛbiɔ tsei ni wa loo ŋmeii ni akɛfee ŋmeii ni akɛfi amɛsɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when the rainy season becomes too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When soil remains waterlogged for long periods, water displaces the air, suffocating the roots and causing rot-causing fungi to multiply.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehi shi ni nu eyi mli obɔ be kakadaŋŋ Nu baaye kɔɔyɔɔ najiaŋ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ feɔ babaoo

english: Why does rice grow well in low, flooded land while my maize crop dies in standing water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu afua shikpɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ gboɔ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal channels in their stems that carry oxygen down to their roots even when submerged in water. Maize roots do not have these channels and drown quickly in waterlogged soil.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ mligbɛ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shi kɛyaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛji akɛ amɛbote nu mli po. Abele shishifãi bɛ nɛkɛ gbɛi nɛɛ ni amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli oya.

english: Why do young cocoa trees wither and die if I clear all the tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei kakadaji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct intense sunlight and high heat. Tall shade trees protect cocoa leaves from sun scorch and help keep moisture in the soil around the young plants.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers drying up and falling off without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when weather temperatures become too hot, when watering is uneven, or when the plant lacks sufficient nutrients like phosphorus during the flowering stage.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ bɛ daa loo kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa tamɔ fɔsfɔs yɛ fɔfɔi be mli.

english: Leaf curl on pepper plants is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like mites, thrips, or aphids feeding on the leaf juices, or by viruses spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mites, thrips, loo aphids ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of leafy leaves but fail to form bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo shi enyɛɛɛ efee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer causes cowpeas to grow leaves instead of flowers. Additionally, tiny insect pests like flower thrips can attack and destroy the flower buds before pods can grow.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha cowpea lɛ afee baai yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Kɛfata he lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ fɔfɔii ashishifãi baanyɛ atutua ni amɛfite fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ aba.

english: Why should I plant plantains on my farm before I plant young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily in bright sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that provide temporary shade and keep the soil moist while the young cocoa trees are establishing themselves.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fũuɔ yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Will planting plantains alongside cocoa steal nutrients away from my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani plantain ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ baaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mi kookoo tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Plantains and young cocoa can share space well if spaced properly. The temporary shade and wind protection plantains provide early on far outweigh the small amount of soil nutrients they use.
ga: Plantains bibii kɛ cocoa baanyɛ aja he jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ amɛto amɛhe jogbaŋŋ. Be kukuoo mli shade kɛ dumɔwui haa kɔɔyɔɔ hebuu mra. Enɛ feɔ sũ mli niyenii fioo ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii lɛ.

english: How long should I leave plantains growing together with my cocoa crops?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ maha plantains kɛ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ afee ekome kɛkwɛ̃?

english: Plantains are usually kept for the first two to three years. Once the cocoa trees grow tall enough to form their own thick canopy and shade the ground, the plantains should be cut down so the cocoa gets full sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ plantains toɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ. Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni efee ŋwɛi ŋta ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, Esa akɛ afo dumɔwui lɛ koni kookoo lɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: What is the proper step-by-step order for preparing a new field for cocoa?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ asaa kookoo shikpɔŋ hee?

english: First, clear the thick bush during the dry season. Next, plant plantains or shade trees, and once they start growing leaves, clear the ground base and plant your young cocoa seedlings at the start of the rainy season.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Nɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ji, du tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo. Ni kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɔi baai lɛ, Tsumɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni odu kookoo tsei bibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: Why is proper timing and planning so crucial when clearing bush for cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be kɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni sa he hiaa waa kɛ́ ajieɔ jwɛi kɛha kookoo lɛ?

english: If you clear bush too early without planting right away, weeds will quickly overgrow the field again. Timing land preparation with the rainy season ensures young plants get immediate water to survive.
ga: Kɛji ojie ojwɛi lɛ oya tsɔ ni oduuu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ekoŋŋ. Kɛ́ asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli kɛha nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ, ehaa tsei bibii lɛ náa nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why is it better for me to clear my farm myself instead of relying completely on hired contractors?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ majie ŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ mihe baafɔ mɔ ko ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Hired contractors often rush to finish land clearing and may accidentally cut down young cocoa seedlings or fail to clear weeds around the plant base properly. Doing it yourself or closely supervising ensures delicate young plants are protected.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ feɔ oya koni amɛgbe he ni amɛtsuɔ nii yɛ lɛ naa. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ oshara afo kookoo tsei bibii loo ejie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ ehiii kwraa. Bo diɛŋtsɛ feemɔ loo kwɛmɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni abu tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe.

english: What damage happens to my cocoa trees if I let my farm become overgrown with weeds?
ga: Mɛni baafite mi-kookoo tsei lɛ kɛji miha jwɛi shwere yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Overgrown weeds steal nutrients, fertilizer, and water from the soil, block sunlight from reaching low branches, and create a damp hideout for destructive insects and crop diseases.
ga: Jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɛɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe. ni amɛfee hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ kɛha kooloi ni fiteɔ nii kɛ tsei ahe helai.

english: Why is it necessary to clear weeds around the base of my cocoa plants instead of just clearing the walking paths?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishi moŋ fe ni ajie jwɛi yɛ gbɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Clearing the base directly around the tree root zone eliminates root competition for food and water, prevents pests from climbing up the stem, and makes it easy to inspect for trunk diseases.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ni ajieɔ shishitoo lɛ he lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ akaŋshii kɛha niyenii kɛ nu lɛ baa shi. Etsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɔ tso lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaana hela yɛ tso lɛ mli

english: Besides clearing weeds, what main things cause diseases to spread on a cocoa farm?
ga: Kɛfata jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he lɛ Mɛni ji nibii titrii ni haa helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kookoo ŋmɔji amli?

english: Diseases like Black Pod spread when a farm is too dark and humid from unpruned trees, when infected pods are left rotting on branches, or when water carries fungal spores from plant to plant.
ga: Helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji ŋmɔji amli ewo duŋ tsɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ kɛjɛ tsei ni afolɔko amɛhe lɛ amli. Beni ashiɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ koni amɛgboi yɛ tsei aniji anɔ, Aloo be mli ni nu woɔ ŋmeii ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ.

english: How does keeping my farm clear of overgrown weeds help prevent cocoa diseases?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ bɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ekɛtsi kookoo hela naa?

english: Clearing bush allows sunlight and fresh air to pass freely between trees. This air flow dries up excess dampness on leaves and pods, which stops fungal diseases from multiplying.
ga: Tsoi bibii ni agbele naa lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ oya. Nɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ nɛɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ baai lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wilt and die when the sun gets too blazing hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade trees like plantains or Gliricidia to protect them from direct sunlight. Direct blazing sun scorches their tender leaves and dries out soil moisture before their roots can grow deep enough to find water.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo glicidia. Bɔni afee ni abu kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ebaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ aya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛna nu.

english: Why is the rainy season in September so important for my cocoa harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ September nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ he hiaa yɛ mi-kokoo kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: September rains provide the heavy water supply needed for cocoa pods to swell and mature during the main crop season. Adequate rain during this month ensures the beans inside the pods fill out properly before harvest.
ga: September nugbɔ lɛ haa nu ni he hiaa koni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ alɛɛ mli ni amɛdara yɛ be titri ni amɛdaraa lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ bɔ ni sa yɛ nyɔji nɛɛ amli lɛ haa kɔfi yibii lɛ eyiɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ dani akpaa.

english: How can I tell the exact month my cocoa pods are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-kokoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ he koni akpa?

english: Cocoa pods are ready for harvesting when their color changes completely—green pods turn bright yellow, and red pods turn orange-yellow. Counting 5 to 6 months from the time the flowers bloom also helps predict the harvest month.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni amɛhe su etsake kwraa lɛ. Pods eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ni ŋmeii tsuji lɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii-ŋmei nyɔji 5 kɛyashi 6 kɛjɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ lɛ, ni no hu yeɔ ebuaa ni atsɔɔ kpamɔ nyɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Does extreme afternoon heat hurt my crop flowers when they are blooming?
ga: Ani latsaa ni naa wa ni baa shwane mli lɛ náa fɔfɔi ni fɔ̃ɔ lɛ anɔ hewalɛ gbonyo?

english: Yes, intense heat causes crop flowers to dry out and drop off before they can be pollinated to form fruits or pods. Planting shade trees and windbreaks helps lower temperatures around the farm canopy.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee pollination ni amɛtsɔ aduawai loo ŋmeii. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsiɔ hei ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo ni ebɔle he lɛ baa shi. Okwaafoi ashishi

english: Why do cocoa trees produce pods at two different times of the year instead of just once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii yɛ afi lɛ mli bei srɔtoi enyɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee pod kome pɛ

english: Cocoa trees follow Ghana's two rain cycles. The major rainy season feeds the main crop harvest (October to February), while the minor rains feed the smaller mid-crop harvest (May to August).
ga: Cocoa tsei nyiɛɔ Ghana nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ haa niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii titri ni akpaa lɛ. (October kɛyashi February) yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ haa nyɔŋ teŋ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ niyenii. (Manyawale kɛyashi Manyawale)

english: Why do my crop pods turn black and rot during heavy rainy months like September?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa tamɔ September lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains combined with cool, moist air promote Black Pod disease, which is caused by a fungus. Pruning excess branches and clearing weeds lets sun and air reach the pods to keep them dry.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ black pod hela baa, ni ŋmei kɛbaa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ojie jwɛi lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe ni amɛgbi.

english: What can I do to protect my crop roots when the sun stays hot without rain for a whole month?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mabu mitso lɛ shishifãi ahe beni hulu lɛ mli edɔɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ nyɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: You can cover the soil around your crops with dry leaves or plant stalks (mulching). Mulch acts as a blanket that traps soil moisture and protects crop roots from baking under the hot sun.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ nibii ni baai egbi loo tsei ashishifãi (mulch). Mulch lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni haa sũ mli nu lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebuɔ tsei shishifãi ahe koni amɛkashã yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why does it take several months between seeing small pods on my cocoa tree and actually picking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni enaa pod bibioo ko Yɛ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ ni eŋɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, eheɔ nyɔji babaoo.

english: After pollination, cocoa pods pass through a long development stage where they build skin thickness, seed structure, and cocoa butter content. This growth process naturally takes 5 to 6 months.
ga: yɛ pollination sɛɛ Cocoa pods lɛ tsɔɔ shweremɔ gbɛ kakadaŋŋ mli. It creates the thickness of the skin. Dumɔwui lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔtoo kɛ bɔ ni kookoo bɔta lɛ fa ha Nɛkɛ dalɛ gbɛ nɛɛ heɔ nyɔji 5 kɛyashi 6 yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do I know the best month to clear and prepare my field before the rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nyɔŋ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ majie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ ni masaa he dani nugbɔ anɛ?

english: Field preparation is best done late in the dry season (January to February). Clearing early ensures your land is prepped so you can plant immediately with the very first consistent rains of the season.
ga: Esa akɛ afee he ni asaa he lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ naagbee. (January kɛyashi February) Ajieɔ jɛmɛ mra. It helps ensure that your land is prepared. Enɛ ji koni onyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ ba daa pɛ.

english: Is it safe to dry my harvested cocoa beans directly under the blazing sun?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaagbi kookoo yibii ni akpa lɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, drying under direct sunlight on raised bamboo mats is ideal, but the beans must be spread thin and turned frequently so they dry evenly without scorching or trapping mould-causing moisture.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmei saatso nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ. Shi ehe miihia ni agbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashwã bibioo ni atsɔ mli shii abɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gĩɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni shãaa loo emɔɔ nu ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or that heavy rains have soaked the ground too much, preventing the roots from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I clear my farm without burning the dry brush and leaves on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni mikɛshãaa jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the rich organic food in the ground and kills good soil insects, whereas letting plant leaves rot naturally feeds the soil and helps it hold water during dry dry spells.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni jara wa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni egbeɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ahe baai ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛgboi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are ready to harvest if I cannot see under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa? Kɛji onyɛɛɛ ona shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Cassava lets you know it is ready when its lower stem leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem with only a small cluster of green leaves at the top, usually 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Yucca haa oleɔ akɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tsoi ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ pɛ eshwɛɔ, bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin, tall, and weak when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe kpaakpa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the young plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving all of them weak and unable to yield well.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why is it necessary for me to put tall wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high on sticks so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight, which gives the plant energy to grow big tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily burn under full sun; they need shade from larger trees or temporary shade crops like plantains to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why does my plantain tree produce small bunches when many new shoots grow around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni ŋmeii heei babaoo baabɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and food from the main plantain tree; cutting them back so only one or two remain ensures the main tree grows a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tsobii krokomɛi loo tsei bibii juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo lɛ sɛɛ bɔni afee ni tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ daa ni etsɔɔ tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant feels stressed from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of plant food needed to hold and mature the fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa koni akɛto yibii lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ni bɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop dark, rotten spots at the bottom while still on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Dark spots on tomato bottoms happen when the plant does not get enough calcium or experiences irregular watering, causing the skin at the bottom to break down.
ga: Tomato tsei anɔ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ baa kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa hewolo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the ground when I plant right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni miduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The first rain after a dry spell often heats up the hot soil without providing enough lasting moisture, causing seeds to germinate and quickly dry out or rot if rains stop for a few days.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be sɛɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya loo amɛgboiɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛ gbii fioo komɛi.
