english: Cocoa flowers require pollination by tiny insects like midges to set fruit. If insect activity is low, or if the tree is under stress from heat, poor soil nutrients, or dry weather, the tree drops its flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii biɔ ni kooloi bibii, tamɔ mɛi ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ afee amɛ pollin koni amɛwo yibii. Kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ loo tso lɛ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ shishi. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do cocoa pods ripen at different times on the exact same tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli yɛ tso kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce flowers continuously over several months rather than all at once. Because pods grow from flowers that were pollinated weeks apart, they mature at different stages throughout the season.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi be fɛɛ be nyɔji babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafɔ fɔfɔi shikome. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ amɛhe otsii babaoo lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ daa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ daa yɛ hei srɔtoi yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How does sunlight affect the yield of my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Te hulu la lɛ saa mi-kokoo tsei ni eda lɛ ayibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: While young cocoa plants need shade to survive, full-grown cocoa trees need controlled sunshine to produce abundant flowers and pods. However, too much direct sun without moisture can burn the leaves and dry out the soil.
ga: Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulutsoo he miihia kookoo tsei bibii koni amɛhi shi. Kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ taoɔ hulu la ni akudɔ amɛ koni amɛ wo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo. Shi kɛlɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ tsɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi.

english: Why are my young cocoa pods shriveling up and turning black before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miiho ni amɛmiitsɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This can be caused by Cherelle Wilt, where the tree naturally discards pods it cannot feed, or by fungal infections like Black Pod disease, which spread quickly in damp, unshaded farms.
ga: Cherelle Wilt, ni etsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni nyɛŋ amɛye niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ baanyɛ aha enɛ aba. aloo kɛtsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ, tamɔ black pod hela, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate a lack of essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, poor drainage causing root rot, or damage from sap-sucking pests like capsids.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. loo nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ nu tamɔ capsids lɛ fiteɔ.

english: What causes the stems of my cocoa trees to swell up and become deformed?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miifu ni efite?

english: Swollen stems are a sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease, which is spread by mealybugs. It severely weakens the plant, reduces pod yield, and can eventually kill the tree.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni efuu lɛ ji cocoa bud virus hela ni mealybugs gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ waa, ehaa pod yibiiwoo baa shi, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbe tso lɛ.

english: What are those tiny, white, cotton-like spots on my cocoa stems and pods?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmeii bibii ni yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo tsei kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Those spots are mealybugs. They feed on the sap of your cocoa trees, weakening the plant and spreading viral diseases from farm to farm.
ga: Nakai hei lɛ ji ŋmeii. Amɛyeɔ nu ni jɛɔ o-cacao tsei lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli lɛ eshwaa.

english: How does heavy rainfall affect my cocoa crop yield?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa mi-kookoo lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Excessive rain creates high humidity, which creates the perfect conditions for fungal diseases like Black Pod to spread, while also making it difficult for pollinating insects to visit cocoa flowers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji lɛ agbɛ ashwã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ewaa ahaa ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ akɛ amɛaayasara kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Dry Harmattan winds strip moisture from the leaves and soil, causing cocoa trees to drop leaves and shed young pods to keep the main tree alive through the dry spell.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Ha kookoo tsei lɛ ajie amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛshwie amɛbii bibii lɛ koni tso titri lɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How does letting weeds grow around my cocoa trees harm pod production?
ga: Aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te mi cacao tso lɛ saa pod feemɔ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal vital water, space, and soil nutrients away from cocoa roots. When weeds compete with your cocoa trees, the trees produce fewer, smaller pods.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ kookoo shishifãi amli. Kɛ jwɛi kɛ kookoo tsei miitswa akaŋ lɛ Tso lɛ baawo ŋmeii fioo ni amɛbaafee bibii.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers. Lifting their leaves off the ground allows them to capture more sunlight to make food, which leads to bigger underground tubers while protecting the leaves from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ gɔŋ. Kɛ́ awó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulu la babaoo ni amɛkɛhooɔ nii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off the small extra shoots growing out from the side of my cocoa tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ cacao tso lɛ masɛi lɛ

english: Those extra shoots, often called chupons, steal water and nutrients away from the main branches. Removing them ensures the tree directs its energy into producing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi nɛɛ akɛ chupons. Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso nine wulu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I remove some of the young suckers growing around the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to compete with the main stem for food and water. Keeping only one or two strong suckers ensures your plantain produces large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ abɔi niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ 1 loo 2 pɛ to lɛ, ebaaha o-plantains lɛ awo niji agboi ni tsii.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient needed for leaf growth, or that heavy rainfall has flooded the roots and prevented them from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ akwɛ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo nugbɔ miinɛ waa, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu, ni ehaaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛye niyenii.

english: Why does my cassava plant have plenty of big leaves above ground but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or foliage growth isn't managed, the plant uses all its energy to build leaves and stems instead of storing energy in the root tubers.
ga: Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai kɛ tsei. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas improve my soil for the next farming season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas have friendly bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ helai ni haa mɔ feɔ naanyo yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What will happen if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the same farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Planting maize seeds too close together causes the plants to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in tall, thin stalks with small or missing cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ dumɔwui bibii loo ni bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why shouldn't I water my vegetable leaves directly during the hot sun at midday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ afɔɔ aduawai anɔ nu tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shwane mli yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Watering hot leaves in bright sunlight causes quick evaporation that can scorch the leaves and creates a warm, humid surface where fungal diseases easily spread.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nu wo baai ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baa oya, ni baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot and dry, or when the soil lacks enough moisture and nutrients like phosphorus to support fruit formation.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni sũ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa, tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni baaye abua ni aduawai afee.

english: Wrinkled or curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap from undersides of leaves, or by viral infections passed on by pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni egbɔjɔ loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi lɛ? Ha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to manufacture food that feeds the growing tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they catch full sunlight and receive good airflow, which prevents leaf fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni miida lɛ niyenii. Staking woɔ tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli. ni tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ naa

english: When crops are crowded, their roots fight each other underground for limited soil food and water, while their leaves block each other from sunlight. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets its fair share of nourishment to produce well.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ niyenii ni sa nɔ koni ekɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and weak root systems that cannot pull up water fast enough to withstand harsh heat. Planting them under fast-growing shade crops like plantains protects them until their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ ajie nu oya bɔ ni sa ni ekɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ naa. Kɛ́ adu tsei nɛɛ yɛ hulutsoo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baashɛ shɔŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for help showing the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and grow leaves. It often happens in tired soil or when heavy rains wash away nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji haomɔ he okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ baai. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ nɔ loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before growing into actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛdara ni amɛbatsɔ pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when exposed to stress, such as severe heat, dry soil, or too much fertilizer. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to conserve energy and stay alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛkɛ haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kpe. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over right when the fruit bunch starts getting large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji aduawai akutsei lɛ je shishi amɛdara pɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow, fibrous roots that stay near the surface. As the fruit bunch gets heavy, the top becomes unbalanced, making it easy for wind or soft wet soil to pull the root system out of the ground.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni yɔɔ fiber ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsii lɛ Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni efɔ lɛ gbalaa shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting inside the ground if heavy rains continue for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa lɛ tee nɔ nɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When soil stays soaked with excess water, air cannot reach the underground tubers. Without air, the tubers drown and rot quickly as harmless bacteria and fungi thrive in waterlogged mud.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Tubers lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboiɔ oya be mli ni bacteria kɛ fungi ni bɛ awui lɛ shwereɔ yɛ muji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize seeds when the rainy season starts?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Seeds need consistent moisture to germinate safely. It is best to wait until the ground has received a few reliable heavy rains that soak deep into the soil, rather than planting after the very first brief shower.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ he miihia amɛ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni naa wa fioo ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Mohu ɔ, du ngɛ kekleekle nugbɔ kuku ɔ se.

english: What is causing tiny holes in the fresh funnel leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ a-cone baai heei lɛ amli

english: Small holes in fresh maize leaves are typically created by hungry caterpillars, like the Fall Armyworm, hiding inside the central leaf roll and chewing through the leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baa lɛ mli dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo lɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai heei amli lɛ.

english: How do wild weeds hurt my crops if there is enough land on the farm?
ga: Te koo mli jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji miyɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Weeds grow much faster and stronger than farm crops. They aggressively steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops while also providing hiding places for insects that attack your plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa ni amɛhe wa fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ yiwalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii ni tutuaa otsei lɛ feɔ he ko ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small ears when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ woɔ toi bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the maize plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to feed well and produce full, large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Abele tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food crops need to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛji niyenii titrii ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards into tight shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking sap from underneath the leaves. Spraying with neem oil or recommended insecticides controls these pests and stops leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ kooloi nɛɛ ni ebaaha baai lɛ afitemɔ akpa.

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers stay healthy and develop into tomatoes.
ga: Tomatoi baagbee shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ miigba enaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Does it matter which way up I insert cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmei niji awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, cassava stems must be planted with the small growth buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting stems upside down causes plants to struggle, resulting in low root yields.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ tso lɛ ni edaa kɛyaa shishi lɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni ajieɔ lɛ faaa.

english: Why do I need to lift my yam vines onto wooden stakes instead of letting them grow along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into the sunlight so the plant can make more food, which feeds the tuber underground. It also keeps leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii babaoo. ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ he. Tsi fungal helai anaa

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help improve my soil for the next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. When the crop is harvested, that natural fertilizer remains in the ground to nourish the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How does spreading dry grass around my crops help them grow better during dry spells?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket. It prevents sunshine from drying out the soil, keeps plant roots cool, and reduces weed growth.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni eha jwɛi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ aba shi

english: What is eating small ragged holes through the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni miitsɔ mi-bibii ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ yeli?

english: Ragged holes in the central leaves of corn are a classic sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide deep inside the growing funnel of the plant to feed on tender young leaves.
ga: Bu ni mli efo ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ahe okadi ni ale waa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ dalɛ gbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai bibii.

english: How far apart should I space my crops when planting them in the field?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ miidu yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Proper spacing, such as leaving 40 centimeters between plants, ensures each crop gets enough soil nutrients, water, and sunlight to grow strong without competing with neighboring plants.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa, tamɔ sɛntimitai 40 ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akaŋ akaŋ.

english: What happens to my crop yield if I plant my crops closer together than recommended?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe fe bɔ ni awo he ŋaa lɛ?

english: Planting too closely forces plants to fight for food and light, which results in weak stems, smaller leaves, and a smaller overall harvest, while also making it easier for diseases to spread.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ kɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi niyenii kɛ la he ta. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa, baai bibii kɛ yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ faaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: How can I measure the correct planting distance in my field if I do not have a tape measure?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu dumɔwui adumɔ he ni sa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he? Kɛji obɛ tsɔne ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe lɛ

english: You can cut a stick or a piece of rope to the exact required length—like 40 centimeters—and use it as a simple guide between planting holes to maintain uniform spacing.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofo tso nine loo kpã kɛyashɛ he ni osumɔɔ, tamɔ sɛntimita 40, ni okɛtsu nii akɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo. yɛ dumɔ bui lɛ ateŋ koni sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni yɔɔ ekomefeemɔ mli lɛ ahi shi

english: Why do different types of crops require different amounts of spacing between them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi biɔ ni tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Different crops grow to different sizes both above ground and below ground; larger crops with wide roots and big leaves need wider spacing than smaller crops to thrive.
ga: Nibii sɔrɔtoi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ dalɛi srɔtoi amli yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi fɛɛ. Tsei wuji ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ kɛ baai wuji lɛ he miihia ni amɛná he ko ni mli kwɔ fe tsei bibii lɛ koni amɛshwere.

english: Why should I put only two seeds in a single planting hole instead of a whole handful?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui enyɔ pɛ awo dumɔ bu kome mli yɛ dumɔwui fioo ko najiaŋ?

english: Putting just two seeds gives you a backup if one fails to germinate, while ensuring the growing seedlings do not overcrowd each other and starve for soil nutrients.
ga: Dumɔwui enyɔ pɛ ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa sɛɛfimɔ baa kɛji eko nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekwɛɔ koni dumɔwui ni miida lɛ akafee mɛi ni eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to remove extra weak seedlings if too many sprout in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ majie dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ titri lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Removing weaker seedlings—a practice called thinning—leaves only the strongest plants to absorb the available water and fertilizer, leading to a healthier crop.
ga: Dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ - nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ thinning - lɛ haa tsei ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ. Ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa

english: Does planting my crops in neat, straight rows actually help them grow better?
ga: Ani mitsei lɛ ni mikɛduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Straight rows give every plant equal access to light and air, while making farm tasks like weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much faster and easier.
ga: Nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni ja lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaanyɛ afee ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi tamɔ jwɛi ŋmɔmɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ oya ni efee mlɛo kwraa.

english: How can I tell if my young crops are suffering from getting too much sunlight?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi dumɔwui lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tsɔ?

english: Young crops getting burnt by intense sun will show drooping, yellowed, or scorched leaves, indicating they need temporary shade plants or better soil moisture retention.
ga: Tsei bibii ni hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ baafite, amɛbaafee ŋmɔŋ, loo amɛbaashã amɛbaai lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli loo ni nyɛɔ amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia amɛ.

english: Why is it important to choose a farm location near an accessible road?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ahala ŋmɔ mli he ko ni bɛŋkɛ gbɛ ni mɛi baanyɛ aya nɔ lɛ?

english: A farm near a road makes it much easier and cheaper to carry fertilizers and tools to your land and to transport harvested crops quickly to the market before they spoil.
ga: Okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa ni ejara hu waaa akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nitsumɔ dadei aya oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ aya jara nɔ oya dani amɛfite.

english: Why should I teach my family members the exact planting measurements used on our farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔɔ miweku lɛ mli bii lɛ dumɔwui pɔtɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ wɔŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dalɛi?

english: Farming is a shared effort, and when family members understand the correct spacing and planting methods, work gets done faster and mistakes that lower harvest yields are prevented.
ga: Okwaayeli ji mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ni akɛ he woɔ mli. Ni kɛ weku lɛ mli bii lɛ nu gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii kɛ gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii lɛ shishi lɛ Abaagbe nitsumɔ lɛ naa oya ni abaatsi tɔmɔi ni haa ŋmaa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi lɛ anaa.

english: Why can't I just plant my crop seeds directly on the main farm instead of raising them in a nursery first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ madu dumɔwui lɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli moŋ fe ni makwɛ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Nursery environments protect delicate young seeds from harsh sunshine, heavy rains, and pests, giving them a safe place to build strong roots before facing the tougher conditions of the open field.
ga: Shihilɛ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ buɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe, ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ naa he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná shishifãi ni wa dani amɛkɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ akpee.

english: Why do some farmers bring crop seeds or planting materials from neighboring countries like Ivory Coast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ dumɔwui loo nibii ni akɛduɔ nii kɛjɛɔ maji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tamɔ Ivory Coast lɛ amli baa lɛ?

english: Farmers often source varieties from neighboring areas because those specific crops may be bred to handle dry weather better, resist diseases, or produce higher yields under similar climate conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi lɛ heɔ tsei kɛjɛɔ hei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ekolɛ atsɔse nakai tsei pɔtɛɛi lɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛkpee shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ anaa jogbaŋŋ, amɛte shi amɛwo helai, loo amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ shishi.

english: Why do my young seedlings need daily attention instead of just being left to grow on their own in the nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ midumɔwu bibioo lɛ daa gbi lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha eda lɛ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings in nursery bags have very little soil and small roots, so if they are left unattended without regular watering, shade adjustments, and weed control, they can dry out and die within a day or two.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli kotokui lɛ amli lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ fioo ko pɛ kɛ shishifãi bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ ashi ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ ni afɔɔɔ lɛ nu daa, atsakeee hulutsoo, ni akwɛɛɛ jwɛi anɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ mli.

english: What is the difference between planting fresh seeds and using dry seeds for my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui heei ni miduɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni egbi ni mikɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Dry seeds can be stored for longer periods without spoiling or rotting, whereas fresh seeds contain moisture and must usually be planted quickly before they lose their ability to sprout.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ ato be kakadaŋŋ ni efiteee loo egbooo. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, dumɔwui heei lɛ mli edɔ ni bei pii lɛ ehe hiaa ni adu oya dani amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young plants get weak and wilt when I move them from the nursery out into the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛgboi beni mijieɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Moving seedlings causes root shock, and if they are suddenly exposed to strong direct sunlight in dry field soil without extra care, their small roots cannot absorb water fast enough to keep them healthy.
ga: Dumɔwui ni tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa trukaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni atsuuu he nii krɛdɛɛ ko lɛ, amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to build a shade cover over my crop nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ma hulutsoo nɔ ko yɛ mi-nursery lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Strong sunlight can burn fragile new leaves and cause the water in small nursery polybags to evaporate rapidly, while shade keeps the soil cool and moist for early growth.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai heei ni waaa lɛ. ni eha nu ni yɔɔ gbekɛbii akwɛmɔ kotoku bibioo lɛ mli lɛ atsɔ oya. yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwereɔ oya.

english: Why do diseases spread so quickly among young plants while they are in the nursery stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ oya yɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ?

english: In a nursery, young seedlings are kept close together, creating a warm and humid micro-environment where diseases can easily jump from one plant to another if the farmer does not inspect them regularly.
ga: yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Akɛ dumɔwui bibii lɛ toɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa shihilɛ bibioo ko ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛjɛ tso kome mli kɛya ekroko mli oya. Kɛji okwaafoi lɛ ekwɛɛɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli daa

english: Will a seed variety that yields well in Ivory Coast perform the exact same way on my soil in Ghana?
ga: Ani dumɔwui srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ivory Coast lɛ baatsu nii nakai pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ nɔ?

english: Not automatically; even in nearby regions, differences in soil fertility, local rainfall pattern, and local pests mean imported crop varieties need careful nursery setup and soil management to yield properly.
ga: not automatically Yɛ hei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ po Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ jɛmɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei srɔtoi ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ biɔ ni asaa amɛhe jogbaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ koni amɛná yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: How does dry weather affect young crop plants differently than mature plants?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young plants have shallow root systems that cannot reach water deep in the soil, making them suffer quickly in dry conditions, while older crops have long taproots that can draw water from deeper underground.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ nu he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛnaa amanehulu oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli. Shi tsei ni edara lɛ yɛ shishifãi kakadaji ni baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know when my crop seedlings in the nursery are mature enough to be moved to the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu kɛya ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Seedlings are ready when they have developed a firm stem, a few sets of fully formed green leaves, and a root mass that holds the nursery soil together tightly without falling apart.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo kɛji amɛje shishi amɛfee tsei ni wa. Baai eŋɔlii ni eda ni ato he gbɛjianɔ enyɔ loo etɛ. kɛ shishifãi ni haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ekome shiŋŋ ni etseee lɛ.

english: What should I do if my crops get sick and the farm medicine takes too long to arrive?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hela mɔ amɛ ni ŋmɔ mli tsofai lɛ heɔ be babaoo tsɔ dani akɛbaa?

english: If modern chemical treatments are delayed, you should immediately remove and destroy the heavily infected leaves or plants to prevent the disease from spreading. You can also safely apply local remedies like wood ash or diluted neem leaf juice to slow down pests while waiting for official help.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsofai ni akɛtsaa hela lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ Esa akɛ ojie baai loo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ waa lɛ ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã. Obaanyɛ okɛ maŋ lɛ mli tsofai tamɔ tso sũ loo neem baa nu ni akɛwo mli lɛ hu atsu nii shweshweeshwe. koni akɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ asɛɛ afo be mli ni amɛmiimɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni jɛ maŋ onukpai adɛŋ lɛ

english: Are local remedies like wood ash or neem leaf water safe to use on my diseased crops?
ga: Ani maŋ lɛ mli tsofai tamɔ tso sũ loo neem baa mli nu lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛbaatsu nii yɛ mitso ni hela emɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, local remedies like wood ash and neem leaf extracts are safe and natural ways to protect crops. Wood ash suffocates small chewing insects and reduces soil acidity, while neem juice stops bugs from feeding on plant leaves without burning the crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, maŋ tsofai tamɔ tso sũ kɛ neem baa mli nu ji shweshweeshwe kɛ adebɔɔ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Tso ashwishwɛ lɛ muɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ nii lɛ. ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli acidity lɛ baa shi Neem nu lɛ, yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ehaa kooloi bibii yeɔ baai lɛ ni amɛshãaa tso lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant roots are damaged by insects, or the soil is too waterlogged to breathe and absorb nutrients. Heavy rains can also wash fertilizer away before the crop's roots get a chance to drink it in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ koolooi efite tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ emu ni eŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii dani tsei shishifãi lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛnu lɛ.

english: Why do dark spots appear on my crop leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Rainy weather creates damp, humid conditions that allow fungal diseases to thrive and spread through water splashes. Spacing your crops properly and clearing weeds helps air flow through the farm so leaves dry faster.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Curling cassava leaves are usually a sign of the Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. The best solution is to plant disease-resistant cassava stems provided by agricultural offices.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii eyɛŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni adu ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ kɛhaa lɛ.

english: Is it better to spray my crops with pest medicine in the morning or in the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baashwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ leebi loo shwane?

english: It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the evening when temperatures are cool. Spraying under hot afternoon sun causes the medicine to evaporate too quickly and can burn the sensitive leaves of your crops.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie nɔ lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha tsofa lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ, ni ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: How can I protect my young seedlings from insects eating them right after planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu midumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni shwieɔ amɛ lɛ ahe beni midu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Clearing old crop debris and weeds before planting destroys insect hiding spots. You can also sprinkle dry wood ash around the stem bases of young seedlings to create a mild barrier that stops crawling pests.
ga: Tso mli jwɛi momo kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ dani aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ hei ni kooloi kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ tso sũ ni egbi hu ashwie he fɛɛ he. Tsei bibii lɛ ashishi feɔ gbɛtsii nii ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tsiɔ kooloi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant suffers from heat stress, erratic watering, or a lack of calcium in the soil. Consistent watering at the root level helps the plant hold onto its flowers until fruit sets.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my crops growing very short and weak even though there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛhe waaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Stunted growth during heavy rain happens when excessive water fills all air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots. It can also mean essential nutrients were washed too deep into the ground where roots cannot reach.
ga: Nɔ ni yaa hiɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baa kɛji nu babaoo eyi kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ obɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ hu akɛ, afɔɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ, he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are sick from bugs or just suffering from hot sunshine?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi cacao tsei lɛ hela mɔ amɛ kɛjɛ kooloi amli loo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Sun damage makes leaves dry up evenly brown from the edges, whereas insect pests like capsids leave clear signs like ragged holes, dark gummy spots on branches, or deformed green pods.
ga: Hulu ni fiteɔ nii lɛ haa baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛyashɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ po, yɛ be mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids lɛ shiɔ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ tamɔ bu ni etse kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ. loo pods eŋɔli ni efite

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow very quickly and provide broad leaf canopy shade, which protects the fragile young cocoa trees while maintaining moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ekɛ baai ni mli kwɔ haa hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ni waaa lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings wilt in the afternoon heat even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, tomato plants lose water through their leaves faster than their young roots can take it up from the soil. Providing temporary shade covers during intense sun stops this stress.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ha yɛ be mli ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akpa haomɔ nɛɛ.

english: When maize lacks nitrogen, the plant moves what little nitrogen it has from older, bottom leaves up to nourish new growth at the top. Yellowing lower leaves mean your farm needs nitrogen fertilizer or manure.
ga: Kɛji nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa mli lɛ Tsei jieɔ nitrogen fioo kɛjɛɔ tsei ni edara lɛ amli. Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ daa koni amɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ aya hiɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: This is a symptom of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies. The virus prevents the leaf from producing food properly, leading to stunt growth and poor tuber yield.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ akɛ mɛi ni hiɛɔ lɛ Virus lɛ tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛnáaa tuber yibii kpakpai.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when temperature levels get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates heavily between extremely wet and dry. Consistent watering prevents flower drop.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ waa teŋ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ akashwie shi.

english: Why is my cassava crop growing so tall with thick leaves, but giving me tiny tubers at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni mli tse lɛ? Shi ani oooha bulb lɛ afee bibioo kɛ́ ookpa nii?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil encourages cassava to spend all its energy growing heavy branches and leaf canopy above ground rather than storing starches down in the roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmei hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo tsei niji ni tsii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why do armyworms suddenly appear on my young maize leaves right after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cutworms jeɔ kpo trukaa yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fall armyworm moths lay eggs on the undersides of leaves, and higher air moisture from early rains triggers rapid hatching. The newly hatched caterpillars begin feeding aggressively on tender shoots.
ga: Autumn mli ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ baai lɛ ashishi. Ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa ni jɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ oya. Kplukai ni efɔ ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛyeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my groundnuts producing pods that are completely empty inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ yɛ pods ni fɛɛ ehiɛ efolo yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods, known as 'pops', happen when the soil lacks enough calcium or when the ground stays too dry while the pegs are growing into the soil to form nuts.
ga: Peanut pods ni bɛ nɔ ko, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ ‘pea pods’ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and weak with small cobs when I plant many seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ Dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too closely forces the young crops to fight each other for limited sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients, leaving every plant malnourished.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ awuu koni amɛná hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei fɛɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need stakes to climb on instead of just trailing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooonyiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight. Lifting the leaves prevents fungal leaf diseases from the damp soil and increases tuber growth.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Baai lɛ ni awóɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ baa hela ni ji fungal lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ, ni ehaa tuber lɛ daalɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and turn yellow when I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ beni mijieɔ tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to protect their sensitive leaves from harsh sunlight and retain soil moisture. Clearing all big trees exposes the young cocoa to extreme heat stress, causing the leaves to sunburn and dry out.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ taoɔ hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha kookoo bibii lɛ aná dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa hulu ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground when the rainy season gets too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped in the soil for too long because the roots drown without oxygen. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away so the roots can breathe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning pale yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow green leaves. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to the newer top leaves to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why are holes suddenly appearing in my young maize leaves with tiny green droppings inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji eje kpo trukaa yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ nɔ ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ baa lɛ mli?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars eating the leaves. Catching them early allows you to spray neem leaf extract or recommended treatments before they destroy the central growing tip of the plant.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ baai. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu lɛ loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ shwieɔ nɔ dani efiteɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã ni miida lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows specific pests to build up in the dirt. Switching crops gives the soil time to recover and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans between my main crops help my soil grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans gather nitrogen gas from the air and trap it inside the soil. This acts like a natural fertilizer that feeds your main crops and keeps the soil rich.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Ebuaa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa otsei titrii lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Why does leaving dry leaves and grass on top of the soil around my plants help them grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ashi baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ? No hewɔ lɛ, mitsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass (mulch) traps moisture in the ground so plants stay hydrated longer, keeps the roots cool during hot days, and stops weeds from getting light to grow.
ga: Kɛ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (Mulch) wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaná la koni amɛkwɛ̃

english: Why do my tomato plants get sickly and yield smaller fruits when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ hela mɔ amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When tomato plants are too close, they fight each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. The crowded leaves also block air movement, creating damp conditions where leaf diseases spread quickly.
ga: Beni Tomato Tsei lɛ Ebɛŋkɛ Tsɔ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Foji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ hu tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa hulutsoo baa yɛ he ni foliar helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and soft before the fruit even ripens?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efee blɛoo dani ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by uneven watering and a lack of calcium reaching the fruit as it grows. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant transport calcium into the tomatoes.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be kɛ calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli beni edaa lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ calcium lɛ yaa tomato lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the young suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi tsɔne titri lɛ

english: If too many young shoots grow at once, they steal food and water from the main plant, resulting in small plantain bunches. Keeping only two or three strong shoots ensures the main plant produces big, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ shikome Ebaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji plantains bibii bibii. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo niji agboi ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves at the bottom of my young maize plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize plants usually show a lack of nitrogen, which is essential for healthy green growth. When the soil runs low on nitrogen, the plant moves what little it has left to feed the new top leaves, causing the older bottom leaves to turn yellow and die off.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ bɛ nitrogen. ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Beni nitrogen fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baajie nɔ fioo ni eshwɛ lɛ koni ekɛ ŋwɛi baai heei akwɛ̃. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into a cup shape during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants roll their leaves inward on hot days to protect themselves from losing too much moisture to the scorching heat. As long as the leaves unroll and look fresh again by evening or early morning, the crop is simply conserving water and is not sick.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe koni hulutsoo ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akafite amɛ babaoo. Shii abɔ ni baai lɛ baaje kpo ni amɛfee ehee ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa lɛ, Nibii ni adu lɛ miihere nu kɛkɛ ni hela mɔmɔɔɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my small cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the stems before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii So mine lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani edaa lɛ?

english: This blackening is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet, damp, and shaded conditions. Clearing weeds and trimming extra cocoa branches lets sunshine and fresh air dry out the farm, which stops the fungus from destroying young pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ duŋ nɛɛ baa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yaa hiɛ yɛ hei ni efɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ hulutsoo be. Cocoa niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni afoɔ lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa agbi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ akpata ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with green dirt inside the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni etse kɛ muji eŋɔli yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that crawls into the hidden inner funnel of the maize plant to eat soft young leaves. Catching them early and spraying recommended remedies directly into the central funnel will destroy the worms before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni shwieɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ amli gbɛi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ amli koni eye baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baafite ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when heavy rainwater collects around them and cannot drain away. Cassava roots need air to breathe, so planting them on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water run off easily and prevents root rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nu buaa amɛhe naa lɛ. ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli oya, ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my watermelons crack open while they are still growing on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ miitswa be mli ni amɛmiidara yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Watermelons split when they receive a sudden surge of water after a dry period. The inside of the fruit absorbs water very quickly and expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the fruit to burst open.
ga: Watermelons baatswa kɛji amɛná nu ni fa trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ nu oya waa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. gbee aduawai lɛ amli

english: Tomato plants shed their blossoms when heat becomes too extreme or when watering is irregular. High temperatures make it hard for the flowers to pollinate, so the plant drops them to conserve its energy until conditions improve.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛ́ la lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa. He ni dɔɔ waa lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ akɛ amɛbaafee pollin. No hewɔ lɛ tsei shiɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over before the fruit bunch is fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miigbee shi dani aduawai akutsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that struggle to anchor tall stems under heavy rain or high wind, especially when carrying heavy fruit bunches. Propping up the main stem with a strong bamboo fork or wooden pole gives the plant extra support until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛmɔmɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa shishi. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ oohiɛ aduawai ni awo mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei loo tso ni akɛfee tso lɛ tsu nii ni akɛfi tso lɛ shishitoo titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná yelikɛbuamɔ kroko kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in my field after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients, leaving the land tired after harvest. Leguminous crops like groundnuts and cowpeas put nitrogen natural fertilizer back into the soil through their roots, restoring fertility for your next season's crop.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii haa nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Koni ekɛ fɔmɔ aku sɛɛ aha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I put fertilizer right next to the main stem of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifã titri lɛ masɛi?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts that can burn delicate plant roots and stems if placed in direct contact. Placing fertilizer in a small ring a few inches away from the plant stem allows roots to draw in nutrients safely as they reach outward.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli ŋmei ni mli eyi obɔ ni baanyɛ ashã tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ waa kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli Kɛ́ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnáa niyenii kpakpai yɛ mli shweshweeshwe beni amɛyaa kponɔgbɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my harvested maize will stay fresh long enough if I decide to hold onto it until market prices go up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ baahi shi be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa? Kɛji mikpɛ miyiŋ akɛ mahiɛ mli kɛyashi jara nɔ jara lɛ baaya ŋwɛi.

english: Maize can be stored safely for months if it is properly dried to around 12-14% moisture content (when grains are hard enough that your thumbnail cannot dent them) and kept in airtight bags or cool, dry granaries to prevent mold and weevils.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmãa ato shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo kɛji akɛ agbi lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni shɛɔ aaafee 12-14% (be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni oniji ahe tsɔi lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli) ni akɛto vacuum bags loo ŋmãa ni mli ejɔ ni egbi mli koni ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa akabote mli.

english: Why do my tomatoes rot so quickly after I pick them, and how can I make them last long enough to get a good market price?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maha ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni maná jara kpakpa yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Tomatoes ripen and soften rapidly after harvest because they release ethylene gas. Picking them at the 'breaker stage'—when green fruit just starts showing a pink tint—and storing them in a cool shade extends their shelf life for transport and sale.
ga: Tomatoi lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo oya yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ yɛ ethylene gas ni ajieɔ lɛ hewɔ. Nibii ni akɛtoɔ yɛ ‘breaker period’ lɛ mli beni aduawai eŋɔli lɛ jeɔ shishi ejieɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛ kɛkɛ lɛ. Ni kɛ́ akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛha tsɔne ni akɛyaa he kroko ni akɛjaa.

english: Why do my yams spoil from the inside after I harvest and store them to sell later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ emli kɛ́ akpa ni mikɛto koni sɛɛ mli lɛ ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Internal yam rot usually happens when tubers are bruised or wounded during digging, allowing fungal spores to enter. Carefully harvesting and curing yams in a shaded, well-ventilated area for a few days helps skin heal and prevents decay during storage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato mli mli fitemɔ baa kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbo loo amɛpila yɛ be mli ni atsaa lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ abote mli. Kɛ́ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ kpa sweet potatoes ni okɛtsa he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ lɛ gbii fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua hewolo lɛ ni etsa ni ebaatsi fitemɔ naa yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: I want to start selling cassava instead of just growing it for my family, but how do I know when the roots are fully grown and ready for market?
ga: Miisumɔ ni mabɔi ŋmei hɔ̃ɔmɔ moŋ fe ni makwɛ miweku lɛ. Shi te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni amɛfee klalo kɛha jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava is typically ready for commercial harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is mature when the lower leaves yellow and drop, and digging up a test plant reveals firm, starch-filled roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ edara kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ fee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ni tsei ni aka amɛ akwɛɔ lɛ ni atsa lɛ jie shishifãi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ starch kpo.

english: Why do some of my pepper plants produce small, wrinkled fruits that buyers refuse to pay a good price for?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ekomɛi miiwo aduawai bibii ni egbɔjɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ kpooɔ akɛ amɛbaawo nyɔmɔ kpakpa yɛ he lɛ?

english: Small, wrinkled peppers are usually caused by irregular watering or viral diseases spread by tiny insects like aphids. Maintaining consistent soil moisture and protecting plants from pests ensures smooth, plump peppers that fetch top prices.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni egbɔjɔ lɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ tsei ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jara wa waa.

english: Why are my plantains coming out small, and what can I do so I get large bunches that sell for higher prices?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ? Ni mɛni manyɛ mafee koni maná jwɛi wuji ni ahɔ̃ɔ kɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ?

english: Plantain bunches remain small when too many sucker shoots compete with the main plant for soil nutrients and water. Pruning away excess suckers to leave only 2-3 per stand concentrates plant energy into producing larger, heavier bunches.
ga: Plantain ŋmeii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kɛ tso titri lɛ miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ni ashi ŋmeii 2-3 pɛ yɛ shidaamɔhe kome mli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii wuji ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my cabbages split open right before I am ready to take them to the market to sell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ mli gbalaa dani mifeɔ klalo akɛ mikɛbaajara lɛ?

english: Cabbages split when there is a sudden heavy intake of water after a dry spell, causing the inside to grow faster than the outer head can stretch. Harvesting mature heads immediately before heavy rains prevents splitting and loss of market value.
ga: Kaabaji baatswa kɛji nu ni anuɔ trukaa trukaa yɛ hɔmɔ be ko sɛɛ. Enɛ haa mligbɛ lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Tuber ni eda ni akpaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ tsiɔ mligbalamɔ kɛ jarayeli jara ni baa shi lɛ naa.

english: If I am facing financial hardship and need quick income from my farm, which crops grow and mature the fastest in Ghana?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mikɛ shika he naagbai miikpe ni ehe miihia ni maná shika oya kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli. Mɛɛ tsei daa ni amɛshwereɔ oya fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghana?

english: Short-duration crops like leafy vegetables (kontomire/cocoyam leaves, amaranth), cucumbers, and okra mature in 4 to 8 weeks, providing rapid cash returns compared to long-term staple or tree crops.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai (contomir/coconut baai, spinach), kukumba kɛ okra shwereɔ yɛ otsii 4 kɛyashi 8 mli, ni ehaa shika baa oya kɛ akɛto be kakadaŋŋ mli nibii ni aduɔ loo jwɛi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Can I grow watermelon on the same land where I grow my main crops to make extra cash, or will it harm my primary crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu watermelon yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ miŋmɔshi nii titri yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ koni maná shika kroko? Aloo ebaaye miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ awui?

english: Yes, watermelon can be intercropped because its spreading vines act as living cover to reduce weeds. However, it requires full sunlight and extra soil nutrients so it does not compete with your primary crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ adu watermelon yɛ he kroko ejaakɛ wain tsei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni hiɛ ka ni haa jwɛi lɛ baa shi. Shi kɛlɛ, amɛbiɔ hulu ni yeɔ emuu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii krokomɛi ni fata he. No hewɔ lɛ ekɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yeee akaŋ.

english: If I save seeds from the vegetables I harvested and liked, will the next crop produce the exact same high-quality vegetables for selling?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ aduawai ni mikpaa ni misumɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ to lɛ, Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baaha aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛbaahɔɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ aba?

english: Not always. If you harvested from hybrid seed varieties, saving those seeds will often result in weaker plants with small or uneven fruits. Purchasing certified fresh seeds each season ensures uniform, high-market-value produce.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be kɛji okpa kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome mli. Bei pii lɛ, nakai dumɔwui lɛ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii loo amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛhe. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haa jarayeli jara ni yaa hiɛ be fɛɛ be kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What is the best month of the year for me to plant new cocoa seedlings in the ground?
ga: Mɛni ji nyɔŋ ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli ni akɛduɔ kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: The best time to plant cocoa in Ghana is at the beginning of the main rainy season, usually around May or June. Planting during this window gives the young seedlings enough moisture to grow strong roots before the dry season arrives.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛduɔ kookoo yɛ Ghana ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ May loo June mli. Kɛ́ adu yɛ samflɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei bibii lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba.

english: How much space should I leave between my cocoa trees when I am planting them?
ga: Gbɛ enyiɛ esa akɛ mashi yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: You should space your cocoa trees about 3 meters by 3 meters apart (around 10 feet by 10 feet). Giving them this space ensures that their roots and leaves do not fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ o-cacao tsei lɛ ato he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3 x mitai 3 (aaafee ninetalɔi 10 x 10). Kɛ́ aha amɛ gbɛ nɛɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ etswaŋ akaŋ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees on the same land where I am growing young cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kookoo bibii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very delicate and can easily burn under full, direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide temporary shade and keep the soil moist while your cocoa trees are young.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ waaa kwraa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa lolo lɛ.

english: How many years will it take for my new cocoa trees to start producing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ mli ni mi cacao tso hee lɛ baaje shishi ewo ŋmɔtɔ?

english: If you plant modern hybrid cocoa varieties, they usually start producing pods within 2 to 3 years. Traditional cocoa varieties take longer, usually around 4 to 5 years before you see your first major harvest.
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ cocoa hybrids Bei pii lɛ Amɛjeɔ pods feemɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli. Kusum nifeemɔi amli kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ be babaoo, bei pii lɛ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani onaa oklɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ wulu lɛ.

english: Why do so many small flowers fall off my cocoa trees without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Amɛteŋ mɛi enyiɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: It is normal for cocoa trees to shed up to 90 percent of their flowers because the tree naturally selects only what it can feed. However, excessive flower drop can happen if the tree lacks water or if tiny insects called thrips are damaging the blossoms.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ cacao tsei baafɔfɔi lɛ amli oha mlijaa 90 ejaakɛ tso lɛ halaa nɔ pɛ ni ebaanyɛ ekɛha lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi kɛlɛ, fɔfɔii ni baa shi fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aba kɛji nu bɛ tso lɛ mli loo kɛji kooloi bibii baye nɔ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ thrips lɛ miifite fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: How do I know if the soil on my land is good enough for cocoa farming?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Good cocoa soil is dark, deep, well-drained, and soft enough for roots to spread easily. If water sits on your land like a pond for days after rain, the soil is too wet and will rot cocoa roots.
ga: Esa akɛ kookoo shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ afee ediŋŋ, mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni eyɛ blɛoo bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo Kɛji nu hi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ nubu gbii babaoo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni ebaanyɛ eha kookoo shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Why is it necessary for me to prune or cut branches off my growing cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo loo majie niji kɛjɛ kookoo tso ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or extra branches so sunlight and air can pass through the tree. This helps prevent fungal diseases and directs the tree's energy into growing healthy cocoa pods instead of extra leaves.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni egboi loo ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tso lɛ mli baa lɛ anaa, ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ kookoo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai krokomɛi baafata he.

english: How often should I clear weeds from my young cocoa farm?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ bibioo lɛ mli?

english: In a young cocoa farm, you should clear weeds every 2 to 3 months during the rainy season. Weeds grow very fast and will steal fertilizers, water, and sunlight from your young cocoa trees if left unchecked.
ga: Yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli Esa akɛ okɛ jwɛi atsu nii daa nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa ni ebaaju ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ o-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ amli kɛji akɛ mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, dark, and excessively wet conditions. You can reduce it by pruning shade trees to let in sunlight and quickly removing infected pods from the farm.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni edɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe nine. Obaanyɛ oha enɛ aba shi kɛtsɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ ni ooofo koni hulu la babaoo aba lɛ nɔ. ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya.

english: How many bags of cocoa can I expect to harvest from one acre of land?
ga: Cocoa kotokui enyiɛ manyɛ makpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre kome nɔ?

english: With good farming practices, proper weeding, and pest control, a well-managed acre in Ghana can produce between 5 to 8 bags of dried cocoa beans (64kg each) per year once the trees reach full maturity.
ga: kɛ okwaayeli nifeemɔi kpakpai Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ Shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana lɛ baanyɛ ajie kookoo ŋmeii ni egbi ni falɛ ji kotokui 5 kɛyashi 8 (eko fɛɛ eko kilogram 64) daa afi kɛ́ tsei lɛ eda.

english: What happens if I plant my yam seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu sweet potato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When yam seeds are planted too close, their vines and roots fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in many small, thin tubers instead of large, healthy ones.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu sweet potato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Weintsei kɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when the plants are still short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tsei lɛ yɛ kuku lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is the nutrient responsible for healthy green leaves and strong growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or animal manure early helps them recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni haa baai eŋɔli lɛ mli waa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ Nitrogen ni yɔɔ mli loo kooloi ashishifã ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhe ajɔ amɛ.

english: Why is it bad to plant pepper on the same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting pepper repeatedly on the same land drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and fungal diseases that attack pepper plants to multiply in the ground. Rotating with legumes like beans helps clean and restore the soil.
ga: Pepper ni aduɔ shii abɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ baajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa pepper tsei lɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsake shikpɔŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ he tseɔ ni ehaa ehe hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava tuber rot is usually caused by water staying around the roots for too long or fungal diseases in wet soil. Planting on raised ridges or mounds helps rain water drain away so the roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. aloo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ Dumɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus, or severe stress from hot weather and lack of water. Protecting young plants and watering regularly keeps them healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo haomɔ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nu ni faaa mli baa Tsei bibii ahe ni abuɔ amɛhe ni awoɔ amɛ nu daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my maize after the long dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the soil gets a good, deep soak from two or three steady rains rather than planting after the very first light rain, which prevents seeds from drying out and dying in the hot dirt.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ baabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Mohu ɔ, mo du mɛ ngɛ kekleekle hiɔmi nɛ ɔ se, nɛ enɛ ɔ ma ha nɛ duwu ɔmɛ ko nɛ e gbo nɛ a ko gbo ngɛ zugba nɛ mi dɔ ɔ mi.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my okra plants without producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi gumbo lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Okra flowers fall off when the plant suffers from sudden water stress, extreme heat, or lack of pollination from bees. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the flowers stay attached and form pods.
ga: Roselle fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu he haomɔ trukaa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo ŋmeii ni haaa tso lɛ aná fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are some of my cowpea seeds failing to sprout after I put them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea seeds may fail to sprout if the soil is too dry, if insects damaged the seeds during storage, or if they were buried too deep in the dirt where oxygen cannot reach them.
ga: Ekolɛ cowpea dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Kɛji kooloi bibii kpata dumɔwui lɛ ahiɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ Aloo kɛji akɛ afu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my sweet potatoes are mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Sweet potatoes are usually ready when the leaves begin to turn yellow and die back. You can also dig up one tuber and cut it; if the milky juice dries white quickly without turning black, the crop is mature.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato lɛ efee klalo akɛ ayeɔ kɛ́ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi. Obaanyɛ otsa yitso kome hu ni ofo mli. Kɛji akɛ mliki nu lɛ gĩ oya ni etsɔɔɔ ediŋŋ Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ.

english: Can I grow food crops on land that stays swampy or flooded with water?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ loo nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, but you must manage the water flow first. While crops like rice thrive in wet conditions, most crops need raised soil beds or small drainage channels so their roots do not drown in standing water.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi ehe miihia ni okwɛ bɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ ehaa lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli moŋ, shi tsei babaoo biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ he gbɛ bibioo ko. koni eshishifãi lɛ akabote nu ni damɔ shi mli.

english: Why do my crop roots rot when water sits on my farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu hi miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air in the soil to breathe just like people do. When water fills all the spaces in the dirt for days, air cannot get in, causing the roots to choke, turn soft, and rot.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu, tamɔ bɔ ni adesai feɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he lɛ mli gbii babaoo Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ abote mli.Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛfeɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ.
