english: What happens to my crops if rainwater flows too fast across my field?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu ho oya tsɔ kɛtsɔ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ?

english: Fast-flowing water washes away the fertile topsoil where crop food lives and can pull young seedlings out of the ground. Making simple water paths helps guide the water safely away without damaging your plants.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ hoɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii, ni ebaanyɛ egbala tsei bibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nu gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ooofee Ebaaye ebua bo ni otsɔ nu lɛ mli shweshweeshwe ni ofiteee tsei lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my low-lying land needs drainage ditches before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he miihia nu ni hoɔ nu kɛjɛɔ mli dani mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: If water forms deep pools that sit on the soil surface for more than two days after rain, the ground is too wet for normal roots, meaning you need to dig small channels to let excess water flow out.
ga: Kɛji nu lɛ fee nubu ko ni mli kwɔ ni ta shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nɔ ni fe gbii enyɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ kɛha shishifãi ni sa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ otsa bu bibioo ko. koni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli

english: How does applying a little fertilizer early on make the base of my crops strong?
ga: Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo baafata he mra Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mitso lɛ shishitoo lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer gives young crops essential food like phosphorus and nitrogen, which helps them build thick main stems and deep roots. A strong base anchors the plant against strong wind and heavy rain.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa tamɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ nitrogen. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso titri ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ baa. Shishitoo ni wa baaha tso lɛ ahi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why do crop leaves turn yellow when the ground stays soaked in water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Excess water washes key plant food out of the dirt and stops roots from taking up nutrients. Without these nutrients, the plant leaves lose their healthy green color and cannot grow properly.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii titrii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Kɛji niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ bɛ lɛ, tsei ahe baai lɛ baaje amɛsu ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Where exactly should I place fertilizer around my plant so it gets the most benefit?
ga: Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mitsei lɛ ahe koni maná he sɛɛ babaoo?

english: Apply the fertilizer in a small ring around the base of the plant near the soil surface. The main feeder roots grow right below the stem, allowing the plant to easily drink the food before weeds steal it.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ kooyigbɛ bibii amli. Yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he lɛ Niyenii shishifãi titri lɛ daa yɛ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa ewaaa akɛ tsei lɛ baanu amɛ niyenii lɛ dani jwɛi lɛ aju.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting beans alongside my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Beans are special plants that pull natural fertilizer directly from the air and store it in their roots. Planting them next to other crops helps feed the soil naturally while giving you an extra crop to harvest.
ga: Beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛji oodu yɛ tsei krokomɛi ahe lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni eha bo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni obaakpa.

english: How do bean plants help protect the ground from heavy sun and rain?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii tsei buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he?

english: Bean plants spread wide leaves close to the dirt like a green carpet. This cover shades the soil so it does not dry out under hot sun and breaks the force of rain that washes topsoil away.
ga: Bean tsei lɛ gbɛ amɛbaai ni mli kwɔ lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ he tamɔ kapɛti eŋɔli. Nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ nɛɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ yaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Will leaving old bean plants in the ground after harvest help my next crop grow better?
ga: Ani bean tsei momo ni mashi yɛ sɛɛ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, leaving the roots and leaves of harvested bean plants to break down in the field turns them into rich organic compost that feeds the soil for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ oha ŋmeii tsei ni akpa lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ fite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni fa babaoo ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmeii kɛha ŋmeii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil needs fertilizer before I plant my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu ŋmãa?

english: If your previous crops grew slowly, had pale green or yellowish leaves, or produced small yields, your soil is likely low in nutrients. Observing weak weed growth or getting a simple soil test can also confirm if your field needs compost or fertilizers like NPK before planting.
ga: Kɛji onibii ni odu tsutsu lɛ dara blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. loo ewoɔ nibii fioo Ekolɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ hu faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ adalɛ kwɛmɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni afeɔ. Ebaanyɛ ema hu nɔ mi akɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK dani okɛdu.

english: Why does my pepper crop produce plenty of big leaves but very few flowers and fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ baai wuji waa shi fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai fioo pɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer makes them focus all their energy on growing tall and lush leaves instead of producing food. Pepper plants need nutrients rich in phosphorus and potassium to encourage flower blooming and fruit development.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe niyenii ni amɛbaafee. Pepper tsei lɛ he miihia niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium koni eha fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes during the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ shwane hulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves inward during hot afternoons to reduce the surface area exposed to sunlight. This is a natural defense mechanism that helps the plant conserve water and prevent it from drying out during high heat.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni ehaaa amɛgbi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ.

english: Why do my cabbage plants turn pale and wilt even when the ground is wet from heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kaabeji lɛ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: When soil gets flooded or waterlogged, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing them to suffocate and rot. Damaged or rotted roots lose their ability to drink water and absorb food, making the plant wilt despite being surrounded by moisture.
ga: Kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ kɛ fitemɔ baa Shishifãi ni efite loo ni egbo lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛnu nu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe po.

english: Why are the blossoms dropping off my cowpea plants before any bean pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Flower shedding in cowpeas is usually caused by tiny insect pests like thrips attacking the delicate flower buds, or by excessive heat and water stress that prevents successful pollination.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi yɛ cowpea mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine kɛ nu mli haomɔ ni tsiɔ pollination ni yeɔ omanye lɛ naa lɛ mli.

english: Why should I leave wide spaces between my cassava stems when planting instead of putting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi he ko ni da yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ amɛ ama amɛhe lɛ

english: Cassava needs ample space underground for its root tubers to expand. If you plant them too close together, the plants will compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in many small, thin roots instead of large tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia cassava koni eha shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã. Kɛji odu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa yɛ bulb wuji najiaŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees need taller shade trees growing around them in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni tsei kakadaji ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ aye abua mi-kokoo tso lɛ?

english: Young and growing cocoa plants naturally prefer mild sunlight. Tall shade trees cool the atmosphere, protect fragile cocoa leaves from sun scorch and strong winds, and help keep the soil moist for longer periods.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii ni eda lɛ nyaa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ebuɔ kookoo baai ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling upward and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Curling and yellow leaves on tomato plants are frequently caused by viruses spread by tiny insects like whiteflies. It can also be a sign of uneven watering or nitrogen deficiency in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. Ebaanyɛ efee okadi hu ni tsɔɔ akɛ afɔɔɔ nu be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What is eating small holes into the leaves and central whorl of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai kɛ amɛteŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Holes chewed into young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They crawl deep inside the growing center of the plant to feed on tender new leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa. Amɛkpãa kɛyaa tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ dani amɛje kpo.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers turn soft and rot quickly in my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ oya yɛ mi-shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot easily if they receive scratches or cuts during harvest, allowing fungi and bacteria to enter. Storing them in warm, damp, or poorly ventilated spaces speeds up this decay process.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ loo afo amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ boteɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, loo kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ lɛ, ebaaha nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ aya oya.

english: Why does some rice smell very sweet when cooking while other rice has no smell at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa komɛi ahe ŋɔɔ waa kɛ́ ahoo lɛ, yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu ŋmãaa kwraa lɛ?

english: The sweet smell (aroma) comes naturally from the specific variety of seed planted, not from added chemical treatments. Improved aromatic seeds are bred to naturally produce grains with rich scents that fetch higher market prices.
ga: Aroma (aroma) lɛ jɛɔ dumɔwui pɔtɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Jeee kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛfataa he lɛ mli Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ŋɔɔ ni atsake lɛ koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli dumɔwui ni ŋɔɔ waa ni haa jara lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ aba.

english: How can I tell if a rice seed variety is improved or just traditional saved seed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ atsake ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ loo eji kusum naa dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛkɛ?

english: Improved rice seeds are bred in certified facilities for specific uniform traits like fast growth, pest resistance, or high aroma, whereas saved seeds from previous harvests gradually lose these strong characteristics over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ hei ni aŋmala he odaseyeli awo mli lɛ koni amɛná sui ni yaa nɔ daa, tamɔ amɛdalɛ oya. Nɔ ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo nɔ ni ŋɔɔ waa Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ baaje mli fiofio. Efiteɔ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Can I make my regular harvested rice smell scented by spraying something on it after harvest?
ga: Ani manyɛ maha ŋmãa ni akpaa daa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛtsɔ nɔ ko ni mikɛshwieɔ nɔ beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, artificial sprays can ruin the taste and make the rice unsafe to eat. True aromatic rice gets its pleasant smell naturally through its seed genetics while growing in the field.
ga: Dabi, nibii ni akɛfee ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ lɛ ni eha ŋmãa lɛ afee nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ. Omɔ ni ŋɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa-kɛ-ŋma kɛtsɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli wala yibii lɛ anɔ kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: If I put my aromatic rice through a polishing machine, will it lose its natural smell?
ga: Kɛ okɛ ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ waa wo tsɔne ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ Ani ŋmãa lɛ baafite bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ?

english: Polishing removes the outer husk and bran layer to make the rice clean and white. While it slightly reduces the outer scent, the natural aroma bred inside the core of the grain remains intact.
ga: Kɛ́ ashɛre ŋmãa lɛ, ejieɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ kɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ koni ŋmãa lɛ he atse ni efee futafuta. Eyɛ mli akɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔlɔ lɛ baaye abua ni eha kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔlɔ lɛ aba shi fioo moŋ. Shi adebɔɔ mli tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ni aduɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ kã he ehiɔ shi.

english: How do small stones end up in my harvested rice, and why is that a problem?
ga: Te tɛi bibii feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛboteɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli? Ni mɛni hewɔ naagba ko yɛ lɛ?

english: Stones usually get mixed into rice when the crop is threshed directly on bare ground. Removing these stones using a destoning machine makes the rice safe to eat and allows you to sell it to commercial buyers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ tɛi futuɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli kɛ́ ashwie ŋmãa lɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ shredder tsu nii ni okɛjie tɛi nɛɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni obaanyɛ oye, ni ebaaha onyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ oha jarayelɔi ni heɔ lɛ.

english: What is the difference between simply hulling my rice and fully processing it with destoning and polishing?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ mi-rice lɛ ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ kɛ chiseling kɛ polishing ni akɛtsuɔ nii kwraa lɛ teŋ?

english: Hulling only removes the outer hard husk, leaving brown rice. Full processing includes removing dirt and stones with a destoner and polishing off the bran layer to produce clean, shiny white rice that city markets prefer.
ga: Ejieɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa lɛ pɛ. Nɔ ni eshwɛ ji ŋmãa ni tsuɔ. Nɔ ni fata nitsumɔ ni yeɔ emuu lɛ he ji ni akɛ nɔ ko ni akɛjieɔ tɛi lɛ ajie muji kɛ tɛi kɛjɛ mli, ni ajie ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ mli koni aná ŋmãa yɛŋ ni he tse ni kpɛɔ ni maŋtiasei amli jarayeli hei lɛ biɔ lɛ.

english: Why does some of my rice shatter into small broken pieces when I send it to the local milling machine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shi bibii bibii kɛ́ mikɛmaje ŋmãafeemɔ he ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Rice breaks during milling if it was dried too quickly in harsh direct sunlight, harvested too late when overly dry, or if the milling machine is not properly adjusted for that specific grain size.
ga: Omɔ baagba yɛ be mli ni ashɛɔ lɛ kɛji egbi oya tsɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Kpamɔ sɛɛ tsɔ beni egbi tsɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ atsakeee ŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛha nakai ŋmaa pɔtɛɛ lɛ dalɛ.

english: When is the best time to harvest my rice to keep the grain quality high?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa koni ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Rice should be harvested when about 80 to 85 percent of the grains on the panicle turn golden yellow. Harvesting too late makes the grains brittle, causing them to crack easily during processing.
ga: Esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa be mli ni ŋmãa ni yɔɔ toi lɛ nɔ lɛ mlijaa oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 etsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmaa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ fãa oya yɛ be mli ni atsuɔ he nii lɛ.

english: Why does my stored rice lose its quality and good smell after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni ehiɛ ŋɔɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rice loses its quality and aroma if it is stored with too much moisture or kept in hot, humid spaces exposed to pests. Paddy must be dried properly until hard before storing in clean, dry bags.
ga: Omɔ baafite ekpakpafeemɔ kɛ enaa ŋɔɔmɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ loo hei ni edɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aba. Esa akɛ agbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaawa dani akɛwo kotokui ni mli tse ni egbi amli.

english: Why do commercial buyers offer higher prices for processed rice compared to raw paddy rice straight from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayelɔi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ ŋmãa ni afee lɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ haa kɛ akɛto ŋmãa ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Buyers pay more for processed rice because it has already been cleaned, destoned, and polished, making it ready to cook immediately without extra labor or processing costs.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ ŋmãa lɛ woɔ ŋmãa ni afee lɛ nyɔmɔ babaoo ejaakɛ atsuu he, ajie tɛi kɛjɛ mli, ni afee lɛ fɛfɛo, ni no haa efeɔ klalo akɛ ahooɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni nitsumɔ loo shika kroko ni akɛbaatsu he nii fataaa he.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get burnt easily under harsh, direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantain or cassava nearby creates living umbrellas that give young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi.

english: Why do I see small holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars hiding inside the stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ anɔ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. They feed on young leaves and stem tops; checking your field early in the morning and applying approved biopesticides or neem extract helps protect your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii kɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli leebi ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii ni eye ebua ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies carrying plant viruses. Spraying neem water or insecticidal soap early on keeps these pests away and stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni hiɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Neem nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ amɛhe ni ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too high, when the plants receive uneven watering, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients like calcium. Consistent watering and mulching help keep the soil cool.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ afɔɔ tsei anɔ nu be fɛɛ be Aloo kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why should I not plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same plot drains specific soil nutrients and lets maize pests build up in the ground. Rotating your farm with legumes like cowpea or groundnuts restores nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abele ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ haa sũ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi hoɔ, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting under the soil before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and sits in the soil for too long. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa ni ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my maize field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo mi-ŋma ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Apply NPK fertilizer within 1 to 2 weeks after planting when the seedlings sprout, and follow up with a top-dressing of Urea 4 to 6 weeks later when the maize reaches knee height to support strong growth.
ga: Okɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ otsi kome kɛyashi enyɔ mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃. ni okɛ urea ni akɛwoɔ nɔ lɛ nyiɛ sɛɛ yɛ otsii 4 kɛyashi 6 sɛɛ beni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ enaji ahe koni eye ebua dalɛ ni mli wa lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over easily when the fruit bunches start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots stay close to the surface and cannot hold up the heavy weight of full bunches during strong winds. Supporting the main stem with sturdy bamboo or wooden forks prevents the plants from falling.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfi tso nine muu lɛ fɛɛ ni tsii lɛ nɔ. Abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tso loo tso ni akɛfee ŋmei ni wa fi tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekagbee shi.

english: Why are my harvested seed yams sprouting early in storage before the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ kwɛ̃ oya yɛ nitoohe dani nugbɔ lɛ nɛ lɛ?

english: Yams break dormancy and sprout when stored in warm, poorly ventilated spaces. Keeping seed yams on raised racks inside a shaded, cool, well-ventilated yam barn keeps them sleeping until planting time.
ga: Sweet potatoes baaya ni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ atomɔ dumɔwui lɛ ato adekai ni awó nɔ yɛ atomɔ shĩa ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Ye obua amɛ ni amɛwɔ kɛyashi be ni esa akɛ amɛdu nii lɛ ashɛ.

english: How do weeds growing around my crops reduce my overall harvest?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ŋmaa lɛ fɛɛ shi?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, water, and soil fertilizers meant for your crops. Clearing weeds during the first 3 to 6 weeks after planting gives your main crops the space and food they need to produce a large harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la ni he hia, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Kɛ́ otsi jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 3 kɛyashi 6 mli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha otsei titrii lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ agbo.

english: Why do small insects suddenly appear on my crops right when the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii jeɔ kpo trukaa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi pɛ?

english: Rain creates high humidity and lush foliage, which encourages dormant pest eggs to hatch and attracts insects searching for fresh leaves to feed on.
ga: Nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa kɛ tsei ahe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Enɛ woɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni wɔɔ lɛ ahe hewalɛ koni amɛfɔ ni egbalaa kooloi ni taoɔ baai heei ni amɛyeɔ lɛ.

english: Why do pests keep coming back to my farm even after I have already sprayed chemicals on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yaa nɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai shwieɔ nɔ moŋ

english: Chemicals often kill adult insects but miss hidden eggs, or pests from neighboring farms fly into your field after the chemical power wears off.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai lɛ gbeɔ kooloi bibii ni eda lɛ shi efoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ amli. Aloo, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni jɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ foɔ kɛboteɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli beni tsofa lɛ hewalɛ efo lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to apply pest control on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Early morning or late afternoon is best because heat during mid-day can weaken the chemical, and insects are most active during cooler hours.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli Enɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ la ni tsoɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai lɛ agbɔjɔ. Ni kooloi bibii tsuɔ nii waa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know if the damage on my crops is caused by insects or by a plant disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmeii loo tsei ahe helai ji nɔ ni efite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Insect damage usually leaves visible holes or chewed leaf edges, while diseases show up as spots, wilting, powdery coatings, or yellowing without eaten parts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ haa buji ni anaa loo baai ni atsɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. Yɛ be mli ni helai srɔtoi Efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ fãi komɛi yeee.

english: Why are my regular planting months like August and September no longer working the way they used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nyɔji ni miduɔ nii daa tamɔ August kɛ September lɛ tsuuu nii tamɔ tsutsu lɛ dɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weather patterns have shifted due to climate change, causing rains to start earlier or later than usual, so planting must now depend on soil moisture rather than fixed calendar dates.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi miitsake. Ehaa nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi mra loo sɛɛ mli fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ moŋ fe kalanda gbii pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ.

english: How does heavy rainfall during the main farming season affect my crops' health?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ okwaayeli be titri lɛ mli lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahewalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rain can wash away essential soil nutrients, rot roots in waterlogged soil, and create damp conditions where fungi and pests thrive.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui baanyɛ ada yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: What should I do to protect my crops if the rain stops unexpectedly during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Adding mulch around crop roots helps keep moisture in the soil longer and protects the ground from baking under the hot sun.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ muji wo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekashã yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and start falling off before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔi gbee dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, is getting too much or too little water, or is under attack by tiny leaf-sucking pests.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nu babaoo loo fioo ni ooona? loo ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ baai lɛ tutuaa amɛ.

english: Why do my plants grow lots of big green leaves but fail to yield good fruits or seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli shi ebɛ yibii loo dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer makes them focus only on leaf growth instead of developing flowers and fruits, which require balanced nutrients like phosphorus and potassium.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama baai lɛ adalɛ pɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai baa lɛ Enɛ biɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasiɔm ni sa.

english: How can I prevent pests from attacking my crops without spending too much money on chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkatutua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni mikɛ tsofai babaoo tsuuu nii?

english: Clearing weeds around fields, rotating different crops each season, and clearing farm waste after harvest breaks the pest life cycle naturally.
ga: Jiemɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ. Tsɔmɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Ni ŋmɔ mli jwɛi ni ashɛrɛɔ ashwieɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ adebɔɔ mli wala shihilɛ kpaa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their leaves when the dry Harmattan wind starts blowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ ahe baai babaoo fiteɔ kɛ́ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ je shishi etswa lɛ?

english: During the dry Harmattan season, water becomes scarce and humidity drops. Cocoa trees drop some of their leaves on purpose to reduce water loss through evaporation, which helps the main tree survive the dry weather until the rains return.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, nu faaa ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi. Cacao tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ekomɛi yɛ yiŋtoo ko hewɔ koni amɛkɛba nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ shi kɛtsɔ la ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it good for my farm if I plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa fee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together is a great practice. Maize grows quickly and can be harvested in about three months, while the cassava grows slower and takes over the land after the maize is harvested, giving you two different crops from one plot.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa. Abɛi daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo ni eyeɔ jɛmɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why do people say I should plant groundnuts or beans on my land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which means their roots naturally feed nitrogen into the earth. Planting them first enriches the soil with natural nutrients, acting like free fertilizer for the maize crop that follows.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans yɛ legume weku lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ nitrogen woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shishijee lɛ, tsei nɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii babaoo baa. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmãa ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to produce big, healthy tubers under the ground. Staking also keeps the foliage off the damp soil, which prevents leaves from rotting and catching fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli koni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa baai lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: What is causing the leaves on my cassava plants to turn yellow and curl up tightly?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi yucca tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe waa?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing on cassava is usually caused by the Cassava Mosaic Disease. This sickness is carried and spread from plant to plant by very small flying insects called whiteflies.
ga: Kasava lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela kɛbaa. Koolooi bibii ni foɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ hela lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ.

english: Why did my maize seeds fail to come up out of the ground after I planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize seeds may fail to germinate if they were buried too deep in the dirt, if insects or birds ate them under the surface, or if heavy rain flooded the soil and starved the seeds of air.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. kɛji kooloi bibii loo okpoi ye amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi Aloo kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ ni eha hɔmɔ ye dumɔwui ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Can watering my vegetable crops too much actually cause them to die?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛwoɔ aduawai amli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ agbe amɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, excessive water fills up all the tiny air pockets in the soil, which smothers the plant roots. Without air, the roots begin to rot, causing the plant to turn yellow, wilt, and eventually die.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ amli, ni efiteɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ baabɔi fitemɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, egbɔjɔɔ, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egboɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before any peppers grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as severe heat, dry soil, or lack of pollination from bees. The plant drops flowers to conserve its energy so it can stay alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛna haomɔi, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmeii ni bɛ fɔfɔi lɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are big enough to harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efooo?

english: You can tell cassava is maturing when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem, and when you see cracks forming in the soil right around the base of the stem where the tubers are swelling.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmei ko miida kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Bare stems left Ni kɛ́ ona ŋmeii ni miifee yɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ tso lɛ shishi he ni ŋmeii lɛ efuu lɛ.

english: How do I know if the bush land I want to clear has good soil for planting crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji jwɛi bibii ni misumɔɔ ni mafo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛbaadu tsei?

english: Look at the weeds and natural vegetation growing there; if wild plants grow tall, thick, and deep green, the soil is fertile. Soil that is dark in color and crumbles easily in your hand also shows good soil quality.
ga: Kwɛmɔ jwɛi kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ. Kɛji koo mli tsei dara, amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii Shikpɔŋ ni su yɔɔ diŋŋ ni efoɔ oya yɛ nine mli lɛ hu ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my young pawpaw plants will bear fruit before they grow big and start flowering?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mipapaya tso bibioo lɛ baawo yibii dani eda ni ebɔi fɔmɔ?

english: You cannot easily tell the sex of a pawpaw plant when it is a small seedling. You must wait until it matures and begins to flower, as male flowers grow on long dangling stems, female flowers grow close to the trunk, and hermaphrodite flowers have both male and female parts.
ga: Onyɛŋ ole bɔ ni pawpaw tso ji lɛ mlɛo kɛ́ eji dumɔwu bibioo. Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi ebaada ni ebɔi fɔfɔi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, fɔfɔi hii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei kakadaji ni fĩɔ shi lɛ anɔ. Fɔfɔi yei kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. ni fɔfɔi ni kɛ hii feɔ yakayaka nii lɛ yɛ nuu kɛ yoo fãi fɛɛ.

english: Why do so many small flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Kookoo tsei enyiɛ ni yɔɔ mi kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers but can only support a small fraction as full pods. Flower drop happens due to natural self-thinning, lack of tiny pollinating insects like midges, or dry weather stress.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi ebaanyɛ eye ebua fã bibioo ko pɛ. Beni pod lɛ eyi lɛ pɛ kɛkɛ ni fɔfɔi ni laajeɔ lɛ baa yɛ adebɔɔ mli shwiemɔ hewɔ. Pollinators bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards and twisting during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl during intense heat as a defense mechanism to reduce water loss. However, if the curling comes with yellowing or stunted growth, it often means whiteflies have infected the crop with a leaf curl virus.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa be mli akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Shi, kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛdaraaa lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ ená leaf curl virus yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Why do my pepper plants shed their blossoms when the heat gets very intense?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, pepper plants experience heat stress. They shed their blossoms to conserve water and energy until cooler conditions return.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ baaná hulutsoo be mli haomɔ. Amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds sprout up and grow so much faster than my crop seeds right after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ ni amɛdara oya fe midumɔwui lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie buried in the soil in huge numbers and are naturally adapted to germinate and grow rapidly at the slightest moisture, while domestic crop seeds need more stable conditions to establish.
ga: Akɛ jwɛi dumɔwui babaoo ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni amɛtsake amɛhe yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara oya kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, shia dumɔwui biɔ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ babaoo dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛto amɛhe shi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that the maize plant is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient needed for leaf growth, or that waterlogged soil is preventing the roots from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha baa lɛ dalɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall stems and leafy tops, but the tubers underground are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishifãi kakadaji kɛ baai kakadaji waa lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or water, the cassava plant directs all its energy toward growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa baai kɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why shouldn't I place fertilizer directly against the stem of my young crop plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mitsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated mineral salts. If placed directly against tender young stems, it draws water out of the plant tissues and burns both the stem and roots.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ mineral salts ni mli eyi obɔ. Kɛ akɛwo tsei bibii anɔ tɛ̃ɛ Ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ fãji amli ni eshãa tso lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to remove some of the young shoots growing around the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ

english: The small suckers growing around the main plantain stem share the same root system and compete for water and soil nutrients. Pruning extra suckers ensures the main stem gets enough food to produce a large, healthy bunch.
ga: Tso bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Plantain tsei wuji lɛ ahe lɛ shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ yeɔ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni jɛɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii lɛ amli ekoŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso agbo ni mli wa.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting green shoots in the barn even without soil or rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shweremɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers enter a natural resting phase (dormancy) after harvest. Once this resting period naturally expires, internal plant hormones automatically trigger new sprouts to prepare for the next growing season.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ boteɔ shihilɛ mli (wɔɔ) yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji hejɔɔmɔ be nɛɛ ba naagbee yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, tso lɛ mli tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ tsirɛɔ tso lɛ mli ŋmeii heei koni amɛdara koni amɛkɛsaa amɛhe kɛha shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. It can also happen when the soil is soaked with too much water and the roots cannot breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nu babaoo ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas in my field make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas have tiny natural helpers on their roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the dirt. This leaves natural fertilizer in the soil that feeds your next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii bibii ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How does putting dry grass or leaves around the base of my pepper plants help them stay healthy in dry weather?
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni pepper tso lɛ shishifãi haa amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi lɛ amli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass acts like a blanket over the soil. It stops the hot sun from evaporating soil moisture and keeps the roots cool so your pepper plants need less water.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Enɛ baaha nu fioo pɛ he ahia o-pepper tsei lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak with small yields when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli tseee ni ebɛ hewalɛ shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Spacing them properly ensures every plant gets enough food and light to grow thick stems and heavy fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to push tall wooden stakes into the ground for my yams to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy that feeds the tuber underground. Staking holds the vines up in the sun and keeps the leaves off damp soil where they could easily rot or pick up diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking haa wain tso lɛ hiɔ hulutsoo be mli ni ehaa baai lɛ taraaa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi oya loo hela aba amɛnɔ lɛ.

english: Too many young shoots fight with the main plantain tree for food and water. By cutting away extra suckers and keeping only one or two strong ones, the main tree gets full energy to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tsobii bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ baawu koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Afeɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ ni ahiɛɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ. Tso titri lɛ baaná hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many of their small flowers before pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Mɛi enyiɛ dani pods lɛ feɔ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers but drop them if the soil gets too dry, if there is too much sun, or if tiny insects called midges have not pollinated them. Proper shade trees help keep moisture in the air and protect the flowers.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi ebaagbee shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Hulu la fa tsɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ eshɛko pollination lolo. Tsei ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ mli fɛ̃i yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without making any peppers during very hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ pepper baaa yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Very high temperatures damage the pollen inside pepper flowers, preventing seeds and fruits from forming. When flowers fail to pollinate due to extreme heat, the plant sheds them to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa waa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ pepper fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Ehaa dumɔwui kɛ aduawai akafee Beni fɔfɔii lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee pollin yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa hewɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting quickly if I leave them underground too long after they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛdara sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once cassava roots are fully grown, excessive soil rain or cracks in the ground let water and soil bacteria into the tubers, causing them to decay while still in the ground.
ga: Beni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu kɛ sũ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ abote bulb lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgboiɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lolo lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up tightly and stopping the fruits from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa ni amɛtsiɔ aduawai lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus, or by the plant trying to shield itself from extreme heat and dry soil. Controlling insects early keeps the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Mra Be mli Kooloi Ahe Nitsumɔ Yeɔ Ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ mli waa

english: Why are my harvested tomatoes soft and full of too much water inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes become watery and soft when given too much water or excess nitrogen fertilizer close to harvest time. Reducing watering right before picking and balancing fertilizer helps produce firm tomatoes with longer shelf life.
ga: Tomato bafeɔ nu ni efeɔ blɛoo kɛji akɛ awo mli nu fe nine loo akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli fe nine beni kpamɔ be lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔtsemɔ dani ajieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tomato ni wa ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: How do I know when my young nursery seedlings are ready to be replanted on the main farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu ekoŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings are usually ready for replanting when they have 4 to 6 true leaves and strong stems, typically 3 to 4 weeks after planting. It is best to transplant them early in the morning or late in the afternoon to avoid heat stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha dumɔ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ amɛyɛ baai diɛŋtsɛ 4 kɛyashi 6 kɛ tso ni mli wa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ tsei awo he kroko leebi loo shwane mli. Bɔni afee ni ajie dɔlɛ he haomɔ

english: Why is it necessary for officers to test the soil on my farm before I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni onukpai lɛ aka shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amɛkwɛ dani amɛdu nii lɛ?

english: Soil testing tells you which exact plant nutrients are missing from your land and whether the soil is too acidic. This helps you buy only the specific fertilizer your crops need, saving you money and increasing yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa baatsɔɔ bo tsei amli niyenii ni bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ? Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa otsei lɛ pɛ. Okɛ shika ato ni oha nitsumɔ lɛ aya hiɛ

english: What should I do when some of the seeds I planted fail to germinate in the field?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekomɛi nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should replant new seeds in those empty spots within one to two weeks of the first sprouting. Replanting early ensures that all your crops grow together evenly and mature around the same time.
ga: Esa akɛ odu dumɔwui heei yɛ nakai hei ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ yɛ otsi kome kɛyashi enyɔ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ. Tsei heei ni ooodu mra Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ feɔ ekome ni amɛdaraa yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why do my fresh tomatoes rot quickly after I harvest them and put them in crates?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato hee lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mikpa ni mikɛwo adeka mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes spoil fast if picked when extremely ripe, bruised during harvest, or packed into tight containers without air movement. Harvesting them when they just start changing color and keeping them in ventilated crates preserves them longer.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ajie lɛ beni ekwɛ̃ waa. Akɛwoɔ mli yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi ko ni mli wa mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akpa amɛ be mli ni amɛjeɔ su tsakemɔ shishi kɛkɛ ni akɛ amɛ woɔ adeka ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What kind of assistance can I get when an extension officer comes to inspect my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ yelikɛbuamɔ maná kɛji extension officer ko ba koni ebakwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: During an inspection, the officer examines your crops for early signs of disease, insect damage, and soil problems. They provide direct guidance on correct crop spacing, chemical application, and overall plant health management.
ga: Yɛ kwɛmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ Nitsulɔi lɛ baakwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli koni amɛna helai ahe okadii mra, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ naagbai, ni amɛbaahã bo ŋaa tɛ̃ɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ he. Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ tsei ahewalɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni ja

english: How can I tell if I am giving my crops too much water on the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ nu miiwo miŋmɔshi nibii amli fe nine yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Excess water causes crop leaves to turn yellow, stems to get soft or root-rotted, and fruits to turn watery. The soil should stay damp to the touch, not soggy like mud.
ga: Nu babaoo haa tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Tso lɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ loo shishifãi ni egboi ni aduawai lɛ tsɔɔ nu Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛji akɛ ota he. Jeee ni efɔ tamɔ muji

english: Why do my young seedlings wilt and die right after I move them out of the shade nursery into full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crops suffer from transplant shock when suddenly exposed to full sun. You need to gradually expose nursery plants to sunshine a few days before replanting and water them well immediately after moving them to the farm.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ bibii lɛ naa shoofeemɔ he amanehulu kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Esa akɛ okɛ tsei bibii lɛ awo hulu la mli fiofio gbii fioo komɛi dani okɛ amɛ adu ekoŋŋ ni okɛ nu aha amɛ bɔ ni sa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni okɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do officers take sample leaves and fruits from my farm to run tests on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ ŋɔ baai kɛ aduawai ahe saji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛka amɛkwɛ lɛ?

english: Testing plant samples allows officers to identify hidden pests, viruses, or fungal infections inside the plant tissue that cannot be seen with the naked eye, allowing for early treatment before the disease spreads.
ga: Tsei ahe nɔkwɛmɔnii ni akaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa onukpai lɛ ni amɛyɔseɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ tsei amli ni anyɛɛɛ akɛ hiŋmɛi ana. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ atsaa lɛ mra. Dani hela lɛ baagbɛ eshwa

english: What causes my vegetable crops to produce weak, tasteless, or pale fruits?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-vegetables lɛ miiwo yibii ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni ŋmɔlɔ bɛ mli, loo ni mli tseee?

english: Pale and weak fruit usually results from a lack of essential soil nutrients like potassium and calcium, or from over-watering during fruit growth. Adding organic manure or balanced fertilizers improves crop flavor and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium kɛ calcium ni bɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ aduawai ni mli tse ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa fe nine yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ amli ŋɔɔmɔ kɛ hewalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is even ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani abele lɛ po feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on young maize often mean the plants are starving for nitrogen, which is a key plant food, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients too deep for the roots to reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii titri lɛ Aloo, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe kɛtee shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow lots of leaves but very few pods when I give them plenty of fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ baa babaoo shi amɛmli ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo haa amɛ lɛ?

english: If you give cowpeas too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plant gets confused and spends all its energy growing big leaves instead of making flowers and seed pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oha cowpea nitrogen babaoo lɛ, Tso lɛ futuɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ baai wuji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui ŋmɔji

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thick leaves but produce tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ baai ni mli tse shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are crowded closely together, the cassava focuses its energy upward toward sunlight rather than storing starch in its roots underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei ebɔle amɛhe. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ lɛ yaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa hulu la lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ starch baato eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my yam mounds when the yam vines are already tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi yɛ sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ he be mli ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ekwɛ momo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water and plant food from the soil, and they also shade the low parts of the yam vine, which prevents the roots from getting the energy needed to form big tubers.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli. Ehaa sweet potato wain tso lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ hu ahe. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sun. Plantains grow fast with broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, providing shade and trapping soil moisture for the cocoa.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa hulutsoo ni ehiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛhaa kookoo.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and soft on the tree during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cold, wet conditions. When weeds are high or tree branches are too thick, damp air gets trapped, allowing the black pod disease to multiply.
ga: Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Beni jwɛi lɛ kwɔ tsɔ loo niji lɛ egbɔ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ baamɔ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, black pod hela lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why should I cut off the small green shoots growing near the base of my mature cocoa tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo tso ni eda kwraa lɛ shishi

english: Those extra shoots, called chupons or suckers, drink up water and food meant for the main tree, reducing the amount of health cocoa pods your tree can produce.
ga: Nɛkɛ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he nɛɛ, ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons loo tsei lɛ, nuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha tso titri lɛ. Enɛ haa kookoo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni otso lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ baa shi.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the weather is extremely hot and dry or when the soil lacks moisture, which stops the flower from completing pollination.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ akafee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my garden egg plants curling up and turning pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ mli ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or aphids that attack the underside of leaves, or by a virus carried by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids, ni tutuaa baa lɛ shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ

english: Why shouldn't I place fertilizer right against the main stem of my young crop plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mitsei bibii lɛ ashishifã titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer dissolves in moisture and creates a strong salt concentration that can burn the stem and roots, killing the young plant instead of feeding it.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmei ni naa wa ni baanyɛ ashã tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ baa. Gbemɔ tsei bibii moŋ fe ni oooha amɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient plants need to build strong, healthy green leaves. Heavy rains can also wash this nutrient out of the topsoil, leaving the plant hungry.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji tso ko ni yɔɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni baaha baai eŋɔli ni mli wa aba. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ afɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ he kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up tight during the middle of a hot day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up to shield themselves from strong sun and cut down on water loss. It is the plant's natural defense to conserve moisture so it does not dry out during extreme heat.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni amɛha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Eji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni ekɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, egbiɛɛ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark black and rot while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, overly shady farms. Pruning thick tree branches to let sunshine and air inside helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. niji ni mli tse ni afoɔ Koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli lɛ aye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are small insects eating the flowers off my tomato plants before fruit can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye fɔfɔi ni jɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ dani yibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Pests like thrips and caterpillars target tender blossoms because they are soft and full of food. If flowers are destroyed, the plant cannot produce tomatoes, so protecting flowers early is key to getting a good harvest.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ thrips kɛ caterpillars lɛ kwɛɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni niyenii eyi mli obɔ. Kɛji akɛ akpata fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo tomato. No hewɔ lɛ, bu fɔfɔi ahe mra. No hewɔ lɛ, no ji nɔ titri ni haa anáa nikpamɔ kpakpa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when we get heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess water sits in the ground for too long without draining, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing them to suffocate and decay.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔɔɔ. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ kɛ fitemɔ baa

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first light rain. Wait until the rain has soaked into the soil deeply enough for a few continuous days so seeds do not dry out and die right after sprouting.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ gbii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ koni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily whenever strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be weakened by microscopic pests called nematodes or heavy bunch weight. Staking trees with sturdy wooden poles and mounding rich soil around the base gives them better support.
ga: Plantains shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo ŋmeii ni tsii baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Tso lɛ ni akɛ tsei ni wa duɔ ni akɛ sũ ni jara wa toɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enyɛɔ ekwɛɔ ehe jogbaŋŋ.

english: What makes my yam tubers grow small and twisted instead of big and straight?
ga: Mɛni haa mi sweet potato tubers lɛ feɔ bibii ni ebɔleɔ shi moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni eja?

english: Yams need loose, soft soil to expand smoothly. Hard ground, hidden rocks, or tiny worm-like pests in the soil block the tuber from pushing straight down, causing it to bend and stay small.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa, tɛi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. loo ŋmeii bibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni tsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsi amɛhe kɛya shi tɛ̃ɛ. Ha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee bibioo.

english: Why do some weeds come back even faster a few days after I clear them with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi komɛi kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa oya gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni mikɛ dade shwie amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Slashing only removes the top part of the weed. Many tough weeds have creeping roots underground that quickly shoot up new leaves unless you dig out the root systems completely.
ga: Slashing jieɔ jwɛi lɛ yiteŋ pɛ. Jwɛi babaoo ni wa lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni woɔ baai heei oya. Ja otsi shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli.

english: Why does my pepper plant drop its young fruits before they are ready to pick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho aduawai bibii dani amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their fruit when stressed by sudden changes in weather, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like calcium. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the plant hold onto its fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛyibii lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa lɛ ha amɛhao. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ calcium ni bɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field without any trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very delicate and sensitive to strong sunlight. Without shade from larger plants, the intense heat dries them out and kills them before their roots can properly develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa waa, ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ nuɔ he waa. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo bɛ tsei wuji ahe Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baaha amɛgbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛshishifãi lɛ anyɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens to young cocoa plants if the hot sun shines directly on them all day?
ga: Mɛni baa kookoo tsei bibii anɔ kɛji akɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ ni shɛɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Direct sun scorches the leaves of young cocoa, causes rapid water loss, and can easily burn and kill the seedlings before they have a chance to mature.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa kookoo baai bibii. ni haa nu fiteɔ oya ni eshãa ni egbeɔ dumɔwui lɛ oya dani amɛdaraa kwraa.

english: Is it bad practice to leave my newly cleared farm without shade crops when starting a cocoa farm?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ gbonyo akɛ aaashi ŋmɔ hee ni ajie lɛ kpo ni tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli bɛ mli beni ajeɔ kookoo ŋmɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Yes, leaving a newly planted cocoa field completely open exposes young seedlings to extreme heat and sun scorch, which leads to high seedling death rates.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ashi kookoo ŋmɔji ni adu ehee lɛ agbele lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui bibii lɛ aná dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni gboiɔ lɛ fa babaoo.

english: Why do farmers usually plant plantain together with young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ kookoo tsei bibii feɔ ekome kɛduɔ plantains lɛ?

english: Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas. They provide essential shade to shield young cocoa trees from the sun while helping keep the surrounding environment moist.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Amɛhaa hɔɔŋ ni he hiaa koni akɛbu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shihilɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How does growing plantain next to my young crops keep them cool during hot weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ plantains ni miduɔ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants cast broad shade over nearby crops, blocking strong sun rays and trapping humidity underneath their leaves to create a cool microclimate.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ haa hulutsoo babaoo yɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ baai lɛ ashishi koni ekɛfee kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko ni mli ejɔ

english: Will planting plantain close to my young cocoa trees harm the cocoa or help it?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baaye kookoo lɛ awui loo ebaaye ebua lɛ?

english: It helps the cocoa greatly in its early stages. The plantain acts as a protective cover that shelters the cocoa from intense heat and harsh weather.
ga: E yeɔ bua Cocoa wawɛɛ ngɛ sisije be ɔmɛ a mi. Plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa he.

english: Why are plantains considered good nurse crops for fragile young plants like cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abuɔ plantain akɛ eji tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ kookoo lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly to form a canopy of shade and retain moisture, giving young, fragile seedlings the protection they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya koni ekɛfee hulutsoo ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Ehaa dumɔwui ni waaa, ni waaa lɛ hebuu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why does the soil under plantain trees stay wet even when the sun is strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sũ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ mli edɔ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ hulu lɛ miitso waa moŋ lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves block direct sunlight from hitting the ground, which slows down water evaporation from the soil and keeps the ground cool and damp.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ blɛoo. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: How does a plantain tree help share moisture with neighboring young crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ plantains yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ jaa ŋmɔtɔ?

english: By shielding the soil from direct sunlight, the plantain prevents water in the ground from evaporating quickly, ensuring nearby young plants have access to moist soil.
ga: Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Plantain baatsi nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya. Enɛ baaha tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ aná shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ.

english: Can planting large-leafed crops near small crops help save water in the soil?
ga: Ani tsei wuji ni aduɔ yɛ tsei bibii ahe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni nu akafite shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, large-leafed crops like plantains cover the ground, keeping the soil shaded and moist so small neighboring crops don't dry out fast.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni baai wuji yɔɔ mli, tamɔ plantains ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Bɔni afee ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ ni yɔɔ bibii lɛ akagbi oya.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow from the tips even when it rains well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛyitseiaŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves from the bottom up usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green foliage. Rain can wash nitrogen deep into the soil where roots cannot reach, so applying split doses of fertilizer or organic manure helps restock it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Nugbɔ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he yɛ fãi amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain suckers alongside my young cocoa seedlings on a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui kɛfata kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ ŋmɔ hee mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong direct sunlight during their first couple of years. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as natural sunshades, keeping the soil moist and protecting the tender cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo ni mli tse lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot in the soil before harvest time arrives?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in heavy soil for too long, cutting off oxygen to the roots and letting soil fungi attack them. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away naturally.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ kɛha shishifãi lɛ. ni eha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ atutua ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or beans together with my maize will help my soil stay rich?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ du ŋmei loo ŋmei lɛ, ebaaye ebua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which can capture nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. This naturally feeds neighboring crops like maize without relying entirely on bought fertilizers.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji legumes, ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ aye niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛ ehe efɔɔɔ ŋmãa ni aheɔ lɛ nɔ kwraa.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, won't I harvest much more food from my small land?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ makpa niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Ani minine shɛɛɛ minɔ̃ lɛ nɔ babaoo?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and underground water. Spacing your crops properly gives every plant enough room to grow big leaves, strong roots, and maximum yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaa wuji baakwɛ̃. shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ yibiiwoo ni fe fɛɛ

english: Why are tiny green caterpillars hiding inside the central funnels of my corn stalks and chewing holes in the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ amli buji lɛ?

english: Those are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets the softest new growth inside the corn leaves. Checking your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts right into the funnels stops them before they ruin the grain head.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kwɛɔ ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ anɔ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ yi lɛ awo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Etsiɔ amɛnaa dani amɛkpãtãa dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme hot weather, dry spells between waterings, or a lack of calcium in the soil. Maintaining regular soil moisture and applying mulch helps stabilize temperature and save the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Be ni mli egbi yɛ nu ni akɛhaa loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ teŋ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni eha fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why should I start my pepper seeds in a protected nursery bed instead of sowing them straight into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu pepper dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni abuɔ he lɛ nɔ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ

english: Pepper seeds are very tiny and delicate, so heavy rain, strong sun, or soil insects can easily destroy them in an open field. A nursery lets you give them special water and shade until they grow into sturdy seedlings ready to survive outside.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ ji bibii waa ni amɛhe yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, hulu la ni naa wa loo kooloi ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ baanyɛ akpata amɛhiɛ yɛ ŋmɔji amli mlɛo. He ni akwɛɔ tsei yɛ lɛ haa onyɛɔ ohaa amɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo babaoo kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ dumɔwui ni he wa ni esaa amɛhe koni amɛhi kpo nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak even if I apply fertilizer to the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and steal the food, water, and sunlight you meant to give your plants. Clearing weeds early ensures all the fertilizer you apply goes directly into growing your actual harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni osusu akɛ obaaha otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ náa ŋmɔshi nibii diɛŋtsɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I pour all my chemical fertilizer into the ground on the exact day I sow my crop seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbi ni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Newly planted seeds and tiny sprouts do not have enough roots to absorb large amounts of fertilizer, so most of it gets washed away by rain or burns the tender seed. Applying fertilizer in small amounts as the plant grows ensures none of it goes to waste.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛ ŋmeii ni adu ehee lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, nugbɔ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ babaoo loo eshãa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko fata he beni tso lɛ miida lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko nɔ ko fiteɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: When maize leaves turn yellow starting from the bottom, it usually means the plant is starving for nitrogen, a key food it needs from the soil. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to its newest top leaves to survive, leaving the older lower leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
