ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni ehi shi. Ha baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi.

english: Why are the bottom tips of my green tomato fruits turning black and rotting before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ naagbeei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil while the fruit is growing rapidly. It is often caused by irregular watering or dry spells that prevent the roots from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida oya lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo hulutsoo be ni haaa shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why did my groundnut seeds fail to sprout after I planted them right before a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut seeds need moist soil to sprout, but too much water sitting in the soil starves the seeds of air and causes them to rot underground before they can send up shoots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ he miihia ŋmei dumɔwui koni amɛkwɛ̃. Shi nu babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Which way up should I stick my cassava stem cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, nɛgbɛ esa akɛ ŋmei lɛ aya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the small leaf buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the plant will waste energy trying to twist its roots and shoots in the right direction, leading to weak growth and poor tuber yields.
ga: Esa akɛ adu fɔfɔii bibii ni afolɔ yɛ cassava mli lɛ. tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu tsei ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Tsei lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tuber yibiiwoo ni ehiii baa.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small shoots growing around the root of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajieɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Those extra shoots, called suckers, steal water, light, and soil nutrients away from the main mother plant. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main stem grows thick enough to produce big, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi nɛɛ, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu, la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yitso lɛ mli tseɔ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ tsei wuji ni tsii baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and wrinkling like wrinkled paper?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe tamɔ wolo ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap under the leaves, or by a virus carried by whiteflies. As these pests feed, they distort the leaf tissue and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Kɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ye niyenii Amɛfiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni amɛtsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without turning into actual cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee cacao ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they are stressed by drought, extreme heat, or pest attacks. Flowers also fall off unfertilized if tiny insects called midges have not visited them to transfer pollen from flower to flower.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai hao amɛ. Fɔfɔi hu shwieɔ shi ni amɛfɔɔɔ kɛji kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ eyaaa amɛŋɔɔ koni amɛjie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi amli kɛya fɔfɔi krokomɛi amli.

english: Why do my crops look completely droopy and limp during the hot afternoon even if the ground has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo ni egbɔjɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: When the afternoon sun is very hot, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it up from the ground. Wilting or drooping is the plant's natural way of reducing the leaf surface area exposed to the sun to conserve water until the cooler evening.
ga: Kɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Wilting, loo egbee shi ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehaa ebaai lɛ anɔ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni ekɛto nu he kɛyashi gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be baa.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize on the exact same piece of land three seasons in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ bei etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil pulls out the exact same nutrients season after season, leaving the land depleted. It also allows maize-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the soil, leading to smaller harvests each year.
ga: Abele ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ mli daa be. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kpokpaa lɛ bɛ dɔŋŋ. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ hu faa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, daa afi lɛ, nikpamɔ ni baa lɛ faaa.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from my yam mounds as soon as the shoots start climbing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi sweet potato ŋtayaa lɛ mli kɛji ŋwɛi ŋtayaai lɛ je shishi amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Young yam shoots grow slowly at first and need all the sunlight, soil nutrients, and water they can get. Fast-growing weeds will quickly choke the delicate vines, block sunlight, and rob the soil of nutrients needed to grow large yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei bibii lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni amɛbiɔ hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu babaoo bɔ ni obaanyɛ ona Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ shwieɔ wain tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ oya, ni etsĩɔ hulu la naa ni ejuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji lɛ.

english: Why do cash crops like cocoa and coffee grow much better in regions like Western and Eastern Ghana than in other parts of the country?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shika ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo kɛ kɔfi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpokpai tamɔ Ghana anaigbɛ kɛ bokagbɛ fe maŋ lɛ hei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Certain crops need consistent rainfall, high humidity, and rich forest soils to thrive. Regions in the forest belt, like Western and Eastern Ghana, naturally provide these ideal moisture and climate conditions.
ga: Tsei komɛi taoɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa, hulutsoo babaoo, kɛ koo mli shikpɔŋ kpakpa koni amɛshwere. Kpokpai ni yɔɔ kooi amli tamɔ Ghana anaigbɛ kɛ bokagbɛ. Eyɛ hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni sa jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my farm in the Central Region is fertile enough for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Central Region lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tse bɔ ni sa kɛha okwaayeli?

english: Fertile soil usually has a dark, rich color from decomposed leaves and organic matter, feels soft and moist when squeezed, and allows water to drain slowly without turning into sticky mud.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kɛjɛɔ baai ni fiteɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ ashɛre lɛ. ni oha nu lɛ atsɔ fiofio ni etsɔko muji ni shwieɔ shi

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up and droop during the hottest hours of the afternoon in the Bono Region?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔɔ fe fɛɛ yɛ Bono Kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plants curl their leaves as a protective measure to reduce water loss through evaporation during intense heat, helping them survive until temperatures drop later in the day.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi yɛ gbi lɛ naagbee.

english: Why are farmers in the southern regions of Ghana able to plant and harvest crops twice a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ghana wuoyigbɛ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛduɔ ni amɛkpaa nii shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli lɛ?

english: Southern and central Ghana experience a bimodal rainfall pattern, meaning they get two distinct rainy seasons each year (major and minor), allowing for two full planting cycles.
ga: Ghana wuoyigbɛ kɛ teŋgbɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ gbɛi enyɔ nɔ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi enyɔ nɔ daa afi. (Agbo kɛ bibioo) haa aduɔ shii enyɔ ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and die when water collects and stays around their stems after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa ni ehi shi yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? Trunk yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When water sits around the roots for too long, it cuts off oxygen, suffocating the roots and causing them to rot.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaafo kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why are the crops growing under large shade trees on my land tall and skinny, but producing very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: When plants don't get enough direct sunlight, they use all their energy stretching upward toward the light instead of using that energy to produce flowers and fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ni amɛkpãa kɛyaa la lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ jamɛ a he wami ɔ tsuɔ ní kɛ woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii.

english: Can I plant the same cassava variety that grows well in the Volta Region on a dry farm in northern Ghana?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei srɔtoi ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Volta kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli egbi ni yɔɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ mli?

english: Crop varieties are adapted to specific local conditions. A cassava variety bred for moist forest zones like Volta may struggle or yield poorly in drier, hotter soils unless it is a drought-resistant variety.
ga: Atsakeɔ tsei srɔtoi lɛ kɛyaa shihilɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ. Cassava henɔi ni fɔɔ yɛ kooi ni mli edɔ waa, tamɔ Volta lɛ baanyɛ abɔ mɔdɛŋ loo amɛtsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔji ni egbi ni edɔ waa lɛ anɔ. Ja eji tso srɔtoi ni baanyɛ akpee hɔmɔ naa.

english: Why do my crops grow faster and greener on land that was recently cleared from virgin forest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ajie koo ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ lɛ mli etsɛko lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Forest soil accumulates natural fertilizer over many years from decaying leaves, branches, and organic matter, giving young crops an abundance of immediate nutrients.
ga: Koo mli shikpɔŋ buaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii anaa yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli kɛjɛɔ baai, tsei aniji, kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fiteɔ lɛ amli. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ babaoo

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers without growing any peppers during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shi ni eduuu pepper yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When a plant experiences severe water stress, it enters survival mode and sheds its flowers to conserve moisture and energy for its main stem and leaves.
ga: Kɛ tsei kɛ nu he haomɔ ni naa wa kpe lɛ Eyaa wala shihilɛ mli ni eshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛto ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha eshishifãi titrii kɛ ebaai lɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant them very close together to fit more on my piece of land?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leading to weak stems, higher risk of disease, and smaller total harvests.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tso lɛ shishi gbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara babaoo kɛha helai kɛ nibii fɛɛ ni afeɔ lɛ faaa

english: What is a screen house, and why should I consider using one for my young plants?
ga: Mɛni ji filta shĩa? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu he akɛ mikɛ greenhouse baatsu nii kɛha mi dumɔwui lɛ?

english: A screen house is a frame covered with fine netting that lets in sunlight and air while keeping out destructive insects and heavy rain. It acts as a nursery shelter, giving delicate young seedlings a safe space to grow strong before they face the open field.
ga: Greenhouse ni akɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ebɔ he lɛ ji ŋtayaai ni akɛ ŋtayaai bibii ni haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli lɛ ehà nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ nii kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ahe. Etsuɔ nii akɛ gbi mli kwɛmɔhe. Ehaa dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ naa he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa dani amɛkɛ ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ akpee.

english: Why do insects damage my crops so easily in the open field, but crops inside a netting structure stay healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ oya lɛ? Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ trellis lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: In the open field, pests like whiteflies and aphids fly freely to eat leaves and spread crop diseases. The fine netting of a protected structure physically blocks these insects from reaching your plants, reducing the need for chemical sprays.
ga: Yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ, kooloi tamɔ whiteflies kɛ aphids fɔ̃ɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛye baai ni amɛgbɛ tsei ahelai amɛshwã. Nɔ ni abuɔ he lɛ mli ŋmeii bibii lɛ tsiɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ koni amɛkabote otsei lɛ amli. Ehaa tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he hiamɔ baa shi.

english: How long should my seedlings stay in the nursery before I transplant them into my main farm?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ midumɔwui lɛ ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛ amɛ aya miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Most vegetable and crop seedlings need about four to eight weeks (one to two months) in a nursery. This gives them enough time to build strong roots and sturdy stems so they do not die when moved to the main field.
ga: Aduawai kɛ tsei babaoo amli dumɔwui biɔ aaafee otsii ejwɛ kɛyashi kpaanyɔ. (nyɔji kome kɛyashi enyɔ) yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Enɛ haa be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛfeɔ shishifãi ni wa kɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Bɔni afee ni amɛkagboi kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Why do my seedlings sometimes wither and die right after I move them from the nursery to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by transplant shock, which happens when young plants are suddenly exposed to harsh sun and dry wind. You can prevent this by watering them thoroughly, transplanting late in the afternoon, and providing temporary shade.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji shoofeemɔ ni jɛɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ mli baa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei bibii lɛ shɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ he. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ nu ni oooha lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Akɛwoɔ mli yɛ shwane mli ni ahaa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko

english: How can I tell if my crops are growing at the right speed during their first two months?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji enyɔ lɛ amli?

english: During the first two months, healthy plants should regularly produce new, bright green leaves and growing stems. If the growth stalls or leaves turn yellow, the crops likely need extra nutrients, water, or weed control.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ, esa akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ajie baai heei kɛ ŋmeii ni kpɛɔ daa. Kɛji akɛ tso lɛ dalɛ sɛɛ fo loo baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia niyenii krokomɛi, nu, loo jwɛi ni akɛbaatsu nii.

english: How do plants produce their seeds or young shoots, and do all crops multiply the same way?
ga: Te tsei feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛwoɔ dumɔwui loo ŋmeii bibii? Ni te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ afɔ bii yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ hu?

english: Crops multiply in two main ways: through flowers that produce seeds (like maize, tomatoes, and peppers) or through vegetative parts like stem cuttings, tubers, or suckers (like cassava, yams, and plantains).
ga: Tsei fɔɔ yɛ gbɛi titrii enyɔ nɔ: kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni woɔ dumɔwui (tamɔ ŋmãa, tomato, kɛ shito) loo kɛtsɔ tso lɛ fãi, tamɔ tso lɛ yibii ni afolɔ, tsei ayibii, loo tsei ashishifãi (tamɔ ŋmãa, atomo, kɛ plantains).

english: If I harvest seeds from my best-performing crop this year, will they grow into equally strong plants next season?
ga: Kɛji mikpa afi nɛɛ tsei ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ dumɔwui lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ baatsɔ tsei ni he wa tamɔ nɛkɛ. Kɛfata he yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli loo daabi?

english: Not always. Many modern seed varieties are hybrids, meaning their offspring may not inherit the exact same strength or yield as the parent plant. Buying certified seeds often yields more reliable results.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui srɔtoi babaoo ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ seshibii lɛ nyɛŋ aná hewalɛ loo yibiiwoo tamɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ haa yibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ babaoo.

english: Why do plantain plants sprout young shoots at their base, and can I use them to start new plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ? Ni ani manyɛ mikɛtsu nii kɛje tso hee ko shishi?

english: Those young shoots are called suckers, which are natural offspring produced by the mother plant. You can carefully dig up healthy suckers and replant them elsewhere to grow new plantain trees.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii, ni ji adebɔɔ mli seshibii ni jɛɔ nyɛ tso lɛ mli. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni okɛdu yɛ he kroko koni okwɛ plantain hee.

english: Why does a crop variety grow very well in one region like Akropong, but struggle when planted in a different town?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpokpaa kome nɔ tamɔ Akropong shi amɛnaa amanehulu kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ maŋ kroko nɔ lɛ?

english: Different areas have unique soil types, temperatures, and rainfall patterns. Crop varieties are often bred for specific local environments, so a crop that thrives in cool, rainy hills may suffer in hotter, drier plains.
ga: Hei srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi srɔtoi, dɔlɛ, kɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa. Bei pii lɛ, afɔɔ tsei srɔtoi kɛha shihilɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ yɛ gɔji ni mli ejɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ana amanehulu yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some of my crops produce flowers very quickly while others take many months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi fɔɔ fɔfɔi oya waa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ nyɔji babaoo lɛ?

english: Flowering timing is controlled by the plant's natural life cycle and environment. Short-season crops like beans flower quickly to complete their cycle in a few months, while permanent crops like cocoa or citrus must grow for years to mature before flowering.
ga: Tso lɛ wala shihilɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ kudɔɔ fɔfɔi fɔmɔ be lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ ŋmeii, fɔɔ oya koni amɛgbe sɛɛkuu lɛ naa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. yɛ be mli ni esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hiɔ shi daa tamɔ kookoo loo citrus akwɛ̃ afii babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ dani amɛwo fɔfɔi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I clear all the shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijieɔ hulutsoo tsei fɛɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Shade trees protect the young plants from heat stroke and keep the soil moist while the cocoa builds strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dɔlɛ he ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fũuɔ, yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ feɔ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from my young crops early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ amli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal the water, sunlight, and soil food that your crop needs to grow strong and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning pale yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and produce large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛsu eŋɔli lɛ mli ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when the rains are very heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the field for too long, it drowns the roots and causes rot fungi to grow.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ aba.

english: How does adding rotten leaves and animal dung to my farm help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egboi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛfataa miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Organic manure acts like a slow-release food for the soil, helping it hold moisture longer during dry heat while feeding crop roots naturally.
ga: Organic fertilizers tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi blɛoo lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni akɛduɔ shishifãi.

english: Why do my corn plants grow tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni miduɔ amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving none of them with enough strength to make large cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwu ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛaafee ŋmei agbo.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a hot dry period that dries out the ground, which will kill tender newly sprouted seeds before the main rains begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui heei akwɛ̃ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ aje shishi.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to gather energy. Staking gets leaves off the ground so the plant can feed its growing underground tuber.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulu la lɛ mli koni amɛbua hewalɛ naa. Staking jieɔ baai lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ aye abua shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: What is eating small holes in the center of my young corn plants and leaving dark powder behind?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ni mishi powda ni tsuɔ diŋ yɛ sɛɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the inner leaves of the corn plant and feeds on the soft growth.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei amli baai amli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off before producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when the plant lacks important minerals like calcium during flowering.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ minerals ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium yɛ fɔfɔi be mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and burning in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight and dry air when they are small. Planting shade crops like plantain or cassava alongside them provides shade and keeps the soil cool while the cocoa roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ kɛ́ tsei lɛ darako. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ. Kɛfata he lɛ, ekɛ hulutsoo haa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Why should I cut down extra shoots growing at the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo shweremɔ kroko ni yɔɔ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, known as suckers, fight with the main plantain tree for food, water, and sunlight. Pruning them away leaves only one or two strong suckers, which helps the main tree produce much larger and heavier bunches.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ akɛ ŋmeii. Ebaawu eshi plantain wulu lɛ koni ená niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ afolɔ lɛ, ebaashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaye abua tso titri lɛ ni ewo niji ni dara ni tsii kwraa.

english: Yellowing starting at the leaf tips is a clear sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, a key food plant needs to stay green. Applying NPK or Urea fertilizer around the plant roots helps restore the green color and supports cob growth.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anaa lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titri ni he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii, ni akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo urea fataa he Tso shishifãi lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa cob lɛ dalɛ.

english: Why is it good practice for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm before planting maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmãa yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it naturally in the soil through their roots. When you plant maize afterward, it feeds on this trapped nitrogen and grows better with less need for artificial fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ebaaye nitrogen ni emɔmɔ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmãa ni akɛfee lɛ he ehiaaa tsɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and turning light yellow in patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a sickness spread by tiny whiteflies and infected stem cuttings. You can prevent this by planting disease-resistant cassava varieties and using healthy cuttings from uninfected farms.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ afolɔ Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni jɛ ŋmɔji ni hela bɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, reducing disease and producing much bigger yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni eha niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Ehaa helai baa shi ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni da fe tsutsu lɛ baa

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by severe heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Regular watering during hot spells and using balanced fertilizer keeps the flowers intact to form fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe daa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite kɛyashi amɛbaawo yibii.

english: This rot is caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, usually brought on by dry spells or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and adding agricultural lime or compost helps stop the rot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni faaa loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ba daa ni okɛ lime loo okwaayeli mli ŋmɔtɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpa ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and sawdust-like dirt inside the center shoots?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli lɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows inside the leaves to eat the tender central shoot. Spraying safe biopesticides or neem seed extract early in the morning or late evening controls the pest.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo neem dumɔwu mli nu lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye kooloi lɛ anɔ.

english: How does covering the bare soil around my crops with dry grass help my field?
ga: Mulching bare soil around Te miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛ jwɛi tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi akutso lɛ mli tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the soil from hot sun, stops water from evaporating too quickly, keeps weeds down, and rots into natural plant food over time.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ, ehaaa jwɛi akabote mli, ni ehaa tsei aniyenii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: This is black pod disease, which is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet conditions and heavy shade. Pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and air to reach the pods, which dries them out and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela, ni ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ aniji lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaaa ŋmei lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow and wilting even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your crops are suffering from a sickness like swollen shoot disease or a lack of proper plant food in the soil. Checking the stems for swollen spots or feeding the soil with fertilizer can help fix the problem before the plant dies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela ko tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu loo tsei niyenii ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miipiŋ oŋmɔshi nii lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ tso lɛ yitso lɛ mli koni ona hei ni efuu loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni asaa naagba lɛ dani tso lɛ agbo.

english: My cocoa trees are very old and do not produce as many pods as before, do I have to clear the whole land to fix this?
ga: Mi-cocoa tso lɛ egbɔ waa ni ewooo ŋmeii babaoo tamɔ tsutsu lɛ. Ani esa akɛ majie jɛmɛ fɛɛ koni manyɛ masaa?

english: You do not need to clear everything at once. You can practice farm rehabilitation by cutting down the oldest, weakest trees in small sections and planting new seedlings under the remaining shade so you still get harvests while the new trees grow.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni ofɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ he shikome. Obaanyɛ okase bɔ ni ooofee oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ tsei ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ ni ooofo mli bibii bibii lɛ nɔ. Ni odu dumɔwui heei yɛ hulutsoo ni eshwɛ lɛ shishi koni oya nɔ oná ŋmaa be mli ni tsei heei lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do my healthy-looking tree crops stop bearing fruit after many years of heavy harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ekpa yibiiwoo yɛ afii babaoo ni mikɛkpa nii babaoo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: As trees age, their roots find it harder to pull nutrients from deep in the dirt, and mature branches become too thick to feed new fruits properly. Trimming old branches and feeding the soil gives the tree new energy to bloom again.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ eda lɛ Ewaa kɛhaa amɛshishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛbaagbala niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Ni tsei niji ni eda lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii heei jogbaŋŋ. Niji momoi ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ hee ni ekɛbaafɔ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it good to plant cassava or plantains together with my young tree crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mikɛ midumɔwui lɛ baadu ŋmei loo plantains lɛ?

english: Young cash crops like cocoa burn easily under strong heat. Planting fast-growing food crops like plantain beside them creates shade to protect the young plants, while giving you food to harvest while you wait for the main crop to mature.
ga: Shika ŋmɔshi nibii bibii tamɔ kookoo shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa shishi. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ lateral plantains ni aduɔ lɛ Baaha hulutsoo aba koni ebu tsei bibii ahe. Kɛfata he lɛ, ebaaha bo niyenii ni obaakpa yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ tsei titrii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my seeds very close together to fit more on my farm?
ga: Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ miŋmɔ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: No, planting too close makes your crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants with small fruits. Giving crops proper space allows each plant to grow big and bear a full yield.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ odu ohe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii baa. He ni sa ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ ni akɛaaha lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni edara ni ewoɔ ŋmaa ni fa babaoo.

english: Why does my land produce less food every year even though I plant the exact same crop every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii faaa daa afi lɛ? Ni miduɔ tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi?

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the exact same nutrients from the dirt without giving the soil time to recover. Rotating your main crop with legumes like groundnuts or beans puts essential nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake oŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I keep my crops from drying out and dying when the rains stop unexpectedly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi beni nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ trukaa lɛ?

english: Covering the ground around your crop roots with dry grass, leaves, or crop waste keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating quickly, helping your crops survive short dry spells.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ ni oooha Otsei lɛ ahe jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo mli.

english: How can I stop weeds from taking over my large farm when I do not have enough laborers to clear them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi jwɛi ni yeɔ miŋmɔ agbo lɛ nɔ lɛ naa? Akɛni mibɛ nitsulɔi ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baajie jwɛi lɛ hewɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cover crops like mucuna or cowpeas over empty farm land covers the ground tightly, blocking light so weeds cannot grow while also improving the health of your soil.
ga: Nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shading tsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to cut off healthy green branches from our tree crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔfolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ kɛjɛ wɔ tsei ni damɔ shi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Cutting off unnecessary branches, called pruning, forces the plant to send its food and strength directly into growing bigger fruits rather than wasting energy on feeding extra leaves.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni ajieɔ Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsei ni afoɔ. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ gbɛ koni ewo aduawai wuji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ ni okɛyeɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and dry during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct sunlight and intense heat. Without shade trees or plantains to shield them, the leaves lose moisture faster than the roots can take it up from the soil, causing the foliage to scorch and dry out.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni baaha nɔ ko bɛ lɛ Baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat the middle leaves of my maize plants and leave ragged holes?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni amɛshiɔ buji ni etsilɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm. The moths lay eggs on the leaves, and once hatched, the caterpillars crawl inside the central shoot (whorl) to feed on the tender young leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ (whorl) koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ dani amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my tomato plants turning yellow and dropping off one by one?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi komekomei lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by soil-borne fungal diseases like early blight. When rain drops or irrigation water splash wet soil onto the lower leaves, fungal spores attach to the plant and cause the leaves to rot, turn yellow, and fall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ mra be mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ nugbɔ loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Fungal spores lɛ kpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ he ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ. Etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbee shi

english: Which part of a cassava stem should I choose when cutting sticks for planting?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei tso lɛ fã esa akɛ ohala beni ofoɔ tsei niji koni okɛdu lɛ?

english: You should use mature, healthy cuttings taken from the middle section of the stem. The soft green top parts dry out too quickly, while the very bottom section near the roots is overly woody and slow to sprout.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tso nine ni mli wa ni eda ni ajie kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ atsu nii. Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni ji eŋɔli ni mli tse lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya tsɔ. yɛ be mli ni shishigbɛ naagbee ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ ji tso tsɔ ni ehiɛɛɛ mlɛo.

english: Why do I need to plant my pepper seeds in a nursery before transferring them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu pepper dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛya shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds are very small and fragile. A nursery bed allows you to easily shade, water, and protect the young seedlings from pests and torrential rain until they develop strong roots and stems.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ daraaa kwraa ni amɛhe waaa. Nursery saatsoi lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ hulutsoo, nu, ni obuɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ahe mlɛo kɛyashiɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni wa baa.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall with bushy green leaves but fail to produce large fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ waa kɛ baai eŋɔlii akui shi ewooo yibii wuji lɛ?

english: This usually means the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough phosphorus or potassium. High nitrogen encourages lush foliage growth, but crops need balanced nutrients to trigger flowering and fruit development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo ni ebɛ fɔsfɔs loo potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ adalɛ yaa hiɛ. Shi niyenii ni ja he miihia tsei koni ekanya fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my crops so quickly even when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa oya kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli po lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from your crops. When weeds are present, they consume the nutrients first, leaving your main crop starved.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji jwɛi yɛ lɛ Amɛbaaye niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii titrii lɛ.

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves off the ground toward sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves dry and well-lit, which boosts energy production for tuber growth and prevents soil-borne diseases.
ga: Atomɔ tso ji wain tso ni esa akɛ ewó ebaa nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ. Staking baaha tsei ahe tsei ni egbi kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni anáa kɛha tuber lɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it dangerous for me to sow my maize immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛha mi akɛ madu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a short dry spell. If seeds germinate after the initial rainfall, the delicate seedlings will dry up and die when the rains temporarily stop.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa be kukuoo ko.

english: Why should I remove the extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain stand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain shishitoo lɛ jie

english: Extra shoots, known as suckers, draw nutrients, water, and energy away from the main fruiting stem. Pruning away excess suckers leaves enough energy for the main plant to yield a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tsobii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ, gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ aduawai lɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafo lɛ haa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tsei wuji ni tsii yɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does rice need so much water to grow properly in my field compared to other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Rice thrives in flooded conditions because water helps control unwanted weeds and keeps the soil at a steady temperature, allowing the plant roots to constantly absorb nutrients needed to produce heavy grain heads.
ga: Omɔ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni nu afua yɔɔ mli lɛ amli ejaakɛ nu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛɔ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ anɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛná dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii.

english: Why is planting rice in straight, spaced rows better than just scattering the seeds randomly across my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja, ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hi fe dumɔwui ni aduɔ trukaa lɛ? yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Planting in straight rows ensures that every single plant gets enough sunlight, air, and soil nutrients without fighting its neighbors, while also making it much easier for you to weed and apply fertilizer.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ awuu. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: How can I tell the exact time my rice crop is ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ esa akɛ akpa?

english: Rice is ready to harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grain heads turn from green to a golden-yellow color, and the individual grains feel hard and firm when you bite them.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni ŋmãa yitsei lɛ amli aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ mli lɛ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko baanu he akɛ ewa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ okɛ ohe wo mli.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall with lush green leaves but produce very little actual grain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa kɛ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi dumɔwui diɛŋtsɛ fioo pɛ amɛwoɔ lɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they put all their energy into growing tall leaves and stems instead of forming flowers and grains. Balancing nitrogen with phosphorus and potassium helps the plant produce more food and grain.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni miida kɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, a peeɔ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwuhi. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium to he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young rice plants turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient that plants need to create green energy and grow strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye oŋmɔshi nibii ni ji nitrogen lɛ. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná hewalɛ ni haa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do weeds harm my young crops so much more during the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ midumɔwui lɛ awui babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛduɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crops are small and weak, so aggressive weeds can easily steal the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before your crop's root system has a chance to establish itself.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni mli wa lɛ baanyɛ aju hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do stem borer insects target the inside of my grain crop stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ stem borers lɛ miikwɛ mi dumɔwui tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Stem borers burrow into crop stems because the inner core is soft, moist, and full of nutrients. Once inside, they block the plant's natural flow of water and food, causing the central leaves to dry up and die.
ga: Stem borers lɛ shwieɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli ejaakɛ mligbɛ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ́ ebote mli lɛ, etsĩɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni tso lɛ jɛɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: What happens to my rice plants when there is no rain for two weeks straight?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛko otsii enyɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: When water is scarce, rice plants roll up their leaves to reduce water loss through evaporation. While this saves their life, it slows down growth because the roots cannot take up food from dry soil.
ga: Kɛ nu faaa Omɔ tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Kɛji enɛ here amɛwala po. Shi ehaa dalɛ hu baa shi ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why don't all the seeds I saved from my last harvest sprout when I plant them in the new season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui fɛɛ ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ kwɛɛɛ beni miduɔ amɛ kɛhaa be hee lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their strength over time if they are stored in hot or damp places. Additionally, seeds saved from hybrid varieties do not grow as strong or uniformly as fresh, certified seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baafite hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli kɛji akɛ akɛto hei ni mli edɔ loo hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Kɛfata he lɛ, dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ edaŋ waa loo amɛbaafee ekome tamɔ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested rice spoil or turn moldy so quickly inside the storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya loo efoɔ yɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice spoils in storage when it is bagged while still holding too much moisture. Drying the harvested grain thoroughly under the sun until it is hard and dry prevents mold and insects from destroying your store.
ga: Omɔ fiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ awo kotoku mli shi eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo lolo. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu shishi kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi akafite oshwapo lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I clear all the big trees away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight scorches their tender leaves and dries out the topsoil. Leaving a few large trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa provides shade and preserves soil moisture until the cocoa plants grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ oshi tsei fioo komɛi ni edara loo odu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo lɛ masɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing tall and thin with very small cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Planting maize with proper distance allows each stem to get enough food and light to develop thick stalks and large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛkwɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You can tell it is mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack open due to the swelling tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ edara kɛji baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ ŋmei ni efuu ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my pepper plants turning yellow even though I give them enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves are often a signal that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient plants need to stay green and grow leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or compost around the plant feeds the soil and turns the leaves green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛŋɔli lɛ mli ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Kooloo ŋmei loo ŋmei ni egbo ni akɛwo Tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ni eha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When they grow beside maize, they naturally feed the soil with this nutrient, helping the maize grow better without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa Amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni edaa jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ ŋmãa ni jara wa tsuuu nii.

english: Why are small holes appearing in my cabbage leaves, and how can I control the insects without buying costly chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kaabaji baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Te mafee tɛŋŋ makudɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa?

english: Insects like caterpillars chew on leafy crops to feed themselves. You can protect your crops naturally by crushing leaves from the neem tree, soaking them in water overnight, and spraying the solution onto the crop leaves to repel pests safely.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii ŋmɔɔ tsei ahe baai kɛtaoɔ niyenii. Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ neem tso lɛ baai ni oootsi lɛ nɔ. Okɛwo nu mli nyɔɔŋ kome. ni okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ tsei ahe baai anɔ koni ekɛshwie tsɛŋemɔ helai shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get dark spots and rot whenever heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ diji ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain splashes mud containing hidden fungal spores onto lower leaves, causing rot. Trimming the lower leaves near the ground and covering the soil beneath the plants with dry grass mulch stops raindrops from splashing infected soil onto the leaves.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa muji ni ŋmeii tsɛŋemɔ helai yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shishigbɛ baai lɛ anɔ, ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ. Kɛ́ afo baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaatsi nugbɔshiimɔi anaa koni ekashwie shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do I need to heap up large soil mounds before planting my yam setts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee shikpɔŋ agbo ko dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow deep underground and need soft, loose soil to expand fully. Building high earth mounds keeps the soil loose for easy tuber growth and helps excess rainwater drain away so the yams do not rot in soaked soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli edɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kwraa. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni bulbs lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ mlɛo. ni ehaa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa Enɛ ji koni sweet potato lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my food crops, and why must I remove them while my crops are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe mi niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie amɛ kɛjɛ mihe be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that quickly steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Removing weeds early gives young crops uninterrupted access to plant food so they can establish strong root systems.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛju nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ naa tsei niyenii be fɛɛ be. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ afee shishifã gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli wa.

english: How do I decide the exact time to sow my seeds during the early rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ adũ dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ he?

english: It is best to sow seeds after two or three continuous, heavy rains when the ground is thoroughly moist. Sowing into dry soil after just one light shower can cause the seeds to sprout and then die if rain stops for a few days.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko pɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo komɛi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to survive because direct sunlight dries out their delicate leaves and soil too fast. Keeping or planting shade trees protects them until they are strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo be fioo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya tsɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo adumɔ baaye abua ni abu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a major food crops need to stay green and grow well. Applying the right fertilizer early in the season supplies this nutrient and restores healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii titri ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaha niyenii nɛɛ aba ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I put fertilizer on my crops when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so the roots can absorb it. Putting chemical fertilizer in dry soil can scorch or burn the crop's roots and waste your money.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite shika.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas in my field help my soil for the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that catch nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When they die, that nitrogen stays in the soil and feeds the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ amɛgboi Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because the roots cannot breathe in waterlogged soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu kɛbote shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do I need to clear the ground and erect tall sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie he ko ni mikɛ tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight to make energy. When the leaves get enough sun, they send food down into the soil to grow large, healthy yam tubers.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa Etsuɔ niyenii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why are there holes in the middle leaves of my young maize with small brown dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ yɛ bu yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ kɛ muji bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ emli lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar feeding on the soft inner leaves of the maize. Finding and spraying them early in the leaf funnel prevents them from destroying the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli baai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ otao tso lɛ baai lɛ amli mra ni okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naagbeehei lɛ afitemɔ naa.

english: Leaf curl is often brought by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread plant sicknesses, or by extreme heat. Controlling insect pests early keeps the plants healthy enough to bear good fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ tsei ahe helai eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo nɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa Mra Be mli nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: If too many shoots grow from the same spot, they steal water and plant food from each other, resulting in small bunches. Leaving only one main plant and one or two suckers ensures large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ kɛjɛ he kome lɛ Amɛbaaju nu ni amɛdu niyenii kɛjɛ amɛhe. ni kɛ tso bibioo ko baa Kɛ́ ashi tso titri kome kɛ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha plantain lɛ afee agbo ni etsii.

english: Why do I need to start my pepper seeds in a nursery bed before planting them on the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu pepper dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds are very small and fragile, making them easy targets for heavy rains, heat, and bugs. A nursery bed lets you give them special protection until they grow strong enough to survive in the open field.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, latsaa, kɛ kooloi bibii nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe oya. Nursery saatsoi lɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ amɛhe babaoo kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: I keep seeing tiny red insects crawling all over my farm soil. Are they harmful to my crops?
ga: Mina kooloo tsuru bibioo ko. Amɛmiikpã muji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ nɔ Ani amɛyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Some small red soil pests, like red spider mites or certain types of ants, can suck sap from roots and leaves or damage young roots, causing crops to wither. Identifying the exact pest helps extension officers recommend the right organic or chemical treatment to protect your soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii komɛi ni ji red spider mites loo ŋmeii komɛi fata he. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ nu ni jɛ shishifãi kɛ baai amli lɛ atsu nii. loo shishifãi bibii ni efiteɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbi. Kɛ́ oyɔse tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ pɔtɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ bɔ ni esa akɛ afee nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni sa ni akɛbu oshikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: What causes holes in the leaves of my crops, and how can I stop insects from eating them?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bulɛ baa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi ni yeɔ lɛ anaa?

english: Leaf holes are usually caused by chewing pests like caterpillars or beetles. You can control them by clearing surrounding weeds where pests hide, handpicking visible insects, or spraying natural Neem tree seed extract on the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli buji baa. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni ooojie kɛjɛ mli lɛ nɔ. He ni kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ Halamɔ kooloi bibii ni anaa lɛ kɛ onine. Aloo okɛ adebɔɔ mli neem dumɔwui ni ajieɔ lɛ afɔ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I properly prepare my land before planting so my crops grow strong without dying early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani madu nii koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkagboi oya?

english: Proper land preparation involves clearing weeds, loosening compacted soil so roots can breathe and penetrate deep, and removing pest-harboring debris. This gives young plants the best start and reduces farm maintenance later.
ga: Nɔ ni fata shikpɔŋ he saamɔ kpakpa he ji jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. Gbalamɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛbote mli jogbaŋŋ. ni ojie jwɛi ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmɔ mli saamɔ baa shi yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my land is fully ready for me to start sowing seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ eshɛ dumɔwui adumɔ he?

english: Your field is ready when the soil has been loosened to a soft texture, major weeds and stumps are removed, rows or mounds are formed for proper drainage, and the soil has enough moisture from the early rains.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ajieɔ jwɛi wuji kɛ tsei akutsei lɛ. Afeɔ ŋmeii loo gɔji koni nu lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ mli nu ni fa bɔ ni sa

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has enough nutrients to grow a good crop of maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha aná ŋmãa kpakpa?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark, crumbles easily in your hand, and holds moisture well. If your crops grow pale yellow or remain stunted, the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen, which can be fixed by adding compost or manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli tseɔ, efiteɔ oya yɛ nine mli, ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji otso lɛ mli tse loo egbɔjɔ lolo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ nitrogen, ni abaanyɛ asaa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall with lots of green leaves, but fail to produce good fruits or seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi enyɛŋ ewo yibii loo dumɔwui kpakpai.

english: This usually happens when there is too much nitrogen in the soil but not enough phosphorus or potassium. Nitrogen encourages stem and leaf growth, while phosphorus and potassium are needed for strong roots, flowers, and fruit production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi fɔsfɔs loo potasium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ daraa. Yɛ be mli ni phosphorus kɛ potassium he hiaa kɛha shishifãi, fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai ni mli wa lɛ afeemɔ.

english: How do I protect my young seedlings from dying under intense heat right after planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu midumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛkagboi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ shishi beni midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Young plants need protection from direct sunlight. You can create temporary shade using palm fronds or plant fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby to provide shelter and keep the soil moist.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Obaanyɛ ofee hulutsoo be kukuoo mli kɛtsɔ ŋmei tsei loo hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni ooodu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ nɔ. Koni ekɛ wɔɔhe aha ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my crop roots stay short and weak instead of growing deep into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ kuku ni amɛhe waaa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Roots cannot grow deep if the soil underneath is too hard and compacted. Tilling or breaking up hard soil layers during land preparation allows roots to go deep in search of water and nutrients.
ga: Shishifãi nyɛŋ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo akuɔ mli yɛ be mli ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ boteɔ mli jogbaŋŋ koni amɛyatao nu kɛ niyenii.

english: Why is clearing weeds early so important for the survival of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ani ehe hiaa koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for light, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the available food and moisture they need to establish strong stems and leaves.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni wa.

english: Why do my crops dry up quickly during short dry spells even when planted during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be kuku lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli po.

english: Soil that lacks organic matter loses water quickly through evaporation. Adding dried leaves, compost, or mulch around the base of your crops helps trap moisture in the ground during dry days.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya yɛ la ni hoɔ lɛ hewɔ. Baai ni egbi, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛbaabɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or the field is waterlogged. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo jɛmɛ edɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same spot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same soil drains the same specific nutrients every year and lets maize-specific pests and diseases multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaná niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi. ni ehaa kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ ayi fa babaoo. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ehaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa.

english: What causes my yam tubers to grow small and bent instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni haa mi sweet potato tubers lɛ feɔ bibii ni ebɔleɔ shi moŋ ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Hard, rocky, or compacted soil prevents yam tubers from expanding downward. Making high, soft mounds or ridges filled with loose, fertile topsoil gives the tubers space to grow large and straight.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo ni mli edɔ lɛ baatsi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã kɛya shi. Kɛ́ afee gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baa nii eyi mli obɔ lɛ, ebaaha bulb lɛ aná he ko ni da ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in excess shade and wet conditions. Pruning heavy cocoa branches to let sunlight in and removing infected pods quickly prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be babaoo mli kɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kookoo tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi waa koni hulu la babaoo aba mli, ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up and turning wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking sap from under the leaves. Spraying early with neem extract or an recommended insecticide controls these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Akɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra. Abaanyɛ akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ.

english: Tomatoes shed flowers when they suffer from high heat, lack of water, or low nutrients like phosphorus. Consistent watering during dry spells and applying balanced fertilizer helps flowers stay on to set fruit.
ga: Tomatoi fɔ̃ɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni faaa lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli daa yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ aya nɔ akwɛ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do weeds keep sprouting back so quickly right after I clear my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ekoŋŋ oya nɛkɛ beni mijie miŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie buried in the soil for a long time and germinate as soon as clearing exposes them to direct sunlight and rain. Covering bare soil with organic mulch or planting cover crops blocks light and suppresses weed growth.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulu la kɛ nugbɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni akɛ jwɛi ni wala yɔɔ mli loo mulch tsei ni aduɔ lɛ baaha jwɛi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cassava field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei?

english: Cassava is typically mature between 9 and 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping, and the soil around the stem base begins to crack as roots swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Should I plant my maize seed right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting after the first rain is risky because the weather can dry up again for weeks, killing fresh seeds. It is safer to wait until rains become steady and soil moisture stays continuous.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ shihilɛi lɛ baagbi ekoŋŋ otsii babaoo. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui heei lɛ agboi. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ anɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baafee shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to produce a bunch after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ ŋmeii beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers require deep moisture, abundant organic matter, and shade protection when young. If planted in poor soil or left without shade during dry periods, their growth slows down drastically.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ hia ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. ni ebu hulutsoo lɛ he beni eji gbekɛ Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ loo ashi lɛ ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ, Edalɛ baa shi waa.

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow starting from the tip, the plant is hungry for nitrogen fertilizer. Maize needs this plant food to stay green and build big cobs, especially after heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the ground.
ga: Beni ŋmãa lɛ shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmãa. Abɛi he miihia tsei niyenii koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ewo ŋmeii wuji. Titri lɛ, beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Beans and cowpeas have natural helpers in their roots that take plant food straight from the air and trap it in the soil. When the leaves and roots decay, they leave behind free nitrogen fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas yɛ adebɔɔ mli yelikɛbuamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Eheɔ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fite Ebaashi nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: If I add a lot of extra fertilizer to my crops, will it make them produce twice as much food?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ Ani ebaaha tsei lɛ awo niyenii ni fa fe shii enyɔ?

english: Adding too much chemical fertilizer can burn plant roots and cause the crop to grow plenty of tall green leaves without forming fruits or seeds. Balance is important so the plant flowers properly instead of wasting energy.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni eha tsei lɛ ashi baai kakadaŋŋ agboi babaoo ni amɛwoɔ yibii loo dumɔwui. Balance is important No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ baafɔ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hewalɛ ni eeefite lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like straws during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize rolls its leaves to protect itself from losing water in the dry heat. Shrinking its leaf size acts like closing a window to hold moisture inside until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Okɛ ŋmãa baai abɔ he koni nu akafite yɛ la ni mli egbi lɛ mli. Baai lɛ agbɔjɔmɔ ni abaaba shi lɛ tamɔ samflɛ ni aŋaa koni ŋmɔtɔ awo mli kɛyashi gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: What makes my cassava roots rot under the ground when the rains become too heavy?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rainwater sits on the field for too long, it drowns the roots, allowing damp rot to set in, which is why planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water run off.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Ha nu lɛ agbo ni efu. Enɛ hewɔ ni dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees dropping all their flowers instead of forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miishwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakumɔ amɛfee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they get too hot, lack shade, or do not get enough water. Planting shade trees nearby keeps the soil moist and protects the flowers so they can turn into young pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji edɔ tsɔ, amɛbɛ hɔnɔ, loo amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ bibii.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and rotten while still hanging on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efite lɛ? Ani ekã tso lɛ nɔ lolo?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when the plant cannot pull up enough calcium from the dirt. Irregular watering stops calcium from moving through the plant, causing the bottom of the tomato to turn dark.
