ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ haaa calcium lɛ atsɔ tso lɛ mli. Ehaa tomato lɛ shishi feɔ duŋ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start growing shoots in the storage barn even when I have not planted them in soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ miduko amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Yam tubers are living seed bodies that naturally wake up after a period of rest. Warm air and moisture signal to the yam that it is time to grow a new vine, even if it is resting on a barn rack.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji dumɔwui ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛjɔɔ amɛhe be ko sɛɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo tsɔɔ sweet potato akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ adu wain tsei heei. Kɛji akɛ ehiɛ tsɔne ko nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli po.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tightly and twisting into little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ekpɛtɛ shi shiŋŋ ni etsɔ kɔɔpoi bibii amli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the undersides of the leaves. Controlling these tiny pests early keeps the leaves flat so the plant can catch sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la.

english: Why are my new plantain suckers taking so long to show leaves after I put them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tsoji heei lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛjieɔ baai kpo yɛ be mli ni mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers must spend their first few weeks building strong roots deep in the soil before sending up big green leaves. If the ground is dry or hard, leaf growth will remain slow until the roots establish.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ he miihia klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani amɛtsu baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ Baai lɛ daaa blɛoo kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ baa.

english: How can I get my cocoa trees to produce pods continuously throughout the year?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ oha kookoo tso lɛ awo ŋmeii be fɛɛ be afi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: While cocoa has main and minor harvest seasons, good farm practices like regular pruning, weed control, and maintaining proper shade allow healthy trees to bear pods throughout most of the year.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ kookoo yɛ shishijee kɛ sɛɛ mli ŋmaakpamɔ be moŋ, shi ŋmɔ mli nifeemɔi kpakpai tamɔ jwɛi ni afoɔ daa Kɛ hulutsoo ni sa ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why is cocoa often described as a mother to farmers in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ abuɔ kookoo akɛ eji okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ anyɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa is seen as a mother because once established, it provides reliable income year after year, helping farmers take care of family needs, school fees, and household expenses.
ga: Anaa kookoo akɛ nyɛ ejaakɛ kɛ́ ato shishi pɛ lɛ, ehaa anáa shika ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Eyeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛkwɛɔ amɛweku lɛ hiamɔ nii, skul nyɔmɔwoo, kɛ shia shika.

english: Why are the young flowers on my cocoa trees falling off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi dani amɛfee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flower drop happens when trees experience heat stress, lack nutrients, or get attacked by insects. Providing adequate shade, organic mulch, and pest control helps flowers set into healthy pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii tutua amɛ. Ni akɛ hulutsoo ni sa haa Organic mulch Kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why does the ground under a mature cocoa tree canopy stay cool like a cold room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ shishi lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ fɛ̃i tamɔ tsu ko ni mli ejɔ lɛ?

english: The broad leaves of mature cocoa trees block direct sunlight and slow down hot winds, which traps moisture in the soil and creates a cool protective environment for the roots.
ga: Kakao tsei ni eda lɛ ahe baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my cocoa trees look weak and stressed during dry hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛhaoɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Strong sun and dry harmattan winds cause cocoa leaves to lose water faster than the roots can take it up. Planting permanent shade trees helps shield your cocoa from intense heat.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa kɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ haa kookoo baa lɛ mli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni ebu o-cocoa lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he.

english: How do shade trees help protect my soil during long dry spells?
ga: Te tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu mishikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Shade trees drop leaves that form a protective layer over the ground, keeping the soil damp, reducing heat, and preventing moisture from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ jieɔ baai ni feɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ehaa dɔlɛ baa shi, ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya tsɔ.

english: Why is cocoa farming so important for the nation of Ghana as a whole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hia Ghana fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Ghana earns a large amount of foreign income by exporting premium cocoa, which the government uses to fund public services, national development, and farming support programs.
ga: Ghana naa maŋsɛɛ shika babaoo kɛjɛɔ kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ. ni nɔyeli lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii akɛ shika kɛha maŋ nitsumɔi maŋ hiɛyaa kɛ okwaayeli yelikɛbuamɔ nitsumɔi

english: Why do I need to invest money in pest spraying if my cocoa trees look green and fine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ shika awo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛhe yɔɔ fɛo?

english: Preventative spraying protects developing pods from hidden pests and fungi before damage occurs, ensuring that your heavy investment yields maximum pod output.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ buɔ ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ ahe dani efiteɔ. Enɛ haa onáa nɔmimaa akɛ oshika ni tsii ni okɛwo mli lɛ baaha pod yibii babaoo aba.

english: What causes cocoa pods to turn dark and rot directly on the branches?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ?

english: This is usually Black Pod disease, caused by excess humidity and fungi. Pruning extra leaves to allow air movement and harvesting ripe pods promptly prevents the infection from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ black pod hela baa. Baai ni afolɔ afata he koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli kɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ akpamɔ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How do I ensure that my cocoa farm continues to yield good harvests when the trees grow old?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ aya nɔ awo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Regularly pruning dead branches, managing shade levels, replenishing soil nutrients with organic compost, and replacing unproductive old trees will keep your farm yielding well for decades.
ga: Niji ni egboi lɛ ashishitsɔɔmɔ daa shade level management Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni akɛ organic compost baafata shikpɔŋ lɛ he Ni akɛ tsei momo ni wooo yibii lɛ baatsake lɛ baaha oŋmɔ lɛ awo yibii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to build green leaves and produce good ears, so adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or NPK early in the season will help restore their color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli kɛ toi kpakpai aba. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds closer together, will I get a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together actually reduces your yield. The crops end up competing against each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stems and very small ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ́ odu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aba shi. Esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atswa akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii waa baa.

english: Why does growing groundnuts or cowpeas in my field make my soil better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, this extra nitrogen stays in the earth, acting as natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni okpaa amɛ Nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves burn easily and dry out. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby creates a canopy that shields the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya ni amɛgbiɔ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la fɛɛ.

english: Should I cut off the extra shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle ehe lɛ fɛɛ? Ani ajie plantain tsei titrii lɛ?

english: Yes, you should prune extra shoots. If you leave too many shoots growing around the mother plant, they will steal nutrients and water, resulting in smaller bunches of plantains. It is best to keep only three shoots: the main fruiting mother, one medium shoot, and one small sprout.
ga: Yes, you should prune additional shoots. If you leave shoots around Too much mother plant It will steal nutrients and water. Enɛ haa plantains bibii shwieɔ shi. It is best to keep only three shoots: the main mother shoot, one middle shoot, and one small shoot.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight for photosynthesis, which feeds the growing tuber below. Staking also keeps the leaves dry and away from soil-borne diseases that cause rots.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo kɛha fotosintɛsis. ni baaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ agbiɔ ni ekɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ akashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot underground if I leave them in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When heavy rain saturates the soil with excess water, air cannot reach the roots. Standing water causes fungal rots to attack the tubers underground, so harvesting before peak waterlogging occurs prevents crop loss.
ga: When heavy rain falls, the soil is soaked with excess water. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa dani nu lɛ shɛɔ he ni eshɛɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akafiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without making any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers mainly due to extreme heat stress, poor watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When the plant gets too hot or stressed, it sheds its blossoms to save energy instead of forming fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ dɔlɛ hewɔ. nu ni ehiii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Kɛji tsei lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo amɛmiifee basaa Ebaafɔlɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: What is causing tiny caterpillars to eat the middle funnel leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Ye mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ.

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworms, a pest that hides inside the central growing tip of maize plants to feed on soft tender leaves. Catching them early and applying appropriate controls prevents them from destroying the growing shoot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa ni miida yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli koni amɛye baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ji bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids that feed on plant sap and spread viruses. Spraying the plants early to control these pests keeps the leaves flat and allows fruit to develop properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsoi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Bɔni afee ni akudɔ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ, ha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni oye obua aduawai lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and burning up in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight because their root systems are still small and weak. They need temporary shade plants like plantains planted beside them to block the sun and keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ daraaa lolo ni amɛhe waaa. Tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni abu he kɛjɛ hulu la he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the middle of the day even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ yɛ gbi mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During the hottest part of the afternoon, pepper leaves lose water through evaporation faster than the roots can take it up from the soil. The leaves wilt temporarily to protect the plant from losing more moisture, and they will usually bounce back as the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane be ni mli edɔɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni tso lɛ akafite ŋmɔtɔ. ni bei pii lɛ, efoɔ ehe kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Yellow lower leaves are a clear sign that your maize lacks nitrogen nutrient in the soil. The plant naturally starves its older lower leaves to send what little nitrogen it has to the new growing leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ niyenii ni ji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, tsei yeɔ hɔmɔ yɛ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe koni amɛkɛ nitrogen fioo pɛ amaje baai heei ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: What will happen if I put fertilizer on my farm when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so that plant roots can draw it in safely. Applying concentrated fertilizer to dry soil can scorch and burn the plant roots, which can damage or kill your crops.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ awo mli shweshweeshwe.Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nii ni mli wa tsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni esha amɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite loo efite onibii.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans on my land make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans have tiny beneficial organisms on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, acts as a natural fertilizer for crops like maize planted afterwards.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha sɛɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why should I cut away some of the young shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mitso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: If too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they steal food, water, and light from the main plant. Removing extra shoots allows all the plant's energy to go into producing one large, heavy bunch of plantain.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe Plantain kome Ejuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafo lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni akɛfee ŋmeii agboi ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds off my farm early before my crops get tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli mra lɛ? Before the crops are high?

english: Weeds grow very fast and aggressively steal nutrients, water, and sunlight from young crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the soil food they need to establish strong stems and leaves.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni wa.

english: Tomato plants shed their blossoms when heat becomes too extreme or when they do not get steady water. High stress prevents successful pollination, causing the plant to drop flowers to save its own energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛnáaa nu ni yaa nɔ daa. Haomɔ ni mli wa baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollination naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ afɔ̃ fɔfɔi koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready to be dug up from under the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ esa akɛ ajie ŋmei shishifãi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically ready to harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, leaving a mostly bare stem, and the soil around the base of the stem starts cracking from the expanding tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Enɛ ha tsɔne lɛ mli fã ko nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ bulb ni miigbɛ eshwa yɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunshine to make food that grows the big underground tuber. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground, preventing leaf rot and allowing the leaves to trap maximum sunlight.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji amli. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni oha baai lɛ amɔmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. They require temporary shade crops, like plantains or bananas, planted alongside them to filter the sunlight until their canopy matures.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo banana, ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni ekɛ hulu la lɛ atsu nii kɛyashi ŋwɛitsu lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes next to my growing yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama emasɛi lɛ? Amɛduɔ sweet potato wain tsei

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs to lift its leaves off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible. Staking helps the leaves make more food, which leads to larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii babaoo. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellowing starting at the tip and moving down the center leaf vein usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main nutrient maize needs to build green leaves and grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anaagbɛ ni etsɔɔ baa lɛ fãji lɛ ateŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ baai eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why should I avoid spreading dry fertilizer on my field when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Crops cannot absorb dry fertilizer directly through their roots. The soil needs water or rain to dissolve the fertilizer into a liquid form that roots can drink.
ga: Tsei nyɛŋ atsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Nu loo nugbɔ he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ koni etsɔ nu ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu.

english: Why should I cut off the extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Leaving too many small shoots, or suckers, causes them to steal water and food from the main mother tree. Cutting them back leaves only one or two strong stems, which produces larger plantain bunches.
ga: Ajieɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ babaoo fe nine lɛ baaha amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo sɛɛ lɛ, tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baashi, ni no baaha plantain lɛ agbo.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant the seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crowded plants end up fighting each other for light, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin plants with small fruits or ears.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei komɛi woɔ yibii bibii loo toi.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their yellow blossoms before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when the plant experiences stress, usually caused by extremely hot weather, irregular watering, or a lack of calcium and other key nutrients in the soil.
ga: Tomatoes bloom when plants are stressed. Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo calcium kɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why do groundnut stems bend down and push themselves into the dirt after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are unique because their flowers are pollinated above ground, but the actual nuts grow underground. The stem naturally bends downward to push the growing seed pod into the soil to mature safely.
ga: Peanuts yɛ srɔto kwraa ejaakɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ, shi ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi diɛŋtsɛ. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shi koni amɛkɛtsi dumɔwui ni miida lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdara shweshweeshwe.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young corn leaves and powdery dust inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ lɛ ŋmãa baai amli ni sũ yɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: This damage is typically caused by the fall armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central stem of young maize plants and eats the tender inner leaves, leaving behind dark waste that looks like sawdust.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni ji cutworm caterpillars, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli ni amɛyeɔ mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Eshiɔ jwɛi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are mature and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakumɔ?

english: Cassava is generally ready for harvest when the stem turns thick and woody and the lower leaves start to turn yellow and drop off, usually between 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni eshishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ tsei. ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted compost helps the leaves turn green so they can feed the plant and make big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli koni ekɛha tso lɛ niyenii ni efee ŋmeii wuji.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans help my soil produce better maize next season?
ga: Te ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ewo ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants decay, they release this natural plant food into the soil, making it richer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei fite Amɛjieɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii nɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ nii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings get scorched easily under direct sun. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that shade the young cocoa plants and keep the surrounding soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui shãa oya kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and dry up on the trees?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Blackened pods are usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, shaded conditions. Pruning excess leaves to let sunlight and air circulate through the tree helps prevent it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ enaa.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up tightly and show yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curled, spotted leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties is the most effective way to protect your harvest.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ onibii ahe.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their flowers without growing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shi ni ekwɛɛɛ pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when exposed to extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the roots helps the flowers stay on the plant and form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ebɔle he lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why does putting dry grass around the base of my crops help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, prevents soil water from evaporating under the hot sun, stops weeds from growing, and keeps the plant roots cool.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaatsi nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ la yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Why are my tomato fruits rotting at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ egbo yɛ shishigbɛ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Bottom rot in tomatoes happens when plants cannot absorb enough calcium, usually caused by irregular watering. Giving tomatoes a steady supply of water prevents the fruit bottoms from turning black.
ga: Tomato shishigbɛ fitemɔ baa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaatsi tso yibii lɛ ashishi lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ediŋŋ.

english: Why are my yams rotting inside the soil before I even dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikɛ amɛ po shwie shi lɛ?

english: Yam rot underground happens when water collects around the tubers without draining. Building high soil mounds and ensuring good drainage prevents water from sitting around the tubers.
ga: Sweet potato shikpɔŋ shishi fitemɔ baa kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe ni nu bɛ mli. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee kɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baatsi nu naa koni ekabɔle bulb lɛ he.

english: When is the right time for me to apply fertilizer to my maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-abele lɛ mli?

english: The best practice is to apply the first dose of fertilizer about two weeks after seeds germinate, and a second dose when the maize reaches knee height so the plants get nutrients during rapid growth.
ga: Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo mli aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. kɛ shi ni ji enyɔ lɛ beni ŋmãa lɛ shɛɔ tsitsi nɔ lɛ. koni tsei lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa oya lɛ

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or the plants are getting too much standing water. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer like NPK can supply the missing food and restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo tso lɛ miiná nu ni damɔ shi babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant doesn't get enough water during flowering. Keeping the soil constantly moist and providing light shade during very hot afternoons helps the fruit to set.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua aduawai lɛ ni amɛma shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when the sun gets too bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and short roots that burn and dry out easily under harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains near them creates a canopy that shields the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops curl up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up during hot afternoons as a natural defense to save moisture and stop water from evaporating too quickly. If the leaves uncurl when the sun goes down, the plant is fine, but if they stay curled in the morning, the crops need urgent watering.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni tsiɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ. Kɛji baai lɛ shwieee shi beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ Tso lɛ hi. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe leebi lɛ, ehe miihia ni afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ nu oya.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my crops after the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ yɛ hɔmɔ sɛɛ?

english: You should wait to plant until after the soil has been thoroughly soaked by two or three steady rains, rather than planting after the very first light rain. This ensures there is enough moisture stored in the ground so seeds can germinate without drying out.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni odu nii kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the soil before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and stays around the soil for too long, suffocating the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the tuber area.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa ni ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ he be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tuber he lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up while still hanging on the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black pods are caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during very wet and humid weather. Pruning extra branches lets air and sunlight flow through the farm, which keeps the pods dry and reduces the disease.
ga: Black pods hela ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi waa lɛ. Afoɔ tsei krokomɛi koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa helai baa shi.

english: What causes tiny white insects to collect under the leaves of my pepper plants?
ga: Nɔ ni haa ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ Buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ ashishi.

english: These insects are usually whiteflies or mealybugs that suck sap from the leaves, causing the plant to weaken and leaves to dry up. You can manage them early by spraying the underside of the leaves with a mix of soapy water or neem oil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji ŋmeii yɛŋ loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni baai lɛ hu egbiɔ. Obaanyɛ otsu he nii mra. Kɛtsɔ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I rotate different crops on my plot instead of planting cassava every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni madu ŋmei daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows specific pests and soil diseases to build up. Rotating crops, especially adding beans or groundnuts, restores soil nutrients naturally and breaks the life cycle of pests.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, titri lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni akɛfataa he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ

english: Why do weeds grow faster right after I apply fertilizer to my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer feeds all plant life in the soil equally, including weeds. To make sure your crops get the food, you must clear all weeds around the base of your plants before putting fertilizer down.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni jwɛi hu fata he. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ náa niyenii. Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi fɛɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ dani awoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there is intense sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing companion crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides temporary shade and keeps the surrounding air moist while the young cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Hefatalɔi tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo baa be kukuoo mli, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking nutrients from the undersides of the leaves. Spraying an organic neem solution or approved pest control helps clear the insects so new, healthy leaves can open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ organic neem solution loo tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baaye abua ni egbe kooloi lɛ koni baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Yellow leaves on maize plants usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which plants need to make food. Applying animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer around the base of the plants helps them turn green and build strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa tso lɛ kɛha niyenii lɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛbɔleɔ Tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni efee ŋmei ni wa.

english: Can I use rotted market refuse and organic waste as fertilizer for my vegetable farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ jara nɔ jwɛi ni egbo kɛ jwɛi ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ atsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha mi aduawai aŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, fully decomposed organic waste acts as rich compost that adds nutrients to the soil. It improves the soil's ability to hold water and feeds the plants naturally without burning their roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fiteɔ kwraa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ehaa tsei lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eshãaa shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground when the heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in heavy rains because stagnant water stays around the roots and starves them of air. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to flow away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa ejaakɛ nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ joɔ foi shweshweeshwe.

english: Maize seeds need consistent moisture to germinate and establish strong early roots. If you plant in dry soil before regular rains start, the heat can bake the seeds and stop them from sprouting.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa. Kɛji odu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ, Dɔlɛ baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui lɛ ni eha amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my crops produce very small fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight for the same water and nutrients in the soil while their leaves block each other from sunlight. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to grow large and healthy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni abuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la lɛ he Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ agbo ni efee hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear extra suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain tso titri lɛ

english: Extra suckers steal water and nutrients from the main plantain tree. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers allows the mother plant to focus its energy on growing a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama plantains akui wuji ni tsii ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do I need to lift my yam vines onto wooden stakes off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miwoɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines onto stakes helps their leaves catch maximum sunlight to make food for the tubers. It also keeps leaves off the wet ground, reducing the risk of fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa ehe tsei lɛ náa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebaatsiɔ baai anaa koni ekahi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Ha fungal leaf helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures are too high or when the plant lacks adequate water and nutrients like potassium. Regular watering and feeding the plant balanced compost helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai tamɔ potassium. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ha lɛ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong, direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or cassava planted around them during their first few years to protect their leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo yucca ni adu yɛ he fɛɛ he yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli koni ebu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Is it better to plant my maize in straight lines or scatter the seeds everywhere?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ loo aaagbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã he fɛɛ he?

english: Planting maize in straight lines with proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. It also makes weeding and applying fertilizer much easier compared to scattering seeds.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ he.

english: Why is my farm producing smaller harvests each year even though I use the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same piece of land year after year removes all the nutrients from the soil. Rotating your crop with legumes, such as cowpeas or groundnuts, helps restore natural nitrogen to the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if my crop leaves turning yellow means they need fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiitao ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: When older leaves at the bottom of plants like maize turn yellow starting from the tip, it usually means the plant lacks nitrogen. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ tsei ashishigbɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛdalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and covered in tiny white insects?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ ehà amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curled leaves covered in white insects are usually caused by mealybugs or whiteflies that suck sap from the plant. Using healthy, disease-free stems for planting and removing infected leaves early helps prevent this spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ŋmeii yɛŋ ehà nɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ mli lɛ atsu nii kɛji oodu ni ojie baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: What makes my tomato fruits develop black, rotten bottoms before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ diŋ lɛ miifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani ekwɛ̃?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes are caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium or experiences irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant take up calcium properly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ jɛ fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops dry up quickly during the dry season even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ amɛmli moŋ?

english: In hot weather, water on bare soil evaporates quickly before root systems can absorb it. Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground much longer.
ga: yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Mulching around Kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the rain is enough for me to start planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nugbɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: You should wait until the rain wets the soil down to at least the depth of your hand, usually after two or three steady rains. Planting in soil that is wet only on the surface causes seeds to germinate and then die when the sun comes out.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ashɛ kɛ hoo lɛ nine mli. Bei pii lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni yaa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ pɛ efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ.

english: Why do some of my maize cobs have missing grains instead of full rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ ekomɛi amli ŋmeii ni elaaje yɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Missing grains happen when the maize flowers are not fully pollinated, often caused by severe drought, extreme heat, or planting stalks too far apart from each other for wind to carry pollen.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa beni ŋmãa fɔfɔii lɛ eshɛko amɛhe kwraa lolo lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni naa wa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yaa shɔŋŋ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɔ ekɛ pollen lɛ baa lɛ kɛbaa.

english: Why should I harvest my yams as soon as the plant leaves dry up and turn brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makpa sweet potatoes kɛji baai lɛ egbi ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛ?

english: Brown leaves mean the yam plant has finished growing and stored all its energy in the tuber. Leaving yams in the ground after this stage increases the risk of rot, insect attacks, and loss of quality.
ga: Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ egbe edalɛ naa ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ eto ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi sweet potato yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ ebaagbo, kooloi baatutua lɛ, ni ebaafite lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my maize crops dry up and turn yellow during the dry harmattan season in November?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ harmattan be ni egbi yɛ November mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During November and the harmattan, dry dusty winds pull moisture out of the leaves faster than the roots can drink from the dry soil. This severe water loss causes the leaves to scorch and turn yellow.
ga: Yɛ November kɛ Harmatta mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Nu ni fiteɔ waa nɛɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why should I plow my land before the major rains arrive rather than waiting until after the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii dani nugbɔ wulu lɛ aba moŋ fe ni mamɛ ni nugbɔ wulu lɛ aje shishi?

english: Plowing dry ground opens up hard soil so it can soak up the very first rainfall. If you wait until after heavy rains, the land becomes muddy and machinery or tools will compact the wet soil, making it hard for roots to breathe.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ ŋmɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ. Kɛji omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baatsɔ muji. ni tsɔnei loo nitsumɔ dadei baaha shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa ewaa ahaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaamu

english: Why do my young cocoa trees scorch and die when I plant them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily in full sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them creates a canopy that protects them from direct heat until they are strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ, yɛ emasɛi Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewaa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thick green leaves but give me small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: If cassava gets too much shade or too much nitrogen fertilizer, it spends all its energy growing heavy leaves above ground instead of sending food down to grow big tubers under the ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ ná hulutsoo be babaoo loo nitrogen ŋmei babaoo lɛ, Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ baai ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii kɛba shi koni ekɛdu bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the air is extremely hot or when the soil lacks water. The plant intentionally sheds flowers to conserve water and survive the heat stress.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ nu efo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ jwɛŋɔ amɛfɔfɔi koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi wala mli yɛ dɔlɛ mli.

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during hot afternoons to reduce the leaf surface exposed to the scorching sun. This is a natural behavior that helps the plant save water.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli koni hulu ni tsoɔ yɛ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli subaŋ ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up completely above ground before I harvest the tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mikpaa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: When yam plants mature at the end of the rainy season, the vine naturally dies because the plant is transferring all its remaining food and nutrients down into the tuber to store for the dry season.
ga: Beni sweet potato tsei lɛ daraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ Wein tso lɛ baagbo yɛ ehe diɛŋtsɛ be mli ni sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ niyenii kɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli koni akɛto yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do weeds sprout much faster right after I tractor-plow my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa beni mitsu ŋmɔ lɛ mli nii sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plowing turns the soil upside down and brings old, sleeping weed seeds buried deep underground up to the surface where light and air trigger them to germinate quickly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ shishi ni ehaa jwɛi dumɔwui momo ni ehiɛ edɔ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. La kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ woɔ amɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do my groundnut leaves turn pale yellow even when the ground is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Groundnut leaves turn yellow when soil is waterlogged or compacted, which blocks air from reaching the roots and prevents the plant from taking in nitrogen.
ga: Peanut baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ebɔle ehe. Enɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ehaaa tso lɛ aŋɔ nitrogen.

english: Why do my plantain suckers produce smaller bunches when planted close to big forest trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Big trees have massive roots and heavy branches that steal water, plant food, and sunlight from nearby plantains, leaving them with less energy to produce large fruit bunches.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ shishifãi wuji kɛ niji ni tsii ni juɔ nu, tsei aniyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haaa amɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛkɛwo aduawai wuji.

english: How do I know when the main cocoa harvesting season begins in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni kookoo kpamɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ Ghana?

english: In Ghana, the main cocoa crop season typically starts around September or October, following the major rainy season, when the majority of pods turn yellow or orange, signaling they are mature.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, kookoo dumɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi aaafee Alemle loo Alemle. Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ masɛi Beni ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ Okadi akɛ ahoo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their flowers before pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi babaoo dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but only a small percentage turn into pods. Flower drop happens due to incomplete insect pollination, dry weather stress, or the tree naturally shedding excess flowers it cannot support.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ bafeɔ pod. Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa yɛ kooloi ni feɔ pollination ni eshɛɛɛ he lɛ hewɔ. Haomɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli Aloo tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni anyɛɛɛ akwɛ nɔ.

english: Why do young cocoa pods sometimes shrivel up and turn black while still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Small pods shrivel due to physiological pod wilt, which is the tree's natural way of managing its pod load, or due to black pod fungal disease caused by excess moisture and lack of sunlight.
ga: Pods bibii lɛ gboɔ yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ pods ni shwieɔ shi lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekwɛɔ ŋmeii ayibɔ nɔ. aloo yɛ fungal hela ni yɔɔ pods diji amli ni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine kɛ hulu la ni bɛ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ

english: Why do extension officers advise keeping shade trees on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni sɛɛkwɛlɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Shade trees protect young cocoa from intense sunlight, maintain soil moisture, reduce weed growth, and shield cocoa branches from severe winds during dry seasons.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu kpɛɔ lɛ buɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i Ha jwɛi lɛ adalɛ aba shi ni obu kookoo niji ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he yɛ hɔmɔ be mli

english: Why is it necessary to prune the extra branches and suckers from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ niji kɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes non-productive growth so the tree can direct its nutrients straight into pod production, while improving airflow to reduce fungal diseases.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ dalɛ ni wooo yibii lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛya pod feemɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛba tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ shi.

english: How long will it take for my new hybrid cocoa seedlings to start bearing pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi-hybrid cocoa dumɔwui heei lɛ aje shishi amɛfee pods?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties in Ghana generally begin producing their first pods within 2 to 3 years under proper care, compared to traditional varieties which take 4 to 5 years.
ga: Cocoa henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana lɛ jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ afeemɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli yɛ kwɛmɔ kpakpa shishi. Akɛ enɛ toɔ blema kookoo henɔi ni heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves during the dry season are a survival reaction to heat and water stress; the cocoa tree drops older leaves to save water until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ ji wala yibiiwoo ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ nu mli haomɔ mli baa. Kokoo tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai momo lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛto nu kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Can I plant food crops like cassava right next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii, tamɔ ŋmei, yɛ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ masɛi?

english: It is best to avoid planting cassava near young cocoa because cassava roots feed aggressively and compete heavily for underground water and nutrients, which can stunt young cocoa seedlings.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi yeɔ nii oya ni amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ waa. ni baanyɛ afite kookoo tsei bibii lɛ

english: How does applying fertilizer during the rainy season help my cocoa crop grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Rainfall helps dissolve soil fertilizers so the plant's roots can absorb essential nutrients easily, promoting healthy leaf growth, stronger flowering, and larger pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hia lɛ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa Fɔfɔi lɛ wa. ni ŋmeii lɛ dara fe no

english: Why must I ferment my harvested cocoa beans under plantain leaves before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-kookoo ni akpa lɛ woɔ plantain baai ashishi dani migbiɔ lɛ?

english: Fermentation generates natural heat that stops the seed from sprouting, removes bitter tastes, and develops the chocolate flavor and brown color needed to meet market quality standards.
ga: Fermentation haa adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ ni tsiɔ dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃, ejieɔ ŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaa tsokolate kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni he hiaa koni ashɛ jarayeli he mlai lɛ ahe lɛ baa.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees dry up and fall off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the dry Harmattan season, harsh dry winds pull moisture out of cocoa leaves faster than roots can draw water from dry soil. Trees shed leaves to conserve water and prevent total drying out.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan be mli ni nu lɛ mli egbi lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni mli egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ kookoo baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛkagbi kwraa.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when strong winds and heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems near the surface rather than deep taproots. When heavy rains soften the soil, roots lose their grip, causing top-heavy plants to collapse under strong wind.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Shishifãi lɛ baafee mɛi ni nyɛŋ amɔmɔ amɛhe. Ehaa tsei ni tsii shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant nutrient responsible for leaf greenness and growth. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ baai lɛ shweremɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ, ni eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant cowpea or groundnuts on my farm to improve the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpea and groundnut have tiny root swellings containing helpful bacteria that take nitrogen directly from the air and trap it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the land for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi ni efu fioo ni bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ mli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why am I seeing small holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the central shoots of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central growing whorl to feed on tender leaves, leaving behind chewed leaves and waste that looks like sawdust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni daa koni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Eshiɔ baai ni ashɛre kɛ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmei.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, or viruses they transmit. These pests suck sap from fresh shoots, causing leaves to twist and stunt growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, whiteflies, loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei heei amli lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛdaraaa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged or heavy clay soil that retains too much water during long rains. Soil fungi spread rapidly in soggy conditions, rotting the tubers before they can be harvested.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni hiɛɔ nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ dani akpaa.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce many flowers, but the flowers fall off without growing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko?

english: Tomato flowers drop without forming fruit when temperatures get too high, water supply is irregular, or pollinators are lacking, preventing proper fertilization of the bloom.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ eyaaa nɔ daa. loo ŋmeii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ faaa lɛ faaa Etsiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ afɔmɔ ni sa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb up instead of trailing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high into sunlight and air. Maximum sunlight exposure allows leaves to make extra food through photosynthesis, which flows down to build bigger underground tubers.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛyaa hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii krokomɛi kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi koni efee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji

english: Why do my okra pods get tough and hard to cut if I leave them on the plant for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni ewa akɛ abaakpa kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Okra pods quickly develop thick fibers and hard seeds as they mature to prepare for reproduction. Harvesting pods while they are small and tender keeps them soft and encourages the plant to produce more fruit.
ga: Okra ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ dumɔwui ni wa oya beni amɛdaraa koni amɛkɛsaa amɛhe kɛha fɔmɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwie shi beni amɛji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee blɛoo ni ewo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow instead of deep green when they start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food crops use to build strong green leaves. Adding animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps the plant turn green and grow strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii tso titri ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni wa, eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmɔŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for my farm if I burn the bushes and crop remains every year before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ mishã jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ daa afi dani midu lɛ, eyeɔ miŋmɔ lɛ awui lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the rich topsoil and kills beneficial insects and worms that help crops grow. Leaving the weeds and crop remains to rot naturally in the soil acts as free manure and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ, ni egbeɔ kooloi kɛ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under full sun. They need shade from larger trees or temporary shade crops like plantains to protect their leaves and keep the soil cool during their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛbu baai lɛ ahe ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava plants lose all their leaves during the dry season, and are they dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ fiteɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves on purpose during dry weather to save water and stay alive. The plant is not dying; it is simply resting and protecting its roots underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi wala mli. Tso lɛ gbooo, ejɔɔ ehe kɛkɛ ni ebuɔ eshishifãi ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are small worms eating the center leaves of my young maize plants early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: These worms are likely Fall Armyworms, which feed on tender inner leaves of young maize. Checking your farm regularly and applying recommended natural or chemical sprays early prevents them from destroying the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii mra. Ebaatsi ŋmɔji anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do flowers drop off my pepper plants without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants often drop flowers when the air gets too hot, when they lack water, or when they have too much nitrogen fertilizer. Consistent watering and balanced plant food help flowers stay on and grow into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔmɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ, be mli ni nu bɛ, loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe daa kɛ tso niyenii ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I put many seeds together in one single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo feɔ bu kome lɛ?

english: When too many seeds grow in one spot, they compete with each other for space, water, and soil nutrients. Planting fewer seeds per hole and spacing them correctly allows each crop to feed well and yield more.
ga: Be mli ni dumɔwui babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he kome. Nakai dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui fioo yɛ bu kome mli ni akɛto he jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso fɛɛ tso aná niyenii kpakpa ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the same nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or beans puts nutrients back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops right after the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with very strong roots that absorb water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops a chance to take in nutrients without competition.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi lɛ wa waa ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn powdery or grow mold inside my storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ miitsɔ powda loo ŋmãa ni miida yɛ mi nitoohe lɛ?

english: Maize spoils when it is put into storage with too much moisture left inside the grains. Thoroughly drying your harvested maize under the sun until the grains are hard prevents mold and webbed insects from ruining your grain.
ga: Abɛi baafite kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo eshwɛ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ogbala o-abele ni okpa lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu shishi kɛyashi eshishifãi lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ akafite o-abele lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or is receiving too much water, which stops the roots from absorbing key nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ.

english: Why is it helpful for me to plant cowpeas in the same farm with my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which naturally feeds the maize and improves soil health.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa ŋmãa niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ lɛ

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot under the soil before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani manyɛ makpa amɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays too wet for too long during heavy rains, allowing soil fungi to infect and break down the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aná hela ni amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why are small holes appearing on my cabbage leaves, and how does this affect my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ anɔ Ni te enɛ saa mikpamɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Holes on cabbage leaves are usually caused by caterpillars feeding on the crop, which reduces the plant's ability to gather sunlight and produce a firm head.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ abua hulu la naa ni efee bulbs ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in open sunlight without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kooko tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse ni hulutsoo bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily in strong sunlight; shade crops like plantains protect them until their roots are strong enough to withstand heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli tamɔ plantains lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛyashiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulutsoo be lɛ naa.

english: Staking exposes yam leaves to direct sunlight, which helps the plant generate more food energy to grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ niyenii hewalɛ babaoo koni ekɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Planting seeds too closely causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stems and smaller harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni akpaaa nii babaoo.

english: How do weeds growing around my young crops slow down their growth?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi dumɔwui lɛ aha amɛdalɛ aba shi?

english: Weeds steal essential moisture, sunlight, and fertilizer from the soil, effectively starving your young crops before they can establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hia, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye otsei bibii lɛ dani amɛná shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plant before producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off without setting fruit when temperatures get too high or when the plant experiences extreme dry spells between waterings.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo beni tsei lɛ naa bei ni mli egbi waa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ lɛ teŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout if a dry spell happens right after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji hɔmɔ ba beni midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds require steady moisture to start germinating; if the soil dries out completely after planting, the tiny embryo inside the seed dies.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa yɛ be mli ni adu fɔmɔ kotoku bibioo lɛ Dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ baagbo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. It can happen when the soil runs out of food or when heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the ground where roots cannot reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba be mli ni niyenii he hɔmɔ yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ loo be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: If I do not have money to buy chemical fertilizer this season, what natural materials can I put in my soil to feed my crops?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mibɛ shika ni mikɛbaahe tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ be nɛɛ mli hu? Mɛɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii manyɛ mikɛfata shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni mikɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii?

english: You can feed your soil for free by mixing well-rotted animal manure, dried composted leaves, or wood ash into the dirt before planting. These natural materials decompose and slowly release nutrients to your plants.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ ni okɛ kooloi aŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, baai ni egbi, loo tso sũ baafutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani okɛdu. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii nɛɛ fiteɔ fiofio ni amɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ amɛhaa tso lɛ.

english: Can I use natural plant extracts like neem leaves to protect my vegetables from insect pests?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei amli nibii tamɔ neem baai lɛ abu mi-aduawai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, pounding bitter leaves like neem or hot peppers and soaking them in water creates a natural liquid spray that repels leaf-eating insects without requiring expensive chemical pesticides.
