ga: Hɛɛ, baai ni mli edɔ tamɔ neem loo chili ni mli edɔ lɛ ni akumɔɔ. Kɛkɛ ni kɛ́ akɛwo nu mli lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli nu ni shwieɔ kooloi ni yeɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tsofai ni jara wa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers fall off the tree during the hot dry season without producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni efeee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when water is scarce to save energy and protect themselves from drying out. Providing shade trees helps keep the area cool and retains soil moisture during dry spells.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ nu faaa koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛtsi amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Shading yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa jɛmɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black patches at the bottom before they fully ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ yɛ okadii diji yɛ shishi dani amɛshwereɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often caused by irregular watering or drying out of the roots.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ amɛ shishifãi lɛ loo amɛgbiɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds on my farm grow much faster than the cassava stems I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe ŋmei tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants with deep roots designed by nature to grab water and soil nutrients much faster than domesticated farm crops, which is why early weeding is necessary.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni adebɔɔ fee koni ejie nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei ni akwɛɔ amɛ yɛ shia lɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia

english: Curled leaves with yellowish patches are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, a sickness spread from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ.

english: How do worm-like insects manage to get inside my young maize stems and eat them from the inside?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kooloi bibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ boteɔ mibi lɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ mli?

english: Moths lay eggs on the maize leaves, and when the tiny caterpillars hatch, they bore into the stem where it is soft, wet, and rich in food, hiding away from rain and predators.
ga: Kpɔŋɔi fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa baa nɔ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɔ lɛ, amɛfoɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli, he ni amɛyɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe efɔ, ni niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Tsɔ ohe kɛjɛ nugbɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe.

english: What happens to my pepper crop if I plant the seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When planted too close, pepper plants compete with each other for sunlight, soil food, and air. This makes them grow tall and weak, resulting in fewer and smaller peppers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu Pepper tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, sũ mli niyenii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he, ni no haa amɛdaraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ, ni no haa Pepper tsei lɛ faaa ni amɛfeɔ bibii.

english: Why did the maize seeds I saved from my last harvest fail to grow when I planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikpa yɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu lɛ?

english: Saved seeds can fail to sprout if they were not completely dried before storage, which allows moisture, mold, or insects to destroy the tiny living embryo inside the seed.
ga: Ekolɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji amɛgbiko kwraa dani akɛto. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ loo kooloi bibii kpataaa ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni hiɛ ka lɛ ahiɛ. yɛ dumɔwu lɛ mli

english: Yellowing from the bottom up usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or planting legumes like cowpeas before your maize season helps restore this nutrient to the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he loo aduɔ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii dani ŋmãa be lɛ baashɛ lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii nɛɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my soil produce smaller harvests every year even though I plant the same crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Planting the exact same crop in the same spot every year drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating your crops—like planting groundnuts or beans after maize—helps the soil recover its natural fertility.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei sɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni enáa bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling upwards and turning pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Removing badly affected plants early and managing whiteflies using neem oil sprays or recommended insecticides helps stop the disease from spreading across your field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Tsei ni ena naagbai waa lɛ ajiemɔ mra kɛ whitefly nɔkwɛmɔ kɛtsɔ neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa flowers dry up and drop off before forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi bibii lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛmiifee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree is under severe stress from heat, lack of shade, or attacks by tiny sap-sucking insects called mirids (capsids). Keeping mature shade trees in your farm and protecting young trees from insect attack helps pods form properly.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ yɛ haomɔ ni naa wa mli kɛjɛ dɔlɛ, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni atsɛɔ amɛ mirids (capsids) lɛ atutua amɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni obu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni baatutua amɛ lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ ama shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the fruit bunches start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall over because their roots are naturally shallow and can be destroyed underground by microscopic worms (nematodes) or root weevils. Supporting heavy trees with bamboo props and using clean, healthy suckers when planting keeps roots strong.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ akpata amɛhiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. (Nematodes) loo shishifãi amli ŋmeii. Akɛ ŋmei nibii fiɔ tsei ni tsii sɛɛ. Ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsu nii kɛ́ adu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ ahiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water suffocates them because the soil does not drain well. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to run off, keeping the roots safe from rotting.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ ŋmɛ shi, ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. ni etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite

english: How do I know if the soil has enough moisture for me to start planting after the first rain?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ oje dumɔ shishi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season can be misleading and may be followed by a dry spell that kills fresh seeds. It is best to wait until 2 or 3 steady rains have soaked the soil at least as deep as your hand before sowing your seeds.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni lakaa mɔ, ni ekolɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni gbeɔ dumɔwui heei lɛ baanyiɛ sɛɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa shii 2 loo 3 lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛ hoo lɛ tamɔ onine dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Why do my pepper plants shed their flowers when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers during high heat to save water and protect themselves from dying. Watering your crops early in the morning and spreading dry grass around the base of the plants keeps the soil cool and helps flowers stay on.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he. Okɛ nu awo tsei lɛ amli leebi ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi ashwã amɛhe. Tso lɛ shishi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Why do I need to mount tall stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to produce energy, which then travels down to grow large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves into the light and keeps them off the hot ground where diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ hia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛkɛ ni efã gbɛ kɛba shi koni eyadu ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ anɔ kɛyaa la mli ni ehaaa amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ hulutsoo be mli, he ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow lots of thick green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli tse babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cowpeas to put all their energy into making leafy stems instead of flowers and pods. Avoiding high-nitrogen fertilizers on cowpeas helps the plant focus on producing pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tsina ŋmei mli lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa pod feemɔ nɔ.

english: Why do so many flowers on my cocoa tree fall off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Most cocoa flowers fall off because they were not fertilized through pollination. Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but only a small fraction get pollinated by tiny insects called midges to successfully grow into pods.
ga: Kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ. Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi fã bibioo ko pɛ yɔɔ mli. Kplukai bibii pɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ lɛ pollin. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. bɔni afee ni eye omanye ni etsɔ pod

english: How does hand pollination work, and can it really help me get more cocoa pods from my farm?
ga: Te nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa tɛŋŋ? Ni ani ebaaye ebua mi ni maná kookoo ŋmeii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Hand pollination means using a small tool or brush to manually transfer pollen from one cocoa flower to another. Doing this ensures more flowers get fertilized, which can double or even triple the number of pods your trees produce compared to natural insect pollination alone.
ga: Nine nɔ fɔfɔi ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ dɛŋdade bibioo loo brɔsh tsuɔ nii ni akɛ niji jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛjɛɔ kookoo fɔfɔi kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli. Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ aná fɔmɔ nii babaoo. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii ni otso lɛ woɔ lɛ ayibɔ afee enyɔ loo etɛ. Kɛ akɛto adebɔɔ mli pollination ni kooloi pɛ feɔ lɛ he.

english: What kind of insects pollinate my cocoa flowers, and how can I keep them on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ kooloo kooloi shwieɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mahã amɛhi miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The main pollinators are tiny insects called midge flies. They thrive in damp, shady places with rotting organic material, so keeping decomposed plantain trunks or leaf litter on the farm floor gives them a safe place to breed.
ga: Mɛi titri ni haa ŋmeii lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midge flies lɛ. Amɛshwereɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fiteɔ yɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ahe tsei loo baai ni egboi ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ji he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni abaanyɛ afɔ bii yɛ.

english: Why do cocoa flowers grow directly on the main trunk and big branches rather than just on the leafy tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ kɛ niji wuji lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally grow flowers on their main trunk and large branches so that the thick wood can support the heavy weight of full-sized cocoa pods as they develop and mature.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛtso wulu lɛ kɛ amɛniji wuji lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni tso ni mli tse lɛ anyɛ akwɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ amli tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ nɔ beni amɛdaraa ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: How does pruning my cocoa trees help them produce more flowers and pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ cacao tso ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes unwanted shade branches and dead wood, allowing air and sunlight to reach the main trunk. Good airflow reduces diseases that destroy flowers, while sunlight stimulates the tree to produce fresh flower buds.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji kɛ tsei ni egboi lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ tso titri lɛ he. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ haa helai ni gbeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ baa shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulu la tsirɛɔ tsei lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi heei.

english: Why are some cocoa trees on my farm full of pods while the ones next to them have almost nothing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi eyi kɛ ŋmeii yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ eshwɛ fioo ni amɛbɛ eko kwraa lɛ?

english: Yield differences happen because of flower pollination success, access to soil nutrients, or tree variety. Trees that get better shade balance and attract more pollinating insects will produce far more pods than neglected neighboring trees.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ yibiiwoo mli lɛ baa yɛ pollination omanyeyeli hewɔ. nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nine shɛɔ nɔ loo tsei srɔtoi Tsei ni naa hulutsoo kpakpa ni gbalaa ŋmeii babaoo kɛbaa lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo fe tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni aku hiɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it important to control weeds under my cocoa trees during the flowering season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akudɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei ashishi yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital nutrients and water from the soil that the cocoa tree needs to feed its flowers. Clearing weeds ensures the tree has enough energy to retain its flowers and grow healthy young pods.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni cacao tsei he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ̃ fɔfɔi lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛkwɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ ni ekɛ ŋmeii bibii ni he wa baa.

english: When is the best time of the year for me to prepare my farm for peak flowering and pollination?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ masaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo aba?

english: The best time is right at the onset of the rainy season. The moisture triggers heavy flowering and creates the damp ground conditions that pollinating midges need to multiply quickly.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee. Fɛ̃i lɛ haa fɔfɔii babaoo baa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni ehe hiaa ni pollination lɛ aya hiɛ oya lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers and produce fewer pods during hot, dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: During hot and dry spells, cocoa trees shed their flowers to save water and protect themselves from dying. Additionally, the tiny midge flies that pollinate flowers cannot survive easily in dry conditions.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he. Kɛfata he lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why do some of my very small, young cocoa pods turn shriveled and black shortly after forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ beni amɛfee lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: This is often a natural tree response called cherelle wilt, where the tree thins out extra pods it cannot afford to feed. However, it can also be caused by fungal diseases or insect pests attacking the young pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hetoo ni ale lɛ akɛ Cherelle Wilt, he ni tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aha lɛ niyenii lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, ŋmeii helai loo ŋmeii ni tutuaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ hu baanyɛ aha eba.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cocoa pods so I don't pick them too early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ? koni akabua naa oya tsɔ

english: Cocoa pods change color when they mature—green pods turn yellow, and reddish pods turn orange-yellow. Harvesting when the color change is complete ensures the seeds inside have fully developed the sugars needed for good fermentation.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Pods eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Ni ŋmeii tsuru lɛ baatsake ni etsɔ ŋmeii-ŋmei. Nikpamɔ beni su tsakemɔ lɛ egbe naa lɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ sugar ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What will happen to my cocoa crop if I am only able to visit my farm to harvest on weekends?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ manyɛ maya ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mayakpa nii yɛ otsii lɛ anaagbee pɛ?

english: If ripe cocoa pods are left on the tree for more than two to three weeks, they can become overripe, attracting pests, rodents, and fungal diseases like black pod rot, which ruins the quality of the beans.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ fe otsii fioo komɛi lɛ, ekolɛ nakai kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ tsɔ. Egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai, ŋmeii, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe nibii.

english: Why are some of my cocoa pods turning black and rotting right on the branch before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in wet weather and thick shade. Clearing surrounding weeds and removing infected pods right away keeps the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Ajieɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I leave harvested cocoa pods lying in a pile on the farm ground for a long time before breaking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ yɛ ŋtayaa mli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ dani mifoɔ mli lɛ?

english: Leaving harvested pods on the ground for more than five days causes the seeds inside to start sprouting or drying out prematurely, which ruins their flavor profile and lowers the grade price cocoa buyers will offer you.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ fe gbii enumɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ loo amɛbaagbi oya. Enɛ fiteɔ bɔ ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ. Ni enɛ haa kookoo grade ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛhaa bo lɛ jara baa shi.

english: Will cutting off the extra shoots growing out of my cocoa tree trunk damage the crop?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ amli lɛ ni ooofo lɛ baafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: No, removing those extra shoots (called chupons) actually helps the tree. It prevents the plant from wasting nutrients on useless leaves and directs energy into producing bigger, healthier cocoa pods.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii ni fa fe nine (ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons) ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Etsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekafite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ, ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and dropping off during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get stressed quickly under direct heat and strong sun. Without larger shade plants or plantains growing nearby to protect them, their leaves scorch and dry out to prevent the main stem from dying.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ haoɔ oya yɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛji akɛ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ koni ebu amɛhe lɛ bɛ lɛ, Ashãa amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ koni tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ akagbo.

english: Why do the young shoots and pods on my cocoa tree look burnt and covered in tiny dark spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã ni ŋmeii diji bibii ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by mirid insects (capsids) that suck moisture from the fresh parts of the plant. Spraying your farm with approved insecticides during their active season protects new growth from dying back.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji kooloi bibii babaoo (capsids) ni shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ fãi heei lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni kooloi lɛ tsuɔ nii waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kooloi heei ni eda lɛ ahe kɛjɛ gbele he.

english: Can I leave the empty cocoa pod husks near the base of my trees after breaking them open?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi kookoo ŋmɔji ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ beni mifo mli sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to move empty husks away from active crop areas because fresh husks trap moisture and harbor mold spores that can infect your healthy cocoa trees with fungal diseases.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ abaajie ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ yibii heei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ aha cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aná tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ haaa.

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce so many flowers, but only a few of them grow into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ daa diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of tiny flowers, but many drop off naturally because they were not pollinated by tiny insects (midges) or because the tree lacks enough soil nutrients and water to support that many pods.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi bibii akpei abɔ, shi amɛteŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ejaakɛ kooloi bibii (teŋgbɛ tsei) kɛ amɛhe wooo mli, loo akɛni tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli ni baanyɛ akwɛ fɔfɔi babaoo anɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Can I plant food crops like cassava inside my mature cocoa farm to get extra harvest?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii, tamɔ ŋmei, yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ ni eda mli koni makpa babaoo?

english: Cassava roots grow deep and heavy, competing heavily for soil moisture and nutrients that your mature cocoa trees need to form pods. It is better to plant food crops only when cocoa trees are still young.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛhe wa. Amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa o-cacao tsei ni eda lɛ koni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii beni kookoo tsei lɛ darako pɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops look weak even though I water them every day with well water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nubu mli nu shwieɔ amɛnɔ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Well water can contain unseen impurities or high mineral levels that alter its pH balance. If the water's pH is unbalanced, crop roots struggle to absorb nutrients from the soil, making the plants look weak and undernourished despite daily watering.
ga: Ekolɛ muji ni anaaa yɛ nubu mli nu mli loo minerals ni baatsake pH ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛji nu lɛ pH lɛ ejaaa lɛ, Tse lɛ shishifãi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɛ́ afɔse tsei lɛ nu daa gbi po lɛ, etamɔ nɔ ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnáaa niyenii kpakpa.

english: How does using dirty stream water affect the way my crops absorb food from the soil?
ga: Te nu ni mli ewo muji ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ saa bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Muddy or impure water contains solids and microorganisms that can block small root hairs. This prevents crops from drinking efficiently and taking in essential soil nutrients needed for healthy leaf and fruit growth.
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji loo nɔ ni he tseee lɛ mli nibii ni wa kɛ nibii bibii ni baanyɛ atsĩ shishifãi ahe yitsɔi bibii anaa lɛ yɛ mli. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ anu nu jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkaná shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná baai kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does natural rainwater make my crops grow faster than the pond water I store on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya fe nubu ni mikɛtoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rainwater is naturally clean, free of heavy chemical impurities, and has a slightly lower, balanced pH level that crops prefer, allowing roots to take in food immediately without stress.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni he tse kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli Ebɛ tsofai ni tsii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli, ni eyɛ pH ni baa shi fioo ni tsei taoɔ. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ tsuɔ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ akɛ niyenii ni haomɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato plants develop spots and drop their flowers when I irrigate with untreated dam water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji mikɛ dam nu ni asaaa lɛ shwie amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Untreated dam water often carries high impurities and unbalanced acidity levels that stress tender crops. High stress causes plants to drop flowers to save energy instead of producing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dam nu ni asaaa lɛ yɛ muji babaoo kɛ acidity ni ejaaa ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii haoɔ. Haomɔ ni mli wa haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: What does 'pH level' mean when officers talk about farm water, and how does it affect plant growth?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘pH level’ shishi kɛji onukpai wie ŋmɔ mli nu he? Ni te enáa tsei adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: pH level is simply a measurement of how acidic or alkaline water is on a specific scale. Crops prefer balanced water; if the pH is too high or too extreme, it can stunt plant growth and cause yellow leaves.
ga: pH lɛ ji bɔ ni nu lɛ ji acidic loo alkaline lɛ he susumɔ kɛkɛ. Nu ni ja he miihia tsei. Kɛji pH lɛ fa tsɔ loo eshɛ tsɔ lɛ, Ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: How can I test the water on my farm to know if it is safe for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka nu ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ makwɛ kɛji ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: You can use simple test strips or a basic meter provided by extension agents to check the water's pH score and purity level. Checking the record number helps you know whether to treat the water before giving it to plants.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ kaa strips ni yɔɔ mlɛo loo shishijee mita ni ojarayelɔ lɛ kɛha lɛ atsu nii ni okɛkwɛ pH yibɔ kɛ bɔ ni onu lɛ mli tse ha. Kɛ́ okwɛ yibɔ ni aŋmala ashwie shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona kɛji ehe miihia ni atsu nu lɛ he nii dani okɛha otsei lɛ.

english: Will adding water treatments to balance pH damage the natural soil on my farm?
ga: Ani nu ni atsuu he ni akɛfataa he koni pH lɛ afee ekome lɛ baafite adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: No, when you lower or balance water pH to the correct recommended level, it actually protects the soil. Safe water allows good soil microbes to thrive and help plant roots take up nutrients.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ okɛ pH ni yɔɔ onu lɛ mli lɛ ba shi loo okɛto he ni sa ni atsɔɔ akɛ eshɛ he lɛ. Ebaaye ebua diɛŋtsɛ ni abu shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Nu ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves burn after I mix and spray my chemicals using borehole water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ shãa beni mikɛ tsofai efutu ni mikɛ borehole nu lɛ shwie nɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Borehole water often has high pH or impurities that react badly with farm chemicals. Adjusting and reducing the water's pH level before mixing ensures the chemical dissolves properly without scorching tender leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni jɛɔ nubui amli lɛ pH lɛ fa loo muji ni kɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai lɛ yeee jogbaŋŋ yɛ mli. Kɛ́ atsake nu lɛ pH lɛ ni aba shi dani akɛfutu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsofai lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ashãaa baai bibii lɛ.

english: Why do some extension officers suggest reducing the pH level of water before spraying crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi komɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ aba pH ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ shi dani akɛ tsofa afɔ tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: Reducing high pH levels brings farm water into a safe range where pesticides and fertilizers work at full strength. It prevents active ingredients from breaking down in dirty or alkaline water before plants can benefit.
ga: pH ni nɔ kwɔ ni aba shi lɛ baaha ŋmɔ mli nu lɛ ahi he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe. he ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ lɛ Etsiɔ nibii ni tsuɔ nii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ nu ni mli ewo muji loo nu ni mli ewo muji mli dani tsei lɛ aná he sɛɛ.

english: Can dirty farm water reduce the power of the pest sprays I buy from the store?
ga: Ani ŋmɔ mli nu ni mli ewo muji baanyɛ aha tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ shi?

english: Yes, impurities and high pH in farm water bind to active chemical ingredients, weakening their effectiveness. Cleansing the water or adjusting its pH level ensures your sprays control pests properly.
ga: Hɛɛ, muji kɛ pH ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli nu mli lɛ kɛ tsofai ni tsuɔ nii lɛ kpaa gbee. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji bɔ ni nitsumɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ. Nu lɛ mli ni oootsumɔ loo pH lɛ tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa o-spray lɛ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ ebuaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are dying from a serious disease or just showing normal changes as they grow?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji helai ni naa wa miigbe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ loo amɛmiitsɔɔ tsakemɔi ni sa kɛkɛ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Serious diseases cause rapid wilting, rotting roots, or foul-smelling stems that kill the plant. Normal crop behavior includes losing lower leaves as the plant grows tall or dropping extra blossoms during hot weather, which will not destroy your harvest.
ga: Hela ni naa wa haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya. Aloo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ gbonyo ni haa tso lɛ gboɔ. Tsei adalɛ subaŋ ni yɔɔ daa lɛ baa ni baa shi be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ fata he. Aloo fɔfɔii krɛdɛɛi ni shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ yɛ. ni fiteŋ onitsumɔ lɛ

english: Why do my bean plants shed some of their blossoms before producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Bean plants naturally produce more flowers than they can nourish. Shedding excess blossoms is a normal behavior to save energy for forming strong, healthy pods, so it does not mean you made a mistake in caring for them.
ga: Pea tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛha amɛ niyenii. Fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine lɛ ji subaŋ ni afɔɔ feemɔ koni akɛto hewalɛ he koni akɛfee pods ni he wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, etsɔɔɔ akɛ otɔmɔ beni okwɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: What makes the 'Gyaa mu' bean variety special compared to the traditional seeds I usually plant?
ga: Mɛni haa ‘Gyaa mu’ ŋmeii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto kɛ akɛto blema dumɔwui ni miduɔ daa lɛ ahe?

english: Gyaa mu beans are an improved crop variety selected to mature faster, withstand dry spells better, and yield more uniform pods than older local varieties when planted according to recommended guidelines.
ga: Gyaa mu beans ji tso henɔ ko ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛtsɔ halamɔ ni ehalaa akɛ ebaada oya lɛ nɔ Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi amli ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yaa nɔ daa fe maŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii srɔtoi ni etsɛ kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ yɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii lɛ naa.

english: Why do extension officers encourage all farmers in our community to adopt the same improved seed varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ okwaafoi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ wɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛŋɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛmli lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: When an entire community plants the same strong variety, it lowers the chance of pest outbreaks spreading between fields and makes it easier for commercial buyers to come purchase large amounts of uniform crop after harvest.
ga: Kɛji akutsei muu fɛɛ du tsei ni wa lɛ nɔŋŋ Enɛ baaha hegbɛ ni yɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔji ateŋ lɛ aba shi. Ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ akɛ amɛbaahe ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ babaoo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my bean plants have small bumps on their roots, and should I be worried about them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ, ni ani esa akɛ mahao yɛ he?

english: Those bumps are called nodules and are a sign of a healthy plant. Friendly soil bacteria live inside them, taking nitrogen from the air to feed your crop naturally without damaging the root system.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii lɛ akɛ nodules, ni eji tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ he okadi. Shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ hiɔ amɛmli. Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni ekɛha onibii lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni efiteee shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my bean leaves turn yellowish when the pods are almost ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bean baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni eshwɛ fioo ni abaakpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: This is a natural process where the plant moves all its energy and nutrients out of the leaves and into the seeds inside the pods. As long as it happens toward the end of the season, it is completely normal.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ amli. Shii abɔ ni ebaa yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ. Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: If I followed every planting step taught in the agricultural program, why are my crops growing slower than my neighbor's?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui ahe gbɛjianɔtoi fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ yɛ okwaayeli gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii. Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo fe mikutsoŋbii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Even when following the same program, small differences in soil depth, shade, or how much rain settled on your land can cause crops to grow at slightly different speeds without affecting the final quality.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ amɛnyiɛɔ gbɛjianɔtoo kome nɔ moŋ. Srɔtofeemɔi fioo po ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ, hulutsoo, loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei akwɛ̃ yɛ oyaiyeli ni yɔɔ srɔto fioo mli ni enaaa naagbee su lɛ nɔ hewalɛ.

english: Will small spots or minor insect holes on my crop leaves destroy my entire harvest?
ga: Hei bibii loo ŋmeii bibii Ani baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baafite miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ?

english: No, crops can lose a small amount of leaf surface to minor pests or cosmetic leaf spots without losing their ability to produce a full yield, so there is no need to panic at the sight of small spots.
ga: Dabi, tsei baanyɛ afite baa lɛ nɔ fioo ko kɛtsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii loo baa lɛ nɔ hei ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ anɔ. ni nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛbaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ efooo No hewɔ lɛ, ehe ehiaaa ni oshe gbeyei kɛ́ ona ŋmei bibioo ko.

english: How do I know my beans are fully mature and ready to pick without leaving them too long in the sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ ajie amɛ ni mishieee amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Beans are ready for harvest when the pods turn dry and straw-colored, and you can hear the seeds rattle inside when shaken. Harvesting at this stage prevents them from rotting or shattering in the field.
ga: Beni ŋmeii lɛ egbi ni amɛhe yɛ jwɛi su lɛ, no mli lɛ ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ. Ni obaanu dumɔwui lɛ ni hosoɔ yɛ mli kɛji akpokpo. Kɛ́ akpa yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekafite loo egbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Can I save seeds from my harvested bean crop to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahere dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmeii tsei ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ ato ni madu amɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you can save seeds from healthy pods by drying them well and storing them in airtight containers, though replacing them with fresh certified seeds every few seasons keeps your yields at their highest.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui akaje ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli kɛtsɔ amɛ ni oooha amɛgbi jogbaŋŋ ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ tsake lɛ daa bei fioo komɛi po lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni onifeemɔ lɛ aya nɔ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ moŋ.

english: Why do my corn seeds fail to grow if I plant them right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry spell that heats up the soil. If seeds germinate during this brief wet patch, they quickly dry out and die before the main rainy season fully establishes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui kwɛ̃ yɛ be kukuoo mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ, amɛgbiɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi kwraa.

english: How far apart should I space my maize seeds when planting them in my field?
ga: Te esa akɛ makɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ abɔ he kɛyashi tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Spacing maize about 75 centimeters between rows and 25 centimeters between seeds gives each plant enough room, sunlight, and soil nutrients to grow strong without competing with its neighbors.
ga: Gbɛ ni kã ŋmãa ni ato lɛ teŋ lɛ ji aaafee sɛntimita 75 ni dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji aaafee sɛntimita 25, ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa tso lɛ mli hewalɛ ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ yeee akaŋ.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on cassava are usually a sign of cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies feeding on the plant's sap.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ yucca nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Whiteflies bibii ni yeɔ tsei amli nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: This is often caused by a natural process called cherelle wilt, where the tree drops extra pods it cannot support due to a lack of water, shade, or soil nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherry wilt lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Biɛ ji he ni tso lɛ shĩɔ ŋmeii babaoo ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ yɛ nu, hulutsoo loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants get black, rotten spots at the bottom of the fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɛ aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: This black rot at the bottom is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, which often happens when watering is irregular during hot weather.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ akɛ blossom end ŋmeii. ni calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ejaaa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What is causing small green caterpillars to eat the middle leaves of my maize?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a pest that hides in the funnel of the plant and eats young leaves; catching them early allows you to protect your crop with safe pesticides or neem extract.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei amli ŋmeii amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii. Amɛ ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ehaa okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ buɔ onibii ahe.

english: Is it helpful for my farm if I plant groundnuts in the same field as my maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ baaba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, groundnuts fix nitrogen from the air into the soil through their roots, which acts as a natural food to help the maize grow healthier.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni enáa hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has run out of nutrients for planting cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha makwɛ ŋmei?

english: If your previous crop grew slowly, had thin stems, or produced very small tubers, the soil lacks key nutrients and needs plant manure or fallow time to recover.
ga: Kɛji akɛ onibii ni okɛtsu nii tsutsu lɛ dara blɛoo, eyɛ tsei bibii, loo eyɛ bulbs bibii waa Shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni ehe miihia ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do hybrid maize seeds bought from the agro-shop yield better than seeds I save from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni aheɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli shwapo ko mli lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ?

english: Agro-shop hybrid seeds are specially bred in a laboratory for high yields and disease resistance, but the seeds harvested from them lose those special strengths in the next generation.
ga: Akɛ agro-shop hybrid dumɔwui lɛ fɔɔ yɛ laboratori lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛná yibii babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ. Shi dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ nakai dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ nakai hewalɛi krɛdɛɛi lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know the exact time my yam tubers are ready to be harvested from under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines turn yellow and dry up naturally, showing that the plant has finished sending energy down into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛbaa shi kɛyaa eyitso lɛ naa.

english: Why are there tiny holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars eating inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? kɛ ŋmeii bibii Yeɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: This is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana. The young caterpillars hide inside the central leaves (the whorl) and chew holes, but spraying recommended neem extracts or early-stage insecticides can protect your crop before severe damage occurs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kplukai bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli (rings) kɛ bu ni amɛfoɔ mli lɛ amli, shi neem mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ baanyɛ abu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani nɔ ko ni mli wa aba.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up into tight balls and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips, or a virus spread by them. Removing heavily affected leaves early and spraying with soapy water or neem oil helps stop these insects from spreading to healthy plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Ajie baai ni ena hela waa lɛ mra Ni akɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem fɔ afɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akagbɛ amɛshwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when there is no cover above them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni nɔ ko bɛ ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong direct sunlight because their roots are shallow and their leaves burn easily. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain alongside them acts like a natural umbrella, keeping the seedlings cool and moist during their early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, kɛ shĩa tsei ni aduɔ lɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are my cassava roots turning black and rotting in the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water sits around them for too long, especially during heavy rains in poorly drained soil. Planting your cassava stems on raised ridges or mounds allows excess rainwater to flow away so the roots can breathe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Yucca tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Should I cut off some of the small shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani mi plantain shishifãi lɛ miida?

english: Yes, leaving too many shoots (suckers) forces the main plantain tree to share its food and water, leading to smaller bunches. Keeping only one or two strong suckers per main plant ensures you get large, healthy plantain bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, suckers (tso) babaoo ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha plantain titri lɛ ajara niyenii kɛ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei niji lɛ feɔ bibii. Kɛ́ okɛ tso wulu kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha oná plantain tso agbo ni mli wa.

english: Yam vines need to climb upward so their leaves can get plenty of sunlight to make food for the tuber below. If the vines lay flat on the ground, the leaves get shaded, wet, and diseased, which results in much smaller yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii. Kɛji wain tso lɛ kã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ebaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni hela baamɔ lɛ, ni no baaha sweet potato lɛ afee bibioo kwraa.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil needs fertilizer before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani mibɔi dumɔwui?

english: If your previous crops were pale green, grew very slowly, or yielded small harvests, your soil is likely low in nutrients. Adding well-rotted animal manure or the right mineral fertilizer before planting rebuilds the soil so your new crops grow strong.
ga: Kɛji akɛ onibii ni odu tsutsu lɛ ji ŋmɔji ni mli tse, amɛdaraa blɛoo waa, loo amɛwooo yibii fioo ko pɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo mineral ŋmei ni sa wo mli dani odu lɛ, ebaatswa shikpɔŋ lɛ ema shi ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than the food crops I carefully plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe niyenii tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that quickly steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients from your crops. Clearing weeds while your crops are still young prevents the weeds from choking your plants and taking over the field.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ onibii amli oya. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie shi be mli ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni jwɛi lɛ akamɔ otsei lɛ ni amɛye ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without turning into small green tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the heat is extreme, when watering is irregular, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Consistent watering at the roots during hot dry spells helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛhaa shishifãi lɛ daa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why is it important for me to plant my maize right at the beginning of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Planting early with the first main rains allows seeds to sprout in warm, moist soil and establish strong roots. Delaying your planting means the crop might run out of water before it finishes producing grains at the end of the season.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi wuji lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. ni amɛma shishifãi ni wa Dumɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii dani dumɔwui aba yɛ be lɛ naagbee.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and broad, providing living shade umbrellas that keep young cocoa cool and moist in their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛfeɔ wuji. Ha hulutsoo ni haa kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Cocoa trees lose water quickly in dry winds. Without shade trees or enough soil moisture, the tree drops its leaves to save water and prevent itself from drying out completely.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi mli. Kɛji tsei bɛ ni baaha hulutsoo loo ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baashwie baai lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ekɛtsi ehe gbɛ koni ekagbi kwraa.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas on the plot where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmãa yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Maize consumes heavy amounts of soil nitrogen. Cowpeas naturally capture nitrogen from the air and return it to the soil, renewing fertility for future plantings.
ga: Abɛi kɛ nitrogen babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni fɔmɔ aya hiɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii

english: How can I tell if my crops are struggling from lack of nutrients instead of lack of water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ miipiŋ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ fe nu ni faaa?

english: Plants short on water wilt and curl up during hot hours, while plants short on nutrients turn pale green or yellow even when the soil has plenty of water.
ga: Tsei ni nu efo mli lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaabɔle amɛhe yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ amɛhe lɛ baatsɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa po.

english: Why are some of my maize cobs only half-filled with corn grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ fã pɛ eyi kɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Maize needs pollen to hit every silk thread on the cob. High heat or drought during flowering damages pollen, preventing full grain development on the cob.
ga: Abɛi he miihia pollen koni ekɛtswa siliki kpã fɛɛ kpã ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ni baa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ fiteɔ fɔfɔii lɛ. Etsiɔ dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkayi ŋmei lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots become watery and soft if I delay harvesting until the major rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo kɛji mikɛ kpamɔ lɛ to nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: When heavy rains return, mature cassava uses stored starch from its roots to grow new stems and leaves, which reduces root quality and makes them watery.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ, ŋmei ni eda lɛ kɛ ŋmei ni ato kɛjɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai heei. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ ahe afee fɛo, ni ebaaha nu ahi mli.

english: What makes small ragged holes appear in the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miifee buji bibii ni etse amɛhe lɛ?

english: This leaf damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed inside the central leaf funnel of young maize plants as they grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ anɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Black spots on the bottom of tomatoes are caused by calcium deficiency, usually triggered by irregular watering that disrupts how the plant absorbs soil nutrients.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. ni haaa tso lɛ aná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous maize harvest perform worse than newly bought certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui heei ni ahe ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds lose their high-yielding genetic strength after the first crop cycle. Replanted seeds produce weaker plants with lower yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ laajeɔ amɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu aba shi.

english: Why do weeds start growing so much faster than my crops after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds live long in the soil and are adapted to sprout rapidly, stealing surface water and nutrients before crop seeds can fully establish roots.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Ejuɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii dani dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛwoɔ shishifãi kwraa.

english: Why do some crops produce more food when I plant them together in a group rather than alone in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi woɔ niyenii babaoo kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ fee ekome yɛ kui amli moŋ fe ni mikome too midu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certain crops help each other when planted together. For example, legumes like beans fix nitrogen in the soil which feeds nearby cereal crops like maize, while taller plants protect shorter ones from harsh winds and intense sunlight.
ga: Tsei komɛi hu yeɔ amɛbuaa amɛhe kɛ́ amɛfee ekome kɛkwɛ̃. Nɔkwɛmɔnɔ, ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa saa nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni haa ŋmãa nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa niyenii, yɛ be mli ni tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ buɔ tsei kukuji ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ hulutsoo he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big forest trees from my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ dani midu lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees originally grow under forest canopies. They cannot handle direct hot sunlight, so they need shade trees or plantains nearby to provide shelter and keep the soil moist while their roots develop.
ga: Shishijee lɛ, cacao tsei bibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ koo lɛ shishi. Amɛnyɛŋ amɛtsu hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ he nii. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni haa amɛnáa he ko ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: How does a young plantain sucker get its food while it is still attached to the main plant?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ aha plantain tsei bibii lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni amɛkpɛtɛ tso titri lɛ he lolo lɛ?

english: The young plantain sucker relies on the mother plant for nutrients and water through an underground stem connection. Once the sucker grows its own green leaves and roots, it becomes independent and feeds itself.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ damɔ tso nyɛ lɛ nɔ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tso lɛ shishifãi ni kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee lɛ anɔ. Beni sucker lɛ ná lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ebaai kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ Ebaafee mɔ ni yeɔ ehe nɔ ni eyeɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eniyenii.

english: What work do the leaves that fall from my crop plants actually do in the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ nitsumɔ baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mitsei lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Fallen leaves decay and turn into organic matter, acting as natural fertilizer. They feed the soil microbes, keep the ground cool and moist, and return valuable nutrients back to the crop's root zone.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, ni amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛhaa nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ niyenii. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. ni ekɛ niyenii ni jara wa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he

english: How do deep roots help my cassava survive long dry seasons when there is no rain?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ yeɔ ebuaa mi-cassava lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava roots grow deep into the ground where moisture remains trapped long after the top layer of soil has dried out, allowing the plant to drink water during dry spells.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, he ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã lɛ egbi sɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsei nuɔ nu yɛ hɔmɔ be mli.

english: Why do crops that yield heavily in the forest regions of Ghana fail to produce well in the northern savanna?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ Ghana kooi lɛ amli lɛ wooo yibii tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ savannah lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops are adapted to specific climate conditions like humidity, rainfall, and temperature. Forest crops need frequent moisture and high humidity, whereas savanna crops are adapted to intense sunshine and lower rainfall.
ga: Atsakeɔ dumɔwui kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi pɔtɛɛ tamɔ latsaa, nugbɔshiimɔ, kɛ dɔlɛ. Koo mli tsei biɔ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo shii abɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, savannah tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli.

english: What is the best time of day for me to apply liquid fertilizer to my crop leaves?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli?

english: Early morning is best because plants open microscopic pores on their leaves to absorb moisture before the sun gets too hot. Applying fertilizer at midday causes it to evaporate before the plant can drink it.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ tsei lɛ baagbele buji bibii. yɛ baai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛjie ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ adɔ tsɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ, ebaaha etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani tso lɛ anu.

english: How do my maize plants know when it is the right time to start producing tassels and cobs?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni mi-abele tsei lɛ leɔ be ni sa ni esa akɛ amɛje ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii afeemɔ shishi?

english: Maize plants respond to the length of daylight, warm temperatures, and their own age. Once they collect enough energy and water, they naturally shift from growing leaves to growing cobs.
ga: Abɛi hereɔ hulu la nɔ. hulutsoo ni mli edɔ kɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ afii Kɛ amɛbua hewalɛ kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa naa lɛ, Ebaatsake yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛjɛ baai ni miida lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas on my plot after harvesting maize instead of planting maize again right away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmãa ekoŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients and attracts pests. Cowpeas do a different job by adding nitrogen back into the soil, restoring fertility for the next season.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛdaraa lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai. Cowpeas tsuɔ yiŋtoo kroko he nii kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni ekɛ babaoo aba ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli

english: Why do my cassava plants stay alive in the soil for over a year while my maize plants dry up and die after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nɔ ni fe afi yɛ be mli ni mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize is an annual plant designed to complete its entire life in a few months, whereas cassava is a perennial crop built to store energy in underground roots and stay alive across multiple seasons.
ga: Abɛi ji tso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ daa afi ni afee lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Yɛ be mli ni cassava ji tso ni yeɔ daa lɛ, ama lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli ni ehiɔ shi bei babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves at the bottom of my maize plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leaf growth. The plant starves its older bottom leaves to move available nitrogen to the newer top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Tsei yeɔ hɔmɔ yɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ aya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods change color from green or red to bright yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa pod lɛ su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru kɛtee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods change color to yellow or orange as a natural signal that the beans inside have fully matured, developed their sugar content, and are ready for harvesting.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa. Sugar ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. ni asaa he kɛha kpamɔ

english: Why do my oil palm trees produce mostly male flowers and no fruit bunches during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi hii babaoo ni ewooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Oil palms produce male flowers during dry periods as a survival strategy to save water and energy, delaying fruit bunch creation until moisture returns.
ga: Mu tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni akɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Tsɔɔmɔ aduawai akuu lɛ feemɔ kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why should I plant my crops in straight lines instead of scattering seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni magbɛ dumɔwui ashwã he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines ensures each crop gets equal access to sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, while making weeding, fertilizer application, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi shwiemɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why does my land get hard and dry so quickly after I burn the bush before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbiɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mishã mi jwɛi lɛ dani midu nii sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the protective layer of organic leaf cover and soil organisms that keep ground soft and moist, exposing bare soil to heat which bakes it dry.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni buɔ mɔ he ni ji baai kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni edɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ naa dɔlɛ ni haa egbiɔ.

english: Why do my plantain plants easily fall over in heavy rain even without strong winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli, kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko bɛ po lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches. Rain softens the soil around the shallow roots, making top-heavy plants tip over under their own weight.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ewoɔ aduawai babaoo. Nugbɔ haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ blɛoo, ni ehaa tso ni tsii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etsiimɔ shishi.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before producing any fruit when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ yibii beni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and damages their pollen, preventing successful pollination. Without pollination, the plant sheds the useless flowers to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni efiteɔ pollen lɛ. ehaa pollination lɛ yeee omanye Kɛ́ pollination bɛ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are mature enough to harvest for sale?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa koni akɛhɔ̃ɔ?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting when lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and cracks begin to show in the ground around the base of the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Ni ŋmeii bɔi kpojiemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap from young leaves, or by viral diseases carried by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ amli

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting or decaying shortly after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ loo egboɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams sprout when exposed to warmth and light because they naturally prepare to regrow, while decay happens when minor cuts or bruises during harvest allow fungal infections to enter the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes baakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛwo hulutsoo kɛ la mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛsaa amɛhe koni amɛfee ehee yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Rotting baa kɛji akɛ fãji bibii loo fãji bibii yɛ nikpamɔ be mli ni haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko boteɔ ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize plants stay alive even when the rains stop for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛko otsii fioo komɛi nɛ lɛ?

english: Maize plants have roots that search for hidden moisture deep in the soil, and they roll up their leaves to trap water inside so they can keep growing until the next rain comes.
ga: Abɛi tsei yɛ shishifãi ni taoɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Ni amɛfoɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛkɛ nu ato mli koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baanɛ.

english: Can giving my crops too much water harm them just like giving them too little?
ga: Ani nu ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aye amɛ awui tamɔ nu ni mikɛwoɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Yes, too much water fills up all the air spaces in the soil, which drowns the crop's roots, causes them to rot, and turns the leaves yellow.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu babaoo eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli. ha egbo ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ

english: How are crops like cowpea able to produce beans even when we get very little rainfall?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmei awo ŋmei eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ wɔ?

english: Cowpeas are naturally tough plants with deep roots and small leaves that need very little water to survive, allowing them to make seeds even during light dry spells.
ga: Cowpeas ji tsei ni wa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ kɛ baai bibii ni he hiaa nu fioo ko pɛ koni amɛhi shi. Enɛ haa amɛwoɔ dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni hɔmɔ fioo ko pɛ yeɔ lɛ po.

english: How does a crop take just a little rain water and turn it into food and fruit for me?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nugbɔ nu fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛha mi niyenii kɛ aduawai?

english: Crops use water like blood to carry nutrients from the soil up into their leaves, where sunshine turns those nutrients into food that builds the leaves, grains, and fruits.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ nu tamɔ lá tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya baai lɛ amli. Hulu la tsakeɔ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ ewoɔ niyenii ni feɔ baai, dumɔwui, kɛ aduawai.

english: Why do some of my crops leave behind dry, thin leaves just before the fruits mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi shĩɔ baai ni egbi ni yɔɔ mlɛo dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: As crops mature, they move almost all their stored energy and water out of their old leaves and directly into the fruit or seeds, leaving the leaves to dry up while saving the main harvest.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Amɛjieɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ amɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu ni amɛto lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo lɛ ahe kɛyaa aduawai loo dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ha baai lɛ agbi yɛ be mli ni okwɛɔ nibii titri ni afee lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop during the hottest part of the afternoon even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po?

english: Plantain leaves droop in high heat to hide from direct sunlight and stop water from evaporating too fast; they rest and stand back up when the evening cools down.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni amɛkɛ amɛhe akawo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli, ni amɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ. Amɛjɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛteɔ shi beni amɛhe jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables rot so quickly if I leave them in the sun after picking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli beni mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Once picked, crops can no longer suck water from the ground, so the sun rapidly dries them out and creates heat that attracts bugs and rot.
ga: Kɛji abua Nibii ni adu lɛ anaa lɛ nyɛŋ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, hulu la lɛ haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ oya. ni ekɛ dɔlɛ ni gbalaa kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii baa.

english: How can I stop my harvested maize grains from getting ruined by mold during the damp season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-abele lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni ŋmeii akafite amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: You must dry the maize grains completely in the sun until they are hard before putting them in airtight bags or raised cribs to keep damp air and moisture away.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmãa lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa dani okɛwo vacuum kotokui loo tsɔnei ni akɛwoɔ ŋwɛi ni awo nɔ lɛ amli koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo he.

english: What should I do with the old cassava stalks and dead leaves left on my field after harvest?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee ŋmei tsei momo kɛ baai ni egbi ni eshwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli beni akpa kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Instead of burning them, leave them on the field to break down into the soil, where they act as natural manure to feed your next crop.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshã lɛ, shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli koni efo kɛya shikpɔŋ. He ni amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛkɛhaa onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I cover the soil around their stems with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts like a blanket over the dirt, keeping the soil cool, trapping moisture so it doesn't dry out fast, and slowing down weed growth.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Eŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli koni ekagbi oya. ni eha jwɛi lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo

english: Why do my cocoa pods look fine on the outside, but when I break them open, the beans inside are black and rotten?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ fɛo yɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ? Shi be ni ajie lɛ Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ji ediŋŋ ni egbo?

english: This is often caused by internal fungal infections like Black Pod disease. The fungal spores enter through tiny, unseen cracks or insect bites on the pod surface, and because the inside of the pod is warm and humid, the fungus rapidly rots the beans before the outer husk fully turns dark.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ mli, tamɔ black pod hela kɛbaa. Fungal spores lɛ boteɔ ŋmeii bibii amli. Kplukai ni anaaa loo ni shwieɔ mɔ nɔ yɛ ŋmei lɛ hiɛ Ni akɛni ŋmei lɛ mli mli edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ hewɔ lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ oya dani kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ feɔ duŋ kwraa.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa farm has a disease starting before all my pods get damaged?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ afite?

english: You can spot early signs by regularly checking for small dark brown spots on young green pods, yellowing leaves, or white powdery growth on the stems. Catching these early signs allows you to treat the trees before the disease spreads to the beans inside.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona mra be mli okadii lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ amlipɛimɔ nɔ. Daa yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni tamɔ powder ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ omɔ mra be mli okadii nɛɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ otsaa tso lɛ dani hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli.

english: What actually causes cocoa pods to start rotting while they are still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Pod rot is caused by tiny water molds or fungal spores that thrive in wet, cold, and humid conditions. When rain droplets splash soil or spores onto the pods, the moisture helps the fungus grow directly into the pod husk.
ga: Nu mli ŋmeii bibii kɛ pod rot baa. Aloo fungal spores ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ, ni mli ejɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli beni nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ loo spores lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ. Fɛ̃i haa ŋmeii lɛ daa yɛ pod lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do I see more rot on my cocoa pods when my trees are crowded and have thick leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii babaoo yɛ kookoo ŋmeii anɔ be mli ni mitsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ?

english: Excessive shade and bushy branches trap damp air and moisture inside your farm. Fungus needs continuous moisture to grow, so overgrown trees create the perfect environment for pod rot to spread quickly.
ga: Shade ni fa fe nine kɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Mold biɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli be fɛɛ be dani enyɛ eda. No hewɔ lɛ tsei ni eda fe nine lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni sa kɛha pod rot ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: What should I do with cocoa pods that are already infected with rot on my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kookoo ŋmeii ni tsɛŋemɔ hela emɔ amɛ momo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You should pluck off all diseased pods immediately and bury them outside the farm or burn them. Leaving infected pods hanging on the tree or dropping them on the ground allows rain and wind to carry fungal spores to healthy trees.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ofu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ kpo nɔ loo oshã amɛ. Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ loo okɛshwie shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aŋɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe ŋmeii lɛ kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does planting my cocoa in swampy or low-lying parts of my land make the trees sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu kookoo yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ loo hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ yeɔ hela lɛ?

english: Standing water suffocates cocoa roots and keeps humidity very high around the trunk. Damp, waterlogged soil breeds the fungal pathogens that climb up the trunk and rot lower cocoa pods.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa kookoo shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ amɛhe. Tso lɛ mli kwɔ waa. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ ni ehaa kookoo tso lɛ shishigbɛ fãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: How often should I harvest my ripe cocoa to prevent pods from getting diseased?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa kookoo ni ekwɛ̃ koni ŋmeii lɛ akabote mli?

english: You should harvest ripe pods every two weeks during the main season. Leaving ripe pods on the branch too long makes their husks soft and weak, making it very easy for insects and rot to penetrate the beans inside.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ daa otsii enyɔ yɛ be titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ kɛ gbɔjɔmɔ. Enɛ haa ewaaa kwraa akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi bibii ni egboi lɛ baabote kɔfi yibii lɛ amli.

english: How does spraying copper fungicide help save my cocoa pods from rotting?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ akɔɔble tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite?

english: Copper sprays cover the outside of your cocoa pods with a protective shield. When disease spores land on a sprayed pod, the copper kills the spores before they can break through the husk and ruin the beans inside.
ga: Akɔɔble ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ haa kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ kponɔgbɛ kɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ he. Kɛ́ hela mli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ gbee shi yɛ ŋmeii ni akɛshwie nɔ lɛ anɔ Akɔɔble lɛ gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ dani amɛboteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Can insects like ants or mirids cause my cocoa pods to start rotting inside?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo mirids baanyɛ aha mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ aje shishi amɛgboi yɛ mli?

english: Yes, insects pierce or chew on the pod husk to feed on the sweet juices. These feeding wounds leave small open holes that allow fungal spores from rain or air to easily enter and rot the cocoa beans.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kooloi bibii tsɔɔ loo amɛfoɔ pod lɛ mli koni amɛná nu mli nu. Nɛkɛ niyenii he pilamɔi nɛɛ shĩɔ ŋmeii bibii. No haa ŋmeii ni jɛɔ nugbɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ boteɔ mli ni ehaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Will putting a few rotten cocoa beans together with good ones during fermentation spoil my whole harvest?
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni egboi ni akɛfataa he Kookoo ŋmeii fioo komɛi kɛ kokoo ŋmeii kpakpai komɛi. Ani yɛ ŋmɔtɔ be mli lɛ, ebaafite minibii lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Yes, mixing diseased or rotten beans with healthy ones during fermentation spreads bad fungi and bacteria. This turns the entire batch sour or moldy, resulting in low-quality cocoa that buyers will reject or pay less for.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ loo ni efite lɛ futu dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛhooɔ lɛ, ebaagbɛ ŋmeii kɛ helai fɔji ashwã. Enɛ baaha batch muu lɛ fɛɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa anáa kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ baakpoo loo amɛbaawo nyɔmɔ fioo.

english: Which side of the cassava stem stick should face up when I am planting it in the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ fã esa akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ akwɛ kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Make sure the small raised nodes or buds on the stem stick point upwards toward the sky, because that is where new leafy shoots will grow out toward the sunlight.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni anaaa ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii bibii komɛi. Kɛ́ awó nɔ yɛ ŋshɔkei ko anɔ lɛ, etsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Ejaakɛ jɛmɛ ji he ni ŋmeii heei baaje kpo yɛ hulu la lɛ mli.
