english: How close together should I plant cassava stems on my land to get a good yield?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu ŋmei tsei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni maná yibii kpakpai?

english: Planting cassava stems about 1 meter apart gives each plant enough space, sunlight, and soil nutrients to grow large, healthy roots without competing with its neighbors.
ga: Cassava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni shishifãi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃ ni ekɛ akutsoŋbii lɛ akaŋ akaŋ.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stems to cut for my new farm setup?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mafolɔ kɛha miŋmɔ hee lɛ?

english: Select thick, healthy stems from mature plants that are 8 to 12 months old and show no signs of disease or pest damage on their bark and buds.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni eda ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 ni hela loo tsɛŋemɔ helai efite tsei lɛ ashishi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe tsei ni mli wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during dry periods to save water and protect the food tubers stored under the ground until rain returns.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ŋmeii ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why does cassava manage to grow in poor soil where my maize always dies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ yɛ he ni mi ŋmãa lɛ fɔɔ gbele yɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep, tough root systems that excel at drawing scarce water and nutrients out of tired soils where crops like maize easily starve.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni baanyɛ ajie nu kɛ niyenii ni he ehiaaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ he ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa yeɔ hɔmɔ oya lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cassava plants curling up and twisting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ woɔ amɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ.

english: How often do I need to clear weeds around my cassava farm?
ga: Ehe miihia ni mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ. Shii enyiɛ okwɛɔ ŋmei?

english: You need to weed regularly during the first 3 to 4 months; after that, the cassava canopy grows thick enough to shade out weeds on its own.
ga: Ehe baahia ni okɛ jwɛi lɛ atsu nii daa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ mli, ni no sɛɛ lɛ, jwɛi lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ehe baaha jwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Is cassava a good crop to plant if my family only lets me use the land for one short season?
ga: Ani ŋmei ji ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpa kɛji miweku lɛ ŋmɛɔ mi gbɛ koni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii be kukuoo ko pɛ?

english: Cassava needs 9 to 12 months or longer to mature fully underground, so it requires land you can control for at least a full year.
ga: Cassava heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 loo nɔ ni fe nakai dani ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, ebiɔ he ko ni kɛ hoo lɛ obaanyɛ okudɔ afi muu fɛɛ.

english: Can I plant quick crops like okra or pepper in between my new cassava stems?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ okra loo ŋmɔtɔ oya. Ani abaanyɛ akɛto ŋmei tsei heei ateŋ?

english: Yes, intercropping with quick vegetables works well during the first two months before the cassava grows large branches and blocks the sunlight.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ aduawai du mra lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji enyɔ lɛ mli dani ŋmei lɛ woɔ niji wuji ni etsiɔ hulu lɛ naa.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots underground are big enough to harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is ready to harvest when the bottom leaves fall off, the main stem turns woody, and the ground around the base of the plant starts cracking open.
ga: Cassava efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ gbee shi. Tso titri lɛ tsɔɔ tso. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade to survive because their delicate leaves scorch easily under direct sun. Leaving mature shade trees or planting shade crops creates a cooler environment and keeps the soil moist while the young cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ taoɔ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo hulutsoo tsei ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: When is the best time for me to plant new cocoa seedlings on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best time to plant seedlings is at the start of the main rainy season, usually around May or June in Ghana. Planting early gives the young roots several months of steady rainfall to establish deeply before the harsh, dry Harmattan season arrives.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛduɔ dumɔwui ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ May loo June mli yɛ Ghana. Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Ehaa shishifãi bibii lɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be nyɔji babaoo dani Harmattan be ni mli wa ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ baashɛ.

english: This blackening is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives and spreads rapidly in cold, wet, and humid weather. Trimming overgrown branches lets sunlight and air flow through the farm, which dries out the moisture and reduces the fungus.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ duŋ nɛɛ baa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ shihilɛi amli. Niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ aba shi.

english: Why are ants building nests on my cocoa trees, and are they damaging my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii miitswa amɛ ŋmeii yɛ mi koko tso lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni ani amɛfiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Ants are usually drawn to tiny insects called mealybugs that suck sap from your cocoa trees. While the ants themselves might not eat the tree, they protect the mealybugs, which can spread the destructive Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii sumɔɔ ŋmeii bibii. Atsɛɔ amɛ mealybugs, ni nuɔ kookoo tsei amli nu lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ekolɛ ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ yeee tso lɛ moŋ, shi amɛbuɔ he kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ji mealybugs lɛ ahe. ni baanyɛ agbɛ cocoa bud hela ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen in the soil. Heavy rains can wash nutrients deep underground away from the roots, so applying nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my land is good enough for growing healthy cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa kɛha kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ dumɔ?

english: Good cocoa soil should be deep, dark, soft, and easy for roots to penetrate, while allowing excess rainwater to drain away easily. Soil that turns into hard clay, stays flooded like a swamp, or is very rocky will cause cocoa roots to rot or stall.
ga: Esa akɛ kookoo shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ afee nɔ ni mli kwɔ, ni eyɛ ediŋŋ, ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ abote mli oya. Kɛtsɔ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ehoɔ oya lɛ nɔ. shikpɔŋ ni ebatsɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa Nu afua ba tamɔ ŋshɔ. Aloo tɛi babaoo ni oyɔɔ lɛ baaha kookoo shishifãi lɛ agbo loo amɛfee ais.

english: Why should I cut off the small extra shoots growing at the bottom of my cocoa tree trunks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Those extra shoots, called chupons, act like freeloaders that steal water and food from the main trunk. Removing them forces the tree to direct all its energy into growing big leaves, flowers, and healthy pods higher up.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ amɛhe, ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli. Amɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo baai wuji, fɔfɔii, kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa.

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa trees falling off before they turn into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ anɔkwa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the tree is stressed by drought, poor soil nutrients, or insect attacks like capsids. Ensuring the trees have adequate shade, water, and protection from pests helps the flowers mature into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hɔmɔ ha tso lɛ hao. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni tutuaa amɛ, tamɔ capsids. Kɛ́ akwɛ koni tso lɛ aná hulutsoo, nu, kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing far fewer pods now than they did five years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso momo lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo fioo fe afii enumɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 25 years, their natural vigor declines, soil nutrients get exhausted, and old branches carry disease. Heavy pruning, adding fertilizer, or gradually replanting with improved hybrid seedlings can bring yields back up.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao tsei ye afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, amɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ baa shi. Niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baafite. Ni niji ni egbɔ lɛ kɛ hela baa. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi waa, ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, loo ni akɛ dumɔwui ni afee lɛ srɔtoi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ aduɔ ekoŋŋ fiofio. baanyɛ ekɛ nibii ni anáa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba

english: Can I plant cassava right next to my young cocoa trees on the same plot?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ kookoo tsei ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: It is better to avoid planting cassava close to young cocoa because cassava roots are very aggressive and drain all the water and nutrients out of the soil. This starves the young cocoa plants and slows down their growth.
ga: Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo bibii lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ basabasa waa ni amɛjieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa cacao tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa edaaa oya.

english: If I secure land to start farming today, which crops grow quickly enough so I can harvest within a few months?
ga: Kɛji akɛ miná shikpɔŋ ni mikɛje okwaayeli shishi ŋmɛnɛ Mɛɛ tsei baakwɛ̃ oya bɔ ni sa ni abaakpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli?

english: Short-duration crops like maize, tomatoes, pepper, and vegetables take between 3 to 4 months to yield, allowing you to get quick returns compared to tree crops like cocoa or oil palm which take years.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ ŋmãa, tomato, ŋmãa kɛ aduawai heɔ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 ni ekɛbaatsu nii, ni ehaa onine shɛɔ oya kɛ akɛto afi mli nibii tamɔ kookoo loo mu ŋmãa ni heɔ afii babaoo lɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves but give me small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are shaded by trees, cassava puts all its energy into growing stem and leaves above ground instead of sending nutrients down to swell the roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei ewo tsei ahe ŋmɔlɔ. Yucca kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye níhi kɛ baa si konɛ e ha nɛ sisifã ɔmɛ nɛ a tsɔ.

english: Why does planting the exact same crop on my farm every single year make the harvest smaller each time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ji ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ? afi lɛ mli, ni ehaa nikpamɔ lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Growing one crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the earth, which weakens future harvests unless you rotate crops.
ga: Tso kome ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ lɛ Ebaafite niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmaakpamɔi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Ja otsake ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Can I plant groundnuts together with my maize, or will they fight each other in the soil?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa? Aloo amɛbaawu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Groundnuts and maize actually help each other; groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and feed the soil, which naturally fertilizes the maize while keeping weeds down.
ga: Peanuts kɛ ŋmãa yeɔ ebuaa amɛhe diɛŋtsɛ. Peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be mli ni egbeɔ jwɛi lɛ.

english: How do I know if my newly acquired land has healthy soil for crop roots to spread?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ hee ni miná lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã?

english: Healthy soil is dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture without becoming swampy, and is full of earthworms which loosen the soil for roots to breathe and spread.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã lɛ eyi mli obɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crops curl up tightly during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up inward to reduce their surface area exposed to heat, which acts as a defense mechanism to stop water from evaporating out of the plant too fast.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ mli koni ekɛba ŋmãa ni hulutsoo baa lɛ shi. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ nu naa koni ekajɛ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants dropping off without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Hot dry winds or irregular watering stress pepper plants, causing them to shed their flowers to save water and survival energy instead of producing fruit.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa ni mli egbi loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi yɛ yibii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and stop growing when there is too much heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excess standing water fills all air spaces in the soil, effectively drowning the roots so they cannot breathe or absorb nitrogen, which turns the leaves yellow.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu loo amɛhe nitrogen. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, won't I get more harvest from my small piece of land?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Mi nɔ loo daabi?

english: Planting too close creates fierce competition for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing crops to grow thin and weak with smaller yields than properly spaced plants.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daa ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo fe tsei ni akɛ amɛ ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than the actual crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei diɛŋtsɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive tough conditions, so their root systems steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight away from domestic crops far more aggressively.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ basabasa babaoo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ shia tsei amli lɛ jumɔ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and curling up during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves curl and turn yellow when exposed to direct, harsh sunlight without sufficient shade. Young trees need shade crops like plantain or shade trees to shield them from intense heat until they mature.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ baakumɔ ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ tɛ̃ɛ, hulu la ni naa wa ni hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ mli. Tsei bibii lɛ he miihia tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Koni akɛbu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he kɛyashi tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale yellow starting from the tip down the middle of the leaf?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing down the center of maize leaves usually means the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main plant nutrient needed for leaf growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves regain their deep green color.
ga: Abɛi baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ adara Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I see small holes in my maize leaves and sawdust-like powder inside the plant core?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmãa ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: The sawdust-like substance is produced by stem borer caterpillars feeding inside the stem. Catching this early allows you to apply appropriate pest control before the caterpillar damages the main growing shoot.
ga: Nɛkɛ nɔ ni tamɔ tso lɛ mli sũ nɛɛ ji nɔ ni stem borers ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ feɔ. Ni ooomɔ lɛ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oyeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ dani ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii titrii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground even when the leaves above look green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when planted in waterlogged soil that does not drain well. While the top stem can handle rainy conditions, water trapped around the roots cuts off air and causes the tubers to decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ ni nu shwieee nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi tso lɛ baanyɛ adamɔ nugbɔ shihilɛi anaa moŋ. Shi nu lɛ kpɛtɛ ehe Shishifãi lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehaa bulb lɛ fiteɔ.

english: What happens to my yam tubers if I leave the vines to grow on the ground instead of staking them?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi wain tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni makɛ stake awo mli?

english: Yam vines need to climb stakes so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to build large tubers. Leaving vines on the ground exposes leaves to hot soil and diseases, resulting in much smaller yields.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso ko nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee bulbs agboi. Kɛ́ ashi wain tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ helai yeɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ faaa kwraa.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the small shoots growing around my main plantain tree remain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ? ni miida yɛ Midumɔwu titri lɛ he lɛ eshwɛ.

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow creates competition for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Pruning extra suckers so only one or two remain ensures the main plant grows strong and yields large fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaaha akaŋshii aba kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ koni tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ daa waa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when daytime temperatures get too high or when water supply is inconsistent. Providing regular watering and light shade during heatwaves helps the flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants crinkling and twisting up into small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ egbɔjɔ ni etsɔ kɔɔpoi bibii amli lɛ?

english: Crinkled pepper leaves are caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or viruses spread by them. Managing these insects early stops the leaves from curling and keeps the plant producing peppers.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni egbɔjɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing large green leaves but not forming tight heads in the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ehiɛɛɛ eyitso teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to head when they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or irregular water. Balanced feeding and steady moisture encourage the plant to fold its inner leaves tightly into a firm head.
ga: Cabbage nyɛŋ ajie eyitso kɛji enine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ loo akɛ nu haa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Niyenii ni ja kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ebaai lɛ shwieɔ emli jogbaŋŋ ni efeɔ bulb ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the dry soil around my crops with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he? ŋmɔshi nibii ni jwɛi loo baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, keeps moisture from evaporating in the sun, cools the root area, and suppresses weed growth.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ akatsɔ hulu la lɛ mli. Ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ ni etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and drying up early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for growth, or that excess water around the roots is preventing the plant from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ loo nu ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekaye niyenii.

english: What makes some rice plants produce many stems while others produce only a few?
ga: Mɛni haa omɔ tsei komɛi woɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ?

english: Rice plants produce extra stems, called tillers, when they have enough space between plants, sufficient nitrogen fertilizer early on, and proper water depth in the field.
ga: Omɔ tsei woɔ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ tillers lɛ kɛ́ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ kɛjɛ shishijee. kɛ bɔ ni nu lɛ mli kwɔ ha ni sa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil for too long during heavy rains, creating a wet environment that allows destructive fungi to attack and break down the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ewo fɔ baa ni haa ŋmei ni fiteɔ nii lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni efiteɔ amɛ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up to catch direct sunlight, which gives the plant maximum energy to build large underground tubers while keeping the leaves away from soil disease.
ga: Staking Wo sweet potato baa lɛ nɔ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ ohe tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees burn and die when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ shã ni egbo beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to full sunlight and high heat. They need temporary shade from larger trees or food crops like plantains to keep cool and hold moisture in their leaves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains adɛŋ koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli.

english: What causes my plantain trees to fall over easily once the fruit bunch starts growing?
ga: Mɛni haa mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya beni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantains fall over because tiny worms called nematodes or stem borer pests attack their shallow roots and stem base, making the plant too weak to hold up the heavy bunch.
ga: Mikɛ ekãa migbee shi yɛ ŋmei bibioo ko hewɔ. Ale amɛ akɛ nematodes loo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ tso lɛ, amɛtutuaa shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ etsu ŋmeii ni tsii ahe nii.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies, or it can be the plant's natural reaction to conserve water during extreme heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Aloo ebaanyɛ efee adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni tsei feɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu he yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress, extreme dryness, or sudden heavy rains, which causes the plant to protect itself by shedding flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo latsaa he haomɔ mli. ŋmɔlɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa trukaa Enɛ haa tso lɛ buɔ ehe kɛtsɔ efɔfɔi ni ekɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas in my field help improve the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to a family of crops that pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas fata tsei akuu ko ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What is eating holes into the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing whorl (funnel) of the young maize plant and feeds on the tender expanding leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni miida lɛ amli ŋmeii (cones) lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa blɛoo lɛ.

english: What is 'blast' disease, and why does it destroy my young crops so quickly?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘blight’ hela ni mɛni hewɔ efiteɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Blast' is a fast-spreading fungal disease that commonly attacks crops like rice and maize. It produces spots on leaves and rots the stems or roots, making young plants wither and pull out of the ground easily before they can mature.
ga: Blast’ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni bei pii lɛ etutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa baai lɛ anɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ shishi loo shishifã lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni amɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my young seedlings suddenly collapse and die right after coming out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛje kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by soil-borne fungal diseases (commonly called damp-off). Excessive moisture and poor soil drainage create a breeding ground for fungi that attack the soft, tender stems of new seedlings right at the soil level.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa ŋmeii ni tutuaa dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɔɔ yɛ.

english: What simple steps can I take to stop diseases from entering my farm before my crops get sick?
ga: Ma nyɛ ma nyɛɛ blɔ nya tomi komɛ a nɔ. Mɛni abaanyɛ afee koni helai akabote ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hela?

english: You can prevent diseases by using certified disease-resistant seeds, clearing weeds that harbor pests, rotating your crops every season, and burning or burying infected plants away from your field so sickness doesn't spread.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsi hela naa kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yɔɔ mli lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa be. ni oshã loo ofu tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ oŋmɔji lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ. Koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã

english: Why do the flowers on my crop drop off without turning into fruit or grain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai loo dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Flowers often fall off due to stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, lack of essential nutrients, or pest damage. When a plant is stressed, it sheds flowers to conserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Bei pii lɛ fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi yɛ haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, kɛ niyenii ni he hia ni bɛ. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai akpãtãa Kɛ́ tsei miihao Efɔɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: How can observing the flowers on my crops help me know if my harvest will be good?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ ni mikwɛɔ lɛ baaye abua mi ni male kɛji mikpamɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi?

english: Flowers are the reproductive organs of the plant. Healthy, abundant flowers indicate proper nutrition and good pollination by insects or wind, which directly leads to more pods, ears, or fruits forming.
ga: Fɔfɔi ji tsei fɔmɔ nibii. Fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa babaoo lɛ tsɔɔ niyenii ni sa kɛ fɔfɔi kpakpai ni kooloi loo kɔɔyɔɔ kɛbaa lɛ. Enɛ kɛ pods, toi loo aduawai babaoo baa tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow even when I am giving them water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is starving for key nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is waterlogged, which smothers the roots and prevents them from breathing and absorbing food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni ehaaa amɛmu ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu niyenii.

english: Why does planting my seeds just a few weeks late reduce my crop yield so much?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ sɛɛ otsii fioo pɛ lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi waa lɛ?

english: Crops rely on a precise balance of rainfall, sunlight, and cooler soil to grow. Delayed planting forces plants to flower and set fruit during harsher, drier weather, which stunts their growth and reduces yields.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nugbɔshiimɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ nɔ, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ koni amɛ dara. Kɛ́ adu nii asɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ mli egbi ni mli wa waa lɛ. Enɛ haaa dalɛ aya hiɛ ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: How does spacing my crops too close together cause diseases to spread faster?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni gbɛ ni kã miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ abɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ aha helai agbɛ ashwã oya?

english: Overcrowded crops block air circulation and sunlight. Moisture gets trapped between the leaves, creating a damp environment where fungal spores thrive and jump quickly from plant to plant.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la naa. Fɛ̃i ni tsiɔ baai lɛ ateŋ ni haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa Biɛ ji he ni fungal spores lɛ daa ni amɛjoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ oya.

english: What key signs should I look for on my sick crops before calling an agricultural extension officer?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii ni he hiaa esa akɛ matao yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli dani matsɛ okwaayeli he nitsumɔ he nitsulɔ?

english: Check for visible symptoms like unusual leaf spots, white or dark powders on stems, strange insect holes, stunted growth, or rotting roots. Bringing a fresh sample of an affected leaf helps the officer diagnose the problem accurately.
ga: Kwɛmɔ okadii ni anaa tamɔ baai lɛ ahe ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa. Powda yɛŋ loo ediŋŋ ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ, kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ, shishifãi ni edaaa loo shishifãi ni egboɔ Baai ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe nɔkwɛmɔnii heei ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa onukpai lɛ ni amɛnaa naagba lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell the difference between a crop suffering from bad weather and one infected by a pest or disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni naa wa efite lɛ kɛ nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ hela ko loo hela ko emɔ lɛ teŋ?

english: Weather damage usually affects almost every plant across the field equally (such as widespread wilting in a drought). Pests and diseases typically start in smaller patches or target specific parts of the plant, like individual leaves or stem bases.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi saa nɔ ni miihe ashɛ tso fɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ (tamɔ shwiemɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli). Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai jeɔ shishi yɛ hei bibii. loo ekɛ ehiɛ afɔ tso lɛ fãi pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ, tamɔ baai aŋkroaŋkroi loo eshishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are drowning in too much water. Applying the right fertilizer or manure gives the plant the food it needs to turn green and produce a good yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen he miihia oŋmɔshi nii lɛ, loo shishifãi lɛ ebote nu babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from heat stress, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil moist and adding compost helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they can turn into healthy peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe bɔni afee ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my farm soil get hard and dry very quickly even after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni egbiɔ oya waa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil dries out quickly when it lacks organic matter to act like a sponge. Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool and helps it hold water longer for your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni baaha etsu nii tamɔ sponji. Kɛ́ okɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ onibii amli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with many leaves but small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ, ni eyɛ baai babaoo, shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much leaf-growing fertilizer without enough root-building nutrients, they put all their energy into top leaves instead of storing energy in the roots to make big tubers.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa baai lɛ daa lɛ babaoo ni niyenii ni haa shishifãi lɛ maa shi lɛ bɛ mli lɛ, Amɛkudɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ he wami ngɛ tso ɔ sisije ɔmɛ a mi konɛ e pee bulb nguahi.

english: Why do tiny worms keep eating holes in my crops early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii sumɔɔ ni amɛye miŋmɔshi nibii mra lɛ?

english: Insects like fall armyworms feed on tender green leaves during cooler hours to grow. Catching them early and applying natural sprays like neem leaf extract or recommended chemicals stops them before they ruin your harvest.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ fall armyworms yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛdara. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofai ni ajieɔ yi lɛ atsu nii. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite onibii.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, won't I get more harvest from my plot?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close causes the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and food to produce larger, healthier yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants wilting and dying even when the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: Wilting in wet soil is often caused by soil diseases that attack and rot the roots, preventing them from taking up water. Rotating your crops each season prevents these diseases from living in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ helai ni tutuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ, ni no haa amɛnyɛŋ amɛmɔmɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai nɛɛ akahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my maize so it does not spoil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? No hewɔ lɛ, egbooo?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the outer husks turn brown and dry, and the grains become hard. Harvesting too early causes mold, while waiting too long allows pests and birds to destroy the crop.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi. ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa Nikpamɔ mra tsɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mɛmɔ be kakadaŋŋ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ okpoi fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant cowpeas or beans alongside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that pull nitrogen food out of the air and put it into the soil. This naturally feeds the neighboring crops and keeps the soil rich for future seasons.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why does leaving weeds in my field reduce the total amount of food I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa niyenii fɛɛ ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm by drinking the water and stealing the soil food intended for your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to produce a full harvest.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ nu ni amɛnuɔ kɛ niyenii ni amɛjuɔ yɛ sũ mli kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo amɛŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know when the soil is ready for me to plant my maize at the start of the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu ŋmãa yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Wait for the first two or three steady rains so the ground is soaked deep down. Planting in dry soil after just one light shower can scorch your seeds when the hot sun comes back out.
ga: Mɛɛ klɛŋklɛŋ bei fioo ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Tu kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ ashã kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds too close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kome mli lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots fight over the same water and plant food in the soil, and their leaves block each other from sunlight. Giving them proper space lets each crop grow bigger and yield more food.
ga: Kɛ tsei ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kome kɛ tsei niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni amɛbaai lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu he. He ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso daa ni ewoɔ niyenii babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava turning yellow and falling off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nutrients like nitrogen, or it is suffering from drought or pest attacks. Adding compost or manure around the base of the plant feeds it and keeps the leaves healthy.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, loo hɔmɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui miigba enaa. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii baafata he kɛbɔle Shishitoo lɛ he lɛ baaha niyenii aba ni eye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on instead of just growing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛkɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to lift their leaves up toward full sunlight. The more sunlight the leaves catch, the more energy the plant produces to grow larger tubers under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Babaoo ni hulu la ni baa lɛ naa lɛ, tso lɛ baajie hewalɛ babaoo kpo ni ekɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops, and why must I remove them quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi lɛ oya lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that quickly steal water, sunlight, and nutrients meant for your crops. Removing them early ensures all the nourishment in the soil goes directly into your crop's growth.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛju nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ oya. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ haa niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yaa tsei lɛ adalɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my crops get more diseases when I plant maize on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa helai babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Pests and fungal diseases that attack maize live in the soil and build up in number when maize is always planted there. Switching to crops like groundnuts or beans starves those pests and restores nutrients to the soil.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmeii ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛbuaa amɛhe naa babaoo kɛ́ adu ŋmãa be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nakai kooloi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some of the seeds I saved from last year's harvest fail to sprout when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi nikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their strength if stored in warm, damp places where insects or mold can reach them. Keeping dried seeds in cool, sealed containers with wood ash protects them so they sprout reliably.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baaje mli kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ he ni kooloi loo ŋmeii baanyɛ ashɛ he. Dumɔwui ni egbi ni akɛtoɔ tsɛnsi ko ni mli ejɔ mli ni akɛ tso sũ tsiɔ naa lɛ baabu dumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛnyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my tomato plants are getting too much water or not enough during hot weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo amɛmiiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: If leaves droop and feel dry to the touch, the plant needs water. If leaves turn pale yellow and the stem feels soft or rotted, the roots are drowning in too much standing water.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ gbee shi ni enu he akɛ egbi kɛji akɛ ota he. Etsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia tso lɛ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo loo egbo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ ebote nu ni yɔɔ dioo lɛ mli tsɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my maize so it doesn't spoil in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? No hewɔ lɛ, egbooo yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the outer cob husks turn dry and papery white, and the silk at the tip turns dark brown. Leaving it in the field past this stage exposes it to birds, rain mold, and insects.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ feɔ eyɛŋ tamɔ wolo ni egbi lɛ. ni siliki ni yɔɔ naagbee lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ. Kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaagbala okpoi, ŋmeii, kɛ kooloi bibii.

english: What causes my harvested grains to rot or get destroyed by insects inside my storage bags?
ga: Mɛni haa dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ loo kooloi ni yɔɔ mi-nitoo kotokui lɛ amli lɛ fiteɔ amɛ?

english: Grains rot when they are bagged before being completely sun-dried, as moisture breeds mold and heat. Insects also hatch from tiny eggs if grains aren't clean and kept in airtight bags or treated storage containers.
ga: Ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ akɛwo kotoku mli dani agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulutsoo be lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dɔlɛ aba. Kplukai hu fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ wɔji bibii amli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmaa lɛ he tseee ni akɛto vacuum kotokui amli loo nibii ni akɛtoɔ nibii ni atsa mli lɛ amli lɛ,.

english: Why do people recommend planting beans together with my maize on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans capture natural nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, which feeds the maize plant and helps it grow taller and greener without requiring as much expensive commercial fertilizer.
ga: Beans lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhiɛɔ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni jarayeli ŋmãa ni jara wa waa he ehiaaa amɛ.

english: Will planting beans between my rows of maize make the two crops fight for sunlight and water?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mi-abɛi lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaha tsei enyɔ lɛ abɔi hulu la kɛ nu he akaŋ?

english: When spaced correctly, maize grows tall to catch sunlight while beans stay low to shade the ground, which actually helps preserve moisture in the soil for both plants.
ga: Kɛji akɛ he ni jɛkɛmɔ lɛ sa lɛ, Abɛi daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, akɛ ŋmeii lɛ toɔ shi koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni no yeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi kɛhaa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Can growing beans alongside my maize help reduce insect pests on my farm?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, mixing beans with maize creates a mixed plant canopy that confuses pests like stalk borers, making it much harder for them to find and destroy your main maize crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmãa lɛ haa tsei ni efutu ni futuɔ ŋmeii tamɔ stem borers lɛ, ni ehaa ewaa kwraa kɛhaa amɛ akɛ amɛaana ŋmãa titri ni oduɔ lɛ ni amɛfite.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen or getting too much water, preventing the roots from taking up essential nutrients from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen loo eená nu babaoo. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my bean plants produce plenty of flowers, but many fall off without forming bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi tsei babaoo gbeeɔ shi ni amɛwooo ŋmeii?

english: Bean flowers drop off when the crop experiences sudden heat stress or drought, causing the plant to save its energy rather than produce seeds.
ga: Pea fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei na dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ trukaa. Enɛ haa tsei kwɛɔ hewalɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo dumɔwui.

english: Why does my maize crop grow weak and fall over whenever a strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni egbeeɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ?

english: Maize stalks become weak and fall over if the plants are planted too close together or if the soil lacks key nutrients like potassium, which hardens the stem structure.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni no baaha tso lɛ shishi tsɔne lɛ mli awa.

english: Why is it bad if I put three or four seeds in a single planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ wo dumɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole causes the seedlings to crowd each other out for light, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak plants that yield very small cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ abua amɛhe naa ni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ baa.

english: How do I know the correct distance to leave between my maize rows?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni sa ni kã ŋmãa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Leaving about two to three feet between maize rows ensures each plant gets enough air circulation and sunlight while leaving enough space for you to weed and care for the crop easily.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee ninetalɔi 2-3 lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ hulu la. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eshiɔ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ okɛjie jwɛi lɛ oya ni okwɛ onibii anɔ.

english: How can I easily tell that my maize is mature enough to harvest from the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the outer husks dry completely and turn brown, and the kernels become hard enough that pressing them with your fingernail leaves no dent.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ egbi kwraa ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ wa bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ okɛ onineshi tsɔne lɛ anyɛ nɔ ni okɛ ŋmeii akafee.

english: Why must I dry my beans thoroughly in the sun before putting them into storage sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbi mi-kɔfi ŋmɔji lɛ kwraa dani mikɛwo kotokui amli lɛ?

english: If beans are stored while still holding moisture, mold will rot the crop and grain beetles will quickly multiply, destroying your stored harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ to be mli ni amɛmli edɔ lolo lɛ, Mold haa ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ ni dumɔwui amli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ babaoo oya. ni fiteɔ nibii ni okɛto lɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field with full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to strong direct sunlight and high heat. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees to shelter them from burning and to keep soil moisture high while their roots grow strong.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ aya hiɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plant is starving for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or well-decayed animal manure will help the leaves regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛná amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees always fall over when heavy winds blow during the fruiting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ yaa nɔ egbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ yibiiwoo be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and heavy fruit bunches, making them top-heavy. Propping up the main stem with strong bamboo or wooden forks prevents the wind from knocking them over before harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. kɛ muji babaoo baa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsei loo tsei ni akɛfee ŋmei tsu nii kɛfi tso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ akatswa lɛ shi dani akpa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when water sits on my farm for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni nu ehi miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi nɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water, the roots suffocate and harmful fungal rot develops, which is why planting on raised mounds or ridges helps drain water away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi. Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui baaje kpo. Enɛ hewɔ ni dumɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants drying up and falling off before producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when soil moisture fluctuates wildly, or when insects fail to pollinate them. Mulching around the roots and regular watering keeps the plant cool enough to hold its flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ waa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee pollination Mulching around Shishifãi kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa koni ehiɛ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to lift my yam vines onto wooden stakes instead of letting them crawl on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ woɔ tso nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much direct sunlight as possible to build large underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves into the sun and prevents soil-borne diseases from attacking wet leaves on the ground.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la mli ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akatutua baai ni efɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: If I plant cowpeas in the same field as my maize, will they steal food from the maize plants?
ga: Kɛji midu tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ Ani tsina ŋmãa baaju niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmãa tsei amli?

english: No, cowpeas actually feed the soil. Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the earth, which helps nourish the surrounding maize plants when spaced correctly.
ga: Dabi, tsina ŋmeii yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmãa tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ niyenii. Kɛji akɛ ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the deep inner leaves of my young maize plants overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: This is likely the fall armyworm, a pest that burrows into the leaf whorl where new leaves grow. Applying recommended control treatments directly into the funnel of the maize plant kills the caterpillars before they destroy the plant's growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛ ji fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ. Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni shwieɔ baai lɛ amli he ni baai heei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ni akɛba lɛ wo ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do seeds I saved from my last maize harvest yield much less than certified seeds I buy from the agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni mihe kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred hybrids designed for maximum strength and yield in their first generation. When you plant seeds saved from that harvest, the hybrid traits split, producing weaker plants with smaller cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ji dumɔwui ni afee amɛ srɔtoi ni afee amɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ babaoo kɛ yibiiwoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ Hybrid sui lɛ baafite. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnáa ŋmeii bibii.

english: What happens if I put chemical fertilizer on my crops right before a heavy rain falling?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ fata miŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani nugbɔ nɛ waa?

english: Heavy rainfall will sweep the fertilizer away in surface water runoff or wash it too deep into the soil for the roots to reach. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after rain, not right before a storm.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsɔɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ loo efoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Jeee dani ahum lɛ baatswa amrɔ nɔŋŋ

english: Young cocoa plants have soft leaves that easily burn under direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted next to them to block excess sun and keep the soil moist while the young roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Bɔni afee ni hulu la ni tsoɔ fe nine lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni shishifãi bibii lɛ mli wa lolo lɛ

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaf tips on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main food plants use to stay green and build strong stalks, so adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves stay green and produce large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ni amɛma amɛshishifãi ni wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do I know which direction to plant my cassava stem cuttings into the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava ŋmɔtɔi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stems have small buds or 'eyes' where the new leaves sprout. You must always plant the stem with these buds pointing upwards toward the sky so the plant grows straight up without wasting energy.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘ŋmeii’ ni baai heei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mli. Esa akɛ odu tso lɛ shishi be fɛɛ be ni eshishifã lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Koni tso lɛ adara tɛ̃ɛ ni efiteee hewalɛ

english: What is causing small holes and saw-dust dirt inside the center leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Ni sũ ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central shoot (whorl) of the maize plant to eat the soft new leaves before the corn cob can form.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii (rings) amli koni amɛye ŋmeii bibii heei dani ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ afee.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without forming fruit when the weather becomes too hot or when the soil lacks enough moisture. Extreme heat stresses the plant and prevents the flower from pollinating correctly.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ bɔ ni sa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crops with dry grass and fallen leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he sũ? Nibii ni jwɛi gboi kɛ baai ni egbee shi yɔɔ mli?

english: Covering the ground (mulching) acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation during dry days, and prevents weeds from taking light and food away from your crops.
ga: Mulching (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Ha nu lɛ mli shwiemɔ aba shi yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekajie la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why do I need to place tall wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to spread out high up in the sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking also lifts leaves off the damp soil to protect them from rot and ground diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni ená hewalɛ ni akɛbaakwɛ bulbs lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni ekɛtsi ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ anaa.

english: Why shouldn't I put chemical fertilizer on my farm when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need water to dissolve so plant roots can safely drink them up. Applying fertilizer on dry soil can burn the crop roots and kill the plant instead of helping it grow.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu amɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso shishifãi ni egbe tso lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye ebua lɛ ni eda

english: Why is it bad practice for me to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ gbonyo akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the field, leading to poorer harvests over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why is it better for me to water my pepper plants at the root instead of pouring water over the top of the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ nu yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni mafɔse nu yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Wet leaves stay damp for a long time, creating a warm, moist home for fungal diseases and spots to sprout on the plant. Watering directly at the roots keeps the foliage dry and healthy.
ga: Baai ni efɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli be kakadaŋŋ. Ehaa shia ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ kɛhaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow fast, or when too much water in the soil drowns the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni biɔ ni tsei ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Aloo be mli ni nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli.

english: Why does my maize crop grow very tall and thin without making big cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni efeee ŋmãa wuji lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants compete with each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, causing them to grow tall and weak instead of putting energy into developing big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji lɛ najiaŋ.

english: How do I know when my maize is fully ripe and ready for harvesting as dry grain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa akɛ ŋmãa ni egbi?

english: Maize is ready for dry harvest when the leaves and husks turn completely brown, the seeds become hard, and a small black mark appears at the tip where each kernel attaches to the cob.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni egbi beni baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa, ŋmeii lɛ mli wa ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii diji. Ejeɔ kpo yɛ naagbee he ni dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko kpɛtɛɔ ŋmei lɛ he lɛ.

english: What is the difference between a chemical that kills weeds and one that kills insects on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Herbicides (weedkillers) are designed to destroy unwanted grass and weeds around your crops, while insecticides are made specifically to kill insect pests that eat your leaves and fruit.
ga: herbicide (Herbicides) lɛ ji nɔ ni afee koni ekɛfite jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni ataooo ni bɔle oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ, yɛ be mli ni afee tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni ekɛgbe kooloi ni yeɔ obaai kɛ oyibii lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to spray chemical pesticides right before it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaafɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ anɔ dani nugbɔ anɛ lɛ?

english: Rain washes the chemical off the plant leaves before it has time to work, which wastes your money and can wash dangerous chemicals into nearby rivers or soil.
ga: Nugbɔ shwieɔ tsofai kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli dani be ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ shɛɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ shika, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara awo faai loo shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to wear protective gear like boots and masks when spraying my farm with chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo nibii ni buɔ mɔ he tamɔ atadei kɛ mask lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Farm chemicals can enter your body through your skin, eyes, or breath, which can cause long-term chest problems, skin burning, or severe illness over time.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ abote ogbɔmɔtso lɛ mli kɛtsɔ ohewolo, ohiŋmɛii, loo omumɔ nɔ, ni baanyɛ ekɛ naagbai ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ, shãa, loo hela ni naa wa aba ogbɔmɔtso lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do pests keep destroying my crops even after I spray them with agrochemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai yaa nɔ efiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ okwaayeli tsofai shwieɔ shi moŋ.

english: Pests can build resistance if you use the exact same chemical all the time, or you might be spraying at the wrong time of day when insects are hiding under leaves.
ga: Tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii be fɛɛ be lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aná hewalɛ ni teɔ shi woɔ hela lɛ. Aloo obaanyɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ yɛ be ni esaaa mli beni kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up during the hottest time of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Leaves roll up as a natural defense to protect themselves from intense heat and slow down the amount of water escaping from the plant into the air.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on the same land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ beni mikpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts naturally put nutrients back into the soil through their roots, which refreshes the field after heavy-feeding crops like maize have used up the soil's strength.
ga: Nuts kɛ peanuts lɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa jɛmɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ beni niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa, efite shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ sɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are sick from a disease or just drying up from heat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji helai miiye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ loo amɛmiigbi kɛkɛ kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ mli?

english: Plants drying from heat will bounce back and look fresh once temperatures cool down in the evening, whereas plants sick with a disease will show spots, yellow rings, or rot that stay no matter the time of day.
ga: Tsei ni egbi kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ mli lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ amɛ kɛ́ latsaa lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baajie ŋmɔtɔ kpo. eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ekɔɔɔ he eko gbi lɛ mli be

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen. Nitrogen is essential for growth, and when soil runs low, the plant pulls food from its older bottom leaves to keep the new top leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Nitrogen he miihia waa kɛha dalɛ. Ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ fioo pɛ eshwɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli koni amɛkwɛ ŋwɛi baai heei.

english: Why do my cassava plants have lush, big leaves but produce very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen and not enough potassium from the soil, it spends all its energy producing leaves above ground instead of sending energy down to swell the underground tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa jɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaa baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni eeetsu kɛba shi koni eha ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I avoid putting dry fertilizer on my soil when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni mikɛaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he beni egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve so that crop roots can absorb it. Applying dry fertilizer to dry soil leaves the nutrients trapped on the surface, and intense heat can burn plant roots.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baanyɛ aha tso shishifãi ashã.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily burn under intense sunlight. Fast-growing plantain leaves act as natural umbrellas, shielding young cocoa trees with shade and humidity until they grow strong.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain baai ni daa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashi tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to put stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high up to catch sunlight so they can manufacture food for tuber growth, while keeping the leaves off damp ground to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ koni ekɛ niyenii aha tuber lɛ dalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akashɛ ohe.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as severe heat, dry soil, or poor nutrient levels. The plant drops flowers to save its own energy when conditions are tough.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ. Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhewalɛ he kɛji shihilɛi lɛ mli wa.

english: Why is water so critical during the exact week my maize starts showing silks and tassels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu he hiaa waa yɛ otsi ni mi-abele lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ siliki kɛ ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Silking and tasseling is the reproductive stage where maize cobs fill with grains. A lack of water during this short window dries up pollen, leading to cob ears that are half-empty or bare.
ga: Silking kɛ brushing ji fɔmɔ gbɛi ni akɛ dumɔwui eyi ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ mli obɔ. Nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli yɛ be kukuoo mli Enɛ baaha pollen lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa nu lɛ fã pɛ eshwɛɔ loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field help the crop I plant next season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas out of the air and store it in their roots. When the crop harvest ends, that stored nitrogen stays behind in the soil to naturally fertilize your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ ba naagbee Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling tightly and turning pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato leaf curl is typically caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and spread plant viruses, or by extreme heat and drought stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni shwieɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ mli.

english: Why do weeds lower my harvest even if I give my crops plenty of water and fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds grow aggressively and steal water, light, and plant food right out of the soil before your main crop can absorb it, starving your crops of essential resources.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei amli dani oŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ nibii ni he hiaa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually indicate that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient crops need to build strong green leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or compost around the plants helps restore this vital nutrient to the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Koolooi amli ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ni akɛwoɔ Tsei ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people say I should plant groundnuts or beans on the field where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. Planting them after heavy feeders like maize naturally restores nutrients to your soil without buying expensive chemicals.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ niyenii agboi, tamɔ ŋmãa tsu nii lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai ni jara wa.

english: Why is it a bad idea for me to spread fertilizer on my farm right before a big rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ magbɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ashwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ anɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes granular fertilizer off the topsoil and away into streams before your crop roots have time to drink it in, which wastes your money and deprives your plants of food.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli kɛyaa faai amli dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ. Enɛ baafite shika ni ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and dying in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains alongside them provides living shade and keeps the surrounding soil moist while the cocoa roots grow deep.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Nurse tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains ni bɛŋkɛɔ Enɛ baaha hulutsoo aba ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds around my young crop seedlings when the seedlings are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Mi tso bibioo lɛ He ni dumɔwui lɛ yɔɔ bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings have small, fragile roots that cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for soil food, sunlight, and water. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the available resources to grow strong.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni waaa ni nyɛɛɛ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ ashi akaŋ kɛha niyenii yɛ sũ, hulu la, kɛ nu mli. Ebaaha onibii lɛ aná nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ kɛha dalɛ ni mli wa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when a strong wind blows before the fruits are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ dani eyibii lɛ shwere lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and heavy stems. When heavy fruit bunches grow at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy, so supporting the main stem with strong wooden poles or bamboos prevents the wind from pushing them over.
