ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tso ni mli wa. Kɛji aduawai akui ni tsii kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baaná ŋwɛi shwiili babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tso loo ŋmei tso ni mli wa fi tso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ akatsɔ mli.

english: Why do I have to put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ koni makwɔ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in the air to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food. Guiding the vines up tall stakes helps the plant produce energy to swell the big tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ wo tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baa koni ekɛ bulbs wuji akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when heavy rains flood my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eha miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain sits on flat land and creates waterlogging, the roots suffocate and fungal rot sets in, which is why planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ nɔ ni ehaa nu shwieɔ shi. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ boteɔ mli. Enɛ hewɔ ni ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and twisting into small shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe bibii bibii lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves to suck out the sap, which carries plant viruses that distort new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛnu nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni fiteɔ baai heei lɛ adalɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are all the flowers falling off my tomato plants without turning into any tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get extremely hot or when they lack consistent water, because the plant stresses and sheds its blooms to conserve water rather than feeding new fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ loo amɛbɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ baahao amɛhe ni amɛbaajie amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii heei.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tips along the middle vein?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaagbee nɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves in maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is a vital nutrient for leaf growth and green color. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or NPK early in the plant's growth helps it recover and produce strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ kɛ su ni ji eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo NPK fata he mra yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily in full sunlight and high heat. They require shade crops like plantains or gliricidia trees planted around them to block harsh sunlight and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Amɛmiisumɔ ni adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo glicidia tsei yɛ amɛhe. Koni ebu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. When heat stress occurs, the plant drops its blossoms to save energy and water rather than producing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛji dɔlɛ he haomɔ ba Yɛ yibiiwoo najiaŋ lɛ, tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap from young leaves, or transmitting a plant virus. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or recommended sprays protects new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo egbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ eshwaa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ nɔ lɛ ebaaye ebua ni ebaatsi baai heei adalɛ naa.

english: Why am I finding ragged holes inside the central leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa bu ko ni elaaje yɛ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These holes are caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center whorl of the corn plant to eat tender new leaves. Applying pest control directly into the center of the plant early prevents severe crop loss.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli koni amɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ buji nɛɛ. Ni akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ baawo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii ni naa wa waa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn dark and soft and smell bad when I harvest them during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ akpa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because excess water prevents air from reaching the roots, causing underground fungal diseases to spread. Planting cassava on raised ridges helps water drain away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi tsɛŋemɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋshɔŋlooi lɛ amli.

english: Why do officers advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field with my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas fix nitrogen from the air into the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil, giving nearby maize plants extra food without having to buy as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ náa niyenii babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛhe tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ babaoo tamɔ nɛkɛ.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on instead of letting them run on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tsei ama shi koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha ejo foi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need their leaves lifted off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight to make food for the root. Staking also keeps leaves dry and prevents soil-borne diseases from ruining the leaves and reducing tuber size.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmeii awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shishifãi lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ egbiɔ ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni fiteɔ baai lɛ ni ehaa tuber lɛ dalɛ baa shi lɛ naa.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ ekomɛi?

english: If too many sucker shoots grow around one plantain parent tree, they all fight for the same soil food and water, resulting in small plantain bunches. Keeping only one or two strong suckers ensures large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ, dumɔwu kome Amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, plantains lɛ baaja mli awo ŋmeii bibii amli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha efee ŋmeii agbo ni tsii.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable plants with dry leaves or straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Aduawai ni baai egbi loo jwɛi yɔɔ mli?

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating quickly under the hot sun, keeps the root zone cool, and prevents weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ akatsɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need plantains grown right next to them in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ yɛ plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to direct, intense sunlight and can easily burn or dry out. Plantains grow very fast and produce broad leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa trees and keeping the soil moist while they establish themselves.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. ni ebaanyɛ eshã loo egbi oya Plantains daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛtswaa shi lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young corn plants turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on young corn usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green, healthy leaves. Feeding the soil with compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves turn green again and boost plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep drying up and falling off before any small tomatoes can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi dani tomato bibii lɛ baanyɛ ada lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of calcium in the soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting plants from harsh weather helps the flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni abuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do some of my cassava stem cuttings rot in the ground while others sprout fresh leaves quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ekomɛi miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi woɔ baai heei oya lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings rot if they are planted upside down, if the stem cuttings come from diseased old plants, or if the soil holds too much water without draining properly. Using fresh, healthy stems cut from mature plants and planting them with the buds pointing upward ensures fast sprouting.
ga: Kasava niji fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ ŋwɛi. Tsei niji jɛɔ tsei ni egbɔ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni nu hoɔ yɛ gbɛ kpakpa nɔ. Kɛ akɛ tsei ni edara lɛ ahe tsei heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsu nii ni adu amɛ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kwɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ, ehaa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: Why is it important for me to stake my yam vines with tall wooden sticks instead of letting them creep on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei kakadaji atswa mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha ekplekeshi shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Lifting yam vines on wooden stakes allows the leaves to catch as much sunlight as possible, which gives the plant the energy it needs to grow big tubers underground. It also keeps the leaves off damp soil where fungal diseases like to spread.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebaa lɛ koni ekahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai sumɔɔ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã lɛ.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat up the fresh leaves inside my young maize shoots overnight?
ga: Mɛni ha ŋmeii bibii lɛ ye baai heei ni yɔɔ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworms, which lay eggs on corn plants so their larvae can feed on the tender young leaves. Checking your field early in the morning and using recommended organic or chemical sprays as soon as you see tiny holes prevents total crop destruction.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii tsei anɔ koni amɛ ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ aye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ leebi ni okɛ tsofa ni ji organic loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ awo mli kɛji ona buji bibii pɛ. Ebaatsi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akpãtãmɔ kwraa naa.

english: Why is my harvest getting smaller every time I plant maize on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ feɔ bibioo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every single season and allows pests that attack corn to build up in the ground. Rotating corn with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts refills nitrogen in the soil and breaks the cycle of pests.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni amɛbuaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ebaaye ebua ni akɛ nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni efo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do people tell me to cover the soil around my pepper plants with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dried plant materials—a method called mulching—acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool under hot sun, stops moisture from evaporating quickly, and prevents weeds from taking over your garden bed.
ga: Mulching kɛ tsei ni egbi nibii - gbɛ ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching - tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya ni etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekaha obɔɔ mli saatsoi lɛ anɔ.

english: How does the dusty Harmattan wind harm my crops, and what can I do on my farm to protect them?
ga: Te Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ? Ni mɛni manyɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mabu nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ ahe?

english: Harmattan winds carry dry, cold air that rapidly sucks moisture out of plant leaves and topsoil, causing plants to wilt and dry out. You can protect your farm by planting rows of tall trees along your farm borders to block heavy winds and by watering crops early in the morning.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni egbi baa. ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli oya Ehaa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ. Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ tsei kakadaji ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa koni obu ohe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he kɛ nu ni oooha otsei lɛ leebi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cabbage plants grow big, spread-out leaves but refuse to form tight, hard heads in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage tso lɛ daa, ni baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shi eŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ ni yitso ni mli wa ni wa aba teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to head when the weather is too hot or when they get too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus only on growing wide leaves. Planting during cooler months and using balanced fertilizers encourages the plant to form solid heads.
ga: Cabbage nyɛŋ ajie eyitso kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ enine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai ni mli kwɔlɔ pɛ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ nyɔji ni mli ejɔ lɛ amli, ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tsu nii lɛ, ebaawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfee bulbs ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is a major food source for plants, and when there is not enough in the soil, the plant moves what little it has to the upper leaves to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei náa. ni kɛ́ nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ kɛ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ yaa ebaa lɛ nɔ koni eya nɔ eda.

english: Why are my yam vines growing big leaves but only producing small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ baai wuji shi amɛbulb bibii lɛ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: When yam plants produce lots of leafy vines but tiny tubers, it often means the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium or phosphorus. Potassium helps the plant store energy down in the roots to make large tubers.
ga: Beni sweet potato tsei lɛ woɔ wain tsei ni yɔɔ baai babaoo shi amɛji ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni potassium loo phosphorus ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Potassium yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is it helpful for me to plant cowpea together with my maize on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This extra nitrogen feeds the maize crop, making the soil richer without needing to buy extra fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen gas mli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nitrogen ni yaa hiɛ nɛɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmãa lɛ aye nii. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck the juice out of young leaves, or by a plant virus carried by those insects. Controlling pests early stops the curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni ji nakai kooloi lɛ ahe nibii ni kɛ nakai kooloi lɛ baa lɛ nɔ Early Pest Control Ekpaa ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground even when the top of the plant looks fine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long around the roots without draining away properly. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater flow away so the roots can breathe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni enyɛɛɛ etsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Why are there small ragged holes appearing inside the center leaf funnel of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Holes inside the growing tip of young corn are typically caused by caterpillars like fall armyworms feeding on the fresh leaves. Checking the plants early allows you to treat them before the pest destroys the growing center.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ, ni egbee shi ni eye baai heei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ashishifãi amli lɛ baa. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsaa amɛ dani tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa saplings turn brown and dry out during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under strong sunlight and heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides a natural leaf cover that protects them from drying out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, kɛfata kookoo bibii ahe lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ feɔ nɔ ni buɔ amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant does not get steady moisture in the soil. Consistent watering and keeping grass mulch around the stem helps keep the root zone cool and hydrated.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ nɔ. Nu daa ni oshi ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle he. Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ haa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall, thin, and weak when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe waaa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the crops compete with one another for light, air, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each crop enough room to build strong stems and produce a good harvest.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, kɔɔyɔɔ, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni wa baakwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops grow so slowly even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than main crops and quickly steal water, sunlight, and plant food from the soil. Clearing weeds early in the planting season ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya.

english: Why are my crops struggling to grow on land that was previously dug up and cleared?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ atsu nii yɛ nɔ ni ajie lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When land is cleared and topsoil is scraped away, the essential nutrients and helpful soil organisms that crops feed on are lost, making it difficult for roots to take hold and nourish the plant without soil restoration.
ga: Kɛji ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajie sũ ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ Niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ sũ mli nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni tsei yeɔ lɛ laajeɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaatswa tso lɛ shi ni amɛha lɛ niyenii ni amɛhaaa sũ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting cover crops help restore bare and exhausted soil over time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni efite ni egbiɔ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cover crops spread across the ground to shield the earth from harsh sun and erosion, while their roots break up hard ground and drop organic leaves that rot into rich food for future crops.
ga: Tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he. Beni amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ ni amɛshiɔ bɔɔ nii ni fiteɔ lɛ, amɛhaa niyenii babaoo kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing small and twisted in hard, packed ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ bibii ni amɛtsake yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni edɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers expand by pushing easily through loose soil. Hard or packed soil physically squeezes the tubers, preventing them from expanding properly and causing them to stay small and misshapen.
ga: Sweet potato tsei amli lɛɛɔ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe mlɛo lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baaha bulb lɛ afee mlɛo. Enɛ haaa enyɛ egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ. ni ehaa amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ

english: Why do cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off when the weather gets too hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees lose water rapidly through their leaves under high heat. Dropping their leaves is a defense mechanism to conserve internal moisture and keep the main trunk alive during dry spells.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ shishi. Baai ni ashwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛha mligbɛ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni eha tso titri lɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why do cassava plants survive long dry seasons much better than maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmei lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves and stores water deep inside its underground roots during dry weather, whereas maize relies on shallow surface moisture and wilts quickly without rain.
ga: Yucca shwieɔ baai lɛ ni ekɛ nu toɔ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ lɛ. Shi ŋmãa lɛ, ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ he eko nɔ, ni egboɔ oya kɛ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and die when floodwater stays on my farm for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni nu afua lɛ hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need to breathe air contained in the soil. Standing floodwater fills all the tiny air pockets, suffocating the roots and causing them to rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni tsei shishifãi lɛ amu kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nu afua mli nu lɛ eyi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii lɛ fɛɛ amli obɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves look burnt after I water them in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã beni mikɛ nu wo amɛmli yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Water droplets left on leaves can act like small magnifying glass lenses under intense direct sunlight, scorching the leaf tissue while hot sun evaporates the water before roots can drink it.
ga: Nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii tamɔ ŋmɛlɛ bibii ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Eshãa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ beni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi dani shishifãi lɛ nuɔ lɛ.

english: When plants are overcrowded, they compete intensely for limited sunlight and soil nutrients, spending all their energy stretching upward to reach light instead of producing fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkpãa ŋwɛi koni ekɛ la aba moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas have beneficial bacteria on their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil, leaving natural fertilizer behind for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ ahaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my cultivated crops after a rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni midu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni nɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive in harsh, poor soils with minimal nutrients, allowing them to react instantly to rainwater faster than sensitive farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa, ni niyenii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛtsuɔ nugbɔ he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ fe ŋmɔ mli tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ waa lɛ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and dry up while still on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is usually black pod disease, which is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in wet and humid weather. You can manage it by pruning cocoa branches to allow sunlight in and clearing out infected pods immediately.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Obaanyɛ otsu enɛ he nii kɛtsɔ kookoo niji ni oookpa koni hulu la abote mli lɛ nɔ, ni ooojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build strong green leaves. Applying organic manure, compost, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer can help bring back the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How can I tell if fall armyworms are eating my maize field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ fall armyworms miiye mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Look for ragged holes in the main leaves and small dark droppings that look like sawdust inside the leaf curls. If you unroll the young leaves, you will see small caterpillars hiding inside.
ga: Taomɔ buji ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ baai wuji lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ diŋ. Nɔ ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji ŋmeii. Kɛ́ ogbele baai bibii lɛ, obaana ŋmeii bibii. Ekɛ ehe tee mli

english: When is the best month for me to plant cassava in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ nyɔŋ ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ Ghana?

english: Cassava is best planted at the beginning of the rainy season, around March to April in southern Ghana or May to June in the north, so the stem cuttings get enough soil moisture to root properly.
ga: Ahi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aduɔ ŋmei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli. Aaafee March kɛyashi April yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ. loo May kɛyashi June yɛ kooyigbɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yɛ sũ mli nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛshishifãi aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow thin and bent instead of long and thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ amli tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers struggle to grow when the soil is hard, rocky, or compacted. Planting yams in high mounds or deep ridges filled with soft soil allows the tubers to expand straight down without resistance.
ga: Ewa akɛ aakwɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋmeii ni mli kwɔlɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni mli tse eyi mli obɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daa tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa shi. ni shitee-kɛ-woo bɛ mli

english: Roots rot when heavy rain leaves standing water around the roots for too long. Planting cassava on raised mounds or slopes helps excess rain water drain away from the tubers.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha nu hi shifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Watering your plants regularly at the base and providing slight shade during extreme heat helps hold flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ shishi daa, ni okɛ hulutsoo be fioo ko ha lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ehiɛ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why are my bean plants growing lots of green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen or too much rich manure. The excess nutrient causes the bean plant to spend all its energy growing leaves rather than producing flowers and pods.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmeii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni eeefee fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Young crop plants are weak and must compete with weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to sunlight and food so they grow fast and stay healthy.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni esa akɛ amɛkɛ jwɛi lɛ abɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ye obua otsei lɛ ni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii babaoo. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ adara oya ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do the seeds on some of my grain crops fall off onto the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ dani mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: This natural process is called seed shattering. Some crop varieties naturally drop their mature seeds easily to reproduce in the wild, but in farming, harvesting early or choosing improved seed varieties helps prevent losing your yield.
ga: Atsɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ dumɔwui amlijaa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ekomɛi shĩɔ dumɔwui ni eda yɛ amɛsɛɛ koni amɛfɔ yɛ koo lɛ mli mlɛo. Shi yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ, ŋmaakpamɔ mra Loo dumɔwui srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ahala lɛ baaye abua ni akafite yibiiwoo.

english: Why do strong winds cause my crop pods to spill their seeds on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa shwieɔ mi dumɔwui ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry heat and strong winds shake mature plants, causing brittle seed pods to split open and scatter seeds. Planting windbreaks like tall grass or hedge trees around your field edges helps block harsh winds and protects your harvest.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli egbi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa hosoɔ tsei ni eda lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni shwieɔ shi lɛ fãa ni amɛgbɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ amɛshwãa. Kɔɔyɔɔ he tsei tamɔ jwɛi kakadaŋŋ loo tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ adumɔ. Gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baabu ohe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he, ni ebaabu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest so the wind doesn't scatter my seeds on the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa nii? Koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ akagbɛ midumɔwui lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: You should harvest as soon as the plant leaves turn yellow and the seed heads fully mature, but before the pods become dry and brittle enough to crack open in the midday sun and wind.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa kɛji tso lɛ baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ eda pɛ. Shi jeee dani ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhe afee shoo bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala yɛ shwane hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why does one crop variety hold onto its seeds tightly while another variety spills them easily in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome hiɛɔ edumɔwui lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni ekroko hu shwieɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ mlɛo lɛ?

english: This is due to crop genetics. Improved agricultural seed varieties are specifically bred to hold their pods tightly closed until threshing, whereas traditional or unselected seeds split open easily.
ga: Enɛ jɛɔ tsei amli wala yibii ahewɔ. Afeɔ okwaayeli dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi kwraa kɛyashi be mli ni abaakpa. yɛ be mli ni kusum mli dumɔwui loo ni ahalaaa lɛ mli gbalaa mlɛo.

english: Can I plant my crops by just putting the dry seeds directly into the ground without preparing a nursery?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni misaaa he ko ni akɛduɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, many hardy crops like maize, beans, and okra grow well when planted directly into moist, loose soil without needing to be nursed first.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni wa, tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ okra lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni atsu he nii klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why do some crops need very little effort to sprout while others require so much extra care?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi biɔ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ fioo ko pɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi biɔ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko lɛ?

english: Different crops have different seed vigor and moisture requirements. Seeds with tough coats or large food reserves germinate easily in basic soil, while delicate crops require precise shade, nursery care, and rich soil to start.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ dumɔwui ahewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa lɛ srɔtoi. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ nɔ ko ni wa loo niyenii babaoo ni ato lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ shishijee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ biɔ hulutsoo pɔtɛɛ. Nursery nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni akɛjeɔ shishi

english: Is it normal for some crops to grow into strong plants just from direct seeding without adding heavy fertilizers?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni ja akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi baakwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii fataaa he kɛkɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, certain crops are very efficient at extracting natural nutrients already present in the soil, though adding compost or fertilizer later will still increase your final harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei komɛi tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jiemɔ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha onaagbee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ lolo moŋ.

english: Why do some plants in my farm give a heavy harvest while the ones right next to them yield almost nothing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni mɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ? Ani amɛwooo yibii ko kwraa kwraa?

english: Plants compete for soil nutrients, moisture, and sunlight. Uneven soil quality, localized pest attacks, or differences in individual seed quality can cause neighboring plants to produce very different yields.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la, ni no haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ekome. Spot pest attacks loo srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mli Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ awo yibii sɔrɔtoi kwraa.

english: Why do some crop pods look full from the outside but turn out to have very few or light seeds inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ashishifãi komɛi tamɔ nɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ shi etsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ mli loo amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This happens when plants lack sufficient water or nutrients during the grain-filling stage, or if hot winds interrupt proper pollination while the flower is developing.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni awoɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ. Aloo kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: What causes one farm field to yield full seeds while another nearby field yields light, thin seeds?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔ mli yiɔ kɛ ŋmaa? yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ kroko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ woɔ dumɔwui ni mli tseee ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Seed weight depends heavily on soil fertility, water availability during seed development, and seed quality. Fields with better soil organic matter and timely water retainment produce fuller, heavier seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ tsiimɔ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ. Nu ni yɔɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ akwɛmɔ be mli kɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ lɛ nɔ kwɔ waa Gbɛjegbɛi ni shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ nu ni ahiɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ woɔ dumɔwui ni jara wa, ni tsii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil or getting too much water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or manure helps restore their green color so they can produce healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo amɛyɛ nu babaoo tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni toi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it helpful to plant cowpeas in the same field where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that fix nitrogen from the air into the soil. This naturally enriches the soil and provides extra food for the maize plants without requiring extra expensive fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ náa niyenii kroko ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa babaoo he ehiaaa.

english: Which direction should I point my cassava cuttings when pushing them into the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu ŋmei lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ otsɔɔ?

english: Always plant cassava stem cuttings with the leaf buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the shoots struggle to grow properly and you will get very few tuber roots.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, dumɔ ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu ŋwɛigbɛ Shoots lɛ baawa ni obaagbe naa kɛ shishifãi fioo ko pɛ.

english: How do I choose the best sucker from my plantain bush to start a new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala suckers ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ jwɛi mli koni mikɛje dumɔ hee shishi?

english: Select a 'sword sucker' which has a broad base and narrow, sword-like leaves. These suckers have strong reserves and produce healthy, heavy-yielding plantain trees much faster than broad-leaf suckers.
ga: Halamɔ ‘klante sucker,’ ni shishigbɛ lɛ mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ klante. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ yɛ nɔ ko ni akɛtoɔ he ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ.

english: Why are all the small flowers on my cocoa trees falling off instead of turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ kookoo ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by severe drought, lack of shade, or insect pests like mirids. Ensuring proper shade and keeping the soil moist helps flowers turn into full cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji hɔmɔ ni naa wa, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ pollen miigba tso lɛ naa. Kɛ́ aha fɔfɔi lɛ hulutsoo be ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and rot before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium or irregular watering while the fruit is growing. Keeping water supply steady and adding compost or lime to the soil helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Nu jɛɛhe ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push little stems back down into the dirt after they flower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miitsi eshishifã bibioo lɛ kɛmiijɛ mli lɛ? Ku osɛɛ oya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni fɔfɔi lɛ efo lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Groundnut flowers open above ground, but the fruit grows underground. After pollination, the stems grow downwards into 'pegs' that push into the soil where the groundnut pods can safely mature.
ga: Peanut fɔfɔii gbeleɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi aduawai lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. after pollination Tso lɛ yitsei lɛ daa kɛbaa shi ni amɛfeɔ ‘pegs’ ni ashɛɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ ada shweshweeshwe yɛ lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves into the sun and keeps them off the wet ground, reducing soil-borne diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ aje hulu la mli ni ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ baa shi

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up into tight cups and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi ni mli wa ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny pests like thrips or aphids sucking juices from underneath the leaves. Spraying with neem oil or mild soapy water helps get rid of them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni mli ejɔ baashwie nɔ Ebaaye ebua ni ajie nibii nɛɛ kɛjɛ mli.

english: Why does putting dry grass around the base of my vegetables keep them alive during dry weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ mi-aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts as a protective blanket that traps moisture in the dirt and cools plant roots during hot weather.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni ŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong leaves. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the crop's growth keeps the leaves green and boosts your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he mra yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eye ebua ni onibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is it bad to burn the grass and leftover stalks on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mashã jwɛi kɛ tsei ni eshwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani adu lɛ?

english: Burning destroys organic matter that keeps the soil soft and rich. Leaving crop remains to rot naturally puts nutrients back into the dirt, holds moisture during dry spells, and saves you money on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni tso lɛ mli nibii lɛ fite yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. ni eye ebua bo ni okɛ shika ato tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe

english: Planting the exact same crop on the same ground season after season drains specific soil nutrients and lets pests build up in the dirt. Rotating crops—like following maize with cowpeas—gives the soil a chance to rest and rebuild its strength.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi baa shi. ni eha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsɔmɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa hegbɛ ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ ehewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a small fungus that spreads fast in damp, shaded conditions. Pruning excess branches and removing infected pods lets sunlight into the tree canopy, which dries up moisture and stops the disease.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso bibioo ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafolɔ ashwie shi ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ Enɛ baaha hulu la lɛ akpɛ kɛbote tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi ni helai akpa.

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites that attack young leaves and spread plant diseases. Spraying neem tree extract mixed with soap and water can clean off these pests before they ruin your harvest.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni tutuaa baai bibii ni egbɛɔ tsei ahe helai eshwaa Neem tso mli nu ni akɛ samla kɛ nu efutu mli lɛ baanyɛ agbe nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when we get heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water suffocates them underground. Planting your cassava stems on raised dirt mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to drain away so the roots can breathe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi lɛ, ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: How do I know the right day to plant my seeds when the rains are no longer coming at the normal times?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ dɔŋŋ yɛ be ni afeɔ daa lɛ mli?

english: Do not plant based on traditional months alone. Wait until the soil receives two or three steady, deep rains that soak deep into the dirt so your seeds have enough moisture to germinate without drying up.
ga: Kaadamɔ kusum nyɔŋ lɛ pɛ nɔ odu nii. Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni mli kwɔ ni boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni eha odumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without growing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when the soil gets too dry, temperatures become extremely hot, or the soil lacks nutrients like calcium. Mulching around the base of the stem with dry grass keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Tomato baafɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Dɔlɛ ni mli wa waa Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ calcium. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: How does planting groundnuts in the same field help my maize crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When you plant maize after groundnuts, the maize eats that free stored plant food and grows taller.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa masɛi ŋmãa lɛ baaye tso niyenii ni ato ni aheee nɔ ko lɛ ni ebaada.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after I clean the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds produce thousands of hidden seeds that stay dormant in the soil waiting for sunlight. Clearing weeds while they are still tiny prevents them from flowering and scattering new seeds across your field.
ga: Jwɛi woɔ dumɔwui akpei abɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni kã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛmiimɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ, ebaatsi amɛnaa koni amɛkawo fɔfɔi ni amɛkagbɛ dumɔwui heei amɛshwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize plants turn light yellow after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes away key soil nutrients like nitrogen deeper into the ground where young roots cannot reach them. When maize lacks nitrogen, it cannot make chlorophyll, causing the green leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ, kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Beni nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa mli lɛ Enyɛŋ efee klorofil. Ehaa baai eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy green leaves, but produce tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves and branches above ground instead of storing food in the roots below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai kɛ niji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso sisifãhi nɛ a ngɛ zugba a sisi ɔ a mi.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as very hot daytime temperatures, lack of soil moisture, or a lack of bees and insects to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ, tamɔ hulutsoo be mli latsaa be mli. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and droop during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho ni amɛmiiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: On hot days, tomato leaves lose water into the air through evaporation faster than the roots can drink water from the soil. The plant droops temporarily to reduce heat exposure and usually recovers by morning.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei baagbee shi be kukuoo ko koni hulutsoo ni baa lɛ aba shi. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi leebi

english: Why do my cocoa leaves dry up and turn brown when I remove all the shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ beni mijieɔ shade tsei fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without shade trees to filter the sun and keep the air moist, the leaves burn, lose too much water, and die.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ tsei haaa hulutsoo ni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔ lɛ, baai lɛ baashã, nu babaoo baaje mli, ni amɛbaagboi.

english: Why do caterpillars like Fall Armyworm hide deep inside the funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-bibii ŋmei tsei lɛ atsɔnei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The inner leaf funnel of young maize is soft, tender, and moist, which gives the caterpillars a safe shelter from predators, heat, and chemical sprays while they feed on the growing heart of the plant.
ga: Abɛi bibii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ naa he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui, dɔlɛ, kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ ahe beni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ tsui ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster and stronger than my cultivated crops after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ dara oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that have adapted over centuries to survive harsh conditions. Their seeds wake up quickly after rain and consume soil nutrients and water faster than domesticated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ kooi amli ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Dumɔwui teɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ oya fe shia tsei.

english: Why does my land produce fewer bags of maize when I plant maize on the same plot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on specific soil nutrients. Planting it continuously on the same field drains those specific nutrients and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the soil.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ hoɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ayi fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I save and plant seeds from my harvest of hybrid maize for the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two unique parent plants to give high yields. The seeds saved from a hybrid harvest lose these special parent qualities, resulting in uneven plant growth and poor yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ fɔɔ tsei enyɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraaa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do I need to leave proper distance between my yam mounds instead of packing them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ ato he jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni makɛ amɛ awo tsɔne mli ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yam plants need space for their underground tubers to expand and for their vines to capture sunlight. Planting mounds too close makes the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia he ko ni amɛ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni wain tsei lɛ hu he miihia hulu la. Gɔŋ ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ.

english: Why do my crops refuse to grow well on soil that was previously cleared for gold mining?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ ajie shika tsuru ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mining strips away the rich topsoil where plant nutrients live and leaves behind tightly packed earth mixed with harmful chemicals. Crops cannot extend roots or absorb water until you rebuild the soil with organic matter like animal manure and cover crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni atsaa lɛ jieɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni tsei ahe nibii yɔɔ mli lɛ. ni eshiɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ shishifãi loo amɛŋɔ nu kɛyashi obaakɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmeii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni okɛha nibii ni adu lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow much stronger when I leave dead plant leaves to rot on the soil instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli wa waa nɛkɛ beni mishiɔ tsei ahe baai ni egboi lɛ koni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys topsoil nutrients and leaves the ground dry and exposed. Letting dead leaves rot creates natural compost that retains soil moisture, keeps the ground cool, and feeds beneficial organisms that help plant roots absorb food.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbeleɔ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ baai lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi lɛ baa. ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi ni amɛŋɔ niyenii lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants turn pale yellow and stay small when I plant them under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɔ shi bibioo kɛ́ midu yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Maize needs direct sunlight to create its own food through photosynthesis. When planted under heavy shade, the crop starves for sunlight, causing its leaves to turn pale and its growth to stunt.
ga: Abɛi he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eniyenii kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tsei lɛ bɛ hulu la. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdaraaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing fruit when the weather gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Very high temperatures dry out the pollen inside tomato blossoms, preventing fertilization from taking place. Without fertilization, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa waa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Kɛji fɔmɔ bɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: Curled, spotted leaves on cassava are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant stems provided by the local agriculture office prevents this virus from destroying your crop.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Kɛ́ odu tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli nitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛha lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ akafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn black and rot during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, dark environments. Pruning extra shade tree branches lets sunlight and wind into the farm to dry out the pods and prevent fungal growth.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nibii ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ekɛtsi ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why do my corn plants produce tiny cobs when I plant four or five seeds together in a single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ

english: Planting too many seeds in one spot forces the roots to fight each other for the same small amount of water and soil food. Spacing plants properly gives each root system enough room to grow big cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ awuu koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Tsoi lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa baaha shishifãi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmei agbo ko akwɛ̃.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my yam plants right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi sweet potato tsei lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are tough wild plants adapted to quickly absorb the first drops of rainfall and nutrients before crop plants can establish deep roots. Clearing weeds early ensures your yams get those resources instead.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ nugbɔshiimɔi kɛ niyenii kpakpai klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ oya dani tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atswa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ, ebaaha sweet potatoes lɛ aná nakai nibii lɛ moŋ

english: Why does planting cowpeas in the same field with my maize make the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni midu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ haa ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to a plant family that pulls nitrogen gas out of the air and traps it in the soil through their roots. This acts as a natural fertilizer for neighboring crops like maize that need lots of nitrogen.
ga: Cowpeas fata tsei aweku ko ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni biɔ nitrogen babaoo lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall, dark green leaves but no fruit when I apply too much chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ daa lɛ? Baai ni tsuɔ waa shi ebɛ hewalɛ ko kɛji mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo fata he?

english: Excess nitrogen fertilizer tricks the plant into putting all its energy into growing leaves and stems rather than flowers and fruits. Crops need a balanced mix of nutrients, including phosphorus and potassium, to produce healthy yields.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ lakaa tsei ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai kɛ tsei ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai baatsu nii lɛ, niyenii ni ja he miihia Tsei. Fosfɔs kɛ potasium fata he Koni aná nibii ni haa mɔ he waa

english: Why should I clear my land right after the Christmas season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ Blonya sɛɛ?

english: Clearing your land during the dry period around January and February allows cut bushes to dry properly for burning, making the soil ready just before the early major rains start.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli ni miihe ashɛ January kɛyashi February lɛ baaye abua ni jwɛi ni afo lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shãa. ni ofee shikpɔŋ lɛ klalo dani nugbɔshiimɔi wuji lɛ aje shishi.

english: What is the best time of the year for me to start planting my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ mabɔi tsei akwɛmɔ?

english: The best time to plant is right after the dry season ends and the first steady rains begin, giving young seeds and shoots enough moisture to build strong roots.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ji beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eba naagbee ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi ni wa aba.

english: How does clearing all the bushes on my plot help my new crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni mijieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ?

english: Clearing bushes removes weeds and wild plants that steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients away from your planted crops.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie tsei bibii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ jwɛi kɛ koo mli tsei ni juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ otsei ni miida lɛ amli lɛ.

english: If I clear a fresh patch of forest, what crop should I plant first?
ga: Kɛji mijie koo hee ko Mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ madu klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Freshly cleared forest soil is rich in organic nutrients, making it ideal for heavy-feeding food crops like plantains and yams before you establish long-term crops.
ga: Koo mli shikpɔŋ ni ajie ehee lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa ehi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ niyenii babaoo tamɔ plantains kɛ sweet potatoes. Dani obaafee ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why is it better for me to plant my yams and plantains in straight lines rather than anywhere I like?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu sweet potatoes kɛ plantains yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe he fɛɛ he ni misumɔɔ?

english: Planting in straight lines gives every plant enough space and sunlight, makes weeding and applying fertilizer easier, and prevents you from damaging roots while walking through the farm.
ga: Ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ hulu la. Enɛ haa jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ feɔ mlɛo. ni etsĩɔ shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ naa beni enyiɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How far apart should I space my plantain shoots when planting them in rows?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ mi-plantains lɛ abɔ he beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Spacing plantains about 3 meters apart in straight rows gives their large leaves enough room to spread and capture sunlight without blocking air and light from neighboring plants.
ga: Kɛjɛkɛmɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji aaafee mitai 3, ni ehaa baa agboi lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkpɛ ni amɛŋɔ hulu la. ni etsĩii kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la ni jɛɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ anaa

english: Why do you recommend that I plant my yams on mounds arranged in straight rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ adu ŋmeii yɛ gɔji anɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni ja lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Arranging yam mounds in neat lines keeps the farm organized, improves water drainage around the tubers so they do not rot, and makes harvesting much easier.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Ha nu ni hoɔ yɛ bulb lɛ he lɛ aya hiɛ koni amɛkafite. Ni ehaa nikpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: What should I do to protect my soil right after I finish planting my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mabu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛji midu ŋmɔtɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: After planting yams, cover the mounds with dry leaves or grass (mulching) to shade the soil from harsh sun heat, keep soil moisture in, and prevent rain from washing the mounds away.
ga: Beni adu sweet potato sɛɛ lɛ Okɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulch) aha gɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni otsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa koni ekashwie gɔji lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over when the fruit starts growing, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi beni aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and heavy fruit bunches that make them top-heavy; propping the stem with a strong bamboo or wooden stick helps support the weight against strong winds.
ga: Plantains shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni aduawai akui ni tsii, ni no haa amɛfeɔ tsii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni wa fĩ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ muji lɛ afi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ naa.

english: What main tasks must I keep doing on my farm after I finish planting my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ nitsumɔi titrii ehe hiaa ni magbe naa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni midu ŋmɔshi nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Farming requires continuous care after planting; you must regularly weed the field, inspect for pests and crop diseases, add nutrients, and prune dead leaves so the plants produce high yields.
ga: Okwaayeli biɔ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ jwɛi atsu nii yɛ oyale mli daa. Kwɛmɔ kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai yɛ. kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ afata he Ni ofolɔ baai ni egboi lɛ koni tso lɛ awo yibii babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I use fire to clear my land before planting this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ la tsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ shikpɔŋ dani aduɔ nii yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Burning your field burns away valuable soil nutrients, kills helpful soil insects like earthworms, and leaves the ground dry and hard. Clearing without fire leaves cut bush to rot naturally, which feeds the soil and keeps it moist for your crop roots.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni ashãa lɛ shãa sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ agbe jwɛi lɛ ni la bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha jwɛi lɛ agbo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How does proper land preparation help my seeds grow better than just clearing and planting directly?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ kpakpa yeɔ ebuaa midumɔwui lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe nɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni aduɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Properly preparing and loosening the soil makes it easy for tender young roots to spread out, reach deep underground water, and soak up plant food easily, leading to stronger stems and bigger crop yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni asaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi bibii lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa. Shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mlibotemɔ ni ekɛ tsei aniyenii shwieɔ mli oya Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ waa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: What is the best way to clear thick bush on my plot if I am told not to burn it?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ ojie brɔshi ni mli wa yɛ mi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛɛ bo akɛ kaashã?

english: You can cut down the vegetation and either pile it along the edges or spread it across the field as mulch. Over time, the cut green material rots down into rich natural fertilizer that feeds your plants.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofolɔ aduawai lɛ ni okɛto amɛhe yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa loo okɛ ŋmɔtɔ aha ŋmɔ lɛ he. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni afo lɛ baafite ni etsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli kɛha otsei lɛ.

english: Why does my soil dry out so fast shortly after the rains stop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ?

english: When land is burned or left uncovered, the sun bakes the bare ground and steals water quickly. Leaving cut plant materials on top of the soil acts like a grass roof, keeping the dirt cool and holding rainwater much longer.
ga: Kɛ́ ashã shikpɔŋ loo ashi lɛ ni egbele lɛ Hulu lɛ shãa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ oya ni ejuɔ nu. Tso nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ jwɛi ŋtayaa. Ehaa muji lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi be babaoo.

english: Why do my crops look weak even when I plant high-quality seeds from the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni jɛ jara nɔ lɛ moŋ?

english: Good seeds need healthy ground structure to perform well. If the soil was damaged by fire or is too packed down, the crop roots struggle to absorb nutrients, making the growing plants look pale and thin.
ga: Dumɔwui kpakpai he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji la efite shikpɔŋ lɛ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso ni miida lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How can I protect my young crops from being washed away during heavy downpours?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahe koni nugbɔ akafo amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Proper land preparation across slopes and keeping plant remains on the ground slow down rushing rainwater. This stops the top layer of rich soil and your seeds from getting swept into the gutter.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni asaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ kɛ tsei ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ fioo. Enɛ baatsi shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛ odumɔwui lɛ anaa koni akaho kɛya nubu lɛ mli.

english: Why are earthworms and tiny soil bugs good for my farm crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Earthworms dig small tunnels in the ground that allow air and water to reach crop roots easily. They also digest plant material and produce rich, natural plant food directly inside your soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii foɔ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu anyɛ ayashɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe mlɛo. Efiteɔ tsei ahe nibii hu ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei niyenii babaoo baa oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What basic changes do I need to make to turn my small backyard farm into a successful business?
ga: Mɛɛ tsakemɔi titrii esa akɛ mafee koni manyɛ matsake mishia sɛɛ ŋmɔ bibioo lɛ? mi lɛ kɛtee jarayeli nitsumɔ ko ni yeɔ omanye mli.

english: Commercial farming requires shifting from old burn-and-shift methods to permanent soil care. By preparing the land properly and building up soil fertility year after year, you can grow high yields on the same plot continuously.
ga: Jarayeli okwaayeli biɔ tsakemɔ kɛjɛ blema gbɛi ni akɛshãa nibii ni akɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee afi fɛɛ afi lɛ nɔ. Ebaanyɛ eya nɔ ewo yibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why are agricultural extension officers telling us to stop shifting from land to land every few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkpa shikpɔŋ kome nɔ tsakemɔ kɛmiiya ekroko nɔ daa afii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Shifting land happens because soil loses nutrients when burned or poorly managed. If you prepare and protect your land modernly, the soil stays rich, allowing you to harvest continuously from one piece of land.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ shimɔ baa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ laajeɔ kɛji ashã loo akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji osaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ he ni obu he yɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ gbɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni baa nii. Ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: How long does it take for soil to recover its strength if I stop burning my fields?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛji mikpa ŋmɔji lɛ ashãa?

english: Your soil will begin improving in the very first season you stop burning. Within two to three seasons of returning organic matter into the ground through proper clearing, the land becomes noticeably richer and yields grow significantly larger.
ga: Oshikpɔŋ lɛ baaje shishi ehi jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be ni obaakpa shãa lɛ mli. Yɛ bei enyɔ loo etɛ mli ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ ni ebaawo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when planted in an open field without big plants around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kooko tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and thin bark that cannot handle direct heat from the sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or Gliricidia near them creates shade that keeps the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ amɛhewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo glicidia ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my growing maize plants turning light green and yellow from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves, especially starting from the tip down the central vein, usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen is the plant food responsible for deep green leaves and healthy growth, and rain often washes it out of sandy soil.
ga: Kaadii ni ji ŋmɔŋ, titri lɛ kɛjɛ ŋwɛigbɛ kɛyashi ŋwɛigbɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehaa amɛdaraa waa. Ni nugbɔ lɛ fɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋã sũ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwiemɔ.

english: Why should I leave proper space between my cassava sticks instead of planting many close together to get more yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are too close, their roots compete underground for food and space, leading to many small, thin roots. Giving them proper space lets sunlight reach the leaves and gives the tubers room to swell big and heavy.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii kɛ he ko. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo babaoo baa. He ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ baai lɛ ahe. ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ
