english: Tomato flowers drop off when the daytime temperatures get too high or when the plant experiences sudden water stress. Without enough moisture or under intense heat, the plant drops its flowers to save water for its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ trukaa. Kɛji hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa loo latsaa ni naa wa shishi Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto nu kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop and look wilted during the hot afternoon even when the soil was watered in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu leebi?

english: In intense heat, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it up from the soil. Curling or drooping leaves is the plant's natural trick to reduce the surface exposed to the sun so it loses less moisture.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai ni shwieɔ shi loo ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli ŋaa ni ekɛbaa hulutsoo be lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ akaje mli.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm with my maize make the soil better for next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have special nodules on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop season ends, those roots decay and leave natural fertilizer behind for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Nakai shishifãi lɛ baafite ni amɛbaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts are fully mature and ready to dig up under the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ o-peanuts lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akumɔ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts show maturity above ground when the leaves start turning yellow and dropping off. You can test by pulling up one plant; if the inside of the pods has dark brown or black spots and the seeds fill out the shells tightly, they are ready.
ga: Peanuts daa yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ tso kome ni ooogbala kɛya ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ pod lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ediŋŋ ni dumɔwui lɛ ebɔle amɛhe jogbaŋŋ lɛ, no lɛ efee klalo.

english: Why do weeds always grow so much faster than my crop seeds after the first heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit naturally in the soil for years waiting for rain, and because they are wild, they have aggressive root systems built to grab water and fertilizer instantly, growing faster than domesticated crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo, ni amɛmɛɔ nugbɔ. Ni akɛni eji koo mli dumɔwu hewɔ lɛ Eyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni ama koni ekɛgbala nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Amɛdaraa oya fe dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shia mli.

english: Why does maize grown from seeds I saved from last year's harvest produce smaller cobs than certified hybrid seeds from the office?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa bibii fe dumɔwui ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni Nitsumɔhe lɛ etsɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their strength, disease resistance, and high yield power after one generation. Certified seeds are specially bred to give strong, uniform cobs with higher resistance to local pests and weather changes.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baafite hewalɛ. Helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ helai kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa yɛ yinɔ kome sɛɛ Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo dumɔwui ni mli wa ni yaa nɔ daa. ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cabbage plants full of tiny holes even when I don't see large insects on them during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii eyɛ mli akɛ minaaa kooloi wuji yɛ nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Tiny holes are usually caused by small pests like flea beetles or young caterpillars that feed during the early morning, late evening, or underside of leaves to hide from the hot daytime heat and birds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii leebi maŋkpa, gbɛkɛ, loo baai ashishi koni amɛkɛtee amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo kɛ okpoi ahe yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii baa.

english: How long does it take for a new coconut tree to start producing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei tso hee ko jeɔ shishi ewoɔ yibii?

english: Coconut trees are long-term crops; dwarf varieties usually start bearing fruit in 3 to 4 years, while traditional tall varieties can take 6 to 10 years.
ga: Kokoo tsei ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, tso ni ji dwarf lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema tso ni kɛlɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 6 kɛyashi 10.

english: How many months after planting can I harvest my maize?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ sɛɛ beni adu ŋmãa lɛ abaanyɛ akpa ŋmãa?

english: Most common maize varieties in Ghana mature quickly, usually taking between 90 to 120 days (3 to 4 months) from planting to harvest depending on rainfall.
ga: Abɛi henɔ ni afɔɔ naa waa yɛ Ghana lɛ daa oya. Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ gbii 90 kɛyashi 120 (nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4) kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ nii kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ mli. Edamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ falɛ nɔ

english: Can I plant maize and cassava together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, maize and cassava work very well together because maize grows quickly and is harvested in a few months, leaving space for the slower-growing cassava to expand later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, abele daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ haa gbɛ haa ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ koni egbɛ eshwa sɛɛ mli.

english: Is it good to grow short-term crops while waiting for my tree crops to mature?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu tsei ni yeɔ be kukuoo be mli ni mimɛɔ ni mi tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Yes, planting quick crops like maize or vegetables between young trees provides food and income during the early years before long-term trees like coconut begin yielding.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ oya, tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai. Niyenii kɛ shika jɛɛhe baafee tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Dani tsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ baabɔi yibiiwoo

english: How far apart should I space my coconut trees when planting?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi gbɛ ko yɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ?

english: Coconut trees need wide spacing, usually about 7 to 9 meters apart, so their leaves can spread out to catch sunlight without shading neighboring trees.
ga: Kokoo tsei biɔ gbɛ ni da. Bei pii lɛ, amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 7 kɛyashi 9 bɔni afee ni baai lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ ni amɛtsĩii tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ anaa.

english: What type of soil is best for growing cassava?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ̃ ji nɔ ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Cassava grows best in loose, well-drained sandy-loam soil where the tubers can expand easily underground without rotting in standing water.
ga: Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Tubers lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi oya ni amɛgbooo yɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli.

english: Why do coconut trees grow so well near coastal areas and sandy soils?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋshɔnaa hei kɛ shikpɔji ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Coconut palms have deep roots that absorb groundwater easily and are naturally adapted to handle high sunlight, warm weather, and sandy soil.
ga: Kokosu tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ oya. ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo hulu la ni tsoɔ waa, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize plants turn light yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or that heavy rains have washed nutrients out of the root zone.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why does cassava stay good under the ground even if I do not harvest it right away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei hi lolo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ? Ni mikpaaa nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Cassava roots naturally store energy and water underground, allowing mature plants to remain safely in the soil for several months until you are ready to harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi kɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa tsei ni eda lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo kɛyashiɔ be mli ni obaafee klalo akɛ obaakpa.

english: Why is it bad to plant cassava on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmei yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Cassava pulls a lot of nutrients out of the earth, so planting it continuously on the same soil without fertilizer or crop rotation causes the soil to become weak and reduces future yields.
ga: Cassava jieɔ niyenii kpakpai babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ fataaa he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa wɔsɛɛ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do some of the flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without ever turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi komɛi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off if they are not pollinated. Cocoa flowers rely on tiny midges or manual hand pollination to transfer pollen from one flower to another; without this transfer, the plant cannot form a pod and sheds the flower.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ afeee amɛ pollin. Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔɔ adesai bibii loo nine nɔ fɔfɔi ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ nɔ koni amɛkɛ fɔfɔi fɔfɔi lɛ ajɛ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛya ekroko mli. Kɛji akɛ nɛkɛ tsakemɔ nɛɛ bɛ lɛ, tso lɛ nyɛŋ afee pods ni ebaafite fɔfɔi.

english: How does hand-pollinating my crops actually help me get a bigger yield?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ miniji wo mitsei lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua mi ni mawo yibii babaoo?

english: Hand pollination ensures that pollen is transferred directly and reliably to every healthy flower, overcoming shortages of natural insect pollinators and resulting in more flowers successfully developing into full-sized fruits or pods.
ga: Nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ yaa tɛ̃ɛ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. Adebɔɔ mli fɔfɔi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ faaa lɛ anɔ kunimyeli Ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ aduawai loo ŋmeii ni da babaoo.

english: Why does my maize crop produce flowers at the top before I see any corn ears developing on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ ŋwɛi dani minaa toi ni shwereɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: The tassel at the top of the maize plant produces pollen first so that when it drops, it can land on the sticky silks of the young ears growing lower down, fertilizing them so kernels can form.
ga: Tassels ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ feɔ pollen klɛŋklɛŋ. koni kɛ́ egbee shi lɛ Ekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ siliki lɛ he. ni ji toi bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa shi akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii koni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃

english: Why does my crop produce plenty of big green leaves but very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo shi aduawai fioo pɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on growing leaves instead of flowers. Plants need balanced nutrients, especially phosphorus and potassium, to trigger flowering and fruit growth.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ baama baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii. Niyenii ni sa he miihia tsei. titri lɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium Koni ekɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai adalɛ mli hewalɛ

english: Why do my young seedling cocoa plants start wilting when the afternoon sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and small roots that lose water faster than they can absorb it in full sunlight, which is why planting shade crops like plantains alongside them keeps them cool and hydrated.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii. ni nu fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ enɔ Nɔ hewɔ ni aduɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, yɛ amɛmasɛi Enɛ baaye abua ni eha kookoo tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a defense mechanism. The plant rolls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which helps it conserve internal water until the temperature drops.
ga: Baai lɛ ni abɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop their lower leaves during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baa shi yɛ shishigbɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally sheds its lower, older leaves during droughts to reduce water loss, allowing the plant to keep its main stem and root tubers alive until rain returns.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa ni egbɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni nu ni elaaje lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ eshishifã titri lɛ kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and tall with small ears if I plant seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛtoi bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants compete heavily for sunlight, soil nutrients, and root space, leaving each plant with too few resources to grow thick stems and large ears.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ waa. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ shishifãi amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii fioo tsɔ ni ekɛbaakwɛ tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli tse kɛ toi wuji.

english: Why should I prune away dead or diseased branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tso niji ni egboi loo hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Cutting away diseased or dead branches stops infections from spreading to healthy limbs and prevents the tree from wasting energy on damaged parts, redirecting nutrients toward pod growth.
ga: Niji ni hela emɔ amɛ loo egboi lɛ ni afoɔ Ehaa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ. ni etsĩ tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ hei ni efite lɛ anɔ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ yaa pod lɛ dalɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do insects like bees and flies congregate around my vegetable farm when my crops start blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa lɛ? Mi aduawai ŋmɔ lɛ beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ fɔfɔii lɛ

english: Insects are attracted to the nectar in blooms, and as they move from flower to flower, they carry pollen on their bodies, which is necessary for crops like tomatoes, cucumbers, and peppers to produce fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi amli nu lɛ gbalaa kooloi. Ni beni amɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli lɛ, Amɛhiɛɔ pollen kɛyaa. Ehe hia koni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tomato, kukumba, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo yibii.

english: People talk about buying 'medicine' for crops, but what exactly does crop medicine do for my farm?
ga: Mɛi wieɔ ‘tsofa’ ni akɛbaahe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he, shi mɛni tuuntu tsei ahe tsofai feɔ kɛhaa miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Crop 'medicine' refers to agrochemicals like pesticides, fungicides, or fertilizers. Pesticides kill insects eating your crops, fungicides cure diseases caused by fungi, and fertilizers provide plant nutrients to help weak crops grow strong and produce healthy yields.
ga: Tso "tsofa" tsɔɔ okwaayeli tsofai tamɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi, ŋmeii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ onibii lɛ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ tsaa helai ni ŋmeii kɛbaa lɛ. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii haa tsei lɛ amli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are actually sick and need chemical treatment rather than just more water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela miimɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ tsofai babaoo atsu he nii fe nu ni fata he kɛkɛ?

english: Sick crops show specific signs like brown spots on leaves, rotting stems, white powdery patches, or leaves eaten by caterpillars. If your plants have wet soil but their leaves are still dying, turning yellow in patterns, or showing spots, they likely have a disease or pest problem rather than a lack of water.
ga: Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ baajie okadii pɔtɛɛ komɛi akpo, tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ. tso lɛ mli fãi ni egbo ni powda yɛŋ loo baai ni ŋmeii yeɔ Kɛji otso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ shi baai lɛ gboi lolo Nɔ ni afee lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ. aloo otii komɛi yɛ ni esa akɛ ana Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ tsei nɛɛ yɛ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagbai. yɛ nu ni baa shi lɛ najiaŋ

english: Is it safe to buy crop medicine from vendors selling bottles out of cars with loudspeakers in our village?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooohe tsei ahe tsofa kɛjɛ jarayelɔi ni hɔ̃ɔ tɔi ni jɛɔ tsɔnei ni yɔɔ wiemɔ tsɔnei amli lɛ adɛŋ yɛ wɔ akrowa lɛ mli?

english: It is very risky. Unofficial mobile vendors often sell fake, expired, or improperly mixed chemicals that can burn your crops, poison your soil, or harm your health. It is safer to buy inputs from registered agro-dealers who can show proper licensing and provide accurate instructions.
ga: Eyɛ oshara waa. Bei pii lɛ, mɛi ni jaa tɛlifoŋ ni bɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ hɔ̃ɔ tsofai ni ji amalei, ni be eho, loo ni akɛfutu mli jogbaŋŋ. ni baanyɛ ashã oŋmɔshi nibii Poison ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo ebaanyɛ eye ohewalɛ nɔ awui Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooohe saji kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ ni baanyɛ ajie gbɛŋmɛɛ woji ni sa kpo ni amɛkɛ ŋaawoo ni ja aha lɛ adɛŋ.

english: How do I know which specific medicine to buy when insects are eating my maize leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofa ni esa akɛ mahe kɛ́ kooloi ye mi ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ?

english: Different pests require different types of chemical treatments. Pluck a fresh sample of the damaged leaf and bring it along with the insect to your local extension officer or a licensed agro-dealer so they can identify the pest correctly and give you the right product.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui srɔtoi lɛ biɔ tsofai srɔtoi ni akɛtsaa amɛ. Bua baai ni efite lɛ ahe nɔkwɛmɔnii heei anaa ni okɛ amɛ kɛ kooloi bibii lɛ aya he ni oyɔɔ lɛ extension agent loo okwaayeli jarayelɔ ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ ŋɔɔ. Enɛ ji koni amɛnyɛ amɛyoo tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛha bo nɔ ni sa.

english: What should I do if a chemical seller offers me a bottle that has no label or clear instructions on it?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji tsofa-kɛ-ŋma hɔlɔlɔ ko ha mi tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ni aŋmalako nɔ ko loo gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ bɛ nɔ?

english: Do not buy or use it. Unlabeled containers may hold dangerous industrial chemicals or expired mixtures that will ruin your crop yield, poison your farm family, or damage the soil. Genuine agricultural products always have clear manufacturer labels, dosage guides, and safety warnings.
ga: Kaahe loo okɛtsu nii. Tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ nitsumɔhei loo nibii ni be efite ni baafite onibii lɛ baanyɛ ahi tsɛnsii ni aŋmalako nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ amli. Poison oŋmɔ mli weku lɛ. loo efite shikpɔŋ lɛ Esa akɛ okwaayeli nibii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ aná mɔ ni fee lɛ wolo. Tsofafeemɔ He Gbɛtsɔɔmɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwefeemɔ he kɔkɔbɔɔi ni mli ka shi faŋŋ be fɛɛ be

english: Will spraying more chemical than the bottle instructs heal my sick crops faster?
ga: Ani tsofai ni fe tɔ kome ni mikɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaha mitsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ atsa oya?

english: No, applying extra chemical will burn your crop leaves, waste your money, and leave dangerous chemical residue on your harvest. Always follow the exact mixing ratios provided on the product label or by your extension officer.
ga: Dabi, tsofai krokomɛi ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ baashã oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai, ebaafite shika, ni ebaashi tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara yɛ onikpamɔ lɛ mli. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, nyiɛmɔ futumɔ mlijaa ni atsɔɔ yɛ nibii lɛ ahe wolo lɛ nɔ loo o-extension agent lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do insects keep returning to my farm even after I spray them with crop medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yaa nɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tso tsofa ko wo amɛmli moŋ.

english: Pests return if neighboring farms are infested, if new insect eggs hatch after spraying, or if you use the exact same chemical repeatedly, which allows pests to become immune. To prevent this, rotate different types of spray chemicals and clear out infected plant material around your fields.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba kɛji akɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ebote mli. Kplukai afɔfɔi heei fɔɔ yɛ be mli ni ashwie amɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii shii abɔ ni haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛye nɔ Koni atsĩ enɛ naa Tsɔmɔmɔ tsofai srɔtoi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ. ni ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Can I use human medicine or household soap to cure diseases on my crop plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ adesa tsofa loo shia samla atsu nii kɛtsa helai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Human medicines do not work on plant diseases and can harm your crops. While mild soapy water can clear away tiny soft pests like aphids, plant diseases need real agricultural fungicides or recognized organic remedies designed specifically for crop leaves.
ga: Adesa tsofai nyɛɛɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei ahe helai ahe, ni ebaanyɛ eye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui. Yɛ be mli ni nu ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ Abaanyɛ ajie tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo tamɔ aphids lɛ, shi tsei ahe helai biɔ ni akɛ okwaayeli mli tsofai ni gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diɛŋtsɛ loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ atsu nii. ni afee lɛ pɔtɛɛ aha tsei ahe baai lɛ

english: Are there natural ways I can protect my crops from pests without spending money on chemical sprays?
ga: Ani adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ko yɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ni mikɛ shika tsuuu tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, you can rotate your crops each season, plant pest-repelling crops like onions or marigolds around your field edges, remove infected leaves by hand early, and make natural sprays using crushed neem tree leaves or wood ash.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ otsake onibii lɛ kɛjɛ be mli kɛya be kroko mli. Dumɔ tsei ni gbeɔ kooloi tamɔ sabolai loo marigolds yɛ ehe. oŋmɔ lɛ naa Okɛ onine ajie baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. ni okɛ neem baai ni atswa loo tso sũ afee adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ.

english: Can the medicine I spray on my crops stay in the harvest and make my family sick when we eat it?
ga: Ani tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli ni eha miweku lɛ he ajɔ amɛ kɛ́ wɔye?

english: Yes, if you harvest too soon after spraying. Every crop medicine has a safety waiting period called a 'Pre-Harvest Interval' printed on the label. You must wait the full number of required days after spraying before picking your crops so the chemical breaks down safely.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji okpa mra tsɔ yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ Tsei tsofai fɛɛ yɛ be ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛmɛɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘Pre-harvest’ ni akala yɛ wolo lɛ nɔ Esa akɛ omɛ gbii ayibɔ pɔtɛɛ ko yɛ tsofa ni okɛshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ato koni tsofai lɛ akumɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from my harvest produce smaller and weaker crops when I replant them the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ beni miduɔ amɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred to give high yields only in their first planting. When you save and replant those seeds, their genetic traits separate, resulting in uneven growth, smaller fruits, and unpredictable yields compared to buying fresh commercial seed.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Beni okɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ toɔ ni oduɔ lɛ Ajaraa dumɔwui lɛ amli fɔmɔ sui lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Yibii lɛ ji bibioo fe no. ni ekɛ yibiiwoo ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ baa kɛ akɛto jarayeli dumɔwui heei ni aheɔ lɛ he.

english: If I plant sweet pepper right next to hot pepper on my farm, will my sweet pepper fruits become spicy?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ masɛi Ani mi bell ŋmeii aduawai lɛ baafee ŋmeii?

english: Cross-pollination happens when insects carry pollen between nearby plants, but it only affects the seeds inside the fruit, not the fruit you harvest this season. Your sweet peppers will stay sweet, but if you save those seeds to plant next year, the new plants may produce spicy peppers.
ga: Krɔs-pollination baa kɛji kooloi woɔ pollen yɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ ateŋ. Shi enáa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ pɛ nɔ hewalɛ. Jeee aduawai ni okpaa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ ji no. O bell peppers ɔ maa pee nɔ́ nɛ ŋɔɔ lolo. Shi kɛji akɛ okɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ to ni okɛdu afi ni baa lɛ hu? Tsei heei hu baanyɛ awo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ.

english: Why did my crops burn and turn yellow after I applied fertilizer during a hot, dry week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ otsi ni mli edɔ ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizers are concentrated salts that need soil moisture to dissolve safely. Applying them when the soil is dry causes the fertilizer to pull water out of the plant roots instead of feeding them, which scorches the roots and turns the leaves yellow.
ga: Fertilizers ji ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ ni biɔ ni nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Enɛ baashã shishifãi lɛ ni ebaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does my field yield less harvest every year when I keep planting maize in the same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Ani ooodu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows specific pests to build up. Rotating your maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and disrupts pest life cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi baa amɛhe shi. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ Ekɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashihilɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear away all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive under direct, intense sunlight. Keeping larger shade trees or planting plantains alongside new cocoa provides a canopy that cools the soil and protects the young cocoa leaves from scorching until they mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo hee masɛi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together to get more plants on my land, why do I end up with a smaller total harvest?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hu? Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo fɛɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops planted too tightly compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to develop strong stems, deep roots, and larger, healthier fruits or cobs.
ga: Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli wa, shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, kɛ aduawai loo ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants twisting and turning yellow even though I cleared all the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ? Akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Yellow, twisted leaves are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies or infected stem cuttings. Removing infected plants early and switching to certified disease-resistant stem varieties stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni etse ehe lɛ baa. ni ji ŋmeii bibii loo tsei niji ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ahe nitsulɔi Ajieɔ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ mra ni atsakeɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ helai ni yɔɔ he odaseyeli lɛ anɔ. Ebaaha helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do some farmers spread dry grass and leaves around the base of their vegetable plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ? Amɛ aduawai tsei lɛ ashishitoo?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material is called mulching. It keeps the soil cool under direct sun, prevents moisture from evaporating quickly, and stops weeds from sprouting around your crop roots.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ tsei ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa oya ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ otsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce many flowers, but the flowers keep falling off before making tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani afee tomatoi lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when plants suffer from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of key nutrients like calcium. Maintaining consistent soil moisture through regular watering and using balanced fertilizer helps the plant convert its flowers into fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsakeɔ fɔfɔi amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Does leaving weeds in my maize field during the first few weeks really harm my yield if I clear them later?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni mashi yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ baaná miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii kɛji mikɛ jwɛi shwie amɛnɔ sɛɛ mli?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and consume the water and fertilizer meant for your seedlings during their critical early growth stage. Weeding within the first 3 to 4 weeks ensures your maize builds a strong foundation for full cobs.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. ni oye nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha odumɔwui lɛ yɛ amɛ shishijee dalɛ bei ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni o-ŋmã lɛ afee shishitoo ni wa kɛha ŋmãa ni eyi obɔ.

english: What is the difference between the major rainy season and the minor rainy season for my crops in southern Ghana?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni ji shishijee kɛ nɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ teŋ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ Ghana Anaigbɛ lɛ?

english: The major season brings longer and heavier rains, making it best for main crops that take many months to grow like cassava and late-maturing maize. The minor season has shorter rains, which are better suited for quick-growing crops like vegetables, cowpeas, or early-maturing grains.
ga: Be ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni naa wa baa. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani ekwɛɔ, tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni shwereɔ sɛɛ. Be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ, nugbɔ baanɛ fioo. Amɛhi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ aduawai, tsina ŋmei, loo dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting when the major season rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: You should wait until the soil stays consistently moist for a few consecutive days after the rains start, rather than planting right after the very first light rainfall, so your seeds do not dry up in the dirt.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ eje shishi lɛ sɛɛ. Mohu ɔ, duɔ amlɔ nɔuu ngɛ kekleekle nugbɔ nɛ nɛ ɔ se. Koni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Which crops are best for me to plant during the minor season when rains are shorter?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ makwɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni ji enyɔ, ni ji kuku lɛ mli?

english: Crops that mature quickly and require less water—such as tomatoes, peppers, garden eggs, beans, and short-duration maize—thrive during the minor season because they finish yielding before the dry period sets in.
ga: Tsei ni daa oya ni amɛbiɔ nu fioo, tamɔ tomato, ŋmɔtɔ, abɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ be kukuoo. Ebaanyɛ eda yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli ejaakɛ agbeɔ nifeemɔ lɛ naa dani hulutsoo be lɛ baashɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like tubes when the sun is very hot during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When maize leaves curl up, the plant is protecting itself from losing water in the intense heat. By rolling its leaves, it reduces the area exposed to the hot sun to survive until cooler weather or rain arrives.
ga: Beni ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ Tsei buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ he. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu lɛ shɛɔ lɛ baa shi bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ loo nugbɔ baanɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants dropping their leaves during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during dry spells to conserve water and survive. Even though the stems look bare, the roots below the ground remain healthy and fresh leaves will sprout as soon as rain returns.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi shi. Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ nɔ ko moŋ Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ mli wa lolo ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ pɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce very small harvests when I plant them late in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu yɛ be ni shɛɔ lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Late-planted crops run out of rainfall before they can fully form flowers, fruits, or grains. Without enough water during their flowering stage, the plants stop growing early and yield very little harvest.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ baagboi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi, aduawai loo dumɔwui kwraa. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ Tso lɛ baakpa dalɛ oya ni ebaawo yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Should I leave my farm bare or plant cover crops during periods when I am not actively farming?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ loo madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ yɛ be mli ni mikɛ ekãa tsuuu ŋmɔ lɛ he nii lɛ?

english: It is best to cover the soil or plant leguminous cover crops like cowpeas or mucuna. Leaving soil bare exposes it to scorching sun and heavy rain that wash away valuable plant nutrients, whereas cover crops keep the soil healthy and weed-free.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo odu ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo mucilagina. Kɛ́ ashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baashɛ enɔ, ni no shwieɔ tsei amli niyenii ni jara wa lɛ kɛyaa. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni jwɛi bɛ nɔ.

english: How does spreading dry leaves around my crops help them grow during warm weather?
ga: Baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry grass or leaves around the roots (mulching) acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the soil, keeps root zones cool under hot sun, and gradually breaks down into natural food for your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni agbɛɔ ashwãa shishifãi lɛ ahe (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli, ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa shishifã lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi, ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha onibii.

english: Is it good to continue farming short-term crops during the minor season instead of leaving the land idle?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kuku yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni aaashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, planting short-term crops like beans or vegetables during the minor season makes productive use of your land, provides income between major harvests, and protects the topsoil from wind and erosion.
ga: Hɛɛ, be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo aduawai ni ooodu yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Feemɔ shika yɛ kpamɔ wulu lɛ mli. ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋshɔkei ahe.

english: Why is it important for me to clear my land weeks before the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ otsii komɛi dani nugbɔ anɛ lɛ?

english: Clearing early allows plant material time to decompose into manure, gives you time to prepare ridges or mounds, and ensures you can plant immediately after the first good rains arrive without wasting growing time.
ga: Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ haa tso lɛ mli nibii lɛ be ni ekɛfiteɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa onáa be ni okɛsaa ŋshɔ lɛ loo gɔŋ lɛ. Ni ehaa onyɛɔ oduɔ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ kpakpa lɛ eba lɛ ni ofiteee dumɔ be ko kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build strong, green leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps restore their green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ni yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when there is bright sunlight for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain or banana next to them provides cover, keeping the soil cool and moist while the cocoa grows stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ waa kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo banana yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ amɛ ato, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa waa lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes too hot and dry, or when the plant doesn't get enough water regularly. Keeping the moisture in the soil consistent by watering regularly at the base helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ daa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni shwereɔ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests and diseases that love maize to build up in the field. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans help make my farm soil richer for future crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni jara wa kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and turn it into soil plant food. When you harvest them and leave their roots and stems to decay, they leave free fertility in the soil for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa efeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa ni oshi shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛgboi lɛ, Amɛbaashi ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket that stops the hot sun from evaporating moisture out of the soil. It also suppresses weeds and slowly turns into rich organic matter as it breaks down.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekajie ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ekɛ jwɛi lɛ tsiɔ naa ni fiofio lɛ Ebafeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why does planting my crops too close together lead to smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mitsei lɛ ni miduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots and leaves fight each other for limited water, sunlight, and soil food. Giving each plant proper space allows it to grow full roots and leaves, resulting in larger fruits and seeds.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji aduawai kɛ dumɔwui wuji.

english: You should dig into the soil with a stick or cutlass after the rain. If the ground is thoroughly wet down to the depth of your hand, it is safe to plant; if only the top thin layer is wet, seeds may germinate and dry up quickly.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tso loo dade atsa shikpɔŋ lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛyashɛ shishi lɛ Abaanyɛ adu lɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛji ŋwɛi fã lɛ pɛ mli efɔ lɛ Dumɔwui baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi oya.

english: Which part of a cassava stem is best for me to cut and plant for a good yield?
ga: Mɛɛ tso lɛ fã ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaafo ni adu koni aná yibii kpakpai?

english: The best stem cuttings come from the mature middle section of a healthy, fully grown cassava plant, not the green top or woody base. Choose cuttings that are about a hand length long with several healthy buds visible.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ jɛɔ ŋmei tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eda lɛ teŋgbɛ fã ni eda lɛ mli. Jeee tso ŋmɔŋ loo tso shishi. Halamɔ tso nine ni kɛlɛ ji aaafee nine kome ni fɔfɔii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni anaa lɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat and make holes inside the center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeɔ nii ni amɛfoɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, pests that hide inside the funnel of young maize leaves to chew the fresh growth. Checking your fields early and spraying recommended bio-pesticides or neem leaf extracts directly into the center funnel stops them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmãa tsei heei. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli mra ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tso lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ afɔ ŋshɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which helps them build strong green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away from the roots deep into the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji feɔ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and feeling dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that suck the plant juices and spread diseases, or by extreme hot weather when the plant curls its leaves to save water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ tso mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli beni tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat, lack of water in the soil, or when they have received too much chemical fertilizer that makes them grow leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hao amɛ waa, ni no haa baai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when heavy rain falls close to harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni ebɛŋkɛ kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil starves cassava roots of air, allowing harmful fungi sitting in the wet soil to attack and decay the roots before you can dig them up.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ akashɛ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ha ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni ta shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ atutua ni amɛfite shishifãi lɛ dani obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do my corn stalks grow tall and thin with small cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They spend their energy stretching high for light instead of growing thick cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Akɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛgbala kane lɛ mli moŋ fe ni amɛaatsɔ ŋmei ni mli edɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers start sprouting in the storage barn before the rains even arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ shĩa lɛ mli dani nugbɔ lɛ po baa lɛ?

english: Yam tubers have a natural internal clock. When the temperature inside the storage barn rises, the tuber senses that it is time to wake up and begins growing sprouts for the next planting season.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa. Kɛji hulutsoo be ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tee hiɛ lɛ Bulbs lɛ baanu he akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛte shi ni amɛje dumɔwui adumɔ shishi kɛha ŋmɔ lɛ mli shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are caterpillars eating the inner leaves of my corn plants mostly in the early morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ babaoo leebi maŋkpa lɛ?

english: Caterpillars like fall armyworms hide deep inside the center funnel of the corn plant during hot afternoons to stay cool, coming out to feed on soft leaves during the cooler morning hours.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ cutworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛha amɛhe afee fɛ̃i. ni ebaaje kpo ebaye baai bibii lɛ Leebi lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas make my soil better for the next crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants have a special partnership with good bacteria in the soil that pull food from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that food stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for maize.
ga: Cowpea tsei kɛ bacteria kpakpa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ yɛ tsakpaa krɛdɛɛ ko. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai niyenii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster and bigger than my planted crops after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛdaraa fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally tough and well adapted to local soils, allowing their roots to drink rainwater and soak up plant food much quicker than tender cultivated crop seeds.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔji lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ nuɔ nugbɔ nu ni amɛmɔɔ tso mli niyenii oya fe dumɔwui ni adu blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why does the government take several years before giving us new crop seed varieties to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ nɔyeli lɛ afii babaoo dani ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei haa lɛ? koni wɔdu?

english: Agricultural researchers must test new seed varieties across different regions and weather seasons for years to ensure the plants resist local pests, survive droughts, and produce high yields before distributing them to farmers.
ga: Esa akɛ okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi aka dumɔwui srɔtoi heei amɛkwɛ. yɛ kpokpai srɔtoi anɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli afii babaoo koni tsei lɛ akpee tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anaa. ejo hɔmɔ naa foi ni ewo yibii babaoo dani aja aha okwaafoi

english: Why do the improved maize seeds I buy give a bigger harvest than the seeds I save from my own farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ ni miheɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are specially bred by scientists to have strong traits like disease resistance and higher yield. When you harvest and plant seeds from those crops, they lose those special traits over time and produce less.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi ekwɛ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛná sui ni mli wa tamɔ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo. Kɛji okpa ni odu dumɔwui kɛjɛ nakai tsei lɛ amli Dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, which the plant needs to grow healthy green leaves and strong stems.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, ni he hia tso lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ tsei ni wa.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce small fruits when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui babaoo Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which starves the individual plants and reduces yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei aŋkroaŋkroi ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: This is usually caused by bacterial or fungal diseases in the soil that attack the roots and block water from moving up into the stems and leaves, making the plant wilt despite wet soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, muawai loo ŋmeii hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tutuaa shishifãi lɛ ni etsĩɔ nu naa koni ekaya tso lɛ shishi kɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efɔ ŋmɔtɔ po.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds when the rains do not come at the usual time anymore?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui? Beni nugbɔ lɛ baaa dɔŋŋ yɛ be ni afɔɔ enɛɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the ground receives steady, deep rain over several days to soak the soil properly, rather than planting right after the very first light shower which can dry up quickly.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo dani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Mohu ɔ, duɔ amlɔ nɔuu ngɛ kekleekle nugbɔ nɛ nɛ nɛ ma nyɛ maa gbi oya ɔ se.

english: Why do some cassava varieties survive long dry seasons while others wither and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ? yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Drought-tolerant varieties are developed to grow deeper root systems that reach underground moisture and have leaves that retain water better during dry periods.
ga: Afee tsei srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa koni amɛkwɛ̃ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔtɔ he, ni amɛyɛ baai ni hiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant yam on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same plot every year drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the earth.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my stored cowpea seeds get full of small holes and fail to grow when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni ato lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni enyɛŋ eda kɛji midu lɛ?

english: Insects called weevils lay tiny eggs inside stored beans and eat the seeds from the inside out; storing seeds in airtight containers or using safe grain protectants stops this damage.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ wɔji bibii. Akɛ ŋmeii lɛ toɔ mli ni ayeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tsu nii lɛ, ehaa nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ kpaa.

english: Why do my crops burn or die when I apply fertilizer directly near their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shãa loo amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is very strong salt; putting it directly against plant stems draws water out of the plant roots and causes fertilizer burn. It should be applied a short distance away from the stem in moist soil.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli ŋmei fa babaoo waa. Kɛ́ okɛwo tsei ashishifãi anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaagbala nu kɛjɛ tsei ashishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ashã. Esa akɛ akɛ he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ fioo atsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Why do I see small insects attacking the tender tips of my cocoa branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa kooloi bibii ni tutuaa mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Insects like mirids or capsids target the fresh tips of cocoa branches because they are soft and full of nutrients. Sucking sap from these tips weakens the tree and stops healthy new leaves from growing.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ mirids loo capsids lɛ shwieɔ kookoo niji heei lɛ ashishigbɛ. Ejaakɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Kɛ́ mɔ ko nu nu ni jɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ amli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ daalɛ kpaa.

english: How can I check my cocoa farm to catch pests before they destroy my harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mana tsɛŋemɔ helai dani amɛfite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Inspect your trees tree by tree, checking under leaves, on pod stems, and at the trunk base. Spotting pests early allows you to remove them before they multiply into a large outbreak.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mli aŋkroaŋkroi. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi, yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi, kɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ojieɔ amɛ dani amɛshwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela wulu ko.

english: Is it useful to manually pick pests off my cocoa trees one by one?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ akɛ niji baajie tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛ cacao tsei aŋkroaŋkroi amli, tso komekomei?

english: Yes, picking off pests by hand when you first notice them prevents small pest populations from growing into major infestations, saving your crop without immediately needing costly chemicals.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ onine kpata kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahiɛ beni oyɔse amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji. Ehaa okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii toɔ ni tsofai ni jara wa he ehiaaa bo amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds and debris around the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛ sũ ni ebɔle kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Clearing the soil around the tree trunk removes hiding spots for pests and prevents fungal diseases from breeding in wet leaf litter and spreading up into your cocoa pods.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni asaa he ni bɔleɔ Tsei akutsei lɛ ahe lɛ jieɔ hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ kɛyaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baafɔ yɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ amli ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kookoo ŋmɔji amli.

english: Is it safe for me to drop cut branches and pruned leaves directly under my cocoa tree?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mashi tsei niji ni afo lɛ ni mafo baai lɛ yɛ cacao tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Only drop leaves and branches if they are healthy. If you leave pest-infested or diseased branches on the ground under the tree, the pests can easily climb back up and attack the tree again.
ga: Shĩ baai kɛ tsei aniji kɛji amɛyɛ hewalɛ pɛ. Kɛji oshi tsei niji ni tsɛŋemɔ helai emɔ amɛ loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ akwɔ ekoŋŋ oya ni amɛtutua tso lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What is the difference between pest damage and tree disease on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii kɛ tsei ahe helai ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ teŋ?

english: Pests are insects or animals that physically chew, bite, or suck on the tree, while diseases are spread by microscopic germs like fungi or viruses that cause pods to rot or the tree to wither.
ga: Kooloi bibii ji koolooi loo kooloi ni shwieɔ, amɛkɔɔ, loo amɛnuɔ tsei. Yɛ be mli ni helai srɔtoi Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ helai bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo helai ni haa ŋmeii loo tsei shwieɔ shi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do crop diseases cause more damage to my cocoa yield than regular insects?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai fiteɔ mi kokoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fe kooloi krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Insects usually damage specific parts like leaves or pod surfaces, but diseases like Black Pod spread rapidly through water and air, completely rotting whole pods and spreading quickly across your entire farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii fiteɔ fãi pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ baai loo pod lɛ hiɛ, shi helai tamɔ pod diŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Ehaa pods fɛɛ fiteɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What should I do if I find a rotting pod hanging on my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina ŋmeii ni egboi ni efo cacao tso ko nɔ?

english: You should pick off the rotting pod immediately and remove it from the tree. Leaving it hanging allows rain and wind to scatter disease spores onto healthy pods nearby.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ojie kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ oshi lɛ ni egbele lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ agbɛ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cut off the damaged tips of my cocoa branches when pests attack them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo niji ni efite lɛ ashishifãi beni tsɛŋemɔ helai batutua mi lɛ?

english: Cutting off pest-damaged tips prevents rot and dieback from traveling deeper into the main branch, encouraging the tree to sprout new, healthy green shoots.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai efite lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii kɛ gbele naa koni amɛkabote tso lɛ nine wulu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Wo tsei hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do young pods fall off my cocoa trees after insects bite them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii shwieɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ beni kooloi emɔ amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When insects suck sap from young pod stalks, the tree gets stressed and short on nutrients, causing it to drop small pods to protect its main trunk and root system.
ga: Kɛji kooloi bibii miinu nu ni jɛ tsei bibii amli lɛ Tso lɛ baaná haomɔ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ hu bɛ. ni haa egbeeɔ ŋmeii bibii amli Koni ebu tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe

english: If rain falls heavily right after I finish planting my maize, does that mean I can stay home for a few weeks without visiting the farm?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu ŋmãa lɛ, Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ manyɛ mahi shia otsii fioo komɛi ni ehe ehiaaa ni maya ŋmɔ mli?

english: Rain helps your seeds sprout, but it also causes aggressive weeds to germinate at the same time. If you do not visit your farm regularly after planting, weeds will quickly overtake your seedlings and starve them of soil nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ yeɔ ebuaa odumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Shi ehaa jwɛi ni baa shi lɛ hu kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be kome too mli. Kɛji oyaaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ baaye odumɔwui lɛ anɔ oya ni ebaaha hɔmɔ aye amɛ kɛjɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Is it true that cassava crops can grow successfully on their own without much attention after planting?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ ŋmei tsei baanyɛ adara amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni adu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cassava is tough, but young cassava cuttings need constant clearing of weeds during their first three months. If weeds choke the young plants early on, the roots cannot develop properly and your yield will be very small.
ga: Kasava wa. Shi ehe miihia ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmeii bibii ni afo lɛ amli be fɛɛ be yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ amli. Kɛji jwɛi lɛ shwie tsei bibii lɛ anɔ mra lɛ, Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ adara jogbaŋŋ ni onibii ni obaaná lɛ baafee bibioo kwraa.

english: How often should I visit my young cocoa farm after transplanting the seedlings?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ maya mi-kokoo ŋmɔ bibioo lɛ mli beni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ ewo he kroko lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should check young cocoa seedlings at least twice a week. Young seedlings burn easily in strong sunlight and are vulnerable to insect attacks, so frequent visits help you spot problems early and provide necessary shade.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ o-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ amli shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli. Dumɔwui bibii shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli ni kooloi baanyɛ atutua amɛ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, saramɔ shii abɔ Ebaaye ebua bo ni ona naagbai mra. ni ekɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa aha.

english: Why do my maize leaves start turning yellow a few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni adu lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil or that weeds are stealing the plant food. Checking your crops early allows you to weed and apply fertilizer before the crop is ruined.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo akɛ jwɛi miiju tso lɛ niyenii. Nibii ni adu lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ojieɔ jwɛi lɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli dani nibii ni adu lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ tomato ko kwraa wooo lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat stress, irregular watering, or lack of key soil nutrients. Regular farm visits help you maintain steady watering and soil care to keep the flowers alive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Saramɔ ni oooya ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ tsuɔ nii koni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to bear fruits compared to other farms in my community?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ akɛto ŋmɔji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ mi akutso lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Plantain plants delay fruiting when too many extra suckers grow around the main stem and fight for food. You need to inspect the farm regularly and trim away excess suckers so energy goes into producing fruit.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baaha yibiiwoo lɛ asɛɛ afo kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ amɛhe. main trunk ni okɛ niyenii he akaŋshii Ehe miihia ni okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa ni ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ koni eha hewalɛ kɛha aduawai afeemɔ.

english: Why does my cowpea farm produce plenty of green leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ?

english: Cowpeas produce excess leaves when there is too much nitrogen in the soil or when insects attack the young flowers. Inspecting your crop during the flowering stage helps you manage pests before they destroy the pod production.
ga: Cowpeas woɔ baai ni fa fe nine kɛ́ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tutuaa fɔfɔi bibii Onibii ni okwɛɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔi be lɛ mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ dani amɛfiteɔ pod feemɔ.

english: What causes my pepper plant leaves to curl up and stop growing after planting?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛkpaa dalɛ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the sap from young leaves. Visiting your farm frequently allows you to catch these insects early before they spread disease throughout the whole plot.
ga: Nɔ ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ. Kɛ́ oya oŋmɔ lɛ mli shii abɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni omɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ oya dani amɛgbɛ helai amɛshwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my yam leaves turn brown and dry up long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Early leaf browning in yams is often caused by leaf spot diseases or stem rot. Regular monitoring helps you stake the vines off the damp soil and clear diseased leaves early to protect the subterranean tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo shishifãi ni egbo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai asarasu mra okadii ni yɔɔ atomo mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ mli daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni okɛ wain tso lɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ, ni ojie tso lɛ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. koni akɛbu shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ahe

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster on my field than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni midu jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to compete aggressively for sunlight, water, and space. If you leave your field unattended after planting, weeds will easily outgrow your crops and ruin the money you spent on seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni sa kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ ŋwɛi akaŋshii. Kɛji oshi ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ beni odu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ baakwɛ̃ fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mlɛo ni ebaafite shika ni okɛdu dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Yellow and curling leaves are usually a sign that your crop is stressed, often caused by a lack of nutrients like nitrogen in the soil or an attack by pests like fall armyworms. Checking under the leaves early helps you identify if insects are feeding on the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miihao. Bei pii lɛ, niyenii mli nibii tamɔ nitrogen ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ cutworms ni tutuaa mɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi mra. Enɛ baaye abua bo ni ona kɛji kooloi yeɔ tsei lɛ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungal infection that thrives in high humidity and wet weather. Pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and air to dry the pods, which helps prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: What should I inspect on a chemical bottle before applying it to my crops?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma tsɛnsi mli dani mikɛtsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: You should always check the expiration date, ensure the container seal is unbroken, and confirm that the chemical is specifically approved for your type of crop. Using damaged or expired products can burn your crops or prove completely ineffective against pests.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ gbi ni ekɛbaatsu nii lɛ be fɛɛ be. Kwɛmɔ akɛ tsɛnsi lɛ mli naatsii lɛ efiteee. ni oma nɔ mi akɛ akpɛlɛ tsofa lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Nibii ni efite loo nibii ni efite ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã onibii loo etsɔɔ akɛ etsuuu nii kwraa yɛ hebuu mli kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why is it unsafe for me to mix different farm chemicals together before spraying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ebɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni jɛ ŋmɔji srɔtoi amli lɛ baafutu lɛ? ekome dani akɛshwie nɔ?

english: Combining chemicals without expert guidance can trigger harmful chemical reactions that weaken their effectiveness, damage your crop foliage, or leave toxic chemical residues in the soil.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛfataa he ni ŋaalɔi akudɔɔɔ amɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara aba ni baaha tsofai lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba shi. Kpata oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ ahiɛ loo shi tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the plant directs all its energy into growing top foliage rather than storing energy in its underground roots. Balanced soil nutrition keeps root development on track.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen babaoo fe nine kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe lɛ, Tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛyaa hiɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off instead of forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of insect pollinators. Maintaining consistent soil moisture and encouraging bees nearby helps ensure flowers successfully turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa loo kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ faaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ hewalɛwoo yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔii feɔ aduawai yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: How does planting my plantains too close together affect their growth?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ saa amɛdalɛ he?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots and leaves compete directly for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to build thick stems and carry heavy bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii baa.

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to support a new crop before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei anɔ dani madu?

english: Healthy soil should be dark, hold moisture without staying waterlogged, and contain visible organic matter or earthworms. Pale leaves or stunted plants from previous seasons indicate that soil nutrients need to be restored with compost or fertilizer before planting.
ga: Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa afee ediŋŋ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni nu bɛ mli ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni anaa yɛ jɛmɛ Baai ni tsuɔ loo tsei ni egbɔjɔ kɛjɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii aku sɛɛ aku sɛɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii lɛ awo mli dani adu.

english: Why do some of my seeds fail to sprout after I plant them in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are planted too deep in the soil, lack adequate moisture, or were damaged by heat or insects during storage. Inspecting seeds for pest holes and keeping the seedbed moist ensures higher germination rates.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ mli loo latsaa loo kooloi ni fiteɔ lɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ amli kwɛmɔ kɛji ŋmeii bu yɛ mli ni aha dumɔwui lɛ ashishi afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ babaoo.

english: How can an agricultural extension officer assist me on my farm?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Extension officers provide expert, government-backed training on recommended farming techniques. They can visit your farm to diagnose crop diseases accurately, guide safe chemical administration, and help improve overall yield.
ga: Amralofoi lɛ tsiɔ tsɔsemɔ ni nɔyeli lɛ fiɔ sɛɛ ni akɛhaa ŋaalɔi ni kɔɔ okwaayeli he ŋaai ni ajieɔ yi lɛ he lɛ he hewalɛ. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛyasara oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛyakwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli helai jogbaŋŋ. Tsɔɔmɔ tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe he ŋaa ni eye ebua ni eha nitsumɔ fɛɛ aya hiɛ

english: Why am I getting very few bags of harvest from my large four-acre farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ nibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ agbo ni dalɛ ji acre ejwɛ lɛ mli lɛ kotokui fioo pɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Having a large piece of land does not automatically mean a big harvest. If the soil lacks essential nutrients, plants cannot produce to their full potential regardless of field size.
ga: Shikpɔŋ wulu ni mɔ ko yɔɔ lɛ etsɔɔɔ akɛ ebaakpa nii babaoo kɛkɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee amɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ekɔɔɔ he eko bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ da ha.

english: How can I double the harvest I get from my current farm without buying more land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafee nibii ni miwoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ni miyɔɔ mli amrɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ toi enyɔ ni miheee shikpɔŋ babaoo?

english: You can double your output on the same land size by adding proper plant food like fertilizer, using quality seeds, and maintaining proper plant spacing to maximize soil potential.
ga: Obaanyɛ oná yibiiwoo lɛ shii enyɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ kɛtsɔ tsei aniyenii ni sa, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ. ni akwɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛ ni sa nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ babaoo.

english: Is spending money on fertilizer really worth it, or will it just lower my profits?
ga: Ani eji shika fitemɔ diɛŋtsɛ akɛ ooohe ŋmɔshi nibii loo ebaaha sɛɛnamɔi ni anáa lɛ aba shi kɛkɛ?

english: Fertilizer is an investment that usually pays off. Although it costs money upfront, the significant increase in yield—often nearly doubling your harvest—covers the cost and leaves you with more profit overall.
ga: Fertilizer ji shika ni akɛwoɔ nitsumɔ mli ni bei pii lɛ, sɛɛnamɔi kpakpai baa. Kɛji akɛ esa akɛ owo shika kɛtsɔ hiɛ po. Shi yibiiwoo ni yaa hiɛ babaoo lɛ—bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni miihe ashɛ okpamɔ lɛ toi enyɔ—haa shika ni he hiaa lɛ he nyɔmɔ ni ehaa onáa sɛɛnamɔ babaoo yɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: What does fertilizer actually do to make crops produce more harvest?
ga: Mɛni ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ diɛŋtsɛ? Koni aná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akpa?

english: Fertilizer acts as food for crops, supplying essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus that strengthen plant roots, keep leaves healthy, and help crops produce bigger, more abundant fruit or grains.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. ni woɔ tsei shishifãi hewalɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ mli waa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai loo ŋmaa wuji ni fa babaoo.

english: If I can only afford a small amount of fertilizer, should I spread it thinly over my entire farm?
ga: Kɛji manyɛ mahe ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko pɛ. Ani esa akɛ magbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: It is better to apply the full recommended amount of fertilizer to a smaller portion of your farm than to spread it too thin. Crops given too little fertilizer will still underperform.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ fɛɛ awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli he bibioo ko moŋ fe ni ooogbɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashwã tsɔ. Tsei ni ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ nine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baaya nɔ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my farmland produce less yield now than it did when I first started farming it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo fe be mli ni mibɔi okwaayeli lɛ?

english: Every time you harvest crops, they draw nutrients out of the earth. Over time, the soil gets exhausted and worn out, leading to lower yields unless you actively replenish it with fertilizer or organic matter.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii Ebaajie niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaafite. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi. Ja okɛ hiɛdɔɔ miifata ŋmɔshi nibii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ahe.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning pale and yellow even after I clear all the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mijie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that crops are hungry for nutrients like nitrogen in the soil. Clearing weeds reduces competition, but plants still need nutrient-rich soil or fertilizer to stay green and healthy.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ nitrogen, he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ haa akaŋshii baa shi. Shi shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ he miihia tsei lolo koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Can leaving old crop stems and weeds on the field give my soil enough food without fertilizer?
ga: Ani tsei bibii kɛ jwɛi ni egbɔ ni mashi yɛ shia lɛ mli lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awooo mli?

english: Decomposing plants help build organic soil texture, but heavily farmed soils often lack enough concentrated nutrients. Adding fertilizer provides the fast boost crops need for major yield increases.
ga: Tsei ni fiteɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni etswaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ emaa shi. Shi bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ waa lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ oya koni eha ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo aya hiɛ.
