english: How do I measure whether my farm is making progress from year to year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ miiya hiɛ daa afi?

english: Track progress by recording the number of bags harvested per acre every season alongside your total expenses; an increase in bags harvested per acre indicates your soil productivity is improving.
ga: Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni oyaa hiɛ ohaa lɛ kɛtsɔ kotokui ayibɔ ni akpaa yɛ acre kome mli daa afi kɛ shika fɛɛ ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni oooŋmala lɛ nɔ. Baagi ni akpaa yɛ acre kome mli lɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni anáa lɛ etee hiɛ.

english: How do I keep my land producing high yields every year without the soil breaking down?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mishikpɔŋ lɛ awo yibii babaoo afi fɛɛ afi ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieee shi?

english: Consistent high yields require feeding the soil regularly with proper fertilizers, rotating crops to keep soil healthy, and practicing good weed and pest control so the land never becomes completely exhausted.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni yaa hiɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ biɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa aha shikpɔŋ lɛ daa. Tsɔmɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. ni akase jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ajiemɔ jogbaŋŋ. koni shikpɔŋ lɛ akaho

english: Why do my maize crops grow much taller and greener when I put animal manure on the soil compared to when I use nothing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ daa ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto be mli ni mikɛ nɔ ko kwraa tsuuu nii lɛ he lɛ?

english: Animal manure is rich in essential nutrients like nitrogen. When added to the soil, it breaks down and feeds the roots, helping the maize leaves produce energy faster and grow strong.
ga: Nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛfata sũ lɛ he lɛ, egboɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ niyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ oya ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: If I use runoff water from my fish pond to irrigate my crop field, will it burn my plants?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ loo ŋshɔ mli lɛ tsu nii kɛshwie ŋmɔ mli nu Ani tso lɛ baashã?

english: Fish pond water will not burn your plants; it actually helps them. Water from fish ponds contains natural waste and organic matter that act as a gentle, nutrient-rich fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ loo ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ shãŋ otsei lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ waa diɛŋtsɛ. Loo ŋshɔ mli nu lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli jwɛi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli kɛhaa onibii lɛ.

english: Can I process leftover crop residues like cassava peels and maize stalks into feed for farm animals instead of throwing them away?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ŋmɔ mli nibii ni eshwɛ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ mafee ŋmɔ mli kooloi aniyenii moŋ fe ni mashɛrɛ amɛ ashwie?

english: Yes, crop residues can be dried, ground, or fermented to make safe livestock feed or composted to return valuable nutrients back to your soil for the next planting season.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ agbi tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ, atsɔ mli loo afee amɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni akɛfee kooloi aniyenii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe. Aloo feemɔ lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and drop off during the dry season, and does it mean the crop is dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigboi?

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during dry spells to conserve water and survive the heat. The plant is not dying; the tubers beneath the ground remain healthy and will grow fresh leaves when the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi shi yɛ dɔlɛ mli. Tso lɛ gbooo, ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why do my vegetable crops wilt during the hot afternoon sun even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛ Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ awo amɛ nu leebi?

english: In intense midday heat, plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the soil. Wilting is their natural defense to reduce water loss, and they usually recover by evening as it cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛba nu ni fiteɔ lɛ shi. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ beni edɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear away all the tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate strong, direct sun. Tall shade trees act as natural shields that protect tender cocoa leaves from intense sunlight and keep the surrounding air and soil humid.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ni buɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: If I plant cowpeas alongside my maize in the same farm, will the cowpea plants steal nutrients from the maize?
ga: Kɛ midu tsina ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa masɛi yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ, Ani tsina ŋmãa tsei lɛ baaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ?

english: No, cowpeas actually share nutrients. Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air into the soil through their roots, which helps fertilize the nearby maize naturally.
ga: Dabi, tsina ŋmeii jaa niyenii mli hewalɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ aná adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I plant three or four maize seeds together in one small hole?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii etɛ loo ejwɛ fee ekome yɛ bu bibioo kome mli?

english: Planting too many seeds in one spot forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stems and small or missing maize cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. ni ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii loo amɛbɛ.

english: Why do insect pests attack my tomato plants heavily while leaving the pepper plants right next to them untouched?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa mi tomato tsei lɛ waa yɛ be mli ni amɛjieɔ pepper tsei ni yɔɔ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Ani ashiɔ lɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko etaaa he?

english: Insects are attracted to specific scents and leaf textures. Tomato plants release odors that draw certain pests in, while pepper plants produce natural compounds that many insects dislike.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ aŋɔli kɛ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ha lɛ gbalaa koolooi. Tomato tsei jieɔ ŋmɔlɔ ko ni gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni kooloi bibii babaoo sumɔɔɔ lɛ kpo.

english: Why do my harvested cowpea grains develop tiny holes and turn to powder after storing them in sacks for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui ni mikpaa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni etsɔɔ powda beni akɛto kotokui amli nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ.

english: Weevil insects or their eggs get onto the seeds during harvest. Inside storage sacks, the eggs hatch into larvae that feed on the inside of the grains, leaving holes and dust as they emerge.
ga: Kplukai loo amɛwui lɛ kpɛtɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. inside storage sack Wɔlɔi lɛ fɔɔ kɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Amɛshiɔ bu kɛ sũ kɛji amɛje kpo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, an important food for growth. When nitrogen is lacking in the soil, the plant pulls it from older leaves at the bottom to feed new leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen Tso lɛ gbalaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ahe koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do people tell me that planting groundnuts or cowpeas will make my soil richer for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni midu lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas have small bumps on their roots that trap natural plant food from the air and put it into the earth. When you harvest them, that trapped food stays behind to nourish your next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, emɔɔ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Beni okpaa amɛ lɛ Niyenii ni ekã shi lɛ baakã he ahi sɛɛ koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before any pods start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by dry spells or hot winds like the Harmattan. The tree drops its flowers to save water and energy so it can stay alive through the harsh weather.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji ahum ni mli egbi loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ tamɔ Harmattan lɛ tswa amɛ. Tsei baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Koni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli

english: Why do my pepper plants keep dropping their flowers instead of forming peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when the weather gets extremely hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when the soil lacks essential minerals like phosphorus needed for fruit formation.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛ́ sũ lɛ mli egbi kwraa loo be mli ni sũ lɛ bɛ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs, ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai afeemɔ.

english: Why are there small holes and ragged edges in the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii kɛ amɛhe ni etse lɛ?

english: These holes are usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center funnel of the young maize plant during the day and feeds on new leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. ni oye baai heei lɛ dani amɛje kpo

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up tightly and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up mostly when tiny insects like whiteflies infect the plant with a virus, or when the plant is reacting to extreme heat and dry soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ ye tso lɛ nɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei feɔ amɛnii yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy rain or wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots naturally stay close to the top of the soil, but tiny worms called nematodes can eat away those roots, destroying the tree's anchor and causing it to collapse under heavy fruit weight.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli plantain shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Shi ŋmei bibioo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes lɛ baanyɛ aye nakai shishifãi lɛ. Efiteɔ tso lɛ ŋmei lɛ, ni ehaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ tsiimɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting under the ground before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when heavy rain stays trapped in wet soil for too long without draining, suffocating the roots and allowing mold to grow.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa, ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie nu. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daa.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines to grow up wooden stakes instead of spreading on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔse sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ tsei lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Lifting yam vines onto stakes helps the leaves catch more sunlight to feed the tubers, while keeping the foliage off wet ground to prevent diseases from spreading.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni awóɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo ni amɛkɛhaa bulb lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water, leaving all of them thin, weak, and with small yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni adu lɛ kɛ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋ, ni no haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ baa.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight. Without shade trees like plantains, the intense heat burns their delicate leaves and dries out the moisture they need to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains lɛ bɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ shãa tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ agbi.

english: Why do small pods on my cocoa tree turn black and rot before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboi dani amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in high humidity and damp conditions. Pruning excess branches lets air and sunlight in to dry out the trees and prevent the fungus.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa tso lɛ gĩɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii baa.

english: Why do my cassava plants have big green leaves but very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or is too hard, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing big leaves above ground instead of storing food in its underground roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ wa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ amli.

english: How does planting groundnuts alongside my maize help my crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni mikɛduɔ yɛ ŋmei masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, which feeds the maize plants and makes the soil richer.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ

english: How can I tell if my maize crops are suffering from lack of water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu ni faaa yɛ mi-abele lɛ mli miipiŋ?

english: When maize plants don't get enough water, their leaves roll up tightly into thin tubes during the heat of the day to save moisture, and lower leaves turn yellow.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ, ashɛɔ ebaai lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ ni afeɔ ŋmãa bibioo ko. Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do caterpillars suddenly appear and eat my maize leaves right after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baa trukaa ni amɛbayeɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Moths lay their eggs right as the rainy season starts so that the young caterpillars hatch at the exact time tender, fresh green leaves are growing for them to eat.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi pɛ kɛkɛ ni ŋmeii fɔɔ amɛwui. koni ŋmeii lɛ afɔ yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ni baa bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ koni amɛye lɛ mli.

english: What happens to my plants if I put chemical fertilizer right against the stem?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ he?

english: Placing chemical fertilizer directly against the stem will burn the plant's skin and roots through harsh chemical heat, which can weaken or kill the crop.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ hewolo kɛ eshishifãi lɛ ashã yɛ tsofai ni mli wa lɛ amli dɔlɛ hewɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ loo egbo.

english: When the weather gets too hot or the plants don't get steady water, the pepper plant drops its flowers to save energy so it doesn't die from heat stress.
ga: Be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo tsei lɛ náaa nu daa. Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, hulutsoo he haomɔ gbooo bo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa po lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that act like thieves under the ground, stealing soil food and water before your crops' roots get a chance to drink them.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni feɔ amɛnii tamɔ shikpɔŋ shishi julɔi. Ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛnuɔ.

english: Why should I water my vegetable farm early in the morning instead of at noon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afɔ aduawai abɔɔ lɛ nɔ nu leebi moŋ fe shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning gives plants time to drink before the hot sun arrives, whereas watering at noon causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the roots can take it in.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa tso lɛ náa be ni ekɛnuɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni afɔɔ nɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔɔ.

english: How do I know which seed variety is best for my farm when there are so many options on the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ? Beni nibii babaoo ni abaanyɛ ahala yɛ jara nɔ lɛ.

english: Different crop varieties are bred for specific traits like drought tolerance, disease resistance, or high yield. Choosing a variety recommended by local extension officers ensures it matches your area's soil and climate conditions.
ga: Afɔ tsei srɔtoi kɛha sui pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ hɔmɔ tsuishitoo. Helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ helai loo yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo Tsei srɔtoi ni okpokpaa lɛ nɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ ni ohalaa lɛ baaha tso srɔtoi lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ akpã gbee.

english: Why do buyers in the market prefer certain crop varieties over others even when they look similar?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ sumɔɔ tsei srɔtoi komɛi fe ekrokomɛi eyɛ mli akɛ amɛhe yɛ tamɔ amɛhe moŋ?

english: Market buyers look for specific qualities like longer shelf life, better taste, or suitability for cooking and processing, which makes certain named varieties much easier to sell at higher prices.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ taoɔ nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi tamɔ nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ, nibii ni ŋɔɔ, loo nibii ni sa kɛha nihoomɔ kɛ nitsumɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaahɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ gbɛi lɛ kɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: Why do some crop varieties allow me to harvest multiple times in one season while others only produce once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi komɛi haa mikpaa nii shii abɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ? yɛ be mli ni henɔi krokomɛi Woɔ yibii shikome pɛ?

english: Some varieties keep producing flowers and fruits continuously over several months, while single-harvest varieties mature all at once, allowing you to clear the land for the next planting.
ga: Henɔi komɛi baaya nɔ awo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai nyɔji babaoo. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa shikome lɛ fɛɛ shwereɔ shikome. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ojieɔ he ko kɛha odumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How can I increase the number of harvests I get from my vegetables in a single year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha ŋmɔshi nibii ni minine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-aduawai lɛ amli lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ afi kome mli?

english: Using short-duration crop varieties that mature quickly allows you to plant and harvest two to three times within a single major and minor rainy season.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ni yeɔ be kukuoo ni shwereɔ oya tsu nii lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ oduɔ nii ni okpaa shii enyɔ kɛyashi shii etɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu kɛ bibioo kome mli.

english: What is the benefit of buying certified seeds instead of saving seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni awo he hewalɛ ni aheɔ lɛ he moŋ fe ni akɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baato?

english: Certified seeds are carefully produced to guarantee high germination rates, disease resistance, and strong uniform plants, whereas saved seeds often lose vigor and produce lower yields over time.
ga: Afee dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni ekwɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ helai kɛ tsei ni he wa be fɛɛ be Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ fɔɔ hewalɛ ni baa shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How should I store my unused seeds so they do not spoil before the next planting season?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ dumɔwui ni akɛtsuuu nii lɛ ato koni amɛkafite dani be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba?

english: Store your seeds in sealed containers in a cool, dry, and dark place to protect them from humidity, heat, and insect damage that destroy their ability to germinate.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui ato tsɛnsi ko ni atsĩ naa mli yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni egbi, ni yɔɔ duŋ koni ŋmɔtɔ, dɔlɛ, kɛ koolooi ni baanyɛ afite amɛnyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and drop flowers during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and water stress cause crops to drop flowers to conserve energy, but shade plants, adequate watering, and mulch can keep soil moist and protect young plants.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu he haomɔ haa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Shi kɛji akɛ aha tsei lɛ hulutsoo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu tsei bibii ahe.

english: Why do my plants produce plenty of leafy green branches but very little fruit or tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ woɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ aduawai loo ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes crops build excessive leaves instead of flowers and fruit, so balancing nitrogen with phosphorus and potassium is necessary for good yield.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tsei woɔ baai babaoo yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai najiaŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, nitrogen kɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium ni aaakwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ he miihia waa koni yibii kpakpai aba.

english: When is the ideal time to sow my seeds to catch the main rainy season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui koni anyɛ ashɛ nugbɔ be titri ni nɛɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ he?

english: Sowing right at the steady onset of the rainy season allows young roots to establish deeply before heavy rains or unexpected dry spells occur.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ daa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ tswaa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa loo hɔmɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ baa.

english: Can I grow high-yielding vegetable varieties during the dry season without an irrigation machine?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ni mikɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Yes, if you select drought-tolerant varieties, use organic mulch to trap soil moisture, and practice manual watering during early mornings or late evenings.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji ohala ŋmeii srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ. Kɛ organic mulch atsu nii ni okɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ni okɛ ohe awo nu mli leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ.

english: Why should I buy local maize seeds instead of seeds brought in from neighboring countries?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ dumɔwui ni akɛjɛ maji ni bɛŋkɛ wɔ lɛ amli lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Local seeds are naturally adapted to Ghana's weather and soil, making them stronger against local diseases and pests compared to foreign seeds that were bred for different conditions.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛhaa Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛyeɔ maŋ lɛ mli helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ yɛ shihilɛi srɔtoi amli lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the seeds I save from my harvested corn produce weaker plants when I replant them the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ beni mikɛwoɔ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many improved corn varieties lose their strength and uniformity after the first harvest, so their offspring often produce smaller yields and are more easily attacked by pests and diseases.
ga: Abele henɔi babaoo ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ daa lɛ baa shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛbii lɛ fɔɔ yibiiwoo babaoo, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baatutua amɛ oya.

english: Is it safe for me to buy corn grains from the local food market to use as seeds on my farm?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mahe ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli niyenii jarayelihe lɛ koni mikɛtsu nii akɛ dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Market grain is meant for cooking, not planting; it often carries hidden seed-borne diseases, has poor germination rates, and will yield poorly compared to certified planting seeds.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni akɛhooɔ nii, shi jeee nɔ ni akɛduɔ, ni bei pii lɛ, eyɛ helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli baa ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. eyɛ shweremɔ ni baa shi kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ahe

english: How can I tell if my corn plants are suffering from a disease or just lacking water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ emɔ hela loo nu efo amɛmli?

english: Drought causes leaves to roll up and dry evenly across the field, whereas diseases usually cause irregular spots, yellow streaks, molds, or stunted growth even when the soil is moist.
ga: Hɔmɔ lɛ ha baai lɛ shwie shi ni amɛgbi yɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ. Yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ hela lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni ejaaa baa Yellow streaks, mold, loo ŋmeii ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Why do some types of corn get diseases easily while others stay healthy in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu yɛ hewalɛ tamɔ nɛkɛ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Different corn varieties have different genetic resistance; varieties adapted to your area have built-in natural defenses against local fungi and viruses that easily destroy susceptible varieties.
ga: Abɛi henɔ fɛɛ henɔ yɛ bɔ ni gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ yeɔ egbɔ lɛ srɔtoi. Srɔtoi ni atsake amɛhe kɛya he ni oyɔɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu ni akɛwo maŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii, ŋmeii, kɛ helai ni gbeɔ henɔi ni nyɛɔ etswaa lɛ ahiɛ oya lɛ amli.

english: What makes a local crop variety stronger against crop sickness compared to foreign varieties?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei srɔtoi ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ tsei ahe helai anɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto maŋsɛɛ tsei ahe?

english: Local varieties have evolved over many generations alongside local plant diseases, allowing them to develop natural resistance that foreign varieties do not possess.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli tsei srɔtoi lɛ etsake yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli yɛ akutso lɛ mli tsei ahe helai ahe. Enɛ haa amɛnáa adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni maŋsɛɛ tsofai lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do pests like fall armyworms attack young corn plants so aggressively?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworm lɛ tutuaa ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ waa nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Young corn leaves are soft, tender, and rich in nutrients, making them an ideal food source for caterpillars to feed on and grow quickly early in the season.
ga: Baby corn baa lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛyeɔ ni amɛdaraa oya yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: Why do pests and diseases seem to get worse every year when I plant corn on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ mli woɔ wu daa afi kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously leaves crop residue that allows pest populations and disease spores to survive in the soil and multiply heavily year after year.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ shĩɔ tsei amli sũi ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai amli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛfɔɔ babaoo afi fɛɛ afi lɛ sɛɛ.

english: If my neighbor plants a different corn variety right next to my field, will it affect my crops?
ga: Kɛji mikutsoŋnyo lɛ du ŋmãa kroko yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ, Ani ebaana miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, corn is wind-pollinated, so pollen from your neighbor's plants can mix with yours, potentially changing the taste, appearance, and seed quality of your harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ shwieɔ ŋmãa nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, pollen ni jɛɔ okutsoŋnyo tsei amli lɛ baanyɛ afutu otsei lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha okpamɔ lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ, ehefɛo kɛ dumɔwui lɛ atsake.

english: Why are tiny insects eating up my stored corn even though the grains looked completely clean at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ? Ni dumɔwui lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe tse kɛji akpa?

english: Storage pests like weevils often lay invisible eggs inside the corn grains while the crop is still standing in the field, which then hatch and multiply later inside your warm barn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe, tamɔ ŋmeii, woɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa yɛ ŋmeii amli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ damɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. Sɛɛ mli lɛ, amɛbaafɔ ni amɛfɔ yɛ otsu lɛ mli latsaa lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow after all this heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa nɛkɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excessive rainfall floods the soil and suffocates crop roots by removing oxygen. Without oxygen, the roots cannot absorb nutrients like nitrogen from the ground, causing the crop leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji oxygen bɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa tso baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away the top layer of soil on my farm, and how does it hurt my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni te eyeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy raindrops hit bare ground with force and break up the soil, creating streams of water that carry away the fertile topsoil. This removes the essential nutrients and organic matter your crops need to grow strong.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tswa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ lɛ nɔ ni efo shikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa nu ni hoɔ ni hoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara waa lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crops with dry grass and leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, acts as a blanket that protects the soil from being washed away by heavy raindrops and helps keep soil moisture balanced.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akahole lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting underground when there is too much rain in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need well-draining soil to stay healthy. When water sits in the ground for too long without draining, harmful fungi and bacteria thrive and cause the tubers to rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ kɛyaa. Fuji kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ daa ni amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and spoil when the weather stays very wet?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa?

english: Continuous rain and wet weather create high humidity, which causes a fungal infection called Black Pod disease to spread rapidly across cocoa trees and destroy the pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod disease lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli fɛɛ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without turning into fruits during periods of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain knocks off delicate blossoms and keeps bees from pollinating the flowers. Additionally, wet conditions cause stress to the plant, making it drop its flowers instead of growing tomatoes.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛwo amɛmli. Shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ hu haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. Ha amɛgbee shi moŋ fe ni oookwɛ tomato.

english: Why do chemical sprays stop working on my crops when rain falls right after I apply them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ kpaɔ nitsumɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Rainwater washes liquid sprays off the crop leaves before the plant or pests can absorb them, rendering the chemicals useless and wasting your effort.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ tsei ahe baai anɔ lɛ he dani tsei loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehaa tsofai lɛ feɔ nɔ ni he ehiaaa ni efiteɔ ohewalɛ.

english: Why is it risky to plant my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain often moistens only the top layer of soil. If a dry spell follows, the soil will dry out quickly and kill the young germinating seeds before deep rains establish.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ mli fũuɔ. Kɛji hɔmɔ ba nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni egbeɔ dumɔwui bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baa.

english: Why do extension officers advise making raised earth mounds for vegetables instead of planting on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afee shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ koni akɛdu aduawai moŋ fe ni aaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting on raised earth mounds lifts crop roots above waterlogged ground, allowing excess rainwater to flow away in the furrows so the roots do not drown.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ ŋshɔ lɛ mli kɛje kpo. Koni shishifãi lɛ akabote nu mli

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my main crops after a heavy rain pouring?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally hardy wild plants that absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops, allowing them to shoot up rapidly whenever water is abundant.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ baajie nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛ̃ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya be fɛɛ be ni nu babaoo yɔɔ.

english: Lower leaves turning yellow usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential for green growth. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps the plant regain its color and grow strong, healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ená ehiɛ su ekoŋŋ ni ená toi ni wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans make my farm soil better for my next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop is harvested, that stored food remains in the ground to naturally feed whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Niyenii ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii aha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and covered in tiny white flies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ ehà amɛhe lɛ?

english: Tiny whiteflies suck sap from cassava leaves and spread the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which causes the leaves to curl and stunting. Clearing surrounding weeds and planting resistant cassava varieties or applying natural pesticides can protect your farm.
ga: Fɛ̃i bibii yɛŋ lɛ nuɔ ŋmei baa mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ amɛshwãa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ ni odu ŋmei srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ hela lɛ loo okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and die suddenly even when the soil has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually caused by fungal or bacterial root rot from waterlogged soil. Rotating your crops each season and ensuring proper soil drainage stops these organisms from attacking the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi trukaa lɛ baa. Tsɔɔmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa afi ni okwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Etsiɔ bɔɔ nii nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkatutua shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn under harsh, direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside your cocoa creates living umbrellas that shelter the young trees until they grow strong enough.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa. kɛyashi tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa

english: How deep should I bury my maize seeds in the soil when planting during the rainy season?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ, te esa akɛ afu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ?

english: Maize seeds should be planted about 3 to 5 centimeters deep. Planting too deep prevents the sprout from reaching oxygen and light, while planting too shallow risks rain washing the seeds away or birds eating them.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ mli aaafee sɛntimita 3 kɛyashi 5. Kɛ́ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la. Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nɛɔ ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ baaje mli loo okpoi baaye amɛ.

english: Does my yam crop really need wooden stakes, or can I let the vines trail on the ground?
ga: Mi sweet potato lɛ he miihia tso tso diɛŋtsɛ. Aloo obaanyɛ oha weintso lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food that grows large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves lifted toward the sun and off the hot ground, preventing rot and dramatically increasing your harvest weight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛfee niyenii, ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa baai lɛ woɔ amɛhe nɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa ni ehaa okpamɔ nii lɛ tsiimɔ yaa hiɛ waa.

english: Should I cut off the extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ani ajie plantain tsei titrii lɛ?

english: Leaving too many shoots (suckers) forces the main plant to share its food and water, resulting in small bunches. Pruning extra suckers so that only one or two remain ensures your main plant grows big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Suckers (shoots) babaoo ni ashiɔ lɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji niji bibii Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he koni eshi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha otso titri lɛ adara ni etsɔ plantain jwɛi agbo ni tsii.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my tomato plants without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Extreme heat or inconsistent watering causes tomato plants to drop their flowers as a stress response. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch around the plant roots helps stabilize temperature and keeps flowers attached so fruit can form.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ nɔnyɛɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsei shishifãi ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be, ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he koni amɛwo yibii.

english: When is the right time for me to apply NPK fertilizer to my maize field after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni midu nii sɛɛ?

english: Apply your first round of NPK fertilizer about 7 to 14 days after the seeds sprout, once roots are established. Applying fertilizer too early can burn tender seeds, while waiting too long starves the plant during its rapid growth phase.
ga: Okɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ awo mli aaafee gbii 7 kɛyashi 14 yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Beni shishifãi lɛ daraa Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli oya lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ ashã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mɛmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ aye hɔmɔ yɛ be mli ni edaa oya lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually indicate that the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does adding dried animal manure to my farm make my crops grow so much stronger than plain dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ?

english: Animal manure feeds the soil with natural plant nutrients and acts like a sponge to hold water during dry days, making it easier for crop roots to feed and grow.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei amli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ sponji ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu mli yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛ baaye nii ni amɛdara.

english: Why should I plant plantains alongside my young cocoa trees when starting a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛ́ mije ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Fast-growing plantain plants produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture needed to survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up tightly and stop growing new shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni ekpa ŋmeii heei ni shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's juices. Spraying neem leaf water or recommended sprays clears these pests so leaves can expand again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ nu loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwie nɔ lɛ shwie neem baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ koni baai lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for my crop yield if I plant my seeds very close together in the row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibiiwoo lɛ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants end up fighting each other for sunlight, soil food, and water, resulting in thin stems and small harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu, ni no haa amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛkpaaa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves up toward direct sunlight to generate the energy required to swell tubers underground. Staking keeps leaves clean, healthy, and fully exposed to light.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ he tseɔ, ehiɛɔ hewalɛ, ni ehaa hulu tsoɔ waa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when there is heavy rain for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots require air in the soil to stay alive. Waterlogged soil prevents oxygen from reaching the roots, causing them to suffocate and decay, which is why planting on mounds or ridges helps drain excess water.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni ji oxygen lɛ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ kɛ fitemɔ baa Enɛ hewɔ ni dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the blossoms dropping off my tomato plants before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and sudden dry spells put tomato plants under severe stress, causing them to drop flowers to preserve water. Keeping soil moisture consistent with mulch helps protect the blossoms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ kɛ tomato tsei lɛ woɔ haomɔ ni naa wa shishi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ ashɛrɛ fɔfɔi ashwie koni nu akafite. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akɛ muji tsuɔ nii be fɛɛ be lɛ baaye abua ni abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Is it better to buy certified seeds from a agricultural supplier or re-use seeds from last year's harvest?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ mɛi ni kɛ okwaayeli nibii haa lɛ adɛŋ loo okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii ekoŋŋ?

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred to produce higher yields and resist common local plant diseases, whereas saved seeds from previous harvests gradually lose strength and produce smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛnyɛ amɛshi helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ tsei amli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni ato kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ Hewalɛ baa shi fiofio ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo

english: How do weeds reduce my crop growth even when there is plenty of rain on the farm?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ aba shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds steal essential plant food and sunlight directly from your crops, while also sheltering harmful insects and plant diseases that can spread to your crops.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsei ahe helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã onibii amli lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea early in the plant's growth helps restore green leaves and increases crop yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea fataa he yɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ shishijee bei amli. Ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil needs manure before I start planting tomatoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ dani mabɔi tomato dumɔ?

english: If your soil is hard, sandy, pale, or dried out quickly after rain, it lacks organic matter. Adding well-rotted manure improves soil structure, helps it hold water, and supplies nutrients tomato roots need to build strong stems.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, ŋã yɔɔ mli, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo egbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shi ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ haa tomato shishifãi lɛ koni amɛma tsei ni wa

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like whiteflies, thrips, or mites that suck sap from the leaves and spread plant viruses. Neem oil spray or recommended organic insecticides can help control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies, thrips, loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers drop off the tree before turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off without setting pods when the tree is under stress from prolonged heat, lack of soil moisture, or damage from sap-sucking insects like mirids (akate). Adequate farm shade and pest control protect the flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii kɛji tso lɛ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ shishi be kakadaŋŋ. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nibii ni kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mirids (akate) lɛ fiteɔ. Okwaafoi ahe shade ni sa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi ahe.

english: Why do people advise me to plant plantains next to my new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ mi-cacao tso hee lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and develop huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade, cooler temperatures, and moisture young cocoa needs during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛfeɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hɔɔŋ, ni haa hɔɔŋ kɛ dɔlɛ ni mli ejɔ. kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo lolo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why is it bad if I plant my cassava suckers too close to one another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji mikɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are too crowded, their roots and leaves fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant room to develop large, heavy tubers instead of thin, woody roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsũ fɛɛ tsũ ni kwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ bulb agboi ni tsii. Yɛ tso shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo najiaŋ

english: Why should I wait for the major rainy season to start before sowing my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ dani madu ŋmãa?

english: Maize seeds need consistent moisture to germinate and grow strong early roots. Planting in dry soil before steady rains arrive causes seeds to rot or sprout into weak seedlings that wither under heat.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni yɔɔ daa kɛha kwɛ̃mɔ kɛ shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛ daa lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbo loo amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa be lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even when the plants grow plenty of healthy green leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Excessive foliage with tiny tubers often happens when the soil has too much nitrogen but lacks potassium, or when water logging prevents root swelling. Potassium helps plants direct their energy down into building heavy tubers.
ga: Baai ni fa fe nine lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo shi potassium bɛ mli. aloo be mli ni nu ni hoɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafu. Potassium yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ feɔ bulbs ni tsii.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings die right after I move them from the nursery to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young plants suffer from transplant shock when moved abruptly into intense field sunlight. Exposing seedlings to outdoor sun gradually over a few days and transplanting late in the afternoon helps them adjust and survive.
ga: Dumɔwui naa piŋmɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ ahe gbeyeishemɔ mli kɛji ajie amɛ kɛtee hulu la ni tsoɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli trukaa. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo kponɔgbɛ hulu la mli fiofio yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli, ni okɛ amɛ wo he kroko yɛ shwane mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛtsake amɛhe ni amɛhi shi.

english: How do I know that my yam crop is fully ripe and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yam tubers are mature when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and begin to dry up. This signals that the plant has finished transferring nutrients into the tubers below the ground.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni baai lɛ kɛ wain tso lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ekɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need taller plants like plantains planted beside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ aná tso kakadaŋŋ tamɔ plantain ni adu yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil. Planting fast-growing plantains nearby creates a natural canopy that provides shade and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle the sun.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye hulu lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is a vital food for leaf growth. When the soil runs out of nutrients, adding nitrogen fertilizer or animal manure helps the leaves turn green again so the plant can produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ lɛ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ koni tso lɛ anyɛ awo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I rotate my crops instead of planting maize in the same field every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ fe ni madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and attracts pests that target that specific plant. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil naturally and breaks the lifecycle of crop pests.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kwɛɔ nakai tso lɛ nɔ lɛ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni ekpa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready for harvesting under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is maturing when the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, and the ground around the base of the main stem begins to crack as the tubers expand underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ miikwɛ̃ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni he ni ebɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni yitso lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my maize seeds too close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures that every stem grows thick and strong enough to support full, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifã fɛɛ shishifã lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua tso lɛ shishifã ni eyi obɔ ni mli wa lɛ.

english: Why are small worms eating the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: These worms are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on the soft growth points of young maize. Catching them early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts protects the growing point before the plant gets destroyed.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmei bibii ni daraa yɛ lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu dalɛ he dani tso lɛ afite.

english: Why do my tomato leaves drop and wilt during the afternoon heat even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it up from the soil. They temporarily droop to conserve internal moisture, but they usually perk back up in the cooler evening once water loss slows down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaatsi amɛhe yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli. Shi amɛfɔɔ sɛɛkuu yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli beni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and stronger than my crops after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to local soil and rainy conditions, allowing them to absorb available water and nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing light and food from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ shihilɛi amli. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ oya fe tsei ni miida lɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju kane kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme midday heat, too little water, or a lack of soil nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil consistently moist and applying compost helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔ kpe, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli. nu fioo tsɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akpɛtɛ he ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can spread out and capture maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which travels down the stem to feed and build large, thick tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛbaa lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni nyiɛɔ tso lɛ shishi koni eyatao niyenii ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni mli tse.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I put wooden stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get full sunlight and prevents leaf diseases caused by contact with damp soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la ni fa lɛ aba ni ekɛtsi baai lɛ ahe helai ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: When plants are crowded, their roots and leaves compete with each other for food, water, and sunlight. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and soil nutrients to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, a key plant food, or the soil is too full of water. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. tso niyenii ni he hiaa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or if the plant lacks water during flowering. Regular watering helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo nu bɛ tso lɛ he yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔii lɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my sorghum plants stop growing whenever those small plants with purple flowers appear near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sorghum tso lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ be fɛɛ be ni maná tso bibioo ko lɛ? ni fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ

english: That purple-flowered plant is a dangerous weed called Striga. Its roots attach directly to your crop's roots under the soil and suck out the water and nutrients meant for your sorghum.
ga: Tso ni fɔfɔi yɔɔ mli lɛ ji jwɛi ko ni yɔɔ oshara ni atsɛɔ lɛ striga. Eshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. ni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ haa o-sorghum lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my maize leaves with tiny brown dirt left inside the funnels?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni etse yɛ mi-abele baai lɛ amli kɛ muji bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baa? ni eshwɛ yɛ kɔni lɛ mli lɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides deep inside the growing center of the maize plant, chewing the young leaves and leaving behind its dark droppings.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ dalɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Okɛ baai bibii lɛ atsu nii ni oshi ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ yɛ sɛɛ.

english: Planting maize continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every year and allows maize-specific pests to build up. Swapping with crops like beans or peanuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. ni ehaa ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ahe jarayeli Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does adding dried poultry manure to my soil help my crops grow better than relying only on rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ kooloi ashishifãi ni egbi fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe nugbɔ pɛ ni mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Poultry manure acts as rich food for the soil. It adds essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus while helping the soil hold water longer around the plant roots.
ga: Kooloi ashishifãi tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni jara wa kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Okɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus afata he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn dark and start rotting just a few days after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Once cassava is dug up, its roots react to oxygen and spoil within two to three days. Processing them quickly into gari or flour, or keeping them buried in moist sand, prevents rapid decay.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aaakumɔ ŋmei Eshishifãi lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli. Akɛ oyaiyeli tsuɔ he nii ni akɛfeɔ gari loo ashikishaŋ. loo afu yɛ ŋã ni mli efɔ mli Etsiɔ fitemɔ oya naa

english: How often should I water my young cocoa trees during the dry season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need regular watering about 2 to 3 times a week during the dry season because their root systems are shallow and cannot reach water deep underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni afɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ nu daa shii 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ otsi mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni enyɛɛɛ eshɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he.

english: The best time to water your crops is early in the morning or late in the evening. This prevents the hot sun from evaporating the water before the plant roots can absorb it.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu ji leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Enɛ haaa hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ afee nu dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ.

english: Can giving my cocoa plants too much water harm their roots?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛhaa cacao tso lɛ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aye eshishifãi lɛ awui?

english: Yes, overwatering can drown crop roots because plants need air in the soil just as much as water. Excess water causes root rot and stops the plant from growing properly.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli. Akɛni kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu hu hewɔ lɛ, nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaaa tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I water my cocoa trees immediately after applying fertilizer?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo mi-kookoo tso lɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ?

english: Yes, light watering after applying dry fertilizer helps dissolve the nutrients into the soil so the roots can absorb them easily. Without water, the fertilizer cannot feed the plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni afɔɔ nɔ fioo beni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi efata he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ mli oya. Kɛ nu bɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛŋ aha tso lɛ niyenii.

english: How can I tell if my young cocoa trees are getting enough water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: A healthy, well-watered cocoa tree has firm, bright green leaves and fresh shoots. If the leaves start drooping, curling, or turning brown at the edges, the plant is lacking water.
ga: Cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni nu yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ kɛ ŋmeii heei. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ bɔi gbee shi lɛ, ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nu.

english: Why are small cocoa pods falling off my trees before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii To gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa pods often drop early due to water stress, lack of soil nutrients, or insect attacks. Ensuring steady water supply and adequate shade helps trees retain their pods.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔji bibii lɛ fɔɔ gbee oya yɛ nu he haomɔ hewɔ. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni tutuaa lɛ Nu ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ hulutsoo ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What specific signs should I look for when checking my farm every week?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii pɔtɛɛ esa akɛ matao beni mikwɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa otsi lɛ?

english: Check for changes in leaf color, signs of pest damage under leaves, weed growth around the base, and whether the topsoil feels dry. Catching these early prevents major crop losses.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tsakemɔi yɛ baa lɛ su mli. Okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai efite yɛ baai lɛ ashishi Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he kɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi. Ni ooomɔ lɛ mra Ebaaye ebua ni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: How will keeping a water source close to my farm help my cocoa project succeed?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu jɛɛhe ko ni mikɛaaha bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ baaye abua ni mi-kookoo nitsumɔ lɛ aye omanye?

english: Having water nearby allows you to water seedlings consistently during dry spells and easily mix crop protection sprays without relying solely on unpredictable rainfall.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ Haa okɛ nu shwieɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsofai ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ afutu mli mlɛo ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ pɛ nɔ.

english: Can I use water from a nearby river or stream directly on my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii loo mafo kɛho miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, natural river water is generally good for crops because it carries natural minerals, provided the river is clean and free from illegal mining or chemical pollution.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, faa mli nu ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahewɔ. Kɛji akɛ esa akɛ faa lɛ mli atse ni shika tsuru ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo tsofai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Will watering my cocoa trees continuously make them produce pods all year round?
ga: Ani kɛ́ akɛ nu wo cacao tso nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaawo ŋmeii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: While water keeps cocoa trees healthy and reduces flower loss, cocoa trees still follow natural seasonal flowering cycles influenced by daylight, temperature, and tree age.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nu yeɔ ebuaa ni cacao tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ehaa fɔfɔii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi moŋ, shi cacao tsei lɛ nyiɛɔ adebɔɔ mli fɔfɔii ni yaa nɔ yɛ be mli lɛ sɛɛ lolo. Hulu la, dɔlɛ kɛ tso lɛ afii náa enɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I buy packaged seed varieties instead of using saved seeds from my last maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui srɔtoi ni akɛwo kotoku mli lɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Improved seed varieties are specially developed to resist local diseases, handle dry spells better, and yield significantly more harvest than seeds saved from previous crops.
ga: Afee dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kwɛmɔ fɛ̃i be lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni aŋmala ashwie shi kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why is my neighbor getting far more bags of maize than I do from the exact same size of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ nine shɛɔ ŋmãa kotokui babaoo nɔ fe mi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Higher yields usually come from using certified high-yielding seed varieties combined with applying the right fertilizer at the correct time and keeping the farm clean of weeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo jɛɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni awo he odaseyeli akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be ni sa mli kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe tsemɔ fata he.

english: How does fertilizer actually help my crops grow bigger and produce more food?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo niyenii babaoo?

english: Fertilizer acts like nutritious food for crops, putting back essential minerals like nitrogen and phosphorus that soil loses over time so plants can grow strong, green, and heavy with food.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli kɛhaa tsei. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. ni shikpɔŋ ni elaaje yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa. Koni tsei lɛ adara ni amɛhe wa, amɛfee eŋɔli ni amɛtsii kɛ niyenii.

english: How can I tell if my cassava or maize plants are starving and need fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye mi-cassava loo ŋmãa lɛ ni ehe miihia ni awo lɛ ŋmãa?

english: When crops lack nutrients, their leaves often turn pale yellow instead of deep green, their growth becomes stunted, and their stems remain thin and weak.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Dalɛ baafee mlɛo. Ni tso lɛ mli tsɔne lɛ mli etsii lolo ni ebɛ hewalɛ.

english: Can I use leftover plant waste and animal manure to feed my crops instead of buying chemical fertilizer?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni eshwɛ kɛ kooloi ashishifãi afee niyenii yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahemɔ najiaŋ?

english: Yes, decaying crop waste and animal manure rot down into natural organic fertilizer (compost) that feeds the soil and helps it hold moisture during dry periods.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ kɛ kooloi ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii (compost) ni haa sũ lɛ hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why does my farm produce less food every year if I plant maize in the exact same spot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niyenii ni miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ lɛ faaa daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific soil nutrients that crop needs and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in your land.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ daa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ hoɔ. ni oye obua tsei pɔtɛɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant my seeds very close together to try and fit more crops on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni mabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni makwɛ tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When plants are overcrowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in tall, thin, weak plants that produce very small yields.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔi tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ enɛ mli baa ji tsei kakadaji, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm—they quickly steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients from the ground before your main crops have a chance to use them.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli—amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why do the leaves on my crop turn brown and curl up when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat makes leaves lose moisture faster than roots can draw water from the soil, causing leaves to curl to protect themselves and turn brown from dehydration.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa baai lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why are dark spots appearing on my tomato leaves and making them drop off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ tomato baai anɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Dark spots are usually signs of fungal diseases that spread during rainy or humid weather, which weaken the plant's leaves and stop it from making food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii diji ji ŋmeii hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ loo hulutsoo be mli lɛ he okadi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ekpaa niyenii feemɔ.

english: Why do some of my local maize seeds survive dry periods better, but produce smaller cobs than the new store-bought seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimaŋ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ? Shi ha amɛ dumɔwui ni darako fe dumɔwui heei ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ.

english: Local crop varieties have naturally adapted over time to withstand tough weather and local diseases, making them hardy. However, because they use much of their energy just to survive, they often produce smaller yields or smaller fruit compared to high-yielding hybrid seeds.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ etsake amɛhe yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa kɛ helai ni baa jɛmɛ lɛ anaa. Shi kɛlɛ, enɛ haa amɛhe wa, ejaakɛ amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi kɛkɛ. No hewɔ lɛ amɛfɔɔ yibiiwoo fioo loo amɛwooo yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my traditional cassava plants rarely get diseased, while the new fast-growing varieties spoil easily?
