ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi shishijee cassava henɔi lɛ hela mɔɔɔ amɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei henɔ hee lɛ daa oya lɛ, ani ebaafite oya?

english: Traditional varieties often build strong natural resistance to local pests and diseases over generations. Fast-growing or high-yielding varieties focus most of their energy on producing quick food, which sometimes leaves them with weaker natural defenses against infections.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kusum mli henɔi lɛ maa adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni teɔ shi ewoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii kɛ helai yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Henɔi ni daa oya loo amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ niyenii ni ayeɔ oya lɛ feemɔ he nii. Bei komɛi lɛ, enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni tsiɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ helai ahe lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my plantain plants falling over when the fruit bunches grow too large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ dara tsɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain stems are not solid wood; they are made of soft leaf layers. When a variety produces a very heavy bunch, the weight creates physical strain that the plant's trunk and root system cannot support on their own without wooden stakes.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ jeee tsei ni wa. Akɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ fee amɛ. Beni tso lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni tsii waa lɛ Muji lɛ kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nɔnyɛɛ baa ni tso lɛ shishifã kɛ shishifãi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ nɔ kɛji tsei bɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before any pepper begins to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience physical stress from high heat, drought, or poor soil nutrients. The plant drops its flowers to save energy and water so it can keep itself alive during tough conditions.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛna gbɔmɔtsoŋ nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛ latsaa, hɔmɔ, loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ mli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Koni ehi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants have huge green leaves but only tiny tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi tomato bibii pɛ yɔɔ jɛmɛ.

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich manure, they put all their energy into growing leafy stems instead of fruit. This leaves the plant with very little energy to grow large, healthy tomatoes.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ tsei ni miida ni baai yɔɔ mli yɛ aduawai najiaŋ lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ko kwraa ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ tomatoi wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up into tight tubes during the sunny afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is a protective behavior. When the sun is hot, the maize leaf curls up to hide its surface area from the heat, which traps moisture inside and prevents water from evaporating too fast.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji subaŋ ni buɔ mɔ he. Kɛ hulu lɛ miitso lɛ, Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛ amɛhiɛ he lɛ ato la lɛ he. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when planted out in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and sensitive to strong sunlight. Without shade trees like plantain or forest trees to shield them, the intense sun burns their leaves and dries out the soil moisture they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nuɔ he waa. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo kooi ni buɔ he lɛ bɛ lɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kɛha wala lɛ gĩɔ.

english: Yam tubers grow long and thin when the soil is too hard or compacted for the root to expand wide, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients like potassium that help the tuber swell.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã babaoo. Aloo be mli ni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and skinny with small cobs when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmli ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ? Akɛni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ hewɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The plants stretch upward to compete for light, leaving little strength to build thick stalks or big cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei baagbala amɛhe koni amɛye la he akaŋ. Hewalɛ fioo pɛ eshwɛ ni akɛbaafee ŋmeii ni mli tse loo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do some of my cowpea seeds rot in the soil while others sprout quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ?

english: Seeds need a warm, moist environment with air in the soil to break out of their shell. If the soil is waterlogged or the seed is planted too deep, it suffocates and rots before it can sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui hia shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baagbala ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo adu dumɔwui lɛ mli tsɔ Ebaafo ni ebaagbo dani ebaakwɛ̃.

english: Why does crop rot spread to my neighboring farm even when my plants do not touch theirs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ egbɛ eshwa miŋmɔ ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ mi tsei lɛ eshɛɛɛ amɛhe po?

english: Many crop rots are caused by tiny organisms called fungi that travel like light dust in the wind. Even if farms do not physically touch, air currents carry these invisible fungal spores across long distances from one field to another.
ga: Nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fiteɔ. Atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmei ni nyiɛɔ tamɔ sũ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔji lɛ bɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ tsakpaa kɛ amɛhe moŋ, Shi kɔɔyɔɔi kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni anaaa nɛɛ yaa he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli.

english: What is this white powder-like substance I see on my cassava leaves when it rains?
ga: Mɛni ji powda yɛŋ ni minaa yɛ ŋmei baa nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ?

english: That white powder is a type of fungus growing on the leaf surface. Fungi are distinct living organisms that thrive in damp, humid weather and feed on the plant's juices, weakening the crop.
ga: Pauda yɛŋ lɛ ji ŋmei henɔ ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ baai anɔ. Fungi ji nibii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ tsei amli nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ

english: How can my crops get sick if the soil I planted them in is fresh and clean?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hela kɛji shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ mli tse ni ehe tse?

english: Crops can catch sickness from the air, not just from contaminated soil. Fungal spores float freely in the atmosphere like microscopic dust and can land on healthy leaves from miles away.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ aná hela kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Jeee kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ pɛ mli. Fungal spores lɛ hoɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli tamɔ sũ bibii bibii waa. ni ebaanyɛ ehi baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ ni kɛ jɛmɛ jɛkɛmɔ ji kilomitai babaoo.

english: Why do my crops rot faster during the humid rainy season than in the dry harmattan?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe Harmattan ni egbi lɛ?

english: Fungi, which cause most crop rots, need moisture and warm air to sprout and multiply. Humid rainy weather creates the perfect wet environment for fungal spores to grow and spread rapidly across your field.
ga: Fuji ni kɛ tsei amli fitemɔ helai babaoo baa lɛ biɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ koni ekwɛ̃ ni eshwere. Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ oya.

english: If I cut a sick crop with my cutlass, can I use the same cutlass on a healthy crop?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ mi-knife lɛ fo tso ko ni hela mɔ lɛ Ani manyɛ mikɛ nakai kpãa lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ?

english: No, using the same cutlass will transfer microscopic fungal spores from the sick plant directly into the fresh cuts of healthy plants, introducing the sickness to your uninfected crops.
ga: Dabi, dagger ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔŋŋ baajie fungal spores bibii ni anaa kɛjɛɔ tso ni hela mɔ lɛ mli kɛya tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni afo ehee lɛ mli. Kɛ hela aba oŋmɔshi nibii ni hela emɔɔɔ bo lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does planting my crops too close together make them rot more easily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ midu mitsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛgboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Tightly packed crops block wind movement and trap damp air between the leaves. This stagnant, moist air allows floating fungi to easily multiply and move quickly from plant to plant.
ga: Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nyiɛmɔ naa ni emɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ ni yɔɔ dioo lɛ haa ŋmeii ni hoɔ yɛ nu lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ babaoo ni amɛyaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ.

english: Is the mold growing on my stored maize an insect pest or a plant weed?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni mikɛtoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ji ŋmei loo jwɛi?

english: Mold is neither an insect nor a weed; it belongs to a separate group of living things called fungi. They do not have roots or leaves and grow by absorbing nutrients directly from your stored grains.
ga: Fungi jeee kooloi bibii loo jwɛi. Efata nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ akuu kroko ni atsɛɔ amɛ fungi lɛ he. Amɛbɛ shishifãi loo baai ni amɛdaraa kɛtsɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ni okɛtoɔ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does crop disease keep returning to my field every year even after I clear the old plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa miŋmɔji amli daa afi beni mijie tsei momoi lɛ po lɛ?

english: Fungal spores can hide and survive in the soil or old crop remains over the dry season. When fresh crops are planted and the rains return, these resting spores wake up and infect the new plants.
ga: Fungal spores baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni etsɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni amɛhi shi. Kɛ adu tsei heei ni nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni eshwɛ nɛɛ teɔ shi ni amɛhaa tsei heei yeɔ hela.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and soft during continuous heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a water-loving fungus. Raindrops splash microscopic fungal spores from the ground or infected pods onto healthy pods, spreading the rot quickly.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni sumɔɔ nu. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya.

english: How do spray treatments protect my crops from airborne sickness?
ga: Te tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli baa lɛ ahe aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Fungicide sprays create a protective shield on the leaves. When floating fungal spores land on a sprayed leaf, the chemical kills the fungus before it can enter and harm the plant.
ga: Tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ amɛhe. Beni fungal spores lɛ shwieɔ baai ni ashwie nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ. Tsofai lɛ gbeɔ ŋmei lɛ dani enyɛɔ etutuaa tso lɛ.

english: Why do I need to make raised mounds or ridges before planting my yams and cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo gɔji loo ŋshɔkei anɔ dani madu sweet potatoes kɛ cassava lɛ?

english: Mounds and ridges loosen the soil, making it soft and easy for root tubers like yams and cassava to expand big and deep underground. Raised mounds also help excess water drain away so the crop roots do not sit in water and rot.
ga: Gɔji kɛ ŋshɔkei lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni efeɔ mlɛo kɛha shishifãi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii. koni egbɛ eshwa ni ebote shikpɔŋ shishi Gɔŋ ni awo nɔ lɛ hu haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shishifãi lɛ boteee nu mli ni amɛgboi.

english: Can I plant cassava and yams together on the same field at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ be kome mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping cassava and yams is a common practice. Since yams grow faster and are harvested earlier than cassava, careful spacing allows you to harvest your yams first while the cassava keeps growing to use the remaining space.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛ sweet potato teŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, sweet potatoes daa oya ni akpaa oya fe cassava. Kɛ́ okɛ ohe wo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa o-sweet potato lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Beni ŋmei lɛ yaa nɔ edaa lɛ koni ekɛ he ni eshwɛ lɛ atsu nii

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves up toward the sunlight, which helps the plant make food to grow large tubers underground. Staking also keeps leaves off wet soil, preventing diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia shishitoo nɔ ni amɛaatsɔ nɔ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ niyenii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu buɔ tsei ahe tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ koni helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut large yam tubers into smaller seed pieces before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji amli mifeɔ dumɔwui bibii dani miduɔ lɛ?

english: Cutting clean, healthy tubers into smaller seed yams helps you multiply your planting material so you can plant a larger field. Each healthy seed piece contains eyes that will sprout into new plants.
ga: Kɛ́ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli owo sweet potato dumɔwui bibii amli lɛ, ebaaha okɛ nibii babaoo ni akɛduɔ nii afata he. No hewɔ lɛ abaanyɛ adu yɛ shikpɔji wuji anɔ. Dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ ŋmei ni baakwɛ̃ ni etsɔ tso hee.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting on their own while stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ be mli ni mikɛtoɔ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams go through a natural resting phase after harvest, but once this period ends, the tuber wakes up and naturally tries to sprout a new vine to grow again. Storing them in a cool, well-ventilated barn slows this process down.
ga: Sweet potatoes yaa adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Shi kɛ́ be nɛɛ ba naagbee lɛ, bulb lɛ baate shi ni ebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ wain tso hee akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nifeemɔ nɛɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do my yam vines die back and dry up around harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbiɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: When yam tubers reach full maturity, the plant naturally stops growing leaves and transfers all remaining energy down into the underground tuber, causing the above-ground vine to dry up naturally.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato tubers lɛ dara kwraa lɛ, tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ haa baai lɛ adalɛ kpaa ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ yaa shikpɔŋ shishi. Ha wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ agbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: How do I choose the right cassava stem cuttings to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmeii ni sa ni mikɛbaadu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should select strong, disease-free stems from the middle portion of a mature cassava plant. Avoid using the very woody base or the soft, green tips because middle cuttings sprout stronger and faster.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ mli kɛjɛ ŋmei tso ni eda lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ mli. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tso shishitoo loo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he. Ejaakɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ baadara waa ni amɛbaafee oya.

english: Why does my cassava crop stay alive during dry weather while other crops wither?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi gboɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava is a tough crop with deep roots that search for water underground. During severe dry spells, it naturally drops its leaves to conserve water and goes into a resting state until the rains return.
ga: Cassava ji tso ko ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni taoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu. yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbote hejɔɔmɔ shihilɛ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How do I know when my cassava is mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmei lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting when lower leaves yellow and drop off. You can gently dig up one plant to check if the roots are thick and filled with starch.
ga: Cassava henɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ Obaanyɛ Ofo tsei lɛ eko mli fiofio koni ona kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plant curling up and showing yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies or by using infected planting stems. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties is the best way to keep your crop healthy.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ anɔ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay healthy and green. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the maize regain its rich green color and grow strong.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmei lɛ ni eku esɛɛ eba eŋɔli ni mli edɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni etsɔ hewalɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of phosphorus in the soil. Consistent watering during dry spells and adding compost helps the plants hold onto their blossoms to form fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo fɔsfɔs ni faaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ, ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni ewo yibii.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade from taller plants, such as plantains or leguminous shade trees, to keep them cool and moist during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo nut tsei amli koni amɛná hulutsoo ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do caterpillars always attack the tender center fold of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa mi ŋmã tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋta lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: The center whorl of a maize plant is soft, moist, and protected from the hot sun, making it the preferred place for pests like fall armyworms to hide and eat the youngest, sweetest leaves.
ga: Abɛi tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ haa efeɔ he ko ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ sumɔɔ waa. Koni ekɛtee ni eye baai bibii ni ŋɔɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my pepper crops very close to each other so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná he ko ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ babaoo lɛ?

english: When pepper plants are crowded together, they struggle against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to small plants and poor harvests. Good spacing also lets air flow through, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ebua amɛhe naa Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei bibii kɛ ŋmaa ni ehiii He ni jɛkɛmɔ kpakpa hu haa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ mli. Tsi fungal helai anaa

english: Why is it necessary to clear weeds from around my yam mounds even when the yam vines look strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? mi ŋmeii ni ato lɛ Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii wain tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ

english: Weeds steal valuable soil nutrients, fertilizers, and moisture that your yams need to build large underground tubers. Weeds also attract harmful pests that can damage the yam vines.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ sũ mli niyenii, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa o-sweet potato lɛ koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔshi nibii wuji akwɛ̃. Jwɛi hu gbalaa kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara ni baanyɛ afite sweet potato wain tsei lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava field is getting too much water after heavy rains?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ oŋmɔji lɛ miihe nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: If cassava plants sit in waterlogged soil for too long, their leaves will yellow and drop off early, and the tubers underground will start to rot and smell bad. Cassava needs loose, well-drained soil where water does not gather.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ ehi shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Ebaai lɛ baafee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaagbee shi oya. Ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baabɔi fitemɔ ni amɛbaaŋɔ ŋmɔlɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni mli ewo muji ni nu buaa ehe naa lɛ he miihia cassava.

english: Why are my transplanted plantain suckers taking so long to start producing new leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani plantain tsei ni midu lɛ jeɔ baai heei shweremɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers pause their top growth after transplanting because they need to focus on establishing new roots first. If the soil is too dry or lacks organic matter, this root recovery process takes much longer.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baakpa dalɛ ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he shɛɛmɔ beni adu amɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, esa akɛ wɔkɛ wɔjwɛŋmɔ ama shishifãi heei afeemɔ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli lɛ Gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsakeɔ shishifãi lɛ baahe be babaoo.

english: What causes the leaves on my papaya tree to curl up and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ papaya tso nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in papaya is usually caused by a plant virus spread by tiny insects like whiteflies. Once infected, the leaf growth slows down, so controlling sap-sucking insects early keeps your trees healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso mli hela ko ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ papaya baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji akɛ hela lɛ mɔ lɛ, baai lɛ daaa blɛoo, no hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni akudɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ mra. Ebaaha otsei lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: If I plant cowpeas between my cassava rows, will the cowpeas damage or help my cassava?
ga: Kɛji midu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ Ani tsina ŋmeii baaye mi ŋmeii lɛ awui loo eye ebua mi?

english: Planting cowpeas between cassava actually helps your crop because cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. They also cover the soil, preventing weed growth and keeping the earth moist.
ga: Cowpeas ni ooodu yɛ ŋmei teŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua onibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu shwieɔ shi, amɛtsiɔ jwɛi ni shwereɔ lɛ naa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are market traders telling me that my harvested crops have too much water in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayelɔi kɛɔ mi akɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli nu fa tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are harvested too early or not dried properly, they hold excess moisture inside. Traders reject this because excess water causes crops to rot quickly during transport and storage, reducing their market value.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii mra tsɔ loo amɛgbiko jogbaŋŋ Tso lɛ toɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ mli. Jarayelɔi kpooɔ enɛ ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ oya yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji jarayeli jara ni baa shi.

english: How does harvesting my crops right after a rainstorm affect their quality?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Harvesting immediately after rain causes crops to soak up excess water, making them wet and heavy. This high moisture leads to mold growth and spoilage before you can sell them to buyers.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ tsii. Nɛkɛ hulutsoo be ni fa nɛɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa ni amɛfiteɔ dani obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ oha mɔ ko ni baahe lɛ.

english: How does waiting a little longer before harvesting change the amount of water inside my crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ be fioo ni mimɛɔ dani akpaa nii lɛ baatsake nu ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: As a plant reaches full maturity, it naturally stops pumping excess water into its seeds or fruits and begins to dry out. Waiting for proper maturity naturally reduces crop moisture.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Ebaakpa nu ni fa fe nine ni ekɛwoɔ dumɔwu loo aduawai lɛ amli lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ oomɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, no baaha tso lɛ mli nu ni mli edɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do I know when my harvested crops are dry enough to sell to buyers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mikpamɔ lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ maha mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ?

english: For grains, you can test dryness by biting a grain—if it cracks sharply instead of denting softly, or by using a simple salt-in-a-jar test, it means the moisture level is low enough for the market.
ga: Kɛha ŋmaa lɛ, obaanyɛ oka kɛji egbi kɛtsɔ ŋmaa lɛ ni oooye lɛ nɔ. Kɛji efo oya moŋ fe ni eeefo blɛoo Aloo okɛ ŋoo ni akɛwoɔ tɔ mli lɛ kaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa kɛha jarayeli lɛ.

english: Why do my stored crops turn moldy and soft after just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛto lɛ mli ewo ŋmɔtɔ ni efee blɛoo yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Mold grows when crops are bagged or stored while still damp. Trapped water and heat create the perfect environment for fungi to feed on your produce and make it rot.
ga: Mold baanyɛ adara kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo kotoku mli loo akɛto be mli ni amɛmli edɔ lolo. Nu kɛ la ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmei baanyɛ aye onibii ni okɛwo mli lɛ ni eha egbo.

english: What simple steps can I take on my farm to dry my harvest properly?
ga: Ma nyɛ ma nyɛɛ blɔ nya tomi komɛ a nɔ. Mɛni manyɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni miŋmɔ mli nibii lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Spread your harvested crops in a thin layer on clean tarpaulins elevated off the bare ground in a sunny, breezy area, and turn them frequently so all sides dry evenly.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli. Yɛ tarpaulin ni he tse ni awó nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ yɛ he ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa yɛ lɛ nɔ, ni atsakeɔ shii abɔ koni fãi lɛ fɛɛ agbi pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do buyers pay less for my crops even when I produce a large weight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ fioo eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Buyers care about quality indicators like low moisture, clean produce, and long shelf life. Excess water adds temporary weight that disappears when the crop dries, which traders know and adjust prices for.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ buɔ nibii kpakpai tamɔ fɛ̃i ni baa shi, nibii ni he tse lɛ akɛ nɔ ni jara wa. kɛ shihilɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ be kukuoo mli muji ni laajeɔ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩɔ lɛ fataa he. ni jarayelɔ lɛ le ni etsakeɔ jara lɛ

english: Why do crops grown from the same batch of seeds perform well on one plot of land but stay wet and poor on another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui akuu kome mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛyeɔ ohia yɛ shikpɔŋ kroko nɔ lɛ?

english: Different soils retain water differently. Soil that holds too much water or lacks proper drainage keeps crops damp and soft, even if you used high-quality seeds from the same batch.
ga: Shikpɔji srɔtoi kɛ nu toɔ yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ bɛ mli lɛ baaha tso lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee bɔdɔɔ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni jɛ kuu kome mli lɛ tsu nii po.

english: How can officers from the Ministry of Agriculture help me if traders complain about my crop quality?
ga: Te onukpai ni jɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ kɛji jarayelɔ ko wie huhuuhu yɛ bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hi ha lɛ he?

english: Extension officers can visit your farm to test your soil drainage, teach you correct drying methods, and show you how to meet the specific quality standards local market traders want.
ga: Extension nitsulɔi baanyɛ aya oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛka shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ amɛkwɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ bo gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbiɔ. ni etsɔɔ bɔ ni aaafee ashɛ shishitoo mlai pɔtɛɛ ni jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ biɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Where can I get crop varieties that naturally hold less water and dry better for market?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana tsei ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ amɛhiɛɔ nu fioo ni amɛhe egbi kɛha jarayeli?

english: You can visit your local Ministry of Agriculture office or certified seed suppliers to get improved seed varieties bred specifically to produce firmer yields that store and dry better.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyasara Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ loo dumɔwui ahe nitsumɔhe ko ni aŋmɛ gbɛ. Koni enine ashɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsɔse amɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii ni fa babaoo lɛ anɔ. ni toɔ ni egbiɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ

english: Why are my young cocoa leaves turning yellow and drying up when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without fast-growing shade trees or plantains nearby to block the heat, the leaves burn, turn yellow, and dry out before the crop can establish itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni shwereɔ oya bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ni baatsi latsaa lɛ naa lɛ, baai lɛ baashã, ni amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. ni egbiɔ dani tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dirt inside the plant stem?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli?

english: This is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides deep inside the center whorl of the maize plant, feeds on the tender leaves, and leaves behind sawdust-like waste.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fall armyworm caterpillars ji nɔ ni kɛbaa, ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ, amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni amɛshiɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward into tight balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee bɔɔlu ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap from the leaves, or by a virus carried by those insects. Controlling these tiny bugs early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ kooloi bibii akudɔmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why is it good for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ tsina loo ŋmei kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts catch nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds the maize and improves soil fertility for future seasons.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ bei.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my crops so the rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni nugbɔ akashwie amɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is damp but not during heavy downpours. Placing it a few centimeters away from the stem and covering it lightly with soil helps the roots absorb it before rain washes it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Okɛ sɛntimita fioo ko kɛjɛ tso lɛ he ni okɛ sũ aha nɔ fioo. Enɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ lɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ ashwie lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when a strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow close to the surface and do not go very deep into the soil. When the tree forms heavy fruit bunches, the top becomes heavy, so strong winds easily uproot it unless you prop it up with sturdy wooden sticks.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ni amɛyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ yɛ aduawai ni tsii babaoo mli lɛ, ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ baafee tsiimɔ, no hewɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ atswa ni ejie lɛ oya. Ja okɛ tso ni mli wa fiɔ sɛɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without draining. Planting on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food for big tubers underground. Staking holds the vines off the wet ground so the leaves stay healthy and receive full sunlight.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa wain tso lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ ahe koni eha tso lɛ yibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: How can I store my harvested maize so that small insects do not turn the grains into powder?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato? Koni kooloi bibii akatsɔ powda?

english: Insects like weevils multiply when grain is not completely dry. Drying your maize until it is hard and storing it in airtight (hermetic) bags suffocates the insects so they cannot destroy your harvest.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ faa babaoo kɛ́ ŋmaa lɛ egbiko kwraa. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa waa ni okɛwo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha kooloi bibii lɛ agbɔjɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, efiteee nibii ni ofeɔ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get extremely hot, when the soil gets too dry, or when the plant lacks proper nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers stay attached and produce tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ tomato.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow strong green leaves. Applying organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer early in the plant's life restores its health and increases your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ organic loo nitrogen fertilizer wo oshihilɛ mli yɛ oshihilɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni oná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni eha onibii ni onáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do farmers spread dry grass around the stems of young crops during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi shwieɔ jwɛi ni egbi amɛshwãa amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass or crop leaves around plants is called mulching. It acts like a protective blanket that holds moisture in the soil, keeps the roots cool under the hot sun, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo tso baai ni agbɛɔ ashwãa tsei ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with thick green leaves but giving me very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or plants are overcrowded, cassava spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of roots below. Proper spacing and balanced soil nutrients encourage the plant to send energy down to build heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo tsei lɛ yɛ babaoo lɛ Yucca kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ja lɛ haa tsei lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni amɛfee bulbs ni tsii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up to catch maximum sunlight, which the plant turns into food to build big tubers underground. Keeping the leaves off the hot ground also prevents fungal diseases and rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. Tsei lɛ bafeɔ niyenii koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ́ akɛ baai lɛ to hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ hu, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ fitemɔ naa.

english: Does local rice always need to grow inside standing water, or can I plant it on dry land?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni adu maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo manyɛ madu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ?

english: Not all rice needs standing water. Upland rice varieties are bred to grow on dry agricultural land using normal rainfall, while lowland or paddy rice varieties require swampy fields that retain water.
ga: Omɔ henɔi komɛi biɔ nu ni damɔ shi. Akwɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmãa henɔi koni akɛdu yɛ okwaayeli shikpɔŋ ni nɔ egbi nɔ kɛtsɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa henɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kplanaa nɔ loo ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ he hiaa hei ni ŋmeii yɔɔ koni amɛkɛ nu ato.

english: Is it good to plant cowpeas together on the same land with my maize crop?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ wɔbaafee ekome kɛdu tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas alongside maize is very beneficial. Cowpeas naturally take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps feed the maize plant while covering the ground to retain soil moisture.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmãa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my tomato plant flowers keep falling off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by irregular watering, extreme heat, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus. Keeping the soil evenly moist and protecting plants from extreme heat helps fruits set successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ hao kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be ni abuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni aduawai lɛ yeɔ omanye.

english: Why are my pepper fruits getting dark, soft spots at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɔɔ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This issue is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant or uneven watering. Adding lime or well-rotted manure to the soil and watering regularly helps peppers grow firm and healthy.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei amli loo nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ akɛ lime loo ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni afɔ nɔ nu daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdara shi shiŋŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How can I protect my vegetable crops from small insects without spending money on chemical sprays?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-vegetables lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ahe ni mikɛ shika tsuuu nii yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ahe?

english: You can prepare a natural pest spray by soaking crushed neem tree leaves in water overnight with a little mild soap. Spraying this mixture on your crops repels harmful insects without damaging your soil or costing money.
ga: Obaanyɛ osaa adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛtsɔ neem baai ni atswa lɛ ni okɛ samla fioo ni mli ejɔ baawo nu mli nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa nɛɛ shwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, ebaashwie kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni efiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ loo efiteee bo shika.

english: Why does my harvested maize get full of tiny holes and powder when I store it in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ eyi kɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Insects called weevils attack stored grain that still holds moisture or is kept in warm, open spaces. Sun-drying your harvested maize thoroughly until the grains are very hard before sealing them in airtight bags prevents weevils from multiplying.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ tutuaa dumɔwui ni ato ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo loo akɛto hei ni mli edɔ ni mɛi yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa waa dani awo mli yɛ vacuum kotokui amli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafɔ.

english: Why do the lower leaves on my maize plants turn yellow and dry up before the cobs are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to grow healthy green leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in the crop's growth helps keep the leaves green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ŋmãa babaoo koni ebaakwɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he mra yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests every year even when the rainfall is good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Every crop harvest takes nutrients out of the ground. When crops are grown repeatedly without adding manure, compost, or resting the soil, the soil becomes depleted and loses its ability to feed new plants.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɔ tsei shii abɔ Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo aŋmɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ tsei heei anɔ dɔŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help improve my soil for the next season's crop?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha be ni baa lɛ mli dumɔ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When the plants decay, that nitrogen stays in the soil, acting as free natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Kɛ tsei lɛ fite Nakai nitrogen lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn dark brown, dry up, and die on the tree?
ga: Why are my young cocoa pods turning dark brown? Tsei ni egbi ni egboi?

english: This is typically caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, shaded conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let in sunlight and clearing infected pods early helps prevent it from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la aba kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ gbɛfaŋnɔ naa.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like aphids or mites that transmit viruses to the plant. Spraying with neem leaf extract or insecticidal soap helps control these pests early before damage spreads.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ yaa tsei amli Kɛ́ akɛ neem baa mli nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra. dani nɔ ni efite lɛ agbɛ ashwã

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during light winds before the fruit is ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ be mli dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Tiny underground pests called root nematodes or banana weevils eat through the roots and stem base, destroying the plant's anchorage in the soil so it cannot support heavy bunches.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ root nematodes loo banana ŋmeii yeɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifã lɛ shishi. Efiteɔ he ni tsei yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ enyɛŋ eye ebua kuu ko ni tsii.

english: Why do some of my cassava plants produce huge top leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ekomɛi yɛ ŋwɛi baai wuji shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or too much water, the plant directs all its energy into growing green foliage instead of storing starch in the root tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli moŋ fe ni ekɛ starch baato shishifã lɛ mli.

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a shortage of calcium in the plant during fruit formation, often triggered by irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the plant uptake calcium properly.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei amli yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my yam vines develop black spots and wither early in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ diji ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: This is anthracnose, a fungal disease spread by rain splashes in humid weather. Staking vines high off the ground keeps leaves dry and helps reduce the spread of the fungus.
ga: Enɛ ji antraknosis. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Wein tsei ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop and wilt during hot afternoons even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni mi lɛ shwieee lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In intense sun, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can draw it up from the soil. Covering the soil around the plants with dry grass (mulching) keeps the roots cool and retains soil moisture longer.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry up when I plant them in an open field without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves dry up in open fields because young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Plantains or shade trees act as living umbrellas, keeping the leaves cool and protecting the soil moisture so the plants survive.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ baagbi yɛ ŋmɔ mli ejaakɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa baai lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ he koni tso lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants use to grow green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores their healthy green color.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛbaai eŋɔli lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shi waa.

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same patch of land year after year lead to smaller harvests each time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests that feed on that specific crop to build up in the ground, weakening future harvests.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nibii ni afeɔ wɔsɛɛ lɛ baafee nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rain sits on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain sits on the ground without draining, it suffocates the roots and creates damp conditions where harmful rot fungus thrives.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni nɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu bɛ mli lɛ Ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ baa he ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines produce bigger tubers when I stake them up off the ground with wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ bulbs wuji fe tsutsu lɛ beni mikɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ duɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up off the ground into direct sunlight and air. This allows the leaves to trap light more effectively to make food, which the plant then sends down to enlarge the tuber.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ la jogbaŋŋ koni amɛfee niyenii. ni tso lɛ baatsu kɛba shi koni ekɛgbala ŋmeii lɛ amli

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and weak with small cobs if I plant seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants compete against each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leaving no single plant with enough energy to produce large cobs.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei komɛi bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking leaf juices or spreading plant viruses, which damages the leaf structure and stunts plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu loo tso mli helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Enɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni etsĩɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too hot, water is lacking, or when wind and insects fail to shake the pollen inside the flower to form a fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ, nu bɛ, loo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ atswa pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛfee aduawai.

english: Why shouldn't I apply chemical fertilizer to my crops during a long dry spell without rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so plant roots can safely drink it in. In dry soil, concentrated chemical fertilizer sits directly on the roots and burns them, damaging the plant.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu amɛ shweshweeshwe. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ taraa shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛshãa amɛ. ni kɛ fitemɔ baa tsei anɔ lɛ

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly even after I apply fertilizer to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa fiofio eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing root systems that steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops, taking away the nutrients before your plants can use them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Kɛtsɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni ajuɔ dani tsei baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and stay thin when I plant them very close together on my plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ beni midu amɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded together, their roots fight for the limited water and nutrients in the soil while their leaves block sun from each other. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures it gets enough sunlight and soil food to grow tall, green, and strong.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ eyi amɛhe obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni fa fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa enáa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃, efee eŋɔli, ni ehe wa.

english: How does planting groundnuts together with my maize help the soil without me buying expensive fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe ŋmãa ni jara wa?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. This natural nitrogen feeds the nearby maize plants, helping them grow healthy without needing costly chemical fertilizers.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii. Ye obua amɛ ni amɛdara waa ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe ehiaaa.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains next to my young cocoa trees when starting a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei ahe kɛ́ mije ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the cocoa trees the soft shade and cool soil moisture they need to survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ naa hulutsoo ni mli jɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers without growing any peppers during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni eduuu pepper ko yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high and water is low, pepper plants drop their flowers as a survival mechanism to conserve moisture and energy. Giving them shade cover and regular watering helps the plant stay cool enough to hold its flowers and form fruits.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni nu lɛ hu faaa lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hulutsoo kɛ hewalɛ he. Tso lɛ he ŋmɔlɔ ni oooha lɛ nu daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehaa ehe jɔɔ bɔ ni sa koni ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii.

english: Why shouldn't I cut down all the large shade trees on my land before making mounds for my yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifoɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ dani mafee gɔŋ kɛha mi-sweet potatoes lɛ?

english: Large trees act as windbreaks and keep the surrounding soil cool. If you clear every tree, the strong heat will dry out your yam mounds quickly, and heavy rains can easily wash away the rich topsoil needed for large yam tubers to form.
ga: Tsei wuji tsuɔ nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsiimɔ ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli jɔɔ. Kɛji ojie tso fɛɛ tso Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baaha o-sweet potatoes ni okɛto lɛ agbi oya. Ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji lɛ anɔ oya.

english: If I don't have money to add fertilizer, why should I leave part of my cassava land to rest for a season?
ga: Kɛji obɛ shika ni okɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ, mɛni hewɔ obaashi ŋmei he lɛ be kome?

english: Leaving land fallow allows wild grasses and plants to naturally grow, decay, and rot into the soil. This process restores essential organic nutrients, loosens the hard earth, and prepares the ground to feed your crops again naturally.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ haa jwɛi kɛ koo mli tsei kwɛ̃ɔ, amɛgboiɔ, ni amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ, ehaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni esaa shikpɔŋ lɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha onibii ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What causes the middle leaves of my young maize plants to dry up and die early in the season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra?

english: This damage is usually caused by stem borer caterpillars that hatch inside the stem and eat the inner growing tissues. Spotting tiny pinholes on the leaves early allows you to treat the plants before the center leaf dries out completely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, stem borers ni fɔɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ fãji ni miida yɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni ona bu bibioo ko yɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ mra Enɛ baaha onyɛ otsa tso lɛ dani baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ agbi kwraa.

english: Why do my vegetable seeds wash away every time heavy rain falls on my newly raised seedbeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ ni naa wa baanɛ yɛ mi saatso ni midu ehee lɛ nɔ lɛ, nu lɛ shwieɔ mi-vegetables dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Freshly dug nursery soil is soft and easily washed away by strong raindrops. Covering the seedbed with a light layer of dry palm leaves or straw breaks the force of the falling rain, keeping the tiny seeds safely buried in the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akumɔ ehee yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa lɛ hoɔ oya. Ni akɛ ŋmei tsei loo jwɛi ni egbi ni mli tseee aha dumɔwui lɛ asa lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ hewalɛ baa shi. feemɔ dumɔwui bibii ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and rot while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato aduawai lɛ ashishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This issue, called blossom-end rot, happens when the plant cannot draw enough calcium from the soil into the developing fruit. It is usually caused by irregular watering routines or soil that dries out completely between waterings.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ baa kɛ́ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛya aduawai ni miida lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo shikpɔŋ lɛ ni egbiɔ kwraa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ.

english: How can I tell if my small cassava patch is doing well enough to justify clearing more land for expansion?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ sa? Ani minɔ lɛ miitsu nii jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni ejie he kroko ni akɛbaagbɛ eshwa?

english: Look for thick stems, healthy green leaf canopies without widespread yellowing, and large tuber roots at harvest. Strong performance on a small piece of land shows your soil management and crop care are working well enough to scale up.
ga: Taomɔ tsei ni mli tse. Baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ŋmɔŋ bɛ mli fɛɛ. kɛ shishifãi wuji kɛji akpa Nitsumɔ ni mli wa yɛ shikpɔji bibii anɔ Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni okɛbaashɛ sɛkɛl he.

english: Why do my crops look pale and yellow after heavy rains wash across my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛ waa nɛ yɛ miŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes away essential nutrients from the topsoil—a process called leaching. Without these nutrients, the leaves cannot produce their deep green color or food, leaving the plants weak and pale.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he. Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ leaching. Kɛji niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ bɛ lɛ, baai lɛ nyɛŋ afee niyenii loo amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do the roots of my pepper plants rot when rain leaves standing water on my land for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ ni ehaa nu hiɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air from the soil to breathe just like humans do. When water sits on the field for too long, it cuts off oxygen to the soil, drowning the roots and causing them to rot.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaafo kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ekɛ shishifãi lɛ woɔ nu mli ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and dry in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to harsh sunlight. Without shade trees to cover them, the intense sun burns their fragile leaves and dries out the moisture they need to grow.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã amɛbaai ni waaa lɛ. ni egbiɔ nu ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants grow better when I plant plantains next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu plantains yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that shade young cocoa seedlings from intense direct sunlight, keeping the soil cool and moist while the cocoa establishes its root system.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ maa shishifãi lɛ.

english: Dropping leaves is a cassava plant's defense mechanism to conserve water during dry weather. The plant goes partially dormant to save energy while keeping the cassava tubers under the ground alive.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛhaa ŋmei tsei koni amɛbu nu he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli. Tsei lɛ fã ko ŋmɛɔ koni amɛbu hewalɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛhaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do I need to guide my yam vines onto wooden tall stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ awo tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to capture sunlight for growing big tubers underground. Staking also keeps leaves off the hot, damp soil where fungal diseases can easily infect them.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaatsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni ekahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ atswa amɛ oya lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout when I bury them deep inside the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: A seed contains a limited amount of stored energy to push its shoot up to the surface. If buried too deep, the shoot exhausts its energy before reaching sunlight and air, causing it to die underground.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ hewalɛ fioo ko ni ato ni amɛkɛtsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Hewalɛ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baaho dani eshɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he. ha egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why are there small holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars hidden inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ani akɛtee tsɔne lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by pests like stem borers or fall armyworms that hatch on the leaves and eat their way into the plant stem to feed on its soft internal tissues.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ stem borers loo cutworms ni fɔɔ baa nɔ ni amɛyeɔ niyenii yɛ tsei ashishifãi amli koni amɛye fãji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil, but leguminous crops like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground, naturally restoring fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni okɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aba ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn small and weak even when there is plenty of space on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miyɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that aggressively steal soil nutrients, fertilizer, and water away from your crops long before your crops can absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ onibii amli dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ amɛ.

english: How do I know when my short-duration maize is ready to harvest so I don't leave it in the farm too long?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmãa ni yeɔ be kukuoo lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa? No hewɔ lɛ kaashi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Maize is usually ready when the husks turn brown and dry, and the grains become hard. Leaving mature maize in the field too long exposes it to field pests, birds, and mold from unexpected rains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ ŋmãa lɛ tsɔ ŋmãa ni egbi. ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa Eshiɔ ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaaha ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai, okpoi kɛ ŋmeii aba ŋmɔ mli kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do some crops produce food in just three months while others take years to yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi woɔ niyenii yɛ nyɔji etɛ pɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛwoɔ niyenii lɛ?

english: Crops have different natural growth cycles. Short-season crops like cowpea or maize mature fast (around 80 to 90 days) to give quick food, while long-term crops like cocoa build deep roots and strong trunks first so they can keep producing yields for many years.
ga: Tsei yɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ gbɛjianɔtoi srɔtoi. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ tsina loo ŋmãa lɛ daa oya (aaafee gbii 80 kɛyashi 90) koni ekɛ niyenii aha oya. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ, tamɔ kookoo lɛ, shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni wa baa klɛŋklɛŋ bɔni afee ni amɛwo yibii afii babaoo.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my seeds as soon as the very first rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ ji oshara kɛha mi lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry spell before the main rainy season starts. If you plant immediately, the seeds might germinate and then die from drought; it is safer to wait until the rains become steady.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Dumɔwui baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi yɛ hɔmɔ hewɔ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: What can I do to make my cassava produce bigger tubers instead of just growing plenty of leaves?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni mi-cassava lɛ akwɛ bulbs wuji moŋ fe ni maná baai babaoo kɛkɛ?

english: Cassava grows leaves instead of big tubers when the soil has too much nitrogen and lacks potassium. Using compost or manure and ensuring the farm gets full sunlight encourages the plant to store energy underground in the roots.
ga: Cassava kwɛɔ baai yɛ ŋmeii wuji najiaŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium hu bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii ni akwɛ koni ŋmɔ lɛ aná hulu la ni fa lɛ, ebaawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops grow very green in one part of my land but stay short and yellow in another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miikwɛ̃ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã ko nɔ nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ kuku lolo ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ fã kroko mli.

english: Soil nutrition varies across a farm. Yellowish, short plants usually indicate that specific spot lacks nutrients like nitrogen or has poor water drainage, which can be improved by adding compost or manure.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii mli nibii lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ kukuji lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ he ko, loo nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ. Abaanyɛ aha enɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: How does growing beans on my land after harvesting maize help my soil stay fertile?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii baa?

english: Legume crops like beans and cowpeas have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, natural fertilizing the ground for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha tsei fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us not to plant our seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkadu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to grow strong and produce a bigger harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni amɛduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ eda ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before making any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they face heat stress, extreme dry soil, or lack of nutrients. Giving them regular water and mulching the soil around them helps the plant keep its flowers to form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli. shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ Nu daa ni okɛ sũ awo he ni ebɔle he lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ fɔfɔi ahe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up during hot periods to trap moisture and prevent the plant from drying out, though it can also be a sign of sap-sucking insects like whiteflies.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛtsi tso lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Eyɛ mli akɛ enɛ hu baanyɛ afee kooloo ko ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ he okadi moŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines need long wooden stakes to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can spread out and catch direct sunlight. The more sunlight the leaves get, the more energy the plant creates to grow a large yam tuber underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akwɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Babaoo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ baa lɛ náa lɛ, babaoo ni tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen fertilizer. The plant automatically moves the remaining nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the new top leaves and growing ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii. Tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ jieɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛ nɔ ni miiya hiɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with plenty of big leaves, but producing very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ, ni eyɛ baai wuji, shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or manure, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of sending energy down to expand the food-storing roots below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmei babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsu lɛ kɛba shi koni eyakwɛ shishifãi ni toɔ niyenii yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot survive direct, intense sunlight. They need shade from nurse crops like plantain or tall trees to protect their leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛkwɛɔ amɛ tamɔ plantains loo tsei kakadaji amli. Koni akɛbu baai lɛ ahe koni akashã amɛ. kɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the small shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: If too many small shoots (suckers) grow around the main plantain tree, they steal water, plant food, and sunlight from the main mother plant, resulting in smaller bunches and weak stems.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu, tso lɛ mli niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei niji bibii kɛ tsei akutsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without fruiting when temperatures get too hot, when water is inconsistent, or when insects fail to pollinate them, forcing the plant to drop unfertilized flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ Enɛ haa tsei shiɔ fɔfɔi ni awoko amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and becoming small and hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding under the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies that disrupts the natural growth of the foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like pencils during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ pensil yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's natural defense against heat and drought. By curling into a tight tube, the leaf reduces its exposed surface area to save water from evaporating in the sun.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ he. Kɛtsɔ lɛ ni oootsɔ mli ewo tsɔne ni mli wa mli lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ haa amɛhiɛ he lɛ baa shi. Bɔni afee ni nu akatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulu la lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can capture maximum sunlight to make food. If they crawl on the ground in the shade of weeds, they catch diseases more easily and yield tiny tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Kɛji amɛkplekeshi shikpɔŋ yɛ jwɛi ŋmɔlɔ mli lɛ Helai yeɔ amɛ oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have beneficial bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Muawai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa mli yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: How do I know when my cocoa pods are fully ripe and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cocoa pods change color when mature—green pods turn bright yellow, and red or purple pods turn orange-yellow. This color change signals that the beans inside have reached full size with sweet pulp.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Pods eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ni ŋmeii tsuji loo ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baatsake kɛya ŋmɔtɔ-ŋmɔŋ. Nɛkɛ su tsakemɔ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kɔfi yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees drop their leaves when they get too much direct sunlight and lose water faster than their roots can take it up. Planting plantain trees alongside cocoa provides living shade that keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo shɛ amɛnɔ. ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aná Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do I see small holes in my young maize leaves and tiny green caterpillars inside the stems?
