ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana that eats the growing center of maize plants. Checking fields early and applying recommended sprays or neem extracts stops them before they destroy the entire harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ hei lɛ. Kwɛmɔ hei ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mra ni akɛ neem spray loo tsofa ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ atsu nii. Ekpaa jɛmɛ dani efiteɔ nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by small whiteflies and infected planting sticks. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by extension officers keeps the plants healthy and produces bigger tubers.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ Adumɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni extension officials lɛ kɛhaa lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe wa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does my land produce smaller crop yields every year even when I plant at the right time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ nii yɛ be ni sa mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the soil every season, so planting the same crop repeatedly starves the land. Rotating crops like beans or groundnuts with maize helps put natural nitrogen back into the soil to rebuild its fertility.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the young shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: When too many shoots grow together, they fight for the same soil food and water, resulting in thin plants and small fruits. Leaving only two or three strong shoots focuses all the tree's energy into producing large plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ fee ekome kɛdara tsɔ Amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ aduawai bibii baa. Kɛ́ oshi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ atsu plantain jwɛi agbo ko feemɔ he nii.

english: Why do my tomato plants look strong in the morning but droop down completely during the heat of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa leebi lɛ? Shi fɛɛ ni miigbee shi yɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes wilt in hot weather because their roots cannot supply water as fast as the hot sun dries the leaves. Covering the bare soil around the plants with dry grass or leaves holds moisture in the ground and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aha nu oya tamɔ bɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa baai lɛ gĩɔ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwieɔ Tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why is it bad to spray pest medicine on my farm late in the morning when the sun is strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaafɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ anɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ leebi be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Strong sunlight makes liquid chemical sprays evaporate quickly before they can work, and hot sun on sprayed leaves can burn the plant. Spraying early in the morning or late in the afternoon allows the plants to safely absorb the medicine.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani amɛtsuɔ nii. Ni hulu ni tsoɔ yɛ baai ni ashwie nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ leebi loo shwane lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa tsofa lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do I need to spend time putting tall wooden sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ be kɛwo tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ amli lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch sunlight, which allows the leaves to make the food needed to grow big tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off damp ground where diseases easily spread.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akɛ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni aná bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: Why do extension agents encourage me to plant cowpeas in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ wo mi hewalɛ koni madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the dirt. Planting them alongside maize acts as natural fertilizer, improving soil health and giving you two crops from one field.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ baa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Why do my young pepper seedlings collapse and die near the soil line even when I give them plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui bibii lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛmiigboi yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu babaoo moŋ?

english: Overwatering young seedlings creates soggy conditions where soil fungi thrive and rot the delicate stems at ground level. Watering lightly only when the topsoil feels dry prevents stem rot and encourages deep root growth.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei bibii amli fe nine lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ baa. Biɛ ji he ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ daa yɛ ni tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ nu fioo pɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anaa, ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Plants move nitrogen to their newest leaves to keep growing, causing the older lower leaves to turn yellow and starve.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei kɛ nitrogen yaa baai heei lɛ amli koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara. Enɛ haa shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for next season's crop?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the roots decay in the soil, they leave natural fertilizer behind for future crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi bibii amli beni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛbaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is it important for me to clear young shoots growing at the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, compete with the main stem for sunlight, water, and nutrients. Removing extra suckers leaves enough food for the main plant to produce large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ, kɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to put wooden poles next to my yam vines as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo emasɛi lɛ? Sweet potato wain tso beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves off the damp ground into full sun. Staking improves sunlight exposure for growth and protects leaves from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ kɛyashi amɛbaaná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Staking haa hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my tomato stems with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops sunlight from drying out the earth quickly, keeps soil temperatures cool, and prevents weeds from taking light and water.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu la akagbi shikpɔŋ lɛ oya. Helps maintain cool soil temperatures. ni ehaaa jwɛi akabote la kɛ nu mli

english: Why are there small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with small caterpillars hidden inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii, amɛshishigbɛ ni etsilɛ, kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛtee mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They burrow into the central leaves of young maize to feed, which weakens the stalk if not treated early.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛfoɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli koni amɛye niyenii. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishi lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and becoming tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on young leaf sap, which can also spread stunt-causing plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni baanyɛ agbɛ tsei amli helai ni haa mɔ shwieɔ shi lɛ ashwã

english: Why is it bad for me to spray chemical pesticides during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ shi shwane mli lɛ ehiii kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Hot afternoon weather causes chemical sprays to evaporate into the air before working properly, and high sunlight combined with chemicals can scorch green plant leaves.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli dani amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni akɛ tsofai fata he lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ahe baai eŋɔli lɛ ashã.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before turning into young cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔii dani amɛbatsɔ cacao ŋmɔji bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when stressed by dry weather, intense heat, or pest attacks. Adequate shade, soil moisture, and pest control help trees keep flowers and grow pods.
ga: Cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hao amɛ. shade ni fa bɔ ni sa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ Ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves yellow and drop off, stem bark darkens, and cracks begin to open in the soil surrounding the base of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ yitso lɛ mli yɛ ediŋ. Ni ŋmeii bɔi gbelemɔ yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and drying up in the full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight and harsh winds. Plantain trees or shade trees need to be planted nearby to provide shade, cool the soil, and keep moisture in the ground while the cocoa grows.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa shishi. Ehe miihia ni adu dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ koni hulutsoo aba. ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli be mli ni kookoo lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when there is heavy rain for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess water sits in the soil for days, it suffocates the roots and encourages mold to grow, causing the tubers to rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbii babaoo. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ewo ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso ni egbo

english: Why do my yam plants need tall wooden stakes to climb on to produce big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce food for the tuber through their leaves. Lifting the leaves off the ground on tall stakes gives them maximum sunlight, which translates into bigger and healthier yam tubers below ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ niyenii haa amɛ ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale yellow down the middle instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential plant food. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure gives the crop the energy it needs to grow green and healthy.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ ŋmãa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my maize harvests get smaller every year when I keep planting on the exact same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ bibioo daa afi kɛ́ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize draws the same nutrients out of the soil every season. Rotating your maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts helps rebuild the soil's nutrients naturally for future harvests.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ama shi ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmaakpamɔ.

english: Why does my orange tree produce a huge harvest one year and then almost no fruit the next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-citrus tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo afi kome shi afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, eshwɛ fioo ni ebɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ?

english: Citrus trees use up massive reserves of food to produce a heavy fruit crop. Without proper feeding and pruning, the tree requires a full year to recover its energy before it can bear heavy fruit again.
ga: Citrus tsei kɛ niyenii babaoo ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo yibii ni tsii. Kɛji akɛ niyenii ni sa kɛ tso lɛ ŋmɔmɔ bɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ he miihia afi muu fɛɛ dani enyɛ ewo yibii ni tsii ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat or irregular watering. Shedding flowers is the plant's way of saving energy when it feels too stressed to support growing fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Fɔfɔi ni ashwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he beni amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛmiifee basaa tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants crinkling and curling upwards like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the underside of the leaves. Controlling these insects early prevents leaf damage and stops viruses from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ baai lɛ afitemɔ naa ni ehaa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why are my plantain bunches getting smaller when many young shoots grow around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii be mli ni ŋmeii bibii babaoo miida yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young shoots, called suckers, steal water, food, and sunlight from the main stem. Pruning away excess suckers leaves the main stem with all the energy needed to grow big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛkwɛ dumɔwui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow lots of thick green leaves but very few seed pods during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo lɛ? Shi dumɔwui ŋmɔji fioo pɛ yɔɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Excess water and rich soil encourage cowpeas to focus all their energy on growing leafy stems rather than flowers. Less water stress encourages the plant to switch into producing flowers and seed pods.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ yeɔ ebuaa cowpea ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa edalɛ nɔ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii. Nu he haomɔ ni baa shi lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛtsake kɛya fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui ashishifãi afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their tender leaves and dries out the soil moisture too quickly. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains creates a cooler environment for cocoa trees during their first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ koni amɛná hɔnɔ fioo koni amɛhi shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ebaa bibii lɛ, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ baa cacao tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Does staking my yam vines really make the tubers grow bigger, or is it just extra work?
ga: Ani mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ ni mikɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ haa bulbs lɛ daa diɛŋtsɛ loo eji nitsumɔ kroko kɛkɛ?

english: Staking lifts the vine leaves off the ground toward sunlight, allowing the plant to produce more food through photosynthesis. This extra energy goes down into the soil, helping the plant grow much larger and healthier yam tubers.
ga: Staking baaha wain tso lɛ baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ he. Ehaa tsei feɔ niyenii babaoo kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. Hewalɛ ni fa nɛɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edara ni ehiɛɔ sweet potato tubers babaoo.

english: This yellowing is usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen. When a maize plant does not get enough nitrogen from the soil, it steals the nutrient from its older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ejuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmãa hee ni eda yɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my chemical fertilizer burn my crops if I put it right next to the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shãa miŋmɔshi nibii kɛji mikɛwo tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers contain concentrated salts that draw moisture out of tender plant stems and roots if touched directly. Fertilizer should always be placed a few inches away from the stem in a ring or line so the roots can reach it safely.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ashishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ amɛshishifãi amli kɛji akɛ amɛbashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo 2-3 inches kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ ring loo line mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe.

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because flooded ground cuts off the oxygen supply that roots need to stay healthy. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa shishifãi lɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot or when soil moisture changes suddenly from dry to wet. Consistent watering and proper shade help the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo ni sa yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛmɔɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do caterpillars hide deep inside the leaves of my young maize plants during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ teɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm hide deep inside the central leaf funnel of maize to escape hot daytime sun and birds. They feed safely from the inside out, damaging leaves before you can easily see them.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛjo hulu kɛ okpoi anaa foi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Amɛyeɔ niyenii shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Kpatamɔ baai lɛ ahiɛ dani obaanyɛ ona amɛ mlɛo.

english: Why shouldn't I spray my pest chemicals in the afternoon when the sun is high?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ shwane mli beni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Spraying in hot afternoon sun can burn your crop leaves and cause the chemical to evaporate too quickly before working. Additionally, middle-of-the-day spraying harms beneficial insects like bees that pollinate your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ baai lɛ ni eha tsofai lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ dani ebɔi nitsumɔ. Kɛfata he lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ awui.

english: If I plant cassava and maize together on the same plot, will they fight each other for food?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa fee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Ani amɛbaashi akaŋ yɛ niyenii he?

english: Maize grows rapidly and feeds early, while cassava grows slowly at first and matures much later. If spaced correctly, they share the land without heavy competition because they use nutrients at different times.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni ayeɔ oya. Yɛ ŋmei gbɛfaŋ lɛ, edaa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni edaa blɛoo waa. Kɛji gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ ja Amɛbaajara shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni akaŋshii ni mli wa bɛ mli ejaakɛ amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ bei srɔtoi amli.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants with deep root systems and quick seeds adapted to survive tough conditions. Farm crops need extra care, so clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing water and nutrients from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ni wa ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ oya ni tsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Okwaayeli mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Why do some farmers grow sweet peppers inside plastic greenhouse structures instead of open fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmei yɛ plastic ŋtayaai amli moŋ fe ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Greenhouses protect delicate sweet peppers from harsh tropical sun, heavy rainfall, and outdoor pests, allowing you to grow high-quality produce continuously throughout the year.
ga: Greenhouses buɔ bell peppers ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kponɔgbɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe. Ehaa oyaa nɔ oduɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Is it okay for me to keep my greenhouse completely closed all day to keep insects away?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ mahã ŋmɔ lɛ mli ahi shi gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ koni mikɛshwie kooloi bibii?

english: No, a fully sealed greenhouse traps intense heat, which cooks the plants. Cracking open vents or doors allows cool outside air to circulate and keep temperature levels safe for your crops.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔ ni mli edɔ ni atsĩ naa lɛ baahi dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni haa tsei lɛ shwereɔ lɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ loo shinaa ni agbele lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni jɛɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ abɔle he ni eha hulutsoo be ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why is breeze or air movement so important inside an enclosed farm structure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni nyiɛɔ lɛ he hiaa yɛ ŋmɔ mli gbɛjianɔtoo ni agbe naa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Air movement cools down the environment, dries extra moisture off leaves to prevent fungal diseases, and supplies fresh carbon dioxide that plants need to make their food.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni nyiɛɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha baai lɛ agbi fe tsutsu lɛ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote mli. ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hee ni ji carbon dioxide ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkɛfee niyenii lɛ haa

english: How does severe afternoon heat affect my pepper plants?
ga: Te shwane mli latsaa lɛ saa mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants, causing their leaves to wilt, flowers to drop off prematurely, and fruit growth to slow down or stop completely.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei anɔ. haa baai lɛ gboɔ Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. ni aduawai lɛ adalɛ baa shi loo ekpaa kwraa

english: Pepper flowers usually drop off when the surrounding temperature gets too high or when there isn't enough airflow to keep the plant cool and help with pollination.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ni baaha tso lɛ mli ajɔ ni eye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What simple steps can I take to cool down my crops when the weather gets extremely hot?
ga: Ma nyɛ ma nyɛɛ blɔ nya tomi komɛ a nɔ. Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mikɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: You can open structure vents to let outside air pass through, apply shade nets to block extreme sunlight, and ensure you water early in the morning before the day gets hot.
ga: Obaanyɛ ogbele tsɔnei ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ atsɔ mli. Okɛ hulutsoo ŋshɔŋloo awo mli koni ebu ohe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he. Ni kwɛmɔ ni okɛ nu awo mli leebi dani hulu lɛ adɔ.

english: Will my crops survive if the temperature inside my greenhouse feels much hotter than outside?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baahi shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ waa fe kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: Crops can only handle short periods of high heat. If it stays too hot inside, the plants will stop producing, so you must let outside air in to balance the heat.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ atsu dɔlɛ ni naa wa he nii yɛ be kukuoo mli pɛ kɛji edɔ tsɔ lolo yɛ emli. Tso lɛ baakpa yibiiwoo. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ oha kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ abote mli koni hulutsoo lɛ afee ekome.

english: What does it mean when an extension worker tells me a crop variety is 'hardy'?
ga: Kɛji akɛ extension nitsulɔ ko kɛɛ mi akɛ tso henɔ ko ‘wa’ lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ?

english: A 'hardy' crop variety is strong and tough, meaning it has been bred to withstand difficult conditions like extreme heat, slight drought, or local diseases better than normal crops.
ga: hardy’ tsei srɔtoi lɛ wa ni amɛhe wa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ atsɔse lɛ koni enyɛ edamɔ shihilɛi ni mli wawai tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ ni baaa shi lɛ anaa. loo maŋ lɛ mli helai ni hi fe tsei fɛɛ

english: How do I choose the best pepper seeds to plant if I want to grow them under cover?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala pepper dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu kɛji miisumɔ ni madu yɛ nɔ ko shishi?

english: Select pepper seeds specifically labeled as heat-tolerant and suited for protected farming, as these varieties handle warm, enclosed environments much better.
ga: Halamɔ pepper dumɔwui ni aŋmala nɔ akɛ enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ dɔlɛ naa ni ehi kɛha okwaayeli ni abuɔ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ tsei srɔtoi nɛɛ tsuɔ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni afo he lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: Can sweet bell peppers handle the hot weather here in Ghana?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsu kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ he nii?

english: Sweet peppers prefer moderate warmth, but if you choose hardy, heat-tolerant varieties and manage the temperature properly, they can thrive and yield very well in Ghana.
ga: Bell peppers sumɔɔ hulutsoo ni fa fioo. Shi kɛji akɛ ohala nɔ ni wa, ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ dɔlɛ naa, ni okwɛɔ dɔlɛ mli jogbaŋŋ pɛ. Bell peppers kwɛ̃ɔ ni ewoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ Ghana.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because their leaves burn easily under full sun. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to young cocoa creates a living canopy that blocks harsh sunlight and traps soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ Cocoa tsei lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ haaa hulu la ni naa wa lɛ aná hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. Adding organic compost or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant make food and regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛná su ni hi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward to catch maximum sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, which prevents leaf diseases and helps the plant produce larger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji.

english: Does it matter which direction I push cassava stem cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Kɛji oodu lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ odu ŋmei ni afo lɛ?

english: Yes, cassava stems must be planted with the buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down causes the new sprouts to struggle to reach the surface, resulting in weak growth and fewer tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Dumɔwui heei ni aduɔ lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa edalɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why do people recommend planting groundnuts on the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil and feeds neighboring heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa niyenii haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my maize leaves overnight?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ nyɔɔŋ kome

english: Ragged holes inside the central leaves of maize plants are usually caused by Fall Armyworms, a common caterpillar pest in Ghana that feeds on young growing shoots if not managed early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ naa yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist right after light rain, but avoid applying it right before a heavy rainstorm or during dry spells when plants cannot absorb it.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ he ni okɛbaatsu nii dani nugbɔ anɛ waa loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after I clear my plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit naturally in the soil and are adapted to sprout instantly when sunlight hits cleared land, whereas domestic crop seeds take longer to germinate and establish roots.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji hulu la lɛ shɛ he ni agbele lɛ nɔ pɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shia dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the dirt each year and creates a permanent home for soil pests that specialize in attacking that specific plant.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni efee shia ni baahi shi daa aha shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni he esa waa yɛ nakai tso pɔtɛɛ lɛ tutuamɔ mli lɛ.

english: How do I know if my harvested maize grains are dry enough to put into storage bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-corn kernel ni akpa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛwo kotoku mli ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe?

english: Grains are properly dry for storage when they are hard enough to crack cleanly between your teeth rather than denting, showing that moisture levels are low enough to prevent mold and rot.
ga: Agbiɔ ŋmaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni akɛto be mli ni ewa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ eshwa onyanyɔji ateŋ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha ŋmeii aba lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii akafite.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient in the soil. It can also happen when heavy rains flood the field and waterlog the plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi ŋmɔji amli ni eha tsei ashishifãi lɛ nu.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool in hot sun, holds water in the soil longer, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Ha nu ahi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃

english: Why is it risky to sow my maize seeds immediately after the very first rainy day of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long hot dry spell. If you plant too early, the seeds will sprout and then dry up and die in the hot soil before the main rainy season starts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ waa nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before the pods start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop extra flowers if they don't have enough water or nutrients, or if there aren't enough tiny insects, like midges, present in the farm to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Cacao tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔi krokomɛi kɛji nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch full sunlight so the leaves can make energy, which helps the yam tuber grow large underground while keeping leaves off the damp, diseased ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, baai baanyɛ afee hewalɛ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai yɔɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I have to cut away some of the small shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso lɛ shishi lɛ he

english: Too many small shoots suck food and water away from the main stem. Cutting them off lets the plant concentrate its energy on producing larger bunches of fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ shishi bibii babaoo tsɔ baaŋɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he. Tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa yibii wuji ni ewoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: What makes the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips that suck the juices from young leaves, or by a virus carried into your field by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛyaa oŋmɔji amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and rotting while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering during warm weather.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad practice for me to plant maize in the exact same field every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli be fɛɛ be lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ abuɔ be mli nifeemɔ akɛ eji nifeemɔ gbonyo.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests and soil diseases that feed on maize to multiply in that field.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni sũ mli kooloi kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ babaoo yɛ nakai ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell when my cassava roots are fully ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves start to turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the main stem begins to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Officer, why are the leaves on my maize farm turning yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Ofisa Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the crop is hungry for Nitrogen, an essential nutrient for growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted compost around the base will help the leaves turn dark green and healthy again.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ abɔle tso lɛ he. Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's natural defense to save water during high heat. By curling up, the leaf reduces water loss, but if leaves stay rolled in the cool early morning, it means the crops are severely dehydrated and urgently need water.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni ekɛbu nu he yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ abɔle baai lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe lolo yɛ hulutsoo be mli leebi maŋkpa lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu efo ŋmɔshi nibii amli waa ni nu he miihia amɛ oya.

english: What causes tiny holes to appear all over my cabbage leaves, and how does it hurt the crop?
ga: Mɛni haa bu bibioo lɛ feɔ? ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ kaabe baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by caterpillars feeding on them. When leaves are damaged, the plant cannot properly capture sunlight to make its food, which stops the cabbage from forming a large, solid head.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ baa. Kɛji baai lɛ fite lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ amɔmɔ hulu la ni amɛkɛfee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haaa cabbage lɛ yitsei wuji ni wa lɛ adara.

english: Cocoa trees shed their flowers when they suffer from water stress, when insect pests like mirids attack them, or when the soil lacks nutrients. Managing shade properly and controlling insect pests helps the flowers stay on the tree and mature into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji nu he haomɔ miipiŋ amɛ. Beni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Mirids lɛ tutuaa kookoo tsei loo be mli ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shade nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers instead of growing peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi shi moŋ ni eeekwɛ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when soil becomes too dry, when temperatures get too high, or if there is an excess of nitrogen fertilizer. Mulching the soil and keeping it evenly moist helps the plant keep its flowers to produce fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nitrogen fertilizer fa tsɔ Mulching kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ daa lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekwɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: How do I know when my stored yam setts are ready to be planted in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmeii ni ato lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Yam setts are ready to plant when small buds, known as 'eyes', begin to sprout on the tubers in storage. Planting them when these sprouts appear ensures the crop emerges quickly and reliably once put into the soil.
ga: Sweet potato kui lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ beni fɔfɔi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘buds’ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ anɔ lɛ. Dumɔ beni nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii aba oya ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛ akɛfata shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long or when soil fungi attack. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess rainwater to drain away, keeping the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu bua amɛhe naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ loo kɛ́ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutua amɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli.

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and weak stems that struggle under the heavy weight of large bunches, especially during strong winds. Supporting the main stem with strong wooden or bamboo stakes keeps the plant upright until harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ jwɛi wuji ni tsii lɛ ashishi. Titri lɛ, yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tso loo ŋmei tso ni wa fi tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: If I apply fertilizer right after planting, why does it seem to make weeds grow faster than my crop?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu lɛ Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Weeds have stronger root systems and grow faster than young crops, so they quickly steal the fertilizer intended for your plants. You must always clear all weeds from around your crops before applying any fertilizer.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni amɛdaraa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ otsei lɛ amli lɛ oya. Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi fɛɛ kɛjɛ onibii amli dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Can I plant cowpeas in the same farm with my maize, or will they compete and spoil my crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ? Aloo amɛkɛ amɛhe baatswa akaŋ ni amɛfite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Planting cowpeas with maize is actually beneficial because cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. This enriches the ground and helps the maize grow better while giving you two harvests from the same plot.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he diɛŋtsɛ ejaakɛ tsina ŋmãa lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Why do my maize crops need a different type of fertilizer than my cassava crops if they are growing in the same soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ srɔto fe mi ŋmãa tso lɛ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Even though all crops draw food from the ground using their roots, different plants 'eat' differently. Maize is a heavy feeder that requires high nitrogen to grow tall and produce grain, while root crops like cassava need more potassium to build large, starchy tubers underneath the soil.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi anɔ moŋ, Shi esoro bɔ ni tso fɛɛ tso ‘yeɔ’ nii ehaa. Abɛi ji niyenii ni tsii ni biɔ nitrogen babaoo koni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo dumɔwui. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei yɔɔ mli lɛ he miihia potassium babaoo koni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Do all the crops on my farm grow using the same basic internal process?
ga: Ani akɛ shishijee mligbɛ gbɛjianɔtoo kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, every crop uses the same basic internal system. They all use sunlight, water, and gases from the air to manufacture their own food. While their external shapes and nutrient needs differ, their internal engine works the same way.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ kɛ shishijee mligbɛ gbɛjianɔtoo kome tsuɔ nii. Amɛ fɛɛ amɛkɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii. Eyɛ mli akɛ amɛhefɛo kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ yɛ srɔtoi moŋ, Shi mligbɛ tsɔne lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ.

english: Why do my plant roots need air in the soil when the leaves are already out in the open air?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ he hiaa shikpɔŋ kɔɔyɔɔ be mli ni amɛhe ehiaaa lɛ? He ni baai lɛ efo kɛtee kɔɔyɔɔ mli momo lɛ?

english: Plant roots are alive and need to breathe oxygen from tiny spaces in the soil just like humans need air. If the soil is too tightly packed or waterlogged, trapped gases cannot exchange, causing the roots to drown and rot.
ga: Tsei ashishifãi yɛ wala mli ni ehe miihia ni amɛmu kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ jɛɔ hei bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, taakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa adesai lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ atsake Trapped gases. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why does my compost heap get warm and produce gas before I put it on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-compost pile lɛ mli edɔɔ ni gas yɔɔ mli dani mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tiny unseen organisms inside the compost pile actively break down leaves and manure. As they eat and digest this matter, their natural bodily processes generate heat and gases, transforming the waste into rich plant food.
ga: nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli Anaaa amɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ mli, ni ekɛ ekãa kpataa baai kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahiɛ. Beni amɛyeɔ ni amɛyeɔ enɛ lɛ Amɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɔmɔtsoŋ nifeemɔi lɛ feɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ. kɛ jwɛi ni atsakeɔ awoɔ tsei aniyenii babaoo mli

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up and droop during the hottest hours of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: In extreme heat, plant leaves lose moisture quickly. Curling up helps the plant reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, conserving internal water until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ, tso lɛ baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya. Curling yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ ehiɛ lɛ baa shi. Ehaa nu hiɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do crops planted under big shade trees produce smaller yields even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ wooo yibii fioo ko pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Crops require direct sunlight to drive their internal food-making system. Without enough light, the plant cannot process nutrients efficiently, resulting in weak growth and smaller harvests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛtsu amɛmli niyenii feemɔ gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ ahe nii. Kɛji la ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ atsu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why do my green plantains ripen much faster when I keep them stored together in a closed sack?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains eŋɔli lɛ shwereɔ oya kwraa kɛ́ mikɛto kotoku ko ni aŋã mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: As plantains mature, they naturally release a invisible ripening gas. Keeping them in a closed space traps this gas, which signals all the fruits in the bundle to soften and turn yellow together.
ga: Kɛji akɛ plantains lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Amɛjieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni anaaa ni akɛhooɔ nii lɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ́ okɛto he ko ni afo he lɛ, ebaamɔ gas nɛɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ kuu lɛ mli lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli.

english: Why is it necessary to dry my harvested cocoa beans in the heat of the sun before storing them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbi kookoo yibii ni akpa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani akɛto lɛ?

english: Sun heat evaporates the excess water trapped inside fresh beans. Removing this moisture stops mold from growing and allows essential natural processes inside the bean to lock in flavor.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine ni ekpɛtɛ kɔfe yibii heei lɛ amli lɛ feɔ la. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ dalɛ kpaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli ŋɔɔ.

english: Why does one variety of maize grow much faster than another variety planted on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔ kome daa oya fe ŋmãa kroko ni adu yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Different varieties carry different internal instructions inherited from their parent seeds. Some are bred to process food and mature quickly to escape drought, while others take more time to build larger stalks.
ga: Henɔi srɔtoi yɛ mligbɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi srɔtoi ni anáa kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ seshi lɛ mli. Akwɛɔ kooloi srɔtoi komɛi koni amɛtsu niyenii he nii ni amɛdara oya koni amɛjo hɔmɔ naa foi. yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ be babaoo dani amɛfeɔ tsei wuji.

english: Why do dry seeds need moist, warm soil to wake up and start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ he hiaa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ koni amɛte shi ni amɛbɔi dalɛ?

english: Warmth and moisture trigger the sleeping seed's internal engine. Water softens the seed coat and dissolves stored energy inside, allowing the young plant to break out and push through the soil.
ga: Dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ haa dumɔwu ni ewɔ lɛ mli tsɔnei lɛ tsuɔ nii. Nu haa dumɔwui lɛ ahe tsɔne lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa hewalɛ ni ato yɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ fãa ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How many bags of maize can I expect to harvest from one acre of land in Ghana?
ga: Abele kotokui enyiɛ manyɛ makpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre kome nɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: Yields depend on seed quality, weather, and soil care. With good hybrid seeds, timely planting, and proper fertilizer use, a farmer in Ghana can harvest between 15 to 25 bags (50kg each) of maize per acre instead of just 3 to 5 bags from local seeds.
ga: Yibiiwoo damɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ. kɛ dumɔwui kpakpai ni akɛfee ekome Dumɔ yɛ be ni sa mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ Okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ baanyɛ akpa ŋmãa kotokui 15 kɛyashi 25 (kg 50 eko fɛɛ eko) yɛ acre kome mli, yɛ ŋmãa kotokui 3 kɛyashi 5 pɛ ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui amli lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why does my neighbor get more bags of harvest than I do when we planted the same crop in the same village?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ nine shɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ kotokui babaoo nɔ fe mi beni wɔduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komekomei yɛ akrowa kome mli lɛ?

english: Harvest amounts differ because of seed quality, planting depth, weed management, fertilizer timing, and soil health. Using certified seeds and clearing weeds early gives the crop more nutrients to produce more bags.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa lɛ ayibɔ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahewɔ. dumɔ mli jwɛi ahe nitsumɔ Be ni akɛbaatsu nii kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ mra lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ aná niyenii babaoo koni ekɛwo baagi babaoo.

english: Should I plant corn, rice, or beans on my land if I want a reliable harvest for food and income?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo ŋmãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ? Kɛji miisumɔ ni makpa nii kɛha niyenii kɛ shika ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ

english: Maize is a strong daily staple with a constant local market, beans grow fast and naturally improve soil health, and rice grows best in low swampy ground. Choosing depends on whether your soil stays wet or dry and what buyers in your area demand.
ga: Abɛi ji daa gbi niyenii ni mli wa ni maŋ lɛ jarayeli hei lɛ yɛ be fɛɛ be. Beans lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ni ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni ŋmeii yɔɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni obaahala lɛ damɔ kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efɔ lolo loo egbi. Ni mɛni mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ taoɔ?

english: Why does my rice crop need so much more water to grow compared to my corn or beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa mi ŋmãa tso lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ fe ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally thrive in waterlogged soil where other crops would drown, because rice stems have air passageways that carry oxygen down to their roots even when underwater.
ga: Omɔ tsei daa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nibii krokomɛi ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbo ejaakɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu shishi po.

english: Why do elders say planting beans on my farm will help my next corn crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nuumo lɛ kɛɛ akɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua miŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Beans are legumes, meaning their roots pull natural food (nitrogen) out of the air and put it back into the soil. When the bean plants die, they leave richer ground for the next maize crop.
ga: Beans ji ŋmeii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ gbalaa niyenii (nitrogen) kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ ŋmei tso lɛ gbo lɛ Ebaashi shikpɔŋ ni baa nii babaoo hu kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Can I plant corn and beans together on the same piece of land, or will one crop ruin the other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ? Aloo ŋmɔshi nibii kome baafite ekroko?

english: You can plant them together; this is called intercropping. The tall corn stalks give light support to climbing bean vines, while the beans feed nutrients into the soil that help the corn grow strong.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ afee ekome. Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli. Abɛi tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaaa ŋmei tsei lɛ fioo ko pɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii haa niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni edaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know the right market price per bag for my crops so I do not sell at a loss?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male jara ni sa kɛha kotoku kome kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Bɔni afee ni mikahɔ̃ɔ kɛ shika ni mifite?

english: Market prices change based on harvest season and regional demand. Checking with local agricultural extension officers, farming groups, or market queen mothers before selling helps you calculate your total costs and set a profitable price per bag.
ga: Guɔyeli jara tsakeɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be kɛ kpokpaa nɔ taomɔ naa. Kwɛmɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔ kuu Loo jarayeli he hiɛnyiɛlɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ baaye abua bo ni obu shika fɛɛ ni okɛbaahe lɛ he akɔntaa ni okɛ jara ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he ato baagi kome he.

english: How do I know when my maize crop is fully mature and ready to harvest into bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋma lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa ni akɛwo kotoku mli?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the outer husks turn completely brown and dry, and the grains become hard enough that pressing them with your thumbnail leaves no dent.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa ni egbi. Ni dumɔwui lɛ wa bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ okɛ onineshi tsɔne lɛ anyɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛkashi ŋmeii komɛi.

english: How can I stop insects from destroying my bagged corn and rice while waiting for market prices to rise?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi ni fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa kotokui lɛ anaa yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni jara nɔ jara aya hiɛ lɛ?

english: Dry your grains until they are completely hard, then store them in airtight hermetic bags. These bags suffocate insects and prevent mold from spoiling your harvest while you wait for better prices.
ga: Gbimɔ dumɔwui lɛ aahu kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛwo vacuum kotoku mli. Nɛkɛ kotokui nɛɛ haa kooloi bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa ŋmeii afite onibii lɛ yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How can I have assurance that the money I spend on seeds will actually feed my family and leave extra to sell?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ shika ni mifiteɔ yɛ dumɔwui ahe lɛ baaha miweku lɛ niyenii diɛŋtsɛ ni eshwɛ kɛha jarayeli krokomɛi?

english: Assurance comes from reducing risks: buy certified disease-resistant seeds, plant right when the rainy season starts, protect your crops from weeds early, and arrange buyers or storage before harvest time.
ga: Nɔmimaa jɛɔ oshara ni baa shi lɛ mli: Hemɔ dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ. Dumɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli. Buu onibii ahe kɛjɛ jwɛi ahe mra. ni asaa mɛi ni baahe loo ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe lɛ dani kpamɔ be lɛ aba

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and dropping during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sun. Planting fast-growing food crops like plantains alongside your cocoa creates shade and keeps the air cool, protecting the young trees until they grow stronger.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Niyenii nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ.

english: Why is my maize turning pale yellow instead of dark green after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil food. Adding fertilizer or well-rotted manure gives the plants the nutrients they need to produce green leaves and big cobs.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do I know if I planted my cassava stems too close together in my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: If cassava is planted too close, the leaves block sunlight from reaching each other and the roots compete for space. The plants will grow tall and thin, producing small tubers instead of thick, healthy ones.
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmei ni obɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. ni shishifãi lɛ baatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná he ko Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni ebaafee bibioo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ enɛ mli baa ji yitso bibioo yɛ yitso ni mli wa ni mli wa najiaŋ.

english: Why do my small maize plants have ragged holes eaten into their young leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tso bibioo lɛ ehiɛ bu ni egbɛ eshwa ni eyeɔ ebaa bibii lɛ?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are usually caused by caterpillars like Fall Armyworm that hide in the center of the plant. Checking your farm early and using recommended controls prevents them from destroying the growing tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa ŋmeii bibii amli. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baatsi ŋmɔ lɛ naa koni ekafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts on my farm before planting maize next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmei afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and leave it in the soil through their roots. When you harvest groundnuts, the soil becomes richer, helping your next crop grow faster without buying extra fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmli ni amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛshiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji okpa ŋmeii lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ. Ye obua onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ oya ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up tight like tubes during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ jwɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in afternoon heat is a plant's way of saving water. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun so water does not dry out of the leaves too fast.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ nu he. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. koni nu lɛ akagbi oya tsɔ

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to stay small even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibioo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa po lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast growing and steal nutrients, space, and water directly from the roots of your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures that your main crop gets all the food and water from the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, he ko, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii titri lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I trim off extra shoots from my mature cocoa trees when I want more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso ni eda lɛ mli ŋmeii krokomɛi be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo he miihia mi lɛ?

english: Removing unwanted shoots and dead branches lets air flow through the tree and allows sunlight to reach the trunk. This reduces fungal diseases like black pod and helps the tree focus its energy on growing pods.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsei niji ni ataooo lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli ni ehaa hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ maa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting inside the wet soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When soil stays soaked in standing water for too long, plant roots drown because they cannot get air. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess rainwater drain away so tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ wo nu ni ekã shi mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: How can I apply fertilizer to my crops so that heavy rain does not wash it away?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie amɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist right after rain, rather than right before a heavy storm. Digging a small ring or hole near the plant root, placing the fertilizer inside, and covering it with soil protects it from being washed off.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛbaatsu nii dani ahum ni naa wa aba. Afomɔ ŋwɛi ŋta loo bu bibioo ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ, ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ni akɛ sũ aha nɔ koni ekaho.

english: Why do my maize plants produce smaller cobs when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii beni midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. Proper spacing gives each maize plant enough resources to grow strong and produce large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa he lɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmãa wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the green color and improves growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes and powdery waste inside the center leaves of my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ amli bu kɛ sũ ni etse lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: This is damage caused by fall armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the leaves. Identifying them early allows you to apply safe remedies or treatments before they destroy the growing plant tip.
ga: Enɛ ji nɔ ni ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ amli lɛ fiteɔ. Amɛyoomɔ mra Enɛ haa okɛ tsofai loo tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tsuɔ nii dani amɛfiteɔ tsei ni miida lɛ ashishifãi.

english: Why does it matter which way I stick my cassava stem cuttings into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bɔ ni mikɛ mi-cassava lɛ duɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he hiaa lɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava stems have small buds that point upward toward the sky. If you plant the stem upside down, the plant wastes energy bending its new shoots to grow upward, leading to weak stem growth and fewer tubers underground.
ga: Kasava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ Tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ŋmeii heei shwieɔ shi koni ekwɛ̃. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi dalɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ hu faaa.

english: Yam vines produce tubers underground by collecting sunlight through their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they catch maximum sunlight and stay clean from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛbuaa naa kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. ni eha ehe atse kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and die when planted in an open field without plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni plantains bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting plantains alongside them provides living shade umbrellas that cool the air and trap moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ lɛ naa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and remaining very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee bibioo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites living under the leaves. Treating these pests early stops them from stunting the plant and spreading plant diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Tsɔɔmɔ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkagbɛ tsei ahe helai amɛshwã.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress from irregular watering or extreme weather heat. Keeping the soil evenly moist throughout the flowering period helps the flowers set healthy fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ afeemɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on my plot after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil, but legumes like groundnuts and beans absorb nitrogen from the air and put it back into the earth. Rotating them restores soil fertility naturally for your next crop.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ otsake amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aba ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Covering bare soil with dry leaves or grass acts like a blanket that shades the ground. This practice traps moisture in the soil longer and prevents harsh sunlight from drying out plant roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa koni ekaha tsei shishifãi lɛ agbi

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is essential for leafy growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost early in the growing season helps the plant regain its bright green color and produce larger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ wo mli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji ni mli tse ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep dropping off before growing into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often fall off when the plant suffers from extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and adding mulch around the roots helps stabilize moisture and keeps flowers attached.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i mli ni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ he.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines off the ground using bamboo tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ ŋmei tsei kakadaji atsu nii ni mikɛjie mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need full sunlight to produce energy for their underground tubers. Lifting vines onto stakes keeps the leaves exposed to sunlight, prevents leaves from rotting on damp ground, and yields much larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu ni fa babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛtee tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ nɔ. ni enine shɛ yam ko ni da fe no kwraa nɔ

english: Why should I spread dry grass or leaves on the soil around my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ashwie shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Covering soil with dry organic matter, called mulching, protects the ground from the harsh Ghanaian sun. It traps moisture in the soil, lowers soil temperature, and prevents weeds from taking light and nutrients away from your cocoa.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ Ghana hulu ni naa wa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i baa shi ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ kookoo lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I apply chemical fertilizer onto my crops when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ tsuɔ nii be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve so crop roots can safely absorb the nutrients. Applying chemical fertilizer to bone-dry soil can scorch crop roots and waste expensive nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wu yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite niyenii mli nibii ni jara wa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the soil when we get heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water sitting in heavy soil starves cassava roots of oxygen, allowing fungal diseases to rot the tubers. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds helps excess rainwater drain away from the root zone.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ lɛ baaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ yibii lɛ baanyɛ akpɔ̃. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by microscopic pests like mites or aphids feeding on sap from the undersides of leaves. Spraying with neem water or insecticidal soap helps control these pests so leaves can expand normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ neem nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ koni baai lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are black spots spreading across the pods of my cocoa trees during the rainy period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black spots on cocoa pods are caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, humid conditions. Pruning excess branches lets sunlight and breeze dry out the trees, which stops the fungal spores from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ cocoa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aha tso lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why should I plant plantains next to my newly transplanted cocoa saplings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tso ni adu ehee lɛ masɛi?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and easily burnt by full sun. Fast-growing plantain trees act as natural umbrellas, shading young cocoa plants and keeping the microclimate humid until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni hulu lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni oha kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko ahi mli kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant groundnuts in the same field as my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil. Mixing groundnuts with maize improves soil fertility for the maize without exhausting the soil.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei futu mli lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ kɛha ŋmei ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteee.

english: Why are my cocoa trees not producing as many pods as they used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ wooo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo tamɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age, or if the soil loses its natural food, yields decrease. Low production is usually caused by lack of soil nutrients, pest damage, overgrown shade trees blocking light, or unpruned branches wasting the tree's energy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ eda loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ fite lɛ Nibii ni ewoɔ lɛ baa shi. Bei pii lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni haa yibiiwoo baa shi. Nibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ Tsei lɛ edara fe nine aahu akɛ amɛtsiɔ la lɛ naa. Aloo niji ni afolɔɔɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crop turn yellow and dry up during the sunny months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nyɔji ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ amli lɛ?
