english: Yellowing and drying leaves mean the plant is stressed. This happens when there is not enough water in the soil, too much direct hot sunlight, or a lack of key nutrients like nitrogen in the ground.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Hulu la ni mli edɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fa babaoo tsɔ. aloo niyenii mli nibii titrii tamɔ nitrogen ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why do flowers fall off my crops before turning into real fruits or pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani amɛfeɔ aduawai loo ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or insect pests. It can also happen if beneficial insects like midges or bees are not present to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ miihao amɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ bɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to spray chemical medicine on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Chemicals work best when sprayed early in the morning or late in the afternoon when it is cool and not rainy. Spraying right before rainy season insect outbreaks start helps protect the crop before damage occurs.
ga: Tsofai lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛshwie nɔ leebi loo shwane mli be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ dani ŋmeii baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani efiteɔ.

english: No, using too much fertilizer can burn the plant's roots and kill the crop. Crops only need a specific amount of food at a time, so applying extra damages the soil and wastes your money.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ niyenii abɔ ko yɛ be kome mli, ni no haa nɔ ni fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yaa hiɛ ni efiteɔ oshika.

english: Why does my land stop growing good crops after farming on it for many years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ekpa ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai akwɛmɔ yɛ afii babaoo ni mikɛtsu nii yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Every time crops grow and produce food, they pull nutrients out of the earth. If you do not put food back into the soil using compost, manure, or fertilizer, the ground becomes weak and tired.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni tsei baakwɛ̃ ni amɛwo niyenii Ebaajie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsuuu nii ekoŋŋ kɛfataaa sũ lɛ he lɛ, sũ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my small cocoa pods turn black and die before they get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo dani eda lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet, overly shady, and humid conditions. Pruning excess branches to let air and sunlight in helps stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, hulutsoo, kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la abote mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do insects attack my farm more during certain times of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Insects multiply fast when warm weather and fresh crop leaves appear together. rainy season changes create moist conditions that help insect eggs hatch in large numbers.
ga: Kplukai babaoo yaa hiɛ oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni tsei ahe baai heei je kpo yɛ he kome. Tsakemɔ ni baa nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni yeɔ ebuaa kooloi bibii babaoo ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need shade trees planted next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have soft leaves and delicate roots that easily burn under full, hot sun. Shade trees act as living umbrellas to protect them and keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni hiɛ ka koni ebu amɛhe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops struggle even when I give them fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ amɛmli moŋ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer faster than your crops can. Clearing weeds regularly ensures your plants get all the food you put in the soil.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi lɛ shwie shi daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni okɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do I know if my harvested rice or maize is dry enough to put into bags for long storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa loo mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛwo kotoku mli koni akɛto be kakadaŋŋ?

english: You can test grain dryness by biting a grain or using the salt test in a glass jar. If the grain cracks loudly between your teeth without feeling soft, or if salt doesn't stick to the inside of the jar, the grain is dry enough to bag without rotting or molding.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka bɔ ni ŋmaa lɛ egbi ha lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmaa lɛ ni oootsɔ mli loo okɛ ŋmei kaa ni yɔɔ glase tsinsii mli lɛ atsu nii lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ŋmaa lɛ mli gbala waa yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ ni enuuu he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo Aloo kɛji ŋmei lɛ emɔɔɔ tɔ lɛ mli. Ŋmãa lɛ baagbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ awo kotoku mli ni efiteee loo efoŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I store my bags of harvested grain directly on the bare floor inside my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ kotokui toɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ yɛ tsu lɛ mli lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Bare concrete or dirt floors pull moisture up from the ground into the bottom of the bags, which causes dampness, mold, and rot. Always place your bags on raised wooden pallets off the ground and away from walls to allow air to circulate.
ga: Kɔnkrit loo muji ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa kotoku lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ obaagi lɛ awo tsei ni awó nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ gbogboi ahe koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli.

english: What causes small black beetles to appear inside my bagged grains even when the bags are tied tightly?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii diji bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi dumɔwui ni awo amɛ kotoku mli lɛ amli eyɛ mli akɛ akɛ kotokui lɛ ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: These insects are weevils, and their tiny eggs were likely already laid inside the grains while they were still in the field or drying. To prevent them, dry your grains thoroughly in the sun and store them in sealed hermetic (airtight) bags that suffocate insect pests.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii, ni eeenyɛ efee akɛ amɛwuji bibii lɛ wo dumɔwui lɛ amli beni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo loo amɛmiigbi lɛ. Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi Ha egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni no sɛɛ lɛ okɛto vacuum (vacuum) kotoku ko ni atsĩ naa mli, ni baaha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akagbo.

english: Is it safe to feed my farm animals with grain that has turned moldy or was treated with storage chemicals?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ maha miŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ ŋmaa ni mli ewo muji loo akɛ tsofai ewo mli yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: No, moldy grain contains invisible toxins that cause severe illness or death in animals, and chemical storage powders are poisonous to livestock. Always keep treated seeds and spoiled crops away from animal feed.
ga: Dabi, tsofai fɔji ni anaaa ni kɛ hela ni naa wa loo gbele baa kooloi anɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ dumɔwui amli. ni tsofa ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli powda lɛ ji tsofa fɔŋ kɛha kooloi. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, ha dumɔwui ni atsa amɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite lɛ ahi he ko kɛjɛ kooloi aniyenii he.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow at the tips and drying up from the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ ni amɛmiigbi kɛmiijɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the leaf tip and spreads down the middle of lower leaves is a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help the plants turn green and produce healthy ears.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anaagbɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa baa lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni eha toi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young rice plants turn yellow and stop growing when water sits too deep in the field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Although rice needs water, young roots still need air to breathe. When water is too deep for days, the roots drown and turn black, preventing the plant from absorbing nutrients, which turns the leaves yellow.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nu he miihia ŋmãa moŋ Shi shishifãi bibii lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ lolo koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu lɛ mli kwɔ tsɔ gbii babaoo Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaatsɔ ediŋŋ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants shed all their leaves during the dry season, and does it mean the crop is dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbo?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry periods as a self-defense mechanism to save water and survive heat. The roots under the ground remain healthy and stored with starch, and new leaves will sprout quickly once rain falls.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaai lɛ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli akɛ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe koni ekɛbu nu he ni enyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ naa. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ yaa nɔ ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛbuaa ŋmɔtɔ naa. Ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ.

english: Can I plant the rice or maize grains I bought from the local market for cooking on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ahe kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ jara nɔ koni mikɛho yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Grains sold for food at the market may not grow well because they might be old, damaged, or poor varieties suited only for eating. It is best to plant certified seeds from an accredited seller or extension officer to ensure high germination and a good harvest.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmaa ni ahɔ̃ɔ akɛ niyenii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ edaŋ jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ekolɛ egbɔ, efite loo esaaa akɛ ayeɔ kɛkɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ kɛjɛ jarayelɔi loo mɛi ni kwɛɔ nɔ lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkpa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it difficult to grow wheat successfully in southern Ghana compared to crops like maize or cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ abaadu ŋmaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Wheat requires cool temperatures and dry weather to form grain heads, whereas southern Ghana is warm and humid. High humidity causes fungal diseases on wheat, which is why tropical crops like maize and cassava perform much better in our climate.
ga: Ŋmaa he miihia hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi koni ekɛfee dumɔwui ayitsei. yɛ be mli ni Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ mli edɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa ŋmaa mli. Nɔ ni haa tropical ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kwraa yɛ wɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster than my crop seedlings right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that are naturally adapted to steal water, sunlight, and plant food from the soil very aggressively. Clearing weeds early in the first four weeks gives your crops the head start they need to establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni atsake amɛ koni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ aju nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ lɛ haa onibii lɛ feɔ klalo mra koni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa.

english: What happens if I bury my maize seeds too deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Planting seeds too deep traps them under heavy soil. The seed exhausts all its stored energy trying to push through the heavy dirt and dies before reaching the sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ baamɔmɔ amɛ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ nɔ ni amɛgboi dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Why are my young crop shoots failing to break through the ground after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain followed by strong sun bakes the top layer of soil into a hard crust. The tender shoots get trapped underneath and cannot break through unless the hard layer is gently loosened.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni hulu la ni naa wa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ batsɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa. Tsobii bibii lɛ kpɛtɛɔ shishigbɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛbote mli ja ajie fã ni wa lɛ mli blɛoo.

english: Why do I need to plow my field thoroughly before planting instead of just digging small holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo ŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani madu nii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mafo bu bibioo ko lɛ?

english: Plowing loosens hard, compacted soil, creating soft spaces that allow young roots to push deep down easily and absorb food and water without getting blocked.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa gbɛ ko baa ni haa shishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsiɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ mlɛo. ni ekɛ niyenii kɛ nu shwieɔ shi ni nɔ ko tsiii enaa

english: How deep do I need to dig mounds for my yam setts to grow properly?
ga: Te ehe hiaa ni mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ koni mi-sweet potato lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yams need deep, soft soil to expand. Making high, soft mounds gives the growing tuber room to stretch downward easily without hitting hard ground that restricts its growth.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni egbɛ eshwa. Gɔŋ kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni afee lɛ haa bulbs ni miida lɛ tsu lɛ yaa shishi oya ni enaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni tsiɔ dalɛ naa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants turn yellow when water stays on my land for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni nu ehi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Roots need air to breathe. When water sits on the field for too long, it smothers the roots underground, preventing them from taking up nutrients and causing the plant to turn yellow.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baaho kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why are the roots of my tomato plants rotting under the wet soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When water gets trapped around plant roots without proper drainage, soil diseases thrive and destroy the soft root tissues, causing the roots to decay.
ga: Kɛ nu ebɔle tso shishifãi ahe ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ Helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ daa ni amɛfiteɔ shishifãi bibii lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why is my cocoa seedling growing so slowly above the ground during its first few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ miida blɛoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: In its early stages, a young cocoa plant focuses its strength on pushing roots deep into the earth to anchor itself and find moisture before growing large leaves above.
ga: Yɛ shishijee mli lɛ, cacao tsei bibii maa amɛhewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi ni amɛtsiɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ mi koni amɛma amɛhe shi ni amɛna ŋmɔtɔ dani amɛduɔ baai wuji yɛ nɔ.

english: What will happen if I plant my pepper crops too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: Planting too close forces the roots to fight for limited space and food underground, leaving all the plants weak and unable to reach their full strength.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ shishifãi lɛ atswa akaŋ koni amɛná shikpɔŋ shishi he ko ni faaa kɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ etsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my young crops with dry leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle tsei bibii ahe lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves keeps the soil cool and moist, preventing the sun from baking the dirt hard and protecting delicate young roots near the surface.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Etsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekaha muji lɛ mli awa. ni ebuɔ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Should I put all my fertilizer on my crops at once when I start planting?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli kɛji mibɔi amɛdumɔ pɛ?

english: Young plants have small roots that cannot handle too much fertilizer at once. Feeding crops gradually as they grow allows them to absorb nutrients safely without burning their roots.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii. Enyɛŋ eba akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baawo mli shikome. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ niyenii fiofio be mli ni edaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii shweshweeshwe ni eshãaa shishifãi lɛ.

english: Yellowing of the lower leaves usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential food for plant growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizers like Urea or NPK around the roots at the right time helps the leaves stay dark green and produce bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK wo shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛwo ŋmɔtɔi wuji.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu tsina loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. Planting them alongside maize improves soil fertility, reduces the need for expensive chemical fertilizers, and gives you two crops from one piece of land.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛkɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Ehaa ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ atsu nii, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ jɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under the strong sun. Plantains grow very quickly and have broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa shade and protecting soil moisture during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo bibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my maize seeds very close together?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: No, planting too close makes the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin stalks and tiny cobs. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow strong and yield large cobs.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hewalɛ baawo ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds after the first rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until two or three heavy rains have thoroughly soaked the soil deep down. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die if a dry week follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji hɔmɔ otsii babaoo nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Curled leaves with yellow patches are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. To prevent this, always plant disease-resistant cassava stem varieties recommended by officers.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Bɔni afee ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa Be fɛɛ be lɛ, dumɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ taakɛ onukpai lɛ etsɔɔ lɛ.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving brown dirt in the center?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the tender inner leaves of young maize. Inspecting your farm early and spraying recommended insecticides or neem leaf extracts will stop them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem baa mli nu lɛ afɔ nɔ. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to irregular watering, extreme heat, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Watering your plants consistently at the base and adding well-rotted manure helps the flowers stay attached and turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ shishi daa ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my vegetable plants with dried grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-vegetable tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, traps moisture in the soil so you water less, keeps the ground cool, prevents weeds from growing, and adds organic manure as it rots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi haa Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli shii abɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ Ni ekɛ organic fertilizer fataa he be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: How can I keep insects from destroying my dried maize after I harvest it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite mi-ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Insects like weevils attack grain that still has moisture or is stored loosely. Drying your maize until it is fully hard and storing it in airtight PICS bags suffocates insects and keeps your harvest safe for months without chemical dusts.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii tutuaa dumɔwui ni mli edɔ lolo loo ni akɛto he ko ni bɛ ŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ ogbala o-corn lɛ mli kɛyashi ebaawa kwraa ni okɛwo PICS vacuum bag mli lɛ, ebaaha kooloi lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni ehaa okpamɔ lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo ni tsofa sũ bɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the young cocoa with essential shade and moisture during its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo bibioo lɛ ni enáa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Should I plant my cassava cuttings straight up or at an angle in the soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu mi yucca tsei lɛ aniji lɛ ja loo mafee ŋwɛigbɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a 45-degree angle helps the plant grow deeper and wider roots, making it produce more tubers and stay firmly anchored in heavy winds.
ga: Kɛ́ adu yucca tsei lɛ yɛ 45 degree ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ená shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ ajieɔ yitsei babaoo ni anyɛɔ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do I have to make big dirt mounds before planting my seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa shikpɔŋ ŋmɔ agbo dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose, and well-drained soil to grow long and thick tubers. Mounds give the tubers room to expand easily while preventing excess rainwater from rotting them.
ga: Sweet potatoes hia shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii kakadaŋŋ agboi. Pile lɛ haa tuber space lɛ mli waa yɛ be mli ni etsĩɔ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ naa koni ekafite.

english: Is it safe for me to plant my maize right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become steady. The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell, which can scorch newly germinated maize seeds before they take root.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ ashã dani amɛwo shishifãi.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or manure helps bring back the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress, lack of water, or poor pollination. Keeping the soil moist and avoiding extreme dryness helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo pollination ni ehiii. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni fe nine lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the land for the next crop season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What is eating the center leaves of my corn plants and leaving small holes?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ ni eshiɔ bu bibioo ko?

english: This is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Checking your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract into the leaf funnels can control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. Ni kɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye amɛnɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and becoming small and bunchy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii ni amɛfee ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling whiteflies early prevents the virus from spreading throughout your plot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Early Whitefly Kudɔmɔ Ebaatsi helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa okpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves getting yellow spots and turning brown at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: This is often cassava mosaic disease or bacterial blight, spread by insects or infected planting sticks. Using disease-resistant cassava stems for planting is the best way to prevent it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni baa lɛ baa lɛ. Kplukai loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ dumɔ mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, a vital soil nutrient needed for leaf growth, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ akwɛ Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Cassava sheds its leaves when water is scarce to prevent moisture loss. The plant goes into rest mode while keeping its energy safely stored in the roots under the ground until the rain comes back.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ kɛji nu faaa koni ekɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa. Tso lɛ yaa hejɔɔmɔ gbɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ mli shweshweeshwe yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why does my yam vine stop growing if it cannot find a wooden stick to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ ekpa shweremɔ lɛ? Be mli ni onyɛɛɛ ona tso nine ni okwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam is a climbing plant that needs tall support to lift its leaves into direct sunlight. Without a stake, the vine stays near the ground, gets shaded by weeds, and produces much smaller tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ yelikɛbuamɔ ni nɔ kwɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la lɛ aba amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji akulashiŋ ko bɛ Wein tso lɛ baabɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Jwɛi ni haa hulutsoo yɛ. ni ehaa yitso bibioo kwraa

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa tree turning black and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛhe feɔ blɛoo lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, overly wet, and shady conditions. It spreads when raindrops bounce off infected leaves or soil onto healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ Eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ, egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ shwieɔ baai loo shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ.

english: Why are my maize stalks snapping near the ground before the farm is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ fãa yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ dani ŋmɔ lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Stalks usually snap because stem borer insects have chewed inside the stem, making the stalk hollow and weak so that light wind can break it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fãa ejaakɛ kooloi ni shwieɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ mli tseɔ ni egbɔjɔ aahu akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ akumɔ.

english: Why do my stored cowpea beans get full of small holes after a few weeks in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Eyi obɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi ni akɛwo baagi mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Small holes in stored beans are caused by bean weevils. The insects often lay tiny eggs inside the pods while the crop is still in the field, and the larvae hatch and eat their way out during storage.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ kɔfi ŋmɔji ni ato lɛ amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmeii amli. Bei pii lɛ, kooloi fɔɔ wɔji bibii. Yɛ pod lɛ mli be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. Ni ŋmeii lɛ baafɔ ni amɛye amɛ gbɛ kɛje kpo yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat or dry soil, which causes stress and prevents the plant from having enough water to support new fruit growth.
ga: Pepper tsei baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Enɛ haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli, ni ehaaa tso lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni aduawai heei akwɛ̃.

english: Why are my tomato fruits rotting at the bottom while the rest of the fruit looks green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miifite yɛ shishigbɛ yɛ be mli ni aduawai ni eshwɛ lɛ feɔ eŋɔli lɛ?

english: Rot at the bottom of tomatoes, called blossom-end rot, happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering.
ga: Rot ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ Atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: How do I know my groundnuts are mature and ready to dig up without spoiling them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ edara ni esa akɛ atsa ni efiteee?

english: Groundnuts are mature when the leaves start turning yellow and shedding, and when you open a few pods, the inside lining of the shell has turned dark brown or purple.
ga: Peanuts lɛ shɛɔ shweremɔ he beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Ni kɛ́ ogbele ŋmeii ayibɔ ko naa lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ amli tsɔɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ loo ŋmeii.

english: Why should I remove rotten cocoa pods and dead leaves from my farm instead of leaving them on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie kookoo ŋmeii ni egboi kɛ baai ni egboi lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Leaving infected or rotten plant parts in your field allows diseases like black pod rot to stay alive in the soil and spread to healthy trees through rain splashes and insects.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi tsei ahe nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ loo amɛmiifite lɛ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha helai tamɔ black pod rot lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛ kooloi bibii anɔ.

english: Can using my cutlass on a sick crop and then using it on a healthy crop spread disease across my farm?
ga: Ani mi-dagger lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ, kɛ no sɛɛ lɛ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ lɛ baagbɛ hela ashwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Yes, farm tools can carry invisible plant germs from one crop to another. Cleaning your cutlass after trimming sick plants prevents you from transferring diseases across your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔ mli nibii baanyɛ ajie tsei amli helai ni anaaa lɛ kɛjɛ tso kome mli kɛya ekroko mli. Kɛ́ otsumɔ o-daggers lɛ ahe beni ofo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why does leaving old crop remains in my field after harvest cause problems for my next planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii momo ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ kɛ naagbai baa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Old crop waste often harbors hidden pest eggs and fungal spores. Clearing the field thoroughly gives your fresh crops a clean start without leftover pests attacking the young seedlings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite lɛ hiɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai. Kɛ́ ojie jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni eshwɛ lɛ etutuaaa dumɔwui bibii lɛ.

english: Why should I clear away fallen, thick rubbish and heavy brush from under my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi ni eyi obɔ kɛ jwɛi ni tsii ni egbee shi kɛjɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Accumulated rubbish under cocoa trees creates damp, dark conditions that promote black pod disease and provide hiding places for destructive pests and snakes.
ga: Jwɛi buaa ehe naa yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi, ni ehaa hulutsoo kɛ duŋ baa. ni kɛ black pod hela baa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ onufui ni fiteɔ nii lɛ naa he ko ni amɛhiɔ amɛhe.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds around my crops regularly instead of just letting them grow together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ daa Moŋ lɛ, ha amɛfee ekome kɛkwɛ̃.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Keeping your farm clear ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: How does keeping my cassava farm free of wild bushes help reduce insect attacks?
ga: Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni koo mli jwɛi bɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha kooloi ni baatutua mi lɛ aba shi?

english: Overgrown bushes around your field act as breeding grounds and homes for insect pests. A clean, weeded farm removes these hiding places and keeps pests away from your cassava.
ga: Tsoi bibii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine ni bɔle oŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ ji hei ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ fɔɔ kɛ amɛshihilɛhei. Jwɛi ŋmɔ ni mli tse baajie nɛkɛ teemɔŋ hei nɛɛ kɛya, ni ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai akashɛ o-cassava lɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato plants turn yellow and weak when the weeds around them grow too high?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ dara tsɔ lɛ?

english: Tall weeds shade tomato plants from sunlight and trap excess moisture around the leaves, which starves the tomatoes of energy and creates ideal conditions for leaf diseases.
ga: Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ haa hulu lɛ shɛɛɛ tomato tsei lɛ ahe, ni emɔɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ he kɛbɔleɔ baai lɛ ahe, ni no haa tomato lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. ni efee shihilɛi ni sa kɛha foliar helai.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I keep neat rows and proper space between them instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ miyɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ fɛo kɛ gbɛ ni sa yɛ amɛteŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ

english: Proper spacing allows air to flow freely between plants to keep leaves dry and prevents roots from fighting each other for soil nutrients and water.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jogbaŋŋ koni eha baai lɛ agbi ni eha shishifãi lɛ akatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ.

english: Why should I trim off the lower leaves of my garden egg plants that touch the bare soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mibɔɔ mli ŋmei tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ kpeɔ lɛ?

english: Soil contains natural fungi and bacteria. Trimming leaves that touch wet dirt stops ground diseases from jumping onto the main plant.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ. Kɛ́ afo baai ni taa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akatswa tso titri lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it harmful to let standing water collect in my crop field after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mahã nu ni damɔ shi lɛ abua naa yɛ miŋmɔji amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Stagnant water drowns crop roots by blocking air from reaching them, causing the roots to rot and leading to yellowing and plant death.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ shwieɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni etsĩɔ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ.

english: Why do my young green cocoa pods turn black and dry up right on the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani edaa lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather when excess shade or weeds trap moisture around the trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ waa mli. Beni hulutsoo loo jwɛi babaoo mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce plenty of flowers, but most of them fall off without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ miifɔlɔ babaoo lɛ? Shi amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges for pollination, and if the air is too dry or shade trees have been cut down, these insects cannot survive to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ nakai midge kɛha ŋmɔtɔ. Ni kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo afo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ nyɛŋ afee fɔfɔii amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the tip of the lower leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to build green leaves and grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ebaakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting under the ground before it is time to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without draining away, causing underground fungi to attack the wet roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejeee kpo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa shishifãi ni efɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing very long and thin instead of getting thick and big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ shwiili ni amɛfeɔ shwiili moŋ lɛ?

english: Yams grow thin when the soil mound is too shallow or hard, forcing the tuber to push downward through tough ground instead of expanding sideways in soft soil.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafee bibioo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. ni nyɛɔ yitso lɛ nɔ koni etsɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ etsɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ Moŋ lɛ, amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛyaa sɛɛgbɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo nɔ.

english: Why are the middle sections of my maize stalks snapping and falling over before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ fãa ni egbeeɔ shi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: This is often caused by stem borer caterpillars that hatch from moth eggs and eat the inside of the stalk, weakening the stem until wind breaks it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, stem borers ni fɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmei wuji amli ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over completely once the fruit bunch starts getting heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi trukaa beni aduawai akui lɛ mli tsiimɔ wa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that cannot support heavy fruit bunches on their own, especially when tiny underground pests like nematodes damage the root system.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ akwɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ anɔ. by yourself Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes fite shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling upward and turning yellow at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is typically caused by a virus spread by whiteflies, tiny white insects that feed on the sap of young plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni ji kooloo bibioo ko ni yɔɔ futafuta ni yeɔ tsei bibii amli nu

english: Why does my pepper farm produce many flowers, but very few of them turn into actual pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔii fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfeɔ pepper aduawai.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when temperature levels get too high or when there is sudden water stress, causing the plant to save its energy rather than produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛna nu he haomɔ trukaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ toɔ hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why does my farmland dry out and crack open wide just a few days after heavy rain stops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi ni egbɛ eshwa gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kpa lɛ?

english: Soil cracks when it has a high clay content and lacks organic matter like leaves or manure, which normally acts like a sponge to hold moisture in the ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fãa kɛji shikpɔŋ sũ babaoo yɛ mli ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai loo ŋmeii bɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji koni ekɛha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Is it helpful to plant beans together with my maize in the same field?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ baaba akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ baadu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans alongside maize improves your harvest. Beans capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, which acts as a natural fertilizer to feed your maize plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ odu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ. Beans mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa ŋmãa tsei niyenii

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly with wide leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my tomato plants fall onto the soil and rot when the fruits appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ aduawai lɛ je kpo lɛ?

english: Heavy tomatoes pull unsupported stems to the wet ground, where fungus easily damages them. Tying your plants to wooden stakes keeps the leaves and fruits elevated, dry, and disease-free.
ga: Tomato ni tsii baagbala tsei ni bɛ sɛɛfimɔ kɛya shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Fuji lɛ baafite amɛ oya. Tsei ni akɛfiɔ tsei ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai kɛ aduawai lɛ feɔ shɔŋŋ, amɛgbiɔ, ni helai bɛ amɛhe.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize crop turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the lower leaves indicates that your maize is hungry for nitrogen. Applying well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer supplies the nutrients needed to make the leaves green again.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa koni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant pepper in the same place where I just harvested tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he ni mifo tomato lɛ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Peppers and tomatoes are in the same plant family and attract the same pests and soil diseases. Planting them continuously in one spot allows crop diseases to build up in the soil and attack your new crop.
ga: Pepper kɛ tomato yɛ tsei akuu kome mli ni amɛgbalaa sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ oya nɔ okwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha tsei ahe helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtutua oŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply chemical fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes the fertilizer away off the topsoil before your crop roots have time to drink it, wasting your money and leaving the plants unfed.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛnuɔ. Shika ni afiteɔ ni ashiɔ tsei lɛ ni ahaaa amɛ niyenii

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating big holes in my cabbage, and how can I stop them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ? Ni maye bu agbo ko yɛ mi-cabbage lɛ mli Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛnaa?

english: Caterpillars target soft cabbage leaves for food. You can control them naturally by boiling crushed neem leaves in water and spraying the cooled solution onto the leaves to repel the pests.
ga: Kasɛtii lɛ kwɛɔ kaabii bibii lɛ anɔ akɛ niyenii. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ neem baai ni atswa lɛ ni oooho yɛ nu mli ni okɛ tsofa ni mli ejɔ ni oooshwie baa lɛ nɔ koni ekɛshwie tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ anɔ.

english: Should I trim off the small extra stems growing between the main branch and leaves on my tomato plant?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ani ajieɔ nɔ ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nine wulu lɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, snapping off those extra side shoots (suckers) helps the plant direct its water and energy into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes instead of excess leafy stems.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛgbɛ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ (ŋmeii) lɛ ni aaafo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ̃ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ.

english: How can I tell when my cassava roots are ready to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ofee klalo akɛ obaafo ŋmei shishifãi lɛ?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the ground directly around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl inward during hot afternoons as a defense mechanism to save water from evaporating. If the leaves stay curled or drop off in the evening, it means your soil needs watering.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ nu naa koni ekaho. Kɛji baai lɛ shwie shi loo amɛgbee shi gbɛkɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my crops regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe daa lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy thieves in your farm. They steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops, causing your crops to grow weak and small.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi hiɛjoolɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi ni amɛfeɔ bibii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green and strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or animal manure can fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye oshikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni esa akɛ ŋmãa ahi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do I need to rotate my crops instead of planting maize in the same field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsake ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ fe ni madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows pests that love maize to multiply. Rotating with beans or groundnuts puts good nutrients back into the soil and starves pests.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ daa afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa niyenii kpakpai baa sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ, ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When land stays flooded for too long, water blocks the air, causing the roots to drown and rot. Planting on raised mounds helps water drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Nu lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboiɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when it gets too hot, when they don't get enough water, or if the plant lacks key nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps save the flowers.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Why does my watermelon plant produce many flowers but very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Watermelon plants produce male and female flowers. Bees must transfer pollen from male to female flowers for fruit to grow; if there aren't enough bees visiting, the flowers drop without making fruit.
ga: Watermelon tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei fɛɛ. Esa akɛ wuobii ajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi hii amli kɛya fɔfɔi yei anɔ bɔni afee ni aduawai lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni abaayasara lɛ bɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: Why are my plantain bunches much smaller than the ones on my neighbor's farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ ji bibioo kwraa fe plantain ni yɔɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Small plantain bunches happen when too many suckers grow around one mother plant, competing for food. Pruning excess suckers allows the plant to focus all its energy into making larger fruit.
ga: plantains akuu bibioo Ebaa kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe. Tso ni ji nyɛ kome lɛ kɛ niyenii yeɔ akaŋ. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo aduawai wuji.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids sucking juice out of the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Spraying neem seed extract or safe insecticides can help control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ neem dumɔwui amli nu loo tsofa ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and die early before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines dry up early when beetles or fungal diseases attack the base, or when the soil gets too hot. Staking your yam vines onto sticks keeps leaves off the hot ground and protects them from disease.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii helai tutua shishigbɛ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ o-sweet potato wain tso lɛ fɔ tsei aniji anɔ lɛ, ebaabu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ ahe, ni ebaatsi helai anaa.

english: Why do I need to clear the weeds and brush under my cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi ni mafolɔ mikoo tsei lɛ ashishi daa lɛ?

english: Clearing weeds reduces competition for water and soil nutrients, removes hiding spots for pests, and makes it easier to move through the farm to inspect and harvest your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa akaŋshii ni yaa nɔ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he lɛ baa shi. Jiemɔ hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ. ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ oootsi ohe kɛya ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni oyakwɛ ni okpa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What should I do with the weeds and small branches after I slash them down on my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee jwɛi kɛ tsei niji bibii? Beni egbe amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: Leaving slashed weeds and leaves on the soil surface creates a natural layer of mulch, which conserves soil moisture during hot dry periods and breaks down into organic fertilizer over time.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi kɛ baai ni afolɔ ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be baa lɛ. ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli

english: Why should I cut off healthy-looking branches from my cocoa trees instead of letting them grow naturally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, ha nɛ e wa bɔ nɛ e ngɛ ɔ.

english: Pruning excess branches allows fresh air and sunlight to pass through the canopy, which lowers humidity around the tree to prevent fungal diseases like black pod while encouraging the tree to focus its energy on growing fruit.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la boteɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. ni haa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baa shi koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ anaa, yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ tsei hu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama aduawai ni amɛduɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: What extra steps can I take right after pruning to help my cocoa trees recover and yield better?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii krokomɛi manyɛ mafee beni mifo tso lɛ sɛɛ koni eye ebua kookoo tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya nɔ ni ewo yibii kpakpai?

english: Applying compost or fertilizer and ensuring good soil moisture right after pruning gives the open trees the boosted nutrients they need to grow strong new shoots and abundant flowers.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli ni akwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ tso ni afo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso ni agbele lɛ lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛ ŋmeii heei ni he wa kɛ fɔfɔi babaoo akwɛ̃.

english: Why do many of the flowers on my cocoa trees wither and fall off without producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers require effective pollination by midges or by hand within a short window; if the flowers do not get pollinated or if the tree lacks water and nutrients, it naturally drops the unfertilized flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ biɔ ni mɔ ko loo nine atsu he nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii. Fɔfɔi ni afɔɔɔ amɛ fɔ lɛ baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: How does hand pollination work to increase the amount of cocoa pods on my farm?
ga: Te nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa tɛŋŋ koni eha kookoo ŋmɔtɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ayi afa?

english: Hand pollination involves manually transferring pollen from a male flower part to a female flower part, ensuring that flowers turn into healthy pods even when natural pollinating insects are scarce.
ga: Nine nɔ fɔfɔi ji fɔfɔi nuu lɛ ni akɛ niji shwieɔ fɔfɔi yoo lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa. Shi kɛlɛ, adebɔɔ mli pollinators lɛ faaa.

english: Can clearing the overgrown bush around my crops help reduce insect attacks on my cocoa pods?
ga: Ajieɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aha kooloi ni tutuaa mikoo ŋmɔji lɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, keeping the ground under your trees clear eliminates damp, dark shelter where pests like capsids and mirids hide and breed, making it harder for them to swarm your crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, he ni tsei lɛ yɔɔ lɛ ni oooha efee faŋŋ lɛ baajie shĩa ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ kɛya. he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ capsids kɛ mirids kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli ni amɛfɔɔ bii lɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa amɛ akɛ amɛaawo onibii amli.

english: How does removing dead or diseased branches stop fungal diseases from spreading through my crop?
ga: Te niji ni egboi loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ akagbɛ ashwã kɛtsɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Diseased wood carries fungal spores that spread through rain droplets and wind; cutting and removing infected branches stops the disease from spreading to healthy pods and neighboring trees.
ga: Fungal spores ni nugbɔshiimɔi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ yɛ tso ni hela lɛ emɔ mli lɛ mli. Niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni aaafolɔ ni ajie lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: What is the best time of the year in Ghana to prune and clear under my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghana ni mikɛbaakpa mikoo tsei lɛ ashishi ni mikɛbaajie amɛ?

english: It is best to prune and clear early in the main rainy season so the trees can use the abundant rainwater to sprout fresh foliage and start forming new pod-bearing flowers.
ga: Esa akɛ afolɔ mli ni ajie kɛjɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ amɛkɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nu babaoo lɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛwo baai heei ni amɛje fɔfɔii heei afeemɔ shishi.

english: How do national cocoa board programs for pruning and spraying assist smallholder farmers?
ga: Te National Cocoa Board nitsumɔ ni kɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi bibii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Government and Cocoa Board initiatives provide trained labor teams, specialized tools, and chemical treatments that help farmers clear large acres safely and correctly, leading to higher overall crop yields across the region.
ga: Nɔyeli lɛ nifeemɔi kɛ Cocoa Commission lɛ haa kui ni atsɔse amɛ. Nibii krɛdɛɛi kɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii Ni yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛjieɔ ŋmɔji wuji ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ shweshweeshwe kɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ etee hiɛ yɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are very delicate and burn easily under the hot sun. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa plants need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa oya. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, dark environments. Heavy rains paired with thick leaf canopies create excess moisture, allowing the fungus to attack and destroy the pods.
ga: Fɛ̃i ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ kɛ black pod hela baa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni akɛ ŋwɛi tsei ahe baai ni mli tse fataa he lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine baa. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni efiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why do I have to make large soil mounds before planting my yam seed pieces?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afee shikpɔŋ wulu ko dani adu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow downwards straight into the ground. Large loose soil mounds make it easy for the roots to expand into long, healthy tubers without fighting hard or compacted dirt.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Shikpɔŋ agboi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ bulbs kakadaji ni mli wa ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ muji ni wa loo ni mli edɔ lɛ akpee.

english: Why do my cassava roots get tough and woody if I leave them in the ground too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots store starch for the plant to use later. If left past maturity, the plant converts that soft starch into tough woody fiber to support new leaves and stems, making the root hard and difficult to cook.
ga: Cassava shishifãi kɛ starch toɔ koni akɛtsu nii sɛɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni eho afii ni tso lɛ daa lɛ he lɛ, tso lɛ tsakeɔ nakai ŋmei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ewoɔ tso mli ŋmeii ni wa mli koni ekɛfi baai kɛ ŋmeii heei asɛɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ewaa akɛ aaaho.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to stay green and grow. Heavy rains can wash this nutrient deep out of reach of the plant's roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛjɛ tsei shishifãi amli.

english: Cowpeas and beans are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through small nodules on their roots. When the crop is harvested, this stored nitrogen stays in the ground to act as natural food for your next maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni efee adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my tomato plants without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too high or when there is dry wind. Extreme heat prevents the pollen inside the flower from fertilizing, causing the plant to shed the unused blossom.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ko ba. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baatsi pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekafee fɔfɔi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni akɛtsuuu nii.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant sap. Extreme heat can also cause leaves to curl up to save water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha baai lɛ abɔle amɛhe koni nu akafite.

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and steal nutrients, water, and sunlight directly from your crop's roots. Without clearing weeds early, your crops will starve even if the rains are good.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ wɔjieee jwɛi kɛjɛɛɛ jɛmɛ kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ, Hɔmɔ baaye nyɛŋmɔshi nibii kɛji nugbɔ kpakpa nɛ po.

english: Why is it good to cover the soil around my vegetables with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi baawo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, shades the soil from the hot sun so water does not evaporate quickly. It keeps the ground moist, prevents weeds from sprouting, and slowly turns into organic manure.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni nu akatsɔ oya Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni fiofio lɛ etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves usually mean your maize is lacking key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or pests such as fall armyworms are feeding on the plant's juices. Applying nitrogen rich fertilizer early or using safe pest control methods can help the maize recover and stay green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ o-ŋmã lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli, loo akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ, tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ miiye. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ baawo mli mra Aloo, kɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛgbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ ni ehi shi ŋmɔŋ.

english: What causes dark spots to spread across my cocoa pods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Dark spots on cocoa pods are caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in high humidity and wet weather. It spreads through splashing rain droplets, infected tools, or contact with diseased pods left on the tree.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii anɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ ni ashi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme weather, such as intense heat, lack of water, or too much rainfall. When stressed, the plant sheds flowers to conserve energy until conditions stabilize.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni naa wa waa, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee shiŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants with deep seed reserves in the soil that germinate immediately when water is present. They naturally absorb nutrients and water faster than domesticated crops, which is why early and regular weeding is necessary.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni dumɔwui yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji nu ba pɛ. Amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu oya fe shia tsei. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra kɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my crop roots burn or die when I place fertilizer directly next to the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shãa loo amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains high concentrations of mineral salts that can pull moisture out of the plant roots if touched directly. Fertilizer should be placed in a circle or line a few inches away from the stem so roots absorb it safely from the moist soil.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli ŋmeii ni fa babaoo ni baanyɛ agbala ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ tsei shishifãi amli kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ kooyigbɛ loo yɛ he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi 2-3 koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why is it recommended that I plant cassava together with my maize on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa adu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Intercropping cassava and maize lets you make full use of your land because maize matures quickly while cassava grows slowly. The early maize covers the soil to reduce weed growth, and after harvesting maize, the cassava expands without competing for space.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa teŋ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa daa oya yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa daa blɛoo. Akɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli koni jwɛi lɛ akakwɛ̃. ni kɛ́ akpa ŋmãa lɛ, Cassava lɛ baagbɛ eshwa ni ekɛ he ko akaŋ akaŋ.

english: Reusing seeds saved from hybrid maize usually yields weaker crops with smaller cobs in the next season. Hybrid seeds are specially bred for one generation of high yield, so it is best to buy fresh certified seeds each planting season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ ni akɛbaa ekoŋŋ lɛ haa ŋmãa ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii baa yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni ekɛ yibii babaoo aba yinɔ kome. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: When is the best time of day for me to water my vegetable crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu?

english: The best time to water vegetables is early in the morning before the sun gets hot. Morning watering allows the leaves to dry off quickly while giving the roots enough moisture to withstand the afternoon heat.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ aduawai anɔ nu ji leebi, dani hulu lɛ adɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa baai lɛ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛgbiɔ oya kɛtsɔ shishifãi lɛ ni ehaa amɛnáa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ shwane latsaa lɛ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot quickly even when stored under a shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya eyɛ mli akɛ akɛtoɔ hulutsoo shishi moŋ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they sustain minor bruises during harvesting or if moisture accumulates around them in storage. Storing yams on raised, airy racks in a well-ventilated barn keeps them dry and prevents fungal rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ŋmeii fioo komɛi yɛ he yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ bua amɛhe naa. yɛ nitoohe Sweet potatoes ni akɛtoɔ tsɔne ni awo nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ehiɛ agbi ni ekɛtsi fungal rot naa.

english: How do I know if my soil is ready and rich enough for me to plant tomatoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo ni ehi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ tomato nɔ?

english: Rich soil for tomatoes feels soft and crumbly, retains water without remaining waterlogged, and contains organic matter like decomposed leaves. Sinking a cut stalk into dark, worm-filled earth usually indicates high soil fertility suitable for healthy crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni baa nii kɛha tomato lɛ baanu he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ekɛ nu toɔ ni ekɛ nu ehiɛɛɛ mli ni eyɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni fiteɔ Kɛ́ tso ni afo lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmeii ebɔle he lɛ mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo, ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to protect them from harsh sunlight and heat. Without big shade trees or nurse crops like plantains, the intense sun dries out the leaves and soil, which kills the young seedling.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo be koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he. Kɛji tsei wuji ni baaha hulutsoo loo tsei tamɔ plantains bɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha baai kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso bibioo lɛ agbo.

english: What happens if I plant my cassava stems too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the roots compete for water, nutrients, and sunlight. This results in tall, thin stems with small tubers underground instead of large, heavy cassava roots.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, niyenii kɛ hulu la he akaŋ, ni no haa ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmei shishifãi wuji ni tsii lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or that too much water is drowning the roots. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or improving soil drainage helps restore the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my pepper plants without forming any pepper fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni pepper yibii ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as dry soil, excessive heat, or over-fertilizing. The plant discards flowers to conserve water and energy to survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛyashɛ nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo he. Tsei shiɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my maize help my soil?
ga: Te tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa fataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This acts as a natural fertilizer that nourishes neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen gas mli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛɔ mli baa tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, traps moisture in the ground so it doesn't evaporate quickly in the sun. It also prevents weeds from growing and decomposes into rich plant food.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ, mɔ̃ɔ sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ bɔni afee ni hulu la lɛ akafo oya. Etsiɔ jwɛi hu naa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkafite tsei aniyenii ni jara wa lɛ.

english: Why do fall armyworms cause so much damage to my young maize plants so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ fiteɔ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Fall armyworms hide deep inside the central leaf funnel of young maize plants where rain and chemicals cannot easily reach them. They feed rapidly on new growing tissue, destroying the plant's ability to develop.
ga: Autumn cutworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ. ni nugbɔ kɛ tsofai ni anáa lɛ bɛ mlɛo. Amɛyeɔ fãji heei ni miida oya. ni fiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛbaakwɛ nii lɛ

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in cool, wet, and high-humidity weather. Splashing rain drops carry fungal spores from infected leaves and soil onto healthy pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛɔ baai kɛ shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to climb stakes so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food for the plant. Lifting vines off the damp soil also prevents fungal diseases and leads to larger yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso ko nɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha tso lɛ. Wein tsei lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa, ni ehaa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready to harvest without digging up the whole stand?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is generally ready for harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare main stem. You can carefully dig up just one side of a plant stem to inspect the tuber size before harvesting the entire farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Ashi tso lɛ tso titri lɛ efolo. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu tso lɛ shishifã lɛ fã kome pɛ he nii koni okwɛ bulb lɛ dalɛ dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the bottom leaves going upwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to stay green and grow strong. When the soil runs out of nitrogen, the plant steals it from older leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛji niyenii titrii ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Tso lɛ juɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.
