english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like beans or groundnuts feeds the soil and starves pests.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: Why do my plantain stems produce smaller bunches when I leave all the young shoots growing around the main trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii beni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: All those extra shoots, called suckers, are competing with the mother plant for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Cutting them away to leave only one or two strong suckers allows the mother plant to produce a much larger, heavier fruit bunch.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi nɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii. Ekɛ tso nyɛ lɛ miitswa akaŋ koni ena nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli koni ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ ni ewo yibii akui ni dara ni tsii kwraa.

english: Won't cutting off some branches from my cocoa trees reduce the amount of cocoa pods I get?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tsei lɛ aniji ni mifoɔ lɛ haŋ cocoa ŋmeii ni minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi?

english: Pruning unnecessary branches actually increases your yield. It lets sunlight and fresh air reach the stem and main branches, which prevents fungal diseases like black pod from spreading and encourages the tree to put its energy into growing big pods.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baaye abua diɛŋtsɛ ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ niji wuji lɛ ahe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods lɛ akagbɛ eshwa. ni ekanyaa tsei koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmeii wuji

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in the direct sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking also keeps the foliage off the damp ground, preventing leaf rot and fungal infections.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli koni ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ baai ni fiteɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Flower drop usually happens when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when tiny pests like thrips attack the blossoms. Without proper moisture and temperature, the plant sheds flowers to protect itself.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips tutuaa fɔfɔii. Kɛji hulutsoo kɛ latsaa ni sa bɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and twisting like little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, mites, or whiteflies hiding under the leaves, or by a virus carried by these insects. They suck the juice from new leaves, causing them to grow deformed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, mites, loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ hiɛɔ lɛ nɔ Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai heei amli lɛ, ni no haa amɛfeɔ shoo.

english: How does covering the bare soil around my crops with dry leaves or grass help them grow?
ga: Mulching bare soil around Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu miŋmɔshi nibii kɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara?

english: This practice is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that keeps soil cool under the hot sun, holds in water so you water less, stops weeds from growing, and slowly rots into organic fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehiɛɔ nu mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akafɔ shii abɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ fiofio akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops as soon as I plant the seeds, or should I wait until they sprout?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛji midu amɛ pɛ loo esa akɛ mamɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Seeds carry their own initial food to germinate, so putting concentrated fertilizer directly on seeds can burn them. It is best to wait until the seedlings sprout and develop green leaves so their small roots are ready to take up nutrients.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishijee niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ ashã. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee baai eŋɔli koni shishifãi bibii akwɛ̃. Amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaaná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are mature and ready for harvesting without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can tell cassava is maturing when the lower leaves naturally dry up and fall off, leaving a bare stem with leaves only at the top, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack open from expanding tubers.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmei ko miida kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ gĩ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ yitso ni bɛ nɔ ko ni baai yɔɔ nɔ lɛ pɛ eshwɛ, ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle shishigbɛ lɛ ebɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ bulb lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ mli.

english: Why do my yam plants need tall wooden sticks to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ koni ekɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam is a vine that needs to spread its leaves in full sunlight to make food for its roots. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, which prevents fungal diseases and helps the tuber underground grow much bigger.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni ehe hiaa ni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he bɔni afee ni amɛha amɛshishifãi lɛ niyenii. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa, ni ebaaye ebua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdara babaoo.

english: When maize plants are crowded together, they fight each other for water, sunlight, and food in the dirt. This competition leaves all the plants thin and weak, resulting in very small cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ abɛi tsei bua amɛhe naa lɛ, amɛshiɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and food from the main plantain tree. Removing most of them leaves only the main tree strong enough to carry a heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Tsofai krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo baaha tso titri lɛ pɛ ahi shi ni ehe wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ awo aduawai babaoo.

english: Why should I plant cassava stem cuttings at an angle instead of straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi yucca tsei lɛ aniji lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mafee nɔ ni ja?

english: Planting cassava stems at a slant helps the roots grow horizontally near the soil surface, allowing the tubers to expand easily and making them much easier to dig up during harvest.
ga: Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tubers lɛ mli lɛɛɔ mlɛo. ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaatsu nii yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a maize plant mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which gives plants their green color. The plant is moving its remaining food to top leaves, signaling that your soil needs fertilizer or manure.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli Tso lɛ miitsɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ nɔ kɛmiiya baai lɛ amli. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground, naturally enriching the soil with food for the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ ni baai egbi loo jwɛi?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves keeps the hot sun from drying out the earth, keeps plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing easily around your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ mlɛo yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why do I need to cut off healthy-looking extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ aniji ni fa fe nine ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Trimming extra branches lets fresh air and sunlight flow through the tree canopy. This dries up hidden moisture, preventing wet-weather diseases like black pod from ruining your harvest.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ agbi. Tsi kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ waa, tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite onibii.

english: Why are tiny worms eating holes inside the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the soft, growing centers of maize plants. They hide deep inside the leaves to feed safely, which can stunt or kill the crop if left untreated.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye nii shweshweeshwe. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii afee mlɛo loo efite kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Do my crops also need air to breathe and survive just like human beings and farm animals?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia miŋmɔshi nii lɛ lolo koni amɛmu ni amɛhi shi tamɔ adesai kɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Yes, plants need air to stay alive. During the daytime, leaves take in carbon dioxide from the air to make food and give out fresh oxygen. At night, when there is no sunlight, they absorb oxygen from the air to break down that food for energy, releasing carbon dioxide.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei koni amɛhi shi. yɛ gbi mli lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji carbon dioxide lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛkɛfee niyenii ni amɛjieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni ji oxygen ni he tse lɛ kpo gbɛkɛ, be mli ni hulu la bɛ lɛ. Amɛheɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛgbala nakai niyenii lɛ mli ni amɛfee hewalɛ. ni ejieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji carbon dioxide lɛ kpo

english: Is it true that my crops and farm bushes behave differently during the night than during the day?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ gbɛkɛ fe shwane?

english: Yes, crops work differently at night. During the day, they use sunlight to produce food and oxygen. At night, because there is no sun, plants stop making food and instead rest and absorb oxygen to use up the food energy they stored during the day.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ gbɛkɛ. Yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ, amɛkɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Gbi gbɛkɛ lɛ, yɛ hulu la ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ lɛ, no sɛɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ kpaɔ nihoomɔ ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛŋɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ koni amɛkɛ niyenii hewalɛ ni amɛto yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do I find water droplets on my vegetable leaves early in the morning when it did not rain overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ aduawai ahe tsei anɔ leebi be mli ni nugbɔ enɛko nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: That water comes from dew and plant breathing. During the cool night, water vapor in the air settles on leaves, and plants also release extra moisture through tiny openings in their leaves while resting.
ga: Nakai nu lɛ jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsei amumɔ mli. Gbi gbɛkɛ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Nu mli lasu ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ kpɛtɛɔ baai lɛ ahe. Ni tsei jieɔ nu kroko kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni amɛgbeleɔ lɛ anɔ. yɛ baai lɛ anɔ be mli ni ejɔɔ ehe lɛ hu

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and fold during the hot afternoon sun but stand up again by morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi te shi ekoŋŋ leebi?

english: Leaves droop in extreme heat to protect themselves from losing too much water. Once the sun goes down and the air cools, the plant's roots drink up moisture from the soil to restore the leaves by morning.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. Kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha baai lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ leebi.

english: Why is sunlight so necessary for my yam and cassava plants to grow big roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulu la he hiaa koni mi-sweet potatoes kɛ mi-cassava lɛ aná shishifãi wuji lɛ?

english: Sunlight acts as fuel for plants. Green leaves capture light energy to turn water and air into nutrients, which travel down to feed the plant and allow the tubers underground to grow large.
ga: Hulu la tsuɔ nii akɛ tsofa kɛhaa tsei. Baai eŋɔli lɛ mɔɔ kane hewalɛ ni ekɛtsakeɔ nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ amɛfeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi koni eyaha tsei niyenii ni eha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ dara

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die if I remove all the tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei kakadaji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Tall shade trees act as a screen, keeping the air moist and cool while protecting the young plants from heat stress.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Why do wild grass and weeds in my farm make my maize plants grow thin and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds and wild grass are fast growers that steal water, soil nutrients, air space, and sunlight away from your maize, leaving the crop with too little energy to grow strong.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ji jwɛi ni daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ hulu la jieɔ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni ekɛbaadara ni ewa.

english: Does clearing dense bush and weeds around my field help my crops get better air to grow?
ga: Ani tsei bibii kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle miŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ ni mijieɔ lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa koni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Yes, clearing heavy bush allows sunlight to reach the lower crop leaves and improves airflow through the farm, which helps crops breathe properly and prevents damp fungal diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe. ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni emuɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ hela ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves mean the plant is under stress, often because the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or because the roots are getting too much water or suffering from a pest attack.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ haomɔ shishi. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛni shishifãi lɛ enine eshɛ nu babaoo nɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai etutua amɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers drop off before turning into actual pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛmiitsɔ pepper aduawai diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from high heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients, because the plant saves its remaining energy to stay alive rather than producing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ toɔ koni amɛhi wala mli moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to nourish new top leaves, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow and die early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the plants without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without setting fruit when temperatures get too high, during severe dry spells, or when the soil lacks sufficient nutrients like phosphorus during the flowering stage.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa lɛ mli loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa tamɔ fɔsfɔs yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling up and twisting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies feeding on the leaves, or by a plant virus carried into the field by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛyaa ŋmɔji amli lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my cocoa leaves burn and wither when I plant them in an open field without trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain beside young cocoa creates a canopy that protects tender leaves from sunburn and helps retain soil moisture.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi tsei ni buɔ baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he lɛ baa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi

english: Planting seeds too closely causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition leads to thin, weak stems and very small or empty cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Why is it helpful to cover the soil around my vegetable roots with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi baawo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-vegetable shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) blocks direct sunlight from drying out the soil, keeps plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over your vegetable plot.
ga: Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekagbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye o-vegetable shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the central leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that burrows into the growing center of maize plants. Catching and treating them early with approved sprays or neem mixtures stops them from destroying the growing tip.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ adalɛ mli. Ni ooomɔ amɛ ni otsa amɛ mra Neem tsofa loo tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water stays pooled in the soil for too long. Excessive water cuts off oxygen to the roots, allowing harmful fungi and bacteria in the soil to break down and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nu babaoo ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ muawai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why should I avoid growing cassava on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and lets soil-borne pests and diseases build up. Rotating cassava with legumes like cowpeas restores nutrients like nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa sũ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ hoɔ, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Cassava kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ cowpea ni akɛtsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster and stronger than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to survive harsh conditions, meaning they absorb available water and soil nutrients much faster than domesticated crops unless cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ shia lɛ. ja ajie kɛjɛ mli oya.

english: Why do my dried cowpeas grind into a fine powder instead of splitting into clean halves during processing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ajieɔ mi-cowpeas ni egbi lɛ ni efeɔ powda kpakpa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaajara mli awo fãi ni he tse mli yɛ be mli ni atsuɔ he nii lɛ?

english: When cowpea seeds are completely dry and low in natural moisture, their internal structure becomes very brittle. When processed in a grinding mill, this brittleness causes the whole seed to crush into fine powder rather than neatly cracking open.
ga: Kɛji akɛ cowpea dumɔwui lɛ egbi kwraa ni amɛmli nu ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ faaa lɛ, Dumɔwu lɛ mligbɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli shwieɔ shi waa. Kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii amli lɛ Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ haa dumɔwui muu lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ powda kpakpa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefo mli fɛfɛo.

english: Why do some of my harvested beans feel much harder to grind than others from the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-kɔfi ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ wa fe ŋmeii krokomɛi lɛ? kɛjɛ ŋmɔ kome mli

english: Beans that grew on plants facing water shortages develop thicker, tougher outer skins. These seeds retain less internal moisture, making them much harder and requiring more mechanical force to grind during post-harvest processing.
ga: Beans ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei ni nu faaa lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni mli wa. Dumɔwui nɛɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko yɛ amɛmli. Enɛ haa ewaa kwraa ni ebiɔ tsɔne hewalɛ babaoo ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ be mli.

english: Why do my harvested cowpeas turn into dust and empty shells after storing them for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ni mikpa lɛ batsɔ sũ kɛ ŋmei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli beni mikɛto nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Storage pests like cowpea weevils lay tiny eggs on the beans. When the eggs hatch, the larvae eat the inside of the seed, leaving behind empty shells and powdery waste that looks like dust.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ nibii amli tamɔ tsina ŋmei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli niyenii. Nɔ pɛ ni eshwɛ ji ŋshɔŋloo ko ni nɔ ko bɛ mli kɛ sũ ni tamɔ sũ.

english: Why do my cowpeas spoil and smell bad if I bag them immediately after picking them from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ fiteɔ ni eŋɔɔɔ kɛji mikɛwo baagi mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Freshly picked cowpeas still carry high natural moisture inside the seed. If you bag them without sun-drying, this trapped moisture creates a warm, damp environment where mold and fungi grow rapidly.
ga: Cowpeas ni ajie ehee lɛ hiɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nu ni fa babaoo yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ kotoku lɛ wo mli ni okɛ hulu lɛ egbiko lɛ Nɛkɛ nu ni emɔ mli nɛɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. he ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii shwereɔ oya yɛ lɛ

english: Why do my cowpea pods burst open on their own and drop seeds on the soil before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmeii lɛ amli gbalaa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ dumɔwui amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ dani mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: When cowpea pods reach full maturity under hot sunshine, the pod walls dry out, shrink, and twist tightly. This natural behavior forces the pod to shatter and scatter its seeds so the plant can reproduce.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ gbogboi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ, amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe waa. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli subaŋ nɛɛ nyɛɔ pod lɛ nɔ ni efoɔ ni egbɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ eshwaa koni tso lɛ anyɛ afɔ.

english: How do my cowpea plants show me that they are mature enough and ready for harvesting?
ga: Mi-cowpea tsei lɛ tsɔɔ mi bɔ ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Cowpea plants signal maturity by changing color. The green leaves will turn yellow and start dropping off, while the seed pods turn from soft green to dry, crisp brown or straw-colored.
ga: Cowpea tsei tsɔɔ amɛdalɛ kɛtsɔ amɛsu tsakemɔ nɔ. Baai eŋɔlii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbeeɔ shi. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli ni mli tse kɛyaa ŋmɔshi, asasu ni egbi loo jwɛi su.

english: Why do the seeds inside my dry cowpea pods start sprouting while still hanging on the plant during heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ be mli ni ekã tso lɛ nɔ lolo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High humidity and continuous rain convince mature seeds that they have been planted in damp soil. The moisture triggers their natural growth cycle, causing them to break through the pod and sprout prematurely.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ haa aduɔ dumɔwui ni eda yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Fɛ̃i woɔ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ ni yaa nɔ lɛ he hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ mra.

english: Can I grind the dry stems and leaves left on my farm after picking cowpeas to feed my livestock?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafolɔ tsei kɛ baai ni egbi ni eshwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa tsina ŋmeii lɛ koni mikɛha kooloi niyenii?

english: Yes, cowpea vines and leaves retain high protein levels even after the seed pods are harvested. Grinding or chopping these dry crop residues provides nutritious feed for cattle, sheep, and goats.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, cowpea wain tsei kɛ baai lɛ yɛ protein babaoo lolo yɛ be mli ni akpa dumɔwui lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ po sɛɛ. Nɛkɛ tsei ni egbi nɛɛ ni ashwieɔ loo afoɔ lɛ haa tsinai, tooi, kɛ tooi niyenii kpakpa.

english: Why do my maize crops grow stronger when I plant them on land where I previously grew cowpeas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa waa kɛ́ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ miduɔ tsina ŋmãa nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant naturally decays, it releases this trapped food into the soil for future crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei fite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe Ejieɔ niyenii ni amɔmɔ lɛ awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛhaa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing lots of thick green leaves but very few flowers and pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: If cowpea plants receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or excessive rain early on, they focus all their energy on vegetative leaf growth instead of shifting into their flowering and pod-producing phase.
ga: Kɛji akɛ cowpea tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo nugbɔ babaoo mra lɛ, Cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a tsakeɔ kɛ yaa fɔfɔi kɛ pod fɔmi be ɔ mi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open, sunny field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted nearby to protect their delicate leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni ebu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ shãa he. kɛ koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested plantains spoil so quickly when I transport them in a closed truck from the farm to the city market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo lɔle ko ni agbe naa mli kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ?

english: Plantains continue to breathe and ripen after harvest, releasing natural heat and gas. When trapped in a closed truck with poor ventilation, the heat builds up rapidly and causes the fruit to rot before reaching the market.
ga: Plantains yaa nɔ emuɔ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Ajieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli la ni ji gas lɛ kpo. Kɛji akɛ akɛwo lɔle ko ni aŋã ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ buaa ehe naa oya ni ehaa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ dani eshɛɔ jara nɔ.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge green leaves above ground but very small stems under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani tso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer and not enough potassium, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves instead of expanding its underground tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo ni potassium faaa lɛ, Tsei hu kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Why do buyers in the market pay higher prices for firm, dry maize seeds compared to soft ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni wa ni egbi lɛ jara babaoo fe ŋmãa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ?

english: Firm and properly dried maize contains low moisture, which prevents mold growth and insect damage during long storage and transport, making it safer and longer-lasting for buyers.
ga: Abɛi ni wa ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo. ni tsiɔ ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii anaa yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ be kakadaŋŋ kɛyaa he kroko lɛ. Ehaa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young corn plants look like they have tiny gunshot holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ tu bibii bibii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Small holes in young maize leaves are caused by pests like fall armyworms feeding on the tender plant tissues, which reduces the plant's ability to make food from sunlight.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworms ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛ hulu la feɔ niyenii lɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I avoid putting four or five maize seeds into a single planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii ejwɛ loo enumɔ ni mikɛwoɔ ŋmãa bu kome mli lɛ he?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole causes the seedlings to crowd each other, forcing them to fight for sunlight, water, and soil food, which results in weak, thin stems and very small cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ abua amɛhe naa. Anyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛwu amɛha hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants fall off before any peppers actually form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, lack of water, or poor nutrients in the soil, which prevents the flower from setting fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛna haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. ni tsiɔ fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkawo yibii

english: Why do my tomato leaves droop in the hot afternoon even if I watered the soil in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛgboi moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu leebi?

english: On hot days, plants lose moisture through leaves faster than their roots can pull water from the soil. Deep watering early in the morning helps moisture reach lower roots and reduces afternoon wilting.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nu ni mli kwɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ shɛɔ shishifãi ni eba shi lɛ ahe, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa shi yɛ shwane mli.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and taller than my food crops right after the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkwɔ fe mi niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to quickly capture rainwater and nutrients before cultivated crops can. Clearing weeds early gives your crops room to grow and capture sunlight.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛmɔmɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya dani tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ ni emɔ hulu la lɛ.

english: Why can some cassava varieties be left in the ground for over a year while others rot if not harvested early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ashiɔ ŋmei henɔi komɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔ ni fe afi lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni henɔi komɛi baanyɛ afite kɛji akɛ akpaaa amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Different cassava varieties mature at different rates; quick-maturing varieties are designed for early harvest and rot if left too long, while late-maturing varieties can be safely stored alive in the soil until needed.
ga: Cassava henɔi srɔtoi Amɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Afee tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ koni amɛkpa mra ni amɛgboi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ sɛɛ lɛ ato shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe kɛyashi ehe baahia.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food, or that the soil is overly waterlogged, preventing the roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo tsɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why should I wait for two or three steady rains before planting my maize seeds at the start of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ dani maduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: The very first rain of the season is often a false start followed by hot, dry weeks; waiting ensures the soil has deep moisture so your seeds do not germinate and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ ji amale shishijee. Otsi ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ. Mɛɛmɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ ni amɛgbi.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy leaves but yield very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baa ni kɛlɛ waa, ni efee ŋmɔji shi ewoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes the cassava plant to focus its energy on growing top leaves instead of storing food in its underground roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ eŋwɛi baai lɛ akwɛmɔ he nii moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb tall wooden stakes to give me big yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ koni enine ashɛ sweet potato agbo nɔ aha mi lɛ?

english: Yam leaves produce food for the tuber using sunlight; lifting the vines onto stakes spreads the leaves out to catch maximum sunlight instead of rotting on the damp ground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa tuber lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ashwã koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ he babaoo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Why do many of the small green cocoa pods on my tree dry up and turn black before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ No hewɔ lɛ, mitso lɛ nɔ fã ni fa lɛ mli egbi ni eyɛ ediŋŋ dani edaa lɛ?

english: This is often 'cherelle wilt,' a natural process where the tree drops young pods it cannot feed, though it can also be worsened by insect pests like capsids or extreme heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji ‘cherel wilt’, ni ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ni tsei shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni anyɛɛɛ aha amɛ niyenii lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi tamɔ capsids loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha ehiɛ afee shoo moŋ.

english: When too many young shoots grow together, they compete with the main plant for water and nutrients, resulting in smaller, lighter bunches of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii lɛ dara yɛ he kome tsɔ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa plantains bibii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of insects to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny pests like thrips, mites, or aphids sucking sap from the leaves or transmitting a viral infection to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why is it good practice for me to plant groundnuts on my farm before planting corn the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for nutrient-heavy crops like corn.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why does spreading dry grass or leaves around my vegetable plants keep the ground moist during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-aduawai lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Dry grass acts as a protective blanket over the soil, lowering ground temperature, preventing soil moisture from evaporating quickly, and keeping weeds from growing.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi tsuɔ nii akɛ kuntu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa baa shi Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekaho oya. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why should I plant crops like soybean or cowpea in the same field where I plan to plant maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ soybeans loo cowpeas yɛ ŋmɔ ni mito gbɛjianɔ akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Legume crops like soybeans and cowpeas have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When you plant maize in that same soil later, the maize uses that natural plant food to grow tall, green, and produce larger yields without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ soybeans kɛ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ odu ŋmãa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa kɛ nakai adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃, efee ŋmɔŋ ni ewo yibii babaoo ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my crops grow faster and greener when I plant them after growing beans on that land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji kɛ́ midu amɛ beni midu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bean plants leave behind rich organic matter and nitrogen in the soil after harvest. Crops planted in that field afterward absorb this leftover plant food easily, causing them to grow faster and look healthier.
ga: Bean tsei shĩɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ nitrogen babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ amli oya. Ehaa tsei daa oya ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil is missing the nutrients my crops need to grow well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni tsei akwɛ̃ lɛ bɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: When soil lacks nutrients, crop leaves often turn pale green or yellow instead of deep green, plant growth stays short and weak, and the harvest is light. Planting high-protein cover crops like legumes helps rebuild soil richness naturally.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ mli lɛ Bei pii lɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Tsei adalɛ baafee kuku ni ebɛ hewalɛ. ni ŋmaa lɛ ji bibioo Dumɔ nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ ni protein babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ ŋmeii. Ebaaye ebua ni etswa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do the leaves on my soybean plants turn yellow and drop off just before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi soybean tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani abakpa lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is normal behavior for soybeans when they reach maturity. The plant naturally sheds its leaves so all its remaining energy and moisture go directly into drying the pods and seeds for harvest.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji subaŋ ni afɔɔ feemɔ kɛha soybeans be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Tso lɛ baajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ ehe. No hewɔ lɛ, hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ yaa tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔi kɛ dumɔwui lɛ agbimɔ mli koni akɛkpa.

english: Why are the leaf tips of my young maize plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaf tips usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food crops use to make leaves green and strong. You can fix this by adding compost, manure, or rotating the land with bean crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishifãi ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛ baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Obaanyɛ osaa enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaafata he, loo he ni okwɛɔ bean lɛ nɔ lɛ ni oootsake lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do groundnut plants push their flower stems into the ground to form nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei tsiɔ fɔfɔii ahe ŋmeii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ koni amɛfee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated above ground, the stems peg downward into the soil. The nuts grow and ripen underground where they are protected from hot sun, wind, and surface pests while absorbing soil moisture.
ga: Beni afee ŋmei fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ pollination sɛɛ lɛ, abaawo ŋmei tso lɛ shishi. Beans kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi he ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu, ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni ejieɔ lɛ

english: Why do my crop flowers drop off without making any pods during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When weather gets too hot and water is scarce, crops drop their flowers as a survival defense. The plant sheds the flowers to save energy and water so the main stalk does not dry up and die.
ga: Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni nu faaa lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baashi fɔfɔi yɛ amɛsɛɛ koni ekɛtsi amɛwala naa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Bɔni afee ni tso titri lɛ akagbi.

english: How does growing protein-rich crops like soybean help improve my children's health?
ga: Nibii ni protein eyi mli obɔ tamɔ soybeans ni ooodu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni obii lɛ ahewalɛ yaa hiɛ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná minɔ lɛ?

english: Protein-rich crops contain nutrients that build strong muscles, bones, and body organs. Feeding foods made from soybeans or cowpeas to growing children helps prevent malnutrition, keeps them active, and gives them special physical strength.
ga: Niyenii nibii ni haa gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli faji, wui, kɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nibii feɔ mlɛo lɛ yɛ tsei ni protein eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli koni ehe awa Soybeans loo cowpeas ni akɛhaa gbekɛbii ni miida lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ niyenii ni esaaa ni ayeɔ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa gbekɛbii ni amɛfeɔ ekãa. ni ehaa amɛnáa gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛ ni nɔ bɛ.

english: What makes Quality Protein Maize different from the regular white maize I have always farmed?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ protein lɛ feɔ srɔto yɛ ŋmãa yɛŋ ni mikwɛɔ daa lɛ he?

english: Quality Protein Maize looks and yields like regular maize, but its grains contain higher amounts of essential nutrients called amino acids. These extra nutrients make it far more nourishing for children and farm animals than ordinary corn.
ga: Abɛi mli protein ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ sui kɛ yibiiwoo tamɔ abɛi ni yɔɔ daa lɛ nɔŋŋ. Shi niyenii ni he hiaa ni atsɛɔ lɛ amino acids lɛ fa babaoo yɛ ŋmãa mli. Nɛkɛ niyenii ni fa nɛɛ haa efeɔ niyenii ni haa gbekɛbii kɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi babaoo fe ŋmãa ni ayeɔ daa lɛ.

english: Why should I dedicate part of my farm to growing legumes instead of only planting cassava or yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã ko nɔ kɛha ŋmeii akwɛmɔ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmei loo ŋmei kɛkɛ?

english: Root crops like cassava provide energy, but legumes like beans and soybeans provide protein needed for body growth and health. Balancing your farm with protein crops improves your family's diet while making your soil richer for future seasons.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei haa hewalɛ. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ soybeans Haa protein ni he hiaa kɛha gbɔmɔtso lɛ dalɛ kɛ hewalɛnamɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ protein lɛ to oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha oweku lɛ niyenii aya hiɛ yɛ be mli ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni jara wa kɛha bei ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and burn when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. They require temporary shade trees, like plantains or bananas, to protect their leaves from scorching and to keep the soil moist while their roots develop.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo banana. Koni akɛbu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he. kɛ koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot before they are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy seasons when humidity is high. Removing infected pods and trimming excess shade branches improves airflow and helps keep the pods dry.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afolɔ niji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni eye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my cocoa trees if I want them to yield more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo niji komɛi kɛji miisumɔ ni maná ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or non-producing branches, allowing sunlight and air to circulate through the canopy. This prevents disease and forces the tree to direct its energy into producing fruits rather than leaves.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni wooo yibii lɛ. Ha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ helai anaa ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni etsɔɔ ehewalɛ lɛ nɔ koni ewo yibii yɛ baai najiaŋ.

english: How can I tell if my farmland is exhausted and needs rest or fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efo ni ehe miihia ni mafo mli loo mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli?

english: Exhausted soil usually shows in crop behavior: plants grow much slower than usual, stay short, have thin stems, and develop pale green or yellowish leaves even when there is enough rain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ jieɔ ehe kpo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli: Tsei lɛ daaa blɛoo kwraa fe bɔ ni amɛfeɔ daa lɛ. Amɛyɛ kuku, amɛyɛ tsei bibii, ni amɛyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po.

english: If I leave my land unused for two years, will my crops really grow better when I return to farm it?
ga: Kɛji mishi shikpɔŋ lɛ ni mikɛtsuuu nii afii enyɔ Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ kɛ́ miku misɛɛ kɛtee okwaayeli mli?

english: Yes, resting the land allows natural vegetation to decay and restore organic nutrients to the soil. This break also reduces pest populations that built up during continuous farming.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ lɛ fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei lɛ ni ehaa niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Nɛkɛ fãmɔ nɛɛ hu haa ŋmeii ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli lɛ ayibɔ baa shi.

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans trap nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. When you plant maize afterward, it feeds on this natural nitrogen, which acts as a free crop fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Eyeɔ nitrogen yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni tsuɔ nii akɛ tso ŋmãa ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with very small ears when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛtoi bibii waa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves compete with each other for space, water, nutrients, and sunlight. This competition weakens the individual plants, resulting in poor yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná he ko, nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso gbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi

english: Why do pepper and vegetable leaves curl up tight during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural mechanism plants use to protect themselves from excessive heat. By curling their leaves, plants reduce the surface area exposed to the sun to hold onto internal moisture.
ga: Baai ni akpɛɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ baa shi yɛ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi emli.

english: Why do weeds on my farm shoot up much faster than my planted crops immediately after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe tsei ni miduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, highly resilient plants with deep root systems already established in the soil. They are adapted to grab available water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi waa ni amɛshishifãi ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ momo. Atsake lɛ koni ejie nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: How do I know if the crop protection chemical I sprayed on my farm is working effectively?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofai ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsu nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Signs of effective crop medicine include the stoppage of leaf yellowing, dead pests on or under the leaves within 24 to 48 hours, and clean, healthy new growth appearing at the tips of the plant.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsofa ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ he ji baai ŋmɔŋ ni akpaa. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ gboiɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ loo amɛshishi yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 kɛyashi 48 mli, ni ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to strong sunlight and can burn easily. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist while the young cocoa trees grow.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã oya. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves in maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen in the soil or the ground is waterlogged. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps the plant regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛfeɔ amɛhe ŋmɔji ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know which end of a cassava stick to plant into the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei lɛ naagbee ni esa akɛ madu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the small bumps or buds along the stem where leaves used to grow. These buds should point upwards toward the sky so the stem can grow buds and roots properly.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmei bibioo lɛ. loo fɔfɔii bibii ni shwieɔ shi Ebɛŋkɛɔ tso lɛ shishi he ni baai lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ be ko ni eho lɛ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni sa aba.

english: Yam plants are natural climbing vines that need sunlight to build large tubers underground. Staking raises the leaves off the damp ground so they can catch direct sunlight and stay safe from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni he hiaa hulu la koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei wuji. Staking baajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Pepper flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil gets too dry. Giving the plants consistent moisture and mulching the soil around them keeps the root area cool so fruits can set.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Okɛ nu awo tsei lɛ amli daa ni okɛ sũ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ awo mli. Ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni aduawai lɛ anyɛ atswa.

english: Why are small worms eating the center of my young corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: These worms are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets young corn leaves. Checking your fields early and applying recommended bio-pesticides into the central funnel of the plant can stop them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ anɔ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli mra. Ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛwo tsei lɛ ateŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ amɛnaa dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo mi-ŋma lɛ mli?

english: The best practice is to put the first fertilizer (NPK) about 1 to 2 weeks after the seeds sprout, and then a second dose (Urea) when the plant is knee-high, so the crop gets food when it grows fastest.
ga: Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii (NPK) lɛ awo mli aaafee otsi 1 kɛyashi 2 sɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii (urea) ni ji enyɔ lɛ awo mli beni tsei lɛ eshɛ amɛkuɛ he lɛ. Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ aná niyenii yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa oya fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants natively suited to the land, so they suck up rain and soil food faster than young crops. Clearing them within the first three weeks prevents them from stealing light and nutrients from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kpãa gbee. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛmɔɔ nugbɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli.

english: Why should I water my tomato plants early in the morning instead of late in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi moŋ fe gbɛkɛ?

english: Watering in the morning gives plants moisture to face the sun's heat during the day. Late evening watering leaves the soil and leaves wet all night, which attracts fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ leebi lɛ haa amɛnáa nu ni amɛkɛkpeɔ hulu ni tsoɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ naa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ, ni no gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why should I remove some of the extra shoots growing at the bottom of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Too many shoots around one main plantain stem fight for the same soil food and water. Leaving only 1 to 3 healthy shoots ensures the main tree gets enough energy to yield heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo ni ebɔle tso titri kome he lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa shikpɔŋ kome nɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii 1 kɛyashi 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or vegetables under my coconut trees while they are still young?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo aduawai yɛ ŋmei tso shishi be mli ni miji gbekɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, you can intercrop under young coconut trees because they leave plenty of open space and sunlight in their early years. Planting food crops like cassava, maize, or legumes helps maximize your land use and provides income before the coconuts start producing fruit.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmeii bibii ashishi ejaakɛ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ, ŋmeii tsei lɛ baaná he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kɛ hulu la babaoo. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yaa hiɛ kɛyashɛɔ sɛɛnamɔ babaoo he. ni ekɛ shika aba dani ŋmeii lɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi

english: Why should I keep some tall trees on my land when planting young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahã tsei kakadaji ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni miduɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Tall shade trees protect young cocoa plants from harsh direct sunlight and heavy winds that can burn leaves and dry out the soil. The shade trees also drop leaves that rot and turn into natural plant food for your cocoa trees.
ga: Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi lɛ he. Shade tsei hu shwieɔ baai ni egboi ni amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei niyenii kɛhaa o-cacao tsei lɛ.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is tired and needs manure or fertilizer before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli dani adu?

english: Tired soil often looks pale, forms hard crusts when dry, or produces weak crops with pale green leaves and small harvests. Adding animal manure or compost returns organic matter back into the ground, making the soil rich, soft, and full of food for new crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Efeɔ ŋshɔŋloo ni wa kɛji egbi. aloo ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyɛ blɛoo ni niyenii eyi mli obɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei.

english: Why is it bad to plant maize on the exact same spot on my farm every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize on the same spot every year drains the same specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that feed on maize to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility and starves out crop diseases.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ, ni ehaa tsei ahe helai baaa.

english: Maize leaves roll up during the hot afternoon as a natural defense mechanism to stop water from evaporating too fast from the plant. When the sun is hot and dry, the plant protects itself until temperatures cool down, but it is a clear sign your field needs water soon.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he koni nu akajɛ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ. Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baabu ehe he kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ. Shi eji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ hu akɛ nu he baahia oŋmɔji lɛ etsɛŋ.

english: Pepper flowers often fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the plant doesn't get enough water, or if beneficial insects like bees aren't around to pollinate them. Keeping the soil moist and avoiding heavy chemical spraying during flowering helps flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ shigbeemɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii nyɛɛɛ afee ŋmeii. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni ajie tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ babaoo yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ woɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔii lɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight over soil nutrients and water, while their leaves block sunlight from each other. This causes thin, weak stems and very small harvests because none of the plants get enough resources to grow strong.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ahaaa tso ko tso ko nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops turn pale green and grow slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi tso titri lɛ miifee eŋɔli ni edaa blɛoo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow aggressively and steal vital soil nutrients, water, and sunlight directly from your main crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to soil food and light so they can grow healthy and dark green.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ la fɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Which direction should I face my cassava stems when I push them into the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ ootsi ŋmei awo shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ ekwɛ?

english: You should always plant cassava stem cuttings with the small growth buds pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the stems will struggle to push out of the ground, resulting in small, twisted root tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmeii bibii adu o-cassava ŋmeii lɛ. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu lɛ kɛtee shishi lɛ Ebaawa akɛ oootsi tso lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii ni efite lɛ baa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my coconut seedlings turning bright yellow and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei ashishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on young coconut trees usually happen when the soil lacks essential nutrients like potassium or nitrogen, or when roots are sitting in waterlogged soil without proper drainage. Applying balanced fertilizer and clearing weeds around the base helps the tree recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei bibii anɔ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium loo nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ tara shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa atsu nii ni ojie jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. Konii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ shi.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because their leaves burn easily under direct harsh sunlight. Keeping shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects the young plants until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their natural healthy color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha su lɛ aku sɛɛ aba bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my cassava roots are growing well without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can tell cassava tubers are growing big beneath the ground when the base of the stem gets thick, the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and small cracks start appearing in the soil around the plant stem.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmei shishifã ko miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ ŋmei shishifã lɛ mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. kɛ ŋmeii bibii Amɛjeɔ shishi amɛjeɔ kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, usually caused by extremely hot daytime temperatures or sudden changes from very dry soil to heavy flooding.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ he. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji hulutsoo be mli latsaa ni naa wa waa loo tsakemɔ ni baa trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa nɔ kɛyaa nu afua ni naa wa nɔ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster on my cleared farm than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ miŋmɔ ni ajie lɛ mli lɛ fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native plants with seeds that sit naturally in the soil, ready to sprout instantly when exposed to rain and sun, whereas farm crops take longer to germinate and adapt to the soil.
ga: Jwɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni amɛdumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Efee klalo akɛ ebaakwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ kɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe fe shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: What will happen to my maize crop if I plant four or five seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ fee ekome yɛ bu kome mli?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole causes the crops to fight with each other for space, sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stalks and very small or missing cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awuu yɛ ŋwɛi, hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii he. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa loo ni bɛ mli baa.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain is often followed by several hot, dry days that dry up the soil and kill tender newly germinated seeds; it is safer to wait until the rains become regular.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ nyiɛɔ gbii babaoo ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ ni efiteɔ dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into tight little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee kɔɔpoi bibii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites feeding under the leaves, which causes the leaf tissue to twist as it grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ fiteɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily just when the heavy fruit bunch starts to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be mli ni aduawai ni tsii lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems rather than deep taproots, so when the fruit bunch becomes heavy at the top, strong winds can pull the weak roots out of the moist soil unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ moŋ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. ja akɛ tsɔne ko ni akɛ tsei fee tsu nii

english: Why do my yam plants need tall sticks to climb on to produce big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa niji ni kwɔlɔ koni ekwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji aba lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb upward to spread their leaves in full sunlight; capturing bright sunlight allows the plant to manufacture more food, which flows down to build large roots.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa tsei woɔ niyenii babaoo. ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ shishifãi wuji

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees keep turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your cocoa trees are starving for essential nutrients like nitrogen. When the soil lacks nutrients, the plant cannot produce the green color it needs to make food and grow strong.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-cocoa tso lɛ kɛha niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen. Beni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ ajie su ni ji eŋɔli ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ kpo.

english: Is chicken manure safe to put directly on my crop roots, or will it damage them?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ baawo mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ? Aloo ebaafite shishifãi lɛ?

english: Fresh chicken manure is very strong and can burn plant roots if used right away. It is best used when dried or aged into organic fertilizer so it releases nutrients gently without scorching the crops.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni afee ehee lɛ mli wa waa, ni ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi kɛ akɛtsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Esa akɛ akɛtsu nii kɛji egbi loo etsa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli. Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii jeɔ kpo blɛoo ni eshãaa tso lɛ.

english: Why do my crops seem to dry up quickly during the dry season even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu moŋ lɛ?

english: Soil without organic material cannot hold onto water for very long. Adding organic fertilizers like manure helps the soil hold moisture like a sponge, keeping water available for roots longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli lɛ nyɛŋ ahi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli tamɔ spunji. Ehaa nu baa kɛha shishifãi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my cocoa farm actually needs extra fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: If your cocoa trees grow very slowly, have pale leaves, or produce few pods each season, the soil nutrients are likely depleted and need extra food to help the trees recover.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cacao tso lɛ daa blɛoo waa, eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ, loo ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo komɛi yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Ekolɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hu etã ni niyenii krokomɛi he baahia koni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does animal waste make crops grow faster and stronger than leaving the soil as it is?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ashwiemɔ haa ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe shikpɔŋ ni ashiɔ lɛ?

english: Animal waste is rich in natural plant foods like nitrogen and phosphorus. These nutrients help plants build thick stems, green leaves, and strong roots much faster than poor soil can.
ga: Koolooi ashwiei amli eyi obɔ kɛ tsei aniyenii tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. Niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa, baai eŋɔli, kɛ shishifãi ni wa oya fe sũ ni ehiii.

english: Why do some of my cocoa trees drop their flowers before the pods even form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ekomɛi miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ po feɔ lɛ?

english: Trees drop their flowers when they are weak or stressed. If the tree does not have enough nutrients or water, it sacrifices the flowers because it lacks the strength to grow them into full cocoa pods.
ga: Tsei baashwie fɔfɔii kɛji amɛgbɔjɔ loo amɛmiifee basaa. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehe baahia ni akɛ fɔfɔi hu ashã afɔle ejaakɛ amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaadara ni amɛtsɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: What causes cocoa pods on my farm to stay small instead of growing big and heavy?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi bibii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ agbo ni amɛtsii?

english: Small pods usually happen when the tree lacks sufficient nutrients during the growing period. Without proper feeding, the tree cannot push enough energy into filling out the cocoa beans inside the pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii baa kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ahaaa niyenii ni sa lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aha hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ amli.

english: Can feeding my crops with organic fertilizer help them stay healthy against diseases?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hewalɛ kɛjɛ helai ahe?

english: Yes, just like well-fed people get sick less often, crops given proper organic nutrients build strong stems and roots, making them naturally more capable of surviving pest and disease attacks.
ga: Hɛɛ, taakɛ mɛi ni eye nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ hela mɔmɔɔɔ amɛ shii abɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni nine shɛɔ niyenii ni sa nɔ lɛ baaná shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni wa. Enɛ haa amɛjeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa amɛnɔ lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why is it better to feed my crops while they are actively growing rather than after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mahã miŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni amɛmiida lɛ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛ niyenii yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Crops consume the most energy while they are forming leaves, flowers, and fruits. Giving them fertilizer during active growth ensures they have food right when they need it to build your harvest.
ga: Tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii fe fɛɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ baai, fɔfɔi, kɛ aduawai. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo amɛmli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛkwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do crops planted in rich, dark soil perform better than those in hard, pale soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni edɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Dark soil usually contains decaying organic matter and manure, which makes it soft, full of plant food, and easy for crop roots to spread out and drink water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ yɔɔ mli. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo Eyi obɔ kɛ tsei niyenii Ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛnu nu mlɛo.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I clear away all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive. Tall trees act like huge umbrellas that block harsh sunlight, keep the air humid, and protect tender cocoa leaves from burning before their roots grow deep enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi. Tsei kakadaji feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akpɔlɔi wuji ni tsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni obuɔ kookoo baai ni mli tse lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he dani shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Plantains have shallow roots near the surface rather than a deep taproot. When the soil becomes soaked and heavy fruit bunches grow, strong winds easily push the tree over unless you support the stem with wooden props.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni aduawai babaoo kwɛ̃ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ashɛre tsei kɛba shi mlɛo. Ja okɛ tso ni akɛfee tsɔne lɛ fiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does my maize grow greener and stronger when I plant cowpeas or beans in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ shi ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɛɔ shi waa kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to grow, so planting legumes alongside it acts like a natural fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni aduɔ kɛfataa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.
