english: The first rain is often a 'false start' followed by days of hot sun. If you plant too early, the seeds will sprout but then dry up and die before the real rainy season settles in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ji ‘amale shishijee’ ni hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi amɛbaagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ aba.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and build high stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ni mafee tsei ni kwɔlɔ koni mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need full sunlight on their leaves to make food and grow large tubers. Lifting the vines off the ground on tall stakes keeps them out of shade and prevents moisture diseases from attacking the leaves.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛshɛ amɛbaai lɛ ahe kɛha nihoomɔ, ni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs agboi. Kɛ́ akɛ tso kakadaŋŋ wo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni wain tso lɛ akabote hulutsoo be mli, ni ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ helai ni fiteɔ baai lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my cassava roots become hard and woody if I leave them buried for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are at their best between 10 to 12 months. If left in the ground past their maturity, the plant starts drawing energy back from the root, turning soft starch into tough fibers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ yɛ nyɔji 10 kɛyashi 12 teŋ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛho amɛdalɛ be lɛ he. Tso lɛ baaje shishi ejie hewalɛ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ekoŋŋ. ni otsake starch ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ owo fibers ni wa mli

english: Why does mixing animal manure into my sandy soil help my crops during dry weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Animal manure acts like a sponge in the soil. It holds rainwater long after the surface has dried, giving crop roots a steady drink during short dry spells.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ sũ mli. Ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi sɛɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu be fɛɛ be yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli.

english: Why should I leave dry crop leaves on top of my soil instead of burning them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ moŋ fe ni mashã lɛ?

english: Leaving dry crop leaves on the soil creates a natural blanket called mulch. This blanket stops sunlight from drying out the earth, prevents heavy rain from washing topsoil away, and breaks down into food for your next crops.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ baa. Kuntu nɛɛ tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small balls and stopping fruits from forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee bɔɔlu bibii ni amɛmiikpa aduawai ni baa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out plant juices. Spraying early with neem oil or recommended insecticides stops the insects so the leaves can open up and bear fruit.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ nɔ mra. Etsiɔ kooloi bibii anaa koni baai lɛ agbele ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and soft before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the soil dries out completely between waterings or lacks calcium, causing the tip of the tomato fruit to starve and collapse.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ kwraa yɛ nu ni awoɔ lɛ teŋ loo calcium bɛ mli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tomato aduawai lɛ ashishi ni efoɔ.

english: Why is it necessary to keep shade trees on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees, especially young ones, need protection from intense sunlight and harsh winds. Shade trees keep the air humid, reduce heat stress on cocoa leaves, and protect the soil from drying out too fast.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei, titri lɛ tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Tsei ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli tseɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo baai lɛ anɔ lɛ shi. ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi oya tsɔ

english: How can I tell if my cocoa farm has too much shade or not enough shade?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be babaoo loo ebɛ hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: If there is too much shade, cocoa trees grow very tall and thin with few leaves and pods, and dampness can cause fungal diseases. If there is not enough shade, leaves burn, turn yellow, and the trees dry out easily under the hot sun.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ lɛ Cacao tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛbɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ. Ni hulutsoo baanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai aba. Kɛji hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ lɛ, baai lɛ baashã, ni amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Ni tsei lɛ baagbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi oya.

english: Why do pests keep multiplying on my cocoa farm even after I try to remove them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayi miifa lɛ? Yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli Eyɛ mli akɛ mibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni majie amɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ moŋ.

english: Pests often hide and breed in thick weeds, unpruned branches, and uncleared brush on the land. If the farm is overgrown and has no clear pathways, pests find safe places to survive and multiply quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ teeɔ amɛhe ni amɛfɔɔ yɛ jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli. Niji ni afolɔko amɛhe kɛ jwɛi ni mli tseee ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyi tsɔ ni gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ bɛ lɛ Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ naa he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛhi shi ni amɛfɔ oya.

english: Why should I clear paths and rows through my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie gbɛi kɛ linei ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Clearing paths allows sunlight and air to move freely through the farm, which dries out damp areas where pests and diseases thrive. It also makes it easier for you to walk around, monitor tree health, and harvest pods.
ga: Gbɛ ni agbele lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya. Enɛ haa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai yɔɔ lɛ agbiɔ. Eyeɔ ebua bo hu ni onyiɛɔ he fɛɛ he. Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ hewalɛnamɔ Ni ŋmeii lɛ akpamɔ hu waaa.

english: How does bushiness on my farm attract insect pests to my crops?
ga: Te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɔmɔ nii lɛ gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛbaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ?

english: Overgrown bushes trap moisture and create cool, dark hiding spots where harmful insects like capsids and mirids hide during the daytime before coming out to feed on your cocoa pods.
ga: Tsoi bibii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu ni amɛfeɔ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni yɔɔ duŋ. Kplukai ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids kɛ myrids lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ gbi lɛ mli dani amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye o-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ.

english: Why am I struggling to get good results when I apply chemicals to my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni maná yibii kpakpai beni mikɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Chemicals fail when they are applied at the wrong time, in wrong amounts, or onto land thick with weeds. If weeds cover the soil, the chemical cannot reach the target area, or it gets washed away by rain before working.
ga: Tsofai lɛ baafee nɔ ni ehiii kɛji akɛ akɛwo be ni esaaa mli, yɛ falɛ ni esaaa mli, loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni jwɛi eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji jwɛi komɛi yɛ ni ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsofai lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ loo nugbɔ baaho amɛ dani amɛtsu amɛnitsumɔ lɛ.

english: Can spraying weedkiller chemicals on my land harm my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mikɛshwieɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, if weedkillers touch the green stem or leaves of young cocoa trees, they can burn or kill the plant. Chemicals must be applied carefully away from the cocoa roots and lower stems.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ ta cacao tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi loo baai eŋɔli lɛ ahe. Amɛ baanyɛ ashã loo amɛ kpata cacao tsei hu ahiɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ tsofai awo mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ko ni kɛ kookoo shishifãi kɛ shishigbɛ shishifãi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ.

english: What is the safest way to treat my land with chemicals without destroying the soil?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mikɛ tsofai atsu mishikpɔŋ lɛ he nii ni mifiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Always measure chemicals according to instructions, wear protective gear, and avoid over-spraying. Using chemicals alongside manual weeding keeps the soil healthy while keeping weeds down.
ga: Susumɔ tsofai lɛ ahe be fɛɛ be yɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi anaa. Wo nibii ni buɔ mɔ he. ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ jwɛi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ fe nine lɛ he Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛfataa jwɛi ni akɛ niji tsuɔ he nii lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni egbeɔ jwɛi hu.

english: How do I manage the growth of my cocoa trees so they produce more pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ dalɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ŋmeii babaoo aba?

english: You manage cocoa growth by pruning off unnecessary branches and vertical shoots called chupons. This directs the tree's food and water into developing healthy flower cushions and big cocoa pods.
ga: Okwɛɔ kookoo lɛ dalɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ ni he ehiaaa, ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ ni ofoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ heɔ tso lɛ niyenii kɛ nu koni enyɛ efee fɔfɔi akushɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ kookoo ŋmɔji wuji.

english: What happens if I let my cocoa trees grow wild without trimming them?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji miha kookoo tso lɛ da yɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ naa ni mifolɔko tso lɛ he?

english: Untrimmed cocoa trees develop dense, tangled leaves that block light from reaching inner branches. This reduces pod production and traps humidity, causing pods to rot on the tree.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni afolɔko amɛhe lɛ feɔ baai ni ebɔle amɛhe ni tsiɔ la naa koni ekashɛ tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa pod ni ajieɔ lɛ baa shi ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it needs to grow leaves and stems. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted chicken manure to the soil will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsina ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my farmland has good soil before I clear it to plant crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa dani mafo mli koni madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Dark, crumbly soil that holds moisture well without becoming a muddy swamp is usually fertile. You can also look at wild weeds—if big, leafy green weeds grow quickly on the untouched land, the soil usually has enough natural nutrients for healthy crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli ewo muji ni hiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ ni etsɔɔɔ nubu ni mli ewo muji lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ. Obaanyɛ okwɛ koo mli jwɛi hu. Kɛji jwɛi ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ baai wuji lɛ kwɛ̃ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko eshɛko nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating small holes into the central leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. The caterpillars hide deep inside the funnel of the plant where leaves are softest, so applying neem oil or recommended sprays directly into the center of the plant early in the morning helps stop them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ agbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni baai lɛ ji bibii fe fɛɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpa amɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the liquid from the leaves, or by a plant virus they spread. Clearing weeds around the farm and spraying organic pest repellant helps keep these insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ajiemɔ Okwaayeli kɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi nɛɛ ahe.

english: Why do experienced farmers advise me to plant cowpeas or beans inside my maize farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. This acts like natural fertilizer for the maize while providing you with two different crops to harvest from the same plot of land.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa bo ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni obaakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight and heat. Fast-growing plantain trees produce broad leaves that act like giant umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa with shade and keeping the soil damp during hot months.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni miida oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela wuji. Ye obua ni abu kookoo tsei ahe kɛ hulutsoo. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nyɔji ni mli edɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their blossoms without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɛɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when weather gets extremely hot or when the soil gets too much nitrogen fertilizer, causing the plant to produce leaves instead of fruit. Gentle wind or insects shaking the flowers also helps them self-pollinate to form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli jɔ loo kooloo ko ni hosoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do some of my cassava tubers turn out small and woody when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmeii lɛ ekomɛi feɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ tsei beni mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots remain thin if weeds steal nutrients during the early months, or if the soil is too hard and compacted for the tubers to expand. Clearing weeds early and mounding loose soil around the base allows big roots to develop.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛji jwɛi ju niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ nyɔji lɛ amli. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa bulb lɛ agbɛ ashwã. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra kɛ sũ ni etse ehe ni abua naa yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ haa shishifãi wuji shwereɔ.

english: How can I tell the exact time my cassava crop is ready to be dug up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ?

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the earth near the base of the stem begins to crack open as expanding tubers push against the soil, typically around 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ shwereɔ kwraa kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni yitso ni mli elɛɛɔ lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees fall over in the wind right before the bunch matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains ni tsii lɛ miigbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and do not grip deep underground, so top-heavy bunches make the plant unstable. Supporting the main stem with a strong, Y-shaped wooden pole (staking) prevents strong winds from uprooting the tree.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛkpãaa shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, niji ni tsii lɛ baaha tso lɛ akafee nɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ. Tso tso (tso) ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni tamɔ Y ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekajie tso lɛ shishi.

english: Do I always have to wait for seeds to sprout before putting them into the soil?
ga: Ani be fɛɛ be lɛ, mimɛɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ dani miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: No, many crops can be planted directly into the soil as raw seeds without waiting for them to germinate or sprout first, saving you time and extra work.
ga: Dabi, abaanyɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni akwɛɛɛ ni amɛmɛɛɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ loo amɛkwɛ̃ klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ haa be kɛ nitsumɔ kroko baa shi.

english: What is the advantage of planting seeds directly into the ground instead of sprouting them first?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aaakwɛ̃ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ he?

english: Direct planting reduces handling hassle and avoids damaging tender young sprouts, allowing the seed to establish roots naturally in its final resting place.
ga: Dumɔ tɛ̃ɛ haa nɔkwɛmɔ feɔ mlɛo ni ehaaa tsei bibii lɛ afite. Enɛ haa dumɔwu lɛ shishifãi shwieɔ shi yɛ enaagbee he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: How long does it usually take for a coconut to sprout before it is ready to be planted?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ dani eshɛɔ he ni aduɔ?

english: Coconut germination is a slow process; it normally takes from 11 months onwards for a seed nut to produce a sprout that is mature enough for planting.
ga: Kokoo kwɛ̃mɔ ji nɔ ko ni yaa nɔ blɛoo. Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ nyɔji 11 kɛyaa dani ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii wuji ni fa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu.

english: How do I know that a coconut seedling is mature enough to put in the field?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei tso ko da bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ odu yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: A coconut sprout is typically ready for field planting when the sprout develops a sturdy, brown color, showing that it has matured past the tender initial green stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tsei feɔ klalo kɛha dumɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli beni tsei bibii lɛ ahe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei lɛ edara yɛ ŋmei ni mli tse lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Can I plant a freshly harvested coconut straight into my farm ground?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Unlike simple crops that can be planted right away, coconuts require a keeping period in a nursery until they sprout and reach maturity before being transferred to the field.
ga: Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ tsei ni afɔɔ namɔ ni abaanyɛ adu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ ahe. Ehe miihia ni akɛ be ato ŋmeii akwɛmɔhe lɛ kɛyashi amɛbaakwɛ̃ ni amɛdara dani abaanyɛ adu amɛ awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do coconut seeds take so much longer to sprout than regular farm crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei dumɔwui heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Coconuts have thick, tough outer husks and large inner reserves, making their natural germination process much slower—often taking almost a year—compared to small vegetable or grain seeds.
ga: Kokooi yɛ kponɔgbɛ fã ni mli tse, ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ, kɛ mligbɛ fã ko ni da waa. Enɛ haa amɛ adebɔɔ mli kwɛ̃mɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ yaa hiɛ fioo kwraa. Amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ (ni bei pii lɛ eheɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ afi) kɛ akɛto aduawai bibii loo ŋmaa ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ he.

english: Is it normal for a coconut sprout to turn brown, or is my seedling dying?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ ŋmei tsei baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ? Aloo midumɔwu lɛ miigbo?

english: It is completely normal; a sprout turning brown is a natural indicator that the shoot is maturing and becoming tough enough to survive outdoor field conditions.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kwraa. Tsofɔi ni tsɔɔ blɔfo lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsoi lɛ miida ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ kponɔgbɛ shihilɛi amli.

english: Why do different crops require different planting preparation methods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi biɔ gbɛi srɔtoi ni akɛduɔ lɛ?

english: Crops vary in their seed skin thickness and growth habits; some seeds sprout fast in moist dirt, while heavy tree seeds like coconuts need a long nursery period before field planting.
ga: Tsei lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishifã kɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa lɛ mli. Dumɔwui komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ sũ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni tsii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ dani aduɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: What happens if I try to plant a coconut before the sprout matures?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mibɔ mɔdɛŋ akɛ madu ŋmei dani tso lɛ kwɛ̃?

english: If you plant a coconut too early without waiting for the sprout to mature, the young plant may struggle to survive pests, harsh weather, and dry soil conditions.
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmeii oya tsɔ ni omɛɛɛɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ, Tsei bibii lɛ baanyɛ abɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛhi shi kɛjɛ ŋmeii amli. kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi shihilɛ

english: Do I need to keep coconut seed nuts in a special area before moving them to the farm?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmei dumɔwui ato he ko krɛdɛɛ dani ajie kɛya ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, coconuts are usually kept in a shaded nursery area where they can be monitored undisturbed for 11 months or more until their sprouts are ready.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, akɛ ŋmeii toɔ he ko ni ŋmeii yɔɔ ni abaanyɛ akwɛ nɔ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko gbaaa amɛnaa nyɔji 11 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ baafee klalo.

english: Why do I need to leave my freshly harvested cocoa beans in a pile for a few days before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishiɔ kookoo yibii ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi dani amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Fresh cocoa beans are covered in a sugary white pulp that must ferment and 'settle' first. This natural process breaks down the pulp, stops the bean from sprouting, and develops the rich chocolate flavor that buyers look for.
ga: Akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ futafuta ni esa akɛ atsɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ ni 'akɛwo shi' lɛ haa kookoo yibii heei ahe. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ nɛɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ. Kpaa ŋmeii dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni oná tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ.

english: Can I dry my cocoa beans in the sun immediately after breaking the pods open?
ga: Ani manyɛ magbi cocoa ŋmeii lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ ŋmeii lɛ etswa?

english: No, drying raw beans immediately without letting them ferment makes them purple, slaty, and bitter. The beans must first sit in a heap to ferment so the chocolate flavor can develop before sun drying.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ ogbi ŋmeii ni ahoko lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ohaaa amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛhe wa, ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ awo ŋmei mli klɛŋklɛŋ koni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ koni tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ lɛ aya hiɛ dani akɛwo hulu lɛ mli.

english: Why does liquid juice drip out from my cocoa heap during the first few days after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni ji nu jeɔ mi-kokoo ŋtayaa lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii fioo ni nyiɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: That liquid is called 'sweatings.' It is the sugary pulp melting away as yeast breaks it down, which allows the heap to settle and heat up properly for fermentation.
ga: Atsɛɔ nu lɛ 'latsaa'. Eji tsɔne ko ni sugar yɔɔ mli ni shwieɔ shi be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni edɔɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How do I know when my piled cocoa beans have finished fermenting and are ready to be spread out?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cocoa ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ egbe ŋmɔtɔ naa ni efee klalo akɛ abaagbɛ ashwã?

english: As cocoa settles during fermentation, the beans turn from purple to reddish-brown and smell sweet and vinegary. Once the juice stops dripping and the inside of the beans turn brown, they are ready for drying.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo ba yɛ ŋmɔtɔ be mli lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baatsake kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛya ŋmɔtɔ-ŋmɔlɔ mli. ni eŋɔɔɔ tamɔ vinegar. Beni nu lɛ kpaɔ shwiemɔ ni dumɔwu lɛ mli tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Amɛfee klalo kɛha ŋmɔlɔ.

english: What happens to my cocoa if I pour out the beans to dry too early before fermentation finishes?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo lɛ nɔ kɛji migbi kookoo lɛ yibii lɛ oya tsɔ dani ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ba naagbee?

english: If you end fermentation too early, the beans remain acidic, purple, and bitter inside, which significantly lowers the market quality and price of your cocoa.
ga: Kɛji ogbe ŋmɔtɔ lɛ naa mra tsɔ lɛ, Cocoa yibii lɛ baakã he afee acidic, purple, kɛ bitter, ni no baaha cocoa ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ kpakpa kɛ ejara aba shi waa.

english: What should I do if I harvest a huge volume of cocoa all at once?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mikpa kookoo babaoo shikome?

english: When handling a large harvest, break the beans into manageable heap sizes. Piling too much cocoa together without proper spacing can cause the center to overheat unevenly or rot before it ferments properly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ootsu nibii babaoo ni anáa lɛ he nii Jaa ŋmeii lɛ amli awo ŋmeii ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii amli. Kɛ́ akɛ kookoo babaoo to he ni gbɛ ni sa bɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha emli adɔ fe nine, efee nɔ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee loo efite dani edɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to turn or stir my heap of cocoa beans after two days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni atsake loo atsake kookoo ŋmeii lɛ yɛ gbii enyɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Turning the heap mixes the hot center beans with the cooler outer beans. This introduces air and ensures that the entire batch ferments uniformly without burning or developing mold.
ga: Nibii ni abua naa lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ ni mli ejɔ lɛ futuɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ baa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ shãa pɛpɛɛpɛ ni shãaa loo ŋmɔtɔ baaa.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to cover cocoa heaps with plantain leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛkuu nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ wɔ akɛ wɔkɛ plantain baai aha kookoo ni ato lɛ he lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves trap the heat and moisture produced by the beans, working like a living blanket that helps the heap reach the right temperature for even fermentation.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ni ŋmeii lɛ kɛbaa lɛ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni hiɛ ka ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋtayaa lɛ hiɔ hulutsoo be ni sa mli kɛha ŋtayaa.

english: Why does my cocoa bean heap get very hot inside after sitting for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ mli edɔ waa yɛ mli beni mita shi gbii fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heat is a sign of good fermentation. Microscopic organisms are actively breaking down the pulp sugars, generating heat that kills the bean germ and transforms the color and flavor inside.
ga: Dɔlɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa he okadi. Nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ miifite sugar ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ waa. Enɛ haa dɔlɛ ni gbeɔ ŋmei mli helai lɛ baa. ni etsake su kɛ emli ŋɔɔmɔ

english: How does careful management of my cocoa heap help me get a better price at the buying depot?
ga: Te mi-kookoo ni mikɛtoɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ ni maná jara kpakpa kɛjɛ mi-kookoo nitoohe lɛ?

english: Managing the heat, moisture, and turning schedules keeps the beans uniform, prevents mold, and ensures a deep brown color, which earns you a top quality grade from cocoa buyers.
ga: Dɔlɛ, fɛ̃i, kɛ okɔɔkpe nɔ nyiɛmɔ be yeɔ ebuaa ni anaa kɔfe yibii daa. Tsi fungus kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ naa Enɛ haa onine shɛɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ mɛi ni heɔ kookoo lɛ adɛŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without shade plants like plantains or temporary tree canopies, the leaves lose moisture faster than the roots can drink, causing them to burn and yellow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui loo ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni yɔɔ be kukuoo mli lɛ bɛ lɛ, Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. Ekɛ shãa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa.

english: What is making holes in my maize leaves and leaving sawdust-like dirt inside the plant stems?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi ŋmãa baai lɛ miifee bu ni amɛshi muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the leaf funnel during the day to feed on the tender young leaves, leaving behind small holes and chew marks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii. kɛtsɔ bu bibioo ko ni eshiɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ he okadii lɛ nɔ

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up, turning yellow, and staying very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle, eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ bibioo waa lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. The disease stops the leaf from producing enough food for the plant, which stunts leaf growth and reduces cassava root yield.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa Hela nɛɛ haaa baai lɛ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha tso lɛ. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ akakwɛ̃ ni ebaaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ayibii aba shi.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or cowpeas helps improve the soil for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that work with good soil bacteria to pull nitrogen directly from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants die, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil as natural food for your next crop.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai kpakpai tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii aha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do we need to make high dirt mounds to plant yam instead of just digging a small hole in flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni wɔma gɔji ni kwɔlɔ koni wɔkɛdu ŋmeii lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofo bu bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow large and long underground, so they need loose, deep soil to expand easily. Mounding creates soft soil space and improves drainage so water doesn't pool around the tuber and rot it.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ekɛ ehe afɔ̃ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli edɔ nɔ koni enyɛ egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Mounding haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baatsi nu ni ebɔle bulb lɛ he lɛ naa ni efite.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds as close together as possible so I can harvest more crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe bɔ ni manyɛ koni manyɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: If crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Spacing them properly allows every plant to get enough sunlight and food to produce larger, healthier cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu He ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry spell. If seeds germinate after one rain but don't get follow-up moisture within a few days, the delicate young sprouts will dry out in the warm soil and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ shi amɛnáaa ŋmɔtɔ gbii fioo komɛi. Tsei bibii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ baagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛbaagboi.

english: Watering early in the morning allows plants to absorb moisture before the sun gets too hot. Afternoon watering causes most of the water to evaporate instantly into the hot air before reaching the roots.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani hulu lɛ mli woɔ la tsɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and stronger than my planted crops after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive hard conditions with very deep roots. They quickly grab water and soil nutrients before your cultivated crops can establish their root systems.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ waa. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya dani onibii ni oduɔ lɛ baanyɛ ato shishifãi ahe gbɛjianɔ.

english: Why should I prune or snap off the extra small shoots growing out from my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ tomato tso lɛ mli lɛ

english: Removing extra side branches (suckers) focuses the plant's energy and nutrients into growing bigger tomatoes rather than wasting power trying to feed useless extra leaves.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ esɛɛ (tso lɛ tsei) ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa tomatoi wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oha lɛ baai ni fa fe nine ni he ehiaaa lɛ.

english: Why does my rice crop need to sit in water while other crops die in wet soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ nu awo ŋmãa tsei amli shi tsei krokomɛi gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air tubes in their stems that allow oxygen to reach their roots underwater, while flooding also protects them by drowning out competing weeds.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ shɛɔ nu shishi shishifãi lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu afua hu buɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ ni efoɔ amɛmli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the heads of my rice plants turning white and empty before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ futafuta ni nɔ ko bɛ mli dani akpaa lɛ?

english: White, empty rice heads are usually caused by stem borer insects that eat the inside of the plant stem, stopping nutrients from reaching the grain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi ni shwieɔ tso lɛ shishi ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmãa yitsei yɛŋ ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa. Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii nyɛɛɛ ashɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my rice so the grains do not drop onto the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? Koni ŋmãa lɛ akagbee shikpɔŋ?

english: Rice is ready to harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grain heads turn golden brown and the lower part of the stem starts to dry out.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ amli aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 batsɔ shika tsuru. ni tso lɛ shishigbɛ fã lɛ jeɔ shishi egbiɔ

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow instead of staying deep green during growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on growing corn usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants use to build green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to rotate my maize field with soybeans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔtsake ŋmãa ni atsakeɔ awoɔ soybeans mli lɛ?

english: Soybeans take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, which leaves free fertilizer in the ground for the next maize crop.
ga: Soybeans jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my corn stalks fall over when strong rain and wind hit the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Stalks fall over when roots are shallow due to compact soil, when plants are crowded too close together, or when insect damage weakens the stem base.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ hewɔ. Kɛji abua tsei anaa babaoo tsɔ loo kɛji kooloi bibii efite ni eha tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ gbɔjɔ.

english: Why do insects attack my crops more during dry spells between the rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hɔmɔ be mli, yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ lɛ?

english: Hot, dry weather stresses crops and makes their natural defenses weak, while warm temperatures cause pest insects to reproduce much faster.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ, ni egbi lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe lɛ baa shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulutsoo be lɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ oya kwraa.

english: What happens to my young crops if I apply too much chemical fertilizer at once?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsu nii tsɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Excess fertilizer pulls water away from plant roots like salt, burning the plant tissues and causing leaves to dry up and turn brown.
ga: Nyɔŋtsere ni fa fe nine gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso shishifãi amli tamɔ ŋoo, tso fãji ni shãa. ni ehaa baai lɛ gĩɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe niyenii ni adu lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants with deep roots designed to absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than domesticated crops can.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni afee koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe shia tsei.

english: How can I tell if my soil is ready for planting after the first rains arrive?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ eshɛ kɛha nidumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Squeeze a handful of damp topsoil; if it forms a soft ball that crumbles easily when gently tapped, it has the right balance of moisture and air for seed germination.
ga: Pinch off some moist topsoil. Kɛji akɛ etamɔ bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni fãa oya kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ blɛoo lɛ, no lɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa yɛ kɛha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Is it better for me to water my crops early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mitsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning allows the soil to absorb moisture before the sun gets hot, reducing evaporation and preventing heat shock or leaf burning on your crops.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani hulu lɛ mli woɔ la. Ha la ni hoɔ lɛ aba shi ni otsi latsaa loo baai ni shãa yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my crop leaves wilt during the hot afternoon even if the soil still has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo moŋ?

english: During peak afternoon heat, plants protect themselves by resting and closing their leaf pores to conserve water, which causes them to look limp temporarily until the sun cools down.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ shwane mli Tsei buɔ amɛhe he kɛtsɔ hejɔɔmɔ kɛ baai lɛ amli ŋmeii ni amɛŋaa koni nu ahi mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ be kukuoo ko kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulu lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do some of my crops grow poorly when I plant them right next to certain other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Just like people, crops have preferences; some plants release natural chemical substances into the soil or aggressively steal the exact same nutrients, which stunts neighboring crops.
ga: tamɔ gbɔmɛi Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ nɔ ni amɛsumɔɔ. Tsei komɛi jieɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofai kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo amɛkɛ ekãa juɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ baaha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ akã shi.

english: Tomatoes shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or water is inconsistent, because severe stress prevents the flower from pollinating and setting fruit.
ga: Tomato baajie efɔfɔi lɛ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu lɛ ejaaa. Yɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa hewɔ lɛ, fɔfɔi nyɛɛɛ afee pollination ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why shouldn't I work in my bean farm while the leaves are still wet with morning dew?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mitsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmei ŋmɔ mli be mli ni baai lɛ efɔ kɛ leebi ŋmɔtɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Moving through wet crops easily spreads fungal and bacterial diseases from plant to plant on your hands, clothes, and farm tools.
ga: Kɛ́ otsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli efɔ lɛ amli lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oniji, otadei, kɛ okwaayeli nibii anɔ oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and burn when exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to intense heat and need temporary shade trees like plantains to protect their delicate leaves while their roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Ni ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛbu amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ ema shi lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When maize is planted too tightly, the stalks compete fiercely for sunlight and stretch upward instead of putting energy into building thick stems and large ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa ni eyi obɔ lɛ tsɔ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ kɛ ehe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛma ŋmãa ni mli tse kɛ ŋmãa wuji.

english: How do I know my cassava is mature and ready for harvesting without digging up all the tubers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava lɛ edara ni efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ ŋmei muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can tell cassava is maturing when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and shed, and the soil around the base begins to crack open from the tubers expanding underground.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmei ko miida kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmei lɛ mli shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually a reaction to tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites, which drain the plant's energy and distort leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Enɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni efiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why does my soil turn into a hard crust after heavy rain instead of staying soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall on bare soil washes away light organic matter and packs the soil particles tightly together, forming a hard top crust that blocks future rainwater from soaking in.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ hoɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni waaa lɛ ahe. ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii bibii lɛ feɔ ekome jogbaŋŋ Efeɔ ŋmei ni wa yɛ nɔ ni tsiɔ nugbɔ nu ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ naa koni ekabote mli.

english: Young cocoa leaves are tender and lose moisture rapidly under full sun. Planting shade crops like plantains beside them creates a cool canopy that protects young trees from heat stress until they mature.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛmli shwieɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛyashiɔ tsei lɛ daraa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize crop turning yellow and dying off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the bottom of a maize stalk usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore leaf greenness and grain production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni dumɔwui lɛ hu aba.

english: How do I know if my cassava tubers are mature enough to harvest underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest when the main stem leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack due to expanding root tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha ŋmaa kɛji tso lɛ tso lɛ baai titrii lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifã lɛ mli shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why are my oil palm trees producing small bunches with very little oil in the fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii shi fɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Oil palms require consistent water and high potassium levels in the soil to form oil-dense fruits. Extended droughts or nutrient-depleted soil reduce both fruit size and oil volume.
ga: Nu kɛ potassium ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia mu tsei lɛ koni amɛwo yibii ni mu eyi mli obɔ. Hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ haa aduawai lɛ adalɛ kɛ fɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off before any fruits can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and sudden changes in soil moisture cause stress in tomato plants, leading them to drop their flowers as a survival mechanism rather than setting fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni tsakeɔ trukaa lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii amɛshwieɔ shi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: What is causing ragged holes and brown waste inside the leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni etse kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: Ragged holes with sawdust-like waste inside the leaf whorl are a sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which nest inside the growing tip of young maize plants.
ga: Buji ni egbɛ eshwa ni jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni feɔ amɛ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni miida lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ he okadi.

english: How does planting cowpeas on my farm help my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Te tsina ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to local soil conditions, allowing them to absorb water, sunlight, and nutrients more aggressively than cultivated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai fe tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines to climb wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔse mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni enyɛ ekwɔ tso tso nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha ekpã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking lifts yam leaves toward the sunlight so they can make food efficiently while keeping the foliage away from damp soil diseases that cause rot.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he koni enyɛ ehoo nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ehaa baa lɛ hu tsiɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ ahe.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are commonly caused by sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites, which damage young leaves and can spread plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Enɛ fiteɔ baai bibii ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwa tsei amli.

english: Yellow lower leaves are usually a sign that your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil food that keeps leaves green and healthy. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season helps prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. Enɛɛmɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Planting the same crop on the same plot year after year drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases to build up. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores soil fertility and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai bua amɛhe naa. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ ni ehaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with lots of leaves but only small roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ, ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi shishifãi bibii babaoo yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Excessive leafy growth with small tubers usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are shaded. Cassava needs full sunlight and balanced soil nutrients to direct its energy into growing big underground roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yaa hiɛ fe nine ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Hulu la ni fa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ja he miihia Cassava koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha eshishifãi wuji ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani maná yibii babaoo?

english: Planting too close forces your crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in weak plants and small yields. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to grow strong and produce heavily.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo ŋmaa babaoo.

english: How do I know when it is the right time to start planting after the first rain falls?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni sa akɛ odu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain because the soil underneath may still be dry. Wait until you have two or three strong rains that soak deep into the dirt so your seeds have enough lasting moisture to germinate.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi lolo. Mɛɛ ni oná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni eha odumɔwui lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Covering soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool and stops water from evaporating quickly in the hot sun, helping your crops survive dry spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Help your crops survive drought conditions.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily scorch in full, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates a protective shield until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaha gbɛtsii nii ko ni buɔ mɔ he aba kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye hulu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when the plant gets too hot or suffers from inconsistent watering. Keeping the soil constantly moist and cool helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ miipiŋ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi ni baatsɔ aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Why do small weeds harm my crops even if my crops are much taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi bibii miiye miŋmɔshi nibii awui lɛ? Shi kɛlɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ kwraa fe jwɛi lɛ.

english: Weeds steal vital water and soil food from beneath the ground before your crop roots can get them. Clearing weeds early ensures all the water and fertilizer go directly to feeding your crop.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aná. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are small holes suddenly appearing in the leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu bibii je kpo trukaa yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Small holes in young corn leaves are usually caused by caterpillars, such as fall armyworms, feeding on the plant. Checking your field early allows you to control them before they destroy the growing center of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ cutworms, ni egbee shi ni eye tsei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ baa. He ni okwɛɔ lɛ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okudɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ dani efiteɔ he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and drying up even when I water them with river water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ faa nu shwieɔ amɛnɔ moŋ?

english: If the river water is polluted with mud or chemicals from illegal mining (galamsey), it damages the root system instead of nourishing it. Polluted water prevents crops from taking up nutrients, causing leaves to yellow and wilt.
ga: Kɛji akɛ muji loo tsofai ni jɛɔ shika tsuru ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ (galamsey) mli lɛ ewo faa mli nu lɛ mli lɛ, ebaakpãtã shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ moŋ fe ni eeeha amɛ niyenii. Nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ baatsi tsei anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Is it safe for me to use muddy river water from nearby mining sites to irrigate my tomato farm?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ faa mli nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛ shika tsuru ŋmɔ ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ baatsu nii kɛshwie mi-tomato ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ nu?

english: Using river water contaminated with heavy mud and toxic chemicals clogs soil pores, smothers plant roots, and can transfer harmful substances into the crop, making the vegetables stunt or become unsafe to eat.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ faa mli nu ni muji ni tsii kɛ tsofai fɔji ewo mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsĩ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ anaa, efite tsei ashishifãi, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ feɔ mlɛo loo amɛhe ehiaaa ni ayeɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight and intense heat. They need shade crops like plantains planted around them to block direct heat and keep moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiisumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛhe. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni akɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily whenever there is a little wind or rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ loo nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy bunches of fruit. Poor soil conditions or removing too many supporting shoots can weaken the roots, making the plant easily uprooted by wind.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo ŋmeii ni fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ shwieɔ tsei lɛ oya.

english: Why does my farmland feel hard like concrete and refuse to absorb rainwater?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli wa tamɔ kɔnkrit ni ekpooɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ?

english: When topsoil is stripped away or heavy machinery compacts the earth, the soil loses its natural sponge-like structure. Without organic material, rainwater runs off the surface instead of soaking into the roots.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ loo tsɔnei ni tsii miitswa sũ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ tamɔ sponji lɛ. Kɛji akɛ nɔ ko bɛ ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ Nugbɔ nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with lots of leaves, but the tubers underground are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii?

english: When soil has an imbalance of nutrients or has been disturbed by land pollution, cassava puts all its energy into leaf growth rather than building starchy root tubers under the ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ejaaa loo mujiwoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbaa enaa lɛ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa lɛ. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ sisifã nɛ ngɛ kaa powder ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: Why is my maize staying very short and taking too long to produce ears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kooloi lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛjeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Stunted growth happens when soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, often caused by land degradation, nutrient runoff, or planting in exhausted soil without proper organic cover.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ fitemɔ hewɔ. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni hoɔ loo dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite nɔ ni nɔ ko ni wala yɔɔ mli ni sa bɛ nɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or poor soil conditions. Dropping flowers is the plant's way of saving energy to survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo latsaa he haomɔ mli. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, overly humid conditions. When cocoa trees lack proper air movement or canopy trimming, excess moisture allows the rot to take over the pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod rot baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli fe nine. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli loo afo ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ, Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbo ni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster on my farm than my main crops after the rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep, tough root systems designed to survive harsh conditions and grab water and nutrients faster than cultivated domestic crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tso ko ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni amɛhe wa. Afee amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli ni amɛjie nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ amɛmaŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops start to wilt and suffer after just a few weeks without rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛnaa amanehulu yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Crops need a constant supply of water to carry food and nutrients from the soil up into their leaves. When rain stops for a few weeks, the top layer of soil dries out, forcing plants to use up their internal water reserves until they begin to wilt under the hot sun.
ga: Tsei hia nu ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛkɛ niyenii kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya baai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ otsii fioo komɛi Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baagbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ atsu nu ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ he nii kɛyashi amɛbaabɔi ŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why is cantaloupe able to stay standing in my field during dry weather when other plants wither?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cantaloupe baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi gboɔ lɛ?

english: Cantaloupe is a naturally hardy crop with deep roots and tough stems that allow it to reach hidden moisture far below the dry surface soil and hold onto water better than delicate crops.
ga: Cantaloupe ji tso ko ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni wa ni haa enyɛɔ enine shɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ nɔ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni waaa kwraa lɛ.

english: What does it mean when people call a crop 'hardy'?
ga: Kɛ́ gbɔmɛi tsɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akɛ ‘hardy’ lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ?

english: A hardy crop is a tough plant that can endure harsh conditions like strong heat, poor soil, or long periods without rainfall without easily dying or losing its fruit.
ga: Nidumɔ nii ni wa ji tso ni wa ni baanyɛ adamɔ shihilɛi gbohii tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii, loo be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ ni egbooo loo ewooo yibii oya.

english: How can I tell if my crops are just thirsty or if they are permanently dying from heat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kumai miiye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛkɛ loo amɛmiigboi kɛmiiya naanɔ yɛ latsaa lɛ hewɔ?

english: If your plant leaves droop during the hot afternoon but bounce back in the cool evening, the crop is just thirsty. If the leaves stay dry, brown, and crispy even at night, the plant is dying from severe lack of water.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli shi eku esɛɛ eba yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tee nɔ amɛgbi, amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ, ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ gbɛkɛ po Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miigbo yɛ nu ni faaa waa yɛ emli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Is transporting water by containers from far away enough to keep my farm healthy during a dry patch?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛyaa he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ kɛtsɔ tsɛnsi nɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha miŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Carrying water manually helps save crops from dying, but it usually only waters the soil surface. Because crops need deep water soaking to build strong roots, hand-transported water is often only a short-term survival fix.
ga: Nu ni bo diɛŋtsɛ ooowo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii akagboi. Shi bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ pɛ afɔɔ nɔ nu. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehe miihia ni tsei lɛ atsɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. No hewɔ lɛ nu ni akɛ niji haa lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahiɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli pɛ.

english: What happens to the soil on my farm when it does not receive rain for almost a month?
ga: Mɛni baa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ nɔ aaafee nyɔŋ kome?

english: Without rain for several weeks, soil bakes under the sun, hardens, and loses its moisture. This makes it difficult for plant roots to breath, absorb nutrients, or grow deeper into the ground.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ otsii babaoo lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ shãa yɛ hulu lɛ shishi, ewaa, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa shi. Ehaa tsei ashishifãi lɛ muɔ ni amɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ loo ewaa akɛ amɛaakwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ

english: How can I keep the moisture in my soil from disappearing so quickly during dry weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekalaaje oya yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: You can place dry grass, crop leaves, or straw around the base of your plants. This layer, called mulch, acts like a blanket that shades the dirt and stops the sun from evaporating the water in the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi, baai, loo jwɛi abɔle tso lɛ shishi. Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋtayaa nɛɛ akɛ mulch. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni tsiɔ muji naa, ni ehaa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: What main problems will I face if I try to expand my crop farming to a larger scale?
ga: Mɛɛ naagbai titrii mikɛbaakpe kɛji mibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Scaling up a farm requires much more water, labor, seeds, and equipment. If you expand without guaranteed water sources or community and financial support, a sudden dry spell can destroy a much larger investment.
ga: Ni aaaha ŋmɔ ko mli alɛɛ lɛ biɔ nu, nitsumɔ, kɛ dumɔwui. kɛ nibii babaoo Kɛji oogbɛ onitsumɔ lɛ oshwã ni nu jɛɛhe ko ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ loo akutsoŋ kɛ shika he yelikɛbuamɔ bɛ mli lɛ, Hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni baa trukaa lɛ baanyɛ afite shika babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow slowly even though I put in hard work on my farm every single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ mitsuɔ nii waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Hard work clears weeds and prepares the land, but crops rely heavily on water, sunlight, and soil nutrients to grow. Without adequate water or plant food, hard labor alone cannot force crops to develop faster.
ga: Nitsumɔ ni wa yaa mli yɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ mli. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ waa koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji nu loo tsei niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Nitsumɔ ni wa pɛ nyɛŋ anyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni amɛya hiɛ oya.

english: Which types of crops should I choose to plant if rainfall in my area is unreliable?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ mahala kɛji akɛ anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: It is best to choose drought-tolerant crops like cantaloupe, cassava, millet, or sorghum. These plants have natural defense mechanisms that allow them to survive long breaks between rains.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohala tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa tamɔ cantaloupe, cassava, ŋmei, loo ŋmei. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoi ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hejɔɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants dropping off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during dry spells to save water and protect itself from drying out. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing normally.
ga: Yucca shwieɔ ebaai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eda bɔ ni sa.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food for leaf growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore the green color and makes the crop grow strong.
ga: Abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cocoa flowers often drop if the tree does not get enough water, lacks nutrients, or lacks tiny insects like midge flies to pollinate them. High heat and extreme dry weather can also cause the tree to shed flowers to save energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni baaha amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ mli. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa baanyɛ aha tsei afɔlɔ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my tomatoes turning black and rotten before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when the tomato plant cannot get enough calcium or experiences irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant take up the nutrients it needs to produce healthy fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i be fɛɛ be lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens to my pepper plants if I sow the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When pepper plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves them weak, thin, and prone to diseases, resulting in much smaller fruit yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, amɛhe waaa, amɛhe waaa, ni helai srɔtoi nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibii ni anáa lɛ faaa kwraa.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and bushy in one section of my farm but stay short and weak in another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ ni amɛmiifee jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã ko nɔ lɛ? Shi eyɛ kuku lolo ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ fã kroko mli.

english: Soil quality varies across a farm due to differences in organic matter, shade from surrounding trees, or water drainage. Adding compost or fertilizer to the weaker areas helps equalize growth across your whole field.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su yɛ srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ hewɔ. Shade ni jɛ tsei ni ebɔle ohe lɛ amli loo nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ jɛmɛ lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo hei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii po aya hiɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Is it a good idea for me to plant my crops right next to a riverbank?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ madu tsei yɛ faa lɛ naa?

english: Planting near a river provides good moisture during dry periods, but roots can rot if the soil stays constantly waterlogged. Strong floodwaters can also wash away young crops and fertile topsoil during heavy rains.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ faa ko masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo be kpakpa baa. Shi shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbo kɛji akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Nu afua ni naa wa baanyɛ ashwie ŋmɔshi nibii bibii kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my vegetables curl up and turn brown during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ brown yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl during intense midday heat to limit water loss through evaporation. If the soil has enough moisture, the leaves usually recover and relax by late afternoon as temperatures cool down.
ga: Ha ni ebɔle ehe yɛ shwane mli latsaa be lɛ mli koni nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, baai lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhe ajɔ amɛ ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe beni shwane shɛɔ. Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ

english: How do I know beneath the ground that my cassava roots are mature enough to dig up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mafo mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack as the enlarging tubers push the ground upward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni tso lɛ ni eda lɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot so quickly after I dig them out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if their skin gets cut or damaged during harvesting, allowing fungi and bacteria to enter. Curing the yams in a cool, shaded, and well-ventilated area helps wounds heal and extends storage life.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ afo hewolo lɛ loo efite yɛ kpamɔ be mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi baanyɛ abote mli. Kɛ́ atsa sweet potatoes yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ, lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsa ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do some seeds split open when they start growing in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi tswaa kɛ́ amɛbɔi kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seed splitting is a natural step during germination. Water softens the outer coat and causes the inside of the seed to expand, breaking the hard shell open so the green shoot can grow up and the root can grow down into the soil.
ga: Seed separation is a natural step during germination. Nu haa kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa dumɔwu lɛ mligbɛ lɛ mli lɛɛɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yibii ni wa lɛ gbeleɔ koni ŋmeii eŋɔli anyɛ akwɛ̃ ni shishifãi anyɛ akwɛ̃ kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my palm nuts take so many months to sprout compared to other crop seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-palm dumɔwui lɛ heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛ akɛto dumɔwui krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Palm nuts have a very hard outer shell and a period of natural sleep called dormancy. They require heat and moisture over a long time to break the shell and wake up the living seed inside before it can sprout.
ga: Palm ŋmeii yɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa waa ni amɛtsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe be ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy lɛ mli. Amɛhe miihia ni amɛná dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ koni amɛgbala ŋmei lɛ mli ni amɛte dumɔwui ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shi dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Can I plant fresh cocoa seeds straight from a ripe pod onto my land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo yibii heei tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli?

english: Yes, fresh cocoa seeds can grow directly from a ripe pod, but you must plant them almost immediately. Cocoa seeds dry out very fast once removed from the pod and will lose their power to sprout within a few days.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kookoo ŋmeii heei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Shi ehe miihia ni odu lɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya waa kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. ni ebaafite nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli.

english: Why do my seeds need soft, moist soil around them to germinate well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni mli edɔ he hiaa mi dumɔwui lɛ? Koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Soft soil holds essential moisture and makes it easy for fragile new roots to push deep into the earth. If the soil is too hard, the young sprout wastes energy trying to push through and can die before reaching the surface.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa lɛ hiɔ shi, ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa shishifãi heei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ akɛ amɛbaatsi amɛhe kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ mli lɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi dani amɛshɛ nu lɛ hiɛ.

english: How can I tell if a young sprout breaking through the soil will grow into a healthy plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwu ni afo awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baatsɔ tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: A strong sprout will have a thick, firm stem and deep green leaves. This shows that the seed had strong stored energy and its root system is successfully pulling water and nutrients from the soil.
ga: Tsei bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ tsei bibii ni mli wa, ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛ baai eŋɔli ni tsuɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ko ni ato ni mli wa. Ni eshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: Is it better for me to plant seeds saved from my own harvest or buy new ones from agro-dealers?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ loo mahe dumɔwui heei kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ?

english: Seeds saved from your farm are cheap, but certified seeds from agro-dealers are specially bred to resist diseases and produce much higher yields than traditional local seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ jara waaa. Shi akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni jɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni akɛtsuɔ nii tsutsu lɛ.

english: Can I just pick any palm nut from a wild tree on my farm to grow a new oil palm tree?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafo ŋmei dumɔwui kɛjɛ koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli koni mikɛdu mu tsei heei?

english: While wild palm nuts will grow, they often yield trees with thick shells and very little palm oil. Certified nursery seedlings are bred to give thin-shelled nuts with much more oil and heavier fruit bunches.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ koo mli tsei ni atsɛɔ amɛ palm lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ moŋ Shi esumɔɔ ni eha tsei ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmei fɔ fioo ko pɛ. Akwɛ ŋmɔ mli dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ koni amɛfee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni fɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Do crops like cocoa or oil palm have distinct male and female seeds when I plant them?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo loo mu tso lɛ yɛ dumɔwui hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi kɛ́ midu amɛ?

english: No, the seeds themselves are not male or female. A single crop seed contains the genetic material to grow a tree that will produce both male parts (to shed pollen) and female parts (to produce the fruit).
ga: Dabi, seshi lɛ jeee nuu loo yoo. Dumɔwu kome pɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ fɔmɔ nii ni baaha tso ko akwɛ̃, ni baaha nuu kɛ yoo fãi fɛɛ aba. (koni ajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi amli) kɛ yoo fã lɛ (koni ekɛwo)

english: Why do so many flowers on my trees drop off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Crops produce male flowers solely to release pollen to fertilize the female flowers. Once the male flowers finish shedding their pollen, their job is done and they naturally drop off the tree.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi hii ni jieɔ pollen pɛ koni fɔfɔi yei awo amɛmli. Kɛ fɔfɔi hii lɛ egbe pollen lɛ jiemɔ naa lɛ, Amɛnitsumɔ lɛ egbe naa ni amɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do some of the fruits on my crops split open before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Fruit splitting usually happens when a dry spell is suddenly followed by heavy rain. The plant drinks up a large amount of water quickly, making the inside of the fruit expand faster than the skin can stretch.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai amli gbalamɔ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ nyiɛ sɛɛ. Tsei nuɔ nu babaoo oya. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ amli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why should I plant soybeans on my farm instead of only growing maize?
