ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu soybeans yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ŋmãa kɛkɛ?

english: Soybeans add natural nutrients like nitrogen back into your soil to keep it fertile. They also sell for good prices because feed factories need them to make rich protein feed for livestock.
ga: Soybeans kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii tamɔ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eha ehi shi jogbaŋŋ. Amɛhɔ̃ɔ amɛ hu yɛ jara kpakpa nɔ ejaakɛ niyenii afeemɔ hei biɔ ni amɛfee niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ protein kɛha kooloi.

english: Which crops can I grow in Ghana that provide the highest protein for livestock?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ Ghana ni haa mikooloi lɛ náa protein babaoo fe fɛɛ?

english: Soybeans and groundnuts are among the best protein-rich crops you can grow. These crops store high amounts of protein in their seeds, which animals need to grow strong and produce eggs or milk.
ga: Soybeans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni protein babaoo yɔɔ mli ni obaanyɛ odu lɛ ateŋ ekomɛi. Tsei nɛɛ toɔ protein babaoo yɛ amɛdumɔwui amli. ni ehe hiaa ni kooloi lɛ adara ni amɛhe wa ni amɛwo ŋmeii loo mliki

english: Can I feed freshly harvested raw soybeans directly to my goats and pigs?
ga: Ani manyɛ maha soybeans ni akpa ehee lɛ niyenii? Ani manyɛ mikɛha mitooi kɛ tsinabii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, raw soybeans contain natural compounds that make it hard for farm animals to digest them. You need to roast or heat-process the beans first so the animals can safely absorb the rich protein.
ga: Dabi, adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa ewaa kɛhaa ŋmɔ mli kooloi akɛ amɛaaye nii yɛ soybean ni ahoko lɛ mli. Esa akɛ oshã loo okɛ la atsu nii klɛŋklɛŋ bɔni afee ni kooloo lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ protein ni fa babaoo lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: What is soya meal, and how is it made from the soybeans I grow?
ga: Mɛni ji soybean niyenii? Ni te afeɔ tɛŋŋ kɛjɛɔ soybeans ni miduɔ lɛ mli?

english: Soya meal is the solid protein material left behind after oil is squeezed out of dried soybeans. It is ground up and mixed with other grains to make feed for poultry, pigs, and fish.
ga: Soybean niyenii ji protein ni mli wa ni ashiɔ yɛ be mli ni ajie fɔ kɛjɛ soybean ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Agbɛɔ ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmaa krokomɛi. akɛ niyenii kɛha kooloi, tsinai kɛ loo

english: Why do my pigs and chickens need different types of feed made from my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niyenii srɔtoi he hiaa mi tsinai kɛ kooloi lɛ? ni akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii fee

english: Chickens and pigs build their bodies differently and have different digestive systems. Laying hens need feed with specific minerals for eggshells, while pigs need feed structured for building heavy meat.
ga: Kooloi kɛ tsinabii yɛ gbɔmɔtsoi srɔtoi kɛ niyenii ni amɛyeɔ lɛ srɔtoi. Niyenii ni mineral pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɔɔ mli kɛha amɛwui lɛ he miihia kooloi ni fɔɔ bii lɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ he miihia tsinai koni amɛná loo ni tsii.

english: Why do feed makers combine maize with soybeans when making animal food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni feɔ kooloi aniyenii lɛ kɛ ŋmãa kɛ soybeans feɔ ekome beni amɛfeɔ kooloi aniyenii lɛ?

english: Maize gives farm animals energy to move and stay warm, while soybeans give them protein to build muscle and repair body tissues. Combining both gives the animals a balanced, complete diet.
ga: Abɛi haa ŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛtsi amɛhe ni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, soy haa amɛ protein ni haa amɛfeɔ fãji ni amɛsaa gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli fãji lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii enyɔ nɛɛ futu mli lɛ, ehaa kooloo lɛ naa niyenii ni yeɔ emuu ni sa.

english: How do I know the right amount of soybean feed to give my farm animals at different ages?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male soy abɔ ni sa ni mikɛbaahã miŋmɔ mli kooloi ni eye afii srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Young animals need higher protein feed made with more soybeans so they can grow fast. As they get older, they need more energy grains like maize, so you change the feed mix based on their age group.
ga: Koolooi bibii lɛ he miihia niyenii ni protein babaoo yɔɔ mli ni akɛ soybeans babaoo fee lɛ koni amɛdara oya. Kɛ amɛdara lɛ Amɛmiitao ŋmaa ni haa hewalɛ babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa, koni onyɛ otsake niyenii ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ mli yɛ amɛ afii akuu lɛ naa.

english: How does growing a crop of soybeans help improve the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ soybeans ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soybeans are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies after harvest, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Soybeans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛ tsei gboi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Nakai nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni odu lɛ niyenii.

english: How should I store my harvested soybeans so they do not spoil before selling them?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ mi-soybeans ni mikpa lɛ ato koni ekafite dani mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Make sure the grains are thoroughly dried under the sun until they are hard. Store them in clean bags raised off the floor on wooden planks in a dry room to keep out mold and bugs.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la shishi kɛyashi ebaawa. Okɛ amɛ awo kotoku ko ni mli tse mli ni awo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tso shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ tsu ko ni mli egbi mli. Koni akafee ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi bibii

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in damp, wet weather. Clearing weeds and trimming overgrown shade tree branches helps air flow through the farm to dry the pods faster and prevent the fungus.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi oya ni ekɛtsi ŋmeii anaa.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants full of holes with sawdust-like dirt inside the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu ni muji tamɔ ŋmei yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm damage. The caterpillars hide deep inside the growing tip (whorl) of the maize plant and eat the leaves, which can stunt the crop's growth if not caught early.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ efite nii. Kplukai lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shishigbɛ (rings) ni miida lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsei adalɛ naa kɛji akɛ amɔmɔɔɔ amɛ mra.

english: Why are my cassava leaves twisting, curling up, and turning yellow with green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ, ebɔle ehe, ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Your cassava plant has Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by small whiteflies or by using infected stem cuttings. The disease weakens the plant's leaves so it cannot make enough food, resulting in very small tubers.
ga: O ŋmei tso lɛ yɛ ŋmei mosaic hela. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ. Hela lɛ haa tso lɛ baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni ehaaa enyɛ ewo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, yitso lɛ ji bibioo kwraa.

english: Why do I need to cut away the extra small suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Leaving too many suckers around one plantain tree causes them to compete for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, ensuring your main tree produces large, heavy bunches.
ga: Ni aaashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he Dumɔwu kome pɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ojie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi, ni no baaha otso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do my yam vines produce bigger tubers when I stake them with wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ bulbs wuji fe tsutsu lɛ beni mikɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants use their leaves to catch sunlight to make food. Lifting the vines off the ground with stakes allows the leaves to get maximum sunlight and airflow, which feeds the underground tuber so it grows thick and healthy.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ hulu la ni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo. ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii koni eha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before they form any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers from heat stress, irregular watering, or lack of soil food. When the soil gets too dry during hot days, the plant drops its flowers to save water for its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni ashwieɔ shi yɛ be ni sa mli loo niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto nu kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛshihilɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas first make my soil better for maize in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special root nodules that pull nitrogen from the air and leave it in the soil. When the crop is harvested, that natural plant food stays in the ground to nourish your next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni eshiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Why does chemical fertilizer burn my crops if I place it right against the plant stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shãa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji mikɛma tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain concentrated salts. Placing them directly against the stem or root crown draws moisture out of the plant tissues, scorching them. Fertilizer should always be applied in a ring a few inches away from the stem.
ga: Fertilizer lɛ yɛ ŋoo babaoo. Kɛ́ okɛwo tso lɛ shishi loo shishifã lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli. ni charred them Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ring mli ni kɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetables with dry grass during the hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔleɔ aduawai ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves (mulching) acts like a blanket. It stops the sun from drying out the moisture in the ground, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from sprouting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ akagbi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Why do weeds make my young crop turn yellow and grow so slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi dumɔwui lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiida blɛoo waa lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that quickly suck up water, light, and soil nutrients before your young crops can reach them. Without enough nutrients, crop leaves turn pale yellow and growth stalls.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni wa ni baanyɛ agbala nu, la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli oya dani tsei bibii lɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni edalɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow and my harvest getting smaller every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mikpamɔ lɛ miifee bibioo daa afi lɛ?

english: When leaves turn yellow and yield drops, it often means a crop disease like swollen shoot is blocking the tree from taking up water and food. The tree slowly weakens, producing fewer pods until it dies.
ga: Kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yibiiwoo lɛ ba shi lɛ Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso hela ko, tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ miitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekaŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii. Tso lɛ baagbɔjɔ fiofio ni ebaawo ŋmeii fioo komɛi kɛyashi ebaagbo.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa farm is producing less pod because of a disease or just because the trees are getting old?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo yɛ hela hewɔ loo tsei lɛ miigbɔ kɛkɛ?

english: Old trees slow down production gradually across the whole farm. A disease causes sudden drops in yield, creates swollen stems, deforms pods, or leaves patches of dying trees next to healthy ones.
ga: Tsei momo lɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi fiofio yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Hela lɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi trukaa, ni eshishifãi lɛ efuu, eshishifãi lɛ etsake, loo ashɛrɛ ashwie shi. ni ji tsei ni miigboi ni bɛŋkɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce small, withered pods that stop growing before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? No shwieɔ ni ekpaa dalɛ dani eshɛɔ?

english: When a cocoa tree is infected with a virus, it loses the strength to feed its pods. The pods starve, remain small, turn black or dry, and fail to mature properly.
ga: Kɛji kookoo tsei lɛ ná hela ko ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ Enyɛŋ eha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ, amɛfeɔ bibii, amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ loo amɛgbiɔ. ni enyɛŋ eda jogbaŋŋ

english: How does a crop disease move from one tree to another on my farm?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Diseases spread through tiny insects like mealybugs carried by ants, through direct root contact underground, or through cut tools that were used on sick trees and then on healthy ones.
ga: Hela nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs ni ŋmeii woɔ lɛ anɔ. kɛtsɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni akɛbaatswa tɛ̃ɛ loo kɛtsɔ nibii ni akɛfoɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa trees look healthy even though the trees right next to them are dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ekomɛi tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa eyɛ mli akɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ miigboi moŋ?

english: A tree can carry a virus for several months before showing visible signs like yellow leaves. It may look healthy today, but the disease could already be working inside it.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ aŋɔ hela lɛ nyɔji babaoo. dani ejie okadii ni anaa tamɔ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ Ŋmɛnɛ ekolɛ ebaafee tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ. Shi hela lɛ nyɛɔ etsuɔ ​​nii momo.

english: Can a disease on my neighbor's farm cross over and ruin my crops?
ga: Ani hela ko ni yɔɔ akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ afo mli ni efite minibii?

english: Yes, insects, wind, animals, and shared farm tools carry diseases across farm boundaries. Working together with neighbors to manage sick trees helps keep everyone's farm safe.
ga: Hɛɛ, koolooi, kɔɔyɔɔ, kooloi, kɛ okwaayeli nibii ni ajaa hiɛɔ helai kɛtsɔɔ okwaayeli husui lɛ anɔ. Akutsoŋbii ni akɛ amɛ tsuɔ nii koni akɛkwɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ŋmɔ lɛ feɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut down my cocoa trees when they get sick instead of giving me chemical sprays?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mifo kookoo tso lɛ beni hela mɔ mi lɛ moŋ fe ni eeeha mi tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Viral diseases live inside the tree's sap where chemical sprays cannot reach. Cutting down the infected tree is the only proven way to kill the virus and stop it from spreading to the rest of your farm.
ga: Helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli, ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni aaafo lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni ana he odaseyeli ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbeɔ hela lɛ ni atsĩɔ enaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa hei krokomɛi. ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: If I cut down my sick trees, won't I lose all my farm income?
ga: Kɛ mifo tso ko ni hela mɔ lɛ Ani shika ni mináa yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ baaje midɛŋ?

english: Cutting sick trees feels like a loss today, but leaving them allows the disease to spread and kill your entire farm. Cutting the sick ones saves your remaining trees so you keep earning money.
ga: Tso ni hela mɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eji fitemɔ yɛ nɛkɛ gbii nɛɛ amli. Shi kɛ́ oshi lɛ pɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni egbe oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ. Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ baaye abua ni ohere tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ ayiwala koni oya nɔ oná shika.

english: Is there any strong fertilizer I can apply to heal a diseased cocoa tree and bring back the yield?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi yɛ ni abaanyɛ akɛtsa kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ni akɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba ekoŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer helps healthy trees grow, but it cannot cure a viral disease. Applying fertilizer to a sick tree only feeds the leaves temporarily while the virus continues to spread underground to nearby trees.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa waa. Shi enyɛŋ etsa helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa wo tso ni hela mɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ená niyenii yɛ be kukuoo mli yɛ be mli ni hela lɛ yaa nɔ egbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: How long do I need to wait after cutting down infected cocoa trees before I can safely plant new seedlings?
ga: Kɛ́ ofo kookoo tso ni hela emɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani obaanyɛ odu dumɔwui heei shweshweeshwe?

english: You should wait until all the old roots are completely dead and cleared, usually a few months, so that disease-carrying insects leave the area and cannot infect your new young plants.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shishifãi momo lɛ fɛɛ gboi ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ nyɔji 2-3 dani ŋmeii ni hiɛ hela lɛ shiɔ jɛmɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo dumɔwui heei amli hela.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and scorching in the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade from taller plants like plantains or shade trees because direct sunlight burns their tender leaves before their root system is fully developed to draw enough water.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui biɔ hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ebaai bibii lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why is my maize turning yellow starting from the lower leaves going upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ baai lɛ ashishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the lower leaves of maize usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient the plant needs to build strong green leaves and healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and smaller or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers before any tomatoes start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani tomatoi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when they experience extreme heat or when soil moisture fluctuates too drastically between being too dry and completely flooded.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa ba amɛnɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ tsakeɔ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ kɛ nu ni eyi mli obɔ lɛ teŋ.

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry hot spell that can dry out the upper soil and kill young seeds that have just germinated before the main rains stabilize.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nyiɛɔ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ ni baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ agbi ni efite dumɔwui bibii ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ aba shi.

english: How do I know if Fall Armyworms are attacking my maize leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji Fall Armyworms miitutua mi ŋmãa baai lɛ?

english: Look inside the central funnel of the plant for ragged holes on leaves and small brown, sawdust-like droppings left behind by the caterpillars.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ koni ona bu ni ekumɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Brown, ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii shwieɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ lɛ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high up into full sunlight so the plant can produce more energy, which flows down to build large, heavy yam tubers underground.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛnáa hulu la ni fa babaoo. koni tsei anyɛ ajie hewalɛ babaoo Efoɔ kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ yam ŋmeii wuji ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do weeds lower my crop yield even if I apply fertilizer to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and will absorb the applied fertilizer, water, and sunlight first, effectively starving your crops of the inputs you provided.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. ni ebaaŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ hulu la klɛŋklɛŋ Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye onibii kɛjɛ nibii ni okɛhaa lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cover the dry soil around my crops with dried grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he? ŋmɔshi nibii ni jwɛi loo baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli

english: Covering the soil with organic material (mulching) keeps the ground cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly in the sun, and suppresses weed growth.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa

english: How do I choose the right cassava stems to cut for planting my next crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tso ni sa ni mafo kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Select thick, mature stems from strong, disease-free plants that are 8 to 12 months old, ensuring the stem nodes are healthy and close together.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ amɛhe ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 lɛ amli tsei ni mli tse ni eda ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning yellow during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants curl and drop leaves during long dry spells to conserve water and protect themselves from heat, but yellowing can also mean the plant is stressed by mealybugs or lacks key nutrients in dry soil.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Shi ŋmɔŋ baanyɛ atsɔɔ hu akɛ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ mealybugs mli loo niyenii titrii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize plants grow taller and greener when I plant cowpeas in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji beni miduɔ tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpea roots capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural food source that nourishes nearby maize plants and helps them grow stronger.
ga: Cowpea shishifãi lɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why are all the blossoms falling off my pepper plants without producing any actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather becomes too hot or when the soil lacks adequate water and nutrients like potassium, preventing the fruit from setting.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa tamɔ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ shwieee shi.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and bent instead of long and thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam roots require loose, deeply cultivated soil to expand easily; when soil is hard, stony, or poorly prepared, the roots struggle to push down, resulting in bent or small tubers.
ga: Sweet potato shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni egbɛ eshwa oya kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo asaaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Shishifãi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi kɛya shi. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi loo efeɔ bibioo.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the tree before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in dark, overly humid conditions where trees are shaded too densely and lack sunlight or fresh air flow.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Fungal hela ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni fa fe nine. he ni tsei ahe ŋmɔlɔ yɔɔ tsɔ ni hulu la loo kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ko bɛ ni tsɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves look like they have tiny holes chewed into them and dry powder inside the shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ buji bibii ni atsɔ mli kɛ powda ni egbi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central shoot of the maize plant during the day, eating the leaves and leaving behind sawdust-like droppings.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ ŋmeii amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai ni amɛshiɔ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce a huge clump of green leaves but almost no big tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi tomato agbo ko kwraa bɛ lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen causes them to put all their energy into growing leaves instead of fruits. Switching to fertilizers richer in phosphorus and potassium encourages flowering and fruit size.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ haa amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛduɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my oil palm seeds take so many months just to sprout after I put them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm dumɔwui lɛ heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Oil palm seeds have an extremely hard, thick shell that takes months to absorb enough heat and moisture to break open naturally before the internal shoot can grow out.
ga: Mu tso dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni wa waa, ni mli tse ni heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani ekɛ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ shwieɔ shi koni egbɛ eshwa yɛ adebɔɔ naa dani ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: Why do my harvested plantains turn soft and spoil so quickly before I can get them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya dani mikɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains release a natural gas as they mature that speeds up ripening. Storing them in tight, hot spaces or bruising them during transit causes this gas to build up, making them spoil faster.
ga: Dumɔwui jieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ, ni no haa amɛshweremɔ yaa oya. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo hei ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ loo okɛ amɛ shwie shi yɛ be mli ni okɛ amɛ yaa lɛ, ebaaha gas nɛɛ abɔle amɛhe ni ebaaha amɛfite oya.

english: Why do my plantain suckers produce small bunches when I plant them at the tail end of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee?

english: Plantains need heavy, continuous moisture when they form their fruit stalks. Planting too late causes the fruiting stage to coincide with dry weather, leading to small, light bunches.
ga: Plantains biɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa aba be fɛɛ be kɛ́ amɛmiifee aduawai ahe tsei. Kɛ́ adu nii sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha yibiiwoo be lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ akpã gbee. Efeɔ tso bibioo ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do my corn leaves curl up when it hasn't rained for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi beni nugbɔ enɛko gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Corn leaves curl to protect themselves and reduce water loss through their surface during dry or hot periods.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe ni amɛha nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ aba shi yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ loo hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning yellow and dropping off during this dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ nɛkɛ hɔmɔ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Without enough rain, crops shed their older leaves to save water and keep their main stem alive until moisture returns.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ bɔ ni sa lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baajie amɛbaai momo lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛkwɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my vegetable crops wilt during the hot afternoon even if the soil has some moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ?

english: Crops lose water faster through their leaves than their roots can pull from the soil in peak heat, though they usually recover once the sun goes down.
ga: Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi moŋ.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because plants can absorb moisture before the sun heats up, preventing water from evaporating quickly into the air.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu dani hulu lɛ adɔ amɛ. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Can I give my crops too much water if I start using water pumps on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu fe nine? Kɛji mibɔi nu pɔmp kɛ nitsumɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, over-watering can drown crop roots by cutting off their oxygen supply, causing roots to rot and leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baafo mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Will storing stream water in large tanks for irrigation affect how good it is for my crops?
ga: Ani nu ni mikɛtoɔ tsɛnsii wuji amli kɛha nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baaná miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ kpakpa?

english: Stored water remains healthy for crops as long as the tanks are kept clean, though water left in direct sunlight can get hot and should cool down before being applied to delicate plants.
ga: Nu ni ato lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be fɛɛ be ni nu tsɛnsi lɛ mli tse lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni ashiɔ yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni mli edɔ moŋ, shi esa akɛ ahã edɔ dani akɛwo tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ waa lɛ anɔ moŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing fruit when the sun is very intense?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ewooo yibii be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and sterilizes their pollen, causing flowers to drop off instead of developing into fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni egbeɔ pollen. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai.

english: Why are the traditional planting months no longer working well for my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kusum naa dumɔwui nyɔŋ lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ dɔŋŋ kɛhaaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Changing weather patterns mean rainfall comes at unpredictable times, so planting must now depend on actual soil moisture rather than fixed calendar dates.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ bei ni anyɛɛɛ atsɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ dumɔ adamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ diɛŋtsɛ nɔ moŋ fe kalanda gbi pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ.

english: How do shade trees help my young crops survive when there is little rain?
ga: Te tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Shade trees lower the air temperature around young crops, reducing water evaporation from the soil and protecting delicate leaves from sun scorch.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. ni ebuɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he

english: Why do my crops grow so much slower now compared to how they used to grow years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo kwraa fe bɔ ni amɛji afii komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Higher temperatures and irregular rain put constant stress on crops, forcing them to spend energy on survival rather than quick growth.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ be fɛɛ be. ni nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ atsu nii kɛha wala moŋ fe ni amɛaadara oya.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the nutrient responsible for green leaves and strong growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen out of the soil, so applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps the plant regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? When I plant so many seeds in one hole?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Spacing your seeds properly allows each plant enough room and food to build strong stems and produce large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekwɛ̃ tso ni mli wa ni ekɛ dumɔwui wuji ni eyi obɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why does my bean crop have plenty of bushy green leaves but very few flowers and pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii babaoo lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes leguminous crops focus all their energy on growing lush foliage rather than producing flowers. Reducing nitrogen and using balanced nutrients encourages the plant to switch its energy into making flowers and pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi. Nitrogen ni abaaba shi kɛ niyenii ni ja ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛtsake hewalɛ kɛya fɔfɔi kɛ pod feemɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when there are no bigger plants surrounding them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni cacao tsei ko bɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate strong, direct sunlight and harsh wind. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around them creates a protective canopy that cools the soil and keeps moisture around the young seedlings until they grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains yɛ ehe lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ hiɔ shi. dumɔwui lɛ kɛyashi amɛbaadara ni amɛhe wa

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without forming any fruits during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil cause stress to tomato plants, making them shed their flowers to survive. Giving the plants consistent water at their roots and providing light shade helps preserve the blossoms so they can turn into tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ afɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ nu daa yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi koni amɛtsɔmɔ tomatoi.

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting shoots even when I haven't planted them in the farm yet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miduko amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: Yams have a natural resting period called dormancy. Once warm temperatures and air humidity rise, the yam tuber senses that conditions are right for growth, triggering its internal biological clock to sprout.
ga: Atomɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ lɛ, Sweet potato tubers lɛ baanyɛ ana akɛ shihilɛi srɔtoi sa kɛha dalɛ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, atswaa wala yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe ŋmɛlɛtswaa lɛ ama shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upward and shrinking into tight bundles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, mites, or aphids feeding on the plant sap and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these small insects early prevents the leaf damage and stops viruses from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ fiteɔ ni ekpaa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black and dry up during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive wetness and shade create a moist environment where a fungal disease called Black Pod thrives. Pruning excess tree branches to let air and sunlight through, along with harvesting ripe pods quickly, helps reduce the spread of the fungus.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ hulutsoo haa shihilɛ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Biɛ ji he ni tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. Agbɛnɛ hu, kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmei lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot inside the ground when left in very wet soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ sũ ni mli efɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need oxygen in the soil to breathe. When land stays flooded for too long, water displaces the air in the soil, causing root suffocation and inviting decay fungi to rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Nu baaye kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. ni efɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ nine koni amɛgboi.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during strong winds when they start bearing large bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ fɔfɔii wuji amli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that struggle to support the heavy weight of a mature fruit bunch. Supporting the stem with a bamboo prop or wooden pole prevents the heavy fruit from pulling the tree down before harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai akui ni edara lɛ amli tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei loo tsei ni akɛfee tso lɛ fiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ehaa tso yibii ni tsii lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbala tso lɛ shi dani akpa tso lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly when it has not rained for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa lɛ? Gbii babaoo nɛ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up to reduce the surface area exposed to the hot sun, which helps the plant conserve water during dry spells. It is a natural self-defense mechanism against heat and moisture stress.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i haomɔi ahe.

english: How do I know if my tomato plants are getting too much water from my irrigation system?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo kɛmiijɛ amɛ nu ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ mli?

english: If tomatoes receive too much water, their lower leaves will turn yellow, feel soft or limp, and the roots may start to rot. The plant might also shed its flowers before setting fruit.
ga: Kɛji tomatoi lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Henumɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ loo bɔdɔɔ Ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aje shishi amɛgboi. Tso lɛ baanyɛ ashwie efɔfɔi lɛ dani ewo yibii.

english: Why do cassava plants drop their lower leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally sheds its lower leaves during dry periods to conserve moisture. The plant enters a semi-resting state to survive the heat until water becomes available again.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ eshishi baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Tsei boteɔ shihilɛ ko ni mli edɔ fioo mli koni amɛhi shi yɛ latsaa be lɛ mli kɛyashi nu baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I use water directly from a river to irrigate my vegetable farm throughout the year?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛɔ faa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ awo mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu afi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Yes, river water is suitable for vegetables, but you must ensure it is free from harmful chemicals or high salt content, and you will need a pump or channel system to transport the water to your field.
ga: Hɛɛ, faa mli nu lɛ hi kɛha aduawai. Shi esa akɛ okwɛ koni tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo ŋmei babaoo akafee nɔ ko yɛ nu lɛ mli. Ni pɔmp gbɛjianɔtoo loo gbɛ ko he baahia bo ni okɛ nu lɛ aya oŋmɔji amli.

english: Will drilling a borehole give me enough water to farm crops during the dry season?
ga: Ani nu ni afoɔ lɛ baaha nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: A borehole can provide a reliable year-round water supply, but the acreage you can cultivate depends on the underground water table level and the capacity of the pump you install.
ga: Nubui baanyɛ aha nu aba yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ gbɛ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. Shi shikpɔŋ ni obaanyɛ otsu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ nɔ kɛ bɔ ni pɔmp ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii aha lɛ nɔ.

english: How far away from a river can I clear land and still successfully grow water-thirsty crops?
ga: Te manyɛ mafo shikpɔŋ kɛjɛ faa lɛ he ni manyɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kumai yeɔ lɛ yɛ omanyeyeli mli lolo?

english: You can farm at any distance from a river as long as you have the equipment to transport the water, but setting up closer to the water source reduces the energy and piping costs needed to feed your crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsu okwaayeli he nii yɛ he ko ni kɛ faa lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji, kɛji oyɛ nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii kɛwo nu mli. Shi kɛ́ okɛto he ko ni bɛŋkɛ nu jɛɛhe lɛ, ebaa hewalɛ kɛ paipii ni he hiaa koni akɛha onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop producing flowers when the weather gets very hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ fɔfɔi beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When pepper plants lack sufficient moisture during hot periods, they save energy by dropping their blossoms to avoid trying to nourish fruits they cannot support.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ koni amɛkabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛha aduawai ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees look wilted even when the top of the soil feels slightly damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo moŋ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees have deeper root systems. If only the top layer of soil is damp, the deeper roots may still be dry, preventing the tree from getting enough water to keep its leaves firm.
ga: Cacao tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ fe tsutsu lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbi lolo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ baai lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my yam tubers stay small and dry up early when the rains stop before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛgbiɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa dani akpa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need steady soil moisture to swell. If the water supply cuts off early, the tuber stops expanding, hardens prematurely, and results in a small yield.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ koni amɛfuu. Kɛji akɛ afo nu lɛ mli oya Shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ baakpa shweremɔ. Erection mra ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii bibii ni afeɔ.

english: Is it better for my crops if I water them heavily once a week or lightly every day?
ga: Ani ebaahi kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu shwie nɔ babaoo shikome yɛ otsi mli loo fioo daa gbi?

english: Deep, less frequent watering encourages crop roots to grow deeper into the soil searching for moisture, making the plants stronger and more drought-resistant than light daily watering.
ga: Nu ni awoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni anyɛɛɛ awo mli shii abɔ lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ adara kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni amɛtao ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe wa ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa fe nu ni akɛhaa amɛ fioo daa gbi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plant turning yellow in a V-shape pattern?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: This is a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. When maize lacks nitrogen, it takes the nutrient from its older bottom leaves and sends it to the newer top leaves, causing the bottom leaves to yellow and dry up.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa mli lɛ Ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ lɛ amli ni ekɛyaa ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ amli. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ.

english: Why did my maize crops dry up and die after I put granular fertilizer close to the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ beni mikɛ granular fertilizer fata he yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer too close to the stem causes 'fertilizer burn.' The concentrated chemical salts draw water out of the crop's roots instead of feeding them. Fertilizer should always be applied a few centimeters away from the plant stem in moist soil.
ga: Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ he tsɔ lɛ, ekɛ 'ŋmɔshi nibii shãa' baa. Tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeebote mli. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi sɛntimitai fioo komɛi.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up, becoming small, and showing yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe, amɛji bibii ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi lɛ?

english: Your cassava is affected by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is transmitted by tiny insects called whiteflies. The virus prevents the leaves from developing normally, reducing the plant's ability to grow large tubers underground.
ga: O-cassava lɛ hela ni ji cassava mosaic lɛ emɔ o-cassava lɛ mli. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ kɛ hela lɛ baa. Virus lɛ tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛbaakwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baa shi.

english: What is eating the soft leaves inside the central funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni hi akɛ ayeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The pest hides inside the central whorl of the maize plant during the day to feed on the tender young leaves before emerging at night.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaai amli yɛ gbi mli koni amɛye baai bibii dani amɛje kpo gbɛkɛ.

english: Why does spear grass keep growing back on my field even after I clear and burn the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akpɔlɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mijie jɛmɛ ni mishã jɛmɛ po lɛ?

english: Spear grass has deep underground stems called rhizomes that remain alive underground even when fire burns the surface. Once the fire goes out, these roots use stored energy to quickly push new leaves above the ground.
ga: Spear jwɛi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ rhizomes ni hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji la shã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po. Kɛ́ la lɛ gbo lɛ, nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛtsiɔ baai heei oya kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off instead of growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or a lack of wind and bees to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na shwane mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa Aloo kɔɔyɔɔ loo ŋmeii bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmeii.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt during the afternoon heat even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: On hot days, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it up from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to close its pores and conserve moisture, usually recovering by evening.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛŋa eshishifãi lɛ ni ekɛto ŋmɔtɔ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehaa ehe feɔ shoo yɛ gbɛkɛ mli

english: Why do my yam vines yield bigger yams when I support them with wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ sweet potatoi wuji fe tsutsu lɛ beni mikɛ tsei ni akɛfee tsei fiɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves off the ground so they can catch more sunlight to produce food for the underground tuber, while also keeping the foliage dry to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo ni amɛkɛfee niyenii amɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ agbi koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that get scorched easily by intense sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide broad leaves that offer necessary shade and keep the surrounding air cool and humid for the cocoa.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ shãa oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa lɛ. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ kɛhaa kookoo lɛ

english: Why should I wait for two or three good rains before planting cassava cuttings instead of planting after the first light rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ kpakpa? ŋmɔtɔ fioo dani adu ŋmɔtɔ tsei Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain only dampens the top layer of soil. Cassava stem cuttings need deep moisture so their roots can establish; planting too early leaves the stems vulnerable to drying out if a brief dry spell follows.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ mli fũuɔ. Cassava tso lɛ mli tsei ni afolɔ lɛ biɔ nu ni mli kwɔ bɔni afee ni amɛshishifãi lɛ anyɛ afee. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baagbi kɛji akɛ be kukuoo ko pɛ ba ni amɛgbi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to grow green and strong. The plant moves nitrogen from older leaves to nourish the new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni ekɛha shweremɔ hee lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in a field with no shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside them provides living shade and moisture while the seedlings establish themselves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli lɛ adumɔ, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baaha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ ama shi lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when the plant experiences water stress, which prevents successful pollination.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Enɛ haaa pollination lɛ aye omanye.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is ready to harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni atsaaa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You can tell cassava is mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and cracks appear in the soil near the base of the stem due to the swelling roots.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmei ko egbɔ kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Ni ŋmeii je kpo yɛ sũ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli yɛ shishifãi ni efuu lɛ hewɔ.

english: What is making small ragged holes inside the young leaves of my maize plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the leaf whorl and feeds on fresh plant tissue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai amli ni amɛyeɔ tsei ahe fãji heei lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking sap from the leaves, or by a viral infection spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli

english: Too many shoots compete with the main stem for soil nutrients and water, which results in smaller bunches. Leaving only two or three healthy shoots keeps the main fruit big.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii baa. Kɛ́ ashi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso yibii titri lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Staking gets yam leaves off the ground so they get full sunlight to produce energy, while also keeping them away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Staking baajie sweet potato baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni helai akaba shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts help make my soil better for other crops later?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi aha tsei krokomɛi yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Legumes like groundnuts capture nitrogen gas from the air through their roots and store it in the soil, which acts as a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Is it better for my crops if I water my vegetable garden early in the morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii kɛji mikɛ nu wo mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering in the early morning allows plants to absorb water before the hot sun causes rapid evaporation or scorches wet leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ leebi lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa efoɔ oya loo eshãa baai ni efɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up tightly into tubes when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves during extreme heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This helps the plant retain moisture inside and prevents water from evaporating too quickly during dry spells.
ga: Abele tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop most of their leaves when rain doesn't fall for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ mli babaoo shwieɔ shi be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's natural survival strategy during drought. By shedding leaves, the plant stops losing water through transpiration and rests until the rains return, at which point it quickly sprouts fresh leaves.
ga: Baai ni ashwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala yɛ ŋmei be mli. Kɛji baai lɛ gbee shi lɛ Tsei lɛ baakpa nu ni amɛbaafite kɛtsɔ la ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ nɔ. ni jɔɔ ohe kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ Biɛ ji he ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do my pepper plants shed all their blossoms without forming any peppers during high heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fɛɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni pepper ko bɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Excessive heat causes stress in pepper plants and destroys the pollen inside the flowers. To protect itself from wasting energy when pollination fails, the plant naturally drops the flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei anɔ ni efiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hewalɛ ni efiteɔ lɛ he kɛ́ pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii. Tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛjɛɔ ebɔɔ su mli.

english: Why can I leave cassava roots underground for months without spoiling, while my tomatoes rot days after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishiɔ ŋmei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nyɔji babaoo ni amɛfiteee lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mi-tomato lɛ miifite yɛ gbii babaoo ni mikɛto lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cassava roots act as the plant's underground food storage vault and stay alive as long as they remain attached to the living stem in the soil. Tomatoes are delicate fruits designed to rot quickly after ripening to release seeds into the ground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi tsuɔ nii akɛ tso lɛ shikpɔŋ shishi niyenii ni akɛtoɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ tsei ni hiɛ ka yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe. Tomato ji aduawai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni afee koni amɛgboi oya kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ koni amɛjie amɛdumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my stored maize grains develop tiny holes and powder after a few weeks in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii kɛ sũ lɛ? Beni otsii fioo komɛi ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: Maize weevils and insects lay tiny eggs in the grain during harvest or storage. As the larvae hatch, they eat the inside of the kernel, leaving small exit holes and dusty powder.
ga: Abele ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii fɔɔ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ dumɔwui amli yɛ kpamɔɔ loo nitoo be mli Beni ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ Amɛyeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Bu bibioo ko ni akɛjeɔ kpo kɛ sũ eshwɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees dry up and die when I clear away all the plantain plants around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie dumɔwui ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ? Tsei lɛ fɛɛ je kpo.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots and delicate foliage that burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees act as temporary nurse plants, providing necessary shade and cooling the surrounding soil until the cocoa trees grow strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui tsuɔ nii akɛ be kukuoo mli tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ. Ha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ mli ajɔ kɛyashi kookoo tso lɛ baaná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why does maize grow greener and yield better when I plant groundnuts on the same field first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni ewoɔ yibii kpakpai kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that gather nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural fertilizer through root nodules. When the groundnut roots decay, they leave this rich plant food in the soil for the next crop of maize.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni buaa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa ni etsɔɔ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii amli. Kɛji ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ amɛshiɔ tso niyenii ni jara wa nɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha amɛ ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do cowpeas give me food in just two months, while my yam takes almost a full year to mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmei ha mi niyenii yɛ nyɔji enyɔ pɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi-sweet potato lɛ he nɔ ni miihe ashɛ afi muu fɛɛ dani ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are fast-growing annual legumes programmed to complete their life cycle rapidly before rains stop. Yams require a long season to build up large, starch-filled tubers deep in the ground to feed the plant through dry months.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya daa afi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛgbe amɛshihilɛ naa oya dani nugbɔ lɛ akpa. Sweet potatoes heɔ be babaoo dani efeɔ ŋmeii agboi ni eyi obɔ kɛ starch ni kã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni ekɛha tso lɛ niyenii yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do fall armyworms attack my maize field relentlessly, but barely touch the cassava field right next to it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cutworms lɛ tutuaa mi ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛkpaaa lɛ? Shi eshɛɛɛ ni eshɛɔ ŋmei ŋmɔ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ he?

english: Fall armyworms prefer grasses like maize because the leaves are soft, easy to digest, and offer sweet nutrients. Cassava leaves contain bitter chemical compounds that deter these specific caterpillars from feeding.
ga: Autumn cutworms sumɔɔ jwɛi tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ amɛbaai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni amɛyeɔ oya kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ hewɔ. Tsofai ni mli wa yɛ cassava baai amli ni haaa ŋmeii aye amɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants easily fall over during heavy rains and winds even when they look big and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: Plantains do not have a deep taproot; instead, they have a wide cluster of shallow roots near the surface. When heavy bunches of fruit make the top heavy and rain softens the soil, strong winds can easily pull the roots out of the ground.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ sisifãhi agbohi nɛ a mi ku we nɛ a kɛ nyu ɔ hɛ mi kpata. Beni aduawai ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ haa amɛyitsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: Why do my young tomato seedlings need a roof cover over them during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni aha mi tomato dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy raindrops can easily snap fragile tomato stems, wash soil away from root systems, and splash ground fungi onto leaves, causing rot. A overhead cover shields plants from direct rain damage while letting them grow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ akumɔ tomato tsei ni waaa lɛ. Efɔɔ sũ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Ni ŋmei ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ haa amɛgboiɔ oya. Nɔ ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ buɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, yɛ be mli ni ehaa tsei lɛ daraa.

english: How does a shade net house help my young vegetable plants survive the intense heat?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni shade ŋshɔŋloo ko aaabu midumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he?

english: Shade structures block scorching direct sunlight while allowing fresh air to flow freely. This prevents high heat stress and stops water from evaporating too quickly from the soil and leaves.
ga: Shade gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa yɛ be mli ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli oya. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa hulutsoo ni naa wa waa aba, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ baai lɛ amli.

english: Why is it important for air to blow freely through my crop drying shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ miŋmɔshi nibii agbimɔhe lɛ mli oya lɛ?

english: Moving air carries away trapped moisture from harvested crops like maize or cocoa. Without good airflow, humidity builds up and creates a warm, damp space where mold and rot spoil your yield.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ ehe lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa, tamɔ ŋmãa loo kookoo mli lɛ yaa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ lɛ, Fɛ̃i buaa ehe naa ni ehaa he ko ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baafite onibii lɛ.

english: How does keeping rainwater off my stored maize keep it from getting ruined?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nugbɔ nu ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ ŋmãa lɛ naa koni ekafite?

english: Dry grains remain dormant and safe, but when rain leaks onto stored maize, it triggers the seeds to rot and creates ideal conditions for dangerous mold like aflatoxin to grow.
ga: Dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ baakã he ahi shi ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe. Shi kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ yɛ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ nɔ Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbo. ni efee shihilɛ ni sa kɛha ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ aflatoxin lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend building raised mesh tables to dry cocoa beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nitsumɔhe lɛ nɔ lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ ama ŋshɔŋ okpɔlɔ ni awo nɔ koni akɛgbi kookoo yibii lɛ?

english: Raised mesh tables allow breeze to circulate underneath the cocoa beans, drying them evenly while keeping them off the damp ground where pests and dirt can reach them.
ga: Mesh okpɔlɔ ni awo nɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ashishi. Enɛ haa kookoo yibii lɛ gĩɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni ehaa amɛyaa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ muji baanyɛ ashɛ kookoo yibii lɛ ahe lɛ hu.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers spoil faster if they are wet when I put them in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mikɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Water left on yam skin creates a breeding ground for bacteria and fungal spores, which enter small cuts in the tuber and cause soft rot during storage.
ga: Nu ni ashiɔ yɛ sweet potato hewolo nɔ lɛ feɔ he ko ni helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ. ni baabote ŋmeii bibii ni afo yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ amli ni eha amɛgboi yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I touch or shake my newly grafted mango branches too often?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ ataa mango nine ni akɛwo mli ehee lɛ he loo akpokpoɔ lɛ shii abɔ lɛ?

english: Graft joints are like fresh wounds. Frequent handling or moving can break the delicate tissues trying to join together and can introduce rot-causing germs from your hands.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛtsa he lɛ tamɔ pilamɔ hee. Ni akɛtsuɔ nii shii abɔ loo ajieɔ lɛ Ebaanyɛ eha fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni miitao ni amɛmɔ amɛhe lɛ akumɔ. ni ebaanyɛ ehiɛ helai ni fiteɔ yɛ oniji anɔ

english: Can touching diseased leaves with my hands spread sickness to the healthy crops in my farm?
ga: Ani kɛ́ akɛ nine taa baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbɛ hela eshwa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, many plant viruses, bacteria, and fungal spores cling to human hands and farming tools. Touching a sick plant and then a healthy one transfers the disease directly.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei amli helai, helatsɛmɛi, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ adesai aniji kɛ okwaayeli nibii ahe. Kɛ́ mɔ ko ta tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe lɛ, hela gbɛɔ eshwaa tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants turn yellow and wilt if rainwater collects around their bases for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air in the soil to breathe. Standing water suffocates the roots, causing root rot, which leaves the plant unable to draw up nutrients even though it is surrounded by water.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai eyɛ mli akɛ nu ebɔle amɛhe moŋ.

english: Why should I leave enough space between my cassava plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ

english: Proper spacing allows wind and sunlight to pass through the leaves. Good air movement dries wet foliage quickly after rain, preventing humidity-loving diseases from spreading.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la boteɔ baai lɛ amli. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ baaha baai ni efɔ lɛ agbi oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Tsi helai ni sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harmattan brings dry, hot winds that quickly strip moisture from young plant leaves. Plantain trees planted alongside young cocoa grow fast and have broad leaves that create living shade, keeping the air humid and protecting the young cocoa trees until they are strong enough.
ga: Harmattan kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi ni gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ oya kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii ahe baai amli lɛ baa. Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i ni obu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my tomato leaves turn yellow and curl up before the plants produce any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe dani tso lɛ woɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling whiteflies early using neem oil or insecticidal soap and planting disease-resistant tomato varieties protects your crop from this virus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Mra Be mli Whitefly Kudɔmɔ Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi anɔ. Ni tomato henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe kɛjɛ hela nɛɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves, but give me very tiny roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi moŋ eha mi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil encourages cassava to put all its energy into growing top leaves instead of storing food in its underground tubers. Balanced soil fertility and proper harvesting timing ensure the plant forms larger, heavier cassava roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yucca hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ awo ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ, Shikpɔŋ ni shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be ni sa lɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi ni dara ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ baa.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off before turning into hot peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani ebatsɔ pepper ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like calcium. Watering consistently around the base of the plant early in the morning helps retain flowers and produce healthy peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium. Kɛ́ afɔ nu awo tso lɛ shishigbɛ he daa leebi maŋkpa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: If I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year, why does my harvest keep reducing?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ebaa shi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally returns nitrogen to the soil and resets pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ebaaku esɛɛ ekɛ nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni okɛ pest cycle lɛ ato ekoŋŋ.

english: When is the correct time for me to apply fertilizer to my maize farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-abele ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize needs fertilizer at two main stages: a basal application at or shortly after planting to build healthy roots, and a second top-dressing application 4 to 6 weeks later when the stem starts growing rapidly toward flowering.
ga: Abɛi he miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ gbɛi titrii enyɔ nɔ: Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ shishijee loo yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ koni shishifãi ni wa aba. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ ni ji enyɔ yɛ otsii 4 kɛyashi 6 sɛɛ beni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa oya kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to manufacture food for tuber growth below ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal rot and ensuring maximum sunlight exposure.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ hia hulu la ni tsoɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha tuber lɛ dalɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ fungal rot naa ni ehaa hulu la ni fa babaoo baa.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plant for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Keeping only one main plant and one strong replacement sucker ensures the main tree produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Tso titri kome pɛ kɛ tso kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtoɔ sucker najiaŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ awo dumɔwui wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant groundnuts or cowpeas in between my rows of cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ mi-cassava ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. Planting them between cassava rows improves soil health while providing a quick food harvest before the cassava matures.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei ŋtayaai ateŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ yɛ be mli ni ehaa niyenii hu baa oya dani ŋmei lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade because intense heat and direct sunlight dry out their delicate leaves faster than their short roots can pull water from the soil. Providing shade mimics their natural forest habitat and helps them build strong roots.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha baai bibii lɛ agbi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi kukuji lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛhe ni akɛ shade woɔ mli lɛ kaseɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli koo mli shihilɛhe lɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black and dry up while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in high humidity and excess shade. Good air circulation through proper pruning and clearing wet fallen leaves helps prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni fa fe nine yɔɔ lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai ni efɔ lɛ ni afoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ amɛhe ni afɔɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: How does heavy rainfall during the flowering season affect my cocoa yield?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ saa mi-kookoo lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Excessive rain can knock delicate cocoa flowers off the branches before tiny insects like midges can pollinate them. Without pollination, flowers drop and cannot turn into cocoa pods, leading to a smaller harvest.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbo kɛjɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ dani kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii baanyɛ afee amɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji akɛ pollination bɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛtsɔ kookoo ŋmeii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni afee lɛ fioo.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow instead of staying rich green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green foliage. Applying compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy leaf color and grain size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ su kɛ dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge bushy leaves above ground but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients like potassium, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stem instead of storing energy in its roots. Balancing soil nutrients leads to bigger cassava tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nine kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi tamɔ potassium he lɛ, tsei kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ɔ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ daraa.

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop and turn brown during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves drop and brown to conserve moisture when dry winds blow and soil water is low. Mulching around the base of the plant holds moisture in the root zone and reduces water loss during dry periods.
