ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi tswa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ faaa. Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shishifã lɛ mli, ni ehaa nu ni laajeɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Can I grow food crops like yam and cassava on the same land as my young cocoa without damaging the cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-kokoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ ni mifiteee kookoo lɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping early on is beneficial if planned well. Fast-growing food crops can provide temporary shade for young cocoa and feed your family, provided you space them properly so they don't block light or steal nutrients from the cocoa roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ mra. Sɛɛnamɔi yɛ he kɛji akɛ ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo ŋmeii lɛ aná be kukuoo mli ŋmɔlɔ ni amɛha wekui niyenii. Esa akɛ ato he lɛ he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni ekatsĩ kane naa loo ekaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ kookoo shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than my food crops after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara oya ni amɛhe wa fe miniyenii tsei lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that have adapted to absorb water and soil nutrients instantly after drought. Planted crops often take longer to establish roots, making early weeding essential to stop weeds from smothering your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ kooi amli ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni adu lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛfeɔ shishifãi. Ha efee nɔ ni abaanyɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ mra. Ehe miihia ni okpa jwɛi ni fiteɔ onibii lɛ.

english: Why do my crop yields keep dropping every year when I plant on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛ́ midu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Plants take nutrients out of the earth every growing season. If those nutrients are not put back into the soil through manure, fertilizer, or crop rotation, the soil gets exhausted and produces smaller harvests.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be mli ni amɛdaraa. Kɛji akɛ akɛ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ efataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he ekoŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmaa lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I tell if my soil is healthy enough to support both food crops for eating and cash crops for income?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shika ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, holds moisture well after rain, breaks apart easily without forming hard crusts, and contains natural life like earthworms. These indicate rich organic material that supports strong root growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ Efoɔ mli oya ni efeee ŋmɔtɔ ni wa. ni adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɔɔ mli lɛ, amɛtsɔɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fiɔ shishifãi ni wa lɛ adalɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my harvested grains mold when I pile them together inside my house?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa ni mikpaa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mibua naa yɛ shĩa lɛ?

english: Piling freshly harvested crops traps moisture inside the stack. This warmth and dampness create a perfect environment for mold and rot to quickly grow and ruin your yield.
ga: Tsei ni akpa ehee ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ aba ŋshɔ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i nɛɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni baakwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteɔ onibii oya.

english: Why do my maize kernels break into pieces and go to waste after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshiɔ jwɛi yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize kernels break when they are dried too rapidly under intense heat or when wet crops are handled roughly. Gentle drying and careful handling keep the kernels intact.
ga: Abɛi mli ŋmeii lɛ fãa kɛji amɛgbi oya tsɔ yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa shishi loo kɛji akɛ atsu tsei ni efɔ lɛ ahe nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Kɛ́ agbi lɛ blɛoo ni akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akafite.

english: Why should I spread my harvested crops in a thin layer instead of a thick pile when drying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa lɛ ashwã ŋmɔtɔ bibioo mli? Mohu ɔ, e buaa e he nya wawɛɛ ke e gbi.

english: Spreading crops in a thin layer allows sunlight and fresh air to reach every single grain evenly, preventing moisture from getting trapped at the bottom.
ga: Gbalamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo mli. Enɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu he pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni no haaa ŋmɔtɔ akamɔ shishigbɛ.

english: What can I use to dry my crops properly if I do not have a raised drying rack?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mikɛtsu nii koni mikɛgbi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ? Kɛji akɛ obɛ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ ŋwɛi ni akɛgbiɔ nii lɛ

english: If you do not have a drying rack, you can spread a clean plastic tarp on flat ground in direct sunlight. The tarp keeps the crops off the dirt while the sun dries them.
ga: Kɛji atadei atoohe ko bɛ Obaanyɛ okɛ plastic tarp ni he tse ashwã shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tarp lɛ haaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee muji be mli ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to dry my harvested crops directly on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mi akɛ magbi mikpamɔ nii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Bare soil contains groundwater, insects, and dirt. Placing crops directly on the ground draws moisture up into your harvest, causing dirt contamination and decay.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kooloi bibii, kɛ muji yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaagbala ŋmɔtɔ kɛba okpamɔ lɛ mli. Ekɛ muji ni fiteɔ nii kɛ fitemɔ baa.

english: How does using a plastic tarp under the sun help dry my crops better?
ga: Te plastic tarpaulin ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛgbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: A tarp acts as a clean barrier that stops ground moisture from soaking into your crops. It also allows you to gather and cover your harvest quickly if unexpected rain comes.
ga: Tarp tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni he tse ni baatsi shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ naa koni ekabote onibii amli. Eyeɔ ebua bo hu ni obuaa oŋmɔshi nibii anaa oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ trukaa.

english: How does direct sunlight stop my harvested crops from spoiling?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ mikpamɔ lɛ naa koni ekafite?

english: Direct sunlight removes water from harvested crops. Without water inside the crop, harmful bacteria, fungi, and insects cannot survive, allowing your food to store safely for a long time.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ jieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akpa lɛ amli. Kɛ́ nu bɛ tsei amli lɛ, muawai, ŋmeii, kɛ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi. Ha oniyenii lɛ ato he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What happens to my crops if rain falls on them while they are drying outside?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ be mli ni amɛmiigbi yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ?

english: Rain wets dry crops again, causing them to absorb moisture quickly. This leads to rapid discoloration, mold growth, and rotting, which destroys their market value.
ga: Nugbɔ haa tsei ni egbi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ekoŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu oya. Enɛ haa ehiɛ su tsakeɔ oya. fungal dalɛ kɛ fitemɔ ni fiteɔ jarayeli jara

english: How can I tell if my harvested grains are dry enough for long-term storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Well-dried grains feel very hard and make a sharp cracking sound when you bite or press them. If they feel soft or leave dampness on your hands, they need more sun drying.
ga: Nibii ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa waa ni amɛfeɔ gbee ni tswaa kɛji akɛ akɔmɔ loo anyɛ amɛnɔ. Kɛji enu he akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ loo eshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ onine nɔ Ehe miihia ni ajie lɛ kpo yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni egbi babaoo.

english: Why do I need to harvest my crops quickly as soon as they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makpa ŋmɔshi nibii oya kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Leaving mature crops in the field for too long exposes them to unpredictable weather, strong sun, and pests, which damages the crop quality before you can collect it.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmɔshi nibii ni edara lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ, hulu la ni naa wa, kɛ kooloi ni baa amɛnɔ lɛ baa amɛnɔ, ni baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: Should I wait for my coconut nut to sprout before planting it in the ground, or can I just bury it dry?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mamɛ ni akoo lɛ akwɛ̃ dani madu yɛ shikpɔŋ loo esa akɛ mafu lɛ koni egbi?

english: Waiting for the coconut nut to sprout in a controlled space first ensures that you only spend time and land planting seeds that are alive and healthy, leading to an even and reliable harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ oomɛ ni ŋmeii akwɛ̃ yɛ he ko ni akudɔɔ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ehaa oheɔ obei ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ dumɔwui ni hiɛ ka lolo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa anáa kpamɔ ni yaa nɔ daa ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if a coconut nut is healthy enough to sprout into a good tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei mli wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ tso kpakpa?

english: A good planting nut should feel heavy, slosh with water when shaken, and show no signs of cracks, insect holes, or soft moldy spots on its surface.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmei ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni tsii. Nu lɛ bafeɔ muji kɛji akpokpo. ni ŋmeii, kooloi bibii, loo ŋmeii ni mli ejɔ fioo ko bɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some of my seeds take a very long time to sprout after I put them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need the right balance of moisture, warmth, and soft soil to wake up; if the ground is too dry, too hard, or buried too deep, the seed stays asleep or struggles to sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ, latsaa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ teŋ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛhi shi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ, ewa tsɔ, loo eyɛ mli tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ wɔɔ loo amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do extension officers recommend applying fungicide medicine to seed sprouts before planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii awo dumɔwui anɔ dani adu lɛ?

english: Young sprouts are soft and easily attacked by hidden fungal spores in the soil; applying fungicide acts like a protective shield that kills unseen rot and keeps the baby plant safe while it roots.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa amɛ oya. Tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa lɛ, ni ehaa tso bibioo lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe beni ewoɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Can a young crop sprout look healthy on the outside even if it is rotting on the inside?
ga: Ani dumɔwu lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ eyɛ mli akɛ eefite yɛ emli moŋ?

english: Yes, fungal germs and small pests can enter the seed or stem internally without immediate outer signs, which is why treating sprouts before planting prevents sudden plant death later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii baanyɛ abote dumɔwui loo ŋmeii amli ni okadi ko bɛ kponɔgbɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni kɛ́ atsa dumɔwui lɛ dani adu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ gboɔ trukaa yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Will putting anti-disease chemicals on my seed sprouts damage or kill the young crop?
ga: Ani tsofai ni tsiɔ hela naa ni mikɛwoɔ midumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ anɔ lɛ baafite dumɔwui lɛ loo ebaafite amɛ?

english: When used in the recommended amounts, crop protection chemicals do not harm the plant; they only target the destructive fungi and pests that try to feed on the tender sprout.
ga: Kɛ akɛ tsofai ni buɔ tsei ahe lɛ tsu nii yɛ bɔ ni sa lɛ mli lɛ, eyeee tsei awui. Amɛtutuaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛye tsei bibii lɛ pɛ.

english: Why do my tender young crop sprouts sometimes wilt and die suddenly right after coming out of the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji amɛje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by soil fungi attacking the delicate stem at ground level when the soil is overly wet, cutting off the sprout's ability to draw up food and water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni tutuaa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso bibioo lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛgbalaa niyenii kɛ nu lɛ laajeɔ.

english: How deep into the soil am I supposed to bury a sprouted seed when moving it to the farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafu dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ yaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You should cover the roots and seed body securely with soil for support, but leave the green leafy sprout above the ground so it can breathe and capture sunlight.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ sũ aha shishifãi lɛ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ koni eye ebua. Shi shi tsei bibii ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛmu ni amɛhe hulu la lɛ.

english: Do newly sprouted crops need full hot sunlight or should I give them shade?
ga: Ani tsei ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ he miihia hulu loo hulutsoo be fɛɛ?

english: Freshly sprouted shoots have delicate leaves that easily scorch under harsh sun, so giving them light shade helps them establish strong roots before facing full sunlight.
ga: Tsobii ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ aha ŋmeii lɛ hɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewaje shishifãi lɛ dani hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ aba amɛnɔ.

english: Why is it better to sprout tree crop seeds in a small nursery area instead of planting them directly across the whole field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaakwɛ dumɔwui ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ yɛ he bibioo ko ni akɛduɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii yɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: A nursery allows you to easily water, monitor, and treat many small sprouts against pests in one place, ensuring you only transfer the strongest plants to your main field.
ga: Nursery lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ nu haa. Kwɛmɔ dumɔwui bibii anɔ ni otsa amɛ Abaanyɛ ana tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yɛ he kome. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ tsei ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ yaa oŋmɔ titri lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees get burnt very easily by strong sunlight. Planting plantains alongside cocoa provides fast-growing shade that protects the cocoa leaves and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya waa kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa shɛ amɛnɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo ni daa oya ni buɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during the hottest part of the day to protect themselves from losing too much water. It is the plant's natural way of saving moisture until the weather cools down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. Eji tsei adebɔɔ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Can pouring too much water on my pepper plants actually damage them?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛwoɔ pepper tsei amli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ?

english: Yes, giving crops too much water fills up all the small air spaces in the soil, which smothers the roots. Without air, the roots cannot absorb food, causing the leaves to turn yellow and drop off.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni okɛwoɔ onibii amli fe nine lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ obɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Yam plants need their leaves high off the damp ground to catch as much sunlight as possible. Staking keeps the leaves dry to prevent rotting and helps the plant produce larger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato tsei lɛ baai lɛ ahi ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ agbi koni akafite ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: What will happen if I plant my cassava cuttings too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the roots fight underground for water and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin plants with very small, light cassava roots.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmei tsei lɛ daraaa kwraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do weeds harm my tall crops even if the weeds are small and low to the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi tutuaa mi tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛji bibii ni amɛba shi kɛyashɛɔ shikpɔŋ moŋ?

english: Weeds steal water and manure from the soil underground before your crop roots can get to them. Even short weeds rob your crops of the food they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi dani tsei shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ he. Jwɛi kukuji po Ejuɔ onibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Yellow lower leaves mean your soil is running out of nitrogen fertilizer. The maize plant is taking whatever food is left in its old bottom leaves and sending it to keep the new top leaves alive.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii. Abɛi tso lɛ kɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ yɛ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni eye ebua ni ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do elderly farmers tell me to plant cowpeas or beans in the same farm as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special crops that can take natural food from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This natural fertilizer feeds the maize and makes the soil richer.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni baanyɛ ajie adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off before making any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tomato lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant does not get enough water. When stressed, the plant sheds its flowers to conserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are fully grown and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lowest leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the dry soil around the base of the stem starts to crack open from the swollen roots beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi shishifãi ni efuu yɛ shishi lɛ ahe fãmɔ.

english: How do I know if my farm land is fertile enough before I plant my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse jogbaŋŋ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Fertile soil usually has a dark color, holds water well, feels soft, and contains lots of decaying leaves and earthworms. You can also tell land is fertile if wild grass and trees grow very tall and dark green on it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ su feɔ ediŋŋ. Ehiɛɔ nu jogbaŋŋ, enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo ni baai ni fiteɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ mli. Obaanyɛ ona hu akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baa nii kɛji jwɛi kɛ koo mli tsei lɛ dara waa ni amɛfee eŋɔli.

english: What can I do to make my farm land richer if the soil is poor?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii?

english: You can enrich poor soil by adding animal manure, compost made from decayed leaves, or planting legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts, which naturally feed nutrient-rich nitrogen back into the ground.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ kooloi ashishifã afata he. Kompost ni akɛ baai ni egboi loo tsei amli ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii fee. ni kɛ nitrogen ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ

english: Why do my crops produce less yield when I plant on the same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving the ground time to recover. Swapping your crops each season keeps the soil balanced and rich.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Does burning the bush on my land before planting destroy the soil?
ga: Ani tsei bibii ni ashãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani aduɔ lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, burning destroys important organic matter and kills tiny helpful insects and worms in the soil. Clearing without burning leaves good plant matter behind to rot and fertilize your land.
ga: Hɛɛ, la ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni egbeɔ kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ otsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oshãaa lɛ, eshiɔ tsei kpakpai yɛ sɛɛ koni amɛgboi ni amɛwo oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight over water and plant food in the soil, and their leaves block sunlight from each other, resulting in thin, weak plants.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Can I grow two different crops on the same piece of land at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsei srɔtoi enyɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, this is called intercropping. Planting compatible crops together, like cassava and maize, helps make full use of your space as long as one crop does not steal all the sunlight and nutrients from the other.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ intercropping. Nibii ni kɛ amɛhe kpãa gbee tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei dumɔ Ebaaye ebua bo ni okɛ ohegbɛ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Shii abɔ ni tso kome juuu hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai fɛɛ ni jɛɔ tso kroko lɛ mli lɛ,

english: Why do my young seedlings yellow and dry up quickly when the sun is too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ oya kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ wo amɛmli lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings have delicate roots that cannot pull water from deep underground yet. High heat causes them to lose water faster than they can absorb it, so shade trees or cover crops can protect them.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa nu lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii baanyɛ abu amɛhe.

english: Weeds are wild plants that naturally adapted to survive harsh conditions and take up soil nutrients and water very fast, which is why clearing them early is necessary so your crops get enough food.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ oya. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie amɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okwɛ koni onibii lɛ ana niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does my soil turn hard like stone shortly after the rains stop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wa tamɔ tɛsaa beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil turns hard when it lacks organic matter like decomposed leaves and compost that usually keep it loose and spongy. Adding manure helps the soil hold moisture and stay soft.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni fiteɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ehaa efeɔ blɛoo.

english: How do leguminous crops like groundnuts and beans help the other crops on my farm?
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi. yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. When they die, that natural plant food remains behind for the next crop to feed on.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. kɛ amɛgboi Nakai adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii lɛ hiɔ sɛɛ koni ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aye.

english: How deep into the soil should I push a young seedling when planting it in my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ matsi dumɔwui bibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashɛ tɛŋŋ beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting too deep can cause the stem to rot underground, while planting too shallow leaves the roots exposed to dry out. A safe depth is usually about 2 to 3 centimeters (1 inch) so the roots are fully covered while the stem remains freely above the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ni mli kwɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. yɛ be mli ni dumɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbi. Bei pii lɛ, ŋshɔ lɛ mlibotemɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ ji aaafee sɛntimitai 2 kɛyashi 3 (inch 1), no hewɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Does it matter which direction the roots point when I place a seedling in the ground?
ga: Ani gbɛ ni shishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ he hiaa beni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, roots must point straight down into the soil hole so they can reach deep water and anchor the plant firmly. If roots are bent sideways or pointed upward, the plant will struggle to grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ shishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ bu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ bɔni afee ni amɛyashɛ nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ni amɛmɔmɔ tso lɛ shi shiŋŋ yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛtee afã loo amɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ shweremɔ baafee nɔ ni wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I plant them in a field with direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sun and lose moisture quickly. Planting shade crops like plantains nearby provides a natural shelter that keeps the young cocoa cool and humid.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi, ni amɛmli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni haa kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cassava plants roll up and drop off during dry weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When water is scarce, cassava plants drop their leaves to conserve moisture and keep their underground tubers alive until the rains return.
ga: Kɛ nu faaa lɛ, Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings wilt right after I move them from the nursery to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Moving plants causes transplant shock if roots are broken or exposed to harsh afternoon heat. Transplanting late in the afternoon and watering immediately helps seedlings recover quickly.
ga: Tsei ni tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛhe afee shoo kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ fã loo amɛbote shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shwane mli ni awo amɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ oya.

english: When is the right time to start putting fertilizer on my young seedlings?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi mitsei bibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔ?

english: It is best to wait about one to two weeks after transplanting before applying fertilizer, giving the roots time to settle so strong chemicals do not burn them.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛwo mli lɛ, esa akɛ omɛ otsi kome kɛyashi enyɔ dani ekɛ fɔmɔ nii awo mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛjieɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã.

english: What happens to my maize crop if I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When planted too close, maize plants compete against each other for sunshine, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin stalks and smaller cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Abɛi tsei kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Why do weeds stop my yam crop from growing well even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi tsiɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the fertilizer, soil nutrients, and light intended for your yam, leaving the yam tubers small and underdeveloped.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ la kɛha o-sweet potato lɛ Enɛ haa sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛdarako.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is holding too much standing water around the roots.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I cut off yellow or diseased leaves from my vegetable plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo hela ni yɔɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Removing sick or dead leaves prevents diseases from spreading to healthy parts of the crop and helps the plant send energy into growing fresh shoots and fruit.
ga: Baai ni hela mɔ amɛ loo ni egboi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni hela akagbɛ ashwã tso lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ yaa ŋmeii ni miida kɛ aduawai heei amli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is hungry for nitrogen. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or NPK helps the plant build strong, green leaves to catch sunlight and grow healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ urea loo NPK fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa ni ekɛbaaŋɔ hulu la lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato fruits rotting and turning black at the bottom end while they are still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ miifite ni amɛmiifee ediŋŋ yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni amɛmiida lolo lɛ?

english: This happens when tomato plants do not get enough calcium from the soil, often caused by irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the roots pull up calcium to form healthy, firm fruit bottoms.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ calcium koni ekɛfee aduawai ashishi ni wa ni ehi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Twisted or curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves. Spraying with neem water or recommended pest treatments stops them from draining the plant's strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni etsɔ loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Neem nu loo gbɛi krokomɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite ehewalɛ.

english: Why are the young cocoa pods on my trees turning black and shriveling up before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is often caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly during the rainy season when moisture stays on the pods. Clearing weeds and trimming excess shade trees helps air flow through the farm and dry out the pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni nu shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea flowers drop off the plants before making any bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Flower dropping is usually caused by small insect pests like thrips that feed on the delicate blossoms. Protecting the crop during the early flowering stage helps the blossoms turn into full bean pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni yeɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kɛ́ abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ashishijee be lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are fully grown under the ground if I cannot see them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji minyɛɛɛ mana amɛ?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to swell and crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why do some of my plantain suckers grow strong and produce big bunches while others stay small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ekomɛi daa waa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ji bibii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Sword suckers with thin, narrow leaves grow stronger stems and bigger fruit because they draw deep nutrients from the mother plant, whereas broad-leafed maiden suckers grow weaker and yield smaller bunches.
ga: Klante tsei ni baai bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ woɔ tsei ni wa kɛ aduawai wuji. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni tsei bibii ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to get enough sunlight to make food for the plant. Staking also keeps the leaves off the wet soil, which prevents leaf diseases and allows bigger tubers to form underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛha tsei lɛ niyenii. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa baa lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ tsei ahe helai anaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei wuji feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my valley rice grow better when there is shallow standing water in the field during its early growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ mijɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ shishijee be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Standing water cools the soil around young rice plants and smothers competing weeds, allowing the rice stalks to tiller well and produce full heads of grain.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli gbiɔ. Ha ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni ojie jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ kɛjɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui yitso ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why should I trim off the lower dead fronds on my oil palm trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ baai ni egboi lɛ?

english: Removing dead or yellow fronds allows sunlight and air to reach the trunk, prevents pests like rats from nesting in the tree, and makes it easier for new fruit bunches to form.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie baai ni egboi loo ni miifee ŋmɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ shishi. Tsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee amɛ ŋmeii yɛ tsei amli. ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaafee aduawai akui heei

english: How can I tell if my farm land is up to one acre in size?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shɛɔ acre kome?

english: An acre is approximately 4,047 square meters, which is roughly the size of a standard football field. You can measure it using a measuring tape by marking out a plot that is about 60 meters long by 65 meters wide.
ga: Acre kome dalɛ aaafee sqɛɛ mitai 4,047, ni ji aaafee bɔɔlutswaa he ko ni afɔɔ bɔɔlutswaa he lɛ dalɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ tsɔne ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe lɛ asusu kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ko ni kɛlɛ ji aaafee mitai 60 kɛ elɛɛmɔ aaafee mitai 65 lɛ nɔ.

english: What basic tools do I need to accurately measure and lay out my farm rows?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee dɛŋdadei he hiaa mi koni manyɛ masusu miŋmɔ lɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ ni mikɛto gbɛjianɔ?

english: You only need a long measuring tape, wooden pegs or sticks to mark your corners, and a strong string line stretched between the pegs to keep your planting rows straight.
ga: Teep kakadaŋŋ he miihia bo kɛkɛ. Tsoi loo tsei ni akɛtoɔ ŋwɛigbɛ kɛ kpãa ni wa ni akɛkpãa ŋwɛigbɛi lɛ ateŋ koni eha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for tomatoes or if I should plant a different crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha tomato loo esa akɛ madu tso kroko?

english: Tomatoes prefer well-drained, loose soil with good sunlight and easy access to water. If your soil holds too much water and stays muddy for long periods, crops like rice or sugarcane will perform better than tomatoes.
ga: Tomato sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ jɛmɛ. kɛ nu ni anáa mlɛo Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni eyɛ muji be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ fe tomato.

english: What steps should I take to prepare my land before putting any seeds in the ground?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mikɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ dani madu dumɔwui?

english: First, clear all weeds and bushes, then turn over the soil to loosen it so root systems can grow easily. Adding compost or dry animal manure to the soil before planting provides essential food for young crops.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii fɛɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha egbɔjɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani adu lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa waa.

english: Why is it important to use a tape measure for planting distance instead of just placing seeds by eye?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tɛi ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe lɛ asusu dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ moŋ fe ni aduɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Measuring precise distances ensures that every crop gets its fair share of sunlight, air, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing prevents crowding, which reduces plant stress and stops fungal diseases from spreading fast.
ga: He ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ susumɔ ni ja lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa amɛ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni sa. He ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa yeɔ ebuaa koni akafee mɛi babaoo. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe haomɔ baa shi, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: How far apart should I plant my tomato seedlings when moving them to the main field?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ ha tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ miiwo shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ?

english: Space tomato plants about 45 to 60 centimeters apart within a row, and keep rows about 75 to 90 centimeters apart. This leaves enough room for you to walk through, weed, and stake the plants as they grow.
ga: Okɛ tomatoi lɛ abɔ he aaafee sɛntimita 45 kɛyashi 60 yɛ sɛɛ mli. Ni ha ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee sɛntimita 75 kɛyashi 90. Enɛ baaha gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa aha bo ni obaanyɛ otsɔ mli, okɛ jwɛi atsu nii ni okɛ ohe awo mli be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and turn yellow during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often a defense mechanism to conserve water in severe heat, but yellowing usually indicates a lack of plant nutrients like nitrogen or an attack by a insect-transmitted virus like leaf curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ni abɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he koni nu akafite yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Shi bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ mli niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, loo hela ko ni kooloi bibii kɛbaa, tamɔ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops look wilted during the afternoon heat even if the soil was wet in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ leebi lɛ?

english: During peak afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull water from the soil. As long as the soil stays moist, the plants will recover and stand upright again in the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli be mli ni latsaa lɛ mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ ni edamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: How do I measure if my young crops are growing at the right size for their age?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu kɛji mi dumɔwui lɛ miida kɛyashɛ amɛafii lɛ ahe?

english: Check their height, stem thickness, and leaf color weekly; healthy young crops should maintain dark green leaves and a thick, sturdy main stem rather than growing tall, thin, and pale.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ ni okɛ baai lɛ awo mli daa otsi Esa akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahiɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tso titri ni mli wa ni mli wa lɛ mli. Mohu ɔ, e daa, nɛ e peeɔ munyu, nɛ e peeɔ hɛ mi nyami.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than the crop plants I spent money to cultivate?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni mifite shika yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive easily in local soils, allowing them to drink water and absorb fertilizer much faster than farm crops. Removing them early stops them from choking your investment.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe oya koni amɛhi shi yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔji anɔ. Enɛ haa amɛnuɔ nu ni amɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Ajieɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni oshika ni okɛwo mli lɛ akatsi ohe.

english: Can crop diseases really travel on the bottom of my farm boots from one field to another?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã miŋmɔ mli atadei lɛ ashishi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛya ekroko mli?

english: Yes, soil sticking to your footwear can carry tiny fungal spores, bacteria, or worms from an infected farm directly into a healthy field, spreading disease without you seeing it.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ ni kpɛtɛɔ okotokui ahe lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai bibii, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii. Kɛjɛ ŋmɔji ni hela lɛ emɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa hei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Enɛ haa hela gbɛɔ eshwaa ni onyɛɛɛ ona.

english: If yams naturally grow in the dirt, why does outside mud on my feet harm my farm?
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potatoes kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ Mɛni hewɔ sũ ni yɔɔ kpo nɔ yɛ minaji ahe lɛ ji oshara kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: The soil on your own farm may be clean, but mud brought from outside can introduce foreign germs and pests that your crop has no resistance against.
ga: Ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli tse. Shi klon ni akɛjɛɔ kponɔgbɛ kɛbaa lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ maŋsɛɛ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni oŋmɔshi nibii nyɛŋ ashi lɛ aba.

english: Why should I wash my cutlasses and hoes before moving to clear another part of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafɔ mi dadei kɛ mi ŋmɔji lɛ ahe dani mikɛ amɛ aya miŋmɔ lɛ fã kroko lɛ?

english: Farm tools easily carry infected plant sap and diseased soil. Cleaning them prevents you from transferring sickness from an unhealthy plant directly into the cuts of a healthy crop.
ga: Okwaafoi anitsumɔ he nibii baanyɛ aŋɔ tso mli nu ni hela emɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ lɛ oya. Hetsemɔ baatsi bo gbɛ koni okagbɛ hela kɛjɛ tso ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛya tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fãi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ anɔ.

english: Are insects the only thing that bring diseases to my yam crop?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii pɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ hela baa mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: No, while insects carry many plant viruses, diseases can also travel through infected soil, dirty water, contaminated farming tools, or diseased seed yams.
ga: Dabi, eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi bibii hiɛɔ tsei amli helai babaoo moŋ, shi helai hu baanyɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ nɔ, nu ni mli ewo muji, okwaayeli nibii ni mli ewo muji lɛ anɔ. loo ŋmeii ni hela yɔɔ mli

english: Why do some of my yams rot inside the ground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Yam rot in the ground is usually caused by fungal or bacterial diseases entering the tuber through tiny wounds made by soil pests or nematodes, especially in waterlogged soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato fitemɔ ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni ji fungal loo bacteria ni boteɔ tuber lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ pilamɔi bibii ni sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai loo nematodes kɛbaa lɛ nɔ, titri lɛ yɛ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do small insects actually pass sickness to my crops?
ga: Te kooloi bibii feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛgbɛɔ helai amɛshwãa miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Insects like whiteflies or aphids feed on the sap of a sick plant, pick up the disease, and then inject it into healthy plants when they bite them to feed.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids yeɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli nu lɛ, amɛŋɔɔ hela lɛ, ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛwoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli kɛ́ amɛye koni amɛye nii.

english: Is it safe for me to use seed yams saved from a field that had diseased plants last season?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ sweet potato dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ yɛ mli yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: No, seed yams harvested from a sick field often carry the infection hidden inside them, which will grow into weak or rotting plants in your new season.
ga: Dabi, bei pii lɛ, sweet potato dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ yɛ helai ni yɔɔ mli ni akɛtee. Enɛ baakwɛ̃ ni etsɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni miifite yɛ obe hee lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my crop is dying because of insects or because of something in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigboi yɛ kooloi loo nɔ ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ?

english: Pest damage usually shows as holes, bites, or visible bugs on the leaves, while soil diseases typically cause the whole plant to wilt, turn yellow, or rot at the base near the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ jieɔ amɛhe kpo akɛ bu, ŋmeii ni anaa yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ helai haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi. etsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo egbo yɛ shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ

english: Why do the leaves on my yam vines start turning yellow long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ be saŋŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Early yellowing is a sign of distress, often caused by root-damaging pests, nutrient shortages in the soil, or fungal diseases attacking the vine base.
ga: Yellow mra ji haomɔ he okadi. Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa wain tso lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Does burning the old crop remains on my field help stop diseases for the next planting season?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii momoi ni ashãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ helai anaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, burning diseased stems and roots destroys hidden insect eggs and fungal spores so they cannot survive in the soil to attack your next batch of crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei kɛ shishifãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ashãa lɛ kpataa kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ ahiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛtutua oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I clear all the weeds from my plot before I plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu nii lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and will steal water, sunlight, and nutrients from the soil. Clearing weeds before planting gives your seeds a clean start so they can grow strong without competing for food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛbaaju nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi dani odu lɛ, ehaa odumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛdara waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛye akaŋ yɛ niyenii he.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji mikɛ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. This overcrowding results in thin, weak stalks and very small cobs of maize.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni adu lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ fe nine nɛɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: If soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves above ground instead of growing tubers below. Cassava needs balanced soil nutrients and potassium to build big root tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ potassium he miihia cassava koni enyɛ efee shishifãi wuji.

english: Yam plants are vines that produce energy through their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they can catch maximum sunlight and avoids leaf rot caused by wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ni kɛ hewalɛ baa kɛtsɔɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. ni etsĩɔ baai ni sũ ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa trees turning brown and burning during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under full sun. They need shade crops like plantains grown beside them to act as living umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the leaves and stems of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common maize pest. They hide inside the leaves to eat the tender heart of the plant, but they can be controlled early by putting ash or safe recommended pesticides into the center leaf swirl.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmei ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ amli koni amɛye tso lɛ mli fã ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Shi abaanyɛ akudɔ lɛ mra. Kɛtsɔ sũ loo tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛwoɔ kooloo ko mli yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plant leaves curl up and get dark spots after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ diŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rainwater splashing up from the ground carries fungal spores that attach to tomato leaves and cause leaf blight. Removing the leaves closest to the ground prevents the soil water from infecting the plant.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni haa baai lɛ shãa lɛ yɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie baai ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi shikpɔŋ nu lɛ naa koni ekatswa tso lɛ hela.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same field drains the soil of the specific nutrients maize needs and allows maize pests to live permanently in the soil. Rotating with cowpeas or groundnuts refills the soil with nitrogen and starves the pests.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi he hiaa lɛ. ni ehaa ŋmãa mli ŋmeii hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa. Kɛ́ okɛ cowpeas loo peanuts tsake lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ ayi obɔ kɛ nitrogen ni ebaaha hɔmɔ abagbe kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ.

english: Fertilizer works best when plants have already developed small roots, usually a few weeks after sprouting, and when the soil is damp so the nutrients can dissolve into the ground.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ shishifãi bibii, bei pii lɛ, otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. kɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔni afee ni niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ anyɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is healthy enough to produce a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Healthy farm soil is usually dark in color, feels crumbly when squeezed, holds moisture without becoming muddy, and has living organisms like earthworms crawling inside it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kpakpai amli lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enuɔ he akɛ egbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ ashɛre lɛ Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni etsɔɔɔ muji Ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ ni shwieɔ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off as soon as the dry Harmattan season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛji harmattan fɛ̃i be lɛ je shishi pɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their leaves during dry conditions to reduce water loss through evaporation. Planting shade trees like plantains or Gliricidia near young cocoa helps preserve soil moisture and protects leaves from direct dry winds.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ aba shi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ tsei bibii loo gliricidia ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ebuɔ baai ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that are easily weakened by pests like root nematodes or stem borers. Staking plants with strong Y-shaped sticks and keeping soil healthy gives roots stronger anchorage against winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes loo stem borers lɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni tamɔ Y lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ, ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ hi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ anyɛ atswa kɔɔyɔɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting early in the storage barn before I am ready to plant or sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ mra yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mifeɔ klalo akɛ madu loo mahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Yams sprout when exposed to high temperatures and light, which signals to the tuber that it is time to grow. Storing yams in a cool, well-ventilated, shaded barn delays sprouting by keeping the tubers in a resting state.
ga: Sweet potatoes baakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛwo hulutsoo be ni mli wa kɛ la mli. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ naa akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ eda. Sweet Potatoes ni Akɛtoɔ Cool Barn Mli Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulutsoo baaha ekwɛ̃mɔ asɛɛ afo kɛtsɔ bulbs lɛ ni eeeha amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that attacks the growing center or 'whorl' of maize. Catching them early and applying recommended biological or chemical controls prevents them from destroying the plant's growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ shweremɔ hei loo ‘rings’ lɛ. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua. Ni kɛ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop dark, rotten spots on the bottom while they are still growing on the bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato yibii lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ jwɛi lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is a condition called Blossom End Rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often triggered by irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture consistent helps the plant deliver calcium to the fruit properly.
ga: Enɛ ji shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Blossom End Rot, ni calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ calcium baa aduawai lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or attacks by tiny pests like thrips. Ensuring steady watering and providing light shade during extreme heat helps the plant retain flowers to form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa amɛ, nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of green leaves but yield very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? baai eŋɔli babaoo Shi kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to focus all its energy on leaf and stem growth instead of root development. Balanced soil nutrients, especially potassium, encourage the plant to send energy down to swell the tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe nii. yɛ shishifãi ni baa lɛ najiaŋ Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja titri lɛ potassium Wo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ amaje shi koni eha bulb lɛ mli alɛɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me that planting groundnuts or cowpeas makes soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special root nodules that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop dies, this natural nitrogen remains in the soil to feed the next crop, like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii gboi Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaba wɔsɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know if my soil needs poultry manure or chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia kooloi ashishi loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Poultry manure improves soil structure, holds moisture, and releases nutrients slowly, while chemical fertilizer provides quick nutrients to plants in immediate need. Using both together gives fast growth while improving long-term soil health.
ga: Kooloo ŋmei haa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛo, ehiɛɔ nu mli, ni ejieɔ niyenii kpakpai blɛoo. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei ni he hiaa amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ niyenii oya. Kɛ́ akɛ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ daa oya yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Does lowland paddy rice always need to sit in deep water to grow properly?
ga: Ani esa akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ ahi nu ni mli kwɔ mli be fɛɛ be koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Lowland rice thrives in standing water because water suppresses weeds and regulates soil temperature, but rice roots actually need oxygen too. Controlled flooding and draining cycle techniques allow rice to grow well using less water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli ejaakɛ nu lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi anaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ yaa hiɛ. Shi kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu he miihia ŋmãa shishifãi. Nu afua nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ he ŋaai yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ nu fioo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if the seed maize I bought from the market is clean and free from seed-borne diseases before I plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ he tse ni helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli baa lɛ bɛ mli dani mikɛdu?

english: Healthy planting seeds should be uniform in size, free from cracks, insect holes, or discoloration. Purchasing certified seeds from accredited agricultural dealers ensures your seeds are pure, have high germination rates, and are free from hidden seed-borne diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui ni adu ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ adalɛ afee ekome. Ebɛ ŋmeii, ŋmeii bu loo su tsakemɔ. Dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ni ooohe kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ haa odumɔwui lɛ ahe tseɔ. Eyɛ shweremɔ ni yaa hiɛ ni helai ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛbaa lɛ bɛ mli

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and die suddenly even when the ground is full of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by soil-borne bacteria or fungi living in the land that choke the plant's water veins. Rotating tomatoes with non-related crops like maize or cassava starves these soil pests and keeps your land clean for future seasons.
ga: Bei pii lɛ nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji muawai ni yɔɔ sũ mli loo ŋmeii ni tsiɔ tso lɛ nu paipii lɛ anaa. Tsɔɔmɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ tsakpaa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ebaaha hɔmɔ aye nɛkɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. ni oye obua ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atse yɛ bei ni baa lɛ amli.

english: Why is my farmland producing much smaller yam yields today than it used to produce ten years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ, miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo kwraa fe afii nyɔŋma ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Farming on the same plot year after year without rest drains essential plant nutrients from the soil. Adding compost, animal manure, or proper chemical fertilizers restores these missing nutrients so your soil can feed big yams again.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kome nɔ okwaayeli afi fɛɛ afi ni hejɔɔmɔ bɛ mli lɛ haa tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ falɛ ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aku sɛɛ aba. Bɔni afee ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ akwɛ ŋmeii wuji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do agricultural officers always encourage me to plant cowpeas or beans on the same plot where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ woɔ mi hewalɛ koni madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmã yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas have roots that pull nitrogen out of the air and trap it in the soil. This naturally fertilizes the land, feeding hungry crops like maize planted afterward without extra cost.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii ni awooo he nyɔmɔ kroko.

english: Why are the leaves of my young pepper plants turning yellow even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a signal that your plant is starving for nitrogen, a key nutrient needed to keep leaves green and strong. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted chicken manure gives the crop the boost it needs to stay green.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni tsei lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo loo tsina ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why are the seasonal rains coming much later in the year than they used to when my father was farming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baa sɛɛ fe nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ beni Ataa tsuɔ okwaayeli he nii lɛ?

english: Global climate patterns and local deforestation are changing weather behavior across Ghana. Because rainfall seasons are now unpredictable, farmers need to check local weather forecasts and plant short-duration or drought-tolerant crop varieties.
ga: Jeŋ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ kooi ni afoɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ miitsake kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe subaŋ yɛ Ghana fɛɛ. Ejaakɛ amrɔ nɛɛ, anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ okwaafoi akwɛ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi yɔɔ ha yɛ amɛmaŋ lɛ mli ni amɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo loo ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa.

english: What are these tiny worms appearing in the leaves of my maize after heavy rains, and how are they attacking my field?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii ni jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-abele baa lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ nɛɛ? Ni te amɛfeɔ tɛŋŋ amɛtutuaa miŋmɔji lɛ?

english: These are pests like the Fall Armyworm, which travel through wind currents across long distances. They eat the growing center of maize plants, preventing the plant from making leaves and reducing your harvest if not sprayed early with safe insecticides.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni fãa gbɛ kakadaŋŋ kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Amɛyeɔ hei ni ŋmãa tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Enɛ baatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaje baai ni ebaaha okpamɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ shwieee nɔ mra.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their flower buds before turning into healthy cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho amɛ ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛbatsɔ cacao ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Flower drop happens when cocoa trees suffer from extreme heat, prolonged dry spells, or sap-sucking pests like mirids. Planting temporary shade trees like plantains and keeping the root zone covered with leaves helps hold moisture so the flowers stay attached.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji akɛ cacao tso lɛ na hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ nu tamɔ pollen Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aaadu ni akɛ baai aha shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ akpɛtɛ he.

english: What makes my harvested cassava roots taste bitter and woody sometimes instead of sweet and soft?
ga: Mɛni haa bei komɛi lɛ, mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ tso moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee blɛoo?

english: Cassava plants produce natural bitter chemicals when they face extreme water stress or grow in nutrient-poor soil. Harvesting cassava at the right age and keeping the soil moist during growth keeps the roots soft and sweet.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ feɔ tsofai ni mli wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji amɛkɛ nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa kpe loo amɛdara yɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii kpakpai bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmei yɛ afii ni sa mli, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How can I stop insects and weevils from destroying my harvested maize and cowpeas while stored in my barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa kɛ tsina-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ hiɛ be mli ni mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa?

english: Insects thrive where there is trapped air and moisture. Completely drying your harvested grains in the sun and storing them in sealed, airtight storage bags (like PICS bags) suffocates insects without requiring dangerous chemical powders.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ni agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni akɛtoɔ kotokui ni akɛ nibii toɔ mli ni nɔ ko bɛ mli (tamɔ PICS kotokui) amli lɛ baaha kooloi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni akɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees on the same land where I am planting my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ he ni miduɔ kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and get scorched easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have wide leaves that create living shade to protect the young cocoa plants and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I avoid burning all the dry grass and leftover stalks on my field before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ jwɛi kɛ tsei ni eshwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashãa dani madu nii lɛ he?

english: Burning destroys the good organic matter that feeds the earth. Leaving dead plant material to rot on the farm feeds beneficial organisms in the soil, preserves soil moisture, and prevents heavy rain from washing away your topsoil.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii kpakpai ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii lɛ. Tsei ni egboi ni ashiɔ koni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni otsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my growing maize plants turning yellow along the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei ni midu lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means your soil is running low on nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main nutrient that gives crops their deep green color and strength to grow big stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni haa tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ kɛ hewalɛ yɛ tsei wuji amli.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas or beans in the same field alongside my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas have special roots that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds your corn and improves the overall quality of your farm soil.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa o-ŋmãa lɛ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ feɔ fɛo.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with plenty of green leaves, but the tubers underground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When there is too much foliage growth, it often means the soil has too much nitrogen or the plants are crowded. The cassava plant puts all its energy into growing leaves above ground instead of sending food down to build thick roots.
ga: Beni baai lɛ daraa babaoo lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ yaa si konɛ e pee sisi nɛ mi wa.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop in the middle of the afternoon even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: On hot days, tomato leaves lose water through evaporation faster than the roots can drink it up from the soil. This temporary wilting protects the plant from overheating, and it will normally stand back up when the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ shwiemɔ ni baa be kukuoo nɛɛ buɔ tso lɛ he koni ekadɔ fe nine. Ni bei pii lɛ, tsei teɔ shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why do I need to push tall wooden poles into the ground for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi tso kakadaŋŋ ko kɛya ŋwɛi lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni mi sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to produce the energy needed for big tubers. Keeping the leaves off the damp ground also protects the foliage from soil-borne rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa kɛha bulb agboi lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ sũ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the juices from under the fresh leaves, or by a virus carried by those insects. Treating the pests early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai heei ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Ni ajieɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why shouldn't I save and plant the seeds from the hybrid maize I harvested last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni ji hybrid corn ni mikpa yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to give a strong, high yield for only one season. If you plant the seeds saved from that harvest, the resulting crop will grow unevenly, give a poor yield, and be easily attacked by diseases.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ be kome pɛ mli. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ Nibii ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ, amɛbaawo yibii fioo, ni helai baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ oya.

english: How can I tell if the soil has enough moisture for me to start sowing my seeds after the early rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Take a handful of soil from a few inches deep and squeeze it into a ball. If it holds its shape comfortably without dripping water and easily crumbles when you press it, the ground has enough moisture for seeds to germinate without rotting.
ga: Okɛ sũ ni mli kwɔ ni ji inchi fioo komɛi awo mli ni okɛmimɔ mli ni okɛfee bɔɔlu. Kɛji ehiɛ egbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ Ni nu shwieee shi ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛji onyɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboŋ.

english: If I save seeds from my best maize crops and plant them next season, will the new plants look and yield exactly like the mother plant?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-ŋmãa ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ to ni midu amɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, Ani tso hee lɛ baaná sui kɛ yibiiwoo tamɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Not always. Local open-pollinated crops tend to pass on similar traits, but hybrid crops mix genetic traits from two parent plants. Seeds saved from hybrid crops often produce smaller yields and unpredictable traits compared to the mother plant.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Tsei ni yɔɔ akutso lɛ mli ni amɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ fɔɔ sui ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ amɛhaa. Shi tsei ni akɛ amɛhe ewo mli lɛ kɛ fɔmɔ nii ni jɛ fɔlɔi tsei enyɔ amli lɛ feɔ ekome. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ni amɛyɛ sui ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba kɛ akɛto fɔlɔ tso lɛ he.

english: Why do my maize cobs sometimes grow with mixed yellow and white grains on the very same cob?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛ ŋmãa ni ji ŋmɔŋ kɛ eyɛŋ ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmãa kome mli lɛ?

english: Each kernel on a maize cob gets fertilized individually by pollen from the air. If pollen blown from a neighboring yellow maize field lands on your white maize silks, those specific kernels will inherit the yellow color from the male parent.
ga: Akɛ pollen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ fɔmɔ nii. Kɛji akɛ pollen ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli lɛ bagbee oŋmãa siliki yɛŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Nakai ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ baaná amɛŋmãa su lɛ gboshinii kɛjɛ amɛfɔlɔi hii lɛ adɛŋ.

english: If I plant seeds saved from a very sweet tomato crop, will the new tomato plants produce fruit with the exact same sweet taste?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ tomato ni ŋɔɔ waa ni mikwɛɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Ani tomato tso hee lɛ baawo yibii ni ŋɔɔ waa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: If the original tomato was cross-pollinated by another tomato variety nearby, the seeds carry mixed traits from both parent plants. The new fruits might end up tasting different or growing with a different shape.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shishijee tomato lɛ kɛ tomato kroko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ wo mli lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ baafee fɔlɔi tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni akɛfee ekome. Yibii hee baanyɛ afee srɔto loo eda kɛ su srɔto.

english: If I harvest a small yam tuber, will planting setts from it automatically result in small yams next year?
ga: Kɛji mikpa sweet potato ŋmeii bibii Ani sweet potato ŋmeii ni adu yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmeii bibii aba lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Not necessarily. Tuber size is heavily influenced by growing conditions like soil fertility, water, and rainfall. A small sett cut from a healthy plant can still produce a large tuber if grown in rich, moist soil.
ga: Dabi, shihilɛi tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ, nu, kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ náa bɔ ni bulb lɛ da ha lɛ nɔ hewalɛ waa. Tsei bibii ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ awo bulbs wuji lolo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning brown and changing color instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛhiɛ su tsakeɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf discoloration is usually a sign of environmental stress, lack of essential nutrients like nitrogen, or attacks by pests like mealybugs. Changing color is the plant's natural reaction when it is struggling to absorb food and water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ahe su ni tsakeɔ lɛ ji shihilɛ mli haomɔ he okadi. Niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen ni bɛ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mealybugs lɛ tutuamɔ. Su ni tsakeɔ lɛ ji nɔ ko ni tso lɛ feɔ kɛ́ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii kɛ nu.

english: Why do my bean leaves have dark brown spots and speckled patches all over them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi yɛ amɛhe fɛɛ lɛ?
