english: Speckled or brown spots on bean leaves are typically caused by fungal or bacterial diseases. High humidity and rainwater splashing soil onto the lower leaves help spread these leaf spot organisms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai loo bacteria helai ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ baa. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ nugbɔ nu ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nɛkɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my pepper fruits change color from green to bright red or yellow as they grow on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli nɔ kɛyaa etsuru loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ beni amɛdaraa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Color changes are a natural behavior showing that the pepper fruit is reaching full maturity. As the fruit ripens, green chlorophyll breaks down and reveals bright pigments that carry the plant's natural variety traits.
ga: Su tsakemɔ ji adebɔɔ mli subaŋ ko ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ yibii lɛ miida. Beni aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ, klorofil eŋɔli lɛ mli gbalaa ni ejieɔ tso lɛ su srɔtoi ni kpɛɔ lɛ kpo.

english: If I plant two different varieties of sweet potato side by side, will they mix underground and change each other's skin color?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmɔtɔ henɔi enyɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, Ani amɛbaafutu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛbaatsake amɛhewolo nɔ su?

english: No, the tubers growing underground this season will retain their own variety's skin and flesh color. Cross-pollination only affects the genetic traits inside the seeds produced by flowers, not the root tubers you harvest.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baahiɛ amɛhewolo kɛ amɛheloo su lɛ mli. Cross-pollination lɛ saa fɔmɔ nii ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni jɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ pɛ he. Jeee shishifãi ni okpaa lɛ ji no.

english: How can I tell if a crop seed variety will give me high yields just by looking at the color or size of the seed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔwui lɛ baawo yibii babaoo yɛ amɛhe su loo amɛdalɛ naa?

english: You cannot tell a seed's yield potential just by physical appearance. High yields come from genetic traits bred into the seed over time, along with good soil nutrients, proper watering, and farm care.
ga: Onyɛŋ otsɔɔ bɔ ni dumɔwu ko baanyɛ awo yibii yɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ pɛ nɔ. Yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo jɛɔ fɔmɔ nii ni aduɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ mli. kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli Nu ni sa kɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before forming small green fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when exposed to extreme heat, water stress, or when pollination fails. Without successful transfer of pollen inside the flower, the plant aborts the bloom instead of developing fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni naa wa waa he. nu mli haomɔ loo be mli ni pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii Kɛji akɛ anyɛɛɛ ajie pollen lɛ kɛya fɔfɔi lɛ amli yɛ omanyeyeli mli Tso lɛ baakpa fɔfɔi fɔmɔ yɛ yibiiwoo najiaŋ.

english: Why are my young cocoa leaves turning yellow and drying up when exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn under hot sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates living umbrellas that give cocoa the cool shade and soil moisture it needs to survive its early stage.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni haa kookoo lɛ naa hulu ni mli ejɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eshishijee bei amli lɛ baa.

english: How does planting groundnuts alongside my maize help my soil and main crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil. Planting them with maize acts like a natural fertilizer, feeding the soil and helping your maize grow stronger without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ abele duɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Feed the soil Ni eyeɔ ebuaa o-corn lɛ ni edara waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma babaoo atsu nii.

english: Yellowing at the bottom leaves usually shows that the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the key nutrient for leaf growth. Adding animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea early in the season will restore the green color and boost your crop yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ baai lɛ ashishi ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo ŋmei ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with big leafy branches but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ niji kɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together or given too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plant uses all its energy to grow stems and leaves above ground. Giving each plant proper spacing forces it to push energy into growing large tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo akɛ nitrogen babaoo wo mli. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ tsei kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso fɛɛ tso ha gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ebaanyɛ hewalɛ nɔ koni ekɛya bulbs wuji ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it necessary for me to build stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni matswa tso ko kɛha mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni makwɔ?

english: Yes, staking yam vines lifts the leaves toward maximum sunlight and keeps them away from damp soil diseases. Leaves exposed to plenty of sunlight produce more food energy, resulting in much larger yam tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, sweet potato wain tsei ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ baaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná hulu la babaoo ni ebaatsi helai anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Baai ni naa hulu la babaoo lɛ Baaha niyenii hewalɛ babaoo aba. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy rains and wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy bunches of fruit during storms. Digging deeper planting holes and building mounds of soil and compost around the base gives the roots a firmer grip in the earth to stay standing.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii lɛ yɛ ahum be mli. Ni aaaku dumɔ bu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ Ni ama muji kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbɔleɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it critical for me to clear weeds while my maize plants are still very young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ be mli ni mi-abele tsei lɛ darako kwraa lɛ?

english: Young crop plants are weak and will lose the battle for water, light, and soil food against fast-growing weeds. Clearing weeds in the first month allows your maize to grow big quickly and shade out future weeds on its own.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛbaaye kunim yɛ ta ni amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli amɛshiɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha o-abele lɛ ada oya ni ekɛ jwɛi ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without setting any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat, uneven watering, or insect attack on the blooms. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and spraying organic pest deterrents helps the flowers stay healthy and develop into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa Aloo kooloi komɛi yɛ ni tutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛtsɔ tomatoi.

english: Why do I see ragged holes inside the funnels of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji ni etse yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in young maize foliage are caused by armyworm caterpillars hiding in the center leaves. Checking your farm early in the morning and applying recommended neem oil or bio-pesticide straight into the leaf funnel will stop them before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ abele baa bibii amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi ni okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ko ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni atsɛɔ amɛ bio-insecticide lɛ awo tsei lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa amɛkpaa dani amɛfiteɔ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn to powder and get tiny insects inside after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ miitsɔ powda ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ? Yaa mli beni ato he gbɛjianɔ nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ.

english: Small insects called grain weevils attack stored maize that still has moisture in it. Drying your maize thoroughly until the grains are hard and storing them in airtight bags or clean cribs prevents weevils from multiplying and eating your harvest.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ grain moths lɛ tutuaa ŋmãa ni ato ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa ni okɛto vacuum kotokui loo ŋmãa ni mli tse mli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmãa ni ji ŋmãa lɛ naa koni ekafa babaoo ni eye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why should I plant plantains next to my new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei heei ahe?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under the full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: How does burying clay pots filled with water near my vegetable beds help my plants?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ sũ tsɛnsi ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni mikɛfuɔ yɛ mi aduawai aŋmɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi tsei lɛ?

english: Unglazed clay pots allow water to slowly seep through their porous walls directly into the deep soil, giving plant roots constant moisture without wasting water to evaporation.
ga: Terakota tsɛnsii ni glase bɛ mli lɛ haa nu lɛ yaa hiɛ fiofio. Ebaanyɛ etsɔ gbogboi ni mli ewo muji lɛ amli kɛbote shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso shishifãi ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli daa ni amɛfiteee nu kɛha ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my crops stay greener when I leave cleared weeds and dead leaves on top of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ eŋɔli kɛ́ mishi jwɛi kɛ baai ni egboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving dead plant material on the soil acts like a protective blanket, keeping the ground cool, trapping moisture, and feeding the soil as the leaves decompose.
ga: Tsei ni egboi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i, emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii be mli ni baai lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and fall off when the long dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry weather to reduce water loss. The plant goes quiet above ground while keeping its edible tuber roots safe and alive beneath the soil.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni egbiɔ lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Tso lɛ hiɔ shi dioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ehaa eshishifãi ni ayeɔ lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe ni ehiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they get stressed by high afternoon heat, irregular watering, or soil that lacks balanced nutrients, saving energy until conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ shwane latsaa lɛ hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo shikpɔŋ ni niyenii ni sa bɛ mli Enɛ haa hewalɛ baa shi kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens if I plant too many maize seeds in one small hole?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu bibioo kome mli?

english: When seeds are crowded together, the young plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin, weak stalks and small or missing cobs.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ fee ekome yɛ kui amli lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ dumɔwui bibii loo ni bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings wither and die right after I move them from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Moving plants causes transplant shock because hot sun dries out damaged root tips. Moving seedlings late in the afternoon gives roots time to settle in cool soil overnight.
ga: Tsei ni tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ kɛ shoofeemɔ baa ejaakɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi ni efite lɛ gĩɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa be koni amɛhi shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ lɛ nɔ nyɔɔŋ kome.

english: Why do worms appear inside the funnel of my maize leaves before the cobs even form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-abɛi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli dani ŋmeii lɛ po feɔ lɛ?

english: Moths lay eggs on soft young maize leaves, and the hatched caterpillars, like fall armyworms, hide inside the whorl to eat tender leaf tissue before moving into the cobs.
ga: Kpɔŋɔi fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii anɔ. kɛ ŋmeii ni efɔ momo, tamɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ amli fãji dani amɛyabote ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do white powdery spots spread across my tomato leaves during warm, humid weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powder yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-tomato baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ?

english: High humidity and wet leaves create ideal conditions for airborne fungal spores to land, sprout, and spread across leaf surfaces, weakening the plant's food production.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa kɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kɔɔyɔɔ mli fungal spores lɛ koni amɛba shikpɔŋ, amɛkwɛ̃, ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã baa lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, niyenii ni tsei feɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my field make my next harvest of maize grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mi-ŋmei kpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli waa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the groundnut crop finishes, that stored nitrogen acts as a free natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ agbe ŋmei dumɔ naa lɛ Nitrogen ni ato lɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmei ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants lose all their leaves when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry spells to conserve water and survive extreme heat. Once the rains return, the stems use energy stored in underground roots to quickly shoot fresh green leaves again.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba Tso lɛ shishi lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ oya ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the stems before forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani aduawai jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather gets too hot or when the soil dries out completely. Heat stress prevents the flowers from pollinating properly, so the plant sheds them to protect itself.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Heat haomɔ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei jieɔ lɛ kpo koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why is my maize plant flowering when it is still very short and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi fɔfɔi lɛ ji kukuji ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: When maize suffers early from drought or poor soil nutrients, it senses danger and rushes to produce flowers early to make seeds before dying. Providing early fertilizer and moisture helps stalks grow tall before flowering.
ga: Kɛ́ hɔmɔ loo sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ye ŋmãa nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa nuɔ oshara he ni ekɛ oyaiyeli woɔ fɔfɔi amli mra. Koni adu dumɔwui dani amɛgboi Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your maize lacks nitrogen fertilizer. The plant naturally pulls nitrogen from older leaves at the bottom to keep the young green leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Tsei gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni eha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ.

english: Why do my young maize seedlings have dark purple leaves instead of bright green ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn dumɔwui lɛ baa ni ji purple ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize indicate that the plant is struggling to absorb phosphorus from wet or cold soil. As the weather warms and roots expand, applying phosphorus-rich starter fertilizer resolves the color issue.
ga: Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miitao ejie fɔsfɔs kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ nɔ. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli woɔ la ni shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ, Kɛ́ okɛ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii ni fɔsfɔs babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua yɛ kɔla he naagba lɛ he.

english: Why is my cowpea crop full of thick green leaves but producing very few flower pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ eyi kɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli tse shi ewoɔ fɔfɔii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: When cowpeas receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, they put all their energy into growing leaves instead of fruits. Cowpeas generate their own nitrogen from the soil, so extra fertilizer causes heavy leaves with low pod yields.
ga: Kɛji tsina ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ lɛ, ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Cowpeas feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee tsiimɔ kɛ pod yibiiwoo ni baa shi.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling downwards and turning crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle shi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or aphids under the leaves. They drain sap from young tissues, making the leaves twist and stunting fruit development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Amɛjieɔ mliki lɛ kɛjɛɔ fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad canopy shade that creates the cool, humid climate cocoa shoots need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo ni haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my yam plants grow better tubers when I give them wooden stakes to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ tsei ni akɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ ha amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb toward sunlight to make food for growing underground tubers. Staking keeps leaves spread out toward the sun and elevated above damp soil where foliage diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa hulu lɛ he ni ewoɔ amɛ nɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ, he ni baa helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily right when the fruit bunch starts growing heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ mli tsii lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and easily weakened by soil pests like root nematodes or stem borers. Supporting fruiting trees with strong wooden poles prevents wind from pushing over heavy bunches before harvest.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes loo stem borers lɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ oya. Yibii tsei ni akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsii akatswa tsei lɛ akui lɛ anɔ dani akpa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees burning and turning yellow in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides shade and keeps the soil cool so the young cocoa can grow safely.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji koni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ada shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tips inward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ mligbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen fertilizer. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and produce large, heavy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii aba.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes in the middle leaves of my young maize crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms, a common pest that hides in the central leaves of maize during the day and feeds at night. Spraying appropriate pest control early in the morning or late evening protects the young crops before they are destroyed.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji fall asraafoi. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni ekɛ ehe teeɔ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli yɛ shwane mli, ni eyeɔ nii gbɛkɛ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe dani akpata amɛhiɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is ready to harvest under the ground without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, and cracks begin to appear in the soil around the base of the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Ni ŋmeii bɔi baa yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on wooden stakes to lift their leaves toward the sun. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which travels down to grow big, healthy yam tubers beneath the ground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ anɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ he. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. Enɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛhe wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: When too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they steal nutrients and water from the main tree, resulting in small fruit bunches. Leaving only two or three healthy shoots ensures high yield and large plantains.
ga: Beni dumɔwui babaoo ni miida yɛ plantain kome he lɛ Ebaaju niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa anáa aduawai bibii. Kɛ́ ashi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha yibii babaoo kɛ dumɔwui wuji aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling tightly together and growing small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa ni amɛfee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a plant disease, or by extreme heat. Using nets to block flies and watering regularly keeps the plants healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ tsei ahe helai eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli Fly netting ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the air is too hot and dry or when the soil lacks moisture. Providing consistent water and light shade during hot spells helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. or when the soil lacks moisture Consistent water and shade during hot weather help the flowers persist and produce fruit.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests when I plant maize in the same spot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil continuously. Rotating maize with beans or groundnuts puts natural nitrogen back into the soil and keeps harvests high.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baa.

english: Why do some farmers spread dry leaves or grass around the bottom of their crops during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shwieɔ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi amɛshwieɔ amɛtsei lɛ ashishi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Spreading dry leaves or grass on the soil, called mulching, acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the ground, keeps the plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni ŋmɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why do many of the tiny young cocoa pods on my tree turn black and shrivel up before they can grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ, mɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboi dani amɛdara.

english: This natural process is called cherelle wilt. The cocoa tree produces more young pods than it can support, so it deliberately starves and drops the extra ones to ensure it has enough nutrients to grow the remaining pods to full size.
ga: Atsɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni darako tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye amɛbua amɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ejɛ etsui mli ekɛ hɔmɔ ye lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ shwie shi koni ena nɔmimaa akɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ni baaha ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ adara kɛyashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear away all the big shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikpaa cacao tsei wuji lɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense direct sunlight and high heat. Shading crops like plantains or tall trees act as protective umbrellas, keeping the air cool and preserving soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei kakadaji tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo ni buɔ mɔ he. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔɔ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why are the stems on some of my cocoa branches swelling up and making the tree drop its leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mi kookoo niji lɛ anɔ lɛ efuu ni ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Swollen stems are a clear sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Disease, which is caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called mealybugs. The swelling chokes the tree's internal tubes, preventing water and food from moving up to the leaves.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei ni efuu lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ kookoo bud hela yɛ. Virus ko ni koolooi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Fuumɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ mli paipii lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe. Etsiɔ nu kɛ niyenii naa koni amɛkaya ŋwɛi kɛyashɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to stay green and grow, so when the soil runs low, the plant pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ fioo pɛ eshwɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans on my plot make the maize I plant there next season yield better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha mi ŋmãa lɛ yibiiwoo aya hiɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts have special bacteria in their roots that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. When the legumes are harvested, that extra nitrogen remains in the dirt, acting as free natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei yɛ helai krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does putting dry leaves and dead grass around the base of my crops keep them alive longer when rain stops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi ni egboi baabɔle he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ani mi tsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa?

english: This practice is called mulching. The layer of dead leaves acts like a protective blanket over the dirt, stopping the hot sun from evaporating water directly out of the soil so the roots stay damp and cool.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Baai ni egboi lɛ amli fã lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ muji he. Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Koni shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe ajɔɔ

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small, thin bunches when I leave all the young shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ fãa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni ashiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni bɔleɔ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ

english: The young shoots, called suckers, share the same root system as the main mother plant. Leaving too many suckers creates competition, so they steal water and nutrients that the mother plant needs to form a large, heavy fruit bunch.
ga: Tso bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ tso titri lɛ nɔŋŋ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha akaŋshii aba. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tso nyɛ lɛ koni enyɛ ewo aduawai akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden poles to climb up if I want to harvest big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ lɛ? Ani oosumɔ ni ohiɛ yitso agbo mli?

english: Yam leaves are the factories that produce food stored in the tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves high into the air and sunlight, preventing them from overlapping or rotting on the damp ground, which allows the plant to make much more food.
ga: Sweet potato baai ji tsei ni woɔ niyenii ni akɛtoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa amɛfee nɔ ko loo amɛkagbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up into strange shapes with yellowish patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, a viral infection transmitted from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. The virus disrupts the leaf's structure, stopping it from making food properly and leading to much smaller cassava roots.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ anɔ. Virus lɛ gbalaa bɔ ni baai lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa anyɛ ahoo niyenii jogbaŋŋ. ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii kwraa.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants keep falling off without turning into tomatoes when the hot season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the delicate pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fertilization. When a flower fails to get pollinated, the plant automatically drops it to avoid wasting precious water and energy on a fruit that cannot form.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. etsĩɔ fɔmɔ naa Beni anyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ fɔfɔi Tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi amɛ diɛŋtsɛ koni amɛkafite nu kɛ hewalɛ ni jara wa yɛ aduawai ni nyɛŋ afee lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential for green growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-based fertilizer helps the plant regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi aŋmɔji, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom fronds of my young oil palm trees turning bright orange-yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ-ŋmɔlɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Orange or yellowing lower fronds on oil palm trees usually point to a lack of potassium in the soil. Applying potassium-rich fertilizer or spreading wood ash around the base of the palm restores leaf health and improves fruit yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mu tsei anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ potassium faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ akɛ potassium ni fa babaoo tsu nii loo tso sũ ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai lɛ aya hiɛ ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop most of their small flowers before they turn into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Nɔ ni fe fɛɛ lɛ dani ebatsɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but only a small portion get pollinated by tiny insects like midges. Hot dry winds, excessive shade, or lack of soil moisture can cause the tree to shed unpollinated flowers to save energy.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi fã bibioo ko pɛ yɔɔ mli. Kplukai bibii tamɔ ŋmeii pɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ lɛ pollin. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi Shade babaoo Loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ afɔ̃ bɔni afee ni amɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers instead of growing peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi shi moŋ ni eeekwɛ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when temperatures get too high or when there is sudden water stress. Irregular watering or extreme heat prevents proper pollination, causing the plant to shed its blooms.
ga: Pepper tsei baafɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛji nu he haomɔ ba trukaa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo la ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ baatsi pollination ni sa naa. haa tsei shwieɔ shi

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing very bushy with lots of leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ miida ŋmɔ mli nɛkɛ lɛ? Ani eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cowpeas to focus all their energy on growing leaves instead of flowers and pods. Since cowpeas fix their own nitrogen from the air, avoid adding high-nitrogen fertilizers to them.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni miida lɛ ahe nii moŋ fe fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsina ŋmei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baasaa nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ni okɛaawo mli lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground when heavy rains fall continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni naa wa miinɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Excessive water fills the soil's air spaces, suffocating the tubers and allowing fungal rot to spread quickly in soggy ground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hei lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl upward during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes during hot afternoons is a natural defense to reduce water loss through the leaves. If the leaves uncurl in the cooler evening, the plant is simply protecting itself from heat stress.
ga: Tomato baai ni ajieɔ yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ shi. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwie shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miibu ehe kɛmiijɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that struggle to anchor the heavy weight of mature stems and fruit bunches. Supporting them with bamboo stakes or planting in wind-protected areas keeps them standing until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛmɔmɔ tsei ni eda kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii fiɔ tsei lɛ asɛɛ loo aduɔ amɛ yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ buɔ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when planted in a completely cleared field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot withstand harsh, direct sunlight because their young leaves burn easily. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa protects the seedlings until they grow strong enough for full light.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe la babaoo.

english: Why do my harvested yams start growing green shoots while resting inside my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃mɔ be mli ni mijɔɔ mihe yɛ mi tsũ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living plant parts that naturally wake up from dormancy after a few months to start a new growing cycle. Keeping the storage barn cool, well-ventilated, and shaded slows down this natural sprouting process.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii ji tso lɛ fã ni hiɛ ka. Eteɔ shi kɛjɛɔ wɔɔhe mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ koni eje dalɛ hee ko shishi. Oshĩa lɛ mli ni oooha efee fɛ̃i Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ. Ni kɛ́ oná hulutsoo lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: How can I know if my land is good enough to give me a high harvest of maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni ebaawo ŋmãa babaoo?

english: Good maize land has dark, crumbly soil that holds moisture without getting waterlogged. If wild plants and weeds grow thick and dark green on the field, it is usually a sign that the soil is rich enough to yield a good harvest.
ga: Abɛi shikpɔŋ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni nu bɛ mli. Kɛji koo mli tsei kɛ jwɛi kwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo nii jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni ebaawo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my crops yield fewer bags of harvest on the same land after a few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ kotoku lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops draw nutrients out of the soil every single season. If you keep planting the same crop on the same piece of land without adding compost, manure, or fertilizer, the soil becomes tired and hungry, leading to smaller harvests.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ odu tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni hɔmɔ baaye lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: Is it better to clear my land by burning the bushes before I plant?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaatsumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ jwɛi lɛ ashãmɔ nɔ dani adu nii?

english: While burning clears the land quickly, it destroys rich organic matter and kills helpful organisms in the soil. Clearing without burning leaves organic material that breaks down to feed your soil and retain moisture.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, la ni ashãa lɛ haa jɛmɛ tseɔ oya. Shi efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo lɛ, ni egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ashãaa lɛ, eshiɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fiteɔ koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: How does spacing my crops properly help me get a bigger harvest at the end of the season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ to he ni sa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua mi ni makpã nii babaoo yɛ be lɛ naagbee?

english: Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, air, and soil nutrients to grow strong. When plants are planted too close together, they fight for food and light, resulting in weak stems and smaller yields.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ la he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do some of my crops grow very tall and bushy but produce very little grain or fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji shi amɛwoɔ dumɔwui loo aduawai fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: This usually happens when there is too much nitrogen in the soil or when plants receive too much shade. The crop spends all its energy developing leaves and stems instead of putting energy into fruits or grains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo kɛ́ tso lɛ ná hulutsoo babaoo. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai kɛ tsei. Mohu ɔ, ngɔ he wami kɛ wo tso yiblii aloo ngma mi.

english: Rotating crops breaks the life cycle of pests and diseases that build up in the soil. Different crops also feed on different nutrients, so switching crops keeps the soil balanced and healthy.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ fiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ashihilɛ gbɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahenɔi srɔtoi hu naa niyenii mli hewalɛ srɔtoi. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow even when there is plenty of rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves during rainy weather often mean the soil is waterlogged, which prevents the roots from breathing and absorbing food. Heavy rains can also wash away important plant nutrients like nitrogen deep into the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛmu niyenii. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa hu baanyɛ ajie tsei amli niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop their leaves when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shwieɔ baai yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry weather as a natural way to protect itself from losing water. Once the rains return, the plant quickly sprouts fresh leaves and continues growing underground.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni egbiɔ lɛ. Eji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ naa. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baawo baai heei oya ni ebaaya nɔ eda yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up tight during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up to shield themselves from direct sunlight and reduce water loss. It is the plant's natural way of saving water until the temperature cools down in the evening.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he ni amɛha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Eji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ nu he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: What causes my tomatoes to get dark rot spots at the bottom before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa tomatoi lɛ shishi feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ diŋ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa?

english: This rot is usually caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, which happens when watering is irregular. Uneven soil moisture stops the plant's roots from consistently taking up nutrients from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ ekomefeemɔ lɛ tsiɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: How can I tell if my crops are sick from a virus or if they just need more water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ emɔ hela kɛjɛ hela ko mli loo nu babaoo he miihia amɛ?

english: Thirsty crops usually wilt during the hot sun and recover after watering or rain. A viral disease, however, causes permanent symptoms like yellow patterns, leaf curling, or stunted growth that water alone will not fix.
ga: Tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ fɔɔ shwiemɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni ehiɛ baa shi yɛ nu loo nugbɔ ni enɛ sɛɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli kɛbaa lɛ kɛ okadii ni hiɔ shi daa tamɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi, baai ni ebɔle ehe, loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu pɛ nyɛŋ asaa lɛ baa.

english: How often should I walk through my farm to check for sick plants?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mayakwɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: It is best to inspect your farm at least once or twice a week. Regular monitoring helps you catch early signs of pests or diseases before they multiply and spread across your entire crop field.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome loo shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ mli daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ahe okadii mra. Dani amɛbaafee babaoo ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants have yellow patches and twisted shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ ni efite lɛ?

english: Yellow patches and twisted leaves are classic signs of the cassava mosaic virus. It distorts leaf growth and stops the plant from producing large, healthy tubers.
ga: He ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ baai ni etsilɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. Efiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can a plant disease travel from my neighbor's farm to my new farm?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai baanyɛ aya kɛjɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛya miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: Yes, plant diseases like viruses easily travel between farms. Insects carrying the virus, contaminated farm tools, wind, and even farm workers walking between fields can bring diseases into a new farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aya ŋmɔji ateŋ mlɛo. Kplukai ni kɛ helai baa ŋmɔ mli nibii ni efite, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi po ni fãa kɛyaa ŋmɔji ateŋ lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ hela aba ŋmɔ hee mli.

english: Why do small insects like flies or bugs make my crops sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii haa miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ hela lɛ?

english: Insects like whiteflies or aphids feed on plant sap. When they bite a sick plant, they pick up the virus and inject it into healthy plants on their next feed, acting like mosquitoes spreading sickness.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids yeɔ tsei amli nu. kɛ amɛye tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ Amɛheɔ hela lɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli be kroko ni amɛbaaye nii. Feemɔ onii tamɔ ŋmeii ni gbɛɔ helai eshwaa

english: Can using my cutlass on different farms spread sickness to my crops?
ga: Mikɛ mi dagger lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔji srɔtoi amli Ani hela baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Yes, infected plant sap sticks to tool blades. If you use an unwashed cutlass or hoe on a sick plant and then clear healthy crops, you directly transfer the disease into the cuts made on the healthy plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso mli nu ni hela emɔ lɛ baakpɛtɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Kɛ okɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni afɔɔɔ he tsu nii yɛ tso ko ni hela mɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, jiemɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Obaajie hela lɛ kɛya tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ ni afo lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: If I clear a fresh piece of land, will my new crops automatically be safe from diseases?
ga: Kɛji mijie he ko hee Ani miŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ baafee shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ helai ahe kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe?

english: Not automatically. Even on fresh land, crops can get sick if you plant diseased seed cuttings, or if insects carry viruses from nearby older farms into your new field.
ga: not automatically Yɛ sũ shikpɔŋ nɔ po Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ aná hela kɛji odu tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ momo ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli kɛtee oŋmɔji heei lɛ amli.

english: If I find one sick crop in my field, should I pull it out immediately or try to cure it?
ga: Kɛji mina ŋmɔshi nibii ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ani esa akɛ mitsi mihe kɛjɛ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo mabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni matsa lɛ?

english: You should pull it out and destroy it immediately. Most plant viruses have no chemical cure once inside the plant, so removing infected plants early protects the rest of your healthy field from catching the disease.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie kɛjɛ mli ni okpãtã hiɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Tso mli helai babaoo bɛ tsofa ko ni akɛbaatsu he nii kɛji amɛbote tso lɛ mli pɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu hei ni eshwɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛ helai ahe.

english: How do I know if the cassava cuttings or seeds I want to plant are safe to use?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmei loo dumɔwui ni misumɔɔ ni madu lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛbaatsu nii?

english: Always collect planting materials from mother plants that look strong, lush green, and completely free of leaf spots or twisting, or buy certified disease-free seeds from reliable agricultural officers.
ga: Bua dumɔ nibii anaa kɛjɛ tso nyɛ lɛ mli ni tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ, eŋɔli, ni baa mli ŋmɔtɔ loo nɔ ko ni efite bɛ mli. Aloo hemɔ dumɔwui ni ana he odaseyeli akɛ hela bɛ mli lɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ lɛ adɛŋ.

english: What should I do if many farms in my community get the same crop disease at the same time?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji ŋmɔji babaoo ni yɔɔ mi akutso lɛ mli lɛ ná tsei ahe hela kome yɛ be kome mli?

english: Farmers in the community must work together to remove infected plants simultaneously and inform the agricultural extension officer. If one farmer leaves sick crops standing, insects will keep spreading the virus back to everyone else's fields.
ga: Esa akɛ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ afee ekome kɛjie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ be kome mli ni amɛha okwaayeli he nitsumɔ he nitsulɔi lɛ ale. Kɛji okwaafonyo ko shi tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ, kooloi lɛ baagbɛ hela lɛ amɛshwã mɛi krokomɛi aŋmɔji amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly when the weather gets very hot and there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl or roll up to protect themselves from losing too much water through heat. It is the plant's natural way of saving moisture inside its leaves during dry spells so it does not dry out and die.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo abɔleɔ he koni nu ni fa fe nine akafite kɛjɛ dɔlɛ mli. Eji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ebaai lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. No hewɔ lɛ, egbiɛɛ ni egbooo.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my pepper plants without turning into peppers during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When a pepper plant does not get enough water in intense heat, it gets stressed and drops its flowers to save energy and stay alive, rather than spending scarce water on growing heavy fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Ebafeɔ haomɔ ni ekɛ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he ni ehi wala mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nu ni anaaa lɛ baatsu nii ni akɛdu aduawai ni tsii.

english: Why do my cowpea crops stay green in dry soil while my leafy vegetables wilt and die quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ hiɔ shi ŋmɔji yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ be mli ni mi-ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants grow long taproots that reach deep underground to find hidden water, whereas leafy vegetables have short roots near the surface that dry out as soon as the topsoil loses moisture.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ woɔ shishifãi kakadaŋŋ agboi ni yaa shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatao nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli nu lɛ sɛɛ fo pɛ.

english: Will my tomatoes grow just as well if I water them with stored rainwater during the dry season?
ga: Ani mitatoi lɛ baakwɛ̃ nakai nɔŋŋ kɛji mikɛ nugbɔ nu ni ato lɛ ha amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, stored rainwater is very good for crops because it is naturally free from harmful minerals and soft on roots, allowing tomato plants to feed and fruit properly even when natural rains stop.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ nu ni ato lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ejaakɛ kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, sũ mli nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui bɛ mli, ni eyɛ blɛoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛnaa niyenii kɛ aduawai jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔ lɛ kpa po.

english: Why do my ripe tomato fruits split open when heavy rain falls after a long dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tswaa kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When a dry plant suddenly absorbs a large amount of water, the inside of the fruit expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to burst open.
ga: Beni tsei ni egbi trukaa lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo. Yibii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Why does putting dry grass around the roots of my crops keep the soil wet longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛfataa mitsei lɛ ashishi he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts as a protective blanket called mulch. It blocks direct sunlight from heating the soil, which prevents underground moisture from evaporating quickly into the air.
ga: Hay lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch. Etsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adɔ. Enɛ haaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ atsɔ oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and die when rainwater sits around their roots for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu ta shishifãi lɛ ahe gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air from the soil to breathe. When excess rainwater stands around the roots for too long, it drowns them by cutting off oxygen, causing root rot and leaf yellowing.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu. Kɛ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ha shishifãi lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ Ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava plants are losing too much water during the heat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ miifite nu babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Cassava plants show water stress by dropping their lower leaves to conserve moisture for the top growing stem. If only the bottom leaves fall while the top stays green, the plant is managing its water loss.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ jieɔ nu he haomɔ kpo kɛtsɔ baai ni amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he kɛha tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ gbee shi ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ tee nɔ efee eŋɔli. Etsɔɔ akɛ tsei miikwɛ nu ni laajeɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens to my maize seeds if I plant them in dry ground before the rains begin?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ enɛ?

english: Seeds remain asleep in dry soil until moisture arrives. However, if there is just a tiny amount of moisture, the seed might sprout and then quickly wither if a full rain does not follow immediately.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ baa. Shi, kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui hu baanyɛ akwɛ̃ oya ni amɛgbo kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow much faster during the rainy season than when I water them by hand in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe be mli ni mikɛ niji shwieɔ nu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Rainwater cools down the air and high humidity prevents water loss from leaves. Rain also brings natural nutrients from the atmosphere that simple bucket watering cannot easily replicate.
ga: Nugbɔ nu haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ akajeɔ mli. Nugbɔ hu kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni nu ni akɛwoɔ baagi mli ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ nyɛŋ afee nakai lɛ baa.

english: What is certified seed, and why does it grow better than the seeds I save from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji dumɔwui ni awo he odase? Ni mɛni hewɔ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are produced by certified growers under strict quality controls so they have high germination rates, disease resistance, and strong yields. Saved seeds often lose their vigor over generations, leading to weak plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ yɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni mli wa shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, eyɛ shweremɔ ni yaa hiɛ, helai ni tsiɔ ehe naa kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo. Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ fɔɔ hewalɛ ni baa shi kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: How do I know how many kilos of seed I need to buy for one acre of my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male dumɔwui kilogram enyiɛ ni esa akɛ mahe kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ mli acre kome?

english: The quantity of seed needed per acre depends on the seed type and planting distance. Following the recommended seed rate ensures your crop has enough space, soil nutrients, and sunlight to grow strong without overcrowding.
ga: Dumɔwui abɔ ni he hiaa yɛ acre kome mli lɛ damɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahenɔi kɛ he ni aduɔ lɛ jɛkɛmɔ nɔ. Dumɔwui ayibɔ ni atsɔɔ lɛ sɛɛnyiɛmɔ baaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekwɛ̃ waa ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli fe nine.

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's natural defense against heat stress. The plant rolls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, helping it conserve internal water during hot, dry periods.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ mli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and skinny instead of developing thick, strong stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni amɛhe wa lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Crops stretch tall and thin when they are planted too close together or shaded. The plants are competing with each other and stretching upwards to reach for sunlight.
ga: Tsei lɛ baashɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaafee bibioo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tsei lɛ miitswa akaŋ ni amɛmiigba amɛhe kɛmiiya ŋwɛi koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow when there is heavy rainfall on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When soil becomes waterlogged from heavy rain, plant roots cannot get air and lose their ability to absorb nitrogen from the soil. Lack of nitrogen causes the leaves to lose their green color and turn yellow.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ. Tse shishifãi nyɛŋ aŋɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dɔŋŋ. Nitrogen ni faaa lɛ haa baai lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why are my crop flowers dropping off the plant before turning into fruits or pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ aduawai loo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant suffers stress from excessive heat, severe dry spells, or a shortage of key nutrients like phosphorus. Stress prevents proper pollination, causing the plant to abort the flowers.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni fe nine kpe. hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ, haomɔ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Ehaa tsei kpaɔ fɔfɔi

english: Why are my plants starting to flower early while they are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi mra be mli ni eji bibioo kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Crops often flower early as a survival mechanism when threatened by drought or poor soil nutrients. The plant senses stress and tries to produce seeds quickly to reproduce before it dies.
ga: Tsei sumɔɔ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi mra akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi kɛji hɔmɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ wo amɛhe gbeyei. Tsei nuɔ nɔnyɛɛ he ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwo dumɔwui oya koni amɛfɔ dani amɛgboi.

english: Why do my crops mature at different times even though I planted all the seeds on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ moŋ?

english: Uneven crop growth happens when seeds are planted at different depths, when soil moisture varies across the field, or when mixed seed varieties with different growth rates are planted together.
ga: Tso lɛ dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji adu dumɔwui yɛ hei srɔtoi ni mli kwɔ. Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ srɔtoi yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ naa loo be mli ni aduɔ dumɔwui ni efutu ni amɛdaraa yɛ srɔtoi yɛ he kome lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn pale and stop growing so fast early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkpaa kwɛ̃mɔ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal fertilizers, soil moisture, and sunlight away from your crop. Early weed competition starves young crop roots, causing stunted growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ yaa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi akaŋshii mra baaha tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ

english: Why do the lower leaves of my crop turn purple or reddish during cool mornings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso lɛ shishi baai lɛ feɔ purple loo etsuru yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Purple leaves usually indicate that the plant is struggling to absorb phosphorus from cold or waterlogged soil. Phosphorus is vital for root energy, and its temporary absence causes reddish-purple discoloration.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ejie fɔsfɔs kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Fosforo he hiaa kɛha shishifã hewalɛ. Ni be kukuoo mli ni ebɛ lɛ haa su tsakeɔ kɛyaa magenta nɔ.

english: Why do seeds fail to sprout when I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain often only wet the surface and heats up the dry ground without soaking deep enough. Seeds need steady moisture to wake up, so waiting for two or three good rains ensures the soil stays wet enough for seeds to germinate safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛ nu lɛ efɔɔɔ mli bɔ ni sa. Dumɔwui he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛte shi. No hewɔ lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ kpakpa fioo ko ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do crops planted too close together grow tall and thin with very small harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded together, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each plant proper spacing allows its leaves to catch full sunlight and its roots to spread out and feed the plant properly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa Amɛyeɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa amɛbaai lɛ naa hulu la ni fa babaoo. Ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni ehaa tso lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or beans together with maize makes the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa du tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas have natural helpers in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into soil food. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to grow strong, so growing them together naturally feeds the soil and helps the maize.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas yɛ adebɔɔ mli yelikɛbuamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsɔɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu nii yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ŋmãa lɛ ni eha kooloi niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize turning light yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen or that too much water is trapped around the roots. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the rich green color necessary for good growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ loo nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when rainwater settles around them for too long, preventing the roots from breathing. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away, keeping the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu hi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the sap from the leaves. Spraying the plants with mild neem leaf extract or soapy water helps clear the insects so the leaves can expand again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni haa chili baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ neem baa mli nu ni mli ejɔ loo nu ni mli edɔ shwie tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi bibii lɛ koni baai lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers drop off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the air gets too hot and dry or when the soil lacks steady moisture. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and planting during cooler periods helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɛ be fɛɛ be Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛduɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why does my soil dry out and turn hard so much faster nowadays than it used to years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ miigbi ni eefee mlɛo oya fe bɔ ni eji afii ni eho lɛ?

english: Repeated farming and clearing of bushes reduce the organic matter that acts like a sponge in the soil. Adding dry leaves, crop leftovers, or compost back into the soil helps it retain moisture much longer during hot spells.
ga: Okwaayeli ekoŋŋ kɛ brɔshi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Nibii ni egbi ni akɛbaafata he Aloo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aku sɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do young cocoa trees wither and die when there are no bigger trees planted around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Taller plants like plantains provide necessary shade and keep the air humid while the cocoa establishes its root system in its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo baaná shishifã yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly after a rain while my planted crops take longer to start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ? Beni tsei ni miduɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛjeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants already fully adapted to the local soil and quick to grab any water and sunshine. They grow fast to steal available nutrients, which is why clearing weeds early gives your crops the head start they need.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ kwraa. ni ehe hiaa nu kɛ hulu la oya Amɛdaraa oya koni amɛju niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni onibii lɛ aná hesaamɔ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow tall and skinny and fall over when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close to each other, they fight for sunlight and stretch upward too fast. This makes their stems thin and weak, so giving each plant enough space allows them to grow thick stalks that withstand strong winds.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe oya tsɔ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ afee mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ tsei ni mli tse ni baanyɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build leaves. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps bring back their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee baai Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a virus, or by extreme heat and lack of water. Protecting young plants from pests early on helps keep the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni faaa mli Tsei bibii ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: What causes small holes to appear all over my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa bu bibioo lɛ feɔ? ni shwieɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually made by caterpillars or beetles feeding on the leaves. Checking under the leaves regularly and using natural sprays like neem oil can stop these insects before they ruin the harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ladybugs ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni baa cabbage baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akwɛ baai lɛ ashishi daa, ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ neem fɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves get white powdery spots on them during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: White spots are usually caused by a fungal infection called powdery mildew, which thrives in warm, dry weather. Spacing plants well so air can move between them helps prevent this fungus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew kɛ hela yɛŋ baa. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Shi tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ atsɔ amɛteŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even after waiting many months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ lolo yɛ be mli ni amɛmɛ nyɔji babaoo po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose soil to swell and grow big. If the ground is packed too hard or lacks nutrients, the plant spends all its energy surviving above ground instead of growing heavy tubers below.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛfuu ni amɛdara. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu shishigbɛ ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, usually from severe heat or sudden dry spells. Keeping the soil moist around the roots helps the flowers stay attached and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ he. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nugbɔshiimɔ ni baa trukaa. Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my watermelon fruits turn black and rot at the bottom before they get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelons lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ shishigbɛ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Bottom rot in watermelons happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil, usually because of irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist prevents the fruit from rotting.
ga: Watermelon shishigbɛ fitemɔ baa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ba daa lɛ, ebaatsi aduawai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: Why do the seeds I save from my harvest produce smaller crops than the store-bought seeds I planted originaly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii bibii fe dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ shwapo mli ni mikɛ blema gbɛi tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ lɛ?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are specifically bred to yield heavily in their first generation. Seeds collected from those grown crops lose those special strengths, resulting in weaker plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nakai tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ krɛdɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why should I start my vegetable seeds in nursery boxes before moving them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔi mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ yɛ adeka mli dani mikɛ amɛ aya shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young sprouts are very delicate and can easily be washed away by heavy rain or destroyed by pests. Nursery boxes let you protect and care for the fragile seedlings until they are strong enough to survive on the main farm.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ ahoo amɛ oya. Nursery adekai lɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe ni okwɛɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Why are there small holes in my young maize leaves and worms hiding inside the plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn kɛ caterpillar baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Akɛtee tso ko mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm. The young worms feed on tender leaves, which slows down the plant's growth unless they are controlled early with appropriate sprays or natural remedies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai bibii yeɔ baai bibii, ni no haa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi. ja akɛ tsofai ni sa loo adebɔɔ mli tsofafeemɔi akudɔ lɛ mra

english: Why do people advise me to plant plantains on the same plot as my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu banana yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa needs during its first few years.
