ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei bibii lɛ daa oya waa, ni amɛyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛha wala. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Should I cut off the extra small shoots growing at the bottom of my plantain tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii? Ani ajieɔ nɔ ni fa fe nine ni miida yɛ dumɔwu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yes, removing extra shoots is important so that only one or two strong suckers remain. Leaving too many shoots forces the main plant to share water and nutrients, resulting in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia ni ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai aha. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nutrients, especially nitrogen, or that the soil is holding too much water. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my crops growing very slowly even though it rains regularly in my area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo waa eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Rain provides water, but crops also need nutrients from the soil to grow strong. If the land has been farmed for many years without adding compost or fertilizer, the soil loses its food, causing crops to stay small.
ga: Nugbɔ haa nu, shi ŋmɔshi nibii hu he hiaa niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdara waa. Kɛji otsu okwaayeli afii babaoo ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baafite. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii.

english: What will happen if I plant my cassava cuttings too close together on the farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When cassava plants are crowded together, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition prevents the roots from expanding, leaving you with thin, small tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã. Ehaa onáa yitso bibioo ni yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: Pepper flowers drop off mainly when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out, or when insects attack the blossoms. Keeping the soil moist and protecting plants from extreme heat helps fruits form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tutua fɔfɔi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsei ahebuu kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ baaye abua ni aduawai aba.

english: Why do I see bees visiting the flowers on my watermelon vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii ni miisara fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-watermelon wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Bees are carrying pollen from male flowers to female flowers. Watermelon plants need this transfer to happen, otherwise the female flowers will drop off and no fruits will develop.
ga: Wuobii miiwo fɔfɔi hii kɛmiiya fɔfɔi yei amli. Ehe miihia ni watermelon tsei lɛ ajie enɛ kɛya he kroko. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, fɔfɔi yei lɛ baagbee shi ni aduawai ko bɛ.

english: This sudden wilting is often caused by root rot or fungal disease in the soil. When soil stays overly wet, fungi attack the roots and destroy them, stopping the plant from taking up water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni egbo loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ shwiemɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ baa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ ni efiteɔ amɛ. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Rain can wash nitrogen deep into the soil out of root reach, so applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps bring back the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Nugbɔ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites, or a virus transmitted by them. Inspecting under the leaves and spraying with neem oil or appropriate insecticide early helps protect new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ Baai lɛ ashishigbɛ kwɛmɔ mra ni akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu dalɛ hee he.

english: When soil contains too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, cassava puts all its energy into growing big stems and leaves instead of expanding its roots. Adding wood ash or potassium-rich fertilizer encourages the plant to store food in large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium faaa yɛ shishifãi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ najiaŋ lɛ, ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji. Kɛ́ akɛ tso mli sũ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ato bulb agboi lɛ amli.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my cocoa trees without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the tree is stressed by dry spells, high heat, lack of shade, or a lack of tiny pollinating midges. Maintaining moderate shade trees and keeping soil moist helps flowers stay on the tree and turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ shɛ hulu la ni egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo pollination ni bɛ fioo lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ wo hulutsoo be ni sa mli, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hu hiɔ shi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: It is best to leave only two to three strong suckers of different heights per plantain parent stem. Leaving too many suckers creates competition for nutrients and water, which results in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 2-3 pɛ ni amɛlɛɛmɔi srɔtoi yɛ dumɔwu lɛ tso kome mli. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ekɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu. Enɛ haa plantain lɛ feɔ bibioo.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to produce energy for tuber growth. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where diseases spread and exposes them to maximum sunlight so the plant can grow larger yams underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha tuber lɛ dalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Gbalamɔ ni oná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni obaanyɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How do I know it is the right time to plant my maize after the first rain falls?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eji be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until the soil gets thoroughly wet down to about a hand's depth after two or three good rains. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die if a dry week follows.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kwraa kɛyashɛ tso ko mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji hɔmɔ otsii babaoo nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does elephant grass keep growing back so quickly after I clear my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shwuɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ beni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Elephant grass has thick underground stems called rhizomes that store lots of energy even after you cut the top off. To stop it, you must dig up the underground roots or treat the young shoots with grass herbicide.
ga: Shɔji jwɛi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli tse ni atsɛɔ amɛ rhizomes ni kɛ hewalɛ babaoo toɔ kɛji ofo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ po. Bɔni afee ni okpa lɛ Ehe miihia ni okɛ shishifãi lɛ atsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi loo okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi bibii lɛ atsu nii.

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot and happens when the plant cannot pull up enough calcium, usually because watering is uneven. Keeping the soil consistently moist prevents the bottoms of developing tomatoes from turning black.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot ni ebaa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ hewɔ ni enɛ baa lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaatsi tomato shishi ni miiya hiɛ lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ediŋŋ.

english: Why should I add poultry manure to my soil instead of relying only on chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ kooloi ashishifã afata sũ lɛ he moŋ fe ni mikɛ mihe baafɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli lɛ pɛ nɔ?

english: Poultry manure improves the physical structure of the soil, helping it hold water and organic nutrients longer during dry periods, whereas chemical fertilizers only feed the plants for a short period without improving the soil.
ga: Kooloi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ shihilɛ yaa hiɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii yɛ be kukuoo mli pɛ. ni afeee shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ

english: How long will it take for an oil palm tree to start producing fruit after I plant it on my farm?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani mu tsei lɛ baabɔi yibiiwoo beni midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: Improved hybrid oil palm varieties usually start producing fruit 3 to 4 years after planting, while older or wild varieties can take up to 6 or 7 years. They need those initial years to build strong roots and trunks before they can support heavy palm fruit bunches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 sɛɛ beni adu amɛ. Yɛ be mli ni tsofa-kɛ-ŋma henɔi ni etsɛ loo koo mli mu lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 6 loo 7 lɛ, be he miihia amɛ yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Koni etswa shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni wa dani enyɛ eye ebua tsei akui ni tsii.

english: Why shouldn't I just save and plant maize seeds from my previous harvest instead of buying new seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooohe dumɔwui heei

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their strength in the second generation, leading to smaller cobs and weaker plants. Buying certified nursery seeds ensures high yields, disease resistance, and uniform growth across your field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli akɛ amɛfɔ̃ɔ lɛ ahemɔ baaha yibiiwoo babaoo aba, helai nyɛŋ amɔ amɛ, ni ebaaha amɛdara be fɛɛ be yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight and can easily dry out. Fast-growing plantains provide instant shade and retain soil moisture, acting as natural protection while the young cocoa trees establish themselves.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. ni ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi mlɛo Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Etsuɔ nii koni ebu adebɔɔ he yɛ be mli ni atoɔ kookoo tso bibioo lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn out very thin and small when I plant the stems very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bibii waa beni miduɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their roots compete heavily with each other for space, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each stem enough room in the soil to expand into large, thick tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko he akaŋ waa. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso lɛ yitso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni egbɛ eshwa ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tso agbo ko ni mli edɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up like tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ shwieɔ shi efeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves inward during peak sun hours to minimize water loss through evaporation. It is a natural protection mechanism the plant uses to preserve moisture until the heat dies down.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha hulutsoo lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi hulutsoo lɛ baaho aya.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my growing maize turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni miida lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen. The maize plant automatically moves nutrients from its older, lower leaves up to nourish the new growth at the top when nitrogen in the soil is low.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen lɛ faaa.

english: Pepper flowers often drop due to extreme heat stress, poor soil nutrients, or improper watering. Without proper pollination or under harsh weather conditions, the plant sheds its flowers to save energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu ni esaaa Kɛji akɛ pollination ni sa bɛ loo yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni esaaa mli lɛ, Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why does letting weeds grow around my young palm trees slow down their growth so much?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni oha jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ? Mi-palm tso bibioo lɛ miiha edalɛ miiba shi babaoo?

english: Weeds and tall grasses act as thieves that aggressively pull water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from the young palm's root zone, delaying the time it takes for the palm to mature and produce fruit.
ga: Jwɛi kakadaji kɛ jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi ni miitao amɛgbala nu, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ heɔ be dani edaa ni ewoɔ yibii fiofio.

english: Why are my tomato plants wilting and dying even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miigboi ni amɛmiigboi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by soil-borne fungal or bacterial wilt diseases that attack the plant's vascular system, blocking water from moving up the stem and causing the leaves to droop despite wet soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungi loo muawai hela ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni tutuaa tso lɛ lá gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ haa nu lɛ nyɛɛɛ aya ŋwɛi ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po

english: How can I tell that my yam tubers are fully ripe and ready to be dug out of the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yams indicate maturity above ground when the leaves and vines stop growing green, turn dry and yellow, and begin to die back naturally at the end of the rainy season.
ga: Sweet potatoes tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ dalɛ kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ kpa ŋmɔŋfeemɔ. egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔi gbele yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there are no plantain trees planted around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ko bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight. Plantain leaves act like shade umbrellas, protecting young cocoa from heat stress and keeping moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees get older and stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Plantain baai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo. Buu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa ni ehaa ehe waa.

english: Why do I need to put wooden poles for my yam vines to climb on instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso he hiaa mi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes helps the leaves catch more sunlight to make food for the root, and it prevents fungal diseases that spread easily when leaves touch damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo ni amɛkɛhaa shishifãi lɛ niyenii. Ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛji baai lɛ ta shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves often mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient in the soil. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away soil food or when weeds steal the nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fite niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo jwɛi ju niyenii.

english: Planting maize in the same spot every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans restores soil fertility.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for me to apply chemical fertilizer on dry soil when rain has not fallen for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ awo mli lɛ? Ani ehiii kɛha mi akɛ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ otsii babaoo nɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it. When put on dry soil, concentrated chemical fertilizer can actually burn and damage the roots.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛshwie shi bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with big leaves but giving me very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ waa kɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or too much moisture, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing green leaves on top instead of storing food in the roots to build thick tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ baato niyenii yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli ni miida yɛ nɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni mli tse.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my maize seeds after the long dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui beni nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ eho lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should wait until the ground gets two or three good, deep rains that soak into the soil, rather than planting right after the very first light shower which can dry up quickly and scorch young sprouts.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni mli kwɔ baagbee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo lɛ. Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ, ni baanyɛ agbi oya ni eha tsei bibii lɛ ashã.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant without ever turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the air gets too hot, when the soil becomes too dry, or when there is sudden heavy rain. Extreme weather stresses the plant, causing it to shed flowers to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa trukaa Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my young maize leaves look like someone shot holes through them with insects hiding in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ tamɔ mɔ ko ni etswa bu ko ni kooloo ko kɛ ehe ewo mli lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed inside the central whorl of the maize plant. They hide in the center leaves during the day and chew holes as the leaf unfolds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ bu beni baa lɛ mli tsɔɔ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow bottom leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for leafy growth. The plant starves its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves at the top, so applying nitrogen fertilizer or compost will fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Tso lɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ baa momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ koni ekɛha baai heei ahi ŋwɛi. No hewɔ lɛ, nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up into tight tubes during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Curling leaves is the plant's natural shield against heat. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the amount of surface area exposed to the hot sun and dry air, which stops water from evaporating out of the plant too quickly.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ hebuu. kɛtsɔ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ Tsei haa hulu la ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ baa shi. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ.

english: Cassava tubers rot when excess water collects around the roots in heavy or poorly drained soil, allowing fungi to grow. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine bua amɛhe naa. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii baanyɛ adara. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when extreme heat or drought stresses the plant, or when there is no wind or insects to move pollen around inside the flower. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting at the right time helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ha tso lɛ hao. Aloo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi bibii ni tswaa pollen lɛ bɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ooodu yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni ewo yibii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under direct sunlight and dry out quickly. Plantains grow fast and provide tall, broad leaves that shade the young cocoa plants like an umbrella until they are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai kakadaji ni mli kwɔ ni haa kookoo tso bibioo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ agbo bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push their flower stems back down into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miitsi efɔfɔi lɛ aku sɛɛ kɛmiiba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are unique plants that flower above ground but mature their fruit under the soil. Once insects pollinate the flower, the stem naturally grows downward into the earth where the peanut pod can safely develop in the dark.
ga: Peanuts ji tso ko ni yɔɔ srɔto ni fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shi edaa ni ewoɔ yibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji kooloi bibii shwie fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ, Bean tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Bean pods lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ duŋ mli.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to produce energy to grow big tubers underground. Guiding the vines up tall wooden stakes keeps leaves off the wet ground—where diseases spread—and exposes them to maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Wein tsei lɛ ni agbɛɔ ashwãa yɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akagbee shi yɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ. ni ji he ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni ehaa baai lɛ naa hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are naturally aggressive at soaking up water, sunlight, and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Removing weeds early stops them from stealing the food your crops need to grow big.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju niyenii ni he hiaa onibii koni amɛdara lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the middle of the day even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ yɛ gbi mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During intense afternoon heat, pepper leaves lose moisture into the air faster than the roots can suck water out of the soil. As long as the soil remains moist, the plant will revive itself once the sun goes down and temperatures cool.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Pepper baai lɛ fiteɔ nu ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ Tsei lɛ baa wala mli ekoŋŋ beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant maize in the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously in the same field drains the specific nutrients maize needs and allows soil pests that target maize to multiply. Swapping maize with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores natural fertility to the soil and starves pests.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ daa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abele lɛ hoɔ. ni ehaa sũ mli kooloi ni ji ŋmãa lɛ yiŋtoo lɛ ayiɔ babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why are so many flowers falling off my cocoa trees onto the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo miiho kɛmiijɛ mi kakao tso lɛ nɔ kɛmiiba shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but the tree can drop up to 95% of them because it does not have enough water, nutrients, or insect pollination to turn every single flower into a full pod.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi tsei ni fa fe 95% baanyɛ ajie amɛbaai lɛ shi ejaakɛ nu, niyenii mli hewalɛ loo kooloi ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi fɛɛ fɔfɔi afee ŋmɔtɔ ni eyi obɔ.

english: How do tiny cocoa flowers actually get pollinated to become full pods?
ga: cocoa fɔfɔi bibii Te ooofee tɛŋŋ okɛ pollination awo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni pods lɛ eyiɔ obɔ?

english: Cocoa flowers are pollinated by tiny insects called midge flies that live in damp fallen leaves on the farm floor, not by regular honeybees or wind.
ga: Kplukai bibii shwieɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ. Atsɛɔ amɛ midge ŋmeii. Ehiɔ baai ni egbee shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Jeee kɛtsɔ wuo loo kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my crop flowers drop without turning into fruit when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain can wash away the tiny insects that pollinate flowers, damage delicate flower stems, and cause dampness that leads to fungal diseases which rot the flowers before fruit can form.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie kooloi bibii kɛya. fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ Efiteɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Ni enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa, ni no kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ fiteɔ dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ baa.

english: Why do some of my young cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in wet and overly shaded conditions, or by the tree naturally shedding extra pods it cannot support.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ hulutsoo fe nine mli. Aloo tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why is it dangerous to leave dead or rotten cocoa pods lying on the farm ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaashi kookoo ŋmeii ni egboi loo ni egbo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rotting pods on the ground contain fungal spores and harbor pests that splash onto healthy trees during rains, spreading disease across the whole farm.
ga: Nibii ni fiteɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hiɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni shwieɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: Why do my cocoa pods stay small and stunted for a long time instead of growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ ehi shi bibii ni egbɔjɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ agbo lɛ?

english: Stunted pods happen when the tree suffers from a lack of soil nutrients, prolonged dry weather, or sap-sucking pests like mirids (capsids) that damage the young pod.
ga: Dwarfed pods baa kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ. loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mirids (capsids) ni fiteɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ.

english: How does pruning my cocoa trees help them grow more flowers and pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ cacao tso ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes useless or diseased branches so sunlight and air can reach the trunk, directing the plant's energy and nutrients into producing healthy flowers and fruit.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajieɔ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ ashɛ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cocoa tree have plenty of green leaves but very few flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi fɔfɔi fioo pɛ amɛyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Too much shade or an overload of nitrogen fertilizer causes trees to focus all their energy on growing leaves and stems instead of flowering.
ga: Shade babaoo loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ eshishifãi ni miida lɛ ahe nii moŋ fe ni eeewo fɔfɔi.

english: Why should I leave fallen dry leaves on the soil under my crop trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi baai ni egboi ni egbee shi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ nɔ?

english: Fallen leaves act as mulch that keeps the soil cool and moist, decays into natural fertilizer, and creates a home for helpful flower-pollinating insects.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekɛfeɔ shia kɛhaa kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ

english: Why do crop leaves turn yellow during dry spells in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves indicate heat stress, water shortage, and a lack of nitrogen, causing the crop to drop leaves to protect itself from drying out completely.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ. nu ni faaa kɛ nitrogen ni faaa Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shiɔ baai lɛ koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi kwraa.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full, direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a living umbrella that shields the young cocoa leaves and keeps the soil moist while they get established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I leave space between my maize plants instead of planting them close together to get more crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Planting maize too close causes the plants to compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and food to grow strong stems and large, full cobs.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tsei ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, typically 9 to 12 months after planting depending on the variety. You can also carefully dig around the base of one plant to inspect the tuber size before harvesting the whole farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai lɛ je shishi amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Edamɔ tso lɛ henɔ lɛ nɔ Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa tso kome shishi hu koni okwɛ bulb lɛ dalɛ dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is essential for healthy leaf growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps feed the roots and keep the leaves green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa kɛha baai ni wa lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ ni eha baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to heat stress or irregular watering. Giving the plants consistent water and maintaining steady soil moisture helps the flowers stay attached and form healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes holes in my young corn leaves and sawdust-like dirt inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides and feeds inside the growing center of the plant. Applying recommended treatments early in the morning into the central shoot helps destroy the caterpillars before they ruin the plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe teeɔ ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ he lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ tsu nii yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efite ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite tso lɛ.

english: Pepper and tomatoes belong to the same crop family and share the same pests and soil-borne diseases. Planting them repeatedly on the same plot allows these pests and fungi to build up in the soil and attack your new crop.
ga: Pepper kɛ tomato yɛ tsei akuu kome mli ni amɛyɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ tamɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ odu nii shii abɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nɛkɛ kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtutua oŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam plants and lift the vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo mi-sweet potato tso lɛ nɔ ni mawo wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high on tall wooden stakes so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight, which provides energy to grow large tubers underground. Keeping vines off the wet ground also prevents leaf rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. ni haa hewalɛ ni akɛkwɛɔ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Wein tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ baai ni fiteɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the soil when I plant them immediately after a very heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa waa sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil lacks air, which seeds need to breathe and sprout. When seeds sit in water-soaked ground, fungi attack them before they can germinate, so it is better to wait until the soil is moist rather than muddy.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ. Esa akɛ dumɔwu lɛ amu ni ekwɛ̃. Beni dumɔwui lɛ ta ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa dani dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ moŋ fe ni ooofee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Having too many shoots (suckers) forces them to steal food and water from the main plantain tree, resulting in small bunches. Pruning the extra shoots and leaving only 2 or 3 healthy ones allows the main plant to produce big, heavy fruit.
ga: Suckers (shoots) babaoo ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ plantain wulu lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji niji bibii Kɛ́ afolɔ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi niji 2 loo 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso titri lɛ ni ewo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the plant are a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for green leafy growth, and adding compost, manure, or nitrogen-based fertilizer restores healthy green leaves.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ ji okadi ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha baa eŋɔli lɛ dalɛ. Ni kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why does heavy rain seem to wash away the effect of the fertilizer I apply to my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ jieɔ hewalɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ tsuɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains cause nutrient leaching, where water pushes soluble fertilizer deep into the soil below the root zone where plants cannot reach it. Applying fertilizer in smaller split doses and using organic mulch helps keep nutrients near the roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii shwieɔ shi. He ni nu tsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nu mli shwieɔ shi lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ashishi he ni tsei nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli fioo fioo ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii mli nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ abɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. In waterlogged soils with poor drainage, excess water smothers the roots and creates ideal conditions for soil fungi and bacteria to rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ anɔ koni amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines turn brown and dry up long before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi be kakadaŋŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Premature drying of yam vines is commonly caused by anthracnose, a fungal disease that spreads fast in warm, humid weather. Using healthy seed yams and clearing infected crop leaves helps protect the foliage until harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, anthracnose ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbiɔ oya. Enɛ ji fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ tsu nii ni ajie tso lɛ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu baai lɛ ahe kɛyashi be mli ni abaakpa.

english: Why are my garden egg flowers falling off without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Garden egg flowers drop when plants suffer heat stress, lack of soil moisture, or a shortage of insect pollinators. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and avoiding harsh chemical sprays during flowering encourages fruit set.
ga: Eggplant fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni bɛ Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ daa ni ajie tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: This natural dropping of small pods is known as cherelle wilt, which happens when the tree lacks sufficient nutrients or water to support all pods, or from pest attacks. Pruning excessive shade and improving soil fertility helps trees retain more pods.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii lɛ agbeemɔ Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ Cherelle Wilt, ni baa beni tso lɛ bɛ niyenii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ mli tsei lɛ fɛɛ aye abua lɛ. aloo kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atuatsemɔ mli Tso lɛ ŋmɔmɔ, ni ehaa hulutsoo fe nine kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ eshishifãi babaoo mli.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get dark, flat spots on the bottom as they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, usually triggered by irregular watering. Water plants evenly so the roots can continuously draw up calcium from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Ha tso lɛ nu daa bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be.

english: Why are my pepper plants staying short and stunted with curled leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɔɔ kuku ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and stunted growth in pepper plants are usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or whiteflies that suck plant juices and spread viruses. Protecting plants with neem oil or targeted insect sprays keeps them growing strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tsei lɛ amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ahe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ amɛdalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ bu tsei ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that cannot easily hold up heavy fruit bunches, especially in soft soil or strong winds. Supporting the heavy stems with strong wooden or bamboo props prevents them from snapping or uprooting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ aduawai akui ni tsii oya, titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli jɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni wa fi tsei ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkakumɔ loo amɛkaje shishi.

english: When crops are crowded, they compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, causing them to stretch upwards for light instead of developing thick, healthy stems. Proper planting spacing gives each plant room to yield well.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ena la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmeii ni mli wa ni mli wa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsu fɛɛ tsu ni daa lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, keeping young cocoa cool and moist so it can survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: If I plant my crops very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my small plot?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too close together causes crops to fight over water, sunlight, and soil food. This makes all the plants weak and small, leading to less harvest overall than if they were spaced properly.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni efeɔ bibioo. Enɛ haa ŋmaa fɛɛ ni akpaa lɛ feɔ bibioo fe kɛji akɛ ato he ko jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and leafy. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer early will bring back the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ mli mra lɛ baaha eŋɔli su lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my soil dry out so fast just a day after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa gbi kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil dries quickly when it lacks organic matter to act like a sponge, or when bare soil is exposed to direct hot sun. Leaving dead leaves as mulch on top of the soil helps trap moisture much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni baaha etsu nii tamɔ sponji. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ shɛɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ Kɛ́ ashi baai ni egboi akɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-free cassava stems from agriculture officers prevents this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ŋmei bibioo lɛ ji nɔ ni hiɛɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ Nibii ni hela bɛ mli ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi kɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: What is eating small holes inside the young shoots of my maize crops?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ bu bibioo ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide deep inside the center of maize plants. Applying ash, sand, or recommended bio-pesticides directly into the plant center early stops them from killing the plant.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Akɛ sũ, ŋã loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii mra yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akagbe tso lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper fruits get soft and rot right before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper yibii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛfeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: Soft rot in peppers is often caused by fruit flies laying eggs inside or fungal spots triggered by water splashing off the ground. Picking off damaged peppers immediately and keeping weeds low prevents it from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai amli ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa. loo ŋmɔtɔ ni nu ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛbaa Kɛ́ ojie ŋmɔtɔ ni efite lɛ oya ni okɛ jwɛi lɛ ahi shi lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when the plant lacks nutrients like phosphorus. Consistent watering and feeding the soil helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa Aloo kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ fɔsfɔs lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa sũ lɛ ni akɛhaa lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do I need to weed around my yam mounds when the vine is already climbing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi yɛ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ he be mli ni wain tsei lɛ miikwɔ omo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer and water under the ground that the yam roots need to swell. Keeping the mound area clean ensures all nutrients go directly into growing large yam tubers.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni sweet potato shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aha gɔŋ lɛ he tse lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ aya sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it dangerous to sow my seeds right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long dry, hot spell. If you plant too early, seeds will sprout and then quickly wither and die in the hot, dry soil before the main rains arrive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ.

english: How do I know if the maize seeds I bought are good quality before I plant them in my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ dani mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Good quality seed germinates quickly and grows into strong plants. You can test your seeds by placing 10 seeds in a moist cloth or wet soil for a few days; if 8 or more sprout strongly, the seed batch is healthy and ready to plant.
ga: Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tsei ni he wa. Obaanyɛ oka dumɔwui lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni okɛaawo mama ni mli efɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji 8 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kwɛ̃ lɛ, no lɛ dumɔwui akuu lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ adu.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my corn seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ ehiii lɛ?

english: When corn seeds are planted too close together, the young plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition results in weak, thin stalks and tiny corn cobs, reducing your overall yield.
ga: Kɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei bibii baatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ kɛhaa amɛhe Akaŋshii nɛɛ haa ŋmãa bibii kɛ ŋmãa bibii baa. Enɛ haa onitsumɔ lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: How deep into the soil should I push my corn seed when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ matsi mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashɛ he ni tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Corn seeds should be planted about 3 to 5 centimeters deep. If you plant them too deep, the sprout will run out of energy before reaching the surface, and if planted too shallow, birds or hot sunshine will ruin the seed.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ mli aaafee sɛntimita 3 kɛyashi 5. Kɛji odu mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Tsei bibii lɛ ahewalɛ baaho dani amɛyashɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. ni kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ Okpoi loo hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baafite dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do my young crop leaves turn yellow, and how do I fix it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or the roots are drowning in waterlogged ground. Adding balanced nitrogen fertilizer or manure and improving drainage will help the leaves return to a dark, healthy green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ ekã sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he ni aha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛbafee ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How does clearing weeds early help my corn grow stronger?
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Te ebaanyɛ eye ebua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni efee tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight away from your main crop. Removing weeds early—especially during the first month after planting—gives your young plants room and food to build deep root systems.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Titri lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni adu sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha tso bibioo lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni ekɛma shishifãi ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why does adding animal manure to my farm help crops survive dry weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔ lɛ mli kooloi ashishifãi ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Manure acts like a sponge in the dirt that holds water when it rains and slowly releases moisture to plant roots during hot, dry weather while feeding the soil with nutrients.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ muji mli, ni ehiɛɔ nu mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ, ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ fiofio koni ekɛdu shishifãi yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. kɛfata shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛ niyenii kpakpai haa lɛ he

english: Why should I mount or heap extra soil around the base of my growing corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ muji krokomɛi ama shi loo mabɔle he lɛ? Abɛi tso ni aduɔ lɛ shishitoo?

english: Heaping extra soil around the base, known as earthing up, supports new roots, stabilizes the stalk so strong winds do not blow the plant over, and covers roots exposed by heavy rains.
ga: Shikpɔŋ krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ abɔleɔ Atsɛɔ shishitoo lɛ hu akɛ grounding. Ebaaye ebua ni efi shishifãi heei asɛɛ. stabilize the stem Koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa akatswa tsei. ni amɛha shishifãi ni nugbɔ ni naa wa etswa lɛ anɔ

english: How can I protect my maize crop from pests like armyworms attacking the leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-ŋmã lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ asraafoi aŋmãa ni tutuaa baai lɛ ahe?

english: Regularly check the funnels of young leaves for small holes or caterpillar waste. Catching armyworms early allows you to apply recommended pest control treatments before they destroy the growing point of the stalk.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai bibii lɛ amli gbɛi lɛ daa kɛji buji bibii yɛ mli. loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni amɔɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛgbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ tsuɔ nii dani amɛfiteɔ he ni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ daa lɛ.

english: How do I store my leftover seeds so insects do not eat them before the next planting season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ dumɔwui ni eshwɛ lɛ ato? Enɛ ji koni kooloi akaba ni amɛbaye amɛ dani be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba.

english: Store thoroughly dried seeds in airtight containers or sealed ash-treated bags in a cool, dark room. Sealing out air and dampness stops storage insects like weevils from breeding inside the seeds.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui ni egbi jogbaŋŋ awo tsinsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo kotoku ni atsĩ naa mli yɛ tsu ko ni mli ejɔ ni mli ewo duŋ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni atsiɔ naa lɛ haaa kooloi ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ afɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli.

english: Why do some of my corn plants grow big but fail to produce any cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ miida shi ewooo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Corn plants usually fail to make cobs because of extreme heat stress during flowering, poor soil fertility, or overcrowding. Giving plants enough space and applying fertilizer at knee-height ensures every plant produces full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa tsei nyɛɛɛ afee ŋmãa yɛ dɔlɛ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ hewɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii faaa. loo eyi obɔ tsɔ He ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataa he yɛ amɛnajiaŋ lɛ haa tsei lɛ fɛɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build green leaves and grow strong. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure around the base will help them regain their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni bɔle Shishitoo lɛ he lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller crop yields every year even when I plant at the right time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Kɛji midu yɛ be ni sa mli po.

english: Crops pull food out of the soil every season they grow. If you do not replace those nutrients using compost, animal manure, or fertilizers, or rotate your crops with beans and groundnuts, the soil becomes exhausted and produces weaker harvests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be ni aduɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsakeee nakai niyenii lɛ, loo okɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii tsakeee oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafite ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them in full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and get scorched by strong sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain alongside your cocoa creates living umbrellas that shelter the young trees from heat and hold soil moisture until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ. Dumɔ tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ o-cocoa lɛ masɛi. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa.

english: How do I select the best plantain suckers to plant on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala banana tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Look for maiden suckers that have thick bases and narrow, spear-like leaves. Make sure the root bulb is clean, firm, and free from dark rot holes or worm marks, as healthy suckers grow faster and produce heavier bunches.
ga: Taomɔ tsei bibii ni amɛshishigbɛ lɛ mli tse kɛ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ akpɔlɔi. Kwɛmɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tse, amɛhe wa ni ŋmeii diji loo ŋmeii akadi ko bɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, suckers ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ niji ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava bushes curling up and showing yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting improved, disease-resistant cassava stems from an extension office will protect your farm from this problem.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Cassava tsei ni asaa amɛhe ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ Extension Office lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ naagba nɛɛ he.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my yam mounds when the yam vines are already tall and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi yɛ ŋmeii akuu lɛ he be mli ni ŋmeii wain tsei lɛ ekwɛ ni amɛhe wa momo lɛ?

english: Even if yam vines look big above ground, hidden weeds compete beneath the soil for water and nutrients. Clearing weeds ensures all the plant's food goes directly into swelling the yam tubers underground.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ, Shi jwɛi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ yeɔ akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Jwɛi ni agbeɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ niyenii lɛ fɛɛ aha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and soft while still on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo be mli ni amɛyɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by irregular watering which prevents the plant from absorbing calcium from the soil. Keeping your soil evenly moist with regular watering helps the plant deliver calcium to developing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ be fɛɛ be ni haaa amɛŋɔ calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ calcium aha aduawai ni miida lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they get stressed by intense heat, drought, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Watering them consistently and providing light shade during very hot weeks helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ nu kɛ hulutsoo daa yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my watermelons crack open before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ miitswa dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Watermelons split when a heavy rain comes right after a dry period. The inside absorbs water so fast that it bursts through the skin, so providing steady, light watering during dry spells prevents sudden cracking.
ga: Watermelon lɛ tswaa kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa ba yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Mligbɛ lɛ gbalaa nu oya aahu akɛ eboteɔ hewolo lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa ni fioo yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ baatsi ŋmeii ni baa trukaa lɛ anaa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant cowpea seeds that I bought from the food market for cooking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tsina ŋmei dumɔwui ni aheɔ yɛ niyenii ajarayelihe lɛ koni akɛhoo nii lɛ?

english: Market seeds are meant for eating and may be treated with storage chemicals, damaged, or infected with diseases. Certified seeds from agricultural suppliers are tested to sprout evenly and resist common crop illnesses.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni aye ni tsofai ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite loo aŋɔ hela awo mli. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ odaseyeli ni jɛ okwaayeli nibii ahe nitsulɔi adɛŋ lɛ akwɛɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛte shi amɛwo tsei ahe helai ni afɔɔ namɔ.

english: Why do my crops behave differently if I plant them during the cool August dry spell instead of the major rains in April?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ August nugbɔshiimɔ be ni mli ejɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ April mli lɛ najiaŋ

english: August usually brings a temporary lull in rainfall and cooler temperatures in Southern Ghana. Crops planted during this time grow slower because they receive less sunlight and steady water compared to crops planted during the main rainy season in April.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, August kɛ nugbɔ baa kɛ be kukuoo mli dɔlɛ ni mli ejɔ yɛ Ghana wuoyigbɛ. Tsei ni adu yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ blɛoo ejaakɛ amɛnáaa hulu la kɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa fe tsei ni adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli yɛ April mli lɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to plant quick-maturing crops like cowpeas during the minor rain break in August?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ tsina ŋmeii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo yɛ August mli lɛ mli?

english: Yes, short-duration crops that mature in 60 to 70 days can do well if planted towards the end of the August break, as they will catch the minor rainy season that follows and require less total water to produce yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni yeɔ be kukuoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbii 60 kɛyashi 70 mli lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ August naagbee gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyiɛ sɛɛ ni nu fioo pɛ he baahia koni akɛwo nibii amli.

english: Why are my maize cobs yielding far fewer grains now compared to what my elders harvested years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa kɛ akɛto nɔ ni mi onukpai lɛ kpa nakai afii fɛɛ ni eho lɛ he lɛ?

english: Over time, weather patterns have shifted and soil nutrients have depleted. Without enough soil organic matter and steady rainfall during the flowering stage, the plant cannot properly form full rows of grains on the cob.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tsakeɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ faaa. Kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa yɛ fɔfɔi be lɛ mli lɛ, Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ yɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if the seeds inside my bean pods are filling up properly before harvest time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-bean pods lɛ eyi obɔ dani kpamɔ be lɛ aba?

english: You can gently squeeze the pods along their length; properly developing seeds will feel firm and distinct. If the pods feel hollow or spongy, the crop is suffering from a lack of water or nutrients needed to fill the seeds.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ pod lɛ atsu nii blɛoo yɛ elɛɛmɔ lɛ he. Dumɔwui ni yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa mɔ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ shiŋŋ ni eyɛ srɔto. Kɛji akɛ tso lɛ mli eyi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo edumɔwui lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my garden eggs look healthy on the outside, but inside the seeds are tiny and dark?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ? Shi dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ ji bibioo ni eyɛ ediŋŋ?

english: Underdeveloped or dark seeds inside healthy-looking fruit usually happen when the plant experiences extreme heat or a lack of calcium while the fruit is forming, affecting internal seed growth without destroying the outer skin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni edako loo ni tsuɔ nii yɛ aduawai ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli lɛ baa beni tso lɛ naa dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo calcium ni faaa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifee lɛ. Enɛ saa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ adalɛ he ni efiteee kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ.

english: Extension officers keep telling us that seasons have changed, so why should I stop using the traditional planting months my father taught me?
ga: Extension nitsulɔi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛkɛɔ wɔ akɛ bei lɛ tsakeɔ. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makpa kusum nyɔji ni akɛduɔ nii ni mitsɛ tsɔɔ mi lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ?

english: Scientific studies show that rain patterns in Ghana have shifted over recent decades, making historic planting dates unpredictable. Following updated weather advice helps you avoid planting right before unexpected dry spells that destroy young seedlings.
ga: Jeŋ nilee mli nikasemɔi tsɔɔ akɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ etsake yɛ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli. Enɛ haaa anyɛ atsɔɔ gbi ni abaadu nii yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he ŋaawoo ni atsake lɛ sɛɛnyiɛmɔ baaye abua bo ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ahe dani hɔmɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ ni gbeɔ tsei bibii lɛ aba.

english: Why do the agricultural reports recommend buying fresh certified seeds instead of planting saved seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Okwaafoi Amaniɛbɔɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ ahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe ni aaadu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mikpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their vigor over time and become susceptible to local diseases. Certified seeds brought by agricultural researchers are specially bred to resist modern climate challenges and produce high yields consistently.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli, ni helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ oya. Atsɔse dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi kɛba lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe naagbai anaa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their blossoms before any peppers can actually grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fɛɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ baanyɛ ada diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by sudden heat, dry soil, or weak nutrients. The plant sheds its flowers to save energy so it can survive until conditions get better.
ga: Pepper tsei baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni baa trukaa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my vegetable plants turn yellow during periods of long cloudy weather in August?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ atatu gbii kakadaji ni yɔɔ August mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When the sun is hidden by clouds for days, plants cannot make enough food through their leaves. Combined with cool weather, this slows down root activity and causes lower leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Beni atatui kɛ hulu lɛ tee gbii babaoo lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ atsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ amɛfee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ fata he lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ anitsumɔ baa shi ni ehaa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits split open on the plant right after a heavy rain following a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato yibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ hulutsoo be sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When a dry tomato plant suddenly receives a large amount of rain water, the inside of the fruit expands faster than the skin can stretch, causing the outer skin to burst open.
ga: Kɛ́ tomato tsei ni egbi lɛ ná nugbɔ babaoo lɛ, Yibii lɛ amli lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ fãa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow and dropping off during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing and falling leaves in wet weather are often early signs of Black Pod disease or waterlogged roots. When soil stays too wet, roots cannot breathe, making it easy for fungal diseases to attack the tree.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ black pod hela loo shishifãi ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ yɛ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baatutua tsei.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when I leave too many big shade trees on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni mishiɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ babaoo tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need a balanced mix of shade and sunlight to make food and form flowers. Too much shade blocks the sun and traps damp air, which stops pods from growing and encourages fungal rots.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ taoɔ hulutsoo kɛ hulu la ni sa koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛwo fɔfɔi. Shade babaoo tsiɔ hulu la naa ni emɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ. Enɛ haaa pod lɛ adara ni ewoɔ fungal rot he hewalɛ.

english: How does cutting off extra side branches help my cocoa tree produce bigger pods?
ga: Te niji ni yɔɔ esɛɛ ni afoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-cacao tso lɛ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches so the tree does not waste food and water on them. This allows the tree to focus all its energy on feeding and growing large, healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ejieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ koni tso lɛ akafite niyenii kɛ nu. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa niyenii kɛ kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do many of the small flowers on my cocoa trees drop off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Ani tsei babaoo shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: A cocoa tree naturally produces far more flowers than it can feed, so it drops many of them. However, if too many fall off, it can be caused by dry soil, lack of nutrients, or tiny insects failing to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, babaoo gbeeɔ shi. Shi, kɛji egbee shi tsɔ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ ni egbi, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii baanyɛ aha eba. Enyɛɛɛ ekɛ fɔfɔii awo mli

english: What causes small dark spots on my young cocoa pods that make them dry up early?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii baa? Yɛ mi kookoo ŋmɔji bibii ni haa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ anɔ.

english: Dark spots on young pods are usually caused by mirids (capsids), which are small insects that suck the sap out of the pods. Their bites damage the pod skin and allow diseases to enter, causing the pod to die early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mirids (capsids), ni ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Kpɔmɔ lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ hewolo ni ehaa helai boteɔ mli, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ gboɔ oya.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa farm soil is lacking nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa?

english: If your cocoa trees grow very slowly, have pale leaves instead of deep green ones, or stop producing good pod yields despite getting enough rain, the soil has likely run out of essential food like nitrogen and potassium.
ga: Kɛji o-cocoa tso lɛ daa blɛoo waa Eyɛ baai ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. aloo ekpaa ŋmeii kpakpai feemɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po. Shikpɔŋ lɛ hu bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium.

english: How can I be sure that a cocoa pod is fully ripe and ready for picking?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ ajie?

english: A cocoa pod is ready to harvest when its color changes completely—usually turning from green to bright yellow, or from dark red to orange-yellow. Picking pods too early affects the quality of the cocoa beans inside.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji amɛhe su etsake kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. loo kɛjɛ tsuru ni mli edɔ nɔ kɛtee ŋmɔŋ-ɔranji nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaana bɔ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hi ha lɛ nɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the branches on some of my cocoa trees swelling up and taking strange shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ efuu ni amɛhe yɔɔ naakpɛɛ lɛ?

english: Swollen branches are a clear sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease (CSSVD). This virus is spread by mealybugs and slowly weakens the tree until it stops producing pods and dies.
ga: Niji ni efuu lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli hela (CSSVD) lɛ yɛ. Mealybugs gbɛɔ hela nɛɛ eshwaa ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ fiofio. Kɛyashi ebaakpa pods feemɔ ni egbo.

english: Why is it bad to plant my cocoa seedlings very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ ehiii lɛ?

english: Planting cocoa trees too close together causes their roots and leaves to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. It also prevents air from flowing between trees, creating high moisture that spreads diseases easily.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ hu hoɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ. Bɔɔ hulutsoo be ni mli wa Helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya

english: Why do the leaves of my cocoa trees curl up and dry out during the Harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ shwie shi ni amɛgbi yɛ Harmattan beaŋ lɛ?

english: The Harmattan wind brings dry, hot air that quickly sucks moisture out of the soil and leaves. Cocoa trees curl or shed their leaves to conserve water and protect themselves from dying during the severe dry spell.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ baai lɛ amli oya. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ loo amɛshwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe lɛ?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves usually mean your maize is missing key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or it is under attack from pests like the fall armyworm. Applying the right fertilizer or early pest control helps restore leaf health so the plant can grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ o-ŋmã lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ miitutua lɛ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa loo mra be mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ Ebaaye abua ni eha baai lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ koni tsei lɛ anyɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kooko tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense heat and full sunlight. Keeping shade trees or planting plantains alongside them acts like a natural canopy, protecting the tender young cocoa from burning and holding moisture in the soil.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la he waa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ akwɛmɔ loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ebaatsu nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from sudden heat stress or uneven watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist during flowering helps the plant hold onto its blossoms so they can develop into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna haomɔ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo trukaa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli baa. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ fɔfɔii lɛ amli koni amɛtsɔ yibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even though the leaves look big and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, cassava puts all its energy into growing large green leaves above ground instead of feeding the tubers below. Using balanced soil nutrients ensures the plant directs its energy into building fat cassava roots.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii lɛ, ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Niyenii mli nibii ni sa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛmaa ŋmei shishifãi ni yɔɔ fɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes in the exact same spot where I harvested peppers last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-tomato lɛ yɛ he ni mifo mi-peppers lɛ yɛ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Tomatoes and peppers belong to the same crop family and share the same soil pests and diseases. Rotating to a different crop family starves out these diseases, preventing them from attacking your new plants.
