ga: Tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsei akuu kome mli, ni amɛyɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee tso weku kroko mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ helai nɛɛ anaa. ni otsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkatutua otsei heei lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and weak with small cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ mli tse ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the maize plants to compete for sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures it gets enough nourishment to grow strong stalks and big cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why shouldn't I use seeds saved from my last hybrid maize harvest for planting next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their strength and disease resistance in the second generation, leading to uneven plant growth and much lower yield compared to buying fresh certified seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraaa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛnáa yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa fe be mli ni aheɔ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ.

english: Why do buyers refuse to buy my vegetables if they have small insect spots on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ akɛ amɛbaahe mi-aduawai lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Buyers and international markets demand clean produce because insect damage can cause food to rot rapidly during transport and signals that proper farming health standards were not followed.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii kɛ majimaji ateŋ jarayeli hei biɔ nibii ni he tse. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ kooloi bibii fite niyenii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha niyenii lɛ afite oya kɛ́ akɛmiiya. ni eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ atsuuu okwaayeli he hewalɛnamɔ he mlai ni sa ahe nii.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my tomatoes so they do not spoil before reaching the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa tomato? Koni tomatoi lɛ akafite dani amɛyashɛ jara nɔ?

english: Tomatoes should be harvested when they just begin to change color from green to light pink. This allows them to stay firm during transport and ripen perfectly without getting soft or bruised.
ga: Esa akɛ akpa tomato kɛji ebɔi su tsakemɔ kɛjɛ eŋɔli mli kɛtee pinki ni mli tse mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ yaa lɛ, ni amɛhoɔ nii kɛyashɛɔ emuuyeli mli ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ loo amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ.

english: Why is it wrong to spray pest chemicals on my crops right before I harvest them for sale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ejaaa akɛ mafɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ anɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ dani makpã amɛ koni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Chemicals need a specific waiting period to break down naturally on the plant. Spraying right before harvest leaves toxic residues on the crop, making the food unsafe to eat and causing buyers to reject it.
ga: Tsofai biɔ be krɛdɛɛ ko ni akɛbaamɛ koni amɛfite yɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani akpaa nii lɛ shĩɔ nibii ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni eshwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haaa niyenii lɛ afee nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ, ni ehaa mɛi ni heɔ lɛ kpooɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize farm turning yellow before the corn is ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: When the lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip, it usually means your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient crops need to maintain healthy green foliage.
ga: Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and becoming tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a virus into the plant, or by the plant protecting itself against extreme heat and lack of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, ni gbɛɔ muawai eshwaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my yam leaves developing black spots and the vines drying up early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii diji ni wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ?

english: This is commonly caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose, which spreads quickly in wet, humid conditions and stops the yam tuber beneath the soil from growing large.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose kɛ enɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ mli ni etsĩɔ shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkadara.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme sun, dry Harmattan winds, or water shortages, saving their energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ hao amɛ. harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi loo nu ni faaa Enɛ haa hewalɛ baa shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shihilɛi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce many flowers but fail to form any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo pepper lɛ?

english: Very high temperatures during the hot season can damage the pollen inside pepper flowers, causing them to fall off before insects can pollinate them into fruits.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baanyɛ afite pollen ni yɔɔ pepper fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, pollen lɛ shwieɔ shi dani kooloi nyɛɔ amɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ amli pollen.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings grow better under plantain shade than in open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ dumɔwui ashishi fe bɔ ni amɛdaraa yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants naturally grow in forest understories and burn in harsh sunlight; plantain leaves provide living shade and keep the air cool and humid around the young trees.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kooi ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe, ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ mli. Plantain baai lɛ haa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa dumɔwui lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when the rain and wind come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems holding up a very heavy bunch, making them top-heavy, especially if small soil pests like nematodes have damaged their roots.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii ni tsii waa. Ha amɛfee nɔ ni tsii waa Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes fite eshishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds always grow much faster and stronger than my cultivated crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that are naturally hardier and adapted to steal water and soil nutrients much faster than domesticated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni amɛhe wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei ni akwɛɔ amɛ yɛ shia lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot underground if I leave them after heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil pushes air out of the dirt, suffocating the roots and creating ideal conditions for soil bacteria and fungi to attack and rot the cassava.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfite.

english: Why do tiny weevil bugs show up in my harvested maize even when I dried it before storing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ Nakai ejie ehe kpo yɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ migbi lɛ dani mikɛto moŋ.

english: Weevils often lay invisible eggs inside the maize kernels while the crop is still standing in the field, which then hatch into active bugs inside warm storage bags.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii fɔɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa lɛ awoɔ ŋmeii amli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ damɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛfɔɔ amɛfeɔ kooloi bibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ amɛkotokui ni mli edɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout after I store them in a hot room for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo tsu ko ni mli edɔ mli otsii fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds are living things in a sleeping state. High heat and trapped air inside a warm room damage the living center inside the seed, leaving you with weak or dead seeds that cannot germinate when planted.
ga: Dumɔwui ji nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni bɛ shihilɛ mli. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛitsu ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ wala hei ni yɔɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ loo egboi ni kɛ́ adu lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How can I stop my harvested tomatoes from getting soft and rotting while transporting them for hours in a warm vehicle to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tomato ni akpa lɛ naa koni ekafee blɛoo ni efite yɛ be mli ni mikɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo woɔ tsɔne ni mli edɔ mli kɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Harvested tomatoes continue to produce internal heat when packed tightly. Transporting them in closed bags traps this heat and causes rapid decay. It is best to travel during cool hours, use open wooden crates for airflow, and keep them covered from direct sun.
ga: Tomato ni akpa lɛ baaha emli dɔlɛ aba lolo kɛji akɛ awo mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo kotokui ni aŋã mli lɛ mli lɛ, emɔɔ dɔlɛ nɛɛ ni ehaa amɛfiteɔ oya. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofã gbɛ yɛ nyɔji ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Kɛ adeka ni agbele naa lɛ atsu nii koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli. ni ekɛtee hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when planted in direct sunlight without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender roots and thin leaves that lose water very quickly under hot sun. Without living shade like plantains to lower the surrounding temperature, the heat dries them out faster than their roots can pull water from the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni nu fiteɔ oya waa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko bɛ tamɔ plantain ni baaha hulutsoo ni ebɔle he lɛ aba shi lɛ. Dɔlɛ lɛ baaha amɛgbi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam tubers start rotting and feeling warm when I stack them inside my storage shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ ni amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛhe miiwo la kɛ akɛto shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harvested yams naturally release moisture and warmth as they breathe. When stacked closely without air circulating around them, heat builds up, creating a hot and damp environment where decay and mold spread quickly.
ga: Atomɔ ni akpa lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli fɛ̃i kɛ dɔlɛ be mli ni amɛmuɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ato amɛhe jogbaŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ko bɛ ni bɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ, Dɔlɛ baabɔle amɛhe. Enɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni edɔ waa. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense against heat. When temperatures rise too high, the plant rolls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, helping it conserve water until the air cools down.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni akɛ nu toɔ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: How can I keep my plantain suckers healthy if I have to transport them for several hours before planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha plantain tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ? Kɛ ehe bahia ni akɛ amɛ aya he kroko ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo dani adu

english: Plantain suckers dry out easily when exposed to hot air and wind during travel. Keep them shaded, cover their bases with damp jute sacks or banana leaves, and never seal them inside tight plastic bags where heat can build up.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ agbiɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛbote kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ gbɛfaa mli. Ha ehi hulutsoo be mli. Okɛ jute kotoku loo banana baai ni mli efɔ aha shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ. Ni kaawo plastic kotoku ni mli wa mli, he ni dɔlɛ baanyɛ aba lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested cassava spoil and turn dark within just a few days of harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ ni efeɔ ediŋŋ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once cassava is dug up, exposure to air and heat triggers internal chemical changes that spoil the root. High storage temperatures speed up this process, so cassava must be processed quickly or kept buried in moist, cool soil or sawdust to last longer.
ga: Beni akuɔ ŋmei Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ dɔlɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa tsofai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsakeɔ ni efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ. Nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli latsaa ni nɔ kwɔ baaha nifeemɔ nɛɛ aya oya. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ atsu cassava he nii oya loo afu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni mli ewo fɔ loo tso mli koni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does the inside of my grain sack feel hot when I put my hand inside it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ mikɛ minine wo mli lɛ, ŋmãa kotoku lɛ mli lɛ mli dɔɔ lɛ?

english: Heat inside a sack means the grain was bagged before it was completely dry, or insects and mold are actively feeding inside. Their activity generates trapped heat and moisture, which will ruin the rest of the grain if not spread out to cool and dry.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ ŋmaa lɛ woɔ kotoku mli dani egbiɔ kwraa. Aloo ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii komɛi yɛ ni baa ni amɛbayeɔ mli. Amɛnitsumɔ lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ŋmɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ baafite ŋmãa ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛji akɛ agbɛɛɛ amɛ ashwãaa kɛyashi amɛhe baajɔ ni amɛgbi.

english: Why do my leafy vegetables wither so fast if I harvest them in the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji mikpa amɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: During the afternoon heat, plants lose much of their internal water to the air. Harvesting when the plant is hot leaves it with very little water reserves, whereas harvesting early in the morning when it is cool ensures the leaves stay crisp and fresh longer.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei baafite amɛmli nu babaoo kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ akpa tsei lɛ be mli ni edɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ aná nu fioo ni amɛkɛto. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akpa ŋmaa lɛ leebi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ ahi shi ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested onions rot quickly when I store them in sealed fertilizer sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-onions ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛto ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ kotokui ni atsĩ naa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Onions require constant dry airflow to stay fresh. Airtight sacks trap the natural moisture and heat given off by the onions, creating warm conditions that encourage fungal rot and premature sprouting.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ he miihia sabolai koni amɛhiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Vacuum kotokui lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ ni anáa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ baa ni woɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is an important nutrient for growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the soil where young roots cannot reach it yet, so adding manure or fertilizer helps the plant grow healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aho nitrogen lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ená baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni eŋɔli.

english: Why do my crop plants grow tall and thin with small fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They spend all their energy stretching upward to catch light instead of putting energy into making strong stems and big fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Akɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛgbala amɛhe koni amɛhe la lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛbaafee tsei ni wa kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep dropping off without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress from high heat, dry soil, or lack of nutrients. When stressed, the plant sheds its blossoms to save its own strength rather than spend energy making tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ mli. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛhiɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhewalɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛfee tomato

english: Why are tiny young cocoa pods turning black and drying up on my tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii Koni amɛtsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ mi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa pods turning black can happen due to high humidity causing fungal diseases like black pod, or because the tree has produced more pods than it can feed and naturally sheds the extra ones. Pruning shade trees to let in sunlight and air helps prevent moisture diseases.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni tsɔɔ ediŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aba ejaakɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo kɛ ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji baa, loo ejaakɛ tso lɛ woɔ kokoo ŋmeii babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ eye ni ejieɔ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ ŋmɔtɔ hela naa.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem. You can also dig carefully around one plant to check if the tubers are thick and firm before harvesting the whole farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Ashi tso lɛ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli hu. Dumɔ tso kome jogbaŋŋ koni okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ shiŋŋ dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Pepper leaves curl and droop in the hot afternoon sun to reduce leaf surface area and prevent water loss. As long as the soil has moisture and the leaves bounce back in the cooler evening, it is a normal way for the plant to protect itself.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Koni akɛba baa lɛ nɔ he ni nu lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ shi. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee ŋmɔtɔ ni baai lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, Abuɔ lɛ akɛ eji gbɛ ni sa ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe he.

english: Why do tiny holes keep appearing all over my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? ni shwieɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ

english: Tiny holes in cabbage leaves are caused by small insects or caterpillars feeding on the crop. Checking under leaves early in the morning allows you to spot these pests early before they eat through the whole harvest.
ga: Kplukai bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii Kɛ́ okwɛ baai ashishi leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona ŋmeii nɛɛ mra. Dani amɛbaaye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ

english: Why do weeds slow down my young yam plants so much more than older plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi sweet potato tsei lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ babaoo fe tsei ni egbɔ lɛ?

english: Young yam vines grow slowly at first and need all the sunlight and soil food they can get. Fast-growing weeds steal water and light, smothering the young yam shoot before it can form strong tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni ehe miihia ni amɛná hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii babaoo bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná. Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ juɔ nu kɛ la. Ye ŋmeii bibii dani amɛfee ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Seeds saved from hybrid maize lose the yield strength and disease resistance of their parents. Planting saved hybrid seeds usually leads to uneven growth and smaller cobs compared to buying fresh certified seed each year.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yeɔ wala yɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ yibiiwoo hewalɛ kɛ helai ni amɛfɔlɔi yɔɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ dalɛ ni ejaaa kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he hewalɛ ni aheɔ daa afi lɛ he.

english: Why does mixing dried poultry manure into my soil make my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ kooloi ashishifãi ni egbi futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Poultry manure improves soil by slowly releasing essential nutrients to plants while helping the soil hold onto water like a sponge, keeping crops fed and hydrated longer during dry periods.
ga: Kooloi ashishifã haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛtsɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni ejieɔ lɛ fiofio kɛyaa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ, yɛ be mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli tamɔ sponji. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni amɛnáa nu be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops rot and die when the river overflows and covers my farm with water for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni faa lɛ hoɔ ni ehaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu bɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When floodwaters cover your field for too long, they suffocate the roots, preventing the plant from taking up nutrients and causing it to rot.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu afua ha oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ehaa egboɔ.

english: Why should I plant my crops right at the start of the rainy season instead of waiting for the heavy rains to settle in?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni ekɛha nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting early gives seeds time to sprout and grow strong root systems while the soil is moist. Strong roots help the crops withstand heavy downpours and waterlogging later in the season.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ be ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná shishifãi ni mli wa yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ. Shishifãi ni wa yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛdamɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my crops grow so well during the major rainy season but produce very little during the minor rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ mli shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa shi fioo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Different crops require different amounts of water and sunshine. Major season rains provide steady, deep moisture required for heavy crops, while minor season rains are shorter and best suited for quick-maturing, light crops.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi biɔ nu kɛ hulu la babaoo. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be mli lɛ haa nugbɔ ni mli kwɔ, ni yaa nɔ daa ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ faaa, ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants yellow and drop off during the long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry periods as a self-defense trick to save water. By losing leaves, the plant stops losing moisture to the hot sun and keeps its underground tubers alive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ amɛhe nɔ koni akɛbu nu he. Baai ni laajeɔ lɛ haaa tso lɛ mli nu ni jɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli baa lɛ akafite. ni okɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do the leaves on my vegetable crops turn yellow when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excessive rain washes away important soil nutrients like nitrogen from around the roots. It also saturates the soil, preventing roots from drinking in the food the plant needs to keep its leaves green.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ hoɔ sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hu feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ anu niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni eha baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli lɛ.

english: What will happen to my maize if I leave it on the farm for too long after it is fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni ekwɛ̃ kwraa sɛɛ?

english: Leaving ripe maize in the field exposes it to mold, pest attacks, and sudden rains. This causes the grains to rot or be eaten by insects before you can harvest and sell them.
ga: Abɛi ni ekwɛ̃ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ kɛ ŋmeii, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ fiteɔ loo kooloi yeɔ lɛ dani obaanyɛ okpa ni ohɔ̃ɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are mature and ready to harvest before the bad weather sets in?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa dani kɔɔyɔŋ fɔŋ aba?

english: Crops show clear physical signs when mature: stalks begin to dry, leaves change color from green to yellow or brown, and the seeds or fruits become firm and dry.
ga: Tsei lɛ baajie gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo beni amɛdaraa lɛ, ni nɔ ni fata he ji: Tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ. Baai lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo asarasu. ni dumɔwui loo aduawai lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbi.

english: Why does my farm yield fewer crops each year even though I plant the exact same crop every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi moŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving the land time to rebuild. Rotating different crops or adding manure restores soil food for future harvests.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛsaa ehe. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ Aloo, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmaakpamɔi.

english: Why do my crops grow tall, thin, and weak when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe kpaakpa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, they fight for the same limited sunlight, air, soil nutrients, and water, causing all of them to grow weak instead of strong.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. kɛ nu ni falɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ hewalɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do crops grow better on land that has been left to rest for a season compared to land that is used continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ashi ni akɛtsuuu nii be kome lɛ nɔ kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Resting land allows nature to rebuild organic matter and restore lost nutrients naturally, making the soil rich and fertile again for the next planting cycle.
ga: He ni ajieɔ hejɔɔmɔ yɛ lɛ haa adebɔɔ lɛ saa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe ekoŋŋ ni ekɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni elaaje lɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa shi ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What is the main difference between 'agric' crops and my traditional local crops?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ ‘kwaayeli’ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ mi maŋbii akusum ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ?

english: Agric' crops are modern varieties selected to produce high yields quickly using commercial fertilizers and sprays, whereas local crops are traditional varieties adapted to natural soil without relying on synthetic chemicals.
ga: Okwaayeli’ tsei ji ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei srɔtoi ni ahala kɛha yibiiwoo ni fa oya kɛtsɔ jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, maŋ lɛ mli tsei ji maŋ lɛ mli tsei srɔtoi ni etsake amɛhe amɛwo adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tsofai ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi ahe ehiaaa.

english: Why do crops grown with chemical fertilizers mature so much faster than my local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ mli lɛ daa oya fe mimaŋ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers give crops a quick boost of concentrated nutrients like nitrogen, which accelerates leaf and stem growth much faster than the slow release of natural soil nutrients.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa babaoo, tamɔ nitrogen, oya, ni no haa baa kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daraa oya fe adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo blɛoo kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Do crops grown without chemical fertilizers really taste different from agric crops?
ga: Ani tsei ni aduɔ ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ bɛ mli lɛ ahe ŋɔɔ yɛ srɔto diɛŋtsɛ yɛ okwaayeli tsei ahe?

english: Yes, local crops grown without chemical fertilizers often grow at a natural pace, allowing them to accumulate natural sugars and minerals that give them a richer, traditional flavor.
ga: Hɛɛ, maŋ tsei ni aduɔ ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fataaa he lɛ fɔɔ shweremɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa ebuaa adebɔɔ mli sugars kɛ minerals anaa, ni no haa efeɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, ni ji kusum mli ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do local seeds seem to store longer after harvest than seeds from chemical-grown crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ fe dumɔwui ni jɛ tsei ni akɛ tsofai edu mli lɛ?

english: Crops grown naturally without excess chemical nitrogen usually contain less water weight at harvest, making them less prone to quick rotting, mold, and pest damage during storage.
ga: Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni tsofa ni ji nitrogen babaoo bɛ mli Bei pii lɛ, nu ni tsiimɔ bɛ mli lɛ faaa kɛji akpa amɛ. Enɛ haa tsei nɛɛ fiteee, ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmeii fiteɔ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do traditional crops from Northern Ghana survive dry weather better than other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ blema tsei ni jɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Northern crops like millet, sorghum, and specific cowpea varieties have developed deep root systems and tough leaves that retain moisture, allowing them to withstand heat and low rainfall.
ga: Kooyigbɛ tsei tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa titri lɛ ená shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni mli wa ni hiɛɔ nu mli. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ edaa dɔlɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ naa.

english: Can I successfully plant traditional northern crops on my farm in the south without applying chemicals?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kooyigbɛ kusum nibii yɛ anaigbɛ ŋmɔ ko mli ni mikɛ tsofai tsuuu nii?

english: Yes, you can, but you must ensure your field has good soil drainage, as heavy southern rainfall can rot northern crops if the soil holds too much water.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ, shi ehe miihia ni okwɛ koni oyale lɛ mli aná sũ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ kooyigbɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ lɛ agbo kɛji nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are so many crop farmers moving their farming operations to Northern Ghana these days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe okwaafoi babaoo miifã amɛ okwaayeli nitsumɔi lɛ kɛmiiya Ghana kooyigbɛ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ?

english: The North offers vast, flat, and fertile land suitable for large-scale grain and legume production, along with a dry climate that naturally reduces fungal diseases in crops.
ga: Kooyigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa wulu ni baa nii babaoo. Ehi kɛha ŋmaa kɛ ŋmeii babaoo afeemɔ. kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baa shi lɛ fata he.

english: If I do not buy chemical fertilizer, how can I feed my local crops so they yield well?
ga: Kɛji oheee tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, te ooofee tɛŋŋ oha tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii koni amɛná yibii kpakpai?

english: You can feed local crops naturally by adding animal manure, compost, or planting nitrogen-fixing legumes like groundnuts in rotation to enrich the soil naturally.
ga: Obaanyɛ oye obua shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa nitrogen-fixing legumes tamɔ ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ.

english: Will using too much chemical fertilizer harm the soil on my farm over time?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Yes, overusing synthetic fertilizers can increase soil acidity and kill beneficial earthworms and microbes, making the soil hardened and dependent on chemicals for future crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha sũ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbe shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eheɔ tsofai kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Are local crop varieties naturally better at defending themselves against pests than agric varieties?
ga: Ani tsei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe okwaayeli mli tsei lɛ?

english: Local varieties have naturally evolved thicker skins and bitter natural compounds that repel local pests, whereas high-yielding agric varieties often lack these natural defenses and need protective sprays.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli henɔi lɛ yɛ hewolo ni mli wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni adebɔɔ mli nibii ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ akutso lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, okwaayeli mli tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ bɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu ni amɛbiɔ ni akɛ tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ afɔ amɛnɔ.

english: Why do some of my harvested rice grains turn out small and thin while others on the same field are full and large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ji bibii ni eyɛ mlɛo yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa krokomɛi bɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ eyi obɔ kɛ elɛɛ?

english: Grain size depends on the rice variety and how much water and plant food the crop receives while forming seeds. If parts of your field lack water or nutrients during the flowering stage, those rice plants produce smaller, underfilled grains.
ga: Bɔ ni ŋmãa lɛ da ha lɛ damɔ ŋmãa henɔ lɛ nɔ. Nu kɛ tsei niyenii abɔ ni tsei nine shɛɔ nɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Kɛji he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii kpakpai yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ Nakai ŋmãa tsei lɛ baawo ŋmãa ŋmeii ni baa shi fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ.

english: Why do my rice grains break into tiny pieces when I take them to the mill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ fãa bibii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be akɛyaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Rice grains break easily during milling if they were dried too quickly in hot sun or harvested when overly dry. Drying your harvested paddy slowly in shade or light sunlight helps keep the grains whole and strong.
ga: Omɔ ŋmeii lɛ fãa oya yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ lɛ kɛji amɛgbi oya tsɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. aloo akpaa be mli ni egbi tsɔ Ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ ni egbiɔ blɛoo Yɛ hulutsoo loo hulu la ni mli jɔ mli Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni eye emuu ni ehe wa.

english: What causes my bagged grains to spoil and smell bad even after I harvest them dry?
ga: Mɛni haa miŋmaa ni mikɛwo kotoku mli lɛ fiteɔ ni eŋɔɔɔ kɛji mikpa lɛ ni egbi po?

english: Grains often carry hidden moisture inside them even if the outside feels dry. If bagged before reaching the right dry level, trapped moisture causes heat and mold growth inside the bag, which ruins the quality.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmaa yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtee amɛmli. Kɛji akɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi po. Kɛji akɛ awo kotoku lɛ mli dani eshɛ he ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Trapped moisture haa dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ baafite su lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually show that the crop is starving for nitrogen in the soil or that heavy rains have washed away nutrients. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea early enough helps the crop regain its rich green color and grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli mra lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper and vegetable plants drop their flowers before turning into food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers kɛ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani amɛfeɔ niyenii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or damage from tiny sucking insects. Giving the crops regular water and checking for pests during flowering helps the blossoms stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ fite tso lɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu daa, ni akwɛ kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai yɔɔ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why does rice need flooded water around its roots to grow well while crops like cassava die in too much water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni nu ashɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe bɔni afee ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei gboiɔ kɛjɛɔ nu babaoo mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally have special air channels in their roots that allow them to breathe in waterlogged soil. Other crops like cassava lack these air channels, so too much water rots their roots and kills the plant.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui krɛdɛɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni haa amɛmuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsei krokomɛi tamɔ ŋmei bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui. No hewɔ lɛ, nu babaoo baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo ni egbe tso lɛ.

english: How can I tell if an improved local rice seed will perform better on my land than my traditional saved seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe blema dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ?

english: Improved local seeds are specifically bred by researchers in Ghana to give higher yields, resist local pests, and produce uniform grain sizes that buyers prefer, whereas saved seeds gradually lose their strength over time.
ga: Nibii amlitaolɔi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ ji mɛi ni fɔ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. bɔni afee ni ená yibii babaoo Eteɔ shi ewoɔ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni ewoɔ dumɔwui ni dalɛ tamɔ amɛhe bɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ taoɔ lɛ yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baafite fiofio Hewalɛ ni baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli

english: Why do seeds I save from my previous harvest produce weaker crops when I plant them the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii ni bɛ hewalɛ beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ be kroko mli lɛ?

english: Many modern crop varieties lose their strong traits after the first generation. Storing saved seeds in warm, humid conditions also lowers their energy, causing weaker growth compared to fresh certified seeds.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei srɔtoi babaoo laajeɔ amɛsui ni mli wa lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni ato yɛ he ni edɔ, fɛ̃i hu baa hewalɛ shi. Enɛ haa edalɛ baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster than my planted crops even when I clear the land completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ? Ni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Weed seeds can lie sleeping in the soil for years waiting for rain, and wild weeds are naturally tougher at grabbing food and water than domesticated crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops the head start they need to shade out new weeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ akã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo ni amɛmɛ nugbɔ. Ni jwɛi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa be ni wa ni amɛkɛbaamɔ niyenii kɛ nu fe shia tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee klalo jogbaŋŋ koni amɛha jwɛi heei anɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my grain so the crop quality stays high for buyers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmaa? Koni aha mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ aná ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ

english: Your crop is ready when most of the field changes color to a golden yellow and the seeds become firm when bitten. Harvesting too early leaves you with shriveled grains, while waiting too long causes seeds to fall off and waste in the dirt.
ga: Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efee klalo beni kpokpaa lɛ nɔ hei babaoo etsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ. ni dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ akɔmɔ amɛ Nikpamɔ mra tsɔ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ mɔ ko mɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ ashwie shi ni ashɛrɛ amɛ ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because intense direct heat scorches their leaves and dries out their delicate root systems. Planting shade trees or plantains creates a cool canopy that protects young cocoa until its roots and branches are strong enough to handle sunlight.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi kɛ eniji lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la.

english: Why is it helpful to plant plantains together with young cocoa trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu plantains kɛ kookoo tsei bibii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas. They provide essential shade to protect young cocoa trees from heat while keeping the soil moist, and they also give the farmer food and income while waiting for cocoa to mature.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni akɛbu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa okwaafoi lɛ niyenii kɛ shika hu be mli ni amɛmiimɛ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow instead of remaining green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves whatever nutrients it has left from its older bottom leaves up to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛji nitrogen faaa Tsei lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛkɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of soil nutrients. When the plant feels stressed by bad weather or poor feeding, it drops its flowers to save energy just to survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ amɛmiihao kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii loo niyenii ni ehiii mli Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato koni ehi shi kɛkɛ.

english: What is causing large holes in my corn leaves and dark waste inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli kɛ jwɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The pest crawls into the growing center (whorl) of the corn plant to feed on tender young leaves before they open up, leaving ragged holes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ (ring) ni amɛdaraa lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃. Enɛ haa buji ni ekpɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do weeds reduce my crop harvest even if they are not touching my plants directly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ? Kɛji amɛtaaa mitsei lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ po.

english: Weeds compete silently under the ground and in the air. Their roots steal water and soil nutrients that your crop needs to feed on, while their tall stems block sunlight from reaching your crop's leaves.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli dioo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli fɛɛ. Amɛshishifãi lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ehe hiaa ni otsei lɛ aye lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, amɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ baatsi hulu la naa koni ekashɛ otso lɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the ground during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped around them for too long because heavy water blocks air from reaching the roots. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away quickly, keeping roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ŋmɛ amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ejaakɛ muji lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Ha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why should I spread dry grass around my vegetable crops during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ni egbi mashwã mitsei lɛ ahe yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass or leaves around plants (called mulching) covers the soil like a blanket. It stops the sun and hot winds from evaporating water from the soil, keeping root zone moist for longer periods.
ga: Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi afɔ tsei lɛ ahe (ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching) koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines climb naturally to lift their leaves up toward the sun. Staking helps leaves capture full sunlight to produce heavy tubers underground, while keeping leaves off the damp soil prevents leaf rot.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Staking haa baai lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ hulu la lɛ fɛɛ koni amɛfee bulbs ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni amɛkafite.

english: Why should I buy new hybrid maize seeds instead of planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa dumɔwui heei ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for strong growth, high yield, and disease resistance in their first planting. If you save seeds from that harvest to replant, the offspring lose that special vigor, resulting in uneven growth and smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee Hybrid lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛdara waa, amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔ mli. Kɛji ohere dumɔwui ni jɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ koni odu ekoŋŋ lɛ, Seshi lɛ baafite hewalɛ kroko. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ yibiiwoo fioo baa.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa trees turn brown and dry up during the Harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and cannot handle direct hot sun and dry winds. Without shade plants like plantains nearby, the intense sun burns the leaves and dries up soil moisture quickly.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ bɛ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi oya.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer on my farm right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aba?

english: Heavy rainfall washes away unabsorbed fertilizer off the top of your soil into gutters or streams before the crop's roots have time to take it in, wasting your investment.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieee shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ kɛyaa nubui loo faai amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛshwieɔ mli. ni kɛ shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fitemɔ baa

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves at the base of maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key food maize needs to build green, healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehiɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni wa.

english: Why is it so important to clear weeds from my maize farm in the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crops have weak, short roots. If weeds grow next to them early on, they steal all the water, sunlight, and nutrients before the crop can grow strong enough to defend itself.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni bɛ hewalɛ. Kɛji jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ emasɛi amɛ kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi tɔ̃ɔ. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ dani tso lɛ daa ni ewa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ efãa ehe.

english: Cassava roots rot when water settles around them in heavy or poorly drained soil during wet seasons. Too much water starves the roots of air and allows soil fungi to decay them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Nu babaoo baaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afite.

english: Yam leaves need to spread high up in the sunlight to produce the food required to grow big tubers underground. Lifting the vines off the ground also prevents soil diseases from infecting the leaves.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã hulu la lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni anyɛ ana niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ anaa koni ekamɔ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when water supply is uneven. Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the flower, causing the plant to shed it instead of fruiting.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ yibiiwoo najiaŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tight and becoming small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck the plant juices and spread viruses that stunt leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Emuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei amli ni egbɛɔ hela ko ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ naa lɛ eshwaa.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small suckers growing around my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Mi dumɔwui lɛ eje kpo.

english: Too many young shoots around one plantain stem fight over the same water and food in the soil. Removing extra suckers leaves enough energy for the main tree to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei bibii babaoo ni ebɔle plantain tso kome he lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Tso yibii ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso titri lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmeii agboi ni tsii.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my field make the soil better for next season's maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni baaba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that can pull nitrogen out of the air and store it in their roots. When the plant breaks down in the soil, that trapped nutrient remains behind to feed the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Niyenii nibii ni amɔmɔ amɛ lɛ hiɔ sɛɛ koni amɛha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their leaves during dry periods to conserve water. Adding shade trees and putting dry grass around the base of the trees helps keep the soil moist and protects the leaves from burning.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni akɛfataa he kɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa baa lɛ ashã.

english: What causes my green cocoa pods to suddenly turn black and rot right on the stem?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ trukaa ni egbo yɛ tso lɛ shishi?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and overly shaded environments. Pruning excess branches lets air and sunlight in to keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ fe nine. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la boteɔ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my maize plant growing very tall with dark green leaves but making tiny corncobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛyɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa shi amɛwoɔ abele bibii lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, or when maize plants are planted too close together, causing them to fight for light instead of developing cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ fa babaoo fe nitrogen. aloo kɛ́ adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmãa ŋmãa.

english: Why does my soil produce less maize every year when I plant on the same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi beni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize takes specific nutrients out of the soil each season. Planting it in the same spot continuously drains those nutrients and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ ajɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are mature and big underground without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifã lɛ edara kwraa ni eda yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni okɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava roots are usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil right around the main stem starts to swell and crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca shishifãi lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ he lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: Yam leaves produce food for the tubers using sunlight. Staking lifts the vines so leaves get maximum sun and keeps them off the damp ground where diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa tuber lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. ni etsi hulutsoo naa yɛ hei ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ

english: Why shouldn't I let all the young shoots grow around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Midumɔwu titri lɛ

english: Too many side shoots struggle with the main tree for water and food. Keeping only one or two healthy shoots ensures the main stem produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Side shoots babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso wulu lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yitso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ awo tsei agboi babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop to the ground without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot, when the plant doesn't get enough water, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients like phosphorus.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling upwards and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread viruses, or by severe heat stress when the plant loses water faster than its roots can take it up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa, beni tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ lɛ.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to the local environment, and their seeds sit dormant in the soil ready to sprout immediately when water hits, outracing domestic crops for sunlight.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe kɛtee he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. Ni amɛdumɔwui lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe yɛ sũ lɛ mli, ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji nu lɛ tswa amɛ pɛ. Ha tsei ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná hulu la.

english: Why should I clear and loosen the soil on my land with a tractor before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ trakta ajie sũ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni mafolɔ mli dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Ploughing breaks up hard soil so that young plant roots can easily spread deep to find water and nutrients. It also buries weeds and allows rain to soak into the earth rather than washing away your topsoil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ gbálaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã shɔŋŋ koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii. Efuɔ jwɛi hu ni ehaa nugbɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeefɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What is a net house, and how will building one on my farm protect my vegetables?
ga: Mɛni ji trellis ŋmɔ? Ni te ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ mli ŋtayaai amamɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu mi-aduawai lɛ ahe aha tɛŋŋ?

english: A net house is a simple frame covered with fine mesh netting. It acts as a shield that allows sunlight, air, and rain through while blocking destructive insects and pests from attacking your vegetables.
ga: Trellis greenhouse ji tsɔne ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛ ŋshɔŋloo kpakpa eha he. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni haa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ nugbɔ tsɔɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ anaa koni amɛkatutua o-vegetables lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and stay thin when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops must fight each other for nutrients, soil water, and sunlight. This competition starves the plants, causing their leaves to turn yellow and slowing down their growth.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Esa akɛ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe atswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii, shikpɔŋ nɔ nu, kɛ hulu la. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei yeɔ hɔmɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa amɛdalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need plantain crops grown right beside them in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Cocoa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily burn under direct hot sun. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that shade young cocoa trees while keeping the soil cool and moist around their roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my land produce smaller cassava tubers if I plant cassava on the exact same farm every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmei shishifãi bibii kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year. Rotating your cassava with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores vital plant food naturally back into the ground.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. O-cassava lɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ cowpeas loo peanuts baatsake Enɛ baaha tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku esɛɛ kɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers when the soil stays dry for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Making fruits requires a lot of water and energy. When pepper plants do not get enough moisture from dry soil, they shed their flowers to save water and protect the main plant from dying.
ga: Yibii afeemɔ biɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ babaoo. Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu tso titri lɛ he koni ekagbo.

english: Why is it better to place fertilizer near my crop's roots instead of scattering it all over the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer near the base of your crop ensures the roots swallow the nutrients directly. Scattering it everywhere feeds wild weeds, which will grow faster and steal light and space from your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Niyenii ni akɛhaa koo mli jwɛi baagbɛ ashwã he fɛɛ he. Enɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni ebaaju la kɛ he ko kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why should I pinch off the small extra shoots growing out of my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ tomato tso lɛ mli lɛ

english: Removing extra branch shoots stops the tomato plant from wasting its energy on useless leaves. This directs all the plant's food and strength into growing larger, healthier tomato fruits.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine ni ooojie lɛ haaa o-tomato tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baatsɔɔ niyenii kɛ tsei ahewalɛ kɛya tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my yam mounds with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the soil from hot sun so water does not evaporate quickly. It also stops heavy rains from baking the earth hard or washing away good topsoil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni nu akafee oya Etsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ais loo ekɛ sũ kpakpa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ afɔ.

english: Why do wild weeds sprout and grow faster than my crop seeds after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ beni nugbɔ be lɛ eje shishi lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and already resting in the soil waiting for moisture. When the first rains fall, weeds wake up instantly and steal soil food before sown seeds have time to develop strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛmiijɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ momo ni amɛmiimɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Beni nugbɔ nɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ Jwɛi lɛ teɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani dumɔwui ni adu lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛ shishifãi ni wa baa.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle full, direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily and dry out. They require shade from bigger trees or plantains during their first few years to retain moisture and survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya ni amɛgbiɔ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo plantains amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli koni amɛná hulutsoo ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with small cobs when I plant them under big tree shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni adu yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Maize needs full, direct sunlight to make food and grow strong stems. When grown under shade, the plant stretches upward toward the light, using up all its energy instead of building strong stems and thick cobs.
ga: Hulu la he miihia ŋmãa tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii kɛ ŋmeii ni wa. Kɛji adu yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tso lɛ baakpã kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya la lɛ he. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ ni ekɛfeɔ tsei ahe tsei ni wa kɛ tsei bibii ni mli tse.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the plant mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key plant food. Adding nitrogen rich fertilizer or compost helps the leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge green leaves above ground but very tiny tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, cassava puts all its energy into growing leafy branches instead of storing food underground. Cassava needs balanced soil nutrients to develop large tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei kɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei niji kɛ baai. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja he miihia Cassava koni enyɛ ená ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my farm make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmeii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as natural food for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni okpa amɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off during the peak hot season without making peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni egbeee pepper lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the plant, making it drop its flowers to save water and stay alive. Giving the plants enough water during dry spells helps them hold onto flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Ha egbee shi koni ekɛhere nu ni ehi wala mli. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa tsei yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛmɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the dirt when heavy rains flood my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha ŋmɔji amli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits on the land for too long, oxygen is blocked, causing fungal rot to set in and destroy the tubers underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Oxygen lɛ baatsi enaa. Enɛ haa ŋmei ko ni fiteɔ ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and twisting tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the juice out of young leaves, or by viruses spread by those insects. Controlling these small bugs early stops leaf twisting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ virus ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ kooloi bibii akudɔmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Ekpaa baai lɛ ashishijee.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with small worms hiding in the leaf centers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a destructive pest that feeds on the soft center leaves of maize. Checking fields early and applying appropriate treatments in the whorl kills them before major damage happens.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fiteɔ nii ni yeɔ ŋmãa teŋgbɛ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. He lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ tsamɔ ni sa baatsu nii yɛ kooyigbɛ lɛ baagbe amɛ dani afite nii wuji.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the small shoots grow around my main plantain stem at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso wulu lɛ he yɛ be kome too mli lɛ?

english: When too many shoots grow together, they fight each other for water, light, and soil nutrients. Keeping only one or two strong shoots makes the main plantain produce larger, healthier bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ fee ekome tsɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha plantain titri lɛ awo niji ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Shading trees act as natural umbrellas that protect young cocoa leaves from burning and help keep the soil moist during hot days.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my young crops with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves creates a protective blanket over the soil. This stops the hot sun from drying out the moisture quickly and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he. Enɛ haa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi oya, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my growing maize plants turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plant is lacking nitrogen, which is a key food for plant leaves. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves turn green and produce a better harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji tso baai lɛ niyenii titri Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Is it good for my farm if I plant beans in the same field alongside my maize?
ga: Ani ehi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ ŋmãa masɛi?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very beneficial. Beans take food from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps feed the maize plant and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Beans jieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil when we get too much heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ wɔná nugbɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots cannot breathe when they sit in soaked, watery ground for too long. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds allows excess rain to drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu kɛji amɛtara shikpɔŋ ni nu ewo mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry break before the real rainy season starts. If seeds sprout and then run out of rain water immediately, the tender young roots will dry up and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hejɔɔmɔ kuku nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ baaje shishi Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni nugbɔshiimɔ faaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ Shishifãi bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Yam vines need to reach high up so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. When leaves get plenty of light, they generate more energy to grow bigger yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɛ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná la ni fa bɔ ni sa Ebaaha hewalɛ babaoo aba ni ekɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do weeds in my crop field make my farm yield so much smaller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ haa nibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ faaa kwraa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight meant for your crops. When weeds grow too close, your crops don't get enough food to produce big grains or tubers.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Beni jwɛi lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ tsɔ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ enaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui wuji loo bulbs aba.

english: Why are the yellow flowers on my tomato plants dropping off without growing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni miduuu tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plant gets stressed from lack of water. Keeping the soil regularly watered helps flowers stay on and become tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ hao yɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tomato.

english: Why are small worms creating ragged holes in the middle of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii feɔ bu ni etse ehe yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These worms are pests that hatch from eggs laid by small moths. They hide inside the central leaves of young maize because the leaves are soft and easy for them to eat.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni woɔ amɛwui amli lɛ amli. Ekɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai amli ejaakɛ baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni eyeli waaa.

english: Why are there small holes in my young maize leaves with sawdust-like dirt inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni yɔɔ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides deep inside the leaf funnel to feed on the tender shoots. Spraying recommended treatments directly into the funnel early in the morning or late in the evening helps get rid of them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ shwie ŋmeii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie amɛ.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from young leaves and passing on viruses. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or appropriate sprays prevents the leaves from twisting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni shwieɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ni amɛhaa hela lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo spray ni sa nɔ lɛ ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and stay short instead of growing dark green and tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee kuku yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowish, stunted maize is a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green leaves and strong stems. Applying compost or a balanced nitrogen fertilizer early in the crop's growth will restore its green color and height.
ga: Abɛi ni ji yellow dwarf lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli kɛ ŋmeii ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ni sa wo tso lɛ mli yɛ tso lɛ shishijee be mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ su lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ekɛlɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas make my soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. When the leaves and roots decay, they leave behind natural fertilizer that nourishes the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ, amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry periods to reduce water loss through evaporation and protect their roots underground. Once the rains return, the stem will quickly produce fresh leaves and continue growing normally.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi, ni ebu amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei oya ni eda bɔ ni sa.
