english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or sudden dryness, causing it to save energy rather than produce seeds. Watering the soil consistently at the roots helps the plant hold onto its blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hulutsoo ni baa trukaa lɛ miigba tsei lɛ anaa. Ekɛ hewalɛ baa shi moŋ fe ni eeefee dumɔwui. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu daa yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines onto tall stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the plant, which is stored below ground as the tuber. Lifting the vines on stakes exposes maximum leaf area to the sun, producing much bigger and heavier yams.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha tso lɛ. ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi akɛ ŋmeii Wain tso lɛ nɔ ni ooowo nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ baai lɛ aná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmɔtɔ ni da ni tsii kwraa.

english: Why should I prune off some of the young suckers growing around my main plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain wulu lɛ he lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Having too many suckers causes them to compete with the main stem for water, light, and soil nutrients. Keeping only one main plant and one or two replacement suckers ensures the main stem produces large, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo haa amɛ kɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ekwɛɔ tso titri kome pɛ kɛ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ awo yibii ni tsii ni dara.

english: Why shouldn't I use the soft, green tips of cassava stems for planting new fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ lɛ?

english: Soft, green stem tops dry out quickly and rot in the soil before they can sprout strong roots. Using mature, woody middle sections of the stem guarantees higher survival rates and stronger sprouting.
ga: Tso lɛ yiteŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ji eŋɔli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani shishifãi ni wa baa. Kɛ akɛ tso ni eda ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa wala yibiiwoo ni yaa hiɛ babaoo kɛ ŋmeii ni he wa.

english: Why does my lowland rice field need standing water around the roots during the growth stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ hiɛ nu ni damɔ shi ebɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Standing water smothers competing weeds that try to choke the young rice plants and provides continuous moisture for root development. The water is drained later when the grains are ready to dry and ripen.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni egbeɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi ŋmãa tsei bibii anaa lɛ, ni ehaa nu ni yaa nɔ ehaa shishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ. Abaajie nu lɛ kɛjɛ mli sɛɛ mli beni ŋmaa lɛ egbi ni ehoo lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them directly under full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in direct sun because their roots cannot absorb water fast enough. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects the cocoa seedlings from hot sun and helps retain soil moisture until they mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ kookoo tsei lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ daraa.

english: Why do I need to use wooden stakes to support my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso he hiaa mi koni mikɛwo mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight, which allows the leaves to manufacture food for growing big tubers underground. Elevating vines off the damp soil also prevents leaf fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Wein tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa baai lɛ anɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when heavy wind and rain hit my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni naa wa ba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and very heavy tops, especially when bearing fruit. Supporting the main stem with a propping pole made of bamboo or wood prevents strong winds from snapping the stem or uprooting the tree.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu tsii waa. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ ewo yibii Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ fi tso titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekakumɔ shishitoo lɛ loo ekajie tso lɛ shishi.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which plants need for healthy green growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-decomposed manure will restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in the same farm help my maize grow better next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baaye abua ni mi-ŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant leaves and roots decay in the soil, they feed and enrich the ground for demanding crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyaa amɛshishifãi amli. Beni tsei ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi gboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛhaa niyenii ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my crop harvests keep getting smaller every year when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ faaa daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Rotating your crops with leguminous plants or leaving the land to rest replenishes essential nutrients naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tsake oŋmɔshi nibii loo oshi shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aba ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn black and rot underground during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water logs the soil and cuts off air to the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away so roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu bote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni efo kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or whiteflies sucking leaf sap and spreading viral diseases. Spraying a mild solution of neem oil or insecticidal soap helps control these insects early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baa lɛ mli nu ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ blɛoo shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the plants experience severe heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist by mulching around the roots helps the plant retain flowers and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛtsɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my okra plants growing tall with big leaves but producing very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ daa kɛ baai wuji shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen causes them to focus on growing tall leafy branches instead of producing flowers and fruit. Switching to a fertilizer rich in phosphorus encourages blooming and fruit production.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ haa amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa tsei niji ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee fɔsfɔs ni fa babaoo mli lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi kɛ yibii aba.

english: Why do my tomato plants wither and dry up so quickly when the sun is hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ oya kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants have soft stems and leaves that lose water very quickly in high heat. If their shallow roots cannot find water in the soil, the plant loses its strength and wilts rapidly to protect itself from dying.
ga: Tomato tsei yɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛ baai ni nu fiteɔ oya waa kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa mli. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana nu yɛ sũ lɛ mli, Koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ gbele he lɛ, tso lɛ hewalɛ baaje mli oya ni ebaagbi.

english: How can I keep moisture in my soil for a long time during the dry season?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: You can cover the soil around your crops with dried grass or leaves, a method called mulching. This acts as an umbrella over the dirt, stopping the sun from baking the soil and evaporating all the water.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi akpɛ onibii lɛ. Atsɛɔ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii lɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ hulu lɛ naa koni ekashã shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ nu lɛ fɛɛ afee lasu.

english: Why do my plant leaves droop during the middle of the day even when the soil still feels damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ edɔ lolo moŋ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it up from the ground. The temporary drooping is the plant's natural way of reducing leaf surface exposed to heat to conserve water.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Be kukuoo mli tso lɛ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehaa tso lɛ baa lɛ nɔ hulutsoo baa shi koni ekɛbu nu he.

english: Why do crops grown in developed countries mature much faster than the ones we grow here in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ maji ni etee hiɛ lɛ amli lɛ shwereɔ oya fe tsei ni wɔduɔ yɛ Ghana biɛ lɛ?

english: Farmers in developed countries often use hybrid seeds bred specifically for rapid growth, along with controlled greenhouse environments and drip irrigation systems that feed the plant the exact amount of water and food it needs every day without delay.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi ni yɔɔ maji ni ebɔi shweremɔ lɛ amli lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni akwɛɔ koni amɛdara oya lɛ tsuɔ nii. Nɔ ni fata enɛ he ji shihilɛ ni akudɔɔ nibii ni haa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ kɛ nu ni hoɔ ni haa tsei lɛ náa nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ daa gbi ni ekɛ be sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ.

english: What is the benefit of buying certified packaged seeds instead of planting seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni awo mli ni awo he odaseyeli he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ he yɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Seeds saved from old harvests lose their strength over time and produce smaller yields. Certified seeds are carefully developed by plant scientists to grow faster, resist local diseases, and give you a larger harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ momo mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli ni ebaawo yibii babaoo. Tsei ahe nilelɔi efee dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛdara oya. helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa bo ni okpaa babaoo.

english: Why are my tomato plants remaining short and not producing flowers after several weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ yɔɔ kuku lolo ni amɛwooo fɔfɔi yɛ otsii komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Stunted growth usually happens when the plant lacks key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or when the soil is too hard for the roots to spread out and feed properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛji sũ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛye niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn yellow even when I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are often a sign that the plant is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. Giving too much water can also wash away essential nutrients from around the roots, causing the plant to turn pale.
ga: Bei pii lɛ baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nu babaoo baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Ebaanyɛ eha tsei afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why is it bad to plant my crops right at the very end of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Young crops planted late in the season will not have enough time to grow deep, strong roots before the rains stop completely, causing them to dry up as soon as the heat begins.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ naaa be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaatsɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛhe wa dani nugbɔ lɛ akpa kwraa, ni no baaha amɛgbi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ je shishi pɛ.

english: How does bad weather cause my tomatoes to spoil on the stem before I can harvest them?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii lɛ ha mi-tomato lɛ fite yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ dani akpa amɛ?

english: Extremely hot sun combined with sudden heavy rain causes uneven water intake by the plant, which makes the skin of tomato fruits split open and rot before they mature.
ga: Hulu ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ haa tsei lɛ naa nu ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Enɛ haa tomato aduawai lɛ ahewolo lɛ mli fãa ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ.

english: Why do some crops need shade when they are young, while others need full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ahe hiaa hulutsoo be mli ni amɛdarako lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi hia hulu ni fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young or delicate crops burn easily under direct heat because their leaves cannot retain much water yet. Full-sun crops like maize have tough structures designed to process heavy sunlight into energy once established.
ga: Tsei bibii loo tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu babaoo lolo. Tsei ni naa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ yɛ gbɛjianɔtoi ni wa ni afee koni ekɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ atsu nii kɛji ebɔi shikome.

english: Why do people tell me to plant my seeds as soon as the first rains start in the Upper East Region?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ midu dumɔwui kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ je shishi pɛ yɛ Upper East Region lɛ?

english: The rainy season in northern regions like the Upper East is short, and water does not stay in the soil for long. Planting early ensures your crops get enough rainfall throughout their growth before the dry period arrives.
ga: Nugbɔ be ni nɛɔ yɛ kooyigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ, tamɔ ŋwɛi bokagbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ kuku. Ni nu lɛ ehiii sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ aná nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛdalɛ be fɛɛ mli dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba.

english: What will happen to my crops if I wait too long and plant them late in the season?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mimɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni midu yɛ be ni shɛɔ lɛ mli?

english: Late-planted crops will run out of water before they are ready to yield. The rains will stop while the plants are still growing, causing them to dry up and leave you with a poor harvest.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ nu bɛ amɛhe dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaawo yibii. Nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ yaa nɔ amɛdaraa lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ehaa onáa ŋmaa kpakpa.

english: Why do farmers in dry regions need a different planting schedule compared to farmers in wetter regions?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ hei ni nu bɛ lɛ yɛ be ni amɛduɔ nii yɛ srɔto fe okwaafoi ni yɔɔ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Dry regions have shorter rainy seasons and hotter weather where water evaporates quickly. Farmers there must plant immediately when rains begin, whereas wetter areas have longer rain cycles and more flexible planting times.
ga: Hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ lɛ yɛ kukuoo kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ ni nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Esa akɛ okwaafoi adu nii kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ pɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ lɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ kɛ be ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ hu tsakeɔ.

english: Why does the water on my farm dry up so fast just a few days after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Some soils are sandy or lack organic matter, which prevents them from holding onto water. Adding dry compost or manure helps the soil act like a sponge to keep moisture available for your crops longer.
ga: Shikpɔji komɛi yɛ ŋã loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli. ni haa enyɛŋ ehiɛ nu mli Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ sponji koni ehiɛ nu mli kɛha onibii lɛ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tight into tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl inward to protect themselves from the hot sun and reduce the amount of water escaping into the air. It is a natural signal that the plant is trying to conserve water.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli koni amɛtsi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa ni amɛha nu ni hoɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ aba shi. Eji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsei miitao ni amɛbu nu he.

english: Why did my seeds fail to sprout after I put them in the soil during a dry week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ otsi ni nu bɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds need constant moisture to wake up and send out roots. If the soil dries out right after planting, the young plant inside the seed dies before it can push above the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa nu be fɛɛ be koni amɛte shi ni amɛjie amɛshishifãi lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu lɛ Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ baagboi dani abaanyɛ ashɛre amɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are some farmers covering the soil around their crops with dry grass and weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (called mulching) shades the soil from the hot sun. This prevents water from evaporating quickly and keeps the ground cool and moist for the crop roots.
ga: Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching.) Ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ haaa nu lɛ atsɔ oya, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Which crops can I plant if the weather in my area is very dry and water disappears quickly?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ makwɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni nu lɛ hoɔ oya?

english: Crops like millet, sorghum, and cowpeas are naturally tough against drought. They require less water and have roots that dig deep, making them ideal for areas with short rainy seasons.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa. Nu fioo pɛ he hiaa ni eyɛ shishifãi ni tsɔɔ shɔŋŋ. Ehi kɛha hei ni nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo yɔɔ.

english: How does planting shade trees or cover crops help keep water in my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Trees and cover crops block direct sunlight from hitting the bare earth. Less sun exposure means lower temperatures on the ground, which stops moisture in the soil from drying out fast.
ga: Tsei kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii tsiɔ hulu la ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Hulu la ni baa shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ baa shi. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya.

english: How can working with an agricultural extension officer help me avoid crop failures on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nitsumɔ ni mikɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baatsu lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi koni ŋmɔshi nibii akafite yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Extension officers understand local rainfall patterns, soil conditions, and crop types. They can guide you on the exact right time to plant and how to manage water so your crops grow successfully without problems.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ nuɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ shihilɛ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii henɔi shishi. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo bo ŋaa yɛ be ni sa ni esa akɛ odu nii kɛ bɔ ni ooofee okwɛ nu nɔ koni onibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni naagba ko akafee bo.

english: Why are my maize plants near the edge of my neighbor's big trees growing small and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mikutsoŋnyo tso agbo lɛ naa lɛ bibii ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Big tree roots spread wide underground and drink up most of the water and nutrients from the soil. Their tall branches also block the sunshine, leaving crops along the border hungry and shaded.
ga: Tsei wuji ashishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛnuɔ amɛnu kɛ niyenii kpakpai babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛniji kakadaji lɛ hu tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ husu lɛ naa lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛfeɔ hulutsoo.

english: If I plant my crops very close together to fit more on my land, why do I get smaller harvests?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mihe lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ hu? Mɛni hewɔ mitsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots fight each other for the limited water and food in the soil, while leaves block each other's light. Spacing plants properly allows each crop to grow strong and yield larger fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe la naa Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni ewoɔ yibii wuji.

english: Can I plant living hedge trees along my farm boundary without them ruining my food crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋtayaa ni hiɛ ka yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ he ni miyeee miniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, as long as you choose plants with deep taproots that dig deep down rather than spreading near the surface, and trim their leaves regularly so they do not block sunlight from your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ obaahala tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Ni ŋmɔ baai lɛ daa koni amɛkatsi hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli lɛ naa.

english: Why do my crops still turn pale even after I spent a lot of money applying chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lolo yɛ be mli ni mifite shika babaoo yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can wash away expensive fertilizer before roots drink it, or soil that lacks organic matter cannot hold onto the nutrients. Adding compost or dry leaves helps lock fertilizer in the soil so plants can absorb it.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa dani shishifãi lɛ anu. Aloo shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli lɛ nyɛŋ ahiɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo baai ni egbi fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why does my farmland produce less yield every year even though I plant the same crop every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil until it is exhausted. Rotating your crops with beans or groundnuts naturally puts fresh food back into the soil for free.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ooodu lɛ baaya nɔ ejie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi amɛbaafite. Kɛ́ okɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha niyenii hee aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers instead of making fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when they suffer from intense heat or lack of regular water. The plant conserves its remaining energy to survive the drought stress rather than spending it on fruit production.
ga: Tomato baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa yɛ emli daa lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Tso lɛ toɔ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ hɔmɔ haomɔ mli. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ aduawai afeemɔ mli

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and stop water from evaporating too quickly during the hottest part of the day.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbaa hulu la ni shɛɔ enɔ lɛ shi. ni otsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cowpeas grow long leafy vines without producing pods when planted under tall cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea wain tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ wain tsei ni baai kakadaji ni efeee ŋmeii kɛji akɛ adu yɛ yucca ni kɛlɛ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas need full, direct sunlight to flower and form pods. Heavy shade forces the plant to spend all its energy stretching upwards to find light instead of making seeds.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛfee ŋmeii. Shade ni tsii haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni shɛɔ ŋwɛi kɛyaa la lɛ he lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni eeewo dumɔwui.

english: Cassava roots rot when water settles in heavy soil for too long, suffocating the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than the pepper seedlings I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe ŋmɔtɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛ hiɛdɔɔ du lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants adapted to grab water, light, and soil food much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks gives your crops a fair chance to take root.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ kpakpa ni amɛwo shishifãi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains around them to block strong sun and keep the soil moist until they grow stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ koni amɛha hulu ni naa wa lɛ ashɛ amɛhe ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to stay green and grow leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛkwɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting under the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them without draining away. Clay soils or low ground that stays soaked for too long drown the roots and encourage fungal rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. ni ajieee nu kɛjɛɛɛ mli Shikpɔŋ sũ loo hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu ewo mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shishi ni ewo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off instead of growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air gets too hot or when soil moisture changes suddenly from very dry to very wet. Keeping the soil evenly moist and planting at the right season prevents flower drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛyaa nɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni adu yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaatsi fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ anaa.

english: Why do I need to heap the soil into mounds before planting my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato shikpɔŋ mawo gɔŋ nɔ dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft earth to push deep into the ground and grow thick tubers. Mounds hold loose soil together and protect tubers from getting waterlogged.
ga: Sweet potatoes biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni ekɛtsi ehe kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni eha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Gɔŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ feɔ ekome ni ebuɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ nu ni shwieɔ amɛnɔ lɛ he.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close to each other, why do I get small cobs instead of a bigger harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa bibioo nɔ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooona yibii babaoo?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots fight each other for water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block light from one another, causing weak stalks and smaller yields.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking juices from under the leaves, or by viral sicknesses spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why do my crops droop and look dead during afternoon heat even when the ground is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni egboi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense midday heat, plants lose water from their leaves faster than roots can drink it up. They temporarily wilt to save water and will recover when the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Ehe miihia ni amɛto nu he gbɛjianɔ be kukuoo ko, ni amɛbaaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn pale and grow so slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdaraa blɛoo waa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and steal the fertilizer, soil water, and sunlight that your main crops need to grow strong, leaving your crops hungry and weak.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, sũ mli nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei titrii lɛ koni amɛdara waa lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii ni ogbɔjɔ.

english: Why are there small holes chewed into my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Holes in leaves are usually caused by caterpillars or beetles feeding on the plant. Checking under the leaves early helps you catch and remove these insects before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei loo ŋmei ni yeɔ tso lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu yɛ baai lɛ amli. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi mra. Ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni ojie amɛ dani amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main food it needs to grow healthy green leaves. It can also happen when the soil is overly flooded with water, causing the roots to choke and fail to absorb nutrients.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply my fertilizer right when heavy rain is falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa?

english: Heavy rains will wash away the fertilizer into drains and streams before the crop roots have time to drink it up. It is best to apply fertilizer when the ground is moist but not during heavy rainfall.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa nugbɔshiimɔi kɛ faai amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi otsi ohe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why do all the flowers on my cocoa trees keep falling off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the farm is too hot and dry, or when tiny pests like mirids attack them. Maintaining good shade trees and controlling sucking insects help the flowers stay on the tree and turn into cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni egbi. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen tutua amɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be mli ni akudɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and soft while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium or water regularly while the fruit is growing, causing the bottom tissue of the tomato to collapse.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana calcium loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Enɛ haa fãji ni yɔɔ tomato lɛ shishi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the plant juices, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies. Controlling these tiny insects early prevents the leaf twisting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. ŋmeii bibii akwɛmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Ebaaye ebua ni ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsake.

english: Yam leaves need plenty of direct sunlight to make food. When the vines climb up stakes, their leaves spread out to catch sunlight, which sends energy down into the ground to make the yam tubers grow big.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛhoo. Kɛ́ wain tso lɛ kwɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ Ebaai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa koni emɔ hulu la lɛ. Enɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adara.

english: Is it good for me to plant cassava and maize together on the same land at the same time?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together works well because maize grows quickly and is ready for harvest in three months, while cassava grows slowly at first. After harvesting the maize, the cassava takes over the farm space.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya, ni eshɛɔ he ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei baakwɛ̃ fiofio yɛ shishijee mli lɛ. Kɛji akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Cassava baaye ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce tiny yields if I don't clear them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo yibii fioo kɛji mijieee amɛ?

english: Weeds steal the food, soil water, and sunlight meant for your crops. If weeds cover your farm, your crops become starved and cannot produce big fruits or grains.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii, shikpɔŋ nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛji jwɛi ha oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hɔmɔ baaye amɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii loo dumɔwui wuji.

english: Why will my crops suffer if I plant the seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ yeɔ awui kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their leaves block each other from sunlight and their roots fight under the ground for water and nutrients, resulting in weak, thin plants.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa lɛ baa.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn brown and snap during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛkuɔ yɛ harmatta be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry harmattan winds suck moisture out of plant leaves very fast. When the soil is dry and roots cannot supply enough water, the outer leaves dry up and break to help the main stem preserve its remaining water.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aha nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Baai ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛjaraa koni eye ebua tso titri lɛ ni ekɛ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ ato.

english: Yellowing in a V-shape starting from the leaf tips usually means your soil is low in nitrogen. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or planting legumes like cowpeas in rotation will help feed the soil and make the leaves dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, su ni tamɔ V ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli loo ni aduɔ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant many seeds close together in one hole to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo bu kome mli ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: When plants are crowded together, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems and small yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and food to produce a larger harvest.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Why do weeds make my young crops look weak and stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔwui lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your main crop. Clearing weeds early, especially during the first four weeks after planting, allows your crops to grow strong without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii titrii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ ni adu sɛɛ lɛ mli. Ye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdara waa ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting under the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpa lɛ?

english: Tuber rot happens when the soil stays too wet for long periods or when soil fungi attack the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges improves drainage and keeps the roots from soaking in excess water.
ga: Tuber rot baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ loo kɛji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tutua shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ aya hiɛ, ni ebaatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni nu ni fa fe nine akabote shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the centers of my young maize leaves and leaving brown powder behind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ni amɛshiɔ powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. They hide inside the central funnel of the plant. Applying recommended biological controls or target treatments early in the morning or late evening will help protect your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛkwɛɔ nibii anɔ loo tsofafeemɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsu nii taakɛ atsɔɔ lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Extreme heat, lack of water, or irregular watering causes stress that makes tomato plants drop flowers to save energy. Keeping the soil consistently moist using mulch and regular watering helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsu nii ni okɛ nu wo mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them grow during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around lɛ mikɛ jwɛi duɔ miŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground and shields the soil from hot sunlight. As the dry grass breaks down, it also adds rich organic matter back into your soil.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi lɛ fite Ekɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli hu baaku sɛɛ aba oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves wilt in the hot afternoon sun even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the ground. As long as they recover by evening, it is a natural defense, though mulching around the roots helps reduce heat stress.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu. Eyɛ mli akɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shi moŋ, shi.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct, intense sunlight and burn easily. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains alongside cocoa provides temporary living umbrellas that shield the young cocoa until it establishes strong roots.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛshãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ni buɔ kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni etswaa shishifãi ni wa.

english: Plantains have shallow root systems, and heavy bunches make the tree top-heavy. When heavy rain softens the soil, strong winds easily push them over. Supporting the fruit-bearing stem with a sturdy wooden Y-fork prop prevents them from falling.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. ni jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ haa tsei lɛ ayitsei feɔ tsiimɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa kɛhoɔ oya. Akɛ tso ni wa fee Y-shaped fork posts fiɔ aduawai ahe tsei lɛ asɛɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni ekagbee shi.

english: Why do the seeds I save from my harvested maize produce smaller cobs than the original seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni mikɛtoɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa bibii fe shishijee ŋmãa ni mihe lɛ?

english: Commercial hybrid seeds are specifically bred from two distinct parent plants to produce strong, high-yielding crops in their first generation. When you save and replant those harvested seeds, the offspring lose that special balance and revert to weaker traits, producing smaller plants and lower yields.
ga: Akɛ jarayeli dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔ̃ɔ tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ amli tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa, ni woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji okɛ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ to ni okɛdu ekoŋŋ lɛ Seshibii lɛ baafite nakai jɛkɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ lɛ ni amɛbaaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba sui ni bɛ hewalɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do some cassava cuttings grow strong tubers while others from the same field barely yield anything?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi komɛi yɛ shishifãi ni wa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ eshwɛ fioo ni amɛbaawo yibii kwraa lɛ?

english: Cassava plants pass down their health directly through the stem cuttings used for planting. If a cutting is taken from an old or diseased parent plant, the new plant will be weak from the start, whereas cuttings from young, healthy parent stalks produce strong roots and heavy yields.
ga: Cassava tsei tsɔɔ amɛ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ afolɔ niji kɛjɛ nyɛ tso ni egbɔ loo hela emɔ lɛ mli Tsei heei lɛ baagbɔjɔ kɛjɛ shishijee. Yɛ be mli ni niji bibii ni he wa lɛ baawo shishifãi ni wa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants curling inward during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves as a natural defense mechanism during hot, dry periods to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This helps the plant conserve water and prevent moisture from evaporating too quickly from its tissues.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛ baai lɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo yɛ dɔlɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Koni akɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ fãji lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ shi oya tsɔ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience sudden stress, such as intense heat, insufficient water, or a sudden change in nutrients. When the plant feels threatened, it conserves energy by dropping flowers rather than trying to feed growing fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛi trukaa, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. aloo niyenii mli nibii ni tsakeɔ trukaa lɛ Beni tsei nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe miiwo gbeyei Ebaaha hewalɛ aba shi kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni ejieɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eha aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the trees during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives and spreads rapidly in wet, humid conditions. Rain drops splash fungal spores from the soil onto the low pods, causing them to rot and shrivel.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Nugbɔ nɛɔ, ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. ni haa amɛgboiɔ ni amɛgbiɔ

english: Why do my garden eggs get black soft spots at the bottom while they are still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ amɛshishi be mli ni amɛdaraa lolo lɛ?

english: This condition, known as blossom-end rot, is caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit. It usually happens when watering is irregular, preventing the roots from taking up calcium consistently from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa.

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful soil microbes to capture nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their roots. When the cowpea plant dies and decays, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as rich food for the next maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛwo amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsina tsei lɛ gboi ni amɛgboi Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ niyenii babaoo aha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava peels make the soil hot and yellow my plants when I bury them raw in the garden?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ehaa mitsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ mifu amɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fresh, raw plant waste requires soil bacteria to break it down, and these bacteria temporarily consume all the available nitrogen in the soil to do their work. Composting the peels first allows them to break down safely so they feed your soil instead of starving it.
ga: Tsoi ahe jwɛi ni afee ehee kɛ nɔ ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ biɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛfite. Ni helatsɛmɛi nɛɛ kɛ nitrogen fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ amɛnitsumɔ lɛ be kukuoo ko. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo ŋmei lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaakumɔ ŋmei lɛ shweshweeshwe. koni eye muji moŋ fe ni hɔmɔ baaye lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large, broad leaves that create vital shade and preserve soil moisture, acting as natural umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa baa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo be mli ni cacao tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow thin and crooked instead of thick and long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kɛlɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow straight and thick when the soil beneath them is soft, loose, and deep. If the soil is hard or compacted, the tuber struggles to push downward and expand outward, resulting in small, misshapen tubers.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli edɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, Yitso lɛ baaná naagba yɛ shi ni eeetsi kɛmiiya kponɔgbɛ. Enɛ haa yitso bibioo ni ehiii lɛ baa.

english: Yellow and curled leaves on cassava are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava varieties helps prevent this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ yucca nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black and rot before they are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, high-humidity environments. Pruning thick branches to allow sunlight and air into your farm helps prevent the rot from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Kpojiemɔ ni mli wa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akagbɛ ashwã.

english: What causes my plantain leaves to turn brown and dry out early?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi oya?

english: Early drying of plantain leaves is often caused by Black Sigatoka, a fungal disease favored by high rainfall and humidity. Cutting off affected leaves and maintaining proper plant spacing helps keep the farm healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Black Sigatoka, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ plantain baai lɛ agbiɔ oya lɛ baa. Kɛ́ afo baai ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ, ni akwɛ koni tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: When is the best time for me to start planting maize in southern Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ?

english: In southern Ghana, planting typically starts with the major rainy season around March or April, and the minor season around August or September. Planting right after the first steady rains ensures good germination.
ga: southern ghana Bei pii lɛ, dumɔ jeɔ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli yɛ March loo April he. ni be ni ji enyɔ lɛ ji aaafee August loo September. Kɛ́ adu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil lacks steady moisture. Watering your plants regularly and providing light shade during very hot afternoons helps fruit set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa ni aha lɛ hulutsoo yɛ shwane mli ni edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: How can I know if my farmland needs extra fertilizer before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ he miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi awo mli dani madu nii?

english: If your previous crops grew slowly, had pale yellowish leaves, or yielded poorly, your soil is likely low on essential nutrients. A simple soil test or consulting an extension officer can confirm what nutrients are missing.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ dara blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. loo ekɛ yibii ni ehiii baa Ekolɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo Loo kɛ extension nitsulɔi lɛ agba sane baanyɛ ama nɔ mi akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni elaaje lɛ.

english: Why is it harmful for me to plant maize on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or cowpeas restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baafite shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii komɛi be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmãa ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ.

english: How can cover crops help my farm during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Cover crops like mucuna or cowpeas act like a protective blanket over the soil. They trap moisture in the ground, shade out weeds, and add rich organic matter back into the soil when they decompose.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei tamɔ mucilagina loo cowpea tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, amɛhaa jwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛkɛ nibii babaoo ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛfiteɔ lɛ.

english: What is eating small holes in the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Buji bibii ni ayeɔ Mɛni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Small holes in young maize leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworms. Inspecting your field early and applying approved pest control treatments as soon as damage appears saves the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mra. Ni kɛ akɛ tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ tsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni nɔ ko efite lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ahere ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: How does heavy rain in forest areas like the Western Region affect pest and disease growth on my farm?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ hei ni kooi yɔɔ tamɔ Anaigbɛ lɛ saa kooloi kɛ helai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy and continuous rain creates warm, damp conditions that allow fungal diseases and certain pests to multiply rapidly. Good field drainage and proper weed clearing help lower humidity around your crops.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔɔ kɛ fɛ̃i baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi kɛ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yaa hiɛ oya. Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ aba shi.

english: How many cocoa pods can I expect a single healthy tree to produce in a good season?
ga: Pods enyiɛ manyɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ cacao tso kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baawo yɛ be kpakpa mli?

english: A well-managed mature cocoa tree can yield anywhere from 100 to over 200 pods a year if the soil is fertile and you clear weeds and prune regularly.
ga: Cacao tso ni eda ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmeii 100 kɛyashi nɔ ni fe 200 yɛ he fɛɛ he daa afi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse. Ni okɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shi ni ofoɔ tsei lɛ daa.

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing fewer pods than my neighbor's trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo fe mikutsoŋnyo cacao tso lɛ?

english: Yield differences usually come down to crop care; trees give fewer pods if they lack soil nutrients, have too much shade, or suffer from unmanaged pests and diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ yibiiwoo mli lɛ damɔ bɔ ni akwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ ahaa lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baawo ŋmeii fioo kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Shade babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ tsɔ. loo amɛyeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods rot and turn black right on the tree before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miifite ni amɛmiifee ediŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Pods rot on the tree due to fungal diseases like Black Pod, which thrive in wet, overcrowded conditions where air cannot flow through the branches.
ga: Pod fitemɔ yɛ tsei anɔ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ pod diŋ, ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ gbɔmɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ hewɔ. ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ amli lɛ

english: What happens if I delay harvesting my ripe cocoa pods and leave them on the tree?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ be ni mikɛkpaa kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shwie shi ni mishi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree causes them to overripe, decay, or attract pests, meaning the cocoa gets spoiled and lost before you can take it home.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ekwɛ̃ fe nine, ebaagbo, loo ebaagbala kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, kookoo lɛ baafite ni ebaalaaje dani okɛya shia.

english: How does cutting off extra branches help my cocoa trees yield better pods?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi cacao tso lɛ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Pruning lets sunlight and air reach all parts of the tree, which prevents diseases and directs the tree's energy into growing big, healthy pods.
ga: Tso lɛ mlifomɔ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ hei fɛɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai baaa mɔ nɔ, ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: How often should I go to my farm to check on my cocoa crops?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ maya ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni miyakwɛ kookoo tsei lɛ?

english: Visiting your farm at least once or twice a week helps you spot diseases early, clear weeds, and pluck ripe pods before they rot or go missing.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, kɛ́ oya oŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome loo shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni oyoo helai mra, ojie jwɛi lɛ, ni ofolɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ dani amɛgboi loo amɛlaaje.

english: Why do many of my small cocoa pods wither and drop off before growing full size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii So mine lɛ gboɔ ni egbeeɔ shi dani edaa kɛyashɛɔ dalɛ ni sa lɛ he.

english: Young pods drop off due to natural thinning, lack of water or nutrients, or insect damage, which cuts down your total harvest early in the season.
ga: Pods bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ hewɔ. nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo kooloi bibii ni bɛ lɛ fiteɔ Enɛ baaha nibii fɛɛ ni afeɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: How can I stop bush animals and pests from destroying my pods on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi koo mli kooloi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite mi-pods ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Keeping the farm perimeter clean, harvesting ripe pods without delay, and using safe pest control keeps animals like squirrels and insects away from your yield.
ga: Kwɛmɔ hetsemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ nɔ Kpamɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ni okɛ be akafee nɔ ko. Ni kɛ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii akaje onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ ahe.

english: Why is clearing weeds around my cocoa trees so critical for a good harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ he miihia waa kɛha ŋmaa kpakpa.

english: Weeds steal vital water and fertilizers from the soil that your cocoa trees need to form and feed healthy pods.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa o-cacao tsei lɛ koni amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Will applying fertilizer help my old cocoa trees carry more pods again?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Yes, applying the right cocoa fertilizer restores nutrients to the soil, helping older or tired trees produce more flowers and sustain more pods to maturity.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ akɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni egbɔ loo ni efite lɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛkwɛɔ ŋmeii babaoo nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains to protect them, the intense heat scorches their leaves and dries out the soil, causing the young seedlings to turn yellow and die.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ bɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baashã amɛbaai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn dark brown or black and rot during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and dark conditions. Pruning excess branches to let air and sunlight in, along with removing infected pods quickly, stops the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ duŋ shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la abote mli. Kɛfata he lɛ, ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ oya. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Yellowing starting from the leaf tip usually means your soil is short on nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and produce strong ears, so applying NPK fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help correct this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jɛɔ baai lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekɛ toi ni wa aba. No hewɔ lɛ, NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why are my maize crops staying tiny even after I apply fertilizer near those small purple-flowered weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ ji bibioo lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa woɔ mli yɛ jwɛi bibii ni fɔfɔi yɔɔ mli ni ji purple lɛ ahe lɛ? Nomɛi po

english: That weed is likely Striga, also known as witchweed. It is a parasite that attaches directly to the roots of your maize underground and steals the water and nutrients before the crop can use them.
ga: Ekolɛ jwɛi lɛ ji Striga, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ Witchweed. Eji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ ni ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii dani tso lɛ baanyɛ ekɛtsu nii.

english: Cassava roots do not like sitting in waterlogged soil. Excessive water prevents the roots from breathing and encourages fungal diseases in the soil that cause the tubers to decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi sumɔɔɔ ni amɛtaraa shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to catch direct sunlight to feed the underground tuber. Lifting the vines on stakes helps the leaves get maximum sun and good airflow, preventing leaf diseases and giving you much bigger yams.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Wein tsei lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni tsɔɔ mli. Tsi baa helai anaa Ni ehaa bo sweet potatoes ni da fe no kwraa.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that transmit a virus to your tomato plant. As they suck sap from the leaves, they spread the virus, causing leaves to curl and stopping fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai kɛyaa tomato tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Beni amɛnuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ Amɛbaagbɛ hela lɛ amɛshwã. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my pepper plants falling off without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the weather gets extremely hot and dry, or when the plant experiences water stress. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and regular watering helps the flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa. aloo be mli ni tsei kɛ nu he haomɔ kpeɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fũu kɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy wind and rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that struggle to hold heavy bunches in wet, soft soil. Supporting the stems with wooden props (bamboo poles) helps hold the weight when wind blows.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛmɔ fɔfɔi ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne lɛ mli (bamboo tsei) fiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ tsɔne lɛ mli tsiimɔ lɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa.

english: Why did my cowpea plants start flowering early before growing tall, giving me very few beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ? Eshi mi kɛ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Cowpeas often flower early if they face sudden heat stress or drought. The plant panics and tries to make seeds early to survive rather than spending energy on growing foliage and yielding a full harvest.
ga: Cowpeas fɔɔ fɔfɔi oya kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo hulutsoo loo hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ mli. Tso lɛ he feɔ gbeyei ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni efee dumɔwui mra. koni ehi shi Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni ekɛ yibiiwoo ni yeɔ emuu baa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and shriveling under the midday sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings do not have thick leaf cuticles yet and burn under direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or bananas nearby provides shade and keeps the air humid while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ bɛ baai ni mli tse lolo ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains loo banana ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ebaaha hulutsoo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my small cocoa pods turn black and rot while still attached to the tree during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii Mine lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ No kã tso lɛ he lolo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in high humidity and excess shade. Pruning dense branches lets sunlight in and lowers moisture, preventing the fungus from multiplying.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni fa fe nine lɛ mli. Dense pruning haa hulu la boteɔ mli ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi. Koni ŋmeii akafee babaoo

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and turning yellow instead of growing wide and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellow mosaic patterns are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, spread by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings for planting keeps the leaves healthy so the plant can produce big tubers.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ mosaic ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei niji ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ dumɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ baai lɛ koni tsei lɛ anyɛ awo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become soft and rot underground when left in the wet soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Excess water in heavy soil cuts off oxygen to the roots, causing fungal root rot. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps rain drain away easily and keeps the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii mli lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Ehaa ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ hoɔ oya. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni eha yitso lɛ mli egbi ni ehiɛ hewalɛ

english: Why do my plantain trees snap or fall over easily when the bunch of plantains starts growing heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ fãa loo amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and heavy fruit bunches shift their center of gravity. Supporting the main stem with a wooden prop or bamboo stake prevents strong winds from blowing the heavy tree over.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni aduawai akui ni tsii tsakeɔ hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso loo ŋmei tso fiɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekakumɔ tso lɛ.

english: If I plant maize on the exact same piece of land year after year, why do my crops yield less fruit each season?
ga: Kɛji miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the topsoil. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nitrogen into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and skinny without producing big fruit when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii wuji beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves compete fiercely for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough space and light to build strong stems and big fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo tsei ni wa kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and roll up during the hottest part of the afternoon even when the soil isn't completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbiko kwraa po.

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's natural defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, preventing excessive water loss through evaporation during intense heat.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbaa hulu la ni shɛɔ enɔ lɛ shi. Etsiɔ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ naa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than my planted crops immediately after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are native plants adapted to quickly absorb surface nitrogen and water faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early in the season stops them from stealing vital nutrients from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni yɔɔ koo mli lɛ ji tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ ni atsake amɛ koni amɛjie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ nu mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ehaaa amɛju niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ onibii bibii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young crops full of small chewed holes every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai bibii lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? No ji nɔ ni ayeɔ daa leebi?

english: Night-feeding insects like caterpillars and beetles feed on tender leaves while it is cool. Applying natural neem oil spray or inspecting plants early in the morning helps control these pests before they destroy the crop foliage.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yeɔ baai bibii kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ adebɔɔ mli neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo tso lɛ mlikwɛmɔ leebi lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite tso lɛ baai lɛ.

english: Why did my corn crop fail when the rains stopped coming at the usual times?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ?

english: Corn plants need regular water, especially when they are flowering and forming cobs. If dry weather strikes during these critical stages, the plant gets stressed and cannot develop healthy cobs.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmãa tsei daa. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ eewo fɔfɔi ni ekwɛ̃. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ba yɛ haomɔ be mli Tso lɛ haoɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ ŋmei ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba.

english: Why does rain fall on my neighbor's farm while my field nearby remains completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ miinɛ yɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Rain clouds often form in localized patches, meaning they drop water over specific small areas while leaving nearby land dry. It is a natural pattern, even though it creates uneven growing conditions across a community.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ atatui feɔ yɛ hei srɔtoi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛjieɔ nu kɛyaa he bibioo ko. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa hei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Eji adebɔɔ naa nɔ ko. Enɛ ji yɛ dalɛ shihilɛi ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni eba yɛ akutso lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: How can I keep my farm soil moist for my crops when the rains are unreliable?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be mli ni anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ nugbɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: You can cover the ground around your plants with dry grass, straw, or leaves—a method called mulching. This blanket shields the soil from the hot sun and keeps moisture trapped in the ground much longer.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ he ni ebɔle he lɛ atsu nii. Akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, jwɛi loo baai haa tsei ahe, ni eji gbɛ ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching. Kuntu nɛɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ

english: What simple methods can I use to collect and save rainwater on my field for dry days?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii. Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuaa nugbɔ nu naa ni akɛtoɔ miŋmɔji amli kɛha gbii ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: You can dig small trenches or pits across your land to trap runoff water when it rains, or build small earth mounds (bunds) that hold water near your crops' roots instead of letting it run off.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nubu loo bu bibioo ko. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ koni omɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ Aloo ofee gɔŋ bibioo ko (pile) ni kɛ nu toɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha etsɔ mli lɛ

english: Chemical fertilizer is too expensive for me to buy; what simple alternatives can I use on my crops?
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ jara wa tsɔ akɛ mahe. Mibaanyɛ mikɛ gbɛ kroko ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii. Mɛni manyɛ mafee kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: You can use well-rotted animal manure, compost made from decomposed crop waste, or chicken droppings. These natural options enrich the soil, improve its moisture retention, and cost far less than store-bought fertilizers.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo lɛ atsu nii. Akɛ tsei ni egboi ni efite lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. loo tsina ŋmɔtɔ Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii krokomɛi nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ Ni ejara waaa fe ŋmɔtɔ ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer so it is not wasted?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni ekafite?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist, ideally right after a soft rain or just before light rain is expected. If you put it on dry ground, plants cannot soak it up, and heavy downpours will wash it completely away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ enɛ fioo. loo fioo dani nugbɔ lɛ baanɛ Kɛji okɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ nu. ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho fɛɛ kɛya.

english: Why are the leaves on my corn plants turning yellow and failing to grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraaa agbo lɛ?
