english: Yellow leaves usually mean your corn is lacking nitrogen, a key nutrient for green leaves and strong growth. It can also happen when dry soil prevents the plant roots from taking in nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai eŋɔli kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ tsi tso shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farmland needs fertilizer before I start planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: Look at how well weeds or previous crops grew on that field; pale, stunted, or slow-growing plants are a signal that the soil is low on essential food and will need added organic matter or fertilizer.
ga: Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni jwɛi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Tsei ni tsuɔ, ni egbɔjɔ, loo ni edaa blɛoo lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hia lɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe miihia ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he

english: If rain is scarce, should I plant my corn seeds closer together or spread them out?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, ani esa akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe loo mikɛ amɛ agbɛ ashwã?

english: You should give your plants plenty of space. Planting too close forces crops to compete for limited water and soil nutrients, causing all of them to grow weak and produce poor yields during dry spells.
ga: Esa akɛ oha otsei lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi nu kɛ niyenii ni fa fioo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei fɛɛ daaa ni egbɔjɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Which crops can I plant if I am worried that the rains will be weak or unpredictable this season?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ madu kɛji nugbɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ he miihao?

english: Crops like cassava, millet, sorghum, or early-maturing corn varieties survive unpredictable weather best because they either require less water overall or complete their growth cycle before the moisture dries up.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbiɔ nu fioo yɛ fɛɛ mli loo koni amɛgbe amɛdalɛ be lɛ naa dani ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is the plant's main food for green leaf growth. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen deep into the soil away from young roots, so applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps them regain their rich green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji tsei aniyenii titri kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, ni ekɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ teŋ jɛkɛɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná amɛhe ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds cause my maize to grow thin and weak even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-abele lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients out of the soil before your crop can reach them. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks gives your crops full access to food and light so they can grow tall and strong.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni boteɔ mli ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ la kwraa. Koni eha amɛdara ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden stakes next to my yam plants once they start growing vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama mi sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi kɛji ebɔi wain tsei akwɛ̃mɔ pɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible. Staking exposes the leaves to sunlight and air while preventing soil-borne diseases, which helps the plant make more energy to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do small green shoots keep sprouting around the base of my plantain tree, and should I cut them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ No hewɔ lɛ eda kɛbɔle he fɛɛ. Mi plantain shishitoo Ni ani esa akɛ mafo mli?

english: These shoots are called suckers, which are baby plants trying to grow from the main root. If you leave too many, they fight with the parent tree for food and water, resulting in small bunches; you should cut off most suckers, leaving only one or two strong ones to take over after harvest.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ŋmeii, ni ji tsei bibii ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛda kɛjɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli. Kɛji ashi lɛ babaoo Ekɛ tso nyɛ lɛ baawu kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kui bibii. Esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo. Mɔ kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ eshwɛɔ ni baaye nɔ yɛ nikpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does my groundnut plant push its stem branches down into the dirt after the flowers fade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tsiɔ eniji lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni fɔfɔi lɛ efo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants flower above the ground, but after the flower is fertilized, the stem bends down and pushes into the soil because the actual nuts grow and mature underground where it is cool and dark.
ga: Peanut tsei fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi beni awo fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔ sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ shishifã lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejaakɛ anɔkwa ŋmei lɛ daa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ni duŋ yɔɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava stems curling up, turning yellow, and getting small twisted shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Curled and distorted cassava leaves are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a plant virus spread by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-free stem cuttings for planting and removing infected plants early helps keep the disease from spreading across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baa ni ebɔle ehe ni efite lɛ baa. Enɛ ji tso mli hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ tso lɛ yibii ni hela bɛ mli lɛ atsu nii kɛji oodu ni ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my small cocoa pods turn black, shrivel up, and die while still hanging on the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii Mine lɛ tsɔ ediŋŋ, egbo ni egbo lɛ. Ani okɛ ohe ekpɛtɛ tso nine lɛ he lolo?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, damp, and shaded conditions. Pruning extra cocoa branches and clearing thick leaves lets sunlight and wind dry out the farm, stopping the fungus from killing young pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ shade kɛbaa. Cocoa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi kɛ baai ni mli tse lɛ ajiemɔ he miihia. Ebaaha hulu lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ agbi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni ekpaa ŋmeii lɛ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn soft, dark, and rotten before they are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato aduawai ashishi feɔ bɔdɔɔ, ediŋŋ, ni egboɔ dani amɛshwereɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the roots transport calcium from the soil into the developing fruit properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛkɛ calcium lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛyaa aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from heat or drought stress. When temperatures get very high or the soil gets too dry, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and protect itself until water and cooler conditions return.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na hulutsoo loo hɔmɔ he naagba. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi nu kɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba.

english: How can I tell if the leaves dropping off my cassava plants mean the crop is dying or just reacting to the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ yucca tso ko nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miigbo loo eji nɔ ko kɛkɛ ni efee yɛ hɔmɔ ni eba lɛ hewɔ?

english: Cassava naturally drops its lower leaves during the dry season to save water and stay alive while resting. As long as the main stem stays firm and green inside, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he, ni ehiɔ shi be mli ni ejɔɔ ehe lɛ. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ emli lɛ. Tsei lɛ baatswa ni amɛfee baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow even after I spent money to apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ni mifite shika yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant cannot absorb nitrogen properly, often because heavy rains washed the fertilizer away or because the soil was too dry when you applied it. Applying fertilizer at the right moisture level ensures the money you spend turns into green, healthy growth.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nitrogen lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbi loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ beni okɛwo mli lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ hulutsoo be ni sa mli lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many broad leaves but produce very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ, ni ebaa lɛ mli lɛɛɔ, shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen, it spends all its energy growing leaves and stems on top instead of building root tubers underground. Balancing your soil nutrients helps the plant store food where it matters most for your harvest.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootswa shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ niyenii he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtoɔ niyenii yɛ he ni ehe hiaa fe fɛɛ kɛha okpamɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I get a smaller harvest when I plant seeds saved from my last harvest instead of buying certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibiiwoo bibioo nɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo he dumɔwuhi nɛ a wo he odase ɔ.

english: Seeds saved from past harvests lose their vigor over time and can carry diseases from the previous season. Certified seeds are specially selected to resist pests, handle weather stress, and give you high yields that justify the purchase cost.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ aba. Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai. Ni aaakpee kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he haomɔi anaa ni akɛ sɛɛnamɔi babaoo ni kɛ shika ni akɛheɔ lɛ kpãa gbee aha.

english: Why do some crop varieties yield more food than local varieties even when planted on the same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi woɔ niyenii babaoo fe tsei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ po lɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties are bred to convert soil nutrients and water into fruits or grains much more efficiently than older local varieties. Investing in high-yielding seed varieties allows you to get more food out of the exact same size of land.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛtsake shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ amɛfee aduawai loo dumɔwui jogbaŋŋ fe maŋbii srɔtoi ni etsɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ shika wo dumɔwui srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa onine shɛɔ niyenii babaoo nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the afternoon heat even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, pepper plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can draw water from the soil, causing them to wilt to protect themselves. As temperatures drop in the evening, the plant naturally regains its upright shape.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgbiɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa su ni ja.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without producing any tomatoes when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the delicate pollen inside tomato blossoms, which prevents fruit from forming. When temperatures rise too high, the plant sheds its flowers to conserve energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haaa yibii aba. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need plantains planted right next to them in their first year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu kookoo tsei bibii yɛ amɛmasɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full sun. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as living umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool and retaining soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to endure direct heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my plantain trees take longer to bear fruit when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plantain suckers are crowded together, their roots fight with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures every stem receives enough food to mature quickly and produce heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ plantain tsei lɛ efee ekome yɛ kui amli lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifã fɛɛ shishifã naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ oya ni ekɛ ŋmeii babaoo aba.

english: Why are worms eating my maize plants from the inside of the leaves early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Pests like the fall armyworm hide inside the central leaf funnel of young maize because the hidden leaves are soft and nutritious. Treating the plants early stops the worms before they destroy the growing point of the stalk.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmeii abifao lɛ teŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpa. Tsei ahe nitsumɔ mra Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ kpaa dani amɛfiteɔ he ni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Yam tubers rot when excess water collects in heavy soil around the roots, starving the tubers of air and encouraging fungal growth. Planting yams on high mounds helps water drain away easily so the tubers stay healthy until harvest time.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine lɛ bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ. Kɛ́ adu sweet potato yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Koni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell the male flowers from the female flowers on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male fɔfɔi hii kɛ fɔfɔi yei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Male flower parts produce the powdery dust called pollen, while female parts usually have a small swollen base that turns into the fruit. Identifying the male parts lets you know where to collect pollen to fertilize the female parts.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ fã ni ji nuu lɛ jieɔ sũ ni atsɛɔ lɛ pollen. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ fã ni ji yoo lɛ yɛ shishigbɛ bibioo ko ni efuu. ni bafee nɔ ni jɛ mli ba lɛ Kɛ́ oyɔse nuu lɛ fãi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ole he ni obaabua pollen naa yɛ koni okɛwo yoo lɛ fãi lɛ amli.

english: What is the main job of the male part of a crop flower?
ga: Mɛni ji tso fɔfɔi lɛ fã ni ji nuu lɛ nitsumɔ titri?

english: The male part's main job is to produce and release pollen. Without this pollen reaching the female flower part, the plant cannot form seeds or mature fruit.
ga: Nitsumɔ titri ni nuu lɛ tsuɔ ji ni efee pollen ni ejie. Kɛji akɛ pollen ko shɛɛɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fã ni ji yoo lɛ he lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo dumɔwui loo aduawai ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why do my crop flowers drop off without ever producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers often fall off when pollination fails. If wind or insects do not transfer pollen from the male parts to the female parts, the flower dies off without forming fruit, which is why hand pollination is sometimes needed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi bibii kɛ pollen kɛjɛɛɛ nuu lɛ mli kɛtee yoo lɛ mli lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbo ni ewooo yibii. No hewɔ ni bei komɛi lɛ ehe hiaa ni akɛ niji afee pollination lɛ.

english: Why would I need to pollinate my crop flowers by hand instead of leaving it to nature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ miniji awo fɔfɔi ni midu lɛ amli lɛ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛfee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ gbɛ lɛ?

english: Natural pollinators like bees might not always be present on your farm. Hand pollination guarantees that pollen reaches the right flower parts, greatly increasing the amount of fruit your crops produce.
ga: Ekolɛ jeee be fɛɛ be adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa ŋmeii, tamɔ ŋmeii, yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ fã ni sa lɛ he. Enɛ baaha yibii ni otsei lɛ woɔ lɛ aya hiɛ waa.

english: How do I safely collect pollen from my crop flowers to help them bear fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabua pollen ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ naa shweshweeshwe koni eye ebua lɛ ni ewo yibii?

english: You gently remove or tap the pollen out from the male parts of mature, open flowers. That collected pollen is then transferred directly onto the female flower parts to fertilize them.
ga: Okɛ blɛoo loo otswaa pollen kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi ni eda lɛ fã ni ji nuu lɛ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛ pollen ni abua naa lɛ yaa fɔfɔi yoo lɛ fãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛwo fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ mli.

english: Is it safe to gently force open a flower to collect pollen from inside?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oooŋɔ lɛ blɛoo? Gbelemɔ fɔfɔii koni obua pollen kɛjɛ mli?

english: Yes, for certain crops, farmers carefully open mature male flower parts early in the day to collect pollen before wind, heat, or rain washes it away.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ahe lɛ, okwaafoi jieɔ fɔfɔi hii ni eda lɛ jogbaŋŋ leebi maŋkpa koni amɛbua fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ anaa dani kɔɔyɔɔ, latsaa loo nugbɔ lɛ kɛyaa.

english: Why do extension officers recommend working on crop flowers very early in the morning around 6:00 AM?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nitsumɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu fɔfɔi tsei leebi maŋkpa, aaafee ŋmɛji 6:00 a.m. lɛ?

english: Early morning is when pollen is freshest, stickiest, and most active. The temperatures are cool, which keeps the delicate flower parts from drying out during pollination.
ga: Leebi ji be mli ni pollen lɛ feɔ ehee, ekpɛɔ ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ. He lɛ mli dɔlɛ baafee fɛ̃i. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahe nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ akagbi yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Does afternoon sun and heat affect how well my crop flowers set fruit?
ga: Ani shwane hulu kɛ dɔlɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii fɔfɔi ahe?

english: Yes, high afternoon heat can dry out pollen grains and cause delicate flower parts to wither. Doing important flower work like pollen collection early in the cool morning gives you much better results.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, shwane mli la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni eha fɔfɔi lɛ ahe nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbo. Fɔfɔi ahe nitsumɔ ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ pollen ni ooobua naa yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ baaha oná yibii kpakpai babaoo.

english: How do I know when a crop flower is ready for pollination?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni fɔfɔi lɛ efee klalo kɛha pollination?

english: A flower is ready when it fully blooms and opens up. Blooming is the plant's signal that the male part is releasing active pollen and the female part is ready to receive it.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ efee klalo kɛji amɛfɔ̃ kwraa ni amɛgbele amɛhe. Fofɔi lɛ ji okadi kɛha tso lɛ akɛ nuu lɛ fã lɛ miijie pollen ni tsuɔ nii ni yoo lɛ fã lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaaŋɔ.

english: Why does my crop stay in the flowering stage for several months before finishing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ fɔfɔii amli nyɔji babaoo dani aduɔ lɛ?

english: Some crops have extended flowering cycles where male parts continuously produce pollen over several months. This long blooming period gives farmers a continuous window to pollinate and harvest throughout the season.
ga: Tsei komɛi yɛ fɔfɔi be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Hii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ pollen nyɔji babaoo. Nɛkɛ fɔfɔi be kakadaŋŋ nɛɛ haa okwaafoi lɛ náa be ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni amɛkpaa nii yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: This usually happens when your soil runs out of nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe nɔ. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha shweremɔ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or cowpeas makes the soil richer for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas have tiny bumps on their roots that trap natural nitrogen from the air and store it in the earth, providing free soil food for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, emɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko aha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava leaves droop and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry weather to save water. It is the plant's natural way of going to sleep to survive drought until the rains come back.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ, ni egbiɔ koni akɛbu nu he. Eji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ewɔɔ koni ehi wala mli yɛ hɔmɔ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do cocoa flowers grow directly on the thick main stem of the tree instead of on the small branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ fã titri ni mli tse lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe niji bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods grow very heavy as they ripen. The tree produces flowers on its main trunk so that the strong wood can support the weight of the mature pods without breaking.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsii kɛji amɛkwɛ̃. Tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tso ni wa lɛ anyɛ akwɛ ŋmeii ni edara lɛ amli tsiimɔ nɔ ni efoŋ.

english: Why do my pigeon pea plants stay green during the drought while my other crops wither and dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi pigeon pea tsei lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli yɛ fɛ̃i be mli yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Pigeon pea plants grow very long taproots that reach deep underground to pull up moisture from far below where shallow roots cannot reach.
ga: Pigeon pea tsei lɛ daa shishifãi kakadaŋŋ agboi ni yaa shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ koni amɛgbala nu kɛjɛ shishigbɛ he ni shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking holds the leaves up towards the sun so you get much larger yams at harvest.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking hiɛɔ baai lɛ ni kwɛɔ hulu lɛ hiɛ bɔni afee ni oná sweet potato ni da kwraa kɛji akpa.

english: Why should I cut away the small shoot suckers growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ

english: Having too many suckers causes them to fight with the main tree for food and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, allowing the main tree to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ mli ŋmeii babaoo haa ehe bahiaa ni amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ awuu koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa, ni no haa tso titri lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plant gets irregular water. Stress from heat stops the flower from forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ nu jogbaŋŋ. Dɔlɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo yibii.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the underside of new leaves. Treating the plant stops the insects and lets leaves grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai heei lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okwɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha kooloi bibii lɛ akpa nitsumɔ, ni ebaaha baai lɛ adara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does my swamp rice grow well in water while my maize plants rot and die if water sits on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-swamp rice lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu mli yɛ be mli ni mi-corn tsei lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice stems have internal air tubes that carry oxygen down to roots underwater, whereas maize roots have no air tubes and drown if left submerged in standing water.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔnei ni yɔɔ mli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shi kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu shishi. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛ, ni kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ, amɛbaagboi.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate intense direct sunlight. They need shade trees or temporary food crops like plantain to protect them from heat stress and retain soil moisture while their root systems develop.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Does it matter which direction I insert cassava stem cuttings into the ground?
ga: Ani ehe hiaa ni akɛ ŋmei niji awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, direction matters. The buds or nodes on the stem cutting must point upward toward the sky. Planting stems upside down causes shoots to grow weakly and significantly reduces root yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, gbɛtsɔɔmɔ he miihia. Esa akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tsei niji ni afo lɛ anɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Tso lɛ tsei ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ baaha tsei lɛ adalɛ ehiii ni ebaa shishifãi lɛ ayibii shi kwraa.

english: How do I choose the right plantain suckers to transplant onto my new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni sa ni mikɛbaawo miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: Select 'sword suckers,' which have a thick base and narrow, spear-like leaves. These grow faster and produce larger bunches compared to 'water suckers,' which have thin stems and broad leaves.
ga: Halamɔ ‘Sword Bud’, ni yɔɔ shishi ni mli tse kɛ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ. Enɛɛmɛi daa oya ni amɛwoɔ panicles wuji kɛ akɛto ‘suckers’ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahe.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and saw-dust-like dirt inside the top part of the plant?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ tso lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the center of the maize plant. Applying recommended biological or chemical controls early in the morning or late evening helps protect your crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛbuɔ he lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp conditions. Pruning extra shade tree branches to let sunlight and air flow through your farm helps prevent it.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ babaoo lɛ ni oookpa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants turn yellow and curl upward when insects are flying around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛji kooloi bibii fã kɛbɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Insects like whiteflies spread viruses to tomatoes while feeding on them. These viruses cause leaf curl and yellowing, which stops the plant from bearing healthy fruit.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ helai kɛyaa tomato nɔ beni amɛyeɔ lɛ. Nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ awo yibii kpakpai.

english: A V-shaped yellowing starting from the tip of lower maize leaves is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or NPK helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: V-shaped yellowing ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo tamɔ urea loo NPK ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yaa hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas naturally capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This enriches the soil and helps feeder crops like maize grow bigger cobs without using as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni eyeɔ ebuaa niyenii ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii wuji ni amɛkɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for growing tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to more light and protecting the vine from soil-borne rot.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa la babaoo baa, ni ebuɔ wain tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop in the hot afternoon even when the soil is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During peak heat, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it from the soil. The leaves wilt temporarily to preserve moisture and usually recover by evening.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli waa lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he, ni bei pii lɛ, amɛhe jɔɔ amɛ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the corn cobs are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth, or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving no single plant with enough strength to make large cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does my land produce less harvest every season when I plant maize on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmaa bibioo daa afi be mli ni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop needs from the soil; rotating with crops like beans or groundnuts helps restore soil fertility.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii Yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young crop seeds fail to grow when I plant them right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui bibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by hot dry days that heat up the topsoil and dry out seed sprouts before their roots can reach deeper soil moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbi ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔɔ ni egbiɔ dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop all their flowers without forming any cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ fɛɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ni amɛjieee cocoa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they lack tiny pollinating insects like midges, or when the plant experiences extreme heat stress and poor soil nutrition.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ midges bɛ, loo kɛji tsei lɛ naa haomɔ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni ehiii lɛ mli.

english: Why are my cassava roots turning soft and rotting underground when heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much standing water in the soil deprives root crops of oxygen and encourages fungal diseases that cause the tubers to rot.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ babaoo lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa tsei shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ, ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ tuber rot baa lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the inner leaves of my young corn plants overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ye mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a fast-moving pest that feeds on the central leaves of young corn plants during cool hours and nighttime.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yaa oya ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ kɛ gbɛkɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die if I cut down all the large trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mifo tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight; shade trees protect them from heat damage and keep moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo fiteɔ nii, ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa.

english: Why does my harvested maize develop black mold inside the bag after I store it for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ diŋŋ ba kotokui lɛ amli beni mikɛto otsii fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If maize is put into bags before it is completely dry, trapped moisture creates a damp environment where mold rapidly grows and ruins the grain.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ wo kotoku lɛ mli dani egbi kwraa lɛ, Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa. Fuji lɛ daa oya ni efiteɔ omɔ dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and soft while still growing on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo yɛ be mli ni edaa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This issue, called blossom-end rot, happens when tomato plants cannot draw enough calcium from the soil, often due to irregular watering.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize crops turning yellow from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting at the tip and moving down the middle usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize plants need nitrogen to stay green and grow strong, so adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help them recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ kɛyaa teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ amɛ.

english: Why should I wait for fresh chicken manure to dry and rot before putting it around my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni tsina ŋmɔtɔ hee lɛ agbi ni egbo dani madu yɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Fresh chicken manure is too strong and 'hot' because it contains high levels of ammonia and salts that can burn crop roots. Letting it rot and turn into dark compost breaks down these harsh chemicals into safe, soft nutrients that feed the plant gently.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni afee ehee lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ‘edɔ’ ejaakɛ ammonia kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi lɛ fa babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni egbo ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ, efiteɔ tsofai ni mli wa nɛɛ ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni haa tso lɛ niyenii blɛoo.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive harsh, direct sunlight because intense heat burns their tender leaves and dries out their roots. Leaving tall trees or planting plantains nearby creates a protective shade canopy that keeps the farm moist and cool until the cocoa gets older.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni ashiɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Enɛ haa hulutsoo ni haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: What causes tiny holes in my maize leaves and small greenish waste packed inside the shoot?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ jwɛi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni akɛwo ŋmãa lɛ mli shiŋŋ lɛ mli

english: This damage comes from the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a pest that hides inside the central growing point of maize plants to feed. Farmers usually manage this by checking fields early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts into the central leaves.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ jɛɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni teɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛye nii lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi tsuɔ enɛ he nii kɛtsɔ jɛmɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ mra lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ awo baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: How should I position a cassava stem stick in the soil when planting so it sprouts properly?
ga: Kɛ́ adu lɛ, te esa akɛ akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛŋŋ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cassava stems should be planted slanting at an angle with the tiny buds on the stem pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant the stick upside down, the shoots will struggle to emerge, resulting in poor root and tuber growth.
ga: Esa akɛ adu fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ cassava tsei lɛ amli. yɛ tso lɛ yitso lɛ nɔ ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu tsei niji ni okɛ ohiɛ fɔ shi lɛ, ebaawa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ baadara, ni no baaha shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Which type of young plantain shoot is best for me to dig up and plant on new land?
ga: Mɛɛ dumɔwui bibii ni sa akɛ mafo ni madu yɛ he ko hee?

english: You should pick 'sword suckers', which are young shoots with narrow, sword-like leaves and a strong, wide base. These suckers grow faster and produce larger, healthier plantain bunches than 'water suckers' that have wide, broad leaves early on.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala ‘klante tso’, ni ji tso bibioo ko ni baai lɛ mli tse ni tamɔ klante, ni eshishigbɛ lɛ mli kwɔ ni eyɛ shiŋŋ. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ jwɛi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe mra be mli tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from the base of my cassava plants during the first three months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: During the first three months, young cassava grows slowly and cannot outcompete weeds for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. Keeping the farm clean early allows the cassava roots to establish strongly before the crop canopy closes.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ mli lɛ, Young cassava lɛ daa blɛoo ni enyɛŋ ekɛ jwɛi ni jɛɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Ni oooha ŋmɔ lɛ mli atse kɛjɛ shishijee lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ waa dani ŋmei lɛ ŋmɛɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Lifting yam leaves off the ground with wooden stakes allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food. This extra food travels down into the ground to produce larger, heavier yam tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tso wo sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa baa lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aba. Niyenii krɛdɛɛ nɛɛ fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ aba.

english: Is it better for me to water my tomato crop early in the morning or during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the moisture sinks deep into the soil before the heat of the sun evaporates it. Watering in the hot afternoon can stress the leaves and cause quick water loss from the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi koni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani hulu lɛ mli dɔlɛ lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ afee mlɛo ni eha nu lɛ afite oya kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn dark brown and sunken before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efoɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant or irregular soil moisture while the fruit is forming. Keeping the soil consistently damp and adding wood ash or agricultural lime to the soil helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa be mli ni aduawai lɛ miikwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ tso sũ loo okwaayeli mli sũ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why should I start my pepper seeds in a nursery bed before moving them to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu pepper dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani mikɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seeds are very delicate. Starting them in a nursery allows you to protect them from strong heat, heavy rains, and pests while they are small, making sure you only transplant the strongest, healthiest seedlings to your main field.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ waaa kwraa. Kɛ́ oje tsei shishi yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ obuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ dumɔwui ni he wa fe fɛɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ yaa oŋmɔ titri lɛ mli.

english: How do I know when my vegetable seedlings are strong enough to be transplanted to the main field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mawo dumɔwui wuji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Seedlings are generally ready for transplanting when they have grown 4 to 6 true leaves and stem sturdy enough to handle, usually around 3 to 5 weeks after planting depending on the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha adumɔ kɛji amɛyɛ baai diɛŋtsɛ 4 kɛyashi 6 kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu amɛ, bei pii lɛ, otsii 3 kɛyashi 5 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ

english: If I plant my maize very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my plot?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe waa Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too close forces crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes thin stems and tiny ears of corn. Giving each plant proper space ensures larger, healthier cobs and a better total yield.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii baa. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmei lɛ adara. Ehi kɛha hewalɛnamɔ kɛ nitsumɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I clear all the big shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ cacao tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, continuous sunlight. Shade trees act like living umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist and protecting young cocoa leaves from scorching until the plants mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni yaa nɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. ni ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe koni amɛkashã kɛyashi tso lɛ daa.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a warning sign that the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that water is sitting around the roots for too long and suffocating them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji kɔkɔbɔɔ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ, ni eha amɛmiigbɔjɔ.

english: Why is it harmful to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows pests and diseases targeting that crop to build up in the soil. Rotating with crops like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei Yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl up and droop in the hot afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ shwane mli latsaa be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves roll up during peak sun to preserve moisture and prevent water loss. If they bounce back by evening, the plant is self-regulating; if they stay limp, the soil needs urgent watering.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛtsi nu ni elaaje lɛ naa. Kɛ amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba gbɛkɛ mli lɛ Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiye ehe nɔ. Kɛji oogbɔjɔ lolo lɛ Ehe miihia ni awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu oya.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal nutrients and water from the main mother plant. Pruning extra suckers leaves more energy for the main plant to produce a much larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ plantains ni dara ni tsii babaoo.

english: Can I plant cowpeas between my maize rows, or will they damage my maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ? Aloo ebaafite mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and maize work well together. Cowpeas cover the soil to suppress weeds, keep moisture in, and add nitrogen into the soil, which actually nourishes the maize.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmãa tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Akɛ sũ woɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmeii amli koni egbe jwɛi lɛ, ni eha sũ lɛ mli ahi shi, ni ekɛ nitrogen awo sũ lɛ mli. ni ji ŋmãa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ diɛŋtsɛ

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly when the plants experience severe heat stress, dry soil, or damage from tiny pests like thrips before pollination occurs.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi bei pii kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nɔ ni jɛɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips mli fitemɔ mli, dani pollination baa.

english: I have a small empty piece of land behind my house, what is the best food crop I can plant there to feed my family?
ga: Miyɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko yɛ mishia lɛ sɛɛ. Mɛni ji niyenii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ madu koni mikɛha miweku lɛ niyenii?

english: Vegetables like pepper, garden eggs, and okra grow fast in small backyard spaces and give your family fresh ingredients daily while saving you market money.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ ŋmeii, abɔɔ mli ŋmeii, kɛ okra kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ sɛɛgbɛ he bibioo ko. ni okɛ nibii heei ni akɛwoɔ niyenii mli lɛ aha oweku lɛ daa gbi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, okɛ shika toɔ jarayeli he.

english: Why do some farmers clear and burn all the grass on their land before planting, while others leave it to rot on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shwieɔ jwɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni amɛshãa dani amɛduɔ nii lɛ? yɛ be mli ni mɛi komɛi haa egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Burning clears land quickly, but leaving cut weeds and grass on the soil acts like food for the land, keeping it moist, cool, and rich in plant nutrients.
ga: Shãa baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ oya. Shi jwɛi ni ashiɔ kɛ jwɛi ni afolɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsei amli niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli.

english: How do I know the exact right time to start planting my maize when the rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ?

english: Do not plant after the very first rain because the soil underneath is still dry. Wait until you get two or three heavy rains that soak deep into the soil so your seeds do not dry up.
ga: Kaadu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi lolo. Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ baaha odumɔwui lɛ akagbi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds very close to each other so that I can get more food from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops grow too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin, weak plants that produce small yields.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo pɛ baa.

english: Yes, planting them together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested early, leaving space and light for the slower-growing cassava to expand later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa lɛ mra. Shi he ko kɛ la koni ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ agbɛ ashwã sɛɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks essential plant food like nitrogen, or the crop is stressed from long dry weather and needs manure or moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe nibii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ egba tso lɛ naa ni ehe miihia ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔtɔ awo mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without growing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi ni eduuu pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the weather gets extremely hot, when the soil is too dry, or when helpful insects like bees are not visiting to help the flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ ni baaye abua fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt in the afternoon heat even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In hot sun, tomato leaves lose water faster than roots can drink it up. Covering the soil around the stem with dry grass keeps the roots cool and moist all day.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why are dark spots appearing on the leaves of my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji miije kpo yɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Dark spots are usually caused by tiny fungal diseases that spread quickly when plant leaves stay wet for too long or are crowded together without enough air passing through.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii baa. No gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ tsei ahe baai lɛ ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ loo amɛbua amɛhe naa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa hoɔ kɛtsɔɔɔ amɛmli.

english: Why do small insects attack and destroy my stored maize grains a few weeks after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Insects thrive when maize is stored with hidden moisture inside. Drying your maize thoroughly under the sun until the grains are very hard keeps insects away during storage.
ga: Kplukai shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa to mli ni ŋmɔtɔ etee mli. Abɛi ni agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ mli wa waa koni ŋmeii akabote mli yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do farmers plant many cocoa seedlings close together initially if some will be cut down later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi du kookoo dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ shishijee mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ abaafolɔ fãi komɛi amli yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Planting extra seedlings at the start ensures that even if some die from harsh weather or pests, your land remains fully covered. As the surviving trees grow larger and crowd each other, cutting down the weaker ones gives the best trees enough space, light, and nutrients to produce maximum pods.
ga: Dumɔwui krokomɛi ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ shishijee lɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ ekomɛi po baagboi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahewɔ. Shi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛmɔ shi lolo. Beni tsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ daraa ni amɛbua amɛhe naa lɛ Tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ náa he ko, la, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛfee ŋmeii babaoo.

english: What happens to my cocoa crop if I leave too many trees growing close together without cutting any out?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi tsei lɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni mifolɔɔɔ amɛ?

english: When trees are overcrowded, they fight for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. The lack of air movement and excess shade create a damp environment that encourages diseases to spread quickly, resulting in smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni woɔ helai ahe hewalɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are competing too much with each other for space and food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ cacao tsei miitswa amɛhe fe nine koni amɛná he ko kɛ niyenii?

english: If your trees grow tall and skinny with leaves only at the very top, or if they produce few pods despite looking green, they are likely overcrowded and fighting for light and nutrients.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ da ni efee bibioo ni baai pɛ yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ Aloo kɛji tso lɛ bɛ ŋmeii fioo komɛi eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ Etamɔ nɔ ni tsei lɛ baafee ŋmeii tsɔ ni amɛbaafee akaŋ kɛha la kɛ niyenii.

english: That rot is known as black pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, damp, and overly shady conditions. Rain droplets splash the fungal spores from the soil or infected branches onto healthy pods, causing them to turn black and spoil.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai fitemɔ lɛ akɛ black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, hulutsoo, kɛ hulutsoo fe nine lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ shwieɔ fungal spores kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa pods ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Does clearing out some trees and branches help reduce diseases on my farm?
ga: Ani tsei kɛ tsei aniji ni ajieɔ lɛ haa helai baa shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, pruning extra branches and cutting down excess trees allows sunlight to reach the pods and lets air breeze through the farm. Sunshine and good airflow dry up moisture quickly, preventing diseases like black pod from growing.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia ni afo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ahe nibii krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni hulu la ashɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi oya. Tsi helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Is a cocoa tree dying from black pod disease the same as a tree that is just getting too old?
ga: Ani kookoo tso ni black pod hela gbeɔ lɛ kɛ tso ni egbɔ tsɔ lɛ yeɔ egbɔ?

english: No, a tree with black pod disease has a fungus that rots the pods and can spread to nearby healthy trees. An old tree is simply aging naturally and slowing down its pod production over time without spreading an infection.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni yɔɔ black pod hela lɛ hiɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa pod lɛ fiteɔ, ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli. Tsei ni egbɔ lɛ daraa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛhaa amɛ pod lɛ feɔ mlɛo yɛ be ni sa mli ni amɛgbɛɛɛ hela amɛshwãa.

english: Why does cocoa grow so well in the forest regions but struggle in drier places like Accra?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni kooi yɔɔ lɛ? Shi amɛkɛ naagbai kpeɔ yɛ hei ni nu egbi tamɔ Accra.

english: Cocoa trees need deep, moisture-retaining soil, high humidity, and regular rainfall to produce good yields. Drier coastal places like Accra lack the constant rain and rich forest climate that cocoa needs to survive long-term.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli lɛ he miihia kokoo tsei. high humidity Ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa koni aná yibii kpakpai. Ŋshɔnaa hei ni egbi tamɔ Accra lɛ bɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo kɛ koo mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni he hiaa kookoo koni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How do I know when it is time to remove old cocoa trees completely and plant new ones?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ majie kookoo tso momo lɛ kwraa ni madu ehee?

english: When cocoa trees become very old, stop producing good numbers of pods, or show severe signs of declining health despite proper care, it is best to cut them down and replant fresh seedlings to keep your farm profitable.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ egbɔ waa lɛ Kpaa ŋmeii babaoo ni hi loo ejieɔ okadii ni hiɛdɔɔ yɔɔ mli ni tsɔɔ akɛ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ miiba shi yɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni ofolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ni odu dumɔwui heei koni oŋmɔ lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Why do agriculture extension officers visit my farm to check how many trees I have planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ baa miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛbakwɛ tsei enyiɛ midu lɛ?

english: Extension officers inspect farms to guide you on proper tree spacing and planting techniques. They check density to ensure your farm will yield the maximum amount of cocoa and to advise you on preventing disease outbreaks.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baakwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛwo bo ŋaa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ lɛ he. Amɛkwɛɔ bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ fa ha lɛ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ oŋmɔ lɛ miiwo kookoo babaoo ni amɛhaa ŋaawoo yɛ bɔ ni ooofee atsĩ helai ni baa lɛ naa lɛ he.

english: What should I do when extension officers recommend cutting down some of my planted trees?
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ afo tsei ni adu lɛ ekomɛi lɛ, mɛni esa akɛ ofee?

english: You should listen to their guidance on which trees to thin out. Removing overcrowded or weak trees allows the healthiest remaining trees to expand their branches, receive more light, and bear significantly more fruit.
ga: Esa akɛ obo amɛ ŋaawoo ni kɔɔ tsei ni esa akɛ okɛfee bibioo lɛ he lɛ toi. Tsei ni egbɔ fe nine loo ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha tsei ni eshwɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ agbɛ amɛniji lɛ amli alɛɛ. na la babaoo ni ewo yibii babaoo ni sa kadimɔ waa

english: I farm in northern Ghana; which legume crop grows best in our dry savannah weather?
ga: Mitsuɔ ŋmɔ yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ. Mɛɛ ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ wɔ savannah kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli egbi lɛ mli?

english: Soybeans are well-suited savannah crops that thrive in the soil and climate conditions of the northern sector of Ghana.
ga: Soybean ji savannah ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni shwereɔ yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli.

english: How long does it usually take for a soybean crop to mature before harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ bei pii lɛ eheɔ dani soybean lɛ shwereɔ dani akpaa?

english: Soybeans generally take between 110 to 115 days to reach full maturity and be ready for harvesting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, soybeans heɔ gbii 110 kɛyashi 115 dani ekwɛ̃ɔ ni efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: At what point in the farming calendar cycle should I expect to harvest my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be mli yɛ okwaayeli kalanda lɛ nɔ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Depending on your planting schedule, crop harvesting typically takes place around the 8th month of the agricultural season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ yaa nɔ yɛ okwaayeli be lɛ nyɔŋ ni ji 8 lɛ mli. Edamɔ be ni okɛbaadu nii lɛ nɔ.

english: I heard about a crop called Gyangu; what type of plant is it?
ga: Minu ŋmɔshi nibii ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ kyanggu lɛ he. Mɛɛ tso henɔ ji lɛ?

english: Gyangu is a popular variety of soybean that grows well in savannah regions and takes about 110 to 115 days to mature.
ga: Gyangu ji soybean tso ko ni ale waa ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Savannah kpokpaa lɛ nɔ. ni eheɔ aaafee gbii 110 kɛyashi 115 dani eshɛɔ.

english: There are many soybean seeds available; which variety should I plant to make sure buyers will purchase my harvest?
ga: Soybean dumɔwui babaoo yɛ. Mɛɛ srɔtoi esa akɛ makwɛ koni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ ahe minibii lɛ?

english: It is best to plant market-promoted varieties like Gyangu, as they are well-known and preferred by trade buyers and processors.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu ŋmeii srɔtoi ni jara nɔ woɔ he hewalɛ tamɔ Gyangu, ejaakɛ mɛi ni heɔ nibii kɛ mɛi ni feɔ nibii lɛ le enɛɛmɛi ni amɛsumɔɔ.

english: If I produce soybeans on my farm, are there local industries that will buy them?
ga: Kɛji mifee soybeans yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani maŋ lɛ mli nitsumɔhe ko yɛ ni baahe kɛjɛ mli?

english: Yes, soybean production is in high demand because it directly supports up to four major industrial sectors, including food processing and animal feed.
ga: Hɛɛ, soybean feemɔ he miihia waa ejaakɛ eyeɔ ebuaa nitsumɔhei wuji ejwɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Niyenii kɛ kooloi aniyenii ahe nitsumɔ fata he.

english: Why do most farmers in the northern sector choose to cultivate soybeans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooyigbɛ okwaafoi babaoo halaa akɛ amɛbaadu soybean lɛ?

english: Soybean is a savannah crop naturally adapted to northern growing conditions, making it reliable for farmers in that region.
ga: Soybean ji tso ko ni yɔɔ ŋa nɔ ni ekɛ ehe ebɔ kooyigbɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa lɛ ahe. Ehaa okwaafoi ni yɔɔ nakai kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ mɛi ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ

english: Does choosing a specific variety of soybean really affect my success as a farmer?
ga: Soybeans henɔi srɔtoi ni mihalaa Ani enaa omanye ni miyeɔ akɛ okwaafonyo lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, selecting a promoted, market-popular variety ensures better buyer demand and reliable maturity timing compared to unknown seeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui srɔtoi ni awo he hewalɛ ni ehe gbɛi yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ahalamɔ haa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ be ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni aleee lɛ ahe.

english: How many months of rainfall and field management do I need to plan for when growing soybeans?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ acreage he gbɛjianɔtoo he miihia ni mato he gbɛjianɔ koni madu soybeans?

english: You need to plan for roughly 3.5 to 4 months (110 to 115 days) of active growth before the soybeans are ready for harvesting.
ga: Esa akɛ oto gbɛjianɔ kɛha aaafee nyɔji 3.5 kɛyashi 4 (gbii 110 kɛyashi 115) ni shwereɔ waa dani soybeans lɛ afee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why is the extension service encouraging us to plant soybeans instead of relying only on traditional grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsumɔi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ woɔ wɔ hewalɛ koni wɔdu soybeans moŋ fe ni wɔkɛ wɔhe aaafɔ̃ blema dumɔwui anɔ lɛ?

english: Soybeans offer strong market opportunities, support multiple manufacturing industries, and are highly suited to dry savannah farmlands.
ga: Soy haa jarayeli hegbɛ ni mli wa. Efiɔ nibii afeemɔŋ nitsumɔhei srɔtoi asɛɛ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ titri kɛha savannah okwaayeli hei ni egbi lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and drop off when the long dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during dry spells to save water and keep from drying out completely. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout new green leaves and continue growing normally.
ga: Yucca shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ekɛtsi enaa koni ekagbi kwraa. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni eŋɔli ni eda bɔ ni sa.

english: Staking lifts the vine leaves up into the sunlight so they can make more food, while keeping them off the damp soil where fungal diseases can rot the plant, helping you get much larger tubers.
ga: Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la mli koni enyɛ ehoo nii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ akabɔ he, he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ aha tso lɛ agbo lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Ehaa onáa yitso ni da kwraa.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, why do I end up with small ears instead of big cobs?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Mɛni hewɔ miyɛ toi bibii yɛ ŋmãa wuji najiaŋ lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition weakens every plant, so none of them get enough energy to grow full, large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso gbɔjɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso ko bɛ ni nine shɛɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii wuji lɛ akwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Why should I cut away the extra shoots that grow around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain tso titri lɛ

english: Extra suckers steal water and food from the main plantain mother stem. Keeping only one or two strong suckers ensures the main stem gets enough nourishment to yield a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui titrii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo plantains babaoo ni tsii.

english: Pepper flowers often drop when the soil gets too dry, temperatures get too hot, or if too much nitrogen fertilizer is used, which makes the plant focus on leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Dɔlɛ lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe aduawai lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my ripening tomatoes turning black and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit, usually due to inconsistent watering. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the roots feed calcium to the developing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. ni calcium ni faaa lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛkɛ calcium haa aduawai ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt in the hot afternoon sun even when the soil has some moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo moŋ?

english: In the hot afternoon, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can pull it up from the ground. As long as the soil is damp, the leaves will bounce back once the afternoon heat cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba be mli ni shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my orange tree covered in a sticky black powder?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni powda diŋ ni shwieɔ shi ehà mi-orange tso lɛ nɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: The black coating is a mold that grows on the sugary waste left behind by tiny insects like aphids or scale insects. Controlling those insects will stop the black mold from spreading on your trees.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ sugar ni kooloi bibii, tamɔ aphids loo scale kooloi lɛ shwieɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ oye nakai kooloi lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii diji lɛ akagbɛ ashwã otsei lɛ anɔ.

english: How does growing cowpeas or groundnuts in my farm help make the soil better for maize next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas have friendly bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas out of the air and convert it into plant food in the soil, naturally enriching it for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ helai ni haa mɔ he feɔ naanyo yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa efeɔ niyenii kɛhaa tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli sɛɛnamɔ baa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ.

english: Why do cocoa trees grow better and survive longer when they are young if I plant shade trees over them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛ́ amɛji gbekɛbii kɛji midu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily in full sunlight and lose water too fast. Shade trees protect them from harsh sun and strong winds while keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya tsɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he, yɛ be mli ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to weed my maize farm within the first two weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii enyɔ lɛ mli beni midu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young maize plants need all the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients they can get to grow strong roots. Weeding early prevents weeds from stealing these resources and stops them from crowding out your delicate crops.
ga: Abɛi tsei bibii hia nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni shishifãi ni wa atsɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaatsi jwɛi naa koni amɛkaju nibii nɛɛ. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ.

english: How does clearing weeds early help prevent insect pests from attacking my maize?
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkatutua mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Weeds often serve as shelter and breeding grounds for crop-eating insects. Clearing them early removes hiding spots and forces pests away from your young maize seedlings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ shĩa kɛ he ni kooloi ni yeɔ jwɛi lɛ fɔɔ yɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ejie hei ni teɔ shi yɛ lɛ ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai akashɛ o-bibii ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ahe.

english: Can weeds growing near my young maize plants affect how much grain I harvest later?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baaná dumɔwui abɔ ni makpa yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, if weeds starve your crop of nutrients during its first few weeks, the maize stalk will remain weak and stunted, which results in smaller corn ears and a much lower yield at harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ jwɛi lɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ he naagbai ba yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli. Abɛi tsei lɛ baakã he ahi shi ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa toi lɛ feɔ bibii, ni ŋmãa ni anáa lɛ hu baa shi kwraa.

english: How often should I inspect my young maize plants for pests after planting?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ makwɛ kɛji miyɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛji midu gbekɛbii abele?

english: You should check your farm regularly starting in the first two weeks after planting. Catching pests right when they first appear makes them much easier and cheaper to control before widespread damage occurs.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii enyɔ ni okɛdu nii lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛje kpo klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛhe nitsumɔ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛjara hu waaa kwraa dani amɛfiteɔ nii babaoo.

english: What early signs should I look for to know if pests are starting to attack my maize?
ga: Mɛɛ mra be mli okadii esa akɛ matao koni mana kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai miibɔi mi-ŋma lɛ tutuamɔ?

english: Look closely at the young leaves for small chew marks, tiny ragged holes, scraped leaf surfaces, or insect droppings near the center shoot of the plant.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai bibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔtɔ he okadii bibii, buji bibii, baa lɛ hiɛ ni atsɔ mli. loo kooloi bibii ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ.

english: Why are young maize plants so much more vulnerable to pests than mature plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ amɛ fe tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young maize leaves are soft, tender, and easy for insects to eat. Because the seedling is still small, losing even a few leaves to pests can kill or permanently stunt the entire plant.
ga: Abɛi bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni koolooi yeɔ amɛ oya. Ejaakɛ dumɔwui lɛ daraaa lolo Kɛ́ ŋmeii fioo po fite amɛ yɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbe tso muu lɛ fɛɛ loo eha egbɔjɔ kwraa.

english: Why do agricultural officers ask farmers to stay vigilant for pests during planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ biɔ okwaafoi lɛ ni amɛkwɛ amɛhe nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni okwaayeli lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: Pest populations rapidly increase when rainy seasons begin and new crops start sprouting. Being on high alert allows you to spot early outbreaks across the area before pests spread from farm to farm.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ oya beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi ni ŋmɔshi nibii heei jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Hiɛdɔɔ ni nɔ kwɔ yeɔ ebua bo ni onaa helai ni baa lɛ mra. yɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ fɛɛ Dani tsɛŋemɔ helai baagbɛ ashwã kɛjɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛya ekroko mli

english: What causes insect pests to suddenly appear in my field right after my seed sprouts?
ga: Mɛni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa miŋmɔji amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Pest insects or their dormant eggs often lie hidden in the surrounding bush or soil, waiting for fresh, green crop shoots to emerge as a convenient food source.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ jwɛi loo shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. koni amɛmɛ tso eŋɔli heei ni ekwɛ̃ akɛ niyenii jɛɛhe ni hi

english: Why do pests sometimes come back to my maize crop even after I have treated the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli beni mikɛ ŋmɔji lɛ etsu nii po lɛ?

english: Pests re-emerge because unhatched eggs might survive initial treatments, or new insects may fly in from neighboring unweeded fields looking for food.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa ejaakɛ ŋmeii ni afɔɔɔ amɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shishijee tsofafeemɔ mli. loo kooloi heei Amɛbaanyɛ amɛfo kɛjɛ ŋmɔji ni jwɛi bɛ mli ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli kɛba koni amɛbatao niyenii.

english: What steps should I take if I notice pests returning to my maize farm a second time?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina akɛ ŋmeii miiku amɛsɛɛ amɛba mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli shii enyɔ nɔ?

english: If pests reappear, inspect the farm immediately to assess how far they have spread, ensure your farm is free of weeds, and consult an extension officer for proper treatment methods to stop the cycle.
ga: Kɛji tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ je kpo ekoŋŋ Kwɛmɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ona bɔ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã amɛha. Kwɛmɔ ni jwɛi akafee oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ni okɛ extension officer lɛ agba sane koni ena tsofafeemɔ ni sa ni baaha nɛkɛ sɛɛkuu nɛɛ akpa.

english: Officer, why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Ofisa Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?
