english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil or the roots are sitting in too much water, which prevents the plant from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop and curl up during the hot afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Plantain leaves curl during the hottest part of the day to protect themselves from losing too much moisture to the intense sun; as long as they recover by evening, it is a normal protective behavior.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni hulu ni naa wa lɛ akafite amɛ babaoo. Shii abɔ ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ Eji hebuu subaŋ ni afɔɔ feemɔ.

english: What causes the flowers on my tomato plants to fall off without growing into fruit?
ga: Mɛni haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering, which causes the plant to drop its flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why is it better for my farm if I clear weeds without burning the land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji mijie jwɛi lɛ ni mishãaa he ni miyɔɔ lɛ dani midu nii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable nutrients and micro-organisms in the soil, while clearing without burning leaves plant material to rot into natural compost that feeds future crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ ni ashãaa lɛ haa tso lɛ mli nibii lɛ fiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same soil where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, restoring fertility after nutrient-hungry crops like maize have harvested.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni aku sɛɛ aha fɔmɔ aba ekoŋŋ yɛ be mli ni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to leave specific distance between my pepper plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Proper spacing allows sunlight and fresh air to reach every part of the plant, preventing diseases from spreading easily while giving each plant enough soil space for its roots.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Tsi hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa mlɛo Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha tso fɛɛ tso shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha eshishifãi.

english: How can I check my young corn field early to know if fall armyworms have arrived?
ga: Mikwɛɔ mi-baby corn ŋmɔji lɛ amli mra. Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ana kɛji ŋmeii ebashɛ?

english: Inspect the center funnel of young corn plants for small ragged holes in the fresh leaves and tiny sawdust-like droppings left behind by feeding caterpillars.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmãa gbekɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ kɛji ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli yɛ baai heei kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli. Etamɔ ŋmei ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ niyenii lɛ shĩɔ yɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does cassava mosaic disease spread so quickly across my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cassava mosaic hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: The disease is spread by tiny whiteflies that feed on infected plants and carry the virus to healthy ones, as well as by taking stem cuttings from sick plants for new planting.
ga: Hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii yɛji bibii ni yeɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ ni amɛkɛ hela lɛ yaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. Nakai eji yɛ tsei niji heei ni afo kɛjɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ adumɔ he.

english: Why are my okra plants growing very tall with big leaves but producing very few okra pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ waa kɛ baai wuji shi ewoɔ okra ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they put all their energy into leafy growth and tall stems instead of flowering and setting fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kakadaji kɛ tsei ashishifãi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii lɛ

english: How do I know the best time to plant cassava cuttings after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eba naagbee lɛ?

english: Plant your cassava cuttings after the land has received two or three heavy rains, ensuring the soil is wet deep enough to support early root formation.
ga: Dumɔ o-yucca tsei lɛ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni naa wa shii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ. Kwɛmɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa bɔ ni sa koni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara mra.

english: Can using the same cutlass to prune my cocoa trees spread disease from a sick tree to a healthy one?
ga: Ani dade kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛfoɔ cacao tso lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ hela ashwã kɛjɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ?

english: Yes. When you cut an infected tree, the plant's sap sticks to your cutlass blade. If you cut a healthy tree next, that infected sap enters the fresh cut and spreads the disease, much like how infected blood transfers illness.
ga: Hɛɛ. Kɛ́ ofo tso ni hela emɔ lɛ Tso lɛ mli nu lɛ baakpɛtɛ otsitsi lɛ he. Kɛji oya nɔ ofo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ Nu ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ boteɔ tso hee lɛ mli ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa. Tamɔ bɔ ni lá ni hela emɔ lɛ tsɔɔ hela mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: If my neighbour's cassava field has a plant disease, will my cassava also catch it if the leaves touch across the farm line?
ga: Kɛji okutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmei ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ tso hela Ani mi ŋmei lɛ baaná hela kɛji baai lɛ fo tso lɛ line lɛ mli?

english: Usually, simple leaf touching does not spread most plant diseases. Most crop illnesses need insects to suck the plant sap or require infected sap to enter a cut made by farm tools to actually infect a healthy plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ko ni akɛtaa he kɛkɛ lɛ Egbɛŋ tsei ahelai babaoo ashwãa Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe helai babaoo biɔ ni kooloi bibii aŋɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Aloo amɛmiisumɔ ni nu ni hela emɔ lɛ abote pilamɔi ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii anɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛ hela awo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if a stem cutting from my cassava plant is healthy enough to plant for the next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii ni mifo kɛjɛ mi-cassava tso lɛ mli lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Cut the stem open and check the inside. Healthy stem cuttings have clean, light-coloured inner tissue without dark streaks, holes, or strange oozing sap that indicates internal infection.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ tso lɛ ni okwɛ emli. Tso lɛ yibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni afo lɛ baaná mligbɛ fã ni he tse, ni su yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Linei ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ, bu, loo latɛs ni hoɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ bɛ jɛmɛ. ni tsɔɔ akɛ hela ko yɛ mli

english: Tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies are sucking the sap out of your plant leaves and leaving behind viruses. Controlling these insects early prevents them from spreading sickness through your crop's sap flow.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies Ekɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ miinu ni eshiɔ hela lɛ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbɛ helai amɛshwã kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli nu ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and collapse even when the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛshwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli egbi moŋ lɛ? Ani ebaafee ŋmɔtɔ?

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt. Bacteria enter through the roots or cuts in the stem and block the internal tubes that carry water, causing the plant to dry up even in moist soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, muawai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Muawai boteɔ shishifãi loo pilamɔi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ amli ni amɛtsiɔ paipii ni yɔɔ mli ni kɛ nu yaa lɛ anaa. Ehaa tsei lɛ gĩɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ po nɔ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain suckers close to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that create shade, keeping the soil cool and moist for the cocoa until it gets older.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ koni kookoo lɛ atsɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant many seeds together in one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives every plant enough resources to build strong stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tsei ni wa kɛ tsei wuji.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn turning yellow in a V-shape while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn lɛ shishi baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This yellowing shows that your soil lacks nitrogen. The corn plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves, signaling that it needs fertilizer or organic manure.
ga: Nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin instead of growing big and fat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe tseee yɛ agboi ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose soil and nutrients like potassium to swell up. If the soil is hard or poor in nutrients, the roots stay thin and woody instead of storing starch.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ niyenii tamɔ potassium he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛfuu. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ, Shishifãi lɛ baafee mlɛo ni amɛbaafee tsei yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaabua ŋmeii anaa.

english: Why do my yam seeds rot in the ground before they even sprout stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ po lɛ?

english: Yam seeds rot when planted in waterlogged soil or when the seed yam already had minor rot or pest damage inside its skin before planting. Using clean seeds and planting on raised mounds prevents this.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ loo kɛji akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fite fioo loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ hewolo lɛ mli lɛ efite amɛ dani adu. Dumɔwui ni he tse ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I plant them alone in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikome too midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries up the moisture in their roots. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain alongside cocoa provides living shade that protects the young trees until they grow strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ gĩɔ. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe. Kɛyashi tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees need fertilizer to produce more pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: If your cocoa trees have yellowish leaves, drop their leaves early, or produce tiny, few pods despite getting enough rainfall, it usually means the soil lacks essential nutrients. Applying the right cocoa fertilizer replenishes the soil and encourages healthy pod growth.
ga: Kɛji o-cocoa tso lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ Shi baai lɛ mra loo ŋmɔtɔ bibii afee kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po. Bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is at the start of the rainy season when the soil is moist. Wet soil helps the roots absorb the fertilizer quickly, whereas applying it during intense dry heat can burn the roots or waste the fertilizer.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ loo eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite.

english: Why are my plantain trees producing small bunches even though the rainfall was good this year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ jogbaŋŋ afi nɛɛ moŋ.

english: Good rainfall alone isn't enough; plantain trees are heavy feeders that pull large amounts of nutrients from the soil. If the soil is weak or if too many suckers are growing around one main plant, the nutrients get shared, resulting in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Nugbɔ pɛ kɛkɛ faaa. Dumɔwui ji niyenii ni tsii ni jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo eyɛ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, dumɔ he fɛɛ he. tso titri kome Abaajara niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: How many suckers should I leave around one plantain tree for maximum yield?
ga: Tsofai enyiɛ esa akɛ mashi yɛ he fɛɛ he? Dumɔwu kome kɛha yibii babaoo.

english: You should keep only one or two healthy suckers alongside the main parent plant. Leaving too many suckers creates competition for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water, which results in smaller bunches for all the plants.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kome loo enyɔ pɛ ato nyɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ haa akaŋshii baa kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la kɛ nu mli, ni no haa tso fɛɛ tso fãi bibii baa.

english: Why do some parts of my farmland produce high crop yields while other parts right next to it give low yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli hei komɛi miiwo yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni hei krokomɛi hu wooo yibii lɛ? Mɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo.

english: Soil quality can vary even within a short distance on the same farm due to differences in soil depth, water retention, past weed cover, or nutrient levels. Testing or observing where water settles and adding organic manure to poor patches helps balance yield across the farm.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su baanyɛ atsake yɛ gbɛ kukuji po amli. yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ hewɔ Nu ni ahiɔ mli, jwɛi ni akɛhaa nɔ, loo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ srɔtoi Kaa loo akwɛɔ hei ni nu shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni nibii ni anáa lɛ afee ekome yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot before they mature?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, overly damp conditions. Pruning excess branches to allow sunlight and airflow, clearing weeds, and spraying recommended fungicides helps keep the pods healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ fe nine. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli, ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ, ni akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and dry up from the bottom leaves going upwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: As plantains grow, it is natural for older bottom leaves to turn yellow and die as the plant moves nutrients to newer leaves and developing fruit. However, if leaves dry up rapidly, it can also be a sign of poor soil nutrients or a root fungal disease.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ dara lɛ Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi be mli ni tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛyaa baai heei amli ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ gĩ oya lɛ, Ebaanyɛ efee okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kpakpai bɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: Will cutting off some branches from my mature cocoa trees reduce the number of pods I harvest?
ga: Ani cacao tso ni eda lɛ niji komɛi ni mifoɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii ni mikpaa lɛ ayibɔ aba shi?

english: No, careful pruning actually increases your harvest. Removing excess, dead, or diseased branches allows sunlight to reach the inner trunk where pods grow and improves airflow, which prevents diseases and directs the tree's energy into pod production.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni oookpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛ́ ajie tsei niji ni egboi loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai baaa mɔ nɔ, ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers but only a few of them turn into actual cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔlɔ babaoo lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to pollinate them, and many flowers naturally fall off if the tree lacks water or nutrients to support them all. Keeping shade and leaf litter on the farm ground creates a good home for pollinating midges and retains soil moisture.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli. Ni fɔfɔi babaoo baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni haa amɛ fɛɛ amɛyeɔ nii. Shade kɛ baai amli jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shia kpakpa baa kɛha pollination ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees on the same land where I am planting young cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kookoo bibii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Young cocoa trees need protection from direct sunlight while they are small. Plantain trees grow very quickly and produce large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist for the young cocoa to survive.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he be mli ni amɛdarako lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ koni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Can I grow beans together with cocoa, and will it help my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kookoo adu ŋmeii? Ni ani ebaaye ebua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, growing beans with cocoa is very beneficial. Beans absorb nitrogen from the air and naturally put it into the soil, which acts as free fertilizer to help your cocoa plants grow strong.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ kookoo duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Beans shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ ni yeɔ ebuaa o-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I plant plantains, beans, and cocoa together, won't they fight for space and soil nutrients?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ plantains, beans kɛ cocoa fee ekome lɛ Ekɛ he ko kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ etswaŋ akaŋ, aloo jeee nakai?

english: If you space them correctly, they actually support each other. Beans cover the ground and feed the soil early on, plantains provide shade, and by the time cocoa grows big enough to need all the space, the plantains are ready to be removed.
ga: Kɛji okɛ space lɛ to he jogbaŋŋ lɛ Amɛfiɔ amɛhe sɛɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Akɛ ŋmeii woɔ ŋmeii amli ni ahaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii mra. Plantains haa hulutsoo. Ni kɛ́ kookoo lɛ da bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehe miihia ni ená he fɛɛ he. Amrɔ nɛɛ, plantain lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaajie.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and drop from the tree during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive moisture during rainy weather creates a good environment for a fungal disease called Black Pod disease. The fungus attacks the pods, turning them black, rotting them, and causing them to fall off.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi kɛha tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela lɛ baa. Fungus tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ. Etsɔɔ ediŋŋ, egboɔ, ni ehaa eshwieɔ shi.

english: How can I protect my cocoa pods from rotting when it rains a lot?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: You can protect your crop by regularly pruning extra shade leaves to let sunlight and wind dry out the farm, weeding the ground, and plucking off any black or spoiled pods immediately so the disease doesn't spread.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ tsei krokomɛi ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ni oookpa koni hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ akagbi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ojie ŋmeii diji loo ŋmeii ni efite lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: What main farm activities should I focus on during the peak rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ nitsumɔi titrii esa akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: During heavy rains, your main tasks should be controlling weeds, ensuring rainwater drains off the farm smoothly, and continually harvesting ripe cocoa pods quickly before wet weather rots them.
ga: yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli Esa akɛ onitsumɔ titri afee ni okwɛ jwɛi anɔ. Kwɛmɔ ni nugbɔ nu lɛ ajɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni okpa kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ oyaiyeli mli dani kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ afite amɛ.

english: How long does a cocoa farm usually take before it starts giving fruit?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo ŋmɔ ko jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa trees usually start producing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older local varieties can take up to 4 or 5 years before your first harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 loo 5 dani obaaná oklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Is it possible to use a machine to harvest all my cocoa pods at once?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akɛ tsɔnei akpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ shikome?

english: No, cocoa pods mature at different times and must be hand-harvested using long poles with sharp hooks (goosenecks). Using heavy machinery would damage the tree branches and flower cushions where future cocoa pods grow.
ga: Dabi, kookoo ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Esa akɛ akɛ niji akpa amɛ kɛtsɔ tsei kakadaji kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ (goosenecks) nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsɔnei ni tsii tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite tsei lɛ aniji kɛ fɔfɔii akutsei ni yɔɔ he ni kookoo ŋmeii baakwɛ̃ yɛ wɔsɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know when the plantains I planted with my cocoa are ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-kookoo dumɔwui lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Plantain bunches are ready to harvest when the individual fingers look full and rounded instead of sharp and angular, usually between 12 to 15 months after planting.
ga: Plantain kuu ko efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni nineshi nine lɛ eko fɛɛ eko tamɔ nɔ ni eyi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 15 teŋ yɛ dumɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do cocoa buyers care so much if cocoa beans get exposed to rain after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ kookoo lɛ susuɔ he waa kɛji kookoo yibii lɛ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rainwater on harvested cocoa causes mold to grow inside the beans and ruins their flavor. Buyers need thoroughly fermented and sun-dried beans to produce good chocolate and ensure long shelf life.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ kookoo ni akpa lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ shwereɔ yɛ kɔfe yibii lɛ amli ni efiteɔ amɛmli ŋɔɔmɔ lɛ. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ miisumɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni egbi koni ekɛ tsokolate kpakpa aba ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn light yellow when the plants are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen or that heavy rains have washed the nutrients away. Adding a nitrogen-based fertilizer like Urea or NPK helps the leaves turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛtee. Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ urea loo NPK fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: What happens to my crops if I leave fertilizer on top of the dry soil without working it into the ground?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mishi ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni mikɛwooo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Fertilizer left exposed on dry ground loses its active nutrients to the sun heat and air, or gets washed away by rain, which means your crops won't get the food they need to yield well.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baafite niyenii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ kɛha dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ hulu la mli lɛ. loo nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naaa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: How can I know if my crops are suffering from a disease or if they just need water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela emɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ loo nu kɛkɛ he miihia amɛ?

english: A thirsty plant usually recovers and stands firm once you give it water, but a diseased plant will keep showing spots, yellow patches, or leaf rot even after it gets enough rain or water.
ga: Tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhe ajɔ amɛ ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛ́ oha amɛ nu. Shi tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ baaya nɔ ajie ŋmeii, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni fiteɔ lɛ akpo. Kɛji nugbɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po

english: Why do tiny holes appear all over my vegetable leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ aduawai ahe baai anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli.

english: Holes in crop leaves are caused by insects like caterpillars and beetles that multiply during the wet season to feed on soft new leaf growth.
ga: Koolooi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kɛ bu ni yɔɔ tsei baai amli lɛ baa. Amɛfɔɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ.

english: How does applying crop medicine or spray keep my plants from dying?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsofa loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ ni mikɛaatsu nii lɛ aha mitsei lɛ akagboi?

english: Crop medicines contain active chemicals that kill harmful insects and microscopic fungi, stopping them from eating your plant tissue or spreading infection through the field.
ga: Tsofai ni tsuɔ nii ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ tsei ahe tsofai amli. Enɛ haaa amɛye tsei amli fãji loo amɛkagbɛ hela amɛshwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant a lot of seeds close together in one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, their roots fight each other for the limited water and nutrients in the soil while their leaves fight for sunlight, making all of them grow small and weak.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la he akaŋ lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops so much even after I have already put fertilizer on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui waa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔji lɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and will steal the fertilizer nutrients, soil moisture, and sunlight meant for your crops, starving your plants of what they need to produce fruit.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. ni ebaaju niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli sũ mli nu ni mli edɔ kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why does my cassava produce very big stem leaves but only small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei yɛ baai wuji waa shi ŋmei bibii yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava puts all its energy into leaves instead of root tubers when there is too much nitrogen in the soil or when plants do not get enough balance of other nutrients like potassium.
ga: Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai lɛ amli yɛ shishifãi lɛ najiaŋ kɛ́ nitrogen babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii krokomɛi tamɔ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before any fruit starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of plant food like calcium during the flowering period.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ amɛna haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tso lɛ mli niyenii tamɔ calcium ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up and curl into tight shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects hiding under the leaves or by viral infections spread by those insects as they feed on plant sap.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ ashishi loo kɛjɛɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli beni amɛyeɔ tsei amli nu lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shielding the cocoa from extreme heat and preserving soil moisture during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Buu kookoo he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam is a vine that needs maximum sunlight to manufacture food for its underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground toward the sun, prevents soil-borne leaf diseases, and helps the plant produce much larger yams.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Tsi foliar helai ni shikpɔŋ kɛbaa lɛ naa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni dara kwraa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together in the field to get more crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli koni ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ?

english: Placing seeds too close forces the plants to compete against each other for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. This overcrowding results in weak, thin stalks with tiny cobs or no grain at all, whereas proper spacing yields a much bigger harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli loo dumɔwui ko kwraa bɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baaha yibii babaoo aba lɛ.

english: Why do other farmers advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them first enriches the soil naturally, providing essential nutrients for the next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu amɛ mra lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ koni akɛye kooloi.

english: Why is it good for me to cover the bare soil around my tomato plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, prevents water from evaporating quickly under the hot sun, keeps the roots cool, and stops weeds from growing and stealing nutrients from your tomatoes.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ.

english: Why do weeds reduce my crop yield so much if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ baa shi waa kɛji mijieee amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crop plants and aggressively drink up the soil moisture, fertilizers, and sunlight. Clearing them early prevents them from starving your main crop during its critical growth stage.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ, ni amɛmuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la babaoo. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye hɔmɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ.

english: Yellowing that starts at the tips of lower maize leaves usually indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for leafy green growth, so applying balanced fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will restore plant health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha baa eŋɔli lɛ dalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: This condition, known as blossom-end rot, is caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often triggered by irregular watering. Keeping the soil moisture consistent helps the roots absorb calcium evenly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Upward curling leaves are usually a sign of tiny pests like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap from the leaves, or a virus transmitted by these insects. Controlling these small insects early protects the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies miinu nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. loo virus ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kooloi bibii akudɔmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know that my cassava tubers are mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is generally ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the main stem becomes thick. Digging up one test plant allows you to confirm if the tubers are full and firm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Kasemɔ tso kome ni ooofo lɛ haa onyɛɔ omaa nɔ mi kɛji ŋmeii lɛ eyi obɔ ni eyɛ shiŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the roots. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted manure will help them regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What makes my cassava tubers rot in the soil before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛná hegbɛ ni amɛkpa?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without proper drainage, especially during heavy rainy seasons. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away, keeping the roots dry enough to stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Titri lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ agbi bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom tips of my pepper fruits turning black and rotting before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ shishigbɛ fã lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: This is known as blossom end rot, which usually happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium or when watering is irregular. Keeping the soil moisture consistent through regular watering and mulching helps the plant transport calcium to developing fruits.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo kɛ́ afɔɔ amɛ nu be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ calcium yaa aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before growing into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they experience stress from dry weather, insect pests like mirids, or a lack of soil nutrients. Providing adequate shade, controlling pests early, and ensuring good soil nutrients will help the tree hold onto its flowers and produce pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ pollen mli baa lɛ he. loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shade ni sa ni akɛhaa Mra Be mli nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ Ni niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ hi lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ fɔfɔii ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by sap-sucking insects like whiteflies that transmit viruses, or by severe heat stress. Protecting young plants with insect nets, weeding around the field, and watering regularly helps keep the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli Haomɔ ni naa wa ni akɛ buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛtsɔ kooloi amli ŋmeii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shia lɛ he kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the central leaves of my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the tender central leaves (the funnel) of maize. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract solutions directly into the funnels early in the morning can stop them.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo (funnels) lɛ anɔ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. Ni kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ wo kooloi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa amɛ.

english: What happens to my crop yield if I plant my seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots fight each other for soil nutrients and water, while their leaves block sun from reaching one another. Spacing plants according to recommended guidelines ensures each plant gets enough light, air, and nourishment to yield well.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe Gbɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ akatse tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds early when my crops are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? Be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and will quickly steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops. Removing weeds during the first few weeks gives your crops the best chance to establish strong root systems.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni ebaaju nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi lɛ je kpo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛkɛto shishifãi ni mli wa ama shi.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei kakadaŋŋ atswa sweet potato wain tsei lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves high to capture sunlight for making food. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground to prevent disease and allows the plant to gather enough energy to grow big underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ ewo ebaa lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi koni enyɛ emɔ hulu la kɛha nihoomɔ. Staking baaha baai akabote hei ni mli edɔ lɛ koni helai akabote mli. ni ehaa tso lɛ buaa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa naa koni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does my land yield less maize when I plant it on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize on the same land every season drains the specific nutrients that maize relies on, leaving the soil tired. Rotating your crop with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts helps fix natural nitrogen back into the soil, restoring its fertility for future crops.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi lɛ damɔ nɔ lɛ kpo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shikpɔŋ lɛ fitemɔ Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni ekɛ fɔmɔ aba wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ekoŋŋ

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on cassava are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by small whiteflies or contaminated stem cuttings. Using disease-resistant cassava varieties helps keep the leaves healthy and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Agbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii loo tsei niji ni mli ewo muji lɛ anɔ. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni efeɔ eŋɔli.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same plot where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them after maize naturally restores nutrients to the soil so your future crops grow stronger without relying entirely on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ abele sɛɛ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Bɔni afee ni owɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ anɔ kwraa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the shade trees away from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kooko tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei fɛɛ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to survive because strong direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why is my maize flowering and producing tassels when the stalks are still very short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni eyɛ ŋmeii lɛ? Ani tso lɛ shishi lɛ yɛ kuku waa lolo?

english: When maize faces severe stress, such as a long dry spell or poor soil nutrients early in its growth, it tries to produce seeds early to survive. Proper watering and applying fertilizer early in the plant's life prevent premature flowering.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa kpe, tamɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛgbiɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii yɛ ŋmãa shishijee bei amli lɛ, ŋmãa baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ dumɔwui awo mra. koni ehi shi Nu ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli mra yɛ tso lɛ wala mli lɛ baaye abua ni akawo fɔfɔi oya.

english: Is it better for me to water my tomato crops in the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the plants can soak up moisture before the day gets hot. Watering in the afternoon causes water to evaporate quickly, and water droplets on foliage can burn leaves under intense heat.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi maŋkpa koni tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ adɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya. Ni nu ni shwieɔ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛshã yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow faster than my crops right after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer feeds all plants equally, including weeds. Clearing weeds from around your crops before applying fertilizer ensures that your crops get all the nutrients instead of sharing them with weeds.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ niyenii pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni jwɛi fata he. Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli dani awoɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ jwɛi lɛ baaja.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before any peppers actually grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani pepper lɛ miida diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from heat stress, erratic watering, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and using mulch helps protect the plant from heat stress so the flowers can turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo niyenii ni bɛ shiŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ebu tsei ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. koni fɔfɔii lɛ anyɛ afee chili ŋmɔtɔ

english: Why do insects show up inside my stored maize bags even when the bags are tied tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-abele kotokui ni mikɛto lɛ amli eyɛ mli akɛ akpɛtɛ kotokui lɛ ahe waa moŋ?

english: Insect eggs are often laid on the maize ears while they are still in the farm field. If the grain is not thoroughly dried before storage, those hidden eggs hatch inside the bags; drying the grain properly until it is hard and dry kills or prevents these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ kooloi bibii awoɔ ŋmãa toi anɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto Nakai ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ baafɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbi lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbe loo ebu he kɛjɛ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from this year's hybrid maize harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ afi nɛɛ hybrid ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for a high yield in their first planting. If you save and replant those seeds, the second generation loses those strong traits, resulting in uneven growth and a much lower yield.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Kɛji obua nakai dumɔwui lɛ anaa ni odu lɛ Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ baafite nakai sui ni mli wa lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi kwraa.

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the leafy side shoots on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Removing excess side shoots (suckers) directs the plant's energy away from growing useless leaves and puts it into producing larger, healthier fruit and improving air flow to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii (ŋmeii) ni fa fe nine lɛ, ejieɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni he ehiaaa ni miida lɛ amli. ni ehaa tsei woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ koni akaye tsɛŋemɔ hela.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant grow strong and form big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni esa akɛ ŋmãa ahi shi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do weeds hurt my crops even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than main crops and aggressively steal plant food, root space, and sunlight. Even with rain, your crops will stay small because the weeds are taking most of the nutrition from the ground.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛjuɔ tso niyenii, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ hulu la kɛ yiwalɛ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, onibii lɛ baafee bibioo ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ gbalaa amɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer roots when I plant cassava on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shishifãi fioo pɛ baa kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Cassava pulls the same heavy nutrients out of the soil every season. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot drains those specific nutrients, while rotating with crops like beans or peanuts gives the soil time to rebuild its strength.
ga: Cassava gbalaa niyenii ni tsii ni tsii lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ adu shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, no haa nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛtswaa ehewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I remove all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under full direct sun. Large shade trees protect the cocoa from harsh heat and keep moisture in the air and soil while the cocoa plants build strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, cacao tso lɛ feɔ shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks next to my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb upward to spread their leaves towards sunlight. Sunlight helps leaves make food, which is then sent down into the ground to make large, heavy yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛmaje shikpɔŋ koni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain can be a false start followed by weeks of scorching heat. If you plant too early, seeds will sprout but then wither and die when the ground quickly dries up before the real rainy season begins.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ afee amale shishijee. Nɔ ni nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ ji otsii babaoo ni mli edɔ waa. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi amɛbaagbi ni amɛbaagboi be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ baashɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black and dry up during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, damp, shaded environments. Clearing dense weeds and trimming overgrown tree branches lets sunlight and air flow through to dry off the pods and stop the sickness.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Jwɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ekpa hela.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft, watery, and rot when left in the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ, amɛmli nu, ni amɛgboi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When heavy rain leaves standing water around cassava roots for too long, air cannot reach them. The tubers drown and rot from fungi in the muddy soil, so harvesting before prolonged flooding is critical.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ hiɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he. Tubers lɛ miiho nu mli ni amɛmiifite kɛmiijɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ muji lɛ mli lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akpa ŋmaa be kakadaŋŋ dani nu afua aba.

english: Why do small insect holes in my cowpea leaves reduce the number of pods I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii abuji yɔɔ lɛ? yɛ mi-cowpea baai lɛ anɔ ni no haa ŋmeii ni mikpaa lɛ ayibɔ baa shi.

english: Leaves are the factories where plants make their food using light. When insects eat full holes in the leaves, the plant loses energy and cannot produce enough flowers or pods.
ga: Baai ji nitsumɔhei ni tsei kɛ kane feɔ niyenii yɛ mli. Kɛji kooloi yeɔ baai ni bu eyi mli obɔ lɛ Tso lɛ hewalɛ baa shi ni enyɛɛɛ ewo fɔfɔi loo ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni ekɛ pepper ko kwraa baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers stress, such as extreme midday heat, irregular watering, or poor soil nutrition. Keeping the soil covered with dry grass mulching helps cool the soil and retain water.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔ ko kpe, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Sũ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ baaye abua ni edɔ ni ehiɛ nu mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Be ni majie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot withstand direct, harsh sunlight because their leaves scorch easily and lose moisture fast. Leaving shade trees or planting temporary crops like plantains protects young cocoa plants until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaa lɛ shãa oya, ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni ashiɔ loo aduɔ tsei ni yɔɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, will I get a bigger harvest from my small farm?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli. Mi nɔ loo daabi?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the plants to compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition results in weak, thin stalks with tiny cobs. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines to tall wooden sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbee shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce food for the underground tuber using sunlight. Staking the vines raises the leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight and stay safe from soil rots, leading to much bigger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii amɛhaa amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni enyɛ ená hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. ni ehi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni fiteɔ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara babaoo baa.

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out and crack so quickly during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbɛɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses water rapidly through evaporation when exposed directly to the hot sun. Covering the ground around your crops with dried leaves or grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool and locks in moisture for longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Mulching around Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops look pale and produce very little fruit even though it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can wash key nutrients deep into the ground where crop roots cannot reach them, especially in tired soil. Adding organic compost or well-placed fertilizer puts essential food back into the soil so plants can thrive.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa waa lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Curled and yellow cassava leaves are often caused by small insects like whiteflies that spread diseases between plants. Removing affected plants early stops the disease from spreading across your entire field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai eshwaa tsei ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni hela akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Why are weeds growing so fast and making my vegetables look weak and stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni ehaa mi-aduawai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast-growing plants that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds regularly leaves all the nutrients in the soil for your crops to use.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Bei pii lɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shĩɔ koni otsei lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and shaded during hot weather helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do people advise me to plant beans or cowpeas on the same land where I harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpaa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil, but bean crops naturally return vital nitrogen back into the soil through their roots. Planting beans after maize restores the soil's strength for your next crop.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmei tsei lɛ kɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ, ebaawaje shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why did the fertilizer I poured right at the base of my crops cause the leaves to turn brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mitso lɛ shishi lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is very concentrated and can burn roots if applied directly against the plant stem. It should always be placed in a small ring a few inches away from the stem so roots can absorb it safely.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ fa babaoo ni ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Esa akɛ akɛwo ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko mli. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, ekɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko. koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, which acts as the main food for leaf growth, or that the soil is waterlogged and preventing the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why are flowers falling off my pepper plants before any peppers actually grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei anɔ dani ŋmɔtɔ lɛ daa diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from high heat stress, erratic watering, or poor soil nutrients, as the plant tries to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo niyenii kpakpai ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ ji akɛ, tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even when I clear the land well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose soil and space to expand underground; if cassava is planted too close together or in hard, unplowed ground, the roots cannot swell properly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ he ko he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ ni atsuuu he nii lɛ, Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas to protect the cocoa while it establishes roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni shwereɔ oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he yɛ be mli ni etswaa shishifãi lɛ.

english: What is causing the leaves on my tomato plants to curl up and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a virus, or by the plant reacting to sudden dry weather and heat stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ni feɔ amɛnii yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa kɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly even if I planted good seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui kpakpai moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have stronger roots that quickly steal water, light, and fertilizer out of the soil before your main crops have a chance to take them in.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ. Enɛ juɔ nu, la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Dani oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ baaná hegbɛ ni ebote mli.

english: Will putting extra chemical fertilizer on my crops automatically give me a bigger harvest?
ga: Ani tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baaha maná ŋmaa babaoo kɛjɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mihe?

english: No, applying too much chemical fertilizer can burn the crop's roots and damage the soil. Plants only take what they need, so excess fertilizer is wasted and can harm the plant.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite shikpɔŋ lɛ. Tsei kɛ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛ tsuɔ nii. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ fiteɔ, ni ebaanyɛ eye tso lɛ awui.

english: Why does my soil get hard and dusty after just a few harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ sũ yɛ kpamɔ fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it loses organic matter, like decomposed leaves and manure. Continuous planting without adding compost or leaving crop residues drains the soil's natural structure.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ fite. Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsei amli nibii ni efite fataaa he lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii lɛ ajɛ mli.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds after the early rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ?

english: Wait until the rain has soaked deep into the ground over two or three steady rainy days; planting after just one brief shower often causes seeds to germinate and then dry up.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔ yɛ nu ni hoɔ fioo pɛ sɛɛ Bei pii lɛ, mɔdɛŋbɔɔ kome pɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Seeds stored in hot or humid conditions lose their strength over time, and grains saved from certain high-yield varieties do not grow well when replanted for a second generation.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛto shihilɛi ni mli edɔ loo hulutsoo be mli lɛ ahewalɛ baaje mli yɛ be ni sa mli. Ni dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei srɔtoi komɛi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ amli lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu ekoŋŋ kɛha yinɔ ni ji enyɔ.

english: Why should I plant seeds developed by local Ghanaian researchers instead of using seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui ni Ghana maŋ lɛ mli niiamlitaolɔi lɛ fee lɛ? Mohu ɔ, moo ngɔ dumɔwuhi nɛ a je kpami nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ kɛ tsu ní.

english: Seeds developed by local researchers are specifically bred to withstand Ghana's specific climate conditions, local pests, and soil types, giving you higher yields than older saved seeds that weaken over time.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni maŋ lɛ mli niiamlitaolɔi fee lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto lɛ naa. local pests and type soil Enɛ haa onáa yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui momoi ni ato ni baagbɔjɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Will these new improved crop seeds survive if the rainy season stops earlier than expected in my region?
ga: Ani nɛkɛ dumɔwui heei ni asaa amɛ jogbaŋŋ nɛɛ baahi shi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ kpa mra fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ yɛ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Many improved local seed varieties are bred for early maturity or drought resistance, meaning they can mature faster and yield well even if the rains end early.
ga: Akwɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui srɔtoi babaoo ni atsake amɛ koni amɛdara oya loo amɛnyɛ amɛshi hɔmɔ naa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nɛkɛ dumɔwui nɛɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni amɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ba naagbee mra po.

english: How do new seed varieties help me get more bags of harvest from the same size of land?
ga: Te dumɔwui heei baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná ŋmaakpamɔ kotokui babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Improved crop varieties are designed to direct more of their nutrients into making larger cobs, pods, or tubers rather than extra stems and leaves, producing more yield per plant.
ga: Afee tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo ni baaha amɛfee ŋmeii wuji, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ tsohi kɛ baaihi fuu. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, yibiiwoo ni tso fɛɛ tso baaná lɛ baaya hiɛ.

english: Why are my maize plants growing tall stems but not producing full ears of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ miikwɛ̃ ŋmeii kakadaji shi ewooo abele toi ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Maize plants spend energy growing tall instead of forming ears if they lack essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or if they are planted too close together and competing for sunlight.
ga: Abɛi tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara fe bɔ ni amɛfeɔ toi kɛji amɛbɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la.

english: How long should I expect my crop seeds to take to sprout out of the ground after I plant them?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ midumɔwui lɛ baaje kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Most healthy cereal and grain seeds sprout within 4 to 10 days when the soil is warm and moist. If nothing emerges after two weeks, the seeds may have dried out, rotted, or been eaten by insects.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa babaoo baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbii 4 kɛyashi 10 mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ. Kɛji nɔ ko baaa yɛ otsii enyɔ sɛɛ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ agbi, amɛgboi, loo kooloi bibii baanyɛ aye amɛ.

english: Why do my young crop plants turn yellow and thin when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight for the same water and soil food while their leaves block each other's light, leaving all the plants weak and starved.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe la lɛ naa Enɛ ha tsei lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔ ni hɔmɔ ye amɛ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is healthy enough to support a new crop before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei anɔ dani madu?

english: Healthy soil is dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture without staying waterlogged, and naturally supports active weed growth before clearing.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli ni nu bɛ mli. ni eye ebua adebɔɔ mli jwɛi lɛ adalɛ dani ajie.

english: Why is it harmful for my farm if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ, eyeɔ miŋmɔ lɛ awui lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stop growing well even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miitsi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and aggressively steal fertilizer and soil food away from your plants, causing the crops to starve even with adequate rainfall.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. ni ekɛ yiwalɛ juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants start curling up during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling during dry periods is often caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like whiteflies or mites that attack plants when water is low, weakening the leaves to protect themselves from moisture loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. ni tutuaa tsei kɛji nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ akafite.

english: Is it harmful to burn all the dry bushes on my land before planting my crop?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara akɛ mashã jwɛi ni egbi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, burning destroys important organic nutrients in the topsoil and kills beneficial organisms that keep the soil healthy. Leaving cleared plants to decay naturally or using them as mulch protects soil moisture and keeps the ground fertile for your crops.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, shãa fiteɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni tsei ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe loo okɛtsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha onibii.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, works like a blanket. It prevents the hot sun from drying out the soil too quickly, suppresses weeds from growing, and breaks down into natural manure for your plants.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa otsei lɛ

english: Why do the lower leaves of my young maize plants turn light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize is starving for nitrogen, an essential plant food. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer early in growth helps the plant make leaves green again so it can produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he mra yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni efee baai lɛ eŋɔli ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn out very small and thin when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots fight each other underground for food, water, and space. Giving each plant proper spacing allows the roots to expand fully and store energy, resulting in bigger cassava tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ he ko. Kɛ́ aha gbɛ ni sa yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kwraa ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ toɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ agboi.

english: Why does my land yield less maize every year if I keep planting it on the exact same farm plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi kɛji midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating your crop with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores vital nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why am I advised not to spray pest chemicals on my vegetables in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛɛɛ akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ mi-vegetables lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Spraying during hot weather causes the chemical liquid to evaporate into the air quickly before killing pests, and the combination of strong sunlight and chemical residue can scorch and burn crop leaves.
ga: Tsofa mli nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ haa tsofa lɛ mli nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani egbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ. Ni hulu la ni naa wa kɛ tsofai ni eshwɛ ni akɛfee ekome lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ahe baai ni ashã amɛ.

english: Why are tiny insects attacking the flowers on my pepper plants causing the flowers to fall off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni tutuaa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Insects like thrips feed on tender flower parts, causing stress that forces the plant to shed flowers before fruit can form. Inspecting plants early and applying safe insecticidal soap or recommended sprays protects the blossoms so they turn into peppers.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ thrips yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Enɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani amɛwo yibii lɛ baa. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ni kɛ samla loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu fɔfɔi lɛ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe.
