english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when there are no shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo be bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that get sunburned easily under direct sunlight. Shade trees act as living umbrellas, keeping the surroundings cooler and humid until the cocoa grows strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni hiɛ ka. Ha shihilɛ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism crops use to survive water stress. By rolling their leaves, the plants reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and wind to conserve internal moisture.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛye amɛhe kɛjɛ nu mli haomɔ mli. Tsei haa amɛhe ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do seeds I save from last year's maize harvest yield less than new seed packets bought from the agricultural store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni ahe yɛ ŋmɔ mli shwapo ko mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought certified seeds are carefully bred for higher vigor, uniform growth, and pest resistance. Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose these strong qualities in subsequent generations, leading to smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ yɛ shwapoi amli lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛhe awa babaoo. uniform growth kɛ resistance kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ yinɔi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli, ni no haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are crowded, cassava puts all its energy into growing tall stems and leaves instead of tubers. Giving plants enough space and avoiding excessive manure helps the plant focus on swelling its roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei kɛ baai kakadaji amli yɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ajie ŋmeii babaoo kɛjɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi ni efuu lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines start dying off early before harvest time arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miibɔi gboimɔ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Yam vines often wither early if tiny underground pests called nematodes or fungal rot attack the roots and lower stem, blocking water flow. Treating seed yams with wood ash or clean water before planting helps protect them from these soil pests.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi bibii yɛ jɛmɛ. Ale amɛ akɛ nematodes loo fungus rot, ni amɛtutuaa shishifãi kɛ shishigbɛ tsei lɛ. ni haa nu lɛ hoɔ lɛ ehiii Kɛ́ akɛ tso sũ loo nu ni mli tse tsu sweet potatoes he nii dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ahe.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, overly shady, and wet conditions. Pruning extra shade tree branches to let sunlight and air reach the cocoa helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ. Shady tsɔ ni edɔ. Kɛ́ afolɔ hulutsoo be kroko mli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ kookoo lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers dry up and die shortly after I move them to new soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ tee shikpɔŋ hee nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers often fail if tiny soil worms or stem borer insects damaged their base before transplanting. Cleaning the outer root base of the sucker and letting it dry in the shade before planting helps ensure strong root growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain niyenii yelɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii. Aloo kooloi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ fiteɔ amɛshishitoo lɛ dani amɛduɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ otsumɔ sucker lɛ kponɔgbɛ shishitoo lɛ he ni oha egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani odu lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why does my oil palm tree drop its young fruit bunches before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii akui dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Oil palms drop young fruit when they do not get enough water during dry spells or when there are no pollinating insects around. Clearing weeds around the base and applying mulch keeps moisture in the soil so the tree can hold its fruit.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii kɛji amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo kɛ́ ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ bɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ajiemɔ Shishitoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akpa yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow from the bottom upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is essential for green growth. Heavy rain often washes this nutrient away, so applying fertilizer or compost around the base gives the plant back its green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛyaa. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii abɔle he. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ baaha tso lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it good practice for me to plant cowpeas on the same bed where I harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ saatso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ yɛ he ni mikpaa ŋmãa yɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants have roots that capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the ground. Planting cowpeas after maize naturally restores nutrients to the soil so future crops grow better without needing as much bought fertilizer.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Bɔni afee ni wɔsɛɛ tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛhe ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the stem instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are too high or when the soil dries out completely during flowering. Watering the plants regularly at the roots during dry weather helps flowers stay attached and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Kɛ́ afɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling tightly upwards and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe kɛtee ŋwɛi ni efee bibii lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids spreading leaf diseases. Spraying the leaves with organic neem water early in the morning helps clear these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ organic neem nu shwie baai lɛ anɔ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ajie amɛhe.

english: Why do my cabbage heads stay loose and leafy instead of forming hard, tight balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ etse ni eyɛ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee nɔ ko ni wa ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads fail to form tight balls when they do not get steady moisture or if the weather becomes too hot during their growth phase. Regular watering and mulching around the base keeps the root zone cool so the leaves wrap tightly.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee ŋmeii ni mli wa kɛji amɛnáaa hulutsoo be fɛɛ be loo kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shishitoo lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ afee fɛ̃i. koni baai lɛ abɔ he jogbaŋŋ

english: Why are my crops growing so well on one side of my farm, but struggling just a few steps away on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ? Shi ni amɛmiibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiiya he ko ni kɛ jɛmɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji ninetalɔi fioo komɛi pɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Soil properties like depth, sand content, moisture, and nutrients can change dramatically within just a few meters. Testing different areas of your farm helps you understand which spots need more compost or fertilizer to grow healthy crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii tamɔ emlibotemɔ, ŋã ni yɔɔ mli, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii baanyɛ atsake kwraa yɛ mitai fioo komɛi pɛ mli. He srɔtoi ni akaa Oŋmɔ lɛ baaye abua bo ni onu he ni ehe hiaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he koni akɛdu tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do crops planted at the bottom of a slope grow bigger than the ones at the top of the hill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gɔji ashishi lɛ daraa fe tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: When it rains, water carries rich topsoil and dissolved nutrients down the slope. This makes the soil at the bottom deeper, wetter, and more fertile than the dry, washed-out soil at the top.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, nu lɛ woɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni egbɛ eshwa lɛ kɛyaa ŋshɔ lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli kwɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni shwieɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why did the fertilizer that gave me a great harvest last year fail to work on the same crop this year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ anyɛɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wo yibii kpakpai yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii yɛ tsei nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ afi nɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs the right amount of soil moisture to work. If a season is too dry, plants cannot absorb the nutrients, and if heavy rains come right after application, the fertilizer can be washed deep into the soil where roots cannot reach it.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná nu ni sa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ etsu nii. Kɛji be lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ni kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa ba amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ Ebaanyɛ ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Is it better to apply chemical fertilizer to my crops before or after it rains?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ tsofa baawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli dani nugbɔ anɛ loo sɛɛ mli?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist or right before a light rain. This allows the nutrients to dissolve into the soil near the roots, but you should avoid applying it before heavy downpours that wash it away.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo loo fioo dani nugbɔ anɛ. Enɛ baaha niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Shi esa akɛ okpa ekɛ nitsumɔ dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba koni ekɛfɔ lɛ.

english: What happens to my land if I use the exact same chemical fertilizer treatment every single year?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii daa afi?

english: Using the same chemical fertilizer repeatedly without adding organic material like manure can make the soil acidic over time and deplete other essential minerals, leading to declining yields year after year.
ga: Tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii shii abɔ Kɛji akɛ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee acidic yɛ be ni sa mli. ni efiteɔ shika tsuru nibii krokomɛi ni he hiaa waa lɛ, ni no haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi daa afi

english: Why does my crop yield change so much from one year to another even when I plant at the exact same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nibii ni miduɔ lɛ srɔtoi babaoo kɛjɛɔ afi kome mli kɛyaa afi kroko mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ amɛ yɛ be kome mli moŋ.

english: Year-to-year yields change because weather patterns shift, such as when rains start late, stop early, or come with unexpected dry spells. Temperature changes and shifting pest populations also affect how well your crop grows each year.
ga: Nibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ afi mli lɛ tsakeɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tsakeɔ lɛ, tamɔ be mli ni nugbɔ jeɔ shishi sɛɛ, ekpaa mra loo ekɛ hɔmɔ be ni akpaaa gbɛ baa. Temperature tsakemɔi kɛ tsakemɔi ni baa tsɛŋemɔ helai ayibɔ mli lɛ hu saa ŋmɔshi nibii adalɛ he kɛjɛɔ afi kɛyaa afi.

english: How can I protect my crops when the rains stop earlier in the season than expected?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: You can protect your crops by spreading dry grass or leaves around the bases of the plants (mulching) to trap moisture in the soil, clearing weeds that steal water, and planting short-duration crop varieties.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛtsɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni oookɛshwie otsei lɛ ashishi (mulch) lɛ nɔ koni ekɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni juɔ nu lɛ kɛjɛ ohe. ni amɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kukuoo

english: Why does a crop grow easily in a neighboring village, but struggles to grow on my farm in the same district?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ɔ mlɛo yɛ akrowai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli lɛ? Shi mibɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni makwɛ nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ kpokpaa kome lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ mli.

english: Even within the same district, different areas have different soil types, groundwater levels, and rainfall amounts. A crop that loves sandy, well-drained soil in one village will struggle in heavy clay soil in another.
ga: Yɛ kpokpaa kome nɔ po Hei srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ srɔtoi. shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo Nibii ni aduɔ ni sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ akrowa kome mli lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni yɔɔ akrowa kroko mli lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ.

english: How can I tell if a weak patch of crops on my farm is caused by poor soil or by a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ jɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo hela hewɔ?

english: Poor soil usually causes an entire area of crops to look uniformly short or yellowish. Diseases, on the other hand, often start on a few plants with specific spots, wilting, or holes on the leaves and spread outward to neighboring plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ haa ŋmɔji muu fɛɛ feɔ kuku loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, hela jeɔ shishi yɛ tsei fioo komɛi ni yɔɔ hei pɔtɛɛ komɛi, ŋmɔtɔ, loo bu yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ anɔ, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why did the pesticide spray I used work on one section of my farm but fail to clear insects in another section?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã ko nɔ shi etsuuu nii yɛ fã kroko nɔ lɛ?

english: Pesticides can fail if sprayed during the hot sun when the liquid evaporates quickly, or if applied during wind and rain. Additionally, insects might be at a different, tougher stage of growth in different parts of your field.
ga: Ekolɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsuuu nii kɛji akɛ afɔse amɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli ejaakɛ nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Aloo kɛji akɛ ashwie nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ, ekolɛ kooloi bibii hu yɛ dalɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto ni wa fe tsutsu lɛ mli yɛ hei srɔtoi. ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do my cassava stems look dry and stop leaking liquid when I cut them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbi ni nu ko hooo kɛji mifo amɛ lɛ?

english: Healthy cassava stems contain natural sap that flows when cut. When a plant loses this fluid, it is a clear warning sign of stem rot or severe water stress, showing that the plant is becoming sick and losing its vitality.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli nu ni hoɔ kɛjeɔ kpo kɛji afo lɛ yɛ cassava tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei lɛ fite nu nɛɛ Eji kɔkɔbɔɔ okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yitso lɛ egbo loo nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela mɔ tso lɛ, ni ebɛ hewalɛ dɔŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my maize plant is sick inside before the whole crop dies?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-abele tsei lɛ hela mɔ amɛ yɛ amɛmli dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ gboi?

english: You can carefully split open the stem of a struggling stalk. If the inside looks dark, brown, or hollow instead of firm and light-colored, it means fungi or stem borer insects are destroying the plant from the inside out.
ga: Obaanyɛ ogbala tsei ni miibɔi ŋmɔlɔ lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji emli lɛ tamɔ ediŋŋ, ŋmɔtɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee shiŋŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ miifite tso lɛ kɛmiijɛ emli kɛmiiya kponɔgbɛ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen in the soil. The plant copes by pulling nutrients from its older lower leaves to feed the young green leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei kwɛɔ enɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves wilt in the afternoon heat even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: This usually happens when root rot or bacterial wilt attacks the roots underground. Because the root system is damaged, it cannot pump water fast enough to keep the leaves upright during the hottest part of the day.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shishifãi ni egbo loo helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ tutua shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. yɛ shishifãi ni efite lɛ hewɔ No hewɔ lɛ anyɛɛɛ ajie nu oya bɔ ni sa ni baaha baai lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up into tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee kɔɔpoi ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by a virus spread by tiny whitefly insects. The virus disrupts how the plant grows, causing leaves to curl and reducing the plant's ability to produce good fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Virus tsiɔ tsei adalɛ naa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ewoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why are my young cocoa pods turning black and hard while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛhe wa be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, damp conditions. The fungus attacks the pod, killing the tissue inside and turning the outside dark and dry.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela lɛ he okadi. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Fungus tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ. Efiteɔ fãji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa kponɔgbɛ feɔ duŋ ni egbiɔ.

english: Why are my plantain leaves turning yellow and collapsing around the trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: This behavior often points to Panama disease or stem weevils attacking the base of the plant. The damage blocks water and food from moving up, causing the outer leaves to dry out and collapse.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ subaŋ nɛɛ tsɔɔ Panama hela loo stem weevils ni tutuaa tso lɛ shishigbɛ. Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ haaa nu kɛ niyenii aya ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why are full holes appearing in my cabbage leaves when I cannot see any insects on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu lɛ? Be ni minaaa kooloi bibii komɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many crop pests, like moth caterpillars, feed at night or hide underneath the leaves during the day to avoid the sun. Checking under the leaves early in the morning will help you spot them.
ga: Tsei amli kooloi babaoo, tamɔ ŋmeii, yeɔ nii gbɛkɛ loo amɛteeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai ashishi yɛ shwane mli koni hulu la akashɛ amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona amɛ.

english: Why do my crops look weak and pale green even after heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can wash away important nutrients from the topsoil deeper into the ground where short roots cannot reach, leaving the crops undernourished even though they have plenty of water.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ he ni shishifãi kukuji nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ jɛmɛ moŋ.

english: How can I know if my harvested yams are starting to spoil inside without cutting them open?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ ebɔi fitemɔ ni mifolɔɔɔ amɛ?

english: Spoiling yams usually feel soft near the top head or sprout end when pressed gently, or give off a faint sour smell. Sorting these soft tubers out early prevents rot from spreading to healthy yams nearby.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potatoes ni efite lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ loo naagbee ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ he kɛji akɛ anyɛ nɔ fioo loo ejieɔ ŋmɔlɔ fioo. Nɛkɛ bulb bibii nɛɛ ni aaahala mra Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if the first rain of the season is enough for me to start planting my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ?

english: You should not plant immediately after the very first rain because it might be a false start. Wait until the soil is moist down to at least a hand's depth and rain falls consistently over a few days, so your planted seeds do not sprout and dry up in the heat.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ ekolɛ eji amale shishijee. Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ tamɔ onine mli ni nugbɔ enɛɔ daa gbii 2-3 bɔni afee ni dumɔwui ni adu lɛ akakwɛ̃ ni amɛkagbi yɛ latsaa be mli.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same plot of land three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi aba. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act like natural shade umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to capture light and make food. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing diseases and helping the plant produce larger underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu lɛ mli koni amɛná la ni amɛfee niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally adapted to local conditions, allowing them to compete aggressively for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early gives your planted crops the room and food they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha otsei ni miida lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green again so the plant can grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ koni tso lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently damp and providing light shade during very hot weather helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni ehaa hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on maize leaves and funnels. Checking your field early and applying recommended control methods like approved sprays stops them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii. Kwɛmɔ odumɔi lɛ amli mra ni okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akudɔ amɛ tamɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii. Kpa nibii nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What causes my cassava tubers to turn soft and rot inside the ground before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa?

english: Cassava root rot usually happens when excess rainwater settles in heavy soil around the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps surplus water drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fitemɔ baa kɛji nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ gbee shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from last year's maize crop produce smaller yields than certified seeds from the shop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni shwapoi lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Many shop-bought seeds are specially bred hybrids designed to give high yields for only one harvest cycle. Saving and replanting those seeds causes the next generation to lose their vigor, resulting in smaller cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aheɔ yɛ shwapoi amli lɛ ji dumɔwui ni afee amɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be kome mli. Nibii ni abuɔ he kɛ nibii ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ baaha wɔsɛɛ yinɔi lɛ akaná hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dumɔwui bibii.

english: Seeds need equal space, water, and nutrients to grow uniformly. If seeds are planted too close together or if the soil strength varies slightly across the bed, the stronger plants will steal nutrients from the weaker ones, causing uneven growth.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ he ko, nu, kɛ niyenii kpakpai bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ srɔto fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ. Tsei ni he wa lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni jɛɔ dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ mli lɛ amli. ni kɛ dalɛ ni ejaaa baa

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant is missing nitrogen, which is essential plant food. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients out of the reach of the plant's roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ tsei shishifãi amli lɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of proper plant food. The plant drops flowers to save its energy for basic survival.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tso niyenii ni sa ni bɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha shishijee wala.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds from the agro-dealer instead of just planting seeds saved from my last maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔ dɛŋ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i du dumɔwuhi nɛ a he yi kɛ je ye nyagbe ngma kpami ɔ mi ɔ pɛ.

english: Certified seeds are developed through crop research to resist common pests and heat while growing evenly. Seeds saved from past harvests lose their strength over generations and often yield much less food.
ga: Afee dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amlipɛimɔ nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ kɛ dɔlɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa pɛpɛɛpɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli ni bei pii lɛ ewoɔ yibii fioo kwraa.

english: What happens if I plant my crops closer together than recommended so I can fit more plants on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ? Koni anyɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Planting too close forces crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of getting a bigger harvest, you get thin, weak plants that produce smaller fruits or smaller ears of maize.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooona yibii babaoo Obaagbe naa kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii bibii loo ŋmãa toi bibii.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my maize so the rain doesn't wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo ŋmãa mli koni nugbɔ akashwie nɔ?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is already moist, but not during heavy downpours. Placing it a few inches from the stem and covering it lightly with soil helps the roots absorb it before rain can carry it off.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ. Shi esaaa akɛ owoɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli. Okɛto he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ ni okɛ sũ aha he fioo. Enɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ lɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ ashwie lɛ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds from my farm even when my crops are already much taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ fe jwɛi lɛ momo moŋ.

english: Even small weeds under the crop canopy steal water and fertilizer from the soil below ground. Removing them ensures all the food in the soil goes directly to your crops.
ga: Jwɛi bibii po Yɛ tsei ashishi lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie lɛ, ebaatsɔɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ kɛya oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do agriculture officers advise me to plant beans or groundnuts in the field where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ mli yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of soil nutrients. Beans and groundnuts add natural nitrogen back into the soil through their roots, restoring soil fertility naturally for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Beans kɛ peanuts kɛ nitrogen kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Koni akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aba ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up during the hot afternoon even when the soil still has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛfeee nakai moŋ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: Leaves curl in high heat to protect themselves from losing too much water into the air. If the leaves uncurl once the sun goes down, it is a normal way the plant protects itself from the heat.
ga: Ha ni curl lɛ mli adɔ yɛ la ni mli wa nɔ koni nu ni fa fe nine akaje kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji baai lɛ shwie shi beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ Eji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he.

english: Why do my crops grow faster and greener after rain compared to when I water them by hand from the well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto nu ni akɛ niji shwieɔ kɛjɛɔ nu bu mli lɛ he?

english: Rainwater contains small amounts of natural nitrogen absorbed from the air, giving plants an instant food boost. Rain also thoroughly cools the air and wets the soil much deeper than surface watering by hand.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli nitrogen fioo ko ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ nugbɔ nu mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii ni afee klalo. Nugbɔ hu haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ babaoo fe nu ni akɛ niji shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants die when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that burn and dry out quickly under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them creates a protective shield until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ ehe lɛ haa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye hulu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and build leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure around the stem helps restore their green color and growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo baai. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni abɔleɔ he lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when they sit in waterlogged soil for too long because the roots cannot breathe. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away, keeping the roots safe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛtara shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛmu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: Yam leaves need to climb high to capture as much sunlight as possible. The more sunlight the leaves receive, the more energy the plant creates to grow large, heavy yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato baai lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni enyɛ emɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Babaoo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ baa lɛ náa lɛ, babaoo ni tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without growing into any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from hot weather, dry soil, or a sudden lack of water. Keeping the soil consistently moist during flowering helps the plant hold onto its blossoms so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni bɛ trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ewo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling up tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's sap. Spraying the leaves early with soapy water or neem oil helps clear the pests and allows fresh leaves to grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni ooofɔ baai lɛ anɔ mra Nu loo neem fɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ejie tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ, ni eye ebua baa heei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why won't I get a bigger harvest if I plant my seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibii babaoo nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving each plant proper space ensures every single plant grows strong enough to yield maximum produce.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ni sa lɛ, ebaaha eda waa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ yibii babaoo aba.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Having too many suckers causes them to steal food and water from the main mother plant. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant has enough food to produce big, heavy bunches.
ga: Suckers babaoo baaha amɛju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why does my soil dry out and crack so quickly just a few days after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbɛɔ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ lɛ?

english: Soil dries out quickly when it lacks organic matter, which acts like a sponge to hold moisture. Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the soil cool and prevents rainwater from evaporating.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli lɛ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do insects attack my cowpea crop as soon as the flowers start opening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea tsei lɛ kɛji amɛbɔi fɔmɔ pɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet nectar that naturally attracts pests like thrips and pod borers looking for food. Inspecting the field weekly and protecting the crops at the first sign of flowering prevents insects from destroying the young pods.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔii lɛ woɔ nu ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ gbalaa kooloi tamɔ thrips kɛ pod borers ni taoɔ niyenii lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ he ni okwɛɔ lɛ daa otsi ni obu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ewo fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi akafite ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Too much heat burns their delicate leaves and evaporates moisture faster than their roots can drink, causing the leaves to scorch and dry out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ baashã ebaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ aya oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why is my plantain tree producing very small bunches when there are many small shoots growing around its stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: The small shoots, called suckers, compete with the main parent tree for soil nutrients and water. Removing most of the extra suckers allows all the food to go to the main tree so it can form larger plantain bunches.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ suckers. Ekɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni ena niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ateŋ babaoo lɛ, niyenii lɛ fɛɛ yaa tso titri lɛ mli. bɔni afee ni ená plantain tsei wuji

english: Maize leaves curl inward during extreme heat to protect themselves and prevent water loss. Rolling up reduces the leaf area exposed to the sun, helping the plant conserve moisture until the temperature cools down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe ni amɛtsi nu ni elaaje lɛ naa. Kɛ́ ashɛre lɛ, ehaa baa lɛ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn plants turning yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the tips of older leaves usually means the soil is low in nitrogen. The plant is moving whatever nitrogen it has left to nourish the newer leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ miitsi nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know that my cassava tubers are ready to harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifã ko efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lowest leaves start turning yellow and falling off, the soil around the base begins to crack slightly, and the main stem becomes thick and woody.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa fioo. ni tso lɛ tso titri lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ tsei

english: Yam vines need to climb tall stakes to spread their leaves out in the sunlight. Sunlight enables the leaves to make food, which flows down to build large underground yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ ayaje hulu la lɛ nɔ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa

english: Why do my ginger roots rot in the ground when heavy rains make the soil soggy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ginger shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Ginger roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess water sits in the soil without draining away, it suffocates the roots and promotes root-rot fungi that decay the tubers.
ga: Ginger shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi ni fiteɔ nii ni kɛ tuber fitemɔ baa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Curling and twisted leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites, or by a plant virus spread by these insects as they feed on the sap.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa beni amɛyeɔ tsofa lɛ mli nu lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high, when the soil dries out completely, or when too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo be mli ni nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of green leaves but produce very few seed pods when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baa eŋɔli babaoo shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: When cowpeas get too much water and nitrogen, they put all their energy into leafy foliage instead of stress-induced flowering, which is required to form crop pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsina ŋmei nine shɛ nu kɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ lɛ, ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ ebaa lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi yɛ haomɔ hewɔ. ni he hiaa kɛha tsei amli ŋmeii lɛ afeemɔ

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, a vital food for leaf growth. The plant pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves, showing that your soil needs extra organic manure or fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baa lɛ dalɛ Tsei lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baa momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my farm make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmeii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which has roots that capture nitrogen directly from the air and leave it in the soil. This acts as free natural fertilizer for the crops you plant afterwards.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛshiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do small caterpillars crawl into the heart of my maize plants and eat the new leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii shwieɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai heei lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that prefers the soft, young inner leaves inside the whorl. Applying recommended treatments early in the morning when they feed stops them before they ruin the plant's growth point.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni fɔɔ baa ni sumɔɔ baa mli baai ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ tsu nii leebi beni amɛmiiye niyenii lɛ, ebaaha amɛkpa dani amɛfite hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and turn tight like a ball?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe tamɔ bɔɔlu lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips hiding underneath the leaves. These insects drain sap from the plant, causing the leaves to twist and distort as they grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ jieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from my young cassava plants regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmei tsei bibii amli daa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your cassava plants. Clearing them early gives the young cassava enough space and food to build thick stems and strong tubers under the ground.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ o-cassava tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha ŋmei bibii lɛ aná he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii ni wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why is it necessary to lift and tie my yam vines up on wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ awó sweet potato wain tsei anɔ ni akɛfi tsei ahe lɛ?

english: Staking gets the leaves off the wet ground so they catch full sunlight to make plant food. It also keeps the leaves dry and away from soil-borne fungal diseases that can rot the crop.
ga: Staking baajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo ni amɛkɛfee niyenii aha tso lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ hu mli egbiɔ ni ekɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni baanyɛ afite tso lɛ lɛ kpaaa gbee.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the stem without turning into fruits during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the weather is too hot and dry, tomato flowers drop as a defense response so the plant does not lose water trying to support new fruit. Providing shade or adequate watering helps flowers stay attached and form tomatoes.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni egbi Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi akɛ nɔ ni akɛbuɔ he. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ sɛɛ efooo be mli ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ewo yibii heei lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni sa ha lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛmaa shi yɛ tomatoi lɛ amli.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and squishy while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato aduawai lɛ ashishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo beni edaa lɛ?

english: This issue is blossom-end rot, caused by uneven watering that prevents the plant from moving calcium to the developing fruit. Keeping the soil consistently moist prevents the tissue at the base from collapsing.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ji blossom end rot, ni nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni haaa ekɛ calcium aya tso yibii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ baatsi fãji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's hybrid maize harvest grow poorly compared to new seeds from the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni jɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred from two distinct parent plants to produce high yields for one season only. Seeds saved from that harvest lose that special vigor, resulting in uneven sizes and lower yields in the next season.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔ̃ɔ tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ amli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ be kome pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ hewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dalɛi feɔ ekome ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do cocoa seeds fail to grow if I dry them in the sun before planting them in nursery bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ akwɛɛɛ kɛji migbi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani mikɛwo grow bag mli?

english: Cocoa seeds are sensitive seeds that die as soon as their moisture content drops. Unlike maize or bean seeds, cocoa seeds must be planted immediately after removing them from a fresh pod to keep them alive.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni gboiɔ kɛji ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ba shi pɛ. Esoro lɛ yɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa dumɔwui ahe. Esa akɛ adu kookoo ŋmeii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmeii heei lɛ amli lɛ koni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What does 'hybrid seed' mean, and how is it different from the seeds I save from my harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome’ lɛ shishi? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esoro lɛ yɛ dumɔwui ni mikɔ kɛjɛ nikpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: A hybrid seed is created by carefully crossing two different strong plant parents to combine their best traits, like resisting diseases and producing more grain. Seeds saved from your previous harvest lose these special traits over time, whereas fresh hybrid seeds grow into uniform plants that give much higher yields.
ga: Akɛ tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni he wa lɛ fɔlɔi ni akɛfoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ feɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ. koni akɛ sui ni hi fe fɛɛ, tamɔ helai ni nyɛɔ mɔ nɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni fa babaoo lɛ afata he. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee tsofa kroko lɛ daa kɛfeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ sui kome ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How do I choose the right maize variety to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmãa srɔtoi ni sa ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should choose a seed variety based on your area's rainfall pattern, your soil type, and how quickly the crop matures. Extension officers can recommend specific certified varieties that have been tested to perform best in your district.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala dumɔwui yɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ henɔ, kɛ bɔ ni tsei lɛ daa oya. Nitsulɔi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie tsofai srɔtoi pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ he odaseyeli ni aka amɛ akwɛ koni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ kpo.

english: If I plant hybrid maize this season, can I save the seeds from my harvest to plant again next year?
ga: Kɛji midu hybrid corn yɛ be nɛɛ mli Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni madu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: It is not recommended to replant seeds saved from hybrid maize. In the second generation, the crop loses its high-yield strength and will grow unevenly, so you need to buy fresh certified seeds each planting season for the best harvest.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli. Yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafite yibiiwoo babaoo ni ebaakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ koni onine ashɛ kpamɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ nɔ.

english: How can I increase the number of maize bags I harvest from my land this year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha ŋmãa kotokui ni mikpaa kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi nɛɛ aya hiɛ?

english: You can significantly increase your harvest by switching to certified high-yielding seeds, planting in neat rows with correct spacing, applying fertilizer at the right times, and keeping the field clean from weeds.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni yɔɔ odaseyeli lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo ni gbɛ ni ja yɔɔ mli. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ be ni sa mli. ni okwɛ koni ŋmɔji lɛ amli atse kɛjɛ jwɛi ahe

english: Why are some farmers in my district harvesting almost double the bags of maize compared to traditional methods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi ni yɔɔ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ miikpa ŋmãa ni miihe ashɛ shii enyɔ fe blema gbɛi lɛ?

english: Farmers getting higher yields are usually combining improved seed varieties with good farming practices, such as proper soil preparation, exact plant spacing, timely weeding, and balanced fertilizer use.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi ni náa yibii babaoo lɛ kɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛ okwaayeli nifeemɔi kpakpai tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ saamɔ kpakpa feɔ ekome. exact plant spacing Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be naa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni akɛtsuɔ nii

english: Do high-yielding maize varieties require more fertilizer and care than my local seeds?
ga: Ani ŋmãa henɔi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ biɔ ŋmãa babaoo kɛ ekwɛmɔ fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yes, because improved varieties grow faster and produce much larger cobs, they feed more heavily. Giving them adequate fertilizer, water, and weed protection allows them to reach their full harvest potential.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni dara kwraa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛyeɔ nii babaoo fe tsutsu lɛ. Nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa amɛ, nu kɛ jwɛi ahebuu lɛ haa amɛkpaa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants sometimes grow very tall but produce tiny or empty cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa waa shi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Aloo nɔ ko bɛ mli?

english: Tall plants with poor cobs often happen when you plant saved seeds of low quality, plant seeds too close together, or when the plants lack key nutrients and water during the critical flowering stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei kakadaji ni ŋmeii lɛ ehiii lɛ baa kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ehiii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ nu yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli.

english: How does planting my maize in straight rows help the crops grow better than broadcasting seeds?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni ja mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edaa jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Planting in rows ensures every crop gets equal access to sunlight, soil nutrients, and water without competing with neighboring plants. It also makes weeding, fertilizing, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ Ehaa jwɛi shwiemɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Will improved maize varieties survive better if the rain stops early in the season?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ni atsake lɛ baahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra yɛ be lɛ mli?

english: Many improved maize varieties are specially bred to mature early or tolerate dry spells better than local seeds, helping you secure a decent harvest even when the rainy season is short.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmãa henɔi babaoo ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛshwere oya loo amɛŋmɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ anaa jogbaŋŋ fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni onáa yibii kpakpai yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli po.

english: Is it really worth spending extra money to buy packaged seeds instead of using free seeds from my storehouse?
ga: Ani ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ akɛ mafite shika ni fa lɛ kɛhe dumɔwui ni awo mli lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni aheee nɔ ko kɛjɛ mi-stash lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii?

english: Yes, buying certified seed is a smart investment because the extra bags of harvest you get far outweigh the cost of purchasing the seed at the start of the season.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ ji shikawoo ni yɔɔ ŋaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kpamɔ kotokui krokomɛi ni onine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ fa kwraa fe shika ni akɛheɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ.

english: Why should I plant my seeds in nursery bags first instead of planting them directly into my farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli tsɔne mli klɛŋklɛŋ moŋ fe ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Nursery bags allow you to protect tender young seeds from harsh sunlight, heavy rain, pests, and weeds. It helps seeds sprout safely until they are strong enough to survive in the open field.
ga: Grow bags lɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ jwɛi ahe, ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ shweshweeshwe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: What kind of soil should I put inside nursery bags to help my seeds sprout well?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ esa akɛ mikɛwo mi-grow bags lɛ amli koni eye ebua midumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Use fertile topsoil mixed with well-rotted manure or compost. This combination stays soft enough for delicate new roots to grow easily while holding onto the moisture the seed needs to sprout.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ efutu mli lɛ atsu nii. Nɛkɛ futumɔ nɛɛ yaa nɔ ehiɔ shi bɔ ni sa ni ehaa shishifãi heei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ mlɛo yɛ be mli ni ehiɛɔ nu ni he hiaa dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ mli.

english: How often do I need to water my young crop while it is growing inside the nursery bag?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni mawo mi dumɔwui lɛ nu be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Water them lightly once or twice a day, preferably early in the morning or late in the evening. The goal is to keep the soil moist like a squeezed sponge, but not flooded with water.
ga: Nu fioo shikome loo shii enyɔ daa gbi. Esa akɛ afɔ nɔ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Otii ni ma ehiɛ ji ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ sponji ni ashɛre shi ekɛ nu akawo mli.

english: Do I need to take the plastic bag off before I put the plant into the ground on my farm?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni majie plastic kotokui lɛ dani mikɛ tsei awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, always gently slice open and remove the plastic nursery bag before planting. Leaving the bag on prevents the roots from spreading out into the soil, which will eventually kill the crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, be fɛɛ be lɛ, gbelemɔ plastic ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ blɛoo ni ojie mli dani odu. Kɛ́ oshi kotoku lɛ yɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaagbe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How do I know which crops need to be nursed in bags and which ones can go straight into the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni esa akɛ makwɛ nɔ yɛ kotoku mli lɛ? Ni mɛɛ tsei abaanyɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Crops with small, delicate seeds or slow-growing young shoots (like oil palm, tomatoes, and cocoa) need nursing. Tougher, larger seeds like corn, beans, or okra grow fast and can be planted directly in the farm.
ga: Tsei ni dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo loo ŋmeii bibii ni daa blɛoo (tamɔ mu tsei, tomato, kɛ kookoo) biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni wa, ni dara tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo okra daa oya ni abaanyɛ adu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are my palm nuts taking such a long time to sprout in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-palm dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Palm nuts have a very hard outer shell that water cannot easily pass through. They naturally take months to sprout unless you soak them, keep them warm, or crack the shell carefully to help water get inside.
ga: Palm ŋmeii yɛ kponɔgbɛ fã ko ni wa waa ni nu nyɛŋ atsɔ mli mlɛo. Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, amɛheɔ nyɔji babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. ja okɛwo nu mli ni oha amɛhe adɔ Aloo ogbala ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni nu abote mli.

english: Why do my young seedlings wilt and turn yellow when I move them out of the shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ mijie amɛ kɛjɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young plants raised under shade get shocked by sudden direct heat. You must gradually expose them to more sunlight over a week or two so they get used to the open farm conditions.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baahao amɛhe yɛ la ni tsoɔ trukaa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ hewɔ, no hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ hulu la babaoo awo amɛmli fiofio yɛ otsi kome loo enyɔ mli. Koni amɛtsɔse amɛhe kɛgbele ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi amli

english: Why does the way I prepare my farm land depend on the type of planting material I am using?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bɔ ni misaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha okwaayeli lɛ damɔ nibii ni mikɛduɔ nii lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Different planting materials—like seeds, stem cuttings, or nursery seedlings—need different hole sizes, soil depths, and spacing to spread their roots and get enough nutrients to grow properly.
ga: Dumɔ nibii srɔtoi tamɔ dumɔwui, tsei ni afolɔ, loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ. Ehe miihia ni bu lɛ dalɛ afee shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ kɛ he ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ srɔtoi koni akɛgbɛ shishifãi lɛ ashwã ni ana niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell when a seedling in my nursery bag is ready to be planted in the main field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli kotokui lɛ amli lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ saatso wulu lɛ nɔ?

english: A seedling is ready when it has developed a thick stem, several green leaves, and roots that have filled out the nursery bag soil without coiling tightly at the bottom.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo kɛji amɛyɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse. Baai eŋɔlii babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. kɛ shishifãi ni eyiɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ ni ekɛ shishigbɛ lɛ ekpɛtɛɛɛ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will starting my crops in nursery bags give me a better harvest than planting straight into the ground?
ga: Ani tsei ni ajeɔ shishi yɛ grow bags amli lɛ baaha yibii kpakpai aba fe ni aaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, nursing usually leads to a better harvest because it allows you to select only the healthiest, strongest seedlings for your farm while rejecting weak or diseased ones early on.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsɔsemɔ kɛ ŋmaa kpakpa baa. Ejaakɛ ehaa onyɛɔ ohalaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni mli wa fe fɛɛ pɛ kɛhaa oŋmɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ajieɔ dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli mra.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when I clear away all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants behave like shade-loving forest plants; their leaves burn easily under direct sunlight. They need partial shade from larger trees like plantains or timber to keep the surrounding air humid and protect their leaves while young.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ koo mli tsei ni sumɔɔ hulutsoo. Baai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo ko kɛjɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains loo tsei ahe. Enɛ ji koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli ahi fɛ̃i mli, ni ebu ebaai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ oblahiiaŋ ŋmɔnɔ he.

english: Why can I leave my mature cassava plants in the ground for months without the roots rotting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ manyɛ mashi ŋmei tso ni eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nyɔji babaoo ni shishifãi lɛ egbooo lɛ?

english: Cassava plants treat their thick roots as underground storage tanks. As long as the plant remains alive in the soil, the roots stay fresh and keep storing starch until you decide to harvest them.
ga: Cassava tso lɛ hiɛɔ eshishifãi ni mli tse lɛ anɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nutoohe. Be fɛɛ be ni tso lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baahi shi ni amɛhiɛ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛyashi obaakpɛ oyiŋ akɛ obaakpa amɛ.

english: Why do my yam plants need wooden stakes to climb on instead of just spreading on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally seek height to spread their leaves toward maximum sunlight. Lifting the stems off the warm, moist soil prevents fungal diseases and allows the leaves to trap more energy to build larger underground tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei taoɔ he ko ni nɔ kwɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaa lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Kɛ́ ajie tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmeii ahe helai anaa, ni ehaa baai lɛ toɔ hewalɛ babaoo koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up tightly into narrow tubes during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni etsɔɔ tsɔne bibioo ko mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Rolling up leaves is a self-defense mechanism. By curling their leaves inward during hot periods, maize plants protect their leaf pores from direct heat and reduce the amount of water escaping into the dry air.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he. Abɛi buɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ mli yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ. ni eha nu ni hoɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi mli lɛ aba shi

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress or sudden dry soil. The plant drops the flowers to save its strength and water rather than spending energy trying to grow new fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe hulutsoo loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi trukaa lɛ he. Tso lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ ni okɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni odu aduawai heei lɛ

english: Why do new shoot suckers keep growing out from the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei heei miikwɛ̃ kɛmiijɛ mi plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Plantain plants produce underground stems that naturally shoot up suckers. This is how the plant reproduces itself, ensuring a replacement stem grows to take over once the main mother stem produces fruit and dies.
ga: Plantains woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni shwereɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Nɛkɛ ji bɔ ni tsei fɔɔ amɛhe amɛhaa. Enɛ haa tsei ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ lɛ daraa koni amɛye amɛnajiaŋ beni fɔlɔ tso lɛ titri lɛ woɔ yibii ni egboɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cashew trees shed almost all their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves during the dry season is a natural survival strategy for cashew trees. By shedding leaves, the tree stops losing water through evaporation, protecting its trunk and roots until the rainy season returns.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahiɔ shi kɛha cashew tsei. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ haa tso lɛ kpaɔ nu ni efiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Buu etso lɛ kɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants turn yellow when rainwater collects and stays on the field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ bua ehe naa ni ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen from the soil to breathe. When water stays pooled around the roots for too long, the roots suffocate, stop taking up nutrients, and cause the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Tso shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Ekpaa niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does my oil palm tree produce flowers sometimes, but no fruit bunches form on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, mu tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi shi amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees produce separate male and female flowers on the same tree. When the tree suffers from water lack or heat stress, it tends to produce only male pollen flowers instead of the female flowers that produce fruit bunches.
ga: Mu tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi yɛ tso kome nɔ. Kɛ tso lɛ na nu ni faaa loo dɔlɛ he haomɔ Bei pii lɛ, tsei woɔ stamens pɛ yɛ fɔfɔi amli. Yɛ fɔfɔi yei ni woɔ aduawai akuu lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Is it true that planting groundnuts or cowpeas makes the soil better for my next crop of maize?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, leguminous plants like groundnuts and cowpeas have tiny bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, providing natural plant food for the next crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ helatsɛmɛi bibii ni heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. koni akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Why do my crops start getting diseased right after the rainy season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jeɔ hela shishi lɛ?

english: Rain creates wet and humid conditions that allow microscopic fungi and diseases to spread rapidly. Water droplets resting on leaves give plant diseases the perfect environment to infect healthy crops.
ga: Nugbɔ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Nu mli nu ni shwieɔ shi ni kpɛtɛɔ baai ahe lɛ haa tsei amli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ naa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ hela.

english: Can I spread sickness to my crops just by walking through my field?
ga: Ani manyɛ magbɛ hela ashwã miŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛtsɔ miŋmɔji amli ni miiya kɛkɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, walking through wet or infected crops causes your body, clothes, and farm tools to rub against disease spores. You then carry these spores to healthy plants as you walk, spreading the sickness across your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni efɔ loo ni hela emɔ mli lɛ amli nyiɛmɔ haa helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai shwieɔ gbɔmɔtso lɛ, atadei, kɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii anɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ yaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli beni onyiɛɔ lɛ. Gbalamɔ hela lɛ mli yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Is it better to spray my crops before I see diseases, or should I wait until the plants get sick?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaafɔ tsei anɔ tsofa dani hela lɛ ana? Aloo esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi tso lɛ baaye hela?

english: It is always better to spray preventive chemicals before diseases appear. Once a plant is infected and showing symptoms, severe damage has already happened, making it much harder to save your crop and protect your yield.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be akɛ ooofɔ tsofai ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ anɔ dani hela aba. Beni hela lɛ emɔ tsei ni amɛjie hela lɛ he okadii akpo lɛ, afite nibii ni mli wa momo. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ oookwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni obu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: How do I know the right age or time to start spraying my crops with protective medicine?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male afii loo be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi tsofa ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ shwiemɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Most crops need protective spraying when they reach four to five months old, especially when the early rains start, because this is when plants become most vulnerable to fungal attack.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo biɔ ni akɛ tsofa ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ ashwie nɔ kɛji tsei lɛ eye nyɔji ejwɛ kɛyashi enumɔ. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ji mɛi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ atutua amɛ waa.

english: What kind of medicine should I spray to stop dark or moldy spots from killing my crop leaves?
ga: Mɛɛ tsofa esa akɛ mikɛtsu nii koni black spot loo fungus akagbe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai?

english: Leaf spots are usually caused by fungal diseases. Using a copper-based fungicide, such as Funguran, coats the leaves and stops fungal spores from germinating and damaging the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei hela kɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ baa. Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akɔɔble yɔɔ mli, tamɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfite tso lɛ.

english: What happens if heavy rain falls immediately after I spray medicine on my crops?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain can wash away the protective chemical before it has time to dry or be absorbed by the plant. It is best to spray on clear mornings when the rain has paused so the medicine sticks to the leaves.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ dani amɛná be ni amɛgbi loo tsei lɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie nɔ leebi ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa koni tsofa lɛ akpɛtɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Can I mix different crop medicines together to spray my farm faster?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafutu tsofai kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi. kɛfata he koni akɛshwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ oya?

english: Not all crop chemicals can be safely mixed. Mixing the wrong products can burn your plant leaves or destroy the power of the medicine, so you should always ask an extension officer before combining sprays.
ga: Jeee tsofai fɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni abaanyɛ afutu mli shweshweeshwe. Tsofa ni ejaaa ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ baai lɛ loo efite bɔ ni tsofa lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ obi mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ be fɛɛ be dani okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ afutu mli.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly and catch sickness easily when my farm is full of weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ ni helai baa mɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni jwɛi eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and nutrients from your crops, making the plants weak. Weak crops cannot easily fight off sickness, and thick weeds also trap moisture and hide pests that carry disease.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. gbɔjɔmɔ tso lɛ Nibii ni egbɔjɔ lɛ nyɛŋ awuu ashi hela mlɛo. Ni jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛ kooloi ni kɛ helai baa lɛ teeɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow and dropping off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi oya lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves can mean the soil is missing essential food like nitrogen, or that excess water is rotting the root system. Proper field drainage and correct fertilizer application help keep leaves green and healthy.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eha shishifãi lɛ egbo. Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Will applying fertilizer cure the diseases that are currently attacking my crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni etsa hela ni tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: No, fertilizer acts as food to help a plant grow, but it cannot kill diseases or pests. You must use specific disease-fighting medicines like fungicides to stop crop infections.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa. Shi enyɛŋ egbe muawai loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Esa akɛ okɛ tsofai pɔtɛɛ tamɔ fungicides atsu nii ni okɛkpa hela ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ.

english: Why do so many of my young crops die right after I plant them out in the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ateŋ babaoo gboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young plants suffer from transplant shock and have tiny root systems that cannot reach water deep underground. If the topsoil dries out even for a few days right after planting, the seedlings cannot survive.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ naa hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe waa, ni eyɛ shishifã bibioo ko. ni nyɛŋ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ gĩ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi.

english: How do I know the exact right time to start planting when the rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mije dumɔ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain shower, as it might be a false start to the season. Wait until the soil is thoroughly wet deep enough to fit your finger, showing that the steady rainy season has truly established.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ejaakɛ ekolɛ ebaafee be lɛ shishijee ni ejaaa. Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ onine lɛ ashɛ he. Etsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ eje shishi diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Is it better to water my crops heavily once a week or a little bit every day during dry weather?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaaha ŋmɔshi nibii amli nu babaoo shikome yɛ otsi mli loo fioo daa gbi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Watering heavily fewer times a week is better because deep watering encourages roots to grow downward searching for moisture, making the crop stronger and more drought-resistant.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli shii abɔ fioo, shikome yɛ otsi mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ, ejaakɛ nu ni mli kwɔ woɔ shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shishi koni amɛtao ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛshiɔ hɔmɔ.

english: What can I do to keep my young plants alive when the dry season starts earlier than expected?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni midumɔwui lɛ ahi shi beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi mra fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: You can protect young crops by placing temporary shade over them using palm fronds and covering the soil around their stems with dry leaves or grass to lock in whatever moisture is left in the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛtsɔ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo ni okɛaaha tsei lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmei baai ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ. Ni okɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ he koni ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahi shi.

english: How does putting dry leaves or grass around the stems of my crops help them grow?
