ga: Baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he Te tsei ashishifãi yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: This practice is called mulching. It acts like a protective blanket over the soil, stopping the hot sun from evaporating soil water and keeping the roots cool during hot days.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Efeɔ enii tamɔ kuntu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekafee nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Will strong, hot sunshine kill my young crops if the rain stops falling?
ga: Ani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baafite minibii kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛ?

english: Yes, intense sun causes young crops to sweat out water faster than their short roots can pull it from dry soil, causing them to dry up and die quickly.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ latsaa oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi kukuji lɛ baanyɛ agbala amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ gĩɔ ni egboɔ oya.

english: How can I tell if my crops are drooping because of lack of water or because of disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu ni bɛ loo hela hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbee shi lɛ?

english: Water-stressed crops usually droop during the hottest part of the day and perk up in the cool evening, whereas diseased crops remain wilted or show spots and yellowing regardless of the time of day.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni nu bɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ loo amɛnáa ŋmeii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ekɔɔɔ gbi lɛ mli be he.

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out much faster after rain than my neighbor's farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ fe mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Soils with a lot of sand lose water quickly because the particles are big, whereas clay or organic-rich soils hold water like a sponge. Mixing manure or decomposed plant waste into your soil helps it hold moisture longer.
ga: Shikpɔji ni ŋã babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nu fiteɔ oya yɛ bɔ ni ŋã bibii lɛ dara ha lɛ hewɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ sũ loo sũ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ hiɛɔ nu mli tamɔ sponji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsei ni egbo lɛ futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: If most of my crops die during a dry spell, can I plant new ones immediately in the same field?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii babaoo gboi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli Ani manyɛ madu tso hee amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: No, you should wait until regular rains return or proper irrigation is set up, because planting fresh seeds into dry, hot soil will cause the new plants to die just like the first batch.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba loo oto nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui heei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baaha tsei heei lɛ agboi tamɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kuu lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Are there specific crops or seeds I can buy that survive long dry periods better?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii loo dumɔwui pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ mahe ni baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, agricultural extension offices offer improved drought-tolerant seed varieties that require less water and can survive unexpected dry spells much better than traditional seeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ kɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ haa. Amɛbiɔ nu fioo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni akpaaa gbɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe blema dumɔwui.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I clear away all the big shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mijie cacao tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily in direct sunlight and dry out fast. Keeping tall shade trees or planting plantains around them provides shelter and preserves the soil moisture young cocoa needs to grow strong.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛkwɛ̃ waa lɛ ahi shi ni ekwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves at the bottom of my maize stalks turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the plant stay green and grow heavy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. ni ji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛnáa ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce thin roots when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need space underground to expand and soak up nutrients and water. When planted too close, the plants compete with each other, resulting in thin, weak yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he miihia cassava shishifãi lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu. Kɛji adu ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe baatswa akaŋ. Enɛ haa yibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: What is making holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants and leaving small dark droppings?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-baby corn plants lɛ miifee bu yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ ni amɛshiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ diŋ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the center of young maize plants. Checking your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract can protect your crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni taoɔ niyenii yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ yi lɛ atsu nii lɛ baanyɛ abu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: How does adding dead leaves and animal manure around my crops help them grow?
ga: Baai ni egboi kɛ kooloi afɔfɔi ni akɛfataa he lɛ Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Dead leaves and manure break down into organic matter, which feeds the soil, holds moisture like a sponge during dry spells, and provides natural nutrients to your crops.
ga: Baai ni egboi kɛ kooloi afɔfɔi lɛ fãa kɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli tamɔ sponji yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii haa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Having too many shoots (suckers) steals food and water from the main plantain tree. Keeping only two or three strong shoots ensures the main tree bears large, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko ná ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo lɛ, ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ adara babaoo ni etsii.

english: Flowers drop when the weather gets too hot and dry, or if the soil lacks enough water and nutrients. Mulching the soil around the pepper plant and regular watering keeps the plant cool enough to set fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa Mulching ni akɛbɔle Pepper tsei lɛ ahe kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ baaha amɛhe afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why is it good for my soil if I plant cowpeas in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that catch nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil. This naturally fertilizes the ground, which helps the maize grow better without needing as much commercial fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni jarayeli ŋmãa babaoo he ehiaaa lɛ.

english: Why do my planted seeds rot in the ground if I plant right after the very first light rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first light rain often does not soak deep into the soil, leaving the ground hot underneath. If rain stops for several days after, the seeds get trapped in hot, dry dirt and rot before they can sprout.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ eboteee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ yɛ shishi lɛ Kɛji nugbɔ kpa nɛmɔ gbii babaoo yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ muji ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ mli ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread a plant virus. Controlling whiteflies early with soaps or organic sprays prevents the virus from damaging your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Whitefly Kudɔmɔ Mra Kɛ okɛ organic samla loo spray tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ akafite onibii.

english: Why do I often get headaches or feel sick after spraying my maize farm with chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, miyitso tswaa mi loo hela mɔɔ mi beni mikɛ tsofai eshwie ŋmãa ŋmɔ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Chemical pesticides can easily enter your body through your skin or when you breathe in the mist. Wearing protective clothing or switching to natural pest control solutions like neem leaf extracts protects your body from chemical poisoning.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi baanyɛ abote gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli oya kɛtsɔ hewolo nɔ loo kɛ́ omu afua lɛ. Atadei ni buɔ mɔ he loo otsake kɛya adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi tamɔ neem baa mli nu lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu ogbɔmɔtso lɛ he kɛjɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei ahe.

english: Is it safe for my goats to eat weeds that were sprayed with chemical weedkiller?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mitooi lɛ baaye jwɛi ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ efɔ nɔ?

english: No, weedkillers leave poisonous residues on plants that can sicken or kill your farm animals. You must wait several weeks after spraying before letting animals graze near treated areas.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shĩɔ tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni baanyɛ aha oŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ aná hela loo amɛgbe amɛ lɛ anɔ. Esa akɛ omɛ otsii babaoo yɛ be mli ni okɛ tsofa lɛ eshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani oha kooloi lɛ aye niyenii yɛ he ni atsa amɛ lɛ masɛi.

english: Can I get a good crop yield without buying expensive chemical fertilizers?
ga: Ani mana yibii kpakpai ni miheee tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni jara wa?

english: Yes, using cow manure, poultry droppings, compost, and planting leguminous crops like cowpeas returns vital nutrients to the soil naturally, feeding your crops well without costly chemicals.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmei, kooloi ŋmei, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha onibii lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ tsofai ni jara wa akatsu nii.

english: Why does my farmland become hard and dry so quickly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i ni egbiɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Relying only on chemical fertilizers without adding organic matter destroys earthworms and natural microbes that keep soil loose. Adding animal manure and mulching keeps moisture inside the soil longer.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai pɛ tsu nii ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he lɛ, ebaakpata shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii bibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahiɛ. Koolooi ashishifã kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow even after I apply synthetic fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee lɛ woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Too much chemical fertilizer can burn plant roots and spoil the natural balance of the soil. Soil needs organic matter like compost to help roots absorb nutrients properly without getting damaged.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ babaoo baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, koni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛŋɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfiteee.

english: How does burning cleared weeds on my land affect my future crops?
ga: Te jwɛi ni ajie yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ashãa lɛ saa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Burning destroys the rich organic matter, beneficial soil organisms, and moisture needed for crop growth. Leaving cleared weeds to rot back into the ground turns them into natural manure for your next planting.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa lɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ oha jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ shwie shi ekoŋŋ kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What traditional methods can I use to stop pests from destroying my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛɛ blema gbɛi manyɛ matsɔ nɔ matsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkafite mi-pepper tsei lɛ?

english: Planting strong-smelling crops like onions or marigolds next to your peppers naturally confuses and repels insects. You can also spray a natural mixture of soapy water and wood ash to keep bugs away.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni he yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ waa, tamɔ sabolai loo marigolds yɛ ŋmeii ahe lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afutu ni ebaashwie amɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ adebɔɔ mli samla kɛ tso sũ ni akɛfutu mli lɛ hu afɔse kooloi bibii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees suffer from so many diseases compared to the older farms my grandfather managed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ helai srɔtoi yeɔ mi kokoo tsei lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛto ŋmɔ momo ni minaa kwɛɔ nɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Older traditional farms kept diverse shade trees that protected cocoa crops and maintained healthy soil cover. Clearing all trees and depending entirely on chemical sprays lowers the plants' natural resistance over time.
ga: Kusum ŋmɔji ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ yɛ tsei srɔtoi ni haa hulu tsoɔ koni ebu kookoo tsei lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ kwraa ni akɛ he fɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ kwraa lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni ekɛteɔ shi ewoɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and dying even when I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread crop viruses. Spraying a mixture of neem oil and soapy water deters these insects without destroying the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ kɛ nu ni akɛ samla efutu mli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa ni eyeee shikpɔŋ lɛ awui.

english: How can I store my harvested maize without using chemical preservation powders?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ ato ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛbuɔ ŋmãa he lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can mix well-dried maize with clean wood ash or dried neem leaves in tight containers. The ash and neem prevent insects like weevils from damaging the grain safely without contaminating your food.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmãa ni egbi afutu tso sũ ni he tse loo neem baai ni egbi yɛ tsɛnsi ko ni mli wa mli. Ashwishwɛ kɛ neem tsiɔ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii anaa shweshweeshwe koni amɛkafite dumɔwui ni amɛfiteee oniyenii lɛ.

english: Why are tiny worms eating the middle leaves of my young maize plants and leaving holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni amɛshiɔ bu lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by fall armyworms, which hide inside the growing core (whorl) of young maize plants. They feed on the tender young leaves, leaving behind large ragged holes and frass (waste) that looks like sawdust.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fallworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni miida lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ. Eshiɔ buji agboi ni ekpɔtɔ kɛ ŋmeii (shards) ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ yɛ esɛɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark black and dying before they get big enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast during wet, humid weather. It attacks the skin of the pod, eventually destroying the beans inside if the diseased pods are not removed or treated.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso, ni hulu lɛ miitso. Etutuaa pod lɛ hewolo lɛ. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, efiteɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛji ajieee ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ loo atsaaa amɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves have a white dust on them that makes them dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ yɛ sũ yɛŋ ni haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ lɛ?

english: This white powder is powdery mildew, a fungal disease that thrives when airflow around plants is low and humidity is high. It blocks the leaves from absorbing sunlight, causing them to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Nɛkɛ powda yɛŋ nɛɛ ji powda ni mli ewo muji. Eji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni baa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ko bɔle ehe. Tsei lɛ baa shi ni amɛyɛ hulutsoo babaoo. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ hulu la. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, mites, or aphids sucking sap from the leaf undersides, or by a viral infection spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. loo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli

english: Why are my maize plants growing very tall and thin but not producing any cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miida ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ shi amɛbɛ ŋmeii ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Maize plants grow tall and weak without producing cobs when planted too close together or when there is a lack of nitrogen in the soil. The plants spend all their energy fighting for light instead of making cobs.
ga: Abɛi daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ŋmeii bɛ mli kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛwuɔ koni amɛná la moŋ fe ni amɛaama ŋmeii.

english: Why do my cassava leaves drop off when the weather gets very dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods as a natural survival mechanism to conserve water. Once the rains return, the stem will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni bulb lɛ baaya nɔ eda.

english: Why do my okra flowers drop off the stem without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi roselle fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Okra flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress, such as sudden dry spells, extreme heat, or a lack of pollinators like bees to fertilize the blossoms.
ga: Rosella fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na haomɔi tamɔ trukaa ni egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo nibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni baahã fɔfɔi lɛ aná fɔmɔ nii lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall in one part of my farm but stay small and yellow in another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã ko nɔ lɛ? Shi eji bibioo ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ fã kroko?

english: Variations in growth are caused by uneven soil quality, differences in water drainage, shaded spots from nearby trees, or areas where topsoil has washed away during heavy rain.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ dalɛ ni tsakeɔ baa. different drainage He ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ loo hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋwɛi fã lɛ hoɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow in a V-shape from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the tip of the lower leaf and moves down the middle in a V-pattern indicates a nitrogen deficiency, meaning the plant needs organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer to build green foliage.
ga: Su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni etsɔɔ teŋgbɛ yɛ V gbɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei he miihia humus loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the wind blows during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can easily rot or get damaged by root-eating pests (nematodes). When heavy fruit bunches form and the soil becomes soft from rain, the weak roots can no longer hold the heavy tree upright.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni baanyɛ afite oya loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ. (Nematodes) Beni aduawai ni tsii baa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ hewɔ. Shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ nyɛŋ amɔmɔ tso ni tsii ni eŋmɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes rot so quickly before I can transport them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani anyɛɔ akɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes have thin skin and high water content, making them spoil quickly when exposed to sun and heat. Harvesting them early in the morning while it is cool and storing them in airy crates prevents bruising and slows down rotting.
ga: Tomato hewolo lɛ yɛ mlɛo, ni nu babaoo yɛ mli. Enɛ haa tomato fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ shɛ enɔ. Kɛ́ akpa amɛ leebi be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso ni akɛto adeka ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛkafite ni amɛbaafite sɛɛ.

english: Why do small insects turn my stored dried maize into powder after just a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tsɔ mi-ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ mli lɛ etsɔ powda yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize weevils lay eggs inside dry grains and eat them from the inside out. Drying your maize until it is crack-dry and storing it in airtight bags or treating it with approved grain storage dust stops weevils from multiplying.
ga: Abɛi mli ŋmeii woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmeii ni egbi mli ni amɛyeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Kɛ́ ogbala o-corn lɛ mli kɛyashi ebaakpã ni okɛwo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli loo okɛ sũ ni akɛtoɔ ŋmaa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu he nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akafɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers start sprouting and shrinking while stored in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ bɔi shweremɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ beni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally break dormancy after a few months to prepare for new growth. As the sprout grows, it drinks water and energy from the tuber itself, causing the yam to shrivel and lose weight.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ fãa nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ koni amɛsaa amɛhe kɛha dalɛ hee. Kɛji dumɔwu lɛ da Ebaanu nu kɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ eyitso mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why are my maize plants producing smaller cobs this year compared to two years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miiwo ŋmãa fioo ko pɛ afi nɛɛ fe afii enyɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of soil nutrients, especially nitrogen. Planting maize on the exact same plot year after year drains the soil, so rotating the land with legumes like cowpeas restores nutrients for bigger cobs.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. titri lɛ nitrogen Abele ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu atsɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsake he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba ŋmeii wuji lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds around my plantain suckers cause the plants to take much longer to yield fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni bɔle mi dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ miiha tsei lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with plantains for groundwater, sunlight, and fertilizer. Clearing weeds around the plant base ensures the plantain gets all the food it needs to mature quickly and produce heavy bunches.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ plantains yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Shishitoo lɛ haa plantain lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ eda oya ni ewo aduawai babaoo.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, shaded conditions. Pruning shade trees and removing infected pods lets air and sunlight in, stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni aaafolɔ ashwie shi ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la abote mli. Koni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and stop growing during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids that thrive during hot, dry periods. They suck sap from the young leaves, causing them to wrinkle, stunt growth, and produce fewer peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ. haa tsitsii ni etsilɛ lɛ daalɛ baa shi ni ehaa chili fioo pɛ baa

english: Cassava continues to grow underground, but as the plant gets older, it converts soft starch into tough wood fiber. Harvesting at the right age keeps the roots tender and good for cooking.
ga: Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lolo. Shi kɛ́ tso lɛ da lɛ Etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ efeɔ tso tsɔji ni wa. Kɛ́ akpa yɛ afii ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee blɛoo ni ehi kɛha nihoomɔ.

english: Why do my bean plants drop their flowers without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa baaa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat or sudden dry spells during the flowering stage place heavy stress on the plant. To survive, the bean plant sheds its flowers instead of spending energy to produce seeds.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo ŋmɔlɔ ni baa trukaa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tso lɛ nɔ. koni amɛhi shi Bean tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛwo dumɔwui.

english: Cabbage heads split when heavy rain or excessive watering follows a dry period. The inside of the cabbage absorbs water quickly and grows faster than the outer leaves can stretch, causing it to crack open.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei lɛ baagbala kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo nu ni awoɔ fe nine yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei asɛɛ. Kaabeji lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni edaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. kɛ mligbalamɔ baa

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. This can happen if the soil is poor or if heavy rains have washed the nutrients out of reach of the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Enɛ baanyɛ aba mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why are my hot pepper fruits staying small and dropping off before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper yibii lɛ ji bibii ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers and small fruits when they experience stress, usually caused by irregular watering, extreme heat, or a lack of calcium and potassium in the soil.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai bibii. Je kpo kɛ́ okɛ haomɔ kpe. Bei pii lɛ nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni ashwieɔ shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo calcium kɛ potassium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers, but most of them drop off without turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi amɛteŋ babaoo gbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed extra flowers they cannot support, but excessive flower drop happens when the tree lacks water, is attacked by insects like capsids, or doesn't get enough shade during hot spells.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi krɛdɛɛi ni anyɛɛɛ akwɛ nɔ. Shi fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi fe nine lɛ baa kɛji nu bɛ tso lɛ mli. Koolooi tamɔ capsids tutuaa lɛ loo enaaa hulutsoo be ni sa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning black and wet during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads in cold, damp conditions with low light. Excess rain splashes the fungus from the ground onto the lower pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni mli ejɔ, ni edɔ ni la fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa ŋmeii ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting underground before I even dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mifolɔ amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil around them for too long without draining away, creating a damp environment where harmful root fungi can easily grow and destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ lɛ. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa Shishifãi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ adara ni efite ŋmeii lɛ oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling tightly upward and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho kɛmiiya ŋwɛi ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects called whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and spread a virus, or it can be a natural defense mechanism when the plant is short of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly ni shwieɔ tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa Aloo ebaanyɛ efee adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu.

english: Why are the leaves of my plantain suckers turning yellow at the edges and drying up fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ ni amɛmiigbi oya lɛ?

english: This drying is often caused by a fungal infection like Panama disease or Sigatoka, which clogs the stem and prevents water and nutrients from moving from the roots up to the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko, tamɔ Panama hela loo Sigatoka ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ baa. ni tsiɔ tso lɛ shishi ni ehaaa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ akajɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛya baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I plant my cassava on soil mounds or ridges instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ nɔ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmei?

english: Mounds keep the soil loose so the root tubers can expand easily without resistance, while also raising the plant so water drains away quickly and doesn't rot the roots.
ga: Gɔji yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya ni nɔ ko nɔ ko akatsi amɛnaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ewoɔ tso lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni nu lɛ anyɛ aho kɛya oya, ni ehaaa eshishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Why does spear grass keep growing back so quickly on my farm even after I clear it completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ spear jwɛi lɛ miida oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mijie kɛjɛ mli moŋ?

english: Spear grass has deep underground roots called rhizomes that store food. Cutting the grass above ground leaves the roots alive, allowing the weed to push up fresh green shoots within days.
ga: Spear jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni atsɛɔ amɛ rhizomes ni akɛtoɔ niyenii. Kɛ́ afo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi. Ha jwɛi lɛ ashɛre ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli.

english: Why are my yam seed pieces taking so long to sprout after I plant them in the mound?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo gɔŋ ko mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers go through a natural resting phase called dormancy after harvest. If you plant them while they are still dormant, or if the soil inside the mound is too dry and hot, they will delay sprouting until conditions improve.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu amɛ be mli ni amɛwɔ lolo, loo kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni edɔ Ebaaha amɛkwɛ̃mɔ asɛɛ afo kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees yield more pods when I manage a small four-acre farm myself compared to a large farm where I employ caretakers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe be mli ni mi diɛŋtsɛ mikwɛɔ ŋmɔ bibioo ko ni dalɛ ji acre 4 lɛ nɔ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto ŋmɔji wuji ni mihe mɛi ni kwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ahe lɛ,.

english: Cocoa trees respond directly to close attention and regular care. When you personally weed, prune, and check for pests frequently on a smaller plot, the trees stay healthier and produce higher yields than on larger farms where caretakers might miss early signs of disease or neglect maintenance.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ amɛ daa. Beni bo diɛŋtsɛ oojie jwɛi, ookpa jwɛi, ni okwɛɔ kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ he ko bibioo lɛ bei pii lɛ. Tsei lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔji wuji amli. Mɛi ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ana hela he okadii mra loo amɛku amɛhiɛ amɛshwie nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ.

english: Traditional cocoa trees usually start bearing fruit within four to five years, but improved hybrid varieties developed in Ghana can start producing pods in as little as two to three years if they receive good water and soil nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema cacao tsei lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii ejwɛ kɛyashi enumɔ mli. Shi ŋmeii srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni afee yɛ Ghana lɛ baanyɛ aje ŋmeii afeemɔ shishi yɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ mli kɛji amɛná nu kpakpa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kpakpai.

english: Young cocoa trees do not like direct, intense sunlight or severe dry spells. Without enough shade trees or water, the sun burns their leaves and stresses the plant, causing it to drop leaves to save water.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ sumɔɔɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo hulu la ni mli egbi. Kɛji tsei loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha hulutsoo lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu nu he.

english: Why do small cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the tree before they ever grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii Koni amɛtsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ tsei anɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is often caused by a fungal disease called black pod or a natural process where the tree sheds extra pods it cannot support. Excess moisture, bad ventilation, or nutrient shortage usually triggers this behavior.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ pod blackening loo adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni haa tso lɛ shwieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii Loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni fɔɔ nɛkɛ subaŋ nɛɛ baa.

english: How far apart should I space my cocoa trees when planting a new farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo mi-kokoo tsei lɛ amli kɛ́ midu ŋmɔ hee?

english: Cocoa trees should typically be planted about 3 meters by 3 meters apart. If you plant them too close, their leaves block out sunlight and competition for soil nutrients will prevent the trees from growing strong pods.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ adu kookoo tsei aaafee mitai 3 kɛjɛ amɛhe. 3 mitai kɛjɛ amɛhe, kɛji odu amɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ebaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Ni akaŋshii ni akɛtaoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli wa.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa farm's soil is losing its richness and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ehiɛ edɔ ni ehe miihia ni awo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your trees show slow growth, pale green leaves, or produce fewer and smaller pods year after year despite good rainfall, the soil has likely run out of essential nutrients and needs organic or chemical fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ miida blɛoo lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Aloo ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo daa afi yɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni ehe miihia ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ awo mli.

english: Why is it necessary for me to trim the extra shoots growing from the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Those shoots, called chupons, steal water and food from the main trunk without producing good fruit. Cutting them off forces the tree to direct all its energy into growing healthy main branches and big pods.
ga: Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli ni ekɛ yibii kpakpa ko baaa. Amɛ ni afoɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ niji titrii lɛ kɛ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does rain make black pod disease spread so fast across my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ haa black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya lɛ?

english: The fungus that causes black pod disease thrives in high humidity and wet conditions. Raindrops splash the fungal spores from the soil or infected pods onto healthy pods, spreading the infection quickly across the farm.
ga: Fung ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ fungal spores kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya.

english: Can I plant food crops like cassava or maize between my young cocoa trees without hurting the cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ cacao tsei bibii ateŋ ni miyeee cacao lɛ awui?

english: You can plant temporary shade crops like plantain or cocoyam, but heavy feeders like cassava can steal too much water and nutrients from young cocoa roots, slowing down the cocoa trees' growth.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo cocoa. Shi tsei ni yeɔ niyenii babaoo tamɔ ŋmei lɛ baanyɛ aju nu kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ kookoo shishifãi bibii amli. Enɛ baaha kookoo tso lɛ adara blɛoo.

english: Why do I need to ferment and dry my cocoa beans properly before selling them to buyers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni migbiɔ dani mikɛhɔ̃ɔ mɛi ni heɔ lɛ?

english: Fermentation and thorough sun-drying stop the seed from germinating, remove bitterness, and develop the rich chocolate flavor that buyers look for. Properly dried beans also do not spoil or mold during transport to Accra or overseas.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ haaa dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃, ejieɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ehaa tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ baa. Beans ni agbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ efiteee loo ehiɛŋ ŋmɔtɔ beni akɛyaa Accra loo maŋsɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and drying up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct sunlight or high heat when they are small. They need temporary shade crops like plantain trees to protect their soft leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ kɛ́ kakao tsei lɛ darako. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ dumɔwui, koni amɛbu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ shãa he ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller bunches when I leave all the young shoots growing around the main trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii beni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: The extra shoots, known as suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning away weaker suckers and leaving only one or two allows the main plant to produce larger, heavier fruit bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, nu lɛ mli, kɛ hulu la mli. Kɛtsɔ tsei bibii lɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni ashi ekome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso titri lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines on wooden sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ sweet potato wain tsei yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need maximum sunlight to manufacture food for their underground tubers. Staking elevates the leaves into the sunlight and prevents leaf diseases caused by damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa hiɛ kɛyaa hulu la mli ni etsĩɔ baai helai ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat or irregular watering. Providing steady moisture through irrigation during dry periods helps the plant keep its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yibii amli.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow starting from the middle of the leaf moving outwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ teŋgbɛ kɛmiiya kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for green growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure restores the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas on my land after harvesting a crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes up a large amount of nitrogen from the soil. Cowpeas and other legumes capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, naturally restoring soil fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I put dry fertilizer directly against the stem of my young crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer right against the plant stem causes chemical burning to the skin and shallow roots. Fertilizer should be placed a few centimeters away in a ring or side band where roots can safely reach it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha tsofa ashã hewolo lɛ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ jɛmɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimitai fioo komɛi yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta loo ŋtayaa mli yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil retains too much water for long periods, encouraging fungal decay. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii fiteɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the plant sap and spreading viruses. Controlling these pests early with insecticidal sprays stops the curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ tsei lɛ amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaakpa curling lɛ.

english: What causes tiny holes in my young maize leaves with green powder inside the central growing shoot?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ powda eŋɔli yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the central growing point of the maize plant. Spraying approved insecticides or applying neem extracts early prevents them from destroying the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni taoɔ niyenii yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni edaa yɛ lɛ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra loo neem mli nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Ebaaye ebua ni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Can I successfully grow my vegetables inside a greenhouse here in Ghana?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ aduawai yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ Ghana yɛ omanyeyeli mli?

english: Yes, but standard greenhouse designs often trap too much heat in Ghana's warm weather. To succeed, you need greenhouse structures specifically built for hot tropical climates with extra ventilation.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi greenhouse he mfonirifeemɔi ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ haa dɔlɛ babaoo hiɔ shi yɛ Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. koni oye omanye Ohe miihia ni ofee greenhouse ni ama pɔtɛɛ aha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do crops wither or stop producing fruit inside a plastic greenhouse during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii gboiɔ loo ekpaa nibii ni aduɔ yɛ plastic ŋmɔji amli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Many greenhouses imported to Ghana were designed for cold countries to trap heat. In warm Ghanaian weather, heat builds up inside the structure, stressing the crops and burning their flowers.
ga: Afee tsũi babaoo ni akɛbaa Ghana lɛ aha maji ni mli ejɔ lɛ koni amɛhiɛ dɔlɛ mli. yɛ Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Dɔlɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ tsũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni eshãa fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Is growing tomatoes inside a greenhouse better than growing them in an open field in Ghana?
ga: Ani tomato ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hi fe ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ Ghana?

english: Greenhouses protect tomatoes from heavy rain and pests, but they can easily overheat in Ghana's sunny weather unless the structure has proper cooling nets and high roofs.
ga: Greenhouses buɔ tomato he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe. Shi amɛbaanyɛ amɛdɔ fe nine yɛ Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ mli lɛ mli oya. Ja tsũ lɛ yɛ ŋshɔŋloo ni sa ni haa hulutsoo baa kɛ ŋwɛitsu ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: What basic skills do I need to learn before starting a greenhouse farm?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee ŋaa esa akɛ makase dani mije ŋmɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shishi?

english: Greenhouse farming is very different from field farming. You need specific training on managing heat and humidity inside the structure, precise drip watering, and pest control in enclosed spaces.
ga: Esoro greenhouse okwaayeli kwraa yɛ ŋmɔ mli okwaayeli he. Esa akɛ onine ashɛ tsɔsemɔ pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ yɛ bɔ ni ooofee okwɛ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i nɔ yɛ tsũ ko mli. Nu ni hoɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ yɛ hei ni aŋã

english: Why is proper airflow so important for crops growing under a greenhouse cover in our climate?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ he hiaa tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ wɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli lɛ?

english: Ghana's warm weather creates high humidity inside closed structures. Good airflow cools down the plants, brings in fresh carbon dioxide, and prevents fungal diseases from destroying your crop.
ga: Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa fɛ̃i babaoo baa tsũi ni agbe naa lɛ amli. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i. Okɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji carbon dioxide aba Ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ onibii lɛ anaa.

english: I heard some local farmers lost money when they built greenhouses. What usually causes those failures?
ga: Minu akɛ maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi komɛi laaje shika beni amɛma ŋmɔji ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, mɛni kɛ nakai shigbeemɔi lɛ baa?

english: Most early failures happened because farmers bought greenhouse designs made for cold climates that overheated, combined with a lack of proper training on how to manage crops inside plastic structures.
ga: Shishijee mli nijiaŋwujee Enɛ baa mli babaoo ejaakɛ okwaafoi heɔ greenhouse he mfonirii ni ama aha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo fe nine lɛ. Kɛfata he lɛ, tsɔsemɔ ni sa ni kɔɔ bɔ ni atsuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nii yɛ plastic tsũi amli lɛ he lɛ bɛ.

english: How can I modify an imported greenhouse structure so my crops can survive the Ghanaian heat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsake greenhouse ni akɛjɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ Ghana latsaa lɛ mli?

english: You can replace solid plastic side walls with fine insect netting, raise the roof height, and add overhead shading nets to keep hot air moving out of the structure.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ plastic ni wa ni yɔɔ sɛɛ gbogboi lɛ awo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ najiaŋ. Wo tsũ lɛ yiteŋ ŋwɛi ŋwɛi Ni akɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaa fata he koni ekɛjie kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛjɛ tsũ lɛ he.

english: Does growing crops inside a greenhouse mean I will not have issues with crop diseases?
ga: Ani tsei ni mikwɛɔ yɛ greenhouse mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ minaŋ tsei ahe helai ahe naagbai?

english: Not necessarily. While plastic covers protect crops from rain-borne diseases, poor ventilation in hot weather creates high humidity inside, which can breed fungal diseases if not managed well.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Eyɛ mli akɛ plastic ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni nugbɔ kɛbaa lɛ ahe moŋ, shi kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha hulutsoo babaoo aba mli. Enɛ baanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai aba kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does hot local weather affect how I water my greenhouse crops compared to field crops?
ga: Te hulutsoo be ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ saa bɔ ni mikɛ mihe woɔ mi-greenhouse tsei lɛ amli nu mihaa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Because temperature inside a greenhouse gets much higher than outside, crops lose water quickly. You must use controlled drip irrigation and monitor soil moisture constantly to keep crop roots from drying out.
ga: Enɛ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ greenhouse lɛ mli lɛ fa kwraa fe kponɔgbɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya. Esa akɛ okɛ nu ni hoɔ ni akudɔɔ lɛ atsu nii ni okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be koni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akagbi.

english: Which vegetable crops are easiest for a beginner to grow inside a simple greenhouse setup in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ aduawai ji nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ kɛha mɛi ni jeɔ shishi lɛ akɛ amɛaadu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ Ghana ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ mli?

english: Sweet peppers and tomatoes are common, but they require careful temperature control and proper training on crop pruning and ventilation to get good yields in hot weather.
ga: Bell pepper kɛ tomato ji nɔ ni afɔɔ namɔ. Shi ebiɔ ni akwɛ hulutsoo be lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsɔsemɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he koni anyɛ ana yibii kpakpai yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do my neighbor's crops produce a much bigger harvest than mine even though our farms are side by side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe mi nɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ wɔŋmɔji lɛ yɛ he kome moŋ?

english: Differences in harvest size usually come down to soil care, plant spacing, weed control, and seed quality. Even on neighboring land, crops yield much more when the soil is well-nourished, weeds are removed early so they do not steal plant food, and proper spacing gives each crop enough sunlight and room to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ. tsei ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ po nɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kpakpa. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Bɔni afee ni akaju niyenii kɛjɛ tsei amli Ni gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso hulu la kɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛdaa.

english: Why are some of my cassava tubers very large while others on the same farm stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmeii lɛ ekomɛi dara nɛkɛ lɛ? yɛ be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi krokomɛi Okwaafoi lɛ nɔŋŋ ji bibioo.

english: Tubers grow to different sizes based on how much nutrients, water, and sunlight each individual plant receives. Plants that have to compete with heavy weeds or are planted too close to each other cannot develop large tubers, while plants with plenty of space and clean soil grow much bigger.
ga: Tubers baanyɛ adara kɛyashɛ dalɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ naa. Tsei ni kɛ jwɛi akaŋshii ni naa wa kpeɔ loo ni adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛŋ afee bulbs wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ baadara babaoo.

english: Will planting my seeds very close together give me more harvest from my small plot of land?
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ni madu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná ŋmaa babaoo kɛjɛ he bibioo ko. mi nɔ loo daabi

english: Planting seeds too close together actually reduces your total harvest. When crops are crowded, their roots fight over the same soil nutrients and water, and their leaves block sunlight from each other, resulting in thin, weak plants with very small yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ aba shi diɛŋtsɛ. Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa.

english: What is the best way for me to store my harvested maize so that insects do not destroy it?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato? Bɔni afee ni kooloi bibii akafite lɛ?

english: To protect stored maize, the grain must first be dried thoroughly until it is hard so mold cannot grow. Storing the dried maize in airtight bags or clean, sealed drums deprives pests like weevils of air and keeps new insects from getting inside.
ga: Bɔni afee ni abu ŋmãa ni ato lɛ he Esa akɛ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi amɛhe wa bɔni afee ni ŋmãa akakwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni egbi to vacuum bags loo ŋmãa ni he tse ni atsĩ naa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ anijiaŋ aje wui, ni ebaatsi ŋmeii heei ni baabote mli lɛ anaa.

english: How can I tell the exact right time to harvest my yams so they do not rot in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii? Koni ekafite yɛ sũ lɛ mli?

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines turn yellow and start to dry up naturally at the end of the rainy season. Leaving yams in wet soil after the vine dies completely makes them vulnerable to soil pests and fungal rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛje shishi amɛgbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee. Kɛ́ ashi sweet potato yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ beni wain tso lɛ egbo sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ yeɔ amɛ.

english: How does clearing weeds regularly actually help my crops produce a bigger yield?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm by rapidly drinking the water and absorbing the soil nutrients meant for your crops. Removing weeds early ensures all the food in the soil goes directly into growing your crops and producing larger fruits or grains.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ nu ni amɛnuɔ oya ni amɛŋɔɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa koni anyɛ akɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ ni akɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii ni awo yibii loo ŋmaa wuji.

english: How do I know if my farmland needs fertilizer to help my crops grow better?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Signs that your soil lacks nutrients include slow crop growth, pale green or yellow leaves, and small stems. If crops grown on the same land yield less each passing year, the soil is tired and needs organic manure or fertilizer to replenish its food.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he ji tsei ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ tso bibioo Kɛji tsei ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi Shikpɔŋ lɛ he feɔ shoo ni ehe hiaa humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtoɔ niyenii lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Can I save seeds from my current maize harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpaa amrɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: While you can save seeds from traditional crop varieties, saved seeds from hybrid varieties will produce much lower yields and weaker plants in the second season. Purchasing fresh, certified seeds for certain crop types ensures strong plants and reliable yields every year.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ obaanyɛ obua dumɔwui anaa kɛjɛ blema tsei srɔtoi amli moŋ, shi dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛjɛ tsei srɔtoi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baaná yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa ni tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni aŋmala he odaseyeli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ahemɔ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn yellow and drop off before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Premature leaf yellowing is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil, pest damage, or root rot caused by standing water. Healthy green leaves are necessary for the plant to make food, so yellow leaves mean the plant is stressed and needs better drainage or soil nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ kɛbaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ Baai kpakpai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ he hiaa waa kɛha tsei ni akɛhooɔ nii. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao ni ehe miihia ni nu atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kpakpai.

english: Why do my crop flowers fall off without producing any fruit when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain can wash away pollen before bees or wind can fertilize the flowers, preventing fruit from forming. Excess water in the soil can also stress the plant's root system, causing the plant to drop its flowers to save energy.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie pollen lɛ dani ŋmeii loo kɔɔyɔɔ aha fɔfɔi lɛ afee fɔfɔi. Etsiɔ aduawai anaa koni amɛkafee Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ afee nɔ ni haoɔ. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost gives the plant the nourishment it needs to turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Ehaa tsei lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it harmful to plant maize on the exact same farm plot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that prefer that crop to build up in the dirt. Rotating with crops like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ tsei lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei Yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants often shed their blossoms when they experience heat stress, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Ensuring steady watering and partial shade during extreme heat helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ dɔlɛ, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ ahã fɔfɔi lɛ nu daa kɛ hulutsoo be fioo ko lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my yam tubers turn out short and twisted instead of growing long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji kukuji ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eja lɛ?

english: Yam tubers become misshapen when the soil underneath is hard, rocky, or compacted. Yams need loose, deep mounds or ridges so the tubers can expand downward without meeting hard obstacles.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa, tɛi yɔɔ mli, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Sweet potatoes he miihia gɔji loo ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛya shi ni amɛkɛ gbɛtsii nii ni tsii ekpeko.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads in overly damp, shady conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let in sunlight and clearing weeds allows air to dry out the pods and keep them healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la aba mli, ni ojie jwɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ aba tsei lɛ amli ni eha amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or by a virus transmitted by those insects. Spraying with soapy water or neem oil helps manage these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni akɛ saamɔ loo neem fɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ekwɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves wilt during the hot afternoon even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense sun, crops lose water from their leaves faster than roots can absorb it from the soil. The plant temporarily wilts to protect itself from drying out, and it usually recovers as temperature drops in the late afternoon.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii laajeɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi yɛ shwane mli.

english: Why do my cassava stem cuttings dry up and fail to sprout after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava niji lɛ egbi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings need moist soil to trigger root growth. If planted during a hot, dry period without enough ground moisture, the stem loses all its water and dies before roots can establish.
ga: Yucca tsei ni afolɔ lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ koni eha shishifãi lɛ ada. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ mli lɛ, tso lɛ shishi nu lɛ fɛɛ laajeɔ ni egboɔ dani shishifãi lɛ daa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when heavy wind and rain hit the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa tswa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches at the top, making them top-heavy. Supporting them with sturdy wooden poles (staking) prevents the wind from snapping or uprooting them.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akuu ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. make it top heavy Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni wa (staking) fĩ esɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ akakumɔ loo eshishi.

english: How do I know if a new seed variety will grow well on my farm before I plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui heei baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu amɛ?

english: A good seed variety should match your local rainfall, soil type, and temperature. You can verify seed suitability by checking for certified seed labels from local agricultural extension offices or testing a small plot first.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi kpakpai lɛ afee nɔ ni sa kɛha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ henɔ, kɛ hulutsoo be. Obaanyɛ okwɛ kɛji dumɔwu ko sa kɛtsɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe wolo ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ okwaayeli he nitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. loo kaa shikpɔŋ bibioo ko okwɛ klɛŋklɛŋ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the tall trees from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive under strong, direct sunlight. Keeping taller shade trees on your farm protects the tender leaves from sun scorch and keeps the soil cool and moist during dry periods.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my growing maize plants turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso ni miida lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on growing maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen fertilizer, or the soil is too waterlogged. Adding a nitrogen-based fertilizer like urea can help restore the green color and boost crop yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I know which way to plant my cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male bɔ ni aduɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Look closely at the tiny raised buds along the stem cutting; they must point upward toward the sky. Planting stems upside down causes delayed growth and significantly reduces your final tuber harvest.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. ni awó nɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ tso lɛ fã ni afoɔ lɛ he lɛ Esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ haa edalɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni ehaa onaagbee bulb nikpamɔ lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden sticks into the soil for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: Yam vines need plenty of direct sunlight on their leaves to generate energy to swell the tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to light and preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba ni ekɛwo ŋmeii lɛ amli. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Okɛwo la mli ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to a family of crops that take nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that nourishes the maize plants growing alongside them.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas fata tsei ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ hewalɛ.

english: What is eating holes in the central whorl of my young maize plants, and how do I stop it?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ yeli? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Spraying approved pesticides or applying neem leaf extracts into the central funnel early in the morning when caterpillars feed will help protect your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ loo okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu awo ŋshɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ mli leebi maŋkpa beni kooloi lɛ yeɔ niyenii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my vegetable plants with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ? Tsoi ni jwɛi loo baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, called mulching, prevents soil water from evaporating quickly in hot sun, keeps roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking light and food away from your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi lɛ akajie la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why should I cut away extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: If too many shoots grow together, they compete for the same soil water and nutrients. Removing extra suckers and keeping only one or two allows the parent plant to produce a single, large, heavy bunch of plantain.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ he kome lɛ Nakai ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ ni akɛ eko loo enyɔ pɛ to he lɛ, ebaaha fɔlɔ tso lɛ awo ŋmeii agbo kome pɛ ni tsii.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers and wilt whenever the Harmattan wind starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ ni egboɔ be fɛɛ be ni harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baaje shishi lɛ?

english: Harmattan winds bring very dry, hot air that pulls moisture out of plant leaves much faster than the roots can drink it from the dry soil. The plant drops its flowers to save energy and water to stay alive.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi waa. Enɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Is it best to put fertilizer in the hole on the same day I drop my crop seeds?
ga: Ani ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo bu lɛ mli yɛ gbi ni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Putting strong chemical fertilizer directly against fresh seeds can burn and kill the tender seed sprouts. It is better to wait until the plant sprouts roots—usually two to three weeks after planting—before applying fertilizer near the stem.
ga: Tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui heei amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ blɛoo lɛ ni egbe amɛ. Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ (bei pii lɛ, otsii 2-3 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ) dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which maize needs to grow green and strong. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or planting nitrogen-fixing beans in that soil before maize can fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni ehe wa. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛaawo mli loo nidumɔ nitrogen-fixing beans yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani ŋmãa baa lɛ baanyɛ atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same spot on my farm three seasons in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli bei etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific soil nutrients that crop needs and allows pests and diseases to multiply in the ground. Rotating with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nutrients and cleans the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ebaafee niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ebaanyɛ eha amɛyibɔ ​​aya hiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsuɔ nii kɛtsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tseɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive and get scorched under direct sunlight. Leaving taller trees or planting plantains around them creates living shade that cools the seedlings and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa, ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã. tsei kakadaji loo tsei bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ haa hulutsoo, ehaa tsei lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off without producing any tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they suffer from intense heat and lack of water, which prevents fertilization. Providing regular water at the root level and temporary light shade protects the flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. ni tsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifã lɛ he daa kɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Cassava roots rot when excess rainwater collects around them and cannot drain away. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to run off safely, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nugbɔ nu buaa amɛhe naa lɛ. ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why do I find holes and small caterpillars hiding inside the center leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii kɛ ŋmeii? Ekɛtee mi ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli.

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on tender young corn leaves from the inside out. Applying recommended control products early or putting clean dry sand mixed with neem powder in the plant's center destroys them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛyeɔ hela lɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Aloo ŋã ni mli tse ni egbi ni akɛ neem powder efutu mli lɛ ni akɛaawo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baafite nakai nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and growing small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on sap. Controlling these small pests with neem oil or appropriate insect sprays keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi bibii nɛɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and yield smaller tubers if I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ bulbs bibii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients. Spacing seeds out gives each plant enough room and food to grow large yields.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la fioo, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ amli gbalamɔ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why do grass and weeds around my young crops make my crops look weak and stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ Ani mitsei bibii lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the water, light, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Keeping your field weed-free during the crop's early growth ensures all nutrients go directly to your crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaakwɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa waa lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kakadaji ahe hiaa mi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high toward sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking raises the leaves off the damp ground, keeping them healthy and well-lit.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi kɛya hulu lɛ he koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ha amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛná la jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil and rot so quickly compared to other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ ni egboɔ oya kɛ akɛto tsei krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Tomatoes are naturally made of up to 95 percent water. Because they hold so much liquid inside, they are very delicate and break down fast in heat if not stored in a cool place.
ga: Tomato ji nu oha mlijaa 95 yɛ adebɔɔ naa, yɛ nu babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, egbɔjɔ waa ni efiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ edɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛtooo he ko ni mli ejɔ.

english: Is it true that most of the weight in fresh tomatoes is just water?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ, tsɔne ni tsii ni yɔɔ tomato hee mli lɛ mli babaoo ji nu kɛkɛ?

english: Yes, standard tomatoes are mostly water—often between 90 and 95 percent liquid. Only a very small part of the fruit is actual solid food matter.
ga: Hɛɛ, tomatoi ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo yɛ nu. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni fa fe oha mlijaa 90 kɛyashi 95 yɔɔ mli, ni fã bibioo ko pɛ yɔɔ mli. Yibii pɛ ji niyenii ni wa diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do my tomatoes lose weight and shrink when I leave them out in the sun after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa egbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ mishi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli beni mifolɔ amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Since tomatoes are mostly water, heat causes that water inside the fruit to evaporate into the air, making the tomato shrink, wrinkle, and become lighter.
