ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomatoi lɛ ateŋ babaoo yɛ nu. Dɔlɛ lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Ehaa tomatoi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛsu hu shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do traders at the market complain that my tomatoes are too soft and watery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayelɔi wieɔ amɛshiɔ akɛ mi-tomato lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When tomatoes absorb too much liquid late in their growth, their inside becomes mostly water rather than thick flesh, making them easily squished during transport to the market.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomatoi shwie nu babaoo yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ naagbee lɛ, Emli baafee nu babaoo moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ amɛhe mlɛo yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ yaa jara nɔ lɛ.

english: Does giving my tomato plants extra water close to harvest time give me better fruits?
ga: Ani nu babaoo ni mikɛhaa mi-tomato tsei lɛ beni ebɛŋkɛ nikpamɔ be lɛ haa miwoɔ yibii kpakpai?

english: No, heavy watering right before harvest causes the fruit to fill up with mostly water. This dilutes the flavor, makes the skin split, and shortens how long the fruit stays fresh.
ga: Dabi, nu ni akɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ amli babaoo dani akpaa lɛ baaha nu ahi aduawai lɛ amli babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa ehewolo lɛ mli fãa, ni be ni tso yibii lɛ yeɔ lɛ feɔ kuku.

english: How can I get my tomatoes to have thicker flesh instead of just liquid inside?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-tomato lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni nu kɛkɛ ahi mli?

english: To get thicker flesh, you should avoid overwatering as the fruits ripen, use balanced fertilizers like potassium, and choose tomato seed varieties known for firm produce.
ga: Bɔni afee ni oná he ko ni mli tse Esa akɛ okpa nu ni oooha fe nine beni aduawai lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja, tamɔ potassium atsu nii, ni ohala tomato dumɔwui ni ale akɛ amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ.

english: Does heavy rainfall right before I pick my crops make them better to sell?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa dani mikpaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ baaha ahɔ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Rain makes crops heavier because they absorb quick water, but it actually lowers their quality by making them watery, less tasty, and quicker to spoil on the market shelf.
ga: Nugbɔ haa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ mlɛo ejaakɛ amɛmɔɔ nu oya, shi yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, ebaa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ nu ni ehaa amɛfeɔ nu, ni amɛhe ehiaaa ni amɛfiteɔ oya yɛ jara nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Does a bigger tomato always give more food nourishment to my family than a small one?
ga: Ani be fɛɛ be lɛ, tomatoi wuji haa weku ko niyenii babaoo fe tomatoi bibii?

english: Not necessarily. A very large tomato might just be holding extra water content rather than actual solid nutrients like vitamins and minerals.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Tomatoi ni dara waa lɛ baanyɛ ahiɛ nu babaoo fe niyenii ni mli wa, tamɔ vitamini kɛ mineral.

english: Why do some crops fill my stomach longer while tomatoes seem to digest very fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi haa mi musu lɛ mli eyiɔ obɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni etamɔ nɔ ni tomatoi lɛ shwieɔ oya waa lɛ?

english: Crops like tubers have high solid food matter, while crops like tomatoes are up to 95 percent water, which passes through your body much faster.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tubers lɛ yɛ niyenii ni mli wa babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni shɛɔ oha mlijaa 95 yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tomato mli, ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ogbɔmɔtso lɛ mli oya kwraa.

english: How much actual solid food content is inside a standard tomato?
ga: Niyenii ni wa enyiɛ diɛŋtsɛ yɔɔ tomato kome ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ?

english: In a typical tomato, only about 5 to 10 percent is solid food matter containing nutrients and natural sugars, while the remaining 90 to 95 percent is water.
ga: Yɛ tomato ni afɔɔ namɔ mli lɛ, aaafee oha mlijaa 5 kɛyashi 10 pɛ ji niyenii ni wa ni niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli sugar yɔɔ mli, yɛ be mli ni oha mlijaa 90 kɛyashi 95 ni eshwɛ lɛ ji nu.

english: Plantains have shallow roots that do not grow deep into the soil. When the soil becomes soft from rain or when underground pests damage the roots, the heavy plantain bunch makes the stem top-heavy, causing it to tip over easily unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ sũ lɛ mli jɔ loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ. Plantain tsei ni tsii baatsi tso lɛ shishi. Ehaa egbee shi mlɛo ja akɛ tso nibii fiɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my plantain plants turning yellow and brown before the fruit is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ dani aduawai lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the plant lacks soil nutrients like nitrogen or is infected by leaf fungal diseases. As the plant grows, it pulls energy from older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves and growing bunch, causing the lower leaves to dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ enɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo fungal baa hela ko emɔ amɛ. Kɛ tsei lɛ dara Ejieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii. Ha shishigbɛ baai lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my maize plants produce corn cobs when they are still very short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ woɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ? Ni eyɛ kuku waa lolo?

english: When maize plants do not get enough water or nutrients early in their life, they feel stressed. To survive and reproduce before dying, the plant stops growing tall and forces itself to flower and produce small cobs early.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmãa tsei lɛ náaa nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛshihilɛ shishijee mli lɛ, amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛmiifee basaa. Bɔni afee ni ehi shi ni efɔ dani egbo Tso lɛ baakpa dalɛ ni enyɛ ehe nɔ ni ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo ŋmeii bibii klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why should I plant plantain suckers on the same farm with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain plants produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa seedlings essential shade and keeping the soil moist while they establish roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhaa hulutsoo. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava stems grow tall and thin with very few leaves when planted close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛbaai fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight. The cassava plant spends all its energy growing upward to reach the light instead of spreading its leaves and building food storage roots underground.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni eyɔɔ beni edaa lɛ tsuɔ nii koni enine ashɛ la nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a gblaa a ba ɔmɛ a mi nɛ a peeɔ sisi nɛ a toɔ niye ní ngɛ zugba sisi.

english: This is caused by a fungal infection called black pod disease. The fungus thrives in cool, wet, and humid conditions, spreading easily when rain droplets splash dirt and fungal spores onto the pods.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. Fuŋ lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, kɛ he ni edɔ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔi shwie muji kɛ ŋmeii amli ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants curl up and show yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. The disease attacks the leaves, reducing their ability to use sunlight to make food for root growth.
ga: Enɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi, ni koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Hela nɛɛ tutuaa baai lɛ, ni ehaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ hulu la atsu nii ni amɛkɛfee niyenii kɛha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or too much chemical fertilizer. The stress causes the plant to save its energy by shedding flowers it cannot support.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo lɛ nɔ. Haomɔ haa tsei kɛ hewalɛ toɔ kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye amɛbua lɛ ni amɛjieɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain bunches take so much longer to mature during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains need a constant supply of water to transport nutrients from the soil up into the stem and bunch. During dry periods, the plant slows down its food-making process to conserve moisture, delaying fruit growth.
ga: Plantains he miihia nu ni yaa nɔ daa koni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋmeii lɛ ashishi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tsei haa niyenii ni afeɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ fioo koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Ha aduawai lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo

english: Why does my farm soil become very hard and crack after a few days without rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni egbɛ eshwa gbii fioo komɛi ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil becomes hard and cracked when it lacks organic matter like decayed leaves, straw, or manure. Organic material acts like a sponge to hold water, keeping the soil soft and moist even when rain is scarce.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ baai ni egboi, jwɛi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji koni ekɛhiɛ nu mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ kɛji nugbɔ bɛ po.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the large trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their sensitive leaves and dries up soil moisture quickly. Keeping taller shade trees creates a cooler environment that protects the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yellowing leaves in a V-shape are a signal that the soil is running low on nitrogen. The maize plant is moving the remaining nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the newer top growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ V lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei miitsi nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛmiijɛ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛmiiya ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni daraa lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when the rainy season gets too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain leaves standing water in the soil, it blocks oxygen from reaching the roots. Without air, fungal diseases easily infect the cassava roots, causing them to rot.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ kpɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Oxygen lɛ shɛɛɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Fungal helai yeɔ cassava shishifãi lɛ oya ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why should I stake my yam vines instead of letting them spread on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ awo tso nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã eda yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking raises the yam leaves so they can catch more sunlight to feed the growing tubers underneath. It also keeps the leaves off the hot, wet soil, which prevents diseases from spreading.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato lɛ baai lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni hulu la babaoo aye abua bulbs ni miida yɛ shishi lɛ. Etsiɔ baa hu naa koni amɛkashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni efɔ lɛ he. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and sunken before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efoɔ dani edara lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium inside the growing fruit. It usually happens when watering is irregular, making it hard for the plant's roots to draw up nutrients evenly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and looking small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee bibioo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites. As they feed on the leaves, they damage the tissues and can spread plant viruses that stunt leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ Amɛfiteɔ fãji ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ tso mli helai ni tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during light windstorms when they start fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum ni naa wa waa mli beni amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots close to the surface, and a heavy bunch of fruit makes the top very heavy. Propping the stems with strong wooden or bamboo stakes helps support the weight during fruit development.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Ni aduawai ni yɔɔ tsiimɔ babaoo lɛ baaha ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ afee tsiimɔ waa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni wa fiɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efi amɛtsii lɛ sɛɛ yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my cowpea plants producing many flowers, but the flowers drop off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii?

english: Cowpea flowers drop when tiny pests called flower thrips attack the blossom buds. Extreme heat stress or drought can also cause the plant to shed flowers to save its remaining energy.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ flower thrips lɛ tutua fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ. Haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ mli baa lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my stored dried maize grains get full of small holes and white dust after two months in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni sũ yɛŋ ni ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli nyɔji enyɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The holes and dust are caused by grain weevils. Female insects lay hidden eggs inside the dried kernels, and when the larvae hatch, they eat the inside of the grain and push out powdery waste.
ga: Dumɔwui amli ŋmeii kɛ bu kɛ sũ baa. Kpluka yoo lɛ woɔ wɔji ni akɛtee ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ mli. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ Amɛyeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛjieɔ muji ni tamɔ powder.

english: Why does putting dried grass around the base of my crop plants help them survive dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ jwɛi awo he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mitsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass (mulching) acts like a blanket. It blocks the hot sun from evaporating soil moisture and keeps the plant roots cool during dry weather.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekafee sũ mli nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ, ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They require fast-growing shade plants like plantain or cassava nearby to block the harsh sun and keep the soil cool and moist while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo yucca ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ. Koni ekɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are the small green cocoa pods on my trees turning black and shriveling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy seasons when humidity is high. It can also happen when the tree gets stressed by bad weather or lacks nutrients, causing it to naturally drop excess pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ tsei miihao kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that your maize plants are missing nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green leaf growth. This often happens when the soil is worn out from continuous farming or when heavy rains wash nutrients deep beyond the roots.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ efite kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ mli. Aloo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ fe shishifãi lɛ.

english: If your crops from the previous harvest were small, grew very slowly, or had yellowish leaves, your soil is low on nutrients. Soil that stays light in color and feels very sandy also loses nutrients quickly and benefits from compost or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ faaa, eda blɛoo waa, loo eyɛ baai ŋmɔŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋã waa lɛ laajeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya ni amɛnáa ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe sɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛbaafee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays waterlogged for too long after heavy rains. The excess water prevents air from reaching the roots, causing underground rot and allowing soil fungi to destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii baa ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long hot spell before regular rains start. If you plant too early, the heat can dry out the soil and burn the delicate young sprouted seedlings before steady rains arrive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni naa wa nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dɔlɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni eshã dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ aya nɔ anɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off without forming any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo pepper yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as severe heat, dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. When the weather gets too hot, the pollen inside the flower dies, so the plant drops the flower to save energy.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ haomɔ, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gboɔ. Bɔni afee ni tsei akafite hewalɛ lɛ, amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and twisting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up to protect themselves from extreme heat and water loss. It can also be caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading leaf-curl viruses, which cause the leaves to twist and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni haa baai shwieɔ shi lɛ hu baanyɛ ekɛba. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does my plantain tree produce small bunches if I leave all the young suckers growing around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida yɛ kui bibii amli lɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ mishi tsei bibii yɛ plantain lɛ he hu?

english: The main plantain mother tree shares its water and food with every young sucker growing at its base. If you leave too many suckers, they steal nutrients away from the main stem, resulting in smaller bunches.
ga: Nyɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ kɛ gbekɛbii fɛɛ ni daraa yɛ eshishi lɛ jaa nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ Ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in full sunlight to create food for the growing tuber underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground, improves air flow to prevent leaf diseases, and helps the plant yield larger yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã koni hulu lɛ fɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ koni akafoli helai aba. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ sweet potato yibii babaoo

english: Why do I need to plant shade crops like plantain next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ madu tso ko ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantain yɛ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct sunlight and can easily scorch. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide living shade and preserve soil moisture while the young cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi be mli ni kookoo bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape from the tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmã tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves in a V-pattern usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, an essential nutrient maize needs in large amounts to build green leaves and grow healthy ears.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ V mli lɛ fɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni ŋmãa he hiaa yɛ babaoo mli koni ekwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli ni eha toi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts in the same field as my corn help my soil?
ga: Te ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that can take nitrogen from the air and lock it into the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for nitrogen-hungry crops like corn.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa nitrogen, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil when there is continuous heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ ni naa wa miinɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits around the roots without proper drainage, the roots suffocate and soil rot organisms attack them.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ bɛ mli lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni yɔɔ sũ ni miifite lɛ mli lɛ baatutua amɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees give smaller bunches when I let all the suckers grow around the main trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwereɔ bibii bibii beni mihaa ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ shwereɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Too many suckers steal water, light, and nutrients from the main plant. Cutting away extra suckers leaves energy for the main stem to produce a larger, healthier plantain bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo juɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yitso lɛ naa hewalɛ babaoo koni etsɔ plantains akui wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make energy for underground tuber growth. Staking lifts the foliage into the sun and keeps the leaves off wet soil, preventing rot and fungal disease.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni eha hewalɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tuber lɛ dalɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli ni ehaaa amɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ amɛgbee shi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: What causes small ragged holes and powdery waste inside the center whorl of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ sũ ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ ring lɛ mli lɛ baa?

english: This is typical damage caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on the tender young leaves inside the central whorl of the corn plant.
ga: Enɛ ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ fɔɔ fitemɔ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by sap-sucking pests like thrips or aphids feeding on leaf sap, or by extreme heat and irregular watering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa mli

english: Why are the yellow flowers on my tomato plants dropping off without making any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when temperatures get extremely high or when plants experience water stress, which prevents successful pollination and fruit set.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination kɛ yibiiwoo ni yeɔ omanye lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow long leafy vines but very few pods when planted close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ wain tsei ni baai kakadaji yɔɔ mli shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cowpea seeds are planted too close, the plants compete intensely for sunlight, spending all their energy growing tall vines to reach light instead of flowering and setting seed pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu cowpea dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ waa. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ wain tsei ni kɛlɛ koni ená la moŋ fe ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ekɛ dumɔwui akui awo mli.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of maize plants usually indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil or poor drainage. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or beans makes the soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei dumɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi jogbaŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in their root nodules. When the crop dies, those roots break down and leave natural nitrogen fertilizer in the soil for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the large trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot withstand direct sunlight and heat. They require temporary shade from plants like plantains and permanent shade trees to retain humidity and protect their delicate leaves during their early years.
ga: Cocoa tsei nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains kɛ hulutsoo tsei ni baa daa lɛ adɛŋ. Bɔni afee ni hulutsoo ahi shi ni abu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: It is best to wait until rainfall is regular and the soil is wet down to a hand's depth, rather than planting after the very first light rain, which can be followed by a dry spell that kills germinating seeds.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛyashɛ he ko. Mohu ɔ, mo du ngɛ kekleekle nugbɔ nɛ nɛ ɔ se, nɛ eko ɔ, hwɔɔ nɛ gbeɔ hɛ mi nyami ɔ maa nyɛɛ se.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce food for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves toward the sun and keeps them off the hot, damp ground, preventing leaf diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akwɛ hulu lɛ hiɛ ni ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafee hei ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Koni akɛtsi baa helai anaa

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil traps too much water during heavy rains or when infected by fungal diseases. Planting on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rain to drain away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli loo kɛji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko emɔ amɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ bulb lɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites that spread plant viruses. Spraying plants with neem oil or mild insecticidal soap early helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ helai lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Ni akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni waaa lɛ ashwie tsei anɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ tsei lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without setting fruit during periods of extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or lack of pollination. Keeping soil moisture steady and using heat-tolerant seeds prevents this drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ shwane mli latsaa ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo pollination ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ dumɔwui ni nyɛɔ hulutsoo be mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni akatsi nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my fruiting plantain stems keep falling over during strong winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems, and heavy bunches make them top-heavy. Propping the main stem up with strong bamboo or wooden forks supports the extra weight and prevents wind damage.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Ni jwɛi ni tsii baaha efee tsii waa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni mli wa to tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eye ebua muji ni fa lɛ ni ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my garden vegetable leaves droop in the hot afternoon even if the ground is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In strong sun, vegetable leaves lose water faster than the roots can pull it up from the soil. The leaves wilt temporarily to protect the plant from drying out, usually recovering once the air cools in the evening.
ga: yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli Tsofai ahe baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni tso lɛ akagbi. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi ekoŋŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which acts as food for green growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps the leaves turn green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni no ji niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my bean plants make the soil better for my next crop of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tsei lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the bean crop is harvested, that stored nitrogen stays in the soil, working like free fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Beans mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my young vegetables with dry straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle aduawai bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool, holds in soil moisture so you water less, and stops weeds from stealing your crops' food.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i Haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ahi shi bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akashwie nɔ fioo ni etsĩ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and very small cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the large trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive under direct, hot sunlight and heavy wind. They require shade trees to protect them until their roots and branches grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hɔɔ lɛ he miihia amɛ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛniji lɛ aaawa.

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is fully ripe and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting when the bottom leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the ground around the base of the stem starts to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ

english: Why do rice crops need so much water on the field compared to corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa tsei yɛ amɛŋmɔji amli fe ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally thrive in shallow water, which cools their roots and stops weeds from growing, while corn roots go deeper into drier soil to find water.
ga: Omɔ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ, ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi yaa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatao nu.

english: What is eating the center leaves of my young corn and leaving brown powder behind?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ ni eshiɔ powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central funnel of the leaf to feed, and spraying targeted treatments early in the morning or late evening controls them best.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye nii. Ni tsofai ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ koni akɛkudɔ amɛ.

english: Extreme heat, dry soil, or giving the plant too much nitrogen fertilizer causes stress, which makes the plant drop its flowers instead of developing tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen babaoo ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛhao. Enɛ haa tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato ni amɛbaakwɛ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: How do weeds reduce my yield even if I apply fertilizer to my field?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ aba shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔji amli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight that your crop needs to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Is it safe for me to plant my maize immediately after the very first rain of the farming season?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ okwaayeli be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting after just one light rain is risky because a sudden dry period often follows. It is safer to wait until the soil gets soaked by two or three steady rains so there is enough moisture to support young seeds.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi fioo komɛi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua dumɔwui bibii lɛ aba.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow even after heavy rain falls on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can wash away nutrients from the topsoil or cause waterlogging, which drowns the plant roots and prevents them from absorbing plant food properly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ loo ekɛ nu afua aba. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, ni ehaaaa amɛŋɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens to my soil if heavy rain falls right after I put fertilizer down?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ?

english: If a heavy rain falls right after fertilizer application, the water washes the fertilizer away before roots can absorb it, wasting your money and effort.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwo mli lɛ sɛɛ Nu baaho ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Ehaa ofiteɔ shika kɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why is my cassava crop taking over four months to grow big when my neighbour harvested theirs early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ he nyɔji ejwɛ ni ekwɛ̃ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ kpa mra lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties mature at different speeds. Early-maturing varieties grow quickly within three months, while traditional or late-maturing varieties need four months or longer to build strong roots.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi lɛ daraa yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli. Henɔi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ daa oya yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni blema loo srɔtoi ni shwereɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ biɔ nyɔji ejwɛ loo nɔ ni fe nakai dani amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: My tomato plants are four months old, so why are they still not producing any flowers or fruit?
ga: Amrɔ nɛɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ eye nyɔji ejwɛ. Mɛni hewɔ amɛwooo fɔfɔi loo amɛwooo yibii lolo lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer can cause tomato plants to focus only on growing tall stems and leaves instead of flowering, while dry spells can also delay fruiting.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmeii kɛ baai ni kɛlɛ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔi, yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be hu baanyɛ aha aduawai lɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: Why have my pepper plants stopped growing taller after just two months in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ekpa shweremɔ yɛ nyɔji enyɔ pɛ ni ekɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Plants stop growing when their roots hit hard, unploughed soil, or when root-damaging pests and a lack of nutrients like phosphorus slow down early development.
ga: Tsei kpaɔ dalɛ kɛ́ amɛshishifãi lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni atsuuu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. aloo beni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ shishifãi kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs lɛ haaa shweremɔ lɛ aya hiɛ mra.

english: How often should I water my newly sowed vegetable seeds during a hot dry week?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi-vegetable dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ nu yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ amli?

english: Seeds need gentle, regular moisture to sprout. Watering lightly once or twice a day—early morning or late afternoon—keeps the topsoil moist without washing the seeds away.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ blɛoo, ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃. Nu lɛ blɛoo shikome loo shii enyɔ daa gbi. Leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli Enɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋwɛi fã lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ dumɔwui lɛ efɔɔɔ.

english: Should I buy all my farm inputs and seeds months before I even clear my land?
ga: Esa akɛ mahe nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ nyɔji babaoo dani mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po.

english: Buying inputs early helps you prepare financially, but you must store agrochemicals and seeds in a cool, dry place off the ground so humidity does not ruin them before planting time.
ga: Nibii ni akɛfeɔ nii lɛ ahemɔ mra Eyeɔ ebua bo ni osaa ohe yɛ shika gbɛfaŋ. Shi esa akɛ okɛ okwaayeli mli tsofai kɛ dumɔwui ato he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Enɛ ji koni hulutsoo be lɛ akafite amɛ dani be ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ aba.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly if I plant them right after burning the bush on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mishã jwɛi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Burning leaves the soil extremely hot and destroys good soil organisms. Allowing the land to cool down and receive rain once or twice before planting helps restore the soil balance.
ga: Shãa baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adɔ fe nine ni ebaafite shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ wala ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔ ni nugbɔ nɛ shi kome loo enyɔ dani odu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings sprout nicely in the nursery but wither away when I move them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Shi amɛgbi beni mijie amɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Seedlings suffer from transplant shock when moved suddenly from shade to harsh sunlight. You must gradually expose them to sun and slightly reduce watering a week before moving them to the main farm.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ be mli ni amɛjieɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli kɛyaa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli trukaa lɛ biɔ ni okɛ amɛ awo hulu lɛ mli fiofio ni okɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ lɛ aba shi fioo otsi kome dani okɛ amɛ aya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Seeds need a balanced mix of air, mild moisture, and warmth to sprout. If the soil is too wet and packed tightly, the seeds drown and rot before they can grow; using high-quality certified seeds also ensures that most seeds wake up and grow at the same time.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. hulutsoo fioo kɛ hulutsoo yɛ shweremɔ mli Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni ebɔle ehe Dumɔwui lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi dani amɛdara. Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ hu haa dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ babaoo teɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ekome kɛdaraa.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and burn when I clear away all the big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to strong, direct sunlight because their roots cannot absorb water fast enough to replace what burns off their leaves. Leaving shade trees or growing plantains alongside them acts like an umbrella, protecting the young plants until they are strong enough.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛto nibii ni shã ni jɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ najiaŋ. Tsei ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tso bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni enáa hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves on growing maize usually mean the crop is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and build big leaves. It can also happen when water sits on the field for too long, preventing the roots from breathing and feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo baai wuji amli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye nii.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year when I plant maize on the exact same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ faaa daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot every season drains the exact same nutrients from the dirt without giving the soil time to recover. Swapping your crops with beans or groundnuts puts vital nutrients back into the dirt and keeps soil diseases from building up.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsake ŋmei loo ŋmei lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaaa helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Healthy soil feels soft, looks dark, holds moisture well after rain, and is full of living earthworms. If your soil turns hard like rock, stays pale, or dries out immediately after rain, it is low in organic matter and needs compost or manure.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ, ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka eyi mli obɔ Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛ, ehiɛ su, loo egbi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni afee ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil suddenly goes from very dry to very wet. The heat or water shock frightens the plant, causing it to drop flowers to save its own life instead of feeding new fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Nu lɛ mli dɔlɛ loo ekpokpomɔ lɛ woɔ tsei lɛ ahe gbeyei. Ha egbee shi koni ehere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha yibii heei

english: Why does my cassava plant grow tall with plenty of green leaves but produces tiny roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much shade or too much nitrogen fertilizer, it uses all its energy to grow stems and leaves above ground. To build big, heavy food roots under the soil, the plant needs full sunlight and balanced nutrients.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ hulutsoo be babaoo loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo tsei kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Koni afee niyenii shishifãi wuji ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Hulu la ni fa kɛ niyenii ni ja he miihia tsei.

english: Why do my crops droop and look tired in the afternoon even if the ground was wet in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etamɔ nɔ ni etɔ lɛ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: On hot, sunny afternoons, crop leaves lose water into the hot air faster than their roots can drink it from the ground. The plant purposely wilts its leaves to hide from the harsh sun and conserve water, usually standing back up when the evening air cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tso baai lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛtee amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he ni amɛbu nu he. Bei pii lɛ, eteɔ shi kɛ́ gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than the crops I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild survival experts that are naturally adapted to steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early gives your planted crops the room and food they need to win the race.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli wala yibiiwoo he nilelɔi ni atsake amɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛ amɛhe awo nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ aná tsu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛye kunim yɛ akaŋshii lɛ mli.

english: Why do insects destroy my crops more during the dry spell than in the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: In dry weather, wild plants dry up, so insects crowd onto green farm crops to get water and food. Hot, dry temperatures also make insects multiply much faster, leading to quick insect attacks on your fields.
ga: Yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔŋ mli egbi lɛ, koo mli tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ, no hewɔ lɛ, kooloi bibii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. He ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ hu haa kooloi fɔɔ oya kwraa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kooloi bibii tutuaa oŋmɔji lɛ oya.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential for plant growth, or that the field is waterlogged, which prevents the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ. loo hei ni nu damɔ shi yɛ Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛye niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay thin and small even when the plants grow very tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛji bibii lolo eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ kɛlɛ waa moŋ lɛ?

english: If cassava plants are planted too close together or receive too much foliage-promoting nitrogen, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing nutrients in roots underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo enine shɛ nitrogen babaoo ni kanyaa baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye níhi a mi ngɛ tso ɔ sisije ɔmɛ a mi ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before forming small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛjeɔ kpo amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they are stressed by lack of water, lack of essential soil nutrients, or when pests and shade problems prevent proper pollination.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ nu ni bɛ lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo be mli ni kooloi kɛ hulutsoo naagbai tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa.

english: Why is it bad to plant my seeds directly into hard, unploughed soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu dumɔwui tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni aduko nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Hard soil makes it difficult for delicate young roots to push downward to reach water and nutrients, resulting in weak plants that easily fall over in heavy winds.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ haa ewaa ahaa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ akɛ amɛaatsi amɛhe kɛya shi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa amɛ.

english: Why should I not place chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts that can burn and destroy plant stems and roots if placed in direct contact; it must be applied a few inches away in the soil.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ shishifãi kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Esa akɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ he inchii fioo komɛi.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow so much faster than my cultivated crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive harsh conditions, allowing them to steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients from your crops much faster.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli oya kwraa.

english: How can I tell if my maize field is being attacked by fall armyworm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii miitutua mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Fall armyworm damage appears as ragged holes eaten through the leaves, accompanied by dark, sawdust-like waste inside the central funnel of the plant where new leaves grow.
ga: Fall armyworm fitemɔ jeɔ kpo akɛ buji ni ekpɔtɔ ni ayeɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli. kɛ sũ ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli he ni baai heei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ fata he.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get dark brown spots and dry up during rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Rainy weather creates high humidity, which allows fungal diseases like blight to spread quickly across wet leaf surfaces and dry them out.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa baa. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ baa shwiemɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa baa ni efɔ lɛ nɔ oya ni ehaa amɛgbiɔ.

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it from the soil, causing them to temporarily curl up to protect themselves from heat.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ehe kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ he.

english: Why do my vegetable plants dry up and die so quickly when the dry Harmattan season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind sucks moisture out of both the plant leaves and the topsoil very rapidly, requiring organic mulch on the soil to hold water for the roots.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ oya. Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni nu ahi shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do extension officers always tell us to start planting around March in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ kɛɔ wɔ be fɛɛ be akɛ wɔje dumɔ shishi yɛ March aaafee yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: March usually marks the beginning of the major rainy season in Ghana. Planting around this time ensures your seeds or young seedlings get enough soil moisture to build strong roots before dry periods arrive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, March ji nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ shishijee yɛ Ghana. Dumɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwu loo tso bibioo lɛ náa shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa baa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if I delay planting past the recommended start of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ dumɔ lɛ shwie shi fe be ni atsɔɔ akɛ aje shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: If you plant too late after the rains start in March, your crops will miss the main growth period provided by consistent rains. This can lead to stunted growth, weak plants, and a much lower harvest.
ga: Kɛji odu nii sɛɛ tsɔ beni nugbɔ lɛ je shishi yɛ March mli lɛ Onibii lɛ baafo be titri ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ kɛbaa lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ, tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa ni abaakpa lɛ aba shi kwraa.

english: Does natural rain make a big difference for young tree crops like rubber compared to manual watering?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ haa tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ rɔba tsei lɛ feɔ srɔtofeemɔ kpele kɛ akɛto nu ni akɛ niji shwieɔ amɛnɔ lɛ he?

english: Yes, natural rainfall during the main planting season saturates the deep soil layers that tree roots need to expand. Manual watering usually only wets the surface, which isn't enough for tree crops to grow deep roots.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, adebɔɔ mli nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be titri ni tso lɛ daa lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni ehe hiaa ni tsei shishifãi lɛ alɛɛ mli lɛ mli eyiɔ obɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛ niji shwieɔ nɔ lɛ haa ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛ. Enɛ faaa bɔ ni tso lɛ baaná shishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right month to get my land ready for crop planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nyɔŋ ni sa ni esa akɛ masaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha dumɔ nii?

english: In most parts of southern Ghana, land preparation should happen just before March so that the fields are cleared and dug before the first heavy rains begin.
ga: yɛ hei babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ. Esa akɛ asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani March aba. Koni ŋmɔji lɛ amli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni atsa dani klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aje shishi.

english: Why is it necessary to finish land preparation before farm workers arrive to help plant or tap?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ agbe shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ naa dani ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi aba koni amɛbaye amɛbua kɛdu loo amɛtswa pɔmpi lɛ?

english: If the land is not cleared and prepped ahead of time, hired farm workers cannot carry out specialized jobs like planting or tapping. Unprepared land leads to wasted money on labor and missed planting opportunities.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ajieee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni asaaa he kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ, Kontrak ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi nyɛŋ atsu nitsumɔi krɛdɛɛi tamɔ dumɔwui loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atswaa. Shikpɔŋ ni asaaa he lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ ni afiteɔ kɛ hegbɛi ni akɛduɔ tsei ni laajeɔ baa.

english: What steps should I take to get my farm land ready for planting before the main rains start?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni masaa miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha dumɔ nii dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba?

english: Land preparation involves clearing weeds and brush, removing big debris, tilling the soil if needed, and marking planting holes so your field is ready to receive plants immediately when rains begin.
ga: Nɔ ni fata shikpɔŋ he saamɔ he ji jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. Muji wuji ni ajieɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitsumɔ kɛ ehe miihia kɛ dumɔ bui ni akadiɔ koni oyale lɛ afee klalo akɛ ebaaŋɔ tsei kɛji nugbɔ nɛ pɛ.

english: Why can't I just clear the land and plant on the very same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbi kome lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Clearing land takes time and effort. Doing both on the same day can delay planting, tire out workers, and cause you to miss the exact soil moisture window ideal for crop establishment.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ heɔ be kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ. Kɛ́ afee nibii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔ lɛ asɛɛ afo. haa nitsulɔi lɛ nijiaŋ jeɔ wui Ni ehaa obɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ samflɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: What is a 'tappa' on a farm, and what do they do to rubber trees?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘thappa’ yɛ ŋmɔ mli? Ni mɛni ofeɔ kɛ rɔbɔt tso lɛ?

english: A 'tappa' (tapper) is a skilled worker who makes precise cuts into the bark of mature rubber trees to collect liquid latex without harming the growth or life of the tree.
ga: Thappa’ (taper) ji nitsulɔ ko ni he esa ni shwieɔ rɔbɔt tsei ni eda lɛ ahe tsɔi lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ koni ekɛbua latɛs ni mli ewo muji lɛ naa ni efiteee tso lɛ dalɛ loo ewala.

english: Why is proper timing so important when setting up a new rubber plantation?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be ni sa ni akɛtoɔ rɔbɔt ŋmɔ hee he gbɛjianɔ lɛ he hiaa lɛ?

english: Rubber saplings need steady moisture from the early rainy season in March to build thick trunks. Good timing ensures healthy trunk development so the trees can eventually be tapped for latex.
ga: Rɔba tsei lɛ he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be kɛjɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli yɛ March mli koni amɛfee tsei ni mli tse. Be ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, yɛ naagbee lɛ, tsei baanyɛ atswa rɔba.

english: Can bad land preparation affect how well my rubber trees yield latex in the future?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni asaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaná rɔba ni afeɔ wɔsɛɛ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, if the land isn't properly prepared early on, saplings may grow unevenly or suffer high mortality rates, leading to fewer healthy trees available for tapping when the plantation matures.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ asaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ mra. Dumɔwui baanyɛ ada yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo amɛgboi babaoo. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni abaanyɛ atswa be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ daa lɛ faaa.

english: Why is it important to leave specific, equal spaces between my seeds when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mahã gbɛ ni kã midumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ afee ekome ni efee pɔtɛɛ kɛ́ midu lɛ?

english: Leaving equal spaces gives each plant its own room to get enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without fighting with neighboring crops, leading to healthier crops and better yields.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi he ko ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni ekɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ abɔ akaŋ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: If seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete for light and soil food, resulting in thin, weak stems and very small ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli kɛha la kɛ shikpɔŋ kɛha niyenii. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii waa baa.

english: Will putting more crops close together in a small farm give me a bigger total harvest?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwo ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni fa babaoo?

english: No, overcrowding a small space actually reduces total yield because the plants get stressed fighting for resources, producing smaller or lower-quality produce.
ga: Dabi, gbɔmɛi ni eyi obɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi babaoo yɛ he ko bibioo lɛ haa nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ fɛɛ baa shi diɛŋtsɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ miihao yɛ nibii ni he hiaa lɛ ahe tawuu lɛ mli. ni kɛ nibii ni afee lɛ faaa loo nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa shi baa

english: How does keeping equal distance between my crops help make weed clearing easier?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbɛ ni kã miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ feɔ mlɛo?

english: Equal spacing creates neat, straight rows that make it easy to walk through and clear weeds with a hoe or cutlass without accidentally damaging your crops.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ ni yeɔ egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ fɛo, ni ja. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ oootsɔ mli ni okɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei ajie jwɛi lɛ. ni okpataaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ yɛ oshara mli.

english: Does having correct spaces between plants help my crops produce bigger fruit or grains?
ga: Ani gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii loo dumɔwui wuji?

english: Yes, when plants have proper space, their roots spread wide to feed well from the soil, which helps individual fruits, tubers, or grains grow much larger.
ga: Hɛɛ, be mli ni tsei yɔɔ he ni sa. Eshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa babaoo koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa aduawai aŋkroaŋkroi, ŋmeii, loo dumɔwui lɛ feɔ wuji babaoo.

english: How do I measure the right distance between planting holes if I do not have a tape measure?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu gbɛ ni sa ni kã dumɔ bui lɛ ateŋ lɛ he? Kɛji akɛ obɛ tsɔne ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe lɛ?

english: You can cut a simple wooden stick to the right length or tie knots on a rope at fixed distances to keep the space between planting holes equal across your whole farm.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofolɔ tsei ni akɛfee tsei folo. Ha elɛɛmɔ afee nɔ ni sa loo okɛ kpãa lɛ akpɛtɛ kpãa lɛ he yɛ gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ koni gbɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ahi dumɔ bui ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ ateŋ.

english: Why do crops that are planted at the exact same distance grow and mature at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ he kome lɛ daa ni amɛdaraa yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: When crops have identical spacing, they receive equal amounts of sunlight and plant food, allowing them to grow at the same speed and be ready for harvest together.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji ekome lɛ Amɛbaaná hulu la kɛ tsei aniyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ha tsei lɛ ada oya nɔŋŋ ni amɛfee klalo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaakpa.

english: Why do my crops need equal gaps between them just to get enough sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ he hiaa ni amɛná he ko ni tamɔ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ?

english: Equal gaps prevent bigger leaves from casting shade over neighboring plants, ensuring every single crop receives direct sunlight to grow strong.
ga: Gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ po tsiɔ baai agboi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee hulutsoo yɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ naa hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: How does using a planting machine help make my crop rows better than planting by hand?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitso lɛ ni ekɛ nine duɔ?

english: A planting machine automatically drops seeds at exact, equal distances every time, saving you physical effort and ensuring no seed is planted too close or too far from another.
ga: Mɔ ni duɔ dumɔwui lɛ diɛŋtsɛ duɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni jɛkɛmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ toɔ. ni akwɛ koni akadu dumɔwui komɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ.

english: If I hire a seeder machine for my farm, can it adjust the spacing for different types of crops?
ga: Kɛji mihe dumɔwui adumɔ tsɔne kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ Ani tsɔne lɛ baanyɛ atsake gbɛ ni kã dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, planter machines have settings that can be adjusted to leave wider gaps for crops like maize and cassava, or narrower gaps for smaller crops like legumes.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsɔne ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ yɛ gbɛjianɔtoi ni abaanyɛ atsake koni eshi he ko ni da aha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa. loo he ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii bibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: How do I know the right amount of liquid pesticide to mix in my spray tank if I am using local bottle caps to measure?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ji nu lɛ falɛ ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛfutu mi-spray tanki lɛ mli? Kɛ mikɛ tɔ mli tsɔne tsu nii kɛsusu bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ he

english: Using random bottle caps can be dangerous because cap sizes vary; using too much chemical burns your crops and causes leaves to drop, while using too little leaves pests alive. You should always use the calibrated measuring cup provided with the chemical bottle or ask an officer for a standard measuring container.
ga: Tɔ lɛ mli tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii trukaa lɛ baanyɛ afee oshara ejaakɛ tsɔne lɛ dalɛi yɛ srɔtoi. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaashã oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni ebaaha baai lɛ agbo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baai fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Esa akɛ okɛ susumɔ kɔɔpoo ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni akɛha yɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma kɔɔpoo lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii loo obi mɔ ni tsuɔ he nii lɛ ni eha bo nɔ ko ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe ni sa.

english: Why do my crop leaves look burnt and dry a few days after I spray them to clear weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã ni egbi yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni afɔse tsofa kɛha jwɛi lɛ?

english: Crop leaves get scorched when weedkiller or pesticide solutions are mixed too strong, or when spraying is done during the hot mid-day sun. To prevent burning, mix the exact recommended dose and spray early in the morning when the crops are cool.
ga: Tsei ahe baai lɛ shãa kɛji akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ futu mli tsɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ ashwie nɔ yɛ gbi ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ Koni akashã lɛ Futumɔ bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ bɔ ni sa ni okɛshwie nɔ leebi beni tsei lɛ edɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale yellow and stunted even when there is regular rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are suffering from a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which they need to make green leaves and grow strong. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or compost around the base of the plant will help restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-corn tsei lɛ miina nitrogen ni faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ he miihia koni baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛbaabɔle Shishitoo lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni eha tso lɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do insect pests seem to attack and destroy my crops more during dry spells than during rainy times?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry periods, crops experience water stress, which weakens their natural defenses and makes them soft targets for insects looking to drink plant fluids. Keeping soil covered with mulch helps hold moisture so plants remain strong enough to resist pests.
ga: yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ nu he haomɔ kpeɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hebuu nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. ni ehaa amɛfeɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛha kooloi ni miisumɔ ni amɛnu tsei amli nu lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ kwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi bɔni afee ni tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai akpee.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cocoa trees very close together so I can fit more trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting cocoa trees too close causes their branches and roots to compete for sunlight, air, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin, weak trees that yield far fewer pods than properly spaced trees.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ niji kɛ shishifãi lɛ abɔi hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kpakpai ahe akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ fe tsei ni akɛ amɛ ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantain or cassava alongside cocoa provides temporary living shade that keeps the seedlings cool until they mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ni haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off without forming any pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ pepper ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from sudden heat, irregular watering, or a lack of calcium in the soil. Consistent soil moisture and balanced soil feeding encourage flowers to stay attached and turn into healthy peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shɛ la ni tsoɔ trukaa lɛ he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ja yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does removing extra branches and leaves from my tomato plants make the tomatoes grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji kɛ baai ni fa fe nine ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ haa amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Trimming unnecessary side branches directs the plant's energy and food straight to the developing fruits instead of wasting strength on growing extra leaves that do not produce crop yield.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii kɛyaa aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ kɛtsɔ baai ni fa fe nine ni haaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ aba lɛ nɔ.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my crops so the rain does not waste it?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mawo midumɔ nii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii koni nugbɔ lɛ akafite?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is damp after light or moderate rain, but avoid applying it right before or during heavy downpours that will wash the nutrients off the field before root systems can take them in.
ga: Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo loo nɔ ni fa fioo sɛɛ. Shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ amɛwomɔ he dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa loo yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ. Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii jeɔ saatso lɛ nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why do certified seeds I buy from the store grow faster and stronger than seeds saved from my old harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni miheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ mikpamɔ momo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially selected, treated against hidden seed-borne diseases, and tested for high germination power, whereas saved market seeds may carry diseases or have lost their vitality over time.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ. Tsamɔ helai ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛbaa lɛ Ni aka lɛ akwɛ akɛ eyɛ nyɛmɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, jara nɔ dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baanyɛ aná hela loo amɛhe akawo mli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What is a greenhouse, and how can it protect my vegetables from bad weather?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-vegetables lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ ahe?

english: A greenhouse is a covered structure made of clear plastic or glass that creates a protected environment for crops. It guards your vegetables against heavy rains, strong winds, and destructive pests while keeping conditions steady so plants grow faster and healthier.
ga: Greenhouse ji ŋwɛitsu ni akɛ plastic loo glase ni mli tse fee ni haa shihilɛ ni buɔ he kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Ebuɔ o-vegetables lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe. At the same time maintaining a stable condition. To make plants grow faster and healthier.

english: Why does it get so much hotter inside a plastic greenhouse than the weather outside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plastic tsũ ko ni mli edɔ waa fe kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: Greenhouses trap energy from sunlight and convert it into heat that cannot easily escape through the plastic cover. While this extra heat helps crops grow in cooler periods, side vents or netting must be opened on hot days to allow trapped hot air to flow out.
ga: Greenhouses lɛ mɔ̃ɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la mli lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ dɔlɛ ni nyɛŋ atsɔ plastic ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ nɔ ajɛ mli oya. Shi kɛlɛ, nɛkɛ dɔlɛ ni fa nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii daa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Shi, yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ lɛ, esa akɛ agbele sɛɛgbɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai loo ŋtayaai lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ aje kpo.

english: Does the weather outside still affect my crops if I plant them inside a greenhouse structure?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ kpo lɛ nɔ lɛ baaná miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ lolo kɛji midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Yes, because the temperature, sunlight, and air moisture outside directly drive conditions inside. On an extremely hot sunny day outside, heat rapidly builds up inside the structure, requiring you to cool or ventilate the area for your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ dɔlɛ, hulu la, kɛ fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ kudɔɔ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. On a clear day, it is very hot outside. Heat accumulates quickly inside the structure. Enɛ biɔ ni oha he ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ mli adɔ loo okɛ kɔɔyɔɔ awo mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather gets very hot in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji edɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses plants and stops pollen from fertilizing the flowers properly. To save energy and survive the intense heat, the plant naturally drops its blossoms before fruits can form.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa pollen lɛ anyɛ aha amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato ni ehi wala mli yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli Tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ adebɔɔ naa dani ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my crop leaves wilt in the afternoon heat even though I watered the soil in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu leebi?

english: During scorching hot afternoons, water evaporates from leaf surfaces faster than the roots can drink it up from the soil. The leaves temporarily droop to conserve moisture, but they usually recover once temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Nu shwieɔ baa lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do some of my young seedlings need shade nets while other full-grown crops like direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ ekomɛi he hiaa shade netting lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi ni eda tamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ

english: Young nursery seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under full sun. Shade nets reduce light intensity and keep them cool, whereas mature crops like tomatoes need full sunlight to make energy for fruiting.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shading nets haa la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baa shi ni ehaa hulutsoo baa. Beni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ, tsei tamɔ tomatoi lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwo yibii.

english: How does heavy rain damage my vegetable crops beyond just beating down the leaves?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ mi-vegetables lɛ kɛfata baai ni efiteɔ lɛ he?

english: Heavy rainfall washes valuable plant nutrients deep into the soil beyond root reach, packs the ground too tight for roots to breathe, and leaves moisture on plant leaves where fungal diseases can easily multiply.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ tsei amli niyenii ni jara wa lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he. Paki shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ tsɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu. ni eshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ yɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants develop leaf disease and rot quickly during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ náa baai hela ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves dislike being constantly wet. Rain droplets splash disease spores from the soil onto the plant, and high moisture levels create an ideal environment for fungi and bacteria to grow on leaf surfaces.
