ga: Tomato baai sumɔɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa tsei anɔ. Ni hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: How does high air moisture or dampness affect the health of my vegetable crops?
ga: Te hulutsoo loo hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ saa mi-aduawai lɛ ahewalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When the air stays very humid and stagnant around your plants, moisture stays trapped on leaf surfaces for too long. This high humidity encourages leaf spots, white mildews, and rot to spread through your crop.
ga: Beni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle Tso lɛ he lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ dioo. Fɛ̃i baahi baa lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nɛkɛ hulutsoo ni fa nɛɛ woɔ baa mli ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he hewalɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã onibii fɛɛ amli.

english: Why does strong wind make my crop leaves turn brown and dry at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa haa mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Strong dry winds pull moisture out of plant leaves faster than the roots can replace it, causing the leaf edges to scorch and dry out. Windbreaks or shade netting help slow down air movement and retain plant moisture.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ atsake lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ shãa ni egbiɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ mli tsɔnei loo shade ŋshɔŋlooi yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa blɛoo ni ehaa tsei lɛ amli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi.

english: Why should I trim or prune the extra branches off my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ kookoo tso mli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches so air and sunlight can flow through the tree canopy. This lowers humidity around the tree, preventing fungal diseases and encouraging healthier pod growth.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la anyɛ atsɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ. Enɛ haa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ tso lɛ he lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi, ni ehaa pod lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will cutting away branches from my cocoa tree hurt the crop?
ga: Ani kookoo tso niji ni afolɔ lɛ baaná ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ gbonyo?

english: No, removing extra or sickly branches actually helps the tree. It directs the tree's energy away from wasted leaf growth and focuses it on growing stronger stems and bigger cocoa pods.
ga: Dabi, niji ni fata he loo ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Ejieɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni afiteɔ lɛ ni edaa lɛ mli. ni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama tsei ni wa kɛ kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do extension workers tell me to cut down cocoa trees that look sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni sɛɛkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mifolɔ kookoo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Certain cocoa diseases, like Swollen Shoot disease, cannot be cured with chemicals. Cutting down and removing infected trees stops the disease from spreading through the roots or insects to the rest of your healthy farm.
ga: Anyɛɛɛ akɛ tsofa atsa kookoo helai komɛi, tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni oookpa ni ojie lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akatsɔ shishifãi loo kooloi amli kɛya oŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fã kroko lɛ mli.

english: How can I check my cocoa trees to know if a disease is starting to attack them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ koni mana kɛji helai miibɔi amɛ tutuamɔ?

english: Look out for early signs such as swollen stems, yellowing or misshapen leaves, swollen roots, or dark spots on pods during your routine farm walks so you can take action before it spreads.
ga: Taomɔ mra be mli okadii tamɔ tsei ni efuu, baai ni efee ŋmɔŋ loo efite, shishifãi ni efuu loo ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni onyiɛɔ ŋmɔ mli daa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ ofee nɔ ko dani egbɛ eshwa.

english: What is cocoa farm rehabilitation and why does my farm need it?
ga: Mɛni ji Cocoa Faa He Saamɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni asaa miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa rehabilitation means replacing old, unproductive, or diseased cocoa trees with fresh, high-yielding seedlings so your farm can produce abundant cocoa pods again in the coming years.
ga: Kookoo ni atsakeɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ abaato kookoo tsei momoi lɛ anajiaŋ. Yibiiwoo loo hela ko bɛ kɛ dumɔwui heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔ lɛ anyɛ awo kookoo ŋmeii babaoo ekoŋŋ yɛ afii ni baa lɛ amli.

english: How should I care for newly planted cocoa seedlings so they grow strong?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ mi-kookoo tso ni midu ehee lɛ nɔ koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Young cocoa plants need nurturing through proper shade, regular weeding around their base, adequate soil moisture, and protection from leaf-eating insects while their roots get established.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akwɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni sa mli. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. Tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ daa. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ baai lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it important to plant new cocoa seedlings at proper distances rather than close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ he ko ni sa moŋ fe ni aaabɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Giving each seedling enough space prevents them from fighting over soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, ensuring that every tree grows tall and wide without crowding out its neighbors.
ga: Kɛ́ aha dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛye niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ he akaŋshii, ni ehaa amɛdaraa ni amɛshwereɔ ni amɛyeee amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ anɔ kunim.

english: Why do I need to walk through my farm regularly to observe my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa koni makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Regular observation lets you spot crop problems like pest invasions, weed competition, or early signs of sickness early when they are still cheap and easy to manage.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ mli daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona naagbai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli, tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ. Jwɛi akaŋshii loo hela he okadi mra Ejara hu waaa ni ekwɛmɔ waaa.

english: How does working together with neighboring farmers help protect my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ ni mikɛ amɛ feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ he?

english: Diseases and pests easily move from one farm to another. By cooperating with your neighbors to inspect farms and manage diseases together, you protect the entire community's cocoa harvest.
ga: Helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ ajɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛya ekroko mli oya. Kɛtsɔ akutsoŋbii ni akɛ amɛ baatsu nii koni amɛkwɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛfee ekome kɛkwɛ helai anɔ lɛ nɔ. Obaabu akutso muu lɛ fɛɛ kookoo ni akpaa lɛ he.

english: Why is weed control so important when nurturing young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ jwɛi anɔ kɛ́ akwɛɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight from your young cocoa trees, which slows down their growth and makes them weak.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ o-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛdalɛ baa shi, ni ehaa amɛgbɔjɔɔ.

english: This usually happens when your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build strong green leaves. When there isn't enough nitrogen in the soil, the plant moves what little it has from its older bottom leaves up to the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ baajie nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛ baai momo lɛ amli kɛya shweremɔ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I keep my soil fertile and get good crop yields if commercial fertilizers are too expensive for me?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛo ni maná ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai? Kɛji akɛ jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jara wa tsɔ kɛha mi

english: You can enrich your soil without high costs by mixing dried animal manure or composted farm waste into your beds, and by rotating your main crops with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts, which naturally put nitrogen back into the dirt.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni jara wa ni okɛ shika babaoo tsuuu nii kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ mli sũ ni egbi loo ŋmɔ mli sũ ni afee lɛ ŋmɔ mli sũ ni okɛfutuɔ osɛɛ lɛ nɔ. kɛtsɔ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii ni okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii baatsake lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when I plant them in an open field without tall trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full sun. They need fast-growing shade crops like plantains planted alongside them to act as living umbrellas, providing shade and trapping soil moisture during their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ tsei bibii ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii akɛ umbrella ni hiɛ ka Ha hulutsoo ni ehiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why does the ground around my vegetable plants dry out so quickly in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle No hewɔ lɛ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses water fast due to direct sunlight and wind heat. Covering the soil around your plants with dry grass, straw, or leaves (mulching) acts as a blanket that keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dɔlɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi, jwɛi, loo baai (mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow tall and thin with very few fruits when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni efeɔ mlɛo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight for the same food, water, and sunlight. Giving each plant proper space allows it to branch out strong and put energy into producing full fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe miitswa niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kome he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ená niji ni wa ni ekɛ ehewalɛ awo yibii.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce smaller bunches of fruit as the farm gets older?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii bibii lɛ? Beni ŋmɔ lɛ daa lɛ

english: A main plantain tree produces extra shoots called suckers that steal water and nutrients from the main stem. If you cut back extra suckers and leave only two or three strong ones per stool, the main stem gets enough food to make big bunches.
ga: Plantain titri lɛ woɔ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛji ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oshi ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ ŋmeii kome mli lɛ. Tso titri lɛ baaná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha efee panicle agbo.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are ready to dig up if I cannot see them under the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakumɔ? Kɛji akɛ onyɛɛɛ ona shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually mature when the plant's lower leaves naturally dry up and drop off, leaving a bare stem, and the ground right around the stem begins to crack open from the tubers swelling beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca shɛɔ dalɛ he beni tso lɛ shishi baai lɛ egbiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. ni eshiɔ tso ni nɔ ko bɛ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishi jeɔ shishi efoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso ni efuu ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds but leave long wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mihe lɛ? Shi shi tsei kakadaji yɛ sɛɛ. Ha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in direct sunlight to manufacture food for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where they might rot or get shaded out by weeds.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi bulbs ni miida lɛ. Staking baaha tsei ahe tsei lɛ akaje hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi loo jwɛi baanyɛ afee amɛ shade.

english: What causes tiny holes in my corn leaves and green droppings inside the growing tip of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ tsei ni miida lɛ ashishifãi amli lɛ amli

english: This is damage caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar pest that crawls into the center funnel of young corn plants to feed on tender new leaves before they unfold.
ga: Enɛ ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ koni eye baai heei dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kɛbaa.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, long dry spells between watering, or a lack of specific nutrients like calcium. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa miigba tsei anaa. Be kakadaŋŋ ni mli egbi yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ. loo niyenii pɔtɛɛ ko ni bɛ, tamɔ calcium, beni haomɔ Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do strong windstorms keep knocking down my maize plants right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miiha mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miigbee shi dani akpa kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Maize plants have shallow root systems, making them top-heavy when heavy cobs grow. Strong winds easily pull these shallow roots out of wet soil. Heap soil around the base of the stems (earthing up) and plant windbreak trees along your farm boundary to block harsh gusts.
ga: Abɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa gbalaa nɛkɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ oya. Okɛ sũ abɔle tso lɛ shishi (okɛwo shikpɔŋ), ni odu kɔɔyɔɔ he tsɔnei yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa koni obu ohe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato plants break or touch the ground when they start producing a lot of heavy fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fãa loo amɛtaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛ́ amɛbɔi yibii babaoo womɔ?

english: Tomato stems are naturally flexible and cannot support heavy fruit weight on their own. When fruit touches wet soil, it rots or gets eaten by pests. Using wooden stakes or support cages holds the plants upright, keeping fruit clean and air circulating.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛwoɔ aduawai ni tsii lɛ amli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Kɛji aduawai lɛ ta shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ Ebaagbo loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baaye lɛ. Tso ŋtayaai loo ŋtayaai ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni aduawai lɛ ahe tseɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu tsɔɔ mli.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings scorching and drying up under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct heat because their tender leaves lose moisture faster than roots can absorb it. Planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides shade and keeps the surrounding air moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, cacao tso lɛ baai bibii lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo bibii duɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo baa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling tightly during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in hot weather is a natural defense mechanism where the plant reduces its leaf surface area to prevent water from evaporating too quickly. Providing light shade or mulching the soil keeps the roots cool and reduces heat stress.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei haa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ baa shi koni nu lɛ akatsɔ oya tsɔ. Shading loo mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground whenever we receive continuous heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water, the roots drown from a lack of oxygen and soil fungi cause them to decay. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away easily.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ha nu lɛ ahi shi. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why do my pepper crops lose all their flowers after a long dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔfɔi fɛɛ miifite yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When crops experience extreme drought heat, they drop their flowers to save water and energy for basic survival. Regular watering during flower formation prevents heat shock and ensures the flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ kpe lɛ Fɔfɔi baagbee shi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha shishijee wala. Kɛ́ afɔ nu daa yɛ fɔfɔii ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulutsoo akafee nɔ ko, ni ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Planted too closely, crops compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of growing thick stems and big cobs, the plants stretch thin reaching for sunlight. Correct spacing gives each plant enough room to thrive.
ga: adu ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ tsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii wuji. Mohu ɔ, tso ɔ gblaa e niji nyafii ɔmɛ a mi konɛ e ná pu la ɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many small, young pods before they can mature into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmeii bibii bibii lɛ? Mɛi babaoo dani pods lɛ dara kwraa?

english: This natural process is called cherelle wilt, where the tree sheds excess young pods it cannot feed due to lack of water or soil nutrients. Proper pruning and soil fertilization ensure the tree has enough energy to carry its fruit to full maturity.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ Cherelle Wilt, ni ji tsei lɛ jieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aye niyenii yɛ nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsei ni afolɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ewo yibii kɛyashi eda.

english: Why are the fresh leaf shoots on my pepper plants turning wrinkled and stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Wrinkled leaves on young pepper shoots are usually caused by microscopic sap-sucking pests like thrips or mites feeding on leaf juices. Spraying neem oil or insecticidal soap protects new growth from pest damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baa nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni egbɔjɔ yɛ tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why do cowpea crops seem to make the soil healthier for my maize in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina tso baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi ŋmãa lɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen gas from the air and stores it in root nodules. When the plant dies, this nitrogen naturally enriches the soil, feeding the heavy-eating maize planted afterward.
ga: Cowpeas ji legume weku lɛ mlinyo ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nɛkɛ nitrogen nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Amɛhaa ŋmãa ni tsii ni adu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen or getting too much water. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or improving field drainage helps the leaves regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen loo enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baa shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves naturally as a survival mechanism to conserve moisture during hot, dry weather. The plant is still alive underground and will sprout fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaai lɛ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa akɛ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi koni ekɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Tso lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni ebaawo baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: What causes my tomato flowers to fall off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the air is extremely hot, when watering is irregular, or when insects like bees are not around to help pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Nu ni akɛhaaa daa Aloo be mli ni kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ ji koni eye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination.

english: How do I know if my crops are getting enough water in the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: If your crop leaves look limp, curled, or wilted early in the morning before the sun gets strong, the plants are suffering from water stress and need immediate watering.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ, ebɔle ehe, loo egbɔjɔ leebi dani hulu la lɛ mli wa lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miina nu he haomɔ ni ehe miihia ni awo lɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why are my pepper plants remaining short and bushy instead of growing taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɔɔ kuku lolo ni eyɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Stunted pepper plants are often suffering from pest attacks like thrips or mites, or they may be growing in compacted soil that prevents roots from spreading to gather nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ thrips loo mites tutuaa dwarf pepper tsei lɛ. Aloo amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ koni shishifãi lɛ akagbɛ amɛshwã koni amɛbua niyenii mli hewalɛ naa.

english: How do I know when my yam tubers are mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams are ready to harvest when the leaves and vines above the ground dry up and turn brown, indicating that the plant has finished transferring energy into the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛ́ baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ egbi ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: What is the best way to store my harvested maize so that weevils do not destroy it?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato koni ŋmeii akafite?

english: Ensure the maize is dried thoroughly until the kernels are very hard, then store it in airtight hermetic bags or clean sacks placed off the ground in a cool, dry room.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni ŋmãa lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛwo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo kotoku ni mli tse mli ni akɛwo shikpɔŋ yɛ tsu ko ni mli ejɔ ni mli egbi mli.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes rot so quickly after I pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes rot fast if they are picked when already soft, packed tightly in unventilated containers, or stored in hot places, which traps moisture and speeds up decay.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ajie lɛ beni eyɛ bɔdɔɔ lɛ. Okɛwo tsɛnsi ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. aloo akɛtoɔ hei ni mli edɔ, ni no mɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa efiteɔ oya.

english: Why do my plantains ripen all at once and spoil before I can reach the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ fɛɛ shwereɔ shikome ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛshɛɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains release a natural gas that triggers rapid ripening when kept together in hot spaces. Harvesting them while green and keeping them well-ventilated and shaded delays ripening.
ga: Plantains jieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa amɛshwereɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni hulu tsoɔ waa. Kɛ́ akpa nikpamɔ be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni akɛha kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaha ekwɛ̃mɔ lɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: How can I avoid getting low prices from middle buyers when selling my harvested vegetables?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mihe kɛjɛ jara ni baa shi ni jɛɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ he beni mikɛ mi-aduawai ni mikpa lɛ hɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Sorting your produce by size and quality before selling helps you charge higher prices for top-grade crops, and selling together with a local farmer group gives you stronger negotiating power.
ga: Kɛ́ ohala onibii lɛ amli yɛ bɔ ni amɛdalɛ kɛ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ha lɛ naa dani ohɔ̃ɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni okɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ awo nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe. Ni kɛ okɛ okwaafoi akui ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ hɔ̃ɔ nii lɛ, ehaa onáa sanegbaa he hewalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Officer, why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When maize leaves turn yellow starting from the tip down the center vein, it shows the plant is starving for nitrogen in the soil. Applying top-dressing fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted manure gives the crop the food it needs to build green, healthy leaves.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnaagbee kɛtee amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ miiye hɔmɔ kɛha nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ko ni akɛwoɔ nɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ená tso lɛ yibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of insect pollinators. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch and watering regularly helps the plant hold onto its flowers until they turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo pollinators ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni okɛ nu wo mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashi ebaawo yibii.

english: Officer, why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning light yellow?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies or by using infected stems for planting. You can stop it by planting disease-resistant cassava varieties and pulling out infected plants early.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela, ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ dumɔwui amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Obaanyɛ okpa kɛtsɔ ŋmei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie mra lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my plantain tree give small bunches when many suckers are growing around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young suckers act like hungry children competing with the main tree for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Removing extra suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones ensures the main tree gets enough energy to grow large fruit bunches.
ga: Tso bibii lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbekɛbii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ, ni amɛkɛ tso ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, nu lɛ mli, kɛ hulu la mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso ni hereɔ lɛ lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ yibii wuji.

english: Officer, why do my green cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree during the heavy rains?
ga: Ofisa Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi ni eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod Disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, dark, and damp shade. You can protect your cocoa by removing affected pods quickly, pruning tree branches to let sunlight reach the trunk, and keeping the farm weeded.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ fɔ́, ediŋŋ, hɔɔmɔ mli ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Obaanyɛ obu o-cocoa lɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ena hela lɛ oya ni ooojie lɛ nɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei aniji koni hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ shishi. kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why is my seed yam taking over two months to sprout after I plant it in the mound?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ he nɔ ni fe nyɔji enyɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ beni midu amɛ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams go through a natural rest period called dormancy after harvest. During this time, the seed yam rests internally and will not sprout until the dormancy naturally breaks when the soil becomes warm and dry enough.
ga: Sweet potatoes yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ baajɔɔ amɛhe yɛ mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ŋ kɛyashi be mli ni shihilɛ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baafite yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni egbi bɔ ni sa lɛ.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas before maize makes the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu tsina ŋmãa dani adu ŋmãa lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their roots. When the cowpea roots rot in the soil, they leave behind free plant food that feeds the next crop of maize.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔmɔ lɛ yɛ eshishifãi amli. Kɛji cowpea shishifãi lɛ gboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛshiɔ tso lɛ niyenii yɛ amɛsɛɛ akɛ niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Officer, why does my lowland rice grow well in flooded fields, but my maize rots and dies if flooded?
ga: Official Mɛni hewɔ mi-flat ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli lɛ? Shi ani mi-ŋma lɛ baagbo ni egbo kɛji nu shwie nɔ?

english: Rice plants have special internal tubes in their stems that pump air down to their roots under water. Maize roots do not have these tubes, so when trapped under water, they cannot breathe and quickly drown and rot.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ mligbɛ tsɔnei krɛdɛɛi ni shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu shishi. Abɛi shishifãi bɛ nɛkɛ tsɔnei nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ nu shishi lɛ Amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. and quickly drowns and decays

english: Why do my tall maize plants fall over easily whenever strong rain and wind blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ baa lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over when planted too close together or when planted too shallow in soft soil. Planting seeds at the proper depth and piling extra soil around the stem base helps the plant grow strong support roots.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ tsɔ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni sa kɛ sũ krokomɛi ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa.

english: Officer, why are my tomatoes cracking open on the skin right before they get ripe?
ga: Officer Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi lɛ fãa dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Cracking happens when tomato plants go through long dry spells followed by sudden heavy watering or rain. The inside of the tomato grows faster than the skin can stretch, causing the skin to split open.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ baa kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ tsɔ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli. Followed by watering or sudden heavy rain. Tomato lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Young cocoa trees have weak root systems and burn easily under strong heat. During dry months like the Harmattan, intense sunlight and low humidity dry out the leaves. Planting shade crops like plantain beside young cocoa protects them from direct sunlight and holds moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛshãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa shishi. Yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ tamɔ Harmattan lɛ amli lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be ni baa shi lɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. and retain moisture in the soil

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting right on the branches when heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in high humidity and wet conditions. The rain splashes fungal spores from the soil onto the pods. Clearing weeds, pruning dense branches to let in air, and removing infected pods early helps stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli lɛ kɛbaa. Nugbɔ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ewoɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. weeding Niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ekpa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves have holes eaten in them with little black dirt inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ muji diji bibii lɛ? Yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide deep inside the central leaf whorl of the maize plant to feed on fresh leaves, leaving behind their waste which looks like black dirt. Catching them early with recommended sprays or neem extracts prevents them from destroying the plant's growing point.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai heei lɛ. Kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni tamɔ sũ diŋ ni ashiɔ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ nɔ lɛ ebaaye ebua ni amɛkafite hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why does my maize crop turn light green or pale yellow after continuous heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes nitrogen—an essential plant food—deep into the earth below where roots can reach, a process called leaching. Without nitrogen, the plant cannot produce its dark green chlorophyll, causing leaves to turn pale until fertilizer is applied.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen, ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛyaa. Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ lɛ. Nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ leaching. Kɛji nitrogen bɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee klorofil ni ji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli.

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You will notice the lower leaves turning yellow and dropping, and the soil right around the base of the stem will begin to crack open as the tubers expand underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, ni enɛ damɔ ŋmei lɛ henɔ lɛ nɔ. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaje shishi egbɛ eshwa be mli ni tuber lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear away old dry suckers around the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie tsei ni egbɔ ni egbi ni bɔle mi-plantains lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow around one plantain stem creates competition for light, water, and soil nutrients. Keeping only 2 or 3 healthy suckers per mat allows the main plant to produce a much heavier and bigger plantain bunch.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he Plantain kome pɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei bibii 2 loo 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ toɔ mat kome nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ plantains tsei ni dara ni tsii waa.

english: Why must I put tall wooden stakes next to my yam plants once the vines start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko fɔ̃ɔ sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi kɛji wain tso lɛ ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ?

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs maximum sunlight to make food for its underground tuber. Staking lifts the foliage off the hot ground, preventing leaf diseases from damp soil and ensuring the plant captures enough sunlight to build large tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. Tsi tso helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli baa lɛ naa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni emɔɔ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ bulb agboi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting and curling upward like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the underside of young leaves, or by viruses transmitted by these pests. Inspecting leaf undersides and applying appropriate organic or chemical sprays keeps the pest population under control.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ ashishigbɛ nibii ni akwɛɔ mli kɛ tsofai ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii ayibɔ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning dark brown and sunken before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efoɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium to the developing fruit, usually because of irregular watering or dry spells. Maintaining steady moisture around the roots helps the plant transport calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tso lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔɔ daa loo hɔmɔ be ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nibii ni haa hulutsoo be fɛɛ be yɔɔ Shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ calcium yaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my groundnut roots have small round bumps attached to them when I pull them out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ? Ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ he beni mijieɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ muji lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Those small bumps are root nodules containing beneficial bacteria. These bacteria take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural fertilizer for the groundnut crop, which also leaves the soil richer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji shishifãi ni mli ewo muji ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛduɔ ŋmeii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the center leaves of my maize plants, and how do I stop them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that destroys young maize leaves. You can control them by applying recommended pest controls early in the morning or late in the evening when the worms come out to feed.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni fiteɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛyeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsuɔ he nii lɛ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kooloi lɛ jeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some of the maize seeds I buy from the local market fail to grow after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grain sold in open markets is often meant for eating and may be old or damaged. To get seeds that germinate properly, buy certified seeds from registered agricultural dealers who store them correctly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmaa ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni akɛyeɔ ni ebaanyɛ egbɔ loo efite. Bɔni afee ni ona dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ Be fɛɛ be lɛ, hemɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko ni aŋma egbɛi awo wolo nɔ ni toɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ dɛŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Applying the right fertilizer like NPK or Urea at the right time will give the plant the food it needs to stay green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa, tamɔ NPK loo urea wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What causes white powder or dark spots to appear on my crops during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa powda yɛŋ loo ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: These spots are caused by fungal diseases that spread easily in damp, wet weather. Spacing your crops properly to allow air movement and applying suitable fungicides helps protect your farm.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ hei nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ to he jogbaŋŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli, ni okɛ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ atsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: When is the best time to put fertilizer on my maize farm so it doesn't go to waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii koni akafite?

english: Apply the first fertilizer two weeks after the seeds sprout, and the second when the plant reaches knee height. Avoid applying fertilizer right before heavy rains, as the water can wash the nutrients away.
ga: Okɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo mli otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ. ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli shii enyɔ nɔ beni tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛnaji ahe lɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he dani nugbɔ anɛ waa ejaakɛ nu lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ.

english: How can I prevent insects from eating my harvested maize while it is stored in my barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ be mli ni mikɛtoɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils attack maize that is not completely dry or protected. Ensure your grains are dried thoroughly until hard, and store them in airtight hermetic bags or treat them with approved storage powders.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii tutuaa ŋmãa ni egbiko kwraa loo abuuu he lɛ. Kwɛmɔ ni oŋmaa lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaawa. ni okɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli loo okɛ powda ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛtoɔ lɛ ato he.

english: Why does leaving weeds on my farm reduce the size of my maize cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mi-ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ anɔ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crop for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early within the first four weeks gives your maize full access to nutrients, leading to larger cobs.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ lɛ baaha o-ŋmã lɛ aná niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ haa anáa cob ni da fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up and droop during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants curl their leaves to reduce water loss when the sun is very intense. While this is a normal self-defense reaction, prolonged dry weather without water will stunt the crop's growth.
ga: Tsei baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛ́ hulu la lɛ mli wa waa. Eyɛ mli akɛ enɛ ji nɔ ko ni afɔɔ feemɔ ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he moŋ, shi be kakadaŋŋ ni nu bɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil and encourages pests. Legumes like groundnuts naturally put nitrogen back into the soil, making it richer for the next maize season.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ be fɛɛ be ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ. Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛhaa nitrogen kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why is it dangerous to harvest and eat my vegetables immediately after spraying them with farm chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ makpa mi-vegetables lɛ ni maye amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ tsofai eshwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Chemicals leave residues on plants that need a specific waiting period to break down safely. Harvesting too soon leaves poison on the crop, which can cause sickness when consumed.
ga: Tsofai shĩɔ nɔ ko ni eshwɛ yɛ tsei anɔ ni heɔ be babaoo dani efiteɔ shweshweeshwe. Nikpamɔ mra tsɔ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ poison. ni baanyɛ ekɛ hela aba kɛji aye

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that provide vital shade and moisture, protecting the cocoa plants during their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How do I know when the seasonal rains are steady enough to safely plant my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be mli lɛ yaa nɔ daa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu dumɔwui shweshweeshwe?

english: It is best to wait until you have two or three heavy downpours that thoroughly wet the soil deep down, ensuring the seeds will have enough continuous moisture to germinate without drying out.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ náa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yaa nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: How far apart should I plant cassava stems in my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Planting cassava stems about one meter apart gives each plant enough space and light to grow large root tubers underground without competing with nearby plants for soil food.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei lɛ aaafee mita kome lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi wuji akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ abɔi niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he akaŋ

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden sticks next to my yam mounds for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama emasɛi lɛ? Pile sweet potatoes kɛha wain tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves toward the sun, which helps the plant produce more energy to grow bigger yam tubers underneath the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my growing maize plants turning light green and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food the plant needs to grow dark green leaves and strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni tsuɔ waa kɛ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Should I put fertilizer in the hole at the same time I plant my seeds?
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo bu lɛ mli yɛ be kome too mli. Kɛ dumɔwui adumɔ loo daabi?

english: It is usually better to wait until the seed sprouted and formed roots a few weeks later so the plant can actually drink the fertilizer instead of letting rain wash it away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛma shishifãi yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ anu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha nugbɔ lɛ ahoo lɛ

english: Why do some farmers place dry grass and leaves around the stems of their crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai fɔ̃ɔ amɛtsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry leaves keeps the ground cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly in the heat, and stops weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji akɛ edɔ. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and encourages pests to stay; swapping with beans or peanuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be, ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ tsake ŋmeii loo ŋmeii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by fall armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the growing center and require early treatment to prevent leaf destruction.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ cutworm caterpillars ni kɛ amɛhe ewoɔ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baa bibii amli lɛ baa. ni esa akɛ atsa lɛ mra Koni baai lɛ akafite

english: Why is it important for me to prune or cut extra branches off my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo loo majie niji krokomɛi ni fata he kɛjɛ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Trimming unnecessary branches lets sunlight and fresh air flow through the tree canopy, which reduces dampness that causes black pod disease and helps the tree produce more cocoa pods.
ga: Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. Enɛ haa hulutsoo ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baa shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ kookoo ŋmeii babaoo

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient the plant needs to grow strong and green. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted manure around the roots will help the plant regain its green color and grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my harvest drop if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ baa shi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize on the same soil every season drains the exact same nutrients and allows soil pests to build up over time. Rotating your maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts refills nitrogen into the soil and keeps it healthy for your next crop.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tamɔ nakai pɛpɛɛpɛ kpo. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ be ni sa mli. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake o-corn lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni eha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell which way is right-side up when planting cassava stem cuttings?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei ni afo lɛ miikwɛ ninejurɔgbɛ kɛtee ŋwɛi?

english: Look closely at the small buds or nodes along the cassava stem cutting—they should always point upward toward the sky. Planting cassava upside down makes it difficult for the sprouts to shoot up and leads to poor root development.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tsei bibii lɛ. loo nodes bibii Taakɛ ŋmei ni afoɔ lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ Esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha ewa aha dumɔwui lɛ akɛ amɛakwɛ̃, ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ akakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Which kind of plantain sucker is best for me to dig up and plant on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain sucker hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mafo ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Choose 'sword suckers' that have narrow, blade-like leaves and a broad base, rather than 'water suckers' with wide leaves. Sword suckers have stronger energy reserves, establish faster in the field, and produce heavier bunches.
ga: Halamɔ ‘Sword Bud’ ni baai lɛ mli tse, tamɔ ŋmei kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli kwɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahala ‘nu mli ŋmeii’ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ, klante suckers lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ. Bɔɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ofee kuu ni tsii.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat deep holes into the funnels of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that hides inside the young leaves (the whorl) of maize to feed. Spraying approved insecticides directly into the funnel early in the morning or late evening will reach and kill the worms.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa baai bibii (rings) amli koni eye niyenii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie ŋmeii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaashɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe ni egbe amɛ.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, mites, or thrips feeding on leaf sap and spreading plant viruses. Treating your farm with neem oil or targeted insect sprays controls these insects and allows new leaves to grow healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids, mites loo thrips ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ tsu oŋmɔ lɛ he nii lɛ, ebaakudɔ kooloi nɛɛ ni eye ebua baai heei ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers, but most drop off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔlɔ babaoo lɛ? Shi amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi ni amɛfeee pods?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop flowers when they experience stress from prolonged heat, lack of moisture, poor soil nutrients, or insect attacks. Managing farm shade, maintaining soil moisture, and controlling pests like capsids will help more flowers turn into cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ he. Fɛ̃i ni bɛ Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi tutuamɔ Okwaafoi akwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i nɔkwɛmɔ Kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ baaye abua fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛtsɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot and happens when tomato roots cannot absorb enough calcium, usually because of irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist through regular watering and mulching prevents the fruit bottoms from rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni ebaa kɛ́ tomato shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi aduawai ashishi lɛ anaa koni ekafite.

english: Will planting my crops very close together give me a bigger total harvest from my farm?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni jɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ babaoo?

english: No, overcrowding crops causes them to fight for sunlight, water, and soil food, making the plants weak and yields small. Planting with recommended spacing ensures every plant gets enough space and nutrients to produce large, healthy fruits.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa amɛwuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo. Tso ni aduɔ yɛ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ adu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops wilt in the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During intense afternoon heat, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can draw it up from the soil. Placing dry grass mulching around the plant base keeps the root zone cool and retains water in the soil throughout the day.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi wo otsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the dry season, young cocoa trees lose water rapidly through their leaves. Without adequate shade from larger trees to block the direct heat, the plant sheds its leaves to reduce water loss and protect its main trunk from drying out.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, cacao tsei bibii lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ tsei wuji amli bɛ ni baatsi dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. ni ebu tso titri lɛ he koni ekagbi

english: Why do I need to put up tall wooden poles for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants make food for growing underground tubers through their leaves. Staking lifts the vines high off the wet ground so the leaves can catch direct sunlight while remaining safe from soil-borne diseases and rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei haa niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛhiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛ fitemɔ he.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize after the long dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa beni nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ eho lɛ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain event, as the soil underneath is still dry and hot. Wait until the soil receives two or three steady rains so there is enough deep moisture to keep seeds germinating safely.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ lolo. Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ nɛ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni ená ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does my cassava field produce big, leafy stems but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsei kɛ baai wuji shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients like potassium. The cassava uses all its energy to grow leaves and branches above ground instead of sending energy down to swell the roots.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he waa, tamɔ potassium lɛ fa babaoo fe nitrogen. Yucca kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai kɛ eniji lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ, moŋ fe ni eeetsu lɛ kɛba shi koni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: If too many sucker shoots grow together, they fight the main plant for soil nutrients, water, and light. Pruning them away leaves only one or two strong suckers, ensuring your main tree produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii lɛ fee ekome kɛdara tsɔ Ekɛ tso titri lɛ baawuu kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ la. Kɛ́ ofolɔ lɛ, ebaashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ebaaha otso titri lɛ aná ŋmeii wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and eaten centers in the stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Mi ŋmãa gbekɛ lɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni miyeɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves of young maize plants to feed, which stops the plant from growing normally unless properly treated early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli koni amɛye niyenii. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ jogbaŋŋ. ja akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ mra

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their blossoms before any peppers actually grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fɛɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ daa diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences sudden heat stress, prolonged dry soil, or excessive water around the roots. Keeping the soil evenly moist and shaded during peak heat helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ trukaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi be kakadaŋŋ. loo nu babaoo ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee fɛ̃i ni eyɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Does leaving dried weeds and grass covering the base of my crops actually help them grow?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni egbi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛshiɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Yes, leaving dry grass on top of the soil acts as a protective blanket. It keeps the sun from evaporating soil water, stops weed seeds from sprouting, and gradually breaks down into natural food for your crops.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Morning watering is best because it gives the crops moisture to survive the hot sun during the day. Watering in the evening leaves the leaves wet overnight, which creates a damp environment for plant diseases and fungi to spread.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ ehaa tso lɛ nu ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Nu ni oooha amɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ nyɔɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa ni tsei ahe helai kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do crops grow very well in one section of my farm but remain short and weak in another section?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã ko mli shi ebɛ hewalɛ ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ fã kroko lɛ?

english: Soil quality is rarely the same across an entire farm. The weaker section may have lower nutrient levels, harder soil that holds less water, or past erosion, meaning it requires additional organic manure or compost to rebuild its fertility.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su lɛ efɔɔɔ kaa yɛ ŋmɔji amli fɛɛ. Ekolɛ fãi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni baa shi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni nu fioo pɛ ehiɛɔ. aloo efite yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe baahia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he koni akɛtswa eŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green and strong. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK early in the plant's life helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK fata he yɛ tso lɛ wala shishijee mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: How does covering my crop beds with dry leaves or grass help my plants grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi ha mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua mitsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground during hot weather, keeps roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing and stealing food from your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ ni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why is it better to put fertilizer in small holes next to my crops instead of scattering it everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo bu bibioo mli lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ masɛi hi fe ni magbɛ amɛshwã he fɛɛ he?

english: Placing fertilizer near the roots puts the food right where the plant can drink it. Scattering it allows weeds to eat the fertilizer or rain to wash it away before your crop gets a chance to use it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa niyenii lɛ hiɔ he ko ni tsei lɛ baanyɛ anu. Gbalamɔ haa jwɛi lɛ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni ekɛshwieɔ amɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension officer lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them restores natural nutrients back into the ground so your next crop can yield better without buying as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei nɛɛ adumɔ baaye abua ni adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni oha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba yibii kpakpai ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Why should I cut off some of the young shoots growing around my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ ekomɛi?

english: If too many shoots grow around one mother plant, they all fight for the same soil food and water, leaving you with thin stems and small bunches. Keeping only one or two strong shoots ensures big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ single mother tree Amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Enɛ haa onáa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 1 loo 2 pɛ to lɛ, ebaaha plantain lɛ afee agbo ni etsii.

english: Why do I need to support my yam vines with wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei akwɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in the sunshine to produce energy that grows large underground tubers. Lifting the vines up on stakes helps them catch sunlight and keeps leaves off the wet ground where diseases spread.
ga: Esa akɛ agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ daa lɛ aba. Kɛ́ awó wain tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulu la, ni ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when the tree is stressed by excessive heat, lack of water, or attacks from tiny pests like mirids. Maintaining shade trees and controlling pests helps the flowers stay on and become healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine, nu ni faaa, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ fɔfɔi lɛ tutua tso lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei lɛ wo hulutsoo mli ni akwɛɛɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap out of new growth. Spraying recommended neem oil or proper insect control treatments stops these insects and lets new leaves grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ekɛ nu ni jɛɔ dalɛ hee mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. Neem Mu ni Akɛshwieɔ Nɔ loo Kooloi Ahe Nitsumɔ ni Sa ni Atsɔɔ Ehaa kooloi nɛɛ kpaa ni ehaa baa heei daa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do the bottoms of my ripening tomatoes turn dark brown and rot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shishi miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ?

english: This dark rot at the base of the fruit is called blossom-end rot, caused by uneven watering which stops the plant from absorbing enough calcium. Watering your tomatoes regularly keeps the soil evenly damp and prevents it.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tso yibii lɛ shishi nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot. ni jɛɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli daa lɛ mli baa Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni baa lɛ naa.

english: Why are my cassava leaves showing light green patches and twisting sideways?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ji eŋɔli ni etsɔ ehe kɛtee afã lɛ?

english: Twisted leaves with pale patches are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava cuttings provided by agricultural officers prevents this sickness from destroying your farm.
ga: Baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa ekroko nɔ Kɛ okɛ ŋmei shishifãi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛhaa lɛ baaye abua ni hela nɛɛ akafite oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I spread a tarpaulin on the ground before threshing my harvested beans on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tarp awo shikpɔŋ dani mafolɔ ŋmeii ni akpa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Spreading a clean tarpaulin keeps your harvested beans off the bare dirt, preventing soil, small stones, and ground moisture from contaminating the grains and lowering their market value.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tarp ni he tse fɔ shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni muji kɛ sũ akafee okɔfi yibii ni okpa lɛ. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ, tɛi bibii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni amɛkafite dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛha amɛjarayeli jara lɛ aba shi.

english: Can I use a shelling machine for my dry beans just like I do for my corn?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ peeler atsu nii kɛha ŋmeii ni egbi tamɔ bɔ ni mifeɔ kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yes, motorized shelling and threshing machines can quickly separate dry beans from their pods just as they do with corn, saving you time and manual labor.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsɔne ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii ni akɛfoɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli oya tamɔ bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Ekɛ be kɛ nitsumɔ baa shi.

english: Is it better to thresh my beans right on the farm or pack the pods into sacks to process at home?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafo mi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo mawo ŋmeii lɛ awo kotokui amli koni akɛtsu nii yɛ shia?

english: Threshing directly on the farm saves energy and transport costs because you only carry clean, light seeds home instead of bulky, heavy pod waste.
ga: Nibii ni ashwieɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa hewalɛ kɛ shika ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ baa shi ejaakɛ dumɔwui ni he tse ni waaa pɛ okɛbaa shia. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshɛrɛ pods ni tsii ni tsii lɛ ashwie lɛ,

english: How does a combine harvester work when my bean crop is ready to be collected?
ga: Te tsɔne ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mi-beans lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: A combine harvester cuts the crop stalks and threshes the seeds out from the pods all in a single pass across the field, completing days of manual labor in just a few hours.
ga: Nibii ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ feɔ ekome lɛ shwieɔ tsei lɛ amli ni amɛshwieɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ fɛɛ shikome kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Enɛ gbeɔ gbii ni akɛ niji tsuɔ lɛ naa yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi pɛ mli.

english: How do I know when my bean pods are ready for threshing and shelling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-pea pods lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ?

english: When bean pods turn brittle, light brown, and make a dry rattling sound when shaken, the seeds inside are fully mature and will split open easily during threshing.
ga: Beni bean pods lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ Eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni efeɔ gbɛɛmɔ ni mli wa kɛji akpokpo Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ edɔ kwraa ni ebaakumɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ashɛreɔ lɛ.

english: What is the most efficient way to organize my farm workers when harvesting dry beans?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atoɔ miŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ kɛ́ mikpa ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ?

english: Assigning one group of workers to pick and bag the pods while another team prepares the threshing area ensures a continuous workflow and prevents pods from spilling on the ground.
ga: Nitsulɔi akuu kome ni akɛ nitsumɔ woɔ amɛdɛŋ koni amɛjie ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛwo mli yɛ be mli ni kuu kroko saa he ni ashwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nitsumɔ lɛ yaa nɔ daa, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ.

english: Why do my threshed beans often end up mixed with dirt, and how can I keep them clean?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean lɛ mli muji yɔɔ mli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maha ehe atse?

english: Beans pick up dirt when they contact bare ground during shelling; processing them over tarpaulins or elevated threshing tables keeps soil and foreign matter out of your final grain.
ga: Nuts lɛ shwieɔ muji kɛji ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko kpe yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ muji lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tarp loo okpɔlɔ ni awo nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni muji kɛ maŋsɛɛ nibii akabote onaagbee ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: Why do dry bean pods break open so easily under machine pressure without crushing the seeds inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ gbeleɔ amɛhe mlɛo yɛ tsɔnei ni nyɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ shishi ni amɛkuuu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: As bean pods dry out, their outer shells become brittle while the seeds inside remain firm, allowing threshing machinery to crack the pods open without damaging the crop.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbi lɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni mligbɛ dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmaa lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni efiteee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What happens if I leave my freshly picked sacks of bean pods out in the open field overnight?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ ŋmeii ni ajie ehee lɛ kotoku ko shwie shi? Ani ashi yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: Leaving sacks exposed overnight allows night dew or sudden rainfall to soak the pods, which can cause mold growth, seed discoloration, and grain rot.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi kotokui lɛ yɛ kpo nɔ gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ hulutsoo be loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii ada. dumɔwui ni tsakeɔ amɛhe su ni dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ afite

english: Why do we put harvested bean pods directly into woven sacks immediately after picking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔkɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ woɔ kotokui ni akpɛ́ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni wɔkpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Bagging picked pods right away makes them easy to move around the field, keeps them organized for threshing, and prevents loose pods from getting lost in the weeds.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ wo kotoku mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaafã kɛya ŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni akɛshwie ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. ni etsĩɔ ŋmeii ni egbee shi lɛ anaa koni amɛkalaaje yɛ jwɛi amli.

english: Why do people in the market often buy lemons together with fresh vegetables like cucumber and cabbage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ heɔ abonua kɛfataa aduawai heei tamɔ kukumba kɛ kaabɛji he lɛ?

english: Lemons act as a natural, safe sanitizer for vegetables. Their juice kills hidden insects and tiny worms inside cut vegetables without using dangerous chemicals before the food is prepared.
ga: Lemon tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni gbeɔ helai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha aduawai. Amɛ nu lɛ gbeɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ aduawai ni afolɔ mli lɛ amli ni ekɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui tsuuu nii dani esaa niyenii lɛ.

english: Is washing my harvested cabbages with plain water enough to clear out all the tiny insects hidden inside?
ga: Nu ni mikɛbaafɔ mi-cabbage ni akpa lɛ he lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaajie kooloi bibii lɛ kɛjɛ mli. Ani fɛɛ ehiɛ mli?

english: Plain water rinses away surface dirt, but insects hide deep inside the tight cabbage leaves. Using a mild natural acid like squeezed lemon juice forces hidden pests to die and loosen their grip from the produce.
ga: Nu yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ muji ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ. Shi kooloi bibii lɛ ehiɛ amɛhe yɛ kaabɛji baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ adebɔɔ mli acid ni mli jɔ, tamɔ abonua nu ni akɛmiimɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ agboi ni amɛgbee shi kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I make sure the cabbages and cucumbers I harvest are safe from tiny bugs before eating them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ kaabe kɛ kukumba ni mikpaa lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ahe? dani aye nii

english: After slicing open your vegetables, squeezing fresh lemon juice over them kills any remaining insects hiding inside, making the produce safe for consumption.
ga: Beni afolɔ aduawai sɛɛ Abonua nu hee ni ashɛre lɛ baagbe kooloi bibii ni eshwɛ ni ehiɛ amɛhe yɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha niyenii.

english: Why do I always find tiny worms and bugs inside my cabbage heads even when the outside leaves look clean?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii kɛ kooloi bibii lɛ? Be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyɛ kaabe yitso mli Kɛji akɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe tse po

english: Cabbages grow by wrapping tight layers of leaves around a center, which creates dark, moist, and protected spaces that naturally attract insects looking for shelter and soft food away from sunlight and predators.
ga: Cabbage daa kɛtsɔ ebaai ni ekɛwoɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ, ni no haa he ko feɔ duŋ, ŋmɔtɔ, ni abuɔ he. Enɛ gbalaa kooloi ni taoɔ wɔɔhe kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are cabbage plants so attractive to pests compared to many other farm crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai sumɔɔ kaabii tsei waa kɛ akɛto ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Cabbage leaves are soft, full of moisture, and rich in nutrients, making them a ideal feeding ground and laying site for moths, butterflies, and small insects.
ga: Kaabeji baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ. ŋmɔtɔ eyi mli obɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɛ mli Enɛ haa efeɔ niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ he ni ŋmeii, ŋmeii bibii, kɛ kooloi bibii fɔɔ yɛ.
