english: Do insects hiding inside vegetables die on their own once the crop is harvested from the field?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo aduawai amli lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔji amli?

english: No, tiny insects and larvae can stay alive inside harvested vegetables for days because the crop retains moisture and food energy long after being picked.
ga: Dabi, kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ ahi aduawai ni akpa lɛ anɔ gbii babaoo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni akɛto amɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my harvested cucumbers sometimes have tiny worms inside them when I cut them open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, kukuji ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ, kɛ́ mifo mli lɛ, ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Insects like fruit flies often lay eggs on cucumber flowers or young fruit skins. Once hatched, the tiny larvae burrow deep into the soft, watery flesh of the cucumber where they are protected.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii fɔɔ amɛwɔlɔi yɛ kukumba fɔfɔi loo aduawai ahewolo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ nɔ. Kɛji amɛfɔ pɛ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ kukumba loo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu yɔɔ mli ni buɔ amɛhe lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do cucumbers rot so quickly once insects manage to get inside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kukumbai lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji kooloi bote mli pɛ lɛ?

english: Cucumbers contain a very high amount of water. When insects burrow inside, they break the protective skin, allowing bacteria and fungi to enter and spread rot quickly through the watery flesh.
ga: Nu ni fa babaoo yɛ kukumba mli waa. Kɛji kooloo ko tsɔ mli Ebaafite hewolo ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ. Enɛ haa muawai kɛ ŋmeii boteɔ mli ni amɛgbɛɔ fitemɔ amɛshwãa oya kɛtsɔɔ nu lɛ mli.

english: How does lemon juice kill tiny bugs inside cut vegetables?
ga: Abonua nu gbeɔ kooloi bibii. Te ooofee tɛŋŋ onine ashɛ nɔ yɛ aduawai ni afolɔ mli?

english: Lemon juice is very acidic. When applied directly to tiny, soft-bodied insects and worms, the acid breaks down their skin and disrupts their breathing, killing them almost instantly.
ga: Abonua nu lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ acid waa. Kɛ akɛwo kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ gbɔmɔtso ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, acid lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewolo lɛ ni egbaa amɛmumɔ naa. ni egbeɔ amɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Can using lemon juice on sliced vegetables replace chemical insecticides after harvest?
ga: Ani abonua nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ aduawai ni afolɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni agbeɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Yes, for post-harvest preparation, lemon juice is a safe alternative to chemical sprays because it kills pests instantly on contact without leaving toxic chemical residues on food.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ hesaamɔ Lemon nu ji nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtoɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ najiaŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ eshɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni eshiŋ tsofa ko ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni eshwɛɛɛ yɛ niyenii lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or animal manure around the plants helps them turn deep green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaabɔle tso lɛ he Enɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ ni eda waa.

english: Why do people say planting beans or cowpeas makes the soil better for my other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mi tsei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant leaves and roots decay in the soil, they leave natural fertilizer behind for your next crop.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei pɔtɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛ tsei ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer so I don't waste my money?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni mikafite shika?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after rain, preferably early in the morning or late afternoon. Applying fertilizer on dry soil can burn plant roots, while heavy rain can wash it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Esa akɛ awo lɛ leebi loo shwane mli. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi ashã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo tsei shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting before they are ready to pick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛfee klalo akɛ abaajie amɛ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, wet conditions. Clearing weeds and pruning excess leaves lets sunlight and fresh air into your farm to dry out and kill the fungus.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ewo duŋ ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ ni ofolɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni egbi ni egbe ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tight like small balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ bɔɔlu bibii lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant sap. Spraying neem water or appropriate insecticides will clear the insects so leaves can grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem nu loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi lɛ koni baai lɛ anyɛ ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt in the afternoon sun even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Hot midday heat causes tomato plants to lose water faster than their roots can suck it up, causing temporary wilting. If they recover by evening it is just heat, but if they stay wilted, it could be a soil disease affecting the roots.
ga: Gbi teŋ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ekɛ be kukuoo mli shwiemɔ baa Kɛji ehiɛ ba ehe nɔ yɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ, no lɛ hulutsoo lɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ mli. Shi kɛ́ etee nɔ egbi lɛ, ekolɛ eji hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni saa shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How do I make sure I am planting my cassava stem cuttings the right way up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ miduɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Look closely at the tiny raised buds where old leaves used to grow; those buds must point upward toward the sky. Planting stems upside down causes the crop to sprout late and produce small, weak roots.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. ni da yɛ he ni baai momoi lɛ daa lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ Esa akɛ nakai ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ yitso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ ada blɛoo ni ewo shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Should I let all the small suckers grow around my main plantain tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maha tsei bibii akwɛ̃ yɛ midumɔwu titri lɛ he?

english: No, having too many suckers forces them to fight each other for water and soil nutrients. Keep only one or two healthy suckers to take over after harvest and chop down the rest.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii babaoo baaha amɛwuu yɛ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe. Okɛ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ato ni oye yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ ni ofo nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it necessary to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni wɔkɛ tsei awo sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ koni wɔkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the foliage into the air and keeps leaves off the wet ground where pests and diseases spread easily.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa amɛyaaa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my seeds too close together in the row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete for sunlight, root space, and water. Spacing them properly gives each plant enough room to produce maximum yield.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la, shishifãi ahe he, kɛ nu he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo yibii babaoo.

english: How do I manage my farm schedule if I want to grow both rice and cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ mi okwaayeli be lɛ nɔ kɛji miisumɔ ni madu ŋmãa kɛ kookoo fɛɛ?

english: Rice requires heavy attention early during planting and weeding, while cocoa requires intense labor during harvest. Planning your planting calendar so rice maintenance is done before the main cocoa harvest season prevents you from getting overwhelmed.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akwɛ Rice nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ mra. Yɛ dumɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ mli lɛ, yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, Cocoa biɔ nitsumɔ babaoo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli. Too odumɔ kalanda lɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni akwɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ dani ŋmãa kpamɔ be titri lɛ aba koni akawo onɔ jatsu fe nine.

english: Why do many cocoa farmers in Ghana choose to also farm rice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ halaa akɛ amɛbaafee ŋmãa hu lɛ?

english: Cocoa yields money only during specific harvest months, whereas rice grows quickly (harvested in 3 to 4 months) and provides both food for the family and extra cash income during the cocoa off-season.
ga: Afeɔ kookoo yɛ kpamɔ nyɔji pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli pɛ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa oya (akpaa yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli) ni ehaa weku lɛ niyenii kɛ shika kroko fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ bɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to spend so much time at my farm right after planting rice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafite be babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Newly planted rice seeds and young seedlings are very delicate and exposed. Staying on the farm early on allows you to protect the seeds from birds, clear fast-growing weeds, and ensure the seedlings get enough water to build strong roots.
ga: Omɔ ŋmaa kɛ dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ waaa waa ni amɛjeɔ kpo. Ni oooya ŋmɔ lɛ mli mra lɛ Haa obuɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ okpoi ahe. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ kɛjɛ ohe. Ni kwɛmɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ ana nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Can I plant rice underneath my mature cocoa trees to save space?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ kookoo tso ni eda shishi koni mikɛha he ko akafee nɔ ko?

english: No, mature cocoa trees create a thick canopy that blocks sunlight, but rice needs full direct sunlight to produce grains. Rice must be planted in open field areas or lowland valleys with direct sun.
ga: Dabi, kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa. Shi omɔ he miihia hulu la ni eyi obɔ, tɛ̃ɛ koni ewo dumɔwui. Esa akɛ adu omɔ yɛ hei ni gbɛ yɔɔ loo jɔɔ lɛ mli ni hulu la kpɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How long does rice take from the day I plant it until it is ready for harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmãa heɔ kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni esa akɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Most rice varieties commonly grown in Ghana take between 3 to 4 months (about 90 to 120 days) from planting to full maturity, depending on whether it is upland or lowland rice.
ga: Omɔ henɔi ni afɔɔ dumɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 (aaafee gbii 90 kɛyashi 120) kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edara. Edamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know when my rice crop is fully ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Your rice is ready when about 80% to 85% of the grain heads turn from green to a firm, golden-yellow color, and the leaves at the base of the plant begin to dry out.
ga: O-rice lɛ efee klalo beni aaafee 80% kɛyashi 85% ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei amli lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ ni mli wa mli. ni baai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ

english: How often should I harvest ripe pods from my cocoa trees during the peak season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa cacao tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ fa babaoo lɛ?

english: During the main harvest season, you should harvest every 2 to 3 weeks. This allows you to gather enough ripe pods together for proper fermentation while stopping pods from over-ripening.
ga: yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be titri lɛ mli Esa akɛ okpa ŋmaa lɛ daa otsii 2 kɛyashi 3. Enɛ haa obuaa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ anaa kɛha ŋmeii ni sa. yɛ be mli ni etsĩɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ fe nine.

english: What happens if I delay harvesting my cocoa pods when they are ripe?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ akpamɔ be sɛɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: If ripe cocoa pods stay on the tree too long, the seeds inside will start to germinate or rot. Over-ripe pods also attract pests like squirrels and increase the spread of black pod disease.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ hi tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baabɔi kwɛ̃mɔ loo amɛbaafite. Pods ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ hu gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni ehaa black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: How do I tell if a cocoa pod on my tree is ready to be plucked?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaajie?

english: A ripe cocoa pod changes color completely. Green pods turn bright yellow when ripe, and dark red or purple pods turn orange or reddish-yellow.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kwraa. Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse beni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. ni ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ tsakeɔ efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ-tsuru.

english: Why are young weeds more dangerous to young rice plants than to mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi bibii lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ awui fe ŋmãa tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young rice plants have shallow roots and compete directly with weeds for light and soil food. Mature cocoa trees have deep roots and big leaves that shade out weeds naturally.
ga: Omɔ tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛkɛ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná la kɛ shikpɔŋ. Kookoo tsei ni edara lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai wuji ni haa jwɛi lɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow and drying up before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow strong ears. Yellowing lower leaves in a V-shape indicate nitrogen deficiency, meaning the soil lacks food for the crop and needs organic manure or fertilizer added.
ga: Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni eha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni etoi lɛ hu ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tamɔ V lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii, ni ehe miihia humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmã yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas fix nitrogen from the air into the soil through their roots. This naturally feeds the soil, helping neighboring crops like maize grow better without having to buy as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ babaoo.

english: If I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year, why does my yield keep reducing?
ga: Kɛji akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ, mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ yaa nɔ ebaa shi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop relies on and allows soil pests to build up in that plot. Rotating different crops gives the land time to replenish its strength.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tso lɛ kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nibii srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛwajeɔ.

english: If I plant my cassava stakes very close together, will I get more tubers to sell?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani mana yitsei babaoo ni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ?

english: Planting cassava too close causes the roots to compete for water and soil nutrients. This results in many small, thin tubers instead of large, heavy ones, so wider spacing actually yields a heavier harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ abɔi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso bibioo ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ yitso agbo ni tsii najiaŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii baa.

english: Why didn't my maize seeds sprout after I buried them deep in the ground to protect them from birds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni mikɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ okpoi ahe lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds buried too deeply exhaust their stored energy before reaching the surface for light. Planting seeds at a moderate depth—about two thumb-joints deep—protects them while allowing them to sprout easily.
ga: Dumɔwui ni afu amɛ tsɔ lɛ baafite hewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ dani amɛyashɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ koni amɛná la. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ waa. (aaafee tsitsii enyɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mlibotemɔ) lɛ baabu dumɔwui lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni ehaa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ mlɛo.

english: Do weeds really affect how big my cassava tubers grow, or can I just leave them until harvest time?
ga: Ani jwɛi lɛ saa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ adalɛ he diɛŋtsɛ loo esa akɛ mashi amɛ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Weeds steal light, water, and soil nutrients directly from cassava plants, especially during the first three months. Clearing weeds early ensures the plant directs all its energy into growing thick tubers.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmei tso lɛ mli. Titri lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ amli Jwɛi lɛ ajiemɔ mra Enɛ haa tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni mli tse ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them in an open field under full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily scorched by strong daylight and intense heat. Planting shade crops like plantain beside them provides living cover that protects them until they mature.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ shãa amɛ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ bɔɔ nii ni buɔ amɛhe lɛ teeɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa kwraa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during heavy rains and strong winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems and heavy top fruit. If extra shoots (suckers) aren't trimmed and the main stem isn't propped up with a strong wooden pole, wind can easily tip the entire plant over.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ ŋwɛi aduawai ni mli tse. Kɛji akɛ afolɔko ŋmeii (ŋmeii) ni fa fe nine lɛ ahe ni akɛ tso ni wa ko fioo ko fioo ko fioo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ atswa tsei lɛ shi oya.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruits during the dry hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miikwɛ̃ ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High heat combined with low moisture causes stress, making tomato blossoms fall off before fruit can set. Regular watering at the base early in the morning keeps the soil cool and preserves the flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulutsoo ni baa shi lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa. Enɛ haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ nu yɛ shishigbɛ daa leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young corn plants and leaving holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni amɛshiɔ bu lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest that hides in the growing center of the corn plant. Treating the central leaves early stops the worm from destroying the plant's growth point.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ahe nitsumɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akafite hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Is June a good time for me to plant maize in Ghana, or is it already too late in the rainy season?
ga: Ani June ji be ni hi kɛha mi akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ Ghana loo eshɛ sɛɛ tsɔ momo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: In many parts of Ghana, June is towards the end of the major rainy season. Planting in June can be risky because if the rains stop early, the maize will not get enough water to form full cobs. It is usually best to plant right at the start of the rains in April or May.
ga: yɛ Ghana hei babaoo lɛ, June ji nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ naagbee. Dumɔ yɛ June mli baanyɛ afee oshara. Ejaakɛ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra lɛ Abele lɛ naaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmei ni eyi obɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli yɛ April loo May mli.

english: Why do crops planted in the same month perform differently from one year to the next?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ nyɔŋ kome mli lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ kɛjɛɔ afi kɛyaa afi lɛ?

english: Rainfall patterns and temperatures change every year. Even in the same month, a year with steady rains will give a much better yield than a year with long dry spells or sudden heavy downpours that wash nutrients away.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ latsaa tsakeɔ daa afi. Yɛ nyɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli po Afii ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe afii ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa ni shwieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I consider planting groundnuts alongside my main crops like maize or yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ titri, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni ŋɔɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ he?

english: Groundnuts are legumes, which means they take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. Planting groundnuts helps feed and refresh your soil naturally, while also giving you a second crop to sell if your main crop fails.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Peanuts ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni eha oshikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni ekɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ ni obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ehiii.

english: Is it safe for me to plant only one crop, like maize, across my entire large farm?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii kome, tamɔ ŋmãa, yɛ miŋmɔ agbo lɛ mli?

english: Planting only one crop over a large area is risky. If a specific insect pest or disease attacks that crop, or if the rains fail at a critical time, you risk losing your entire farm's harvest instead of having other crops to rely on.
ga: Nibii kome ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni da nɔ lɛ yɛ oshara. Kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai komɛi tutua ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ loo kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ be ni he hiaa waa mli Obaawo oshara mli akɛ obaafite oŋmɔ mli nibii fɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ehe baahia ni ekɛ ehe afɔ̃ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi anɔ lɛ

english: What kind of soil preparation do I need if I want to start growing yams?
ga: Kɛ́ oosumɔ ni obɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ lɛ, mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ esa akɛ osaa?

english: Yams need deep, loose soil to grow large tubers underground. Unlike grain crops that can be planted in flatter soil, yams grow best when you build tall earthen mounds or ridges so the tubers can expand easily without hitting hard ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potato koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Sweet potatoes daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ofee gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ. Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ ŋmãa ni abaanyɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni yitso lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya ni etswaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ.

english: How can I easily tell if insects are attacking my maize field early on?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi bibii miitutua mi-ŋma ŋmɔji lɛ mra?

english: Check your young maize plants for small holes in the leaves, ragged leaf edges, or small greenish-brown droppings inside the central leaves where the new growth comes out. Finding these signs early helps you act before the pests destroy the whole field.
ga: Kwɛmɔ o-baby corn tsei lɛ amli kɛji bu bibii yɛ baai lɛ amli, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni etse, loo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ani eyɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni ŋmɔshi nibii heei miije kpo yɛ lɛ? Okadii nɛɛ ni ooona mra Ebaaye ebua bo ni ofee nɔ ko dani ŋmeii lɛ akpata jɛmɛ fɛɛ hiɛ.

english: Why do insect pests spread so fast when I plant a huge field of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ agbo mli lɛ?

english: When a large area has only maize, pests have an endless supply of their favorite food right next to each other. Without other non-host plants or trees in between to slow them down, insects can multiply and move quickly from plant to plant.
ga: Beni ŋmãa pɛ yɔɔ he ko ni da lɛ, ŋmeii yɛ niyenii ni amɛsumɔɔ waa ni bɛ naagbee. Kɛji tsei loo tsei krokomɛi bɛ fe tsei ni ji gbɔi lɛ ni tsiɔ enaa. No sɛɛ lɛ, koolooi baanyɛ afa ni amɛfã oya kɛjɛ tso kome nɔ kɛya tso kroko nɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build strong leaves. It can also happen if the soil is too waterlogged, preventing the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛmaa baai ni wa Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye niyenii.

english: Why do groundnuts seem to survive dry spells better than maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmei nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts have roots that grow in a way that allows them to hold onto moisture better, and their low bushy leaves cover the ground, keeping the soil cool and reducing water loss compared to tall crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts yɛ shishifãi ni daa yɛ gbɛ ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni jwɛi bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛlɛ tamɔ ŋmãa he.

english: What basic steps should I take to clear and prepare my land before planting?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii esa akɛ mafee koni mikɛjie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni masaa he dani madu nii?

english: Start by clearing weeds and bushes, then loosen the topsoil by tilling or making mounds. Removing thick weeds gives your crop seeds space and sunlight, while loosening the soil allows young roots to spread quickly and absorb water.
ga: Je shishi kɛtsɔ jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni ooojie lɛ nɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, shwiemɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsu loo ŋmɔji ni ooofee lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ ajiemɔ Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ hulu la. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi bibii lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya ni amɛmɔɔ nu.

english: This is usually caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in damp, dark, and wet conditions on the farm.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ, black pod hela lɛ kɛbaa Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ, duŋ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: What causes the branches on my cocoa trees to swell up and stop bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni haa niji ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa yibiiwoo?

english: This is caused by the swollen shoot virus, an infection spread by tiny insects called mealybugs that weakens the tree and eventually kills it if not removed.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tso mli hela ko ni efuu. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egboɔ kɛji ajieee lɛ.

english: How can I tell if a disease on my crops is caused by a fungus or a virus?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela ko ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ jɛ ŋmei loo hela ko ni gbeɔ mɔ mli?

english: Fungal diseases usually cause dark spots, mold, or wet rotting on pods and leaves, while viral diseases often cause physical deformities like swollen stems or patterned leaf discoloration.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii helai kɛ ŋmeii diji, ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii ni efɔ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai lɛ anɔ baa. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nibii ni ejaaa baa, tamɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni efuu loo baai ni tsakeɔ amɛhe yɛ mfonirifeemɔŋ.

english: Can crop diseases spread from my neighbor's farm to mine?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛjɛ akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ mli kɛya shika tsuru ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, fungal spores can travel through wind and rain drops, while viral diseases can be carried across farms by insects like mealybugs.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs nɔ.

english: How does letting wind flow through my farm help my crops stay healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Good air flow dries up excess moisture on leaves and pods, making it much harder for fungal diseases like black pod to take root and spread.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ baai kɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ baawo shishifãi ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my crops get more diseases when the trees are planted too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa helai babaoo kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, air cannot circulate and sunlight cannot reach the ground, creating a dark, wet environment where diseases thrive.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ abɔle he ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ewo duŋ ni hela gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ baa. lɛ baanyɛ adara

english: Is it good or bad if direct sunlight hits the ground on my cocoa farm?
ga: Ani ehi loo ehiii kɛji hulu la shɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: A moderate amount of sunlight hitting the farm helps dry up wet soil and kill harmful fungal spores, though too much sun without shade can dry out young trees.
ga: Hulu la ni fa fioo ni baa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ egbiɔ ni egbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, hulu ni fa tsɔ ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei bibii agbi.

english: Why is it important to prune extra branches from my cocoa trees after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata he kɛjɛ kookoo tsei amli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and wind can penetrate, which keeps the tree dry and healthy for the next growing season.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, egbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ kɛha shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I clear away infected pods from my farm ground after I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Leaving diseased pods on the ground allows fungal spores to live in the soil and infect the new pods that grow during the next season.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛhaa ŋmeii heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ hela.

english: How does keeping my farm well-weeded help protect my cocoa trees from viruses?
ga: Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi ni mikɛwo miŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ abu mi-kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Weeds can hide pests like mealybugs that carry viruses; clearing them exposes these pests to sunlight and predators, reducing disease spread.
ga: Jwɛi baanyɛ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ mealybugs ni hiɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ato. Kɛ́ afɔ amɛhe lɛ, hulu la kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ naa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ baa shi

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to germinate if I plant them right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain after a dry period heats up the dry ground without soaking it deep enough. Waiting until steady rains set in ensures the soil stays wet enough for seeds to sprout safely without drying out.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli adɔ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efɔɔɔ shi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: How can I tell if the rainy season has settled properly so I don't waste my expensive crop seeds?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ eho jogbaŋŋ? No hewɔ lɛ, ofiteee dumɔwui ni jara wa?

english: Wait until you get two or three consistent days of rain that soak the soil deep enough to cover your hand, rather than planting after a single sudden downpour that is followed by heat.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa gbii enyɔ loo etɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekwɔ bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ okɛha oniji ahe. Mohu ɔ, duɔ ngɛ nugbɔ nɛ nɛ trukaa nɛ dɔlɛ nyɛɛ se ɔ se.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves naturally when it is dry to save water and keep their roots alive underground. Once the rains return, fresh green leaves will sprout again.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛgbi koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛha amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Baai eŋɔli heei baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before turning into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛbatsɔ anɔkwa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and lack of moisture stress the cocoa tree, forcing it to drop flowers to protect itself. Providing shade trees helps keep the climate cool so the flowers can turn into pods.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ cacao tsei lɛ agbee shi koni amɛbu amɛhe. Shade ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Kɛkɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ bafeɔ pod.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing big and bushy with leaves but producing very little fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmɔji ni baai yɔɔ mli shi ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen from soil or heavy manure, they put all their energy into growing foliage instead of flowers and fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei ná nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmeii ni tsii mli Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni miida lɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why does the soil in my vegetable bed dry out so quickly even after I water it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo nɔ po lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses water fast when direct sunshine hits it. Covering the ground around your plants with dry grass or leaves keeps the soil shaded, cool, and moist for much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛji hulu la shɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant roots rot when heavy rains fall for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants hate standing in stagnant water because wet soil suffocates their roots. Planting them on raised mounds lets excess water drain away naturally.
ga: Pepper tsei nyɛɔ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli ni amɛdamɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing small and bent instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, deep soil to push downward as they grow. Hard or stony ground stops them from expanding, so making big, loose soil mounds gives them space to grow large.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya mli beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã. No hewɔ lɛ, gɔŋ agbo ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛaafee lɛ baaha amɛná he ko ni da ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take much longer to fruit when planted in open sunny areas without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ ni hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains prefer moist soil and cool air. Hot direct sun dries out their big leaves and slows down their growth, so planting them near shade or retaining soil moisture speeds up fruiting.
ga: Plantains sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ. Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa baai wuji lɛ gĩɔ ni ehaa amɛdaraa oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ odu lɛ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be lɛ yɔɔ loo kɛ́ okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewo yibii oya.

english: Why do insects attack my cowpea flowers as soon as they open up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛfɔ̃ pɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet juice that naturally draws insects in. Checking your field early and using gentle protective sprays keeps the pests away so the flowers can turn into healthy pods.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔii lɛ jieɔ nu ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni gbalaa kooloi. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni buɔ mɔ he ni akɛtsuɔ nii blɛoo lɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ akashɛ he. Bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen or the soil is too soaked with water from heavy rains. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps the plants regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu ni jɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava stem cuttings right at the end of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmei amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava needs steady soil moisture during its first two to three months to build strong roots. Planting just before the dry season starts can cause the stem cuttings to dry up and die before they establish.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ daa lɛ he miihia Cassava yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli koni shishifãi ni wa aba. Kɛ́ adu nii dani fɛ̃i be lɛ je shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei aniji agbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep dropping off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when daytime temperatures get too hot or when the plants do not get enough water. Keeping the soil moist and using mulch around the roots helps protect the flowers so they can form fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛfɔ̃ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do agricultural officers always advise me to plant beans alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa be fɛɛ be akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa afata ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Beans pull nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil through their roots. This acts as a natural, free fertilizer that feeds the nearby maize plants and keeps your farmland healthy.
ga: Beans gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to cut off some branches and leaves from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso ni eda lɛ niji kɛ baai komɛi?

english: Pruning cocoa trees opens up the canopy so sunlight and fresh air can reach the lower branches. This prevents damp conditions that cause fungal diseases like black pod disease and encourages more pods to sprout.
ga: Kɛ́ afo kokoo tso lɛ, egbeleɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe. Bɔni afee ni atsĩ ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela baa lɛ naa ni eha dumɔwui babaoo akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and stop growing after small insects gather under them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛkpaa dalɛ beni kooloi bibii ebua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛshishi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Tiny insects like aphids or thrips suck the sap from pepper leaves and spread plant viruses. This causes the leaves to curl, stopping the plant from growing properly and reducing your yield.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips lɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ pepper baai amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa tso lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ ada jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers rot quickly when I stack them on the floor inside my house?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛto shikpɔŋ yɛ mishia lɛ?

english: Yams rot fast if they are stored in warm, poorly ventilated spaces directly on the ground. Storing them elevated off the floor on open wooden racks in a cool, shady yam barn keeps air circulating and prevents decay.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ jɛmɛ. Ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ yɛ tso adeka ko ni agbele mli yɛ sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli ni ehaaa efite.

english: How deep into the ground should I push my maize seeds during planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ matsi mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ kɛya shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ yɛ dumɔ be mli?

english: Maize seeds should be planted about 3 to 5 centimeters deep into moist soil. If you plant them too shallow, birds will eat them or the heat will dry them out, but planting too deep makes it hard for the seedlings to emerge.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ aaafee sɛntimitai 3 kɛyashi 5 mli. Kɛji odu lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ Okpoi baaye amɛ loo latsaa lɛ baaha amɛgbi. Shi kɛ́ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ewa aha dumɔwui lɛ akɛ amɛakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my watermelon vines look soft and wilted in the afternoon sun even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon wain tsei lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji mikɛ nu wo nɔ leebi po.

english: On very hot afternoon days, watermelon leaves lose water into the air faster than roots can draw it from the soil. As long as the vines perk back up by evening or early morning, the plants are normally healthy.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Watermelon baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni wain tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ yɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it bad practice for me to plant tomatoes on the exact same bed where I harvested garden eggs last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ gbonyo kɛha mi akɛ madu tomato yɛ saatso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ ni mibua ŋmeii anaa yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes and garden eggs belong to the same plant family and suffer from the same soil diseases and pests. Planting them in the same spot repeatedly allows harmful pests and fungi to build up in the soil and damage your next harvest.
ga: Tomato kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ fata tsei akuu kome he, ni helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛbaa lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui. Amɛdumɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Enɛ baaha ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow leaves. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why are my cocoa tree flowers falling off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by dry spells, lack of soil nutrients, or insect attacks. Ensuring the trees have adequate shade and moisture helps the flowers stay on and grow into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi ni baatutua lɛ Kɛ́ akwɛ koni tso lɛ aná hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning black and rotting right on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in very wet, dark, and crowded farms. Pruning tree branches to let in sunlight and removing diseased pods prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ, ni mɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ mli koni hulu la abote mli, ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: What is causing holes in my young maize leaves and leaves dirt inside the shoot?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bulɛ baa mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli ni eshiɔ muji yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the plant shoot and feeds on young leaves. Checking farms early and applying approved organic or chemical sprays keeps them under control.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei ashishifãi amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Okwaafoi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi yɛ kudɔmɔ shishi.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water and lacks air, especially during heavy rain seasons. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away and keeps roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Titri lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli, ni ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during strong winds even when they look green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can easily be damaged by soil pests or waterlogged ground. Supporting fruiting plantain trees with strong wooden props prevents them from falling under the weight of heavy bunches.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni sũ mli kooloi loo sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ oya. Fi plantains ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ kɛ tsei ni wa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekagbee ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ ashishi.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites that feed on plant sap. Spraying plants early with neem oil or soapy water helps clear these insects before they stunt the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Ni akɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni mli edɔ baashwie tsei anɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni ajie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when weather temperatures get too hot or when water supply is uneven. Giving plants steady water at the root level and mulching the soil keeps ground moisture consistent so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi daa bɔni afee ni aduawai aba.

english: Why are my yam leaves turning brown with spots and drying up before the tubers grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yam leaves dry up early when attacked by a fungal leaf spot disease called anthracnose. Staking yam vines off the wet ground and using disease-resistant seed yams keeps the leaves healthy longer to feed the growing tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ hela ko ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ mɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ adu sweet potato wain tsei kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ni akɛ sweet potato ni dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ koni ekɛha bulbs ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my crops growing tall and thin without developing thick stems or good fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida ni amɛmiiya shɔŋŋ ni amɛbɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse loo aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Crops grow tall and weak when planted too close together or under deep tree shade because they are competing for sunlight. Giving plants proper spacing ensures each stalk receives enough light and air to grow thick and strong.
ga: Tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli ejaakɛ amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛ́ akɛ he ko ni sa ha tsei lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe wa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow from the tip downward before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnaa kɛbashi shi dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the leaf tip usually means your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an important food that helps leaves stay green. It can also happen if the soil is too wet and the roots cannot breathe to take up nutrients.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots become soft and watery inside after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When water collects and sits in the soil for too long, cassava roots drown because they lack air. This causes root rot, making the tubers watery and spoiled instead of firm and starchy.
ga: Beni nu buaa ehe naa ni ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Cassava shishifãi lɛ baagboi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ starch.

english: Why do my yam vines grow plenty of bushy leaves but produce very small yams underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ hiɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the yam plant to spend all its energy growing leaves above the ground instead of sending that energy down to build big tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa sweet potato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ nakai hewalɛ lɛ nɔ kɛba shi koni efee yitso agbo lɛ.

english: Why do the tiny pods on my cocoa tree turn black and dry up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is often caused by Black Pod disease, which spreads quickly during cool and rainy weather, or it can be cherelle wilt, where the cocoa tree naturally drops extra pods it cannot feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji black pod hela, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni fɛ̃i kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ. Aloo ebaanyɛ efee Cherelle tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ. Biɛ ji he ni cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aha lɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why is my plantain tree falling over on its own even when there is no strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbeeɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ waaa moŋ lɛ?

english: Tiny worms called nematodes or stem borer pests are likely destroying the roots and inner stem underground, weakening the tree's hold in the soil until the heavy plant topples.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ fɔɔ shishifãi kɛ tsei lɛ amli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ afitemɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ emɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ aahu kɛyashiɔ tsei ni tsii shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and rotten before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This is called Blossom End Rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium, usually because the water supply in the soil goes from very dry to very wet unpredictably.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ Blosom Naagbee Rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ nɔ.

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap from young leaves, or from a virus spread by those insects. Controlling pests early stops the leaf curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Early Pest Control Ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my bean plants drop all their flowers without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa baaa lɛ?

english: Bean plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too hot or when tiny flower thrips attack the blossoms. Planting at the right time in the season helps avoid severe heat stress.
ga: Bean tsei lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ fɔfɔi bibii ni ji thrips lɛ tutua fɔfɔi lɛ, kɛ́ adu yɛ be ni sa mli yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ajieɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up tight during the afternoon heat and open back up in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni amɛgbeleɔ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling up leaves is a plant's self-defense trick to shield itself from the strong sun and prevent water from escaping through the leaf surface during the hottest hours.
ga: Baai ni afoɔ lɛ ji tso ko hebuu ŋaa ni ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni ekɛtsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ baa lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce good crop yields in the first year after clearing, but yields drop significantly by the third year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi ni ajie lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Shi yibiiwoo lɛ ba shi waa yɛ afi ni ji etɛ lɛ mli?

english: Crops pull food out of the soil every season. Without adding compost, animal manure, or proper fertilizer, and without rotating crops, the soil becomes exhausted of its natural nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ faaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fataaa he. ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ bɛ

english: How do I know how many months my cassava needs in the ground before it is ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nyɔji enyiɛ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Most common cassava varieties in Ghana take between 9 to 12 months to mature. Digging them up too early leaves you with thin, watery roots, while leaving them too long makes the tubers woody and hard to cook.
ga: Cassava henɔ ni afɔɔ naa waa yɛ Ghana lɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani ekwɛ̃ɔ. Kɛ́ atsa oya tsɔ lɛ, nu bibioo ko baaha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi. Kɛ́ ashi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afee tsei ni ehoomɔ wa.

english: Plantains require large amounts of water to build strong pseudostems and form fruit. When soil moisture drops during dry months, the plant slows down its growth to save water, delaying fruiting.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia plantains koni ekɛfee pseudostems ni mli wa ni ewo yibii. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ba shi yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ Tsei lɛ baaha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ fioo koni amɛbu nu he. ni ekɛ yibiiwoo sɛɛ tsɛɔ

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without forming peppers when the weather gets very hot around June?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ pepper baaa beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli woɔ la waa yɛ June mli lɛ?

english: Excessive heat causes stress to pepper plants, making them shed flowers to conserve energy and moisture. Providing light shade or watering early in the morning helps the plants retain their blooms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei anɔ. Ha efee fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ akafite. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo loo nu ha tso lɛ leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves on my vegetable crop turn yellow when the heavy mid-year rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-vegetables lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa je shishi yɛ afi lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains soak the soil and wash away essential nutrients like nitrogen from the root zone. Without nitrogen, the plant cannot produce green chlorophyll, causing its leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fũuɔ ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji nitrogen bɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee klorofil ni ji eŋɔli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my late-planted maize crops yield smaller cobs compared to the ones I planted at the start of the rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni midu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa bibii kɛ akɛto ŋmãa ni midu mra lɛ he lɛ?

english: Late-planted maize misses the peak rainfall period during its critical flowering stage. Without steady water when forming cobs, the plant produces smaller, poorly filled grains.
ga: Abɛi ni adu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ naaa nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ nu bɛ be fɛɛ be beni afeɔ ŋmei lɛ, tso lɛ baawo dumɔwui bibii ni ekɛ amɛhe wooo mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded plants compete for sunlight, space, and soil nutrients. Instead of growing thick stems and large cobs, they stretch upward toward the light.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dense plants lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, he ko kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ tso nɛ mi wa kɛ tso agbo. Mohu ɔ, e ngmɛɛ kɛ ya hiɔwe kɛ ya la a he.

english: How can I tell that my yam tubers under the ground are mature and ready for digging?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: When the leaves and vines on your yam plant begin to turn yellow and naturally dry up, it indicates the plant has finished storing food in the tubers, signaling harvest time.
ga: Beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ o-sweet potato tso lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kɛ niyenii eto eyitso mli momo. ni ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nikpamɔ be eshɛ

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes rot so quickly when I pick them after they are fully red on the bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikpa amɛ beni amɛho lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fully red tomatoes on the vine become soft and fragile. Picking them when they just start showing a light pink or yellowish color allows them to ripen safely off the vine and last much longer.
ga: Tomato tsuru ni ekwɛ̃ ni yɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni egbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ shwie shi beni amɛje shishi amɛmiitsɔ pinki loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛshwere shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛhi shi be babaoo.

english: Why do my stored maize grains develop web-like dust and small holes after a few months in the bag?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ feɔ sũ ni tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ buji bibii lɛ? Beni ekɛwo kotoku lɛ mli nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ

english: Insects like grain weevils lay tiny eggs inside the maize before or during harvest. If the maize is not thoroughly sun-dried before bagging, remaining moisture allows these insect eggs to hatch and multiply.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ dumɔwui amli ŋmeii fɔɔ ŋmeii bibii. Abele mli dani akpa loo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli Kɛji akɛ agbiko abele lɛ yɛ hulu mli dani awo mli Fɛ̃i fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ baaha nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ awuii lɛ afɔ ni amɛshwere.

english: Why do my garden egg plants stop bearing fruit even though they keep producing new flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekpa yibiiwoo eyɛ mli akɛ amɛyaa nɔ amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi heei moŋ?

english: As a crop continuously yields, it depletes nutrients in the soil. Without adding compost or manure, the plant loses the energy required to transform flowers into mature fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei tee nɔ amɛwo Nutrients ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaho aya. Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ laajeɔ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛtsake fɔfɔi lɛ amɛfee aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Why should I leave space between my cassava sticks instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: Planting cassava too close causes the plants to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin roots. Spacing them properly gives the tubers enough room underground to expand and grow big.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shishifãi bibii He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛdara.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops every year even when I plant the exact same crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Kɛji akɛ midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ po.

english: Planting the same crop on the same plot every season drains the specific nutrients that crop needs and allows soil pests to build up. Rotating your crops, especially with beans or groundnuts, restores nutrients to the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ lɛ hoɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni amɛbuaa amɛhe naa. Oŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsake Titri lɛ kɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dried leaves or grass help them grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ ni mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi woɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Covering the soil, which is called mulching, keeps the ground cool, retains moisture during dry spells, and prevents weeds from growing and stealing nutrients from your crops.
ga: Mulching, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli.

english: Yellowing leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or is sitting in too much water. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer or improving land drainage helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo eyɛ nu babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is my plantain tree producing small bunches even though the leaves are large and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ dara ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Large leaves mean the plant has enough nitrogen for leafy growth, but small fruit bunches mean it lacks potassium, which is needed for fruit development. Applying potassium-rich fertilizer or wood ash helps increase fruit size.
ga: Large leaves mean the plant has enough nitrogen for leafy growth, but small fruit bunches mean it lacks potassium, which is needed for fruit development. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium eyi mli obɔ loo tso mli sũ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout after a heavy rain right after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu lɛ?

english: Heavy rain can wash away light seeds, push them too deep into the mud, or compact the topsoil into a hard crust that young sprouts cannot break through. Planting at the recommended depth helps protect the seeds.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo ŋmaa bibii kɛya. Tsi dumɔwui lɛ kɛya muji lɛ mli tsɔ. Aloo okɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ afee ŋmei ni wa ni tsei bibii nyɛŋ abote mli. Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ adu lɛ baaye abua ni abu dumɔwui lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa trees are tender and burn under full, direct sunlight. They need shade from larger trees or plantains to protect them from excessive heat and to keep the soil moist while their roots grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo plantains adɛŋ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without forming any fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes severe stress to tomato plants, causing flowers to drop before pollination can occur. Providing light shade and watering near the roots can reduce heat stress and keep the flowers intact.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tomato tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani pollination baa. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be ni mli tse kɛ nu ha yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shi ni eha fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves, or by a viral infection spread by insects. Spraying neem oil or recommended treatments controls these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli Neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofai krokomɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsaa lɛ baaye kooloi bibii nɛɛ anɔ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight allows the leaves to produce food, which flows down to feed and expand the yam tuber underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi koni eye niyenii ni egbɛɔ eshwaa sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli

english: Young cocoa plants get stressed easily by harsh sunlight and dry winds. Without enough shade trees or plantain plants nearby to shield them and keep moisture in the soil, the intense sun burns their leaves and causes them to drop.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ haoɔ oya. Kɛji tsei loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ni baabu shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni eha amɛgbee shi.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and sticky dirt inside the center leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baa mli ni muji ni shwieɔ shi yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves (the whorl) of the young maize plant, eating the tender leaves and leaving behind dark waste that looks like moist sawdust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai (rings) lɛ amli. Eyeɔ baai bibii ni eshiɔ jwɛi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ.

english: Why does clearing weeds early make my young maize grow so much faster than waiting until the weeds are tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni agbalaa mra lɛ haa mibi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya fe ni mamɛ kɛyashi jwɛi lɛ baafee shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Young crops grow fastest when they do not have to compete with weeds for sunshine, water, and soil nutrients. Weeding early ensures that all the natural goodness in the soil goes straight to feeding your maize.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ daa oya fe fɛɛ be mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ jwɛi lɛ ashi akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni adebɔɔ mli hewalɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yaa o-ŋmã lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rain stays on the farm for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When water sits on the farm without draining away, it drowns the roots and creates the ideal conditions for soil fungi to cause root decay.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli Nu lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ mli. ni efee shihilɛ ni sa kɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ koni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ afite.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up to capture maximum sunlight, which the plant uses to manufacture food to build big tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the hot soil where they can catch diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. which plants use for food production to form large underground tubers Staking also keeps leaves out of hot soil, which can become a source of disease.

english: Why is my plantain stand producing very small bunches even though the soil seems good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: If you allow too many young shoots (suckers) to grow around one mother plantain stem, they steal water and plant food from each other. Pruning excess suckers leaves only two or three strong stems that can produce large, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwui akutso kome he lɛ Amɛbaaju nu ni amɛkwɛ niyenii kɛjɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baanyɛ awo yibii wuji ni tsii pɛ aba.

english: Why is it good practice to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my plot after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil naturally. Planting them after maize restores the soil fertility that the maize used up, reducing your need for chemical fertilizers in the next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ abele sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni abele lɛ eŋɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he hiamɔ baa shi yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: How does adding dried animal manure help my crops grow better than relying only on chemical fertilizers?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni mikɛbaafata he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ pɛ nɔ ni mikɛaafɔ̃ nɔ lɛ?

english: Animal manure acts like a sponge in the ground, holding water and plant food in the soil for a long time while improving the soil texture. Chemical fertilizers give a quick supply of food to the plant but do not improve the quality of the soil itself.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ sũ mli. Ehaa nu kɛ tsei ahe niyenii hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii oya shi ehaaa sũ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience high heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of specific soil minerals like calcium. Keeping the moisture level consistent in the soil helps the flowers set fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa he. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo sũ mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ calcium ni bɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why should I spray my vegetable crops early in the morning or late in the evening instead of at noon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ tsofa lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ moŋ fe shwane?

english: Spraying in the hot midday sun causes the chemical liquid to evaporate too quickly before it can work, and the intense sun mixed with chemicals can burn the crop leaves. Cool morning or evening temperatures allow the treatment to work safely and effectively.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ehaa tsofai ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ dani etsuɔ ​​nii. Ni hulu la ni naa wa ni akɛ tsofai efutu mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ahe baai ashã. He ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ haa tsofafeemɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii shweshweeshwe ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves burn and turn brown when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from bigger trees to protect their soft leaves from intense sunlight and to keep the surrounding soil moist while their root systems grow.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni eda lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. kɛ koni eha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why is it good practice for me to plant cassava and maize together on the same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows fast and is harvested in a few months, while cassava grows slowly and stays in the ground longer. Planting them together lets you harvest maize first without stopping the cassava from growing.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Yɛ ŋmei gbɛfaŋ lɛ, edaa blɛoo ni ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Hefatalɔi adumɔ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmãa lɛ mra ni okpaaa ŋmãa lɛ dalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before any fruit actually grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani aduawai lɛ eda diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Too much direct heat or uneven watering stresses the tomato plant, causing it to drop its flowers to conserve energy and water instead of producing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fa babaoo loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in the middle of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmãa be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize plants need to build strong stems and green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa tsei koni amɛná ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli.

english: Why does my crop yield get smaller every year if I plant maize on the exact same patch of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests that attack maize to multiply in the soil.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea crops grow lots of green leaves but give me very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Adding too much nitrogen fertilizer makes cowpeas put all their energy into making heavy leaves instead of flowers and bean pods.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baaha cowpea kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛbaa baai ni tsii yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ.

english: Why do small worms appear and eat the center of my maize plants right after the first rain comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii Jeɔ kpo akɛ amɛyeɔ nii yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ eba lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms hatch quickly in warm weather after early rains and feed on the soft, tender young leaves inside the center funnel of the maize plant.
ga: Autumn cutworms lɛ fɔɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ. ni eyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curled up, small, and covered in yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe, amɛji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies feeding on leaf sap.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Egbɛɔ eshwaa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell the exact time my yam tubers are ready to be harvested?
