ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams are ready to harvest when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up, which signals that the tuber underground has stopped growing.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ekpa shweremɔ.

english: Why do small insects bore holes into my harvested maize even when I tie the storage bags tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shwieɔ bu yɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotokui lɛ fĩɔ shi jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Weevils or their tiny eggs are often already on the grain from the field. If the maize is not completely dried before storage, trapped moisture helps the eggs hatch into bugs that eat the grain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii Amɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anɔ momo. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛtoɔ lɛ Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni etsɔɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ dumɔwui.

english: How do I know if my land in Ghana is suitable for growing rice?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ sa kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Rice grows best in flat, low-lying areas or valley bottoms (inland valleys) that retain moisture well and have fertile clay or loamy soil capable of holding water.
ga: Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ loo jɔɔ lɛ shishi. (mligbɛ jɔɔ) ni hiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ sũ loo sũ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ sũ ni baanyɛ ahiɛ nu mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my young rice plants start turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves typically indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or poor drainage causing root rot. Applying a balanced nitrogen fertilizer like Urea at the right growth stage helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tamɔ urea tsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it better for me to broadcast my rice seeds or plant them in straight rows?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui lɛ loo madu amɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja?

english: Planting in straight rows or transplanting seedlings from a nursery makes weeding, fertilizing, and harvesting much easier, while allowing each plant enough space and sunlight to produce more grains compared to scattering seeds freely.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa jwɛi shwiemɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa. Ha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ewo dumɔwui babaoo. Kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni agbɛɔ ashwãa he lɛ he

english: How long does a typical rice crop take from planting to harvest in Ghana?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmãa ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ heɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔ mli kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ mli yɛ Ghana?

english: Most modern rice varieties grown in Ghana mature in about 3 to 4 months (90 to 120 days), depending on whether it is an lowland or upland variety.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ omɔ ni aduɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwereɔ yɛ aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli (gbii 90 kɛyashi 120), ni enɛ damɔ kɛji eji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my rice plants fall over to the ground before the grains are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo ni abaakpa lɛ?

english: Rice plants fall over (a condition called lodging) when they grow too tall and weak from excess nitrogen fertilizer, or when planted too densely, making them easily blown down by strong winds and heavy rain.
ga: Omɔ tso lɛ gbee shi (shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ lodging) baa kɛji omɔ tsei lɛ dara tsɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hewɔ. loo adu babaoo tsɔ Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ náa enɔ hewalɛ oya.

english: Does my rice farm need to be flooded with water all the time for the plants to grow?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ nu awo mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be koni tsei lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: While rice loves water, flooded conditions are mainly used to suppress weeds; the soil only needs to remain consistently moist, especially during the critical stages of flowering and grain formation.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa sumɔɔ nu moŋ Shi nu afua shihilɛi ji nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii babaoo koni akɛkudɔ jwɛi. Nɔ pɛ ni he hiaa ji ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be. Titri lɛ, yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmaafeemɔ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli.

english: What causes the heads of my rice plants to turn white and stay empty without filling up with grains?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ feɔ futafuta ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni mikɛ ŋmaa fataaa he?

english: White, empty grain heads are usually caused by stem borer pests cutting off nutrients inside the stalk, or by severe water shortage when the plant is trying to form flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni boteɔ tso lɛ mli, ni amɛfoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ dumɔwui yɛŋ yitsei ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa. Aloo nu ni faaa waa beni tsei miitao ni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa?

english: How far apart should I space my rice plants when putting them into the soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ makɛ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ ato he ko beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Spacing rice plants about 20 centimeters by 20 centimeters apart gives each plant enough space to sprout multiple healthy stems (tillers) without competing with nearby plants for nutrients.
ga: Gbɛ ni kã ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji aaafee sɛntimitai 20 x sɛntimitai 20, ni ehaa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmãa tsei ni wa baakwɛ̃ (ekɛ ŋmɔ lɛ atsu nii) ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ abɔi niyenii he akaŋ.

english: Why are weeds growing so much faster than my rice seedlings in the early weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Weeds naturally adapt faster to local soil conditions and aggressively absorb fertilizer and water before young rice seedlings can establish deep roots, making early weeding within the first 2 to 4 weeks essential.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe oya kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ. ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu shwieɔ shi oya dani ŋmãa bibii lɛ baanyɛ atswa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ Enɛ haa ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 2 kɛyashi 4 lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell the exact time my rice is ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa?

english: Rice is ready to harvest when about 80% to 85% of the grain panicles turn a bright golden-yellow color and the grains feel hard and firm when pressed between your fingers.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni ŋmaa lɛ mli aaafee 80% kɛyashi 85% etsɔ shika tsuru ni mli tse. Ni dumɔwui lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe wa ni amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ okɛ oniji nyɛmi nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings withered and die when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting tender cocoa leaves from scorching heat until the crop matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni buɔ mɔ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni obu kookoo baai ni mli tse lɛ ahe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashi tso lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rains wash essential nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the rainfall becomes too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits in the field without draining away, it drowns the root system and causes rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eshwɛɔ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni eha egbo.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat or dry soil. The plant drops its flowers to save energy and survive the weather stress instead of spending energy to grow fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛyashɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, why do I end up with thin stems and small cobs?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Mɛni hewɔ miyɛ ŋmãa bibii kɛ ŋmãa bibii?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, their roots fight underground for the same soil food and water, while their leaves fight for sunlight. Spacing them properly gives each plant enough food to produce big, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ baawu koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛ́ akɛto he ni sa lɛ, ebaaha tso fɛɛ tso aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the juices from the leaves. The damaged leaf loses its strength and can no longer stretch out to catch sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Baai ni efite lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛgbala amɛhe dɔŋŋ koni amɛjie amɛhe kpo yɛ hulu la lɛ mli.

english: Yam feeds very heavily on specific soil nutrients. Planting yam in the same spot year after year drains those specific nutrients faster than the land can rebuild them, leading to weaker harvests.
ga: Sweet potatoes yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Sweet potatoes ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee ehee ekoŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni afeɔ lɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Weeds have strong roots that grow faster than crop roots. They drink up the water and steal the fertilizer from the soil before your main crops have a chance to take them in.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni daa oya fe tsei shishifãi. Amɛnuɔ nu ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my sweet potato plants grow lots of bushy green leaves but produce very tiny potatoes underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii babaoo lɛ? Shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes sweet potato plants focus all their energy on growing tall stems and lush leafy tops instead of sending energy underground to swell up the tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa sweet potato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ ni miida kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baai yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ he wami kɛ yaa zugba a sisi konɛ e ha nɛ bulb ɔ nɛ bli.

english: Why does removing extra shoots from my plantain tree help the main stalk produce a bigger bunch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mi-plantain lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ ni ewoɔ niji wuji lɛ?

english: Every extra sucker attached to the main plantain tree drains water and nutrients away from the mother plant. Removing extra suckers directs all the plant's food into growing one large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Sucker krɛdɛɛ fɛɛ sucker krɛdɛɛ ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ he lɛ jieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ niyenii lɛ fɛɛ daa ni etsɔɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my maize plants produce such small ears when I plant them close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ woɔ toi bibii nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded together, they compete with one another for soil nutrients, moisture, and sunlight. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to develop large, healthy ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ eyi amɛhe obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee toi wuji ni mli wa.

english: Do I need to bring bees to my farm before my tomato plants can set fruit?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ ŋmeii aba miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mi-tomato tsei lɛ awo yibii?

english: No, tomato flowers are self-pollinating, meaning they can fertilize themselves. A gentle breeze is usually all that is needed to move the pollen inside the flower to produce fruit.
ga: Dabi, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ amɛhe. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛnyɛɔ amɛfɔɔ bii. Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa blɛoo. No pɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa koni akɛtsi pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ koni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow better in the open field than under the shade of big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ mli fe tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava needs full, direct sunlight every day to make food in its leaves. Shade prevents the plant from generating enough energy to develop thick, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Hulu la he miihia Yucca tɛ̃ɛ daa gbi koni ekɛfee niyenii yɛ ebaai lɛ anɔ. Shade tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli wa ni mli wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when there are no taller plants around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight and heat. Planting them near fast-growing shade crops like plantains protects them from sunburn and keeps the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛnuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ he. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do weeds harm my groundnut crop so much more than my taller crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui waa fe mi tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts grow low to the ground and cannot easily outgrow taller weeds. Weeds steal water and nutrients from the soil while blocking sunlight from reaching the low groundnut leaves.
ga: Peanuts kwɛ̃ɔ kɛyashɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni enyɛŋ etsɔ jwɛi ni kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ oya. Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ ŋmei baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I plant pepper on the exact same plot where I just harvested tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mifo mi-tomato lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Peppers and tomatoes belong to the same plant family and share similar pests and soil diseases. Planting them back-to-back in the same spot allows harmful organisms living in the soil to quickly attack the new crop.
ga: Pepper kɛ tomato yɛ tso weku kome mli ni amɛyɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni tamɔ amɛhe. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii heei oya.

english: Plantain trees have shallow, fibrous roots and soft trunks filled with water rather than hard wood. When the heavy fruit bunch forms at the top, strong winds easily uproot the plant.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ, ni yɔɔ fiber. ni akɛ nu woɔ tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo amli yɛ tsei ni wa najiaŋ. Beni aduawai akuu ko ni tsii feɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ shwieɔ tsei oya.

english: How do sorghum crops manage to stay green during dry spells while maize wilts?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmãa tsei hiɔ shi eŋɔli yɛ hɔmɔ be mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Sorghum has deep root systems and leaves coated with a natural wax that prevents moisture loss. This natural design allows it to withstand dry, hot conditions far better than maize.
ga: Sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli wax ni tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa lɛ ehà nɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli bɔ ni afee lɛ aha lɛ haa enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi kɛ latsaa lɛ etsui shi jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmãa.

english: Why are my sweet potato vines growing lots of green leaves but giving me tiny tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ehaa mi bulbs bibii lɛ?

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer causes sweet potatoes to direct all their energy into leafy top growth rather than storing food underground in the tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha sweet potato lɛ akudɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛya baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ niyenii ato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ oyitsoŋ lɛ

english: Can I grow a new field of cassava without buying packaged seeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔ hee ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni awo mli lɛ aheee?

english: Yes, cassava does not require true seeds to grow. You simply cut mature stems into pieces and plant them directly in the ground, where they will sprout new roots and branches on their own.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui diɛŋtsɛ he ehiaaa ŋmei koni ekwɛ̃. Okɛ tso lɛ tso ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛkɛ ni okɛduɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbaakwɛ tsei kɛ tsei niji heei.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants turn yellow and dry up when the sun gets too bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ hulu la lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak root systems that cannot handle direct, intense heat. They require shade trees or fast-growing nurse crops like plantains to shelter them and keep the soil moist until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛná he ko ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why do my crops stop growing and shed their leaves during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The Harmattan brings dry air and hot dust, causing plants to lose moisture faster than their roots can absorb from dry soil. Plants drop their leaves to save water and protect themselves until the rains return.
ga: Harmattan kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi kɛ sũ ni mli edɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa tree falling off without turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when there are not enough tiny insects around to pollinate them, or when the tree is stressed by excessive heat and lack of soil nutrients. Maintaining shade and ground leaf cover encourages helpful pollinating insects.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ. aloo kɛ́ hulutsoo ni fa fe nine kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Shade kɛ baai ni akɛhaa lɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa pollinators.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in wet and humid conditions. Clearing tall weeds, cutting excess tree branches, and letting air flow around the trees helps keep pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. jwɛi ni kɛlɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ ni afoɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ahaa kɔɔyɔɔ bɔleɔ he Tso lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn yellow even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often indicate that the soil is missing key nutrients like nitrogen, or that waterlogged soil is choking the roots and stopping them from taking up food from the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli obɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do weeds growing close to my crops reduce my total yield?
ga: Te jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni miwoɔ lɛ aba shi aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. They also act as hiding places for insects and diseases that can weaken your main plants.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛtsuɔ nii hu akɛ he ni kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni baanyɛ aha otso titri lɛ agbɔjɔ lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ amɛhe.

english: How far apart should I plant my cocoa trees to get a good harvest?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-kookoo tsei lɛ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni maná yibiiwoo kpakpa?

english: Spacing cocoa trees roughly 3 meters by 3 meters ensures each tree has enough underground space for its roots and canopy space for sunlight, preventing trees from fighting each other for nutrients.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji aaafee mitai 3 x mitai 3, ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa shikpɔŋ shishi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha shishifãi kɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hulu la baanyɛ ashɛ nɔ. Tsi tsei anaa koni amɛkaye niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ.

english: How does planting cassava close to my young cocoa trees affect the cocoa's growth?
ga: Te ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ saa kookoo lɛ dalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Cassava grows rapidly and has aggressive roots that consume large amounts of water and soil food. Planting cassava too close to young cocoa can starve the cocoa and stunt its growth.
ga: Cassava daa oya ni eyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni yeɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmei bibii lɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmei lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ekɛtsi dalɛ naa.

english: Why is it important for me to prune extra small branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ kɛjɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli

english: Pruning removes useless branches that consume energy without producing pods. It lets sunlight and fresh air reach the inner trunk, which reduces disease and encourages higher pod growth.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa ni kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa helai baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa.

english: Why is it beneficial to leave fallen dry leaves under my crop trees instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mashi baai ni egboi ni egbee shi lɛ yɛ mitsei lɛ ashishi moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ lɛ?

english: Fallen leaves decompose into natural manure that feeds the soil and keeps it moist during dry weather. Burning them destroys valuable organic nutrients and leaves the ground dry and exposed.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi lɛ gbálaa kɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Amɛ ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ niyenii ni jara wa ni yɔɔ wala mli lɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ ni eshwieɔ shi

english: When maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up, it usually means the plant is hungry for nitrogen. The plant moves the little nitrogen it has to the newest top leaves to keep growing, leaving the older bottom leaves to starve.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishi kɛtee ŋwɛi Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ko kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ eda. Kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do people say that planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land helps the soil grow better maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmei kpakpa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are special plants that pull nitrogen gas out of the air and store it in their roots. When the crop is harvested and the roots rot, that trapped food stays in the soil and feeds your next maize crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni shishifãi lɛ egbo lɛ Niyenii ni ekpɛtɛ he lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebaaha oŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn out small and thin when I plant many cuttings close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe tseee kɛ́ adu niji babaoo yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need space, sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to swell up. Planting cuttings too close together forces the crops to fight each other for food, leaving no extra energy to form big tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ he ko, hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛfu. Kɛ́ adu tsei niji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awuu yɛ amɛhe koni amɛye niyenii. Ni hewalɛ ko bɛ ni eshwɛ ni ekɛbaafee yitso agbo.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra suckers growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ ekomɛi?

english: When too many young shoots grow around a single plantain stem, they steal food and water from the main plant. Leaving only one or two strong suckers helps the main tree produce larger, heavier fruit bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni miida yɛ tso kome he lɛ fa babaoo Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso titri lɛ ni ewo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the shade trees off my plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ cacao tsei lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Shade trees act like giant umbrellas that shield cocoa seedlings and keep the air and soil cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai wuji ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop and wilt in the afternoon heat even when the ground is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: On very hot afternoons, pepper leaves lose water into the hot air faster than the roots can drink it up from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from losing more water, but it bounces back when the evening cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nu kroko ni baafite lɛ he. Shi ebaaku esɛɛ kɛji edɔ.

english: How do I know if the soil has enough moisture for me to safely plant my maize after the first dry season rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha makwɛ ŋmãa shweshweeshwe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain often leaves the soil dry just an inch below the surface. Squeeze a fistful of soil from a hand-deep hole; if it forms a soft ball that holds together without dripping, the soil has enough steady moisture for seeds to germinate.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ inchi 1 pɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Okɛ onine atsɔ sũ ni mli kwɔ mli kɛjɛ bu ko ni mli kwɔ mli. Kɛji efee bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni kɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ he ni nu ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sũ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too hot or when the plant experiences drought stress. Extreme heat prevents proper pollination, so the plant drops the flower to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ he haomɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Bɔni afee ni tsei akafite hewalɛ lɛ, amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing very tall and thin, but falling over when the wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi shigbeemɔ beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa lɛ?

english: Maize grows tall and weak when planted too densely or shaded by weeds, as it stretches up to reach light. Without full sunlight on the lower stem, the plant cannot build a thick, strong stalk to hold its weight.
ga: Abɛi daa ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛji adu yɛ hei ni gbɔmɛi eyi obɔ kɛ hei ni jwɛi ebɔle he lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa baagbɛ eshwa kɛya la mli. Kɛji hulu la shɛɛɛ shishigbɛ tso lɛ he lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ama tso lɛ shishigbɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ tso lɛ nyɛŋ ama tso lɛ shishigbɛ tso lɛ ni mli wa ni ekɛfi etsitsinɔnii lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are my vegetables growing very slowly even though I water them every single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ? Ni mikɛ nu haa daa gbi?

english: Watering too much washes essential nutrients deep into the ground where roots cannot reach them and pushes air out of the soil. Plant roots need a balance of both water and air to stay healthy and absorb food.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ, ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛŋɔ niyenii.

english: Why should I wait for the major rainy season to fully settle before sowing my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ dani madu ŋmãa?

english: Planting too early during minor or unpredictable rains can cause seeds to dry out and die in hot soil, or germinate weakly. Waiting for steady rains ensures the soil stays moist enough for seeds to sprout and build strong roots.
ga: Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo loo ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ loo amɛkwɛ̃ fioo. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I remove all the large shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie cacao tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh tropical sunlight. Keeping or planting shade trees like plantains or leguminous forest trees protects the cocoa from heat stress and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ tsei bibii loo ŋmeii kooi lɛ akwɛmɔ loo adumɔ baaye abua ni abu kookoo he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. This often happens when soil is overused without adding compost, manure, or nitrogen-based fertilizers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa kɛji akɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ babaoo tsu nii ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he.

english: Why does my soil turn hard like dry clay after rain, making it difficult for my crops to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wa tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Ni ehaa ewaa ahaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter like decomposed leaves or manure. Adding organic material loosens the soil structure, allowing water to sink in and roots to breathe and spread easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ bɛ mli. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔne lɛ feɔ mlɛo. Enɛ haa nu boteɔ mli ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ amu ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã mlɛo.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get dark rotten spots at the bottom before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ dani etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ po lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom end rot, which is caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit and uneven watering. Ensuring regular watering and maintaining healthy soil prevents the fruit bottoms from drying out and rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli kɛ nu ni akɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ akwɛ koni afɔse nu daa ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi aduawai ashishi lɛ anaa koni ekagbi ni ekafite.

english: Why do I see small holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars hiding inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ mli lɛ anɔ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana. Early monitoring and applying safe bio-pesticides or recommended controls when plants are young prevents them from destroying the crop leaves and stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ ana mra ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ tsu nii jogbaŋŋ Aloo, nɔkwɛmɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa beni tsei lɛ darako lɛ baatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant cassava on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the earth. Rotating with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Legume ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ cowpeas loo peanuts ni atsakeɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to cut off the extra small shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ ahe krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plant for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, resulting in bigger and healthier plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei krokomɛi loo tsei lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds around my pepper plants even when the plants are already bigger than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? mi pepper tso lɛ Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ da fe jwɛi momo moŋ.

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight from your crops below the ground, and they also hide dangerous pests and fungal diseases that can easily spread to your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã onibii titrii lɛ amli oya lɛ hu teeɔ.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines to climb up wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔse mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni ekwɔ tso tso ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up toward the sun, allowing the plant to catch maximum light to make food. Leaves off the ground are also less likely to catch diseases from damp soil, leading to larger yield tubers.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ akwɛ hulu la lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa sweet potato tso lɛ naa la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kponɔ lɛ hu nyɛŋ aná hela kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso ni da.

english: What is the benefit of growing my vegetables inside a greenhouse instead of in an open field?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli moŋ fe ŋmɔ mli lɛ he?

english: A greenhouse protects delicate crops like tomatoes and peppers from heavy rains, harsh sunlight, and pest invasions, creating a controlled environment where plants can grow healthier and yield more produce year-round.
ga: Greenhouses buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Bɔɔ shihilɛ ko ni akudɔ ni tsei baanyɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient. When the soil lacks nitrogen, plants cannot make enough green pigment (chlorophyll) to feed themselves properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. which is an essential nutrient for plants When the soil lacks nitrogen Plants cannot produce enough green pigment (chlorophyll) to properly feed themselves.

english: Why should I spread dry grass or plant leaves on top of the soil around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo madu baai yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Spreading dry grass or leaves (called mulching) keeps the soil moist by stopping the sun from drying it out quickly, prevents weeds from growing, and keeps the soil cool during hot weather.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa Mulching (ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching) lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛtsɔ hulutsoo be mli ni ehaaa egbi oya lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ

english: Fertilizer is most effective when given twice: first when the plant is a few weeks old to help it grow leaves, and again when it reaches knee-height to help it build strong, full corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli shii enyɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ. Klɛŋklɛŋ be ji be mli ni tso lɛ eye otsii 2-3 koni eye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛdara. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu kɛ́ eshɛ tsitsi nɔ koni eye ebua ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees need plantain trees planted next to them when they are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ he hiaa ni adu dumɔwui yɛ emasɛi lɛ? Beni tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily burn under direct hot sun. Plantain trees grow fast and have wide leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and moisture while the cocoa gets established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋtayaai. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: What causes small holes in the leaves of my crops and how does it hurt the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi tso lɛ baai anɔ Ni te eyeɔ tsei awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Holes in leaves are usually caused by insects like caterpillars or beetles feeding on them. When leaves are damaged, the plant cannot catch enough sunlight to produce food, which slows down its overall growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Beni baai lɛ efite lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Enɛ haa dalɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomatoes turning black and rotting before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes, known as blossom-end rot, happen when the plant does not get enough calcium or when watering is irregular during the time the fruit is forming.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. aloo be mli ni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ be fɛɛ mli yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ woɔ lɛ

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetables early in the morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil absorbs the water before the hot midday sun can evaporate it, allowing the roots to stay hydrated throughout the heat of the day.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baaŋɔ nu lɛ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ afee lɛ la. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How do I know that my cassava roots are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves start to turn yellow and drop off, usually around 9 to 12 months after planting depending on the variety.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before turning into actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ebatsɔ pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress, such as extremely hot weather, too much or too little water, or a lack of soil nutrients needed to support fruit growth.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛmiihao, tamɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli ni amɛhaa lɛ nu babaoo loo fioo tsɔ. aloo niyenii ni he hiaa koni aduawai akwɛ̃ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: How can the weeds I clear from my land turn into fertilizer for my crops?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aaatsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha midumɔ nii lɛ?

english: When cut weeds and crop leftovers decompose in the soil, they break down and release rich nutrients back into the earth, improving soil health and feeding your crops naturally without extra cost.
ga: Kɛji jwɛi ni afolɔ kɛ tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛfiteɔ ni amɛjieɔ niyenii kpakpai babaoo kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ aya hiɛ ni oha onibii lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni okɛ shika kroko fataaa he.

english: Is it better to burn cut bushes when clearing my farm or leave them to decay on the land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi ni afolɔ beni mijieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ loo maha amɛgbo yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Leaving cut plants to rot on the farm keeps the soil cool and moist, protects it from heavy rain, and turns into organic manure, whereas burning destroys nutrients and dries out the land.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ koni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Hebuu kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he ni ebafeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɛ be mli ni shãa lɛ fiteɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli gĩɔ.

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to produce a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaawo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Healthy farm soil is usually dark, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture well, and contains living creatures like earthworms that help loosen the earth for crop roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kpakpa mli lɛ mli ewo duŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ Ni bɔɔ nii komɛi yɛ tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛhaa tsei shishifãi.

english: What is the correct way to mix animal manure into my soil so it does not damage my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ ŋmeii futuɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekafite miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Fresh manure produces heat that can burn crop roots. You should let manure dry and decompose for a few weeks before mixing it thoroughly into the topsoil a couple of weeks before planting.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ feɔ dɔlɛ ni baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi. Esa akɛ oha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi ni efite otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛfutu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛdu.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants start turning yellow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen food from the soil, or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away and soaked the roots too much. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps bring back the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Aloo, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni eha shishifãi lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thick leaves but yield very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ waa kɛ baai ni mli tse shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, cassava spends all its energy growing tall stems and leaves instead of roots. Balancing the soil with wood ash or potassium fertilizer encourages larger tuber growth.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ lɛ, ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni kɛlɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso sũ loo potassium ŋmɔshi nibii to shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa bulbs lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: What causes my pepper flowers to fall off before they can form peppers?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ pepper?

english: Flowers fall off when pepper plants experience stress from intense heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like calcium. Keeping soil moist and mulched helps keep the flowers on the plant.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha afee fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tsei anɔ lɛ ahiɔ shi.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop and die suddenly even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tso lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden drooping in wet soil is usually caused by soil-borne bacterial wilt, which enters through the roots and blocks water from moving up inside the stem, causing the plant to dry out from within.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tso lɛ mli tsei ni shwieɔ shi trukaa lɛ baa. Eboteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni etsĩɔ nu naa koni ekaya ŋwɛi yɛ tso lɛ mli. Gbimɔ tso lɛ kɛjɛ emli.

english: Why do some crops grow better when I plant them together on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ fee ekome yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Different crops help each other in the soil; for instance, cowpeas or beans trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the earth, which helps neighboring crops like maize grow bigger.
ga: Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, tsina loo ŋmeii mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ abele, daraa.

english: How can I prevent weeds from overpowering my crop seedlings right after planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye mitso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu lɛ?

english: Covering the bare ground around young seedlings with dry grass or palm fronds blocks light from weed seeds so they cannot grow, while keeping the soil wet for your young crops.
ga: Kɛji akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei tsei baatsi he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni bɔle Saplings lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔ koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛhaa onibii bibii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which acts as food for leaf growth. This often happens when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients, so adding compost, manure, or the right fertilizer restores their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii ni haa baa lɛ daa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: What happens to my crops if I apply chemical fertilizer when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsu nii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn plant roots. Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve into a mild liquid that roots can safely drink without getting scorched by concentrated salts.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi ashã. Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ nu ni mli jɔ. Abaanyɛ anu shishifãi lɛ shweshweeshwe ni ŋmei ni mli ewo muji lɛ eshãŋ amɛ.

english: Why do many small flowers fall off my cocoa trees before turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ gbee shi babaoo dani etsɔɔ cocoa ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can feed. Factors like temporary dry spells or a low population of tiny pollinating midges cause the tree to drop extra flowers it cannot support.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua, nibii tamɔ hɔmɔ ni baa be kukuoo mli loo fɔfɔi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ ayibɔ faaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my seed yams take a very long time to sprout after I plant them in the mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo gɔŋ ko mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seed yams go through a natural resting period called dormancy after harvest. During this time, the yam tuber is dormant and will not sprout until its internal resting phase ends, regardless of soil water.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, Sweet potato tubers lɛ wɔɔ ni amɛkwɛɛɛ kɛyashi amɛmli wɔɔhe lɛ baagbe naa. ekɔɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he

english: Why do my pepper leaves wilt in the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In strong afternoon heat, leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can suck it up from the soil. Placing dry grass mulch around the stems keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he ni ebɔle he lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Why are there tiny holes in my young maize leaves with small caterpillars hiding inside the center shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni Akɛtee yɛ ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. The worms hatch on the leaves and crawl inside the central funnel to feed on soft new leaves, requiring early treatment with recommended sprays or botanical mixtures like neem.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ. Kplukai lɛ fɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni amɛkpãa kɛboteɔ teŋgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli koni amɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Esa akɛ atsa lɛ mra. Kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli tamɔ neem.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground if I leave them in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water fills up all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating cassava roots. This damp, airless environment allows rot-causing soil fungi to multiply quickly and destroy the tubers.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ he fɛɛ he ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Shihilɛ ni mli efɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni miifite lɛ mli lɛ feɔ babaoo oya ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Is it good for my farm if I plant pepper and cassava together on the same plot?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping them works well because pepper grows quickly and is harvested early, while cassava grows slowly at first and draws nutrients from deeper soil, allowing you to maximize land without crops fighting for space.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya ni akpaa amɛ mra. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ, Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ ohe woɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli babaoo ni ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ he ko akaŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crop seeds after the first rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Wild weed seeds are tough and naturally adapted to burst into growth at the very first drop of rain, whereas farm crop seeds take longer to absorb water and break their outer shell to sprout.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛmɔɔ nu ni amɛfoɔ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil so quickly before I can get them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani akɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes spoil fast if picked when fully soft and overripe on the vine, or if left under direct sunlight after harvest. Picking them when they just start changing color from green to pink keeps them firm during transport.
ga: Tomato baafite oya kɛji akɛ ajie yɛ be mli ni wain tso lɛ mli ejɔ kwraa lolo ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ Amɛhe beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli kɛyaa pinki nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ yaa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when there are no shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo be bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, intense sunlight. Shade trees act like living umbrellas, protecting the young plants from heat stress, keeping the soil moist, and helping them establish strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa shishifãi ni wa

english: Why do so many flowers fall off my cocoa trees without ever turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo miiho kɛmiijɛ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee ŋmeii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce many more flowers than they can support. Flowers only turn into pods if they are pollinated by tiny insects called midges; if the tree is stressed by drought or lacks nutrients, it drops unpollinated flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Fɔfɔi bafeɔ pods pɛ kɛji kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ wo amɛmli. Kɛji hɔmɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa Tsei lɛ hu baashwie fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the hot afternoon even when the soil was watered in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi moŋ?

english: During peak heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it from the ground. Wilting is a natural defense mechanism where the leaves curl to slow down water loss until the air cools down.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Withering ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni nu lɛ aya hiɛ fiofio kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge, bushy leaves above ground but very small roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients like potassium, the plant invests all its energy into growing big leaves instead of storing energy in the root tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa babaoo kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi tamɔ potassium he lɛ, tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai wuji ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baato shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency or waterlogging at the roots. When roots are drowned or lack nutrients, the plant cannot produce chlorophyll, which gives leaves their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa loo nu ehiɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ shwie nu mli loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ amɛmli lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee klorofil. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa

english: Why is it bad if I plant my crops very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Planting too close forces crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing them properly allows air to circulate, reduces disease spread, and ensures each plant grows strong.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli. Ha helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ aba shi ni oha tso fɛɛ tso ada waa

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields every year if I keep planting the exact same crop on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛji mitee nɔ midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The same crop continuously pulls the same nutrients from the exact same soil depth every season. Rotating different crops helps balance nutrient use and breaks the cycle of soil-dwelling pests and diseases.
ga: Tsei nɛɛ nɔŋŋ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli daa be. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ atsakeɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ekpaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ asɛɛkuu.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if there is plenty of room in the field?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ gbɛ babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and aggressively steal underground water, soil nutrients, and sunlight from your crop's roots, which stunts crop growth and lowers your harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli lɛ waa Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kpaɔ amɛdalɛ ni ehaa onibii ni onáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads quickly in humid, dark, and damp conditions. Pruning overgrown branches allows sunlight and fresh air into the farm, which dries out excess moisture and prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo, duŋ, kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa naa koni ekabote ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ agbi. ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa

english: Why must I dry my harvested cocoa beans thoroughly before taking them to the buying center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbi mi-kokoo yibii ni mikpa lɛ dani mikɛya he ni aheɔ nii yɛ lɛ?

english: Proper drying lowers the moisture inside the beans to prevent mold growth and preserve flavor quality. Wet or moldy beans spoil quickly in storage and are rejected by buyers because they cannot be processed into good chocolate.
ga: Kɛ́ agbi lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kɔfe yibii lɛ amli lɛ baa shi koni ŋmɔtɔ akakwɛ̃ ni eha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ahi shi. Beans ni efɔ loo ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akɛto, ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ kpooɔ ejaakɛ anyɛɛɛ afee tsokolate kpakpa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and shallow roots that burn easily in strong heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain next to them creates a cool umbrella that keeps the soil moist until the cocoa roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow while the plant is still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen or the soil is too wet. Giving the plants nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea during early growth helps the leaves stay green so the plant can make big ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ he miihia nitrogen loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea ha tsei lɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛbaa lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Will I get fewer crops if I plant cassava and maize very close together on the same land?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo fioo kɛji midu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cassava too close to maize makes them fight for sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving each plant enough space allows both crops to grow strong roots and yield properly.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa he tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off without growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant experiences heavy heat stress, irregular watering, or attacks by tiny pests like thrips. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting plants from pests helps the flowers stay on to produce fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa amɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be fɛɛ be kɛ tsei ahebuu kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with plenty of leaves but producing small roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ, ni eyɛ baai babaoo, shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much shade or excessive nitrogen, it spends all its energy growing stems and leaves instead of tubers. Planting cassava in full sunlight and avoiding high-nitrogen fertilizers encourages bigger roots.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei ná hulutsoo babaoo loo nitrogen babaoo Ebaahe be dani ekɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmei shishifãi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ najiaŋ. Kɛ́ okwɛ ŋmei yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmei ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ adara.

english: What causes small worms to eat the inner leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the fresh middle leaves of maize plants. Checking your farm early and spraying recommended neem oil mixtures or suitable pesticides when the plants are young stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai heei lɛ anɔ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. ni okɛ neem fɔ ni akɛfutu mli loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ nɔ beni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my yam tubers rotting in the ground before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Yam rot in the soil is caused by excess water trapped around the roots or damage from tiny soil worms called nematodes. Making tall mounds for good drainage and planting healthy seed yams prevents rot.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe loo shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ fitemɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato fitemɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni aaafee koni nu atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛ sweet potatoes ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni adu lɛ baaye abua ni akafite.

english: How can I tell if my land has good soil for growing tomatoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛduɔ tomato?

english: Good soil for tomatoes is dark, soft, crumbly, and drains water easily without staying muddy. If your soil is hard or sandy, mixing in well-rotted animal manure or compost improves its strength and feeds the crop.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha tomato lɛ mli edɔ, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni nu hoɔ oya ni ekɛ muji baaa. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo ŋã yɔɔ mli lɛ, ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo kooloi ŋmei ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ baawo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hewalɛ ni eha amɛ niyenii.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that naturally react faster to water and soil nutrients than farm crops. Clearing weeds early in the season prevents them from stealing food, light, and water from your young plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii, la kɛ nu kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why does my harvested maize get small holes and powder on it while stored in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ yɛ bu kɛ powda bibii lɛ? Ani otsi ohe beni okɛtoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Insects called weevils bore into maize grains if the corn is stored before drying completely or if the storage area is damp. Drying your corn thoroughly under the sun and storing it in airtight bags keeps weevils away.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ baabote ŋmãa mli kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ to dani egbi kwraa loo kɛji akɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli edɔ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni akɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa akabote mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the nutrient responsible for healthy leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure will help the plants regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni haa baai lɛ mli waa Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I place dry chemical fertilizer directly against the stems of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing chemical fertilizer directly against the stem causes chemical burn to the plant's delicate stem and roots. Always place the fertilizer in a ring or band a few inches away from the stem and cover it lightly with soil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha tsofa ashã tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo ŋmei loo ŋmei mli ni kɛ ŋmei lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi 2-3 ni okɛ sũ aha nɔ fioo.

english: Why do small green worms eat holes through my maize leaves during the night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ bu kɛtsɔɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that hides inside the plant's funnel during the day and feeds at night. You can control them early by applying recommended crop protection medicines or putting clean sand into the plant funnels.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ ehe woɔ tsei amli gbɛjegbɛi amli yɛ shwane mli, ni eyeɔ nii gbɛkɛ. Obaanyɛ okudɔ lɛ mra. Kɛ tsofa ni akɛbuɔ tsei ahe ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ atsu nii loo okɛ ŋã ni he tse awo tso ni aduɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl upwards and stop growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the plant's juices and spreading diseases. Spraying with neem leaf extract or suitable insecticides early in the morning helps clear these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai amɛshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ kɛjɛ ohe.

english: Why do my crops dry up and die when I spray weedicide on the grass near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwie jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Non-selective weedicides destroy any green plant they touch, not just weeds. To protect your crops, use a spray shield on your nozzle, spray on calm days without wind, or use selective herbicides designed for your specific crop.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni halaaa lɛ fiteɔ tsei eŋɔli ni amɛkɛkpeɔ lɛ. Jeee jwɛi pɛ ni okɛbuɔ onibii ahe Kɛ spray shield awo nozzle lɛ nɔ. Spray yɛ gbi ni yɔɔ kpoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Aloo okɛ tsofa ko ni ahala ni afee aha oŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by strong direct sunlight, dry weather, or insect pests like mirids. Providing good shade trees and protecting the farm from sucking insects helps the flowers stay on and form pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ pollen Tso lɛ he ŋmɔlɔ kpakpa ni akɛhaa kɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during wind storms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum ni tswaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots, and heavy bunches make them top-heavy. Nematodes in the soil can also weaken roots; staking your trees with bamboo poles and planting clean suckers prevents them from falling.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. ni jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ haa yitsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo Nematodes ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hu baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ wo tso lɛ he, ni odu ŋmeii ni he tse lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ akagbee shi.

english: This is known as blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium or experiences uneven soil moisture. Keeping the soil consistently watered and adding calcium or lime to the soil prevents this.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shiŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa ni okɛ calcium loo lime wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Tubers rot underground mostly when water collects around the roots in heavy rain due to poor drainage. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess water flow away, keeping the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Tubers babaoo fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why do my stored seed yams start sprouting too early in the barn before planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi kwɛ̃mɔ oya tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yams sprout early when stored in warm, dark, or poorly ventilated places. Storing your seed yams on raised open racks in a cool, well-shaded, and airy barn slows down early sprouting.
ga: Sweet potatoes baakwɛ̃ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni edɔɔ, duŋ, loo kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ. Atomɔ dumɔwui ni akɛto adeka ni agbele mli yɛ tsũ mli ni mli ejɔ, shade kpakpa, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ baaha ekwɛ̃mɔ aya hiɛ.

english: If I plant my crops at the very start of the rainy season, will I be able to harvest them earlier?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei yɛ nugbɔ be lɛ shishijee mli Ani manyɛ makpa mra?

english: Yes, planting early at the start of the rains allows crops to establish strong root systems quickly and complete their growth cycle faster, enabling an earlier harvest before late-season dry spells set in.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔ mra yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni mli wa oya, ni amɛdaraa oya. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akpaa nii oya dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shɛɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee.

english: Why do my crops take longer to mature when I plant them late in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ midu yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ?

english: Late-planted crops often face reduced soil moisture and irregular rainfall as the season ends. Without enough steady water, the plants slow down their growth process to survive, which delays maturity.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ kpeɔ beni be lɛ yaa naagbee lɛ. Kɛji nu ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ faaa lɛ Tsei lɛ baaha amɛdalɛ aba shi koni amɛhi shi. Enɛ baaha dalɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: Why do my crops wilt so quickly whenever the rain stops for just one week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwieɔ oya be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ lɛ baakpa otsi kome pɛ lɛ?

english: Crops rely on soil moisture to absorb nutrients and stay upright. When rain stops, the topsoil dries out fast under the sun, causing the plant to lose water through its leaves faster than its roots can pull it from the ground.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ, ŋwɛi sũ lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ hulu lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I rely only on rainfall to farm throughout the whole year in Ghana?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mihe afɔ̃ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ pɛ nɔ koni mafee okwaayeli afi muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ Ghana?

english: Relying only on rain limits you to the wet seasons. During the dry season (Harmattan), rainfall is insufficient, so crops will dry up and fail unless you have an alternative water source.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ohe fɔ̃ nugbɔ pɛ nɔ lɛ, no haa oshɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ he. Yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli (Harmattan) lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii baagbi ni amɛbaafee nɔ ko, ja oyɛ nu jɛɛhe kroko.

english: What is irrigation, and how does it help my farm during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni ji nu shwiemɔ? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Irrigation is the practice of manually or mechanically supply water to your crops from sources like wells, rivers, or tanks. It ensures your plants get consistent water even when it does not rain at all.
ga: Nu shwiemɔ ji nifeemɔ ni ji nu ni akɛ niji loo tsɔne haa onibii kɛjɛɔ hei tamɔ nubui, faai, loo nu ŋtayaai amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa nu be fɛɛ be kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po.

english: How can I store rainwater on my farm so I have water to use when the rains stop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ nugbɔ nu ato miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni maná nu kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ?

english: You can collect rainwater using farm ponds, water barrels, or dugouts. Covering stored water or directing runoff into small earthen reservoirs helps keep water available for hand-watering your crops during short dry spells.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔ mli nu ŋshɔi, baagi, loo ŋshɔi ni akɛwoɔ ŋshɔ mli lɛ atsu nii kɛbua nugbɔ nu lɛ naa. Nu ni akɛtoɔ loo kudɔɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ nɔ nubui bibii amli lɛ ni akɛhaa lɛ baaha nu ni yɔɔ ni akɛbaafɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo mli lɛ baaha.

english: How do I know if my crops are getting enough water from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Healthy, well-watered crops have firm, bright green leaves and steady growth. If the soil is dry two inches below the surface and leaves start curling or drooping in the afternoon heat, your crops need water.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni nu yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi aaafee 2 inches yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi ni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ, Etsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia onibii.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops curl up during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a crop's natural defense mechanism against water loss. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to direct sunlight to conserve the water inside it.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛjɛ nu ni laajeɔ lɛ he. Tsei baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ koni nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akafite lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens to crop flowers if there is no water when the plant starts flowering?
ga: Mɛni baaba fɔfɔi tsei anɔ kɛji nu bɛ beni tsei lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi lɛ?

english: Water stress during flowering causes the plant to drop its flowers to save energy and water. Without flowers, the plant cannot produce grains, pods, or fruits, leading to a poor harvest.
ga: Nu mli haomɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Kɛji fɔfɔii bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo dumɔwui, ŋmeii, loo aduawai, ni no baaha ŋmaa lɛ akakpa jogbaŋŋ.

english: What simple method can I use to keep the soil around my crops moist for longer?
