ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii. ni haa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baahi shi be kakadaŋŋ?

english: You can place dry grass, leaves, or crop residues on top of the soil around your plants. This is called mulching, and it shades the soil from the hot sun so water does not evaporate quickly.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ awo sũ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ. Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching. ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he Koni nu akatsɔ oya

english: Why do we make big mounds of dirt before planting tubers like yam or cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔfeɔ shikpɔŋ wuji ni abua naa dani wɔduɔ shishifãi tamɔ sweet potatoes loo cassava lɛ?

english: Making dirt mounds loosens the soil so the roots and tubers can expand easily underground without being squeezed by hard dirt. It also raises the plant up to keep its roots from drowning when heavy rain floods the farm.
ga: Gɔŋ ni ooofee lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi oya ni shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ emɔɔɔ amɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ewoɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni shishifãi lɛ akagbo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eha ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ.

english: Why do my sweet potato plants produce many small tubers instead of a few big ones when I don't heap the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ ŋmeii wuji fioo komɛi najiaŋ be mli ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieee shi lɛ?

english: When soil is flat and packed hard, sweet potato roots struggle to push outward and swell into large tubers. Piling the soil into loose mounds gives the tubers room to grow big and provides soft ground to draw nutrients from.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, sweet potato shishifãi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya kponɔgbɛ ni amɛbaatsɔ bulbs agboi. Shikpɔŋ ni akɛtoɔ ŋtayaai ni etse ehe lɛ mli Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ adara ni eha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni akɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ mli.

english: Why do some farmers plant cassava on long raised ridges while others plant them on individual round mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mɛi komɛi duɔ yɛ gɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Round mounds are easy to make by hand with a hoe on smaller plots, while long ridges are better for larger fields worked with machines or animals, helping to guide rainwater down slopes without washing away the topsoil.
ga: Ewaaa akɛ akɛ shɔvel baatsu nii kɛfee gɔji ni yɔɔ kokroo yɛ he bibioo ko. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii kakadaji hi kɛha ŋmɔji wuji ni biɔ tsɔnei loo kooloi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛɔ nugbɔ nu ni baa shi lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ efɔɔɔ.

english: If maize gets too little water, its leaves will curl inward and turn pale yellow to save moisture. If it gets too much water, the leaves turn bright yellow from the bottom up because the roots are drowning and cannot breathe.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ná nu fioo tsɔ lɛ Ebaai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛji onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛjɛ shishi kɛyashi ŋwɛi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu.

english: Why do the leaves of my vegetables turn yellow and die whenever water collects in one spot on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be fɛɛ be ni nu baabua ehe naa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Standing water fills all the tiny air pockets in the dirt, effectively suffocating the plant roots. When roots cannot take in oxygen, they stop absorbing nutrients, causing the leaves to turn yellow and eventually rot.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii amli obɔ. fɛɛ yɛ muji lɛ mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ Ebaakpa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ŋmɔmɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni naagbee lɛ amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop in the hot afternoon even when the soil feels slightly wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo moŋ?

english: Hot afternoon sun causes leaves to lose water faster than the roots can pull it up from the ground, making the plant temporarily wilt to protect itself. If the plant perks back up by morning, it is a natural defense response and does not mean it needs immediate extra watering.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa baai lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gboɔ be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ehe. Kɛji tso lɛ he wa lɛ leebi lɛ No ji adebɔɔ mli hetoo ni etsɔɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ nu babaoo awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Is it a good idea to plant vegetables in a low-lying area of my farm where water stays close to the surface?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu aduawai yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni nu bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ mli?

english: Low areas are great during dry seasons because the soil stays naturally damp, but during heavy rains, they can easily become waterlogged and drown crops like tomatoes or peppers unless you build raised beds or drainage channels.
ga: Hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Nakai shikpɔji lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni nu baanyɛ atsɔ mli oya ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tomato loo ŋmɔtɔ awo nu mli. Ja ootswa saatso ni awo nɔ loo nu homɔ gbɛ.

english: Can I really trust weather forecast alerts on my mobile phone to know when to sow my seeds?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ mihe afɔ̃ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he kɔkɔbɔɔi ni yɔɔ mi-mobail foŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ diɛŋtsɛ koni male be ni esa akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ.

english: Mobile weather alerts give helpful general predictions about upcoming rainfall and heat, but you should combine that information with local signs on your field, like soil dryness and wind patterns, before planting.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he kɔkɔbɔɔi ni akɛyaa he fɛɛ he haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he gbalɛi ni he hia yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ dɔlɛ ni baa lɛ he. Shi esa akɛ okɛ nakai saji lɛ afata okadii ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa lɛ he, dani okɛdu.

english: If I live in town and only visit my farm on weekends, how can I prevent weeds from taking over my cocoa seedlings?
ga: Kɛji mihi maŋtiase mli ni miyasaraa miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ otsii lɛ anaagbee pɛ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye mi-kokoo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ?

english: You can apply a thick layer of organic mulch, like dry leaves or cocoa husks, around the base of your seedlings. Mulch blocks sunlight so weed seeds cannot sprout easily, while also trapping moisture in the soil while you are away.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse, tamɔ baai ni egbi loo kookoo ŋmɔtɔ awo tsei bibii lɛ ashishi. Mulch lɛ baatsi hulu la lɛ naa. No hewɔ lɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ mlɛo. Kɛ agbɛnɛ hu, ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ooomɔ be mli ni obɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: How can checking crop apps on my phone help me decide if my farm needs watering without me digging into the dirt?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe app ni yɔɔ mifoŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua mi ni makpɛ miyiŋ kɛji akɛ nu he miihia miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Agricultural mobile services use regional weather and satellite data to estimate how much water the soil in your area has lost, helping you know whether your crop field is likely dry or holding enough moisture.
ga: Agricultural Mobile Services kɛ kpokpaa nɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ satelait saji tsuɔ nii kɛbuɔ nu ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ falɛ he akɔntaa. Enɛ haa oleɔ kɛji akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ baagbi loo ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow from the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and grow big leaves. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the crop the food it needs to recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔji kɛ baai wuji amli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my land yield less harvest every year if I keep planting maize on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season without giving the earth time to replenish. Rotating crops, such as planting beans or groundnuts after maize, helps put goodness back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛwo mli ekoŋŋ. Nɔkwɛmɔnɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii amli tsakemɔ, ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei sɛɛ. Ye obua ni okɛ ekpakpafeemɔ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds very close together to get more plants on my acre of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ mi acre kome lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops end up fighting each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space ensures they grow strong and produce bigger, healthier yields.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha eda waa ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and bigger than my crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛdaraa fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that are naturally adapted to spring up fast and grab water and soil nutrients before your crops can. Clearing weeds early stops them from starving your crops of essential food and moisture.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo fɛ̃i be mli oya ni amɛgbala nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ afee nakai. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekaná niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that suck the juice from the leaves and spread viruses. Protecting plants from these tiny bugs keeps the leaves flat and healthy so fruit can grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ kɛ baa lɛ baa. Abuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii ahe Enɛɛmɛi yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ bɔni afee ni aduawai lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do many flowers fall off my cocoa trees without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo miiho kɛmiijɛ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by intense sun, lack of moisture, or insect attacks. Providing shade trees and keeping the soil moist helps the tree hold onto its flowers so they turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Fɛ̃i ni bɛ loo kooloi ni tutuaa lɛ Shade ni akɛhaa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi ni feɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and dry up when the afternoon sun gets very strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ ni egbiɔ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Hot direct sunlight dries out the top layer of soil quickly, causing delicate roots to overheat and lose moisture fast. Covering the soil around the base of the plants with dry grass or leaves keeps the roots cool and moist.
ga: Hulu la ni mli edɔ ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gĩɔ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ mli dɔɔ fe nine, ni amɛmli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why did my cassava grow very tall with many leaves, but the tubers inside the soil stayed thin and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji ŋmeii bibii?

english: If cassava plants get too much shaded sunlight or excessive leaf-boosting nutrients, the plant puts all its energy into growing big top stems and leaves instead of storing energy underground in the tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ nine shɛ hulu la loo niyenii ni tsirɛɔ baai lɛ babaoo nɔ lɛ, Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ oyitsoŋ lɛ najiaŋ

english: Why do my yam tubers rot inside the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot when rain water gathers around the roots in heavy soil without draining away. Building high mounds or ridges helps excess water run off so the tubers stay dry and healthy underground.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ ni efooo. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi ni amɛgbi ni amɛhe wa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Should I start planting my crop seeds as soon as the very first rain falls?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ pɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become steady over a week or two, because a single early rain can be followed by weeks of hot sun that will burn up your young emerging seedlings.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ otsi kome loo enyɔ mli. Ejaakɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha hulutsoo be ni naa wa waa aba otsii babaoo sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui bibii lɛ fɛɛ ashã.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on young maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or poor root health caused by waterlogged ground, which prevents the crop from absorbing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo shishifãi lɛ ahewalɛ ni ehiii ni ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ ewo muji lɛ kɛbaa lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their flowers before any young pods form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛnáa ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience stress from prolonged dry spells, extreme heat, pest attack, or a lack of key nutrients like phosphorus during the flowering stage.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛɔ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ amɛmli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ he.

english: Why is my cassava growing plenty of bushy leaves above the ground but only small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ yɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen fertilizer, it focuses its energy on growing heavy stems and leaves instead of storing food in the root tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ baaha ŋmeii kɛ baai ni tsii ni miida lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and soft before the fruit can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot draw enough calcium from the soil, often due to irregular watering during fruit formation.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over during windstorms even when the roots look intact?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbee shi yɛ ahum ko mli eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ ehiɛɛɛ shi moŋ?

english: Tiny soil pests like nematodes or banana weevils eat away at the inside of the plantain root system, weakening the anchor of the plant until the weight of the bunch causes it to topple.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes loo banana ŋmeii yeɔ plantain shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ gbɔjɔɔ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋta lɛ tsiimɔ haa egbeeɔ shi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from the leaves, or by a viral infection spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb tall stakes to produce big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ koni ekɛ bulbs agboi aba lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to manufacture food, which travels down to swell the underground tuber; unstaked vines get shaded and stay smaller.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii. ni baatsi kɛya shi ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ Wein tsei ni ehiɛɛɛ shi lɛ baafee shade ni amɛbaafee bibii.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete intensely for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients, causing all of them to remain weak and undersized.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ shwɛɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛfeɔ bibii tsɔ.

english: Why do my crop roots rot when heavy rain sits on the farm for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Crop roots require air in the soil to breathe; when water stays on the surface for too long, it pushes air out of the soil and suffocates the roots.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields every season if I keep planting maize on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa be mli kɛji mitee nɔ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the exact same crop repeatedly drains the specific soil nutrients that crop needs and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil year after year.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa tsei lɛ aba shi. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: When lower leaves turn yellow, it usually means your maize is starving for nitrogen. Nitrogen is the nutrient plants use to stay green and grow strong, so when there isn't enough in the soil, the plant moves what little it has to its newer top leaves.
ga: Kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ faaa lɛ Tso lɛ baajie nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I plant my maize seeds very close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa kome mli?

english: Planted too closely, the seedlings will fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of getting many big ears of corn, you will end up with tall, thin stalks that produce very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ ŋmãa toi wuji babaoo najiaŋ lɛ, obaagbe naa kɛ ŋmãa ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni woɔ ŋmãa toi bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Weeds have strong roots that quickly steal food and fertilizer from the soil before your crops can reach them. Even with rainfall, your crops will stay hungry because the weeds are consuming all the available nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni baanyɛ aju niyenii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya dani ŋmɔshi nibii ashɛ amɛhe. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ lolo ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce broad leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture cocoa trees need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Enɛ haa kookoo tsei lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cut off the extra small shoots growing at the base of my plantain suckers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Nɔ krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ.

english: Extra shoots act like extra mouths competing for food. Pruning away the excess suckers ensures that all the nutrients and water from the soil go directly to the main mother plant so it can produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tsoi krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ daaŋ krokomɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii he akaŋ. Kɛ́ afo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yaa tso titri lɛ nɔ koni ekɛfee niji agboi ni tsii.

english: Why do my cassava leaves fold up and droop during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves fold up in severe afternoon heat to slow down water loss through their leaves. It is the plant's natural shield to survive heat stress, and the leaves will open up again once the air cools down.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli koni nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Tsei ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ mli. Ni baai lɛ gbeleɔ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when rainfall is irregular. When stressed by heat or lack of water, the plant drops its blossoms to save its energy rather than trying to develop fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ loo nu ni faaa lɛ miihao lɛ Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni owo yibii lɛ

english: Why do my yam tubers grow short and twisted instead of growing long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji kukuji ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eja lɛ?

english: Yam tubers twist when the soil underground is hard, compact, or filled with stones. As the tuber tries to expand downwards, it hits these hard barriers and is forced to bend and grow around them.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli wa, ebɔle ehe, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ. Beni yitso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni egbɛ eshwa shi lɛ Ekɛ gbɛtsii nii ni wa nɛɛ baakpe. ni anyɛɔ enɔ koni ekoto ni eda yɛ nakai gbɛtsii nii lɛ ahe

english: Why do armyworms suddenly appear in huge numbers right after the early rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cutworms lɛ jeɔ kpo trukaa babaoo beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Warm temperatures following early rain create moisture conditions that trigger armyworm eggs laid in the soil or leaves to hatch all at once. The young caterpillars immediately feed on the tender new leaves produced by the rain.
ga: He ni hulutsoo baa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni haa helminth ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ loo baai lɛ amli lɛ fɛɛ shwereɔ shikome lɛ baa. Amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ŋmeii bibii baaye baai heei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nugbɔ lɛ ebɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings wither and die immediately after I transplant them into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu amɛ yɛ saatso wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Moving plants causes root shock because delicate feeder roots break and dry out under strong sunshine. Transplanting late in the afternoon or on cloudy days gives the roots a cool night to settle into the new soil without drying out.
ga: Tsei ni tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi be mli ni shishifãi ni haa niyenii lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ mli gbalaa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ adu lɛ shwane mli loo yɛ gbi ni atatu yɔɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná gbɛkɛ ni mli ejɔ koni amɛhi shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: How much water do my cocoa trees actually need to grow healthy pods?
ga: Nu enyiɛ he hiaa mi-cacao tso lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need regular, moderate rainfall throughout the year to thrive. Too little water causes the leaves to wither and pods to dry up, while too much water can rot the roots.
ga: Cocoa tsei biɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be ni eshɛɔ he ni sa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ koni amɛshwere. Nu fioo pɛ baaha baai lɛ agbo ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi. yɛ be mli ni nu babaoo baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers fall off without forming pods during a long dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When water is scarce, plants get stressed and drop their flowers to conserve energy and moisture to survive, which prevents pods from forming.
ga: Kɛ nu faaa Tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he koni amɛhi shi. Enɛ haaa pods afee.

english: Why do cocoa pods stay small and fail to develop when rain is delayed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi bibii ni amɛshwereee kɛji nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ?

english: Developing cocoa pods rely on a steady water supply to transport soil nutrients into the fruit. Without enough water, pod growth slows down or stops completely.
ga: Cocoa pod lɛ shweremɔ damɔ nu ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya aduawai lɛ amli. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, Pod lɛ dalɛ baa shi loo ekpaa kwraa.

english: Is it bad for rain water to collect and sit on my farm field after heavy downpours?
ga: Ani nugbɔ nu baabua ehe naa ni ebaata miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: Yes, standing water drowns crop roots by preventing them from breathing oxygen, and it encourages fungal diseases like black pod disease in cocoa.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni damɔ shi lɛ haa tsei shishifãi shwieɔ nu mli kɛtsɔ amɛtsimɔ ni ehaaa amɛmu kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela ni yɔɔ kookoo mli lɛ baa.

english: How can I easily tell if my field's soil has enough water for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Squeeze a handful of soil taken from a few inches below the surface; if it holds together in a soft ball without dripping wet water, the soil moisture is just right.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ fioo ko ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋwɛi ŋta fioo komɛi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ akɛto he kome ni efee bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni nu efɔɔɔ shi lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ sa.

english: Should I manually water my young crop seedlings if the rain stops for two weeks?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ miniji awo dumɔwui bibii lɛ amli nu kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ otsii enyɔ?

english: Yes, young crops have shallow roots that dry out very quickly, so giving them water during sudden dry spells keeps them alive until regular rains return.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya waa. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni awoɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ trukaa lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn brown and drop off when the weather gets hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed leaves in extreme heat to reduce moisture loss through their foliage as a survival mechanism against drought.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni ekɛba nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ shi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe yɛ hɔmɔ mli.

english: How do shade trees help keep my crop farm moist when rain is scarce?
ga: Te tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni mi tsei aŋmɔ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Shade trees block direct hot sunlight, lower field temperatures, and stop the soil from drying out too fast through evaporation.
ga: Tsei haa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he hulutsoo. Ha ŋmɔ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ aba shi ni etsĩ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya tsɔ kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: What is the best way to clearly mark the boundary between my farm and neighboring land?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akadiɔ husu ni ka miŋmɔ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ teŋ lɛ faŋŋ?

english: Planting permanent boundary trees or border plants like Gliricidia creates a visible border without competing heavily for nutrients with your main crop.
ga: Husu ni hiɔ shi daa loo husu tsei, tamɔ glicidia ni aduɔ lɛ haa anaa husu. Ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ohe awo niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo ni jɛ otsei titrii lɛ amli lɛ he akaŋ.

english: Can I safely plant permanent cocoa trees right next to government forest reserve land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo tsei ni baahi shi daa yɛ nɔyeli lɛ kooi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahe shweshweeshwe?

english: Yes, as long as you stay strictly on your side of the boundary line and avoid clearing protected forest trees, though keeping a small border gap is advisable.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ obaahi husu lɛ masɛi pɛpɛɛpɛ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni ajieɔ yɛ kooi ni abuɔ he lɛ amli lɛ ahe. Eyɛ mli akɛ eji ŋaawoo akɛ aaakwɛ husu lɛ teŋ fioo moŋ.

english: Why does my rice crop turn yellow and stop growing when the water level in the field drops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ba shi lɛ?

english: Rice plants need steady soil moisture to draw up essential plant food like nitrogen from the ground. When the soil dries out, the roots cannot collect nutrients, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow and the plant's growth to stall.
ga: Omɔ tsei taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛgbala tso mli niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ, shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ato niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tsei lɛ adalɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: How do I know my rice grains are mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Rice is ready to harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grains turn from green to a firm golden-yellow color. Harvesting too early yields soft, chalky grains that break easily, while waiting too long causes mature grains to fall off onto the ground.
ga: Omɔ lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛ́ ŋmãa lɛ mli aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli mli kɛtee ŋmãa ni mli wa ni tamɔ shika tsuru mli. Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni fiteɔ oya lɛ baa. Kɛ́ mɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui ni edara lɛ agbee shikpɔŋ.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller crop yields every year when I plant on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the earth every season to grow. If you plant the same crop on the same piece of land year after year without adding compost, manure, or rotating with crops like beans, the soil runs out of food and cannot support good yields.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii tsakeee lɛ, Hɔmɔ baaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai anɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants curl up tightly into tubes during the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during the hottest hours of the day as a natural protective response to reduce water loss. By rolling their leaves, the plant protects itself from drying out in direct sunlight, and the leaves usually open back up when the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ tsiɔ ehe naa koni ekagbi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Ni baai lɛ fɔɔ gbelemɔ be mli ni gbɛkɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when there is continuous rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Excess water from heavy rainfall fills up all the air pockets in the soil, suffocating the roots. Without air, the roots weaken and fungal rot organisms in the wet soil easily enter and destroy the cassava tubers.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni jɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baafite ŋmei shishifãi lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off without turning into actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when exposed to extreme afternoon heat, drought stress, or a lack of plant food in the soil. When the plant feels under stress, it drops its flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛje la ni naa wa mli yɛ shwane mli. hɔmɔ haomɔ loo niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei amli ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Beni tso lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaashi fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and stronger than my crops right after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that absorb nutrients and water much faster than young crop plants. If you do not clear the weeds before applying fertilizer, the weeds will eat most of the plant food and crowd out your crop.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ niyenii kɛ nu oya fe tsei bibii. Kɛji ojieee jwɛi lɛ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ yeɔ tsei amli nibii titri ni amɛfiteɔ onibii.

english: Why do my harvested grains develop holes and turn to powder after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ yɛ bu ni amɛtsɔɔ powda yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni akɛto lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Storage insects like weevils hatch from tiny, hidden eggs laid on the crop before or during harvest. If the grain is stored while still slightly damp, these pests multiply rapidly inside the bag and eat the insides of the seeds.
ga: Kplukai ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe tamɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii bibii amli. ni akɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani loo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli Kɛji obua dumɔwui lɛ anaa yɛ be mli ni amɛmli edɔ fioo lolo lɛ, Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kotoku lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to sprout out of the dirt after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are buried too deep in the soil, if the soil is packed too hard for the young shoots to break through, or if the soil is completely dry. Seeds need moisture, light warmth, and air near the surface to wake up and grow.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ŋmeii bibii nyɛŋ atsɔ mli, Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Dumɔwui lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ. la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ koni ekɛte shi ni edara.

english: Why do crops planted under big foliage trees grow tall and thin with very few leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei ni baai wuji yɔɔ mli lɛ ashishi lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo, ni amɛbaai fioo pɛ amɛyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to produce energy and grow strong stems. When shaded by big trees, the crop stretches excessively upward to search for light, resulting in a tall, weak, and thin stem with low produce.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛha amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ. Beni yɔɔ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baagbɛ ashwã ŋwɛi tsɔ koni eyatao la. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa, amɛhe tseee, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their tender leaves from direct sunshine and scorching winds. Keeping large shade trees creates a cooler microclimate and preserves soil moisture, allowing cocoa seedlings to establish safely.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Tsei wuji ni akɛhaa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmaa shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with tall sticks instead of letting them spread across the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ niji ni kɛlɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to manufacture the energy required to grow large underground tubers. Staking lifts leaves toward the sun and keeps them off hot soil where they could rot or catch diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛná shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he ni ehaaa sũ lɛ mli adɔ, he ni ebaanyɛ egbo loo hela aba lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually signal a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is the essential nutrient plants use to stay green and grow leaves, so adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni amɛha tsei ahe tsei lɛ akwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my plot before planting maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen from the air and stores it in the soil through their roots. Planting them first naturally enriches the soil, reducing the need for expensive chemical fertilizers for your next maize crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ mra lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa atsu nii kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Does it really matter which direction I point my cassava stem cuttings when inserting them into the soil?
ga: Ani gbɛ ni ŋmei ni afolɔ lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ he hiaa?

english: Yes, planting cassava stems upside down forces the buds to grow downward before curving upward. This wastes the plant's initial energy, weakens root establishment, and reduces the total harvest yield.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei ni akwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛya shi dani amɛba ŋwɛi. Enɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ shishijee hewalɛ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ fɛɛ baa shi

english: Why should I cut away extra suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra suckers steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from the main mother plant. Pruning away weaker suckers ensures the main plantain receives full nutrition to produce heavy, healthy fruit bunches.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa plantains titrii lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii ni tsii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves inside the center of my maize plants full of ragged holes and small green droppings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ eyi kɛ buji ni etse kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central funnel of the maize plant to feed on young leaves. Applying recommended neem-based sprays or bio-pesticides early directly into the funnel stops them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Akɛ tsofai ni akɛ neem fee loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii mra. Kɛbote cone lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaakpa nibii nɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when extreme heat stresses the plant or when soil moisture fluctuates rapidly between dry and wet. Mulching and maintaining steady watering routines keep root temperatures stable so flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ha tsei lɛ miihao. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ teŋ lɛ. Mulching kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ baaha shishifã lɛ mli latsaa lɛ aya nɔ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ yibii.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) shades the ground from direct sun, preventing soil water from evaporating quickly. It keeps plant roots cool, saves water, and blocks weed seeds from receiving light to germinate.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya. Ehaa tsei ashishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehaa nu hiɔ shi, ni ehaaa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ akabote la mli koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why does removing weeds early in the growing season make such a big difference to my final harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli mra lɛ haa minaagbee ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ feɔ srɔto kwraa nɛkɛ?

english: Weeds grow rapidly and aggressively absorb soil nutrients, water, and sunlight that your young crops need to establish. Clearing weeds early eliminates this competition when your crops are most vulnerable.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ejieɔ akaŋshii nɛɛ kɛyaa be mli ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ oshara mli fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight and can easily dry out or burn. Plantains grow very quickly and provide broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, sheltering young cocoa plants from intense sun and heat during their first two years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. ni ebaanyɛ egbi loo eshã oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves in maize is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and grow strong; when the soil lacks enough nitrogen, the plant moves what little it has to the newest growth at the top, leaving the older lower leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa shweremɔ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ nɔ. Ha ni shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: What benefit do I get if I mix animal dung or chicken manure into my farm soil before planting?
ga: Mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔi maná kɛji mikɛ kooloi loo tsina ŋmeii futu shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli dani midu?

english: Animal manure acts as a natural food for your soil. It slowly releases essential plant nutrients, improves the soil's ability to hold onto water during dry stretches, and encourages beneficial earthworms and microbes that keep soil healthy.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ, ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ fiofio. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me not to plant corn on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ kɛɔ mɛi akɛ amɛkadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating crops breaks pest cycles and gives the soil time to recover.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ fiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe.

english: Why are small green caterpillars chewing holes into the center of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye bu yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on the soft inner leaves (the 'whorl') of young maize. Left untreated, they ruin the plant's ability to grow properly and form healthy ears of corn.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii amli baai ("rings") lɛ. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ, ebaafite nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo ŋmãa toi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before producing any actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shi dani ewoɔ pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Flower drop in pepper plants often happens due to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of specific nutrients like calcium and boron. When the plant feels stressed, it drops its flowers to save energy for survival.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa yɛ dɔlɛ haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli daa loo niyenii pɔtɛɛ tamɔ calcium kɛ boron ni bɛ. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛhi shi lɛ ato.

english: This sudden wilting is often caused by bacterial wilt or root rot. Soil-borne bacteria or fungus attack the stem base and roots, blocking the tubes that carry water up into the plant, causing it to dry out even if water is in the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ baa. Muawai loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ tutuaa tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ. Kɛtsɔ paipi ni kɛ nu yaa ŋwɛi lɛ ni etsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava is ready to be harvested without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni atsaaa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Cassava is usually ready around 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You can tell it is maturing when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil right around the base of the stem begins to crack as tubers swell underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, ni enɛ damɔ ŋmei lɛ henɔ lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baa ko edara kɛ́ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to start sowing my seeds when the rainy season begins?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ miibɛŋkɛ lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the rain has fallen consistently two or three times and soaked deep into the ground. Sowing after just the very first light rain can cause seeds to germinate and then die if a dry week follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ nɛ be fɛɛ be shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo sɛɛ Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji hɔmɔ otsii babaoo nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why is it harmful to allow tall weeds to grow around my crops before I start weeding?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ashi jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abɔle he? No hewɔ lɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii ni midu dani mibɔi jwɛi shwiemɔ lɛ yɛ oshara mli.

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. If you wait until weeds grow tall, they have already taken vital resources away from your young plants and their roots may damage crop roots when pulled out.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji omɛ kɛyashi jwɛi lɛ shwere Amɛjie nibii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ afite tsei ashishifãi kɛji ajie amɛ.

english: Why do my maize crops yield less every year when I keep planting seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi beni miyaa nɔ miduɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Over time, seeds saved season after season lose their natural strength and vigor through genetic degradation and accumulated diseases. Buying fresh certified seeds restores strong growth and high yields.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ yɛ fɔmɔ nii ni fiteɔ kɛ helai ni ebua amɛhe naa lɛ hewɔ. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ baaha dalɛ ni mli wa kɛ sɛɛnamɔi babaoo aba.

english: What does it mean when an extension officer says a crop variety has lost its vigor?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛ́ sɛɛgbɛtsɔɔmɔ he nitsulɔ ko kɛɛ tso henɔ ko bɛ hewalɛ dɔŋŋ?

english: Loss of vigor means the plant variety has become naturally weaker over time, resulting in slower growth, weaker stalks, less resistance to weather or pests, and smaller overall harvests.
ga: Hewalɛ ni baa shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei srɔtoi lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa edaa blɛoo, tsei lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi loo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛye amɛhe. ni kpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ faaa.

english: How do I know the correct quantity of corn seeds I need to buy for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmãa yibɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ mahe kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: The required seed quantity depends on your farm size and recommended plant spacing; using the correct seed rate ensures plants have enough room, nutrients, and sunlight to reach maximum yield without overcrowding.
ga: Dumɔwui abɔ ni he hiaa lɛ damɔ oŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ akwɛ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ayibɔ ni ja ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa he ko, niyenii, kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná yibiiwoo babaoo ni amɛhiɛɛɛ amɛhe tsɔ.

english: What happens to my corn crops if I plant too many seeds in one place?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome?

english: Planting too many seeds forces the crops to compete aggressively with each other for nutrients, water, and sunlight, leading to thin, weak plants with small or empty cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛye niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni dumɔwui bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: How many bags of corn can I expect to harvest if I plant high-quality certified seeds?
ga: Abɛi kotokui enyiɛ manyɛ makpa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odase akɛ amɛdu?

english: Yield depends on management and soil, but using fresh, high-vigor certified corn seeds under good farming practices typically yields around 25 to 35 bags per hectare.
ga: Nibii ni anáa lɛ damɔ bɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ ahaa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui heei ni atsɔɔ akɛ amɛhe wa waa yɛ okwaayeli nifeemɔi kpakpai ashishi lɛ tsuɔ nii. Bei pii lɛ, ewoɔ aaafee kotokui 25 kɛyashi 35 yɛ hectare kome mli.

english: Why should I buy new improved seeds instead of using the local seeds my family has used for generations?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe jogbaŋŋ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni miweku lɛ kɛtsu nii kɛjɛ yinɔi babaoo nɛ lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Traditional seeds lose vigor over decades, while newly developed crop varieties are bred by researchers to grow faster, resist pests and drought better, and produce much higher yields.
ga: Kusum dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, niiamlitaolɔi efɔ tsei srɔtoi heei ni afee lɛ koni amɛdara oya. Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni teɔ shi ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ hɔmɔ. ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo babaoo

english: How often am I supposed to buy fresh seeds for my corn field instead of saving my harvest?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui hee kɛha mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ato?

english: It is best to buy fresh certified seed every season, especially for hybrid corn, because second-generation saved seeds lose their hybrid vigor and produce much smaller yields.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa be. Titri lɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa Enɛ ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ laajeɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmãa lɛ hewalɛ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo kwraa.

english: Why do agricultural researchers keep releasing new varieties of the same crop every few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi jieɔ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kpo daa afii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Researchers develop new varieties because existing varieties naturally decline in strength and disease resistance over time, requiring updated breeds to maintain food production targets.
ga: Nibii amlitaolɔi feɔ tsofai srɔtoi heei Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsofai srɔtoi ni baa adebɔɔ mli lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ helai ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa ehe hiaa ni afɔ bii koni akɛhiɛ niyenii feemɔ he otii lɛ amli.

english: Why are my corn plants growing very thin and weak even though the rain is good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ yɛ nugbɔ kpakpa ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weak growth despite good rain often happens when you plant low-vigor seeds, plant seeds too close together, or use old seed stocks that lack the strength for robust growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dalɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ baa kɛji odu dumɔwui kɛ hewalɛ fioo. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Aloo akɛ dumɔwui momo ni bɛ dalɛ hewalɛ ni mli wa atsu nii.

english: How do I choose the best corn seed variety to make sure I hit my target harvest this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmãa dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ koni mana nɔmimaa akɛ maná yibiiwoo yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Select certified, high-vigor varieties recommended by extension officers for your specific zone, paying attention to maturity period, disease resistance, and potential yield output.
ga: Halamɔ henɔi ni yɔɔ odaseyeli, ni wa waa ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ jieɔ yi kɛha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ asusu dalɛ be lɛ he Helai ahe shiwoo kɛ nɔ ni baanyɛ ajɛ mli aba lɛ

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and drying up in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn under direct sunshine. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them acts as a temporary umbrella, protecting the seedlings from heat while keeping moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ be kukuoo mli shade. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high above the ground to catch as much direct sunlight as possible. When the leaves get sufficient sun, they manufacture more energy to send underground, resulting in bigger and heavier yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ aba mli bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa Ebaajie hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛbaatsu shikpɔŋ shishi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ agboi ni amɛtsiii.

english: Why am I seeing small holes in my young maize leaves and caterpillars hidden in the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛtee baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest that eats young corn leaves. Applying recommended botanical treatments like neem extract or safe insecticides into the central leaf whorl early in the morning kills the caterpillars before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Kɛ akɛ tsofai ni ajieɔ yi akɛ afee tamɔ neem mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ awo baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli leebi koni akɛgbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning soft and black before they can turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ediŋŋ dani etsɔɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by uneven watering which stops the plant from absorbing calcium from the soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist rather than letting it dry out completely between waterings prevents this problem.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. ni jɛɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be mli baa Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ moŋ fe ni oooha egbi kwraa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why does my harvested maize get full of small insects and flour-like dust inside the storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma ni mikpaa lɛ eyi kɛ kooloi bibii kɛ sũ ni tamɔ ashikishaŋ yɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotokui lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Grain weevils attack maize when it is stored with too much moisture. Drying your maize thoroughly until the grains are hard and using airtight hermetic storage bags suffocates pests and keeps the grain clean for months without chemicals.
ga: Grain weevils lɛ tutuaa ŋmãa kɛji ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo mli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa ni akɛ kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ he atse nyɔji babaoo ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce big leafy bushes above ground but very tiny roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ jwɛi wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to focus all its energy on growing top leaves instead of expanding its underground roots. Adding potassium to the soil and avoiding excessive chemical nitrogen helps the plant feed its roots instead.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ adalɛ he nii moŋ fe ni eeeha eshishifãi lɛ aya shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ potassium wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ajie tsofa ni ji nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei ni amɛná niyenii kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli moŋ.

english: Why do people recommend that I plant groundnuts or beans on the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have tiny nodes on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil. When planted with or before maize, they act as natural fertilizer, reducing your need for expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ nodes bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa loo dani adu lɛ Ebaatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he hiamɔ baa shi.

english: Why do some farmers cover the bare soil around their crops with dry leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi haa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle amɛŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This practice is called mulching. Covering the soil acts like a blanket that traps moisture, lowers soil temperature during hot days, stops weeds from sprouting, and eventually rots to enrich the soil with organic matter.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Mulching tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket ni mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ aba shi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni naagbee lɛ amɛfite koni ekɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: It is best to wait until the soil receives steady, soaking rains for about two consecutive weeks. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die if a dry spell immediately follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be, ni ehaa nugbɔ nɛɔ aaafee otsii enyɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Mɔdɛŋbɔɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwu lɛ akwɛ̃ ni egbo kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko nyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when I leave weeds growing around their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛ́ mishi jwɛi yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Weeds act as thieves in your farm because their fast-growing roots steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Removing weeds early allows your crops to consume all available food and grow rapidly.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi ni daa oya lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛye niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ ni amɛdara oya.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide large leaves that shade young cocoa seedlings, protecting them from sun heat and keeping moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni haa kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ mli waa

english: This is Black Pod Disease, caused by a fungus that spreads in wet and cool conditions. Pruning excess branches lets air and sunlight reach the trees, which keeps the farm dry and prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni efɔ, ni mli ejɔ kɛbaa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ he. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Yellowing leaves at the bottom of a maize plant mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential plant food. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK helps the leaves turn green again and restores crop growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo NPK tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni eha tsei lɛ adara ekoŋŋ.

english: Maize takes nitrogen out of the soil, but legumes like groundnuts and beans put natural nitrogen back into the dirt through their roots. Rotating these crops keeps your soil fertile without spending too much money on chemicals.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nibii nɛɛ ni oootsake lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛ tsofai babaoo tsuuu nii.

english: Why do I have to construct large soil mounds before planting yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ama gɔŋ agbo dani adu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yams grow deep underground and require loose, soft soil to expand properly. Soil mounds collect loose topsoil, protect tubers from waterlogging, and make it easier for yams to grow big without hitting hard ground.
ga: Sweet potatoes kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ. Gɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛbuaa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni etse ehe lɛ naa. Buu yitso lɛ he kɛjɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ he. Ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ŋmeii lɛ baadara ni amɛtswaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa.

english: How can I tell that my cassava crops are matured and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting when the lower leaves dry up and drop off, and the soil around the bottom of the main stem begins to crack open from expanding tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ yitso ni mli elɛɛɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and becoming small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato leaf curl is usually caused by viruses spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies, or by extreme heat stress. Keeping your farm free of weeds and spraying organic remedies like neem leaf extract helps control whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni koolooi bibii eyɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly loo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa Oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni jwɛi akafee nɔ ko kɛ tsofai ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli tamɔ neem tso lɛ mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ whiteflies nɔ

english: Why do my crops wilt when I water them in the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Watering under strong midday sun causes hot water evaporation and can shock the plant leaves. It is best to water early in the morning or late in the evening so the soil stays moist and the roots absorb the water properly.
ga: Nu ni oooha yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ shishi lɛ baaha nu ni mli edɔ lɛ atsɔ la, ni ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ baai lɛ akpokpo. Esa akɛ afee nu lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do hybrid seeds bought from the agro-dealer produce more yield than seeds I save from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially developed by crop scientists to produce high yields and resist diseases in their first generation. Saved seeds lose those parent qualities and yield less when replanted in following seasons.
ga: Nibii ahe nilelɔi efee dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛha yibii babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ laajeɔ amɛfɔlɔ tso lɛ mli nibii lɛ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: How does covering my soil with dry leaves and palm fronds help my crops grow?
ga: Te baai ni egbi kɛ tsei ahe tsei ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdaraa ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: This practice is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, prevents moisture from drying out during hot days, stops weeds from growing, and decays into nutrient-rich soil over time.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekagbi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What is a pre-nursery, and why shouldn't I just plant my seeds directly into the main farm?
ga: Mɛni ji gbekɛbii askul ni tsɔ hiɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: A pre-nursery is a small, protected area where delicate seeds are planted first to sprout safely away from severe heat, heavy rains, and pests. Starting seeds in a pre-nursery gives them the best environment to grow strong roots before moving them, leading to much higher survival rates than planting straight into the main field.
ga: Pre-nursery ji he bibioo ko ni abuɔ he ni aduɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo klɛŋklɛŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe. Dumɔwui ni ajeɔ shishi yɛ dani akwɛɔ amɛ lɛ baaha amɛná shihilɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ shishifãi ni wa dani adu amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, yiwalaheremɔ fa babaoo fe dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know when my young seedlings are ready to be moved from the nursery into my main field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Seedlings are generally ready for transplanting when they have developed 3 to 4 strong, dark green leaves and a thick, sturdy stem. Moving them at this stage ensures their roots are well-formed enough to handle the stress of being transplanted without dying.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji amɛyɛ baai 3 kɛyashi 4 ni wa, ni ji eŋɔli kɛ tso ni mli wa ni mli wa. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛnyɛ amɛtsu haomɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ mli baa lɛ he nii ni amɛgbooo.

english: How can I tell if the seeds I bought are good quality and will sprout well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Good quality seeds are usually uniform in size, feel heavy for their size, clean, and free from cracks or insect holes. Sourcing certified seeds from trusted extension officers guarantees high sprouting success and healthy crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ dalɛ tamɔ amɛhe. Enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ tsii yɛ bɔ ni edara ha lɛ hewɔ, ehe tse ni ebɛ ŋmeii loo kooloi amli ŋmeii. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ mɛi ni heɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ haa tsei lɛ yeɔ omanye waa ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my young seedlings wither and die shortly after I transplant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Seedlings often die after transplanting due to 'transplant shock,' which happens when their tender roots are damaged or exposed to sudden harsh sunlight and dry soil. Transplanting on a cloudy day or late in the afternoon, watering immediately, and providing shade helps prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui gboiɔ yɛ be mli ni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kroko nɔ lɛ hewɔ yɛ ‘Transplant shock’ ni baa kɛji shishifãi bibii lɛ fite loo hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ trukaa lɛ hewɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ gbi ni atatu yɔɔ nɔ loo shwane mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli oya kɛ hulutsoo yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need plantains growing right next to them when they are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ yɛ plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ? Beni tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo lɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very sensitive leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing plantains alongside them provides natural shade and preserves soil moisture, protecting the young cocoa trees during their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu nɛkɛ dumɔwui ni daa oya nɛɛ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Is it better for me to water my young seedlings lightly every day or soak them heavily once a week?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ nu fioo daa gbi loo mawo amɛ nu ni mli wa? Shikome yɛ otsi mli?

english: Light, regular watering every day or two is much better because it keeps the topsoil consistently moist without drowning the roots. Soaking the soil heavily all at once can rot delicate young roots and wash away essential nutrients.
ga: Nu daa gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ baafee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieee nu mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ nu mli waa yɛ be kome mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbo ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds and prepare the soil weeks before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ ni masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ otsii komɛi dani madu nii lɛ?

english: Preparing the land early eliminates aggressive weeds that steal nutrients, sunlight, and water from young plants. Loosening the soil early also allows rainwater to sink in and helps young plant roots spread easily once planted.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ mra Egbeɔ jwɛi ni baa shi ni juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, hulu la, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ oya lɛ hu haa nugbɔ nu lɛ boteɔ mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya kɛji adu amɛ pɛ.

english: What will happen if I plant my crops very close to each other to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food, resulting in thin, weak stems and small harvests. Proper spacing allows every single plant to get enough resources to produce a maximum yield.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛshiɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsu nii babaoo lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I cut off yellow leaves or weak extra branches from my growing plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei ni miida lɛ ahe baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo tsei niji bibii ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Removing yellowing or diseased leaves prevents crop illnesses from spreading to healthy parts and stops the plant from wasting energy on dying foliage. This allows the crop to direct all its food toward growing strong stems and heavy fruits.
ga: Baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haaa tso helai agbɛ ashwã hei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ni ehaaa tso lɛ afite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni miigboi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa kɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do long-term tree crops like cocoa or oil palm take several years before they start giving me fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ kookoo loo mu tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ebɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Tree crops spend their first few years building deep root systems and sturdy trunks capable of supporting heavy harvests later in life. Good care and feeding during these early years build the foundation for the tree to produce abundant fruit for 20 to 25 years.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ maa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ni wa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmaakpamɔ ni tsii sɛɛ mli lɛ. Kwɛmɔ kpakpa kɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli Enɛɛmɛi baafee shishitoo ni tso lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo yɛ nɔ afii 20 kɛyashi 25.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in an open field without big trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because their tender leaves burn easily under full sunlight. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains next to young cocoa provides living shelter and holds soil moisture to help them survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tsei ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Cocoa tsei haa amɛnáa he ko ni amɛhiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together in the same farm land at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ be kome mli yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, planting maize and cassava together works well. Maize grows fast and is harvested in about three to four months, while cassava grows slowly at first and takes over the field after the maize is harvested.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji 3-4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni eŋɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ beni akpa abɛi lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yellowing in a V-shape on lower maize leaves usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, which is a major food crops need to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ tamɔ V ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii titrii ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ he.

english: How can I easily tell if my soil is too tired to give me a good harvest this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ egbɔjɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ewo ŋmaa kpakpa yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Tired soil often feels hard and dry, stays pale in color, and grows crops with thin stems, small pale leaves, and poor yields compared to previous years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni etɔ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ ewa ni egbi, ehiɛ su tsakeɔ, ni tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii, baai bibii ni mli tse, ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto afii ni eho lɛ ahe.

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension officers is the best way to stop it.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akpaa.

english: Rainy weather creates damp conditions that spread the fungus causing Black Pod disease. Pruning extra branches to let sunlight and air into the canopy helps keep pods dry and reduces rot.
