ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni egbɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ eshwaa. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote tso lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ baa shi.

english: What causes tiny holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars hidden in the leaves at the top?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni Akɛtee ŋwɛi baai lɛ amli lɛ anɔ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed on tender young leaves. Spraying early in the morning or late evening when caterpillars are active helps control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ji bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ amɛnɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on instead of just trailing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooonyiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves off the ground and capture as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which travels down to grow large tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ko ni baaha amɛwo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni fã gbɛ kɛba shi koni eyadu ŋmeii wuji

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before any peppers can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ baanyɛ ada lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or irregular watering. Mulching the soil around the plants helps keep the soil moist and cool, which stops flower drop.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ Tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why do my tomatoes turn black and soft at the bottom while they are still ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ lolo lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes are usually caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium due to uneven watering. Keeping soil moisture steady prevents this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to plant shade trees or plantains near my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains yɛ mi kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that easily dry out and burn in direct sunlight. Shade trees and plantains create a cooler microclimate and protect the soil from losing moisture, allowing cocoa seedlings to establish strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei kɛ dumɔwui ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo baa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ waa, ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni wa.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the plant usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore green growth.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ lɛ fɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it risky to plant my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the major season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni he hiaa yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry spell that can dry out and kill newly germinated seeds. Waiting for steady, regular rain ensures the soil maintains enough moisture for the seedlings to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ ni baanyɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa, ni baa daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava stems too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmeii tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need space underground to expand into large tubers. When planted too close together, the plants compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in small, thin roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe tseee.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to manufacture food for the tubers underground. Staking keeps leaves off the hot ground, prevents leaf diseases, and helps the plant produce larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni ekahi hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. Tsi baa helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ sweet potatoes wuji

english: Tomato flowers often drop off due to extreme heat, erratic watering, or lack of pollination. Keeping soil consistently moist and providing windbreaks can help flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo pollination ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ ni etsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips, or viruses spread by these insects. Controlling pests early with approved sprays or neem oil prevents leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Early Pest Control kɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo neem fɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akafite baa lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to plant maize on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating crops breaks disease cycles and keeps soil fertile.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ lɛ fiteɔ helai ni baa lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How does planting groundnuts make my soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. After harvest, this leaves natural fertilizer in the ground for the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. kpamɔ sɛɛ Abaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Why do weeds reduce the amount of harvest I get at the end of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa ŋmaa ni minine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your plants. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to give a yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen. Applying fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the soil the strength it needs to feed your plants so they can turn green and grow big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ekɛye ebua otsei lɛ. Bɔni afee ni amɛtsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: How does using chemical fertilizer or crop medicine help my farm when the soil is weak?
ga: Te tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli loo tsei ahe tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizers act like nutrient-rich food for tired soil. Applying the right amount at the correct time restores missing minerals, helping your crops grow strong and give good yields even when soil conditions are difficult.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ ni etɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ shika ni sa tsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shika tsuru ni elaaje lɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Ye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa po nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct, hot sunlight. Planting fast-growing plantains alongside them creates broad leafy umbrellas that provide the cool shade and moisture cocoa trees need to survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu nɛkɛ dumɔwui ni daa oya nɛɛ yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli kwɔ ni haa kookoo tsei lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ baa.

english: How do I stop armyworm caterpillars from chewing the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anaa?

english: Fall armyworms attack the growing center of maize plants. Checking your farm early and applying recommended protection sprays or dropping clean wood ash into the leaf funnels will destroy the worms before they ruin your farm.
ga: Fall cutworm lɛ tutuaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ he lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii loo tso sũ ni he tse ni okɛshwieɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baafite ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it better to plant my seeds in neat rows instead of scattering them across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ dumɔwui lɛ oshwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting in measured rows gives each plant enough space to get sunlight, water, and food from the ground without fighting its neighbors. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Tso ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ ená hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ awuu. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow smaller every year when I plant them on the same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ feɔ bibii daa afi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams take a lot of food out of the ground to grow big tubers. Planted on the same spot repeatedly, they exhaust the soil nutrients; rotating with beans or letting the land rest allows the soil to rebuild its power.
ga: Sweet potatoes kɛ niyenii babaoo baa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa bulbs agboi kwɛ̃ɔ. Aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ. Ebaafite niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tsake loo aha shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa ehewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops dry up so fast even when it rained just a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses moisture quickly to the hot sun. Covering the ground around your crop roots with dry grass or leaves (mulching) acts like a blanket that traps rainwater in the dirt for much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ enɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulching) ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli, ni ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Should I plant my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year falls?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Planting right after the first rain can be risky because early rains often stop for weeks. It is safer to wait until the rain becomes steady so your newly germinated seeds do not dry up and die in the hot dirt.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee oshara ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ kpaa otsii babaoo. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa koni dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies. Using healthy, disease-resistant cassava stems for planting stops the sickness from spreading across your farm.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsu nii kɛdu lɛ, ebaaha hela akagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my harvested maize cobs get ruined by small insects and rot inside my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miifite mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ni amɛmiifite yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Wet or damp maize attracts destructive insects and mold. Sun-drying your maize until the grains are completely hard before storing them keeps them safe and edible for many months.
ga: Abɛi ni efɔ loo edɔ lɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa kwraa dani akɛto lɛ, ehaa ehiɔ shi shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why do my crops wilt and turn yellow when floodwater stays on my farm for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nu afua lɛ hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crop roots need to breathe air in the soil just like humans need air to breathe. When excess water covers the field for too long, it blocks air from reaching the roots, causing the plants to drown, turn yellow, and rot.
ga: Esa akɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ amu kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Taakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa adesai koni amɛmu lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ nu ni fa fe nine ha ŋmɔji anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ baatsi enaa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji tso lɛ ni shwieɔ nu mli. etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efite

english: Why does my soil become hard like stone after heavy rain and sun, making it difficult for seeds to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wa tamɔ tɛsaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo sɛɛ lɛ? Eha ewa aha dumɔwui lɛ akɛ amɛakwɛ̃?

english: Heavy rain packs fine soil particles tightly together, and strong sunshine bakes them hard. Adding decomposed manure or compost keeps the soil loose and spongy so young crop roots can easily push through.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa sũ mli nibii bibii kpɛtɛɔ amɛhe. Ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa amɛwaa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ anyɛ abote mli mlɛo.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce very small roots when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ shishifãi bibii waa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are grown too close, their roots compete with each other for space, water, and food in the soil. Giving each plant proper spacing allows the tubers enough room to grow large and healthy.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ baatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná he ko, nu, kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize plants turn yellow at the bottom while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ kã he eji ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need for leafy growth. Feeding the soil with compost or nitrogen fertilizer will restore their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni baai lɛ adara Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I cut down all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn under full, direct sunlight. Keeping taller shade trees or planting plantains nearby creates a protective shelter that keeps the young cocoa cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ehaa shĩa ko ni haa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do the leaves of my cowpea plants fold up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea leaves fold up in intense heat as a defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, preventing the plant from losing too much water. They reopen once the air cools down.
ga: Cowpea baai lɛ fɔ̃ɔ amɛhe yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Tsi tsei anaa koni amɛkafite nu babaoo tsɔ. Ebaagbele ekoŋŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli bawo wu.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without forming any tomatoes during very hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ otsi ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages tomato pollen, preventing the flowers from fertilizing and turning into fruit. Watering early in the morning and providing light shade helps keep the plants cool enough to hold their flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ tomato mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo fɔmɔ nii ni amɛwo yibii. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ leebi kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ amli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa koni amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why should I build high soil mounds for my yams instead of planting them on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matswa gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ maha mi-sweet potatoes lɛ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow downwards and need soft, loose earth to expand easily. High soil mounds gather loose topsoil in one place, allowing the yam tubers to swell without pushing against hard, unplowed ground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ ni ehe miihia ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni egbɛ eshwa koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ buaa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni etse lɛ naa yɛ he kome. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ amli shwereɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛtsi shikpɔŋ lɛ waa, ni amɛtsuuu nii hu.

english: Why do black spots spread quickly on my pepper leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmeii ahe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rainy weather creates high moisture in the air, which helps fungal diseases spread rapidly on wet leaves. Spacing pepper plants apart lets wind flow through and dry the leaves faster, reducing disease.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli feɔ fɛ̃i waa. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ. Gbɛ ni kã pepper tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni ehaa baai lɛ gĩɔ oya, ni no haa helai baa shi.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops after a light rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that naturally have stronger root systems designed to grab water and nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops do not starve while growing.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ amɛshishifãi ni wa fe tsutsu lɛ. Afee amɛ koni amɛgbala nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ hɔmɔ yeee amɛ be mli ni oduɔ nii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or that heavy rains have flooded the roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted poultry manure helps the leaves turn deep green and make food for the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi shishifãi lɛ amli obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo kooloi aŋmɔŋ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, called mulching, keeps the soil moist by stopping the hot sun from drying it out. It also cools the plant roots, prevents weeds from growing, and adds nutrients to the soil as it rots.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i kɛtsɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ni ebaatsi enaa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi lɛ nɔ. Ehaa tsei shishifãi hu mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he beni egboɔ lɛ.

english: Which short-term crops can I plant to get quick income while waiting for my tree crops to mature?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kukuoo manyɛ makwɛ koni maná shika oya yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni tsei lɛ adara lɛ?

english: Vegetables like tomatoes, pepper, garden eggs, and leafy greens grow quickly and can be harvested repeatedly within two to three months. Planting them gives you regular income while waiting for longer-term crops to produce.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ tomato, ŋmɔtɔ, abɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa amɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ mli. Nibii nɛɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ baaha oná shika babaoo yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni baawo yibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when heavy rains fall for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because the soil cannot breathe. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away, keeping the tubers safe underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: Why do the flowers and small fruits drop off my pepper plants before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai lɛ daraaa nakai lɛ? Ni ejɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ egbee shi dani etsɔ agbo?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or lack of soil nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil consistently moist and feeding the soil helps the plant hold onto its fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ calcium lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and looking smaller than usual?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ bibii fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies transmitting viruses, or by severe hot and dry weather. Controlling pests early with organic neem sprays and watering regularly protects the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ waa ni edɔɔ waa mli Mra Be mli nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ahe nitsumɔ Kɛtsɔ organic neem spray kɛ nu ni akɛhaa daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaabu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why do young cocoa plants grow better under shade trees than under the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Shade trees act like living natural shelters, shielding cocoa from hot sun and harsh dry winds while preserving moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shweshweeshwe shihilɛhe. Buu kookoo he kɛjɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to cut away some of the shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi tsɔne titri lɛ eje kpo.

english: Too many young shoots around a plantain stem steal food and water from the main tree. Leaving only one or two strong shoots allows the main tree to focus its energy on producing large, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei bibii babaoo ni bɔle plantain tso lɛ he lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa plantains akui wuji ni tsii lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: What happens to my maize crop if I plant many seeds too close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ bu kome mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the plants to compete for light, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the maize to grow thin, weak stalks that produce very small cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmãa lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni feɔ ŋmeii bibii waa loo ŋmeii bɛ kwraa.

english: Why do I need to place tall wooden sticks next to my yam plants for the leaves to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso ko masɛi koni baai lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the tubers growing under the ground. Lifting the vines off the ground on wooden stakes spreads out the leaves to catch maximum sunlight, resulting in bigger yams.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ awó wein tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmeii wuji.

english: What do the green leaves on my crops actually do to help them grow?
ga: Mɛni baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ feɔ diɛŋtsɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Green leaves act like a kitchen for the plant. They catch sunlight and use water and air to produce the food that feeds the entire crop. Without healthy leaves, the plant cannot produce food to make fruits or tubers.
ga: Baai eŋɔli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tso lɛ kpataashi. Amɛmɔɔ hulu la ni amɛkɛ nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ feɔ niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ niyenii. Kɛji baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ bɛ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni amɛkɛfee aduawai loo ŋmeii.

english: Why do my crops start to wither and dry up after insects eat all their leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ ni egbiɔ beni kooloi bibii eye amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When insects eat all the leaves, they destroy the plant's food factory. Without leaves to absorb sunlight and produce food, the plant starves and slowly withers away.
ga: Kɛ́ kooloi bibii lɛ ye baai lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, amɛfiteɔ tso lɛ niyenii nitsumɔhei lɛ. Kɛji baai ni baanyɛ aŋɔ hulu la ni afee niyenii lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hɔmɔ baaye tso lɛ ni ebaagbo fiofio.

english: Why do my vegetable plants die when I trim off too many of their leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mifo baai babaoo lɛ?

english: Leaves make all the food the plant needs to survive. If you cut off all or most of the leaves, the food supply stops completely, causing the plant to starve and wither.
ga: Baai ji niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi. Kɛji ofo baai lɛ fɛɛ loo amɛteŋ babaoo Niyenii ni ayeɔ lɛ akpa kwraa. Ehaa tsei yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: How many leaves should I leave behind when I prune my crops?
ga: Baai enyiɛ esa akɛ mashi yɛ sɛɛ beni mifoɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: You should always leave several healthy leaves on every plant. Keeping enough leaves ensures the plant can continue making food to keep growing and stay alive.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo yɛ tso fɛɛ tso nɔ. Kɛ́ akwɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yaa nɔ ewoɔ niyenii koni eda ni ehi shi.

english: Will trimming too many branches off my cocoa trees reduce my harvest?
ga: Ani kookoo tso ni mifoɔ babaoo lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, trimming too many branches removes the leaves that make food for the tree. Without enough leaves to generate energy, the tree becomes weak and cannot produce healthy cocoa pods.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, niji babaoo ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ baai ni haa tso lɛ niyenii lɛ. Kɛji baai ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee hewalɛ bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ ekɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba.

english: What happens to my pepper plants if I pluck off all their leaves at once to stop a leaf disease?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mijie baai lɛ fɛɛ shikome koni mikɛkpa baai hela?

english: Removing all the leaves cuts off the plant's total food supply and shocks it. Without any leaves left to feed the plant, it will quickly wither and die.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, efoɔ niyenii fɛɛ ni tso lɛ yeɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa ehe feɔ shoo. Beni baa eshwɛɛɛ ni akɛbaahã tso lɛ niyenii Ebaagbo ni ebaagbo oya.

english: Can I harvest all the leaves from my cocoyam plant at once for cooking?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabua cacao tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ naa koni mikɛhoo yɛ be kome mli?

english: No, you must leave at least a few leaves on the cocoyam plant. The leaves make the food that feeds the plant, so harvesting every single leaf stops food production and destroys the crop.
ga: Dabi, kɛ hoo lɛ, ehe miihia ni oshi baai fioo komɛi yɛ cacao tso lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛha tso lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, baa fɛɛ baa ni akpaa lɛ haa niyenii ni anáa lɛ kpaa ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava plant stop growing bigger tubers after I strip its leaves to feed my goats?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ kpa bulbs wuji lɛ shweremɔ beni mifolɔ baai lɛ koni mikɛha mitooi lɛ niyenii lɛ?

english: Cassava roots grow big by storing food produced by the leaves. When you strip off the leaves, the plant stops making food, so the roots stop growing.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ daa kɛtsɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛbuaa naa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ojie baai lɛ Tsei lɛ baakpa niyenii feemɔ. Shishifãi lɛ kpa dalɛ.

english: Is it safe to cut off the leafy tops of my tomato plants to make them neat?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaafolɔ tomato tsei lɛ ayiteŋ baai lɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cutting off too many leafy tops removes the main food-producing parts of the tomato plant. Without enough leaf area, the plant stops feeding itself properly, which slows fruit growth or causes the plant to dry up.
ga: Kɛ́ ofo baai babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaajie niyenii titrii ni yɔɔ tomato tso lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ahe gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ kpaɔ ehe niyenii yeli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha aduawai lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo loo ebaaha tso lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my cowpea plants look weak after I pick too many leaves to sell at the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ beni mikpa baai babaoo ni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Picking too many leaves removes the plant's food factories. To keep the crop strong enough to produce new pods, you must always leave enough leaves on the stem to keep making food.
ga: Baai babaoo ni ajieɔ lɛ gbeɔ tso lɛ niyenii tsei lɛ. Enɛ ji koni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei aba. Esa akɛ oshi baai ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be koni oya nɔ ohoo nii.

english: Why do some new coconut trees start bearing fruit so much faster than the ones my father planted years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei heei No hewɔ lɛ ebɔi yibiiwoo mra kwraa fe be mli ni Ataa du lɛ afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Improved or hybrid coconut varieties are specially bred to mature early, often producing fruit within 3 to 4 years compared to traditional varieties that take 7 to 10 years.
ga: Akwɛɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi loo ŋmeii ni akɛfee ekome ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛshwere oya. Bei pii lɛ, amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, ni akɛto afii 7 kɛyashi 10 he kɛha blema ŋmeii.

english: Why are some coconut trees very short but still packed with a huge number of fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei komɛi yɛ kuku shi amɛyi obɔ kɛ aduawai babaoo lolo lɛ?

english: These are known as dwarf varieties. Instead of spending energy growing a tall trunk, they focus their nutrients directly into producing flowers and heavy fruit early in life.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛɛmɛi akɛ dwarf henɔi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni tsii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli mra.

english: How can an improved crop tree give me a much higher yield than my natural local crops?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tso ni atsake lɛ awo yibii babaoo fe mimaŋ, adebɔɔ mli tso lɛ?

english: Improved varieties combine the strongest traits of different parent plants, making them better at taking in water and soil nutrients to produce bigger and more abundant harvests.
ga: Tsoi srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛ sui ni mli wa fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ fɔlɔ tsei srɔtoi lɛ amli lɛ feɔ ekome. Enɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ koni yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ ni ebɔi babaoo.

english: If I plant these fast-yielding crop varieties, do I need to care for them differently than my traditional crops?
ga: Kɛji midu tsei ni woɔ yibii oya nɛɛ Ani ehe miihia ni makwɛ amɛ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe tsei krokomɛi?

english: Yes, high-yielding crops work harder to produce more fruit, so they require regular watering, proper weed control, and extra nutrients through fertilizer or organic manure.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ tsuɔ nii waa koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni afɔ amɛ nu daa. Jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ

english: Can I save seeds from my best hybrid crop harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid kpamɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: It is best to buy fresh certified seeds each time, because seeds saved from hybrid crops often lose their special high-yielding strength in the next generation.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli be fɛɛ be. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ ni haa yibii babaoo fe fɛɛ lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: How can I know if my fruit tree is hungry and needs extra food or manure?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ ni niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi he miihia amɛ?

english: Common signs include yellowing leaves, slow stem growth, small fruits, or flowers dropping early without forming fruit.
ga: Okadii ni afɔɔ namɔ ji baai ŋmɔŋ, tsei ni daraa blɛoo, aduawai bibii, loo fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi mra ni ewooo aduawai.

english: Why do coconut trees grow so well and produce heavily near coastal beach areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ ŋshɔnaa ŋshɔnaa lɛ?

english: Coastal areas provide deep sandy soil, abundant sunlight, high air humidity, and warm weather, which are the exact conditions coconut trees naturally love.
ga: Ŋshɔnaa hei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni ŋã yɔɔ mli. Hulu la lɛ kpɛɔ kɛtsɔɔ mli. kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ Enɛ ji shihilɛ ni ŋmei tsei sumɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my young coconut trees drop their small fruits before they are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tso bibioo lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Fruit drop usually happens when a tree is stressed due to lack of water, insect damage, or a lack of proper soil nutrients needed to hold the heavy fruit load.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ miihao yɛ nu ni bɛ, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii, loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa ni he hiaa koni anyɛ ahiɛ aduawai babaoo lɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: How does dry, hot weather affect the time it takes for my trees to give fruit?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ baaná be ni mitso lɛ baawo yibii lɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Severe drought slows down plant growth because the tree spends all its energy surviving instead of forming flowers, which delays fruit production.
ga: Hɔmɔ ni naa wa haa tsei adalɛ baa shi ejaakɛ tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi. yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ najiaŋ Enɛ baaha aduawai afeemɔ asɛɛ afo.

english: How far apart should I plant my coconut trees so they do not reduce each other's harvest?
ga: Te esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni amɛkaha yibiiwoo aba shi?

english: Planting trees about 7 to 8 meters apart ensures that their roots and leaves do not block each other from getting enough sunlight, water, and soil food.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ aaafee mitai 7 kɛyashi 8 lɛ haaa shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ akabote hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to keep some shade trees on my cocoa farm instead of cutting all of them down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ hiɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mafo amɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young and growing cocoa trees get easily scorched and stressed under direct sun. Shade trees protect cocoa leaves from harsh heat, keep the soil moist, and help the cocoa farm produce healthy pods for many more years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii ni miida lɛ shãa oya ni amɛhaoɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ buɔ kookoo baai ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ afii babaoo ni baa lɛ.

english: Why should I remove the extra suckers growing at the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they fight with the main plant for food and water in the soil. Cutting them off to leave just one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant produces large, heavy bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ plantain tso kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Amɛkɛ dumɔwui titrii lɛ baawu koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli koni eshi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize crop turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build strong green leaves, or that water has logged around the roots and is suffocating them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Aloo nu shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa mɔ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why is it recommended that I plant groundnuts on my plot before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani adu ŋmei yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts put extra nitrogen back into the soil through their roots. When you plant maize after harvesting groundnuts, the maize feeds on that leftover food and grows much better without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ nitrogen kroko kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa beni okpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ ŋmãa lɛ baaye niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ebaada jogbaŋŋ kwraa ni ŋmãa ni jara wa he ehiaaa.

english: Which specific part of the cassava stem should I cut and plant in my field?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei tso lɛ fã esa akɛ mafo ni madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: You should use the middle portion of a healthy, mature cassava stem about the thickness of your thumb, ensuring it has about four to six visible buds pointing upward when planted.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eda ni tamɔ oshishifa lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ atsu nii. Kwɛmɔ ni ŋmeii 4-6 ni anaa lɛ ahi shi ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛji oodu.

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground allows their leaves to catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food, which makes the tubers below grow big and thick while preventing ground diseases from rotting the leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie sweet potato wain tsei kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛbaai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii. Enɛ haa shishigbɛ ŋmei lɛ daa ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaaa helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akafite baai lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, dry soil during flowering, or attacks from tiny insects that feed on the soft parts of the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. loo tutuamɔi ni jɛɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ adɛŋ

english: What is causing the leaves of my pepper plants to curl upward and look wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ekpɔtɔ?

english: Wrinkled and curling pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap out of the leaves, or by viruses carried into the farm by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni egbɔjɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo hela ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Young crop plants have small roots and weak stems. Clearing weeds early stops those wild plants from stealing sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before your crop can establish itself.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Etsiɔ nakai koo mli tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ ama shi

english: Why is it bad practice to spray water on my crop leaves during the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nifeemɔ gbonyo lɛ?

english: Water applied in afternoon heat quickly evaporates before roots can drink it, and wet droplets on leaves under hot sunlight can burn the foliage and encourage fungal diseases to grow.
ga: Nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ shwane mli lɛ shwieɔ oya dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnuɔ. Ni nu ni mli efɔ ni shwieɔ baai anɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ ni ewo tsɛŋemɔ hela he hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and curling up in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe yɛ hulu la lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under strong sunlight. They need shade from surrounding trees or companion crops like plantains to hold moisture and shield them until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe loo tsei ni fata amɛhe, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hebuu mli kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my maize cobs have many empty spaces with missing grains when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ hiɛ hei babaoo ni nɔ ko bɛ mli kɛ ŋmãa ni bɛ mli beni mikpaa lɛ?

english: Missing grains happen when maize plants suffer from heat stress, lack of water, or low soil nutrients during their flowering stage, which prevents the flowers from properly pollinating.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with huge leaves, but the roots underneath stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or gets waterlogged, the cassava plant spends all its energy developing upper leaves and stems instead of storing food in the underground tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ ŋwɛi ŋmei lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: Why are my tomatoes getting dark, sunken black spots at the bottom before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani etsɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Black spots at the bottom of tomatoes are caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit, which often happens when watering is uneven or when the soil gets too dry between rainfalls.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji calcium ni shɛɛɛ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ ni faaa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience stress from high temperatures, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer that encourages leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa he haomɔ he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa Aloo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni woɔ baai hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why am I seeing ragged holes in my young maize leaves with powdery dust inside the center whorl?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli ni sũ yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Holes and powdery waste inside young maize plants are signs of Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide in the central growing leaf and chew through the plant if not controlled early.
ga: Buu kɛ powder ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii amli lɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ahe okadii, ni amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai ni miida yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ amɛ mra.

english: Why do my yam vines start drying up and turning brown long before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines dry up early when fungal diseases attack the leaves or when tiny worm-like pests called nematodes damage the roots underground, cutting off water and nutrients.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ tutua tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ. Aloo be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ tamɔ ŋmei bibioo ko. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Enɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii laajeɔ.

english: Weeds grow aggressively and steal essential nutrients, root space, and sunlight directly from your crops, leaving the crops weak and malnourished.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ amɛmli.

english: Why do my seeds rot and die in the ground instead of sprouting after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds rot when the soil becomes soaked with excess water because roots and seeds need air pockets in the soil to breathe in order to sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui fiteɔ kɛji akɛ nu babaoo wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi kɛ dumɔwui lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu bɔni afee ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvests when I plant many seeds close together in one mound?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ gɔŋ kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too closely forces the crops to compete with each other for water, soil nutrients, and light, causing all of them to stay small and weak.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi nu he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ la haa tsei fɛɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa.

english: How can I grow and harvest crops three times in a single year when the rainy season is so short in my area?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu ni makpa ŋmɔshi nibii etɛ yɛ afi kome mli, be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ faaa kwraa yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: By using simple irrigation systems—like pumping or channeling water from a nearby river or well—you can supply water to your crops during dry periods, allowing you to farm continuously all year round instead of relying only on rainfall.
ga: Kɛtsɔ nu shwiemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ faa loo nubu ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli loo ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ nu aha oŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Ehaa otsuɔ okwaayeli he nii daa afi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ he aaafɔ̃ nugbɔshiimɔ pɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Why do my vegetable leaves turn yellow when I irrigate my farm heavily every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli waa daa gbi lɛ?

english: Too much water drowns the crop roots by pushing all the air out of the soil. Without air, roots cannot breathe or absorb nutrients properly, which causes the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nu babaoo shwieɔ tsei shishifãi anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛhe niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my farm during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Early morning or late evening is best because the sun is gentle. Watering at these times allows moisture to soak deep into the soil for roots to absorb, rather than evaporating quickly in the hot afternoon heat.
ga: Leebi loo gbɛkɛ ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ hulu la lɛ kpɛɔ fioo. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɛkɛ bei nɛɛ amli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ nu. Mohu ɔ, e puɛɔ oya ngɛ shwane nɛ mi mi wa ɔ mi.

english: Why does rainwater sit on top of my field for days without soaking into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ gbii babaoo ni eboteee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This happens when soil is tightly compacted or contains heavy clay, which closes the tiny holes water uses to drain. Digging compost into the soil helps open up channels so water can reach crop roots easily.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ loo shikpɔŋ sũ ni mli tse ni tsiɔ buji bibii anaa lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ. He ni akɛ nu tsuɔ nii kɛhaa nu shwiemɔ Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa nu lɛ tsɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ eshɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe oya.

english: Rolling up leaves is a crop's natural shield against heat. By exposing less leaf surface to the sun, the plant reduces water loss through evaporation until the weather cools down.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ he tsɔne. Tsei haa nu ni laajeɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ baa lɛ hiɛ feɔ fɛ̃i kɛtsɔ baa lɛ hiɛ ni amɛjieɔ lɛ kpo yɛ hulu la fioo ko nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms without setting any fruit when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and dries out pollen, preventing pollination. The plant drops its blossoms to save water and energy until cooler conditions return.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Tsi pollination naa Tsei baafɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baafee fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thin stems when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are spaced too close, they compete fiercely for sunlight. They stretch upward to reach light, spending all their energy on thin, tall stems instead of growing big tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ tsei kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la he akaŋ waa. Amɛkpã amɛhe koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Kɛtsɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: How can I keep my land fertile for decades without the soil losing its strength?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni ehewalɛ sɛɛ efooo?

english: You can keep soil productive over decades by rotating different crop types, adding animal manure or compost regularly, and practicing irrigation correctly so vital nutrients stay in the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii babaoo aya hiɛ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni oootsake lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii afata he daa. ni okɛ nu awo mli jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Which crops grow best in low-lying land near the river where water stays in the soil constantly?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ faai ni nu yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Crops like rice and sugarcane thrive in waterlogged or swampy conditions, whereas crops like maize, cowpeas, and pepper need well-drained soil and will rot if left in standing water.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmei yɔɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, tsina ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni ebaagbo kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop growing even when there is plenty of sunshine every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ hulu la kpɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ daa gbi moŋ?

english: Sunlight is only one part of plant food. If the soil lacks adequate water or nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus, the crop slows down or stops growing to conserve its limited energy.
ga: Hulu la ji tso niyenii lɛ fã kome pɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ daa blɛoo loo ekpaa dalɛ po koni ekɛ hewalɛ fioo ko ato.

english: Why do I need to wash my crop seeds before putting them into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafɔ midumɔwui lɛ ahe dani madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Washing seeds removes dirt, bad fungal spores, and insect eggs that can cause seed rot. Clean seeds have a much better chance of sprouting into healthy, strong crops.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni ahoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ muji kɛjɛɔ mli. ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii kɛ kooloi bibii ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agboi. Dumɔwui ni he tse lɛ yɛ hegbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ amɛbaada ni amɛtsɔmɔ tsei ni he wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Will washing my planting seeds in water spoil them before I plant them?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni adu lɛ ni ahooɔ yɛ nu mli lɛ baafite dumɔwui lɛ dani adu?

english: No, washing seeds briefly does not spoil them. In fact, it protects them from seed-borne diseases and helps kickstart the moisture absorption needed for germination.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui lɛ ahe fɔmɔ ji be kukuoo. Efiteŋ dumɔwui lɛ. Ebuɔ amɛhe diɛŋtsɛ kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli kɛbaa lɛ ahe, ni ehaa nu ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe.

english: Why is it important to rinse my crop seeds multiple times before taking them out to dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afɔ aduawai dumɔwui ahe shii abɔ dani agbi lɛ?

english: Rinsing seeds several times ensures that all dirt, weak disease organisms, and leftover salt are completely washed away so they do not harm the fragile young sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni afɔɔ he shii abɔ lɛ haa muji Helai ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. ni ŋoo ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ baaho kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ, eyeee tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ awui.

english: Why do some farmers add salt to the water when preparing their seeds for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ ŋoo woɔ nu mli kɛ́ amɛmiisaa dumɔwui ni amɛbaadu lɛ?

english: Adding salt creates a dense solution that helps separate good seeds from bad ones. Healthy, heavy seeds sink to the bottom, while light, diseased, or insect-damaged seeds float to the top.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei fata he lɛ, ehaa tsofa ni mli wa ni yeɔ ebuaa ni egbalaa dumɔwui kpakpai kɛ dumɔwui gbohii ateŋ lɛ baa. Dumɔwui ni mli wa ni tsii baagbee shi kɛya shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni he waaa, hela emɔ amɛ, loo kooloi eyi mli obɔ lɛ baafo kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: Will salt water damage my seeds if I use it during preparation?
ga: Ani brine lɛ baafite midumɔwui lɛ kɛji mikɛtsu nii yɛ be mli ni misaa mihe lɛ?

english: Salt water is good for selecting seeds the first time, but if salt is left on the seeds or used repeatedly, it can draw moisture out of the seeds and stop them from growing. You must rinse them with clean water afterward.
ga: Nu ni mli edɔ hi kɛha dumɔwui akwɛmɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa. Shi kɛji akɛ ashi ŋoo yɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ loo akɛtsu nii shii abɔ lɛ, Ebaanyɛ ejie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli ni ekpa amɛdalɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ nu ni mli tse afɔ he yɛ no sɛɛ.

english: Should I add salt every single time I wash my seeds in water?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋoo awo mli be fɛɛ be ni mafɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ nu mli?

english: No, salt should only be used for the very first wash to separate bad seeds. After that, you must use only clean, fresh water so the seeds are not damaged by salt residue.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ akɛ ŋoo atsu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔlɔ mli pɛ koni akɛgbala dumɔwui gbohii lɛ amli. No sɛɛ lɛ, ehe baahia ni okɛ nu ni mli tse pɛ atsu nii bɔni afee ni ŋmei ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akafite dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do some of my grains float to the top when I soak them in water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo nu mli lɛ?

english: Seeds float because they are empty inside, dried out, or damaged by pests. Floating seeds will not grow well, so you should scoop them off and throw them away.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu nɔ ejaakɛ amɛhe efee efolo, amɛgbi loo kooloi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ efite amɛ. Dumɔwui ni hoɔ yɛ nu lɛ nɔ lɛ edaŋ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli ni ashɛrɛ ashwie.

english: How can I easily separate good planting seeds from bad ones at home?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ magbala dumɔwui kpakpai kɛ dumɔwui gbohii amli yɛ shia?

english: You can test them in water: healthy seeds are heavy and sink to the bottom, while bad seeds are light and float to the surface where you can easily remove them.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka lɛ okwɛ yɛ nu mli. Dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ tsii ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛyaa shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui fɔji lɛ baafee mlɛo ni amɛbaafo yɛ nu lɛ hiɛ, ni obaanyɛ ojie amɛ oya.

english: What should I do right after I finish washing my seeds in water?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee beni mikɛ nu efɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe sɛɛ?

english: Once washed, you should collect the good seeds from the water immediately so they do not soak for too long and rot. You can then plant them moist or dry them safely in the shade.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ he lɛ, esa akɛ abua dumɔwui lɛ anaa jogbaŋŋ. Oya ni ojie ohe kɛjɛ nu lɛ mli Bɔni afee ni ekɛ ehe akawo mli be kakadaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaagbo No sɛɛ lɛ obaanyɛ odu yɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ loo ogbi lɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: How does soaking seeds in water affect how fast they grow in my farm?
ga: Te dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ saa bɔ ni amɛdaraa oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Soaking seeds softens their hard outer shells and signals to the seed that it is time to grow, leading to faster and more uniform sprouting once planted in the field.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ haa kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa lɛ feɔ blɛoo. ni etsɔɔ dumɔwu lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ eda Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ ekome.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which helps leaves grow green and strong, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients deep out of reach of the young roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi bibii amli lɛ.

english: Can I put fresh manure from my chicken farm directly onto my growing vegetables?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmeii hee ni jɛ kooloi aŋmɔ mli lɛ afata aduawai ni miduɔ lɛ he?

english: Fresh chicken manure is too strong and burns plant roots because it releases strong heat and ammonia. You need to let it dry and break down into dark compost for a few weeks before mixing it into the soil.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni afee ehee lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi ejaakɛ ejieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ammonia kpo. Obaasumɔ ni oha egbi ni egbɛ eshwa ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛfutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam vines produce long green stems with many leaves but very small yams underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ baai babaoo shi sweet potato lɛ ji bibioo kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plant puts all its strength into growing leaves on top of the ground instead of storing food underground in the tuber.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Tsei yeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛduɔ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ niyenii ato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ oyitsoŋ lɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that get scorched by direct sunlight. They need fast-growing shade plants like plantains to act as natural umbrellas for their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my nursery seedlings bend and grow crooked towards one side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe kɛtee he kome lɛ?

english: Plants naturally search for sunlight to make their food. If your nursery shade blocks light on one side, the seedlings will bend their stems toward wherever the sun reaches them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei taoɔ hulu la koni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo lɛ tsi la naa yɛ fa kome lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baafo amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛya he ni hulu lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry out and fold down quickly during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe oya yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dry harmattan wind strips water from broad leaves faster than roots can drink. The plant intentionally lets older leaves droop and dry to save water for its central growing tip.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ woɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛhaa baai ni egbɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ koni amɛkɛto nu he kɛha ŋmeii ni miida yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow tall and weak with tiny cobs when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. They stretch upward to beat their neighbors for light instead of putting strength into building big cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpã amɛhe koni amɛye amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ anɔ kunim kɛha la, moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛma ŋmei agbo ko.

english: Why do my cassava roots remain thin like sticks even after standing in the ground for a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ tamɔ tsei lolo yɛ be mli ni midamɔ shikpɔŋ afi po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots cannot expand into thick tubers if the soil is packed too hard or contains too much clay. The roots need loose, soft soil to swell as they store food.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ adara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ fa babaoo. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia shishifãi lɛ koni amɛfuu be mli ni amɛbuaa niyenii naa lɛ.

english: Why are all the flowers falling off my pepper plants without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or attacks from tiny insects eating the blossom joints.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo kooloi bibii ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ tutuamɔ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes develop flat black rotten spots while still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lolo lɛ?

english: This is blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot move calcium to the developing fruit, usually because the soil goes from very dry to soaked too quickly.
ga: Enɛ ji blossom end rot, ni baa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium kɛya aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbiɔ waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli oya tsɔ.

english: Cutting unwanted branches, known as pruning, allows sunlight and air to reach all parts of the tree. This stops fungal diseases like black pod from spreading and helps the tree direct its energy into producing bigger, healthier cocoa pods.
ga: Ale niji ni ataooo lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ hu akɛ tsei ni afoɔ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Enɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods lɛ akagbɛ ashwã. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know when it is the right time of year to prune my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa yɛ afi lɛ mli ni esa akɛ afo cacao tsei lɛ?

english: It is best to prune cocoa trees right after the main harvest season or just before the heavy rains start. This timing allows the tree to recover quickly and put its energy into fresh flowering and pod growth.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaafolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ kpamɔ be titri lɛ sɛɛ loo dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aje shishi. Be nɛɛ haa tso lɛ he waaa oya ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛhaa fɔfɔi heei kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa hiɛ.

english: What are those fast-growing straight shoots at the bottom of my cocoa tree, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ? Ni ani esa akɛ majie kɛjɛ mihe?

english: Those shoots are called suckers or chupones. They steal water and food from the main trunk without producing pods, so you should cut them off early to keep the producing branches strong.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii lɛ akɛ suckers loo chupons. Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli ni amɛfeee ŋmeii. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ofo amɛ mra. Koni eha niji lɛ awa

english: Why is my cocoa tree growing plenty of thick leaves but producing very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ baai lɛ mli tse waa shi eshishifãi lɛ faaa kwraa lɛ?

english: When a cocoa tree has too many thick leaves and extra branches, sunlight cannot penetrate to the trunk where flowers grow. Trimming back the heavy top foliage lets in sunlight, which triggers flowering and pod formation.
ga: Beni kookoo tso lɛ baai ni mli tse kɛ niji babaoo tsɔ lɛ. Hulu la nyɛŋ abote tsei ni fɔfɔi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ afo ŋwɛi baai ni mli tse lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa hulu la babaoo boteɔ mli. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi kɛ pod feɔ.

english: Will cutting branches hurt my cocoa tree or make it easy for pests to attack?
ga: Ani tso ni afoɔ lɛ baaye mi-kookoo tso lɛ awui loo ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai abatutua lɛ?

english: If you make clean cuts with sharp tools, the tree heals quickly without harm. Pruning actually reduces pest attacks because insects like mistletoe and mirids prefer dark, overcrowded foliage.
ga: Kɛ okɛ dɛŋdade ni mli wa tsumɔ pilamɔ he lɛ Tso lɛ baatsa oya ni nɔ ko nɔ ko efeŋ lɛ. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baa shi diɛŋtsɛ ejaakɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ mistletoe kɛ mirids lɛ sumɔɔ tsei ahe tsei ni yɔɔ ediŋ ni mli eyi obɔ fe nine lɛ.

english: Does pruning my cocoa farm really give me more sacks of cocoa at harvest time?
ga: Ani mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ baaha kookoo babaoo aba diɛŋtsɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: Yes, pruned trees yield more because the plant stops wasting nutrients on unnecessary wood and foliage, directing all its energy and soil nutrients straight into developing larger cocoa pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baawo yibii babaoo ejaakɛ tsei lɛ kpaɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ tsei kɛ tsei ahe tsei ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. Ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why shouldn't I let my cocoa trees grow as tall as wild trees in the forest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa kookoo tso lɛ shwereɔ tamɔ koo mli tsei lɛ?

english: Keeping cocoa trees at a manageable height keeps energy concentrated on pod growth and makes it much easier for you to harvest pods, prune branches, and spot diseases early.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ cacao tsei lɛ wo he ko ni anyɛɔ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha pods lɛ aná hewalɛ babaoo. ni eye ebua bo ni okpa pods pruning tsei lɛ ni oyɔse hela lɛ mra Much easier

english: Can I use my regular cutlass to trim cocoa branches, or do I need special tools?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsɔne kuku ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ afo kookoo niji? Aloo ehe miihia ni mikɛ dɛŋdadei krɛdɛɛi atsu nii?

english: While a clean, sharp cutlass can work for small shoots, using proper pruning shears or a saw prevents tearing the tree bark, which helps the branch wounds heal faster and stay healthy.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni abaanyɛ akɛ tsɔne ni mli wa ni he tse atsu nii yɛ tsei bibii anɔ lɛ, kɛ akɛ tsɔne ni sa ni akɛfoɔ tsei loo tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi tsei lɛ ahe ŋmeii lɛ anaa. Enɛ baaye abua ni pilamɔi ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ atsa oya ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How much sunlight should be reaching the ground under my cocoa trees after pruning?
ga: Beni afo tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Esa akɛ hulu la ashɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ falɛ enyiɛ?

english: You want dappled sunlight on the soil—meaning small spots of light filtering through the leaves—rather than full sun or full shade. This balances moisture retention with good airflow.
ga: Osumɔɔ ni hulu la lɛ akpɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsɔɔ akɛ he bibioo ko ni tsɔɔ la kɛtsɔɔ baai amli Yɛ hulu loo hulutsoo be ni eyi obɔ najiaŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ mli kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ teŋ ja.

english: What key features should I look for when I visit another farmer's well-pruned cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii esa akɛ matao beni miyasaraa okwaafonyo kroko kookoo ŋmɔ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Look for open spaces between tree crowns, an clear view down the tree trunks, the absence of low suckers, and pods growing clearly on the main stems rather than buried inside dense foliage.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ayiteŋ lɛ ateŋ. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ nibii ni anaa jogbaŋŋ, ŋmeii ni baa shi bɛ, kɛ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni aaafu amɛ yɛ tsei ahe tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ amli.

english: If my land gets enough rain, why are my maize leaves still turning yellow?
ga: Kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ bɔ ni sa Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: Rain provides water, but yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen. Maize needs these nutrients to stay green and grow strong, so adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help fix this issue.
ga: Nugbɔ ji nu jɛɛhe. Shi bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii nɛɛ he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers fall off before any peppers start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers often drop when the plant experiences heat stress, too much water, or a lack of moisture in the soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting plants during extreme heat helps the flowers set into healthy fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu lɛ fa tsɔ. aloo ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni abuɔ tso lɛ he yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and twisted instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose soil to expand downwards easily. If the soil is hard, compacted, or stony, the tubers struggle to push through, resulting in small, bent, or stunted yams. Making high mounds with soft topsoil helps them grow straight and large.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shi oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo tɛi yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaawa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ baatsɔ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii, ni ebɔle, loo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ baa. Gɔji kakadaji ni akɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo feɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa ja ni amɛdaraa.

english: How do tiny insects like whiteflies actually damage my tomato plants?
ga: Te kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies lɛ fiteɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Whiteflies damage tomatoes by sucking the sap directly out of the leaves, which weakens the plant. They also carry harmful viruses from plant to plant and leave a sticky residue on leaves that leads to black soot, blocking sunlight.
ga: Whiteflies fiteɔ tomato kɛtsɔ nu ni amɛnuɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ. Amɛhiɛɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui hu kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ ni amɛshiɔ nɔ ko ni shwieɔ shi yɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni feɔ sũ diŋ ni tsiɔ hulu la naa.

english: Why do the roots of my cassava rot in the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot mainly when water settles around them for too long or when fungal infections present in the soil attack the tubers. Planting your cassava on raised ridges helps excess water drain away and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ titri kɛji nu ta shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutua ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ ŋmei ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli, ni ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: What causes cocoa pods to turn black and dry up on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tsei anɔ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, cool, and overly shady farms. Pruning crowded branches to let sunlight and air reach the trunk, along with removing infected pods immediately, stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ tsɔ, ni ejɔ, kɛ hulutsoo mli lɛ kɛbaa. Nibii ni afolɔ mli babaoo koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ agbɛnɛ hu, jiemɔ pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ebaaha helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How do weeds hurt my corn crop even if I water the farm regularly?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your corn for sunlight, soil nutrients, and root space. Even with enough water, weeds will steal the food your corn needs to develop heavy ears, so clearing weeds early is necessary for a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmãa yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po lɛ Jwɛi hu baaju niyenii ni he hiaa o-ŋmã lɛ koni ená toi ni tsii. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni ayeɔ mra lɛ he miihia koni aná kpamɔ kpakpa.

english: Why is it important to rotate my crops instead of planting maize on the same field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsake miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ moŋ fe ni madu ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets maize-specific pests build up in the ground. Rotating with legumes like beans or groundnuts restores soil nitrogen and breaks pest cycles naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be, ni ehaa abɛi pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsakeɔ Ehaa nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli.

english: How does planting crops too close together affect their final harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ saa naagbee ŋmaa lɛ he?

english: When crops are crowded together, they shade each other from sunlight and fight for nutrients in the soil. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough light, air, and soil nourishment to grow full, healthy crops.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ebɔ he babaoo lɛ Tsei lɛ feɔ amɛhe shade ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops do not retain the high yield and strong disease resistance of the original parent seed. Planting second-generation saved seeds usually results in uneven growth, smaller cobs, and lower yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ nyɛŋ ahi yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo kɛ helai ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni shishijee fɔlɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɔɔ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ayinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ dalɛ ni ejaaa baa. Cob lɛ ji bibioo fe no. ni nibii ni anáa lɛ ba shi

english: If I clear all the big trees on my new farmland before planting, will my crops grow better?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ he hee ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ dani midu hu? Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Not always. While clearing weeds and brush gives your crops sunlight and space, removing all big trees leaves the soil exposed to severe heat and heavy rains, which washes away topsoil and scorches young plants.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be, eyɛ mli akɛ jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni ooojie lɛ baaha otsei lɛ aná hulu la kɛ he ko moŋ. Shi tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ waa ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Enɛ baaho sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ ni ekɛshã tsei bibii lɛ.

english: Does burning the cleared bush on my farm before planting help or hurt my crops?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni ajie yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mishãa dani miduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa loo eyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?
