english: Burning gives a quick burst of ash nutrients for the first season, but it destroys essential organic matter and kills beneficial soil organisms, making the soil weaker in the long run.
ga: Shãa jieɔ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ mli. Shi efiteɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni efiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my crops very close together so I can get more plants on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa bɔni afee ni maná tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting crops too close forces them to compete with each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak plants that produce smaller yields.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ baa.

english: Is it a good idea to plant shade plants like plantain alongside my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ mi-cocoa dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, young cocoa seedlings burn easily in full sunlight. Fast-growing plants with large leaves like plantains act as living umbrellas, keeping the young crops shaded and the soil moist.
ga: Hɛɛ, cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Tsei ni daa oya ni amɛbaai wuji tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii ni amɛnáa hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil without rest, while also allowing pests and diseases that attack that specific crop to build up in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekpaaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do farmers say that planting groundnuts or beans makes the soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ amɛdu ŋmei loo ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi jogbaŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground through their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha tsei fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Healthy soil is typically dark in color, holds moisture without staying waterlogged, crumbles easily in your hands, and shows signs of life like earthworms and decaying leaf matter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni nu bɛ mli Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli ni etsɔɔ wala he okadii, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni fiteɔ.

english: How exactly do weeds stop my maize from growing strong?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ atsĩ mi-ŋmãa lɛ naa koni ekaná hewalɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your maize needs to grow, effectively starving your crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni he hiaa bo koni o-abele lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and stop growing during a short dry spell in the middle of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ yɛ hɔmɔ kuku ko ni baa yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops turn yellow when dry soil prevents their roots from absorbing necessary nutrients, forcing the plant to slow down its growth to conserve energy and water.
ga: Tsei feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ, ni no haaa shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daalɛ baa shi koni amɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper or tomato plants fall off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper loo tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers usually drop off when the crop experiences stress, such as extreme weather heat, irregular watering, or a lack of essential nutrients in the soil needed for fruiting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ miihao, tamɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha yibiiwoo ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to leave wide spaces between my maize plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishiɔ he ko ni da yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Maize plants need plenty of sunlight, air, and soil nutrients to form large cobs. Planting them too close forces them to compete with each other, resulting in thin stems and small or empty cobs.
ga: Abele he miihia hulu la babaoo, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ́ adu amɛ kɛbɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha akaŋshii aba. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb up tall wooden sticks to produce good tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to lift their leaves up to capture maximum sunlight. Elevating the leaves helps the plant produce more energy, which is sent down into the ground to grow bigger and healthier yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Kɛ́ awó baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa hewalɛ babaoo. Akɛ enɛ majeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build healthy leaves. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the maize regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛma baai ni wa. Kooloo ŋmãa loo nitrogen ŋmãa ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni edaa waa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small wrinkled balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni etsɔ bɔɔlu bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the underside of leaves, or by viruses they carry. Spraying with neem water or safe treatments removes the pests so fresh, healthy leaves can open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛhiɛ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ neem nu loo tsofa ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ agbele.

english: Why do my cassava plants fall over during heavy rains, and how do I prevent it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Ni te ooofee tɛŋŋ otsĩ naa?

english: Cassava grows heavy branches while its roots are still soft, making it top-heavy in wet soil. Piling soil firmly around the base of the stems into mounds creates a strong anchor that keeps the plant upright.
ga: Cassava niji shwieɔ shi waa yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ bɔdɔɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ to gɔŋ ko ni mli wa he lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if I am giving my tomato plants too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ nu babaoo miiha mi-tomato tsei lɛ?

english: If tomato roots sit in soggy soil for too long, they cannot breathe and will turn yellow and wilt even though the ground is wet. The soil should feel damp like a squeezed sponge, not flooded.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu tomato shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. ni ebaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebaagbo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po. Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ anu he akɛ edɔ, tamɔ sponji ni ashɛre, shi jeee nu.

english: Why are the flowers on my garden egg plants falling off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or poor pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting flowers nearby to attract bees helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo pollination ni ehiii lɛ miigba tsei anaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adu fɔfɔii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ koni ekɛgbala ŋmeii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant cassava on the exact same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the dirt. Switching to groundnuts or beans rests the land and restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmei loo ŋmei nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aye ehe ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why did some of the maize seeds I buried in the ground fail to sprout out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui komɛi ni mifuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to come up if they were planted too deep for the shoot to reach the surface, if the soil was too dry, or if insects ate the seed underground. Planting seeds at a finger-length depth in moist soil ensures good sprouting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji kooloi yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi dumɔwui Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ ni mli kwɔ fe inchi kome pɛ lɛ baaye abua ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to burn cleared weeds on my land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashã jwɛi ni ajie yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Burning cleared weeds quickly cleans the field surface, kills weed seeds and pests hiding in the soil, and converts dry plant matter into ash that provides quick potassium to help young corn plants start growing.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajie lɛ ni ashãa lɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli tseɔ oya. Egbeɔ jwɛi dumɔwui kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni ehaa tsei ni egbi lɛ feɔ sũ oya ni haa potassium ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛdaraa.

english: Why is it necessary to dig holes for my corn instead of just scattering seeds on top of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ atsa bu ni akɛ ŋmãa lɛ awo mli moŋ fe ni ooogbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Corn seeds need to be covered in moist soil at a proper depth so their roots can anchor firmly into the ground to absorb nutrients and prevent the tall stalks from falling over when heavy wind or rain comes.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ aha ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ anɔ yɛ he ni sa. Enɛ haa eshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he waa koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ni otsi tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa miinɛ.

english: How does poor or quick land preparation affect how my corn crop grows later in the season?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ ni asaaa he jogbaŋŋ loo oya lɛ saa ŋmãa lɛ dalɛ he yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ yaa nɔ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: If land is prepared in a rush, hard soil prevents young corn roots from spreading deep, while uncleared weed roots quickly grow back and steal moisture and food from your corn plants, leading to weak stalks and small cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ oya Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ baatsi gbekɛbii abele shishifãi anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã shɔŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, jwɛi shishifãi ni bɛ faŋŋ lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Why should I spray chemical weedkiller on my farm before planting my corn seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Spraying before planting kills tough weed roots deep in the soil so they do not grow back quickly and compete with your tender corn seedlings for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa shwie nɔ dani adu lɛ, egbeɔ jwɛi shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni ekakwɛ̃ oya ni ekɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ohe lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ akaŋ.

english: Will chemical sprays hurt my maize seeds when they start to sprout in the soil?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baaye mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ awui kɛji amɛbɔi kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ?

english: If applied correctly before planting, pre-emergence chemicals specifically target germinating weeds or break down safely in the soil, leaving your maize seeds free to sprout cleanly without harm.
ga: Kɛ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ dani adu Pre-emergent chemicals lɛ tsɔɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ loo amɛfiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe. Ha o-corn ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni he tse nɔ ni nɔ ko akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my young corn crops on new farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe mi-babi corn tsei ni midu yɛ midumɔ hee lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native, tough wild plants that naturally consume water and fertilizer much faster than farm crops. Clearing and spraying them early gives your maize crop a safe window to grow tall and shade out new weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni kɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ashwieɔ nɔ mra Enɛ baaha o-abɛi lɛ aná samflɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ekwɛ̃ ni eha jwɛi heei lɛ aná hulutsoo.

english: Why do extension officers advise using pegs and ropes to make straight lines when planting corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ pegs kɛ line ni ja atsu nii kɛdu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Using pegs and ropes creates straight rows with equal spacing, ensuring that every single corn plant gets its fair share of sunlight, air, and soil moisture without overcrowding.
ga: Kɛtsɔ ŋtayaai kɛ kpã nɔ lɛ, afee ŋtayaai ni ja ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli fe nine.

english: What happens to my maize crop if I plant the seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When corn plants are crowded, their leaves block sunlight from each other and their roots fight for nutrients, which results in thin, weak stalks and empty or small cobs.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko loo dumɔwui bibii baa.

english: How does planting my corn in neat straight rows make farm work easier for me later?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ fɛo ni ja mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni efee mlɛo akɛ matsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ mli?

english: Straight rows leave clear walking paths, making it simple to walk through the farm to weed, apply fertilizer, spray against pests, and harvest without stepping on or damaging your crops.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni ja ni gbɛi lɛ mli tse. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ oootsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ojie jwɛi lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni okɛ tsofa afɔ nɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote mli. ni okpa ni okpaaa onibii lɛ anɔ loo ofiteee.

english: How deep should I dig planting holes for my corn seeds to make sure they sprout properly?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafo mi ŋmãa dumɔwui adumɔ bu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Corn seeds should be planted in small holes about 3 to 5 centimeters deep, which gives them enough moisture to germinate while keeping them safe from heat drying them out or birds eating them.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ bu bibii amli, ni mli kwɔ aaafee sɛntimitai 3 kɛyashi 5, ni baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa lɛ shɛɛɛ la ni haa dumɔwui lɛ gĩɔ loo okpoi yeɔ amɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when the sun gets very strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni hulu lɛ mli wa waa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are tender and sensitive to direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around them provides a natural canopy that protects them from sun scorch and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛ nuɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ he. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni abɔle amɛhe lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he lɛ baa. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to grow healthy green leaves. Adding poultry manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant stay healthy and produce bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehe miihia ŋmãa babaoo koni ebaakwɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi amli ŋmeii loo nitrogen ŋmeii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil, giving your maize extra nutrients without needing expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ naa niyenii krokomɛi ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to feed the plant. Staking lifts the foliage off the ground, exposing leaves to sunlight and preventing fungal diseases from soil splashes, leading to larger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni eye ebua tso lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ baai lɛ awo hulu la mli ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ mli baa lɛ naa. kɛ yitso ni da fe tsutsu lɛ baa

english: Why do my cassava tubers become soft and rot quickly if left in the waterlogged soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much water in saturated soil cuts off oxygen to the cassava roots, causing root rot organisms to attack the tubers. Harvesting before fields stay waterlogged preserves tuber quality and prevents crop loss.
ga: Nu babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni eyi obɔ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi ni egbo lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ. Nikpamɔ dani ŋmɔji lɛ amli nu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tuber lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies spreading plant viruses. Controlling these pests early using soapy water sprays or neem oil prevents leaf damage and keeps the plant growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ tsei amli helai lɛ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Ni oooye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ mra Nu ni akɛ samla loo neem fɔ tsu nii lɛ baatsi baai lɛ afitemɔ naa ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni eda.

english: High heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients can stress tomato plants, forcing them to shed flowers to save energy. Keeping the soil consistently moist and rich in plant food helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli Loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ajie amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni tsei aniyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: Too many extra shoots (suckers) steal water and nutrients from the main stem. Removing all but one or two suckers ensures the main plant gets enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ shishi (tso lɛ) ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ, ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: What is causing the center leaves of my young maize to look chewed up with small holes?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ buji bibii ni ashɛreɔ?

english: This chew damage is usually caused by caterpillars like Fall Armyworm feeding inside the central leaf whorl. Applying recommended biopesticides or neem extract into the whorl early protects the plant's main growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii nɛɛ baa. Akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ ring lɛ mli mra. Ebuɔ hei titri ni tso lɛ daa yɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables spoil so fast before buyers reach my farm to purchase them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ baashɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛbahe lɛ?

english: Harvesting crops during the hottest part of the day leaves them full of heat, which causes rapid moisture loss and rotting. Harvesting early in the morning keeps crops cool and fresh longer, making them more attractive to buyers.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ amli adɔ waa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya ni efiteɔ. Nikpamɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Ha efee nɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ yɔɔ miishɛɛ waa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to build green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ baai eŋɔli ni etsɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas trap nitrogen food from the air into their roots, which naturally enriches the soil and feeds the neighboring maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen niyenii ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I avoid putting chemical fertilizer on my crop when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ahe beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve safely into the ground. When applied to dry soil, the concentrated chemical acts like harsh salt and burns the young roots.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ Tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi bibii.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain causes standing water, the roots drown because they cannot breathe underground, causing rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni no haa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves to conserve water and protect themselves from drying out, though planting shade trees helps protect them from harsh weather.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe moŋ, shi.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the stems of my crops keep the soil moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ashishifãi yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Dry grass acts as a protective blanket (mulch) that shades the dirt from direct sunlight, preventing water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. (Mulch) ni buɔ muji he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya

english: Why do extension officers advise me to cut off extra suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: Extra shoots steal plant food and water from the main stem. Removing them allows all nutrients to go into making one heavy, healthy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ tso lɛ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ehe koni ekɛfee plantains ni tsii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plant flowers fall off without turning into fruit when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high or water is scarce, tomato plants experience heat stress and shed flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu faaa lɛ Tomato tsei kɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ kpeɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to feed the tubers underground. Climbing stakes lift the leaves high up into the sun and away from ground pests.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Tsoi lɛ anɔ kwɔɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la mli ni ekɛ ehe kpaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling into tight little balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bɔɔlu bibii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or mites sucking the sap from young leaves and spreading plant diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ kɛ tsei ahelai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which acts as plant food. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizers like NPK or well-composted animal manure helps the leaves produce energy and stay green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii kɛha tso lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi ŋmɔji.

english: Why is it bad practice for me to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ gbonyo akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and lets soil-borne pests and diseases multiply. Rotating your crops with beans or cowpeas helps restore soil fertility naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni amɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ. Nibii ni akɛ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if animal manure is ready to put on my farm, or if it will burn my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii efee klalo akɛ akɛbaawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Aloo ebaashã midumɔ nii lɛ?

english: Manure is ready when it is cool to the touch, dark in color, and smells like fresh soil rather than strong ammonia. Hot, fresh manure releases gases and heat that can scorch delicate plant roots.
ga: Manure lɛ efee klalo kɛji edɔ kɛta he, eyɛ ediŋŋ, ni eŋɔɔɔ tamɔ muji hee fe ammonia ni akɛwo mli lɛ. Nuŋtsɔ hee ni mli edɔ lɛ jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ dɔlɛ ni baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow heavy green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil forces cowpeas to focus energy on stem and leaf growth instead of flowering. Adding phosphorus helps the plant shift its energy toward producing strong, full pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsina ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai ni miida lɛ ahe nii moŋ fe ni eeewo fɔfɔi. Fosfɔs ni yaa hiɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsakeɔ ehewalɛ kɛyaa dumɔwui ni mli wa ni eyi obɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot in the soil before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ?

english: Root rot happens mainly when water collects around cassava roots in heavy soil during rainy periods. Planting your cassava on ridges or raised mounds lets excess water drain away quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or mites feeding on the plant juice. Spraying neem seed extract or insecticidal soap helps control these pests before they stunt growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ tso mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Neem dumɔwui amli nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛtsi amɛdalɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience severe heat, irregular watering, or a lack of calcium in the soil. Consistent watering and shading young plants during harsh heat waves helps fruits set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shɛ la ni naa wa waa he. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛhaa tsei bibii daa ni akɛ amɛ woɔ amɛhe shade yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily damaged by full sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have broad leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, protecting cocoa trees during their early growth.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛfiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa oya lɛ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my vegetables during the dry season?
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ afɔ aduawai anɔ nu?

english: Early morning or cool late afternoon is best because the soil absorbs water before the sun evaporates it. Watering during high heat wastes water and causes stress to the plant leaves.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa loo shwane kɛ gbɛkɛ ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ dani hulu lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ nɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ baafite nu ni ebaaha tso lɛ baai lɛ afee nɔ ni haoɔ.

english: Why should I remove weeds from around my crop plants while the crops are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Mi tsei lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow quickly and steal light, water, and soil nutrients meant for your crop. Clearing weeds early ensures young crops get the nourishment needed to grow strong roots and stems.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ mli lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei bibii lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why is it important for me to test my farm soil before I buy and apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maka shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ makwɛ dani mahe ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ?

english: Testing soil tells you exactly what nutrients your land is missing. Applying fertilizer without testing is like taking medicine without knowing your sickness; you might waste money on the wrong fertilizer or even harm your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa baatsɔɔ bo niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ ni bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ fɔmɔ kotoku mli ni okwɛɛɛ mli lɛ tamɔ tsofa ni oooye ni oleee akɛ hela mɔ bo. Obaanyɛ ofite shika yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa lɛ he loo ebaanyɛ eye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui.

english: How can I tell if my land's soil is exhausted and needs food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efo ni niyenii he miihia?

english: When soil is exhausted, your crops will grow slowly, their leaves may turn pale green or yellow early, and your harvest will stay small even when there is plenty of rain.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ, onibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. Ebaai lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ oya. Ni okpamɔ lɛ baakã he ahi shi bibioo kɛji nugbɔ nɛ babaoo po.

english: What will happen to my crops if I put too much fertilizer near their stems?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi tsɔ?

english: Too much fertilizer can burn the roots and leaves of your crops, causing the plant tips to turn brown and wither instead of helping them grow bigger.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ naagbeehei lɛ feɔ blɔfo ni egboɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: When is the best time for me to spread fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaafɔse ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Spread fertilizer when the soil is moist, usually right after a rain in the cool morning or late afternoon. Applying it on dry soil in hot sun causes it to evaporate or burn the plants.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afɔ nɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ nɛɔ sɛɛ yɛ leebi ni mli ejɔ loo shwane mli. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ atsɔ la loo eshã.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need shade crops like plantains planted next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantain ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sun. Plantains grow fast and provide living shade and soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ehaa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa waa.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa tree fall off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by drought, lack of soil nutrients, or insect attack. Good soil management and shade keep the tree healthy enough to hold its flowers.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa lɛ Shikpɔŋ kɛ hulutsoo nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa haa tsei lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and dry while hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: This is usually black pod disease, which spreads rapidly during wet weather. Clearing bushy weeds around the tree and removing the bad pods early keeps the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji black pod hela. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Ajieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ jwɛi tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli ni ajieɔ ŋmeii gbohii lɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Can using machinery or rough harvesting tools damage my cocoa trees for the next season?
ga: Ani tsɔnei loo nibii ni akɛkpaa nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ afite mi-cacao tsei lɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, if heavy tools or machines strip the bark or break the cushion spots on the tree trunk, the tree will not be able to produce new flowers and pods for the next harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ nitsumɔ dadei loo tsɔnei ni tsii gbala tso lɛ shishi loo amɛkumɔ hei ni fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ yɛ lɛ. Tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii heei kɛha kpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and skinny without producing good fruit when planted close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛwooo yibii kpakpai kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight and soil food. They spend all their energy growing tall to reach the sun instead of making fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛshɛɔ hulu lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Can I leave dried cocoa husks and weeds on my farm to feed the soil?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi kookoo ŋmeii ni egbi kɛ jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii?

english: Yes, allowing dry plant waste and husks to rot on the ground turns them into compost, which restores natural food and moisture back into your soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni egbi ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ ŋmeii ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa trees turning yellow and drying up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow root systems that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight and high heat. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to block the harsh sun and retain air moisture, the leaves burn and dry out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ ni baatsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi lɛ bɛ lɛ, Baai lɛ baashã ni amɛbaagbi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. If temperatures get too high or the plant lacks moisture, it cannot successfully pollinate its blossoms and sheds them to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo tso lɛ bɛ nu Amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee fɔfɔi lɛ pollination ni amɛjie amɛ kpo koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why are my pepper plants suddenly wilting and dying even when the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ?

english: This is usually caused by root rot or fungal wilt. When soil stays too wet without good drainage, harmful soil fungi attack the roots, destroying their ability to take up water and causing the plant to collapse.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni fiteɔ loo fungal wilt kɛ enɛ baa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni nu kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ. Efiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛbaaŋɔ nu ni ehaa tsei shwieɔ shi lɛ

english: Why do I see small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and tiny caterpillars inside the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ anɔ

english: This is typical damage caused by the Fall Armyworm. The adult moths lay eggs on young leaves, and once the caterpillars hatch, they feed aggressively on the tender leaves and burrow into the growing point of the maize plant.
ga: Enɛ ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm fɔɔ fitemɔ kɛbaa. Akpɔlɔi ni eda lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ baai bibii anɔ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ Ekɛ yiwalɛ yeɔ baai bibii ni efoɔ bu kɛyaa hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cowpea plants curling downward and turning pale green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle shi ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cowpeas is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids feeding on the undersides of the leaves. As they suck the plant's sap, they weaken the leaves and can spread plant viruses that distort growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ cowpea mli. beni amɛnuɔ tsei amli nu lɛ Amɛhaa baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ tsei amli helai ni fiteɔ amɛdalɛ lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce very thin tubers while my neighbor gets large, thick ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse waa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ná yitso agbo ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots remain small if the soil is packed too hard for tubers to expand, if plants are planted too close together, or if the soil lacks essential nutrients like potassium needed for tuber development.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Aloo kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ potassium, ni he hiaa koni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant maize on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot exhausts specific nutrients from the soil and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground, leading to lower yields each season.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baafite. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why are my crops growing slowly and looking pale even though I cleared all the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mijie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Even without weeds competing for space, crops will remain stunted if the soil lacks organic matter and nutrients. Continuous farming without adding compost, manure, or fertilizer drains the soil's natural strength.
ga: Kɛji akɛ jwɛi komɛi bɛ ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa he akaŋ po. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baakã he ahi shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli awa yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why did my maize seeds fail to sprout after I planted them right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain often moistens only the top layer of soil. If a dry spell follows immediately, the heat bakes the upper soil layer and dries out the seeds before their roots can reach deeper moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ mli fũuɔ. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ba amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ shãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni egbiɔ dumɔwui lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains turn into powder and get full of small insects after a few weeks in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ tsɔɔ powda ni eyi obɔ kɛ kooloi bibii yɛ otsii fioo komɛi ni akɛto lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grain weevils attack stored maize if the grain was not dried completely before storage or if the storage space is not properly sealed. Residual moisture allows insects to breed rapidly and destroy the crop from inside.
ga: Dumɔwui amli ŋmeii baatutua ŋmãa ni ato lɛ kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto. aloo kɛji akɛ atsĩii he ni akɛ nibii lɛ toɔ lɛ naa jogbaŋŋ. Fɛ̃i ni eshwɛ lɛ haa kooloi fɔɔ oya ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ mli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the ears are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani toi lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running short on nitrogen, which is a key food for plant growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps keep the leaves green and boosts ear size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei lɛ daraa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni eha toi lɛ hu aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop dark, sunken rotten spots at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ diŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, usually caused by uneven watering and a shortage of calcium in the plant. Keeping the soil moist continuously helps the roots absorb the calcium needed for smooth, healthy tomatoes.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔ lɛ daa kɛ calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná tomato ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings get burned easily under direct, hot sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide leafy shade that cools the young cocoa trees and retains soil moisture during their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi oya. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ baaha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it important for me to put staking sticks next to my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei ama mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Staking allows yam vines to climb up and spread their leaves wide to catch full sunlight. Better sunlight access helps the plant make more energy, resulting in larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato wain tso lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi ni egbɛɔ efoji lɛ eshwaa babaoo koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa nɔ. Hulu la ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ hewalɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thick green leaves but produce small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ, ni eyɛ baai eŋɔlii ni mli tse, shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or gets over-fertilized, cassava plants put all their energy into leafy growth above ground instead of storing food in their roots. Reducing high-nitrogen feeds encourages the plant to expand its tubers instead.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔtsemɔ baawo tsei hewalɛ ni amɛgbala bulbs lɛ mli moŋ.

english: Why do my garden pepper plants wilt in the afternoon heat even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: Hot midday temperatures cause pepper leaves to lose moisture faster than roots can draw it from the ground. As long as the soil remains moist and the plants stand up straight again by evening, this temporary wilting is just the plant protecting itself from heat.
ga: Gbi mli latsaa ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee ŋmɔtɔ ni tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ be kukuoo mli ŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ ji tso ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he lɛ pɛ.

english: Having too many shoots or suckers causes competition for soil nutrients, water, and space. Keeping only one or two strong suckers allows the main plantain tree to produce bigger and heavier bunches.
ga: Nibii ni shwieɔ shi loo ŋmɔji babaoo lɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha plantain titri lɛ awo niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my young cassava plants right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-cassava tsei lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally adapted to sprout quickly and grab available water and plant nutrients before farm crops do. Clearing weeds early prevents them from crowding out young cassava shoots and starving them of sunlight.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mli oya ni amɛjieɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ lɛ amli dani ŋmɔ mli tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ akafee mɛi babaoo ni eha hulu la akashɛ amɛnɔ.

english: How does growing cowpeas or groundnuts in my field help the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in root nodules. When the crop harvest is done, that stored nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmaa lɛ agbe naa Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why did many of the maize seeds I saved in a jute bag fail to sprout after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo ni mikɛto jute kotoku mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Storing harvested seeds in damp or warm places allows unseen pests and mold to damage the tiny germ inside the seed. Seeds must be thoroughly dried and stored in airtight, cool containers to stay alive until the next planting season.
ga: Kɛ́ aha dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ mli edɔ loo edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni anaaa lɛ akafite helai bibii ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ. ni yɔɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ Esa akɛ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto tsɛnsi ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli koni ehi shi kɛyashi be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I just use the seeds from my previous harvest for my next maize farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛhaa mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from a previous crop, especially improved varieties, lose their strength and yield much less in the next generation. Buying fresh, certified seeds ensures strong growth, high yield, and protection against common diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsutsu ŋmɔshi nibii amli titri lɛ nɔ ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Amɛhewalɛ baa shi ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ haa amɛdaraa waa, amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ahe.

english: Why do I need to plant my cassava on mounds or ridges instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ?

english: Mounds and ridges loosen the soil so cassava tubers can expand easily and grow bigger. They also prevent rainwater from collecting around the roots, which stops root rot during heavy rains.
ga: Gɔji kɛ ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo ni amɛdara. Ehaa nugbɔ nu hu buaa ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why is my oil palm taking so many years to bear fruit after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii beni adu lɛ?

english: Oil palms need time to build a strong root system before bearing fruit. Using improved seedlings from certified seed centers shortens this waiting period, allowing the trees to start producing fruit in about three years.
ga: Be he miihia mu tsei lɛ koni amɛma shishifãi ni mli wa dani amɛwo yibii. Dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe ni jɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhei ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baaha mɛmɔ be nɛɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi aaafee afii etɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees turning yellow and drying up in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and short roots that burn easily under intense sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains next to them creates a protective canopy that keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience sudden stress from extreme heat or lack of water. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps the plant hold its flowers so they turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛkɛ haomɔ ni jɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ mli lɛ kpe trukaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli, ni no haa ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my plantain plant turn yellow and die off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Plantains shed older lower leaves to send available food and water up to the new leaves and growing fruit stem. Giving the soil rich compost or manure prevents premature leaf loss and improves bunch size.
ga: Plantains shwieɔ amɛbaai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni egbɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ lɛ aya baa heei kɛ aduawai tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ akafite oya, ni ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ ayi afa.

english: Why do caterpillars always hide and eat inside the central funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ be fɛɛ be ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ?

english: The inner funnel of the maize plant contains the newest, softest leaves that pests like the Fall Armyworm love to eat. Applying recommended treatments directly into the funnel early protects the growing tip from destruction.
ga: Baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ ni kooloi tamɔ Fall Armyworm sumɔɔ ni amɛye lɛ yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ mligbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ wo ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua. Ebuɔ ŋmei ni miida lɛ he koni ekafite.

english: Tomato leaves curl to protect themselves from harsh sunlight or because small insects like whiteflies are sucking their sap. Providing partial shade and controlling leaf insects keeps the plants healthy.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Aloo akɛni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies miinu amɛ nu lɛ hewɔ. Shade fioo ni akɛhaa kɛ baa mli koolooi akudɔmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni eha tsei lɛ ahi hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly right after I clear my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit hidden underneath the dirt for a long time. Clearing the soil exposes these seeds to sunlight and rainwater, causing them to sprout quickly. Covering open soil with dead grass or cover crops stops them from growing.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe teeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi be kakadaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui nɛɛ naa hulu la kɛ nugbɔ. Ehaa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya Shikpɔŋ ni agbele nɔ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbo loo ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Why do the stems of my yam plants wither and dry up before the yams are big enough?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ dani sweet potato lɛ da bɔ ni sa lɛ?

english: Yam vines dry up early when attacked by leaf diseases encouraged by wet, humid weather. Planting clean seed yams and keeping the farm well-ventilated prevents leaf decay so the tubers can reach full size.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ foliary helai, ni shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ tutua amɛ. Sweet potato dumɔwui ni he tse ni aduɔ kɛ ŋmɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ baaye abua ni baa lɛ akafite bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ ashɛ amɛdalɛ he.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves whatever food it has left to the newer top leaves so it can keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Tso lɛ baajie niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ eda.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. When whiteflies feed on the plant's sap, they pass on the virus, which stunts growth and distorts the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Kɛji whiteflies yeɔ tso mli nu lɛ Amɛbaagbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwã. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa oya, ni ebaa lɛ hu fiteɔ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the soil for days, air gets trapped out, allowing harmful fungi and bacteria to grow rapidly and rot the tubers underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baatsi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ daa oya ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition leaves you with weak plants and tiny harvests compared to giving each plant enough space to spread out.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Foidamɔ nɛɛ haa onáa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa fioo ko. Akɛ enɛ toɔ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ahaa tso fɛɛ tso koni egbɛ eshwa lɛ he.

english: Yam leaves need sunlight to produce energy that builds the tuber below the ground. Climbing up stakes lifts the leaves into the light and keeps them off the damp soil where diseases spread.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ akwɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa la lɛ mli, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, ni no ji he ni helai shwereɔ yɛ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small shoots growing around my plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajieɔ Mi plantain tsei lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main plantain trunk. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the mother plant has enough energy to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ plantain tso lɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja eko loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo fɔfɔi wuji ni tsii.

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the soil from the harsh sun to keep it cool and moist. As the grass decays, it turns into natural food that enriches your soil.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he koni eha edɔ ni edɔ. Beni jwɛi lɛ miifite lɛ Ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Why is it bad to put fertilizer on my crops right before heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash fertilizer away from your crops before their roots can drink it in. This wastes your money and can wash chemicals into nearby streams.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli dani amɛshishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Enɛ baaha ofite shika ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsofai afɔ faai ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their blossoms without producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed blossoms when stressed by drought, poor soil nourishment, or when tiny insect pollinators called midges are missing to fertilize the flowers.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni ehiii Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ bɛ yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ni akɛwoɔ fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their small fruits before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho aduawai bibii dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed young fruit when temperatures get too high or water is irregular. The plant drops extra load to protect itself from drying out and dying during stressful weather.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baawo yibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu lɛ ejaaa. Tsei lɛ baahe jatsu kroko koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni haoɔ mɔ lɛ amli lɛ he.

english: Why should I prune my cocoa trees instead of letting them grow naturally like my elders used to do?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mahã eda yɛ adebɔɔ naa tamɔ bɔ ni mi onukpai lɛ feɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Pruning removes old and diseased branches, letting air and sunlight reach all parts of the tree. This prevents fungal diseases from spreading and directs the tree's energy into growing bigger, healthier cocoa pods rather than just leaves.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egbɔ ni helai emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii helai agbɛ ashwã ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛfee kookoo ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe baai kɛkɛ.

english: Is it better to plant my crops close together to fit more on my land, or should I leave wide spaces between them?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi akɛ madu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ mihe lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ? Aloo esa akɛ mashi gbɛ ni da yɛ nakai tsei lɛ ateŋ?

english: Spacing crops properly gives each plant enough access to soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Planting too close causes trees to fight for resources, making them weak, unproductive, and more likely to catch diseases.
ga: Tsoi lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso naa shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la ni sa. Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nibii ni he hiaa lɛ amli. gbɔjɔɔ tso lɛ ni etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hela

english: How often do I need to walk through my field, and what should I be looking for on my plants?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔji amli? Ni mɛni esa akɛ matao yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ?

english: You should walk through your field at least once a week. Regular visits help you catch problems early by checking under leaves for tiny pests, spotting discolored leaves, and seeing if young fruits are rotting or falling off prematurely.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ otsɔ oyale mli shikome yɛ otsi mli. Saramɔi ni ooofee daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ona naagbai mra. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni oookwɛ kɛji ŋmeii bibii komɛi yɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, taomɔ baai lɛ ahe su ni etsake. ni okwɛ kɛji aduawai bibii lɛ egbo loo amɛgbee shi oya

english: How do weeds growing around my young cocoa trees affect how well the trees grow?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ saa tso lɛ dalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm by stealing soil nutrients, water, and sunlight that your cocoa trees need to thrive. Clearing weeds regularly keeps your trees strong and removes hiding places for damaging insects.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni o-cacao tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shi daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni otsei lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ, ni ejieɔ hei ni kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ.

english: Flowers drop off when the tree is stressed by dry weather, lack of soil nutrients, or insect attacks, or when there are no beneficial insects around to pollinate them. Proper watering, partial shade, and healthy soil help flowers turn into pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi ni baatutua amɛ loo be mli ni kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ ni amɛbaafee pollination lɛ, nu ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ fã ko kɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do young cocoa plants turn yellow and dry up when exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak roots that lose water quickly under full sun. Planting shade crops like plantains or shade trees alongside young cocoa protects them from burning until their roots are deep enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ shãa he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baa mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops every year even though I work it the same way as before?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii faaa daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mitsuɔ nitsumɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the soil every season to grow. If you keep farming the same land without adding manure, compost, or fertilizer to restock those nutrients, the soil becomes tired and worn out, leading to smaller yields.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be koni amɛdara. Kɛji otsuɔ shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he koni ekɛ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite ni ebaafite. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: What can I do to keep my farm soil moist during dry seasons so my plants do not die?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli koni tsei lɛ akagboi?

english: Covering the soil around your plants with dry leaves, grass, or crop remains—a method called mulching—acts like a blanket. It shades the soil, prevents water from evaporating in the hot sun, and keeps plant roots cool.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni okɛ baai ni egboi, jwɛi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ shwieɔ nɔ—nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching—tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning brown and rotting right on the tree during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal disease known as Black Pod, which thrives in cool, damp weather with high humidity. Removing infected pods immediately and pruning extra branches to let sunlight in helps stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Pod, ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya, ni afoɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi koni hulu la aba mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do the young shoots on my cocoa branches look scorched and dry as if burned by fire?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo niji lɛ anɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni shã ni amɛgbi, tamɔ nɔ ni la eshã amɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by tiny sap-sucking insects called mirids or capsids that bite into young shoots and stems. Treating the trees with recommended organic or chemical sprays during peak pest seasons stops them from ruining future harvests.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni atsɛɔ amɛ mirids loo capsids ni ŋmɔɔ tsei bibii kɛ tsei ashishifãi lɛ. Akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ tsuɔ he nii yɛ be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yeɔ tsei lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akafite wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do people tell me to plant plantains on the same land as my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko miikɛɛ mi akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in direct, intense sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act like umbrellas, providing shade and keeping the soil moist so the cocoa seedlings can survive their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha hulutsoo ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji koni kookoo dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow strong stalks and yield large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is a key plant food, or that the ground has too much water logged in it. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or compost helps restore their green color and health.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen, tso lɛ niyenii titri. Aloo etsɔɔ akɛ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehiɛ su kɛ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop every season drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the field. Rotating maize with crops like beans or groundnuts puts natural nitrogen back into the soil and keeps pests away.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ. Enɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ni ebu he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my cassava when the rainy season starts?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: You should plant after two or three strong, steady rains when the ground is wet deep down, rather than after the very first light shower. Planting in dry soil causes the cassava stem cuttings to dry up and die.
ga: Esa akɛ odu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei niji lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them without draining away properly during heavy rains. Planting your cassava on raised soil ridges or mounds allows excess water to run off, keeping the roots safe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. Amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie nu jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. ni oha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off before turning into actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by very hot dry weather, lack of water, or a shortage of essential nutrients like potassium. Regular watering and using balanced fertilizer keep the flowers strong enough to become fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, ni mli edɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium ni bɛ lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do weeds in my field cause my crops to give me a smaller harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm—they steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your main crop gets all the nourishment it needs to produce maximum yield.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli—amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ oŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaaha otso titri lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: What is eating small holes in the center leaves of my maize, and how do I stop it?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? ŋmãa baa teŋgbɛ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms hiding inside the growing point of the plant. Inspecting your field early and spraying safe, recommended insecticides early in the morning or late evening can control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mra. Ni tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my stored grains get moldy and spoil even after I dried them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmaa ni ato lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ kɛ́ akɛwo hulutsoo be mli po lɛ?

english: Grains spoil if there is still hidden moisture trapped inside them before storage, or if the storage space gets humid. Drying grains until they are hard enough to crack cleanly between your teeth and keeping them in sealed, moisture-proof bags keeps mold away.
ga: Nibii ni ŋmaa baafite kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ tee amɛmli lolo dani akɛto. aloo kɛji akɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli edɔ Okɛ ŋmãa lɛ agbi aahu kɛyashi ebaawa bɔ ni sa ni ebaagbala ŋmeii amli jogbaŋŋ Ni okɛto kotoku ko ni mli edɔ ni nu nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli koni eye ebua ni ŋmeii akafee nɔ ko.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, strong sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees to protect them from heat stress and keep the soil moist while they are young.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ gbekɛ lɛ.

english: Extra suckers steal water and nutrients from the main stem. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main plantain tree grows strong and produces a large bunch.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwu titri lɛ adara ni ewo niji wuji.

english: If your previous crops had pale green leaves, grew very slowly, or produced small harvests, your soil is low on nutrients and needs manure or compost.
ga: Kɛji akɛ onibii ni odu tsutsu lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛdaraa blɛoo waa, loo amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do farmers say planting groundnuts or beans together with my maize makes the soil better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ du ŋmei loo ŋmei lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts naturally pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, which helps feed neighboring plants like maize.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni aha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and dry up during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, humid weather. Pruning extra tree branches lets in air and sunlight to keep the pods dry.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji krokomɛi koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la aha ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: Excessive rain makes heavy soil waterlogged, starving roots of air. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away, preventing rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ feɔ nu. Shishifãi ni kɔɔyɔɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ gɔji loo ŋmeii ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ mli. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without growing fruit during the hot, dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil cause heat stress that prevents tomato flowers from setting fruit. Regular watering and light shade during hot spells help flowers stay on.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni haaa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii baa. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or animal manure helps the leaves stay green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli.

english: What is eating small holes in the fresh center leaves of my young maize plants?
