ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ anɔ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the growing tip. Catching them early with recommended biopesticides or ash saves the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni taoɔ niyenii yɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɔmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo sũ ba lɛ, abahere ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: Yam vines need tall stakes so their leaves can reach maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which travels down to swell the tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso kakadaŋŋ koni amɛbaa lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn yellow and rot whenever water gathers on my farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ be fɛɛ be ni nu baabua miŋmɔ lɛ naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When water stays on your land for too long, it fills all the tiny spaces in the soil and pushes out air. Crop roots need air to breathe; without it, they drown, rot, and cannot take up nutrients, causing the plant leaves to turn yellow and decay.
ga: Kɛ nu hi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Nu baayi he bibioo ko mli obɔ. fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ kpo. Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ ebɛ lɛ, ebaagbo nu mli ni enyɛŋ ená niyenii mli hewalɛ, ni no baaha tso lɛ baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi.

english: How can I tell if my farmland is waterlogged and unsafe for regular crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ mli eyi kɛ nu ni ehiii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ daa lɛ?

english: If rainwater sits on top of your soil for days without sinking in, or if walking on your field feels like walking on a soft, muddy sponge that smells bad, your land is waterlogged and needs drainage before planting standard crops.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nu lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli, Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ mli nyiɛmɔ haa onuɔ he tamɔ nɔ ni onyiɛɔ spunji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni mli ewo muji ni ŋmɔlɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe miihia ni ajie nu kɛjɛ mli dani adu tsei ni afɔɔ feemɔ.

english: Why do my crops fall over so easily when planted in soft, wet ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ adu yɛ hei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Soggy soil becomes too soft to hold plant roots tightly. Without firm soil to anchor them, strong winds or heavy rain easily pull the roots out of the mud, causing the crops to fall over.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ emɔ tso shishifãi lɛ amli shiŋŋ yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni baanyɛ ahi shi lɛ bɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ agbala shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli mlɛo. ha ŋmɔshi nibii akumɔ

english: How will digging big gutters across my flooded farm help my crops survive?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋshɔ agbo ko ni mafo yɛ miŋmɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi?

english: Digging wide channels gives trapped rainwater a clear path to flow off your field. Removing excess water allows air back into the soil so your crops' roots can breathe and absorb nutrients properly.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ ni mli kwɔ ni ooofo lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni emɔ mli lɛ naa gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ejoɔ foi kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nu ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu jogbaŋŋ ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Where should I direct the water when I dig drainage trenches on my wet farm?
ga: Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ matsɔɔ nu lɛ gbɛ kɛ́ miifo nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli efɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should dig gutters following the natural slope of your land so gravity pulls the trapped water downhill, leading it safely off your farm into a nearby stream, ditch, or community drain.
ga: Esa akɛ otsa nu ŋshɔi yɛ bɔ ni jɛmɛ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ ha lɛ naa. koni eha hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ agbala nu ni emɔ mli lɛ kɛba gɔŋ lɛ shishi ni ejie kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe kɛya faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ, nubu loo akutso lɛ mli nu ni hoɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important to construct drainage gutters before planting season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ama nu tsɔne dani ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ aje shishi lɛ?

english: Preparing drainage channels when the soil is still manageable prevents sudden floodwaters from drowning young seedlings or washing away your newly planted seeds during heavy rains.
ga: Kɛ́ asaa nu ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ yɛ be mli ni anyɛɔ akwɛɔ nɔ lolo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu afua ni baa trukaa lɛ akafo tsei bibii loo dumɔwui heei ni adu lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: How does making high soil mounds help root crops like cassava survive on low, wet ground?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Building raised mounds lifts the planting zone above standing water. This keeps the crop tubers safe in dry, airy soil while excess water collects harmlessly in the spaces between the mounds.
ga: Awo tsu lɛ nɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ, ni ewoɔ he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa nu ni yɔɔ dioo lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni fa fe nine lɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ hei ni yɔɔ gɔji lɛ ateŋ lɛ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Why should I not leave my swampy land idle and uncultivated?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ mishikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ lɛ nɔ efee efolo ni atsuuu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving wet land idle allows aggressive weeds, bush, and crop pests to multiply freely, making the land harder and more expensive to clear and restore in the future. Active management keeps the soil productive.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi hei ni efɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuuu nii lɛ, ehaa jwɛi, jwɛi, kɛ kooloi ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ayi fa babaoo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni ajieɔ kɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni ejara hu wa waa wɔsɛɛ. Nɔkwɛmɔ ni yaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii.

english: Can I still harvest good crops from land that stays wet for most of the year?
ga: Ani manyɛ maná ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpa lolo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu yɔɔ nɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli be babaoo lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, wet land can be very productive if managed well. You can either build drainage channels to dry the land for normal crops or plant water-loving crops like rice, sugarcane, or cocoyam that thrive in soggy conditions.
ga: Hɛɛ, hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Obaanyɛ ofee nu homɔ gbɛi ni okɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ daa loo odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni sumɔɔ nu tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo kookoo ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli.

english: What happens to seed maize if I plant it directly into waterlogged soil?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmãa dumɔwui anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Maize seeds require oxygen to sprout. If planted in standing water or completely soaked mud, the seeds will rot in the ground before they ever have the chance to germinate.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui he hiaa kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ nu ni ekã shi loo muji ni mli edɔ mli Dumɔwui lɛ baagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛná hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my groundnut plants drop their flowers without producing any pods on the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ ekwɛɛɛ eniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts do not grow pods on their branches. After flowering, the plant sends down long stems called pegs directly into the soil, and the groundnut pods grow underground. Soft soil makes it easier for these pegs to dig in.
ga: Peanuts kwɛɛɛ ŋmeii yɛ amɛniji anɔ. beni ewo fɔfɔi sɛɛ Tso lɛ tsuɔ ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. ni ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa ŋmei lɛ ni efoɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers drop off during very hot dry periods without forming peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli ni ekɛ pepper baaa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air cause severe stress to pepper plants. To save water and survive, the plant naturally drops its blossoms until cooler temperatures or moisture levels return.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa pepper tsei anɔ. Bɔni afee ni akɛ nu ato ni ehi shi Tso lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi yɛ e diɛŋtsɛ ehe kɛyashi hulutsoo loo hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Yams tell you they are ready when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up completely at the end of the rainy season, indicating energy has fully stored in the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes kɛɔ bo akɛ amɛfee klalo beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbiɔ kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ abua hewalɛ naa yɛ yitso lɛ mli kɛyashi eyi.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential plant food. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps restore their green color and growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my watermelon fruits stay small and taste watery instead of sweet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ ji bibioo ni eŋɔɔɔ tamɔ nu yɛ ŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Watermelons need full sunlight and soil rich in potassium to build natural sugars. Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer causes lush green leaf growth but leaves the fruits small and bland.
ga: Hulu ni fa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ he miihia watermelon koni ekɛfee sugars yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baaha baai lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Shi aduawai lɛ baafee bibioo ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does my maize crop fall flat on the ground after strong winds and rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize falls over when its roots do not have enough support in shallow soil. Mounding up dirt around the base of the stalk gives the roots a firm hold against wind and water.
ga: Abɛi baashwie eshishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ eshishifãi lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu.

english: Why are my cowpea leaves covered in clusters of tiny black bugs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii diji akui ehà mi-cowpea baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Those tiny insects are aphids that suck vital plant juices from stems and leaves. Spraying them with a mix of mild soapy water or neem leaf extract controls them naturally.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tsei amli nu ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli ejɔ loo neem tso mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye nibii nɛɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up with yellow patches on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves with yellow spots are a sign of Mosaic Disease, carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems prevents this problem.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ ni miida lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are the seed heads of my sorghum crop turning into black powdery dust?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sorghum dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ miitsɔ sũ diŋ lɛ?

english: This black dust is caused by a fungal disease called smut. The powder contains spores that spread through infected seed, so using certified clean seed stops it from returning.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ soot ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ diŋ nɛɛ baa. Spores ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ dumɔwui ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli yɛ powda lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ dumɔwui ni he tse ni awo he odase lɛ atsu nii koni amɛkaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba.

english: Why do my tomato fruits split open on the sides right before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ afãi dani etsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they receive a heavy burst of water after a long dry period. The inside of the fruit grows faster than the skin can stretch, causing the outer skin to crack.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ kɛji akɛ aha lɛ nu babaoo beni egbi be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli fãa.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and leafy, or when heavy rains have washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii titri ko ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ. aloo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up tight and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies hiding underneath the leaves, or a plant virus passed on by those insects as they feed on the sap.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo tsei amli helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa beni amɛyeɔ tsofa lɛ mli nu lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high, when the soil dries out completely while flowering, or when there is not enough water to help the plant carry nutrients to the blossoms.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ. aloo be mli ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aya fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ bɛ

english: Why are my cassava roots remaining thin like sticks even though the leaves above ground look bushy and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ tamɔ tsei eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛji ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: When soil contains too much nitrogen or gets too much shade, cassava spends all its energy growing big leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo lɛ, ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai wuji lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ ashikishaŋ lɛ baato ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ,.

english: Why do tiny young cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the trees during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii Koni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tsei anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Small cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up due to Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in cold, wet weather when there is too much shade or not enough airflow around the cocoa tree.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ ŋmeii diji hela lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Beni hulutsoo loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔleɔ he lɛ fa babaoo Kokoo tsei ni fa bɔ ni sa

english: Can I put dried cattle manure directly into my farm soil before planting corn?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei ni egbi afata shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ dani madu ŋmãa?

english: Yes, dried cattle manure adds organic matter and plant food to the soil, but it is best to mix it into the soil a few weeks before planting so it can decompose properly without burning young seedling roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmei ni egbi lɛ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ tsei niyenii fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Shi esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi dani adu koni enyɛ efite jogbaŋŋ ni eshãaa dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans together in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that pull nitrogen out of the air and put it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that feeds the maize crop and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines wither and dry up early before the harvest season arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigbi oya dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines dry up early when underground pests like beetles eat the roots, or when root-rot fungi attack the tubers in wet soil, cutting off water supply to the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii ye shishifãi lɛ. aloo beni shishifãi ni egbo lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛyaa baai lɛ amli lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Why does my plantain sucker take so much longer to flower than my neighbor's plantain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain sucker lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi fe mikutsoŋnyo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers grow slowly if planted in packed soil without enough organic mulch, or in heavy shade, because plantains need rich soil, plenty of water, and sunlight to build up energy for fruiting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ blɛoo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli Enɛ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni baa nii, nu babaoo, kɛ hulu la he miihia plantains koni ekɛfee hewalɛ kɛha yibiiwoo.

english: Why do my harvested onions start rotting quickly inside the barn after I bring them in from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-onions ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eba lɛ?

english: Onions rot quickly in storage if they were harvested while the ground was still wet, or if they were not allowed to dry in the shade for a few days to harden their outer skins before storage.
ga: Sabala fiteɔ oya yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ akpa yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ aŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ ni egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli gbii fioo komɛi koni eha kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli awa dani akɛto.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen or the ground is soaked with too much standing water. Applying the right amount of fertilizer like NPK early gives the leaves their green color back so they can produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ miiye nitrogen loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ kɛ nu ni damɔ shi. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tamɔ NPK tsu nii yɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ ahe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ afee ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: How does planting soybeans help improve the soil for my next crop of maize?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ soybeans ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soybeans are special plants that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in tiny nodules on their roots. When you harvest the soy and clear the field, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil, acting as natural food for your next maize crop.
ga: Soybeans ji tso krɛdɛɛ ko ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ eshishifãi bibii amli. Kɛ́ okpa soybean lɛ ni ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha o-corn niyenii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing very tall and thin without giving me big cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛbɛ ŋmeii wuji komɛi lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the maize plants fight each other for sunlight and nutrients, causing them to grow tall and weak. Giving each plant enough space allows them to grow strong stems and feed big, heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Abɛi tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná shishigbɛ ni wa ni ebaaye ebua tso lɛ mli ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: What causes my soybean pods to fall off before the seeds inside grow full?
ga: Mɛni haa mi soybean ŋmɔji lɛ shwieɔ shi dani dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Soybean pods fall off early mainly when the plants suffer from dry weather during flowering or when sucking insects attack the young pods. Keeping the farm free of weeds and controlling insects early stops the plant from losing its pods.
ga: Soybean ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi mra titri lɛ kɛ́ tso lɛ na shihilɛi ni mli egbi yɛ fɔfɔi be mli loo kɛ́ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutua ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Ni aaaha jwɛi akafee ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ kooloi bibii ni akudɔɔ amɛ mra Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite eshishifãi.

english: What is crop medicine, and how do I know the right time to spray it on my maize?
ga: Mɛni ji tso tsofafeemɔ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ afɔ ŋmãa nɔ?

english: Crop medicines are protective chemicals that kill harmful insects or cure crop diseases. You should spray early in the morning or late afternoon when pests are active, and do it as soon as you notice the first signs of damage before the insects multiply.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsaa tsei ahe lɛ ji tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo tsaa tsei ahe helai. Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ leebi loo shwane mli. Beni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ bɔi nitsumɔ Ni okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ pɛ kɛji ona klɛŋklɛŋ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ efite lɛ, dani kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ afɔ.

english: How do I know if fall armyworms are attacking my maize field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ fall cutworms miitutua mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms leave ragged holes in the leaves and leave small piles of saw-dust-like waste inside the funnels of young maize plants. Checking your farm twice a week lets you spot these caterpillars early before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Cutworms ni egbee shi lɛ shĩɔ bu ni etse ehe yɛ baai lɛ amli ni amɛshiɔ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni abua naa yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ atsɔnei lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona ŋmeii nɛɛ mra. dani amɛbaakpãtã ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why did the spray chemical I bought fail to kill the insects on my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni miheɔ lɛ egbeee kooloi ni yɔɔ mi-abele lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Chemicals fail if you buy an fake product, mix it with too much water, or spray at the wrong time of day when rain washes it away. Using approved chemicals at the correct dosage ensures the medicine effectively clears the pests.
ga: Tsofai lɛ baafee nɔ ni ehiii kɛji ohe nɔ ko ni ji amale. Akɛ nu babaoo efutu mli Aloo akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be ni esaaa mli beni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni ekɛ nibii ni akɛfee lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. Tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ayibɔ ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tsofa lɛ gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I just save maize seeds from my last harvest to plant in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their strength over time, resulting in weak growth, uneven fields, and smaller cobs. Certified seeds bought fresh are specially bred to resist local pests, tolerate weather changes, and produce a bigger harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ. Omɔ ŋmɔji lɛ ebɔle amɛhe. ni cob lɛ ji bibioo Akwɛɔ dumɔwui heei ni ahe odaseyeli lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo

english: Why is my maize producing flowers early when the plants are still very short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ fɔ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ? Tso lɛ yɛ kuku waa lolo?

english: Maize flowers early when it faces severe stress like drought or poor soil nutrients, forcing the plant to produce seeds quickly before it dies. Preparing the land well and planting right at the start of the rains helps plants grow tall before flowering.
ga: Abɛi baawo fɔfɔi mra. Kɛji akɛ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa kpe, tamɔ hɔmɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ, Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tso lɛ awo dumɔwui oya dani egbo. Kɛ́ asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni adu kɛjɛ nugbɔ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi.

english: How can I tell when my soybeans are fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-soybeans lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Soybeans are ready when the leaves turn yellow, dry up, and fall off, leaving brown pods on the stem. If you shake a dry pod and hear the seeds rattling clearly inside, the crop is ready for harvest.
ga: Soybean lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛgbi, ni amɛgbee shi, ni amɛshi ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Kɛji okpokpo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi ni onu dumɔwui lɛ ni miihoso yɛ mli lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why should I build a small dam or pond on my land instead of relying only on rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ama faa loo nubu bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni akɛ he aaafɔ̃ nugbɔ nu pɛ nɔ?

english: A farm dam captures and stores rainwater during the wet season so you have a steady water supply to irrigate your crops during dry spells and keep farming continuously.
ga: Dam ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nugbɔ nu ni ekɛtoɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. No hewɔ lɛ oyɛ nu jɛɛhe ni oyɔɔ daa ni okɛbaafɔ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni oha okwaayeli lɛ aya nɔ.

english: Will having a water dam near my fields make my crop roots rot?
ga: Ani faa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ ko masɛi lɛ baaha tsei shishifãi lɛ agbo?

english: No, as long as the water is guided through controlled channels rather than flooding the field completely, a nearby dam keeps the surrounding soil moist without drowning your crop roots.
ga: Dabi, kɛji akɛ abaatsɔ gbɛi ni akudɔɔ nɔ atsɔɔ nu lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeeha ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu afu kwraa. Dam ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieee nu mli.

english: Is stored pond water good for my crops, or does it lose its nutrients over time?
ga: Ani nubu mli nu ni ato lɛ hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii? Aloo ani niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ baaje mli yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Stored rainwater in dams remains very healthy for crops because it settles naturally and often collects rich organic matter that nourishes the soil when used for watering.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni ato yɛ faa lɛ mli lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lolo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ shi ni esumɔɔ ni ebua nibii babaoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ kɛji akɛ awo nɔ nu lɛ anaa.

english: How do small water channels or paths on my farm help my crops grow better?
ga: Gbɛ bibioo loo gbɛjegbɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Water channels direct rain or stored water straight to your crops' roots instead of letting it wash away topsoil, helping the roots absorb steady moisture evenly.
ga: Nu tsɔnei lɛ haa nugbɔ loo nu ni ebua naa lɛ yaa otsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha efɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ nu lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why does heavy rainwater wash away my crops, and how do farm pathways fix this?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ midumɔ nii lɛ? Ni te ŋmɔ mli gbɛjegbɛi lɛ baanyɛ atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Uncontrolled rain rushes across land and erodes soil, but planned pathways and ditches give water a safe track to flow through your farm without damaging crop roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni akudɔɔɔ lɛ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Shi gbɛi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛ nubui baaye abua ni nu lɛ atsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe. ni efiteee tso shishifãi

english: How does digging small trenches along my crop rows affect how water reaches my plants?
ga: Te bibioo ni afoɔ lɛ Teɔ gbɛ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ saa nu ni shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Trenches allow water to soak deep into the soil right near the root zones, encouraging crops to grow deeper, stronger roots that can withstand hot weather.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa nu boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Ewoɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni baanyɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ naa.

english: Where is the best place to make water channels on my farm so all my crops get enough water?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni hi fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ mama nu gbɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Water paths should follow the natural gentle slopes of your land, allowing gravity to easily carry water from your main source down to every crop bed.
ga: Esa akɛ nu gbɛi lɛ anyiɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋshɔkpɔi ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛɔ ewoɔ nu kɛjɛɔ ohe titri lɛ nɔ kɛyaa dumɔhe fɛɛ saatso nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ.

english: How can I keep my vegetable crops alive during the long dry harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-aduawai lɛ ahi shi yɛ harmattan be kakadaŋŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli?

english: By storing water in dams or reservoirs during the rainy season and using water channels, you can continuously water your soil even when the rains stop completely.
ga: Kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛtoɔ faai loo nutoohei amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli kɛ nu gbɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ oya nɔ okɛ nu awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ekpa kwraa po.

english: Why do my crops wither so fast even a few days after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ oya nɛkɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi po sɛɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ lɛ?

english: Soil loses surface water quickly under strong heat, but managing water storage and controlled distribution paths keeps the subsoil moist for much longer.
ga: Shikpɔji lɛ anɔ nu lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi. Shi nu ni akɛtoɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajaa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ shishi sũ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Can I really harvest crops two or three times a year if I keep water on my farm constantly?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ loo etɛ yɛ afi mli kɛji mikɛ nu to miŋmɔ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be?

english: Yes, with a reliable year-round water supply like a dam, your crops receive uninterrupted moisture, allowing you to plant and harvest multiple cycles regardless of the season.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ nu jɛɛhe ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli tamɔ faa lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be. Ehaa onyɛɔ oduɔ nii ni okpaa nii shii abɔ ekɔɔɔ he eko be ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil, which acts like food for green leaves, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikpaa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot when planted in soil that traps too much water during heavy rains, which suffocates the roots and encourages fungal diseases to grow.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu babaoo hiɛɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela he hewalɛ.

english: Why do cowpea plants make my farm soil richer for the next crop I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina tsei baaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni madu lɛ?

english: Cowpeas have small nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and lock it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ bɔɔt bibii. Yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli

english: What is making holes in the leaves and center whorl of my growing corn?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni kɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele ni miida lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baa?

english: These holes are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hatch from eggs laid by moths and eat the tender inner leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni fɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper bushes curling upward and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is often caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap from young leaves, which deforms them as they grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ shoo beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings die when planted in open sunlight without shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo bɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that dry out and burn under full sun, so they need shade trees to protect them until their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni kookoo tsei lɛ aná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants fall off without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high during the heat of the day, or when the soil gets too dry, causing the plant to save energy by shedding flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be lɛ mli. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Ehaa tsei kɛ hewalɛ toɔ kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Yams need stakes to spread their leaves high in the air to catch sunlight, which allows the plant to produce enough energy to grow large tubers below ground.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia tso ko ni amɛkɛbaagbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã kɔɔyɔɔ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛnyɛ amɛmɔmɔ hulu la lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ bulbs agboi baa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why should I cut away small suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: Extra suckers steal water, light, and soil nutrients from the main plant, resulting in smaller bunches of plantain and slower growth.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu, la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa plantains lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛdaraa blɛoo.

english: Why does my rice crop bend over and fall flat to the ground right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shikpɔŋ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Rice plants fall over, or lodge, when given too much nitrogen fertilizer which makes the stalk grow too tall and top-heavy, or when planted too close together.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi loo amɛhiɔ shi kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo wo mli, ni no haa omɔ tsei lɛ feɔ shwiili ni amɛhe wa tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ

english: How can I test if seed maize I bought from the market will actually grow well before I plant my whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ dani madu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You can test a small batch first by placing ten seeds on a wet cloth in a warm spot. If eight or more sprout after a few days, the seeds are good quality and safe to plant across your whole field.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka kuu bibioo ko okwɛ. Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, kɛ dumɔwui 10 awo mama ni efɔ nɔ yɛ he ko ni mli edɔ. Yɛ gbii 2-3 sɛɛ lɛ, dumɔwui 8 loo nɔ ni fe nakai baakwɛ̃. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ, ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer to my maize in two small steps instead of pouring it all at once when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ awo mli yɛ gbɛi bibii enyɔ nɔ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ awo mli shikome beni oduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Maize feeds little by little as it grows. Giving it all the fertilizer at once is risky because heavy rains will wash it away before the young plant's roots are big enough to absorb it.
ga: Ayeɔ abele fiofio be mli ni edaa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli shikome lɛ, eyɛ oshara ejaakɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho lɛ dani tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ adara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Is it risky to plant only cassava on my whole land without mixing in other crops?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni mikome too midu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mikɛ tsei krokomɛi futuuu lɛ yɛ oshara?

english: Planting only one crop is risky because if a specific pest or disease attacks, your entire harvest can be lost at once. Mixing cassava with crops like cowpeas spreads your risk and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Tso kome pɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai komɛi tutua lɛ lɛ, ekolɛ Okpamɔ fɛɛ baafite shikome. Ni akɛ ŋmãa futuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmãa lɛ haa osharai feɔ srɔtoi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting so quickly even when they looked fine when I dug them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ oya nɛkɛ? Ni ehi jogbaŋŋ beni mifo mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that easily catch fungal infections through small scratches made during harvest. Storing them off the ground in a cool, well-ventilated shade prevents moisture buildup and stops rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni hiɛ ka ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ baanyɛ atswa amɛ oya kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni baa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni baa lɛ naa ni ebaakpa ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Leaf curling is a signal that tiny insects like aphids or mites are sucking the sap from your plants and spreading viruses. Treating them early stops the insects before the whole plant stops producing pepper.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites he okadi. Amɛmiinu tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛmiigbɛ hela lɛ amɛshwã. Amɛtsamɔ mra Ehaa kooloi bibii lɛ kpaa dani tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔtɔ feemɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves get dark spots that spread until the whole leaf turns black and dies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni baai lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Dark spots are caused by fungal diseases like Black Sigatoka, which spread through water drops and wind. Cutting off affected leaves and spacing your plantains allows air to flow through and stops the sickness from spreading.
ga: Fungal helai tamɔ Black Sigatoka ni nu mli nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Kpɔ̃ɔ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni oshi gbɛ yɛ plantains lɛ ateŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa roots are shallow and cannot reach deep groundwater, while harsh harmattan winds suck moisture out of their leaves. Planting shade trees or plantains protects young cocoa from direct sun and keeps soil moist.
ga: Kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he. yɛ be mli ni harmatta kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. The plant pauses fruit production until growing conditions become stable again.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Tso lɛ baakpa yibiiwoo yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa mɔ daa lɛ baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cabbage plants grow tall and thin instead of forming a heavy, round head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kaabaji lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ yitsei ni tsii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Cabbage plants stretch upward when they do not get enough direct sunlight. They require full, open sunlight to generate the energy needed to wrap their leaves tightly into a firm head.
ga: Kaabaji tsei lɛ baagbala amɛhe kɛji amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ. Hulu la ni eyi obɔ ni agbele naa lɛ he miihia amɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkɛbɔle baai lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee yitso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds around my cassava plants cause the tubers underground to stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi babaoo ebɔle he lɛ? Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your cassava for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. When weeds steal these resources, the cassava plant lacks the energy needed to expand its roots into large tubers.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ jwɛi ju nibii nɛɛ Cassava tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to intense direct sunlight and heat. Shade trees shield young cocoa leaves from burning and help keep soil moisture steady until the cocoa plants are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ buɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ he waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow and drying up before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is running out of nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the growing upper leaves and ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai ni miida lɛ kɛ toi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with big leaves but giving me tiny roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or water, the cassava plant puts all its energy into leaf and stem growth instead of storing starch in the root tubers underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ ashikishaŋ lɛ baato ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ,.

english: Why do my yam vines produce larger tubers when I train them to climb wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ hiɛ bulbs wuji beni mitsɔseɔ lɛ koni ekwɔ tso tso nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food. Staking spreads out the leaves so they catch sunlight easily, sending more nutrients down into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii. Staking lɛ gbɛɔ baai lɛ eshwaa koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ he mlɛo. Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo baa shi kɛyaa yitso lɛ nɔ.

english: When temperatures get too hot, tomato pollen becomes dry or inactive. Without successful pollination, the plant drops its flowers to save energy rather than forming fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato pollen lɛ mli egbi loo etsuuu nii. Kɛji pollination yeee omanye lɛ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my groundnut plants flower above the ground but form the nuts under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shi efeɔ peas yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated above ground, the plant produces long stems called pegs that grow downwards and push themselves into the soil, where the pod develops safely away from sun and surface pests.
ga: Beni atswa ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs. ni baakwɛ̃ kɛya shi ni ekɛ ehe awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa shweshweeshwe yɛ he ko ni hulu la kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why are my plantain bunches getting smaller each season even though the trees look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: Plantain stools naturally produce suckers (shoot offspring). If too many suckers are left growing around the main mother plant, they steal water and nutrients, resulting in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Plantain poop lɛ diɛŋtsɛ woɔ ŋmeii (ŋmeii bibii). Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ he lɛ, amɛbaaju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why are the new leaves on my pepper plants curling up and twisting together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually a defense or stress response caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking plant sap, or by viruses transmitted by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ ji hebuu loo hetoo kɛha nɔnyɛɛ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ kɛbaa lɛ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cowpeas produce plenty of green leaves during heavy rains but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa mli shi ŋmɔtɔi lɛ faaa kwraa lɛ?

english: Excess rain encourages cowpea plants to keep growing leaves and stems (vegetative growth) rather than switching to flower and seed production, which normally happens when the plant experiences mild water stress.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ woɔ cowpea tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛhiɛ amɛbaai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. (tso lɛ dalɛ) moŋ lɛ etsakeɔ kɛyaa fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui afeemɔ nɔ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ fioo.

english: Does upland rice need to grow in flooded water like the rice grown in valleys?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni adu ŋmɔ mli ŋmãa yɛ nu ni eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli tamɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: No, upland rice varieties are bred to grow in well-drained soil using normal rainwater, unlike lowland rice varieties that require standing water in paddies to thrive.
ga: Dabi, atsɔ ŋmãa henɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ anɔ koni akɛ nugbɔ nu ni nɛɔ daa lɛ atsu nii ni akɛdu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ ŋmãa srɔtoi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni biɔ nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli koni amɛdara lɛ ahe.

english: Why are insects destroying my cocoa pods even after I put so much hard work into cleaning the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miifite mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mitsu nii waa koni mikɛsaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ.

english: Pests like mirids (capsids) thrive when there is too much shade or unpruned branches. Hard work like weeding helps, but pests also require specific pruning to let in sunlight and timely spraying during peak bug seasons to stop them from damaging pods.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mirids (capsids) lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be fa tsɔ loo tsei niji ni afolɔko amɛhe. Nitsumɔ ni wa tamɔ jwɛi ŋmɔmɔ yeɔ ebuaa. Shi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hu biɔ ni afolɔ amɛ krɛdɛɛ koni hulu la ashɛ he. Ni okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ yɛ be mli yɛ be mli ni kooloi bibii lɛ fa babaoo lɛ koni ekpa ŋmeii lɛ afitemɔ.

english: What causes cocoa leaves to suddenly dry up and turn brown when I walk onto my farm?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ trukaa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mibote ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Sudden drying of leaves is often caused by sap-sucking pests like capsids or stem borers cutting off water flow, or fungal attacks at the roots. When insects attack in large numbers, the tree loses water faster than it can draw it from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ capsids loo stem borers ni foɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ agbiɔ trukaa. loo ŋmeii ni tutuaa shishifãi lɛ Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo tutua Tsei lɛ nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛjie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do young cocoa pods on my trees turn black and rot before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and overly shady conditions. Clearing excess shade and removing infected pods early stops the fungus from destroying the rest of your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ tsɔ, ni edɔ waa, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ. Ajieɔ hulutsoo ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni ekafite onibii ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why do pests seem to attack my cocoa farm more than my neighbor's farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo miitutua mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ fe mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Pests prefer farms with dense shade, high humidity, and unpruned trees because it gives them shelter from the hot sun. If your neighbor prunes more often or lets in more light, pests will naturally move to farms with darker, cooler conditions.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui sumɔɔ ŋmɔji ni shade mli wa, fɛ̃i babaoo kɛ tsei ni afolɔko amɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehaa amɛnáa abobaahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Kɛji okutsoŋnyo lɛ shwieɔ tsei lɛ shii abɔ loo ehaa la babaoo boteɔ mli lɛ, Pests lɛ baafã kɛya ŋmɔji ni shihilɛi lɛ mli ewo duŋ ni jɛmɛ ejɔ waa lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa farm will yield many bags of harvest this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ baajie baagi babaoo yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: A high yield of cocoa bags depends on how many young pods (cherelles) survive to full size without drying up or getting infected, which requires good rainfall, adequate sunlight, healthy soil nutrients, and low pest pressure.
ga: Cocoa kotoku mli yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo lɛ damɔ ŋmeii bibii (cherelles) babaoo ni hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ amɛdalɛ mli ni amɛgbiko loo hela emɔɔɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ biɔ ni nugbɔ anɛ jogbaŋŋ. hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kpakpai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shi

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce so many flowers, but very few turn into actual cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges for pollination. High temperatures, lack of moisture, or overuse of harsh chemicals can kill these midges, causing flowers to drop to the ground without turning into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Ale amɛ akɛ pollinating midges, hulutsoo ni naa wa, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ agbe nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ. Ha fɔfɔi lɛ agbee shikpɔŋ ni amɛkatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why does my cocoa harvest drop heavily even when I spend the exact same effort on the farm every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ni mikpaa lɛ eba shi waa nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi moŋ?

english: As cocoa trees age or as nutrients in the soil get used up, standard labor isn't enough. Yields drop unless soil fertility is restored with fertilizers or organic matter, and old or diseased branches are replaced.
ga: Beni kookoo tso lɛ daa loo niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa lɛ, Standard labor lɛ faaa Yibiiwoo baa shi ja akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ba ekoŋŋ. ni akɛ niji ni egbɔ loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ato najiaŋ

english: Why do some crop years turn out very bad for cocoa across Ghana while other years are very good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ehiii kwraa kɛha kookoo yɛ Ghana fɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni afii krokomɛi hi waa lɛ?

english: Cocoa crops rely heavily on predictable rainfall patterns. Severe droughts, extended Harmattan dry winds, or unusually heavy rainy seasons cause widespread pod loss, stress trees, and lower harvests nationwide.
ga: Kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ waa. Hɔmɔ ni naa wa, Harmattan hɔmɔ be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ kɛ pod ni fiteɔ babaoo, tsei ni haoɔ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ maŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ baa.

english: How does severe hot, dry weather affect how my cocoa trees behave?
ga: Te shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa ni egbiɔ waa lɛ saa cacao tsei lɛ ajeŋba he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: During intense heat and drought, cocoa trees drop their leaves and shed young pods (called cherelle wilt) to conserve water and protect themselves from dying, which reduces the total crop yield.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Cacao tso lɛ baashwie baai kɛ eshishifãi bibii lɛ anɔ. (ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherry wilt) koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ gbele he Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ aba shi.

english: How can I protect my cocoa trees from failing when a bad dry season comes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-kookoo tsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbee shi yɛ hulutsoo be ni ehiii fe fɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Planting shade trees alongside cocoa, keeping farm mulch on top of the soil, and avoiding over-pruning right before the dry season helps retain soil moisture and shields young cocoa plants from heat stress.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi Ni aaawo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ni atsi he kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ fe nine dani hulutsoo be lɛ baashɛ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni ebu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and dry up when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains nearby creates shade and traps moisture, protecting young cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ehaa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Buu kookoo bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the tree during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, dark conditions. Pruning excess branches lets sunlight and air into the canopy, which dries out moisture and prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ duŋ shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the leaves on my growing maize plant turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant leaf growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni tso lɛ baai lɛ adara lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ ahe afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni eha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny caterpillars hiding inside the whorl?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni etse ehe lɛ? ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii ni Ehiɛ amɛhe yɛ loop lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed on tender plant leaves. Inspecting leaves early and applying approved pest control methods, like neem seed extract or targeted spraying, stops them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei ahe baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ mra ni okɛ gbɛi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akudɔ kooloi tamɔ neem dumɔwu mli nu lɛ atsu nii. loo targeted spraying Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows maize pests to multiply. Rotating your crop with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ feɔ babaoo. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know which direction to plant cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava niji lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the small leaf buds on the stem cutting and make sure they are pointing upward toward the sky. Planting stems upside down forces shoots to grow downward first, resulting in weak growth or failed crops.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tsei bibii lɛ. yɛ tsei ni afolɔ abɛŋkɛ kpaakpa lɛ anɔ Ni okwɛ koni amɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Tsoi ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ Nyɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shishi klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraaa jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to expose maximum leaf area to sunlight for food production. Keeping leaves elevated also prevents them from touching wet soil where fungal diseases easily spread.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni eha hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ aba baa lɛ he lɛ bɔni afee ni niyenii aba. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ wo ŋwɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ akashɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when there is too much standing water on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ? Ani nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava roots need oxygen in the soil to stay healthy, but flooded soil drowns the roots and encourages rot. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shi shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ewoɔ fitemɔ he hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling upward and turning yellow during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is often spread by tiny insects like whiteflies or caused by heat and water stress. Using insect-proof netting, mulching soil with dry grass to retain moisture, and spraying safe insecticides keeps plants healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ loo dɔlɛ kɛ nu mli haomɔ hewɔ lɛ gbɛɔ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ eshwaa. Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ Akɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ akahi shi. Ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhaa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and applying balanced fertilizer encourages flowers to turn into healthy pepper fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ mli edɔ waa, nu bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct sunlight while their roots establish. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or cassava alongside them shields the tender cocoa leaves from harsh sun and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛma shi lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantain loo cassava kɛfata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the leaf tips usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy green growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure will restore nutrient levels.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do farmers recommend that I plant groundnuts or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans can pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Planting them with maize acts as a natural fertilizer, improving soil health and boosting your maize yield.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ agbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abele ni aduɔ lɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ aya hiɛ ni oha o-abele yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot mainly when rain water accumulates around them without draining. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water flow away from the root system.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ babaoo kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua amɛhe naa. ni nu shwieee shi Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants before producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ tomato tsei anɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plants experience extreme heat, dry soil, or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the root area helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shɛ la ni mli edɔ waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aaaha ebɔle he lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and stopping the plant from growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by small pests like thrips or aphids sucking sap from the leaves. Spraying early with neem extract or soapy water helps control these insects so new leaves grow healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Ni akɛ neem mli nu loo nu ni mli edɔ baashwie nɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ. koni baai heei lɛ akwɛ̃ waa

english: How can I prevent weeds from taking over my farm without using expensive chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi jwɛi ni yeɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa ni mikɛ tsofai ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: Covering the bare soil between your crop rows with dry grass, straw, or leaves (mulching) blocks light from reaching weed seeds so they cannot grow, while keeping the soil moist for your main crop.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi, jwɛi, loo baai (mulching) ha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ odumɔ ŋtayaai lɛ ateŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi la naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ahe. bɔni afee ni ekakwɛ̃ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my maize seeds during the rainy season in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔ be mli yɛ Ghana?

english: It is best to sow maize after the soil has received two or three heavy, steady rains. This ensures the ground is deep moist enough for seeds to germinate without drying out if rain stops for a few days.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu ŋmãa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni naa wa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa ni eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo komɛi.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the air to catch maximum sunlight for producing food. Staking keeps leaves off the wet ground to avoid leaf diseases and helps the plant send more energy down to grow bigger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni foliar hela akamɔ tso lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo woɔ shi koni ekɛ bulbs wuji akwɛ̃.

english: What is making ragged holes in my maize leaves with tiny green droppings inside the funnel of the plant?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ? yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the central shoot of young maize plants. Applying recommended organic remedies like wood ash or registered pesticides directly into the funnel early in the morning kills the caterpillars.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ he nii tamɔ tso mli sũ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni aŋmala awo wolo nɔ lɛ wo ŋmei lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my crops take longer to harvest than the exact number of days I was told they would take?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiye be babaoo fe gbii abɔ ni mikɛɛ ebaahe lɛ?

english: Maturity periods given by seed producers are estimates based on standard conditions, but actual growth time changes depending on local variations in rain, sunlight, and temperature during the growing season.
ga: Be ni dumɔwui lɛ adaramɔ ni mɔ ni feɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛhaa lɛ ji akɔntaabuu ni damɔ shihilɛi ni sa nɔ. Shi dalɛ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ baatsake. Edamɔ he ni nugbɔ nɛɔ, hulu la kɛ latsaa ni tsakeɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops start flowering early when there is a sudden dry spell in the middle of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi mra be mli ni hɔmɔ baa trukaa yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: When crops experience sudden weather changes like mid-season drought, they experience stress and rush to flower early to produce seeds before they dry up.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa kpeɔ, tamɔ hɔmɔ ni baa yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Amɛkɛ nɔnyɛɛ kpeɔ ni amɛfeɔ oya koni amɛyawo fɔfɔi mra koni amɛwo dumɔwui dani amɛgbi.

english: How do I know the best time to plant my seeds now that the rainy season changes constantly?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Instead of relying on fixed calendar dates, wait to plant until the ground has received consistent, deep rain so the soil holds enough moisture to sustain the young seeds.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ohe afɔ̃ kalanda gbii pɔtɛɛ anɔ lɛ, Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaya nɔ be fɛɛ be bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua dumɔwui bibii lɛ.

english: Why does strong wind cause my crop leaves and flowers to fall off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa haa mitsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Strong winds rapidly pull moisture out of plant leaves and physically shake the plant, forcing it to drop flowers and leaves to conserve water and protect itself from snapping.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya. ni ekpokpo tso lɛ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ ajie fɔfɔi kɛ baai koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ he.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer or spray my farm when the weather looks like it might rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ awoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo ashwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ lɛlɛ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni nugbɔ baanɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes away fertilizer and farm sprays off the crops and out of the soil before the plants have a chance to absorb them, wasting your effort and money.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ amɛ. Eji omɔdɛŋbɔɔ kɛ oshika fitemɔ.

english: Why does my land seem to lose its power to grow good crops after farming it for many years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ afii babaoo ni mikɛtsu nii yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil has a natural limit of nutrients, and harvesting crops repeatedly draws out these nutrients without replacing them, leaving the earth exhausted over time.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ji nɔ ko ni niyenii mli hewalɛ faaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ shii abɔ. ni nɔ ko bɛ ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Can I plant many seeds close together on a small plot of land to get a bigger yield?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui babaoo? Dumɔwui lɛ kpɛtɛɔ amɛhe yɛ he bibioo ko. Bɔni afee ni aná nibii babaoo ni jɛɔ mli baa?

english: A fixed piece of land has limited space and nutrients, so planting too closely forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil power, resulting in smaller, weaker crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ bɛ he ko ni eyɔɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: How can I restore the natural power of my soil without buying expensive materials?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ekoŋŋ ni miheee nibii ni jara wa?

english: You can restore soil strength naturally by leaving crop remains to rot on the field, applying animal manure, or rotating your crops so nature can rebuild soil fertility.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ tsei ni eshwɛ ni oooshi koni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ kooloi ashishifãi atsu nii loo otsake ŋmɔshi nibii koni adebɔɔ anyɛ ama shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Leaves roll up or wilt temporarily in intense heat to reduce the leaf area exposed to the sun, preventing the plant from losing too much water.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgboɔ be kukuoo ko yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli koni ebaa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Tsi tsei anaa koni amɛkafite nu babaoo tsɔ.

english: Why do my crops look different from season to season even when I plant the exact same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ srɔtoi yɛ be fɛɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Crops respond continuously to changing environmental conditions like shifting temperatures, wind, and rain amounts, causing their growth behavior and appearance to vary each season.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ shihilɛi ni tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be tamɔ hulutsoo be ni tsakeɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ he nii, ni no haa amɛdalɛ subaŋ kɛ amɛhefɛo lɛ feɔ srɔtoi yɛ be kɛ bei amli.

english: During the dry Harmattan season, cocoa trees lose water quickly through their leaves. Dropping yellow leaves is the tree's natural defense to save water and survive, but planting shade trees reduces this stress and keeps the cocoa canopy greener.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Baai ni egbee shi ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi shi. Shi tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ lɛ haa nɔnyɛɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa Cocoa Roofs lɛ feɔ nɔ ni kɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kpãaa gbee.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees on the same plot with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide big leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting tender cocoa plants during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ cacao tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and tall with small cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ amli tsei ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ Dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, they compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Instead of using energy to grow thick stems and large cobs, they stretch upwards trying to reach sunlight.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii koni akɛkwɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji. Amɛkpãa amɛhe koni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛmɔmɔ hulu la lɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with yellow powder in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ powda ni ji yellow powder yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar eating tender leaf tissue. The yellow powder is its waste, and if left untreated, the pest destroys the growing center of the maize plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ahe fãji. Powda ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji jwɛi. ni kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ he ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why should I plant cassava stem cuttings at an angle instead of sticking them straight down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi yucca tsei lɛ aniji lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni madu shi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems at a slanting angle buries more growth nodes under the soil, encouraging more roots to form and giving you a bigger yield of tubers compared to planting straight up.
ga: Kɛ́ adu cassava tsei yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ, ebaafu shweremɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa su babaoo. ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo kɛ akɛto tsei ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ he

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb up as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food that expands the tuber underground. Staking spreads the leaves out to catch maximum sunlight instead of letting them bunch up or rot on damp soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking gbɛɔ baai lɛ eshwaa koni ená hulu la babaoo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha amɛbua amɛhe naa loo amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crop yields get smaller every season if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa daa afi kɛji miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season. Rotating your maize plot with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts gives the soil a rest and naturally refills lost nutrients.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Abɛi ŋmɔji ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ tsuɔ nii Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ niyenii ni elaaje lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or groundnuts makes the soil better for other crops later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu tsina loo ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes have special nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground as plant food, naturally fertilizing the soil for the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ akɛ tsei aniyenii. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when stressed by severe heat, irregular watering, or poor nutrients. When stressed, the plant sheds flowers to conserve strength for survival rather than making fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaaa amɛ daa loo niyenii ni esaaa Kɛ́ haomɔ ba Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsei lɛ baawo yibii lɛ, amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ mli koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and yellow even when there is good rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, fertilizer, and light away from your crops. Even with good rain, your crops stay hungry because the weeds consume the soil nutrients first.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize plants keep turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to build green leaves. It often happens when the soil is worn out or after heavy rains wash away the nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli Bei pii lɛ ebaa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ efite loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ haa niyenii lɛ laajeɔ.

english: Is it bad if I keep planting cassava on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni ehiii kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi?
