english: Yes, planting cassava in the exact same soil every year drains all the nutrients out of the ground and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil, which leads to smaller harvests over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ajɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ faaa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and cannot handle direct afternoon sun. They need nurse crops like plantain or cassava planted beside them to provide shade and trap moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ shwane mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao nurse tsei tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni ekɛ hulutsoo aha ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baaná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before any tomatoes start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. When the plant feels stressed, it drops its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Tomato tsei baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ latsaa ni naa wa he, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kpakpai. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ ni ekɛha ehe ahi wala mli lɛ he.

english: How can I tell if my pepper leaves are curling because of small insects or because of the sun heat?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmeii bibii ebɔle pepper baai ahe? aloo yɛ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ

english: Leaves curling from sun heat usually bounce back and uncurl during the cool evening or after watering, whereas leaves curled by tiny pests like mites or aphids stay twisted and may look sticky or deformed.
ga: Baai ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ fɔɔ sɛɛkuu ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe yɛ gbɛkɛ mli loo beni awo amɛ nu sɛɛ. yɛ be mli ni baai ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Bei pii lɛ Amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee tamɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛhe ejɔ.

english: Why do caterpillars and worms suddenly appear in large numbers right after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii babaoo baa trukaa babaoo beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The start of the rainy season brings fresh, tender leaf growth, which triggers moth and butterfly eggs resting in the soil and weeds to hatch all at once to feed on your young crops.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee kɛ baai heei kɛ dalɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo baa. Wo ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii akui hewalɛ ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ hu afee ekome ni amɛye oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing small and bent instead of long and thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams struggle to expand when the soil is hard, stony, or compacted. Creating tall, loose soil mounds gives the yam tubers room to stretch and grow deep and fat.
ga: Sweet potatoes baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni egbɛ eshwa kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Gɔŋ kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni afee lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ fɔ.

english: Why does my maize crop grow tall stalks but only produce tiny cobs with missing grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kakadaji shi ŋmeii bibii pɛ yɔɔ lɛ? He ni dumɔwui bɛ lɛ?

english: Tall stalks mean the plant had enough food to grow leaves early on, but missing grains on cobs usually mean the plant lacked water or nutrients during the critical flowering stage when silks were receiving pollen.
ga: Tso lɛ tso kakadaŋŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ mra. Shi bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu loo niyenii bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔii ahe be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli, beni siliki lɛ nine shɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long dry spell. If seeds sprout during this false start, the hot sun will dry out the soil and kill the young seedlings before the main rains return.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ amale shishijee be mli Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni ekpata tsei bibii ahiɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔi wuji lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ aba.

english: Why do weeds always grow back faster than my main crop after I clear my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ be fɛɛ be beni mijie miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and can sleep in the soil for years. When you clear the land, they get immediate access to sunlight and water, allowing them to sprout faster than cultivated crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo. Kɛji ojie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ Amɛbaaná hulu la kɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: Sir, why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build strong leaves. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients or when weeds steal food from the maize.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ loo kɛ́ jwɛi ju niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: What is eating small holes in the middle leaves of my corn stalks and leaving dark brown dust inside?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Abele tso lɛ teŋ baa lɛ ni eshiɔ sũ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide in the center funnel of young maize. Early spraying with recommended insecticides or applying wood ash into the plant funnels helps destroy them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra Aloo, tso mli sũ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni efite amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them on cleared land without shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse ni hulutsoo bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under full sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain or shade trees nearby provides shelter and preserves soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni aduɔ. Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ahi shi ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baaná shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot if heavy rains soak the farm close to harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ ŋmɔji lɛ bɛŋkɛ kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater stays on the land for too long, it smothers the roots, causing waterlogging and rotting in the wet ground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ.

english: Why is it necessary to lift yam vines off the ground using tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes exposes more leaves to sunlight, which the plant uses to produce food and grow big tubers underground. It also keeps leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ owó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la babaoo ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Akɛ tsei lɛ feɔ niyenii ni akɛduɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ he. Tsi fungal helai anaa

english: Why does my maize grow much bigger when I plant it on land where I harvested groundnuts last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa waa nɛkɛ kɛ́ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmãa yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans gather nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their roots. When harvested, they leave this natural fertilizer in the soil, feeding the next crop of maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Ebuaa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa ni ekɛwoɔ eshishifãi amli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my farmland get hard and dry out quickly after using artificial fertilizer for several years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli wa ni egbiɔ oya beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii afii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer feeds the crop but does not feed the soil itself. Adding organic matter like animal manure or compost helps hold moisture in the soil and keeps it loose and rich.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii shi amɛhaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni sũ lɛ mli ahi shi ni eye ebua ni eha sũ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without forming any tomatoes during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen in tomato flowers, preventing them from setting fruit. Giving plants sufficient water and using grass mulch around the base keeps root temperatures cool.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. ni ehaa etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from my pepper seedlings while they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ dumɔwui amli be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Young pepper seedlings grow slowly and easily get choked out by fast-growing weeds that steal water, light, and nutrients. Keeping the field clear early on allows peppers to grow sturdy stems.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui bibii lɛ daa blɛoo ni jwɛi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ haa amɛhe oya. Ni oooha he lɛ afee faŋŋ mra Ebaaha chili lɛ aná ŋmeii ni wa.

english: How can I protect my stored maize grains from weevils without using dangerous chemical powders?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmãa ni ato lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe ni mikɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Drying your maize properly until grains are hard, then storing them in airtight triple-layer hermetic bags suffocates insects and keeps them from destroying your harvest without chemical hazards.
ga: Okɛ o-corn lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ amli baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli, ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli ni yɔɔ fãi etɛ mli ni baaha ŋmɔlɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaatsi kooloi ni fiteɔ onibii lɛ anaa ni tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant different types of crops together in the same field instead of just one?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei babaoo yɛ he kome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ fe ekome pɛ?

english: Mixing crops like maize and legumes helps enrich the soil because certain plants add vital nitrogen back into the ground, which feeds neighboring crops and improves your total field yield.
ga: Nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei komɛi kɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ niyenii ni ehaa onibii fɛɛ ni onáa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why is it important to dig up and turn the soil properly before putting my seeds in the ground?
ga: Mɛni he je nɛ e he hia kaa a tsa zugba a nɛ a tsake lɛ saminya loko a ngɔ dumɔwuhi kɛ wo zugba a mi ɔ?

english: Digging softens hard ground so crop roots can easily push deep down to find water and nutrients, while also allowing air and rainwater to sink into the root zone.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni atsa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ afee blɛoo. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shishifãi baanyɛ atsɔ mli oya koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ nu shwieɔ shishifã lɛ he.

english: Why do birds and small animals start invading my field right after I dig and plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi kɛ kooloi bibii jeɔ shishi amɛtutuaa miŋmɔji amli beni mifo shi ni midu tsei amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Digging turns up fresh soil and exposes seeds, worms, and insects, making your newly planted field an easy feeding ground for birds and animals looking for a quick meal.
ga: Shikpɔŋ hee ni oootsu lɛ baaha dumɔwui, ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii aba shikpɔŋ hee nɔ, ni no baaha he ni odu ehee lɛ afee niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛha okpoi kɛ kooloi. Niyenii ni ayeɔ oya taomɔ

english: What does mixing organic manure into my soil actually do for my young plants?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa midumɔwui lɛ?

english: Mixing manure or compost into the soil feeds essential plant nutrients into the ground slowly and helps the soil hold onto moisture much longer during dry spells.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutuɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ yaa sũ lɛ mli fiofio. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli

english: How can new technologies brought by agricultural officers help improve the way my crops grow?
ga: Okwaafoi anitsumɔ he nitsulɔi kɛ ŋaalee heei eba Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua koni gbɛ ni mitsɔɔ nɔ miduɔ mitsei lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Modern tools and techniques are designed to improve planting accuracy, protect crops from pests, and help crops grow faster with less physical labor and waste.
ga: Afee ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nibii kɛ ŋaai koni ekɛha dumɔwui lɛ aya hiɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Buu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ni eye ebua tsei ni amɛdara oya kɛ nitsumɔ kɛ jwɛi fioo.

english: Why do my crops grow taller and healthier when I leave space between them instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ hewalɛ waa kɛ́ mishi gbɛ yɛ amɛteŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaving enough space ensures each plant gets its own fair share of sunlight, air, water, and soil nutrients without having to fight neighboring plants to survive.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa lɛ. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ awuu koni ehi shi

english: How deep should I cover my seeds when planting so they don't get eaten or washed away?
ga: Te esa akɛ maha midumɔwui lɛ anɔ ashɛ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu koni aye amɛ loo nu akaho amɛ?

english: Planting seeds at a depth about two to three times their size protects them from birds and heavy rains while still allowing them enough warmth to sprout successfully.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ aaafee amɛdalɛ toi 2-3 lɛ baabu amɛhe kɛjɛ okpoi kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ mli dɔɔ bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops droop and turn yellow during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: In extreme heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up, causing them to wilt and shed leaves to save moisture.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni eshwieɔ baai lɛ koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant the exact same crop on the same plot season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Repeatedly planting the same crop completely drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up permanently in your field.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwraa. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa.

english: Why do weeds sprout up so fast right after I clear and dig my land for new planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mijie sũ lɛ ni mifo koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Digging brings buried weed seeds up to the top layer of the soil where sunlight and rain trigger them to sprout quickly alongside your intended crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akumɔ lɛ baaha jwɛi dumɔwui ni afu lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Hulu kɛ nugbɔ lɛ baaha jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ oya kɛfata ŋmɔshi nibii ni osumɔɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it better for me to clear weeds from my farm when they are still very small instead of waiting until they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni Eji bibioo kwraa lolo lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ kɛyashi jwɛi lɛ aakwɛ̃?

english: Weeds are easiest to control before they develop deep roots or spread seeds. If you control them early before they grow big, you prevent them from stealing water and nutrients from your crops.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo fe fɛɛ akɛ abaaye jwɛi anɔ dani amɛwo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo amɛgbɛ dumɔwui amɛshwã. Kɛji okudɔ amɛ mra dani eda Obaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli.

english: Is there a way to stop weeds from coming up before I even see them growing on my plot?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni matsɔ nɔ matsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ dani mana amɛ po ni amɛmiikwɛ̃ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, controlling weeds before they sprout or right as they emerge—using early land preparation, mulching, or pre-emergence weed killers—stops them from establishing strong roots in your soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi ni oookudɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ loo beni amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ—ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ mra, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, loo tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi dani ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ—baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkatswa shishifãi ni wa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: When is the most effective time for me to apply weed killer on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weed killers work best when applied early, before the weeds grow tall and tough. Young, actively growing weeds absorb chemicals much faster and die completely.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛtsu nii mra. Dani jwɛi lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa Young, jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ tsofai lɛ oya babaoo ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: What should I do to my soil before planting to make sure weeds do not overpower my young crop seedlings?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee shikpɔŋ lɛ dani madu koni jwɛi akaye midumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ kunim?

english: Thoroughly clear and prepare your field before planting to destroy germinating weed seeds. Stopping weeds before your crops sprout gives your seedlings the best chance to grow without competition.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ ni osaa he lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani odu koni okpata jwɛi dumɔwui fɛɛ ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ ahiɛ. Kɛ́ okpa jwɛi dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ, ehaa odumɔwui lɛ náa hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛdaraa ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: How can I tell the difference between regular grass and dangerous weeds that will harm my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ jwɛi folo kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ oshara ni baaye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui lɛ ateŋ?

english: Look closely at the leaf texture and stem shape. Stubborn weeds like Cyperus often have distinct sharp, rough edges on their leaves and triangular stems, unlike soft regular grass.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baa lɛ he mfoniri kɛ eshishifã lɛ he jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, jwɛi ni wa tamɔ Cyperus lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛbaai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ jwɛi folo ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ he.

english: Why do some grass-like leaves cut my hands when I try to pull them out of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni tamɔ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ minine nɔ kɛ́ mibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni majie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certain grass family weeds have microscopic, saw-like rough edges along their leaves to protect themselves. These sharp edges make them tough to pull by hand and unpalatable for livestock.
ga: Jwɛi weku mli jwɛi komɛi yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ ahe koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ haa ewaa akɛ akɛ nine baagbala, ni kooloi hu ŋɔɔɔɔ.

english: Are all green plants on my farm that look like tall grass considered weeds?
ga: Ani abuɔ tsei eŋɔli fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni tamɔ jwɛi kakadaji lɛ akɛ jwɛi?

english: Not all, but many wild plants in the grass family grow aggressively and compete with crops. Checking for rough leaf margins or aggressive spreading roots helps you identify if a plant is a harmful weed.
ga: Jeee fɛɛ Shi koo mli tsei babaoo yɛ jwɛi weku lɛ mli ni daa oya ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ akaŋ. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ahe ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shishifãi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ona kɛji tso lɛ ji jwɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly even after I cut them down with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛ dade shwieɔ amɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Many grass-like weeds store energy in underground roots or tubers that survive even after you chop off the top leaves. Controlling them very early prevents these underground storage parts from forming.
ga: Jwɛi babaoo ni tamɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛ hewalɛ toɔ shishifãi loo ŋmeii ni hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni ofo ŋwɛi baai lɛ po sɛɛ. Amɛ nɔyeli mra Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi fãi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkatswa amɛhe amɛma shi.

english: What happens to my maize if I allow grass-like weeds to grow alongside it?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ kɛji miŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi ni tamɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ emasɛi?

english: Grass weeds belong to the same plant family as maize, meaning they feed on the exact same nutrients and water in the soil. Left unchecked, they will starve your crop and drastically reduce your harvest.
ga: Jwɛi jwɛi lɛ yɛ tso weku kome mli kɛ ŋmãa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛji okwɛɛɛ Amɛbaahã hɔmɔ aye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛbaahã yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi waa.

english: Why is this specific weed with sharp, rough leaves so much harder to destroy than broad-leaf weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɛkɛ jwɛi krɛdɛɛ ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ hiɛkpatamɔ wa kwraa fe jwɛi ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds with rough leaves like Cyperus usually have tough outer coats and underground tubers that resist drying out. Controlling them early before they mature is the secret to keeping your field clean.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, jwɛi ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ Cyperus lɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ fãi ni wa kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni nyɛɔ amɛgbiɔ. Kɛ́ oye amɛnɔ mra dani amɛdara lɛ ji teemɔŋ sane ni baaha oŋmɔji lɛ amli atse.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to build strong leaves, so applying fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted animal manure near the base helps keep the crop green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni eha baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he loo akɛ kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crop yields get smaller every time I plant maize on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same land drains the same soil nutrients year after year and builds up soil pests. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpea or groundnuts puts natural nitrogen back into the soil and restores its fertility.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛjɛɔ afi kɛyaa afi, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa sũ lɛ mli. Akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when heavy rains fall in my area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water collects around them in heavy clay soil. Building high mounds or ridges before planting allows excess rainwater to drain away easily so the roots can breathe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni ekã shi lɛ bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ sũ ni tsii lɛ mli. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni afee dani aduɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Why do my pepper leaves wilt during the hottest part of the afternoon even when the soil has some water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu fioo po?

english: Pepper plants wilt in strong sun because their leaves release moisture faster than their roots can suck it up from the dry topsoil. Mulching around the plants with dry grass keeps the soil cool and reduces water loss.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baagbo yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ jieɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up tight and turning light green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling these insects early with neem oil spray or yellow sticky traps keeps the virus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Mra be mli ni akɛbaatsu nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahe nii Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsɔne ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni ji yellow lɛ nɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do the leaves on my yam vines turn black and wither during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Blackening yam leaves during rainy periods are usually caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose. Splashing rainwater spreads the fungus, so staking the vines high off the wet ground helps keep them dry and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato baai ni feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ baa. Nugbɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ gbɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ eshwaa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu wain tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni nɔ kwɔ fe shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmei lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers fall off the tree before forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when sucking insects like mirids attack them or during sudden dry spells. Providing good shade trees and controlling mirids ensures the flowers mature into healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ mirids lɛ tutua amɛ loo yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa trukaa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo kpakpa kɛ la ni yeɔ nɔ lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ, amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees snap and fall over right when the bunches start getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ fãa ni amɛgbeeɔ minɔ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ je shishi amɛdara pɛ?

english: Plantain stems fall over because strong winds push against heavy bunches, or because tiny root pests have weakened the root system underground. Supporting the fruiting stems with bamboo props prevents them from breaking.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ gbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa hewɔ ni amɛtswa jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ. aloo yɛ shishifãi bibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahewɔ Ehaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ yibii lɛ fiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkakumɔ.

english: Why do my maize cobs have missing kernels and empty spots instead of full lines of grain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ bɛ ŋmeii ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Missing seeds happen when dry heat damages the tassels or silks during pollination. Planting maize close together in blocks rather than single lines ensures wind spreads pollen evenly across all silks.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji la ni mli egbi lɛ fite tasel loo silk lɛ yɛ pollination be mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ he kome yɛ blɔkii amli moŋ fe ŋmãa komekomei lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ni ejaraa ŋmãa lɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ siliki lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why does spear grass come back so aggressively even after I clear my farmland completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akpɔlɔ jwɛi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba kɛ yiwalɛ nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mijie miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Spear grass survives because it has tough underground stems called rhizomes that remain hidden under the soil. Simply cutting the top leaves doesn't kill it; you must dig out the underground root network completely.
ga: Spear jwɛi lɛ hiɔ shi ejaakɛ eyɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni wa ni atsɛɔ amɛ rhizomes ni hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ afolɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ lɛ, egbeŋ lɛ. Esa akɛ otsa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if a chemical spray will actually protect my cocoa trees or damage them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baabu mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe diɛŋtsɛ loo ebaafite amɛ?

english: Approved farm chemicals are scientifically tested to target specific cocoa pests without harming the tree. Unapproved or fake chemicals often contain harsh substances that can burn cocoa leaves, ruin soil health, and reduce fruit production.
ga: Akɛ tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ekwɛ jeŋ nilee mli koni akɛtutua kookoo mli ŋmeii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛyeee tsei lɛ awui. Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni bɛ he odaseyeli loo amalei lɛ yɛ nibii ni mli wa ni baanyɛ ashã kookoo baai. efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ ni ehaa yibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn brown and burnt after I spray them with pest medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ efɔ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf burning usually happens when a spray is too strong, improperly mixed, or made with unregistered chemicals that are not suited for cocoa trees. It can also happen if you spray during the hottest part of the day.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa shãa kɛji akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Akɛ tsofai ni aŋmalako amɛgbɛi awoko wolo nɔ ni esaaa cacao tsei lɛ futuɔ mli yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo akɛfee. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: How does using unapproved agrochemicals hurt my cocoa harvest over time?
ga: Te okwaayeli mli tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ saa mi-kookoo ni mikpaa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli?

english: Unapproved chemicals can kill beneficial insects that pollinate cocoa flowers and destroy good soil bacteria. Over time, this leads to weaker trees, lower pod yields, and soil that can no longer support healthy crops.
ga: Tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbe kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni shwieɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ, ni efite sũ mli helai kpakpai. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Enɛ kɛ tso ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Pod yibiiwoo lɛ ba shi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nyɛɛɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ dɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do the small pods on my cocoa tree wither and turn black before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbo ni amɛmiitsɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This issue, often called cherelle wilt, happens when the tree is stressed by bad weather, lack of soil nutrients, or attacks from pests like capsids. The tree naturally drops young fruits it cannot support.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids lɛ tutua lɛ, tso lɛ baajɛ adebɔɔ mli ekɛ aduawai bibii ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves during heavy rains are often a sign of waterlogged soil starving the roots of oxygen, or fungal infections like black pod disease taking hold in high humidity.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ ni hɔmɔ miiye kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shishifãi lɛ he okadi. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli tamɔ black pod hela ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ

english: Why do some branches on my cocoa tree produce plenty of pods while other branches remain bare?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo niji lɛ ekomɛi woɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi woɔ lɛ? Ani oyɛ yaka lolo?

english: Cocoa trees send nutrients to branches that get the best sunlight and air movement. Branches shaded heavily by taller trees or damaged by pests will struggle to flower and produce pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa tsei niji ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ náa lɛ anɔ. Tsei niji ni yɔɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ashishi loo ni tsɛŋemɔ helai efite lɛ baaná naagba yɛ fɔfɔii ni amɛbaafee lɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa pods rot and turn black starting from the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ egbo ni efee ediŋŋ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, shaded conditions. Raindrops bounce off infected soil onto the lower pods, spreading the disease upwards if the farm is not well-pruned.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. ni eha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋwɛi kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do insects attack my young cocoa trees more than the older, bigger trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii lɛ tutuaa mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ fe mi cacao tsei wuji ni dara lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees produce tender, soft shoots and leaves that are easy for sap-sucking pests like capsids to bite through and feed on compared to the tough, thick leaves of mature trees.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanu nu lɛ mli nu lɛ, tamɔ capsids, ni ŋmɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ lɛ. Kɛ akɛto tsei ni eda lɛ ahe baai ni wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees suffer when there are no shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa amanehulu be mli ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo be bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense tropical sunlight. Shade trees act like umbrellas, keeping the soil moist, lowering the temperature, and protecting the young cocoa from harsh heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ, ehaa hulutsoo baa shi, ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa he.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster on my farm than my planted crop seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with deep roots designed to grab water and soil food aggressively. Young crops take much longer to grow strong roots, so weeds easily overpower them if not cleared.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ, ni afee amɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ amɔmɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Tsei bibii lɛ baahe be babaoo dani amɛshishifãi ni wa akwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi lɛ yeɔ amɛnɔ kunim oya kɛji ajieee amɛ.

english: Yellowing leaf tips on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food crop plants need to stay green and grow strong. When the soil lacks nitrogen, the plant moves what little food it has to newer leaves, causing the older leaf tips to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Beni nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baajie niyenii fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛya baai heei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai momoi lɛ anaagbee lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ.

english: Why does my cassava grow very big leafy bushes on top but produces tiny roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ yɛ baai agbo ko ni da waa yɛ nɔ shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen—often from over-applying certain fertilizers or fresh manure—the cassava plant focuses all its energy on growing stem and leaves instead of storing energy in the tubers below the ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa babaoo lɛ Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ. Yucca tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ maa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli lɛ

english: Why do farmers say planting groundnuts on my land will help my maize grow better next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua miŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which have tiny organisms in their roots that pull nitrogen food straight out of the air and put it into the soil. When you harvest the groundnuts, that trapped food stays behind in the earth to feed the next maize crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi amli ni gbalaa nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa ŋmei Niyenii ni ekã lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the young plantain shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: The small shoots—called suckers—compete directly with the main mother plantain for water, light, and soil nutrients. Leaving too many shoots starves the main stem, resulting in smaller bunches of plantain.
ga: Tsobii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ akumɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves fully to catch as much sunshine as possible to produce energy for tuber growth. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and giving the plant maximum sunlight exposure.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli kwraa koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha tuber lɛ dalɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi foliar helai anaa ni oha tsei lɛ aná hulu la babaoo.

english: Why does my maize yield get worse every year if I keep planting it on the exact same spot without resting the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã yibiiwoo lɛ ehiii kwraa afi fɛɛ afi kɛji midu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ mihe lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes the specific soil nutrients that crop loves most, while allowing pests and soil diseases that feed on that specific plant to multiply in the soil year after year.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha sũ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei lɛ sumɔɔ waa lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ sũ lɛ babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into fruit when it gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai kɛ́ edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme sunshine and high temperatures stress tomato plants, causing the pollen inside the flowers to become dry and inactive. When flowers are not pollinated, the plant sheds them to save moisture and survival energy.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa kɛ latsaa ni naa wa haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni etsuuu nii. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why does covering the soil around my cocoa seedlings with dry grass help them survive dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves—called mulching—acts like a blanket that shades the soil from direct sun, keeping the ground cool and stopping soil moisture from evaporating into the air.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi - ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching - tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket, ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why does my cassava plant shed its leaves during the long dry season but stay alive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai lɛ shwie shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli shi eyɛ wala mli lolo lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry weather to reduce water loss through evaporation. It enters a temporary resting stage to protect its underground roots until the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni egbiɔ lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Ebabote hejɔɔmɔ be kukuoo ko mli koni ebu eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ ahe kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do young cocoa leaves turn brown and burn when I clear away all the large trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants naturally thrive under filtered shade. Removing big trees exposes the tender cocoa leaves to harsh direct sunlight, which scorches the tissue and starves the seedling of needed moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tsei wuji ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ shãa fãji lɛ ni ehaa dumɔwu lɛ náa nu ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the tip and moving down the center usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizers like NPK or urea during the early growing stages fixes this and keeps the leaves green and healthy.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ kɛyaa shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be mli ni edara mra lɛ baatsake naagba nɛɛ ni eye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe ajɔ amɛ.

english: Is it better for me to apply fertilizer to my crops before it rains or right after it rains?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo midumɔ nii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii dani nugbɔ anɛ loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer right after a light rain when the soil is moist. Heavy rainfall immediately after applying fertilizer can wash it away, while dry soil prevents the plant roots from absorbing the nutrients.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahoo lɛ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ lɛ, etsĩɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and stopping the plants from growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant juices and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these small pests early with insecticidal soaps or neem oil helps protect the foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei amli helai lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ahe nitsumɔ mra Kɛ akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu baai lɛ ahe.

english: What is making small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with sawdust-like dirt inside the central shoots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ muji tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed inside the central leaves (the whorl). Catching them early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or chemicals protects the plant before the growing point is destroyed.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ (whorls) lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei ahe dani akpata he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ hiɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under intense heat. They need temporary shade trees, such as plantains or leguminous shade trees, to shield them from direct sun and keep the ground cool during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ tsei bibii loo ŋmeii. Enɛ ji koni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small, light bunches when I leave all the young shoots growing around the mother stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo beni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nyɛ tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Leaving too many shoots (suckers) around one plantain tree causes them to fight for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Pruning away extra suckers and keeping only one or two strong ones allows the mother tree to direct its energy into producing large bunches.
ga: Suckers (shoots) babaoo ni ashiɔ yɛ dumɔwu kome he. Enɛ baaha tsei atswa akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni efoɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso nyɛ lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yam vines produce food through their leaves using sunlight, which feeds the growing underground tuber. Lifting the vines off the ground on tall stakes helps the leaves catch more sunlight and prevents fungal leaf diseases caused by ground moisture.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ hulu la ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni miida lɛ niyenii lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ awó wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ náa hulu la babaoo, ni ehaa tsei lɛ ahe helai ni sũ mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same piece of land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be mli lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains the soil of specific nutrients and lets crop-specific pests and diseases multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nine shɛɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi anɔ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛi kɛ tsei ahe helai babaoo. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava roots are fully matured and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically mature between 9 and 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You can tell it is getting ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, or by carefully digging around one stand to check the tuber thickness.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ miisaa amɛhe kɛji baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. aloo kɛtsɔ Stand one lɛ he ni ooofo jogbaŋŋ koni okwɛ bɔ ni yitso lɛ mli edɔ ha lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do experienced farmers cover the dry soil around crop roots with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle tsei shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material (mulching) acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, stops water from evaporating quickly in the sun, and suppresses weeds from sprouting.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni egbi (mulch) wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ. ni ekpaa jwɛi ni shwereɔ lɛ naa

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and burn easily under harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the vital shade and soil moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ehe miihia ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas together with my maize crop on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa adu tsina ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea is a legume crop that pulls nitrogen gas from the air and converts it into plant food within the soil. This natural food stays in the ground to nourish your maize crop, leading to bigger yields without buying extra fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii nɛɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha o-ŋmã lɛ aya hiɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, obaaná yibii babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and twisting into small shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiitsɔ amɛhe bibii lɛ?

english: Twisted and yellowing leaves are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems provided by agricultural extension officers protects your farm from this problem.
ga: Baai ni etsake ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmei bibioo lɛ ji nɔ ni hiɛɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ Kɛ́ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ dumɔ tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ naagba nɛɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize turning purple when they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ purple lɛ? Ni eji bibioo lolo?

english: Purple leaves on early maize show that the crop is starving for phosphorus, an essential plant nutrient needed to grow strong roots. Adding compost or well-rotted animal manure into the planting holes restores the nutrient.
ga: Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ mra lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. ni ji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa koni shishifãi lɛ adara waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi ashishifã ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo dumɔ bu lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like pencils during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ pensil yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing too much water in extreme heat. By hiding part of the leaf surface from the hot sun, the plant conserves its internal moisture until the cooler evening arrives.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite fe nine yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Kɛtsɔ baa lɛ nɔ fã ko ni ekɛteeɔ koni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akashɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli kɛyashi gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ baashɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when bees are absent to spread pollen. Keeping the soil evenly moist and planting flowering herbs nearby to attract bees stops the drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baagbɛ pollen lɛ amɛshwã Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ ni odu tsofai ni woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Koni ekɛgbala ŋmeii ni ekɛ amɛ akashwie shi

english: Why are my yam tubers growing short, bent, and hard instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ kukuji, amɛbɔleɔ amɛhe, ni amɛhe wa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need deep, soft, and loose soil mounds to expand downward easily. When the soil is hard, stony, or compacted, the roots hit obstacles and become deformed while trying to push through.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ he miihia sweet potatoes koni egbɛ eshwa kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, eyɛ tɛi, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ tswaa gbɛtsii nii ni amɛfiteɔ beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why are caterpillars eating holes through the central whorl of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, an invasive pest that hides inside the growing tip of maize plants to feed on soft new leaves. Applying natural controls like neem seed oil spray early in the morning destroys them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni baa mɔ nɔ ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli koni amɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Kɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni akɛkudɔɔ nii tamɔ neem dumɔwui amli fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaafite amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why is burning my farm bush after clearing bad for my future crop yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ashãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ awui lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic matter and kills beneficial earthworms and microbes that build rich soil. It leaves the topsoil naked so heavy rains wash away all the good nutrients your crops need to thrive.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ. Eshiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baajie niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ mli. ni ehe miihia ni otsei lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ mli

english: Why does my harvested maize turn moldy and get destroyed by insects when stored in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Maize rots in storage if it is bagged before it is completely dry inside. Solar drying your shelled maize on clean mats until a grain cracks cleanly between your teeth ensures it stays safe from mold and pests.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ awo kotoku mli dani emli lɛ mli egbi kwraa. Okɛ ŋmãa ni ajie yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ awo ŋmãa ni he tse nɔ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ baagbala jogbaŋŋ yɛ onyanyɔji ateŋ. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui akafee nɔ ko.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to survive because their young leaves burn under harsh direct sunlight and lose moisture quickly. Leaving some tall trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a protective cover until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli, ni amɛmli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni ashiɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi Enɛ baaye abua ni abu he kɛyashi kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: How does putting dry grass or dry leaves around the roots of my crops help them grow better?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil around plants with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool under hot weather, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and stops weeds from crowding your crops.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai gboi woɔ Tsei ahe, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaaa jwɛi akayi onibii amli.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize is a common sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizers or well-decomposed animal manure helps the plants regain their green color and produce healthy cobs.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmãa shishi lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I pour chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my plant or keep it at a distance?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ awo mli loo mafo mli?

english: You should never place fertilizer directly touching the stem because it can burn and damage the plant tissue. Placing it in a small circle or band a few inches away from the stem allows the roots to absorb nutrients safely.
ga: Esaaa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ kɔkɔɔkɔ ejaakɛ enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shã ni efite tso lɛ fãji lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛwo kooyigbɛ bibioo ko mli Aloo, kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows corn pests to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and disrupts pest life cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ koni amɛshwere ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmei tamɔ tsina loo ŋmei tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efoɔ ŋmãa lɛ wala shihilɛ mli.

english: What is causing tiny holes in the leaves at the center of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-abɛi tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ

english: Small ragged holes in the central leaves of corn are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on young growth. Checking fields early and applying approved insecticides or neem leaf extracts into the plant funnel can control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ gbekɛbii bibii ni daraa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo neem baa ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ enɛɛmɛi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids that transmit viruses. Spraying plants early with organic neem oil or recommended pesticides helps keep insect populations under control.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Akɛ organic neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ tsei anɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi ayibɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the soil during heavy rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water accumulates in the soil for too long, cutting off oxygen to the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or soil ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the root zone.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ faaa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my plantain bunches getting smaller every year on the same mat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii daa afi yɛ tsɔne kome nɔ lɛ?

english: As a plantain tree grows, it produces many small shoot suckers that compete with the main plant for soil nutrients and water. Removing extra suckers and keeping only two or three strong shoots per plant ensures larger fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ dara lɛ Ebaawo ŋmeii bibii. Amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni akɛ ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi tso kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha aduawai babaoo aba.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off before setting any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop without producing fruit due to extreme heat stress or erratic watering. Ensuring regular watering during hot spells helps flowers remain healthy and set fruit successfully.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ dɔlɛ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa hewɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ kpakpa ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How long do I have to wait after planting long-term tree crops like cocoa before I can start harvesting and making money?
ga: Kɛ́ odu tso ko ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tamɔ kookoo sɛɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani ebɔi ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ ni ekɛ shika aba?

english: Long-term tree crops usually take between 3 to 5 years before they produce their first full harvest. During these early years, the trees are focusing their energy on building strong roots and branches rather than producing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛshɛɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yeɔ emuu lɛ he. Yɛ nɛkɛ shishijee afii nɛɛ amli lɛ, tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi kɛ niji ni wa ni eeetswa lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: If only a few of my cassava plants look big enough to sell, can I harvest those now and leave the smaller ones in the soil?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei fioo komɛi pɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ. Ani manyɛ makpãtã bianɛ ni mashi ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, this is called selective harvesting. Removing the mature roots leaves more space, water, and soil nutrients for the smaller plants to grow bigger until they are ready to be harvested later.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ nikpamɔ ni ahalaa. Removing mature roots leaves more space, water, and nutrients in the soil for the small plant to grow larger until it's ready to be harvested later.

english: Can I plant fast-growing crops like vegetables between my slow-growing tree crops so I have food to sell while waiting years for the main harvest?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ aduawai yɛ mitsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ ateŋ koni maná niyenii ni mahɔ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ afii babaoo kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ titri lɛ?

english: Yes, this practice is called intercropping. Planting short-term crops like plantains, pepper, or maize between young trees provides immediate food and income while giving necessary shade to the young trees without harming them.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ intercropping. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains, peppers, loo ŋmãa yɛ tsei bibii ateŋ lɛ haa anáa niyenii kɛ shika amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni eyeee amɛ awui.

english: If I want to harvest 1,000 bags of maize, how do I know how much land and seeds I need to start with?
ga: Kɛji miitao makpa ŋmãa kotokui 1,000 lɛ, te mafee tɛŋŋ male shikpɔŋ kɛ dumɔwui abɔ ni he baahia mi?

english: To reach a target yield, you must calculate seed quantity based on spacing guidelines per acre and account for potential crop losses from weather or pests. Planning farm size based on seed rate ensures your land can support your production goal.
ga: bɔni afee ni onine ashɛ nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ nɔ Esa akɛ obu dumɔwui lɛ ayibɔ he akɔntaa yɛ spacing-per-acre gbɛtsɔɔmɔi lɛ anaa. ni esusu ŋmɔshi nibii ni baanyɛ afite yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahewɔ lɛ he. Oŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni damɔ dumɔwui ayibɔ nɔ lɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua otii ni okɛma ohiɛ akɛ obaawo nii lɛ.

english: Why do some farmers plant their crops in batches across different weeks instead of planting the whole field on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ otsii babaoo mli moŋ fe ni amɛaadu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Staggering your planting dates allows crops to mature at different times. This spreads out your harvest work and ensures you have fresh produce to sell continuously over several weeks rather than all at once.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ gbii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ adara yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Enɛ baaha okpamɔ lɛ agbɛ ashwã. ni ekwɛɔ koni oná nibii heei ni abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ otsii babaoo ni sɛɛ efooo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooohɔ̃ɔ fɛɛ shikome lɛ

english: Do crops need protective medicine and treatments just like farm animals do when they get sick?
ga: Ani tsofai ni tsiɔ hela naa kɛ tsamɔ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔ mli kooloi feɔ kɛji hela mɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, crops need protective care similar to animals. Farmers use fungicides for plant diseases, insecticides for insect pests, and fertilizers for nutrition to keep plants healthy and high-yielding.
ga: Hɛɛ, hebuu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kooloi pɛpɛɛpɛ. Okwaafoi kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii tsuɔ nii kɛgbeɔ tsei ahe helai. Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha niyenii koni eha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are my young seedlings drying up in the sun even though I am watering them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ miigbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Young plants have fragile skin and shallow roots that cannot handle intense direct sunlight. They need temporary shade, like palm leaves or shade trees, to prevent the hot sun from scorching them while their root systems establish.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ hewolo ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni tsoɔ waa tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ ŋmei tsei loo hulutsoo tsei. Enɛ ji koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akashã amɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell when my plantain bunch is fully mature and ready to be cut for market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-plantain tsei lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ afolɔ amɛ kɛya jara nɔ?

english: Plantains are mature when the individual fruits lose their sharp edges and become plump and rounded. The dark green skin also lightens slightly, indicating the fruit has finished growing even before it turns yellow.
ga: Plantains lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko sɛɛ efoɔ ni ebafeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Hewolo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ hu mli tse fioo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ aduawai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ po.

english: After I harvest my maize, should I clear out and burn all the leftover stalks or leave them on the ground?
ga: Beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ ni mashã amɛ loo mashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Leaving clean crop stalks on the field to decompose acts as natural mulch. It protects the soil from drying out under the sun, prevents erosion, and breaks down into organic fertilizer for your next planting season.
ga: Tsoi ahe tsei ni he tse ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛgboi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi yɛ hulu lɛ shishi. Tsi shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Why do some of my crops grow very tall and leafy but fail to produce good fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ baai shi amɛtsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Excessive leafy growth with poor fruiting often happens when plants get too much nitrogen fertilizer but not enough potassium or phosphorus, or when plants are crowded too close together and fight for sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni daa fe nine kɛ aduawai ni ehiii lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ ná nitrogen babaoo ni amɛnáaa potassium loo phosphorus ni fa bɔ ni sa. Aloo kɛ́ tsei ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ ni amɛmiitswa hulu la he akaŋ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to shoot up after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishifã lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani etswaa beni midu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers need time to establish underground roots before you see top growth. Preparing proper planting holes with rich soil and trimming old root stumps before planting speeds up early shooting.
ga: Be he miihia dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi dani obaana amɛdalɛ babaoo. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe buji ni akɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe saamɔ kpakpa Kɛ shishifã momo lɛ ni aaafo dani adu lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ oya.

english: How do I know if my plantain crop is getting enough water during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: When plantains lack water, their broad leaves start curling inward, turning yellow, or drooping heavily. Mulching around the base with dry leaves helps soil retain moisture during dry periods.
ga: Kɛ́ nu bɛ plantain lɛ mli lɛ Ebaai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛya mli. Etsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo egbee shi waa Mulching kɛ baai ni egboi yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I plant them in an open field without tall plants nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni midu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily scorch under direct tropical sun. Tall crops like plantains provide living shade and keep the air humid so the young cocoa can survive.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be lɛ yɔɔ lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Can I grow cassava together with my plantain on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmei kɛ plantains yɛ he kome?

english: Yes, cassava and plantain can grow together if spaced correctly. Since cassava roots expand underground and plantains feed closer to the surface, proper spacing prevents them from starving each other of nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei kɛ plantain baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ he kome kɛji akɛ amɛto amɛhe jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni plantains yeɔ nii ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ́ amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ he ni sa lɛ, ebaatsi amɛhe gbɛ koni hɔmɔ akaye amɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and die early before the fruit bunch is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya dani aduawai lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Early yellowing often happens when soil lacks nutrients like nitrogen, or when small soil pests called nematodes damage the roots, stopping the plant from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa mra kɛ́ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo kɛ́ sũ mli kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ fite shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes my plantain trees to suddenly fall over during moderate rains and wind?
ga: Mɛni haa mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that stem borers or underground pests can easily weaken. Heaping fresh, fertile soil around the base of the plant strengthens its hold in the ground.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni haa ŋmeii loo shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi krokomɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ gbɔjɔɔ amɛ oya. Shikpɔŋ hee ni baa nii lɛ ni aaabɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nibii ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ mli waa.

english: How do I pick the best shoot from an old plantain tree to start a new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmeii ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ plantains momoi amli koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Choose 'sword suckers'—young shoots with narrow, spear-shaped leaves and a thick base. They grow faster and yield much heavier bunches than shoots with broad, flat leaves.
ga: Halamɔ ‘tsobii bibii’, ni ji tsei bibii ni baai lɛ mli tse, ni tamɔ lance kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli tse. Amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni tsii fe ŋmeii ni baai lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I remove extra suckers growing around my main plantain tree stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi dumɔwui akuu titri lɛ.

english: If too many suckers grow around one stem, they steal food and water from the main plant, resulting in small, thin plantain bunches. Keeping only two or three shoots gives you bigger harvests.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso kome he lɛ, amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa plantain tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ to lɛ, ebaaha oná ŋmaa babaoo.

english: When is the best month to plant plantains in Ghana for maximum yield?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nyɔŋ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu plantains yɛ Ghana koni ená yibii babaoo?

english: The best time to plant is at the beginning of the major rainy season (around March or April) so the root system develops fully before any dry spell hits.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ji nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ shishijee. Eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ dani hulutsoo be lɛ jeɔ shishi (aaafee March loo April).

english: Why does my maize crop grow tall and thin without producing big ears of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ekɛ ŋmãa toi wuji baaa lɛ?

english: Maize planted too close together competes heavily for sunlight and ground food, causing stems to stretch thin and yield tiny ears. Proper line spacing gives every stalk room to produce big corn.
ga: Abele ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baatswa hulu la kɛ mash he akaŋ. Ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛwoɔ toi bibii. Line ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tsu fɛɛ tsu feɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa agboi.

english: How does growing my vegetables inside a greenhouse shelter help them produce better than in the open field?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mi-aduawai ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai fe ŋmɔ ni mli tse mli lɛ?

english: A greenhouse shelter protects crops from excessive rain, harsh sunlight, and major pests. By controlling the heat, moisture, and pest exposure, plants stay healthy, grow faster, and produce higher yields of clean, disease-free fruits.
ga: Greenhouse shelters buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji ahe. Kɛtsɔ dɔlɛ, fɛ̃i kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ nɔ. Tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ. amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ aduawai ni he tse ni hela bɛ mli babaoo

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up tightly during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural survival mechanism against extreme heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the leaf surface area exposed to the sun, helping it conserve internal water and prevent drying out.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Tsei haa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hiɔ shi, ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbi.

english: Pepper flowers usually drop off when the plant suffers from extreme temperature changes, dry soil, or a shortage of phosphorus. When a plant feels stressed by weather or poor nutrients, it sheds flowers to conserve its remaining energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo tsakemɔi ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo fɔsfɔs ni bɛ mli lɛ na tso lɛ he amanehulu. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo niyenii kpakpai miigba amɛnaa lɛ, Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why are the bottoms of my growing tomatoes turning black and rotting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni midu lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efite lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, which is almost always caused by irregular watering—such as letting the soil get completely dry and then flooding it.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa, tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ahaa egbiɔ kwraa ni no sɛɛ lɛ nu afua.

english: Why do my cabbage plants stay loose instead of forming tight, solid heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage tsei lɛ etse amɛhe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee yitsei ni mli wa ni wa lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to head properly when temperatures are too high or when soil moisture is uneven. High nitrogen levels combined with heat cause the leaves to grow too fast and spread out rather than wrapping tightly around the center.
ga: Kaabaji nyɛŋ atsɔ yitso jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ejaaa. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni fataa latsaa he lɛ haa baai lɛ daa oya tsɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa moŋ fe ni amɛaabɔle teŋgbɛ lɛ he shiŋŋ.

english: Why are my garden egg fruits coming out bitter and tough rather than tender?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ mli edɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Bitterness in garden eggs usually happens when the plant experiences drought stress during fruit growth or when the fruits are left on the branch too long past their ideal harvesting time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, abɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni mli edɔ lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na hɔmɔ he haomɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ. aloo kɛ́ ashi aduawai yɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ fe kpamɔ be ni sa lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is necessary for leaf growth, so when the soil lacks it, the plant moves nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia kɛha baa lɛ adalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and woody instead of swelling into big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛfuu ni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose, light soil and sufficient potassium to swell up. Hard, compact soil physically prevents roots from expanding, while a lack of potassium stops the plant from transferring sugars into the roots.
