ga: Cassava shishifãi hia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli tse kɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa koni efuu. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã. Yɛ be mli ni potassium ni faaa lɛ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkajie sugars kɛya shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable seeds rot in the soil before they can sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Seeds rot when the soil is too wet, cold, or packed too tightly, which starves the seeds of oxygen. Planting seeds too deep or using un-composted manure near seeds can also encourage fungal rot before germination.
ga: Dumɔwui fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ, edɔ tsɔ, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ ana oxygen. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni mli kwɔ tsɔ loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmei lɛ agbo dani ekwɛ̃.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing long green vines with many leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ wain tsei kakadaŋŋ agboi babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes leguminous plants to focus all their energy on leaf and stem growth instead of flowering. Adding excess nitrogen fertilizer encourages tall plants but reduces actual pod production.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baa kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ adalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi. Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli fe nine lɛ baaye abua ni ekwɛ̃ shi ebaaha pod diɛŋtsɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I cut down all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mifo tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to protect them from harsh direct sunlight. Without shade trees or temporary nurse crops like plantains to block the heat, the intense sun scorches their leaves and dries out the soil moisture.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo be fioo ko koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei ni kwɛɔ nɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni tsiɔ dɔlɛ naa lɛ bɛ lɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi.

english: Can I plant cassava together with maize on the same field at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, intercropping cassava and maize works very well. Maize matures quickly and is harvested in about three to four months, while cassava grows slower and takes over the space after the maize is harvested.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa teŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. Abɛi daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo ni eŋɔ he ko beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yellowing in a V-shape starting from the tips of lower leaves means your soil is short of nitrogen. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure will help the plants green up and produce full cobs.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ V su mli ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops every year even though I clear and burn the farm bush before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mishãa amɛ dani miduɔ nii moŋ.

english: Burning farm bush destroys organic matter and beneficial micro-organisms that keep soil soft and fertile. Leaving crop residue to decompose naturally adds nutrients back into the soil and keeps it rich.
ga: Jwɛi ni ashãa yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ehaa niyenii kpakpai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and showing light green patches with tiny white insects under them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ yɛ amɛshishi lɛ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by small insects called whiteflies. The best fix is to plant improved, disease-resistant cassava stems provided by agricultural extension services.
ga: Enɛ ji cassava mosaic hela, ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni abaanyɛ atsu he nii ji ni adu ŋmei tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and overly shaded farms. Pruning thick branches to let air and sunlight in, along with removing infected pods, helps stop it from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ejɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli, ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Niji ni mli tse ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la abote mli Nɔ ni fata he ji ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer from high heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Regular watering during hot dry spells helps the plant hold its flowers and set fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ha amɛ. Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ amli.

english: How do I know the best time to sow my maize during the major rainy season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Wait until the rains become steady for a few days so the soil is deeply moist. Planting right after the very first isolated rain shower can cause seeds to germinate and then dry up if a dry spell follows.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ be fɛɛ be gbii fioo komɛi koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i waa. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow thin, small, and bent instead of large and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji mlɛo, bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni eja lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose, and deep soil mounds to expand easily. If the soil is hard, stony, or the mounds are too small, the tubers struggle to push through and become stunted or misshapen.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia gɔŋ ko ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni mli kwɔ koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo gɔŋ lɛ ji bibioo tsɔ lɛ, Yitso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsɔ mli ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ehiɛ efeee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants suddenly wilting and dying during the day even when the soil has enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: This is usually bacterial wilt, a disease living in the soil that blocks water from moving up the plant stem. Rotating tomatoes with non-susceptible crops like maize or cassava breaks the disease cycle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji hela ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni haaa nu aya tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ. Okɛ tsei ni nyɛɛɛ atswa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ atsake tomato. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni efoɔ helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why are my crops producing less food even though I expanded my farm to a larger plot this year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo niyenii fioo eyɛ mli akɛ migbɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee shikpɔji wuji anɔ afi nɛɛ?

english: Planting a larger area without enough labor, fertilizer, or water spreads your resources too thin. Crops get neglected, leading to lower yields compared to a smaller, well-cared-for plot.
ga: Shikpɔji wuji ni oookwɛ nɔ ni nitsulɔi, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ baaha onibii lɛ afee bibioo tsɔ. Aku hiɛ ashwie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi kɛ akɛto shikpɔji bibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: If I reduce my farm size from 5 acres down to 2 acres, how will that affect my crop yield?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ ba shi kɛjɛ acre 5 kɛtee acre 2 lɛ, te enɛ baaná miŋmɔshi nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Focusing on a smaller plot allows you to give more attention, fertilizer, and weed control to every single plant, which often results in healthier crops and higher yields per acre.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ma he bibioo ko nɔ lɛ, ebaaha onyɛ okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama tso fɛɛ tso nɔ babaoo, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni okɛ jwɛi lɛ atsu nii. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ acre kome mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and stop growing halfway through the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa dalɛ yɛ be lɛ fã mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking key nutrients like nitrogen in the soil or is suffering from water stress, preventing the plant from making food to grow.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ sũ lɛ mli. loo naagbai ni jɛɔ nu mli haomɔ mli baa lɛ Haa tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛwo niyenii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant the exact same crop on the same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and lets crop-specific pests build up in the soil, causing yields to drop each season.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. kɛ gbɛ ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up tightly during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a crop's natural defense mechanism to reduce moisture loss and protect itself from drying out under strong heat and sunlight.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe koni ekɛba ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ shi ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la shishi lɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop their leaves when the dry season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shwieɔ baai yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop leaves during dry spells to conserve water in their roots, allowing the plant to survive heat until rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛ nu ato amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ koni amɛdamɔ hulutsoo be lɛ naa kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my plants grow tall and thin with very small fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, root space, and nutrients, causing them to grow weak stems and produce smaller yields.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce such small harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, soil nutrients, and water away from your crops, effectively starving the plants while they are trying to form tubers or seeds.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la ni he hiaa waa. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Enɛ haa tso lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ jogbaŋŋ beni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni efee bulbs loo dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why should I plant different types of crops together on my farm instead of just one?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ekome pɛ?

english: Mixing crops protects your family's food security because if one crop suffers from a pest or bad weather, the other crop can still survive and produce food.
ga: Nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nibii ni aduɔ lɛ buɔ oweku lɛ niyenii he. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii lɛ ye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi baanyɛ ahi shi lolo ni amɛwo niyenii.

english: How do insect pests cause an entire field of crops to fail so quickly?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Pests feed on crop leaves and stems, destroying the plant's ability to absorb light and nutrients, which rapidly spreads plant disease and stops growth.
ga: Kooloi yeɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi. Efiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛmɔɔ la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛkpaa dalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are short of nitrogen, which is an important food plants need to grow. It can also happen when there is too much water standing around the roots, preventing them from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haaa amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cowpea crops grow well even if I do not add chemical fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ wooo mli moŋ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen gas directly from the air and turn it into food for the plant and soil, reducing the need for artificial fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ehaa efeɔ niyenii kɛhaa tso lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee lɛ atsu nii.

english: When afternoon heat gets too extreme, tomato flowers get stressed and their pollen dries out, causing the flowers to fall off before fruit can start forming.
ga: Kɛ shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ haoɔ ni pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Enɛ haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up into tight tubes during the sunny afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's natural defense mechanism to protect itself. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the strong sun, preventing heavy water loss.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ebuɔ ehe he. Tsei haa he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni nu babaoo akafite.

english: Why do tiny worms keep eating the central leaves of my young maize plants during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yaa nɔ amɛyeɔ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that multiplies quickly in hot, dry weather and feeds on the tender inner leaves of young maize before the plant matures.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni fɔɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ. ni oye ŋmãa bibii lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ dani tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ

english: Planting maize and cassava together helps you maximize your land usage because maize grows quickly and is harvested early, while cassava grows slowly and takes over the space after the maize is harvested.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa fee ekome lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, abele daa oya, ni akpaa lɛ mra. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo ni eyeɔ jɛmɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What happens if I plant my yam seeds too close to each other in the mounds?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu sweet potato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko mli?

english: If yam seeds are planted too close together, their roots will compete fiercely for nutrients, light, and water, resulting in many small, thin tubers instead of large, heavy yams.
ga: Kɛji odu sweet potato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, la, kɛ nu he akaŋ, ni no haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo babaoo baa yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees require shade trees when they are small but need more sunlight as they grow older?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he hiaa hulutsoo beni amɛdara lɛ, shi hulu la babaoo he hiaa amɛ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight, but mature cocoa trees need moderate sunlight to trigger heavy flowering and pod production.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Shi cacao tso ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ewo fɔfɔi kɛ pod babaoo ni efeɔ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why do my harvested plantains turn soft and yellow much faster during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains ni akpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High moisture and warm temperatures cause harvested plantains to release a natural ripening gas called ethylene faster, which speeds up the softening and ripening process.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni mli wa kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ haa plantains ni akpa lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ yaa oya. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ afee blɛoo ni ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why is it important to prune some of the side stems on my cassava plants after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi yucca tso lɛ sɛɛ niji lɛ ekomɛi yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning excess side stems forces the plant to send its energy down into expanding the underground root tubers instead of wasting resources on extra stems and leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ hewalɛ yaa shi koni ekɛgbala shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite nibii yɛ tsei ashishifãi kɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant pulls nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top, showing it urgently needs fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia oya.

english: Why are the inner leaves of my young maize plants twisted together with small holes and powdery dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni sũ hu yɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar hiding inside the growing center of the plant. It chews the soft leaves before they unfold, leaving ragged holes and sawdust-like waste behind.
ga: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding in the plant's growth center. Ekɛ baai bibii shwieɔ shi dani amɛgbeleɔ. Eshiɔ buji ni ekpɔtɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ esɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil when heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains soak the ground for too long, water fills all the empty spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots and causing them to rot underground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nu baayi he ni efee efolo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii baa.

english: Why does my yam crop grow long leafy vines for months before any tuber grows large underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ wain tsei ni baai kakadaji yɔɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ nyɔji babaoo dani ŋmeii lɛ daraa wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: The yam vine acts like a solar panel that collects sunlight. The plant must build a large canopy of leaves first so it can manufacture enough food to store away and swell the tuber later in the season.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulu la, buaa hulu la naa. Esa akɛ tsei afee ŋwɛi ŋta agbo dani amɛfee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛto ni amɛkwɛ bulbs yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli.

english: Cocoa trees produce far more flowers than they can feed. If the tree experiences dry weather, poor soil nutrition, or lack of shade, it naturally sheds extra flowers to save water and energy for its survival.
ga: The cocoa tree produces more flowers than it can support. Kɛji tso lɛ na kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli egbi Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo hulutsoo ni bɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain plants take much longer to fruit when I leave many small shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii beni mikɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ lɛ? babaoo ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ he

english: The small shoots, called suckers, share the same root system as the main stem. When too many grow at once, they steal nutrients, water, and sunlight from the main stem, slowing down its growth.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ suckers. Eyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ dalɛ babaoo yɛ be kome mli lɛ Ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha dalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do my pepper flowers drop off without forming any peppers during hot, dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeee pepper ko kwraa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Extreme heat dries out the pollen inside pepper flowers so seeds cannot form. When it gets too hot, the plant sheds its flowers to avoid wasting water trying to grow fruit during a drought.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa pollen ni yɔɔ pepper fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. No hewɔ lɛ dumɔwui efeee. Beni edɔ tsɔ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkafite nu ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl upward and turn thick and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies. When whiteflies feed on the plant, they pass the virus into the sap, causing the leaves to twist and reducing the plant's yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kɛji ŋmeii yɛŋ ye tsei Amɛtsɔɔ hela lɛ mli kɛyaa mliki lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tsei lɛ ayibii baa shi.

english: Why do my garden eggs look wilted in the afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, leaves lose water into the air faster than roots can pull it from the soil. The plant temporary droops to close its leaf pores and save water, recovering when temperatures drop in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbee shi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛŋa ŋmeii lɛ ni ekɛbu nu lɛ he. Ebaatsa ehe kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea roots have small round bumps on them, and are they damaging my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo yɛ nɔ ni amɛmiifite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Those bumps are root nodules and they are beneficial. Friendly bacteria live inside them, taking nitrogen from the air and turning it into free fertilizer that feeds your crop and improves the soil.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛhe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ. Muawai ni feɔ naanyo lɛ hiɔ amɛmli. Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and staying small even when it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ bibii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, an essential plant food. Even with plenty of rain, crops cannot grow big and green without proper nutrients in the soil or natural fertilizers like animal manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ Kɛji niyenii ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛŋ adara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: Why do my crops seem to produce better harvests when I plant beans alongside my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai beni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes have roots that pull nitrogen directly from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally feeds surrounding crops like maize or cassava without needing extra chemical fertilizers.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛyeɔ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ atsu nii

english: How can I enrich my farm soil naturally if commercial fertilizers become too expensive or unavailable?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa? Ni kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ jara wa tsɔ loo anyɛɛɛ ana hu?

english: You can make compost by piling up animal droppings, green leaves, dry grass, and food waste to rot down into rich plant food, or plant cover crops like velvet beans that restore soil nutrients when mixed into the earth.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni abua naa, baai eŋɔli, jwɛi, kɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ ni oootsɔ nɔ ofee tsei niyenii ni jara wa lɛ nɔ. Aloo dumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ velvet beans, ni baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛfutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce smaller tubers when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded together, their roots fight under the ground for limited nutrients and water, while their leaves block sunlight from each other, leaving less energy to grow large roots.
ga: Kɛ́ abua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu fioo. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ fioo pɛ yɔɔ ni akɛbaakwɛ shishifãi wuji.

english: Why does leaving dry grass or leaves around the stems of my crops help them during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni ebɔle he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Covering the soil around your crops—known as mulching—acts like a protective blanket that keeps the soil cool, stops water from evaporating quickly, and rots down into natural soil food over time.
ga: Ale shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ oya ni efiteɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant tomatoes on the exact same patch of ground every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji miduɔ tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same soil nutrients year after year and gives crop-specific pests and diseases a permanent home to multiply and attack future harvests.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Ni ehaa tsei amli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ náa shihilɛhe ni hiɔ shi daa koni amɛfɔ ni amɛtutua wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves curl up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism where the plant shrinks its leaf surface area to slow down water loss through evaporation during intense heat.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ he lɛ shi koni nu lɛ akafite kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before turning into actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛmiitsɔ pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by sudden dry spells, extreme sun heat, or a lack of essential soil nutrients needed to support fruit growth.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. hulu la ni mli edɔ loo niyenii ni he hiaa koni aduawai akwɛ̃ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow faster and stronger than the crops I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants adapted to steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops, which is why early clearing is essential so your main crops do not starve.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛju nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie lɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni okwɛ koni hɔmɔ akaye onibii titrii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when planted in open sunny fields without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn under full, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them provides necessary shelter and keeps the soil cool until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni he hiaa, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: How can tall cassava plants and low groundnut plants grow together on the same farm without hurting each other?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ adu ŋmei tsei ni kwɔlɔ kɛ ŋmei tsei ni baa shi lɛ ekome yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni amɛyeee amɛhe awui?

english: They feed at different soil levels and heights. Groundnuts have short roots that feed near the surface and spread out close to the ground, while cassava roots go deeper into the soil, so they do not fight for the same food or space.
ga: Amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ srɔtoi kɛ ŋwɛi ŋwɛi ŋwɛi. Peanuts yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni yeɔ nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ No hewɔ lɛ, amɛyeee akaŋ yɛ niyenii loo he kome he.

english: Can I plant cassava and sweet potatoes together in the exact same mound?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ ŋmei kome mli?

english: It is not recommended because both crops grow underground tubers in the top layer of soil. They will push against each other and fight for the same nutrients, leaving you with small tubers from both crops.
ga: Akɛ enɛ haaa ejaakɛ tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ woɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋwɛigbɛ. Amɛbaawuu kɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaawu amɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa ohiɛɔ oyitso bibioo. kɛjɛ tsei srɔtoi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli

english: Why do people say I should plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my field after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize eats up a lot of nutrients from the soil. Cowpeas and groundnuts have a special ability to take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, acting like natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ nyɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni amɛkɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Is it true that cocoa trees will produce less cocoa if I cut down all the big shade trees on my farm?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ kookoo tsei lɛ baawo kookoo fioo kɛji mifolɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Yes, young and mature cocoa trees naturally prefer dappled shade because full direct sunlight overheats the soil and stresses the trees. Leaving selected tall trees creates a cool environment that keeps cocoa healthy.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo tsei bibii kɛ mɛi ni eda lɛ sumɔɔ hulutsoo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adɔ fe nine ni eha tso lɛ aná haomɔ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni ahalaa ni ashiɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni haa kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why does my yam grow so well on dry soil mounds, but my rice needs waterlogged swampy ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gɔji ni egbi lɛ anɔ lɛ? Shi ani shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ he miihia mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Different crops have different natural needs. Yam tubers need soft, well-drained soil so they can expand without rotting, while swamp rice is designed to absorb lots of water without its roots suffocating.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi yɛ adebɔɔ mli hiamɔ nii srɔtoi. Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfiteee. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, afee peat koni ekɛ nu babaoo awo mli ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ akagbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when I plant them too close to my cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When planted too close, both heavy-feeding crops compete fiercely for the same soil nutrients and water, leaving the maize starving and turning yellow due to a lack of nitrogen.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu amɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Niyenii tsei enyɔ ni tsii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye ŋmãa lɛ ni ebaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nitrogen ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants stay small and bear very few fruits when I crowd them tightly together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ daraaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ to he kome shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Every crop needs its own personal space for air, sunlight, and root expansion. When crowded, pepper plants shade each other out and share limited water, which stunts their growth.
ga: Nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ hia amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe gbɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli, hulu la, kɛ shishifãi ni miida. Kɛ gbɔmɛi babaoo yɛ Pepper tsei lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ shade ni amɛjaa nu fioo ko pɛ. Enɛ baaha dalɛ akpa shi.

english: Why do insects damage my crop more when I plant only maize across my whole field instead of mixing it with other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii babaoo beni miduɔ ŋmãa pɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ ŋmãa krokomɛi baafutu lɛ?

english: When you plant only one crop, pests find an endless supply of their favorite food and multiply quickly. Mixing different crops confuses pests with varying smells and shapes, making it harder for them to destroy the whole farm.
ga: Kɛji odu tso henɔ kome pɛ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baaná niyenii ni amɛsumɔɔ waa ni bɛ naagbee ni amɛbaafee babaoo oya. Nibii srɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ mli lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ kɛ sui srɔtoi lɛ futuɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa amɛ akɛ amɛbaakpãtã ŋmɔji muu fɛɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant garden eggs or tomatoes in the same spot where I just harvested pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii loo tomatoi yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mikpa mi-pepper tsei lɛ amrɔ nɛɛ?

english: Peppers, tomatoes, and garden eggs belong to the same crop family and like the same nutrients. They also suffer from the same soil diseases, so planting them right after each other allows hidden pests and diseases in the soil to attack the new crop immediately.
ga: Pepper, tomato kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii yɛ tso weku kome mli ni amɛsumɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome. They also suffer from the same soil diseases. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How does planting pumpkin leaves underneath my tall maize help suppress weeds on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ pɔmpi baai ni aduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa kakadaŋŋ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akudɔɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pumpkin plants spread wide leaves close to the ground, creating a living carpet that blocks sunlight from reaching the soil. Without sunlight, weed seeds cannot sprout and grow.
ga: Pumpkin tso lɛ gbɛɔ ebaai lɛ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he waa. Enɛ haa anáa kapɛti ni hiɛ ka ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji hulu la bɛ lɛ Jwɛi dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ ni amɛdara.

english: Why is it important for me to set up an irrigation plan before the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi lɛ?

english: Planning irrigation early ensures your crops get steady water even when rains are unpredictable, preventing young plants from drying out and dying in the early stages.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ aná nu ni fa daa be mli ni nugbɔ baanɛ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba po. Prevents young plants from drying out and dying in the early stages.

english: What is the simplest way for me to water my crops if the rainfall is not enough?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mawo mitsei lɛ nu kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ bɔ ni sa?

english: Using simple bucket drip systems or shallow watering channels from a nearby water source delivers water directly to plant roots without wasting precious water.
ga: Kɛ akɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ baagi mli ni yɔɔ mlɛo loo nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni jɛɔ nu jɛɛhe ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ekɛ nu lɛ yaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ ni nu ni jara wa lɛ efiteee.

english: How can I tell if my crops are getting too much or too little water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu ni miduɔ lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo fioo tsɔ?

english: Yellowing leaves with soft stems usually mean crops have too much water, while wilting, curling leaves and cracked soil mean the crops need urgent watering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ nu babaoo tsɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ, baai ni ebɔle amɛhe kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbɛ eshwa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni awo amɛ nu oya.

english: How do I know the right time in March to start planting my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa yɛ March mli ni esa akɛ mabɔi tsei akwɛmɔ?

english: Planting should start right after the first steady rains settle into the ground so the soil has enough moisture for seeds to sprout without burning.
ga: Esa akɛ aje dumɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛshãaa.

english: Why do some crops produce more food when planted early in the rainy season compared to late in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi woɔ niyenii babaoo kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli fe sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Early-planted crops benefit from the full length of the rainy season, getting plenty of sunlight and water to mature fully before the dry weather sets in.
ga: Tsei ni adu mra lɛ baaná nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ he sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. Amɛnáa hulu la kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara dani hulutsoo be lɛ aba.

english: What is the best way for me to prepare my farmland before the major planting season begins?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ masaa he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be titri lɛ aje shishi?

english: Clearing weeds, loosening the topsoil, and mixing in organic manure creates a soft, rich environment for young roots to spread easily and absorb nutrients.
ga: weeding Gbalamɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ haa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa koni shishifãi bibii lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: How does hot weather affect how quickly my soil loses water?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ saa bɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Strong sun and high heat cause soil water to evaporate rapidly into the air, which means you must cover the soil with dry grass or mulch to keep it moist.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa kɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ jwɛi loo ŋmɔshi nibii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ehiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to sprout even after I plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if the soil is too dry, if they are buried too deep, or if insects and heat damage the seed before it can grow.
ga: Dumɔwui kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ dɔlɛ kpataa dumɔwui lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛdaraa.

english: Why do I need to leave proper space between my crops when planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi gbɛ ni sa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ kɛ́ midu nii lɛ?

english: Proper spacing prevents crops from fighting each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, allowing each plant to grow strong and yield more.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ye obua tso fɛɛ tso ni ená hewalɛ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why should I test my seeds in a bowl of water before planting them in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka midumɔwui lɛ makwɛ yɛ nu tsɛnsi mli dani madu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Healthy seeds sink to the bottom because they are heavy with nutrients, while damaged or dead seeds float, saving you time from planting bad seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shishi ejaakɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni efite loo egboi lɛ baaho. Enɛ haa oyeɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui gbohii ni ooodu lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them out in the open sun without any big crops around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni ŋmɔshi nibii wuji bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to direct heat and sunlight. Plantain plants or shade trees act like living umbrellas, providing the cool shade and moisture young cocoa roots need to establish before they can handle direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa ni kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ afee dani hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa.

english: Why do I need to build a shade net or palm-frond roof over my crop nursery bed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa hulutsoo ŋshɔŋ loo ŋmei tso ŋta yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ashishi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Tender young sprouts are like tiny newborn infants that cannot survive harsh rainfall or burning sun. A shaded nursery canopy softens heavy raindrops that would wash away small seeds and protects delicate shoots from drying out.
ga: Tso bibioo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ tamɔ abifao bibioo ni afɔ lɛ ehee. ni nyɛŋ adamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa Tsu ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yiteŋ baaha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ afee blɛoo. Enɛ hoɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe ni ebuɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main element crops use to build green leaves and grow big. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost feeds the plant so it turns dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji nɔ titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aku sɛɛ afee eŋɔli ni mli edɔ.

english: Why does my land yield fewer bags of maize each year if I keep planting maize on the exact same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil over and over until the earth is exhausted. Rotating your crops with beans, cowpeas, or groundnuts puts natural food back into the soil.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli shii abɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni sũ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi. Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛ ŋmeii, tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why did my crops wilt and dry up right after I poured chemical fertilizer at the base of their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ewo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts. When placed right against a plant stem without rain or soil mixing, it draws moisture out of the plant roots and burns them, causing the crop to wilt.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli ŋmei babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he ni nugbɔ loo sũ efutu mli Ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi amli ni eshãa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nii lɛ baagbi.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into fruit when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high as a defense mechanism to save water and energy. The heat damages the pollen inside the flower, so the plant drops it to survive.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Dɔlɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ baai koni amɛhi shi.

english: What causes my cassava tubers to rot in the ground before harvest time during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: When soil stays soaked with water for too long, air cannot reach the plant roots. This lack of oxygen causes root suffocation and lets soil fungi easily attack and rot the cassava tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ewo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ tsei shishifãi ahe. Oxygen ni bɛ nɛɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛhaa amɛtutuaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ oya

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn brown and drop off from the bottom during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛjɛɔ shishi amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have large leaves that lose water very quickly in dry winds. During dry spells, the plant deliberately drops its older lower leaves to save its remaining water for the growing stem inside.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai wuji ni nu fiteɔ oya waa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ba. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tsei lɛ baajɛ amɛtsui mli amɛshɛrɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amɛshwie koni amɛkɛto nu ni eshwɛ lɛ he kɛha tso lɛ yitso ni miida yɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small twisted balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni etsɔ bɔɔlu bibii ni efite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny invisible sucking insects, like mites or aphids, hiding under the leaves to drink the plant's sap. Their feeding damages the leaf tissue, causing it to twist and stunt plant growth.
ga: Koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ kɛ baai lɛ akumɔ baa. ni anyɛɛɛ ana, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii Ekɛ ehe teeɔ baai lɛ ashishi koni enu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Amɛ niyenii lɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji. Enɛ haa etsɔɔ ehe ni etsĩɔ tsei adalɛ naa.

english: Why do I see small holes and soft powder inside the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Ni powda ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ yɛ mi-abele tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which crawls deep into the soft central leaves of the maize plant to feed where it is hidden and safe from predators.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatao niyenii yɛ hei ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow before the corn cobs even form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmei lɛ po feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom usually mean your maize plant lacks nitrogen, which is essential plant food. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves stay green so the plant can feed its corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do extension officers say that planting beans or groundnuts helps improve my soil for the next farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha dumɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in small bumps on their roots. When the crop season ends, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ ba naagbee. Nakai nitrogen ni atsĩ naa lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes through the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ko kɛmiitsɔ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on the tender leaf funnel of young maize. Inspecting your field early and putting recommended bio-pesticides or neem seed extracts directly into the leaf funnel controls them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ anɔ. Kwɛmɔ nibii ni odu lɛ amli mra ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem dumɔwui ni ajieɔ yi lɛ awo baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ koni okudɔ amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking juices from the plant and spreading diseases. Spraying your pepper plants with neem leaf solution or insecticidal soap kills the bugs and keeps new leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem baa loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi lɛ ni eha baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because the roots need air to stay healthy. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to drain away quickly so the roots do not suffocate.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why do my harvested yams start growing green sprouts even when kept inside my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃mɔ eyɛ mli akɛ akɛto mi-shĩa lɛ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living plants that naturally wake up and try to grow new vines after a short resting period. Keeping your storage barn cool, shady, and well-ventilated slows down this sprouting process and keeps the yams fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji tsei ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ wain tsei heei yɛ hejɔɔmɔ be kuku ko sɛɛ. Kɛ́ oha otsu lɛ mli jɔ, eyɛ hulutsoo, ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu bote mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ oya, ni ebaaye ebua ni o-sweet potato lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop all their flowers without producing any cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛjieee cocoa ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they lack sufficient water, soil nutrients, or when tiny beneficial insects called midges are not available to pollinate them. Providing good shade and soil organic matter helps the tree retain water and hold onto its blossoms.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ nu faaa. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ Anyɛɛɛ afee nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ pollination. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo kpakpa kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔii amli.

english: What makes my plantain trees fall over so easily whenever a strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni haa mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi mlɛo nɛkɛ be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that can be weakened by tiny worms called nematodes or root rot. Propping up heavy fruiting trees with wooden poles and planting clean, healthy suckers helps keep the plants firmly rooted.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Atsɛɔ nakai feemɔ akɛ nematodes loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni woɔ yibii ni tsii ni akɛ tsei ewo mli lɛ, ni adu tsei ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ená shishifãi ni ma shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do the bottom ends of my green tomatoes turn black and flat before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato eŋɔli shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often brought on by irregular watering. Watering your tomato plants consistently helps them continuously pull calcium from the soil into the developing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyaa aduawai ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops grow much slower and look pale when weeds grow close to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo kwraa ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ beni jwɛi bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, soil food, and water. Clearing weeds early in the crop's life ensures all nutrients go straight to feeding your crops rather than feeding unwanted plants.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu. Jwɛi ni agbeɔ yɛ gbekɛbiiashi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha tsei ni he ehiaaa amɛ niyenii lɛ.

english: Can I use crushed neem leaves to stop insects from damaging my vegetables?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ neem baai ni atswa lɛ atsu nii koni kooloi akafite mi-aduawai lɛ?

english: Yes, neem leaves contain natural medicinal compounds that taste bitter to insects. Spraying neem water on your crops stops pests from feeding and laying eggs without using expensive chemical sprays.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni haa kooloi yeɔ hela lɛ yɛ neem baai lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ neem nu shwie oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi ni yeɔ nii lɛ anaa ni amɛkawo ŋmeii ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Is wood ash from my kitchen fire useful for protecting my crops?
ga: Ani tso sũ ni jɛɔ mi-kpataashi la mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɛbuɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Yes, sprinkling dry wood ash around the base of your plants deters pests like insects and snails, while also adding beneficial potassium into the soil to help plants grow strong.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso sũ ni egbi ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛtsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii anaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ potassium ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni eye ebua tsei ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I plant a very large number of seeds close together, will I get more harvest?
ga: Kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ, ani maná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: No, planting too closely forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak, thin plants with very low yields compared to properly spaced crops.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi waa kɛ akɛto tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: What happens if I plant my cassava sticks too close to one another?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ?

english: Cassava needs space underground to expand its roots. When planted too close together, the leaves shade each other from the sun and the roots stay small and thin.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he miihia cassava koni eshishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, baai lɛ haa hulu lɛ shɛreɔ amɛhe. ni shishifãi lɛ baafee bibii ni amɛhe tseee

english: Why does my cassava crop seem to grow so slowly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa fiofio yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava intentionally slows down its growth when water is scarce to save energy and survive. Once the rains return, the plant recovers and resumes building its tubers.
ga: Cassava jɛɔ etsui mli ehaa edalɛ baa shi kɛ́ nu faaa koni ekɛto hewalɛ he ni ehi shi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ ni efee bulbs heei.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen food from the soil, or the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ amu bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon heat is the plant's natural defense to reduce water loss. If the leaves open up again in the evening, the plant is healthy and just protecting itself from the hot sun.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe koni ekɛba nu ni efiteɔ lɛ shi. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ gbele ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ ni ebaabu ehe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛkɛ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my pepper plants falling off before any peppers grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ŋmɔtɔ lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, lack of water, or when insects fail to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ amɛna nɔnyɛɛ kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli, nu ni bɛ, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops after the rain comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild local plants that are naturally tougher and faster at stealing rain and soil food than domesticated crops, which is why early weeding is necessary to protect your farm.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni juɔ nugbɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii oya ni amɛfeɔ basabasa fe tsei ni yɔɔ shia lɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. Ehe miihia ni abu oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my stored grains spoil so quickly when harvested during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa ni mikɛto lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akpa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grains harvested in wet weather trap moisture inside. If they are not dried completely under the sun before storage, mold and pests quickly multiply and ruin the crop.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ agbiko yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani akɛtoɔ lɛ, Fungi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ faa oya ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each maize plant enough space lets the roots spread out and results in larger, healthier cobs rather than many tiny, weak ones.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni ebaaha ŋmãa ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba. Instead of a small cob many weak

english: Why are small green caterpillars eating the leaves in the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on young maize foliage. Treating them early with recommended organic or chemical remedies prevents them from destroying the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Amɛtsamɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni miida lɛ.

english: Plants lose water quickly through their leaves when the sun is hottest. Adding a layer of dry grass or leaves (mulch) over the soil helps trap moisture, keeping the roots cool and reducing water loss during peak heat.
ga: Plants lose water quickly through their leaves when the sun is hottest. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (Mulch) wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni ehaa nu ni fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ baa shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves often mean the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential food it needs to grow strong. The plant naturally moves nitrogen from its older leaves to support new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nɔ ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha gbɔmɔtsoŋ dalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni eye ebua dalɛ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Planting them after maize naturally restores nutrients back into the dirt for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Planting corn after corn will naturally return nutrients back to the soil for your next crop.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong, direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries them out. Keeping some tall trees or planting quick-growing shade crops like plantains protects them until they are strong enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni amɛgbi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ Loo tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu amɛhe kɛyashi tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high or when plants don't get steady water. Irregular watering or a lack of insects to pollinate the blossoms also prevents fruit from setting.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ nu daa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni bɛ ŋmeii lɛ hu baanyɛ atsĩ aduawai lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are fully mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the main stem becomes thick. You can also carefully dig up one test plant to see if the tubers are plump and firm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli etse Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu kaa tso kome hu he nii koni ona kɛji bulb lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ shiŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines onto wooden tall stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsɔseɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines onto stakes exposes more of the leaves to sunlight, which allows the plant to make more food and grow larger tubers underground rather than letting leaves rot on damp soil.
ga: Kɛ́ owó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la babaoo ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tsei woɔ niyenii babaoo. ni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaha baai lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ,.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a short dry spell before the continuous rains start. Planting too early can cause seeds to germinate and then dry up and die during that dry break.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku sɛɛ. Dani nugbɔ baanɛ be fɛɛ be Dumɔ mra tsɔ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi ni amɛgboi yɛ be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops sometimes look yellow or stressed after I spray chemicals to kill pests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛhaoɔ beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ amɛ lɛ shwieɔ amɛnɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Using strong chemicals or applying them incorrectly can burn the plant leaves and shock the crop. Chemicals can also harm beneficial life in the soil that helps your crops absorb nutrients to stay green and strong.
ga: Tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ ni eha tso lɛ he afee shoo. Tsofai hu yeɔ wala ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ lɛ hu awui.

english: Why are the pests on my farm becoming harder to kill even when I spray chemicals regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ agbemɔ wa fe tsutsu lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai shwieɔ nɔ daa moŋ?

english: Overusing the same chemicals can cause pests to build resistance. Chemical sprays can also accidentally kill helpful insects that naturally eat those pests, allowing the bad pests to multiply faster.
ga: Tsofa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ hela lɛ. Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbe kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ kooloi bibii lɛ yɛ oshara mli lɛ hu. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai fɔji lɛ faa oya.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray my farm without causing problems for my crop flowers?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mafɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni mikɛ naagbai baaa mitsei lɛ afɔfɔi lɛ anɔ?

english: It is best to spray very early in the morning or late in the evening. Friendly insects like bees visit flowers during the day, so spraying when they are inactive protects them and allows your crop flowers to be properly pollinated.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie nɔ lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Kplukai ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo tamɔ ŋmeii yasaraa fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsofa shwie fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ be mli ni amɛtsuuu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe ni eye ebua ofɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfee pollination jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is there a way I can control pests on my farm without relying entirely on chemical sprays?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni matsɔ nɔ makudɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ɔɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ nɔ kwraa?

english: Yes, you can manage pests by clearing diseased plant parts, planting mixed crops, and allowing natural predator insects to live on your farm so you only need to spray when pest damage is very severe.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ oye kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ tsei lɛ ahe fãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni ooodu, kɛ adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ni oooha amɛhi oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ pɛ kɛji tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ efite waa.

english: Why do the flowers on my crop plants keep falling off without forming any fruit or pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii loo ŋmeii ko lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when they are not pollinated. Friendly insects must visit the flowers to transfer pollen from one flower to another; if there are no insects around, the flowers cannot turn into fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ afeee amɛ pollin. Esa akɛ kooloi bibii ni feɔ naanyo lɛ ayasara fɔfɔi koni amɛjie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛya ekroko mli. Kɛji kooloi bɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Fɔfɔi ko nyɛŋ afee aduawai.

english: Are all the insects I see crawling or flying around my crop leaves harmful to my farm?
ga: Kplukai ni mina lɛ fɛɛ miiho loo amɛmiiho kɛmiibɔle amɛhe. Ani mi aduawai ahe baai lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔ lɛ awui?

english: No, many insects on your farm are helpful. Some eat destructive pests, while others act as pollinators that carry pollen between flowers so your crops can produce good yields.
ga: Dabi, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ kooloi babaoo ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe. Henɔi komɛi yeɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii. yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ pollen ni woɔ pollen yɛ fɔfɔi ateŋ. Koni onibii ni oduɔ lɛ awo yibii kpakpai

english: How do small insects actually help my crops produce a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi bibii baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: When insects land on flowers searching for food, they pick up fine grains of pollen on their bodies and drop them on other flowers. This process, called pollination, causes the plant to set healthy seeds, fruits, and pods.
ga: Kɛ́ kooloi bibii tara fɔfɔi anɔ ni amɛmiitao niyenii Amɛjieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛgbɔmɔtsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ni amɛkɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi krokomɛi anɔ. Atsɛɔ gbɛ nɛɛ akɛ pollination. Ehaa tsei náa dumɔwui, aduawai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees need tiny midges and flies around the farm to yield good pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi-cacao tso lɛ afee bibioo ni efo kɛbɔle ŋmɔ lɛ he koni enyɛ ená ŋmeii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers are very small and hidden. Tiny insects like midges are the main ones able to fit inside the flowers to carry pollen, which is necessary for the flowers to turn into cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa waa ni amɛfeɔ teemɔŋ, ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ji gbɔi titri ni baanyɛ abote fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛyawo pollen. Enɛ he miihia koni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: What can I do around my farm field to attract more helpful insects to my crop flowers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maya he fɛɛ he? miŋmɔji lɛ amli koni mikɛgbala kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ babaoo kɛba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afɔfɔi lɛ anɔ

english: You can leave small flower strips or natural vegetation along your farm boundaries and avoid spraying chemicals when your crops are in full bloom so beneficial insects have a safe place to live.
ga: Obaanyɛ oshi fɔfɔii bibii bibii. loo adebɔɔ mli tsei ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ ahe lɛ Ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he beni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ewo fɔfɔi lɛ. Koni aha kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ aná he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛhi

english: Why do my crops yield plenty of leaves and flowers but very few actual fruits during harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ woɔ baai kɛ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii diɛŋtsɛ fioo ko pɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: A lack of insect activity is a main cause. Even if plants produce many healthy flowers, those flowers will wither without making fruit if pollinators are disrupted or killed off by farm sprays.
ga: Kplukai ni tsuuu nii lɛ ji nɔ titri ni kɛbaa. Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ, Shi nakai fɔfɔi lɛ hu baagbo ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ gba pollinators lɛ anaa loo egbe amɛ.

english: Why is it always hard for me to find good rice seeds to buy right when the planting season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaa kɛhaa mi akɛ mahe ŋmãa dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ? Mɛɛ be ji ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ?

english: Most farmers wait until the first rains fall before looking for seeds, creating a sudden high demand that leads to market shortages. Securing or saving certified seeds standard months before planting season begins prevents this problem.
ga: Okwaafoi babaoo mɛɔ kɛyashiɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ dani amɛtaoɔ dumɔwui. Enɛ haa nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ fa babaoo trukaa ni no haa jara lɛ nɔ faaa. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ loo akɛtoɔ nyɔji babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: How can I check if the local rice seeds I bought in the market will actually sprout before I sow them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji akɛ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ dani madu?

english: You can test seed viability by placing 10 sample seeds in a wet cloth for a few days; if 8 or more grow sprouts, your seeds are healthy and good for planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka dumɔwui lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni okɛaawo mama ni mli efɔ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji oyɛ ŋmeii 8 loo nɔ ni fe nakai lɛ, odumɔwui lɛ baaná hewalɛ ni amɛhi kɛha dumɔ.

english: When is the best time for me to plant local rice so that my crop is ready for harvest around August?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa koni ŋmãa lɛ afee klalo kɛha kpamɔɔ yɛ August aaafee?

english: Planting your local rice between April and May allows the crop to use the major rains to grow sturdy, reaching full grain maturity by early August as dry weather sets in.
ga: Omɔ ni ooodu yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ yɛ April kɛ May teŋ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ maŋtsɛ nugbɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ be fɛɛ be. Amɛbaatsɔ dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ yɛ August shishijee gbɛ beni kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi ebaa lɛ.

english: Why does my local rice variety take much longer to grow than the quick-maturing foreign rice varieties sold in agro-shops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimaŋ ŋmãa lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ fe maŋsɛɛ ŋmãa ni daa oya ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ okwaayeli shwapoi amli lɛ?

english: Traditional local rice varieties are naturally adapted to local conditions and have a natural growth cycle of 120 to 150 days, whereas imported hybrid seeds are specifically bred for rapid 90-day cycles.
ga: Akɛ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa henɔi ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ blema lɛ etsake shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. ni amɛyɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ be ni ji gbii 120 kɛyashi 150, yɛ be mli ni afɔɔ dumɔwui ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛdara oya gbii 90.

english: Why do my young rice leaves start turning yellow whenever water dries up on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ be fɛɛ be ni nu lɛ baagbi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants need soil moisture to transport nitrogen and nutrients from the earth into their stems; without water, the plant starves, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Rice plants need soil moisture to transport nitrogen and nutrients from the soil to their stems. Kɛ nu bɛ lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye tsei lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do my local rice plants grow very tall with leafy green stems but produce very few grain heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimaŋ ŋmãa tsei lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to put all its energy into leaf and stem height rather than producing strong flowers and rice grains.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ama baai kɛ eshishifã lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui ni mli wa

english: Why do birds attack my rice farm more heavily during the period when the grains are just forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi tutuaa mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ waa yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: During the early 'milky' growth stage, the developing rice grain contains a soft, sweet liquid starch that is easy and nutritious for birds to feed on before the outer shell hardens.
ga: Yɛ ‘mliki’ lɛ shishijee fãi lɛ amli lɛ, ŋmãa ni miiya hiɛ lɛ mli ŋmãa ni mli tse ni ji nu ni mli ŋɔɔ lɛ yɛ mli. Okpoi yeɔ amɛ mlɛo ni amɛyeɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ dani kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli waa.

english: How do I know that my local rice field is fully ripe and ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mimaŋ ŋmɔji lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ makpa?

english: Your rice crop is ready for harvest when about 80% to 85% of the panicles change from green to a golden-yellow color, and the individual grains feel firm and hard when squeezed.
ga: O ŋmãa tsei lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ be mli ni aaafee 80% kɛyashi 85% ni ji panicles lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ mli. Ni dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko baanu he akɛ eyɛ shiŋŋ ni eyɛ shiŋŋ kɛ́ amɔ mli.

english: Why does my harvested local rice develop tiny insects and go bad when I store it in bags inside my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimaŋ ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ lɛ? Ni efiteɔ kɛ́ akɛwo kotoku mli yɛ tsu lɛ mli?

english: If rice grains are bagged while still containing hidden moisture, the humid air inside the bag attracts fungi and encourages weevil eggs to hatch and feed on the grain.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lolo lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ gbalaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmãa lɛ hewalɛ koni efɔ ni eye ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Why do market traders offer me lower prices for my local rice right around August?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayelɔi haa mi maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa jara ni baa shi yɛ August mli lɛ?

english: August is the peak harvest window when many farmers bring fresh rice to the market at once, creating an oversupply that naturally pushes crop prices down.
ga: August ji kpamɔ be ni fe fɛɛ. Beni okwaafoi babaoo kɛ ŋmãa hee baa jara nɔ shikome lɛ Enɛ haa ŋmãa ni fa fe nine baa jara nɔ, ni no haa ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ jara baa shi.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain or cassava nearby provides shade and keeps the soil cool until the cocoa stems grow mature and tough.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ebaaha hulutsoo ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ajɔɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe wa.
