english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning pale yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow leaves and green up. Adding organic manure or a nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa amɛhe su ekoŋŋ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve into a form that roots can drink. Applying fertilizer to dry soil in hot heat can burn the plant's roots or evaporate into the air, wasting your effort and money.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛtsɔ mli ni amɛfee nɔ ko ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi lɛ ashã loo amɛho kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. ni fiteɔ hewalɛ kɛ shika

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rains stay on my farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air inside the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits on the land without draining, it suffocates the roots and encourages rot-causing fungi to grow underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ta shikpɔŋ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ewo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and turning yellow at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by small sap-sucking insects like whiteflies that spread leaf curl viruses. Controlling these insects early prevents the virus from spreading and stopping fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ whiteflies, ni gbɛɔ helai ni haa baa lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ni ekpa aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: What is eating hole patterns into the central leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ayeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These holes are usually caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm that hide deep inside the center funnel of the corn plant. Catching them early and applying targeted controls prevents them from destroying the growing tip of the stalk.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii tso lɛ teŋgbɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ buji nɛɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ targeted control atsu nii lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tsei ni miida lɛ ashishifãi.

english: Is it good practice to plant groundnuts in the same field alongside my maize?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ mi ŋmei lɛ masɛi?

english: Yes, groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen food from the air into the soil. Planting them with maize enriches the soil for the maize while allowing you to harvest two different crops from one piece of land.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmãa baadu lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni ŋɔɔ kɛha ŋmãa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the small shoots to grow around one main plantain stool?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ? Amɛ fɛɛ amɛdaraa yɛ sɛi titri kome he.

english: Allowing too many shoots to grow causes them to steal water and nutrients from each other, resulting in tiny bunches. Cutting away extra shoots leaves the main trunk with enough food to produce large, heavy plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ dara babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight powers the vine to manufacture energy, which travels down to make the tuber underground swell bigger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Hulu la haa wain tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ hewalɛ. ni tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi koni eha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ mli alɛɛ waa

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat or lacks water. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save water and energy so it can survive.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu bɛ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field without plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily burn under direct sunshine. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that provide shade and keep the air moist, acting like natural umbrellas until the cocoa trees are strong enough to withstand the sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ hulu lɛ naa.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the juices from the undersides of the leaves. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or recommended sprays helps the leaves expand normally again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ nɔ lɛ ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã bɔ ni sa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does letting weeds grow around my crops make my plants stay small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ? Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haa mitsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa?

english: Weeds act like thieves in your farm by quickly stealing water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your main crops. Clearing weeds early gives your plants full access to the food and light they need to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa otsei lɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkpa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning light yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize are a warning sign that the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and grow. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji kɔkɔbɔɔ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas before planting maize on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei dani madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that take natural nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When you harvest them, they leave that extra food behind in the soil, which helps your next maize crop grow better without buying as much fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ amɛhe gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okpa nii lɛ Amɛshiɔ nakai niyenii ni fa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa o-abele henɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tamɔ nɛkɛ.

english: Why is it bad to throw dry fertilizer on my crops when the ground is very dry and there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi baawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi waa ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plant roots can only drink in fertilizer when it is dissolved in water. If you apply dry fertilizer during a dry period without watering, the fertilizer cannot be taken up by the plant and can actually burn the roots.
ga: Tso shishifãi baanyɛ anu ŋmɔshi nibii pɛ kɛji akɛ etsɔ nu mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi fata he yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni okɛ nu wooo mli lɛ, Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when heavy rains flood my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eha ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When rainwater sits in flat soil for too long, it smothers the roots, causing them to rot; planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges lets extra water drain away easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nugbɔ nu hi shikpɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants before any tomatoes start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms often drop off unpollinated when the weather gets extremely hot and dry, or when the soil goes from very wet to very dry. Keeping the soil consistently damp with mulch helps the plants hold onto their flowers and set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni pollination bɛ mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ waa mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ muji wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai amli.

english: If too many sucker shoots grow around one main plantain trunk, they all fight for the same water and nutrients, resulting in small, thin bunches. Leaving only one strong main stem and one or two young suckers makes the main tree yield large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ, Plantain titri kome Plantains nɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni no haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa. Kɛ́ ashi tso titri kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ tso bibioo kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on instead of letting them trail on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo tsei kɛha sweet potato wain tsei koni makwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha enyiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach up high so their leaves can catch full sunlight to make energy for growing large tubers. Raising the leaves off the damp ground also prevents leaves from catching fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni awo sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la ni fa babaoo koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛha bulbs wuji ni yaa hiɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ akamɔ amɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Leaving shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects the young cocoa leaves from burning and helps the soil stay moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo baa.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to yield a fruit bunch after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers require rich soil filled with organic matter and steady moisture. If they have to fight weeds for nutrients or face long dry spells without water, their growth slows down significantly.
ga: Plantain suckers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli daa lɛ eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ ehe bahia ni amɛkɛ jwɛi awuu koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai loo amɛkɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nu bɛ mli lɛ akpee. Amɛdalɛ baa shi waa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, which is an important nutrient for leaf growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the maize leaves become green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. which is an important nutrient for leaf growth Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help corn leaves become green and strong again.

english: How can I tell if my farmland has the right soil for growing cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni sa kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔ?

english: Cassava performs best in loose, sandy soil that lets water drain easily. If the ground is heavy clay that holds water for days, the cassava roots will rot or fail to grow big.
ga: Yucca tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋã kɛ sũ ni haa nu hoɔ oya lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni hiɛɔ nu gbii babaoo. Kasava shishifãi lɛ baagboi loo amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani aduawai jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or sudden dry conditions. Keeping the soil regularly watered and covering the soil with mulch keeps the roots cool and helps fruits set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu daa ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he.

english: Why does my cowpea crop produce plenty of leafy branches but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ niji kɛ baai babaoo shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas grow extra leaves instead of pods if the soil has too much nitrogen or if they receive excessive water. Giving the plant less water during flowering encourages it to produce pods.
ga: Cowpeas baakwɛ baai krokomɛi yɛ pods najiaŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ. Nu ni faaa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ŋmeii aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my garden pepper plants twisting and curling into balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni atsɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tso ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ mli ni atsɔ mli afee bɔɔlu lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from under the leaves. Clearing nearby weeds and controlling these insects restores normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ baaha baai lɛ ada bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do I see small worms hiding and eating inside the center stalks of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ateŋ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ?

english: These worms are Fall Armyworms, which prefer to hide in the tender center of maize plants. Spotting them early and applying safe pest control keeps the central leaf cone healthy so the plant can grow.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ. Ni aaana amɛ mra Kɛ shweshweeshwe nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ shishitoo lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers turn out bent and misshapen instead of growing long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers twist when they hit hard, compacted soil or underground rocks as they try to expand. Making high, soft earthen mounds or ridges gives the yams space to swell easily underground.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ baatsɔ kɛji amɛtswa shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni mli edɔ loo tɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ nɔ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋmeii ni afee lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo.

english: Why are there dark brown spots forming all over my cassava leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni cassava baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Brown spots on cassava leaves are usually caused by fungal leaf spot disease, which spreads when leaves stay wet for a long time. Spacing your cassava plants further apart allows air to flow through and dry the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal leaf spot disease lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ baa, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji baai lɛ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Gbɛ ni kã ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli ni eha baai lɛ agbi.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains or plantain suckers next to my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains loo plantain ŋmeii yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? kookoo dumɔwui heei

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast with broad leaves, acting like umbrellas that provide living shade and keep the soil moist while the young cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta, ni ehaa hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ be mli ni kookoo tso bibioo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: How do I know which direction to place my cassava stem cuttings into the ground when planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole gbɛ ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava niji lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ oodu?

english: You need to check the small nodes or buds along the stem and make sure they point upward toward the sky. Planting stems upside down makes it hard for shoots to grow upwards, resulting in weak plants and poor root yields.
ga: Obaasumɔ ni okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii bibii komɛi yɛ tso lɛ he ni okwɛ akɛ amɛmiitsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ tso lɛ hiɛ shi lɛ, ebaaha ewa aha ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Yellowing of the bottom leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for healthy green leaves. The plant pulls nutrients from its older, lower leaves to feed new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Tsei gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Will planting cowpeas or beans alongside my corn crop spoil my maize yield?
ga: Ani tsina loo ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ baaye ŋmãa ni mifeɔ lɛ awui?

english: No, legumes like cowpeas naturally fix nitrogen from the air into the soil. Intercropping them with maize enriches the soil and helps feed the maize without competing aggressively for nutrients.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ ŋmɛɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ kooloi niyenii ni ekɛ ehe wooo niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋshii mli waa.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to dig inside the center leaves of my corn plants and create ragged holes?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ mi ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛfeɔ bu ni mli ewo muji?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that feeds inside the growing central leaves of maize. Checking plants early and applying approved control methods directly into the leaf funnel stops them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa baa ni miida lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Kɛ gbɛ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛkwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ baaha nakai tsei lɛ akpa.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava bushes curl up and show yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is a symptom of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies and infected stem cuttings. Using disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by agricultural officers prevents this condition.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ Mli ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi kɛhaa lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ shihilɛ nɛɛ naa.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable crops during the middle of the day or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo aduawai anɔ nu yɛ gbi mli loo leebi?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because cool morning soil absorbs water easily, and plants can use the moisture to survive the dry afternoon heat without losing water to sun evaporation.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ leebi shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu oya. Ni tsei baanyɛ amɛkɛ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ atsu nii koni amɛhi shi yɛ shwane mli latsaa ni mli egbi lɛ mli ni nu lɛ elaajeee kɛtsɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper and tomato plants drop off without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when plants face stress caused by severe heat, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Maintaining steady soil moisture helps the blossoms convert into fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers rot quickly when I pile them directly on the floor inside my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛto shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Piling yams directly on dry floors without air movement traps heat and moisture, creating conditions where fungal rot thrives. Storing yams off the ground on raised bamboo racks in cool, airy barns keeps them fresh.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potatoes tswa shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ tsiii ehe lɛ, ebaamɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni rot fungus baanyɛ ada yɛ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potatoes to shikpɔŋ yɛ ŋmeii ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does my dry maize turn into white powder after sitting in my barn for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ etsɔ powda yɛŋ beni eta ŋmɔ mli nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grain weevils burrow inside dry maize seeds to lay eggs, and their young eat the grain from the inside out. Properly drying maize to very low moisture and using hermetic (airtight) storage bags protects the harvest from insects.
ga: Dumɔwui ŋmeii shwieɔ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ amli koni amɛwo amɛwui. ni amɛbii lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi waa, ni akɛ vacuum storage bags tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu ŋmãa lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ahe.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. Large shade trees protect the young plants from drying out, keep the soil cool, and maintain moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ buɔ tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ekwɛ koni hulutsoo be lɛ aya nɔ aahu kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my cassava plants lose most of their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry periods as a self-defense mechanism to save water. By dropping leaves, the plant stops losing moisture through evaporation and keeps its energy stored safely inside the underground tubers until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaai lɛ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli akɛ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe koni ekɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ akafite nu kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. ni akɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli shweshweeshwe kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without forming any fruits during the hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato blossoms, making it impossible for the flowers to pollinate and set fruit. When temperatures get too high, the plant naturally drops the unpollinated flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee pollin ni amɛwo yibii. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Yellowing lower leaves in a V-shape pattern is a clear sign that the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to build green foliage and grow healthy stalks.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ gbɛ ni tamɔ V nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ baai eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant cowpeas or groundnuts before planting maize on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu cowpeas loo peanuts dani wɔdu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly bacteria on their roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays in the ground to feed the next crop like maize naturally.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ naanyobɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa amɛ Nakai nitrogen ni aŋã lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why does using water from a farm fish pond make my leafy vegetables grow faster and greener?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ mli loo ŋshɔi amli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa mi-aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ daraa oya ni ehaaa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ afite lɛ?

english: Water from fish ponds is naturally rich in fish waste, which acts as a liquid fertilizer containing nitrogen and organic matter that leafy crops can easily absorb for fast, green growth.
ga: Nu ni jɛɔ loo ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ loo sũ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni nitrogen kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɔɔ mli ni tsei ahe tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ oya koni amɛdara oya, ni amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: Why do my yam plants produce smaller tubers if I do not stake the vines with sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛji mikɛ niji etswaaa wain tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb up stakes so their leaves can spread out in the air to capture sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food through photosynthesis, which is then sent down to expand the tuber underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso ko nɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ. Hulu la haa baai feɔ niyenii kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. Kɛkɛ lɛ, atsuɔ lɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛgbala ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my plantain plants start producing smaller bunches if I leave all the young suckers growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii bibii feemɔ kɛji mishi ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: Too many young suckers attached to one plantain stool compete with the mother plant for soil nutrients, water, and space. Cutting back extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, ensuring the mother plant gets full energy to build big bunches.
ga: Tso kome mli ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ tso kome he lɛ kɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ ŋwɛi. Excess shoots are cut off. Shi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 1-2 pɛ koni tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ aná hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛfee kuu agbo.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the inner leaves inside the whorl of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest whose moths lay eggs inside the dark, moist center roll (whorl) of young maize plants where the caterpillars can safely feed on the tender young leaves.
ga: This is commonly caused by Fall Armyworm, a pest in which moths lay their eggs within the moist, dark middle of young corn plants. Kplukai lɛ baanyɛ aye baai bibii shweshweeshwe.

english: Why is it bad for me to spray water directly onto my pepper leaves late in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ ehiii kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Leaves that remain wet overnight create a damp, dark environment that allows fungal diseases to germinate and spread easily across your pepper plants before the morning sun can dry them.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ haa shihilɛ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni ewoɔ duŋ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ŋmeii helai baakwɛ̃ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã o-pepper tsei lɛ fɛɛ amli dani leebi hulu lɛ agbi amɛ.

english: When maize plants lack nitrogen—the nutrient that gives leaves their dark green color—they pull it from the older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ, Amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛha ŋmãa hee ni da yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers instead of turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they get stressed, usually from extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant focus on growing leaves instead of holding onto its blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛhao. This is usually caused by extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. This causes the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of clinging to flowers.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark brown and rotting during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, cool, and wet conditions, especially when tree branches are too crowded to let sunlight and air dry out the pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ, ni mli ejɔ, kɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, titri lɛ kɛ́ tsei aniji lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haaa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔji yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural self-defense mechanism to reduce the leaf surface exposed to the hot sun, helping the plant save moisture and survive intense heat.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Koni akɛba baai ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ fɛ̃i mli ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do I get smaller maize ears when I plant many seeds close together in one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa toi bibii anɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots compete heavily for the same water, soil nutrients, and sunlight, leaving no single plant with enough energy to grow big, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ nu he akaŋ waa. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni fa tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are my cassava leaves twisting up and turning yellowish instead of growing broad and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects; the virus damages the leaves' ability to capture sunlight, resulting in stunted tuber growth under the ground.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela, ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Virus lɛ fiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni baai lɛ yɔɔ ni amɛkɛmɔɔ hulu la lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ daraaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn dark and sunken before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efoɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This issue is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often triggered by irregular watering where the soil goes from very dry to flooded too quickly.
ga: Blossom end rot, ni ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ kɛ naagba nɛɛ baa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ je shishi kɛjɛ he ni egbi waa lɛ nɔ kɛtee nu afua oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when planted in full sunlight without shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight; shade plants like plantains shield them and keep the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ hu buɔ amɛhe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does my land produce a smaller harvest every year even though I use the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmaa fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops take nutrients out of the soil with every harvest; if you do not replenish the soil with organic manure, compost, or fertilizer, the soil becomes exhausted and yield drops.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni abaakpa amɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ organic ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow slowly and look pale even when rain falls regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight from the soil faster than your crops can absorb them, depriving your crops of the food they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni onibii ni oduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why are my crops failing even though I plant at the exact same time every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ be kome mli daa afi moŋ lɛ?

english: Weather patterns have shifted, meaning traditional rainy seasons no longer start or end at fixed months, so planting dates must adapt to when the rain actually arrives.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tsakeɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kusum nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ejeee shishi dɔŋŋ loo egbeee naa yɛ nyɔŋ ko mli dɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ atsake gbi ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ koni akɛto be ni nugbɔ lɛ baa diɛŋtsɛ lɛ he.

english: Why are the rains in my area becoming so short and unpredictable?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ kuku ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ?

english: Changing climate patterns cause rainfall to be erratic, leading to longer dry spells and sudden shortages of rain during key growing periods.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ. Enɛ haa nugbɔshiimɔi bei ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ baa yɛ bei ni he hiaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa lɛ amli.

english: Can I still get a good harvest if I do not depend only on rainwater?
ga: Kɛ́ wɔkɛ wɔhe fɔ̃ɔɔ nugbɔ nu nɔ lɛ, ani wɔbaanyɛ wɔkpa ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lolo?

english: Yes, using simple watering methods like drip irrigation or storing rainwater allows your crops to receive steady water and produce good yields even without rainfall.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo nugbɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa nu be fɛɛ be ni ewoɔ yibii kpakpai kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po.

english: How can I keep water in my soil for a longer time during hot days?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha nu ahi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli?

english: Adding organic compost and covering bare soil with dry grass or leaves stops moisture from evaporating quickly under the hot sun.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi wo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Is it possible for a small-scale farmer like me to water crops without expensive pumps?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ okwaafonyo bibioo ko tamɔ mi baanyɛ ashɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe nu ni ekɛ nu pɔmpii ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: Yes, simple methods like bucket drip kits, shallow hand-dug wells, and gravity-fed water channels can effectively water your farm on a budget.
ga: Hɛɛ, gbɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ baagi mli nu ni hoɔ. Buu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni akɛ niji tsu kɛ nu ni jɛɔ mli kɛbaa ni kɛ hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ nu aha oŋmɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ shika hu akatsu nii.

english: How does preparing my soil properly before planting give me a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni asaa jogbaŋŋ dani aduɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha mawo yibii babaoo?

english: Proper land preparation breaks up hard soil, allowing crop roots to grow deep, store extra water, and easily absorb nutrients needed for strong crop growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni asaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ baagbala shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ. Nu krɛdɛɛ ni akɛhiɛɔ mli ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ lɛ shwieɔ mli oya

english: How can I know if my farmland soil is healthy enough to feed my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Healthy soil is crumbly, dark in color, holds moisture well after rain, and contains visible organic matter like earthworms and plant remains.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi, eyɛ ediŋŋ, ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni anaa tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsei ahe nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why does my soil turn hard and dry out so quickly just a few days after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbiɔ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ lɛ?

english: Soil hardens and dries rapidly when it lacks organic compost or when it is left bare and directly exposed to the hot sun.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa ni egbiɔ oya kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli loo kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why am I working so hard on my farm every season but still getting very small yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsuɔ nii waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi ni minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Hard physical labor alone cannot guarantee a big harvest if crops lack consistent water or proper soil nutrients during critical growth periods.
ga: Nitsumɔ ni wa pɛ nyɛŋ aha ŋmaa babaoo aba kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli.

english: What happens to my maize if a dry spell hits right when it starts flowering?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ ena hɔmɔ be mli ni ebɔi fɔfɔii shwiemɔ pɛ?

english: Flowering is the most crucial stage for grain development, so a water shortage during this time prevents seeds from forming properly and drastically reduces your harvest.
ga: Fɔfɔii lɛ ji be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ kɛha dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni faaa yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee jogbaŋŋ, ni ebaaha okpamɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi waa.

english: Why should I leave space between my crop rows instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Leaving space between rows gives crops enough sunlight, air, and soil nutrients to grow strong. It also gives you clear paths to move through with tools like cutlasses without damaging your crops.
ga: Gbɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tsei lɛ naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛdara. Ehaa bo gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ hu ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ otsɔ nibii ni eho tamɔ dadei ni okɛfiteee onibii lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know the right distance to measure between my plant rows when setting up my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni sa ni esa akɛ asusu yɛ tsei akui ateŋ beni atoɔ ŋmɔ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ?

english: Different crops need specific distances, such as 75 centimeters apart, to grow well. Measuring this space ensures plants do not choke each other and gives enough room to work safely with tools.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko aná he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ashɛ sɛntimitai 75, koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. He nɛɛ ni asusuɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa koni tsei lɛ akakpɛtɛ amɛhe. ni eha he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛ nitsumɔ dadei atsu nii shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do extension officers recommend using a measuring stick when laying out rows on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ tso ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe lɛ atsu nii kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ miito ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A measuring stick helps you maintain exact, consistent gaps across your whole field. Uniform spacing ensures every plant gets an equal share of soil nutrients and makes field maintenance much easier.
ga: Tsoi ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni okwɛɔ gbɛ ni ja ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ oyale lɛ mli fɛɛ. He ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ po haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni ehaa ŋmɔ mli saamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Will leaving wide spaces between rows cause my farm to produce less food overall?
ga: Gbɛ ni da ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋ Ani enɛ baaha miŋmɔ lɛ afee niyenii fioo yɛ fɛɛ mli?

english: No, properly spaced crops produce healthier and larger yields. Overcrowded plants grow thin and yield very little food, whereas well-spaced plants produce stronger, bigger harvests that make up for the open space.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni sa lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo aba. Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ daa ni amɛwoɔ niyenii fioo ko pɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni akɛ amɛ ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ tsei wuji ni he wa ni feɔ hei ni gbɛ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves compete fiercely for water, nutrients, and sunlight. This causes them to grow tall, weak, and unable to produce quality fruit or seeds.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tse lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ waa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ shwiili, amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo aduawai loo dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does proper plant spacing help protect my crops from fungal diseases?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe?

english: Good spacing allows breeze to blow freely between plants, keeping the leaves dry. Fungal diseases thrive in dark, damp, crowded spaces, so open gaps keep your crops healthier.
ga: He ni jɛkɛmɔ kpakpa yɔɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ Fungal helai lɛ shwereɔ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni gbɔmɛi eyi obɔ lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ hei ni agbele lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does sunlight affect how far apart I should space my crops?
ga: Te hulu la lɛ saa bɔ ni esa akɛ mikɛ mitsei lɛ ato he ko lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Crops use sunlight to manufacture food for growth. Proper spacing prevents larger leaves from casting shade on neighboring plants, allowing every crop to catch enough light to thrive.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛha dalɛ. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ baatsi baai wuji anaa koni amɛkafee hulutsoo yɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ anɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei fɛɛ ni amɛnáa la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara.

english: Why do some crops need wider spacing between rows than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ahe hiaa ni amɛto amɛhe gbɛjianɔ babaoo fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Crops behave differently as they mature; some spread broad leaves or deep roots sideways. Giving wider crops extra room prevents them from overshadowing and starving adjacent plants.
ga: Tsei feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Ekomɛi yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ loo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛyashɛɔ amɛsɛɛ. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ ni oooya hiɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛtsi tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anaa ni ekɛ hɔmɔ akaye amɛ.

english: Why do I need to leave extra room between plant rows for tools like cutlasses and knives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi gbɛ kroko yɛ tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ kɛha nibii tamɔ dadei kɛ ŋmeii?

english: Leaving sufficient space allows you or your farmworkers to maneuver harvesting knives and cutlasses safely without accidentally chopping into crop stems or hurting yourselves while working.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa bo loo oŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi lɛ nyɛɔ nyɛjieɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ shweshweeshwe ni nyɛfoŋ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe tsei yɛ oshara mli loo nyɛpilaaa nyɛhe beni nyɛtsuɔ nii lɛ.

english: How does proper row spacing make weeding easier for me?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbɛ ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ atoɔ jwɛi lɛ ahe lɛ haa jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛhaa mi?

english: Clear paths between rows give you enough room to swing a hoe or cutlass freely, allowing you to quickly clear weeds without damaging the main stems or roots of your crops.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni yɔɔ sɛɛkuu lɛ teŋ lɛ haa bo gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ okɛ oshovel loo o-dagger lɛ atswa oya. Ehaa onyɛɔ ojieɔ jwɛi lɛ oya ni ofiteee tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ loo shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are there small holes in my young maize leaves and tiny caterpillars hiding inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji ŋmeii lɛ? Mi nɔ lɛ yɛ bu bibioo ko. Ani akɛtee tsɔne lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on maize leaves and burrows into the growing stem, which slows down plant growth and reduces your harvest if left untreated.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai ni efoɔ bu kɛyaa ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni ehaa onibii lɛ baa shi kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn yellow and curl up during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily in direct sunlight and hot Harmattan winds; they need shade trees or plantains nearby to shelter them and keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni amɛha amɛhi shi ni amɛha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts fix natural nitrogen from the air into the soil through their roots, which enriches the land and acts as natural fertilizer for nutrient-hungry crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ tsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛhaa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii babaoo ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha tsei ni he hiaa niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when we get too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ wɔná nugbɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil to breathe. When water sits on the field for too long, it cuts off air to the roots and encourages soil fungal diseases that cause the tubers to decay.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he hiaa cassava shishifãi koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ hela baa lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow very tall and thin with tiny ears when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛtoi bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ, be mli ni adu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leaving none of them with enough energy to produce big, healthy ears.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee toi wuji ni wa.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small bunches of fruit when I leave all the young suckers growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii bibii lɛ? Beni mishiɔ tsei bibii lɛ fɛɛ ni miida yɛ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ.

english: Young shoots surrounding the main plantain tree suck away water and nutrients from the soil, leaving less energy for the main stem to produce a large, heavy fruit bunch.
ga: ŋmeii bibii ni bɔle Dumɔwu titri lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ bɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛbaawo aduawai wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on instead of just trailing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooonyiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes exposes more leaves to direct sunlight so the plant can make food, while also keeping the leaves away from damp soil diseases during the rains.
ga: Kɛ́ owó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ aba tsei lɛ ahe. So plants can make food. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa baa lɛ akamɔ hela yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing fruits when the weather gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: High heat causes severe water stress in tomato plants, so they drop their flowers as a defense mechanism to save energy and survive rather than spending resources on developing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu he haomɔ ni naa wa baa tomato tsei amli. No hewɔ lɛ, tomato shwieɔ fɔfɔi akɛ hebuu gbɛ koni ekɛbu hewalɛ ni ehi shi. Instead of using resources to develop the fruit

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and stronger than my crops right after the rainy season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with deep roots that react instantly to water, allowing them to steal soil nutrients and moisture faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tso ko ni wa, ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni kɛ́ nu bote mli lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ oya fe tsei ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava take much longer to mature when I plant it on unploughed, hard soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Hard, unploughed soil makes it difficult for cassava roots to expand deep into the ground to gather water and nutrients, which slows down the overall growth of the plant.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni atsuuu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛbua nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ naa. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ fɛɛ dalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under harsh sun. Planting shade trees acts like a natural canopy, protecting young cocoa from intense heat while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants fail to produce fruits when I grow them under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ wooo yibii kɛ́ midu yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants require full, direct sunlight to make energy for flowering and fruiting. Under heavy tree shade, the pepper plant uses all its energy trying to grow tall to reach the light, leaving no energy to make peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo. Yɛ tsei ni mli tse lɛ ashishi lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. ni efiteee hewalɛ yɛ chili feemɔ mli

english: Why should I clear my farmland without burning the bushes and weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ ni mikɛshãaa jwɛi kɛ jwɛi?

english: Burning heat destroys natural nutrients in the soil and kills helpful soil organisms. Clearing without burning allows dead plants to decay naturally, turning into organic compost that holds water and feeds your crops.
ga: La ni tsoɔ lɛ mli dɔlɛ fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni egbeɔ sũ mli nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni egboi lɛ ni ashãaa amɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛgboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Ebafeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa nu hiɔ shi ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant tomatoes on the exact same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ makwɛ tomato yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting tomatoes in the same spot year after year allows tomato-specific pests and soil diseases to multiply in the ground. Rotating tomatoes with crops like beans or maize breaks this disease cycle and keeps the soil balanced.
ga: Tomato ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa tomato he tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tomato ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ. Ebaakpa hela nɛɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yes, planting maize and cassava together works very well. Maize grows fast and is harvested within a few months, while cassava grows slowly and takes over the space after the maize is cleared, giving you two harvests from one piece of land.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. Abɛi daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo ni eŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni ajie ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii shii enyɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: What will happen if I plant my maize seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When maize plants are crowded together, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin and weak, producing small, unfilled cobs instead of large, healthy ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ eyi amɛhe obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa ni eyiko lolo lɛ baa. Yɛ ŋmãa toi agbo ni mli wa najiaŋ

english: Yellow leaves on maize are usually a sign that the plant is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil. Adding organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves turn green so the crop can grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ organic fertilizer loo nitrogen fertilizer fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they suffer from water stress during dry spells, insect damage, or lack of soil nutrients. Providing adequate shade and protecting trees from insects helps the flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu he haomɔ kpe amɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo ni sa ha tso lɛ ni abu he kɛjɛ kooloi ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do some of my planted yam setts rot in the ground before they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni adu lɛ ekomɛi fiteɔ yɛ sũ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Yam setts rot mainly because of trapped water in flat soil or fungal infections from damaged seed pieces. Planting on raised mounds allows extra rainwater to drain away, preventing the setts from rotting.
ga: Nu ni etsi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ni jɛ dumɔwui lɛ fãi ni efite lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ titri ni kɛ sweet potato fitemɔ baa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu babaoo hoɔ kɛyaa. Etsiɔ sũ naa koni ekafite.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves dry up and fall off, typically around 9 to 12 months after planting. You can also dig around one plant carefully to check if the tubers are thick and firm before harvesting the whole farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli hu. Akwɛ tso kome mli jogbaŋŋ koni ana kɛji ŋmeii lɛ amli eyi kɛ ŋmeii dani akpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when the rains become too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away nitrogen—the primary food crops need for green growth—deep into the soil where roots cannot reach. When maize lacks nitrogen, its leaves turn yellow starting from the lower tips.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Kɛji nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ Ebaai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is healthy enough to start planting cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmei dumɔ?

english: Healthy soil feels crumbly rather than rock-hard or sticky, holds moisture well, and contains earthworms. Earthworms are a great sign that the soil is rich and easy for cassava roots to expand into.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli etse moŋ fe tɛi loo ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii hu yɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ji okadi kpakpa ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii ni ewaaa akɛ ŋmei lɛ baakwɛ̃ shishifãi.

english: Why does leaving dry plant stalks on my field after harvest help the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso ni egbi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Leaving dry stalks and leaves on the ground covers the soil like a blanket. It keeps the ground cool, retains moisture, and slowly rots into rich compost that feeds your next crop.
ga: Shi tsei ahe tsei kɛ baai ni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ, ni okɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli, ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for growing big tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp earth into the light and protects them from ground rot.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa la mli, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers grow so slowly when I plant them under big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ daraa blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo tso agbo ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Plantains require strong, direct sunlight to build energy rapidly. Large shade trees block sunlight and their big roots steal water and nutrients meant for the plantain.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ he miihia plantains koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba oya. Tso agbo ko ni haa hulu lɛ shɛreɔ Ni amɛshishifãi wuji lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha plantain lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves drop off early even when it is not the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ miiho oya nɛkɛ? Jeee nugbɔshiimɔ be ni?

english: Unseasonal leaf drop usually happens when water gets trapped at the roots due to poor drainage, or when fungal diseases like Black Pod attack the tree's water pathways.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baa kɛji nu lɛ tsɔ shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ tutua tso lɛ nu gbɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of green leaves but very few flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi fɔfɔi fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen-heavy fertilizer makes tomato plants spend all their energy growing tall and bushy instead of producing the flowers that turn into tomatoes.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha tomato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, moŋ fe ni eeefee fɔfɔi ni tsɔɔ tomato.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll up and look squeezed together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiimi amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from new leaves, or by intense heat forcing the plant to curl up to conserve moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai heei amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do my groundnut plants make the soil better for my next crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their root nodules. When you harvest, those roots decay and leave free plant food in the soil for maize.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi amli. Beni okpaa Nakai shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛshiɔ tsei niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amɛhaa ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Why are my sweet oranges dropping from the tree before they mature and turn sweet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet oranges lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara ni amɛbatsɔ sweet lɛ?

english: Early fruit drop occurs when the tree experiences sudden water stress after a dry spell, lacks potassium in the soil, or gets invaded by fruit flies laying eggs inside the fruit.
ga: Yibii ni fiteɔ mra lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Potassium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo aduawai amli ŋmeii ni woɔ wɔji yɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ tutuamɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and dry around the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings get scorched when exposed to too much direct sunlight. They need partial shade from nurse crops like plantain trees or shade trees to protect their tender leaves and retain moisture while their root systems establish.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ shãa kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo shɛ amɛnɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ amɛnɔ, tamɔ dumɔwui loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe ni akɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ maa lɛ.

english: What causes the flowers on my tomato plants to fall off before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii?

english: Tomato flowers often drop without fruiting when temperatures get too high or when there is sudden water stress. Extreme heat prevents proper pollination inside the flower, causing the plant to shed them to conserve its remaining energy and moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu he haomɔ ba trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ naa. Ha tsei lɛ ashwie shi koni akɛto hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why are small green worms eating holes inside the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that burrows into the growing center (whorl) of young maize plants. They feed on the tender emerging leaves, leaving ragged holes and dark waste behind, which severely weakens the plant if not managed early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni shwieɔ ŋmei tsei bibii ni daraa lɛ ateŋ (ring) lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni jeɔ kpo lɛ. Eshiɔ buji ni ekpɔtɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ yɛ esɛɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ waa kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra.

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have special nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When you plant maize afterward, it feeds on this naturally stored nitrogen to grow greener and stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ebaaye nitrogen ni ato yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni ehe wa.

english: Why do I need to push long wooden stakes into the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa tso kakadaŋŋ ko lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need to expose their leaves to sunlight to manufacture food for root development. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground—preventing fungal diseases—and helps the plant direct maximum energy into growing large underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ ni hulu la ashɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha shishifãi lɛ akwɛmɔ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ—ni ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa—ni ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ babaoo awo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔji wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if the soil has enough moisture to safely plant my maize seeds after the first rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui shweshweeshwe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Take a handful of soil from a depth of about 10 centimeters and squeeze it in your palm. If it forms a ball that holds together without dripping water or crumbling instantly, the soil has sufficient moisture for the seeds to germinate safely.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ aaafee sɛntimita 10 ni okɛmimɔ onine mli. Kɛji efee bɔɔlu ni kpɛtɛɔ he ni nu shwieee shi loo efooo amrɔ nɔŋŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during heavy rainstorms and strong winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have a deep taproot; instead, they rely on a shallow cluster of surface roots. When heavy rains soften the topsoil, the roots lose their grip, making top-heavy trees bearing heavy fruit bunches easily fall under strong winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ a hɛ kɛ fɔɔ shishifãhi nɛ a mi kuɔ we ɔ a nɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baafee mɛi ni nyɛŋ amɔmɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi jatsui ni tsii ni woɔ yibii yɛ kui amli lɛ gbeeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa shishi oya.

english: Why does rice grow well in flooded lowlands where my maize crop easily rots and dies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nu afua yɔɔ lɛ, he ni mi ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ oya ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air tubes inside their stems and roots that carry oxygen from the air down to roots submerged in water. Maize lacks these air passages, so its roots suffocate and rot when trapped in standing water for long periods.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa amɛshishifãi ni ebote nu mli lɛ amli. Abɛi bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, eshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo nu ni ekã shi mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and drop off during the dry harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ harmattan ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry spells as a natural survival trick to reduce water loss. By dropping foliage, the plant stops evaporating internal water and goes dormant until moisture returns with the next rainy season.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ ni akɛbaa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ shi. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ akafee nu ni yɔɔ emli lɛ ni ekɛ ehe awo mli kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ baaku esɛɛ aba yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Cassava maturity is shown when the lower leaves yellow and drop off naturally, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack open. You can also dig up a sample plant to inspect if the roots have expanded and developed a thick starch layer.
ga: Atsɔɔ akɛ cassava lɛ eda kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa Obaanyɛ okɛ tsei ni akɛfee nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ hu atsu nii ni okwɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ egbɛ eshwã ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why can't I just leave my farm land to rest for a few years like my father used to do?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mashi miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mayajie mihejɔɔmɔ afii fioo komɛi tamɔ bɔ ni mitsɛ feɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Leaving land fallow lets soil naturally rebuild nutrients and smothers weeds under thick bush. Today, because farmland is scarce, farmers must plant on the same plot every year, which means taking over nature's job by manually feeding the soil and clearing weeds.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ashiɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ eyiɔ ehe ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ejieɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ shishi lɛ. Amrɔ nɛɛ, yɛ okwaayeli shikpɔŋ ni faaa hewɔ lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ Okwaafoi lɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ akwɛ adebɔɔ nɔ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛ niji haa niyenii kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow so well during the very first year after I clear an old bushy field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi ni mijie jwɛi momoi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Land that has rested as a fallow accumulates years of rotting leaves and organic matter. When you clear it, all those stored soil nutrients are available at once, giving your first batch of crops a rich, natural boost.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni egbee shi lɛ buaa baai kɛ nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli. Kɛji ojie lɛ Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ato lɛ fɛɛ baa amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ha oklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee babaoo kɛ adebɔɔ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds come back so fast on my plot every single year after I clear them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ? Afii komɛi asɛɛ beni mijie lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit dormant in the soil for a long time. Clearing the bush opens the field to full sunlight and rain, which signals those hidden seeds to sprout immediately every season.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔji lɛ aná hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ feɔ okadi akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ daa be mli.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if I don't clear them from my farm early?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui? Kɛ mijieee jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mra lɛ,.

english: Weeds are stronger than crop plants and will steal the water, sunshine, and soil food meant for your crops. If you don't clear them early, your crop plants will stay stunted and yield very little.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ he wa fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebaaju nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli. Kɛji okɛ nibii tsuuu nii mra. Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ebaawo yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why does farming the same piece of land every year require more work from me than opening new bush land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ okwaayeli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ biɔ nitsumɔ babaoo kɛjɛɔ midɛŋ fe ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ hee ni agbeleɔ lɛ?

english: Without fallow periods to naturally choke out weeds and restore topsoil, you must manually clear stubborn weeds and maintain soil fertility yourself every year before and during crop growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ fallow be ko bɛ ni akɛbaajie jwɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni akɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ Esa akɛ okɛ onine ajie jwɛi ni wa lɛ ni okɛ onine akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ daa afi dani tsei lɛ adara kɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Is it better to burn the weeds after clearing my plot or leave them on the soil?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaashã jwɛi beni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ loo abaashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Burning clears the field fast, but leaving cut weeds to rot naturally creates a cover that cools the soil, holds moisture, and turns into natural food for your growing crops.
ga: Shãa lɛ jieɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ oya. Shi kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi ni afo lɛ fite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli, ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii haa oŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I keep planting on the exact same plot every year without a break?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli?

english: Crops pull specific nutrients out of the ground every season. If you plant continuously without giving the land a break or adding food back into it, the soil gets tired, and your crop yields will drop each year.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Kɛji odu nii be fɛɛ be ni ojaraaa he lɛ mli loo okɛ niyenii fataaa he ekoŋŋ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni onibii ni obaaná lɛ baa shi afi fɛɛ afi.

english: How can I keep my farm soil rich if I don't have spare land to leave fallow?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee fɛo? Ni kɛji akɛ mibɛ shikpɔŋ ko ni mikɛbaatsu nii hu?

english: You can keep the soil rich by adding animal manure or compost, rotating crops like groundnuts or beans with your main crops, and avoiding burning the organic clearings on your land.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha oshikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ hei ni agbele ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɔɔ mli lɛ ashãa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he.

english: What is the proper way to clear a new plot so my young crops don't struggle?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ saatso hee koni mi tsei bibii lɛ akabɔi ŋmɔlɔ?

english: You should clear the surface weeds and dig out deep roots of aggressive plants so your young crop roots can spread easily without underground competition for space and nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni otsa tsei ni feɔ basabasa lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ bɔni afee ni otso bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo ni okɛ shikpɔŋ shishi he ko kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ akaŋ.

english: Why do my crops look weaker in the second and third year on the same cleared land compared to the first year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ kɛ etɛ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ akɛto klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ he lɛ?

english: The natural fertility boost from clearing the original fallow land gets used up by the first crop. By the second and third years, the soil food is depleted, requiring you to manually nourish the land.
ga: Abaakɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii babaoo ni baa kɛtsɔ tsutsu shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe banee lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsu nii kɛha klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii. Yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ kɛ etɛ lɛ mli lɛ Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaho aya. Ehaa esa akɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because their leaves dry out quickly under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain next to young cocoa creates natural shade and keeps the air cool and humid around the young trees.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei ahe lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo baa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa tsei bibii lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tightly into small rolls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe bibii bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the plant's sap and spreading plant viruses. Clearing weeds around the farm and using safe insecticidal soaps can protect the remaining healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ajiemɔ Okwaayeli kɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ abu baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with small brown dirt inside the central shoot?
