ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni etse kɛ muji bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ? Eyɛ teŋgbɛ tso lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing tip of the maize plant to feed. Checking your field early in the morning and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem oil directly into the central shoot can stop them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi koni amɛye nii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ hei ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ leebi ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ wo tsei lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa amɛ.

english: This yellowing is a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize plants need to build healthy green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer around the plant base will help restore green leaf growth.
ga: Nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii afata he kɛbɔle Shishitoo lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my farm make my soil richer for the next crop?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts have tiny bumps on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When these plants finish growing, the extra nitrogen stays behind in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Beni tsei nɛɛ daraa lɛ Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni odu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or dry soil. Watering your tomato plants consistently early in the morning keeps the soil cool and helps the flowers stay on to turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛhaaa daa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ daa leebi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi kɛyashi amɛbaawo yibii.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves high into the sunlight to make energy for the underground tubers to expand. Staking also lifts the leaves off the wet ground, preventing damp soil diseases from damaging the crop.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ amli koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ akafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots get watery and spoil quickly if I harvest them right after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ akpa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli nu ni amɛgboi oya kɛji akɛ akpa amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains cause cassava plants to absorb lots of water and use their stored root energy to grow new leaves, making the roots watery. Waiting a few sunny days after heavy rain allows the starch levels inside the roots to stabilize again.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmeii tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo. ni ekɛ shishifãi ahewalɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai heei Haa shishifãi lɛ náa nu Gbii fioo komɛi ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ amli starch lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the suckers around my main plantain stool grow at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ? Fees titrii lɛ feɔ ekome kɛdaraa.

english: When too many plantain suckers grow together, they steal water, soil food, and sunlight from each other, resulting in smaller bunches. Keeping only one main fruiting tree, one medium shoot, and one small shoot ensures larger, healthier fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ plantain tsei babaoo ni miidara yɛ he kome lɛ Amɛjuɔ nu, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ elɛɛmɔ baa shi Kɛ́ ohiɛ aduawai tso titri kome, teŋgbɛ tso kome, kɛ tso bibioo kome pɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha aduawai akuu ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Covering soil with dry grass (mulching) blocks direct sunlight so water doesn't evaporate quickly, keeping the soil moist longer. It also prevents weeds from growing and breaks down over time to enrich your soil.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Bɔni afee ni nu akatsɔ oya Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Etsiɔ jwɛi hu naa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkafite yɛ be ni sa mli koni amɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Why do I need to dry my harvested maize before putting it in storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni magbi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ dani mikɛwo kotokui ni akɛtoɔ nii amli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Harvested crops carry a lot of natural water inside them. If you do not dry them to remove this water, molds, fungus, and insects will grow quickly inside the bag and spoil your entire harvest.
ga: Tsei ni akpaa lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli nu babaoo yɛ amɛmli. Kɛ́ ogbiɛɛ lɛ koni nu ajie kɛjɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii, ŋmeii, kɛ kooloi bibii baakwɛ̃ oya yɛ kotoku lɛ mli. ni efite onitsumɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa beans or grains are dry enough to sell to buyers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cocoa ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmaa lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ maha mɛi ni heɔ lɛ?

english: When crops reach the right dryness level (around 11 to 12 percent water content), the grains feel very hard, make a sharp cracking sound when you bite or break them, and rustle like small stones when you shake them in your hand.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ shɛ he ni sa ni egbi lɛ (Nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ aaafee oha mlijaa 11 kɛyashi 12.) Dumɔwui lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe wa waa. Ehaa gbee ni naa wa ni tswaa kɛji okã loo ogbala mli ni efee gbee ni tswaa tamɔ tɛi bibii. Beni okɛ onine shwieɔ nɔ lɛ

english: Why do extension officers tell me to keep turning my crops over while drying them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ kɛba ni mikɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Turning your crops regularly ensures that heat reaches all sides evenly. If you leave them untouched, the dampness gets trapped on the bottom layer, causing that part to rot or grow mold.
ga: Kɛ́ otsake onibii lɛ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni la ni tsoɔ lɛ shɛɔ he fɛɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛji oshi lɛ ni okɛ ohe wooo mli lɛ, Moisture baatsi shishigbɛ fã lɛ nɔ. Ha nakai fã lɛ agbo loo ená ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What happens to the quality of my grain if the water level inside it remains too high?
ga: Mɛni baa midumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛji nu ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ tee nɔ ehi shi tsɔ?

english: High moisture inside grain makes it generate heat in storage. This heat spoils the color, reduces the germination rate of seed maize, and makes buyers offer you a much lower price.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ haa dɔlɛ baa kɛha nitoo. Nɛkɛ dɔlɛ nɛɛ baaha kɔla lɛ afite. Tsɔɔmɔ bɔ ni ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ amɛhaa lɛ shi. ni ehaa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ jara ni baa shi kwraa haa.

english: Why do my dried grains sometimes draw moisture back in and become damp again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ mi-ŋmaa ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛyaa sɛɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Dried crops behave like sponges. If you store them in a humid room, leave bags directly on a cold floor, or open them during rainy weather, they will absorb water from the air and start to spoil.
ga: Nibii ni egbi lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ sponji. Kɛji akɛ okɛto tsu ko ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ Shi kotoku lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Aloo gbelemɔ kotoku lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Baagi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ebɔi fitemɔ.

english: Does lowering the water content in my crops help them stay fresh longer without using chemicals?
ga: Ani nu ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ni mikɛbaa shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni mikɛ tsofai tsuuu nii?

english: Yes, reducing the internal moisture to a very low level puts the crop into a stable sleeping state where insects and bacteria cannot easily feed or multiply, allowing it to store safely for months.
ga: Hɛɛ, mligbɛ fɛ̃i ni aba shi kɛyashɛ he ko ni baa shi waa lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni bɛ shiŋŋ mli. Kplukai kɛ helatsɛmɛi nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii loo amɛfɔ bii mlɛo. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akɛtoɔ he ko shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why does rain touching my crops during the drying process cause them to ruin so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Rainwater rehydrates the outer skin of the crop while the inside is still warm, creating an ideal damp environment for decay bacteria to grow rapidly within a day or two.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ haa tso lɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ mli nu lɛ feɔ nu ekoŋŋ, yɛ be mli ni ehaa emli lɛ mli dɔɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha helai ni fiteɔ lɛ koni amɛdara oya yɛ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ mli.

english: How does using a crop processing machine help me better than drying manually on the floor?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa mifeɔ mɔ ni hi fe nibii ni akɛ niji shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Drying machines can bring down crop moisture to precise target levels quickly regardless of bad weather, while also protecting your yield from dirt, animals, and uneven drying.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛgbiɔ nii lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baa shi oya kɛyashɛɔ he ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ, bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ehiii ha. yɛ be mli ni obuɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ muji, kooloi, kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ he.

english: Why do commercial buyers test the exact water percentage of my crops before paying me?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ kaa nu pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ amɛkwɛɔ dani amɛwoɔ mi nyɔmɔ lɛ?

english: Buyers test moisture levels because crops with water content above 12 percent will spoil during long transport trips in trucks or ships before reaching factories or international markets.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kaa bɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ amɛkwɛɔ ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nu yɔɔ mli fe oha mlijaa 12 lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ mli kɛtsɔ lɔle loo lɛlɛ nɔ dani eshɛɔ nitsumɔhei loo maŋsɛɛ jarayeli hei.

english: Why do living crops on my farm hold so much water before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo dani akpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: While growing in the field, plants constantly pump water to carry plant food into developing seeds. Once you cut the crop, it no longer needs that water, so it must be removed to preserve the food inside.
ga: Beni amɛdaraa yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu be fɛɛ be koni amɛkɛ tsei niyenii aba koni dumɔwui lɛ aya hiɛ. Beni ofoɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ Nu he ehiaaa lɛ dɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ajie koni niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akafite.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks essential plant food like nitrogen, or when excessive rain drowns the roots. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves recover their dark green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall and bushy but producing very small roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni efeɔ ŋmɔji shi eshishifãi lɛ daraaa bibii waa lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together or given too much nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on growing tall leaves to reach light instead of storing food in their underground roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo akɛ nitrogen babaoo wo mli. Ebaakɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ama baai kakadaji ni miida lɛ anɔ koni enyɛ ená la. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ

english: Why are crops on one side of my land growing much faster than crops on the other side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã kome lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ fã kroko lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil quality varies across a farm field. One part of your land may have deeper topsoil, better water drainage, or richer organic matter, while the other side might be stony or lacking nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su lɛ srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli he ni eyɔɔ lɛ naa. Ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fã ko yɛ ŋwɛi sũ ni mli kwɔ fe tsutsu lɛ. Nu ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ jɛmɛ. aloo eyɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo yɛ be mli ni ekolɛ fã kroko lɛ yɛ tɛi loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli.

english: Why does my farm yield less maize every season when I plant it on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi beni miduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests that feed on that crop to build up, leading to poorer harvests over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to hot direct sunlight and harsh winds. Plantain trees or shade trees act as natural umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool and protecting the soil from drying out while the trees are young.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he waa. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop and curl up during the hot afternoon even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni amɛshwieee lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull water from the ground. Curling leaves is the plant's natural way to protect itself from sun damage, and they usually recover when temperatures cool in the evening.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai ni akpɛɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso ko tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: What is causing small round holes to appear all over the leaves of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni haa buji lɛ feɔ bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo? Ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Small holes in leaves are typically caused by leaf-chewing insects like beetles or caterpillars. Checking the undersides of the leaves early in the morning helps you find and manage these pests before they destroy the whole plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni otsa amɛ dani amɛfite tso muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when daytime temperatures are extremely high, when the soil experiences sudden severe dry spells, or when there are no beneficial insects around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli wa waa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi waa trukaa loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ he ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when weeds are left around their bases?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ be mli ni jwɛi eshwɛ yɛ eshishitoo lɛ he lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. When weeds are left around the crops, they steal essential food away from the main plant, causing stunted growth.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ, amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ

english: Why do experienced farmers trim off some side branches from tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛ tomato tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ afã lɛ?

english: Removing extra side shoots allows the plant to send more energy and nutrients directly to the main stem and developing fruits, resulting in larger and healthier tomatoes.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ tsɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ nɔ ni ewoɔ aduawai. Enɛ haa tomatoi lɛ daraa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big trees off my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani midu lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight because intense heat burns their leaves and dries out their roots. Leaving some larger trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides shade and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ, ejaakɛ la ni naa wa lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ gĩɔ. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Is it helpful to plant cowpeas or beans in the same farm alongside my maize crop?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ makwɛ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ masɛi?

english: Yes, cowpeas and beans add extra nutrients like nitrogen directly into the soil. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to grow, so planting them together helps feed the maize naturally and reduces the amount of chemical fertilizer you need to buy.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kɛ niyenii krokomɛi, tamɔ nitrogen fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo ekomefeemɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ aye kooloi lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaha tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli ni esa akɛ ohe lɛ aba shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together so I can get more plants on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures every single plant gets enough food and sunlight to grow strong and yield larger fruits or tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii loo bulbs wuji.

english: Why do I see small holes in my maize leaves and tiny caterpillars hiding deep inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni Akɛtee yɛ tso lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ anɔ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest, which burrows into the leaf whorl to feed on young tissue. Checking fields early and applying recommended treatments directly into the center of the plants before the caterpillars multiply will protect your harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm, ni shwieɔ baai amli koni eye fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Omɔ ŋmɔji amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu nii yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ afɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck the plant's sap and spread viruses. Controlling these small insects early prevents the virus from spreading across the rest of your field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. small insect control Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã hei krokomɛi lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How do I select cassava stems that will produce a healthy crop for next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tso ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Always take stem cuttings from healthy mature plants that show no signs of leaf spots or yellowish curling. Using stems from diseased plants passes the disease straight into the new soil and leads to weak plants with tiny tubers.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, ŋmɔmɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni eda ni bɛ baai lɛ ahe ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ akɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ashishifãi tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ hee nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ bulb bibii

english: Does letting tall weeds grow near my crops cause plant diseases, or do weeds just take up space?
ga: Jwɛi kakadaji ni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ kɛ tsei ahelai baa. Aloo jwɛi lɛ miiye he ko kɛkɛ?

english: Weeds do more than steal nutrients; they act as hiding spots and breeding grounds for insects and plant diseases. Keeping your farm free of weeds prevents pests from jumping onto your main crops and causing secondary infections.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ babaoo fe niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛjuɔ. Amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ he ni kooloi bibii kɛ tsei ahe helai fɔɔ amɛhe yɛ kɛ he ni amɛfɔɔ yɛ. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkaho kɛya oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ anɔ ni amɛkɛ helai krokomɛi aba.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves are a sign that your soil is low on nitrogen, which is the main element crops need to stay green and build foliage. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves turn green again.
ga: Kɛ́ baai lɛ ashishi tsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛya nɔ amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛwo baai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce a lot of flowers, but the flowers fall off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi ko gbeeɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plant experiences irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and watering regularly helps the flowers stay on the plant and develop into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fũu pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves toward the sun, which lets the plant make food to grow large tubers underground. If vines stay on the ground, leaves get shaded and diseased, resulting in much smaller yams.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ niyenii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji wain tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, baai lɛ baatsɔ shade ni hela baamɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii kwraa.

english: Why are my maize stalks staying short and turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing and stunted growth usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which acts as food for the plant to build green leaves and grow tall. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore its strength and dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛha tso lɛ koni ewo baai eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hewalɛ kɛ su ni mli kwɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I get fewer groundnuts when I plant the seeds very close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ ŋmeii fioo nɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmeii akuu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for limited soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, which prevents the plants from expanding and forming many pods underground.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni efee ŋmeii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees grow much better when I leave plantains or forest trees growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ mishɛrɛ plantains loo koo mli tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ ashwie lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn in direct, harsh sunlight. Larger shade plants act like umbrellas, shielding young cocoa from heat and keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry up and fold during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ egbi ni ebɔle ehe yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind sucks moisture out of leaves faster than roots can drink from the dry soil. The plant naturally lets older leaves droop and dry up to reduce water loss and save energy until rains return.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Tsei haa baai momoi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni nu ni laajeɔ lɛ aba shi ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when it rains continuously for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be otsii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the field without draining away, it drowns the roots and allows soil fungi and bacteria to multiply and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu ŋmɛ ŋmɔ mli ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli lɛ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. ni eha ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why does leaving weeds near my yam mounds cause my yams to produce small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ masɛi lɛ haa mi-sweet potatoes lɛ shwereɔ bulbs bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops. Without enough food and light, the yam plant cannot make enough energy to expand its root tuber.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Kɛji niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Sweet potato tso lɛ nyɛŋ ajie hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha eshishifãi lɛ adara.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up into small cups and stopping new fruit from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛfee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ? ni ekpaa aduawai heei ni baa lɛ anaa.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that pass viruses into the plant, or by water stress. Controlling insects early keeps the plant healthy enough to produce fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, ni kɛ helai baa tsei lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ nu mli haomɔ mli Mra Be mli Kooloi Akwɛmɔ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel extreme heat stress or sudden lack of water. The plant drops flowers to protect itself and conserve moisture when conditions are too severe.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛ́ shihilɛi lɛ mli wa tsɔ.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for one high-yield harvest. The seeds saved from that crop lose their special strength in the second generation, resulting in mixed growth and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ kome ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ krɛdɛɛ lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni futuɔ kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why does my stored dry maize turn to powder with small holes after a few months in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ tsɔɔ powda ni eyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Tiny insects called grain weevils chew inside stored maize kernels to feed and lay eggs. Storing grain in airtight bags or treating it with safe grain protectants keeps the insects from destroying it.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ seed moths lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa ni ato kɛha niyenii ni amɛwoɔ wɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to vacuum kotokui amli loo akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi akafite dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves often mean your young cocoa trees are getting too much direct sunlight without enough shade, or the soil lacks nutrients like nitrogen and needs proper fertilizer or compost.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-cocoa tso bibioo lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa awo mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants lose their flowers before any peppers actually grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ miifite dani pepper lɛ miida diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience extreme heat stress, don't get enough water during hot days, or when tiny insect pests attack the blossom stems.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni anáaa yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tutuaa fɔfɔii ahe tsei.

english: Why do extension officers advise us not to burn the bush before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akashã jwɛi dani adu lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the rich organic matter and beneficial organisms in the topsoil that feed your crops, leaving the ground dry, hard, and poor over time.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi, ewa, ni efite yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around the base of my crops regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi daa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, nutrients, and sunlight from your crops, and they also provide hiding spots for insect pests that bring diseases to your farm.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Amɛji he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ ekɛ helai aba oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hu teeɔ amɛhe.

english: Wait until after the first two or three heavy rains that thoroughly soak the deep soil, rather than planting immediately after the very first light shower which can dry up quickly.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa 2-3 lɛ sɛɛ koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Mohu ɔ, o duɔ amlɔ nɔuu ngɛ kekleekle nugbɔ nɛ ɔ nɛ ma nyɛ maa gbi oya ɔ se.

english: Why should I plant my cassava cuttings at a slanting angle instead of standing straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi yucca tsei lɛ aniji lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni madamɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at an angle (around 45 degrees) helps the roots grow deep enough to find underground water while allowing multiple strong shoots to push up easily.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ koŋ nɔ (aafee digrii 45) lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni anyɛɔ anaa shikpɔŋ shishi nu. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo ni mli wa. Shoots tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi mlɛo.

english: How can I tell if Fall Armyworm has attacked my maize farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ Fall Armyworm miitutua mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Look for small ragged holes in the central young leaves of the maize plant and dark, sawdust-like droppings inside the funnel where the new leaves grow.
ga: Taomɔ buji bibii ni etse amɛhe yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋ ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni baa heei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: Why are my sweet potato roots full of tiny holes and smelling bad when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato shishifãi lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔ kɛji mikpa nii?

english: Tiny holes inside sweet potatoes are caused by sweet potato weevils, which dig into the tubers when dry weather causes soil to crack and expose the roots.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ sweet potato lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baa, ni amɛfoɔ amɛboteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ gbá shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛjie shishifãi lɛ akpo.

english: Is it good to plant cowpeas or groundnuts between my rows of maize?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, planting leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts with maize helps fix nitrogen into the soil naturally, which acts as a free fertilizer for your maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa o-corn lɛ.

english: How do I prevent my cocoa beans from developing mold while drying them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni migbiɔ lɛ?

english: Spread your fermented cocoa beans thinly on raised wooden or bamboo drying mats in direct sunlight, and turn them frequently so air flows through them completely.
ga: Okɛ kookoo ŋmeii komɛi ni edɔ awo nɔ. Yɛ tso loo ŋmei ni awo nɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. ni otsake dumɔwui lɛ shii abɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ atsɔ mli

english: How can I tell if a disease is starting on my cocoa trees before the pods actually rot?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ yɛ hela dani ŋmeii lɛ agboi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Early signs of disease like Black Pod include small dark spots on young pods, unusual yellowing, or sudden wilting of shoots. Catching these signs early helps you treat the tree before the whole pod spoils.
ga: Hela he okadii ni jeɔ shishi mra tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ ekomɛi ji ŋmeii diji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ejaaa lɛ anɔ. loo ŋmɔlɔ ni baa trukaa Okadii nɛɛ ni ooomɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha ohere tso lɛ yiwala dani ŋmeii lɛ agbo kwraa.

english: If I notice a diseased branch on my crop, should I cut it off or leave it alone?
ga: Kɛji mina tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ Ani esa akɛ mafo mli loo mashi amɛ?

english: You should cut off infected branches right away and carry them far off the farm to burn or bury them. Leaving diseased parts on the plant allows the sickness to spread to healthy branches and neighboring crops.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni okɛ amɛ aya he ko ni kɛ ŋmɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ koni oyashã loo ofu amɛ. Kɛ́ oshi hei ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã tsei niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why does a plant disease keep coming back on my farm even after I cut down the sick trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai yaa nɔ amɛbaa miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ beni mifo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Diseases can survive in the soil, on farm tools, or in nearby weeds. If you do not clean your cutlass and treat the soil, the sickness will easily attack your new plants.
ga: Hela lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. okwaayeli nibii loo jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli Kɛji otsuuu o-knibii lɛ ahe ni okwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Helai baatutua otso hee lɛ oya.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves usually mean your cassava has Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by whiteflies. Planting stems from healthy, disease-free plants helps prevent it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-yucca lɛ yɛ yucca mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni helai bɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ baaye abua ni atsĩ amɛnaa.

english: Why are my maize plants growing tall and thin without giving me big ears of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛhaaa mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Maize grows tall and weak when planted too close together or when the soil lacks nitrogen. The plants end up fighting for sunlight instead of putting energy into making big cobs.
ga: Abɛi daa ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ loo kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ awuu koni amɛná hulu la moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off the plant without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil needed to support fruit development.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa ni baa shwane mli lɛ mli. Nu ni ashwieɔ shi daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai adalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop in the middle of the day even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than the roots can pull it up. They droop to protect themselves from drying out and usually recover by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie. Amɛgbeeɔ shi koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ he, ni bei pii lɛ, amɛhe jɔɔ amɛ kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: How do I know if my farm soil has become weak and needs a rest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni mafo mihe?

english: If your crops grow slowly, look pale green instead of dark green, and produce smaller harvests than previous years despite good rains, your soil is low on nutrients and needs fertilizer or fallow time.
ga: Kɛji onibii lɛ dara blɛoo Etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. ni ewo yibii fioo fe nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo moŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo be ni ekɛbaatsu nii.

english: Why is it necessary to clear weeds from around the roots of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops. They also attract crop pests and act as hiding places for plant diseases.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai hu kɛbaa, ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ he ni tsei ahelai kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli.

english: Should I save seeds from my current maize harvest to plant next season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpaa amrɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: It is better to buy fresh certified seeds each season. Saved seeds from hybrid harvests often produce weaker crops and much lower yields than original certified seeds.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo fe shishijee dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ.

english: What basic instructions should I follow to properly plant maize at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋaawoi titrii esa akɛ mafee koni manyɛ madu ŋmãa jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Clear your field and plant seeds about 2 to 3 centimeters deep right after the first good rain. Space the plants about two hand-spans apart in rows so each plant gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and water to grow strong.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni okɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashɛ sɛntimita 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Okɛ tsei lɛ ato amɛhe aaafee nine enyɔ bɔni afee ni tso fɛɛ tso aná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha shweremɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sun and need shade to survive. Plantains grow very fast with broad leaves that act like living umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool and maintaining moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi, ni ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi. Plantains daa oya waa kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi.

english: How can I feed my farm soil to make my crops grow strong without buying expensive chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahã shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ niyenii koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: You can nourish soil naturally by spreading well-rotted animal manure, leaving cleared weeds on the ground as mulch, or planting beans and cowpeas, which pull good nutrients into the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ kooloi aŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni oookɛshwie nɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi jwɛi ni ajie lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Aloo dumɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii koni ekɛgbala niyenii kpakpai awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, the main food plant leaves need to stay green and make energy. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer gives the crop back its green strength.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Esa akɛ niyenii titri tsei lɛ baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛjie hewalɛ kpo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie hidden in the soil for years and wake up instantly when rain and sunlight hit the ground. Clearing weeds early in the first month keeps them from stealing food and water from your young crop.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe teeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afii babaoo. ni eteɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ shishijee nyɔji lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without growing into fruits during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil cause tomato plants to drop their flowers to save water. Mulching around the stem with dry grass and watering at the roots keeps the soil cool so fruits can form.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ, ni okɛ nu wo shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ajɔɔ koni ewo yibii.

english: Why are caterpillars eating holes in my cabbage leaves, and where do they come from?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii miiye bu yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ amli lɛ? Ni nɛgbɛ amɛjɛɔ?

english: Small moths lay invisible eggs under the leaves, which hatch into greedy caterpillars. Checking under leaves weekly and spraying water mixed with ground neem seeds will repel them safely.
ga: Kplukai bibii fɔɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa amɛ yɛ baai lɛ ashishi. ni fɔ̃ɔ kɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ Otsi fɛɛ otsi ni akwɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni akɛ nu ni akɛ neem dumɔwui ni atswa lɛ efutu mli lɛ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ baashwie amɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Is it good to plant cassava and maize together on the same farm, or will they fight each other?
ga: Ni aaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ, ani ehi loo nɔmɔ baaba?

english: They work well together because maize grows quickly and is harvested in 3 to 4 months, while cassava grows slowly. Once you harvest the maize, the cassava takes over the field without fighting for space.
ga: Amɛfeɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa daaɔ blɛoo. Kɛji okpa ŋmãa lɛ, Cassava baaye jɛmɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ohe awo mli.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cassava so the tubers don't spoil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Bɔni afee ni akafite yitso lɛ

english: Cassava is ready 9 to 12 months after planting when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off. Digging them up at this stage gives firm tubers that stay fresh longer for market.
ga: Cassava efee klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ehee yɛ jara nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How should I dry and store my harvested corn so that insects do not destroy it in the barn?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ magbi mi-ŋma ni mikpa lɛ ni mikɛto? Enɛ ji koni kooloi akafite ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Dry your corn cobs in the sun until the grains are hard when bitten, then shell and store them in clean, airtight bags to block moisture and keep weevils from eating your harvest.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ fɔ̃ɔ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ mli wa kɛji akɛ amɔ lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, shwiemɔ ni okɛto vacuum bag ni mli tse mli koni ebu he kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ he ni eha ŋmeii akaye onibii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when there are no bigger shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that dry out easily under direct sun. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist until the cocoa roots grow deep enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, dark environments. When heavy rains come, water splashes fungal spores onto the pods, especially if air cannot flow freely through the farm.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ Nu lɛ baashwie fungal spores lɛ nɔ yɛ pods lɛ anɔ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya.

english: Why do I need to prune some of the healthy branches off my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tso niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Pruning removes excess foliage so sunlight and fresh air can reach the inner trunk. This prevents humidity buildup that breeds disease and encourages the tree to channel its energy into growing flowers and pods.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa anyɛ ashɛ tso lɛ mligbɛ. Enɛ haaa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ helai baa lɛ abua naa, ni ewoɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛtsu hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually signal that the plant lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient found in healthy soil. Adding organic compost or appropriate nitrogen fertilizer restores the green color and helps the crop grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my crop roots with dried grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground, also called mulching, traps moisture in the soil, keeps the roots cool during hot days, suppresses weed growth, and gradually breaks down into natural plant food.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ tsei adebɔɔ mli niyenii.

english: Why shouldn't I place fertilizer right against the stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ he ni bɛŋkɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ?

english: Placing chemical fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the outer bark and root tissues. Spreading it a short distance away lets the feeder roots absorb the nutrients safely through the moist soil.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ kponɔgbɛ fãji kɛ shishifãi lɛ ashã. Egbɛɔ eshwaa he ko kuku Enɛ haa niyenii halɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ nɔ amɛjieɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: What is making small, ragged holes in the funnel leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni ekpɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: These holes are typical damage from the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides deep inside the leaf funnel to feed. Early detection allows you to spray approved botanical or chemical controls before the central growing point is destroyed.
ga: Nɛkɛ bu nɛɛ ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye nii lɛ fɔɔ fitemɔ. mra mli ni anaa Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ tsofa ni akɛkwɛɔ tsei anɔ loo tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii dani afiteɔ he ni tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to yield smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds act as silent thieves on your farm, aggressively stealing water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients from the soil that your main crops need to produce large fruits or grains.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi ni efee dioo. yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni ojuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ koni amɛwo aduawai loo ŋmaa wuji lɛ kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell that my cassava crop is fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready around 9 to 12 months after planting, marked by the lower leaves turning yellow and falling off, alongside visible cracks forming in the soil around the main stem base.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, ni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Enɛ fata ŋmeii ni anaa ni eba yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ he.

english: Why should I wait for the main rainy season to settle before sowing my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ dani madu ŋmãa?

english: Planting in consistently moist soil ensures that all seeds germinate at the same time. If you plant too early during erratic rains, a short dry spell can scorch the young sprouts before their roots take hold.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ nɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ mli lɛ, be kuku ni akɛgbiɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii dani shishifãi lɛ aje shishi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient they need to grow green and strong, or the soil is waterlogged, which stops the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa. loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites, or a plant virus, which disrupts normal leaf development and stresses the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ, tamɔ aphids loo mites, loo tso mli helai, ni gbalaa baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa ni ehaa tso lɛ haoɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my cabbage leaves droop during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ miiho yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ miwooo lɛ moŋ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: On very hot days, cabbage leaves lose water into the hot air faster than the roots can draw it up from the soil, so the leaves temporarily wilt to protect the plant from drying out.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, Kaabaji baai lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, baai lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni tso lɛ akagbi.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off instead of turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, when the soil dries out completely during flowering, or if there is too much nitrogen fertilizer causing the plant to grow leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Aloo kɛji nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo lɛ ha tso lɛ kwɛ̃ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do my watermelons split open in the field just when they are almost ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ miitswa yɛ ŋmɔ mli beni kpamɔ be lɛ ebɛŋkɛ lɛ?

english: Watermelons crack open when they absorb a sudden, large amount of water after a dry period, causing the sugary inside to expand faster than the outer skin can stretch.
ga: Watermelon lɛ tswaa kɛji trukaa lɛ, eŋɔ nu babaoo yɛ be ko sɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fã ni sugar yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni epidermis lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that cannot tolerate direct sunlight; they require temporary shade from food crops like plantain to reduce heat stress until their roots go deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ŋmɛɛɛ amɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ niyenii tsei, tamɔ plantains, adɛŋ koni ekɛba dɔlɛ he haomɔ shi kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ mli baawo wu.

english: Why do my yam vines produce bigger tubers when I train them up on tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ hiɛ bulbs wuji beni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ tsɔseɔ lɛ lɛ?

english: Staking gets yam leaves off the ground into full sunlight where they can manufacture more food for the plant, which is then stored underground to build larger tubers.
ga: Staking haa ajieɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulu la lɛ fɛɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ. Enɛ haa amɛwoɔ niyenii babaoo amɛhaa tsei. ni no sɛɛ lɛ akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni efee bulbs wuji.

english: Why shouldn't I leave all the small suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow forces them to compete with the main plantain tree for water and soil nutrients, resulting in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃ lɛ, enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ abɔi akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why does my cassava grow tall with plenty of leaves but produce very thin tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava puts its energy into growing top leaves instead of underground tubers when there is excessive nitrogen in the soil or when the plants are shaded by trees.
ga: Cassava kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ najiaŋ kɛ́ nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ tsei ebɔle tso lɛ he.

english: How do cowpea plants help make my soil better for the next crop I plant on the field?
ga: Te cowpea tsei baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni madu yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants work with beneficial soil microbes to pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil for future crops.
ga: Cowpea tsei kɛ sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔmɔ lɛ amɛwo shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I get higher yields from my crops if I do not have extra land to expand my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli? Ni kɛji akɛ mibɛ shikpɔŋ kroko ni mikɛbaagbala miŋmɔ lɛ mli hu?

english: You can harvest significantly more food from the same size field by using improved seed varieties, planting at recommended spacing, and applying organic manure or fertilizer. This maximizes land use without needing extra acreage.
ga: Obaanyɛ okpa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ he ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni oootsɔ nɔ okɛtsu nii lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ yɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ adu lɛ naa. ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii Gbɛ nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ he kroko afata he.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller and produce less food when I plant the same crop on the same field every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni niyenii ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ faaa kɛ́ midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the exact same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the earth. Alternating crops keeps the soil balanced and healthy.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ baajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ je lɛŋ. Tsei ni akɛtsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What steps should I take with my field right after harvesting so the soil stays fertile for the next season?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔji lɛ amli kɛji akpa ŋmaa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ? Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Instead of leaving the land empty, you should leave crop residues to decompose into the earth or plant cover crops like legumes. This returns vital nutrients back into the soil and protects it from drying out under the sun.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efee efolo Esa akɛ oshi ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo okɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii ahe. Enɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaaa egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Is burning crop stalks after harvest harmful to my farm's soil?
ga: Ani tso shishifãi ni ashãa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ awui?

english: Yes, burning destroys the valuable organic matter and kills tiny, helpful soil organisms that create natural food for your crops. Leaving the stalks to rot or ploughing them under feeds the soil for the next planting season.
ga: Hɛɛ, la ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa lɛ, ni egbeɔ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha onibii lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ oshi tsei lɛ ashishi koni amɛgboi loo oootsu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow, and how can I fix it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer supplies the food your plants need to turn dark green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ kooloi aŋmei, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Which crops can I plant after harvesting maize to put natural food back into my tired soil?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ madu yɛ ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ koni mikɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii aku sɛɛ aba mishikpɔŋ ni etɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Legume crops such as cowpeas, groundnuts, or soybeans naturally trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. Planting them after maize naturally replenishes the soil's fertility.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas, peanuts loo soybeans lɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Abele ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same land without them competing for food?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mikɛ niyenii he akaŋ akaŋ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows fast and is harvested early, leaving plenty of space, light, and soil nutrients for the cassava to mature later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. Enɛ haa gbɛ, la, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my planted crops whenever the rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants adapted to steal water, sunlight, and nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early in the season gives your young crops a head start to grow without competition.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛju nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaha otsei bibii lɛ adara oya ni akaŋshii ko bɛ he.

english: Why do my young seedlings wilt and die in the hot sun even after I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli beni mikɛ nu ewo amɛnɔ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young seedling roots are too small to replace water as fast as the hot sun evaporates it from their leaves. Providing temporary shade or covering the surrounding soil with dry grass (mulching) keeps the roots cool and wet.
ga: Dumɔwu lɛ shishifãi lɛ daraaa tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye nu najiaŋ oya tamɔ nɛkɛ. kɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ebaajɛɔ baai lɛ amli hulutsoo be kukuoo mli hulutsoo loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How can I protect my harvested maize from insects while it is stored in my barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ahe be mli ni mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Insects thrive on moisture and dirt. Ensure your grain is completely dry and hard before storage, clean your barn thoroughly, and use airtight bags or safe storage dust to block pests.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ omanye yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ muji nɔ. Kwɛmɔ akɛ oŋmaa lɛ egbi kwraa ni ewa dani okɛto. Tsumɔ otsu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Ni okɛ vacuum loo sũ kotoku atsu nii ni okɛto he shweshweeshwe koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote mli.

english: Cassava roots do not have a thick protective skin once detached from the plant. When harvested, cuts on the root react with oxygen in the air, causing internal browning and decay within 48 to 72 hours.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewolo ni mli tse ni haa amɛhe kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ he pɛ. Be ni esa akɛ akpa tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ feɔ ekome. Enɛ haa mligbɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efiteɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 kɛyashi 72 mli.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes go soft and rot so quickly when they spend a long time in crates before reaching the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya nɛkɛ, yɛ be mli ni esa akɛ ehi adekai amli be kakadaŋŋ dani eshɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes have delicate outer skins and high water content. Continuous shaking and squeezing in overpacked crates cause internal cell walls to burst, releasing fluids that accelerate rot and attract fungal infections.
ga: Tomato yɛ kponɔgbɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni nu babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ́ oya nɔ akpokpo ni akpokpo yɛ adeka ni eyi obɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha wala yibii lɛ amli gbogboi lɛ agbá. Ejieɔ nu ni haa fitemɔ yaa oya ni egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why does my stored maize turn into powder and get full of tiny black insects after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikɛto lɛ miitsɔ powda ni ŋmeii bibii diji yɔɔ mli lɛ? Eyi obɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ

english: Maize weevils lay tiny eggs inside grain kernels while the crop is still in the field or during drying. If the maize is stored with too much moisture, these eggs hatch into beetles that eat the starch from inside out.
ga: Abɛi ŋmei fɔɔ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli be mli ni tsei lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo loo be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa to he ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Nɛkɛ ŋmãa nɛɛ fɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers start growing long green shoots while they are stored in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ bɔi ŋmeii kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shweremɔ beni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living plant stems that enter a natural dormant rest phase after harvest. Once humidity and warm air break this rest period, the tuber uses its stored energy and water to sprout new vines.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji tsei ni yɔɔ wala mli ni boteɔ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ fite nɛkɛ gbee nɛɛ Bulb lɛ kɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ wain tsei heei.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the main vein of older leaves is a sign of nitrogen deficiency. Maize needs nitrogen to make green leaf chlorophyll, and when soil lacks it, the plant pulls nutrients from old leaves to feed new growth.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli fãji titrii lɛ ahe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛfee klorofil ni baa eŋɔli lɛ. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli etse Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop most of their flowers before small pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo dani ŋmeii bibii feɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of blossoms, but drop them if stressed by prolonged dry weather, lack of nutrients, or poor pollination by tiny midges that require moist, shaded soil litter to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi amɛbaagbee shi kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo ŋmeii ni haaa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ha amɛhao. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ kɛ hulutsoo he miihia amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants shed all their leaves and flowers after heavy rain floods my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai kɛ fɔfɔi fɛɛ shwie shi beni nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper roots require air in the soil to breathe. When water covers the soil for extended periods, the roots drown and stop absorbing nutrients, causing the plant to drop leaves to conserve moisture.
ga: Pepper shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Shishifãi lɛ baafo nu mli ni amɛbaakpa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ koni ekɛto ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy leaves but yield very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ waa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi ewoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi bibii waa lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil encourages cassava to spend all its energy growing leafy stems above ground rather than storing starch underground. Cassava needs balanced soil potassium to produce large tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmei hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ etso ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ powda lɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, ehe miihia ni Cassava aná potassium ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be weakened underground by parasitic root nematodes or stem borers. When the fruit bunch grows heavy, the damaged root system can no longer anchor the tree against its own weight.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ, ni shishifãi ni ji nematodes loo stem borers lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ aduawai akuu lɛ bafee tsiimɔ Shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛŋ amɔ tso lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etsiimɔ he.

english: Why do my maize seeds rot in the soil instead of coming up when I plant them right after a light rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ beni midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need continuous soil moisture to germinate properly. A light rain gives just enough moisture to start the seed swelling, but if the soil dries out quickly afterward, the seed dies and rots from soil fungi before emerging.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ haa fɛ̃i ni fa bɔ ni sa ni haa dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ. Shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ oya yɛ no sɛɛ Dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, which is essential for leaf growth, or that heavy rainfall has waterlogged the roots and prevented them from feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ adara Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, ni haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaaa amɛye nii.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of lush green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When cowpeas have too much nitrogen in the soil, the plant focuses all its energy on growing leaves instead of flowering. Cowpeas naturally make their own nitrogen, so extra fertilizer often hinders pod growth.
ga: Beni cowpea lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni miida lɛ he nii moŋ fe ni eeewo fɔfɔi. Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ nitrogen yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ tsiɔ pod lɛ dalɛ naa.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants curl up into tight tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up when the heat becomes intense to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This is the plant's natural defense to conserve water and protect itself from heat stress during the hottest part of the day.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛji la lɛ mli wa waa koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli hebuu ni ekɛbuɔ nu he ni ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni edɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cowpea plants lose their flowers without forming any pods during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ fɔfɔi fiteɔ ni efeee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and water stress cause crop plants to go into survival mode, shedding flowers to conserve energy and moisture. Managing soil moisture and protecting plants from extreme heat helps them retain flowers and form pods.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu he haomɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shihilɛ mli. Amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛ tsei ahebuu kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔii amli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Covering bare soil with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the ground from direct, harsh sunlight. It regulates soil temperature, keeps root zones cool, and prevents soil moisture from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa nɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ

english: Why shouldn't I place dry fertilizer directly against the stem of my cassava plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated salts that can burn plant stems and roots if placed directly against them. Mixing it into the surrounding soil a short distance from the stem allows roots to safely absorb the nutrients without heat damage.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ashã tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi kɛji akɛ akɛma shi shiŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛfutu shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ fioo pɛ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe ni amɛkɛ dɔlɛ efiteee amɛ.

english: Why do I need to dig and mix the soil thoroughly before planting my vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ otsa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni okɛfutu mli jogbaŋŋ dani odu aduawai lɛ?

english: Turning and mixing the soil breaks up hard ground so roots can easily grow and reach moisture. It also mixes nutrients evenly throughout the root zone and helps bury weed seeds so they cannot easily sprout.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni atsakeɔ ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ gbálaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ oya. Ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ hu futuɔ shishifã lɛ mli fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni efuɔ jwɛi dumɔwui koni amɛkakwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow very tall and thin with few fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded together, they compete for sunlight and soil nutrients. They use all their energy stretching upward toward the sun instead of branching out to produce abundant flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ni amɛkpãa kɛyaa hulu lɛ he lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee niji ni amɛfee fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato plants develop yellow leaves and rotting roots when I water them too heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛmli fe nine lɛ?

english: Excessive water fills air pockets in the soil, preventing roots from breathing oxygen. Without oxygen, roots rot and fail to absorb nutrients, which turns the leaves yellow and weakens the entire plant.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni ebaaha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: How can I tell when my sweet potatoes are mature and ready to be dug out of the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Sweet potatoes are ready for harvest when the leaves begin to yellow and dry up naturally. You can confirm by digging up a test tuber; if you cut it open and the milky sap dries clear without turning dark, it is ready to harvest.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai lɛ je shishi amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Obaanyɛ oma enɛ nɔ mi kɛtsɔ kaa yitso ko ni oootsi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ afo mli lɛ, nu lɛ mli nu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni etsɔɔɔ duŋ. Efee klalo akɛ abaakpa.

english: Why do my cocoa beans become moldy while I am drying them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo yibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ amɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa beans mold if they are piled too thick or left unturned while drying. Stirring and turning them regularly spreads them out evenly, allowing warm air to dry out trapped moisture before fungi can grow.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji akɛ ato amɛhe tsɔ loo ashi amɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ daa ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa anáa mlijaa po. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli lɛ mli egbiɔ dani ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ adara.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout after I leave them to dry on black plastic sheets in the bright sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ beni miha amɛgbi yɛ plastic diŋ ko nɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Black plastic absorbs extreme heat under direct sunlight, which effectively cooks and kills the living embryo inside the seeds. Seeds should be dried in gentle sunlight or well-ventilated shade to preserve their viability.
ga: Plastic diŋ lɛ ŋmɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. ni baanyɛ ahoo ni egbe ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ agbi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa mli loo yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if a new yam seed variety from researchers will produce good yields on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji niiamlitaolɔi lɛ a-sweet potato dumɔwui heei lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Improved yam varieties developed by researchers are specifically bred to resist local pests and diseases, adapt to Ghana's soil, and produce larger, healthier tubers compared to traditional unselected seeds.
ga: Akwɛ sweet potato henɔ ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni niiamlitaolɔi lɛ fee lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni ekɛte shi ewo tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Ekɛ ehe woɔ Ghana shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ waa kɛ akɛto blema dumɔwui ni ahalaaa lɛ ahe.

english: What makes modern improved crop seeds better than the seeds I harvest and save from my own farm every year?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ hi fe dumɔwui ni mikpaa ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Farm-saved seeds can accumulate diseases over multiple seasons and lose their vigor, while improved seeds from agricultural experts are clean, disease-free, and genetically selected for strong growth and uniform yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ abua helai anaa yɛ bei babaoo mli ni amɛhewalɛ aba shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni okwaayeli he nilelɔi fee lɛ he tse, hela bɛ mli, ni ahala amɛ yɛ fɔmɔ su mli koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo yibii daa.

english: What is the difference between planting yam using traditional seed tubers and using modern propagation methods like minisetts?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ sweet potatoes ni akɛ blema dumɔwui ayitsei tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbɛɔ ashwãa tamɔ minnows lɛ teŋ?
