english: Traditional planting uses large pieces of edible yam tuber, which wastes food. Modern minisett techniques cut healthy yams into tiny pieces treated with protectants, allowing you to multiply one tuber into dozens of clean planting seeds.
ga: Kusum nifeemɔi kɛ atomo agboi ni ayeɔ tsuɔ nii. ni baafite niyenii Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ mini-set ŋaa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli bibii bibii. ni akɛ nibii ni buɔ mɔ he ewo nɔ lɛ Ehaa okwɛɔ bulb kome ni etsɔɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni he tse.

english: Why are government extension officers promoting new planting methods instead of how our elders used to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli lɛ mli nitsulɔi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ gbɛi heei ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii lɛ ahe hewalɛ moŋ fe gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nibii ni edara lɛ?

english: Modern methods are designed to solve current challenges like unpredictable weather, reduced soil fertility, and new crop diseases, helping farmers get much higher crop yields from smaller pieces of land.
ga: Ato ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ gbɛ̀i ahe gbɛjianɔ koni akɛtsu ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ naagbai ahe nii, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni bɛ faŋŋ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi kɛ tsei ahe helai heei Eyeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛnáa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔji bibii anɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes or poles to climb on to give me big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso loo tso ni ekɛkwɔ koni eshɛ ŋmeii wuji ahe lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground so they get full sun and reduces the risk of fungal diseases spreading on damp soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulb agboi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo aha, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my yams producing small tubers even though the leaves on the vine look very green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ yɛ bulbs bibii eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ waa ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Lush green leaves mean the vine has plenty of nitrogen, but small tubers happen if the soil lacks potassium, if plants are spaced too closely, or if heavy, compact soil prevents the tuber from expanding underground.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ wain tso lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo. Shi ŋmeii bibii baaba kɛji akɛ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsii ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa bulb lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How can I tell if the yam tubers I saved for planting are healthy and free from diseases?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ mli?

english: Healthy seed yams feel firm to the touch, have undamaged skin without soft rot patches, show no insect holes, and sprout clean, strong buds rather than weak or withered shoots.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ ata he. Eyɛ hewolo ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he ni fitemɔ he okadii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ko bɛ he, kooloi akutsei bɛ mli, ni eyɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni he tse. Yɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni egbi lɛ najiaŋ

english: What causes yellow spots and curling on my yam leaves during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi ni yɔɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellowing and leaf curl are usually caused by viral infections carried by tiny insects like aphids, or fungal leaf spot diseases triggered by high humidity and poor airflow around crowded plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids, loo fungal leaf spot ni hulutsoo babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ he lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. tsei ni gbɔmɛi babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ

english: When is the exact right time to harvest my yams so they don't spoil in the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yams are ready to harvest when the leaves turn yellow and the vines dry up naturally, showing that the plant has finished sending all its energy down into the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni wain tsei lɛ egbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛmajeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ naa.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting or sprouting too quickly in my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ oya tsɔ yɛ mi-shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rotting happens when bruised or diseased yams are kept in warm, poorly ventilated spaces, while early sprouting occurs when stored yams are exposed to moisture or warmth that signals them to grow again.
ga: Nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ akɛ sweet potatoes ni egbɔjɔ loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ to hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni mra be mli shweremɔ baa kɛji akɛ sweet potatoes ni ato lɛ wo ŋmɔtɔ loo hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ amɛbaadara ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing fewer bags of cocoa every year even though the farm size is the same?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ cocoa kotokui fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ yaa nɔ ehiɔ shi nakai nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: A continuous drop in harvest often means your trees are suffering from an underlying disease like Swollen Shoot or Black Pod, or the soil has run out of nutrients needed to nourish cocoa pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmaa lɛ ni yaa nɔ ebaa shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela ko ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ miipiŋ otso lɛ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu loo ŋmeii ni efee ediŋŋ. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha kookoo ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees flower heavily but fail to produce actual cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi waa shi ewooo cocoa ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Flowers fail to turn into pods when the tree is too weak from disease to support pod growth, or when dry weather and lack of pollinating insects prevent the flowers from being fertilized.
ga: Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ afee ŋmeii kɛji tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ kɛjɛ hela mli ni enyɛŋ eye ebua ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ. Aloo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ, ni no haa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: What makes my cocoa pods look smaller and contain tiny beans compared to previous years?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛyɛ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii kɛ akɛto afii ni eho lɛ ahe?

english: Small pods and poor bean quality happen when diseases or pests drain the tree's energy, preventing proper food and water from reaching the growing pods.
ga: Pods bibii kɛ nut ni ehiii lɛ baa kɛji helai loo kooloi ni yeɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ fite. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, niyenii kɛ nu ni sa nyɛɛɛ ashɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know if my cocoa tree is sick before the harvest starts dropping?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ hela mɔ amɛ dani ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi egbeɔ shi?

english: Sick trees show early signs in their leaves and stems, such as yellowing leaf veins, red blotches on young leaves, swollen branches, or unusual leaf dropping before pods even mature.
ga: Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ baajie okadii ni baa mra yɛ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ, tamɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ yɛ baa bibii lɛ anɔ, niji ni efuu, loo baa lɛ ni elaaje yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ dani ŋmɔtɔi lɛ daraa.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cool, overly shaded, and wet conditions, quickly destroying the pods and spreading to nearby trees.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ lɛ Shade kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why are the branches on my cocoa trees developing strange swollen spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ hei ni efuu ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ lɛ?

english: Swollen branches are a key sign of the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, a serious disease spread by mealybugs that slowly reduces your yield and eventually kills the tree.
ga: Niji ni efuu lɛ ji okadi titri ni tsɔɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni ji hela ko ni naa wa ni ŋmeii ni ji mealybugs lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni haa tso lɛ yibiiwoo baa shi fiofio, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egbeɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow and falling off during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excessive waterlogging in the soil or heavy fungal infections during rain can choke the tree roots, causing leaves to turn yellow and drop off prematurely.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe nine loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ni naa wa ni baa mɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi mra.

english: Can a disease on one sick cocoa tree spread to the rest of my farm?
ga: Ani hela ko ni yɔɔ cacao tso kome ni hela mɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã miŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, diseases travel easily from tree to tree through crawling insects like mealybugs, contaminated harvesting tools, wind, rain drops, or direct contact between touching branches.
ga: Hɛɛ, helai fãa gbɛ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ mlɛo kɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii ni shwereɔ tamɔ ŋmeii, ŋmaakpamɔ nibii ni mli ewo muji, kɔɔyɔɔ, nu mli nu ni hoɔ, loo tsei niji ni taa amɛhe lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ nɔ.

english: If my cocoa harvest keeps dropping, should I cut down the sick trees or spray them with medicine?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mi-kookoo ni mifeɔ lɛ tee nɔ eba shi lɛ Ani esa akɛ mafo tso ni hela mɔ lɛ lɛ mli loo mafɔse nɔ?

english: Fungal diseases like Black Pod can be managed with chemical spraying, but viral diseases like Swollen Shoot cannot be cured by spraying and require cutting down infected trees to save the rest of the farm.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji anɔ lɛ atsu nii. Shi anyɛɛɛ atsa helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ ni ehe miihia ni afo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ koni akɛhere ŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ yiwala.

english: Why do weeds growing around my cocoa trees affect how much harvest I get?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mihe lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, cacao tso lɛ saa nibii ni minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Weeds steal water and soil food from your cocoa trees, and they trap excess moisture around the trunks, creating a moist environment where crop diseases thrive.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei amli lɛ. ni emɔɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ he kɛbɔleɔ tso lɛ he, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsei ahe helai baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do I see small worms hiding right inside the central funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: The central funnel (or whorl) of young maize is soft, moist, and protected from the hot sun, making it the perfect feeding and hiding spot for destructive pests like the Fall Armyworm.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ (loo ring) ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ niyenii jɛɛhe ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ baanyɛ ahi.

english: Why does my maize crop look like the leaves are being eaten from the inside before they even open up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyeɔ baai lɛ kɛjɛɔ emli dani ekwɛ̃ɔ po lɛ?

english: Pests lay eggs deep inside the tightly rolled leaves in the center of the plant. As the plant grows and the leaves unfurl, the holes eaten while the leaf was rolled up become visible.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ woɔ amɛwui lɛ yɛ baai ni abɔle amɛhe shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Beni tso lɛ daa ni baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ Buji ni ayeɔ beni baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: How can I tell if there are worms inside my corn plants if I cannot see them directly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli kɛji minyɛɛɛ mana amɛ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Look closely into the central funnel of the plant for moist, saw-dust-like droppings (frass) or ragged, torn edges on the newest leaves growing out from the middle.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tsɔne lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni ona ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ (nibii ni etse) loo ŋmɔtɔ ni etse yɛ baai heei ni jɛɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do pests like Fall Armyworms prefer attacking maize over many other crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworms sumɔɔ ni amɛtutua ŋmãa fe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ? yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Maize forms a deep central funnel that provides both high-nutrition tender leaves and a safe shelter from predators, rain, and intense heat.
ga: Abɛi feɔ gbɛ ko ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni haa baai bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ waa kɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi awui, nugbɔ, kɛ latsaa ni naa wa fɛɛ he.

english: When I spray pesticide over the top of my corn leaves, why do the worms inside still survive?
ga: Beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa baa nɔ lɛ Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ hi shi lolo lɛ?

english: Chemicals sprayed broadly on outer leaves do not reach deep inside the central funnel where the worms hide. To kill them, the spray must drop directly into the center funnel where the pests live.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ he ko ni da yɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ eyaaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni agbe amɛ Esa akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsɔ gbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What is the correct way to hold my knapsack spray wand when treating my maize field?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ sɛɛgbɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ hiɛɔ kɛ́ ookwɛ ŋmãa?

english: Point the nozzle directly downward over the center whorl of each plant so the liquid flows straight into the middle funnel where the pest is located, rather than sweeping side to side.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ nozzle lɛ yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋgbɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni nu lɛ atsɔ gbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshwie kɛya afã

english: Why do some agricultural officers advise placing chemical liquid or granules directly into the center funnel of the corn plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi komɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni ji nu loo ŋmeii awo ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Targeting the center funnel places the chemical exactly where the pest feeds, ensuring direct contact with the pest while reducing chemical waste on outer leaves.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ ohiɛ fɔ̃ gbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ekɛ tsofai woɔ he ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ boteɔ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ ashɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsofai ni fiteɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Does rain wash away the pesticide if it gets trapped inside the middle funnel of my corn?
ga: Ani nugbɔ baajie tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ kɛji amɛbote mi-ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: If applied correctly into the central whorl during dry conditions, the chemical quickly reaches the pest inside the funnel before rain can dilute or wash it off the outer leaves.
ga: Kɛ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ kooyigbɛ yɛ be mli ni egbiɔ lɛ. Tsofai lɛ shɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ahe oya dani nugbɔ baanyɛ aha amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo efɔ amɛhe kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: At what stage of growth is my maize crop most likely to get pests inside the center funnel?
ga: Mɛɛ be mli mi ŋmãa lɛ baanyɛ aná tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ e-mid-growth lane lɛ mli?

english: Maize is most vulnerable from two to six weeks after sprouting, while the central leaves are still young, tender, and forming the funnel shape.
ga: Abɛi ji nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara fe fɛɛ yɛ otsii enyɔ kɛyashi enumɔ sɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Be mli ni baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji gbekɛbii lolo lɛ, amɛhe jɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmei.

english: Can I prevent pests from entering the middle funnel of my corn before they cause heavy damage?
ga: Ani manyɛ matsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkabote ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ dani amɛfite nii waa?

english: Yes, by inspecting the center funnel of your plants early and applying targeted spray or ash mixtures directly into the middle as soon as you spot tiny holes or droppings.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ otsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ ni oookwɛ mra lɛ nɔ. Ni okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo sũ ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni akɛtoɔ hiɛ lɛ awo mligbɛ kɛji ona buji bibii loo ŋmɔtɔi pɛ.

english: Why do birds keep coming to attack my crops right when they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi tutuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa amɛ pɛ?

english: Birds are attracted to ripe crops because the seeds, grains, and fruits become soft, sweet, and rich in nutrients at full maturity. Staying on the farm to guard your field during this period helps protect your crop yield from being eaten right before harvest.
ga: Okpoi sumɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ ejaakɛ dumɔwui, ŋmaa, kɛ aduawai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛmli ŋɔɔ, ni niyenii kpakpai babaoo yɛ mli kɛ́ amɛdara. Kɛ́ ohi ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni obu oŋmɔji lɛ ahe yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe koni akaye amɛ dani akpa.

english: Is burning my farmland before planting a good idea?
ga: Ani ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni ashãa dani aduɔ nii lɛ ji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa?

english: Burning clears weeds and bush quickly, but doing it repeatedly destroys beneficial soil organisms and burns away organic matter. Over time, this makes the soil dry, weak, and less able to support healthy crop growth.
ga: Shãa baajie jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii oya. Shi shãa ni afɔɔ feemɔ Efiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ni eshãa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbiɔ, egbɔjɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ eye ebua tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛdara lɛ.

english: Why do my ripe crops fall off the plants if I leave them on the field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Once crops reach full maturity, the plant naturally stops supplying them with food and nutrients so the seed can drop. If you do not harvest them on time, the stems weaken and the ripe crops fall to the ground where they rot or get eaten by pests.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Tso lɛ kpaɔ niyenii kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛhaa tso lɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ agbo. Kɛji okpaaa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ be naa lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ he ni amɛgboiɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ amɛ.

english: Can I just plant my crop seeds and return to the farm only when it is harvest time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui ni maku misɛɛ kɛya ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ́ be shɛ ni abaakpa nii pɛ?

english: Leaving your farm unattended after planting exposes your crops to weeds, diseases, and pests like birds and rodents. Regular visits allow you to care for the young plants and protect your yield before pests destroy it.
ga: Oshimɔ oŋmɔ lɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛɔ jwɛi, helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ okpoi kɛ ŋmeii baa. Saramɔi ni ofeɔ daa lɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ tsei bibii lɛ anɔ ni obuɔ onibii ahe dani tsɛŋemɔ helai baafite.

english: How can I protect my crop yield from birds if I am unable to stay on the farm all day?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ okpoi ahe? Kɛji minyɛɛɛ mahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ

english: You can use physical deterrents like scarecrows, shiny reflective ribbons, or noise-makers tied around the field. Moving these objects around every few days prevents birds from getting used to them while you are away.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ hebuu tamɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii ni kpɛɔ ni haa hulu kpɛɔ lɛ atsu nii. Aloo abaanyɛ akɛ tsɔnei ni akɛtswaa gbee lɛ akpɛtɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he. Nibii nɛɛ ni oootsi kɛya he fɛɛ he Gbii fioo fɛɛ gbii fioo lɛ baatsi okpoi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔse amɛhe be mli ni obɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my old planting methods not giving me good harvests like they used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii momo lɛ wooo yibii kpakpai tamɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Farming conditions change over time due to shifts in weather, soil health, and increased pest populations. Practices that worked in the past, like leaving fields untended, now require more active management to produce a good harvest.
ga: Okwaayeli shihilɛi tsakeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ, shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nifeemɔi ni etsu nii yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli, tamɔ ŋmɔji ni ashiɔ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ Amrɔ nɛɛ ehe miihia ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni anyɛ ana yibii kpakpai.

english: What happens to my produce if it drops onto the soil before I collect it?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji egbee shikpɔŋ dani mikpa?

english: Produce that falls onto damp soil quickly attracts insects, mold, and rot. Ground moisture causes grains and seeds to spoil or sprout prematurely, making them unfit for sale or consumption.
ga: Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii, ŋmeii ni fiteɔ oya. Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui kɛ dumɔwui fiteɔ loo amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya. ni haa esaaa akɛ ahɔ̃ɔ loo ayeɔ

english: What can I do to clear my farm without using fire?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mikɛjie ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mikɛ la tsuuu nii?

english: You can clear your land manually with cutlasses or hoes and leave the cleared vegetation on the ground as mulch. This organic cover keeps the soil moist, prevents weed growth, and adds nutrients back into the dirt.
ga: Bo diɛŋtsɛ obaanyɛ okɛ dade loo shɔvel ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni oshi tsei ni ajie lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Nɛkɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: At what stage of growth are my crops most vulnerable to being destroyed by animals?
ga: Mɛɛ dalɛ mli miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ oshara fe fɛɛ akɛ kooloi baafite?

english: Crops face the highest danger during early germination when seedlings are tender, and during the final ripening stage when fruits and grains are sweet and mature enough to attract pests like birds and monkeys.
ga: Tsei kɛ oshara ni fe fɛɛ kpeɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ mra beni dumɔwui lɛ darako lɛ. kɛ naagbee be mli ni aduawai kɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli ŋɔɔ ni edara bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ agbala tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ okpoi kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Why do pests cause more damage to my crops during the harvesting season than during the growing stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli fe be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: During the growing stage, plants mostly have green leaves which are harder to digest. In the harvest season, mature grains and fruits are nutrient-dense and easy food sources, attracting larger numbers of hungry pests to your farm.
ga: be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ Tsei babaoo yɛ baai eŋɔli ni ewaa akɛ amɛaaye. yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ, ŋmaa kɛ aduawai ni edara lɛ ji niyenii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli babaoo ni anyɛɔ anáa oya. Gbalamɔ kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ babaoo kɛba oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa the shade and soil moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen nutrients in the soil or that heavy rain is drowning the roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure helps them turn dark green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yes, the small growth buds on the cassava stem must point upwards toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the stems will struggle to grow upwards, resulting in weak plants and very few tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu lɛ kɛtee shishi lɛ Tso lɛ baaná naagba yɛ edalɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛbɛ bulb fioo ko pɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make the food that builds large subterranean tubers. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so leaves get maximum sunlight and avoid rotting on damp soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ. koni baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ, ni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars hiding inside the center shoot?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. These caterpillars eat the growing point of the maize plant, and spraying recommended pest controls early in the morning or late evening stops them before they destroy your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ yeɔ hei ni ŋmeii tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ. Ni tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ haa amɛkpaa nitsumɔ dani amɛfiteɔ oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally puts nitrogen back into your soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat or uneven watering. Watering your plants steadily at the base early in the morning helps the flowers stay attached and form healthy fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa yɛ eshishigbɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it necessary to clear weeds when my crop seedlings are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ be mli ni midumɔwui lɛ darako kwraa lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings are weak and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for water, sunlight, and fertilizer. Weeding early ensures your young crops get all the food they need to establish strong root systems.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otsei bibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa.

english: How can I prevent insects from eating my harvested maize while stored in my barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ be mli ni mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Insects thrive in damp grain. You must dry your harvested maize in the sun until it is hard and crackles when bitten, then store it in clean, airtight storage bags or treated bins to keep pests out.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ omanye yɛ ŋmãa ni mli efɔ mli. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa ni ebaagbala kɛji akɛ okɛ lɛ ŋmɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛto kotoku ko ni mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo tsofafeemɔ tanki mli koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote mli.

english: Why do some farmers spread dry grass or leaves on the soil around their pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass is called mulching. It acts like a protective blanket that keeps the soil cool under hot sun, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and stops weeds from sprouting.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaa jwɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔ

english: How can I tell if the seed maize I bought at the market is high quality before I plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ dani miduɔ?

english: Good quality seed maize should be clean, hard, uniform in size, free from insect holes, and not moldy. You can test quality by wrapping 10 seeds in a wet cloth; if at least 8 or 9 sprout after a few days, the seeds are good for planting.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe atse, ewa, ni elɛɛmɔ afee ekome. Ebɛ ŋmeii bu kɛ ŋmeii. Obaanyɛ oka bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni oookɛwo mama ni mli efɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ, kɛ hoo lɛ, tsei 8 loo 9 baakwɛ̃. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ hi kɛha dumɔ.

english: Why are my cassava stem cuttings failing to sprout after I plant them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava stems usually fail to sprout if they were cut from old or diseased plants, stored for too long, planted upside down, or planted in dry soil. Always cut healthy mature stems from the middle section of the plant and ensure the bud eyes point upwards when planting into moist soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tsei lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛji akɛ afolɔ amɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni egbɔ loo helai emɔ amɛ lɛ amli. Akɛtoɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, aduɔ kɛyaa shishi, loo aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni eda kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋ be fɛɛ be. Ni kwɛmɔ ni fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow along the middle line?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the middle of maize leaves is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency, meaning the plant lacks food to build green leaves. Applying organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer early in the growth period helps restore leaf health and green color.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji okadi ni ale waa ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni baaha ewo baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli mra yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baa lɛ he awa kɛ eŋɔli su ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep dropping off the plant without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when they suffer heat stress, drought, or too much fertilizer. When temperatures get very high or water is scarce, the plant discards its blossoms to save energy rather than trying to feed fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛkɛ haomɔ ni jɛ dɔlɛ, hɔmɔ, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine mli kpe. Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo nu faaa lɛ. Tsei lɛ baashɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtao niyenii kɛha aduawai.

english: Cocoa plants curl their leaves to lower water loss when the air is dry and hot. Leaving suitable shade trees like plantains or leguminous trees on your farm helps cool the air, block harsh wind, and retain moisture for the cocoa trees.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. Tsei ni sa ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo legumes ni oooshi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli Enɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa, ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi kookoo tsei lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and die at the root right after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: When water sits on the soil surface for long, pepper roots cannot get oxygen and rot diseases attack the stems. Planting peppers on raised ridges or mounds allows excess rainwater to drain off quickly, keeping roots healthy.
ga: Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, Pepper shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. ni ŋmɔtɔ tutuaa tso lɛ shishi. Pepper ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo gɔji anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: How do I know if my soil is loose enough to grow long, healthy yams?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ ŋmeii kakadaŋŋ agboi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, deep, and well-drained soil so they can expand easily underground. If the soil is hard clay or compacted, the roots will struggle to push through, resulting in small, bent, or deformed yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Ebaawa akɛ shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii, amɛbɔle amɛhe, loo amɛfite.

english: If I plant my corn seeds very close together, won't I harvest more corn from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani minyɛŋ makpa ŋmãa babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, planting too close creates intense competition among plants for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in thin, tall stalks with tiny or empty cobs, whereas proper spacing yields fewer but far bigger and heavier cobs.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa tsei ateŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. loo nɔ ko bɛ mli Yɛ be mli ni sɛɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baaha ŋmeii fioo pɛ aba lɛ, amɛdara kwraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why is my plantain stand taking so much longer to bear fruit compared to my neighbor's farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii kɛ akɛto mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Plantain plants grow slowly if too many young shoots (suckers) are growing from the same base and stealing food from the main plant. Pruning extra suckers so only two or three remain gives the main stem enough nutrients to fruit quickly.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo ni miida kɛjɛ shishitoo kome mli ni amɛmiiju niyenii kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli lɛ fa babaoo. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ koni tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ eshwɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii oya.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly on my farm even after I cleared and tilled the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miikwɛ̃ oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni mikɛtsu nii moŋ.

english: Weed seeds can rest hidden inside the soil for years waiting for light and water. When you dig or till the soil, you turn these buried seeds up to the warm surface where sunlight triggers them to germinate instantly.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afii babaoo ni amɛmɛ la kɛ nu. Beni otsuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ loo ootsu nii lɛ Ehe baahia ni okɛ dumɔwui ni afu nɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Hulu la lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Officer, how many years will it take for a new coconut tree to start producing fruit after planting?
ga: Official Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei tso hee ko jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Generally, coconut trees take about four years to start producing fruit, but the exact time depends on the specific variety you plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tsei heɔ aaafee afii ejwɛ dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Shi be pɔtɛɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ damɔ tsei srɔtoi ni oduɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: I want to plant hybrid coconuts on my farm; how long do I have to wait before I get my first harvest?
ga: Miisumɔ ni madu ŋmeii ni ji hybrid yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli. Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani maná mi klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa lɛ?

english: Hybrid coconut varieties are relatively fast to mature and typically take about four years to start bearing fruit.
ga: Kokoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ daa oya ni bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee afii ejwɛ dani ebɔi yibiiwoo.

english: Why do some coconut trees take much longer to bear fruit than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei komɛi heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Coconut trees come in different varieties, and each variety has its own natural timing for growth. For example, hybrid types bear fruit in four years, while tall varieties take seven years.
ga: Ayɛ ŋmei tsei srɔtoi babaoo. Ni tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ebɔɔ su mli dalɛ be. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, hybrid henɔi lɛ woɔ yibii yɛ afii ejwɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni henɔi ni kwɔlɔ lɛ baahi shi afii kpawo.

english: How long does it take for the traditional tall coconut tree variety to produce fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani blema tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni ji ŋmeii lɛ woɔ yibii?

english: The tall variety of coconut takes longer to mature than other types, usually requiring about seven years before it starts producing fruit.
ga: Kokoo henɔi ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ fe henɔi krokomɛi. Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee afii kpawo dani ebɔi yibiiwoo.

english: What important timing details should I find out before I buy coconut seedlings to plant?
ga: Mɛɛ saji ni he hiaa esa akɛ male dani mahe ŋmei dumɔwui ni mikɛdu?

english: You should check which variety you are buying because each has a different fruiting timeline; hybrids usually take four years, whereas tall varieties take up to seven years.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ tso ni oheɔ lɛ ejaakɛ tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko yɛ be ni ekɛwoɔ yibii. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ heɔ afii ejwɛ. yɛ be mli ni henɔi ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ afii kpawo.

english: Is there any difference in fruiting time between hybrid coconut trees and the tall ones?
ga: Ani srɔtofeemɔ ko yɛ yibiiwoo be mli yɛ ŋmei tsei ni akɛfee ekome kɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, there is a difference. Hybrid coconut trees generally start producing fruit in four years, while tall coconut trees take about seven years.
ga: Hɛɛ, srɔtofeemɔ ko yɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii ejwɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei tso kakadaŋŋ ko baahi shi aaafee afii kpawo lɛ.

english: If I am planning my farm business, what is the general average waiting time for coconut trees to yield?
ga: Kɛji miito ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ Mɛni ji be ni akɛmɛɔ ŋmei?

english: As a general rule, you can expect a average waiting period of about four years for coconut trees to begin producing fruit.
ga: Taakɛ eji mla lɛ, obaanyɛ okpa gbɛ akɛ kɛ́ aja mli lɛ, ebaamɛ aaafee afii ejwɛ dani ŋmei tso ko aje yibiiwoo shishi.

english: My neighbor says his coconut trees took seven years to produce fruit; did he do something wrong?
ga: Mikutsoŋnyo lɛ kɛɛ e-coconut tso lɛ heɔ afii kpawo dani ewoɔ yibii. Ani efee nɔ ko ni ejaaa?

english: Not necessarily. If he planted the tall coconut variety, seven years is the normal and expected timeframe for that specific type to start producing fruit.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Kɛji edu ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ lɛ, Afii kpawo ji be ni sa ni akpaa gbɛ akɛ nakai ŋmeii srɔtoi lɛ baaje yibiiwoo shishi.

english: Do all coconut tree varieties mature and bear fruit at the exact same age?
ga: Ani ŋmei tsei srɔtoi lɛ fɛɛ daa ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ afii kome mli?

english: No, they do not. Each coconut variety has its own specific timeline; hybrid varieties take around four years, while tall varieties take about seven years.
ga: Dabi, amɛfeee nakai. Kokoo henɔ fɛɛ henɔ yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ebe pɔtɛɛ. Hybrid henɔi lɛ heɔ aaafee afii ejwɛ. yɛ be mli ni henɔi ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii kpawo.

english: Officer, when extension officers analyze coconut crop varieties, what do those results tell us about their growth?
ga: Official Beni mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ pɛi ŋmeii srɔtoi lɛ amli lɛ Mɛni nɔ ni jɛ mli ba lɛ tsɔɔ wɔ yɛ dalɛ he?

english: The analysis shows that growth timing depends on the variety: generally, standard and hybrid coconuts take four years to fruit, while tall varieties take seven years.
ga: Nibii amlipɛimɔ tsɔɔ akɛ be ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ damɔ ŋmei srɔtoi lɛ anɔ: ŋmei ni afɔɔ feemɔ kɛ ŋmei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ heɔ afii ejwɛ dani amɛwoɔ yibii. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni kwɔlɔ lɛ heɔ afii kpawo.

english: Why do older farmers tell me to plant plantains on the same land when I am starting a new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko kɛɛ mi akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ beni mije kookoo ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa shoots are very delicate and burn easily in the strong Ghanaian sun. Plantains grow very quickly and provide broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the shade and moisture they need to survive until they are mature.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ Ghana hulu ni naa wa lɛ mli. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi amɛbaashɛ amɛdalɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low on nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build green leaves and grow strong. It can also happen if heavy rains flood the roots, preventing them from breathing and taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha shishifãi lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ nu. Ehaa mɔ nyɛɛɛ amu ni enine ashɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their blossoms before growing any actual pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fɛɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani midu pepper aduawai lɛ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience extreme stress, such as very high heat, sudden dry spells, or receiving too much nitrogen fertilizer. The plant sheds its flowers to save energy so it can survive the stressful conditions.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi trukaa loo enine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛnyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni haoɔ mɔ mli.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting under the soil before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani manyɛ makpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water and lacks proper drainage during heavy rains. Standing water starves the roots of air and allows soil fungi to attack and rot the tubers underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo tsɔ ni nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa be mli lɛ bɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ. ni eha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atutua ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my maize seeds very close to each other in the field?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together actually reduces your total yield because the plants end up fighting each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to produce full, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ aba shi ejaakɛ tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ kɛ amɛhe feɔ ekome. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are small worms hiding inside the central leaves of my young corn plants and chewing holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛmiiye bu yɛ mli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that prefers to feed inside the tender, rolled-up center of corn plants where it is safe from predators and heat. Identifying them early allows you to treat the center whorl before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni sumɔɔ ni eye niyenii yɛ ŋmãa tsei ni abɔle amɛhe lɛ amli, ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ latsaa he. Amɛyɔsemɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsaa ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ dani amɛfiteɔ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my crops staying short and stunted even though there is plenty of rain and sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛgbɔjɔ yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulu babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops can stay stunted if the soil lacks essential nutrients like phosphorus, or if the soil has become too acidic over time. Even with water and sun, plants cannot grow tall if the soil cannot provide the chemical building blocks they need.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ batsɔ acid tsɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ nu kɛ hulu la po yɛ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ adara babaoo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee tsofai ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up tightly into small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl tightly as a self-defense reaction to extreme sun, heat, or drought to slow down water loss. It can also be caused by viral infections spread by tiny insects like whiteflies.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la, dɔlɛ, loo hɔmɔ he koni nu lɛ aya hiɛ blɛoo. Virus hela ni koolooi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ hu baanyɛ ekɛba.

english: Why do I need to clear the ground and place long wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie he ko ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing heavy tubers underground. Staking keeps leaves off the damp ground where diseases spread and exposes more surface area to sunlight for better growth.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni tsii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ, ni ehaa hulu la lɛ naa he babaoo koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my corn plants producing flowers and tassels when the stalks are still very short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ? Ani tso lɛ shishi lɛ yɛ kuku waa lolo?

english: When corn plants experience severe heat or drought early in their growth, they get stressed and try to reproduce quickly before dying. They produce flowers early to make seeds for the next generation, even if the plant itself hasn't grown fully.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ shɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ he yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ haoɔ ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni efɔ oya dani egbo. Amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi mra. Koni afee dumɔwui aha yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ edako kwraa lolo moŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your soil is running out of nitrogen, which maize relies on to stay green. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season keeps the leaves healthy to feed developing cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni esa akɛ ŋmãa kɛ ehe afɔ̃ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo nitrogen ŋmãa fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni eye ebua ŋmãa ni miida lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with bushy leaves but only produce small tubers at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai bibii pɛ kɛji akpa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or heavy moisture early on, the cassava puts most of its energy into leafy growth above ground instead of storing starch in the roots underground.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo mra mli lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: What causes the leaves of my young corn to have ragged holes with brown dust inside the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni eyɛ sũ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides and feeds inside the growing tip of the plant. Applying natural neem mixtures or recommended sprays early in the morning reaches the pests inside the leaf funnel.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ adebɔɔ mli neem ni akɛfutu loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ wo mli taakɛ atsɔɔ lɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lasu tsuji lɛ amli lɛ akabote mli.

english: Wrinkled or curled pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck sap and spread viruses. Controlling these insects early with soapy water or neem oil stops the leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Nu ni akɛ saamɔ loo neem fɔ tsu nii lɛ baaha baai lɛ afitemɔ akpa.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over during mild winds even when the bunches are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa waa mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ niji lɛ daraaa moŋ

english: Tiny soil pests like nematodes or banana weevils chew through the underground roots, taking away the tree's grip on the soil. Planting clean, pest-treated suckers keeps the root system strong and stable.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes loo banana ŋmeii yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi. Ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ shishifãi ni he tse ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ ahiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when stressed by intense heat or irregular watering. Giving the plants consistent moisture around the roots early in the morning keeps them cool enough to set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Ni akɛ nu haa tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ashishifãi lɛ leebi maŋkpa Enɛ haa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why is it important to stake my yam vines with tall sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu sweet potato wain tsei ni tsei kakadaji yɔɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines need to catch maximum sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Lifting the leaves off the damp soil with stakes prevents leaf decay and helps the tubers grow larger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ okɛ tso wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite, ni ebaaye ebua bulb lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: How do my groundnut plants form nuts under the ground when the flowers open above the ground?
ga: Te mi-peanut tso lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ ewo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated, the plant sends long pegs growing downward into the dirt. Once these pegs penetrate loose soil, their tips swell up to form groundnut pods.
ga: Beni tso lɛ ekɛ ŋmeii fɔfɔi lɛ ebɔi pollen sɛɛ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​ŋmeii kakadaji kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ bote shikpɔŋ ni etse lɛ mli pɛ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ashishi baafu ni efee ŋmeii.

english: Why do my lowland rice plants turn pale green when water stands still in the field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tseee kɛji nu ta ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Stagnant water cuts off fresh air to the roots and causes root decay, making it hard for rice to take up soil nutrients. Draining the field occasionally lets oxygen back into the soil so the plants stay dark green.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa ŋmãa akɛ ebaaŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ ji eŋɔli ni mli edɔ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize plants turn yellow while the rest of the plant is still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni baai krokomɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means your crop is hungry for nitrogen. When the soil lacks enough food, the plant moves what little nitrogen it has from its older lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ ni ji nitrogen fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die if I clear away all the big trees in my bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle hot direct sunlight. Taller forest trees or plantain plants act as shade umbrellas, protecting young cocoa from intense heat and helping the soil retain moisture so the seedlings can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ gbɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Koo mli tsei loo plantains ni kwɔlɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are my cassava plants dropping all their leaves during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods to save water and protect themselves from severe heat. Once the rains return, the plant will push out fresh green leaves and resume growing food in its underground tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ Tso lɛ baatsi baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ lɛ ni ebaakwɛ niyenii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop and stop growing when water stays on my farm for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ be mli ni nu ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like people do. When water stays trapped in the soil for too long, air cannot reach the roots, causing them to drown, rot, and stop taking up nutrients.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni adesai feɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haa amɛshwieɔ nu mli, amɛgboiɔ ni amɛkpaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwiemɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for the next crop I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts have small nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. When the crop finishes growing, it leaves that natural plant food behind for the next crop to use.
ga: Nuts kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Eshiɔ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii yɛ sɛɛ koni ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to come up when I bury them deep in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds carry only a small amount of stored energy to sprout and push out of the dirt. If buried too deep, the young shoot runs out of food before reaching sunlight and dies underground.
ga: Dumɔwui bɛ hewalɛ fioo ko ni ato koni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ aniyenii baaho dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow tall with lots of leaves but produce very few tomatoes when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daa ni amɛyɛ baai babaoo shi amɛwoɔ tomato fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded together, they compete for light, air, and soil nutrients. The plants put all their effort into growing tall to beat their neighbors for sunlight instead of producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ la mli. Tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ fɛɛ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛdara koni amɛye amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ anɔ kunim yɛ hulu la he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai.

english: How can I tell if my yam tubers are ready to harvest without digging up the whole mound?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: When yam tubers finish growing underground, the plant stops sending energy down and the leafy vines naturally turn yellow and dry up. This drying of the leaves tells you the tubers are fully mature.
ga: Kɛji sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ dara yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Tso lɛ baakpa hewalɛ ni ekɛbaa shi lɛ. Ni wain tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaagbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Baai nɛɛ ni egbi lɛ tsɔɔ bo akɛ bulb lɛ egbɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn small and weak even when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal fertilizer, water, and space away from your crops before your plants have a chance to drink it up, leaving your crops hungry.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ he ko kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Dani otsei lɛ baaná hegbɛ ni amɛnu nu ni hɔmɔ aye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do caterpillars suddenly appear on my young crops immediately after the major rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii jeɔ kpo trukaa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Moths lay their eggs just before or as the rains begin because the moisture causes fresh, tender young shoots to grow fast, providing the perfect soft food for newly hatched caterpillars.
ga: Kpɔŋɔi lɛ baawo amɛwui dani loo beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulutsoo be lɛ baaha ŋmeii bibii heei lɛ adara oya. Eji niyenii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni efɔ ehee lɛ.

english: Why are my maize seeds taking so long to sprout after planting them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need a balance of moisture and warmth to break open. If the soil is too dry or planted too deep, sprouting gets put on hold until rains clear up the dry conditions, which can take an extra week or two.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ kɛ latsaa ni sa koni amɛtswa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo adu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, aŋmɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ jieɔ shihilɛ ni mli egbi lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ ahe otsi kome loo enyɔ kroko.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting after the first rainy day of the season?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni sa ni esa akɛ oje dumɔ shishi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait a little while until the soil consistently holds moisture across several days. Planting after just one small rain can cause seeds to rot or dry out if the hot sun comes back immediately.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ahi shi pɛpɛɛpɛ gbii babaoo. Dumɔ ni adu yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbo loo amɛgbi kɛji hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ku esɛɛ eba amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow instead of staying bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves mean the plant is stressed, often because it is hungry for nutrients like nitrogen or sitting in soil with too much trapped water that cannot drain properly.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen he miihia amɛ, loo amɛtara shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu babaoo emɔ amɛhe aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛho jogbaŋŋ.

english: My tomato plants have produced flowers, so why are no actual fruits coming out yet?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi. Shi mɛni hewɔ nɔ ko kwraa jɛko mli kɛba lolo lɛ?

english: Flowers need proper weather, water, and visits from insects like bees to turn into fruit. Extreme heat or water stress can make the flowers fall off before the fruit can start forming.
ga: Fɔfɔi he miihia kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ, nu kɛ saramɔi ni jɛɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii adɛŋ koni amɛtsɔmɔ aduawai. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbɔjɔ dani aduawai aje shishi amɛfee.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop and curl up in the hot afternoon but look fine in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛfeɔ fɛo jogbaŋŋ leebi lɛ?

english: When the hot sun hits, leaves lose water faster than the roots can drink it up. Drooping is the plant's natural way of resting and saving water until the heat cools down.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Drooping ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ejɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ nu toɔ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni latsaa lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow slowly and stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ bibioo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the plant's food, water, and sunlight from the soil. When weeds surround your crops, your plants get starved and their growth gets delayed.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ tsei aniyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni jwɛi ebɔle oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ Otsei lɛ hɔmɔ baaye amɛ ni amɛdalɛ baaya sɛɛ.

english: What happens if I plant my seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe waa koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planting too close forces roots to fight each other underground for nutrients. This causes all the plants to remain thin, weak, and produce much lower yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ awuu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo, egbɔjɔɔ ni ewoɔ yibii ni baa shi kwraa.

english: Why do older farmers cover the soil around young crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni edara lɛ kɛ jwɛi ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a shade blanket. It keeps the soil cool and stops groundwater from evaporating during hot dry spells.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni haa hulu tsoɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why have my yam vines stopped growing upward and started twisting abnormally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ?

english: Stunted vine growth is usually a sign of tiny pests like sap-sucking insects underneath the leaves, which stop the plant from moving food up to its stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, wain tso bibioo ni edaa lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii, tamɔ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ baai. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii kɛya ŋwɛi tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Should I cut off the small extra shoots growing at the bottom of my plantain tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Yes, cutting away extra shoots ensures that all the food and water from the soil go straight into the main tree, helping it produce a much larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yaa tso titri lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ plantains ŋmɔji ni dara ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why do buyers in my local market prefer to buy smaller vegetables instead of very big ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ mimaŋ jarayelihe lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhe aduawai bibii moŋ fe aduawai wuji waa lɛ?

english: Local consumers often prefer smaller vegetables because they are easier to store without refrigeration, fit traditional cooking portions better, and are often perceived to have more concentrated flavor.
ga: Mɛi ni yeɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ sumɔɔ aduawai bibii ejaakɛ ewaaa akɛ akɛtoɔ friji mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ yɛ blema niyeli hei. ni bei pii lɛ abuɔ lɛ akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa fe no.

english: Is it true that I can make more profit selling a higher quantity of small crops than a few large ones?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ manyɛ maná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ fe ŋmɔshi nibii wuji fioo komɛi?

english: Yes, in many local markets, buyers prefer buying produce in smaller sizes or by count. Producing a higher yield of uniform, smaller crops can often net you more total money than selling fewer oversized items.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayeli hei babaoo. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhe nibii bibii loo amɛfa babaoo. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii bibii, ni yaa nɔ daa, ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ baaha oná shika babaoo fe nibii wuji fioo ni ooohɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why are big produce sizes sometimes harder to sell to local traders?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ ewaa akɛ abaahɔ̃ɔ nibii babaoo aha maŋ lɛ mli jarayelɔi lɛ?

english: Traders often find that very large produce spoils faster during transportation, takes up too much container space, and is too expensive for everyday buyers who prefer smaller, affordable portions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, jarayelɔi naa akɛ nibii ni amɛdara waa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akɛ amɛ maje. Eheɔ he babaoo yɛ tsɛnsi lɛ mli Ni ejara wa tsɔ kɛha daa gbi jarayelɔi ni miitao nibii bibii ni jara waaa lɛ.

english: Why do some of my crops produce smaller fruits while others grow very large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi woɔ yibii bibii yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu daraa lɛ?

english: Fruit size depends on plant spacing, water supply, soil nutrients, and crop variety. Closely spaced plants or limited nutrients usually result in smaller fruits.
ga: Yibii lɛ dalɛ damɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ, nu ni akɛhaa, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ tsei henɔi anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ shɔŋŋ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa lɛ haa amɛwoɔ yibii bibii.

english: What will happen to my cassava tubers if I plant the stems very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting cassava stems too close together causes competition for underground space and nutrients, which results in plants forming smaller tubers rather than large ones.
ga: Cassava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa shikpɔŋ shishi he kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa bulb ni ji bibioo fe bulb wuji.

english: If I pluck off some of the tiny fruits on my plant early, will the rest grow bigger?
ga: Kɛji mifo aduawai bibioo ko yɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ mra Ani aduawai ni eshwɛ lɛ baafee agbo?

english: Yes, removing some young fruits (known as thinning) allows the plant to send all its energy and water to the remaining fruits, making them grow larger.
ga: Hɛɛ, aduawai bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ (ni atsɛɔ lɛ thinning) lɛ haa tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ kɛ nu fɛɛ kɛyaa aduawai ni eshwɛ lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji aduawai ni da fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Why do my larger crops get damaged more easily when I transport them on rough roads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii wuji lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ tee gbɛjegbɛi ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Larger produce items often have softer flesh and thinner skin, making them prone to cracking and bruising when bumped around inside transport trucks.
ga: Nibii ni dara lɛ fɔɔ gbɔmɔtsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɛ́ amɛtswa amɛhe yɛ tsɔnei ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ amli lɛ, ewaaa akɛ amɛbaagbala ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Should I harvest my vegetables early when they are small or wait for them to grow very big?
ga: Kulɛ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-vegetables lɛ mra. Beni eji bibioo loo mɛɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa?

english: It depends on market demand. Harvesting early when crops are smaller keeps them tender and preferred by local buyers, whereas leaving them too long can make them tough, woody, or prone to rotting.
ga: Edamɔ jarayeli nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ anɔ mra be mli nikpamɔ Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni no hewɔ lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ taoɔ lɛ waa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ ashi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ afee nɔ ni wa, ni efee tso, loo ebaanyɛ egbo.

english: Will putting too much fertilizer make my crops grow too big and lose their natural taste?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara tsɔ ni amɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋɔɔmɔ lɛ baaje mli?

english: Excessive fertilizer, especially nitrogen, makes plants absorb lots of water and grow rapidly, which can dilute their natural flavor and shorten their shelf life.
ga: ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine titri lɛ nitrogen Haa tsei shwieɔ nu babaoo ni amɛdaraa oya. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ lɛ baa shi ni ehaa be ni akɛtoɔ lɛ feɔ kuku.

english: How do I choose the right seed variety if my local buyers only want small-sized crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui srɔtoi ni sa? Kɛji akɛ hɔlɔ ko ni yɔɔ mimaŋ lɛ miitao ŋmɔshi nibii bibii pɛ.

english: You can ask your local extension officer for seed varieties specifically bred to produce compact, high-yielding crops that match the size and taste preferences of your local market.
ga: Obaanyɛ obi mɔ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ oakutso lɛ mli lɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsɔse amɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ kuku, ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni kɛ oakutso lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ dalɛ kɛ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ lɛ kpãa gbee lɛ he sane.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow when the soil stays too wet after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ lolo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When soil stays flooded, water fills up all the air spaces around the roots. Without air, the roots cannot breathe or absorb nitrogen from the soil, which makes the leaves lose their green color and turn yellow.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli obɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛŋɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ ahe su eŋɔli lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I keep and plant the seeds from the hybrid maize I harvested last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni ji hybrid corn ni mikpa yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are bred from two specific parent plants to produce a high yield. Seeds saved from that harvest lose their special combination of strength, resulting in lower yields, uneven growth, and weaker plants in the second generation.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ fɔɔ tsei enyɔ ni ji fɔlɔi lɛ amli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ hewalɛ krɛdɛɛ ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi. shweremɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme midday heat or sudden dry spells. The plant drops its blossoms to conserve energy and water until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛkɛ haomɔi kpe, tamɔ shwane mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa. Tsei baajie fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does placing chemical fertilizer right against my crop stem burn and kill the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mi tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli lɛ haa tsei lɛ shãa ni efiteɔ lɛ?

english: Fertilization supplies concentrated mineral salts. When placed right against the stem or main root, the salt draws water out of the plant tissues instead of feeding them, causing the plant to dry out and burn.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ fɔmɔ kotoku mli lɛ haa mineral salts ni mli eyi obɔ. Kɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he lɛ, Nu lɛ jieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ fãji amli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas in my field make my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have beneficial bacteria in their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, leaving free nutrients behind for future crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛshiɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and looking patchy light green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ eŋɔli yɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies that feed on sap and pass the sickness from plant to plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmei mli lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow tall and thin instead of thick and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal light, water, and soil nutrients from your crops. When weeds grow fast, your crops are forced to stretch quickly toward the sky to reach sunlight, making their stems thin and weak.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ la, nu, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ oya lɛ, anyɛɔ Oŋmɔshinii lɛ anɔ koni oya oya kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛyamɔ hulu la lɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ

english: This is known as blossom-end rot. It happens when the tomato plant lacks calcium or receives irregular watering while the fruit is growing rapidly, causing the cell walls at the bottom of the fruit to collapse.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ calcium bɛ tomato tsei amli loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida oya lɛ. Enɛ haa wala yibii ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do yam leaves turn yellow and die off when the tubers under the ground are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: When a yam tuber reaches full size, the plant stops making new foliage and transfers all remaining energy from the leaves into the underground tuber, causing the leaves above ground to wither naturally.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shɛ amɛdalɛ he lɛ Tso lɛ kpaɔ baai heei feemɔ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why is the rain no longer coming in the exact same months as it used to when my father was farming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ lɛ enɛɛɛ yɛ nyɔji ni Ataa tsuɔ okwaayeli nii yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli dɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Global weather patterns are changing over time, which causes the rainy seasons in Ghana to start earlier or later than usual and bring unpredictable amounts of water.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ je lɛŋ fɛɛ lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Enɛ haa nugbɔ be ni nɛɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ jeɔ shishi mra loo esɛɛ tsɛɔ fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ. ni ekɛ nu babaoo ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ baa

english: If the rains start late this year, should I still plant my seeds at the traditional time?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ yɛ afi nɛɛ naagbee Ani esa akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ mibe ni mikɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ mli?

english: No, planting seeds in dry soil before steady rains begin can cause the seeds to dry up and fail to germinate; it is safer to wait until the soil holds enough moisture.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛkakwɛ̃. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: How does sudden, heavy rainfall after a long dry period affect my crops?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rain after drought can shock young plants, cause waterlogging that rots roots, and wash away vital topsoil nutrients before the plant can absorb them.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ hɔmɔ sɛɛ baanyɛ aha tsei bibii lɛ ahe afee shoo. Enɛ haa nu shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. ni efoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up tightly during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism where the plant reduces its surface area exposed to strong sunlight to prevent water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei lɛ baaha he ni hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi koni nu lɛ akatsɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop their leaves when there is a long dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods to save energy and stop water loss, allowing the plant to survive underground until rainy weather returns.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛkpa nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why are my maize plants wilting so quickly when the rain stops for just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ shwieɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo komɛi pɛ lɛ?

english: When weather becomes hotter and drier, topsoil loses moisture rapidly, causing shallow-rooted crops like young maize to wilt fast if they cannot reach deeper soil water.
