ga: Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli woɔ la ni egbiɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ baagboi oya kɛji amɛnyɛŋ amɛyashɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce flowers but drop them before any pods can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi shi ashi dani ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees face excessive heat or lack enough soil moisture, they drop flowers to protect themselves from over-exhaustion and preserve water.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tsei lɛ shɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa he loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ tɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he ni amɛhiɛ nu mli.

english: Why do agricultural researchers get so many more bags of harvest from their fields than local farmers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi naa ŋmaakpamɔ kotokui babaoo kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji amli fe maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi lɛ?

english: Researchers get high yields because they use precise plant spacing, seeds bred for current weather conditions, and apply nutrients and water at exact stage-specific times.
ga: Nibii amlitaolɔi lɛ ná sɛɛnamɔi babaoo ejaakɛ amɛkɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ pɔtɛɛ tsu nii. Dumɔ dumɔwui yɛ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ ji lɛ naa. ni okɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu atsu nii yɛ bei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ fã fɛɛ fã mli

english: Why do some improved crop varieties perform better than our traditional seeds when rain is short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi komɛi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe wɔ shishijee dumɔwui lɛ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Improved seed varieties are specifically bred to mature faster or grow deeper root systems, helping them produce good yields even with short or irregular rains.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛdara oya loo koni amɛha shishifãi lɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai kɛji nugbɔ nɛ be kukuoo po. loo nɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee

english: How does spreading dry grass or leaves around my crops help them survive hot weather?
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa kɛbɔleɔ he lɛ Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry materials, called mulching, acts like a protective blanket that shades the soil, keeps it cool, and prevents water from evaporating away.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ nibii ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do some varieties of cassava produce yield faster than the local ones I usually plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi woɔ yibii oya fe ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Improved cassava varieties are specifically bred by agricultural researchers to grow faster, resist common diseases, and absorb nutrients more efficiently than traditional local varieties.
ga: Okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi ekwɛ ŋmei ni atsake lɛ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni ekwɛ̃ oya. Enyɛɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ naa lɛ anaa ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe akutsoŋbii akutseiaŋ tsofai srɔtoi lɛ

english: How do scientists create new seed varieties that can survive long dry seasons in Ghana?
ga: Bɔ ni jeŋ nilelɔi fee dumɔwui heei ni baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli yɛ Ghana

english: Researchers select naturally strong parent plants that tolerate heat and drought, cross-pollinate them over generations, and test them to ensure the offspring produce good yields even with low rainfall.
ga: Nibii amlitaolɔi hala tsei ni ji nyɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ hulutsoo kɛ hɔmɔ. Akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ebɔ he yɛ yinɔi babaoo mli. ni aka koni ana akɛ seshi lɛ baawo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai kɛji nugbɔ fioo po nɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow when water stays on the land for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When water covers the ground for too long, it pushes air out of the soil. Without oxygen, root systems cannot breathe or absorb nitrogen, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Kɛ nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛŋɔ nitrogen. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do flowers fall off my pepper plants before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Flower drop occurs when plants face extreme heat, lack of water, or lack of pollination from insects, causing the plant to shed flowers to conserve its energy.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ shɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa he, nu bɛ, loo kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why should I space my tomato plants apart instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbala mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: Proper spacing prevents plants from competing for sunlight and soil nutrients, and allows fresh air to circulate, which keeps fungal diseases from spreading between wet leaves.
ga: He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akagbɛ ashwã baai ni efɔ lɛ ateŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow short and crooked when the soil is very hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ feɔ kukuji ni ebɔle amɛhe be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa waa lɛ?

english: Root and tuber crops need soft, well-tilled soil so their roots can expand downward without physical barriers blocking their growth.
ga: Shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii biɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni atsuɔ he nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shishigbɛ ni gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ko bɛ ni tsiɔ amɛdalɛ naa.

english: Why do my crops still need fertilizer if my farmland already looks dark and rich?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii lolo kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efee tamɔ nɔ ni edɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii momo lɛ?

english: Even rich soil loses specific nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium after every harvest, so fertilizer is needed to replenish what crops remove during growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ po laajeɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium. Yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ fɛɛ kpamɔ sɛɛ No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia koni akɛto nɔ ni tsei jieɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Weeds are wild species adapted to survive in harsh conditions, making them extremely fast at capturing available sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before cultivated plants can.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli kooloi ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya dani tsei ni miida lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crop damage is caused by insects or by a plant disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii loo tsei ahe helai ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fitemɔ baa?

english: Insects physically eat the crop, leaving visible holes or cut stems, while diseases typically cause leaf discoloration, dark spots, wilting, or mold without any visible bite marks.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni amɛshiɔ bu loo ŋmeii ni anaa. Yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ hela lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmɔlɔ ni anaaa lɛ bɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why is it recommended to trim some leaves off tomato plants while they are growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ afo tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ekomɛi beni aduɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Trimming unnecessary lower leaves allows the plant to redirect its energy and nutrients directly into growing larger, healthier fruits rather than maintaining extra foliage.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ tsɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ koni ekwɛ̃ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe ni eeehiɛ baa krokomɛi amli.

english: Is it bad if I apply fertilizer to my farm a few weeks before the rain actually starts?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi dani nugbɔ lɛ je shishi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer needs water to dissolve so the plant roots can drink it. If you put fertilizer in completely dry soil long before the rain comes, it can sit unused, lose its strength into the air, or burn young roots when the heat is high.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia nu koni amɛtsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu amɛ. Kɛji okɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa dani nugbɔ lɛ ba lɛ, Fertilizer lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni bɛ nitsumɔ. ni akɛtsuuu nii Hewalɛ ni baa shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli loo shishifãi bibii ni ashãa kɛji latsaa lɛ mli wa

english: If I put fertilizer on my crops right before a heavy rainstorm, will the rain wash all of it away?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ Ani nugbɔ lɛ baaho ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Yes, heavy rain pouring over the surface can wash loose fertilizer away into rivers or ditches before it sinks in. It is best to bury fertilizer slightly in the soil or apply it after moderate rainfall when the ground is moist.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni nɛɔ yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ baanyɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe lɛ awo faai loo ŋshɔkei amli dani efo mli. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo okɛwo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I place chemical fertilizer directly touching the stem of my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated salts. Placing it right against the main stem creates chemical heat that burns the delicate skin of the plant, weakening or killing the crop instead of helping it grow.
ga: Fertilizer lɛ yɛ ŋoo babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛwo tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he lɛ, ehaa tsofa mli dɔlɛ ni shãa tso lɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baa. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ loo egbeɔ amɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye ebua lɛ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Can applying too much fertilizer at once kill my crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni mikɛwoɔ mli shikome lɛ baanyɛ akpata miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahiɛ?

english: Yes, too much fertilizer creates a high salt level in the soil which actually pulls water out of the plant roots instead of feeding them. This causes leaf tips to look burnt and can cause the crop to wither.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baanyɛ aha ŋmei babaoo aya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli moŋ fe ni eeeha amɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ ashishi feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã ni ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ agbo.

english: Should I plant my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is usually safer to wait for steady rains rather than the very first shower. Early single rains often vanish for weeks, leaving the newly sprouted seedlings to burn and die in dry soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be fe ni oooho klɛŋklɛŋ. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shikome lɛ laajeɔ otsii babaoo. Ha dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ashã ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves wilt in the hot afternoon even when it rained a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Ni nugbɔ nɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ?

english: During peak heat, plants sweat out water faster through their leaves than their roots can pull up from the ground. If they stand upright again by evening or early morning, it is just normal temporary heat stress.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ latsaa kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa lɛ Eji be kukuoo mli latsaa he haomɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛkɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crop is struggling because of dry weather or because the soil lacks plant food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigba enaa yɛ shihilɛ ni mli egbi loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsei ahe nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ?

english: Drought causes all leaves on the plant to curl or wilt equally during hot hours. Nutrient hunger usually causes specific leaves—like the oldest lower leaves—to turn pale yellow or purple while the rest stay upright.
ga: Hɔmɔ haa tso lɛ nɔ baai lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi pɛpɛɛpɛ. kɛfataa he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ haa baai komɛi, tamɔ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ mlɛo. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔŋ loo purple be mli ni baai ni eshwɛ lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ.

english: How should I store my leftover fertilizer at home so it doesn't spoil before the rainy season?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ato shia koni ekafite dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba?

english: Keep fertilizer bags tightly sealed and elevated off cold concrete floors using wooden planks, inside a dry shed. Moisture in the air causes fertilizer to turn into hard rocks or liquid.
ga: Ŋmɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kotoku lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ lɛ nɔ. Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsɔɔ tɛ ni wa loo nu.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my young crops turn yellow early in the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be ni amɛdaraa lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen. Heavy early rains might have washed nutrients deep past small roots, or the soil simply needs an extra feed of fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa leebi lɛ baanyɛ aha niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii atsɔ shishifãi bibii amli. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Does animal manure take longer to feed my crops compared to bag fertilizer?
ga: Ani kooloi aŋmei heɔ be babaoo ni ekɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli lɛ?

english: Yes, animal manure must be broken down slowly by earthworms and soil insects before plants can eat it, releasing nutrients over months, whereas bag fertilizer dissolves in water for immediate feeding.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ akpata ŋmeii ahiɛ fiofio. kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli dani tsei baanyɛ aye amɛ Amɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii yɛ nyɔji babaoo mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kotoku mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baatsɔ nu mli koni ekɛ niyenii aha amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small shoot suckers growing around the base of my main plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajie midumɔwu titri lɛ shishi.

english: Leaving too many small shoots competing with the main plant forces them to share soil nutrients and water. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the main plant to direct its energy into producing a larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: ŋmeii bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ Efa tsɔ ni ekɛ tso wulu lɛ baaye akaŋ. Enɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛja niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves up high into the sunlight to produce the food needed to grow big tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off wet soil, which prevents disease and rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. ni tsiɔ helai kɛ fitemɔ naa lɛ

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential food in the soil. The maize plant takes whatever nitrogen it has from its older bottom leaves and sends it to the top to keep new growth alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Abɛi lɛ heɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni eyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli ni ekɛtsuɔ nii kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ ahi shi.

english: Is it good for my soil if I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Yes, it is very good. Beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally feeds the soil and helps your maize grow bigger without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehi waa. Beans kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eye ebua o-ŋmã lɛ ni edara ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli.

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer so that rain does not wash it all away?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ akashwie fɛɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is damp after a light rain, but not right before a heavy downpour. Covering the fertilizer with a little bit of soil around the root area also keeps rain from washing it off the field.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi esaaa akɛ ofeɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ fioo ha shishifã lɛ he lɛ, no hu yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ shwieɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the shade trees away from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie cacao tsei lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn under full, direct sunlight. Shade trees or plantain crops act as protective umbrellas, keeping the air cool and moist so the young cocoa can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo ni buɔ mɔ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Black pod is a leaf-and-pod disease caused by microscopic fungi that spread in cold, wet weather. Rain droplets splash the disease from infected soil or rotting leaves onto healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Black pod ji baa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ hela ko ni ŋmei bibioo ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ mli loo baai ni egboi lɛ anɔ kɛyaa kookoo tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny whiteflies that suck leaf juice and spread viruses, or by extreme sun heat. The plant curls its leaves to protect itself from losing too much water, but this stops it from making big fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni shwieɔ baai amli nu ni egbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ eshwaa loo kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli Tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ. Shi ekɛ nɔ ko wulu ko baaa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and produce small harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miifee miŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛmiiwo yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. When weeds are left to grow, they steal the plant food, leaving your main crops starved and weak.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ aŋmɛ jwɛi gbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ Ejuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei amli. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii titrii lɛ ni amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready for harvesting without digging up the farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni akuuu mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves dry up and fall off, and small cracks appear in the soil around the base of the stem, showing that the tubers underneath have expanded.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ Ejeɔ kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli. Etsɔɔ akɛ shishigbɛ yitso lɛ mli elɛɛ.

english: Why do my neighbor's crops yield so much more harvest than mine even though we share the exact same soil quality?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe mi nɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ wɔyɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su kome pɛpɛɛpɛ moŋ?

english: Soil quality is only one part of farming success. Yield depends heavily on active field management, including timely weeding, correct plant spacing, proper fertilizer application, and pest control.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji okwaayeli ni yeɔ omanye lɛ fã kome pɛ. Nibii ni anáa lɛ damɔ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ nɔ waa. Nɔ ni fata he ji jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be ni sa mli ni akɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ja ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ fata he

english: If my land is naturally fertile, why is my maize crop still turning yellow and producing small cobs?
ga: Kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni baa nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo ni ewoɔ ŋmɔŋ bibii lɛ?

english: Good soil alone does not guarantee a good harvest. Maize requires careful management, including weeding so weeds do not steal soil nutrients, and applying the right fertilizer at key growth stages.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa pɛ haaa nikpamɔ kpakpa aba. Abɛi biɔ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni fata enɛ he ji jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi lɛ akaju niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa atsu nii yɛ dalɛ bei ni he hiaa lɛ amli

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves but produce tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava puts its energy into leaf growth instead of tuber formation when there is an imbalance of nutrients in the soil or when weeds compete with the plant early in its growth cycle.
ga: Yucca haa hewalɛ kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ moŋ fe ŋmeii lɛ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ bɛ shiŋŋ loo kɛ́ jwɛi kɛ tso lɛ miitswa akaŋ yɛ eshishijee be mli ni edara lɛ.

english: How long can I leave my cassava tubers in the soil after they mature before they spoil?
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, be enyiɛ abaanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: While cassava roots can stay underground for several months, leaving them too long causes them to become woody, lose starch content, and become vulnerable to rot and soil pests.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei shishifãi baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi nyɔji babaoo moŋ, Shi kɛ́ ashi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ tso. Starch falɛ ni laajeɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ oya kɛha fitemɔ kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over before the fruits are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ miigbee shi dani aduawai lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and heavy fruit bunches. Without proper care, such as staking the trees for support and controlling root-damaging pests like nematodes, wind can easily push them over.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ewoɔ aduawai babaoo. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ tsei lɛ ni akɛwoɔ tso mli koni akɛye abua amɛ ni akudɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ shishifãi tamɔ nematodes lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ atswa amɛ oya.

english: How many small shoots should I allow to grow around my main plantain tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maha ŋmeii bibii lɛ akwɛ̃? growing up around Mi dumɔwu titri lɛ tsei enyiɛ yɔɔ?

english: You should limit the shoots to one main plant, one medium sucker, and one small shoot. Allowing too many shoots creates competition for nutrients and results in smaller fruit bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ ato tso titri kome, ŋmeii ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ, kɛ ŋmeii bibii kome he. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baaha akaŋshii aba kɛha niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ebaaha aduawai bibii aba.

english: Why are the leaves of my young pineapple plants turning reddish-yellow instead of bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pineapple baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ-tsuru yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pineapple leaves change color when the plant is stressed by poor soil drainage, extreme sunlight, or a lack of nutrients like nitrogen and iron, which requires active soil conditioning to fix.
ga: Pineapple baai lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ, hulu la ni fa babaoo, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen kɛ iron ni bɛ lɛ hao tso lɛ. Enɛ biɔ ni afee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛo koni akɛtsu naagba lɛ he nii.

english: How long does it normally take for a pineapple plant to produce fruit after I plant it?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani anana tso ko woɔ yibii beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Pineapples grow slowly and typically take between 12 to 18 months to flower and produce a mature fruit, requiring steady weeding and care throughout that period.
ga: Pineapple daa blɛoo ni bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 18 dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii ni egbɔ. Enɛ biɔ ni ajie jwɛi kɛ kwɛmɔ daa yɛ nakai be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Can I plant maize and cassava together on the same plot without ruining the harvest?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mifiteee yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested within three to four months, leaving the field clear for the slower-growing cassava to expand.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Enɛ haa he ko feɔ mlɛo koni ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: What causes the leaves on my young maize plants to get holes and look chewed up?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ bu ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛye?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm. Left unmanaged, these pests destroy the growing tip of the plant and ruin the entire crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ baafite tso lɛ yitsei lɛ ni amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ.

english: Do I need to grow both male and female papaya plants in my farm to get fruits?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni madu papaya tsei hii kɛ yei fɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, many papaya varieties have separate male and female plants. The female plants bear the fruit, but they need pollen transferred from nearby male plants by insects or wind to form healthy papayas.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, papaya henɔi babaoo yɛ tsei ni ji hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. Yoo tso lɛ woɔ yibii. Shi ehe miihia ni amɛná pollen ni kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ jieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei hii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ amli koni amɛfee papaya ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are some of my maize cobs missing kernels or growing half-empty?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ ekomɛi bɛ ŋmeii loo fã ko etee lɛ?

english: Maize cobs need pollen from the tassels at the top of the plant to reach every single silk on the ear. If dry weather, heavy rain, or weak wind disrupts pollination during flowering, those unpollinated spots remain empty.
ga: Abɛi ŋmeii lɛ ahe miihia ni amɛná pollen kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ amli koni amɛshɛ siliki ŋmeii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ toi lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe. Kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ mli egbi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tsiɔ pollination naa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. He ko ni pollin bɛ mli lɛ baakã he ahi shi efolo.

english: Can my watermelon crop produce fruits without insects visiting the flowers?
ga: Ani mi-watermelon tso lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii ni kooloi bibii baasaraa fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: No, watermelon plants have separate male and female flowers on the same vine. Bees and other insects must carry pollen from the male flowers to the female flowers for the fruit to start growing.
ga: Dabi, watermelon tsei yɛ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi yɛ wain tso kome nɔ. Esa akɛ ajie Pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi nuu lɛ mli kɛya fɔfɔi yoo lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni aduawai lɛ aje shishi eda.

english: Why should I remove the extra small shoots growing on my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ

english: Removing those extra shoots, called suckers, prevents the tomato plant from wasting energy on extra leaves. This directs the plant's nutrients into growing larger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmeii Enɛ baatsi tomato tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaŋɔ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni ebaakwɛ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: If many seedlings sprout together in one spot, why is it bad to leave them all to grow?
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome lɛ Mɛni hewɔ ni ahaa fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ehiii?

english: When seeds sprout too close together, they fight for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Removing the weaker seedlings gives the remaining ones enough space and food to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli. Dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui ni eshwɛ lɛ náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why can't I save seeds from my hybrid maize harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn harvest lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred by crossing specific parent plants to give high yields. Seeds saved from that harvest will lose those special qualities, leading to uneven growth and much lower yields in the next season.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ kɛtsɔ fɔlɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni akɛfoɔ mli lɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli baa.

english: How does cassava produce roots when we plant dry sticks instead of seeds?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei shishifãi kwɛ̃ɔ kɛji wɔdu ŋmeii ni egbi yɛ dumɔwui najiaŋ?

english: Cassava stems have hidden growth points called nodes. When buried in moist soil, these nodes use energy stored inside the stick to sprout root systems underground and new leaves above ground.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ yɛ hei ni amɛdaraa yɛ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ nodes. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi kɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: How many days should I wait before my planted maize seeds come out of the soil?
ga: Gbii enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani mi-abele dumɔwui ni midu lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Under warm weather and good soil moisture in Ghana, maize seeds usually germinate and sprout within 4 to 7 days. If nothing emerges after two weeks, the seeds may have dried up or been eaten by soil insects.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana lɛ shishi lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ gbii 4 kɛyashi 7 mli, kɛji nɔ ko bako yɛ otsii enyɔ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ agbi loo koolooi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aye amɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to stress, such as severe heat, lack of water, or applying too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Weeds are naturally adapted to compete aggressively for water, sunlight, and nutrients. Removing them early prevents them from crowding out your crops and taking away the nutrients your crops need to grow.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛye nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkawo onibii amli ni amɛkajie niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ kɛjɛ amɛmli.

english: What are the main steps I should take to prepare my land properly before planting?
ga: Mɛni ji nibii titrii ni esa akɛ mafee koni mikɛsaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani madu nii?

english: Proper land preparation involves clearing existing weeds, loosening the soil so roots can spread easily, and forming beds or ridges to help hold water and nutrients for your crops.
ga: Nɔ ni fata shikpɔŋ he saamɔ kpakpa he ji jwɛi ni yɔɔ momo lɛ ajiemɔ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo ni efee saatsoi loo ŋmeii ni baaye abua ni nu kɛ niyenii ni haa onibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why is it important for me to start clearing my farm early in January before the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mabɔi miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔ yɛ January shishijee gbɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ aje shishi lɛ?

english: Clearing your farm in January gives you enough time to remove weeds, prepare the soil, and allow plant material to rot into natural manure before the early rains begin, making your land ready for planting on time.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie oŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii yɛ January mli lɛ, ehaa onáa be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni okɛjie jwɛi, okɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ, ni oha tsei lɛ amli nibii lɛ afite ni amɛfee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii dani nugbɔ lɛ aba. Ha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee klalo kɛha okwaayeli yɛ be naa.

english: Should I burn the bushes and weeds I clear from my farm during land preparation?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã tsei bibii kɛ jwɛi ni mijie kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ be mli ni misaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Burning cleared weeds can destroy helpful nutrients and moisture in the topsoil; it is often better to clear them and leave them to rot naturally into compost that feeds your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajie lɛ ni ashãa lɛ baanyɛ afite niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojie amɛ ni oha amɛgboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my land is completely ready for me to start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ nii?

english: Your land is ready when the soil has been loosened, weeds have been removed from the planting spots, and the earth is moist enough after the first good rains to support new seeds.
ga: Oshikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwie shi. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ koni ekɛfi dumɔwui heei lɛ asɛɛ.

english: How many times am I supposed to weed my farm throughout the year?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Most crops in Ghana require weeding between 2 to 4 times a season, depending on the rainfall and how quickly wild grass grows back around your plants.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo biɔ ni ajie jwɛi shii 2 kɛyashi 4 yɛ afi mli. Edamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ falɛ kɛ bɔ ni koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya kɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛbɔleɔ otsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ.

english: How exactly do weeds harm my crops if I do not clear them on time?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji mijieee jwɛi lɛ yɛ be naa?

english: Weeds steal vital water, sunlight, and food from the soil that your crops need to stay strong, causing your plants to become thin, yellow, and produce small yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ.

english: What happens to my young crops if I delay weeding during the early part of the season?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ jwɛi lɛ shwiemɔ sɛɛ fo yɛ be lɛ mli mra?

english: Young crops have small roots and easily get choked by fast-growing weeds; delaying early weeding can stunt your crop's growth so much that it may never fully recover.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii, ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ shwieɔ amɛ oya. Tsɔ jwɛi lɛ ashwiemɔ sɛɛ mra. Ebaanyɛ eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akã shi kɛyashɛ he ko ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛtsake kwraa.

english: Is it better to cut weeds close to the ground with a cutlass or dig them out by the roots?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ kakla baafolɔ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ loo akɛbaatsa shishifãi lɛ?

english: Digging out weeds by their roots prevents them from growing back quickly, whereas cutting them at the surface allows them to sprout again fast and compete with your crops.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe koni amɛkakwɛ̃ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, jwɛi ni ooofolɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ ekoŋŋ oya ni amɛkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ.

english: My neighboring farmer weeds his farm three times a season; should I follow his exact routine on my farm?
ga: Mikutsoŋnyo okwaafonyo lɛ shwieɔ jwɛi yɛ eŋmɔ lɛ mli shii etɛ yɛ afi mli. Ani esa akɛ mafee nɔ ni efeɔ daa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should check your own field first, because weed growth depends on your specific crop type, soil moisture, and shade cover rather than just following what another farmer does.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ adalɛ damɔ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo, moŋ fe ni ooonyiɛ nɔ ni okwaafoi krokomɛi feɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why should I update my farming practices instead of relying only on traditional methods used by older generations?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha mi okwaayeli nifeemɔi lɛ aya hiɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ mihe baafɔ blema gbɛi ni yinɔi ni edara lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii lɛ anɔ kɛkɛ?

english: While traditional knowledge is valuable, weather patterns and soil conditions change over time, so adopting updated techniques helps protect your crops against new challenges and increases your total harvest.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ blema nilee he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ moŋ Shi kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛi tsakeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋaai heei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ni oootsu nii lɛ baabu onibii ahe kɛjɛ naagbai heei ahe, ni ebaaha onibii fɛɛ ni obaaná lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are only a few of my cocoa trees showing yellow leaves while the rest of the field looks green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei fioo komɛi pɛ yɔɔ baai ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔji ni eyɛ hewalɛ.

english: Just like people, individual plants catch diseases or suffer pest attacks at different times. A few yellow trees mean those specific plants are struggling with nutrient loss or pests early, while their neighbors are still strong.
ga: same as humans Tsei srɔtoi baanyɛ aná hela loo tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ atutua amɛ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Tsei fioo komɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nakai tsei pɔtɛɛ lɛ miiwuu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fiteɔ mra loo tsɛŋemɔ helai. yɛ be mli ni akutsoŋbii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛhe wa

english: Do I need to spray pest medicine over my entire maize field if I only see insects on a few plants?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ kɛji mina kooloi bibii yɛ tsei fioo komɛi pɛ amli?

english: No, you should only treat the specific plants that are affected. Spraying the whole field when only a few crops are sick wastes money and can destroy the good insects that help protect your farm.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ otsa tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ pɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa shwie ŋmɔ muu fɛɛ nɔ beni tsei fioo komɛi pɛ hela mɔ amɛ lɛ, eheɔ shika, ni ebaanyɛ efite kooloi bibii kpakpai. ni baanyɛ aye abua ni abu oŋmɔ lɛ he

english: How can I tell if a plant is sick and actually needs medicine?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tso ko hela mɔ lɛ ni tsofa he miihia lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Look out for warning signs on individual plants like spotted leaves, unusual yellowing, stunted growth, or sudden wilting. These symptoms show that the plant's health is failing and targeted treatment is needed.
ga: Kwɛmɔ kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii yɛ tsei aŋkroaŋkroi anɔ, tamɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. stunted growth loo sudden withering Okadii nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni atsa lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some cassava plants get leaf spots while the ones right next to them stay healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei tsei komɛi yɛ baai ahe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ hu yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Ani oyɛ hewalɛ lolo?

english: Fungal and bacterial infections often start on a single vulnerable plant. The spotted plant caught the infection first, while the neighboring plant may have stronger natural resistance or hasn't been exposed yet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ bacteria mli baa lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tso kome ni bɛ hewalɛ nɔ. Tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baaná hela lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ baanyɛ aná adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ babaoo loo ajieee amɛ kpo lolo.

english: Can a disease on one sick plant spread to the rest of my healthy crops if I do not treat it?
ga: Ani hela ko ni yɔɔ tso kome ni hela mɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã miŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ? Kɛji mikɛtsaaa lɛ?

english: Yes, insects, wind, rain splash, and farm tools can easily carry diseases from one sick plant to healthy ones, which is why treating or removing the few infected plants early is so important.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi bibii, kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa. Ni ŋmɔ mli nibii baanyɛ ajie hela kɛjɛ tso kome ni hela mɔ lɛ mli kɛya tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ oya. Enɛ hewɔ ni tsei fioo komɛi ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ atsaa amɛ loo ajieɔ amɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia waa.

english: Should I give chemical treatment to healthy crops as a precaution, or only to the sick ones?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maha tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsofai akɛ nɔ ko ni mikɛbaakwɛ mihe nɔ? Aloo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ pɛ?

english: You should generally reserve medicine for the crops that show clear signs of needing it. Healthy plants do not require medicine, and applying chemicals unnecessarily can stress the plant and increase your expenses.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ tsofa ato kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsɔɔ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ tsofa he miihia lɛ. Tsofa he ehiaaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Ni tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni he ehiaaa lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ aná haomɔ ni eha shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do some tomato plants in my farm wilt while others right beside them look fine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi miigbo yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmasɛi lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting on individual plants is usually caused by soil pests or root rot affecting that specific plant's roots, preventing it from drinking water even if the surrounding soil is wet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ ni saa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ji nɔ ni haa tsei aŋkroaŋkroi lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa, ni no haaa enyɛ enu nu kɛji shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: What should I do immediately when I notice pests on just four or five of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ mina kooloi ni fiteɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsei ejwɛ loo enumɔ pɛ nɔ?

english: Focus your attention directly on those four or five plants by applying the right pest treatment to them immediately before the insects can multiply and spread across your whole farm.
ga: Kɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama nakai tsei ejwɛ loo enumɔ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔ tsofa ni sa ni akɛgbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe lɛ ni oookɛtsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Dani kooloi bibii lɛ baafa babaoo ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ,.

english: Why do crops planted on the same piece of land at the same time react differently to illnesses?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli No hewɔ lɛ amɛyɛ bɔ ni amɛfeɔ amɛnii amɛhaa yɛ hela he lɛ srɔtoi?

english: Each plant experiences slightly different soil conditions, sun exposure, and insect contact. Some individual plants are naturally weaker or under more stress, making them fall ill before others.
ga: Tso henɔ fɛɛ tso henɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ, hulu la kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe shihilɛi ni yɔɔ srɔto fioo. Tsei komɛi yɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛhe feɔ oya loo amɛhaoɔ amɛhe waa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji hela ni mɔɔ mɔ dani henɔi krokomɛi baa.

english: Is crop medicine safe to use on weak plants to help them recover?
ga: Ani tso tsofa yɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛbaatsu nii yɛ tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ anɔ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhe ewa amɛ?

english: Yes, when used correctly according to instructions, specific plant medicines like fungicides, insecticides, or micro-nutrients help weak or infected plants recover their strength and grow normally again.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi anaa. Tsofai komɛi ni akɛgbeɔ tsei, tamɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii, loo niyenii bibii Ebaaye ebua tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ loo hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa.

english: Can I grow other crops directly under my cocoa trees without harming them?
ga: Mibaanyɛ makwɛ tsei krokomɛi. Ani abaanyɛ akɛwo kookoo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ ni eyeee lɛ awui?

english: Yes, certain shade-tolerant crops like cocoyam, ginger, and some shade vegetables can grow under cocoa trees. They benefit from the moist, cool environment created by the cocoa canopy without taking away vital nutrients from the trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ adu tsei komɛi ni nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli tamɔ kookoo, ŋmei, kɛ aduawai komɛi ni sumɔɔ hulutsoo be yɛ kookoo tsei ashishi. Amɛnáa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli ni kookoo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ feɔ lɛ he sɛɛ ni amɛjieee niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do some wild plants grow on their own under my cocoa trees, and are they useful?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli tsei komɛi diɛŋtsɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi cacao tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ?

english: Many wild plants thrive under cocoa because of the rich, shaded soil. Some of these plants are actually valuable traditional herbs, spices, or secondary crops that help hold soil moisture and can be harvested for food or extra income.
ga: Koo mli tsei babaoo yeɔ omanye yɛ kookoo shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ ekomɛi ji blema tsofai ni jara wa, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ niyenii mli loo saatso tsei ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni abaanyɛ akpa kɛha niyenii loo shika kroko ni akɛfataa he.

english: Why do some crops need deep shade from big trees while others die without full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ahe hiaa ni tsei wuji aná hulutsoo yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi gboiɔ ni amɛnáaa hulu la ni yeɔ emuu lɛ?

english: Crops have different light requirements to produce food. Shade-tolerant crops thrive under big trees because direct sunlight burns their leaves, while light-loving crops need full sunshine to grow strong and yield fruits.
ga: Tsei yɛ la srɔtoi ni he hiaa kɛha niyenii feemɔ. Tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hulutsoo shi lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ tsei wuji ashishi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai lɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni sumɔɔ la lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: What is a simple way to store my harvested crops directly on the farm without expensive equipment?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ toɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni akɛ nibii ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: Storing harvested crops under the cool, shaded canopy of big trees on your farm helps reduce heat and moisture loss, keeping produce fresh for longer until you are ready to transport or sell it.
ga: Kɛ́ oha okpamɔ nii lɛ mli jɔ yɛ tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaha dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni obaafee klalo akɛ okɛbaatsu nii loo obaahɔ̃ɔ.

english: How can I prevent my fresh farm produce from spoiling quickly after harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi miŋmɔ mli nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite oya yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: To prevent quick spoilage, keep harvested crops away from direct sunlight, place them on clean elevated racks or mats off the bare ground, and keep them in a cool, well-ventilated farm area.
ga: Bɔni afee ni akafite oya Ha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ akashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Okɛwo adeka loo tsɔne ni awo nɔ ni he tse nɔ yɛ kpo nɔ yɛ he ko ni gbɛ yɔɔ. ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli he ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli.

english: Why should I consider processing my raw farm produce instead of selling it fresh?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu ŋmɔ mli nibii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ahe nitsumɔ he moŋ fe ni mahɔ̃ɔ amɛ ehee lɛ?

english: Processing raw crops into products like flour, chips, or paste extends their shelf life, prevents post-harvest loss, and allows you to sell to specialized buyers at a much higher price.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ ni afee nibii tamɔ ashikishaŋ, chips loo paste yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Tsi nibii ni laajeɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ naa. Ni ehaa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ ohaa mɛi krɛdɛɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ kwraa nɔ.

english: How do I know if the crops I grow can be turned into other products by processors?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ tsɔne ko ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ nɔ etsɔ nɔ kroko?

english: Crops rich in starch, oil, or strong flavors—such as cassava, maize, oil palm, and ginger—are commonly bought by processors because they are easily converted into everyday consumer goods like cooking oil, packaged flour, or snacks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mɛi ni feɔ nibii nɛɛ aheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni starch, fɔ loo tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ waa, tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa fɔ kɛ ŋmãa yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ ji akɛ, abaanyɛ atsake amɛ afee daa gbi nibii tamɔ fɔ ni akɛhooɔ nii, ashikishaŋ ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli loo niyenii ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ mlɛo.

english: How can growing extra food crops alongside my cocoa help my family financially?
ga: Bɔ ni niyenii krɛdɛɛi ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua wekui yɛ shika gbɛfaŋ lɛ.

english: Growing secondary food crops gives you food for household consumption and regular cash flow throughout the year, especially during the months when cocoa is not in peak harvest season.
ga: Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ ni oduɔ lɛ haa onáa niyenii kɛha oshiabii lɛ kɛ shika ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri yɛ nyɔji ni kookoo bɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Who can I sell my extra farm produce to besides the open market women?
ga: Namɔ manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ miŋmɔ mli nibii lɛ maha lɛ? Kɛ ajie yei ni yɔɔ jarayelihe ni agbele naa lɛ?

english: You can sell directly to local cottage processors, school feeding programs, restaurant owners, or commercial crop aggregators who buy in bulk to supply larger factories.
ga: Obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ oha mɛi ni feɔ kratom yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Skul niyeli nitsumɔ niyelihe nuŋtsɔ loo jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsulɔi ni heɔ babaoo koni amɛkɛ nitsumɔhei wuji lɛ aha.

english: Why are extension officers encouraging us to change old ways of managing crops under trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ tsakemɔ ni afeɔ yɛ blema gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ tsei ashishi lɛ he hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Modern agricultural practices show that properly planning what grows beneath main cash trees improves soil fertility, prevents pest outbreaks, and maximizes total earnings from the same piece of land.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli nifeemɔi tsɔɔ akɛ gbɛjianɔtoo kpakpa ni kɔɔ nɔ ni abaadu yɛ shika tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ. Tsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ anaa ni oha shika fɛɛ ni anáa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak root systems that dry out quickly under direct hot sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantain or cassava provides shelter and keeps the soil cool until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall bushes and put stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ amli ni mikɛ tsei awo sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food for the growing tuber under the ground. Staking holds the leaves high off the ground where they get maximum sun and stay safe from heat and soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ yaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ fe fɛɛ yɛ lɛ, ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ helai ahe.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize crops turning yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnaa kɛbashi shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, an essential nutrient the crop needs to grow green and strong. Adding fertilizer or animal manure restores this nutrient.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii nɛɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there are no insects around to shake and pollinate the flowers so they can turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii bɛ he ni amɛbaakpokpo ni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: What causes these small caterpillars to chew holes in the middle of my young corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ shwieɔ bu yɛ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Those caterpillars are known as Fall Armyworms. Night-flying moths lay eggs on young corn leaves, and when the eggs hatch, the caterpillars feed on the soft growing center of the plant before it flowers.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ Fall Armyworms. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni foɔ gbɛkɛ nɛɛ fɔɔ amɛwɔlɔi yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii anɔ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ bibii ni miida lɛ dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground if I leave them too long past harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cassava roots store starch and water, but if left in wet soil during heavy rains after they fully mature, soil bacteria and fungi enter through tiny cracks and cause soft rotting.
ga: Cassava shishifãi kɛ starch kɛ nu toɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli beni amɛdara sɛɛ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ nɔ helai kɛ ŋmeii naa gbɛ kɛboteɔ ŋmeii bibii amli. ni eha egbo

english: Is it helpful to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ makwɛ tsina loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Yes, because legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants die, that nitrogen feeds the soil and helps the maize grow bigger.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni edara.

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots to anchor them, and heavy fruit bunches make them top-heavy. Supporting them with strong wooden or bamboo props helps hold them up until harvest.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baaha amɛfee ekome. kɛ aduawai akuu ni tsii Ebaaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ babaoo. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni wa fi amɛsɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhi shi kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds sprout and grow much faster than my crops right after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds live in the soil for years and are naturally adapted to absorb water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crop seeds, allowing them to germinate rapidly.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ. Ehaa dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ oya

english: When is the right time to put fertilizer around my crops so the rain does not carry it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni nugbɔ akashwie amɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already damp after a light rain, but not during heavy downpours. Covering the fertilizer with a little bit of soil keeps it in place so the roots can absorb it.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ fioo ko ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛŋɔɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves burn easily and the soil dries out too fast. They need temporary shade from fast-growing plants like plantains or shade trees to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu gbɛ́ɔ oya tsɔ. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crops turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong leaves, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients deep away from the plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ tsei shishifãi amli.

english: What is causing holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the center shoot?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa? Minɔ lɛ yɛ teŋgbɛ tso lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which eat the soft inner leaves of the maize plant during the night or cool hours, weakening the stalk if not treated early.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei amli baai bibii lɛ gbɛkɛ loo gbɛkɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishi lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Does it matter which direction the stem buds point when I plant cassava cuttings?
ga: Kɛ́ midu ŋmei lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ niji lɛ baatsɔɔ?

english: Yes, cassava cuttings must be planted with the raised stem buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the new shoots to turn around underground, leading to weak growth and very few tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii heei ashishifãi aba shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ baa.

english: Why do some of my seed yams rot in the mound before they even sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ ekomɛi miifite yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃ po lɛ?

english: Seed yams rot when the soil becomes too waterlogged, or when small cuts on the yam seed allow fungi and bacteria from the wet earth to enter and decay the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni pilamɔ bibioo ko Yɛ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny suckling insects like aphids, thrips, or mites, which feed on the sap and spread plant viruses that stunt leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ, tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites, ni yeɔ nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tso mli helai ni tsiɔ baa lɛ dalɛ naa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are extremely hot, when the soil lacks moisture during flowering, or when insects damage the blossoms before pollination happens.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli loo be mli ni kooloi bibii fiteɔ fɔfɔii lɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo amɛmli.

english: Why do crops grow tall and skinny with very few fruits when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei hiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, they compete for sunlight, soil food, and water. Instead of using energy to grow big fruits, they stretch upward quickly just to reach the light.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛdu aduawai wuji. Mohu ɔ, e ngɔ e he kɛ ya he oya konɛ e ya su kane ɔ he.

english: Why does my land give me a smaller yield every time I plant maize on the same field year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop loves most and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni tsei sumɔɔ waa lɛ pɛ. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How does planting cowpea or groundnuts help make my soil better for the next season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha be ni baa lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legume plants like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the soil as free food for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi bibii amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct, harsh sunlight dries up their leaves and burns them. Leaving some tall shade trees or planting plantains around them protects the seedlings until they grow strong enough to bear direct heat.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbi ni eshã baai lɛ. tsei kakadaji ni ajieɔ lɛ Ha hulutsoo loo dumɔ dumɔwui ebɔle he. Enɛ baaye abua ni abu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Planting seeds too close forces the crops to compete aggressively for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin, weak stalks with very small or missing corn cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ woɔ akaŋshii ni mli wa mli kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa, ni ŋmãa ŋmeii bibii waa loo amɛbɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants curling up tightly during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up as a defense mechanism to reduce water loss through evaporation during hot weather. It is a sign that the soil is getting dry and the plants are trying to conserve moisture.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa. Eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miibɔi gbimɔ ni tso lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekwɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds at the beginning of the rainy season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Wait until the rains become steady for a week or two so the soil holds deep moisture. Sowing after just one light rain can cause seeds to germinate and then dry out if a dry spell follows.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ be fɛɛ be otsi kome loo enyɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why should I not plant cassava on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Cassava absorbs a large amount of nutrients from the soil. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot exhausts the ground, leading to depleted soil, lower yields, and smaller tubers over time.
ga: Cassava ŋmɛɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli, ni kɛ́ adu lɛ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ mli agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, yibiiwoo baa shi, ni ŋmeii bibii hu baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do agricultural officers recommend planting cowpeas or groundnuts before my cereal crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii dani adu miŋmaa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the field, they naturally fertilize the soil, helping crops like maize or sorghum grow better in the next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: What causes the green pods on my cocoa trees to turn black and rot before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛshwereɔ?

english: This rot is caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod disease, which thrives in overly wet, shady, and humid conditions. Pruning excess branches to let air and sunlight in helps stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod hela kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Eshwereɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, hulutsoo, kɛ hulutsoo be fe nine. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la abote mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my tomato plants develop dark, sunken spots on the bottom of the fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji ni egbo yɛ aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit while it is growing, often triggered by irregular watering. Keeping the soil moisture steady helps the plant absorb calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli beni edaa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very bushy with dark green leaves but produce very few flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa shi ewoɔ fɔfɔi fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to spend all its energy growing leaves and stems instead of setting flowers and fruits. Switching to a fertilizer rich in phosphorus encourages blooming and fruit production.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai kɛ amɛshishifãi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofee fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai lɛ, Tsakemɔ kɛmiiya fɔsfɔs ni fa babaoo mli lɛ baaha fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai aba.

english: Why do weeds harm my cassava crop so much even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ awui waa eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young cassava plants and steal essential sunlight, space, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds within the first three months allows the cassava to build strong root systems for large tubers.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmei tsei bibii. ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, ŋwɛi, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ aná shishifãi ni mli wa kɛha ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are my crop leaves burning and turning brown after I sprayed them with pest medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ efɔ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf burning often happens when you apply fake, expired, or improperly mixed chemicals. Genuine crop medicines protect the leaves, but fake or overly strong chemicals shock the plant tissue, causing the leaves to dry out and burn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ baa shãa kɛji okɛ tsofai ni ji amale, ni efite, loo ni akɛfutu mli jogbaŋŋ tsu nii. Tsofa diɛŋtsɛ buɔ baai lɛ ahe. Shi tsofai ni ji amale loo ni mli wa tsɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ ahe feɔ shoo. Ehaa baai lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛshãa.

english: Why are insects still destroying my maize even after I sprayed them with crop medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsei ahe tsofa shwieɔ nɔ moŋ?

english: Pests continue feeding if the chemical you used was counterfeit, diluted, or ineffective. Fake crop medicines lack the active ingredients needed to kill pests, leaving your maize unprotected despite your effort.
ga: Tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baaya nɔ aye bo kɛji tsofai ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ji amalei, ni akɛwo mli, loo amɛtsuuu nii. Tsofai ni akɛfee amalei lɛ bɛ nibii ni tsuɔ nii ni he hiaa koni akɛgbe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ. Enɛ haa o-corn lɛ bɛ hebuu kɛji oka po.

english: Why do my pepper plants look weak and wilted after I spray them in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbo beni mikɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Spraying crop medicine during intense sunlight causes the leaves to absorb the chemical too quickly while losing water. This causes heat stress and leaf wilting. It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the evening.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ fɔ tsei anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ aŋɔ tsofa lɛ oya tsɔ ni nu lɛ hu baaje mli. Enɛ haa hulutsoo he haomɔ baa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie nɔ lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ.

english: What causes my crops to get damaged when I buy chemicals from uncertified roadside sellers?
ga: Mɛni kɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fitemɔ baa kɛ́ mihe tsofai kɛjɛ gbɛjegbɛ nɔ nihɔɔlɔ ko ni bɛ hegbɛ lɛ dɛŋ?

english: Uncertified dealers often sell fake or improperly stored products that have broken down into toxic compounds. These bad chemical mixtures burn crop leaves, stunt growth, and can ruin your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mɛi ni hɔ̃ɔ nibii ni bɛ hegbɛ lɛ hɔ̃ɔ nibii ni ji amalei loo nibii ni akɛtoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ, ni fiteɔ ni etsɔɔ nibii ni yɔɔ gbeyei. Tsofai gbohii nɛɛ baaha tso baai lɛ ashã. dalɛ lɛ kpaa ni ebaanyɛ efite nibii ni ofeɔ lɛ.

english: How do crop medicines actually protect my plants from getting sick?
ga: Te tsei ahe tsofa baanyɛ abu mitsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hela he aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Genuine crop medicines act like a shield or vaccine. Fungicides prevent fungal spores from penetrating plant leaves, while insecticides kill or repel bugs that bite the crop and transmit diseases.
ga: Tsofa ni akɛduɔ nii diɛŋtsɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gãimlibii loo tsofa ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he. Tsofai ni gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkabote tsei ahe baai amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ gbeɔ loo amɛshwieɔ kooloi ni ŋmɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛgbɛɔ helai amɛshwãa lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black even after I apply spray on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa shwie nɔ moŋ?

english: If spraying does not stop black pod disease, the medicine might be fake, applied too late after the infection took root, or washed away by rain before the plant could absorb it.
ga: Kɛji tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsĩ black pod hela lɛ naa lɛ Tsofa lɛ baanyɛ afee amale. Okɛwo mli sɛɛ tsɔ beni hela lɛ etswa shishifãi sɛɛ. loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa dani tsei baanyɛ aŋɔ

english: Why do my tomato plants wither and die so quickly when attacked by diseases?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ oya kɛji hela mɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Diseases like bacterial wilt attack the water channels inside the tomato stem. Once blocked, water cannot travel from the roots to the leaves, causing the entire plant to collapse and die very fast.
ga: Helai tamɔ bacteria wilt lɛ tutuaa nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ. kɛji akɛ atsĩ naa Nu lɛ nyɛŋ ajɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛya baai lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ oya.

english: How can I know if a plant medicine is safe to use on my food crops before spraying?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso tsofa ko yɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ mi niyenii tsei lɛ anɔ dani mikɛshwie nɔ?

english: Safe crop medicines are bought from licensed dealers who issue official receipts. Genuine products have clear labels specifying the correct dosage, target pests, and the exact waiting period required before harvesting the crop safely.
ga: Aheɔ tsei ahe tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni kɛ maŋ lɛ he wolo haa lɛ adɛŋ. Nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ yɛ woji ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ bɔ ni esa akɛ akɛ tsofa lɛ atsu nii aha. Target pests kɛ be pɔtɛɛ ni akɛbaamɛ dani abaanyɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do weeds come back so fast on my farm even when I use weedkiller spray?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiku amɛsɛɛ amɛba oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ tsu nii moŋ.

english: Weeds return quickly if the weedkiller was diluted or counterfeit, or if it was a contact spray that only killed the top leaves without destroying the underground root system.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba oya kɛji akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ mli ewo nu mli loo eji amale. Aloo kɛji akɛ eji tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni gbeɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ ni efiteee shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ.

english: What should I do if a crop chemical I bought causes my cassava leaves to drop off?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni mihe lɛ ha ŋmãa baa lɛ shwie shi?

english: Sudden leaf loss is a reaction to severe chemical toxicity, usually caused by fake or wrong pesticides. Stop using the product immediately, wash the plants with clean water if possible, and bring your receipt and bottle to an extension officer for help.
ga: Baai ni laajeɔ trukaa lɛ ji nɔ ko ni jɛɔ tsofai fɔji ni naa wa mli baa. Bei pii lɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi amalei loo ejaaa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kpa nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛji ebaahi lɛ, okɛ nu ni mli tse afɔ tso lɛ he. ni okɛ resiiti lɛ kɛ tɔ lɛ aya sɛɛgbɛ nitsulɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ koni eye ebua bo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil. Adding fertilizer such as NPK or applying well-rotted animal manure gives the leaves energy to turn dark green and produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK fata he loo akɛ kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop pests build up in the field. Rotating with legumes like beans or groundnuts naturally rebuilds soil health and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ Ejɛɔ adebɔɔ mli etswaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli.

english: How do crops like groundnuts and cowpeas make my soil richer for the next farming season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha okwaayeli be ni baa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small bumps on their roots. When the crop is harvested, those root nodules melt into the ground and leave free plant food for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ amli. Nakai shishifãi ni etse lɛ baatsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛshi tsei niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines onto tall wooden sticks after they start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ fĩɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko he beni ebɔi shweremɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to generate food and build big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves high off the muddy ground, preventing leaf rot and ensuring maximum sunlight reaches the plant.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ hiɔ sũ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa baai lɛ agbo, ni ehaa hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ shɛɔ tso lɛ he.

english: Why do farmers in my area plant plantain suckers right beside young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ duɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense tropical sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shading the tender cocoa plants and keeping the ground moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Okɛ ŋmɔlɔ awo koko tso ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ nɔ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Does it matter which way I push cassava stem cuttings into the soil during planting?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ matsɔ nɔ matsi ŋmei niji awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, always plant cassava cuttings upright or slanted with the leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the stems waste all their energy trying to turn around, resulting in very small or weak tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ adu yucca niji lɛ shi ja loo atsɔ ŋwɛi ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Tso lɛ fiteɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Enɛ haa yitsei lɛ feɔ bibii waa loo amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: My tomato plants produce plenty of yellow flowers, but the flowers keep dropping off without growing tomatoes. What is causing this?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo. Shi fɔfɔi lɛ baaya nɔ agbee shi. ni aduuu tomato Mɛni kɛ enɛ ba?

english: Tomatoes shed their blossoms when high heat or irregular watering stresses the plant. When it gets too hot, the plant sheds flowers to conserve water and survive, so keeping the soil consistently moist during hot spells helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni eyaaa nɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto nu ni amɛhi shi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How can I keep my garden soil from drying out so quickly during the dry season in northern Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ akagbi oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ?
