english: Covering the bare ground around your plants with a thick layer of dry grass, straw, or maize stalks—a method called mulching—blocks direct heat from the sun, keeps the soil cool, and prevents water from evaporating into the air.
ga: Akɛ jwɛi, jwɛi, loo abele tsei aha hei ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe. Ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsi dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli

english: What are these tiny worms eating ragged holes inside the central whorl of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Those worms are Fall Armyworms, a destructive pest that attacks young cereal leaves. You can protect your crop by applying approved botanical sprays like neem leaf extract or targeted pesticides directly into the funnel leaf of the plant early in the morning.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii ni tutuaa ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ baai ni ji cone lɛ amli leebi

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants shrinking and curling upward into small tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies attacking the underside of young leaves, or by a virus carried by these insects. Spraying the leaves with a mild soapy water solution or neem oil helps knock down the pest population.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni tutuaa baai bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ Loo neem fɔ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ aba shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings struggle and burn when I clear all the shade trees from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa beni mijieɔ cacao lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle intense direct sunlight. They need partial shade from fast-growing trees or plantains to protect their sensitive leaves from scorching and to keep the soil cool and moist around their roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ tsei loo plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛkɛbu amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he. kɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do many of my cocoa flowers drop off without turning into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop if the plant lacks enough nutrients, if the weather is too dry, or if there are not enough tiny midges (pollinating insects) around. Keeping soil moist and properly nourished helps the tree convert flowers into pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo eyɛ bibii (Pollinators) lɛ faaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni sa ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsakeɔ fɔfɔi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the young leaves and stems on my cocoa trees drying up and looking scorched?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii kɛ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ egbi ni etamɔ nɔ ni shãa lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by tiny insects called capsids or 'akate' that suck sap from new shoots, leaving dark burnt marks. Protecting young branches from capsids keeps the foliage healthy and growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Atsɛɔ lɛ capsid loo ‘akate’ ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei heei amli lɛ. Eshiɔ shãa he okadi ni tsuɔ waa. Niji bibii ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ capsids he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Maize rolls its leaves when the weather gets hot and dry to protect itself from losing water. Reducing the leaf surface exposed to direct sunlight helps the crop hold onto moisture until conditions cool down.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nu ni elaaje lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie baa lɛ nɔ ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot much faster during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a water-loving fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, shady conditions. Pruning extra leaves and branches lets air and sunlight reach the pods, which dries them out and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni sumɔɔ nu ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Kɛ́ afolɔ baai kɛ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why does placing dry leaves and farm waste around the base of my crops help them stay alive during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni egboi kɛ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around plants with dry organic matter, called mulching, prevents moisture from evaporating into the warm air. It keeps the soil cool and damp, giving crop roots a steady water supply when rain is scarce.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi shwieɔ Tsei ahe Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekatsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ashishifãi ni amɛnáa nu be fɛɛ be kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with lots of big leaves, but producing small underground tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, cassava spends all its energy producing top foliage instead of root storage. A balanced fertilizer encourages the plant to direct its energy into expanding tubers underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei kɛ shishifãi baato lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋwɛi baai lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni ja lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛwo bulbs yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my crop plants turning pale yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves available nutrients from older leaves to feed new upper growth, causing old leaves to fade.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen faaa Tsei lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baai momoi ni shwieɔ shi.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my farm so it doesn't go to waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii koni mikafite nii?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist early in the rainy season, but not during heavy downpours. Fertilizer needs damp soil for roots to absorb it, but torrential rains can wash away the nutrients before the plant gets a chance to feed.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ dani tsei lɛ ana niyenii.

english: Why do weeds make my food crops grow slowly and look yellowish if I leave them in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ daa blɛoo ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients faster than your crops can absorb them. Clearing weeds early leaves all the water and nourishment for your main crops to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaashi nu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni otso titri lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa seedlings the needed shade and humidity to survive their early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize plants usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen gives plants their healthy green color and helps leaves grow, so applying compost or nitrogen fertilizer restores vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛdaraa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my bean plants produce plenty of leafy foliage but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ woɔ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes bean plants to invest energy into leaves instead of flowers. Reducing nitrogen and applying phosphorus-rich fertilizers encourages flowering and pod development.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo woɔ baai amli moŋ fe fɔfɔii. Nitrogen ni abaaba shi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ.

english: Why does my plantain sucker take so long to yield fruit when planted in old, exhausted land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain sucker lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ momo ni egbɔjɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Depleted soil lacks organic nutrients needed for healthy root formation. Plantains require rich, nutrient-dense soil to build strong underground stems capable of producing heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ he miihia plantains koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni wa ni baanyɛ awo yibii ni tsii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the soil when there is continuous heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni nugbɔ ni naa wa miinɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Excess water fills up soil pockets and deprives root tubers of oxygen. Without airflow, naturally occurring soil fungi and bacteria multiply quickly, causing the cassava tubers to decay underground.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ sũ lɛ mli obɔ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ náa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ni tsɔɔ mli lɛ Adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ faa oya. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants droop during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When sunlight is intense, leaves lose water faster than roots can absorb it. Drooping is a temporary self-defense mechanism to reduce moisture loss; plants usually recover once temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Kɛ hulu la lɛ mli wa lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Drooping ji be kukuoo mli hebuu gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ shi. Bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ he baajɔ amɛ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do dark spots spread over my cocoa pods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ kookoo ŋmeii anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Dark spots are caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that thrives in humid, wet weather. Pruning extra branches allows sunlight and air to flow through, drying off pods and preventing fungal growth.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ mli egbiɔ, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my chili pepper plants curling up and twisting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on leaf sap. Applying natural insecticidal soaps or neem oil controls these pests and protects new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ adebɔɔ mli samla loo neem fɔ ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaakudɔ kooloi nɛɛ ni ebaatsi baai heei ni baa lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms drop off the stem before turning into small tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani amɛmiitsɔ tomato bibii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat or sudden dry spells stress tomato plants, preventing successful pollination. When flowers fail to pollinate, the plant drops them to conserve energy and water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. ni ehaa pollination lɛ yeee omanye. Beni anyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔii lɛ pollen lɛ Ashwieɔ tsei koni akɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: Why do my cabbage heads remain soft and open instead of wrapping into hard balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitso lɛ hiɔ shi blɛoo ni egbeleɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa baawo mli lɛ?

english: Cabbages require steady moisture and cool weather to form tightly wrapped heads. Irregular watering or extreme hot weather forces the leaves to grow loose and spread out.
ga: Cabbage he miihia ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ daa koni ekɛha eyitsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baaha baai lɛ agbo ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant many seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo feɔ ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds grow in one spot, the plants are like children competing for a single bowl of food. They stretch upward fighting for sunlight and starve each other of soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and small yields.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome Tsei tamɔ gbekɛbii. niyenii he akaŋ yɛ tsɛnsi kome mli Amɛkpãa amɛhe, amɛwuɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni hɔmɔ yeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or beans together with my maize will help my soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ du ŋmei loo ŋmei lɛ, ebaaye ebua mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans are generous crops that pull nitrogen out of the air and feed it into the earth through their roots, acting like natural fertilizer for neighboring maize plants.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ji tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli eboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yam harvests when I plant yam on the exact same spot three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ baa kɛji midu yɛ he kome afii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that plant needs while giving soil diseases a permanent home. Rotating crops allows the soil to rest and rebuild its strength.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni ejie niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ feɔ shia ni hiɔ shi daa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe ni ehaa ehewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I place my fertilizer right at the base of my crop stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tsei ashishifãi lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Concentrated fertilizer directly touching a stem acts like hot water on skin and can burn the plant. Placing it a few inches away lets the roots reach out safely to drink the nutrients without damaging the stem.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nu ni mli edɔ yɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ. ni ekɛ tso lɛ shãa Kɛ́ okɛto he ko ni kɛ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe ni amɛnu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni efiteee tso lɛ shishifã lɛ.

english: Why is it important to weed around my young seedlings early before the weeds grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Mi dumɔwui kɛjɛ shishijee Ehe miihia dani jwɛi lɛ adara.

english: Young crop seedlings are delicate and easily overpowered. Early weeds steal water, light, and soil food before your crop is strong enough to defend itself.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛtswaa amɛ oya. Jwɛi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ juɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛbu amɛhe

english: Why should I trim off extra side branches from my tomato plants when they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ be mli ni amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ?

english: Extra branches consume food that the plant needs for making fruit. Trimming unnecessary foliage directs the plant's energy straight into producing larger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Niji ni fata he lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ewo yibii. Baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ koni ekɛwo tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable crops with dry palm leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Aduawai ni yɔɔ ŋmei baai loo jwɛi ni egbi?

english: Dry leaves act like a blanket over the soil, keeping the intense sun heat from drying out the ground, conserving moisture, and stopping weeds from taking root.
ga: Baai ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ha hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo shishifãi.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and droop in the middle of the hot afternoon even when the ground is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Plants sweat moisture through their leaves during intense heat. Curling their leaves reduces exposure to the harsh sun, helping the plant hold onto its water until the evening cool arrives.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ latsaa kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants sometimes produce big bushy leaves above ground but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ mi yucca tso lɛ hiɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or excessive shade, it spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo nɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni edaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato bulb ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa the shade and soil moisture it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to build green leaves and grow strong. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods to save water. It is a natural survival mechanism that prevents the plant from drying out while the tubers continue to stay safe underground.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Eji adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekagbi yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crops very close together to get more food from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to feed well and produce larger harvests.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha niyenii kpakpa kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my pepper plants before any peppers grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei anɔ dani ŋmɔtɔ lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress from high heat, lack of water, or poor pollination. Keeping the soil moist and encouraging beneficial insects like bees helps the flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmeii ni ehiii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni awo kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe hewalɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant maize on the same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same land drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows maize-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like cowpeas restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: How do weeds harm my crops even after I have applied fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and will steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight intended for your crops. Removing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. ni ebaaju ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Why do insects attack my crops more heavily during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Warmth and high moisture during the rainy season create ideal conditions for insects to lay eggs and hatch quickly, while fresh green crop leaves provide abundant food for them.
ga: Dɔlɛ kɛ latsaa ni fa babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa kooloi fɔɔ wɔji ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ oya. yɛ be mli ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ji niyenii babaoo jɛɛhe.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous harvest yield less than new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mikpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred for high yields, uniform growth, and disease resistance. Seeds saved from past harvests lose these strong traits over time and can carry diseases from the previous season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. uniform growth and disease resistance Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ sui nɛɛ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ aba.

english: How can I tell when my yams are fully mature and ready to dig up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ mafo?

english: Yams signal that they are mature when their green leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up, showing that the plant has finished sending all its energy down into the tuber.
ga: Atomɔ tsɔɔ amɛdalɛ be mli ni baai eŋɔli kɛ wain tsei lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaa shi kɛyaa bulb lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: How do yield-boosting chemicals actually help my cocoa pods grow bigger and heavier?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsofai ni haa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe waa?

english: Yield boosters supply targeted micro-nutrients directly to the tree during pod formation, helping the pods retain moisture and grow denser beans before harvest.
ga: Nibii ni haa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ lɛ kɛ niyenii bibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ be mli ni efeɔ pod lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani akpaa.

english: Can applying too much fertilizer or spray chemical harm my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aye mi-cacao tsei lɛ awui?

english: Yes, over-applying agrochemicals can burn the tree leaves, damage root systems, and cause young cocoa pods to wither and drop prematurely.
ga: Hɛɛ, agrochemicals ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha tso baai ashã. Efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ni ehaa kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ gboiɔ oya.

english: Is it profitable for me to buy expensive yield chemicals if I only have a small cocoa farm?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ mahe tsofai ni jara wa ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa kɛji miyɛ kookoo ŋmɔ bibioo ko pɛ?

english: For very small farms, high input costs can outweigh the extra income from yield increases; basic practices like pruning and weed control often yield better profit margins first.
ga: Kɛha ŋmɔji bibii waa lɛ Nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo ni fa baanyɛ afee shika ni fa fe shika ni anáa kɛjɛɔ nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ amli lɛ. Nifeemɔi titrii tamɔ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ ehaa sɛɛnamɔ ni hi fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: How do I know if the profit from using crop sprays will cover the money I spent buying them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ sɛɛnamɔ ni jɛɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli baa lɛ baatsu shika ni mifite yɛ he lɛ he nii?

english: Calculate your total spray cost against the extra weight in harvest bags produced; if the price of the additional cocoa sold is higher than the input cost, the chemical application was profitable.
ga: Buu o-spray shika fɛɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ he akɔntaa kɛfata muji ni fata he ni yɔɔ ŋmaakpamɔ kotokui ni afee lɛ amli lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ kookoo ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ jara fe nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo lɛ Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha sɛɛnamɔ aba.

english: What is the best season to apply nutrients to my cocoa trees for maximum yield?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ afata mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe koni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Applying nutrients at the start of the rainy season when trees are flowering allows the roots to easily absorb food and support new pod development.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ wo mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli beni tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mlɛo, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii heei baa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce a large harvest one season and very little the next?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be kome mli, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo yɛ be kroko mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees exhaust their stored energy reserves during heavy harvest seasons, requiring proper rest, soil nutrients, and water to rebuild capacity for the next cycle.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ laajeɔ hewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be ni mli wa lɛ mli. ni biɔ hejɔɔmɔ niyenii ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli koni ekɛma hewalɛ ni ekɛbaatsu nii kɛha sɛɛkuu ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do cocoa flowers fall off the tree without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flower drop occurs when trees suffer from dry weather stress, nutrient deficiencies, or pest attacks, preventing the flowers from setting into young pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. niyenii ni esaaa loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmeii bibii.

english: What causes my cocoa beans to feel light or flat when drying?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo lɛ feɔ mlɛo loo efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ egbi?

english: Flat beans are caused by poor soil nutrition during pod filling, early harvesting of immature pods, or pest damage that drains the bean of nutrients while still on the tree.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii yɛ be mli ni awoɔ pod mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ flat beans baa. Ni aaakpa ŋmeii ni edako mra loo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ afitemɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ.

english: Why should I prune shade trees and cocoa branches before applying crop treatments?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo kɛ kookoo niji dani mikɛ tsofai ni akɛtsaa ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to sunlight and airflow, ensuring spray treatments reach the pods directly and reducing fungus growth from trapped moisture.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shɛɔ pods lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli lɛ mli baa lɛ baa shi

english: How do I tell if my cocoa pods are damaged by chemicals or by black pod disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofai loo black pod hela efite mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Black pod disease creates spreading dark spots with a sour smell, whereas chemical burns cause dry, hard patches only where liquid concentrated on the pod surface.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ haa ŋmeii diji ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ baa. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛshãa nii lɛ haa ŋmeii ni egbi ni wa baa yɛ he ni nu lɛ yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ pɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the food plants need to grow green and strong. Adding well-rotted poultry manure or NPK fertilizer gives the soil the nutrients needed to bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi amli ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo NPK ŋmeii fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛ eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot inside the ground when left during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ ashi amɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil cuts off air to the cassava roots, causing root rot disease. Harvesting mature cassava before the peak rainy season or planting on raised ridges allows water to drain away from the roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli. Nɔ ni kɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ Kɛ́ akpa ŋmei ni eda lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba loo adu yɛ ŋmeii ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ajɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat, poor shade, or damage from sap-sucking insects like mirids. Maintaining temporary shade plants like plantains and managing pests helps the trees keep their flowers and turn them into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafite amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa miipiŋ amɛ. ŋmɔlɔ ni ehiii loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ pollen lɛ efite. Be kukuoo mli tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Leaf curl is often caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling these insects early using insecticidal soap or neem oil prevents the leaves from curling and keeps the plant healthy enough to grow large fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni koolooi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ́ akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe, ni ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni ewo yibii wuji.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during strong winds when they carry big bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli be mli ni eyɛ ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and very heavy tops when fruiting, making them unstable in wind. Supporting the fruit-bearing stems with bamboo or strong wooden poles (propping) keeps the trees upright until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii waa kɛji amɛwo yibii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ehiɛɛɛ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei loo tsei ni wa (fiɔ sɛɛ) fiɔ aduawai akui lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why is it necessary for me to stake my yam vines with tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ tswaa sweet potato wain tso lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to process food and build large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground into the sunlight, improving growth and preventing soil-borne fungal diseases from damaging the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛkɛtsu niyenii he nii ni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa dalɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akafite baai lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants lose all their blossoms when the afternoon sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fɛɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi beni shwane hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat forces pepper plants to drop blossoms to save water and stay alive. Covering the surrounding soil with dry grass (mulching) keeps the roots cool and retains soil moisture, helping the plants keep their flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ nyɛɔ pepper tsei anɔ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi wala mli. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkwɛɔ fɔfɔi anɔ.

english: Why do my groundnut leaves get brown spots and drop off early before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: This is leaf spot disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in humid weather. Rotating crops each season and removing crop remains after harvest stops the fungus from building up in the soil.
ga: Fuŋs ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛ baa he tsɔi baa. Tsɔmɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii daa be ni ojie ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ sɛɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are there tiny holes in my maize leaves with caterpillar dirt inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Kɛ ŋmei ko ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar hiding inside the young leaves. Dropping a little clean sand or neem powder into the central whorl of the plant early in the morning smothers and destroys the worms.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋã ni he tse loo neem powda fioo ko wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋã lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie ŋmeii lɛ ni efite.

english: Why is it better for me to water my vegetable garden early in the morning rather than at noon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu leebi moŋ fe shwane mli lɛ?

english: Water applied in the hot afternoon evaporates quickly before roots can drink it, and hot leaves can scorch. Early morning watering lets the soil absorb moisture so the plants stay hydrated throughout the hottest part of the day.
ga: Nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnuɔ. Ni baai ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ashã amɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei baanyɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: I found tiny insects clinging tightly to the stems of my tomato plants, why are they not moving and are they hurting my crop?
ga: Miyana kooloo bibioo ko ni ekpɛtɛ tomato tso ko shishi waa. Mɛni hewɔ amɛtsiii amɛhe ni amɛyeee miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui lɛ?

english: Those tiny insects are likely aphids or scale insects. They attach themselves to soft stems to suck out the plant's vital sap, which starves the plant of nutrients, causes leaves to curl, and stunts fruit growth.
ga: Ekolɛ kooloi bibii lɛ ji aphids loo kooloi ni ji scale. Amɛkpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ tsei bibii ahe koni amɛmu tso lɛ mli nu ni he hiaa waa lɛ. ni haa tsei lɛ anaaa niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa aduawai lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do I see small worms hiding inside the leaves and central whorl of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-babi corn lɛ baai kɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those small worms are Fall Armyworms. Moths lay eggs on young maize leaves, and once the worms hatch, they crawl deep inside the plant to feed on tender leaves, which can destroy the plant before it flowers if not managed early.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ŋmeii ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii anɔ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ Amɛshwereɔ kɛboteɔ tsei amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai bibii. Enɛ baanyɛ agbe tso lɛ dani ewo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii oya.

english: If I pick pests off my crop leaves with my hands and crush them on the ground, will that be enough to protect my whole farm?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ miniji jie ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe baai amli ni mikɛshwie shikpɔŋ Ani ebaashɛ bɔ ni sa ni baabu miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ he?

english: Hand-picking and crushing pests works well when you have a small garden or when insects first appear, but if the pests have laid tiny eggs under leaves or inside stems, hand-picking alone won't stop a full invasion on a larger farm.
ga: Nine ni okɛbaakpa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni okɛshwieɔ shi lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ oyɛ abɔɔ bibioo ko. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii je kpo klɛŋklɛŋ Shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii lɛ wo ŋmeii bibii Yɛ baai lɛ ashishi loo yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ Ni akɛ niji ŋmɔɔ pɛ nyɛŋ akpa ŋmɔ mli nibii wuji ni akɛboteɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning pale yellow and dropping off even though rain has been falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your crop is missing key nutrients like nitrogen from the soil, or the soil has too much water around the roots, which prevents the roots from breathing and absorbing food properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii, tamɔ nitrogen, ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo, nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe niyenii kpakpai.

english: My garden egg plants are flowering very well, but why are the flowers falling off without growing into fruits?
ga: Egg tso ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miikwɛ jogbaŋŋ waa. Shi mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat shock, lack of water, or when pollinating insects like bees are not visiting. Without proper pollination or under heavy climate stress, the plant drops its flowers to survive.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ waa, nu bɛ, loo kɛ́ ŋmeii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ tamɔ ŋmeii baaa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ pollination ni sa bɛ loo yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni naa wa shishi lɛ, Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my crops grow small and thin whenever grass and weeds are growing right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ be mli ni jwɛi kɛ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Weeds act like aggressive neighbors underground and above ground; their fast-growing roots steal the soil nutrients, fertilizer, and water that your crops need to build strong stems and produce heavy yields.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni yɔɔ basabasa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Shishifãi ni daa oya lɛ juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nu ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings wilt and die right after I move them from the nursery bed into my main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔji akwɛmɔhe lɛ kɛtee miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by transplant shock. When seedlings are pulled up, their tiny feeding roots get damaged and exposed to harsh hot weather; moving them during the cool late afternoon and watering immediately helps them survive.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Kɛji akɛ ajie dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi bibii ni yeɔ Amɛ nibii lɛ baafite ni amɛbaaje kpo yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Amɛ ni ajieɔ amɛ yɛ shwane mli He ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ lɛ baaye abua amɛ ni amɛhi shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and dry out when I remove all the large trees from my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive, thin leaves that scorch in direct sunlight. They need shade trees or temporary nurse crops like plantains to shelter them from heat and keep soil moist while their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo loo tsei ni kwɛɔ amɛnɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground when heavy rains flood the soil for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: When rain saturates the soil for too long, water displaces the air pockets roots need to breathe. Starved of oxygen, the cassava tubers begin to decay, allowing waterborne rot bacteria and fungi to attack.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nu yeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni he hiaa ni shishifãi lɛ amu lɛ najiaŋ. Kasava shishifãi lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ. Enɛ haa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ni kɛ nu lɛ baa lɛ tutuaa.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains develop tiny holes and turn into white dust inside my storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni etsɔ sũ yɛŋ yɛ mi-nitoo kotoku lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by maize weevils. They burrow into stored grains to lay eggs, and the larvae eat the inside of the grain, leaving behind hollow husks and powdery waste if the grain isn't properly dried or treated before storage.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmei mli ŋmeii. Amɛfoɔ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli koni amɛwo wɔji. ni ŋmeii lɛ baaye ŋmãa lɛ mli Eshiɔ ŋmãa ni mli ewo muji kɛ ŋmeii kɛji akɛ agbiko dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ loo atsuuu he nii dani akɛtoɔ.

english: Why do my crops look yellow and weak even after heavy rain falls on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain can wash away key nutrients like nitrogen deep into the soil where plant roots cannot reach them, leaving the leaves yellow and hungry.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ.

english: How does dirty water from nearby mining sites affect the vegetables I water my farm with?
ga: Te nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛɔ shika tsuru jɛɛhe ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli lɛ saa aduawai ni mikɛ nu woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Mining water contains heavy metals and mud that block root intake, poison the plant from inside, and make the harvested crops unsafe to eat.
ga: Dade ni tsii kɛ muji ni tsiɔ shishifãi ni yeɔ nii anaa lɛ yɛ mi nu lɛ mli. Ekɛ poison woɔ tso lɛ mli kɛjɛɔ emli. ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ.

english: Can I still grow healthy food crops on land that was previously dug up for gold mining?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lolo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ ajieɔ shika tsuru yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Mined land loses its rich topsoil and becomes packed tight like concrete, making it hard for crop roots to breathe or absorb nutrients without serious soil restoration.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni aku lɛ nɔ sũ ni baa nii lɛ efite ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ kɔnkrit. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛbaamu loo amɛbaaŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ hiɛdɔɔ haaa sũ lɛ mli hewalɛ.

english: What is the difference between farm medicine that kills weeds and medicine that helps crops grow?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi kɛ tsofai ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa lɛ ateŋ?

english: Weedkillers (herbicides) destroy unwanted plants by stopping their growth, while crop medicines like fertilizers provide nutrients to feed and strengthen your crops.
ga: tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi (Herbicide) Efiteɔ tsei ni ataooo kɛtsɔ amɛdalɛ ni ekpaa lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ahe tsofai, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii haa niyenii ni haa onibii lɛ yeɔ nii ni ewoɔ amɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn black and dry up after I spray them with farm chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ tsofai eshwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Spraying too much chemical or applying it during the hot sun scorches the leaves, as heat causes the liquid to burn the delicate plant surface.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa babaoo shwie nɔ loo okɛwo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ ashã. Yɛ dɔlɛ hewɔ lɛ, nu lɛ shãa tso lɛ hiɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need plantains planted next to them when they are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu kookoo tsei bibii ni dumɔwui awo amɛmasɛi lɛ? Beni tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight, so fast-growing plantains provide living shade to keep the young cocoa cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo baa koni kookoo bibioo lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall with thick green leaves but produce empty or small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi ewoɔ ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli loo ŋmeii bibii.

english: Too much leaf-growing nutrient (nitrogen) makes maize grow tall, but without enough cob-building nutrients (phosphorus and potassium), the cobs stay small.
ga: Niyenii babaoo ni jɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ mli (nitrogen) lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ daa. Shi kɛji akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni feɔ cob lɛ bɛ. (Fosfɔs kɛ potasium) lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow huge branches above ground but give me small roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ niji wuji yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil lacks potassium, the plant puts all its energy into growing leaves and stems instead of storing starch in the underground tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ ashikishaŋ lɛ baato ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ,.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop dark rotting spots at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused when tomato plants cannot get enough calcium from the soil, usually due to irregular watering.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Weeds steal light, water, and soil food away from your crops, leaving your crops starved and unable to grow properly.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ la, nu, kɛ sũ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my okra plants growing plenty of large leaves but very few fruit pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ baai lɛ dara waa shi aduawai amli ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Okra plants put too much energy into leaves when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Using a fertilizer higher in phosphorus encourages the plant to stop making foliage and start producing flowers and pods.
ga: Gumbo tsei kɛ hewalɛ babaoo woɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛ́ nitrogen babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus babaoo yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekpa baai ni ebɔi fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii feemɔ.

english: What causes my okra pods to become hard and woody before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi okra ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni efeɔ tso dani akpaa amɛ?

english: Okra pods mature very quickly once formed. If left on the stalk for more than a few days, they lose tenderness and become tough, so harvesting every two to three days keeps the pods soft and encourages the plant to yield more.
ga: Okra pods lɛ daa oya waa kɛji afee lɛ pɛ. Kɛji ashi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ fe gbii fioo lɛ, ebaafee bɔ ni eyɔɔ mlɛo ni ewa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa gbii fioo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee blɛoo ni ewo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot easily when water sits in the soil for too long. Planting stem cuttings on raised ridges or mounds allows excess water to drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ oya kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: How can I tell when my cassava roots are fully mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves yellow and fall off, and the ground around the base begins to crack. You can also dig up a single root to check if it has grown to a good size before harvesting the whole field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. ni he ni ebɔle shishitoo lɛ he lɛ bɔi fãmɔ. Obaanyɛ otsa shishifã kome hu koni ona kɛji edara kɛyashɛ dalɛ kpakpa he dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How do bean crops help improve the soil for my other crops?
ga: Te ŋmei tsei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ kɛhaa mi tsei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Beans are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, this nitrogen stays in the soil and acts as a natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Beans ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nɛkɛ nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young bean plants turning yellow and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pea tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young beans are often caused by waterlogging in the root zone or tiny pests like aphids sucking sap from the stems. Good soil drainage and early insect control prevent this leaf drop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli loo kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii anɔ lɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ kooloi akwɛmɔ mra yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Can I plant cassava and beans together in the same field without harming my yield?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni enaaa yibiiwoo lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping cassava with beans works well because beans grow quickly and cover the ground, suppressing weeds and adding nitrogen to the soil while the slow-growing cassava is still small.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmeii duɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ daa oya ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa ni ekɛ nitrogen fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ daa blɛoo ni eji bibioo lolo lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops curl up during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the hot afternoon heat is a natural way for crops to reduce their exposed surface area, helping them conserve moisture and prevent drying out until the sun goes down.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tsɔɔ nɔ amɛhaa amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ehaaa egbi kɛyashi hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: What causes my crop plants to grow tall and thin instead of strong and bushy?
ga: Mɛni haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee hewalɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji?

english: Plants grow tall and spindly when they are planted too close together and must stretch upwards to compete for sunlight. Proper plant spacing gives each plant enough light and air to build thick, sturdy stems.
ga: Tsei daa ni amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. ni esa akɛ ekpã ehe kɛya ŋwɛi koni ekɛ hulu la lɛ akaŋ Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ tsei ni mli tse ni mli wa.

english: Why do flowers drop off my plants before developing into fruits or pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ aduawai loo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences sudden stress, such as extreme heat, erratic watering, or a lack of pollinating insects like bees. Maintaining consistent soil moisture helps the plant hold onto its blooms.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔi kpe trukaa, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. loo kooloi ni feɔ pollen tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ faaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen in the soil, or the soil has too much standing water drowning the roots. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nu ni ekã shi babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aahu akɛ shishifãi lɛ miiho. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves droop down during the afternoon heat and stand back up in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli ni amɛteɔ shi gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: This is the plant's natural way of protecting itself. It droops its leaves during peak afternoon heat to lose less water to the hot sun, then recovers when the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Enɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe he. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni shwane mli latsaa lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ koni nu fioo ko akaje hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛkɛ lɛ, ehiɛ baa ehe nɔ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: What causes tiny holes in my young corn leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the center shoot?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli Mi nɔ lɛ etee ehe yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: This is caused by Fall Armyworms. They feed on the tender young leaves inside the central funnel of the plant, which can stunt growth if they are not sprayed or handpicked early.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworms. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ dalɛ naa kɛji akɛ ashwieee nɔ loo ahalaaa lɛ mra.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when the weather gets too hot, when the soil gets too dry, or if the soil lacks nutrients like phosphorus. Keeping the soil moist and adding compost helps the flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii tamɔ fɔsfɔs bɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce small harvests when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa ni mikpamɔ lɛ faaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close, they steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients from each other. Giving each plant proper space lets roots spread and gather enough food to grow strong.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni ebuaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa naa koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my land give me smaller yields when I plant cassava on the exact same spot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating cassava with leguminous crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nutrients to the soil.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting under the ground during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long because the roots cannot breathe. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps extra rainwater drain away so roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like food thieves on your farm; they quickly soak up the water, fertilizer, and sunlight meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛheɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Why don't my harvested seed yams sprout right away after I put them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ ekwɛɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seed yams go through a natural resting phase called dormancy after harvest. They will not sprout until this rest period ends naturally, even if you plant them in wet soil right away.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Amɛkwɛŋ kɛyashi nɛkɛ hejɔɔmɔ be nɛɛ baagbe naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛji akɛ odu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ po.

english: Young cocoa plants have very sensitive leaves that easily scorch under direct tropical sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain next to young cocoa creates a natural umbrella that shields the seedlings and keeps the soil moist while they establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be lɛ yɔɔ lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo baa ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni aduɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over during heavy rain and wind before the bunches mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli dani ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that stay near the soil surface. As the heavy fruit bunch grows, the plant becomes top-heavy, causing it to uproot easily unless soil is mounded firmly around the base or wooden props are used to support the stem.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baaná nɔ ni fe fɛɛ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaawo shishifãi amli ja akɛ sũ lɛ ebɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ Aloo akɛ tso ko ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow at the tips and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛnaagbɛ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaf tips on young maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the maize produce deep green, healthy foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Ni akɛ ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni ewoɔ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa.

english: Why do the leaves of my young corn plants look like they have holes eaten through them overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛye bu nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: Holes in young corn leaves are typically caused by pests like Fall Armyworms feeding inside the central whorl of the leaf during the dark hours. Checking leaf funnels early and applying recommended treatments stops them from eating the growing point of the stalk.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworms ni yeɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa bibii amli lɛ baa. Nibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaye nii yɛ hei ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with thick branches, but the tubers under the ground are thin and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ niji ni mli tse lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛji bibii?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or is planted under dense shade, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of sending food downward to enlarge the underground tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmãa nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo akwɛɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛduɔ baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baatsu nii koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei.

english: Yam vines produce tubers underground by catching sunlight with their upper leaves. Tall wooden stakes lift the leaves high above weeds, maximizing sunlight exposure so the vine can direct extra food down into larger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛkɛ amɛŋwɛi baai lɛ mɔmɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Tso kakadaŋŋ ko woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ fe jwɛi lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ bɔni afee ni wain tsei lɛ anyɛ amɛkɛ niyenii kroko aba shi kɛya sweet potato ŋmeii wuji lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my growing green tomatoes turning black and soft before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli ni miida lɛ shishigbɛ fãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Black, sunken spots at the bottom of tomatoes are caused by calcium deficiency, often brought on by irregular watering. When soil moisture jumps between too wet and too dry, roots cannot draw calcium properly into the developing fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji calcium ni faaa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ tsɔ kɛ nɔ ni egbi tsɔ teŋ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ calcium jogbaŋŋ kɛya aduawai ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling upward and twisting together into tight bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Upward curling on pepper leaves is a sign that tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites are feeding under the leaves, or that a virus spread by whiteflies is disturbing the leaf's growth pattern.
ga: Pepper baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ thrips loo mites, miiye baai lɛ ashishi. Aloo ani hela ko ni whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ miitsi baai lɛ adalɛ naa?

english: Why do the flowers on my garden egg and pepper plants fall off without turning into small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-egg kɛ pepper tsei ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai bibii lɛ?

english: Vegetable plants often drop flowers when they experience severe water stress or extreme heat. The plant intentionally sheds its blossoms to save energy and water so it can stay alive until growing conditions improve.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa kpe. Tso nɛɛ jwɛŋɔ ewoɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ anyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa tso lɛ daa lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi.

english: Why do experienced extension officers recommend planting cowpea or groundnuts on a field before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔji amli dani adu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpea and groundnut work with friendly soil bacteria to take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the legumes are harvested, those root nodules break down and naturally feed the next crop like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts kɛ sũ mli helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa Nakai shishifãi lɛ baakumɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, ni ji ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and dry during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves dry out quickly because harsh Harmattan winds and direct sunlight remove moisture faster than roots can absorb it. Providing shade trees or plantain shade reduces wind speed and sun exposure, keeping the air around the leaves humid so the plant stays green.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ejaakɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo be loo hulutsoo be ha lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ oyaiyeli kɛ hulu la lɛ aba shi. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni tso lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy rains before the fruits are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli dani eyibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and when heavy bunches grow, the tree becomes top-heavy. Wet soil loosens the ground's grip on the roots, causing wind and weight to easily uproot the plant unless you prop it up with sturdy bamboo sticks.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni kɛ́ tso lɛ da lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii. Shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ akpɛtɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ muji baafo tsei. Ja okɛ ŋmei ni mli wa tsu nii kɛfi sɛɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize crops turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the food plants use to make dark green leaves and grow strong stems. Applying compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its green color and grow faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ amɛbaai ni tsuɔ waa kɛ amɛshishifãi ni wa. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When these roots decay in the soil, they release natural fertilizer that helps feed neighboring maize plants and improves soil health for future seasons.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's harvested maize yield smaller cobs than new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa bibii fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred for high performance, but the seeds gathered from their harvest lose that high yield potential in the next generation. Using fresh certified seeds ensures uniform growth, disease resistance, and larger cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ Hybrid dumɔwui lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Shi dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ yibiiwoo babaoo yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei, ni ana he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ naa dalɛ daa. Helai ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ helai kɛ ŋmeii wuji

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes rapidly from dry to wet. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps the plant hold onto its flowers until they develop into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsake oya kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashi ebaatsɔ tomato.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll up into tight cups and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi ni mli wa ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling in peppers is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips hiding underneath the leaves, or by extreme heat stress. Removing affected leaves and spraying neem oil water helps control the insects so new leaves can grow flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa lɛ Kɛ́ ajie baai ni ena hela lɛ ni akɛ neem fɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi lɛ koni baai heei lɛ adara ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce plenty of leafy branches but very thin roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ niji kɛ baai babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, or when plants are crowded too close together, cassava focuses all its energy on growing top leaves instead of storing food in the roots. Proper spacing and balanced soil nutrients encourage the plant to swell its tuberous roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ Cassava lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni miida yɛ nɔ lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, gbɛ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa.

english: Why do crops grow so much slower when weeds are left in the field for even two weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛ́ ashi jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛyashi otsii enyɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal drinking water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your plants. Clearing weeds early leaves all the water and plant food available exclusively for your crop roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu ni anuɔ, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha nu kɛ tso niyenii fɛɛ ahi shi tɛ̃ɛ kɛha otso lɛ shishifãi.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass stop the soil from drying out quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around Feed mi crops kɛ hay bɔni afee ni ekɛtsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or straw, known as mulching, shields the soil surface from direct sunlight. This keeps the ground cool and slows down water evaporation, retaining moisture for crop roots days after it rains.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛhaa tsei shishifãi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ gbii babaoo sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and curling up in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct heat from the hot sun. They dry out quickly and curl up unless they have shade crops like plantains planted near them to block the harsh sunlight during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Amɛgbiɔ oya ni amɛkpãa amɛhe, ja adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛtsi hulu ni naa wa lɛ naa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my cocoa trees very close to each other on my land?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, planting them too close makes the trees compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. It also creates a damp environment where diseases spread quickly, whereas proper spacing gives each tree enough room to produce healthy pods.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu amɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ hu baa ni helai srɔtoi baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mli. gbɛɔ eshwaa oya Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii ni mli wa.

english: Why do many of the small flowers on my cocoa trees fall off before forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ji Tsei ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo miigbee shi dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ?

english: It is natural for cocoa trees to drop some flowers, but heavy flower drop happens when the tree lacks nutrients, suffers from lack of water, or when there are not enough tiny insects like midges around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ekomɛi anɔ. Shi fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi waa lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu bɛ amɛhe, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ midges ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ.

english: Why should I cut off the fresh shoots growing near the bottom of my cocoa tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ cacao tso shishi lɛ?

english: These lower shoots, known as chupons, steal food and energy from the main tree. Removing them allows the tree to send all its food and water up to produce strong leaves, flowers, and cocoa pods.
ga: Atsɛɔ gɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ nɛɛ akɛ Chupon. Ju niyenii kɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ tsei wuji amli. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ tsuɔ eniyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛ kookoo baai, fɔfɔii, kɛ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba.

english: What causes my green cocoa pods to turn black and dry up while hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egbiɔ beni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast during rainy and humid weather. Water drops carry the fungus from infected pods to healthy ones if they are not removed promptly.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nu mli nu ni hoɔ lɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli kɛji ajieee amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: What are those tiny insects under my leaves that make the branches look like they were burned by fire?
ga: Mɛni ji kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ mibaai lɛ ashishi ni haa tsei lɛ aniji feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni la miitso lɛ?

english: Those are capsids, also called mirids. They suck sap from young shoots and pods, leaving dark spots that cause branches to dry up, so keeping shade balanced and spraying recommended organic or chemical treatments helps protect the tree.
ga: Amɛji kapsid. Ale lɛ hu akɛ Mirid Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii amli lɛ. Eshiɔ hei ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni haa tsei lɛ aniji lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akwɛ tsei lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛshwie nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know if my soil is weak and needs fertilizer for my cocoa to grow well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your trees show slow growth, pale yellow leaves instead of deep green ones, or produce very small pods despite good rains, your soil is running low on essential nutrients like phosphorus and potassium.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ miida blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ. Aloo ŋmeii bibii waa jeɔ kpo yɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ phosphorus kɛ potassium faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.
