english: Can I plant cassava together with my young cocoa trees on the same plot?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei kɛ kookoo tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: You can plant cassava, but it should not be too close to young cocoa trees. Cassava grows aggressive roots that compete strongly for water and soil nutrients, which can stunt the young cocoa's growth.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmei. Shi esaaa akɛ ebɛŋkɛɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ tsɔ. Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni jɛɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni baanyɛ atsĩ kookoo bibii lɛ adalɛ naa

english: How can I tell the exact time my cocoa pods are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ esa akɛ akpa?

english: Look closely at the color of the pods. Pods that start as green turn bright yellow when ripe, and pods that start as red or purple turn bright orange, showing that the beans inside have fully matured.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe su jogbaŋŋ. Pods ni jeɔ shishi kɛ eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse beni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Ni pods ni jeɔ shishi efeɔ etsuru loo purple lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Why does my cocoa tree stop producing pods during the long dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ harmattan be kakadaŋŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally slow down growth and shed leaves during the harmattan to save water. Without enough soil moisture, the tree cannot carry new flowers or nurture pods until the rainy season returns.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ haa amɛdalɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ harmatta beaŋ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ afee fɔfɔi heei loo eha eshishifãi lɛ niyenii kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and burning when the sun gets strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under harsh direct sunlight because they need partial shade to build strong roots. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees alongside young cocoa protects them from heat stress during their early years.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebiɔ hulutsoo ko dani enyɛ efee shishifãi ni wa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do I see small holes in my maize leaves and tiny caterpillars hidden inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni Akɛtee baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: This damage is caused by fall armyworms, which feed on young maize foliage. Catching them early and applying recommended natural or chemical treatments inside the center leaf whorl prevents them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji fall flukes, ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Amɔmɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu nii yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ koni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the leaf sap or spreading a plant virus. Controlling these insects early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baa mli nu loo helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and rot before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani edara lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often triggered by irregular watering where the soil gets too dry between rain or irrigation.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with many leaves, but the tubers underground stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has excessive nitrogen relative to potassium, the plant spends all its energy producing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni eeekɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ato.

english: Why do my yam seed tubers rot in the soil before they even sprout stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ po lɛ?

english: Yam seeds rot in the ground when fungi or soil pests attack cut or damaged tuber pieces. Treating the seed pieces with wood ash or fungicide before planting shields them until shoots emerge.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ ŋmeii loo shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutua tsei ni afo loo tuber lɛ fãi ni efite lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso mli sũ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii tsu dumɔwui lɛ ahe nii dani adu lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hebuu kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ baaje kpo.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is missing nutrients before I plant my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ dani madu tsei?

english: Soil that produces stunted plants with pale green or yellowish leaves, or soil that feels thin and sandy without dark organic material, usually lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni feɔ tsei ni egbɔjɔ ni baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. loo shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni ŋã yɔɔ mli ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ bɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, amɛbɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus.

english: The initial rain encourages seeds to sprout, but if a dry heat spell follows immediately, the weak young seedlings will dry out and die before the regular rainy season fully begins.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo kɛ hɔmɔ ba ni nyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be ni sa lɛ jeɔ shishi kwraa.

english: Why do people advise me not to plant maize on the exact same patch of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikadu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes the specific nutrients that crop relies on and allows pests and diseases specialized in maize to accumulate in the soil over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei lɛ damɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni he esa waa yɛ ŋmãa mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my crops even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa oya eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from the soil before your crop roots can reach them, effectively starving your main plants.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii titri lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall with deep green leaves but yield very small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: This usually happens when there is too much nitrogen in the soil relative to phosphorus and potassium. Nitrogen encourages stem and leaf growth, but phosphorus and potassium are required to build large, full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto fɔsfɔs kɛ potassium he. Nitrogen haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ daraa. Shi fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium he miihia koni afee ŋmei agbo ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my crops yield better when I plant groundnuts on the field where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ mli yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the soil for heavy-feeding crops like maize in the following season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii kɛha niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Purple leaves on young maize are a sign of phosphorus deficiency in the soil. Phosphorus is essential for early root development and energy transfer in the plant.
ga: Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Fosforo he hiaa waa kɛha shishifãi ni yaa hiɛ mra kɛ hewalɛ ni akɛyaa tsei amli lɛ.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a major pest in Ghana. They target the tender central leaves of young maize, and early treatment with recommended sprays or wood ash in the leaf funnels can control them.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ. Amɛtutuaa ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. kɛ mra be mli tsamɔ Kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo tso sũ ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ ni ajieɔ yi lɛ nɔ lɛ abaanyɛ akudɔ amɛ.

english: The first rain is often a 'false rain' followed by a dry period. Planting too early means seeds will germinate and then wither and die due to a lack of sustained soil moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ji ‘apasa nugbɔ’ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are ready to be harvested under the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. Key signs include the lower leaves turning yellow and falling off, and small cracks forming in the soil around the base of the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Okadii ni he hiaa lɛ ekomɛi ji baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. ni ŋmeii bibii Forms yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Tomato blossoms drop mainly due to heat stress or irregular watering. When temperatures are too high or water is scarce, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and survive.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa fe fɛɛ ji dɔlɛ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu faaa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi.

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can reach maximum sunlight to feed the growing tubers underground. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground also prevents fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ koni amɛha amɛbaa lɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo koni ekɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ baa helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli baa lɛ anaa.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my crops after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds produce thousands of hardy seeds that lie dormant in the soil for years. Once you clear the ground and rain falls, weed seeds germinate immediately and grow aggressively to outcompete crops for nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi woɔ dumɔwui akpei abɔ ni hiɛ hewalɛ ni ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo Beni ojieɔ jɛmɛ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ. Jwɛi dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛdaraa oya koni amɛye niyenii ni jɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ.

english: How do I know if a newly introduced crop variety will actually grow well in my region in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso henɔ hee ko ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mikpokpaa ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ nɔ?

english: Agricultural extension officers test new crop varieties across specific ecological zones, such as the forest or savanna belts. Certified varieties are specially bred to tolerate local weather patterns, resist common native pests, and handle dry spells better than uncertified local seeds.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ okwaayeli he nii lɛ kaa tsei srɔtoi heei amɛkwɛɔ yɛ shihilɛhei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli, tamɔ kooi loo savanna bɛlts. Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ maŋ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ anaa. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni afɔɔ namɔ. ni etsuɔ ​​ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni bɛ he odaseyeli lɛ.

english: Can I save seeds from the high-yielding hybrid maize I harvest this season to plant again next year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni mikpaa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Saving seeds from hybrid crops is not ideal because the second-generation plants lose their hybrid strength. They usually produce uneven growth, lower yields, and weaker resistance to pests compared to buying fresh certified hybrid seeds each planting season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛbaajɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ jeee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ tsei ni ji yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ fiteɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ ahewalɛ. Bei pii lɛ, amɛdalɛ kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ baa shi. Akɛ enɛ toɔ dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ he yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ he.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants curl up into tight tubes during the sunny afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural defense mechanism against heat. By reducing the surface area exposed to the sun, the plant prevents excess water from evaporating, helping itself survive short periods of heat stress.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ hebuu gbɛ. Kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ ni abaaba shi lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ baatsi nu ni fa fe nine lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ ohe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: When soil lacks sufficient nitrogen, the plant automatically transfers stored nitrogen from its older, bottom leaves up to nourish new growth at the top. Yellow lower leaves are usually a clear sign your crop needs nitrogen fertilizer or organic manure.
ga: Kɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ jieɔ nitrogen ni ato lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii. Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ he miihia otso lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants keep dropping their flowers before producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when exposed to stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer that forces the plant to grow leaves instead of fruit. Ensuring consistent soil moisture and balanced nutrients helps hold the blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ he. Aloo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo lɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly bacteria in their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This naturally enriches the soil, giving nearby hungry crops like maize essential nutrients without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ naanyobɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛhe tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli.

english: How can I test if my farm soil has enough moisture for planting without buying expensive tools?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔ nii ni miheee nibii ni jara wa?

english: Dig down a few inches, scoop a handful of soil, and squeeze it into a ball. If it holds its shape without dripping water and easily crumbles when poked, the soil has the right moisture balance for seeds to germinate safely.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ shi inchi fioo komɛi. Okɛ sũ ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ awo mli ni okɛmimɔ mli ni efee bɔɔlu. Kɛji ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli ni nu shwieee shi ni efoɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sũ lɛ yɛ nu ni sa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: What causes my cassava roots to turn out small and woody instead of big and full of starch?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ tsei yɛ agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ najiaŋ?

english: Cassava roots become woody when planted in hard, compacted soil, when infected by diseases like cassava mosaic virus, or when left in the ground during prolonged dry seasons where the plant consumes its own stored root starches to stay alive.
ga: Kasava shishifãi bafeɔ tso kɛji akɛ akwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ kɛji helai tamɔ cassava mosaic virus lɛ emɔ amɛ. aloo kɛ́ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Tsei kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ato yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees tip over and fall so easily even when there is no heavy storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji ahum ni naa wa po bɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees tip over when microscopic soil worms called nematodes or stem borer insects destroy their underground root foundation. Without healthy roots to anchor the crop firmly in the ground, the heavy plant collapses under its own weight.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ kpata shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ. Kɛji shishifãi ni wa bɛ ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atswa shikpɔŋ lɛ, Tso ni tsii baagbee shi yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etsiimɔ shishi.

english: Why is early weeding so crucial during the first month after my crops sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: During the first few weeks, young crop seedlings have small roots and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures young crops establish strong roots and stalks without being choked out.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, Dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei bibii lɛ náa shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni wa, ni nɔ ko tsiii amɛ gbɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I plant them directly under open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu ni mli tse lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaf tissues and short roots that cannot absorb water fast enough under intense sun. Planting shade crops like plantains or shade trees protects young seedlings from heat stress and conserves soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains loo shade tsei ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why is it harmful to plant my cocoa trees very close together just to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni aná he ko babaoo kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Overcrowding causes trees to compete for sunlight and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stems and low yields. It also creates a dense canopy that traps moisture, making it easier for fungal diseases like Black Pod to spread.
ga: Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi. Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ hu baa. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why should I cut off the fast-growing leafy shoots that sprout near the bottom of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: These shoots, called chupones or water sprouts, steal nutrients and water from the main tree without producing pods. Removing them ensures the tree directs its energy toward growing pods.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ, ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupones loo nu ŋmeii lɛ, juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli ni amɛfeee ŋmeii. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ hewalɛ yaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why do many flowers fall off my cocoa trees without turning into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Flower drop happens when trees lack proper nutrients or water, or when there are not enough beneficial insects like midges around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii loo nu ni sa. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ teŋdamɔlɔi ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ faaa

english: Why do my thirty-year-old cocoa trees yield much less fruit than when they were young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso ni eye afii nyɔŋmai etɛ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe be mli ni miji gbekɛ fioo lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age, their root systems become less efficient at absorbing nutrients, and trunk tissues slow down water transport. Replacing old trees or grafting fresh shoots restores productivity.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ da lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli. ni tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ haa nu lɛ yaa hiɛ fioo Tsei momo ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ loo niji heei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes the pods on my cocoa tree to turn black and hard during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni ewaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a water-borne fungal infection that flourishes in damp, cool conditions. Regular harvesting and trimming extra leaves to let light in helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni yɔɔ nu mli ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Baai krokomɛi ni akpaa ni afolɔ amɛ daa koni la abote mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do capsids cause the tips of my cocoa branches to dry up and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ capsids lɛ miiha mi-cocoa tsei lɛ ayitsei lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Capsids (mirids) are sap-sucking insects that pierce tender branches and inject toxic saliva. This damages the plant tissue, cuts off nutrient flow, and causes the branch tips to die back.
ga: Capsids (mirids) ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni amɛwoɔ tsei aniji bibii amli ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei woɔ mli. Enɛ fiteɔ tsei amli fãji. efo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni hoɔ lɛ mli ni eha tso lɛ nine lɛ naagbee lɛ agbo.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees need extra plant food or fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ he miihia tsei niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi?

english: If leaves turn yellow while the veins stay green, or if the trees produce few, undersized pods despite good rainfall, the soil is likely depleted of essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ amli fãji lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ loo kɛji tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii fioo komɛi yɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium lɛ baaje shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How does the dry Harmattan season affect my cocoa trees, and how can I reduce the damage?
ga: Te harmattan be ni mli egbi lɛ saa mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mahã nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ aba shi?

english: Harmattan winds suck moisture out of the leaves rapidly, causing trees to drop leaves and shed young pods. Leaving fallen leaves on the ground as mulch helps keep the soil moist and protects root systems.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmeii bibii. Kɛ́ ashi baai ni egbee shi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do cocoa buyers insist that I cover harvested beans under plantain leaves to ferment before drying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ kookoo lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ aha plantain baai ashishi koni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani egbi lɛ?

english: Fermentation stops the bean from germinating and creates the natural chocolate flavor and rich brown color required by global markets. Unfermented beans remain bitter, purple, and low in market value.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃. ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ kɛ su ni mli tse ni je lɛŋ jarayelihei lɛ biɔ lɛ baa. Beans ni afeee lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ lolo, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ejara waaa yɛ jara nɔ.

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves during peak heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which helps them save water. Once the air cools down in the late afternoon, the leaves will usually spread open again.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni akɛ nu toɔ Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very tender leaves that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them creates a protective umbrella that keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii waa ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ haa shade ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: No, planting too close forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks with small or empty ears of corn.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ toi bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: How do I know which side of the cassava stem should face up when I plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni esa akɛ makwɛ ŋwɛi kɛ́ midu?

english: Look closely at the tiny bumps or 'eyes' along the stem where leaves used to grow; those nodes should always point upward toward the sky so the shoot can grow straight out.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘ŋmeii’ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ he ni baai lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ be ko ni eho lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ nakai ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do people tell me to plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu tsina loo ŋmãa?

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. Maize needs lots of nitrogen to grow, so planting them together naturally feeds your maize crop.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa ŋmãa niyenii ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli baa.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after a gentle rain, but avoid doing it right before a heavy downpour, which can wash the nutrients off the field before the plant roots absorb them.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi esa akɛ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaafata he amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa. Enɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why am I seeing small holes and ragged edges on my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa bu bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by pests like the fall armyworm caterpillar, which hide deep inside the central funnel of the plant during the day.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni egbee shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ abele baa bibii amli lɛ baa. ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do I need to remove weeds from my field even when the weeds are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ amɛji bibii kwraa lolo po lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, nutrients, and sunlight from your main crop very quickly. Clearing them while they are small keeps your crops strong and saves you harder labor later on.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli oya. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ mli awa ni ebaaha okɛ nitsumɔ babaoo akatsu nii sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to build wooden stakes for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matswa tso kɛha mi sweet potato tso lɛ koni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers. Lifting their vines off the ground allows their leaves to catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to swell the tuber hidden underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ gɔŋ. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa ebaa lɛ naa hulu la babaoo. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛgbala shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why did the seeds I saved from my last hybrid maize harvest give me weak plants this year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ wo tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ afi nɛɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce strong yields for only one planting season. The seeds saved from that harvest lose their special strength and produce mixed or weak results.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ shweremɔ be kome pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ ni fa lɛ ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui ni efutu loo ni yɔɔ blɛoo.

english: Maize seeds should ideally be planted about 75 centimeters between rows and 25 to 30 centimeters between individual plants. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough sunlight, ground moisture, and soil nutrients to produce big, healthy cobs without crowding each other out.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui aaafee sɛntimitai 75 yɛ ŋtayaai ateŋ kɛ sɛntimitai 25 kɛyashi 30 yɛ tsei ateŋ. Nɛkɛ jɛkɛmɔ nɛɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la. sũ mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni baaha afee ŋshɔŋlooi wuji ni he wa ni amɛhe ebɔko amɛhe.

english: Young cocoa trees are soft and burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa seedlings need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do some farmers plant beans or groundnuts together with maize in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa fataa ŋmãa he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into rich soil fertilizer. Planting them alongside maize naturally feeds the soil, improves corn yields, and keeps the soil covered so it does not dry out.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ abele masɛi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha ŋmãa ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaaa egbi

english: What causes the leaves of my young corn plants to turn pale green or yellow?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ?

english: Yellow or pale leaves usually mean your soil is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build strong green leaves. Applying well-decomposed manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the crop regain its deep green color and grow faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni mli tse lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná su ni mli kwɔ ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava stems curling up and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Curled and yellow-spotted leaves on cassava are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. The disease stops the plant from making food properly, which reduces the size and yield of the underground tubers.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ yucca nɔ lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Hela nɛɛ haaa tsei afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the leaves inside the center funnel of my young maize crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ funnel lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a pest that loves to hide in the dark center of young maize plants where tender leaves grow. Identifying them early and applying safe recommended insecticides directly into the plant funnel protects the growing crop from total destruction.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhi amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ he ni baa bibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Ni oooyɔse amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛwo tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɔ kwraa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the plant before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes too hot and dry or when the plant experiences sudden water stress. Regular watering and placing dry grass mulch around the base of the plant helps lower soil temperature and keeps moisture steady.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo beni tsei kɛ nu he haomɔ kpeɔ trukaa lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli Tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli latsaa baa shi ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi daa.

english: Why are my pepper fruits rotting and turning black at the bottom end?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ miifite ni amɛmiifee ediŋŋ yɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Black rot at the bottom of pepper fruits is caused by a lack of calcium combined with irregular watering while fruits are forming. Keeping soil moisture consistent prevents this damage and produces smooth, healthy peppers.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ pepper aduawai lɛ shishi lɛ baa ji calcium ni faaa kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifee lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ naa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my underground yams?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii?

english: Yams are mature and ready for harvest when the leaves and vines naturally dry up and turn brown. This signals that the plant has finished feeding and has stored all its energy into full-sized tubers under the ground.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ edara ni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ egbi ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe niyenii yeli naa ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ eto ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why does my cassava tuber start spoiling so quickly after I dig it out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ bɔi fitemɔ oya beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots contain a lot of water and start a natural chemical breakdown immediately after being cut from the living plant. Processing them quickly into products like gari or cassava flour preserves them before decay sets in.
ga: Nu babaoo yɛ cassava shishifãi amli ni amɛjeɔ tsofai amli fitemɔ shishi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ tso ni hiɛ ka lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ afee nibii oya tamɔ gari loo ŋmei ashikishaŋ lɛ, ebaaha amɛhi shi dani amɛgboi.

english: Why should I plant plantains together with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ adu plantains lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that protect delicate young cocoa seedlings from strong sunlight and retain moisture in the soil, helping the cocoa survive its early growth stage.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo ni ehiɔ shi yɛ shishijee fãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when planted in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive under direct, full sunlight. Without shade from crops like plantains or larger trees, the heat scorches their leaves and drains moisture from the plant.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo bɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei wuji amli lɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaajie nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Will planting plantains on the same farm reduce the growth of my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani plantains ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baaha mi-kokoo tsei lɛ adalɛ aba shi?

english: No, when spaced correctly, plantains actually help cocoa grow better by providing necessary shade and cooling the soil without stealing too many nutrients.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ Plantains lɛ to he ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua kookoo lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛtsɔ hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ekɛhaa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa edɔɔ ni ejuuu niyenii mli nibii babaoo lɛ nɔ.

english: How long do plantains need to stay on the farm to protect my cocoa trees?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ plantains ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ebu mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe?

english: Plantains are usually kept for the first two to three years. After that, the cocoa trees grow large enough to form their own leafy canopy and protect themselves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ plantains toɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, cacao tso lɛ daa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ efeɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ebaa ni ebuɔ ehe he.

english: Can I make money or get food from my new farm while waiting for cocoa to yield?
ga: Ani manyɛ maná shika loo maná niyenii kɛjɛ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli be mli ni mimɛɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yes, planting plantains alongside young cocoa allows you to harvest plantain for food and income within the first year while waiting a few years for the cocoa pods to grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains ni ooodu yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa plantains kɛha niyenii kɛ shika yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ afii fioo komɛi krokomɛi.

english: Why do I need to leave or plant tall trees on my farm alongside my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi loo madu tsei kakadaji yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Tall trees act as windbreaks, lower ground temperature, and prevent extreme heat from damaging cocoa plants and drying out the soil.
ga: Tsei kakadaji tsuɔ nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsimɔ. ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ baa shi ni ehaaa dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa akafite kookoo tsei lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi.

english: How does clearing bush land properly help my new crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mi-hedgerow lɛ ni mijieɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Clearing removes weeds and diseased plants that compete with your young crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, giving your cocoa and plantains a healthy start.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ ni kɛ onibii bibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaajie. Enɛ haa o-cocoa kɛ plantain lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do big trees help my cocoa farm survive the long dry season?
ga: Bɔ ni tsei wuji yeɔ ebuaa mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Big trees reduce water evaporation from the soil and create a cooler microclimate that keeps the air and ground humid even when rainfall stops.
ga: Tsei wuji haa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko ni mli ejɔ baa. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa po.

english: Does leaving trees on my farm make the soil richer for my crops?
ga: Ani tsei ni mashi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Yes, leaves falling from tall shade trees rot over time and act as natural fertilizer, adding organic matter and essential nutrients back into the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei kakadaji anɔ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli, ni amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛtsɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni akɛbaafata shikpɔŋ lɛ he ekoŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important to organize where each crop goes after clearing the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ato he ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko yaa lɛ he gbɛjianɔ beni ajie ŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii lɛ?

english: Proper spacing prevents crops from overcrowding each other, ensuring that shade plants like plantains give right coverage without blocking all sunlight from cocoa seedlings.
ga: He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baatsi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ haa hulu la fɛɛ ni jɛɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings get easily stressed by harsh sunlight and wind. They need temporary shade trees like plantains or bananas nearby to shield them and trap soil moisture until their roots grow deeper.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ haoɔ oya. Tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo banana ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni ebu sũ lɛ he ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baafee shɔŋŋ.

english: Which way am I supposed to put my cassava stem cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ, te esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cassava stems have raised nodes or 'eyes' where leaf buds grow. Always plant the stem cutting with these eyes pointing upward toward the sky so the shoots can grow straight up without wasting plant energy.
ga: Kasava tsei lɛ ewo nodes loo ‘buds’ ni baa ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, dumɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ ada tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛfiteee tso lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow in the shape of a V from the leaf tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛmiijɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaf tips on lower leaves mean your maize crop lacks nitrogen, which gives plants their green color and leaf strength. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure restores plant health.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa baai eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛaawo mli lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines produce bigger tubers when I stake them with tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ naa bulbs wuji beni mikɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ shwieɔ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp soil into the sun and prevents fungal leaf diseases from spread.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking woɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ kɛyaa hulu la mli ni ehaa fungal leaf helai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: What is eating ragged holes in the leaves of my corn plants and leaving dark dust inside the center whorl?
ga: Mɛni ji mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe ŋmeii ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ ni ayeɔ ni ashiɔ sũ ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the growing point of the stalk. Applying recommended organic or chemical insecticides directly into the plant whorl early in the morning controls them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ he ni edara yɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsu nii leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field as my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts capture nitrogen gas from the air and pull it down into the soil. This enriches the soil naturally, helping neighboring or future corn plants grow thicker and healthier.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni egbalaa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ loo wɔsɛɛ be lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my high-yielding hybrid maize crop to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially crossed for high yields in their first planting only. Replanting saved seeds from that harvest results in uneven growth, smaller cobs, and significantly lower yield in the second generation.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ adumɔ kɛ dalɛ ni ejaaa baa. Cob lɛ ji bibioo fe no. ni yibiiwoo lɛ ba shi waa yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: How can I stop my garden soil from drying out too fast when the rains break for a few weeks?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni abɔɔ lɛ mli sũ lɛ akagbi oya tsɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ otsii fioo komɛi?

english: Covering the bare ground around your plant roots with dry grass, corn stalks, or dry leaves—known as mulching—blocks direct sunshine from evaporating moisture and keeps the root zone cool.
ga: Akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ŋmãa tsei, loo baai ni egboi aha hei ni bɛ nɔ ko ni bɔle Root tsei lɛ ahe lɛ. Ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ hulu la ni jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ

english: Why are my tomato flowers drying up and dropping off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too hot or when soil moisture changes suddenly from wet to very dry. Watering plants regularly at the roots and providing light afternoon shade keeps flowers on the plant.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ ni mli egbi waa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe, ni aha lɛ hulutsoo yɛ shwane mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plant twisting up with yellowish-green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies or infected stem cuttings. You can prevent it by planting certified disease-resistant stem varieties and removing infected plants immediately.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Virus ko ni whiteflies bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ni ooodu ni ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa roots grow deep enough to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do I need to cut off the extra small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Ajieɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishi.

english: Those extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and plant food from the main tree. Removing most of them ensures the main plant gets full nutrients to produce big, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso wulu lɛ mli tsei ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni efee tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and soft during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, overly wet conditions. Pruning farm branches and harvesting pods on time improves airflow and keeps the pods dry.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ ni edɔ fe nine lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni afolɔ yɛ be naa kɛ ŋmeii ni akpaa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ mli egbiɔ.

english: Why should I slant my cassava stem cuttings when planting them instead of putting them straight down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-cassava niji lɛ amli kɛji midu amɛ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛhi shi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting stem cuttings at a 45-degree angle helps roots spread out easily near the topsoil, leading to more room for tubers to form and swell.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ 45 degree ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mlɛo. Enɛ haa gbɛ babaoo baa koni bulb lɛ adara ni efuu.

english: Why do I have to cut tall wooden poles for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to make food for the plant. Lifting the vines off the muddy ground keeps leaves healthy, free from rot, and able to produce bigger tubers.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha tso lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ. efiteee ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ yitsei wuji aba

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen. Feeding the soil with compost, manure, or fertilizer restores healthy green growth and helps cobs fill completely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayi obɔ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas in my field help my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Te ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas capture natural nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots, leaving free plant nutrients behind for your next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Shi tso mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn dark brown and rotten before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant lacks calcium or receives irregular water while the fruits are forming.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tso lɛ bɛ calcium loo enine shɛɔ nu nɔ be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifee lɛ.

english: What is making the leaves on my hot pepper plants curl up tightly like little cups?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii?

english: Leaf curl is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites that transmit plant viruses. Spraying plants early with neem oil solution helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni hiɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Akɛ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ tsei lɛ.

english: Why are my garden egg flowers falling off the plants without producing any vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo aduawai ko lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the crop is stressed by dry soil, high temperatures, or a lack of insects like bees to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ ni egbi, latsaa ni naa wa, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that provide the living shade and cool air cocoa needs during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo ni amɛbiɔ kookoo ni yɔɔ fɛ̃i mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize uses to build green leaves and grow strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛfee baai eŋɔli ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmãa ni mli wa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on the sap under the leaf, or a virus spread by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crops very close together so I can get more harvest from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni manyɛ makpa babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stems and very small fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai loo dumɔwui bibii waa baa.

english: Yam plants need their leaves exposed to sunlight to manufacture food for the tubers underground. Staking keeps leaves off the wet ground where they could rot and ensures they catch full sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la kɛha amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baabu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hei ni efɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi yɛ lɛ ahe. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni enáa hulu la ni fa babaoo

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is too hot or dry, or when there are no wind or bees to shake pollen inside the flower to make fruit grow.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ waa. Aloo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo ŋmeii bɛ ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛha aduawai lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How does planting cowpea or groundnuts help make my soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their roots, leaving natural fertilizer behind in the soil for the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Eshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I pour my chemical fertilizer right against the stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer acts like hot salt on fresh plants; touching the stem directly burns the plant tissue and root system instead of feeding the crop slowly.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmei ni mli edɔ yɛ tsei heei anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kpe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, eshãa tso lɛ fãji kɛ shishifãi lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha tso lɛ niyenii fiofio lɛ

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when there is too much rain on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ? Nɛgbɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɔɔ?

english: Waterlogged soil pushes air out of the ground, drowning the plant roots and giving soil fungi the perfect environment to infect and rot the cassava tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. drowning plant roots Ni enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atswa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛfite.

english: Why do insects destroy my stored maize so quickly after I put it in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛwo kotoku mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grains stored while still damp attract standard storage insects and mold. Drying maize completely under the sun until it is hard prevents pests from feeding and breeding inside the bag.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ be mli ni edɔ lolo lɛ baagbala koolooi kɛ ŋmeii kɛba he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa lɛ, no haaa ŋmeii lɛ ana niyenii ni amɛfɔ yɛ kotokui lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them in an open field with full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh sunlight and drying winds during their first two years. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside your cocoa creates a cool canopy that protects the young leaves from burning and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo he lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baa ni buɔ baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower leaves in maize usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient plants need to grow strong green leaves. When nitrogen is low, the plant steals it from older leaves at the bottom to support new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ji eŋɔli. Kɛ nitrogen lɛ faaa Tso lɛ juɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni ekɛ ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ atsu nii.

english: What is eating small holes into the centers of my maize leaves and leaving brown dust behind?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ ŋmãa baa ko teŋ ni eshiɔ sũ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central whorl of the maize plant. Spraying recommended treatments early into the leaf center prevents them from destroying the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsaa hela lɛ shwieɔ shi mra ni ashɛɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baatsi enaa koni ekafite tso lɛ naagbee ni miida lɛ.

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies or by planting infected stem cuttings. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by extension services is the best way to keep your farm healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies loo tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ shwereɔ. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛtsɔ nitsumɔi ni akɛyaa hiɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oha oŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my maize seeds very close together in the same row?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa kome mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together actually reduces your total yield because the plants fight each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients. Giving every plant proper space allows it to produce larger, healthier cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha yibiiwoo lɛ fɛɛ aba shi ejaakɛ tsei lɛ baatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper and tomato plants rot at the stem and die after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excess water sitting in the soil starves plant roots of air and encourages soil-borne fungal diseases to attack the stems. Making raised beds helps water drain away from the root zone, keeping the stems healthy.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni buaa ehe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Saa ni awo nɔ lɛ ni ooofee lɛ baaye abua ni nu lɛ ajɛ shishifã lɛ he. Ha tso lɛ mli awa

english: How can I tell that my underground yam tubers are mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yam plants signal maturity when their leaves and climbing vines turn yellow and naturally dry up. This means the plant has stopped growing leaves and stored all its energy into the tuber below ground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiida kɛji amɛbaai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa baai lɛ akwɛmɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ eto ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: It is best not to replant saved hybrid seeds because they lose their high vigor and disease resistance in the second generation. Buying fresh hybrid seeds each season ensures you get the maximum yield and uniform growth.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu dumɔwui heei ni aŋmala ashwie shi ni ji hybrid lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ helai ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Hybrid dumɔwui heei ni ooohe daa afi lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni onine shɛɔ yibiiwoo babaoo nɔ kɛ dalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my vegetables after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe aduawai yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to take up water and nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Removing weeds early prevents them from stealing food and light from your main crops when they are still young and fragile.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ la kɛjɛ onibii titrii lɛ amli beni amɛji gbekɛbii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ.

english: Why do tiny insects appear in my stored maize grains even when I put them inside bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli. Kɛ mikɛwo kotoku lɛ mli po?

english: Storage weevils often lay microscopic eggs inside the grain while it is still in the field or during drying. Thoroughly drying your grain until it is hard and using airtight storage bags (like PICS bags) suffocates the pests and prevents damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ ŋmaa mli be mli ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo loo be mli ni egbiɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbi dumɔwui lɛ kɛyashi amɛhe wa ni okɛ kotoku ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku) tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaatsi nɔ ni efite lɛ naa.

english: Why is it harmful to burn my bush before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaashã jwɛi dani adu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the natural organic matter and beneficial living organisms in the topsoil that feed your maize. It also leaves the ground dry and exposed, causing heavy rains to wash away valuable topsoil.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ ni haa o-ŋmã lɛ niyenii lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni jara wa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when planted in an open field without trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them provides a natural cover that protects tender leaves from heat and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Yellow leaves are a signal that your crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main food plants use to build healthy leaves, and without it, the plant pulls nutrients from older leaves to keep growing.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛma baai ni wa. Ni kɛji nitrogen bɛ lɛ No lɛ tso lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni eya nɔ eda.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients and weakens the ground. Cowpeas and other beans capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally restoring fertility for your next planting season.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni okɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aku sɛɛ aba kɛha odalɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my seeds fail to grow if I plant right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry, hot spell. If you plant immediately, tender young roots dry out and die before regular, steady rainfall begins to keep the ground continuously moist.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shishifãi bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔ nɛɔ daa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baaje shishi eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that feed on leaf sap and spread plant diseases. This stops the plant from transporting food properly and prevents healthy pepper growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baa mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahelai amɛshwãa lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ aya niyenii jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaaa ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do I need to make mounds of soil when planting cassava or yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afee sũ ŋmɔtɔ beni aduɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni ŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Mounds create loose, well-drained soil that allows tubers to expand without hitting hard earth. Mounding also protects growing tubers from rotting in heavy standing water and keeps roots cool.
ga: Gɔji lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni haa bulbs lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni enaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ. Pile lɛ hu buɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite yɛ nu ni damɔ shi ni tsii mli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to give low yields even when I use fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Weeds have strong root systems that steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight before your crops can use them. This starves your crop plants, leaving them weak and unable to produce full harvests.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye onibii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkpa amɛ yibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to manufacture energy to grow big underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground into direct sunlight and protects them from damp soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ kɛya hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. ni etsĩ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ naa

english: Why do my tomato seedlings wilt and die after I move them from the nursery to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Moving seedlings shocks their roots. If you transplant during the hot midday sun, seedlings lose moisture faster than roots can take it up. Transplanting in the late afternoon gives roots overnight to settle into moist soil.
ga: Kɛ́ otsi dumɔwu lɛ, ebaaha eshishifãi lɛ akpokpo. Kɛji akɛ okɛwo shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ aduɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ nɔ nyɔɔŋ kome.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. The plant moves nitrogen from its older leaves to feed the new top leaves, showing that it needs compost or fertilizer to grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni ekɛya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my land yield less maize if I plant maize on the exact same plot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo kɛji midu ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Maize pulls the same specific nutrients from the soil every season. Planting the same crop repeatedly exhausts those nutrients and allows pests that attack maize to build up in the soil.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ asɛɛ afo. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I burn the dry leaves and cleared weeds on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa baai ni egbi ni mikɛ jwɛi shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys rich organic matter that feeds the soil. Leaving cleared leaves to rot creates a natural blanket that cools the ground, holds rainwater, and feeds your crops over time.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii babaoo ni haa sũ lɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni baai ni he tse lɛ fite lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi, ni ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. Large shade trees protect delicate young cocoa leaves from drying out and keep the surrounding air humid during hot seasons.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo ni amɛbuɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi. ni ekwɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees yield fewer pods when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too closely, their branches block sunlight from reaching inner leaves and trap damp air, which prevents healthy pod growth and encourages diseases like black pod.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsoi aniji tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ baai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe ni amɛmɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ adara, ni ewoɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ ahe hewalɛ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the young suckers growing at the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Too many suckers compete directly with the main plant for soil nutrients and water. Keeping only two or three strong suckers ensures the mother plant has enough energy to produce heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo plantain tsei babaoo.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with thick green leaves, but giving me very small roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi ani eyɛ shishifãi bibii waa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or the area is too shady, cassava puts all its energy into producing foliage above ground instead of storing starch in its roots below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo he ni eyɔɔ lɛ mli ewo hulutsoo tsɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmãa baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat or water stress. Keeping the soil cool with mulch and watering regularly helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they turn into peppers.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants rot on the ground if I don't tie them to wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ fĩii tsei ahe lɛ?

english: Tomato stems are weak and bend under the weight of fruit. Tying them up keeps leaves and fruits off the wet soil, preventing soil-borne fungal diseases and allowing better airflow.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkotoɔ yɛ aduawai lɛ ashishi. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ fĩ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai kɛ aduawai lɛ akajɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my cowpea plants rot and turn yellow after heavy rainwater stays on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ miifite ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Crop roots need to breathe air in the soil just like leaves need light. When water sits trapped on the farm, it drowns the root system, causing roots to rot and the plant to die.
ga: Ehe miihia ni tsei shishifãi lɛ amu kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Taakɛ baai he hiaa la lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ nu ŋmɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Nu baaha shishifãi lɛ abɔ he. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gboɔ ni tso lɛ gboɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my green maize plants turning yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is its main food for growing green. When nitrogen in the soil runs low, the plant takes food from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni akɛhaa tsei eŋɔlii ni kwɛɔ lɛ Beni nitrogen fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha tsei heei ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is my corn producing flowers at the top but no actual corn cobs are forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmãa ko bɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: This happens when corn experiences strong dry heat or lacks water right at the time it flowers. Without enough water, the silk on the young cob dries up too fast and cannot catch the pollen from the top flowers to form seeds.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ ŋmãa lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa, egbi loo nu faaa yɛ emli be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛji nu bɛ Siliki ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya tsɔ ni enyɛɛɛ emɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ ni ekɛfee dumɔwui.

english: Why do my crop plants grow thin and tall with very small yields when I put many seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ ni ekwɛɔ shi ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo fata bu kome he lɛ?

english: Plants behave like farm animals sharing one bowl of food. When planted too close together, they fight for sunshine, water, and soil nutrients, forcing them to grow tall to reach light instead of building strong stems and fruits.
ga: Tsei feɔ amɛnii tamɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni jaa niyenii yɛ tsɛnsi kome mli. Kɛji adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ anyɛ amɛnɔ koni amɛdara koni amɛná la moŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii kɛ aduawai ni wa baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tightly and making the plant stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni ehaa tso lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ lɛ?
