english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or mites hiding under the leaves. They suck out the leaf juices and pass on plant sicknesses, causing the leaves to twist up and stop making energy for new fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛmuɔ baa nu ni amɛhaa tsei ahe helai baa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛkpaa hewalɛ ni amɛnáa kɛhaa aduawai heei lɛ.

english: Why is my farm producing far less corn today than it used to harvest years ago on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ miiwo ŋmãa fioo kwraa ŋmɛnɛ fe bɔ ni akpa afii ni eho nɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Soil gets tired and hungry when the same crop is grown on it year after year without rest or fertilizer. The crops take out nutrients every season, and if those nutrients are not replaced, the soil becomes weak and yields drop.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi ni hejɔɔmɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii akawo mli. Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ daa be mli. Ni kɛji akɛ atsakeee nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots go soft and rot inside the ground when heavy rains stay on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When heavy rain leaves standing water around the roots for days, it drowns the roots and creates the perfect wet condition for soil fungi to attack and rot the crop.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ he fɛɛ he. shishifãi gbii babaoo Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mli edɔ baa koni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ atutua ni amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Beans and groundnuts are special plants that can trap invisible plant food from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that stored food remains in the soil to feed the next crop you plant there.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ tsei aniyenii ni anaaa kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai niyenii ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do tiny beetles start eating holes into my dry corn cobs a few weeks after I store them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ bɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ yeli beni mikɛto otsii fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: These insects, called grain weevils, often lay tiny unseen eggs on the corn while it is still in the field. Once you harvest and store the grain in a warm room, those eggs hatch into tiny bugs that feed on the inside of the seed.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ akɛ ŋmaa ŋmeii. Bei pii lɛ, ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii. Anaaa yɛ ŋmãa nɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Beni okpaa dumɔwui lɛ ni okɛtoɔ tsu ko ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Nakai wuji lɛ baatsɔ kooloi bibii. ni yeɔ dumɔwui amli

english: Why does my harvested corn turn black and fuzzy with powder when I store it during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ akɛto yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: That fuzzy powder is mold caused by dampness. If corn is not dried fully in the sun before being packed away, trapped moisture allows mold to grow on the cobs, which damages the grain and makes it unsafe for people or animals to eat.
ga: Baking soda ji ŋmei ni fɛ̃i kɛbaa. Kɛji akɛ agbiko ŋmãa lɛ yɛ hulu mli dani akɛwo ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ, Trapped moisture baaha ŋmãa akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni ehaaa gbɔmɛi loo kooloi aye amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the seeds I save from last year's big corn cobs produce smaller plants than the packet seeds I buy from the agricultural store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa wuji lɛ amli lɛ woɔ tsei bibii fe dumɔwui ni awo mli ni miheɔ yɛ okwaayeli shwapo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are specially bred from two strong parent plants to give a single powerful harvest. Seeds saved from that harvest lose that special mix of strength, resulting in weaker second-generation plants with smaller cobs.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ woɔ nyɛ tsei enyɔ ni he wa mli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ be kome mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ hewalɛ krɛdɛɛ ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ayinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight and burn easily. Planting tall, broad-leaf crops like plantains next to them provides shade and traps soil moisture, protecting the cocoa plants during their first few years.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛshãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ baai babaoo tamɔ plantains yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow at the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛnaagbee lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaf tips on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding a nitrogen-based fertilizer or rich compost helps the leaves regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting underground after a heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long because the roots cannot get air and start to suffocate. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛbɔi ŋmɔlɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli.

english: Why are flowers falling off my tomato plants without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when the soil gets too dry between waterings. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulch helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the sap under the leaves. Spraying the plants with a mild neem oil solution or soap spray helps clear the insects so leaves grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Neem fɔ ni mli ejɔ ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ Loo samla ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ koni eye ebua ni ajie kooloi bibii kɛjɛ mli koni baai lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over before the fruit is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ miigbee shi dani aduawai lɛ baafee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots, so when the heavy fruit bunch grows, the plant becomes top-heavy and can easily tip over in strong wind. Propping up the main stem with sturdy bamboo poles supports the heavy weight until harvest.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ aduawai ni tsii lɛ akuu lɛ dara lɛ Tso lɛ tsii ni ebaanyɛ efo mlɛo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni mli wa to tso titri lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsɔne ni tsii lɛ kɛyashi ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to use tall wooden stakes for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni mi-sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread out in full sunlight to create energy for big tubers to grow underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground, which gives them more sunlight and prevents leaf diseases caused by damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo koni ekɛfee hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛ bulbs wuji akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha hulu la babaoo aba ni ebaatsi foliar hela ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Groundnut plants produce flowers above ground, but once pollinated, the stems naturally push into the soil so the nuts can grow safely underground. Keeping the surrounding soil soft and loose makes it easier for the stems to burrow.
ga: Peanut tsei woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ akɛ pollin wo mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ fee blɛoo ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ebaaha efee mlɛo aha ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my okra pods becoming very hard and woody instead of soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra ŋmɔji lɛ wa ni amɛfee tamɔ tso moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee blɛoo lɛ?

english: Okra pods turn hard and woody when left on the plant too long after forming. Harvesting the pods every two to three days while they are still small and snap easily keeps them soft and tasty.
ga: Roselle ŋmeii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni efeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ be mli ni ebɔi lɛ sɛɛ. Ni oootsi ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ Gbii enyɔ loo etɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo ni amɛkumɔ waaa lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ afee blɛoo ni ehi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are black spots spreading across my cocoa pods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji jeɔ kpo yɛ kookoo ŋmeii anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black spots on cocoa pods are caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads rapidly in cool, wet weather. Pruning extra tree branches allows sunlight and air to dry out the pods and stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpods ji nɔ ni kɛ helai diji ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ mli lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my imported rice seeds produce lower yields than expected when planted in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ baa lɛ baa shi fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ kɛ́ adu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Imported seeds are often bred for specific climates and high-tech inputs. When exposed to local heat, soil conditions, and humidity in Ghana, their performance drops unless they are adapted or handled with precise fertilization and water management.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afɔɔ dumɔwui ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni he esa waa. Kɛji akɛ ajie lɛ kpo yɛ maŋ lɛ mli latsaa, shikpɔŋ kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛ mli yɛ Ghana. bɔ ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ baa shi ja atsake loo akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu he gbɛjianɔtoo

english: Why do my rice plants grow to different heights and mature at different times in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ daa kɛyashɛɔ hei srɔtoi kɛ bei srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: This usually happens when seeds from different varieties get mixed together or when land isn't properly leveled. Un-leveled land causes uneven water distribution, making some plants grow faster than others.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi amli lɛ futu loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etseee jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tseee lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mlijaa ni ejaaa baa. Enɛ haa tsei komɛi daraa oya fe ekrokomɛi.

english: Why are my rice leaves turning yellow while the crop is still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ shi tso lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for food, specifically nitrogen. It can also mean the field has bad drainage or the soil is too dry, preventing the roots from drinking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ji niyenii bolɔmɔ. titri lɛ nitrogen Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ hu akɛ nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ anu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: What causes my rice stalks to fall flat on the ground right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi ŋmãa toi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ dani akpaa?

english: This is called lodging. It happens when stalks grow too thin due to applying too much nitrogen fertilizer, planting seeds too close together, or heavy winds hitting wet soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ wɔɔhe. Ebaa beni tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo tsɔ yɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ hewɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Aloo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some heads on my rice plants end up empty without any grains inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei komɛi efee efolo ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty grains, or 'chaffiness,' happen when the rice plant experiences heat stress, severe drought, or pest attacks while it is flowering and trying to form grains.
ga: Omɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko loo ‘chaff’ baa kɛji omɔ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. hɔmɔ ni naa wa Loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa lɛ beni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛfee ŋmaa.

english: Why do my rice grains develop dark spots on them while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Dark spots are caused by fungal diseases that thrive in warm, humid weather, or by insects sucking sap from young grains while they are soft and milky.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni yaa hiɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ black spot baa. aloo kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ dumɔwui bibii amli nu lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ mliki lɛ nɔ

english: Why does my harvested rice break into small pieces when it goes through the milling machine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi bibii bibii kɛ́ atsɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Rice breaks during milling if it was dried too fast in harsh sunlight, cracked before milling, or if the milling machine is poorly maintained or set to the wrong tension.
ga: Omɔ fãa yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ egbi oya tsɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Egbɛ eshwa dani awo lɛ pɛnte Aloo kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ tsɔne lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ loo atsake tsɔne lɛ mli tsɔne lɛ mli yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: Does drying my harvested rice directly on bare ground lower its market quality?
ga: Ani mikpamɔ lɛ ni mikɛgbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha ejarayeli lɛ aba shi?

english: Yes. Drying directly on the ground introduces dirt, small stones, and moisture from the soil, which spoils the appearance, damages processing machines, and lowers the selling price.
ga: Hɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni egbiɔ lɛ haa muji, tɛi bibii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa. ni fiteɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ ni ekɛ tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa jara ni akɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does locally grown rice sometimes have a different look and feel compared to foreign rice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ srɔto yɛ maŋsɛɛ ŋmãa he, ni enuɔ he ehaa lɛ?

english: Differences come down to the seed variety, proper parboiling techniques, and modern milling equipment. Better milling machines remove the outer husk cleanly without scratching or breaking the grain.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔ lɛ damɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ anɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ ashɛreɔ la kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nibii ni akɛfeɔ mfoniri Mli ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baajie kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ kwraa ni ekɛ ŋmei lɛ efoŋ loo efoŋ.

english: Will using a mechanical thresher damage my harvested rice crop compared to beating it manually?
ga: Ani tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ baafite ŋmãa tsei ni mikpa lɛ kɛ akɛto ŋmãa ni akɛ niji shwieɔ nɔ lɛ he?

english: Modern threshers actually protect your grain quality better than manual beating. Manual beating on barrels cracks grains and mixes in dirt, while a good thresher gently separates grains cleanly.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ ŋmaa lɛ buɔ oŋmaa lɛ he jogbaŋŋ fe bɔ ni akɛ niji shwieɔ ŋmaa lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ oniji tswa ŋmãa lɛ, efãa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekɛ muji futuɔ mli. Yɛ be mli ni tsɔne kpakpa ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ baajara dumɔwui lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ fiofio lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and burn when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiitswa kɛji mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni ebɔle mihe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong direct sunlight. Leaving taller trees or planting plantains around them provides essential shade and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa is young and vulnerable.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. tsei kakadaji ni ajieɔ loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he lɛ Tsei lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná ŋmɔlɔ ni he hiaa ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight for their leaves. When the leaves get plenty of sun, they produce food that travels down into the soil to make the yam tuber grow big and heavy.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha amɛbaa lɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la babaoo Ehaa niyenii ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛhe afee shwiili.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil runs out of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build healthy green leaves. Adding fertilizer or well-rotted manure restores this nutrient and turns the plants dark green again.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ba shi. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ aku sɛɛ aba, ni ebaaha tso lɛ aku sɛɛ afee eŋɔli ni mli edɔ.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts make my land better for my next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies and rots into the ground, it leaves that natural plant food in the soil for the next crop to use.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei gboi ni amɛgboi kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Eshiɔ nakai adebɔɔ mli tsei niyenii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?
